the Emperor led his generals into the city,
and officials and common people lined the streets, shouting "Long live!"
Beile Jí'ěrhāláng and Sàhālián guarded Yǒngpíng.
The surrendered official Bái Yǎngcuì was appointed as the Governor of Yǒngpíng,
and Mèng Qiáofāng and Yáng Wénkuí as Vice-Generals.
Villagers were allowed to return to their homes.
On this day,
the Emperor led the grand army towards Shānhǎiguān.
Troops from the Àohàn, Nàimàn, Bālín, and Zhālǔtè tribes attacked Chānglí,
but failed to capture it.
Tái Tóuyíng, Ānshānbǎo, Qiān'ān, and Luánzhōu surrendered one after another.
Mǎ Guāngyuǎn, the Assistant Commander of Jiànchāng, defected.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Ming troops attacked Zūnhuà,
and Beile Dùdù defeated them.
Ming troops entered Sāntúnyíng,
and the previously surrendered Hàn'érzhuāng, Xǐfēngkǒu, Pānjīakǒu, and Hóngjiākǒu revolted again.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Dáhǎi and others recaptured Hàn'érzhuāng,
and Beile Ābātài guarded it.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Kālāqìn Bù'ěrgǎdū was besieged by Ming troops,
and an army was dispatched to rescue him.
Before it arrived,
Bù'ěrgǎdū himself defeated them.
The commander, Ming Minister of War Liú Zhīlún, arrived with troops,
and erected barricades.
Our army's cannons destroyed their barricades.
Liú Zhīlún was stationed in the mountains.
Great Beile Dàishàn besieged him,
and urged Liú Zhīlún to surrender,
but he refused.
His camp was broken,
and Liú Zhīlún died from an arrow.
On the *rén'yín* day,
the army moved to Mǎlányù,
and destroyed the fortified villages near the city.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Kālāqìn Sūbùdì wrote a letter to the Ming Emperor,
discussing the benefits of peace and goodwill,
and also urging him to cherish and nurture the border people and show compassion to vassal states.
There was no reply.
Lè tíng revolted again.
In the second month, on the *xīnhài* day, the first day of the lunar month,
the Beile and various officials were instructed:
“All generals and soldiers who have shown bravery and rendered meritorious service
should be excused from the task of attacking cities.”
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the surrendered Ming general Má Dēngyún and others were feasted in the imperial tent.
The Emperor said to them:
“Your Ming lord regards the lives of you generals and soldiers as mere grass and dust,
driving you to your deaths.
I have repeatedly sent envoys to discuss peace,
yet there has not been a single word in reply,
why is this?”
Má Dēngyún replied:
“The Ming Emperor is young and inexperienced,
and the ministers each seek to protect themselves.
If the matter of peace talks
is not heard,
the guilt would be immeasurable,
thus they are afraid and dare not report it.”
The Emperor said:
“If that is the case,
then Heaven assists me,
how can I abandon this and return?
However, stationing troops and garrisoning them
would impede the farming season, which is regrettable.
Moreover, their defenses at Shānhǎiguān and Jǐnzhōu are still strong,
so for now, we should only seize the undefended cities and towns.”
On the *jǐwèi* day,
a letter was sent to the Ming Emperor,
reiterating the plea for peace and goodwill,
and also sending letters to various Ming officials,
urging them to quickly finalize peace talks.
By this point, seven letters had been sent in total.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Wáng Shìxuǎn, the Vice-General of Yúlín in Ming, surrendered.
The Emperor returned with the army.
Beile Ābātài, Jí'ěrhāláng, Sàhālián, and civil officials Suǒní, Níng Wánwǒ, etc., guarded Yǒngpíng;
Bào Chéngxiān guarded Qiān'ān;
Gūshān Èzhēn Tú'ěrgé, Nàmùtài, etc., guarded Luánzhōu;
Chákālā, Fàn Wénchéng, etc., guarded Zūnhuà.
The army was stationed in Luán for three days,
where merits were discussed and rewards bestowed.
On the *rénshēn* day,
an edict stated:
“Heaven has granted us the land and people of Ming;
their people are our people,
so soldiers should be ordered not to harm them,
and violators will be punished.”
When the Emperor arrived at Yǒngpíng,
the surrendered official Lángzhōng Chén Cǐxīn planned to escape;
the matter was discovered, and he was sentenced to beheading.
The Emperor pardoned him,
allowing him to go wherever he wished.
In the third month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
the Emperor returned to Shěnyáng.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the two Beile Āmǐn and Beile Shuòtuō led five thousand troops to guard the four cities of Yǒngpíng,
and Beile Ābātài and others returned.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the four sons' tribes of Ālǔ sent envoys to form an alliance.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
Ming troops attacked Luánzhōu,
but failed to capture it.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Beile Ābātài, Jí'ěrhāláng, and others returned from Yǒngpíng.
The Emperor asked whether the captives obtained in this campaign were more numerous than before.
They replied:
“A great many people were captured on this expedition.”
The Emperor said:
“Wealth and silk are not cause for joy;
only obtaining many people is truly joyful.”
In the fifth month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
an edict was issued to the ministers to treat the surrendered population kindly.
On the day Rénchén,
Āmǐn, Shuòtuō and others abandoned the four cities of Yǒngpíng and returned.
At that time, Míng supervising censor Zhāng Chūn and Jǐnzhōu commander Zǔ Dàshòu and others combined their forces to attack Luánzhōu.
Nàmùtài, Tú'ěrgé, Tānggǔdài and others sallied forth to battle,
repeatedly defeating the Míng forces.
However, their troops were few,
and Āmǐn and Shuòtuō, fearing, did not go to their aid.
The Míng forces used cannons to attack Luánzhōu,
and Nàmùtài and others could not hold out.
They abandoned the city and fled to Yǒngpíng.
Just then, it rained heavily,
and our army broke out of the encirclement.
Over four hundred men who had no horses or were wounded died.
Āmǐn and Shuòtuō, hearing this, were afraid,
and so they killed the surrendered officials Bái Yǎngcuì and others,
massacred all the soldiers and civilians in the city,
collected their gold and currency,
and departed through Lěngkǒu overnight.
Cháhālā and others also abandoned Zūnhuà and returned.
The Emperor had just ordered Bèilè Dùdù to proceed to Yǒngpíng to assist in its defense,
and had also enjoined Āmǐn to treat the officials and people well,
without aggression or violence,
and was preparing to personally lead troops there.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
upon hearing that Āmǐn had abandoned the city,
and had moreover committed a great massacre,
he stopped his preparations.
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
the generals who had abandoned the cities were arrested and imprisoned,
and their crimes were enumerated.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Āmǐn's sixteen crimes were publicly declared in court.
The assembly agreed he should be executed.
The Emperor could not bear to apply the law,
so he imprisoned him.
Shuòtuō, Tānggǔdài, Nàmùtài, Bābùtài, Tú'ěrgé and others were all stripped of their noble titles and dismissed from their posts, with varying degrees of punishment.
Among the generals, those who had fought bravely and killed enemies were released.
Earlier, after Āmǐn had massacred the officials and people of Yǒngpíng,
he had distributed their wives and children to the soldiers.
The Emperor said:
"He has already massacred our loyal surrendered people,
and now he is enslaving their wives and children! "
He ordered them to be registered as civilian households,
and to be provided with houses, clothing, and food.
In autumn, the ninth month, on the day Wùxū,
an edict was reiterated to all ministers and Mǎn-Hàn officials to diligently perform their duties.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
an edict was issued to register and review the able-bodied men in each banner,
and those who concealed them would be punished.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
Hǔ'ěrgá of Nàkāntài's部 led his family to surrender,
and the Bèilè from the four sons'部 of Ālǔ also came to surrender.
On the day Rén Yín,
the Ālǔ Yīsūtè部, hearing that the Emperor treated the people well,
left their部 at the Xīlāmùlún River,
and accompanied our envoy Cháhàn Lāma to pay homage.
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùchén,
Kē'ěrqìn Bèilè Túměiwèizhēng came to pay homage.
In the fifth year, spring, the first month, on the day Gēngchén,
an edict was issued that for deceased meritorious officials who had no heirs,
their family property should be given to their wives for their own sustenance.
On the day Rénwǔ,
a large red-barreled cannon was cast,
and inscribed with "
Heaven's Aid and Might Grand General " .
The manufacturing of cannons in the army began from this time.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Éfù Tóng Yǎngxìng was appointed to oversee all military and civilian affairs of the Han people,
and Han officials were placed under his command.
On the day Jǐhài,
the Emperor visited the Wénguǎn (Literary Hall),
entered Kù'ěrtī Zhífáng's office,
and asked what book he was compiling.
He replied:
"A record of the administrative affairs that have taken place."
The Emperor said:
"In that case,
it is not appropriate for me to view it."
He also reviewed the Wǔquán (Military Treatises) translated by Dáhǎi,
and saw the story of 'pouring out liquor and drinking from the river' (投醪飲河),
and said:
"Ancient good generals cared for their soldiers,
and the soldiers of the three armies were happy to fight to the death for them.
If Éfù Gù Sāntái, when facing the enemy,
sees fallen warriors,
and drags them back with a rope,
how can he gain the desperate efforts of his men! "
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Cháoxiǎn's tribute goods were insufficient,
so they were rejected,
and a letter was sent to denounce their fault.
In the second month, on the day Gēngshēn,
border officials were ordered to be vigilant in their scouting.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Méng'ātú campaigned against Wǎ'ěrkā,
and reported victory.
In the third month, on the first day Yǐhài,
the Gùshān Ézhēn and Éfù Gù Sāntái of the Bordered Blue Banner were dismissed,
and Piāngǔdài, the son of Tàizǔ's younger brother, was appointed in his place.
A letter was sent to the Great Bèilè Dàishàn, the Third Bèilè Mǎnggǔ'ěrtài, and the Bèilè and other ministers,
asking for their frank criticism of mistakes.
On the day Dīnghài,
the Han troops were reviewed.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the families of Liú Xīngzuò and Xīngzhì were executed,
but their mother was pardoned.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Cháoxiǎn again sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Mǎndá'ěrhàn and Dǒngnènmì were sent to secretly deliver a letter to the King of Cháoxiǎn,
demanding warships to assist in attacking Míng.
This was not granted.
In the sixth month, on the day Guǐhài,
the regulations for hereditary official posts for meritorious officials were established.
The five chieftains from Hēilóngjiāng, Yīzhànè, Sàkètí, Jiāqīnnè, Élìkā, and Kāngzhù, came to pay homage.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Jiǎxū,
four chieftains from Hēilóngjiāng's Hǔ'ěrhā部 came to pay tribute.
On the day Gēngchén,
the Six Boards were first established.
Mòlègēndàiqīng Bèilè Duō'ěrgǔn,
Bèilè Dégélèi, Sàhǎlián, Yuètā, Jí'ěrhǎláng, Ābātài and others were put in charge of the Six Boards.
For each board, Mǎn, Hàn, and Ménggǔ officials were separately appointed as Chéngzhèngguān,
and below them, eight Cānzhèng (counselors) were appointed for each,
and one Qǐxīnláng (adviser) for each.
Bākèshí was changed to Bǐtiēshì,
but those still called Bākèshí retained their old title.
The rule that allowed those who accused Bèilè to leave their masters was revised,
and those who made accusations about minor matters were prohibited.
An edict was issued that Bèilè who unjustly judged cases would be punished.
The law of uniformly stripping guilty officials of their posts was abolished;
henceforth, those who committed crimes
would be punished with varying degrees of severity.
Marriage between officials and commoners of the same clan was also prohibited,
and offenders, male and female, would be treated as adulterers.
An edict was also issued to Bèilè and other ministers to reflect on their faults and change their conduct,
and to seek strong admonition.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
four chieftains from Nàoléihǔ'ěrhā部 came to pay tribute.
On the day Guǐsì,
regulations for rewards and punishments for minor matters were established,
requiring Niúlù Ézhēn to handle them,
while major ones were sent to the Boards.
Míng commander Zǔ Dàshòu and others built fortifications at Dàlínghé.
All the Měnggǔ (Mongols) were summoned to lead their respective部s to join the campaign.
On the day Jǐhài,
the main army set out westward,
and Bèilè Dùdù, Sàhǎlián, and Háogé were ordered to remain behind to guard.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the Liáohé River was crossed,
and generals were again warned to care for their soldiers.
On the *rén'yín* day of the eighth month, which was the first day of the month,
the troops encamped by the old Liáohé River.
Various Měnggǔ tribes brought their forces to join.
On the *guǐ'mǎo* day,
all the Měnggǔ *bèilè* were assembled,
and the previous order was reiterated:
no unauthorized killing or looting.
Thereupon, the army was divided into two routes.
The *bèilè* Dégélèi, Yuètuō, and Ājígé led twenty thousand troops from Yìzhōu to garrison between Jǐnzhōu and Dàlínghé,
while the Emperor himself entered Guǎngníng from Báitǔchǎng.
On the *dīng'wèi* day,
the forces met at Dàlínghé
and attacked the city by night.
The order was:
"Attacking the city might harm our soldiers.
We should dig trenches and build ramparts to besiege it.
If they sally forth,
we will fight them;
if external reinforcements arrive,
we will intercept and attack them."
So, the Eight Banners' soldiers were divided to encircle the city,
and the Měnggǔ soldiers were ordered to exploit any openings.
On the *xīn'hài* day,
five hundred Míng cavalry and infantry sallied from the city.
Dá'ěrhā defeated them.
On the *rén'zǐ* day,
letters were shot into the city,
inviting Měnggǔ people to surrender.
On the *guǐ'chǒu* day,
Míng troops sallied from the city to provoke battle.
Túlái advanced first,
followed by Dá'ěrhā.
They attacked from all four sides,
and *bèilè* Duō'ěrgǔn also led his troops in.
Cannons and arrows were fired from within the city.
Túlái was wounded,
and Vice-Generals Mèngdàntán and Túnbùlù, Defense Commander Duōbèi, and Imperial Guard Gēlǐ were killed in action.
The Emperor severely reprimanded
Túlái and others for their reckless advance.
Using red-coated cannons to attack the Míng platforms,
soldiers surrendered one after another.
On the *yǐ'mǎo* day,
a letter was sent to Zǔ Dàshòu, which said:
"Previously, I wished for peace,
but your country's ruler and officials took Sòng as a warning
and did not respond to me.
Your country is not Sòng,
and I am not Jīn.
Why are you so obstinate?
Now I am weary of warfare,
and I send this letter again;
General, please decide."
Dàshòu did not reply.
On the *dīng'sì* day,
two thousand Míng soldiers from Sōngshān came to reinforce,
but Āshān, Láosà, and Tǔlúshí defeated them.
On the *jiǎ'zǐ* day,
*bèilè* Ājígé and Shuòtuō intercepted and attacked Míng reinforcements.
On the *dīng'mǎo* day,
six thousand Míng Jǐnzhōu soldiers came to attack Ājígé's camp.
A great fog enveloped the area,
making it impossible to recognize faces.
Suddenly, a blue vapor rushed towards the enemy camp,
opening like a gate.
Our army advanced through the fog,
fought a great battle,
and defeated them,
capturing one guerrilla commander
and seizing all their armor, weapons, and horses.
On the *xīn'wèi* day,
the Emperor visited *bèilè* Ājígé's camp
and offered golden goblets of wine to reward the generals.
Míng troops suddenly sallied forth.
Our forces counterattacked
and again utterly defeated them.
On the *dīng'hài* day of the ninth month,
the Emperor led troops towards Jǐnzhōu.
Seeing dust rising,
the Emperor ordered all armies to halt.
He personally led two hundred Bǎiyálà soldiers,
and with *bèilè* Duōduó, stealthily advanced along the mountains.
Seven thousand Míng Jǐnzhōu soldiers suddenly sallied forth and advanced upon the Emperor.
The Emperor had just donned his armor;
his followers numbered fewer than two hundred.
They crossed the river and charged the enemy.
The enemy could not withstand them
and scattered.
The main army arrived subsequently
and inflicted another great defeat,
beheading one vice-general before returning.
On the *jǐ'chǒu* day,
another letter was sent to Zǔ Dàshòu.
On the *gēng'yín* day,
the Emperor set an ambush in the mountains,
hoping to lure Dàshòu out
and capture him.
Dàshòu was alarmed and fled,
and from then on, he kept the city gates closed.
At this time, there were only a hundred *shí* of grain left in the city,
all the horses had died,
and their meat was boiled for food,
with saddles used as fuel.
On the *yǐ'wèi* day,
Zhāng Chūn, Supervisor of the Army and Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud,
and Grand Generals Wú Xiāng and Zhōng Wěi, etc.,
arrived with forty thousand cavalry and infantry as reinforcements,
and encamped by Xiǎolínghé.
On the *wù'xū* day,
the Míng reinforcements advanced towards Dàlínghé,
fifteen *lǐ* from the city.
The Emperor led cavalry from both wings to charge them,
but they held their ground.
The right wing suddenly broke into Zhāng Chūn's camp,
and the enemy was then defeated.
Wú Xiāng and Vice-General Sāng'ā'ěrzhài fled first.
Zhāng Chūn and others reassembled the routed soldiers and set up camp again.
A great wind arose,
and the enemy used the wind to set fires,
which were about to reach our army.
Suddenly, it rained,
the wind reversed,
and battle was rejoined.
They were then utterly routed,
and Zhāng Chūn and thirty-three vice-generals were captured alive.
Zhāng Chūn remained unyielding
and begged for death,
but the Emperor pardoned him.
In this battle,
Zǔ Dàshòu still thought we were luring the enemy,
so there was no response from within the city.
That night, Hēi Yúnlóng fled.
On the *dīng'wèi* day of the tenth month in winter,
letters were sent to Zǔ Dàshòu, Hé Kěgāng, and Zhāng Cúnrén, inviting them to surrender.
On the *jǐ'yǒu* day,
another letter was sent to Dàshòu.
On the *rén'zǐ* day,
red-coated cannons were used to attack Yú Zǐzhāng's platform.
The platform was extremely fortified,
but after three days, it was destroyed.
The defending general Wáng Jǐng surrendered,
whereupon more than a hundred platforms, near and far, all fell.
On the *jiǎ'yín* day,
the surrendered general Jiāng Xīn was sent to persuade Zǔ Dàshòu.
Dàshòu also sent guerrilla commander Hán Dòng to meet.
On the *guǐ'hài* day,
the matter of the Third *bèilè* Mǎnggǔ'ěrtài drawing a blade before the Emperor was deliberated.
He was demoted from *bèilè*
and deprived of five *niú'lù* under his command.
On the *yǐ'chǒu* day,
Zǔ Dàshòu arranged for our Vice-General Shí Tíngzhù to discuss surrender.
On the *bǐng'yín* day,
Dàshòu sent his son Kěfǎ as a hostage.
On the *wù'chén* day,
the entire city of Dàlínghé surrendered,
but only Vice-General Hé Kěgāng refused.
Dàshòu took Kěgāng by the arm to the front of the army and had him executed.
That night, Dàshòu arrived at the imperial camp.
The Emperor treated him with great favor,
and Dàshòu then offered a strategy to capture Jǐnzhōu.
On the *jǐ'sì* day,
troops were sent with Dàshòu for a night attack on Jǐnzhōu.
A great fog arose,
they lost formation,
and returned.
On the *gēng'wǔ* day of the eleventh month, which was the first day of the month,
Dàshòu was allowed to return to Jǐnzhōu.
On the *wù'yín* day,
Dàlínghé city was destroyed.
On the *jǐ'mǎo* day,
the army returned.
On the *yǐ'yǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to Shěnyáng.
On the *bǐng'xū* day,
Cháhā'ěr invaded Ālǔxīlāmùlún territory.
*Bèilè* Sàhālián and Háogé moved their troops to conquer them.
Cháhā'ěr had already departed,
so they returned.
On the *gēng'zǐ* day of the intercalary eleventh month, which was the first day of the month,
an edict stated:
"The abandonment of the four cities of Yǒngpíng by our troops
was due to the lack of learning and skill of the *bèilè* and others.
During the recent Dàlínghé campaign,
people in the city resorted to cannibalism,
yet the Míng people still defended stubbornly.
Even after reinforcements were exhausted and the city surrendered,
Jǐnzhōu, Sōngshān, and Xìngchéng still did not fall.
Is this not because their people read books, understood principles, and were utterly loyal to their lord?
From now on, all sons of age fifteen and below, and above eight years old,
shall be commanded to study."
Kù'ěerchán and others were sent to reproach Cháoxiǎn for violating their agreement.
On the *gēng'xū* day,
private construction of temples and monasteries in the country was forbidden.
Lǎma monks who violated the laws were to be defrocked,
and shamans, diviners, and astrologers were also prohibited.
In the twelfth month, on the day Rénchén,
Assistant Commander Níng Wánwǒ requested the establishment of censorial officials [yánguān]
and the standardization of dress codes [fúzhì].
The Emperor praised and accepted his proposals.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
following the suggestion of Lǐ Bólóng, a participating political official of the Ministry of Rites,
the order of the ranks for morning audiences and ceremonies on New Year's Day was revised.
In the spring of the sixth year, in the first month, on the day Guǐhài,
a review of the Han soldiers was conducted.
In the second month, on the day Rénshēn,
the system of honor guards [yízhàng zhì] was established.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the Emperor paid respects at the Mausoleum of Tàizǔ [Tàizǔ Líng]
and performed the seasonal offering ceremony.
On the day Wùzǐ,
an edict was issued that the city defense officials of Háizhōu and other places should report to Shěnyáng
every three years for inspection.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
an edict was issued to the Ministry of Revenue's Bèi Lè Dégélèi, regarding the distribution of Han people from Dàlínghé to the vice-generals and below,
to be provided for and cared for. The population that had been confiscated from Bèi Lè Mǎnggǔ'ěrtài was returned.
In the third month, on the day Wùxū,
the surrendered generals from Dàlínghé were rewarded differently.
Dáhǎi was ordered to analyze the sounds and meanings of the national script.
On the day Gēngxū,
a law was established for punishing those who accused the various Bèi Lè, with sentences varying according to the severity and truthfulness of the accusations.
It was forbidden for children to accuse their fathers and elder brothers, and for wives to accuse their husbands.
Regulations for offering sacrifices and burials for Bèi Lè and high officials were established.
On the day Dīngsì,
a campaign against Cháhā'ěr was launched.
Mongolian troops were conscripted,
and military orders were issued.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the first day Wùchén,
the Emperor led the grand army westward.
Ābātài, Dùdù, Yánggǔlì, Yī'ěrdēng, and Tóng Yǎngxìng remained to guard.
On the day Jǐsì,
they reached the Liáohé.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
they reached the Xīlāmùlún Hé.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
they reached Zhágǔn Wūdá,
where various Mongolian tribal troops successively joined.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
they reached Hānàyá.
Líndān, the Khan of Cháhā'ěr, heard of the arrival of our army,
and was greatly terrified.
He drove the wealthy commoners and livestock from Guīhuàchéng across the river and fled westward,
abandoning all his baggage train.
On the day Gēngyín,
they reached the Dūlè Hé.
Hearing that Líndān of Cháhā'ěr had fled far away,
the Emperor advanced quickly to Guīhuàchéng.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the grand army returned from Ājígē Hé'ěrgē and marched towards Cháhā'ěr.
In the fifth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
an edict was issued to the various tribal Bèi Lè and officials: "Do not advance lightly,
do not retreat,
do not kill those who surrender,
do not scatter people's wives and children,
do not seize people's clothing and property."
On the day Jiǎchén,
they reached Bùlóngtú Bùlákè.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Láosà reported that Cháhā'ěr had long fled,
and pursuing them for three days yielded no sight of them.
The Emperor turned back his army from Bùlóngtú.
On the day Wùshēn,
a plan to conquer Míng was decided upon.
On the day Bǐngchén,
they reached Zhū'ěrgētǔ.
At this time, provisions ran out,
but suddenly, yellow sheep appeared everywhere in the wilderness.
They surrounded and killed tens of thousands,
dried the meat and ate it.
Without water,
a cup of water was exchanged for one sheep to drink.
The Emperor ordered each niúlù to bring water to supply them.
On the day Gēngshēn,
they reached Mùlúhālàqìn.
Bèi Lè Ājígé led the left wing to raid Xuānfǔ and Dàtóng.
Bèi Lè Jí'ěrhāláng led the right wing to raid Guīhuàchéng.
The Emperor, along with the Great Bèi Lè Dàishàn and Bèi Lè Mǎnggǔ'ěrtài, commanded the main army to follow.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Emperor arrived at Guīhuàchéng,
where the troops from both wings converged.
On this day,
the grand army galloped seven hundred *lǐ*,
reaching as far west as the Mùnàhàn Mountains on the Yellow River,
and as far east as Xuānfǔ.
From Guīhuàchéng south to the Míng border,
the Cháhā'ěr tribal people found in those areas were all captured.
In the sixth month, on the first day Dīngmǎo,
some Mongolian tribal people fled to Shāhé Bǎo.
The Emperor sent a letter to the Míng defending official to demand them.
Míng returned three hundred and twenty men and women and over one thousand four hundred livestock.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Níng Wánwǒ, Fàn Wénchéng, and Mǎ Guózhù jointly submitted a memorial stating:
"Regarding the strategy of attacking Míng,
it is advisable to first negotiate peace in writing.
If they do not comply,
we can use this as a pretext,
and seizing the opportunity, penetrate deep,
and thus achieve our objective."
The Emperor praised and accepted their proposal.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the grand army departed from Guīhuàchéng,
heading towards the Míng border.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the defending official of Míng's Shāhé Bǎo sent an envoy with livestock and silks as tribute.
The Emperor did not accept them.
He again sent a letter to the Míng defending official, saying:
"Kù'ěrchán and others from Déshèng Bǎo,
Aìbālǐ and others from Zhāngjiākǒu,
were dispatched separately to Dàtóng and Xuānfǔ to discuss peace.
The letter states: 'Our raising an army
is not necessarily to seize the Míng empire.
The greedy, corrupt, and ignorant defending officials of Liáodōng
incited Yèhè to insult us,
which led to the Seven Grievances.
We repeatedly appealed to your lord,
but Liáodōng obstructed it from reaching him.
Our army's arrival here
is to make your lord aware of this.
When Fǔshùn was attacked,
because merchants from the thirteen provinces each sent letters,
fearing they might not directly reach,
each submitted a letter to their provincial officials,
hoping for a hearing.
Yet, after allowing them to leave,
there was no response.
As the saying goes: "When the sentiments of the lower ranks reach the top,
the world is never ungoverned;
when the sentiments of the lower ranks are obstructed from reaching the top,
the world is never not in chaos."
Now, campaigns are waged everywhere,
and conflicts are incessant.
People die by the sword and arrow.
While this is due to the obstruction of popular sentiment,
is it perhaps also Heaven's will?
Now we truthfully inform you:
though our nation is small,
we only wish for peace and harmony between our two nations,
to engage in mutual trade,
and each to enjoy peaceful farming and hunting,
thus to enjoy great peace.
If our words are insincere,
may Heaven judge us.
Previously, when we repeatedly sent letters,
expressions of indignation and anger
were certainly unavoidable.
This is common in military affairs,
and not worth mentioning.
We hope you quickly make a decision,
which would truly be a blessing for your nation.
We will station our troops for ten days to await your reply.'"
On the day Gēngchén,
they camped outside the Dàtóng border.
Kù'ěrchán, along with a thousand-commander from Míng's Déshèng Bǎo, brought livestock and silks as tribute.
The Emperor did not accept them.
He again sent a letter to the Míng defending official, saying:
"I respectfully embody Heaven's will,
and wish to establish good relations.
If you truly love your people,
you should quickly decide.
If you delay and do not report back,
even if I wish to wait,
what if the army runs out of provisions?
Regarding the titles in the letter,
let's not discuss them for now.
I humble myself to your nation,
but I can be considered above Cháhā'ěr."
On the day Guǐwèi,
they moved towards Xuānfǔ.
The defending official returned to us the twelve thousand five hundred bolts of Cháhā'ěr satin cloth and furs given by the Míng Emperor.
On the day Gēngyín,
they stationed outside Zhāngjiākǒu,
with camps stretching forty *lǐ*.
On the day Guǐsì,
Míng Provincial Governor Shěn Qǐ and Grand General Dǒng Jìshū sent people with cattle, sheep, and food as tribute.
The Emperor feasted them,
and then peace negotiations were settled.
A great market was held at Zhāngjiākǒu.
Three soldiers from the Kē'ěrqìn tribe secretly entered the Míng border,
stole cattle and donkeys.
The one who had decapitated was executed,
the other two were whipped
and had their ears pierced for public display.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Míng Provincial Governor Shěn Qǐ sent an envoy to request an alliance.
The Emperor ordered high officials Āshídá'ěrhā and others to attend,
sacrificing a white horse and a black ox,
swearing to Heaven and Earth.
After the ceremony, Qǐxīnláng Qí Chōnggé was dispatched to escort the Míng envoy back.
Míng presented gold and silks as tribute.
Imperial Prince Háogé was promoted and conferred the title of Héshuò Bèi Lè.
In this month,
Liáodōng experienced great floods.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *dìngyǒu* day,
a letter was again sent to the defending officials of Zhāngjiākǒu of the Míng, renewing the covenant and good relations,
and assuring them of steadfastness from beginning to end.
It was also stated that the peace negotiations included the Liáodōng region,
and that they should dispatch officials to inform them.
The Emperor led the grand army back.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
they arrived at the Shàngdū River.
As the Míng considered the peace negotiations successful,
they came to present gifts.
These were accepted after deliberation.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the various *bèilè* of Měnggǔ took their leave and returned.
On the *gēngxū* day,
they halted at Băisīhā'ér.
Yóují Bākèshīdáhăi died.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the Emperor returned to Shěnyáng.
In the eighth month, on the *dìngmăo* day,
the Míng scholars Wáng Wénkuí, Sūn Yìngshí, and Jiāng Yún were summoned to the palace,
and asked whether the peace matter had been settled.
All three said
that Míng governance was daily in disarray,
and that peace talks were uncertain.
Moreover, bandits were swarming in the Central Plains,
and the people were scattered and in chaos.
They advised the Emperor to proclaim benevolence and righteousness,
employ the virtuous, nurture the people,
and seize the opportune moment to undertake a punitive expedition,
in response to the will of Heaven.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the six ministries were established,
and each was issued a silver seal.
On the *jiăwŭ* day,
the *gùshān'ézhēn* were ordered to investigate the people's hardships
and to clear up criminal cases.
Cháhā'ěr Tăonàchǔhǔ'ěr came to surrender.
In the ninth month, on the *guǐmăo* day,
Gàizhōu city was repaired,
and people were moved in to populate it.
On the *jiăyín* day,
Hùbù *bèilè* Dégélèi and Bīngbù *bèilè* Yuètūo were ordered to extend the old Yàozhōu boundary southwards to Gàizhōu.
In the tenth month of winter, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Emperor visited Kāiyuán.
On the *jiăxū* day,
he returned to Shěnyáng.
Wèizhēng Nángsūlǎma was dispatched to Níngyuăn,
carrying a letter for the Míng Emperor, which read:
"Our state raising arms
is not out of insatiability or a desire for a greater position,
but because border officials' deception and insults
provoked the hostilities.
When campaigning against Cháhā'ěr,
we passed through Xuānfŭ and settled a peace agreement.
Thereupon, we apprehended and executed those who had trespassed and stolen across the border.
Our sincerity can be said to be utmost.
Previously, the border officials failed to elaborate in detail.
Now, if we wish to state everything,
we fear you might suspect us of not forgetting old grievances.
If you send an envoy,
we will tell him everything.
If you believe peace is already made
and there is no need to speak of past events,
we shall also obey your command."
Another letter was sent to the Míng officials, saying:
"When the defending official of Xuānfŭ made an alliance with us,
he covenanted that we should not invade Liáodōng,
swearing it before Heaven and Earth.
Now you have a different opinion.
Can Heaven be deceived?
The governing ministers should understand expediency and adaptability.
Do not merely engage in grand talk,
thereby missing the opportunity.
If you stubbornly refuse to comply,
you will only bring about military conflict,
and the lives of the people will be utterly devastated.
To whom will the blame fall?"
In the eleventh month, on the *rénchén* day,
the defending official of Níngyuăn of the Míng returned the letter we had sent, sealed,
not daring to present it, and requested it be unsealed.
Permission was granted.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Qítātèchuīhǔ'ěrtáijí, belonging to Ālùbù Dūgè'ěrjìnóng, came to join.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
an envoy was sent to Cháoxiăn to set the annual tribute amount.
In the twelfth month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
regulations for court attire and officials' and commoners' everyday clothing were established.
The third *bèilè*, Mănggǔ'ěrtài, died.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Wúbāhăi sent an envoy to report victory in the campaign against Wùzhálà.
In the first month of spring of the seventh year, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
an edict was issued to the various *niúlù'ézhēn* regarding relieving the poor, instructing farmers, and practicing archery.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Cháoxiăn came to pay tribute,
but it was less than the set amount.
On the *dìngwèi* day,
a letter was sent back to reprimand them.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the Emperor's eldest daughter was married to Táijí Bāndì, son of Àohànbù *bèilè* Dūlál'ěrbātúlŭ.
On the *yǐmăo* day,
the army campaigning against Wùzhálà returned.
In the second month, on the *guǐhài* day,
Ālúkē'ěrqìnhàn Chēgēn, accompanied by Gùkèbātúlŭ and Dá'ěrmădàigùn, brought their entire nation to surrender.
On the *jǐmăo* day,
Kù'ěrzhàn was found guilty of a crime and
executed.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Tŭlúshì, Láosà, and others raided Níngyuăn.
In the third month, on the *dìngyǒu* day,
the four cities of Chăng, Lănpán, Tōngyuǎnbăo, and Xiùyán were constructed.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Táijí Gùkè from Guō'ěrlúosībù came to pay respects at court.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Kŏng Yŏudé and Gěng Zhòngmíng, generals of the former Míng Zŏngbīngmáo Wénlóng, sent envoys to negotiate surrender.
In the fourth month of summer, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
Cháhā'ěrl Yăngyì Dàzŏngguăn Tăshíhăihǔlùkèzhàisāng came to surrender.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Envoy Cānhuà Yīng'é'ěrdài and others were sent to borrow grain from Cháoxiăn to supply Kŏng Yŏudé's army,
but they refused.
In the fifth month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
Wūlàtè Táijí Tŭméndá'ěrhàn and others came to court.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
*Bèilè* Jí'ěrhālā, Ājígé, and Dùdù led troops to welcome Kŏng Yŏudé and Gěng Zhòngmíng at Zhènjiāng,
and ordered them to station their forces in Dōngjīng.
In the sixth month, on the *rénxū* day,
an edict was issued to the officers and soldiers not to harass the newly surrendered people of Liáodōng;
violators would be executed along with their families.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Kŏng Yŏudé and Gěng Zhòngmíng were summoned for an audience
and richly rewarded.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Yīng'é'ěrdài was dispatched to deliver a letter to the King of Cháoxiăn, which read:
"Regarding the previous request for grain,
Your Majesty reasoned that Kŏng Yŏudé and others formerly belonged to the Máo clan,
and it was not right to provide grain to support the enemy.
Now that Kŏng Yŏudé has surrendered to us,
their grain supply is sufficient.
However, the soldiers guarding the ships
find transportation difficult.
As they are close to your esteemed country,
it would be very convenient to provide them with grain.
I believe Your Majesty views the Míng as a father
and me as an elder brother.
For father and brother to contend for several years,
while Your Majesty sits by and observes the outcome,
is to have the name of father and brother externally,
but inwardly harbor intentions of opportunistic misfortune.
If you were to vigorously mediate,
cease hostilities, and foster good relations,
not only would our two nations be pleased to see peace,
but your esteemed country would also receive its blessings.
If you still assist the Míng with troops,
uniting to resist us,
then the initiation of conflict will truly come from Your Majesty."
On the *jǐsì* day,
an edict ordered that officials' and commoners' hats and attire conform to the established regulations.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Kŏng Yŏudé was appointed Dūyuánshuài
and Gěng Zhòngmíng Zŏngbīngguān,
and both were granted official patents and seals.
On the *wùyín* day,
Yīng'é'ěrdài reported that Cháoxiăn, following the Míng's advice,
borrowed troops from Wōguó,
and also built fortifications at Yìzhōu Nánlǐng to prepare against us.
All *bèilè* and ministers were gathered to discuss this.
They all said that Cháoxiăn should be set aside and the Míng attacked.
On the *jǐmăo* day,
*Bèilè* Yuètūo and Dégélèi led the Right Wing's Léng'éyè and Yèchén,
the Left Wing's Yī'ěrdēng and Áng'gālā,
as well as Shí Tíngzhù, Kŏng Yŏudé, and Gěng Zhòngmíng, to lead troops to take the Míng's Lǚshùnkǒu.
On the *jiăshēn* day,
Dōnghăi Shĭquănbù *éfù* Sēnggé came to court and offered tribute.
On the *dìnghài* day,
an edict stated:
"All who offer advice,
if my actions are not in accord with righteousness,
should speak directly and without concealment.
If there are errors or improprieties in government affairs,
they should be openly presented without hiding anything.
If the officials of the six ministries are corrupt, deceitful, greedy, or malicious,
or act unfairly,
they should be impeached.
If any officials face hardship,
it should also be reported truthfully.
If one does not strive for direct speech,
but rather makes circuitous analogies,
and plagiarizes haphazardly,
what benefit is there to the matter?"
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *xīnmăo* day,
an edict stated that every Mǎnzhōu household with ten Hàn men would be granted one cotton armor,
and they would be commanded by the former Hànjūn *ézhēn* Mă Guāngyuăn.
On the *rénchén* day,
Táijí Gùkèsīxiábù, son of Ālùbù Sūndùléng,
Zhàisāng Wúbāshí, Āshítú, Bādá'ěrhéshòuqí and others,
and Táijí Ābāgá'ěrdài of Wūlàtèbù
all came to court and offered tribute.
On the *jiáchén* day,
*Bèilè* Yuètūo and others reported the capture of Lǚshùnkǒu.
On the *gēngshēn* day of the eighth month, the first day of the month,
Yīng'é'ěrdài and others returned from Cháoxiǎn.
They brought a reply agreeing to provide provisions for our soldiers guarding the ships.
On the *rénxū* day,
BèiLè Ābātài, Ājígé, Sàhālián, Háogé, and others raided outside Shānhǎiguān in Míng territory.
On the *gēngchén* day,
BèiLè Dégélèi and Yuètū's armies returned.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Vice General Shí Tíngzhù was appointed as Commander-in-Chief.
On the *gēngzǐ* day of the ninth month,
BèiLè Ābātài and others' armies returned.
The Emperor, deeming their advance not deep enough,
reprimanded them.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Yīng'é'ěrdài and others went to Cháoxiǎn for mutual trade.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Cài Bīn and others, who were DūSī of Dēngzhōu in Míng, came to surrender.
In the winter, on the *rénxū* day of the tenth month,
envoys were dispatched to the various tribes of the outer Měnggǔ,
to announce decrees and laws.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
a grand review was held.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
funds were disbursed from the treasury to reward the infantry of the Eight Banners.
On the *jǐsì* day,
an edict stated:
"Since the establishment of officials,
the Boards of Personnel, Revenue, and War have handled affairs perfectly.
The Board of Punishments has delayed trials,
failing to ascertain the truth.
The Boards of Rites and Works both have deficiencies.
The establishment of the Qǐxīnláng [officials]
was intended for them to offer remonstrances as circumstances arose,
to 'enlighten one's heart'.
Yet, when errors occur, no guidance is heard.
Why is this?"
He further said:
"You constantly speak of sailing the seas to take Shāndōng and attacking Shānhǎiguān.
Navigating the seas is fraught with danger;
attacking fortified positions easily causes casualties.
This is but to deceive with empty words,
no different from planning for the enemy.
In military affairs, your words are not needed.
Only if I or the BèiLè commit an error,
then you should speak frankly."
He also instructed the scholarly officials of the Wénguǎn:
"TàiZǔ first ordered Bākèshí É'ěrdéNí to create the national script.
Later, Kù'ěrchán augmented it.
Fearing that there might be imperfections,
it is your duty to record;
you should diligently revise and correct it.
I have succeeded to the great throne.
If the major administrative and military actions of the Imperial Father
are not recorded in detail one by one,
how will future generations know of them?
How can I thus fulfill my filial piety?"
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Mǎ Guāngyuǎn, a Míng general who had surrendered, was appointed as Commander-in-Chief;
Wáng Shìxuǎn and Má Dēngyún were appointed as Third-Class Commander-in-Chief;
Mǎ Guāngxiān, Mèng Qiáofāng, and others were each appointed to various ranks.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Shàng Kěxǐ, Vice General of Guǎnglùdǎo in Míng, sent an envoy to negotiate surrender.
On the *jiǎchén* day of the eleventh month,
Yīng'é'ěrdài again carried a letter to Cháoxiǎn,
reproaching them for ten breaches of agreement.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Jìsīhā and Wúbāhǎi were sent to conquer the Hǔ'ěrhā tribe bordering Cháoxiǎn.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the Emperor hunted in Yèhè.
On the *xīnwèi* day of the twelfth month,
the Emperor returned to Shěnyáng.
In the spring of the eighth year, on the *gēngyín* day of the first month,
the Měnggǔ BèiLè were ordered to comply with our national regulations.
Qiāngtúlǐ and Má'ěrgān of Hēilóngjiāng, leading six clans, came to pay tribute.
On the *guǐsì* day,
an edict declared that those of the imperial clan descended directly from XīngZǔ, the Emperor, were of the lineage of the Six Ancestors,
and were exempted from corvée labor.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Lèng'élǐ, Dūtǒng of the Bordered Yellow Banner and First-Class Commander-in-Chief, died.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
a Hàn Bèiyù complained that the corvée labor for Hàn people was heavier than for Mǎnzhōu.
BèiLè Dégélèi of the Board of Revenue reported this to the Emperor.
The Emperor ordered BèiLè Sàhālián of the Board of Rites to gather the crowd and explain its fallacy.
Hàn Commander-in-Chief Shí Tíngzhù and others seized eight Bèiyù and requested punishment.
The Emperor said:
"If they are punished,
then no one will speak again later."
And released them all.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Tābùnáng and others pursued the routed Cháhār forces at Xí'ěrhā and Xíbótú.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Táijí Élínchén of the Hāoqítè tribe submitted.
On the *dīngsì* day,
half of the able-bodied men (dīng) were exempted for meritorious officials who died without heirs;
only when their wives died would they be liable for service.
This was made into a decree.
On the *rénxū* day of the second month,
regulations for funerals and sacrifices were established:
wives sacrificing themselves for their husbands were permitted
and still commended;
those who forced concubines to sacrifice themselves,
their wives would be sentenced to death.
BèiLè Duō'ěrgǔn and Sàhālián were sent to welcome the surrendering general Shàng Kěxǐ,
and ordered him to be stationed at Hǎizhōu.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Dū Yuánshuài Kǒng Yǒudé impeached Gěng Zhòngmíng for unlawful conduct;
an edict was issued to resolve the matter.
On the *wùchén* day,
Āshān and others were sent to raid Jǐnzhōu.
On the *dīnghài* day of the third month, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse,
and a green rainbow appeared.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Tán Tàil and Tú'ěrgé were ordered to raid Jǐnzhōu.
On the *rénchén* day,
Vice General Shàng Kěxǐ, leading officials and common people from three islands, surrendered
and was stationed at Hǎizhōu.
On the *jǐhài* day,
a grand review was held.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Yīng'é'ěrdài was sent to Cháoxiǎn for mutual trade.
Kǒng Yǒudé, Gěng Zhòngmíng, and Shàng Kěxǐ were ordered to use banners of white with a black border,
to distinguish them from the Eight Banners.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Hàn students (shēngyuán) were examined.
In the summer, on the *xīnyǒu* day of the fourth month,
Tānggǔdài and other sons of TàiZǔ were promoted to Vice Generals, Guerrilla Generals, and Bèiyù in various ranks.
Furthermore, because the descendants of the Hādá and Wūlā tribes had no prominent positions,
Hādákèshènèi was appointed Vice General,
and Wūlābàyán was appointed Third-Class Vice General.
An edict designated Shěnyáng as
"Tiānjuàn Shèngjīng" [Heaven-Bestowed Prosperous Capital],
and Hètú'ālā city as
"Tiānjuàn Xīngjīng" [Heaven-Bestowed Rising Capital].
The Mǎnzhōu official names for Commander-in-Chief, Vice General, Guerrilla General, Youji, and Bèiyù were revised.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Shàng Kěxǐ came to court
and was appointed Commander-in-Chief.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Bàiyīntú, son of TàiZǔ's brother, was appointed as Grand Administrator.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the Board of Rites was first ordered to examine Mǎnzhōu and Hàn people proficient in Mǎnzhōu, Hàn, and Měnggǔ writings and meanings.
Gānglín and sixteen others were selected as Jǔrén,
granted a suit of clothes,
and exempted from four able-bodied men's service.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Jīn Jìmèng and others surrendered from Shíchéngdǎo in Míng territory
and were assigned to Shàng Kěxǐ.
On the *bǐngxū* day of the fifth month, the first day of the month,
Bā'ěrdácí of Hēilóngjiāng came to pay tribute.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Táijí Máoqítàtè of Cháhār came to court.
The names for Mǎnzhōu and Hàn cavalry and infantry were established.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
a campaign against Míng was discussed.
The BèiLè requested to enter through Shānhǎiguān.
The Emperor said:
"Not so.
Cháhār was defeated by our army,
and its BèiLè and ministers will submit to us.
We should proceed directly to Xuān and Dà to intercept them."
Then, all the Dūtǒng were gathered to deploy military affairs.
Guójiù Āshídá'ěrhā was sent to levy Kē'ěrqìn troops,
and a letter was dispatched to pacify the remaining scattered forces in Míng territory.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the merits of all officials were graded,
and imperial decrees were granted.
Those with hereditary titles and those whose official positions ended with themselves
were separately recorded with distinctions.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Jìsīhā and Wúbāhǎi reported victory from their campaign against the Hǔ'ěrhā tribe.
BèiLè Jí'ěrhāláng was ordered to remain and guard Shèngjīng,
BèiLè Dùdù to guard Hǎizhōu,
and Lìbù Chéngzhèng Tú'ěrgé and others were to cross the Liáohé River
and garrison along the Zhānggǔtái River,
both blocking enemy forces.
All were given strategic instructions.
After this was completed,
the Emperor led the main army to depart.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
they reached Dū'ěrbí,
where the various outer Měnggǔ armies successively joined them.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
they reached Nèlǐtèhé River.
In the *xīnyǒu* month of June,
military orders were issued to the various Mongolian *Bèilè* and to Kǒng Yǒudé, Gěng Zhòngmíng, and Shàng Kěxǐ,
saying:
“When on campaign, do not stray from the main banner,
do not make noise,
do not privately go out to plunder.
Those who resist shall be executed;
those who surrender shall be treated kindly.
Do not destroy temples,
do not kill travelers,
do not seize people's clothing,
do not separate husbands and wives,
do not molest women.
Violators will be punished.”
Before this,
Lín Dān of Cháhā'ěr had fled west to Túbáitè.
His followers suffered from Lín Dān's tyranny;
seven or eight tenths of them lingered behind.
When their food ran out,
they resorted to cannibalism,
and continued their slaughter and pillaging,
dispersing in all directions.
By this time,
thousands of households successively came to submit.
On *xīnwèi*,
the army reached Kùhēibùlǐdū.
A discussion was held regarding *Juéluó* Bù'ěrjí and Yīng'é'ěrdài's crime of unauthorized killing of Cháhā'ěr Bùyántú's people,
and their conferred titles were stripped.
On *jiǎxū*,
the army reached Kālātuōluòrù.
The *Bèilè* Dégélèi was ordered to lead troops into Dúshíkǒu
to scout Jūyōngguān,
with a deadline to rendezvous at Shuòzhōu.
On *wùyín*,
the various Mongolian *Bèilè* were instructed:
“Kē'ěrqìn Gá'ěrzhūsàitè'ěr and others rebelled and fled to Suǒlún,
and were pursued, captured, and killed by their clan brothers.
My heart aches for this.
I wish to spread virtuous governance
so that all people may enjoy peace and happiness.
Though these *Bèilè* were executed for their crimes,
it is also because my civilizing influence had not yet reached them.”
He also ordered a reduction in the punishment for Dálāhǎi and others from the Ālǔ tribe for overstepping their boundaries when pasturing.
On *rénwǔ*,
Tǔbājìnóng of Cháhā'ěr led his one thousand households to surrender.
Bāgádá'ěrhàn of the Kā'ěrkā tribe also surrendered.
On *jiǎshēn*,
the Great *Bèilè* Dàishàn and others were ordered to lead troops into Déshèngbǎo,
raid Dàtóng,
and proceed west to the Yellow River.
Vice-Commander Tǔlúshén and Wúbài, etc., were to go directly to Guīhuà to pacify the fleeing Cháhā'ěr people.
All were to rendezvous at Shuòzhōu.
In the seventh month of autumn, on *jǐchǒu*,
the *Bèilè* Ājígé, Duō'ěrgǔn, Duōduó, etc., were ordered to enter Lóngmén
and meet at Xuānfǔ.
The Emperor himself led the main army from Xuānfǔ towards Shuòzhōu,
with the four columns of troops expected to advance simultaneously on a set date.
On *xīnmǎo*,
the border wall was destroyed.
On *rénchén*,
the army entered Shàngfāngbǎo
and reached Xuānfǔ Right Guard.
A letter was sent rebuking the Míng defenders for their breach of alliance,
and also instructing them to send envoys for peace talks.
On *guǐsì*,
the army encamped southeast of the city.
At this time, Ājígé attacked Lóngmén,
but did not take it,
so he was ordered to raid Bǎo'ān.
On *dīngyǒu*,
the army encamped east of the city,
and a letter was sent to the Míng Prince of Dài,
again proposing that he send an envoy for peace talks.
Dàishàn attacked Déshèngbǎo
and took it.
Míng Assistant General Lǐ Quán hanged himself.
The army advanced to attack Huáirén and Jǐngpíng,
but failed to take either,
and consequently encamped at Shuòzhōu.
On *bǐngwǔ*,
the Emperor besieged Yìngzhōu,
and ordered Dàishàn and others to hasten to Mǎyì.
Tǔlúshén arrived at Guīhuàchéng.
Lín Dān's wife of Cháhā'ěr, with her eight *zhàisāng* and 1,200 households, came to surrender.
On *gēngxū*,
Ājígé and others attacked Bǎo'ānzhōu
and took it.
On *rénzǐ*,
Dégélèi entered Dúshíkǒu,
took Cháng'ānlǐng,
and attacked Chìchéng,
but failed to take it.
All converged at Yìngzhōu.
In the eighth month, on *yǐmǎo*,
the generals were ordered to raid Dàizhōu.
Sāhālián raided Guōxiàn
and captured it.
On *bǐngchén*,
Shuòtuō entered Yuánpíngyì.
On *jiǎzǐ*,
Ābātài and others took Wángjiāzhuāng in Língqiūxiàn
and captured it.
The Minister of Rites, Bādūlǐ, died in battle.
The army then attacked Shíjiācūnbǎo in Yìngzhōu
and took it.
On *bǐngyín*,
the Emperor departed Yìngzhōu.
Upon hearing that Míng Grand Coordinator of Yánghé, Zhāng Zōnghéng, and Grand General of Dàtóng, Cáo Wénzhào, were stationed at Huáirén,
he inferred that they would surely flee to Dàtóng that night,
and ordered Tǔlúshén and Wúbài to set an ambush for them.
The army moved slowly,
and Zōnghéng and others escaped.
The Emperor angrily rebuked them.
On *wùchén*,
the Emperor arrived at Dàtóng
and sent a letter to Wénzhào,
ordering him to support peace talks.
He also sent letters to other officials,
demanding the return of Cháhā'ěr remnants who were with the Míng.
Wénzhào challenged,
and was defeated.
The *Bèilè* Ābātài and others captured Língqiū.
The Míng Prince of Dài's mother, Lady Yáng, along with Zhāng Zōnghéng and Cáo Wénzhào, sent a letter requesting peace.
On *xīnwèi*,
an envoy was sent to reply by letter.
On *rénshēn*,
Dàishàn led his army to join.
On *guǐyǒu*,
the army encamped at Dàtóng,
and the Míng imperial clansman Zhū Nǎitíng and a captured monk were sent into the city.
Three requests for a reply letter were made,
but none was received.
Nǎitíng's wife and children, and Zhū Nǎizhèn, were released to return.
On *dīngchǒu*,
the army encamped at Sìshílǐpù.
A Míng spy's letter was intercepted at Běilóukǒu.
A letter was sent in reply, saying:
“The incoming letter refers to Manchuria as a subordinate state.
Indeed, I have never regarded this as incorrect.
However, the officials in Liáodōng have bullied and insulted our nation,
and the Emperor has been misled by the lies of his subordinates.
Though we have been at war for more than ten years,
not a single word of inquiry has been made,
preventing the true sentiments of our nation from being conveyed.
If an envoy were sent to distinguish right from wrong,
then the war would have ended long ago.
To enjoy peace
is merely a matter of time, morning or evening.
Otherwise,
your nation's officials obstruct and deceive,
falsely reporting beheadings and victories.
If our small nation were truly wounded and ravaged,
how could we invade repeatedly?
Can it be that the Emperor's intelligence alone cannot ponder this?
Our sincerity in desiring peace
is known to Hēi Yúnlóng.
I fear he dares not report it fully, lest he incur the wrath of senior officials.”
On *jǐmǎo*,
the main army arrived at Yánghé.
Míng General Cáo Wénzhào craftily used a letter to deceive Zhāng Zōnghéng,
falsely stating that cannons had wounded our soldiers,
and that a banner had been captured, etc.
This was intercepted by our scouts.
The Emperor then sent a letter to Zōnghéng, saying:
“I thought that your Míng state would have loyal and righteous officials who genuinely plan for the country.
Yet now, such deceit and falsehood have reached this point.
Are you not ashamed in your heart?
Now, I make an agreement with you all:
our soldiers are one against ten.
If you can agree on a date to engage in battle,
I shall restrain my troops and await.
If you lie and deceive your sovereign,
bringing harm to the common people,
the misfortune will be endless.”
On *rénwǔ*,
the army reached Huáiyuǎn.
On *guǐwèi*,
the army encamped at Zuǒwèi.
In the intercalary eighth month, on *bǐngxū*,
a letter was sent rebuking the Míng eunuch of Xuānfǔ for deceiving the sovereign and misleading the nation.
On *dīnghài*,
Vice-Commander Tǔlúshén died from his wounds.
Wànquán Zuǒwèi was attacked
and taken.
On *gēngyín*,
the army returned to the capital.
Gá'ěrmǎjìnóng of Cháhā'ěr and others sent envoys to request surrender,
stating that their Khan Lín Dān had died of illness,
and that the Khan's son and the people of the nation all wished to submit.
Thereupon, Āshídá'ěrhā and others were ordered to investigate.
On *dīngyǒu*,
the army moved to Jiùshàngdūchéng.
On *gēngxū*,
the army moved to Kèbàng.
On *xīnhài*,
Cháhā'ěr *zhàisāng* Gá'ěrmǎjìnóng and others, leading 6,000 of their countrymen and offering Dòutǔmén Fújīn, came to surrender.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùchén,
the Resident Bèilè Jǐ'ěrhǎlǎng reported by memorial that Jìsīhā and Wúbāhǎi, in their campaign against the Hǔ'ěrhā, had captured over 1,300 people.
The entire nation of Ālǔ Bù's Máomíng'ān came to pledge allegiance.
On Xīnwèi,
they crossed the Liáohé.
On Rénshēn,
the Emperor returned to Shèngjīng.
In winter, on the tenth month, day Jǐchǒu,
the funerary temple for Tàizǔ's mausoleum was built,
pine trees were planted,
and stone beasts were erected.
On Rénchén,
the merits and demerits of the generals and soldiers from the Xuān and Dà campaigns were assessed.
On Jǐhài,
the Kē'ěrqìn Tái jí Wúkèshàn brought his sister back,
and she was accepted.
On Gēngxū,
to commemorate the victories of the past eight years of campaigns,
a document was issued to Tàizǔ.
On Rénzǐ,
the king of Cháoxiǎn, Lǐ Zōng, sent an envoy with a letter.
The Emperor, finding its words disrespectful,
sent a stern reply.
In the eleventh month, on Yǐchǒu,
officials of the Six Boards were evaluated, and promotions and appointments were made according to their performance.
In the twelfth month, on the first day, Guǐwèi,
the king of Cháoxiǎn sent a letter to apologize.
On Rénchén,
Fù Dūtǒng Bàqílán and Cānlǐng Sàwúshíqià were ordered to campaign against the unsubdued lands of the Hēilóngjiāng.
On Bǐngshēn,
the exclusive administration of zuǒlǐng was allocated among the imperial clan members and Èfù, with varying assignments.
On Dīngyǒu,
Mòlègēnlāmā came to present a golden statue of Mǎhāgálá,
and an envoy was sent to escort it to Shèngjīng.
On Guǐmǎo,
Qí Tātèchē'ěrbèi and Sàilěngbùdūmǎ'ěr of Cháhā'ěr, among others, each led their people to pledge allegiance.
Wúbāhǎi and Jīnggǔ'ěrdài were sent to campaign against Wǎ'ěrkā.
On Jiǎchén,
Zuǒlǐng Liúxuéchén submitted a memorial requesting the establishment of a suburban altar
and diligent attendance at court.
The Emperor said:
"The memorial states that I should attend court diligently, which is correct.
As for establishing a suburban altar,
I do not yet know the will of Heaven.
How dare I act rashly?
If a great enterprise is accomplished,
it will not be too late to discuss it then."
In the ninth year, spring, first month, on Dīngmǎo,
the Emperor personally escorted Kē'ěrqìn Tǔxiètú Jìnóng and others back to their country.
On Guǐyǒu,
meritorious officials were exempted from corvée labor.
On Dīngchǒu,
an edict declared that Tàizǔ's illegitimate sons should be called
"Āgē,"
and the descendants of the Six Ancestors should be called
"Juéluó,"
with the Juéluó wearing red sashes to distinguish them.
Those who reviled their ancestors would be punished with death.
In the second month, on Rénwǔ,
officials were ordered to recommend those of impartial character and skilled in literature and arts who could be entrusted with responsibilities.
On Dīnghài,
the able-bodied men of the Kālèqìn Bù Měnggǔ were organized into eleven banners,
each banner having one Dūtǒng,
assisted by two Fù Dūtǒng and Cānlǐng.
On Wùzǐ,
an imperial decree stated:
"Recently, all those who have spoken have requested an expedition against the Míng.
How could I not be concerned about this?
However, it must be carried out according to circumstances.
Now, Cháhā'ěr has newly submitted,
the hearts of the people are not yet settled,
and the cities have not yet been repaired.
If we rashly send out an army,
how can a great enterprise be accomplished?
Moreover, once a large army is dispatched,
the Míng ruler might abandon his post and flee,
or, fearing, request peace.
Which strategy, attack or resistance,
would be appropriate?
Let Gāo Hóngzhōng, Bào Chéngxiān, Níng Wánwǒ, Fàn Wénchéng, and others deliberate and report back."
On Jǐchǒu,
Shěn Pèiruì proposed establishing military colonies in Guǎngníng and Lǘyáng,
and building boats to transport grain,
as a plan for advance.
The Emperor praised and adopted it.
On Yǐwèi,
Fàn Wénchéng and Níng Wánwǒ proposed that the method of joint punishment should be applied for insincere recommendations.
On Dīngwèi,
Duō'ěrgǔn, Yuètā, Háogé, and Sàhālián were ordered to lead 10,000 elite cavalry
to retrieve È'ěrkèkǒngguǒ'ěrézhé, the son of Cháhā'ěr Líndān.
In the third month, on Wùchén,
an imperial decree stated:
"Recently, the people have been delayed in their plowing and weeding,
which is due to the zuǒlǐng having to build city walls,
and the people suffering from arduous labor.
Henceforth, those who exploit labor to impede agriculture will be punished."
On Gēngwǔ,
Cháhā'ěr Zhàisāngbālài'ěrdù and over 1,400 others came to pledge allegiance.
In the fifth month, on Yǐmǎo,
Bàqílán and Sàwúshíqià campaigned against the Hǔ'ěrhā tribe of Hēilóngjiāng,
completely conquering their territory.
They organized the captured populace and returned,
and their merits were assessed, with promotions and rewards varying.
On Guǐhài,
the Emperor, knowing that the western campaign of the Bèilè had passed through the Xuān and Dà regions,
expected the Míng to transfer troops from Níng and Jǐn as reinforcements.
He sent Bèilè Duōduó to lead an army into Níng and Jǐn to harass them.
On Jǐsì,
the Wénguǎn was ordered to translate the histories of Sòng, Liáo, Jīn, and Yuán.
On Rénshēn,
Bèilè Duōduó reported that 500 Míng soldiers were annihilated outside Jǐnzhōu Sōngshān city,
and their Fù Jiàng Liú Yìngxuǎn was killed.
On Bǐngzǐ,
Bèilè Duō'ěrgǔn, Yuètā, Sàhālián, Háogé and others reported that their troops had reached Xīlàzhū'ěrgé,
where they met Nángnáng Tàifēi of Cháhā'ěr and Tái jí Suǒnuòmù and others, who surrendered with 1,500 households.
They then arrived at È'ěrkèkǒngguǒ'ěrézhé's residence,
and his mother led È'ěrzhé to welcome the surrender.
In the sixth month, on Yǐyǒu,
Bèilè Duōduó returned in triumph,
was bestowed five excellent horses,
and the accompanying generals and soldiers were rewarded according to their merits.
On Dīngyǒu,
Wúbāhǎi and Jīnggǔ'ěrdài's army returned,
and their merits were assessed similarly.
Míng Dēngzhōu Huángchéngdǎo Qiānzǒng Lǐ Jìngōng surrendered.
On Xīnchǒu,
an imperial decree stated:
"Tàizǔ entrusted the people to me;
I must love and nurture them.
The Bèilè's untimely repairs
burden the common people,
who find no peace,
and gradually flee,
which goes against the former will and aids the enemy.
Now Cháoxiǎn is subservient,
and Cháhā'ěr has entirely submitted.
If we cannot pacify and gather their multitudes,
even if we expand our territory later,
how will we manage them?
Let the Bèilè and ministers curb their arrogance and pride to fulfill my intentions!"
On Rén'yín,
Cháhā'ěr Tái jí Suǒnuòmù led his subordinates, 6,800 people, to pledge allegiance.
On Guǐmǎo,
an imperial decree stated:
"Tàizǔ forbade Bèilè's sons and younger brothers from hunting with eagles outside the city,
fearing they would trample fields and disturb livestock.
Now, the number of violators is increasing daily.
As the saying goes: 'If trickles are not dammed,
they will become rivers.'
Strictly prohibit this."
Autumn, seventh month, on Guǐyǒu,
the increase and decrease of Hàn Chinese households were discussed,
and six officials, including Cānlǐng Lǐ Sīzhōng, were promoted,
while eleven officials, including Gāo Hóngzhōng, were dismissed or punished according to their varying offenses.
In the eighth month, on Gēngchén,
Bèilè Duō'ěrgǔn, Yuètā, Sàhālián, and Háogé announced the recovery of the Imperial Seal of State Transmission.
Previously, when Yuán Shùndì fled north,
he took the seal with him,
but later lost it.
Over two hundred years later,
it was found by a shepherd.
Later, it came into the possession of Cháhā'ěr Líndānhàn.
Líndān was also a descendant of the Yuán.
The seal was with Sūtài Tàifēi.
It was presented at this time.
At that time, Yuètā remained in Guīhuà Chéng due to illness.
Duō'ěrgǔn and others led troops to raid Shānxī of Míng,
entering the border from Pínglǔ Wèi,
destroying the Great Wall,
and raiding Xīnzhōu and Dàizhōu,
reaching Guǒxiàn.
On Jiǎshēn,
the illustrated record of Tàizǔ's deeds was completed.
On Yǐsì,
the Emperor, leading Dà Bèilè Dàishàn and other Bèilè, including Duō'ěrgǔn, advanced their army to Pínglǔ Bǎo.
On Dīngwèi,
they crossed the Liáohé
and inspected the fortresses of Jùliúhé.
In the ninth month, on Guǐchǒu,
Bèilè Duō'ěrgǔn and others returned with their army,
presented the imperial seal,
and received it with an announcement to Heaven.
È'ěrkèkǒngguǒ'ěrézhé and his mother came to court.
On Gēngwǔ,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On Rénshēn,
all Bèilè and ministers were summoned, and Dàishàn's crimes were enumerated.
The consensus was to strip him of his titles of Dà Bèilè and Héshuò Bèilè,
to confiscate ten zuǒlǐng.
His son Sàhālián was stripped of two zuǒlǐng,
Hādá Gōngzhǔ was demoted to commoner,
and her husband Suǒnuòmù Jìnóng's noble title was revoked.
The Emperor pardoned them all.
Winter, tenth month, on Jǐmǎo,
as peace negotiations with Míng failed,
and an advance was planned,
envoys were sent with letters to inform the border generals at Míng Xǐfēngkǒu, Dǒngjiākǒu, and other passes.
Héshuò Bèilè Dégélèi, who was in charge of the Board of Revenue, died.
On Guǐwèi,
Wúbāhǎi, Duōjílǐ, Zhāfúní, and Wúshítǎ were ordered to lead four columns of troops to campaign against Wǎ'ěrkā.
On the *dīngwèi* day of the eleventh month, which was the first day of the lunar month,
an order was issued for È'ěrkèkǒngguǒ'ér'ézhé to take his mother and reside on Sūndǎo Xí'ěrhā.
On the *xīnsì* day of the twelfth month,
Lěngsēngjī, a servant of Hádá Princess Mǎnggǔjì, first reported that Bèilè Mǎnggǔ'ěrtài, during his lifetime, conspired with his younger sister Mǎnggǔjì and younger brother Dégélèi to rebel,
and that the princess's husband Suǒnuómù, Túnbùlù, and Àibālǐ were involved in the affair.
It so happened that Suǒnuómù also surrendered himself.
After interrogation confirmed the facts,
Mǎnggǔjì, Mǎnggǔ'ěrtài's son Ébìlún, Túnbùlù, and Àibālǐ were all executed.
The remaining sons of Mǎnggǔ'ěrtài and the sons of Dégélèi were all reduced to commoners.
Suǒnuómù was pardoned for surrendering himself.
Lěngsēngjī was granted the rank of Third Class Assistant General.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
an audience was held at Tàizǔ's mausoleum.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Bèilè Sàhālián, along with the other Bèilè and Grand Bèilè Dàishàn, swore an oath,
requesting to confer an honorable title upon the Emperor.
The Emperor did not permit it.
Then, the Mongolian Bèilè came again to request it.
The Emperor said:
"Cháoxiǎn is a brotherly nation,
it is proper to inform them."
In the first month of spring of the tenth year, on the *rénxū* day,
the second imperial daughter was married to È'ěrkèkǒngguǒ'ér'ézhé.
On the *dīngchǒu* day of the second month,
the Eight Bèilè and the forty-nine Bèilè of the Outer Vassals each sent a letter to Cháoxiǎn,
requesting their king to persuade the Emperor to accept the honorable title.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
envoys were sent to the Míng border at Sōngpéng Lù, Pānjiākǒu, Dǒngjiākǒu, and Xǐfēngkǒu, carrying a letter to the Míng Emperor,
demanding his reply.
The decorations for the hat finials of all officials were regulated.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Níng Wánwǒ was dismissed due to a crime.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day of the third month, which was the first day of the lunar month,
during the Qīngmíng Festival,
an audience was held at Tàizǔ's mausoleum.
On the *xīnhài* day,

the Wénguǎn (Literary Hall) was reorganized into three academies: Nèi Guóshǐ Yuàn (Imperial Historiography Academy), Nèi Mìshū Yuàn (Imperial Secretariat), and Nèi Hóngwén Yuàn (Imperial Academy for the Dissemination of Culture).
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Bèilè Ājígé and Ābātài were sent to build Gáhǎi City.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Wúshítǎ and others campaigned against Wǎ'ěrkā,
and envoys were sent to report the victory.
An edict stated:
"The Mongolians deeply trust lamas,
but they are truly delusional people.
Henceforth, those who hang prayer wheels and cloth banners
should be prohibited."
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Yīng'é'ěrdài and others returned from Cháoxiǎn,
reporting that King Lǐ Zōng did not grant an audience
nor accept the letter,
and they presented his reply letter and the captured edict from Zōng to his border officials.
The Bèilè were enraged
and wanted to deploy troops.
The Emperor said:
"For now, let us send someone to inform them of the advantages and disadvantages,
and demand their sons as hostages;
if they do not comply,
it will not be too late to launch an army."
On the *dīngmǎo* day,

the forty-nine Bèilè from sixteen Mongolian nations of the Outer Vassals, as well as Kǒng Yǒudé, Gěng Zhòngmíng, and Shàng Kěxǐ, all arrived in Shèngjīng to request the conferment of the honorable title.
In the summer of the fourth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
Grand Bèilè Dàishàn,

along with Hèshuò Bèilè Jí'ěrhāláng, Duō'ěrgǔn, Duōduó, Yuètuō, Háogé, Ābātài, Ājígé, and Dùdù, led Manchu, Han, and Mongolian ministers, and the forty-nine Bèilè from sixteen Mongolian nations, to the palace with a three-part memorial, requesting to confer the honorable title, saying:
"We respectfully observe that Our Emperor, sustained by Heaven's favor,
rose in response to destiny.
When the world was in chaos,
Your Majesty cultivated virtue and embodied Heaven's will,
overawing the rebellious,
and pacifying the compliant.
The renown of Your benevolence and mildness
has extended to all people.
You have conquered Cháoxiǎn
and unified Mongolia.
Thus, You obtained the imperial seal,
a clear sign of the Mandate of Heaven,
plainly visible.
Upwardly, it accords with Heaven's will,
downwardly, it conforms to popular sentiment.
Your ministers respectfully present this honorable title,
with all ceremonial preparations complete.
We humbly hope for Your gracious approval."
The Emperor said:
"You, Bèilè and ministers, have urged me to accept an honorable title
for two years now.
Now you repeatedly insist,
and I am reluctant to disregard your wishes,
unable to decline.
Since I have received the Mandate,
I fear that state administration may be lacking;
you should diligently assist me."
The assembled ministers prostrated themselves and expressed gratitude.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Ministry of Rites submitted the ceremonial protocols.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
a fast was observed,
and an altar was erected outside Désgng Mén.
Annals, Volume Three: Annals of Tàizōng, Part Two
In the summer of the fourth month of Chóngdé's first year, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth,
the ceremony of receiving the honorable title was performed,
and the name of the empire was established as Dàqīng,
the era name was changed to Chóngdé.
The assembled ministers conferred the honorable title of Kuān Wēn Rén Shèng Huángdì (Benevolent, Mild, Humane, and Sagely Emperor),
and received congratulations.
It was then decided that cooked offerings would be used for the grand sacrifice to Heaven.
Officials were dispatched to establish the Tàimiào (Imperial Ancestral Temple), posthumously honor the ancestors, and announce it at the imperial mausoleums.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the progenitor was posthumously honored as Zé Wáng,
the great-great-grandfather as Qìng Wáng,
the great-grandfather as Chāng Wáng,
the grandfather as Fú Wáng,
and the father was given the posthumous title Chéng Tiān Guǎng Yùn Shèng Dé Shén Gōng Zhào Jì Lì Jí Rén Xiào Wǔ Huángdì,
with the temple name Tàizǔ,
and his mausoleum was named Fúlín;
the mother was given the posthumous title Xiào Cí Zhāo Xiàn Chún Dé Zhēn Shùn Chéng Tiān Yù Shèng Wǔ Huánghòu.
The clan ancestor Lǐdūn Bātúlǔ was posthumously granted the title Wǔgōng Jùnwáng,
and meritorious officials Fèi Yīngdōng was posthumously enfeoffed as Zhíyì Gōng,
and É Yìdū as Hóngyì Gōng,
to be enshrined alongside the ancestors.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the assembled ministers presented memorials of congratulations.
An edict stated:
"With my meager virtue,
I fear I may fall short of the multitude's expectations.
All you ministers should wholeheartedly assist me,
each diligently performing your duties,
rectifying yourselves and leading your subordinates,
exhausting your loyalty and sincerity,
establishing order and setting regulations,
and pacifying the people and showing compassion to the masses,
so that the ruler may be enlightened and the ministers good,
and governance may be universally prosperous,
thus able to bear Heaven's auspicious mandate."
The assembled ministers prostrated themselves and said:
"Such a sagely edict
is a blessing for the nation."
As the ceremony of receiving the honorable title was completed,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Duōjìlǐ and Hùxí returned from the campaign against Wǎ'ěrkā,
and rewards were distributed according to their merits.
Cháoxiǎn envoys returned to their country.
Initially,
when the Emperor received the honorable title,
the Cháoxiǎn envoys Luō Déxiàn and Lǐ Kuò alone did not bow.
The Emperor said:
"Their king intends to stir up enmity,
wanting me to kill his envoys as a pretext;
release them."
By this time, they were sent back,
and a letter was dispatched to the King of Cháoxiǎn, reproaching him,
ordering him to send his sons as hostages.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
for their achievements,
Grand Bèilè Dàishàn was enfeoffed as Hèshuò Xiōng Lǐ Qīnwáng,
Bèilè Jí'ěrhāláng as Hèshuò Zhèng Qīnwáng,
Duō'ěrgǔn as Hèshuò Ruì Qīnwáng,
Duōduó as Hèshuò Yù Qīnwáng,
Háogé as Hèshuò Sù Qīnwáng,
Yuètuō as Hèshuò Chéng Qīnwáng,
Ājígé as Duōluó Wǔyīng Jùnwáng,
Dùdù as Duōluó Ānpíng Bèilè,
and Ābātài as Duōluó Ráoyú Bèilè;
among the Mongolian Bèilè, Bādálǐ was enfeoffed as Hèshuò Túxiètú Qīnwáng,
Wúkèshàn as Hèshuò Zhuólìkètú Qīnwáng,
Gùlún Èfù Ézhé as Hèshuò Qīnwáng,
Bùtǎqí as Duōluó Zhásākètú Jùnwáng,
Mǎnjiùxílí as Duōluó Bātúlǔ Jùnwáng,
Gǔnchūshì Bātúlǔ as Duōluó Dá'ěrhàn Jùnwáng,
Sūndùléng as Duōluó Dùléng Jùnwáng,
Gùlún Èfù Bāndì as Duōluó Jùnwáng,
Kǒngguǒ'ér as Bīngtú Wáng,
Dōng as Duōluó Dá'ěrhàn Dàiqīng,
Émùbù as Duōluó Dá'ěrhàn Zhuólìkètú,
Gǔlǔsī Xiábù as Duōluó Dùléng,
Dānbǎ as Dá'ěrhàn,
Gěnggé'ér as Duōluó Bèilè,
Kǒng Yǒudé as Gōngshùn Wáng,
Gěng Zhòngmíng as Huáishùn Wáng,
and Shàng Kěxǐ as Zhìshùn Wáng.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Cháoxiǎn envoys left our letter at Tōngyuǎnpù
and did not take it back.
Zháfúní returned from the campaign against Wǎ'ěrkā.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day of the fifth month,
Xīfú was appointed Grand Academician of the Inner Hóngwén Yuàn.
Fàn Wénchéng and Bào Chéngxiān were both appointed Grand Academicians of the Inner Mìshū Yuàn.
Gānglín was appointed Grand Academician of the Inner Guóshǐ Yuàn.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Bèile Sàhàlián died.
Court was suspended for three days.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
cherries were offered for the first time at the Tàimiào.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Dūchá Yuàn was established.
An edict stated:
"If I am excessively extravagant and immoderate,
and mistakenly execute meritorious officials;
or if I indulge in hunting and pleasure,
neglecting governance;
or if I abandon the loyal and employ the treacherous,
making improper appointments and dismissals;
you should speak frankly and without reservation.
If any *bèile* abandon their duties,
corruptly seek wealth, and indulge in ease;
you should impeach them.
If any of the Six Boards make biased judgments,
or delay in reviewing cases;
you should investigate and report.
A bad habit of the Míng court was that
this yamen was also a den of bribery;
it should be guarded against.
Those who impeach others out of personal vendetta
shall be punished according to the law.
If what is said is correct,
it shall be implemented immediately;
if what is said is incorrect,
it shall be ignored."
On the *rénxū* day,
Sàhàlián was posthumously enfeoffed as Héshuò Yǐng Qīnwáng.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Zhāng Cúnrén was appointed Chéngzhèng of the Dūchá Yuàn.
Zǔ Zéhóng was appointed Chéngzhèng of the Lìbù.
Hán Dàxūn was appointed Chéngzhèng of the Hùbù.
Jiāng Xīn was appointed Chéngzhèng of the Lǐbù.
Zǔ Zérùn was appointed Chéngzhèng of the Bīngbù.
Lǐ Yún was appointed Chéngzhèng of the Xíngbù.
Péi Guózhēn was appointed Chéngzhèng of the Gōngbù.
Dūtǒng Yīěrdēng was dismissed.
Túěrgé was appointed Dūtǒng of the Bordered White Banner.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Wǔyīng Jùnwáng Ājìgé, Ráoyú Bèile Ābātài, Gōng Yánggǔlì, and others led troops to campaign against Míng.
The emperor ascended the Xiángfèng Gé and personally instructed them on strategy,
and also admonished them.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the army departed.
On the *jiǎxū* day, the first day of the sixth month,
Mongol defectors Bùěrgǎdū and others were granted varying hereditary ranks.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Yù Qīnwáng Duōduó was ordered to oversee the Lǐbù affairs.
Sù Qīnwáng Háogé was ordered to oversee the Hùbù affairs.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Sàhàlián's son Ādálǐ was enfeoffed as Duōluó Jùnwáng.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Guójiù Āshídáěrhàn was appointed Chéngzhèng of the Dūchá Yuàn.
Níkān was appointed Mongol Chéngzhèng.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *jǐwèi* day,
a dispatch was sent to the Outer Mongol banners to levy troops for the campaign against Míng.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Ājìgé and others joined forces and marched out from Yánqìng Zhōu,
capturing over 15,000 people and livestock.
In the eighth month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
officials were dispatched to offer sacrifices to Kǒngzǐ.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Chéng Qīnwáng Yuètūo and Sù Qīnwáng Háogé were demoted to Duōluó Bèile for their transgressions.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Ruì Qīnwáng Duōěrgǔn,
Yù Qīnwáng Duōduó,
Bèile Yuètūo, and Háogé led armies to campaign against Míng.
In the ninth month, on the *wùshēn* day,
Míng troops entered the field.
Wú Shàn and Jì Sīhā were ordered to lead troops to resist them.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Ājìgé and others reported that their army had passed through Bǎodìng to Ānzhōu,
captured twelve cities,
won all fifty-six battles,
and captured Zǒngbīng Cháo Pīchāng and others, as well as 180,000 people and livestock.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Yīlèshèn and others pursued Míng troops to the Niángniáng Gōng ferry crossing,
where they saw a great many enemy ships
and dared not advance,
reporting this to the court.
Yíxūn was ordered to provide reinforcement,
and Dùdù was again dispatched to lead troops to assist.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Mongols Dálài, Bàihè, Bàiyīndài, and others defected from Tǎshān.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Ājìgé and others returned with their army.
In the tenth month of winter, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
Duōěrgǔn and others returned with their army.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Grand Academician Xīfú and others were dispatched to Cháhār, Kāěrkǎ, and Kēěrqìn departments to investigate household registers,
organize *zuǒlǐng*,
adjudicate common lawsuits,
promulgate laws,
and prohibit banditry and theft.
On the *wùxū* day,
King Lǐ Zōng of Cháoxiǎn sent a letter.
It was rejected.
In the eleventh month, on the *wùshēn* day,
Yuètūo was again ordered to oversee Bīngbù affairs.
Háogé was again ordered to oversee Hùbù affairs.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Wèizhàisāng and others returned from the Mongol Kāěrkǎ department,
and came with their envoy Wèizhēng Lǎma and others to offer tribute.
On the *xīnhài* day,
troops were levied from the Outer Banners.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
an edict stated:
"When I read history,
I know that Emperor Shìzōng of Jīn was a truly wise ruler.
During the reigns of Xīzōng and Wányán Liàng,
all the old systems of Tàizǔ and Tàizōng were abolished,
and there was immoderate indulgence in pleasure.
Upon his ascension, Shìzōng,
fearing that his descendants would imitate the Hàn people,
exhorted them not to forget the ancestral laws,
and to practice archery and horsemanship.
Later generations, failing to observe this,
met their downfall.
Our nation is skilled in archery and horsemanship.
When we fight, we conquer;
when we attack, we capture.
In the past, Bākèshí Dáhǎi and others repeatedly urged me to change Manchu clothing to adopt the Hàn system.
I believe that loose robes
will inevitably lead to the abandonment of archery and horsemanship.
During my lifetime,
how could there be such a change?
I fear that later generations of descendants will forget this,
abandon archery and horsemanship, and imitate the Hàn people.
This is a matter of great concern.
You all should remember this carefully."
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the *Tàizǔ Shílù* was completed.
On the winter solstice, *yǐchǒu* day,
a grand sacrifice to Heaven was performed at the Yuánqiū.
Sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth and the Tàimiào, announcing the impending campaign against Cháoxiǎn.
On the *jǐsì* day,
military orders were issued,
and a dispatch was sent to Cháoxiǎn.
On the *xīnwèi* day, the first day of the twelfth month,
the Mongol kings and *bèile* of the Outer Banners gathered their troops in Shèngjīng.
Zhèng Qīnwáng Jíěrhālāg was left to guard.
