Wǔyīng Jùnwáng Ājìgé was stationed at Niúzhuāng to defend the border.
Ráoyú Bèile Ābātài was stationed at Gáhǎi Chéng to gather border residents and defend against the enemy.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the emperor led Lǐ Qīnwáng Dàishàn and others to campaign against Cháoxiǎn.
The main army reached Shāhé Bǎo.
Ruì Qīnwáng Duōěrgǔn and Bèile Háogé divided their forces and entered Chángshān Kǒu from Kuāndiàn.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Mǎ Fútǎ and others were dispatched with three hundred soldiers disguised as merchants,
to secretly proceed and besiege the capital of Cháoxiǎn.
Duōduó, and Bèizǐ Shuòtuō and Níkān followed with a thousand soldiers.
Jùnwáng Mǎzhūxí Lǐ and Bùtǎqí led troops to join them.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Bèile Yuètūo and Gōng Yánggǔlì assisted Duōduó's army with three thousand soldiers.
The emperor led the main army to set up camp thirty *lǐ* from Zhènjiāng,
ordering Ānpíng Bèile Dùdù and Gōngshùn Wáng Kǒng Yǒudé and others to guard the baggage train at the rear.
On the *gēngchén* day,
they crossed Zhènjiāng to Yìzhōu.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the emperor arrived at Guōshān Chéng.
The Dìngzhōu *yóujī* came to reinforce,
but realizing they were outmatched,
committed suicide.
Guōshān surrendered.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
they arrived at Dìngzhōu.
Dìngzhōu also surrendered.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
they arrived at Ānzhōu,
and sent a letter to the Cháoxiǎn defenders urging surrender.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Duōduó and others advanced and besieged the Cháoxiǎn capital.
King Lǐ Zōng of Cháoxiǎn fled to Nánhànshān Chéng.
Duōduó and others then besieged it again,
and also defeated all the reinforcing armies from various routes.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Wǎěrkā Yèchén and Má Fútǎ, who were in Cháoxiǎn,
heard of the arrival of the main army,
and came to surrender with their followers.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the emperor arrived at the Línjīn Jiāng.
As it happened, the weather was warm and the ice was melting,
making it impossible to cross.
Suddenly, there was a heavy rain,
and the ice froze again,
allowing the entire army to cross.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Dūtǒng Tántài and others were ordered to search and suppress the Cháoxiǎn capital,
leaving Mongol troops with them.
The emperor encircled Nánhàn Chéng with the main army.
That year,
Gǔlùgéchǔhǔ'ěr of the Tǔmòtè tribe,
Élínchén Jìnóng and Táijí Tǔbā of the È'ěrdúosī tribe, and others all came to court.
In the first month of spring in the second year, on the day Rén-yín,
the Commander-in-chief of Jeolla Province of Cháoxiǎn (Korea) came to reinforce.
Yuètī attacked and repelled him.
Yīng'é'ěrdài and Mǎfútǎ were dispatched to carry an imperial edict to the cabinet ministers of Cháoxiǎn,
enumerating their crimes of repeatedly breaking the alliance.
On the day Jiǎ-chén,
the grand army crossed the Hànjiāng River,
and set up camp on its bank.
On the day Dīng-wèi,
the combined forces from Jeolla and Chungcheong Provinces of Cháoxiǎn came to reinforce.
Duōduó and Yánggǔlì attacked and repelled them.
Yánggǔlì was wounded and died.
On the day Gēng-xū,
Duō'ěrgǔn and Háogé's armies captured Chángshān,
winning every battle,
and came to join forces.
Dùdù and others also arrived with artillery carriages.
Cháoxiǎn's situation became increasingly dire.
Lǐ Zōng repeatedly begged for peace in writing.
The Emperor permitted his surrender.
Lǐ Zōng submitted a memorial proclaiming himself a vassal,
but hesitated and dared not come out.
On the day Rén-xū,
Duō'ěrgǔn's army entered Jiānghuá Island,
captured Lǐ Zōng's wife and children,
and escorted them to the army front.
He again sent an edict to Lǐ Zōng saying:
"If you come, your family can be spared,
and your state can be preserved.
I will not break my word;
otherwise, I cannot wait long."
When Lǐ Zōng heard that Jiānghuá Island had fallen,
and his wife and children were captured,
and Nánhànchéng would fall any day,
he then requested to surrender.
On the day Gēng-wǔ,
Lǐ Zōng, King of Cháoxiǎn, led his son and his ministers in court attire to surrender at Sānjiántù on the east bank of the Hànjiāng River,
and presented the imperial seal bestowed by the Míng dynasty.
The Emperor consoled and addressed him, granting him a seat,
and returned his wife and children and the family members of his ministers,
and also generously rewarded them.
He ordered Yīng'é'ěrdài and Mǎfútǎ to escort Lǐ Zōng back to his capital,
keeping his sons Lǐ and Lǐ Hào as hostages.
In the second month, on the day Rén-shēn,
the army returned.
Bèizǐ Shuòtuō and Gōngshùn Wáng Kǒng Yǒudé and others led the Cháoxiǎn navy to capture Pídǎo from Míng.
Lǐ Zōng, King of Cháoxiǎn, submitted a memorial requesting a reduction in the tribute quota.
An imperial edict exempted the tribute goods for the two years Dīng-chǒu and Wù-yín,
and from the autumn season of Jǐ-mǎo onwards,
the tribute would return to the original quota.
On the day Jiǎ-xū,
Duō'ěrgǔn and others were ordered to prohibit plundering surrendered civilians;
violators would be equally punished with their supervising officials.
On the day Xīn-mǎo,
the Emperor returned to Shèngjīng.
On the day Guǐ-sì,
the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to stabilize grain prices and encourage agriculture.
In the third month, on the day Jiǎ-chén,
Hóng Yìhàn, Yǐn Jí, and Wú Dájì, Cháoxiǎn officials of the Censorate, were executed
due to their breach of alliance.
On the day Dīng-wèi,
Wǔyīng Jùnwáng Ājìgé led his army to assist in attacking Pídǎo.
On the day Wù-wǔ,
the construction of Gàizhōu City was halted.
In the fourth month of summer, on the day Jǐ-mǎo,
Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrgǔn arrived in Shèngjīng with the Cháoxiǎn hostage princes Lǐ and Lǐ Hào, and various Cháoxiǎn ministers' sons.
On the day Xīn-sì,
Ājìgé's army captured Pídǎo,
and beheaded Míng Commanders-in-chief Shěn Shìkuí and Jīn Rìguān.
On the day Jiǎ-shēn,
Ānpíng Bèilè Dùdù led the rear guard of the grand army back.
On the day Dīng-yǒu,
Gùshān Bèizǐ Níkān, Luōtuō, Bóluò, and others were ordered to deliberate on state affairs in advance.
Three Deliberative Ministers were added to each banner.
The Emperor gathered his ministers and instructed them, saying:
"Previously, the number of Deliberative Ministers was small,
and when they were dispatched on military campaigns or missions,
I had no one by my side.
Humble officials
could not be allowed to participate in state deliberations.
Now I have specially selected you and placed you in the ranks of the deliberative ministers.
You must consider the welfare of the people as your concern,
and be diligent and not lazy,
nor fail the court.
In the past, Lín Dān of the Cháhā'ěr Měnggǔ was perverse and lawless,
and his ministers did not remonstrate,
leading to the loss of his state.
If I have faults,
you, my ministers, must immediately remonstrate with me directly.
If you outwardly comply but then speak ill behind my back,
shifting blame to me,
you are not loyal ministers."
He further instructed:
"In ancient times, Jīn Xīzōng followed Hàn customs,
wore Hàn clothing and caps,
and completely forgot the language of his own country,
whereupon the achievements of Tàizǔ and Tàizōng declined.
Indeed, archery is our strong suit.
If we do not personally practice riding and shooting,
but only indulge in banquets and pleasures,
then military preparedness will gradually slacken.
Whenever I go hunting,
I hope not to forget riding and shooting,
and to diligently train soldiers.
All princes and bèilè must warn each other,
so that future generations do not change the system of our ancestors."
In the intercalary fourth month, on the day Guǐ-mǎo,
Měnggǔ presented a rare beast,
named Qíhètè.
On the day Rén-zǐ,
Wǔyīng Jùnwáng Ājìgé's army returned.
In the fifth month, on the day Gēng-wǔ,
Lǐ Zōng, King of Cháoxiǎn, sent an envoy to present a memorial expressing gratitude and ransoming the captives.
On the day Dīng-hài,
Lín Qìngyè, the Commander-in-chief of Cháoxiǎn who accompanied the expedition to Pídǎo, was sent back to his country,
and the King of Cháoxiǎn was commended with an imperial edict.
On the day Dīng-yǒu,
Zhāngjīng Níkān and others campaigned against Wǎ'ěrkā,
and subdued them.
The army passed through Cháoxiǎn's Hánjìngdào,
and it took two months to reach them.
They returned at this time.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīn-chǒu,
Āyùshí and others, people from Kālāqìn who had pledged allegiance, were granted official positions.
Míng Qianzǒng Wáng Guóliàng, Dūsī Hú Yìngdēng, Baizǒng Lǐ Zhōngguó, and others surrendered from the sea island.
Mǎnggǔ'ěrtài's son Guānggǔn was found guilty,
and executed.
On the day Yǐ-mǎo,
an edict was issued, stating:
"During the recent Cháoxiǎn campaign,
the army's conduct lacked discipline,
rushing forward at the sight of profit,
completely forgetting state laws.
From now on, thought should be given to how to promulgate laws and regulations and improve institutions."
On the day Bǐng-chén,
due to the subjugation of Cháoxiǎn
and the capture of Pídǎo,
sacrifices were offered to the Tàimiào and Fúlín.
On the day Dīng-sì,
Lǐ Zōng, King of Cháoxiǎn, requested to ransom captives at a flat rate,
which was not permitted.
On the day Jiǎ-zǐ,
the crimes of various generals who violated regulations during the Cháoxiǎn and Pídǎo campaigns were discussed.
Lǐ Qīnwáng Dàishàn was deliberated for removal from his title,
but was pardoned.
Zhèng Qīnwáng Jí'ěrhāláng and those below him were punished differently.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day Jǐ-sì,
Kākǎi and others were dispatched to campaign against Wǎ'ěrkā in separate routes.
On the day Guǐ-yǒu,
Ēnkè, a Councilor of the Ministry of Revenue, was found guilty,
and executed.
On the day Xīn-sì,
Hàn officials were warned against deceiving with empty words.
Zhìshùn Wáng Shàng Kěxǐ's army returned from Pídǎo.
On the day Rén-wǔ,
a grand amnesty was declared.
On the day Guǐ-wèi,
special pensions were granted to the officers and soldiers, including Yánggǔlì, who died in battle in Cháoxiǎn and Pídǎo,
with differing official titles and hereditary positions.
On the day Yǐ-yǒu,
Míng Dūsī Gāo Jìgōng and others surrendered from Shíchéngdǎo.
On the day Gēng-yín,
the Emperor's mother's father, Kē'ěrqìn Bèilè Mǎnggǔsī, was posthumously enfeoffed as Héshuò Fú Qīnwáng.
On the day Rén-chén,
the victories in Cháoxiǎn and Pídǎo were announced to Zǔ Dàshòu.
On the day Yǐ-wèi,
the Hàn army was divided into two banners,
with Commanders-in-chief Shí Tíngzhù and Mǎ Guāngyuǎn appointed as Dūtǒng (Generals-in-chief),
each managing the left and right wings.
In the eighth month, on the day Bǐng-shēn (first day of the month),
further pensions were granted to the officers and soldiers, including Hóng Wénkuí, who died in battle attacking Pídǎo and Cháoxiǎn,
with differing official titles and hereditary positions.
On the day Guǐ-chǒu,
Bèilè Yuètī was demoted to Bèizǐ due to his crimes,
fined,
and relieved of his duties in the Ministry of War.
On the day Bǐng-chén,
Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrgǔn and Ráoyú Bèilè Ābātài were ordered to build Dū'ěrbí City.
On the day Jǐ-wèi,
Āshídá'ěrhàn and others were dispatched to the Bālín, Zhālǔtè, Kālāqìn, Tǔmòtè, and Ālǔ tribes of Měnggǔ to collectively manage legal cases.
In the ninth month, on the day Xīn-wèi,
the Emperor went hunting at Fǔ'ānbǎo,
and sent a letter inviting Shěn Zhìxiáng, the Míng commander defending Shíchéngdǎo, to surrender.
On the day Jǐ-chǒu,
Mù'ěrtài, a Councilor of the Ministry of War, was dismissed from his post due to his crimes.
Bèilè Háogé was fined for the crime of coercing Měnggǔ Táijí Bóluò,
fined,
and relieved of his duties in the ministry.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *yǐwèi* day, which was the first day of the month,
the Mǎnzhou, Měnggǔ, and Hànzì calendars were first issued.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Öölöt Güshi Chéchén Chuòrzǐ sent envoys to present tribute.
As Öölöt was far away,
the envoys were dispatched in the first year of the reign,
and only arrived in the winter of this year.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Yīng'é'ěrdài, Mǎfútǎ, and Dáyún were sent with an imperial edict and seal to enfeoff Lǐ Zōng as the King of Cháoxiǎn.
In the eleventh month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Altar of Heaven.
Lǐ Zōng, King of Cháoxiǎn, sent envoys to present tribute,
and again submitted a memorial requesting the return of his heir apparent,
and describing the disasters and destitution in his country.
The Emperor did not permit it,
but issued an edict of instruction and bestowed gifts.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Jì nóng of Wūzhūmùqín, hearing that the Emperor was good at caring for the people,
led his Bèilè and the entire nation to submit.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Yánggǔlì was posthumously enfeoffed as Wǔxūn Wáng.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Emperor went hunting at Dǎcǎ Tān.
In the twelfth month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
Yèkèshū and Xīngnè led an army to conquer Guà'ěrcá.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
the generals campaigning against Wǎ'ěrkā reported a victory.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Bólúotè and Tuōníluò, Bèilè of the Hāoqílètè tribe, led their dependents to submit.
Ājígé sent Dāndài and others to defeat Míng troops at Qīnghé.
This year,
the Tuōkēluóshì, Kèyìkèlèshì, and Nòuyělèshì clans of the Hǔ'ěrhā tribe,
Bómùbóguǒ'ěr of the Suǒlún tribe in Hēilóngjiāng,
Bā'ěrdácí of Hēilóngjiāng,
and Hùyùbùlù of Jīnggélǐ Hé all came to court.
In the third year, spring, the first month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Bèizǐ Yuètūo was commanded to resume his title of Duōluó Bèilè,
and to oversee banner affairs.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Démùtú was appointed Chéngzhèng of the Ministry of Revenue.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Emperor's ninth son was born;
he was later Shìzǔ Zhāng Huángdì.
In the second month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
the Emperor personally led an expedition against Kè'ěrkā.
Yù Qīnwáng Duōduó and Wǔyīng Jùnwáng Ājígé accompanied him,
while Lǐ Qīnwáng Dàishàn, Zhèng Qīnwáng Jí'ěrhāláng, Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrgǔn, and Ānpíng Bèilè Dùdù remained to guard.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
they reached Kè'ěrzhān,
where the princes and Bèilè of the outer vassal states arrived with their armies to join them.
Hearing this, Kè'ěrkā
fled.
The Emperor hunted west of Dá'ěrnàluò Hú,
and made a temporary stop there.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
they reached Kuítúnbùlāké.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Shěn Zhìxiáng, the Míng Dongjiang Grand General, led the officers, soldiers, and people of Shíchéng Dǎo to surrender.
On the *rénxū* day,
Láosà was sent with a letter to inform the Míng official guarding Xuānfǔ to hasten mutual trade,
and to return the annual tribute to us.
In the third month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day, which was the first day of the month,
they reached Bóshuòduī,
and the princes remaining behind were ordered to build Liáoyáng city.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
they reached Yìxīlǐ.
On the *gēngchén* day,
they reached Dēngnùsūtè and then returned.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
they reached the source of the Shàngdū Hé,
where a spring gushed five feet high from the flat ground west of the river.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day, which was the first day of the month,
they reached Bùkètúlǐ,
and Yèkèshū and others reported a victory from their campaign against Hēilóngjiāng.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
they reached Liáo Hé.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
they reached Dùléng Chéng,
where Gāo Qǐqián, the Míng eunuch of Shānhǎiguān, sent someone to feign peace talks.
On the *wùxū* day,
they reached Zháhānàlìtè.
On the *jǐhài* day,
they reached Chámùhā.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
they reached Éyuèbólúo.
The construction of Dū'ěrbí Chéng was completed,
and it was renamed Píng Chéng.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Guà'ěrcá Zhámànài and others of the Dū'ěrbótè tribe came to pay tribute.
On the *rén'yín* day,
they reached Liáoyáng,
and inspected the new city.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Emperor returned to Shèngjīng.
The armies of Yèkèshū and Xīng that campaigned against Hēilóngjiāng returned.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
the surrendered Míng general Shěn Zhìxiáng was ordered to settle his followers in Fǔshùn.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Nígálǐ and others returned from their campaign against Hǔ'ěrhā.
In the fifth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
the road from Shèngjīng to Liáo Hé was repaired,
with Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrgǔn and Ráoyú Bèilè Ābātài overseeing the work.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Juéshàn, a subordinate of Lǐ Qīnwáng Dàishàn, committed a crime.
Zhèng Qīnwáng Jí'ěrhāláng and others requested his execution,
and deliberated on stripping Dàishàn of his title.
This was not permitted due to the minor nature of the offense,
and Juéshàn was also pardoned.
In the sixth month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
the Lǐfānyuàn was first established,
specifically to manage the affairs of the various Měnggǔ tribes.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *rénxū* day, which was the first day of the month,
the Emperor instructed the princes and high officials, saying:
"Since ancient times, states, when established,
have always set up institutions
to distinguish ranks and authority.
Now, the titles and ranks of Qīnwáng, Jùnwáng, Bèilè, Bèizǐ, Gōngzhǔ, and Èfù
all have established regulations,
yet none are observed,
and established laws are abandoned.
What is in your hearts, truly?
In the past, the founding emperors of Jīn, Tàizǔ and Tàizōng, were united in heart,
and achieved great unity.
When I am laying the foundation of the state,
can you not be united in heart, serve the country, and strictly adhere to the established norms?"
All the princes admitted their faults.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Dá'ěrhàn Nángsū Lǎmā, the envoy from Kè'ěrkā, returned,
and the Emperor instructed him, saying:
"I conquer the disobedient with military force,
and pacify the multitudes with virtue.
Heaven bestowed the various Měnggǔ tribes upon me,
yet your Kè'ěrkā raised an army to invade Guīhuà,
which is extremely inappropriate.
If you have no other choice,
you can only flee and prolong your existence.
Where you can reach,
can my army not reach?
Quickly repent your crimes and submit;
otherwise, I will not pardon you."
On the *rénshēn* day,
Dáyǎqí and others went to Míng Zhāngjiākǒu to discuss annual tribute and mutual trade.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Ministry of Rites was instructed, saying:
"For anyone who disobeys established regulations and disrupts laws and discipline,
princes, Bèilè, and Bèizǐ shall be deliberated for punishment;
officials shall be imprisoned for three days;
and commoners shall be flogged with the cangue before release.
Those who violate protocol in entering, exiting, sitting, or standing,
or who, despite their official ranks and titles being established, still use old names,
shall be admonished.
Those who imitate the clothing and headwear of other countries, or bind their hair and feet,
shall be punished with severe crimes."
The Grand Secretaries Xīfú and others were also instructed, saying:
"I do not value empty formalities,
but only focus on practical governance.
Now the state is prosperous and wealthy,
and governance lies in nourishing the people.
Anyone, new or old, who is impoverished and without a wife, children, or horses,
or who is brave and fit for military service but too poor to wear armor,
is permitted to make their grievances known,
and after verification, shall be provided for."
It was forbidden to sell good family daughters captured in battle as entertainers.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the official system of the ministries and courts was revised,
with specialized Mǎnzhou Chéngzhèng appointed.
Ābài was appointed Chéngzhèng of the Ministry of Personnel,
Yīng'é'ěrdài as Chéngzhèng of the Ministry of Revenue,
Mǎndá'ěrhàn as Chéngzhèng of the Ministry of Rites,
Yísūn as Chéngzhèng of the Ministry of War,
Lángqiú as Chéngzhèng of the Ministry of Punishments,
Sàmùshíkā as Chéngzhèng of the Ministry of Works,
Bèizǐ Bólúo as Chéngzhèng of the Lǐfānyuàn,
and Āshídá'ěrhàn as Chéngzhèng of the Dūcháyuàn.
Bùyán was appointed as a Yìzhèng Dàchén.
In the eighth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Zhù Shìchāng (祝世昌), Minister of the Board of Rites, was dismissed from his post for his crimes,
and exiled to guard the frontier.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Wú Bài (吳拜) and Shā'ěrhǔdá (沙爾虎達) repeatedly defeated Míng troops at Hóngshān Kǒu (紅山口) and Luówén Yù (羅文峪).
They also defeated the Míng troops from Mìyún (密雲),
annihilating them.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
there was an earthquake.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Luó Shuò (羅碩) and nine other successful *jǔrén* (舉人) candidates were granted the rank of *zuǒlǐng* (佐領),
and exempted from four male laborers.
First to third class *xiùcái* (秀才) were granted the rank of *hùjūnjiaò* (護軍校),
and exempted from two male laborers.
Each was bestowed with court robes and silk fabric of varying grades.
Those not yet inducted into the ministries were exempted from one male laborer.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Èqígénuòyán (額齊格諾顏) and others from the Ālǔ'ābàgāi (阿魯阿霸垓) department, and Bóluòtènuòmùqí (博洛特諾木齊) and others from the Hāoqítè (蒿齊忒) department, all came to pay tribute.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrgǔn (睿親王多爾袞) was made Fèngmìng Dàjiàngjūn (奉命大將軍),
commanding the left wing forces.
Bèilè Háogé (貝勒豪格) and Ābātài (阿巴泰) served as his deputies.
Bèilè Yuètāo (貝勒岳託) was made Yángwǔ Dàjiàngjūn (揚武大將軍),
commanding the right wing forces.
Bèilè Dùdù (貝勒杜度) served as his deputy.
They divided their forces to attack Míng.
The imperial edict stated:
"The commander-in-chief is looked up to by the multitude.
If he conducts himself with propriety,
and achieves harmony,
then the Mongols, Koreans, and Han Chinese who have joined us
will naturally be pleased in their hearts and sincerely submit.
If one calculates only personal merit
without regard for the nation's reputation,
that is not what is expected."
On the *dīngsì* day,
Yuètāo (岳託) and Dùdù (杜度)'s armies set out.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Bātúlǔ Zhǔntǎ (巴圖魯準塔) was appointed Měnggǔ Dūtǒng (蒙古都統).
In the ninth month, on the *guǐhài* day,
Duō'ěrgǔn (多爾袞), Háogé (豪格), and Ābātài (阿巴泰)'s armies set out.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the Emperor personally advanced towards Shānhǎi Guān (山海關) to harass the Míng forces.
Kǒng Yǒudé (孔有德), Gěng Zhòngmíng (耿仲明), and Shàng Kěxǐ (尚可喜)'s troops were summoned.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
regulations for granting exemptions to male laborers were established.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the Emperor visited the Yǎnwǔ Chǎng (演武場) (Drill Ground)
to review troops and practice archery.
In the winter, tenth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
Yuètāo (岳託)'s army entered from Qiángzǐ Lǐng (牆子嶺),
and encountered Míng troops.
Míng General-in-Chief Wú Guójùn (吳國俊) was defeated and fled.
On the *wùxū* day,
Duō'ěrgǔn (多爾袞)'s army entered Qīngshān Guān (青山關).
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Emperor commanded the main army and departed from Shèngjīng (盛京).
On the *jiǎchén* day,
they reached Húnhé (渾河).
The Kē'ěrqìn (科爾沁) and Kālāqìn (喀喇沁) each led troops to join.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Shā'ěrhǔdá (沙爾虎達) and others were dispatched to lead troops swiftly to Yìzhōu (義州).
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Jí'ěrhālāg (濟爾哈朗) and Duōduó (多鐸) were ordered to each lead troops separately to Qiántún Wèi (前屯衞), Níngyuǎn (寧遠), and Jǐnzhōu (錦州).
The Emperor personally advanced towards Yìzhōu (義州).
On the *xīnhài* day,
Suǒ Hǎi (索海) led troops to besiege fourteen *túnbǎo* (屯堡) (fortified settlements) on both banks of the Dàlíng Hé (大凌河).
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the Emperor arrived at Yìzhōu (義州).
Kǒng Yǒudé (孔有德), Gěng Zhòngmíng (耿仲明), Shàng Kěxǐ (尚可喜), Shí Tíngzhù (石廷柱), and Mǎ Guāngyuǎn (馬光遠) were dispatched to use cannons to attack its five forts.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
they reached Jǐnzhōu (錦州).
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Duōduó (多鐸) conquered the Sānggá'ěrzhài (桑噶爾寨) fort,
killing its defending general.
Kǒng Yǒudé (孔有德) and others attacked Shíjiā Bǎo (石家堡) and Qījiā Bǎo (戚家堡),
conquering both.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Kǒng Yǒudé (孔有dé) and others attacked the West Terrace of Jǐnzhōu (錦州).
The gunpowder inside the terrace spontaneously ignited,
destroying the terrace,
and it was conquered.
In the eleventh month, on the *jǐwèi* day, the first day of the month,
Duōduó (多鐸) was about to join forces with Jí'ěrhālāg (濟爾哈朗) and proceed directly to Zhōnghòusuǒ (中後所).
At that time, Zǔ Dàshòu (祖大壽) was rushing to aid Běijīng (北京),
and he attacked our forces by night.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Duōduó (多鐸) and Jí'ěrhālāg (濟爾哈朗) returned to Zhōnghòusuǒ (中後所).
Zǔ Dàshòu (祖大壽) was afraid,
and dared not come out.
Shí Tíngzhù (石廷柱) and Mǎ Guāngyuǎn (馬光遠) attacked Lǐyún Tún (李雲屯), Bóshì Tún (柏士屯), Guōjiā Bǎo (郭家堡), Kāizhōu (開州), and Jǐngjiā Bǎo (井家堡),
conquering them all.
Kǒng Yǒudé (孔有德) persuaded Dàfú Bǎo (大福堡) to surrender,
and then attacked Dàtái (大臺),
conquering it.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the main army entered Shānhǎi Guān (山海關).
On the *rénxū* day,
the Emperor arrived at Liánshān (連山).
On the *guǐhài* day,
Wǔlǐhé Tái (五里河臺) was attacked.
Míng garrison commander Lǐ Jìyǒu (李計友) and others led their men to surrender.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor arrived at Zhōnghòusuǒ (中後所),
and met Zǔ Dàshòu (祖大壽) withdrawing his troops into the city.
An envoy was sent to tell him:
"It has been several years since we last met,
and I very much wish to see you.
As for whether you leave or stay,
I will ultimately not force you.
For a general to contend for victory with me
is the way of a general, as it should be.
I do not take this to heart,
and also hope that the general will not be suspicious."
On the *wùchén* day,
an envoy was sent again to inform Zǔ Dàshòu (祖大壽),
but he did not respond.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Jí'ěrhālāg (濟爾哈朗) conquered Mōlóng Guān (摸龍關) and Wǔlǐbǎo Tún Tái (五里堡屯臺).
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the army returned to the capital.
On the *gēngchén* day,
they reached Tú'ěrgēnHé (圖爾根河).
The Mongol armies were dispatched to return to their respective departments.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *dīnghài* day,
there was an earthquake.
In the twelfth month, on the *wùxū* day,
Láng Qiú (郎球), Minister of the Board of Punishments, was dismissed for his crimes.
Suǒ Hǎi (索海), Cānzhèng (參政) of the Dūchá Yuàn (都察院), replaced him.
In this year,
Gǔlùgé (古祿格) from the Tǔmòtè (土默特) department,
Guà'ěrzháchámànài (卦爾察札馬奈) from the Dù'ěrbótè (杜爾伯特) department,
Ābài (阿拜) and Āmǐn (阿閔) from the Xībù (席部) department,
Jǐngnào (井瑙), Mǎkǎo (馬考), Zhànài (札柰), and Sāngjíchá (桑吉察) from the Wùzhálā (兀札喇) department,
Élínchén Jìgōng (額林臣濟農) from the È'ěrdúosī (鄂爾多斯) department,
Èqígénuòyán (額齊格諾顏) from the Ālǔ'ābàgāi (阿魯阿霸垓) department,
Bóluòtènuòmùqí (博洛特諾木齊) from the Hāoqítè (蒿齊忒) department,
Bómùbóguǒ'ěr (博穆博果爾) and Wǎdàigálíng'ā (瓦代噶凌阿) from Hēilóngjiāng (黑龍江), all came to pay tribute.
In the fourth year, spring, first month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
Bèizǐ Shuòtuō (貝子碩託) was demoted to Fǔguó Gōng (輔國公) for his crimes.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the Emperor's third daughter, Gùlún Gōngzhǔ (固倫公主), was married to Kē'ěrqìn Èfù Qítātè (科爾沁額駙祁他特).
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Shěn Zhìxiáng (沈志祥) was enfeoffed as Xùshùn Gōng (續順公).
Mongols, including Lākè (喇克), came to surrender from Jǐnzhōu (錦州).
On the *dīnghài* day,
Táijí Gábùchǔ (台吉噶布褚) and others from the Sūníté (蘇尼特) department led their people to surrender.
In this month,
the Míng appointed Hóng Chéngchóu (洪承疇) as Supreme Commander of Jì (薊) and Liáo (遼).
In the second month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
Wǔyīng Jùnwáng Ājígé (武英郡王阿濟格) was ordered to lead troops to conquer Míng.
On the *rén'yín* day,
the Emperor personally commanded the main army to follow.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
they reached Wēngqǐ'ěrhún (翁啟爾渾).
Ājígé (阿濟格) sent an envoy to report victory.
Mongol departments, including Nàimàn (奈曼), led thirteen banners of troops to join.
On the *gēngxū* day,
they encamped at Sōngshān (松山).
Kǒng Yǒudé (孔有德), Gěng Zhòngmíng (耿仲明), Shàng Kěxǐ (尚可喜), Shí Tíngzhù (石廷柱), and Mǎ Guāngyuǎn (馬光遠) used cannons to attack the various forts outside the city,
conquering them.
Tǎbùnáng Bùyán (塔布囊布顏) was dispatched to lead troops to guard the mouth of the Wūxīn Hé (烏欣河).
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the Emperor ascended the southern ridge of Sōngshān (松山),
and instructed the generals on strategy.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
cannons were arrayed to attack the city,
and the parapets were completely destroyed.
Míng Vice General Jīn Guófèng (金國鳳) resisted stubbornly.
The Emperor ordered scaling ladders to be erected for a swift assault.
Dàishàn (代善) requested to wait until the next day,
and the Emperor acceded to him.
The Míng people then repaired the city parapets,
and our army could not enter.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Ājígé (阿濟格), Níkān (尼堪), Luōtuō (羅托) and others were ordered to besiege Tǎshān (塔山) and Liánshān (連山).
On the *wùwǔ* day of the third month, the first day of the lunar month,
the Míng army reinforced Xìngshān.
Our troops ambushed them,
beheading fifty men.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
we dug tunnels to attack Sōngshān City.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Nàhǎi and others were ordered to gallop and raid Xìngshān.
Shí Tíngzhù and Mǎ Guāngyuǎn attacked Guānmínshān Terrace
and captured it.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Duō'ěrgǔn, Dùdù, and others reported in a memorial that they had traveled from Běijīng to the border of Shānxī,
then returned to Shāndōng,
attacked Jǐnán Prefecture and captured it.
They ravaged thousands of *lǐ*.
The Míng troops scattered at the mere sight of them.
They captured one prefecture, one department, three counties, and fifty-seven towns.
The Grand Coordinator of Xuān-Dà, Lú Xiàngshēng, was killed in battle.
They captured Dédég Wáng Zhū Yóu_móu_, Commander of the Commandery Zhū Cí_móu_, General of the State Guard Zhū Cídǎng, Grand Coordinator Eunuch Féng Yǔnshēng, and others.
They captured over five hundred thousand people
and other goods in proportion.
In this campaign,
the General who Manifests Martial Might, Bèi//lè Yuètō, and the Prince of the State, Mǎzhān, died in the army.
When the Emperor heard, he was greatly saddened
and abstained from food and drink for three days.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Duō'ěrgǔn and Dùdù again reported that they had emerged from Qiān'ān County through Qīngshān Pass,
encountered Míng troops,
and won all twenty-four battles.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
they again attacked Sōngshān City.
Míng Eunuch Gāo Qǐqián and Grand General Zǔ Dàshòu dispatched Deputy Generals Zǔ Kèyǒng, Xú Chāngyǒng, and others from Níngyuǎn to lead troops towards Jǐnzhōu.
Ā'ěrsàlán and others defeated them.
Upon hearing this, the Emperor
rushed to Jǐnzhōu to supervise the army,
beheaded Xú Chāngyǒng on the battlefield,
and captured Zǔ Kèyǒng.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the siege of Sōngshān was lifted.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor stationed at Jǐnzhōu.
Duō'ěrgǔn and others' army returned to Shèngjīng.
In the summer, on the *wùzǐ* day of the fourth month, the first day of the lunar month,
Ājígé raided Liánshān.
On the *rénchén* day,
they met at Jǐnzhōu.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Emperor crossed the Dàlínghé and stationed.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Dùdù and others' army returned.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to Shèngjīng,
wept for Yuètō before entering,
and suspended court for three days.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Kùlǔkè Dá'ěrhàn Ālái and Mǎláxī were appointed Mongol Commanders-in-Chief.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Suǒhún and Sàbìhàn were appointed Deliberative Ministers.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the Prince of the Second Rank Yuètō was posthumously granted the title of Prince Kèqín of the First Rank.
On the *wùwǔ* day of the fifth month,
Bèizǐ Piāngǔ was found guilty
and stripped of his title.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Zhèng Qīnwáng Jí'ěrhāláng led troops to raid Jǐnzhōu, Sōngshān, and Xìngshān.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Sūní//tè Táijí Mǎnggǔsī and É'ěrzhài led their followers to submit.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Xítèkù, Shā'ěrhǔdá, and others defeated Míng troops at Jǐnzhōu.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Jí'ěrhāláng reported in a memorial that they had entered the Míng border
and won all nine battles.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Jí'ěrhāláng's army returned.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Prince of the State Āidùlǐ was appointed Commander-in-Chief.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Yù Qīnwáng Duōduó was summoned and his crimes enumerated.
He was pardoned,
but only for his failure in the Míng campaign
and for not personally seeing off Ruì Qīnwáng when he set out,
he was demoted to Bèilè of the Second Rank.
On the *wùzǐ* day of the sixth month,
the Mongols Ālánchái, Sānggá'ěrzhài, and others reported that Yuètō, during his lifetime, plotted rebellion with his father-in-law Suǒnuòmù.
Dàishàn, Jí'ěrhāláng, and Duō'ěrgǔn all requested a thorough investigation.
The Emperor, considering Yuètō already dead,
did not pursue the matter,
and also pardoned Suǒnuòmù from punishment.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Mǎfútǎ and Bāhānà were dispatched to enfeoff Lady Zhào, the wife of King Lǐ Zōng of Cháoxiǎn, as Queen of Cháoxiǎn,
and her eldest son as Crown Prince.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the Han military was divided into four banners.
Shí Tíngzhù, Mǎ Guāngyuǎn, Wáng Shìxuǎn, and Bāyán were appointed Commanders-in-Chief,
and the banner colors were changed.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the Míng imperial edicts previously received by Hádá, Yèhè, Wūlā, and Huīfā were burned at the Dǔgōngdiàn.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Yī'ěrdēng and Gá'ěrmǎ were appointed Deliberative Ministers,
and Xīngnè concurrently held the position of Deliberative Minister.
In the autumn, on the *dīngsì* day of the seventh month,
officials were dispatched with a letter to the Míng Emperor to discuss peace.
Zhū Yóu_móu_ and others were also ordered to submit memorials,
and it was promised that if an agreement was reached, they would be released and returned.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
King Lǐ Zōng of Cháoxiǎn captured Xióngdǎo
and presented Jiāhāchán as captive.
On the *yǐhài* day,
an edict was issued that any Manchu, Han, or Mongol who could charge and break through enemy lines, be the first to ascend and capture a city,
would be given a horse.
In the eighth month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
members of the imperial clan were granted titles such as Gùshān Bèizǐ, Zhèngguógōng, Fǔguógōng, Zhèngguó Jiāngjūn, Fèngguó Jiāngjūn, varying in rank.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Bèilè Háogé was ordered to manage the Board of Revenue,
Dùdù to manage the Board of Rites,
Duōduó to manage the Board of War.
Sà'ěrjiū and others led troops to campaign against the Kù'ěrkā tribe.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the various *zhāngjīng* of the Huīhuàchéng Tǔmò//tè presented the Míng annual tribute they had received.
On the *yǐmǎo* day of the ninth month, the first day of the lunar month,
as Sūndálǐ and eighty-three others had distinguished themselves by following Ruì Qīnwáng into the pass,
each was granted an official position of varying rank
and awarded the title Bàtúlǔ.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Commander-in-Chief Dùléi was found guilty
and stripped of his office.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Bèilè Háogé was reinstated as Héshuò Sù Qīnwáng.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Ājígé, Ābātài, and Dùdù led troops to raid Jǐnzhōu and Níngyuǎn.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Yuètō's son Luóluòhóng was enfeoffed as Bèilè of the Second Rank.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Láimùbù and Dùshā of the imperial clan were appointed Deliberative Ministers,
Yīng'é'ěrdài as Commander-in-Chief,
and Mǎfútǎ as Vice President of the Board of Revenue.
In the winter, on the *bǐngxū* day of the tenth month,
Háogé and Duōduó led troops to again raid Jǐnzhōu and Níngyuǎn.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Sūní//tè tribe's Mò'ěrgēn Táijí Téngjīsī and other *bèilè*, and the Ābà//gāi tribe's Éqígénuòyán and others, each leading their respective tribes,
came to submit from Kā'ěrkā.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Emperor went hunting in Hádá.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Liú Zhīyuán was appointed Commander-in-Chief,
and Kāzhìhǎi as Deliberative Minister.
On the *jiǎyín* day of the eleventh month, the first day of the lunar month,
Háogé reported in a memorial that Assistant Commander Ālántài led Mongols to submit.
They encountered Míng troops at the northern hill of Níngyuǎn
and defeated them,
beheading Míng Grand General Jīn Guófèng.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Suǒhǎi, Sàmǔshíkā, and others were dispatched to campaign against the Suǒlún tribe.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor went hunting in Yèhè.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day of the twelfth month,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In this year,
Énàbù, Mòyīn, É'ěrpén, and others from Hēilóngjiāng,
Tǔxiètú, Émùbù É'ěrdéní, and others from the Kā'ěrkā tribe,
and various tribes from Kā'ěrkā, Sūní//tè, Wūzhūmùqín, Kē'ěrqìn, Kèxī//kèténg, and Tǔmò//tè,
all sent envoys to pay tribute.
In the spring of the fifth year, on the *jiǎzǐ* day of the first month,
the Cháoxiǎn hostage prince Lǐ Guī was ordered to return to his father due to illness,
and was still required to send another son as hostage.
Wēng'ādài, Duōjìlǐ, and others were dispatched to garrison Jǐnzhōu.
On the *guǐwèi* day of the intercalary first month, the first day of the lunar month,
each banner's Commander-in-Chief was ordered to inspect their affiliated garrisons and villages,
investigate the impoverished,
and redress unjust cases.
In the second month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
Duōjìlǐ was dispatched with three hundred troops from Nínggǔtǎ to campaign against the Wùzhálā tribe.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Vice President of the Board of Revenue Mǎfútǎ died.
Chē'ěrgé replaced him,
and Juéluó Xīhàn was appointed Vice President of the Board of Works.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the third son of King Lǐ Zōng of Cháoxiǎn, _móu_, came as hostage.
In the third month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
Láosà, Wúbài, and others were dispatched to raid Guǎngníng.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Láosà and Wúbài were punished for their dawdling, with varying degrees of penalty.
Sàmǔshíkā and others campaigned against the Hǔ'ěrhā tribe
and captured Yǎkèsà City.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Jí'ěrhāláng and Duōduó were ordered to build Yìzhōu City,
station troops and cultivate land,
and advance towards Shānhǎiguān.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Assistant President of the Board of Revenue Shuòzhān requisitioned Cháoxiǎn naval provisions and rice to the Dàlíng and Xiǎolíng Rivers.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Suǒhǎi and Sàmǔshíkā reported victory in their campaign against the Suǒlún tribe.
In the summer, on the *rénzǐ* day of the fourth month, the first day of the lunar month,
the tradition of princes and *bèilè* presenting gifts on New Year's Day and the Emperor's birthday was abolished.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Suǒhǎi and Sàmǔshíkā returned from their campaign against the Suǒlún tribe.
The Emperor hosted a banquet to reward them at the Shíshèngsì.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Emperor inspected the army at Yìzhōu.
On the *guǐwèi* day of the fifth month,
we crossed the Liáo Hé.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Shuòzhān arrived with the Joseon navy.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Emperor arrived at Yìzhōu.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Sūbāndài and others from the Duōluōtè tribe of Mongolia sent envoys from Xìngshān to pledge their surrender.
The Emperor ordered Jíěrhāláng and others to lead troops to meet them,
cautioning them:
“Do not take many men on this trip.
If the enemy sees our forces are few,
they will certainly come to resist in battle.
Divide our troops into three,
with the vanguard resisting in battle,
and the latter two divisions as support.”
Upon reaching Xìngshān,
Zǔ Dàshòu indeed sent Liú Zhōuzhì and Wú Sānguì to array their forces and press upon us.
Jíěrhāláng and others feigned retreat,
then unleashed their troops in a counterattack,
utterly defeating them.
On the *wùxū* day,
Luōsà, Wúbài, and others were ordered to raid the coast.
Three hundred thirty-seven households of the Suǒlún tribe continued to surrender.
On the *rényín* day,
the Emperor led his army to attack and capture Wǔlǐtái.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Jǐnzhōu was attacked with red-jacketed cannons.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
their grain was reaped, and we returned.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the imperial carriage returned to the capital.
On the *yǐchǒu* day of the sixth month,
Duōěrgǔn, Háogé, Dùdù, Ābātài, Jíěrhāláng, and others garrisoned and farmed at Yìzhōu.
On the *wùchén* day,
Joseon Crown Prince Lǐ arrived.
Previously,
Joseon had sent Commander-in-Chief Lín Qìngyè and others to transport rice with our envoy Hóng Níkā and others from Dàlíng Hé to Sānshāndǎo,
but they encountered a storm,
and half of them capsized and perished.
They also suffered a defeat fighting Ming soldiers.
Therefore, Lěngwǎn was ordered to go to Gàizhōu and Yàozhōu,
leaving one thousand five hundred of his soldiers at Hǎizhōu.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Duōjìlǐ and Kāzhù returned from their campaign against the Wùzhālá tribe.
Joseon King's second son, Lǐ Hào, was sent back to visit his parents.
On the *gēngchén* day, the first day of the seventh month of autumn,
for their merits in the campaign against the Suǒlún,
Suǒhǎi and others were rewarded and promoted to varying ranks.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the crimes of violating regulations during the Suǒlún campaign were determined,
and Sāmùshénkā and others were demoted and punished to varying degrees.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Duōěrgǔn and others reported the capture of eleven towers at Jǐnzhōu,
and requested to divide their troops into two wings for garrisoning.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Ming Governor Hóng Chéngchóu garrisoned Xìngshān with forty thousand troops,
and sent cavalry to challenge us.
Duōěrgǔn and others defeated them.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Wúbài was sent to assist Duōěrgǔn's army.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Xítèkù, Jìxíhā, and others led troops to campaign against the Suǒlún tribe.
The Emperor visited the hot springs at Ānshān.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Duōěrgǔn reported defeating Ming troops at Jǐnzhōu,
and Dùdù again defeated them at Níngyuǎn.
On the *jǐwèi* day of the eighth month,
Xīfú and others were sent to Zhāngjiākǒu for mutual trade.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Duōěrgǔn reported defeating Ming troops at Jǐnzhōu,
and again defeating them at Dàlíng Hé.
On the *yǐyǒu* day of the ninth month,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Jíěrhāláng, Ājígé, Ādálǐ, Duōduó, Luōluòhóng were ordered to relieve the siege of Jǐnzhōu and Sōngshān.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Duōěrgǔn reported defeating Ming troops at Sōngshān.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Fènghuángchéng was re-fortified.
On the *rénxū* day of the tenth month of winter,
Yīngéěrdài and others were sent to Joseon to demand an explanation.
On the *rénshēn* day,
on the occasion of the Emperor's birthday,
a great amnesty was declared.
On the *wùyín* day, the first day of the eleventh month,
an edict exempted Joseon from nine-tenths of its annual tribute rice.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Jíěrhāláng reported defeating Ming troops at Tǎshān, Xìngshān, and beneath the city walls of Jǐnzhōu.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Āmǐn died in confinement.
On the *wùxū* day,
Joseon King's second son, Lǐ Hào, came as a hostage.
On the *gēngxū* day of the twelfth month,
Duōěrgǔn, Háogé, Dùdù, Ābātài were ordered to relieve the siege of Jǐnzhōu.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Joseon King's third son, Lǐ **[missing character, appears as a square in input]**, was sent back.
Xítèkù and Jìxíhā campaigned against the Suǒlún tribe,
capturing Bómùbóguǒěr,
and over nine hundred captives.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Yīngéěrdài and others returned from Joseon,
bringing back four officials, including Minister Jīn Shēnghēiní, in chains.
This year,
the Khalkha tribe's Zhāsàkètú sent envoys to pay tribute.
On the *gēngchén* day of the first month of spring in the sixth year,
Joseon King Lǐ Zōng presented a memorial to express his apologies.
On the *rénchén* day,
Xítèkù, Jìxíhā, and others' army returned.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Xítèkù was promoted to Third-Class Commander-in-Chief.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Emperor's fourth daughter, Gùlún Princess Yǎtú, was married to Bìěrtǎgáěréfù, son of the Kēěrqìn Zhuólǐkètú Prince Wú Kèshàn.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Second-Class Deputy General Luōsà was found guilty,
his title of Shuòwēngkēluóbātúlú was revoked,
and he was demoted to First-Class Brigadier-General.
On the *jǐwèi* day of the second month,
since many people under the Eight Banners' *zuǒlǐng* were impoverished,
the Board of Revenue was ordered to investigate and report.
An edict instructed the *zuǒlǐng* not to indulge in drink and neglect their duties.
Forty-eight individuals who lost their positions due to drinking were all dismissed.
An edict instructed the various princes and ministers to teach their sons and younger brothers archery.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Duōěrgǔn and others reported defeating Ming troops.
On the *jǐmǎo* day of the third month,
Jíěrhāláng and others relieved the siege of Jǐnzhōu.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Prince Héshuò Ruì Duōěrgǔn and Prince Sù Háogé were demoted to Duōluō Jùnwáng,
while Duōluō Bèilè Ābātài, Dùdù, and those below them were fined silver to varying degrees.
At this time,
Zǔ Dàshòu held Jǐnzhōu for the Ming,
and repeatedly refused to surrender.
The Emperor ordered the various princes to take turns besieging him.
However, Duōěrgǔn and others camped thirty *lǐ* outside Jǐnzhōu,
and also frequently sent soldiers home,
hence this order.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Joseon Commander-in-Chief Liǔ Lín and others were sent to lead troops to assist Jíěrhāláng's army.
On the *rényín* day,
Jíěrhāláng reported capturing the outer city of Jǐnzhōu.
Initially,
our army encircled Jǐnzhōu with camps,
deep trenches and high ramparts,
cutting off the Ming troops' access,
causing great fear within the city.
Mongolian Bèilè Nuòmùqí, Tàijí Wúbāshí, and others requested to surrender,
and also promised to offer the East Gate as an inside connection.
Zǔ Dàshòu realized this [plot],
and planned to seize Wúbāshí and others.
Thereupon, the various Mongolians loudly protested,
and engaged in battle with the Ming troops.
Our army responded from outside,
and thus captured their outer city.
Zǔ Dàshòu retreated to defend the inner city.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Nuòmùqí, Wúbāshí, and others came to surrender with over six thousand Mongolians,
arriving at Shèngjīng.
On the *dīngwèi* day of the fourth month of summer,
Āháníkān and others were sent to lead troops to Jǐnzhōu to assist Jíěrhāláng's army.
Jíěrhāláng reported defeating Ming reinforcements at Sōngshān.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Kǒng Yǒudé and Shàng Kěxǐ were sent to assist in besieging Jǐnzhōu.
Duōěrgǔn and others, hearing of the surrender of the Mongolians at Jǐnzhōu,
requested to offer their services to atone for their crimes.
This was not permitted.
On the *dīngchǒu* day of the fifth month,
Ming Governor Hóng Chéngchóu arrived with sixty thousand troops to reinforce Jǐnzhōu,
and camped on the northern hill of Sōngshān.
Jíěrhāláng and others attacked and routed them,
beheading two thousand.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Bāěrdáqí of the Suǒlún tribe surrendered.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Xīfú and others were sent to inspect the camps, moats, and trenches at Jǐnzhōu.
On the *rényín* day,
an edict instructed Guīhuàchéng Commander Gǔlùgé and others to expand the outer city,
build watchtowers,
and deepen the moats,
for defense.
On the *dīngwèi* day of the sixth month,
Duōěrgǔn and Háogé were ordered to relieve the siege of Jǐnzhōu.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Jíěrhāláng, Duōěrgǔn, and others combined forces and defeated Ming reinforcements at Sōngshān.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Academician Luóshuò was sent with Zǔ Zérùn's letter to persuade Zǔ Dàshòu to surrender.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Duōěrgǔn and others again reported defeating Ming reinforcements at Sōngshān.
On the *wùyín* day of the seventh month of autumn,
Manchu Èmókètú, Mongolian Dùdāng, Han Chinese Cuī Guāngqián, and other successful *jǔrén* candidates were each bestowed with a court robe,
while first, second, and third-class *shēngyuán* were given satin and cloth to varying degrees.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Kǒng Yǒudé, Gěng Zhòngmíng, Shàng Kěxǐ, and their deputy commanders were sent to lead troops to assist in besieging Jǐnzhōu.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the merits and demerits of the siege of Jǐnzhōu were deliberated,
and princes and those below were rewarded and punished to varying degrees.
On the *jiǎchén* day of the eighth month,
for the meritorious service of the generals who captured the outer city of Jǐnzhōu,
the ranks of Áobài, Láosà, Yīěrdēng, and others were promoted.
Láosà’s title of Shuòwēngkēluóbātúlǔ was restored.
On the *yǐsì* day,
our army fought a combined battle with the Míng army.
Yáng Guózhù, the Míng garrison commander of Yánghé, was defeated and died.
Zǔ Dàshòu divided his troops from Jǐnzhōu into three,
but was unable to break through the encirclement.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Duōěrjì Jìnóng of the Wūzhūmùqín tribe was enfeoffed as Héshuò Sūlè Qīnwáng,
and Duōěrjì Éqígè Nuóyán of the Ābàgāi tribe as Zhuólìkètú Jùnwáng.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Emperor, knowing that Míng Hóng Chéngchóu, Governor Qiū Mínyǎng, and others were leading 130,000 relief troops to Jǐnzhōu,
who were encamped at Sōngshān,
personally led the grand army to counter them.
Jíěrhāláng remained behind to guard.
The princes, *bèilè*, and high ministers, seeing the Míng army's great strength,
advised the Emperor to proceed slowly.
The Emperor laughed and said,
“I am only afraid that when they hear of Our arrival,
they will secretly flee.
If they do not leave,
We shall crush them as easily as withered wood.”
Thereupon, he rapidly advanced.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
he crossed the Liáohé River.
Hóng Chéngchóu attacked our right flank with his troops,
but Háogé defeated them.
On the *rénxū* day,
the Emperor arrived at Qījiābǎo,
and was about to proceed to Gāiqiáo.
He summoned Duōěrgǔn to bring his troops and meet him.
Duōěrgǔn requested to encamp between Sōngshān and Xìngshān.
The Emperor agreed,
and proceeded to Sōngshān.
The Míng stationed a force on Rǔfēngshān,
and from Rǔfēng to Sōngshān,
arranged seven infantry battalions,
while cavalry encircled the city to the east, west, and north.
Their fortifications were very strong.
Our army encamped, cutting across the main road, from the southern mountains of Wūxīnhé to the sea.
The Emperor said to his generals,
“The enemy is numerous,
their provisions must be insufficient.
When they see us cut off their supply route,
they will surely lose their will to hold out.
We will set up an ambush and await them,
and their entire army can be annihilated.”
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Míng army attacked,
and was repulsed.
They were again defeated at Tǎshān,
and twelve granaries of their stored grain were captured.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Míng army attacked again,
and was again repulsed.
At this time, Hóng Chéngchóu, lacking provisions,
wished to obtain supplies from Níngyuǎn.
The Emperor, knowing he was about to flee,
set up ambushes along various routes,
and ordered his generals to stand firm
and block the roads leading back to Níngyuǎn and fleeing to Tǎshān and Jǐnzhōu.
That night,
Míng Wú Sānguì and six other garrison commanders indeed secretly fled first.
In the darkness,
they were intercepted by our ambushers
and suffered a crushing defeat.
Only Cáo Biànjiāo and Wáng Tíngchén returned to Sōngshān.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
we captured four more of their towers.
Wáng Pǔ and Wú Sānguì fled to Xìngshān.
Cáo Biànjiāo abandoned Rǔfēngshān
and launched a night raid on the Emperor's camp.
After a fierce battle,
Biànjiāo was wounded and fled.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Wú Sānguì and Wáng Pǔ fled from Xìngshān to Níngyuǎn,
where they encountered our ambushers
and were again greatly defeated.
Sānguì and Pǔ barely escaped with their lives.
In this campaign,
fifty thousand heads were taken,
seven thousand horses captured,
and military supplies and weapons were abundant.
Hóng Chéngchóu gathered over ten thousand defeated soldiers and entered Sōngshān,
defending the city from within,
unable to fight.
Our army then dug trenches and surrounded it.
On this day,
Sānggáěr of the Zhālǔtè tribe arrived with his troops.
On the *yǐhài* day of the ninth month,
Qīnwáng Wú Kèshàn of Kēěrqìn Zhuólìkètú arrived with his troops.
Duōěrgǔn and Háogé were ordered to divide their forces and return to guard Shèngjīng.
On the *wùyín* day,
Níngyuǎn was raided.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Consort Chén of Guānjūgōng fell ill.
The Emperor was about to return to the capital,
leaving Dùdù, Ābātài, and others to besiege Jǐnzhōu,
Duōduó, Ādálǐ, and others to besiege Sōngshān,
and Ājígé and others to besiege Xìngshān.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the imperial carriage returned.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Consort Chén passed away.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *guǐmǎo* day, the first day of the tenth month of winter,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Ābài was dispatched to garrison Rǔfēngshān south of Jǐnzhōu.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Kǒng Yǒudé, Gěng Zhòngmíng, Shàng Kěxǐ, and others were dispatched to assist in the siege of Jǐnzhōu.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Consort Chén was posthumously elevated to Yuánfēi,
with the posthumous title Mǐnhuì Gōnghé.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Mòěrgēntáijí Téngjīsī of the Sūnítè tribe was enfeoffed as Duōluó Mòěrgēn Jùnwáng.
On the *yǐhài* day of the eleventh month,
Duōěrgǔn, Luótuō, and Túnqí were ordered to garrison Jǐnzhōu,
and Háogé, Mǎndáhǎi, and others to garrison Sōngshān.
On the *jiǎyín* day of the twelfth month,
Jíěrhāláng and Duōěrgǔn reported the defeat of Hóng Chéngchóu at Sōngshān.
On the *guǐmǎo* day of the second month of spring in the seventh year,
the Emperor went hunting in Yèhè.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Míng Prince Dé, Zhū Yóulù, died,
and was buried with due ceremony.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Ājígé reported the defeat of Míng troops at Níngyuǎn.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Háogé, Ādálǐ, Duōduó, Luóluòhóng, and others reported the capture of Sōngshān,
and the capture of Míng Governor-General Hóng Chéngchóu,
Governor Qiū Mínyǎng,
Garrison Commanders Wáng Tíngchén, Cáo Biànjiāo, and Zǔ Dàlè,
and Guerrilla Commanders Zǔ Dàmíng and Dàchéng.
Previously,
Hóng Chéngchóu's relief was cut off,
and he repeatedly tried to break out of the encirclement but failed.
His副将 Fùjiàng Xià Chéngdé secretly agreed to surrender,
and offered to act as an inside agent,
giving his son Xià Shū as a hostage.
At midnight on the *wùwǔ* day,
Háogé and others scaled the city walls and breached them.
When the victory was reported,
the Emperor distributed the captives and spoils to the officers and soldiers,
and stored the captured weapons in Sōngshān city.
On the *rénxū* day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the *guǐyǒu* day of the third month,
Qiū Mínyǎng, Wáng Tíngchén, and Cáo Biànjiāo were executed.
Hóng Chéngchóu and Zǔ Dàlè were ordered to come to the capital,
while Zǔ Dàmíng and Dàchéng were released into Jǐnzhōu.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Jǐnzhōu was captured,
and Zǔ Dàshòu surrendered with over seven thousand of his troops.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Ājígé and others reported that the Míng had sent Director Mǎ Shàoyú of the Bureau of Military Affairs to sue for peace,
and presented a letter from the Míng Emperor to the Minister of War Chén Xīnjiǎ as proof.
The Emperor said,
“Many of the Míng's official documents are not truthful,
and their language is exaggerated,
showing no sincerity for peace.
However, their true intentions are unknown,
and peace is indeed Our long-cherished wish.
We, for the sake of millions of lives,
if the matter is truly achieved,
each will rule their own country,
allowing the people to live in peace,
then both nations will enjoy the blessings of great peace.
You all convey Our intentions to them.”
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Duōěrgǔn and Háogé were ordered to garrison Xìngshān and Tǎshān,
while Jíěrhāláng, Ājígé, Ādálǐ, and others returned to the capital.
On the *dīngwèi* day of the fourth month of summer,
an imperial edict ordered Wú Sānguì and others to surrender.
On the *gēngxū* day,
two suns, one large and one small, appeared together,
the larger one quickly disappearing.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Jíěrhāláng, Duōěrgǔn, Háogé, and others reported the capture of Tǎshān.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
they reported the capture of Xìngshān.
The three cities of Sōngshān, Xìngshān, and Tǎshān were destroyed.
Jíěrhāláng and others returned with their troops.
Ābātài was left to guard Jǐnzhōu.
On the Jǐsì new moon of the fifth month,
Jì'ěrhāláng and others reported that Mǎ Shàoyú had been dispatched to negotiate peace,
and an envoy was sent to welcome him.
On Guǐyǒu day,
Hóng Chéngchóu, Zǔ Dàshòu, and others arrived.
They entered for an audience and requested death.
The Emperor pardoned them,
instructing them to serve with utmost loyalty and devotion.
Chéngchóu and others tearfully expressed gratitude.
The Emperor asked Chéngchóu,
"The Míng Emperor, seeing captured imperial clan members,
ignored them as if nothing happened.
As for generals and commanders who died in battle, and those who were utterly desperate and surrendered to us,
he killed them and their families.
Is this an old rule,
or a new precedent?"
Chéngchóu replied,
"In the past, there was no such precedent.
Recently, it is due to the unwarranted memorials of civil officials,
that this has occurred."
The Emperor said,
"When the ruler is ignorant and his ministers obscure the truth,
innocent lives are unjustly taken to this extent.
If generals and soldiers are captured and beg for surrender,
even if they could be ransomed,
they should still be ransomed.
How can their wives and children be executed!"
Chéngchóu said,
"Your Majesty is truly a benevolent ruler."
On Wùyín day,
the Shànyǒu heterodox sect was prohibited,
and its leader Lǐ Guóliáng and sixteen others were executed.
On Rénwǔ day,
Míng envoy Mǎ Shàoyú and his party finally arrived.
On Xīnchǒu day of the sixth month,
Dūchá Yuàn Assistant Ministers Zǔ Kěfǎ and Zhāng Cúnrén stated:
"Míng bandits and robbers have been rising daily.
Their military strength is exhausted, and their granaries are empty.
Conscription and levies are not progressing.
The situation is like crumbling tiles.
Eight or nine tenths of the generals defending Liáo have been lost.
Now, having no alternative, they beg for peace.
Their plan must be to move south.
It is fitting to require them to pay tribute and declare themselves vassals,
taking the Huáng Hé as the border."
The Emperor did not accept this.
He replied to the Míng Emperor in a letter, saying:
"Previously, We repeatedly sent letters to cultivate good relations.
Your country did not comply.
What is past is past.
What more is there to say?
We have received Heaven's favor.
From the northeastern coast to the northwest,
including the lands where dogs and deer are used, and foxes and sables are produced,
as well as the Èlútè tribe and the source of the Wò'nán River,
all have submitted to Us.
Ménggǔ and Cháoxiǎn are entirely incorporated into Our dominion.
Therefore, We have proclaimed this to Heaven and Earth,
assumed the rightful position, and changed the reign title.
Recently, Our armies entered your territory,
conquered cities, and broke through formations.
Advancing triumphantly,
what is there to fear?
We, however, are earnestly considering the welfare of millions of lives.
If each can assess misfortune and fortune,
and sincerely make peace,
from this point forward,
all past grievances will be released.
The distinction between superior and inferior
would then be of no concern.
An ancient saying goes: 'When feelings are clear, there is understanding;
when feelings are obscured, there is darkness.'
Envoys will travel back and forth,
aiming for face-to-face meetings,
so that feelings are not obstructed.
In important matters of joy and sorrow,
we will mutually offer congratulations and condolences.
Each year, we will exchange gifts according to the produce of our lands.
Deserters from both countries will also be returned to each other.
Let Níngyuǎn Shuāngshù Bǎo be your country's boundary,
and Tǎshān be Our country's boundary,
with mutual markets established in the central area of Liánshān.
For those traveling by sea,
the east and west of Huángchéng Dǎo will serve as the boundary.
Those who cross it will be punished by their respective authorities.
If your country accepts these words,
the two rulers may personally swear an oath to Heaven and Earth,
or dispatch high ministers to solemnize the alliance.
We shall obey your command.
Otherwise, do not send envoys again."
Thereupon, the Míng envoys and their retinue were generously rewarded,
and sent away.
Later, the Míng deliberations changed,
and the peace settlement ultimately failed.
On Guǐmǎo day,
an edict was issued to the various Wáng and Bèilè,
stating that anyone leading troops or going on a hunt,
who trampled crops, would be punished.
On Jiǎchén day,
the Hànjūn Bāqí were established,
with Zǔ Zérùn and seven others as Dūtǒng.
Bèizi Luōtuō was made Dūchá Yuàn Chéngzhèng,
Wú Dáhǎi was made Xíngbù Chéngzhèng,
and Lángqiú was made Lǐbù Chéngzhèng.
On Yǐsì day,
Duōluó Ānpíng Bèilè Dùdù passed away.
In autumn, on Gēngwǔ day of the seventh month,
an edict was issued to the various Wáng, Bèilè, and high ministers, saying:
"You must all be thoroughly aware of the virtuous and the unworthy among your subordinates.
If you know but do not recommend them,
how can you encourage?
During Tàizǔ's time,
Sūwán Zhá'ěrgùqí Fèi Yīngdōng and others, upon seeing a person with merit,
would first commend them themselves,
and then recommend them;
upon seeing a person with shortcomings,
they would first reprimand them themselves,
and then impeach them.
Thus, people felt no pride
and no complaints.
Now, there are none as impartial and upright as that."
The Wáng, Bèilè, and others all apologized.
On Xīnwèi day,
Chénggōng Suǒhǎi was dismissed from office due to his offenses.
On Rénshēn day,
Niǔhēi was appointed Yìzhèng Dàchén.
On Bǐngzǐ day,
for their merits,
Duōluó Ruì Jùnwáng Duō'ěrgǔn and Sù Jùnwáng Háogé were restored to the rank of Héshuò Qīnwáng.
Duōluó Bèilè Duōduó was promoted to Duōluó Jùnwáng.
Zhèng Qīnwáng Jì'ěrhāláng and others below him received varying rewards.
On Wùyín day,
Fǔguó Gōng Bóhétuō was sent to replace the garrison at Jǐnzhōu.
On Yǐyǒu day,
the offenses of Jì'ěrhāláng and the other generals for violating regulations during the campaign against Jǐnzhōu were discussed.
The Emperor, considering their long service,
pardoned them all.
An edict was issued to the Xíngbù to exercise caution in reviewing legal cases.
On Jǐchǒu day,
Duōluó Jùnwáng Ādálǐ was ordered to oversee the affairs of the Lǐbù.
On Jǐhài day of the eighth month,
cannons were cast at Jǐnzhōu.
On Guǐmǎo day,
Zhènguó Jiāngjūn Bābùhǎi was found guilty,
and demoted to a commoner.
On Guǐchǒu day,
the merits of the generals who conquered Jǐnzhōu, Sōngshān, Xìngshān, and Tǎshān were deliberated,
and they received varying promotions in rank.
In the ninth month,
the various Wáng, Bèilè, and high ministers of the outer dependencies who participated in the campaign against Jǐnzhōu were rewarded in varying degrees for their merits.
On Dīngchǒu day,
Bèizi Luōtuō and others were sent to replace the garrison at Jǐnzhōu.
On Rénwǔ day,
Shā'ěrhǔdá and others were ordered to campaign against the Hǔ'ěrhā tribe.
In winter, on Guǐmǎo day of the tenth month,
Yīng'é'ěrdài and others were sent to interrogate Cháoxiǎn Grand Secretary Cuī Míngjí and others for their offenses.
On Xīnhài day,
Ābātài was appointed Fèngmìng Dàjiāngjūn,
and, together with Tú'ěrgé, commanded troops to attack Míng.
On Rénzǐ day,
the army marched.
On Dīngsì day,
the Emperor was unwell,
and all crimes below capital punishment were pardoned.
On Jǐwèi day,
Duōduó and Ādálǐ were ordered to station troops at Níngyuǎn.
An imperial edict commanded Wú Sānguì to surrender.
Zǔ Dàshòu was also ordered to send a letter inviting him.
Sānguì
was Dàshòu's nephew.
On Jiǎzǐ day,
Zhèng Qīnwáng Jì'ěrhāláng, Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrgǔn, Sù Qīnwáng Háogé, and Wǔyīng Jùnwáng Ājìgé were appointed to adjudicate general political affairs.
Matters they could not decide were to be reported to the Emperor.
On Dīngchǒu day of the eleventh month,
Duōduó reported defeating Wú Sānguì's troops.
On Bǐngshēn day,
Ābātài reported that he had entered through Qiángzǐ Lǐng and conquered the Chángchéng,
defeating Míng troops at Jìzhōu.
On Jiǎchén day of the intercalary eleventh month,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On Jǐyǒu day,
Shā'ěrhǔdá and others received the surrender of over 1,400 people from the Hǔ'ěrhā tribe.
On Bǐngchén day,
Bābùtài and others were sent to replace the garrison at Jǐnzhōu.
On Jǐwèi day,
imperial kinsman Hán Dài was appointed Bīngbù Chéngzhèng.
Regulations were established for penalties concerning accidentally shooting people or horses during hunts.
In the twelfth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor went out hunting in Yèhè.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Jīn Wéichéng was dispatched to lead troops to garrison Jǐnzhōu.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Emperor stopped at Kāikù'ěr.
The Emperor was unwell.
The princes and *bèizi* requested to cease the hunt,
but he did not permit it.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
a lunar halo with three parhelia appeared.
On the *dīnghài* day,
a solar halo with three parhelia appeared.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In this year,
Zhāsàkè Sāilěng of the Dù'ěrbótè tribe came to court.
In the eighth year, in spring, the first month, on the *bǐngshēn* day, which was the first day of the lunar month,
the Emperor was unwell,
and ordered *héshuò qīnwáng* and those of higher ranks,
including *fù dūtǒng*,
to proceed to the Tángzǐ to perform rituals.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Shā'ěrhǔdá and other commanders returned.
Merits were assessed and rewards were distributed accordingly.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Wú Sānguì, the Ming commander-in-chief of Níngyuǎn, replied to Zǔ Dàshòu's letter,
still indecisive.
Therefore, another imperial edict was sent to him.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Tán Bù and others were dispatched to relieve the garrison at Jǐnzhōu.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Duōluó Bèilè Luóluóhóng was stripped of his title due to an offense.
In the second month, on the *yǐchǒu* day, which was the first day of the lunar month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Mǐnhuìgōnghé Yuánfēi was buried.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the construction of temples was prohibited.
In the third month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
an edict was issued to the officials and common people of Cháoxiǎn not to communicate with the Ming.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
there was an earthquake,
with sound from the western corner to the southeast.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Emperor was unwell,
and pardoned those sentenced to death and lesser crimes.
Ā'ěrjīn and others were dispatched to conquer the Hǔ'ěrhā tribe of Hēilóngjiāng.
Yèchén and others were dispatched to relieve the garrison at Jǐnzhōu.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the regulations for punishments by the Six Boards were revised.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
Jīn Wéichéng and others were dispatched to relieve the garrison at Jǐnzhōu.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Duōduó requested a temporary cessation of military campaigns,
to stop public works,
and to focus on agriculture,
to meet the needs of the people.
In the fifth month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
Luóluóhóng was reinstated as Duōluó Bèilè.
Previously,
the Dálài Lǎmā of the Túbáitè tribe had sent envoys to convey greetings and inquiries.
They had stayed in the capital for eight months,
and now,
they were sent back,
and their envoys were also rewarded.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Nǔshān defeated Ming troops at Jièlíngkǒu.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Ābātài reported that our army had entered Ming territory,
capturing the three prefectures of Héjiān, Shùndé, and Yǎnzhōu, eighteen departments, and sixty-seven counties,
and securing the surrender of one department and five counties.
Thirty-nine battles, large and small, were fought against the Ming,
killing Zhū Yīpèi, the Prince of Lǔ, and the five princely lords of Lèlíng, Yángxìn, Dōngyuán, Ānqīu, and Zīyáng,
as well as over a thousand imperial clansmen and civil and military officials.
Hundreds of thousands of people, livestock, and gold and silver were captured.
The census figures were reported.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Ā'ěrjīn reported victory in the campaign against Hǔ'ěrhā.
In the sixth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
Duōluó Ráoyú Bèilè Ābātài's army returned.
Zhèng Qīnwáng Jí'ěrhāláng, Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrgǔn, and Wǔyīng Jùnwáng Ājígé welcomed him in the suburbs.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Ābātài and the generals and soldiers who participated in the campaign were given silver and satin according to their ranks.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
an edict was issued to the princes and *bèilè* saying:
"Those who manage their livelihoods must be frugal;
those who govern a country place importance on land and people.
You must not solely focus on capturing to enrich your relatives.
Instead, each of you should diligently promote agriculture and sericulture to strengthen the fundamental livelihood."
Àidùlǐ was dispatched to garrison Jǐnzhōu in relief.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Lǐ Zōng, the King of Cháoxiǎn, requested that the troops garrisoning Jǐnzhōu be rotated annually.
On the *gēngyín* day,
an edict was issued to the Boards of Revenue and War to thoroughly investigate the Mongolian population,
enroll them into *zuǒlǐng*,
and ensure they all wore armor.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *wùxū* day,
Ā'ěrjīn and other commanders returned.
Merits were assessed and rewards were distributed accordingly.
An edict was issued to the princes not to adorn saddles and bridles with gold.
Regulations for the residences of princes, *bèilè*, *bèizi*, and dukes were established.
On the *rényín* day,
regulations for punishments for princes and *bèilè* missing court assemblies were established.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
ceremonies for mutual greetings between outer feudal princes, *bèilè*, *bèizi*, and dukes, and inner princes, *bèilè*, *bèizi*, and dukes were established.
On the *dīngsì* day,
due to the great victory in the campaign against Ming,
an edict was proclaimed to Cháoxiǎn.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Mǎndáhǎi was ordered to take charge of the Dùcháyùan.
In the eighth month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
Bèizi Luótuō was condemned to death for his crimes,
but was spared from execution
and imprisoned.
On the *wùchén* day,
Gǒng'ādài of the imperial clan was appointed *Lìbù Chéngzhèng*,
Lángqiú as *Lǐbù Chéngzhèng*,
and Xīngnà as *Gōngbù Chéngzhèng*.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Emperor held court in the Chóngzhèng Diàn.
That evening,
at the *hài* hour,
he collapsed without illness,
at the age of fifty-two,
having reigned for seventeen years.
In the ninth month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
he was buried in Zhāolíng.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
his honored posthumous title was: Yìngtiān Xīngguó Hóngdé Zhāngwǔ Kuānwēn Rénshèng Ruìxiào Wén Huángdì.
His temple name was Tàizōng.
Later, his honored posthumous title was: Yìngtiān Xīngguó Hóngdé Zhāngwǔ Kuānwēn Rénshèng Ruìxiào Jìngmǐn Zhāodìng Lóngdào Xiǎngōng Wén Huángdì.
The论 (commentary) states: Tàizōng was both civil and martial,
internally he reformed governance,
externally he diligently engaged in punitive expeditions.
His use of troops was divine,
and he achieved success wherever he went.
Although the great task (unification) was not yet completed,
his successor Shìzǔ ascended the throne for a full year,
and unification was achieved both internally and externally.
This was because the Emperor's plans were far-reaching.
Ming governance was disorganized,
and bandits rampaged.
The Emperor certainly knew that the Ming could be conquered,
but he did not wish to fight hastily and exhaust the people's lives.
He wrote seven letters to Ming generals and commanders,
humbly requesting peace.
The Ming people did not gauge their strength,
and thus destroyed their own country,
which is not worth discussing.
However, the Emperor's way of dealing with neighbors
was truly no different from Tāng's treatment of Gě or King Wén's treatment of Kūnyí.
Alas,
how sagely he was!
Annals, The Fourth. Annals of Shìzǔ, The First.
Shìzǔ Tǐtiān Lóngyùn Dìngtǒng Jiànjí Yīngruì Qīnwén Xiǎnwǔ Dàdé Hónggōng Zhìrén Chúnxiào Zhāng Huángdì,
whose personal name was Fúlín,
was the ninth son of Tàizōng.
When his mother, Empress Xiàozhuāngwén, was pregnant,
red light encircled her body,
spiraling like a dragon.
On the eve of his birth,
she dreamt of a divine being holding a child and placing him in the Empress's arms, saying:
"This is the lord who will unify all under heaven."
She awoke,
and told Tàizōng.
Tàizōng was exceedingly joyful,
saying:
"This is an auspicious sign; the child born will surely achieve great deeds."
The next day, the Emperor was born,
and red light illuminated the palace,
with a fragrant aroma lingering for days.
The Emperor was born with extraordinary endowments;
his hair on the crown of his head stood erect,
he had a dragon-like countenance and phoenix-like features,
and his divine intelligence was heaven-bestowed.
In the eighth year, autumn, eighth month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
Tàizōng collapsed.
The succession to the heir apparent had not yet been determined.
Héshuò Lǐ Qīnwáng Dàishàn, together with the various princes (*wáng*), *bèilè*, *bèizi*, and civil and military officials, deliberated and decided
to enthrone the current heir to the grand position,
swearing an oath to Heaven and Earth.
They appointed Héshuò Zhèng Qīnwáng Jí'ěrhāláng and Héshuò Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrgǔn as regents.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Ājígé Níkān and others led troops to guard Jǐnzhōu.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Duōluó Jùnwáng Ādálǐ and Gùshān Bèizi Shuòtuō plotted to install Héshuò Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrgǔn.
Lǐ Qīnwáng Dàishàn and Duō'ěrgǔn exposed their plot.
Ādálǐ and Shuòtuō were executed.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the various princes, *bèilè*, *bèizi*, and officials offered sacrifices to Tàizōng at the time of the heir apparent’s enthronement.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
sacrifices were offered at the suburban altars and ancestral temples at the time of the enthronement.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the Emperor ascended the throne in the Dǔgōng Diàn.
An imperial edict declared the next year to be the first year of Shùnzhì,
granting a general amnesty to those normally not pardoned.
Edicts of mourning were issued to Cháoxiǎn (Korea) and Měnggǔ (Mongolia).
In the ninth month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
there was an earthquake,
with sounds from the northwest to the south.
On the *rényín* day,
Jí'ěrhāláng and Ājígé campaigned against Míng,
attacking Níngyuǎn Wèi.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the enthronement edict was issued to Cháoxiǎn and Měnggǔ.
Following Tàizōng's last will, Cháoxiǎn's annual tribute was reduced.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Zhāolíng was completed.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the grand army attacked Míng's Zhōnghòusuǒ,
and captured it on the *dīngsì* day.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
they attacked Qiántún Wèi.
Winter, tenth month, on the *xīnyǒu* day, the first day of the month,
it was captured.
Ājígé Níkān and others led troops to Zhōngqiánsuǒ,
and Míng's Commander Huáng Sè abandoned the city and fled.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Jí'ěrhāláng and Ājígé's armies returned.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Piāngǔ, Bóhétuō, Yībài, and Dùléi took turns garrisoning Jǐnzhōu.
In the twelfth month, on the *rénxū* day,
Míng's garrison commander Sūn Yǒubái surrendered from Níngyuǎn.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Cháoxiǎn came to offer congratulations on the enthronement.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the various princes, *bèilè*, and *bèizi* were relieved of their duties managing the boards and offices.
Èluósāichén and Bādùlǐ led troops to campaign in Hēilóngjiāng.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Tántài and Zhǔntǎ took turns garrisoning Jǐnzhōu.
This year,
Cháoxiǎn, as well as the *zhāngjīng* Gǔlùgé of the Tǔmòtè tribe,
Láidákù of the Kù'ěrkā tribe, and twenty-six households of the Yánchǔkùyǎlā clan,
the *zhāngjīng* Chóngnèi of the Suǒlún tribe,
the Tǔxiètú Hàn, Mǎhāsāmǎdì Sàichén Hàn, and Zhāsàkètú Hàn of the Kā'ěrkā tribe,
and Diānqílāmā of the Túbáitè tribe, all came to offer tribute.
In the first year of Shùnzhì, spring, first month, on the *gēngyín* day, the first day of the month,
the Emperor held court to receive felicitations,
and ordered Lǐ Qīnwáng Dàishàn not to bow.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Shā'ěrhǔdá led troops to campaign against Kù'ěrkā.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Láidáhābātúlǔ and others took turns garrisoning Jǐnzhōu.
Zhèng Qīnwáng Jí'ěrhāláng instructed the various officials of the boards and offices
that all matters should first be presented to Ruì Qīnwáng,
with himself taking the secondary position.
In the second month, on the *xīnsì* day,
Àidùlǐ garrisoned Jǐnzhōu.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the Grand Consort Bó'ěrjìjǐn Shì was interred in Fúlǐng,
and Consort Fùchá Shì was reburied outside the mausoleum.
Fùchá Shì
had been granted death for a crime during Tàizǔ's time.
In the third month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
there was an earthquake.
On the *wùxū* day,
it shook again.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Grand Secretary Xīfú and others submitted the abridged translation of the histories of Liáo, Jīn, and Yuán.
This month,
the bandit Lǐ Zìchéng captured Yānjīng (Beijing),
and the Míng Emperor hanged himself.
Zìchéng usurped the imperial title,
calling his dynasty Dàshùn,
and changing the era name to Yǒngchāng.
Summer, fourth month, on the *wùwǔ* day, the first day of the month,
Gùshān Érzhēn Héluòhuì and others impeached Sù Qīnwáng Háogé for rebellious and absurd crimes,
deposing Háogé to commoner status,
and his followers, Èmòkètú and others, were all sentenced to death.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Duōluó Ráoyú Bèilè Ābātài was promoted to Duōluó Ráoyú Jùnwáng.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Grand Secretary Fàn Wénchéng proposed to Ruì Qīnwáng that they enter and pacify the Central Plains.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
sacrifices were offered to Tàizǔ and Tàizōng for the grand army's southern expedition.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Emperor held court in Dǔgōng Diàn,
appointing Héshuò Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrgǔn as the Fèngmìng Dàjiàngjūn (Generalissimo by Imperial Command),
granting him an imperial edict and seal with discretionary powers,
and bestowing clothing and other items of varying grades upon the prince and the various princes, *bèilè*, *bèizi* and others accompanying the expedition.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the army set out.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrgǔn's army reached Wēnghòu.
Míng's Shānhǎiguān commander Wú Sānguì sent an envoy with a letter,
pleading for military aid to suppress the bandits.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the army reached Liánshān.
Sānguì again sent a letter reporting an urgent situation,
and the grand army rushed to his aid.
On the *wùyín* day,
Lǐ Zìchéng led his forces to besiege Shānhǎiguān.
Our army counterattacked them,
defeating the bandit general Táng Tōng at Yīpiànshí.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the army arrived at Shānhǎiguān.
Sānguì opened the gate to welcome them,
and the grand army entered the pass.
Zìchéng led over two hundred thousand troops,
stretching from Běishān to the sea,
arrayed in a formidable formation.
That day,
a great wind blew,
and dust and sand obscured the sky.
Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrgǔn ordered an attack on the rear of the bandit formation,
placing Sānguì on the right wing,
and attacked with a great shout.
The wind soon settled,
and the bandit army was utterly routed.
They were pursued for over forty *lǐ*,
and Zìchéng fled back to Yānjīng.
Sānguì was enfeoffed as Píngxī Wáng (Prince Pacifier of the West),
and ten thousand cavalry and infantry were placed under his command,
to advance directly to Yānjīng.
The generals were sworn not to kill innocent people,
plunder property,
or burn houses.
Those who did not adhere to the oath would be punished.
Officials and common people were informed of the intention to conquer the remnants and not to kill.
The people were greatly pleased,
and those who had fled and hidden in mountains and valleys eagerly returned to their hometowns to surrender.
In all the prefectures and counties through which the grand army passed, and the border generals and officials, all opened their gates and submitted.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Zìchéng abandoned Yānjīng and fled west.
Our army swiftly pursued him.
Fifth month, on the *wùzǐ* day, the first day of the month,
the victory dispatch was proclaimed to Cháoxiǎn and Měnggǔ.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the grand army arrived at Yānjīng.
Former Míng civil and military officials, gentry, and commoners all welcomed them five *lǐ* outside the city.
Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrgǔn entered and resided in Wǔyīng Diàn.
He ordered the generals and soldiers to patrol the city walls,
and servants and others not to enter civilian homes,
so the populace remained peaceful as before.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Ministry of War was ordered to issue proclamations to all directly administered provinces, prefectures, and counties,
stating that officials who submitted would be promoted in rank,
and soldiers and civilians would be exempt from relocation.
