High-ranking civil and military officials were to personally bring household registers, money, grain, and soldiers and horses to the capital.
Those who hesitated would be punished.
Former Míng princes who submitted
would not have their titles stripped.
Officials in the capital and those who had hidden to avoid the bandits
were to be recorded by name and employed.
Soldiers who wished to return to farming were permitted to do so.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
officials, soldiers, and commoners were ordered to mourn for the Míng Emperor.
Mourning dress was to be removed after three days,
and the Ministry of Rites and the Grand Court of Sacrifices were to arrange for his burial with imperial rites.
On the *rénchén* day,
Èluósāichén, Bādùlǐ, Shā'ěrhǔdá, and others returned from their Hēilóngjiāng campaign.
Former Míng Shānhǎiguān Commander Gāo Dì surrendered.
On the *guǐsì* day,
former Míng Grand Secretariat and Ministry and Office officials were ordered to handle affairs in their original positions alongside Manchu officials.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Ājígé and others pursued and attacked Lǐ Zìchéng at Qìngdū,
defeating him.
Tántài, Zhǔntǎ, and others pursued him to Zhēndìng,
and again routed him.
All cities north of Yānjīng, as well as Tiānjīn and the various prefectures and counties of Zhēndìng, all surrendered.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
former Míng Grand Secretary Féng Quán was summoned to the capital.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the former Míng Emperor Zhuāngliè's empress Zhōu Shì and consort Yuán Shì,
Xīzōng's empress Zhāng Shì,
and Shénzōng's consort Liú Shì
were all buried according to regulations.
On the *dǐngsì* day of the sixth month,
Hong Chéngchóu was ordered to continue assisting with military affairs as Minister of War, concurrently with his duties in the Grand Secretariat.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Luò Yǎngxìng was appointed Governor-General of Tiānjīn.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Wáng Áoyǒng, Vice Minister of Revenue, was dispatched to pacify Shāndōng and Hénán.
On the *rénxū* day,
Jiāng Xiāng, former Dàtóng Commander-in-Chief of the Míng, executed the bandit leaders Kē Tiānxìng and others,
and surrendered Dàtóng.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Bāhānà and Shí Tíngzhù were sent with troops to pacify Shāndōng.
Taxes on official residential properties in the capital were remitted for three years,
and for one year for those sharing residence.
Half of the land tax in prefectures and counties through which the grand army passed was remitted,
and one-third in prefectures and counties north of the Yellow River.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrzhùn, along with other princes, *bèilè*, *bèizǐ*, and ministers, decided to establish the capital in Yānjīng.
Fúguógōng Túnqíkā, Hétuō, and Gùshān Èzhēn Hélàhuì were dispatched to escort the imperial carriage.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Gùshān Èzhēn Yèchén was sent with troops to pacify Shānxī.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Lǐ Huàxī, former Grand Coordinator of the Three Borders of the Míng, surrendered.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Emperor dispatched envoys to comfort the troops.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Àidùlǐ, having committed a crime,
was executed.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the spirit tablet of the Míng Tàizǔ was moved to the Temple of Emperors of Past Dynasties.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
official seals were cast using both the national script and Chinese characters.
In the autumn, on the *dīnghài* day of the seventh month,
the calendar was revised and established
as the Shíxiànlì.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Bāhānà and Shí Tíngzhù joined Yèchén's army to pacify Shānxī.
On the *rénchén* day,
Wú Zīchāng was appointed Governor-General of Xuāndà and Shānxī,
and Fāng Dàyóu was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Shāndōng.
On the *guǐsì* day,
sacrifices were offered to Shàngdì and the imperial tombs to announce the relocation of the capital.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Zhū Yóumò, former Prince Dé of the Míng, surrendered.
At this time, Zhū Yóusōng, former Prince Fú of the Míng, had ascended the throne in Jiāngnán,
and adopted the reign title Hóngguāng.
Shǐ Kěfǎ was appointed Grand Secretary
and stationed in Yángzhōu to oversee military affairs.
Grand Commanders Liú Zéqīng, Liú Liángzuǒ, Huáng Dégōng, and Gāo Jié were stationed to guard the north of the Yangtze River.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Zhū Lǎnghóng, Pacification Commissioner of Shāndōng, memorialized that newly appointed officials should still wear gauze caps and round-collared robes when governing and attending to duties.
Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrzhùn issued an edict:
"As military affairs are pressing,
we have not yet had time to standardize official attire, rites, and music.
Newly selected officials
shall provisionally follow the Míng style."
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
officials were appointed for the Míng Chánglíng and the fourteen tombs below it.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the mandated grain, fodder, and cloth contributions for Manchu and Hàn people in Shèngjīng were remitted.
On the *rényín* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed,
and all surtaxes beyond the regular quota were abolished.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
eunuchs were dismissed from collecting taxes on imperial estates in Zhuōzhōu and Bǎochí.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Yáng Fāngxìng was appointed Governor-General of Hénán,
Mǎ Guózhù was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Shānxī,
and Chén Jǐn was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Dēnglái.
Taxes in Shāndōng were remitted
following the example of Héběi.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Ruì Qīnwáng sent a letter to Shǐ Kěfǎ,
advising his lord to relinquish his title and return to his fief.
Kěfǎ's reply was unyielding.
Wáng Wénkuí was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Bǎodìng,
and Luó Xiùjǐn was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Hénán.
The Mongol Vice Ministers of the Six Boards were abolished.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
there was a hailstorm.
In this month,
the Qiánqīnggōng was constructed.
On the *bǐngchén* day, the first day of the eighth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Hélàhuì was appointed General Administrator of Shèngjīng,
and Níkān and Shuòzhān were put in command of the left and right wings
to guard Shèngjīng.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Grand Secretary Xīfú, having committed a crime,
was pardoned.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the *zǒngjiǎ* system was implemented.
On the *wùchén* day,
the regular annual taxes for Jǐngzhōu, Héjiān, Fùchéng, and Qīngxiàn for the current year were remitted.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the salaries of civil and military officials in the capital were determined.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the imperial carriage departed Shèngjīng.
On the *gēngchén* day,
it arrived at Sū'ěrjì.
The Cháhā'ěr Gùlún Princess and Mongol princes, *bèilè* and others paid respects at the imperial travelling palace.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Xiè Shēng, former Grand Secretary of the Míng, was summoned to the Grand Secretariat to handle affairs.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
it arrived at Guǎngníng.
Sacrificial land was granted to the tomb households of the Míng Thirteen Tombs,
and logging and grazing were prohibited.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day of the ninth month,
the imperial carriage entered Shānhǎiguān.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
it arrived at Yǒngpíng.
Strict orders for inspecting and arresting fugitives were first put in place.
On the *jǐhài* day,
a *Tángzǐ* was established in Yānjīng.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the bandit general Táng Tōng killed Lǐ Zìchéng's relatives and sought to surrender.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Hétuō, Lǐ Shuàitài, Émènggé, and others were sent with troops to pacify Shāndōng and Hénán.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the imperial carriage reached Tōngzhōu.
Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrzhùn, along with other princes, *bèilè*, *bèizǐ*, and civil and military officials, paid respects to the Emperor at the travelling palace.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the Emperor entered the palace from Zhèngyángmén.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Venus was seen in daylight.
On the *gēngxū* day,
music for suburban and ancestral temples was first determined.
Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrzhùn, along with other princes and Manchu and Hàn officials, submitted a memorial urging the Emperor to accept the throne.

Zhū Yóusōng, former Prince Fú of the Míng, sent his ministers Zuǒ Màodì, Mǎ Shàoyú, and Chén Hóngfàn, carrying over a hundred thousand taels of silver, a thousand taels of gold, and ten thousand bolts of silk, to seek peace.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the spirit tablets of Tàizǔ Wǔhuángdì, Xiàocí Wǔhuánghòu, and Tàizōng Wénhuángdì were solemnly placed in the Tàimiào.
In the tenth month of winter, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor personally went to the Southern Suburbs to offer sacrifices to Heaven and Earth,
and ascended to the imperial throne.
Officials were dispatched to offer sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple (*Tàimiào*) and to the Gods of Land and Grain (*Shèjì*).
The *Shíxiànlì* calendar was initially promulgated.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Kǒngzǐ's (Confucius') sixty-fifth generation descendant, Yǔnzhí, was granted the hereditary title of Duke Yànshèng.
The Five Classics Scholars (*Wǔjīng Bóshì*) and other officials retained their hereditary titles as before.
On the *dīngsì* day,
because of Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrgǔn's outstanding contributions,
the Ministry of Rites was ordered to erect a stele to commemorate his achievements.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the posthumous title of Emperor Tàizōng was elevated,
and sacrifices were offered at the suburbs, temples, and to the Gods of Land and Grain.
On the *rénxū* day,
Zhào Yìngyuán, a remnant of the rebel bandits, feigned surrender
and entered Qīngzhōu,
killing the Commissioner of Pacification, Attendant Secretary Wáng Áoyǒng.
Hétuō and others pursued and executed him.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Emperor presided at the Huángjí Gate,
issued an edict to the entire realm,
and proclaimed a grand amnesty.
The edict stated:
“Our nation, having received the benevolent protection of Heaven,
was founded in the eastern lands.
Our illustrious ancestors established a grand enterprise,
and Our imperial father expanded upon their former achievements,
thereby acquiring the old domain [of China]
and receiving the new mandate.
When We succeeded to the throne,
though still of tender age,
We reverently thought of continuing the ancestral legacy
and forever securing Our position.
Recently, due to the raging banditry,
which brought extreme calamity to the Central Plains,
We therefore relied on Our worthy kinsmen and virtuous ministers
to rescue the people from their dire straits.
As the drums of war sounded,
order was swiftly restored,
delivering the people from their distress,
not for the sake of enriching the realm.
And now, the imperial princes, various feudal lords, civil and military officials, as well as soldiers, civilians, elders, and seniors, have jointly presented their recommendations,
pleading repeatedly.
Therefore, on the *yǐmǎo* day, the first day of the tenth month of this year,
We reverently reported to Heaven, Earth, the Ancestral Temples, and the Gods of Land and Grain,
established the capital in Yānjīng (Beijing),
and retained the dynastic title of Dàqīng,
with the era name Shùnzhì.
We reflect that the sublime mandate is not easily obtained,
and founding an enterprise is even more arduous.
Especially at the beginning of reforms,
we shall bestow the grace of renewal.
The imperial princes, who assisted in founding the nation,
benefited society and pacified the people,
have rendered great services and deserve special honor.
For the sons, grandsons, younger brothers, and nephews of the princes and commandery princes who are entitled to titles and peerages,
the relevant departments shall amend previous regulations and report their findings.
Manchu officials who founded the nation,
who strategized within the military tent,
and achieved victory in the imperial court,
who earned merits through arduous campaigns,
and expanded the territory,
shall be granted hereditary titles of Duke (*Gōng*), Marquis (*Hóu*), or Earl (*Bó*),
and bestowed with imperial patents.
Since the Grand Army entered the pass,
civil and military officials and gentry
who took the lead in embracing righteousness,
killed bandits, and surrendered,
shall also be universally examined.
All criminals among officials, soldiers, and civilians
before the break of dawn on the first day of the fifth month of Shùnzhì 1,
excluding those guilty of rebellion, the Ten Abominations,
or those who are irredeemably punishable by death,
regardless of the severity of their crimes,
shall all be pardoned and cleared.
Officials who engaged in corruption, bribery, perverted justice,
and exploited the common people,
if their crimes occurred after the first day of the fifth month,
are not included in this amnesty.
Land taxes and grain levies
shall all be collected and remitted according to the former Míng Dynasty's accounting records,
starting from the first day of the fifth month of Shùnzhì 1,
as per the established quota.
All additional levies for Liaodong (*Liáoxiǎng*), new taxes (*Xīnxiǎng*), training levies (*Liànxiǎng*), forced purchases, and similar items
are hereby remitted.
For areas through which the Grand Army passed,
half of the regular grain tax shall still be remitted.
For surrendered prefectures and counties not traversed by the army,
one-third of the current year's tax shall be remitted.
Outstanding arrears of principal and interest on money and grain taxes from the direct provinces,

such as *Jīnhuā*, summer tax, autumn grain, horse fodder, head tax, salt certificates, civilian-military farms, pastureland, kiln taxes, wealthy household taxes, market stall fees, commercial taxes, fishing taxes, horse prices, firewood prices, jujube tree taxes, paper currency tax, fruit taxes, and various items for imperial supply like pigments, wax, tea, sesame, cotton, silk, cloth, and raw silk,
considering the extreme hardship of the common people,
all outstanding arrears
before the first day of the fifth month of Shùnzhì 1
shall be entirely waived.
The dispersion of soldiers and civilians in the capital city
was truly unavoidable.
For those who have already moved out of the three eastern, central, and western cities,
rent and taxes shall be remitted for three years.
For the northern and southern cities, even if they have not moved,
one year's remission shall be granted.
The head tax (*Dīngyín*) had a fixed quota.
In recent years, the population has dwindled,
and the household registers have shrunk daily.
The solitary, poor, elderly, and infirm
are all suffering from incessant demands.
Officials shall investigate and verify,
and the elderly, young, disabled, and infirm
shall also be exempted.
For soldiers and civilians aged seventy and above,
one able-bodied male is permitted to serve them,
exempting him from corvée labor.
For those aged eighty and above,
silk, cotton, rice, and meat shall be provided.
For those renowned for their virtue,
official hats and sashes shall be granted.
For widows, widowers, orphans, the childless, and those with disabilities who cannot support themselves,
the government shall provide sustenance.
Filial sons, obedient grandsons, righteous husbands, and chaste wives
shall be investigated by officials and reported.
Former Míng officials who were dismissed or banished for their remonstrances, and hermits in mountains and forests who possess talent and virtue and are capable of serving the world,
shall be recommended by the Commissioners of Pacification and Surveillance
to come to the capital and be appointed.
Civil and military examinations
shall continue to be held in the *chén*, *xū*, *chǒu*, and *wèi* years for the metropolitan examinations,
and in the *zǐ*, *wǔ*, *mǎo*, and *yǒu* years for the provincial examinations.
Míng imperial clan members who first initiated their surrender
shall still be granted their stipends and support.
For the various imperial tombs of the Míng state,
spring and autumn sacrifices shall be offered,
and tomb-guarding households shall continue to be employed.
Imperial tombs and graves of renowned ministers and virtuous scholars that have been damaged shall be repaired,
and firewood gathering and grazing shall still be prohibited.
Civil and military officials inside and outside the capital who are entitled to imperial patents and inherited titles
shall all be granted them uniformly.
The reduced silver payments for Zhílǐ, Hénán, and Shāndōng,
and the newly reduced silver payments for the two prefectures of Tàiyuán and Píngyáng in Shānxī,
which were already remitted by the former Míng,
as well as the old reduced silver payments for those two prefectures,
and the new and old reduced silver payments for various prefectures,
and silver for the combined personnel of post stations, donkey stations, and transport stations,

and also the silver for materials for the four bureaus of the Ministry of Works remitted by the direct provinces, silver for artisans' wages, silver for brick materials, hemp silver, cart prices, reed worker silver, reed taxes, fishing taxes, wild game taxes, feather taxes, live deer silver, large deer silver, small deer silver, sheepskin silver, silver in lieu of bows and arrows and quivers, deducted remaining freight silver, ox horn and ox sinew silver, goose feather silver, swan silver, civilian labor silver, hay and grain seed silver, *Zhuàngyuán* robes silver, clothing and grain silver, firewood cutter silver, firewood transport silver, kindling wood worker silver, reed taxes and other silver in lieu of goods, and in-kind payments such as helmets and armor, waist knives, bows and arrows, bowstrings, padded jackets, trousers, shoes, fox, muntjac, rabbit, and civet furs, goat wool tax, iron, Rhus chinensis (yellow lacquer tree), betel nut, mulberry, rouge, rosewood, southern jujubes, purple elm, fir strips and other timbers, linden wood, tung wood, planks and boards, ice storage materials, reed mats, bulrush, official paper, porcelain jars, pagoda tree flowers, smoked plums, gardenias, brush handles, straw brooms, bamboo brooms, mat grass, coarse and fine copper wire, iron wire, nickel-plated copper wire, iron bars, rollers, indigo cotton, rosin, smooth-leaf book paper, strict lacquer, topcoat lacquer, tung oil, bamboo varieties (máo, guì, zǐ, shuǐbān, etc.), solid bamboo, palm fiber, white round rattan, kingfisher feathers, millstones, Chuan-type vermilion, raw lacquer, sand leaves, Canton glue, saltpeter, conch shells, and other in-kind money and grain,
which were outstanding arrears owed by the people before the first day of the fifth month of Shùnzhì 1,
shall all be remitted
to alleviate the people's hardship.
Hereafter, they shall be remitted separately
according to current precedents.
For merchants, carters, and other laborers in the capital,
each time they were conscripted,
they were forced to become displaced.
From now on, this shall be permanently abolished.
The salt administration of the Salt Commissioners,
which increased year by year,
including new taxes, training levies, and miscellaneous surcharges,
was deeply detrimental to merchants.
All these shall be completely waived,
and for this year, one-third of the quota of salt certificates shall still be remitted.
Customs duties at passes and ferries,
not intended to harm merchants,
shall be remitted for one year,
and those increased at the end of the Míng Dynasty
shall also be entirely waived.
Scattered small taxes in the prefectures and counties of the direct provinces
are hereby strictly prohibited.
For places that have suffered military disasters and should pay money and grain taxes,
if they were already fully exempted by the former Míng,
they shall still be fully exempted,
and not be subject to the half or one-third remission rule.
Silver for assisting works, reported and remitted by the direct provinces to the Ministry of Works' Department of Military Colonies,
was also an additional levy;
it is hereby waived.
Money and grain remitted by the direct provinces that were robbed and lost by bandits
before the first day of the fifth month of Shùnzhì 1
shall all be waived.
Military and civilians in Shānxi and Shǎnxī who were coerced by roving bandits,
and who repent and reform,
shall all be pardoned and forgiven.
Those who were coerced and surrendered on their own initiative shall not be prosecuted for their past crimes.
The Censors, under the pretext of investigation and arrest,
listened to corrupt yamen clerks
and falsely fined good people,
which was a most corrupt practice.
From now on, this shall be strictly prohibited and abolished.
Powerful families and local bullies
who lent money at exorbitant interest,
causing people to lose their homes and possessions,
are deeply detestable.
From now on, officials shall not permit collection and enforcement.
Unwarranted lawsuits and false accusations
corrupt customs and waste wealth.
After this grand amnesty,
minor disputes concerning households and marriages
shall all be settled by the local officials.
If any litigious tricksters induce ignorant people to come to the capital for unwarranted lawsuits,
they shall be punished with a heavier sentence in reverse.
The establishment of redemption fees
was to encourage people to reform.
However, forced collection and enforcement cause loss of life
and turn into harm for the people.
Hereafter, both are forbidden.
Those who cannot pay [taxes],
shall be promptly excused from collection.
May you, the myriad regions,
be of one mind with Us.
Proclaim this far and wide,
so all may hear and know."
He conferred the title of Shúfù Shèzhèngwáng (Regent Uncle Prince) upon Héshuò Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrgǔn.
On the Yǐchǒu day,
Léi Xīng was appointed Tiānjīn Xúnfǔ (Governor of Tianjin).
On the Dīngmǎo day,
Héshuò Zhèng Qīnwáng Jí'ěrhālā ng was conferred the title of Xìnyì Fǔzhèng Shúwáng (Loyal and Righteous Assisting Regent Uncle Prince),
Háo Gé was re-conferred the title of Héshuò Sù Qīnwáng,
Duōluó Wǔyīng Jùnwáng Ājìgé was promoted to Héshuò Yīng Qīnwáng,
Duōluó Yù Jùnwáng Duōduó was promoted to Héshuò Yù Qīnwáng,
Bèilè Luóluóhóng was promoted to Duōluó Yǎnxǐ Jùnwáng,
and Shuòsāi was conferred the title of Duōluó Chéngzé Jùnwáng.
Yèchén and others captured Tàiyuán.
The former Míng Vice-General Liú Dàshòu came from Jiāngnán to surrender.
On the Xīnwèi day,
Bèizi Níkān and Bóluò were conferred the title of Duōluó Bèilè,
and Fǔguó Gōng Mǎndáhǎi, Tūnqí, Bóhétuō, Tūnqí kā, Hétuō, and Shàngshàn were conferred the title of Gùshān Bèizi.
The annual stipends for various Princes, Bèilè, and Bèizi were fixed.
On the Guǐyóu day,
Yīng Qīnwáng Ājìgé was appointed Jìngyuǎn Dàjiāngjūn (Great General who Pacifies the Distant),
and led troops to the west to suppress Lǐ Zìchéng.
On the Wùyín day,
the regulations for the crown, robes, and palaces of the Regent Prince were established.
On the Jǐmǎo day,
Yù Qīnwáng Duōduó was appointed Dìngguó Dàjiāngjūn (Great General who Establishes the State),
and led troops to conquer Jiāngnán.
A proclamation was issued to the former Míng officials in the south,
enumerating their three crimes: failing to eradicate the bandits and avenge the emperor,
gathering crowds to disturb the people and
causing unrest,
and presumptuously enthroning the Fúwáng without a testament from the deceased Míng emperor.
On the first day of the eleventh month, Yǐyóu,
Mǎnzhōu Sīyè (Director of Studies) and Zhùjiào (Assistant Instructor) positions were established;
children and grandchildren of officials who wished to study Mǎnzhōu script or Hàn script
were all to be admitted to the Guózǐjiān (Imperial Academy) for study.
Chén Hóngfàn, the envoy of the former Míng Fúwáng, returned south.
Midway, he secretly petitioned to retain Zuǒ Màodì and Mǎ Shàoyú,
while he himself wished to lead troops to submit [to the Qīng]
and recruit the generals in the south.
This was granted.
On the Rénchén day,
Shí Tíngzhù, Bāhānà, Xítèkù, and others defeated the bandits at Píngyáng,
and Shānxī was entirely pacified.
On the Gēngzǐ day,
Táng Tōng was conferred the title of Dìngxī Hóu (Marquis who Pacifies the West).
On the Jiǎchén day,
the guards of the former Míng Dìnglíng (Mausoleum) were dismissed,
while for the other twelve mausoleums, two eunuchs were still appointed,
and annual sacrificial offerings were provided as appropriate.
On the Dīngwèi day,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Huánqiū (Altar of Heaven).
On the Gēngxū day,
Lèkèdéhún was conferred the title of Duōluó Bèilè.
The Korean hostage prince Lǐ was sent back to his country,
and his annual tribute was reduced.
On the Dīngsì day of the twelfth month,
treasures from the former Míng imperial treasury were distributed
as rewards to the generals and soldiers of the Eight Banners and Mongolian officials.
The grand army led by Yèchén and others pacified nine prefectures, twenty-seven departments, and one hundred forty-one counties in Zhílì, Hénán, and Shānxī.
On the Dīngmǎo day,
Tàizōng's sixth daughter, Gùlún Gōngzhǔ, was married to Kuāzhā, son of Gùshān Ézhēn Āshān.
On the Wùchén day,
Duōduó's army reached Mèngjīn.
Bandit generals Huáng Shìxīn and others fled,
and fifteen riverside fortresses and strongholds submitted at the sight of the army.
Bandit general Xǔ Dìngguó from Suīzhōu surrendered.
On the Jǐsì day,
Duōduó's army reached Shǎnzhōu,
and defeated bandit general Zhāng Yǒuzēng at Língbǎo.
On the Dīngchǒu day,
the Hùbù (Board of Revenue) was instructed to investigate ownerless wasteland and distribute it to the Eight Banners soldiers.
On the Jǐmǎo day,
Héluòhuì and others were sent to offer sacrifices at Fúlíng,
and Gǒng'ādài and others to offer sacrifices at Zhāolíng,
announcing the military successes.
On the Xīnsì day,
a man named Liú claimed to be the Míng Crown Prince.
The palace eunuch Yáng Yù introduced him into the residence of the former Míng Jiādìng Hóu Zhōu Kuí,
and Zhōu Kuí reported it.
The former Míng palace women and old retainers of the Eastern Palace all stated they did not recognize him.
He was handed over to the Fǎsī (Judicial Office) for interrogation.
Yáng Yù and the conspiring eunuchs Cháng Jìnjí, commander Lǐ Shíyìn, and fifteen others were all executed in the marketplace.
It was also proclaimed throughout the realm
that whoever reported the former Míng Crown Prince would be rewarded,
and the Crown Prince would still be treated with grace and provided for.
That year,
Cháoxiǎn (Korea) and the eight Hǔshíkālǐ clans,
the Jìnóng of the È'ěrdúosī (Ordos) tribe,
Zhāngjīng Ào'ěrtuōmù'ěr of the Suǒlún (Solon) tribe,
Gǔlùgé of the Guīhuàchéng Tǔmòtè (Tumet) tribe,
Sāichén Chuò'ěrjì, Gǔlúndìwǎ Hútúkètú, Yúgǔzhé'ěrlāmǎ, and Tǔxiétú Hàn of the Kā'ěrkā (Khalkha) tribe,
Téngjīsi Ālāhǎi of the Sūnítè (Sunud) tribe,
and Táijí Mǎnz hān of the Wūzhūmùqín (Ujumchin) tribe all came to offer tribute.
In the spring of the second year, on the Wùzǐ day of the first month,
Túlái and others defeated Lǐ Zìchéng at Tóngguān.
The bandits relied on the mountains for their formation.
Túlái led a hundred cavalry to attack them by surprise,
achieving many kills and captures.
By this time,
Lǐ Zìchéng personally led his cavalry and infantry to confront them,
but was defeated several more times,
and the bandit forces scattered.
On the Jǐwèi day,
the grand army besieged Tóngguān.
The bandits dug multiple moats
and fortified their walls to defend.
Mùchénggé and Éluósāichén were the first to ascend,
and the other armies followed,
again defeating them decisively.
Lǐ Zìchéng fled to Xī'ān.
On the Bǐngshēn day,
Ājìgé, Níkān, and others led troops to Tóngguān.
Bandit general Mǎ Shìyáo surrendered,
but was subsequently executed for treachery.
On the Dīngyóu day,
Duōluó Ráoyú Jùnwáng Ābātài was appointed Zǒngtǒng (Commander-in-Chief),
Gùshān Ézhēn Zhǔntǎ as Zǔoyì (Left Wing),
and Méilè Zhāngjīng Tántài as Yòuyì (Right Wing),
to replace Háo Gé in conquering Shāndōng.
On the Gēngzǐ day,
Tàizōng's seventh daughter, Gùlún Gōngzhǔ, was married to Lāmǎsī, son of Nèidàchén Èqí'ěrsāng.
The Yellow River cleared for two days in Mèngxiàn, Hénán.
On the Rényín day,
Duōduó's army reached Xī'ān.
Lǐ Zìchéng fled to Shāngzhōu.
On the Guǐmǎo day,
Grand Secretary Xiè Shēng died.
On the Yǐsì day,
the mountain bandits in Zhēndìng, Dàmíng, Shùndé, and Guǎngpíng were all pacified.
On the Bǐngwǔ day,
Fángshān Xiàn was ordered to offer grand sacrifices annually at the mausoleums of Jīn Tàizǔ and Shìzōng.
On the Dīngwèi day,
half of Shānxī's annual land tax for this year was remitted.
The spirit tablet of Confucius in the Guózǐjiān was changed to Dàchéng Zhìshèng Wénxuān Xiānshī Kǒngzǐ (Great Accomplished, Most Holy, Cultured, and Proclaimed First Teacher Confucius).
On the Gēngxū day,
Bāoyī Dà and others were forbidden from privately accepting Hàn people who sought refuge
and fraudulently occupying their fields and residences.
Violators would be sentenced to death.
On the Rénzǐ day,
the annual land tax for this year in Jìyuán, Wǔzhì, Mèng, and Wēn counties, and half of the tax for Jí, Ānyáng, and other nine prefectures and counties, was remitted.
On the Guǐchǒu day,
over eight thousand border defense laborers were discharged.
On the Bǐngchén day of the second month,
Ābātài defeated the bandits at Xúzhōu.
On the Jǐwèi day,
laws and regulations were revised.
Lǐ Jiàn was appointed Xuāndà Zǒngdū (Governor-General of Xuāndà),
and Féng Shèngzhào was appointed Xuānfǔ Xúnfǔ (Governor of Xuānfǔ).
The surrendered general Xǔ Dìngguó ambushed and killed Míng Xīngpíng Bó Gāo Jié at Suīzhōu.
On the Xīnyǒu day,
Yù Qīnwáng Duōduó was instructed to move his army to pacify Jiāngnán,
and Yīng Qīnwáng Ājìgé to suppress the remaining bandit remnants.
On the Bǐngyín day,
guǎnzhuāng bōshíkù (estate managers) were forbidden from destroying people's graves.
On the Jǐsì day,
Qí Chōnggé was appointed Nèi Hóngwén Yuàn Dàxuéshì (Grand Secretary of the Inner Grand Secretariat).
On the Gēngwǔ day,
Ājìgé suppressed the remaining bandits in Shǎnxī,
captured four cities,
and received the surrender of thirty-eight cities.
On the Dīngchǒu day,
Duōduó's army reached Hénán.
Bandit general Liú Zhōng surrendered.
On the first day of the third month, Jiǎshēn,
sacrifices began to be offered to Liáo Tàizǔ, Jīn Tàizǔ, Shìzōng, Yuán Tàizǔ, and Míng Tàizǔ at the Lìdài Dìwáng Miào (Temple of Emperors of Successive Dynasties),
with their ministers Yēlǜ Gálǔ, Wányán Niánmòhǎn, Wòlíbù, Mùhuálí, Báiyán, Xú Dá, and Liú Jī as accompanying sacrificial subjects.
On the Gēngyín day,
Duōduó's army marched out of Hǔláoguān.
He dispatched Gùshān Ézhēn Bàiyītú and others to pass through Lóngméngguān,
and Bīngbù Shàngshū Hán Dài, Méilè Zhāngjīng Yí'ěrdé, Shìláng Níkān and others to rendezvous at Guīdé via Nányáng.
All places they passed through welcomed and surrendered,
and Hénán was entirely pacified.
On the Xīnmǎo day,
wasteland tax in Shāndōng was remitted.
On the Gēngzǐ day,
the former Míng Grand Secretary Lǐ Jiàntài came to surrender.
On the Yǐsì day,
officials and soldiers of the Eight Banners were dispatched to garrison Jìníng.
On the Bǐngwǔ day,
Lǐ Hào, the second son of the King of Cháoxiǎn (Korea), returned.
On the Jǐyóu day,
the first year's annual land tax for Jìzhōu was remitted.
On the Rénzǐ day,
all bandits in the Tàiháng Mountains were pacified.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
one officer from each of the Eight Banners of the Hàn Army was dispatched to garrison Shèngjīng.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Wáng Wénkuí was appointed Governor-General of Shǎnxī,
Jiāo Ānmín was appointed Patrol Commissioner of Níngxià,
Huáng Tú'ān was appointed Patrol Commissioner of Gānsù,
the former Míng Minister Zhāng Xīn was appointed Patrol Commissioner of Tiānjīn,
Hǎo Jìn was appointed Patrol Commissioner of Bǎodìng,
and Léi Xīng was appointed Patrol Commissioner of Shǎnxī.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the late Míng eunuch Wáng Chéng'ēn, who died a martyr, was buried beside the Míng Emperor's tomb,
allotted sacrificial fields,
and a stele was erected.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Duōduó's army arrived at Sìzhōu.
Āshān and others seized the Huáihé River bridge north of Sì;
the Míng defending general burned the bridge and fled,
whereupon our army crossed the Huái River by night.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
an edict stated:
"The bandit Lí Zìchéng has murdered his sovereign and oppressed the people,
for which both gods and men are indignant.
We, having received the Mandate of Heaven,
are pacifying and settling Zhōnghuá,
yet he still illicitly occupies Qínchuān,
resisting our authority and teachings.
Therefore, We commanded Heshuò Yù Qīnwáng to move his southern expeditionary forces
to strike directly at Xiáo and Hán,
and Heshuò Yīng Qīnwáng to lead his western expeditionary army
to cross from Suídé.
Within a month,
all of Qín was pacified.
Pitying the common people,
We grant them all renewal.
Those who were coerced or misled by the bandits
are all pardoned,
and all outstanding arrears of taxes are remitted.
Where the grand army passed,
half of this year's regular taxes are remitted,
and one-third of the remainder is remitted."
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Yù Qīnwáng Duōduó's army arrived at Yángzhōu,
and he ordered the former Míng Grand Secretaries Shǐ Kěfǎ and Hànlín Academician Wèi Yìngwén, among others, to surrender.
They refused.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Mèng Qiáofāng was appointed Governor-General of Sānbiān in Shǎnxī.
The eighth daughter of Tàizōng, Gùlún Gōngzhǔ, was married to Bāyāsīhùláng, the son of Kē'ěrqìn Tǔxiètú Qīnwáng Bādálǐ.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Bàiyīntú, Túlái, Āshān, and others conquered Yángzhōu;
the former Míng Grand Secretary Shǐ Kěfǎ refused to yield
and was killed.
On the day Xīnsì,
the first martial provincial examination was held.
In the fifth month, on the first day Rénwǔ,
the River Governor-General Yáng Fāngxīng presented auspicious wheat.
The Emperor said:
"Abundant harvests and content people
are themselves auspicious signs;
they do not lie in auspicious wheat.
We should truly cherish and nurture the populace
and redouble our efforts to soothe and unite them."
On the day Guǐwèi,
due to drought, an edict ordered the Ministry of Justice to review prisoners.
It was ordered that the Grand Secretaries FÉNG Quán, HÓNG Chéngchóu, Lǐ Jiàntài, Fàn Wénchéng, Gānglín, and Qí Chōnggé, among others, compile the Míng History.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Duōduó's army arrived at the Yángzǐ Jiāng.
The former Míng Zhènhǎibó Zhèng Hóngkuí and others, with their fleet, defended Guāzhōu and Yízhēn,
while our army was north of the river.
Bàiyīntú, Túlái, and Āshān led their fleet and secretly crossed from the Grand Canal.
Méilè Zhāngjīng Lǐ Shuàitài landed by night.
At dawn,
our army crossed in succession,
and the enemy forces completely collapsed.
On the day Dīnghài,
Wáng Zhìzhèng was appointed Patrol Commissioner of Yánsuí.
The regular taxes for the first year in Gāomì were remitted.
Ice was bestowed upon princes and officials of all ranks,
and this was made a standing order.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the rebellious commoner Liú Bóxì of Xuānfǔ, who plotted rebellion, was executed.
On the day Gēngyín,
Wáng Wénkuí was appointed Governor-General of Huáiyáng,
and Zhào Fúxīng was appointed Patrol Commissioner of Fèngyáng.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Duōduó's army arrived at Nánjīng.
The former Míng Fúwáng Zhū Yóusōng and Grand Secretary Mǎ Shìyīng fled to Tàipíng.
Xīnchéngbó Zhào Zhīlóng, Grand Secretary Wáng Duó, Minister of Rites Qián Qiānyì, and thirty-one others welcomed the army and surrendered the city.
The son of Xīngpíngbó Gāo Jié, Yuánzhào, and Guǎngchāngbó Liú Liángzuǒ, along with twenty-three others, leading over 230,000 cavalry and infantry, successively came to surrender.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Hǎo Jìn was re-appointed Patrol Commissioner of Bǎodìng.
The regular taxes for the first year in Píngdù, Shòuguāng, and six other prefectures and counties were remitted.
On the day Wùxū,
Manchu youths were ordered to attend school,
to be tested and tutored every ten days,
and to practice archery every five days in spring and autumn.
The former Míng Chancellor Zhāng Cháopìn contributed a thousand logs to assist in building palaces
and requested consideration for office.
An edict stated that appointments were based solely on merit,
and there was no principle of granting office based on contributions.
The relevant department was ordered to pay for the logs.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the charges for imperial workshop artisans from Zhāngqiū and Jìyáng were remitted,
and direct provinces were ordered to abolish the artisan household registration, transforming artisans into commoners.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the protocol for the Regent Prince, the Emperor's uncle, was established:
all official documents were to refer to him as "Imperial Uncle Regent Prince."
On the day Yǐsì,
the Empress's rents were remitted,
as well as the rice and wheat taxes at Chóngwénmén.
On the day Gēngxū,
the news of the victory in pacifying Jiāngnán was announced.
The Qiánqīnggōng was completed,
and the Tàihédiàn, Zhōnghédiàn, and Wèiyùgōng were rebuilt.
In the sixth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
the regular taxes for the first year in Xīngjì County were remitted.
On the day Jiǎyín,
two-thirds of this year's regular taxes for the land designated for imperial use in the vicinity of the capital were remitted.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Dīng Wénshèng was appointed Patrol Commissioner of Shāndōng.
On the day Bǐngchén,
an edict commanded military personnel and civilians in southern China to shave their foreheads and wear queues;
those who disobeyed would be dealt with by military law.
This month,
an edict was first issued to the direct provinces, setting a ten-day deadline to shave their foreheads and wear queues as prescribed by law.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Yù Qīnwáng Duōduó dispatched troops to pursue the former Míng Fúwáng Zhū Yóusōng in Wúhú.
Míng Jìngguógōng Huáng Dégōng fought against them,
but Túlái utterly defeated him,
and Dégōng died from a stray arrow.
Commanders-in-chief Tián Xióng and Mǎ Dégōng captured Fúwáng and his consort and presented them.
All the generals surrendered.
Arrears of wasteland taxes for the first year in Yǒngníng and four other counties were remitted.
On the day Bǐngyín,
the order to shave foreheads and wear queues was reiterated.
Arrears of wasteland taxes for the first year in Shēn, Héngshuǐ, and seven other prefectures and counties were remitted.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the demonic bandit Hú Shǒulóng incited rebellion in Shǎnxī,
but Mèng Qiáofāng suppressed him.
On the day Wùchén,
the Empress Dowager passed away.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Hé Luòhuì led his army to garrison Xī'ān.
It was ordered that the provincial examination in Jiāngnán be held in the tenth month.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
an imperial edict stated:
"Our dynasty established its state on the eastern frontier
many years ago;
its territory was already vast,
with no intention of further annexation.
In the past, military campaigns on the borders
were originally meant to seek peaceful reconciliation.
Unfortunately, the extreme calamities brought by the bandits
brought the Míng dynasty to a permanent end.
It was for this reason that We mobilized Our forces and entered the Pass,
avenging the Míng.
Still, as the bandit leader was not yet annihilated,
We had no leisure to rest.
Therefore, We commanded the two princes
to swear their allegiance and march west.
Meanwhile, in southern China, they seized the opportunity to establish a sovereign,
presumptuously usurping an imperial title,
immediately carrying out chaotic policies,
and grievously oppressing the people.
Day and night, We have been reverently fearful,
desiring to rescue the distressed commoners.
Once the western bandits were crushed,
We then undertook the southern expedition.
Our army advanced without bloodshed,
following the Biàn River to the Huái River.
Having just conquered Wéiyáng,
We then pacified the region east of the Jiāng.
The scholars and women of Jīnlíng
bear witness to Our heavenly benevolence.
Having captured Fúfān,
the southern territories are largely settled.
We therefore widely bestow great favors,
and graciously grant renewal.
All officials and commoners in Hénán, Jiāngběi, and Jiāngnán who were implicated or misled
are all pardoned.
All arbitrary levies and outstanding arrears of taxes
are entirely remitted.
Where the grand army passed,
half of this year's regular taxes are remitted,
and one-third of the remainder is remitted."
In the intercalary sixth month, on the day *jiǎshēn*,
Ājìgé defeated Lǐ Zìchéng at Dèngzhōu.
He pursued him relentlessly to Jiǔjiāng,
fighting thirteen battles,
in all of which he decisively defeated him.
Zìchéng fled to Jiǔgōng Shān,
where he hanged himself.
The rebel factions were all pacified.
Zǔo Mènggēng, son of the former Míng Níngnán Hóu Zǔo Liángyù, and Grand Coordinator Yuán Jìxián, among others, led 130,000 cavalry and infantry and 40,000 boats from Dōngliú to surrender.
On the day *bǐngxū*,
the styles for the official hats of all officials from the rank of *gōng* downwards, and of *shēngyuán* and respected elders, were determined.
On the day *jǐchǒu*,
the river burst its banks at Wángjiāyuán.
On the day *gēngyín*,
an imperial edict commanded Ājìgé and others to return with their armies.
On the day *xīnmǎo*,
the system for grain tribute (*cáo*) and white grain (*bái*) in Jiāngnán was changed from private collection by the people to official collection and delivery.
On the day *rénchén*,
an edict stated:
"During the late Míng period, the censorial officials [tái jiàn]
usurped fame and coveted profit,
formed factions to attack each other,
bewildered the emperor's mind,
and ultimately led to chaos and loss.
Now that the empire is newly settled,
all things are to be reformed.
All officials should be loyal and devoted to the state,
each fulfilling their duties,
so as not to follow the old path
and bring about their own downfall."
The grades for Manchurian civil and military officials were determined.
On the day *guǐsì*,
Grand Secretary Hóng Chéngchóu was ordered to pacify and recruit the various provinces of Jiāngnán.
On the day *jiǎwǔ*,
the styles for the official hats of princes, *bèilè*, *bèizi*, and imperial clan *gōng* were determined.
On the day *yǐwèi*,
the punishment of "cutting the tendons of the feet" was abolished.
On the day *guǐmǎo*,
Wú Wéihuá was ordered to pacify Guǎngdōng,
Sūn Zhīxiè to pacify Jiāngxī,
Huáng Xīyǔn to pacify Fújiàn,
Jiāng Yǔxù to pacify Húguǎng,
and Dīng Zhīlóng to pacify Yúnnán and Guìzhōu.
Duōduò dispatched *bèilè* Bóluò, along with Bāyīntú and Āshān, to lead an army to Hángzhōu.
The former Míng Lù Wáng surrendered,
and Huái Wáng came to surrender from Shàoxīng.
The prefectures of Jiāxīng, Húzhōu, Yánzhōu, and Níngbō were all pacified.
General-in-chief Wú Shèngzhào was sent to conquer Lúzhōu and Hézhōu.
On the day *yǐsì*,
Nánjīng was renamed Jiāngnán Province,
and Yìngtiān Fǔ was renamed Jiāngníng Fǔ.
Shǎnxī was ordered to hold the provincial examination in the tenth month.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day, *gēngxū*,
sacrifices were offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the day *rénzǐ*,
*bèilè* Lèkèdéhún was appointed Pacifying the South Great General,
to proceed to Jiāngnán with *gùshān ézhēn* Yèchén and others to replace Duōduò.
Four eunuchs were appointed to guard the mausoleum of Míng Tàizǔ,
and 2,000 *mǔ* of sacrificial land were allocated.
On the day *guǐchǒu*,
former Míng Dōngpíng Hóu Liú Zéqīng surrendered with his troops.
On the day *yǐmǎo*,
Liú Yìngbīn was made Anlú Patrol Inspector,
and Tǔ Guóbǎo was made Jiāngníng Patrol Inspector.
On the day *bǐngchén*,
Xiè Hóngyí was ordered to pacify Guǎngxī.
On the day *wùwǔ*,
it was forbidden for military and civilian personnel, both inside and outside the capital, to wear clothes and hats not conforming to the national system.
On the day *jǐwèi*,
Hé Míngluán was made Húguǎng Patrol Inspector,
Gāo Dǒuguāng was made Piān Yuán Patrol Inspector,
and Pān Shìliáng was appointed Pacification Commissioner for Yúnyáng.
On the day *jiǎzǐ*,
jade books and jade seals for Tàizǔ Wǔhuángdì, Xiàocí Wǔhuánghòu, and Tàizōng Wénhuángdì were presented at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the day *yǐchǒu*,
half of Xi'ān and Yán'ān's tax quotas for the current year were remitted,
and one-third of the rest.
On the day *wùchén*,
the rebel leader Liú Hóngqǐ in Xīpíng was captured and executed,
and Rúníng Prefecture and its counties were all pacified.
The river burst the newly built moon-shaped dike west of Yǎnzhōu.
On the day *jǐsì*,
an imperial edict decreed that from now on, all memorials from within and outside the capital should be sealed and submitted through the Tōngzhèng Sì.
On the day *dīngchǒu*,
Chén Jǐn was appointed Naval Commander of the Jiāng River,
also concurrently managing the duties of Patrol Inspector.
Former Míng Grand Grain Commissioner Tián Yǎng occupied Tōngzhōu, Rúgāo, and Hǎimén.
Fèngyáng Patrol Inspector Zhào Fúxīng and *méilè zhāngjīng* Tán Bù, among others, suppressed and pacified him.
On the day *jǐmǎo*,
Yáng Shēngyuǎn was appointed Dēnglái Patrol Inspector.
In the eighth month, on the day *xīnsì*,
disaster taxes for Bā, Shùnyì, and eight other prefectures and counties were remitted.
On the day *yǐyǒu*,
famine taxes for Zhāngdé, Wèihuī, Huáiqìng, and various prefectures in Hénán were remitted.
On the day *jǐchǒu*,
the army of Yīng Qīnwáng Ājìgé returned.
Gold and silk were bestowed upon the participating Outer Vassal Princes, *tàijí*, generals, and officers, with varying amounts.
On the day *guǐsì*,
disaster taxes for Zhēndìng, Shùndé, Guǎngpíng, and Dàmíng were remitted.
On the day *bǐngwǔ*,
the surrendered general Jīn Shēnghuán attacked the former Míng Yì Wáng,
captured his accompanying official Wáng Yǎngzhèng and others, and executed them,
also capturing Zhōngxiáng Wáng Zhū Zī(xiàng) and nine others.
On the day *dīngwèi*,
Yīng Qīnwáng Ājìgé was found guilty for his actions during the expedition,
and was demoted to *jùnwáng*.
Tán Tàì was stripped of his ducal title [gōngjué],
and demoted to *ángbāng zhāngjīng*.
Áobài and others were punished with varying penalties.
In the ninth month, on the day *gēngxū*,
former Míng Lǔ Wáng's generals Fāng Guó'ān and Wáng Zhīrén attacked Hángzhōu.
Zhāng Cúnrén repelled them.
On the day *guǐchǒu*,
Zhèn Guó Gōng Fùlèhè and Fǔ Guó Gōng Zhákànà, among others, were ordered to lead armies to assist in defending Jiāngxī.
On the day *dīngsì*,
the former Míng Huái'ān Wáng came to surrender.
On the day *xīnyǒu*,
the former Míng Xīnchāng Wáng occupied Yúntái Shān,
and captured Xīnghuà.
Zhǔntǎ attacked and killed him.
On the day *jiǎzǐ*,
wastelands in Héjiān, Luánzhōu, and Zūnhuà were given to the Eight Banners for cultivation,
and remaining lands of former Míng meritorious relatives and court eunuchs were also distributed.
On the day *gēngwǔ*,
Tián Yǎng plundered Fúshān.
Tǔ Guóbǎo defeated him.
On the day *dīngchǒu*,
the eleven prefectures of Nánchāng in Jiāngxī were pacified.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day *guǐwèi*,
Mǎ Guózhù was appointed Governor of Xuāndà.
On the day *wùzǐ*,
former Míng Hanlin scholar Jīn Shēng, by imperial edict of Táng Wáng, raised an army in Huīzhōu,
with over 100,000 men.
Hóng Chéngchóu dispatched Commander Zhāng Tiānlù, who repeatedly defeated them at Jìxī,
capturing Jīn Shēng.
He refused to yield
and was killed.
At this time,
former Míng Táng Wáng Zhū Yùzhāo occupied Fújiàn,
Lǔ Wáng Zhū Yíhái occupied Zhèjiāng,
and Mǎ Shìyīng and others' forces crossed the Qiántáng River and set up camps to resist orders.
On the day *gēngyín*,
famine taxes for Báodǐ County were remitted.
On the day *rénchén*,
disaster taxes for Tàiyuán and other prefectures and sub-prefectures were remitted.
On the day *guǐsì*,
Yù Qīnwáng Duōduò's army returned.
The emperor traveled to Nányuàn to welcome and commend him.
On the day *bǐngshēn*,
Miáo Zuòtǔ was appointed Nángàn Patrol Inspector.
On the day *yǐsì*,
the second daughter of Tàizōng, Gǔlún Gōngzhǔ, was married to Ābùnài, son of the Cháhā'ěr Khān.
On the day *bǐngwǔ*,
Shēn Cháojì was appointed Shānxī Patrol Inspector,
Lǐ Xiángfèng was appointed Jiāngxī Patrol Inspector,
and Xiāo Qǐyuán was appointed Zhèjiāng Patrol Inspector.
On the day *wùshēn*,
Héshuò Yù Qīnwáng Duōduò was elevated to the title of Héshuò Dé Yù Qīnwáng,
and gold and silk were bestowed upon the participating princes, *bèilè*, *bèizi*, *gōng*, and Outer Vassal *tàijí* and *zhāngjīng*, with varying amounts.
Kǒng Yǒudé and Gěng Zhòngmíng were ordered to return to Shèngjīng.
In the eleventh month, on the day *rénzǐ*,
Zhāng Cúnrén was appointed Governor-General of Zhèjiāng and Fújiàn,
and Luó Xiùjǐn was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng and Sìchuān.
On the day *guǐchǒu*,
former Míng Grand Secretary Wáng Yìngxióng and Sìchuān Patrol Inspector Lóng Wénguāng requested to surrender.
On the day *jiǎyín*,
Wú Jǐngdào was appointed Hénán Patrol Inspector.
Bāshān and Kāngkālài were appointed Left and Right Wings,
to be stationed with Hóng Chéngchóu in Jiāngníng.
Zhūmǎlā was stationed in Hángzhōu.
*Bèilè* Lèkèdéhún, with Gǒng'ādài and Yèchén, was to attack the Húguǎng bandits Èrzhīhǔ and others.
On the day *jǐwèi*,
King Lǐ Zōng of Cháoxiǎn requested to establish his second son Hào as Crown Prince,
which was permitted.
On the day *dīngmǎo*,
Zhūmǎlā defeated Mǎ Shìyīng at Yúháng,
and Hétuō defeated Fāng Guó'ān at Fùyáng.
Shìyīng and Guó'ān again attempted to attack Hángzhōu.
*Méilè zhāngjīng* Jíxíhā and others repelled them.
On the day *wùchén*,
Hélùohuì was appointed Pacifying the West Great General.
Bāyán and Lǐ Guóhàn were dispatched to lead an army to join him,
to attack the Sìchuān bandit Zhāng Xiànzhōng.
On the day *wùyín*,
Chén Zhīlóng was appointed Fèngyáng Patrol Inspector.
On the *jǐmǎo* day of the twelfth month, the new moon day,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the former Míng Grand Secretary Huáng Dàozhōu invaded Huīzhōu.
Hóng Chéngchóu dispatched Zhāng Tiānlù to defeat him.
The former Míng General Gāo Jìnzhōng led his troops from Chóngmíng to surrender.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Tóng Yǎnghé and Jīn Shēnghuán advanced to suppress Fújiàn.
They divided their forces to attack Nángàn,
and defeated the former Míng Yǒngníng Wáng, Luóchuan Wáng, Grand Secretary Huáng Dàozhōu, and hundreds of thousands of others.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the court rituals were revised.
For the first time, eunuchs were exempted from court attendance.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Zhū Mǎlā and others defeated Fāng Guó'ān and Mǎ Shìyīng in eastern Zhèjiāng.
The Gùyuán bandit Wǔ Dàdìng rebelled,
and General Hé Shìyuán and others died.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn,
the Jāngjīng Gǔlùgé of the Tǔmòtè tribe of Guīhuà Chéng,
the Lama Tǎ'ěrníqí of the È'ěrdúosī tribe,
the Chechen Qīnwáng of the Wūzhūmùqín tribe,
È'ěrgēnà of the Xíbù tribe,
the Tǔxiètú Hán of the Kā'ěrkā tribe, Gulúndíwǎ Hútúkètú Lama, Shílètú Hútúkètú, and Máhāsàmádì Sàichén Hán,
Dorjí Dálài Bātúlǔ Tái jí, son of Gùshí Hán of the Èlǔtè tribe, and the Huíhuí Guó,
and Tiānfāng Guó all came to pay tribute.
Cháoxiǎn arrived four times.
In the spring of the third year, on the *wùwǔ* day of the first month,
Bèilè Lèkèdéhún dispatched a general to defeat the roaming bandits in Línxiāng,
and then conquered Yuèzhōu.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Gùshān Èzhēn Āshān and Tán Tài committed crimes.
Āshān was dismissed from office,
and Tán Tài was imprisoned.
The roaming bandits Hè Zhēn, Sūn Shǒufǎ, and Hú Xiànghuà attacked Xī'ān.
Hé Luòhuì and others defeated them.
Jīn Shēnghuán dispatched a general to attack the former Míng Yǒngníng Wáng in Fúzhōu,
captured him,
and also captured his son Zhū Zīróng and others,
thus pacifying Jiànchāng.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the former Míng Lù'ān Wáng and Ruìchāng Wáng led troops to invade Jiāngníng.
Vice Minister Bāshān and others defeated them.
On the *wùchén* day,
Sòng Quán was appointed Grand Academician of the Guóshǐ Yuàn.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Sù Qīnwáng Háogé was appointed Jìngyuǎn Dàjiāngjūn,
along with Duōluó Yǎnxǐ Jùnwáng Luóluòhóng, Bèilè Níkān, Bèizǐ Túnqíqiā, Mǎndáhǎi and others, to lead an army to conquer Sìchuān.
The former Míng Táng Wáng Zhū Yùzhāo's forces attacked Huīzhōu.
Hóng Chéngchóu dispatched Zhāng Tiānlù and others to defeat them,
captured their Grand Secretary Huáng Dàozhōu and executed him,
and then conquered Huà.
On the *jǐmǎo* day of the second month,
Bèilè Lèkèdéhún defeated the roaming bandits in Jīngzhōu.
Fèngguó Jiāngjūn Bābùtài and others pursued them to Xiāngyáng,
slaughtering and capturing almost all of them.
The grand army advanced to Yílíng,
and Lǐ Zìchéng's younger brother Lǐ Zī and others surrendered with their troops.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the barren land tax in Mìyún was remitted.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the old bureaus and ministries in Jiāngnán were abolished.
One Mǎn and one Hàn Vice Minister from each of the Hù, Bīng, and Gōng ministries in the capital were dispatched to reside in Jiāngníng,
to handle departmental affairs separately.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Liú Fú, a general of Míng Lǔ Wáng, reinforced Fúzhōu.
Měilè Zhāngjīng Tún Tài defeated him.
Hé Luòhuì dispatched a general to defeat the roaming bandit Liú Wénbǐng in Púchéng,
and the bandit leader Hè Zhēn fled to Wǔgōng.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Liǔ Yīndōng was appointed Sùntiān Xúnfǔ.
Sù Qīnwáng Háogé was ordered to divide his forces and proceed to Nányáng,
to suppress the roaming bandits Èrzhīhǔ, Hǎo Rúhǎi, and others.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Vice Minister Bāshān and Měilè Zhāngjīng Zhāng Dàyóu were dispatched to lead troops to garrison Jiāngníng.
Jiǎlā Zhāngjīng Fù Kuāchán and Měilè Zhāngjīng Lǐ Sīzhōng were dispatched to lead troops to garrison Xī'ān.
The bandit leaders Shí Yīnglián of Qiánshān and Tàihú, along with the former Míng Fánshān Wáng Zhū Cháng..., created chaos.
Hóng Chéngchóu dispatched a general to attack and execute them.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Bèilè Bóluò was appointed Zhēngnán Dàjiāngjūn,
and together with Túlái, he led an army to conquer Fújiàn and Zhèjiāng.
On the *xīnhài* day of the third month,
the Hóngwǔ Bǎoxùn was translated and completed,
and promulgated throughout the empire.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
residents near the capital whose fields and homes were granted to banner people and subsequently reallocated were exempted from rent and tax for one year.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Hé Luòhuì defeated the bandit Liú Tǐchún in Shānyáng.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Wáng Láiyòng was appointed Governor-General of military provisions for Shān, Shǎnxī, and Sìchuān.
Mǎ Míngpèi was appointed Governor-General of grain reserves for the provinces of Jiāngnán.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Fù Yǐjiàn and others were awarded the degree of *jìnshì jí dì* with differing ranks.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Hé Luòhuì attacked the bandit Èrzhīhǔ in Shāngzhōu,
and thoroughly defeated him.
The Chāngpíng commoners Wáng Kē and others robbed the Míngdì Líng,
and were executed.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Duōluó Ráoyú Jùnwáng Ābātài passed away.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Sàilěng of the Sūnítè tribe and Bóluótè of the Hāoqítè tribe were enfeoffed as Bèilè.
Dorjí of the Ābàgāi tribe was enfeoffed as Bèizǐ.
Háogé's army arrived in Xī'ān.
He dispatched Minister of Works Xīngnéng to defeat the bandits in Bīnzhōu,
and Gùshān Èzhēn Dùléi to defeat the bandits in Qìngyáng.
The former Míng Grand Academician Zhāng Sìzhī came from Jiāngnán to surrender.
In the summer of the fourth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
an imperial edict ordered Bèilè Lèkèdéhún to return with his army.
Kǒng Yǒudé, Gěng Zhòngmíng, Shàng Kěxǐ, and Shěn Zhìxiáng each led their troops to the capital.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the house tax in Qiántáng and Rénhé was remitted.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
it was ordered that the provincial examination be held again in the eighth month of this year,
and the metropolitan examination be held again in the second month of next year.
On the *dīnghài* day,
disaster taxes in Suīzhōu, Xiángfú, and other four prefectures and counties were remitted.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the punishment of piercing ears and noses was abolished.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the additional taxes of the late Míng period, namely the Gūxī Qiáo rice tax in Tàipíng Fǔ, the Jīnzhù Shān commercial tax, and the salt tax in Ānqìng Fǔ, were abolished.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the barren land tax in Jìnghǎi, Xīngjì, and Qīngxiàn was remitted.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
bandits from Fúliáng and Yúgàn in Jiāngxī, allied with Fújiàn bandits, attacked Ráozhōu.
Brigadier General Dèng Yúnlóng and others defeated them.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Regent Duō'ěrgǔn ordered the suspension of memorials from princes and high officials.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Zhāng Shàng was appointed Níngxià Xúnfǔ.
The weaving eunuchs were abolished.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
an edict stated:
"Recently, the oppressive and harsh taxes of the late Míng period were abolished,
allowing the people to rest.
However, corrupt officials,
resenting the harm to themselves, removed these items from the records,
thereby preventing the court's benevolent intentions from reaching the lower levels,
and preventing the complete rectification of the late Míng's corrupt policies.
Now, high officials are ordered to strictly investigate and verify,
and the relevant departments are instructed to meticulously compile a complete book of taxes and corvée,
and promulgate it throughout the realm."
An edict ordered the reduction of redundant officials in prefectures and counties.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the Kǒngzǐ Miào in Shèngjīng was repaired.
In the fifth month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
Téngjīsī, Téngjítè, Wúbāndài, Duō'ěrzí Sīkābù, Mǎngwùsī, È'ěrmíkè, Shídá, and others of the Sūnítè tribe each led their tribes in rebellion and fled to Shuòléi of the Kā'ěrkā tribe.
Dé Yùqīnwáng Duōduō was appointed Yángwēi Dàjiāngjūn,
and together with Chéngzé Jùnwáng Shuòsài and others, he led an army to join with the foreign vassal Mongol troops to suppress them.
Wēnbǔ, Dá'ěrhàn Zhuólìkètú, Duōkèxīn, and others of the Sìzǐ tribe pursued and executed Wúbāndài and five other *táijí*.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the law against harboring fugitives was re-emphasized.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Jīn Shēnghuán conquered Nángàn,
and captured its commander Liú Guǎngyìn.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Háogé dispatched Bāyán and Lǐ Guóhàn to defeat the bandits in Yán'ān.
On the *rénxū* day,
the former Míng Lǔ Wáng, Jīng Wáng, Héng Wáng's heir apparent, and eleven others conspired to rebel,
and were executed.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Yè Kèshū was appointed Ángbāng Zhāngjīng,
to garrison Shèngjīng.
Háogé dispatched Bèilè Níkān and others to defeat the bandit Hè Zhēn at Jītóu Guān,
and then conquered Hànzhōng.
Zhēn fled to Xīxiāng.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Bèilè Bóluò dispatched Túlái and others to defeat Fāng Guó'ān, a general of the former Míng Lǔ Wáng, in Qiántáng.
Lǔ Wáng Zhū Yígāi fled to Táizhōu for protection.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the government forces reached Hànyīn.
The roaming bandit Èrzhīhǔ fled to Sìchuān.
Sūn Shǒufǎ fled to Yuèkē Zhài.
Bāyán and Lǐ Guóhàn pursued the Yán'ān bandits to Zhāngguǒlǎo Yá and defeated them.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
half of the barren land tax for the first and second years in Pèi and Xiāo counties was remitted.
In the sixth month, on the *wùyín* day,
the barren land tax in Huáiróu county was remitted.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the White Lotus, Dacheng, Hunyuan, Wuwei, and other sects were prohibited.
On the *rénchén* day,
Gāo Shìjùn was appointed Húguǎng Xúnfǔ.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Zhāng Cúnrén dispatched a general to capture and execute the former Míng Grand Academician Mǎ Shìyīng and Chángxīng Bó Wú Rìshēng and others.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day *jiǎyín*,
Bèilè Lèkèdéhún’s army returned.
On the day *dīngsì*,
Duōduó defeated Téngjīsī and others at Ōutèkè Shān,
beheading their Tàijí Máohài.
He crossed the Tǔlā Hé and attacked and beheaded Téngjīsī’s son Duōěrjì and others,
capturing all their family members, livestock, and baggage.
He also defeated the two sons of Tǔxiètú Hàn of the Kāěrkā tribe upstream of Cházhìbùlākè.
On the day *wǔwǔ*,
Shuòléi’s son arrayed troops at the Cházhìbùlākè pass,
and Bèizi Bóhéwěi and others again thoroughly defeated him.
Shuòléi fled with his remaining troops to Sèlénggé.
On the day *gēngshēn*,
Lǐ Guóhàn, Túlái, and others captured Zhāngguǒlǎo Yá.
On the day *rénxū*,
Lǐ Xiángfèng, the Governor of Jiāngxī, presented forty talismans of the Zhèngyī Zhēnrén.
An edict stated:
“The way to bring blessings
lies in respecting Heaven and diligent care for the people.
Why bother with these?
Put them aside.”
On the day *wùchén*,

Háogé dispatched Bèizi Mǎndáhǎi, Fǔguó Gōng Hāěrdéchúhún, and Gùshān Ézhēn Zhǔntǎ to advance towards Huīzhōu and Jiēzhōu to separately attack the bandit leaders Wǔ Dàdìng, Gāo Rúlí, Jiǎng Dēngléi, Shí Guóxǐ, and Wáng Kěchén.
They defeated them.
Rúlí fled,
while Dēngléi, Guóxǐ, and Kěchén all surrendered.
In the eighth month, on the day *bǐngzǐ*,
Duōluó Yǎnxǐ Jùnwáng Luóluòhóng died in the army.
On the day *dīngchǒu*,
Háogé dispatched Dàozhāngjīng Hāníng'ā to attack Wǔ Dàdìng at Sāntái Shān,
capturing it.
On the day *dīnghài*,
Bóluò captured Jīnhuá and Qúzhōu,
killing the former Míng Shǔ Wáng Zhū Shèngnóng, Lè'ān Wáng Zhū Yíshí, and their generals Wú Kǎi, Xiàng Míngsī, and others.
Their Grand Secretary Xiè Sānbīn, Cabinet Minister Sòng Zhīpǔ, Minister of War Ruǎn Dàchéng, Minister of Justice Sū Zhuàng, and others surrendered.
Zhèjiāng was pacified.
On the day *wùzǐ*,
Kǒng Yǒudé was appointed Píngnán Dàjiāngjūn,
and together with Gěng Zhòngmíng, Shěn Zhìxiáng, Jīn Lì, and Tóng Dài, he led an army to conquer Húguǎng, Guǎngdōng, and Guǎngxī.
Taxes for two years for Tàihú and Qiánshān, and this year’s famine taxes, were remitted.
On the day *guǐsì*,
Shàng Kěxǐ was ordered to lead an army to accompany Kǒng Yǒudé on the southern expedition.
In the ninth month, on the day *jǐyǒu*,
the former Míng Ruìchāng Wáng Zhū Yìlì plotted to attack Jiāngníng.
Government troops attacked and beheaded him.
On the day *jiǎzǐ*,
seven tenths of the famine taxes for thirteen prefectures and counties including Yílíng and Shíshǒu were remitted;
five tenths for four prefectures and counties including Jīngmén and Jiānglíng;
and three tenths for sixteen prefectures and counties including Xìngguó and Guǎngjì.
On the day *bǐngyín*,
the former Míng Chóngyáng Wáng attacked Shèxiàn.
Vice-general Zhāng Chénggōng and others defeated him.
On the day *dīngmǎo*,
the former Míng Governor-General Hé Téngjiāo and others attacked Yuèzhōu.
Government forces attacked and defeated them.
In the tenth month of winter, on the day *bǐngzǐ*,
Zhèng Sìwéi and others captured Yílíng, Zhījiāng, and Yídū.
Húguǎng Chéngtiān Fǔ was renamed Ānlù Fǔ.
On the day *jǐmǎo*,
Héshuò Déyù Qīnwáng Duōduó’s army returned.
The Emperor personally welcomed him in the suburbs.
On the day *xīnsì*,
Jīn Shēnghuán dispatched a general to capture the former Míng King Zhū Chángjiàn and his associate Liǎowù,
and executed them.
On the day *jiǎshēn*,
Hú Quáncái was appointed Governor of Níngxià,
and Zhāng Yútiān as Governor of Jiāngxī.
Jīn Shēnghuán dispatched a general to capture Gànzhōu,
seizing and killing the former Míng Cabinet Minister Yáng Tínglín.
On the day *guǐsì*,
Lǐ Qīfèng was appointed Governor of Ānhuī.
On the day *dīngyǒu*,
disaster taxes for four counties including Huáiníng were remitted.
On the day *jǐhài*,
disaster taxes for Yánsuī and Zhuānglàng were remitted.
On the day *rényín*,
Tàihé Gōng and Zhōnghé Gōng were completed.
In the eleventh month, on the first day *guǐmǎo*,
Bèilè Bóluò, dividing his forces from Zhèjiāng, advanced to capture Fújiàn.
Túlái and others defeated the former Míng Cabinet Minister Huáng Míngjùn at Xiānxiá Guān,
and subsequently captured Pǔchéng, Jiànníng, and Yánpíng.
The former Míng Táng Wáng Zhū Yùzhāo fled to Tīngzhōu.
Ājìgé Níkān and others pursued and beheaded him,
thereby pacifying Tīngzhōu, Zhāngzhōu, Quánzhōu, and Xīnghuà.
They advanced and captured Fúzhōu,
and all their forces surrendered.
Fújiàn was pacified.
On the day *guǐchǒu*,
disaster taxes for Héjiān, Rènqiū, and Dàtóng were remitted.
On the day *dīngsì*,
sacrifices to Heaven were offered at the Huánqiū.
On the day *jǐsì*,
Háogé’s army reached Nánbù.
At this time, Zhāng Xiànzhōng had set up camps in Xīchōng.
Áobài and others marched day and night to attack,
severely defeating him
and beheading Xiànzhōng in battle.
They then divided their troops to attack the remaining bandits,
destroying over one hundred and thirty camps.
Sìchuān was pacified.
In the twelfth month, on the first day *guǐyǒu*,
the former Míng Suípíng Wáng Zhū Shàokūn and his associate Yáng Quán, leading troops at Tàihú,
allied with sea pirates to cause unrest.
Vice-general Zhān Shìxūn and others attacked and beheaded them.
On the day *gēngxū*,
Shāndōng bandit Xiè Qiān attacked and captured Gāoyuàn.
Commander-in-Chief Hǎi Shíxíng attacked and pacified him.
On the day *rénwǔ*,
the former Míng Gāo'ān Wáng Zhū Chángqí and his associate Jiāng Yúdōng raised an army in Wùyuán.
Zhāng Tiānlù attacked and pacified them.
On the day *bǐngxū*,
Yú Qīnglián was appointed Governor of Bǎodìng,
Liú Wǔyuán as Governor of Nángàn.
Disaster taxes for five prefectures and counties including Jì and Fēngrùn were remitted.
On the day *jiǎwǔ*,
Wèiyù Gōng was completed.
On the day *gēngzǐ*,
the Míng Jīnhuá Wáng Zhū Yóu-- (the character for "bì" is missing) raised an army in Ráozhōu.
Government forces attacked and beheaded him.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn,
Měnggǔ, and the Guīhuà Chéng Tǔmòtè tribe’s Gǔlùgé;
the Élǔtè tribe’s Duōěrjì Dáláibātúlǔ and Gùshí Hàn;
the Kāěrkā tribe’s Mǎidálí Hútúkètú, Éěrdéní Hātánbātúlǔ, Dàiqīng Hātánbātúlǔ, and Qīng Tàijí;
the Kēěrqìn tribe’s Duōluó Bīngtú Jùnwáng Sàiléng;
the Hāoqíxītè tribe’s Duōluó Bèilè Éěrdéní;
the Suǒlún tribe’s and Shǐlù tribe’s Lābāqí;
the Éěrdōusī tribe’s Jìnóng Tàijí Chámùsū;
the Kùěrkā tribe’s Láidákù; and the Dálài Lǎma,
as well as Tǔlúfān, all came to pay tribute.
Cháoxiǎn, the Élǔtè Gùshí Hàn, and the Dálài Lǎma all came a second time.
In the first month of spring of the fourth year, on the day *wùshēn*,
Fǔguó Gōng Gǒng'ādài, Grand Minister Wúbài, and others campaigned against Xuānfǔ.
On the day *rénzǐ*,
Vice-Commander Dǒng'ālái was ordered to lead troops to garrison Hángzhōu.
Xìngguó Zhōu bandit Kē Bàochōng allied with the former Míng Governor-General Hé Téngjiāo to attack and capture Xìngguó.
Commander-in-Chief Kē Yǒngshèng dispatched a general to capture Bàochōng and his associate Chén Héngyù and behead them.
On the day *yǐmǎo*,
Yáng Shēngyuǎn was appointed Governor-General of Huái-Yáng,
and Huáng Érxìng as Governor of Shǎnxī.
On the day *xīnyǒu*,
Zhū Guózhù was appointed Governor of Dēng-Lái.
On the day *rénxū*,
Shǎnxī government forces attacked the Yánqìng bandit Guō Jūnzhèn and the Zhōngnán bandit Sūn Shǒufǎ,
defeating them.
Hóng Chéngchóu dispatched a general to attack bandit leader Zhào Zhèng,
severely defeating him.
In the second month, on the day *guǐyǒu*,
Zhāng Rúxiù was appointed Governor of Shāndōng.
On the day *yǐhài*,
Tóng Yǎngjiǎ pacified Wúzhōu.
On the day *dīngchǒu*,
Vice-general Wáng Píng and others attacked the bandit groups of Hè Zhēn and Liú Èrhǔ in Xīng'ān,
defeating them.
On the day *guǐwèi*,
an imperial edict stated:
“I have pacified the Central Plains.
Only eastern Zhèjiāng and all of Mǐn (Fújiàn) still obstruct the spread of our teachings.
The people suffer hardship and distress,
with no one to appeal to.
Therefore, I command the Zhēngnán Dàjiāngjūn Bèilè Bóluò to lead his army forward.
Having pacified eastern Zhèjiāng,
he then captured Mǐnyuè.
Wherever his vanguard reached,
the desperate bandits hid.
The main army pursued them,
reaching Tīngshuǐ.
Yùzhāo was beheaded,
and all the prefectures were pacified.
Considering that those who usurped titles and resisted with arms,
what crime did their people commit?
Therefore, to show great benevolence
and usher in renewal,
all crimes of officials and common people
are hereby pardoned.
Excessive taxes and arrears
are all exempted.
Hermits in mountains and forests
shall each be recorded by name and employed.
Those aged seventy and above
shall be granted silk and rice in varying amounts.”
On the day *jǐchǒu*,
Hóng Chéngchóu captured the former Míng Ruìchāng Wáng Zhū Yìguì and the Hú (Húguǎng) bandit Zhào Zhèng,
and executed them.
On the day *yǐwèi*,
Zhū Yùzhāo’s younger brother Yù (the character for "jiàn" is missing) usurped the title Shàowǔ
and occupied Guǎngzhōu.
Tóng Yǎngjiǎ and Lǐ Chéngdòng led an army to attack him,

beheading Yù (the character for "jiàn") and Zhōu Wáng Sù-- (the character for "bāo" is missing), Yì Wáng Sī-- (the character for "bāo" is missing), Liáo Wáng Shùyǎ, Dèng Wáng Qì-- (the character for "xián" is missing), Jùyě Wáng Shòu-- (the character for "xián" is missing), Tōngshān Wáng Yùnyuè, Gāomì Wáng Hóngyǐ, Rénhuà Wáng Cí-- (the character for "guà" is missing), Yānlíng Wáng Sùruì, Nán'ān Wáng Qǐlǒng, and others.
Guǎngzhōu was pacified.
On the day *wùxū*,
Tóng Guóyì was appointed Governor of Fújiàn.
In the third month, on the day Wùwǔ,
official titles were bestowed upon Lǚ Gōng and others who had successfully passed the jinshi examination, with varying ranks.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Gěng Tūn was appointed Grand Coordinator of Shùntiān,
Zhōu Bódá was appointed Grand Coordinator of Jiāngníng,
and Zhào Zhàolín was appointed Governor of Yúnjīyang.
On the day Gēngshēn,

an edict was issued commanding all capital officials of the third rank and above, as well as all Grand Coordinators (dū), Circuit Intendants (fǔ), Provincial Commanders (tí), and Garrison Commanders (zhèn), to send one son to court for imperial guard duty,
whose talents would be assessed for appointment.
Those without sons were to be represented by a brother or a nephew.
On the day Rénxū,
the salt tax and the horse service silver in Chóngmíng County were remitted.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the Dàqīng Lǜ (Great Qing Code) was completed.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Tóng Yǎngjiǎ conquered the three prefectures of Gāo, Léi, and Lián.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
an order was given that the sacrificial animals for the suburban altars and the altars of earth and grain, the tàiláo, should still be offered raw.
On the day Jǐsì,
Hàn people were prohibited from defecting and joining the Manchus.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the practice of requisitioning private land and residences was abolished;
those already requisitioned were to be compensated.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
Tián Yǎng led his部 (bù) and surrendered.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Gāo Shìjùn captured Chángshā,
and the Angban Zhangjing Fù Kāchán attacked Liú Wénbǐng and Guō Jūnzhèn,
annihilating them.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Bèile Bóluò returned with his army.
In this campaign,
Bèizi Hétuō and Gùshān Ézhēn Gōng Túlài both died in the army.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Shǎnxī official army beheaded Sūn Shǒufǎ.
In the fifth month, on the day Rényín,
the Zhōushān sea bandits Shěn Tíngyáng and others attacked Chóngmíng,
and the official army attacked and captured them.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Hóu Dòngcéng, a former Míng 通政使 (tōngzhèngshǐ) residing at home, sent a spy with a letter to Prince Lǔ,
falsely promising Hóng Chéngchóu and Tǔ Guóbǎo the titles of Duke and Marquis,
to jointly pacify Jiāngnán,
as a counter-espionage scheme.
The Zhèlín Yóujī captured him and reported it.
The Emperor recognized the deception,
and ordered Jiāngníng Angban Zhangjing Bāshān and others, along with Chéngchóu, to thoroughly investigate the matter.
On the day Gēngxū,
the disaster taxes of the previous year for Xīngguó, Jiāngxià, and ten other prefectures and counties were remitted.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Tóng Yǎngjiǎ was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng,
also serving as Grand Coordinator of Guǎngdōng.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Cháng Yìngjùn, Earl of Submission, and Grand Commander Lǐ Jìyù and others were executed for collusion with bandits.
They were put to death.
On the day Guǐhài,
the Emperor visited Nányuàn.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Bāndài, Éqí'ěr, and Húbājīn came from Sūnítè and surrendered.
In the sixth month, on the day Rénshēn,
the disaster taxes of the previous year for Chéng'ān and seven other counties were remitted.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Lǐ Zōng, the King of Joseon, sent his son [missing character] to pay homage at court.
On the day Gēngchén,
Zhū Yóuyǎn, the former Míng Prince Zhào, came and surrendered.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the disaster taxes of the previous year for Suídé卫 (wèi) were remitted.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Bèile Bóluò was enfeoffed as Duōluó Jùnwáng.
On the day Guǐsì,
the Shǎnxī bandit Wǔ Dàdìng seized Zǐyáng,
but Grand Commander Rèn Zhēn attacked and defeated him.
The Húguǎng official army captured Héngzhōu, Chángdé, and the counties of Ānhuà, Xīnhuà, and others.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Wú Shèngzhào, the Provincial Commander of Sūsōng, plotted rebellion,
and was put to death.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the barren land taxes of the previous year for Shāndōng were remitted.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
Héshuò Déyù Qīnwáng Duōduō was further enfeoffed as Fǔzhèng Shū Déyù Qīnwáng.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
a shooting hall was built outside the Zǔoyìmén (Left Wing Gate).
On the day Jiǎchén,
the barren land taxes of the previous year for Xúzhōu were remitted.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Mò'ěrgēnbātúlǔ, the son of Bāndì, the Efù of the Àohàn tribe, was enfeoffed as Duōluó Jùnwáng.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Shēn Cháojì was appointed Governor-General of Xuāndà.
On the day Dīngsì,
Wáng Guāngdài, a bandit in Yúnjīyang, used the Yǒnglì reign title,
and gathered a crowd to rebel.
The Emperor ordered Vice Minister Kāchámù and others to suppress them.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Mǎ Guózhù was reassigned as Governor-General of Jiāngnán, Jiāngxī, and Hénán.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
an imperial edict stated:
"The Central Plains are settled,
and our influence extends far and wide.
However, Guǎngdōng is still obstructed by the Táng (Prince of Tang) faction,
and the people of the Lingnan region have been suffering for not just a day.
Therefore, an expeditionary force was dispatched to the south,
sweeping through Huìzhōu and Cháozhōu,
and reaching the provincial capital.
Considering that its officials and people
were not late in submitting,
all their crimes and offenses
are hereby pardoned and abolished.
Outstanding taxes and arbitrary levies
are all to be remitted.
For people aged seventy and above,
additional grain and silk are to be bestowed.
Chaste and filial individuals everywhere
are to be honored.
Talented and virtuous individuals in mountains and forests are to be recruited.
Nánhǎi (South Sea) states that are able to submit
shall be treated like Joseon."
On the day Bǐngyín,
Zhù Shìchāng was appointed Grand Coordinator of Shānxī.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the Emperor visited beyond the frontier to review military exercises.
On this day,
he stayed at Shāhé.
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Jīn Shēnghuán captured the former Míng imperial clansmen Prince Línbó and Prince Àibó at Lúxī Mountain,
and executed them.
On the day Jiǎxū,
he arrived at Xībā'ěrtái.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
he arrived at Hǎiliútǔhé Kǒu.
On the day Réngwǔ,
he arrived at Cháhànnuò'ěr.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Háogé sent Bèile Níkān and others, who successively captured Zūnyì, Kuízhōu, Màozhōu, Nèijiāng, Róngchāng, Fùshùn, and other counties,
and beheaded over a thousand of the former Míng princes and their associates.
Sìchuān was pacified.
On the day Bǐngxū,
he arrived at Húsūtái.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Zhāng Wénhéng was appointed Grand Coordinator of Gānsù.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
In the ninth month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
an earthquake occurred in Jīngshī (the capital).
On the day Xīnhài,
the Huái'ān bandits Zhāng Huáshān and others used the Lóngwǔ reign title,
and gathered at Miàowān.
On the day Dīngsì,
Lǐ Yóulóng was appointed Grand Coordinator of Tiānjīn.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the official army attacked the Miàowān bandits,
and defeated them.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Wáng Chǎng was appointed Grand Coordinator of Ānhuī.
On the day Rénshēn,
Zhuó'ěrbì of the Kālāqìn tribe and others led their divisions and surrendered.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Wú Wéihuá was appointed Governor-General of Huáiyáng,
and Xiàn Jìn was appointed Grand Coordinator of Piānyuán.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the triennial grand review of officials in the direct provinces was established.
On the day Rénchén,
pearl harvesting in Guǎngdōng, which afflicted the people,
was abolished.
In the eleventh month, on the day Gēngxū,
Chén Tài was appointed General Jìngnán,
to, along with Mèilè Zhāngjīng Dǒng'ālāi, suppress the remaining rebels in Fújiàn.
On the day Xīnhài,
the disaster taxes for the fourteen prefectures and counties including Dài and Jìnglè in Shānxī,
and the six fortresses including Nínghuà,
and the fifteen prefectures and counties including Dé and Lìchéng in Shāndōng were remitted.
The tooth tax and miscellaneous taxes of the Míng period in Shāndōng were abolished.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the Wǔfènglóu (Five Phoenix Tower) was completed.
On the day Guǐhài,
the ceremony to Heaven was held at the Yuánqiū (Altar of Heaven).
On the *wùchén* day of the twelfth month,
taxes on disaster-stricken areas in Bǎodìng, Héjiān, Zhēndìng, and Shùndé were remitted.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Chén Jǐn was appointed Governor-General of Mǐnzhè.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the eleventh daughter of Tàizōng, Gùlún Princess, was married off to Kālrmǎsuǒnàmù.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Taíjí Wúbāshí and others of the Sūnítè tribe came to submit.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the main army recovered Chángshā from Yuèzhōu.
The former Míng Governor-General Hé Téngjiāo and others had already fled.
Next, at Xiāngtán,
they defeated 130,000 troops of Guìwáng's general Huáng Cháoxuǎn at Yànziwō,
and again defeated them at Héngzhōu,
where they were executed.
Then, Bǎoqìng was captured,
and Lǔwáng Zhū Dǐngzhào and others were executed.
They advanced to attack Wǔgāng.
Guìwáng Yóuláng fled,
and was pursued to Jìngzhōu,
where the city was taken.
Yuánzhōu was then recovered.
Mínwáng Zhū Yān Jùn surrendered Lí píng.
Húnán was pacified.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the former Míng general Zhèng Cǎi attacked Fúzhōu.
Vice-general Zōu Bìkē and others defeated and routed him.
In this year,
the various tribes of Kēěrqìn, Kǎlāqìn, Wūzhūmùqín, Áohàn, Wēngniútè, Sūnítè, Zháluòtè, Guōěrluósī, Hāoqítè, and Ābàgāi came to pay tribute.

Cháoxiān, and from the Kǎěrkǎ tribe, Zhásàkètúhán, Mòěrgēnchuòěrjì, Éěrdéníchuòěrjì, Màidálǐhútúkètú, Éěrdénígùxī, Yīlāgúkèsānhútúkètú, Mahāsàmádìsàichénhán, Éwùbùěěrdéní, Sàilèhútúkètú, Mǎnjūxílǐhútúkètú,
and under Zhásàkètúhán, Éwùbùěěrdéní, Bāyánhùwèi, Shèjìnbāndì, Màidálǐhútúkètú,
under Nuòmén hán, Dānjīnhútúkètú,
under Tǔxiètúhán, Zébúzūndānbāhútúkètú,
under Shuòléihán, Yīhè'émùqígélóng, Énsāndélèhātánbātúlǔ,
from the Èlútè tribe, Táijí Wúbàxī, Gùshíhán,
under Luóbùzànghútúkètú, Bāhángélóng, Pénsūkèzhāmùsū,
under Ābùlàinuòyán, Nèménhán, Bātúlǔnuòyán, Dáyúnchuòěrjì, Èjír tú Táijí,
from the Sūnítè tribe, Táijí Wèizhèng,
from the Zháluòtè tribe, Táijí Sāngtú,
from the Èěrdūs tribe, Jìnóng,
from the Guīhuàchéng Tǔmòtè tribe, Zhāngjīng Tuōbókè, Nuòěrbù,
from the Tánggǔtè tribe, and Lābùzhámùchuòěrjì, Lāmābāndìdá, and others, all came to present tribute.
In the spring, the first month of the fifth year, on the *xīnhài* day,
the former Míng Yíchūn Wáng Zhū Yìyǎn occupied Tíngzhōu and caused a rebellion.
Commander-in-Chief Yú Yǒngshòu captured and executed him.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
disaster taxes for the three prefectures of Tàiyuán, Píngyáng, and Lù'ān,
and the three sub-prefectures of Zé, Qìn, and Liáo were remitted.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Héshuò Sùqīnwáng Háogé's army returned.
Yǎnxǐ Jùnwáng Luóluòhóng had died in the army;
his coffin returned at this time.
Court was suspended for two days.
In the second month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
Jīn Shēnghuán and Wáng Dé'rén rebelled at Nánchāng.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the official army of Jiāngnán recovered Wúwéi Zhōu.
The official army of Fújiàn recovered Liánchéng, Shùnchāng, Jiānglè, and other counties.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
disaster taxes for the previous year in Jǐnán, Yǎnzhōu, Qīngzhōu, and Láizhōu were remitted.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Gùlún Princess was married off to Bàlínbù Sàibùténg.
On the *rénchén* day,
Lǚ Féngchūn was appointed Governor of Shāndōng,
and Lǐ Jiàn was appointed Governor of Níngxià.
The former Míng Guìxī Wáng Zhū Chángbiāo and Huīwǔ Bó Xiàng Dēngwèi attacked Yuánzhōu.
Dàozhāngjīng Xiàn Guó'ān and others attacked and executed them.
In the third month, on the *jǐhài* day,
