Bèizi Tūnqí, Shàngshàn, and others impeached Héshuò Zhèngqīnwáng Jíěrhālāg.
The crime implicated Mǎngjiā, Bóbóěrdài, Áobài, Suǒní, and others.
Jíěrhālāg was demoted to Duōluó Jùnwáng,
and Mǎngjiā and others were demoted or dismissed with varying degrees.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Héshuò Sùqīnwáng Háogé was found guilty
and sentenced to death.
The Emperor could not bear to execute him,
and instead imprisoned him.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Tán Tài was ordered to be Commander-in-Chief for the Southern Expedition,
to jointly suppress Jīn Shēnghuán with Hé Luòhuì.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Gěng Dùn was appointed Governor-General of Xuāndà and Shānxī.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Wǔ Dàdìng attacked Níngqiāng.
Guardsman Zhāng Déjùn and others greatly defeated him.
In the fourth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
Yáng Xīngguó was appointed Governor of Shùntiān.
On the *wùchén* day,
disaster taxes for Wèiyuán, Jīnxiàn, and Lánzhōu Wèi were remitted.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the official army recovered Jiànníng,
and executed the former Míng Yúnxī Wáng Zhū Chánghú and others.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Kēěrqìn Dùěrbótè Zhènguógōng Sèlěng was enfeoffed as Bèizi.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Gùshān Érén Ālái and others were dispatched to garrison Hànzhōng.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the main army captured Chénzhōu,
then broke Yǒngníng,
and reached Quánzhōu.
The former Míng Superintendent of Military Affairs Hé Téngjiāo fled.
Guìxī Wáng Zhū Chángbiāo, Nánwēi Wáng Zhū Yínwèi, Chángshā Wáng Zhū Yóuzhì, and others were captured.
The various Miáo and Yáo tribes of Tóngrén, Xīng'ān, and Guānyáng surrendered.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Liú Zhīyuán and Tóng Túlái were appointed General of Pacifying the South,
to garrison Bǎoqìng.
Lǐ Guóhàn was appointed General of Pacifying the West,
to garrison Hànzhōng.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Wú Sānguì moved his garrison from Jǐnzhōu to Hànzhōng.
In the intercalary fourth month, on the *wùxū* day,
Jíěrhālāg's title was restored to Héshuò Zhèngqīnwáng.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Lǐ Guóyīng was appointed Governor of Sìchuān.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Chí Rìyì was appointed Governor of Húguǎng.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Bèizi Tūnqí was ordered to be Commander-in-Chief for Pacifying the West,
to jointly suppress the rebellious Huí in Shǎnxī with Hán Dài.
In the fifth month, on the *jǐchǒu* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *wùchén* day,
the official army defeated the rebellious Huí at Gǒngchāng,
and recovered Líntáo and Lánzhōu.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Guardsman Zhāng Yǒng defeated the rebellious Huí at Mǎjiāpíng.
The former Míng Yáncháng Wáng Zhū Shíyàn was captured
and executed.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Zhào Fúxīng was appointed Governor of Fèngyáng.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Zhū Yánqìng was appointed Governor of Jiāngxī.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the official army defeated Jīn Shēnghuán,
and recovered Jiǔjiāng and Ráozhōu.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Liú Hóngyù was appointed Governor of Ānhuī.
In the sixth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day, the first day of the month,
disaster taxes for the previous year in Xī'ān, Yán'ān, Píngliáng, Líntáo, Qìngyáng, and Hànzhōng were remitted.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Zhōu Wényè was appointed Governor of Gānsù.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Ésài and others greatly defeated the rebellious Huí at Lánzhōu,
and all the remaining remnants were pacified.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
there was a loud earthquake in the capital.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Imperial Ancestral Temple was completed.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
for the first time, Han Grand Secretaries for the Six Ministries and Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate were established.
Chén Míngxià, Xiè Qǐguāng, Lǐ Ruòlín, Liú Yúyòu, Dǎng Chóngyǎ, and Jīn Zhījùn were appointed Grand Secretaries of the Six Ministries.
Xú Qǐyuán was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
In the eighth month, on the *guǐsì* day, the first day of the month,
Jīn Shēnghuán and Wáng Dé'rén attacked Gànzhōu.
The official army defeated and repelled them.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Chén Tài, Lǐ Shuàitài, and others defeated Zhèng Cǎi at Chánglè,
and again defeated him at Liánjiāng,
recovering Xīnghuà.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Héshuò Yīngqīnwáng Ājígé, Duōluó Chéngzé Jùnwáng Shuòsāi, and others were ordered to suppress the local bandits in Tiānjīn.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
private horse rearing and storage of military equipment were prohibited.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Wáng Yīpǐn was appointed Governor of Fèngyáng.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Manchu and Han officials and commoners were permitted to intermarry.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Xià Yù was appointed Governor of Tiānjīn,
and Zhāng Xuéshèng was appointed Governor of Fújiàn.
In the ninth month, on the *rénxū* day, the first day of the month,
the official army captured the former Míng Governor Wú Jiāng and others at Nánkāng Húkǒu
and executed them.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Héshuò Yīngqīnwáng Ājígé suppressed the local bandits in Cáoxiàn
and pacified the area.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Bèilè Lèkèdéhún was enfeoffed as Duōluó Shùnchéng Jùnwáng,
and Bóluò was enfeoffed as Duōluó Duānzhòng Jùnwáng.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Héshuò Zhèngqīnwáng Jíěrhālāg was appointed General of Pacifying the Distant,
to suppress the Húguǎng bandit Lǐ Jǐn.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Bèilè Níkān was enfeoffed as Duōluó Jìngjǐn Jùnwáng.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *rénchén* day,
Héshuò Lǐqīnwáng Dàishàn passed away.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Tóng Túlái recovered Bǎoqìng.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the surrendered general Liú Zéqīng allied with the Cáoxiàn bandits and rebelled.
Zéqīng and his associates Lǐ Hóngjī and others were all executed.
In the eleventh month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Lǐ Chéngdòng, the rebellious general from Guǎngdōng, occupied Nánxióng.
He allied with the Dòngmàn and attacked Gànzhōu.
The Governor Liú Wǔyuán and others defeated and repelled him.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Commander-in-Chief Rèn Zhēn attacked Hè Zhēn
and defeated him.
On the *wùchén* day,
sacrifices to Heaven were offered at the Altar of Heaven,
with Tàizǔ Wǔhuángdì as co-sacrificed.
Four generations above Tàizǔ were posthumously honored: High Ancestor Zéwáng as Zhàozǔ Yuánhuángdì;
Great-Grandfather Qìngwáng as Xīngzǔ Zhíhuángdì;
Grandfather Chāngwáng as Jǐngzǔ Yìhuángdì;
and Father Fúwáng as Xiǎnzǔ Xuānhuángdì.
All their consorts were honored as Empresses.
The Emperor proceeded to the Grand Ancestral Temple to present the imperial seals and tablets.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
with the rites of co-sacrificing to Heaven and conferring imperial titles concluded,
the Emperor presided over a court assembly to receive congratulations
and issued a grand amnesty.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Heshuò Yīngqīnwáng Ājìgé, Duōluó Duānzhòngjùnwáng Bóluò, Duōluó Chéngzéjùnwáng Shuòsài and others led their armies and were stationed in Dàtóng
to guard against the Khalkha.
In the twelfth month, on the first day, *xīnmǎo*,
Prince Wǎkèdá
and Beizi Shàngshàn, Tūnqí and others were ordered to proceed to Ājìgé’s army.
Half of the Eight Banners' nomadic Mongol officers and soldiers were mobilized
to garrison Ā’ěrqítǔ Sūmén Hādá.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Jiāng Xiāng rebelled in Dàtóng.
Governor Gěng Tūn fled to Yánghé.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
disaster taxes were remitted for Píngshān, Lóngpíng, and Qīngfēng.
On the *wùxū* day,
Ājìgé besieged Dàtóng.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Měilèzhāngjīng Ālāshàn and Shìláng Gádáhún were again dispatched to Ājìgé’s army.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
disaster taxes were remitted for Dàtóng.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Yáng Jié and others recaptured Dūchāng,
captured the former Míng Minister of War Yú Yìngguì,
and executed him.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Tóng Yǎnglàng was appointed Governor of Xuāndà.
This year,
the Sūnítè, Zhālǔtè and other tribes came to court.
From Cháoxiǎn,
the Khalkha tribes’ Émùbù’é’ěrdéní, Dàiqīng Nèménhàn Lāma, Sāi’ěrjì’é’ěrdéní Wèizhèng, Shuòléihàn, Màidálǐ Hútúkètú, Zāsàkètúhàn’s subordinate É’ěrdéní Hātán Bātúlǔ;
from the Oirat tribes, Gùshíhàn, Xīlètú Chuò’ěrjì, Nuòmén Hàn;
from the Suǒlún tribe, Ājìbù;
from the È’ěrduōsī tribe, Shāndá;
from the Sūnítè tribe, Téngjītè;
Kē’ěrqìn Beile Zhāng Jìlún;
from Guīhuàchéng, Gùlún Dìwǎ Hútúkètú, Dānjīn Lāmā’é’ěrdéní Zhàisāng;
from the Tǔmòtè tribe, Gǔlùgé;
from Wūsīzàng, the Chanhuà King Wáng Shūkè;
and Tānggǔtè Dálài Lāmā all came to pay tribute.
Cháoxiǎn, the Oirat Gùshíhàn, and Tānggǔtè Dálài Lāmā came again.
In the sixth year, spring, first month, on the *rénxū* day,
the imperial forces recaptured Luóyuán, Yǒngchūn, Déhuà and other counties.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Duōluó Jìngjǐnjùnwáng Níkān and others were ordered to conquer Tàiyuán.
On the *wùchén* day,
an edict stated:
“I desire for all officials and people under Heaven to enjoy peace and prosperity,
and I strive day and night
without daring to be negligent.
In previous years, the roaming bandits caused rebellion,
and the suffering reached its extreme.
Upon entering the pass to suppress the rebels,
officials and commoners pledged their loyalty.
However, in recent years, unruly individuals
have spread false rumors of 'cleansing the people.'
Ignorant commoners easily believed them,
fled in panic,
and rebels often appeared.
I have heard that one who does not delight in killing
can unite the world.
The *Shū* says: 'Whom do the multitude uphold if not the sovereign?
And without the multitude, how can the sovereign guard the state?'
A ruler destroying his people is
a principle utterly denied.
From the first year,
it is now six years;
how could there be anyone who massacres the people without cause?
If the people ponder this,
their doubts will surely vanish like melting ice.
As for those who willingly become bandits,
and are happy to meet their deaths,
there must be some coercion that led them to this.
Is it that the Governors, Lieutenant-Governors, Commanders, and Judicial Commissioners are not the right people,
or that local officials extort and oppress, making it difficult for the people to survive?
Or is it that the promised tax exemptions
are merely nominal, without real effect?
All officials, both internal and external, should earnestly deliberate on policies to promote benefits and eliminate harm,
and I will consider and implement them in due course.”
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Jiāng Xiāng’s faction, led by Yáo Jǔ and others, killed the Jìníng Dao Commissioner Wáng Chānglíng,
and captured Xīnzhōu.
Gùshān Èzhēn Ālái defeated and repelled them.
On the *yǐhài* day,
an edict stated:
“Establishing customs barriers and collecting taxes
was originally to detect cunning and treacherous individuals,
not to quibble over every penny with merchants.
Let all collect taxes according to the original quotas;
do not impose arbitrary levies to fill private coffers.
Violators shall be punished.”
An edict was issued to the soldiers and civilians of Dàtóng, Shānxī,
warning them not to be coerced or enticed by Jiāng Xiāng,
and promising clemency and exemption to all who surrendered.
On the *wùyín* day,
the system of recommendation and collective responsibility was implemented.
On the *gēngchén* day,
an edict stated that if censorate officials’ discussions of affairs were not factual,
court officials should collectively deliberate,
and not readily refer cases to the Ministry of Justice.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Jīn Tíngxiàn was appointed Governor of PiānYuán.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Tán Tàì and Hélàohuì recaptured Nánchāng;
Jīn Shēnghuán drowned himself,
Wáng DéRén was executed,
and Jiǔjiāng, Nánkāng, Ruìzhōu, Línjiāng, and Yuánzhōu were all pacified.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the Shānxī rebel faction led by Liú Qiān invaded Dàizhōu.
Ājìluò dispatched troops to defeat and repel them.
In the second month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Regent Prince Duō’ěrgǔn campaigned against Dàtóng.
Arrears of land tax from before the sixth year in Zhílì province and salt taxes for merchants and people in Sìchuān were remitted.
On the *xīnhài* day,
former Míng imperial clan member Zhū Sēnfǔ and others attacked Jiēzhōu.
Wú Sānguì attacked and executed them.
In the third month, on the *guǐhài* day,
Duō’ěrgǔn captured Húnyuánzhōu.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Han-Qiāng Commander-in-Chief Zhāng Tiānfú pacified the bandit leader Tán Yīhán,
and captured and executed the former Míng Shānyīn Prince and others.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the local bandit Wáng Yǒngqiáng captured nineteen prefectures and counties including Yán’ān and Yúlín.
The Governor of Yánsuī, Wáng Zhèngzhì, and others died.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Yìngzhōu and Shānyīn surrendered.
Duō’ěrgǔn returned with his army,
leaving Ājìgé in Dàtóng.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Duōluó Chéngzéjùnwáng Shuòsài, Duōluó Duānzhòngjùnwáng Bóluò, and Duōluó Jìngjǐnjùnwáng Níkān were promoted to Qīnwáng (Prince of the First Rank).
Wáng Yǒngqiáng captured Tóngguān.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the Prefect of Guǎngxìn Prefecture, Yáng Guózhēn, and others recaptured Yùshān County.
Imperial forces in Níngxià captured Línhé and other forts.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the rebel Húi Muslims Mǐ Làyìn and Dīng Guódòng in Gān and Liáng rebelled again.
The Governor of Gānsù, Zhāng Wénhéng, and others died.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Prince Regent Heshuò Déyùqīnwáng Duōduó died.
The Regent Prince Duō’ěrgǔn, whose army was at Jūyōng,
returned to the capital for the mourning.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the law on concealing escaped persons was leniently adjusted.
Tán Tàì and Hélàohuì greatly defeated the rebels in Nánkāng,
then captured Xìnfēng.
The rebel general Lǐ Chéngdòng fled and died.
Fúzhōu and Jiànchāng were recaptured.
Jiāngxī was pacified.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Bóluò dispatched Áobài and others to utterly defeat Jiāng Xiāng north of Dàtóng.
Wú Sānguì defeated Wáng Yǒngqiáng,
and recaptured Yíjūn and Tóngguān.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Gēngyín,
Luó Shuò and Guà Lǎ were dispatched to garrison Tàiyuán.
On the day Guǐsì,
Àjígé recovered Zuǒwèi.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Bèizǐ Wú Dáhǎi and others were ordered to lead an expedition to Dàtóng.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Wú Sānguì captured Púxiàn.
On the day Guǐmáo,
the official army of Fújiàn recovered Pínghé, Zhào'ān, Zhāngpíng, and Níngyáng.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Liú Zǐzhuàng and others were granted the title of Jìnshì and related ranks, with distinctions.
On the day Yǐsì,
the Empress Dowager passed away.
On the day Rénzǐ,
an edict stated:
"Since the start of the war,
lands have been desolate, and people have fled,
wandering without refuge.
Let the local authorities widely invite and encourage them to return,
granting them wasteland
for permanent livelihood.
After six years,
taxes will then be discussed.

The performance of each prefecture and county in attracting settlers and promoting cultivation, and that of circuits and prefectures in overseeing and urging, will determine their ratings of excellent or poor.
At the end of the year,
the provincial governors and censors will evaluate and report."
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Dǒng Zōngshèng was appointed Governor of Yánsuī.
The official army captured Fúníng,
and Fújiàn was pacified.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the rebel faction captured Fénzhōu,
and Heshuò Duānzhòng Qīnwáng Bóluò was appointed Grand General Dìngxī,
leading the army to suppress them.
Heshuò Jìngjǐn Qīnwáng Níkān moved his army to Dàtóng.
On the day Dīngsì,
Bèizǐ Mǎndáhǎi was enfeoffed as Heshuò Qīnwáng.
In the fifth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Tú Lài was dispatched to lead troops to the Tàiyuán army.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Lǐ Qīfèng was appointed Governor of Guǎngdōng,
and Guō Zhàojī was appointed Governor of Guǎngxī.
Taxes for disaster-stricken areas in the three prefectures of Tàiyuán, Píngyáng, and Fénzhōu,
and the two departments of Liáo and Zé, were exempted.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Kǒng Yǒudé was re-enfeoffed as Dìngnán Wáng,
Gěng Zhòngmíng as Jìngnán Wáng,
and Shàng Kěxǐ as Píngnán Wáng.
Kǒng Yǒudé was ordered to campaign in Guǎngxī,
Gěng Zhòngmíng and Shàng Kěxǐ in Guǎngdōng,
each taking their families to garrison there.
Ten Tóngzhī positions in Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Shāndōng, Zhèjiāng, and Shǎnxī were abolished,
and twenty-one Tōngpàn positions in Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Hénán, Húguǎng, Jiāngxī, and Zhèjiāng were abolished.
Disaster taxes for five years in Bǎochí and Shùnyì were exempted.
On the day Xīnsì,
Wú Sānguì and Lǐ Guóhàn recovered Yán'ān.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the border commanderies of Sìchuān were pacified.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Heshuò Duānzhòng Qīnwáng Bóluò recovered Qīngyuán, Jiāochéng, Wénshuǐ, Xúgōu, and Qí counties.
In the sixth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
King Lǐ Zōng of the kingdom of Cháoxiǎn passed away.
On the day Rénzǐ,
wasteland taxes from six years prior in Cāngzhōu and Qīngyuàn were exempted.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Zhāng Yìngjīng was enfeoffed as Zhèngyī Sìjiào Dàzhēnrén.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
arrears of taxes for the fourth and fifth years in Jiāngxī were exempted.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day Wùwǔ,
the Regent Duō'ěrgǔn resumed the campaign against Dàtóng.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Mǎndáhǎi and Wǎkèdá campaigned in Shuòzhōu and Níngwǔ.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
disaster taxes in Kāifēng and other prefectures were exempted.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Duō'ěrgǔn arrived at Ālǔxíbā'ěrdái,
hunted, and returned.
Dàozhāngjīng Suǒhóng and others were dispatched to reinforce Mǎndáhǎi's army.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the official army pacified over three hundred rebel strongholds in Huángzhōu,
beheading the former Míng prince Zhū Yùnpō and others.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
remaining rebels in Guǎngdōng raided Nángàn,
and the official army attacked and repelled them.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Wú Sānguì and Lǐ Guóhàn recovered the town of Yánsuīzhèn.
In the eighth month, on the day Guǐsì,
the Regent Duō'ěrgǔn returned to the capital.
Rebel factions in Shānxī captured Púzhōu, as well as Línjìn and Héjīn,
but Mèng Qiáofāng suppressed them.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
disaster taxes in Zhēndìng, Shùndé, Guǎngpíng, and Dàmíng were exempted.
Mǎndáhǎi recovered Shuòzhōu and Mǎyì.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Duānzhòng Qīnwáng Bóluò captured Xiàoyì.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Zhèng Qīnwáng Jí'ěrhāláng and others captured Xiāngtán,
capturing Hé Téngjiāo,
who refused to submit
and was executed.
Chénzhōu, Bǎoqìng, Jìngzhōu, and Héngzhōu were all pacified.
They advanced to capture Quánzhōu.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Crown Prince Lǐ Hào of Cháoxiǎn was enfeoffed as King of Cháoxiǎn.
On the day Xīnhài,
Zhāng Xiàorén was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì, Shāndōng, and Hénán.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Yīng Qīnwáng Àjígé, Bèizǐ Gǒng'ādài and others were dispatched to campaign against Dàtóng.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Mèilèzhāngjīng Gēntè and others captured Yīshì.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the Dàtóng rebels, having been long besieged,
starved almost to death.
The bogus commander Yáng Zhènwēi beheaded Jiāng Xiāng and his brother Lín and presented them.
On the day Bǐngchén,
the bogus commander Liú Wěi and others of Níngwǔguān led their followers to surrender,
and the mountain strongholds of Jìnglè and Nínghuà were all pacified.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùwǔ,
Èmùbù was enfeoffed as Duōluó Dá'ěrhàn Zhuólǐkètú Jùnwáng,
and Gá'ěrmá of the Sūnítè tribe as Duōluó Bèilè.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Élínchén, Bùdádài, Gùlù, Àjígézāmsū and others of the È'ěrdōsī tribe surrendered.
Élínchén was enfeoffed as Duōluó Jùnwáng,
Bùdádài's son Yīlǐnchén and Gùlù's son Sèlěng as Gùshān Bèizǐ,
and Àjígézāmsū as Zhènguógōng.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Xià Yù was appointed Governor of Shāndōng.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Gùlún Éfù Qítātè was enfeoffed as Duōluó Jùnwáng.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Mǎndáhǎi and Bóluò captured Fénzhōu and Píngyáng.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Duōní was enfeoffed as Heshuò Qīnwáng,
and Jiéshū as Duōluó Jùnwáng.
On the day Rénchén,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Láoqīn was enfeoffed as Qīnwáng.
The official army recovered Yùnchéng.
On the day Wùxū,
the surrendered general Yáng Dēngzhōu rebelled
and captured Shānyīn.
On the day Jǐhài,
disaster taxes for five years in eighteen prefectures and counties including Dōngpíng and Chángshān in Shāndōng were exempted,
as were the Liáoxiǎng (Liaodong levies) from the late Míng period for six years prior in Jiāngxī.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the Regent Duō'ěrgǔn campaigned against the two Chǔhú'ěr of the Kā'ěrkā tribe.
On the day Yǐsì,
the Shǎnxī Commander-in-Chief Rèn Zhēn attacked the former Míng general Táng Zhònghēng at Túyóubà,
beheaded him,
and also executed the former Míng princes Zhū Chángyīng and Zhū Yóugàng.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the official army recovered Lù'ān.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the official army captured Yúlín.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Mǎndáhǎi and others captured the two departments of Qìn and Liáo.
On the day Gēngxū,
Mǎndáhǎi was ordered to return to the capital,
while Wǎkèdá and others remained to pacify Shānxī.
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngyín,
corvée and taxes in Kāi, Yuánchéng and other counties in Zhílì were exempted,
as were disaster taxes in Mínzhōu, Shǎnxī.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Duō'ěrgǔn returned his army from Kātūnbùlākè.
Disaster taxes in Xuānfǔ were exempted.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Gěng Zhòngmíng's army reached Jí'ān,
where he committed suicide fearing punishment.
In the twelfth month, on the first day Yǐyǒu,
Xìng, Ruìchéng, and Pínglù counties in Shānxī were pacified.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Jiāo Lián, a general of the former Míng Prince Guì, raided Quánzhōu,
but Lèkèdéhún and others defeated him,
advancing to capture Dàozhōu.
Nǔshān and others captured Wūsà city.
Yí'ěrdūqí and others captured Lípíng.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
the official army recovered Línshuǐ and Dàzhú counties.
On the day Gēngxū,
the local bandits in Níngbō, Shàoxīng, and Táizhōu were pacified.
This year,
Cháoxiǎn, and the various tribes of Ābāgāi, Wūzhūmùqín, Tǔmètè;
Ābālāinuòyán of the Èlútè tribe, Jīkèshíhǔ Bātúlǔ Táijí, and Dálài Wūbāshíwēnbù Tábùnáng, son of Gùshí Hán;
Jùnwáng Élínchén of the È'ěrdōsī tribe;
Tǔxiètú Hán, Shuòléi Hán, Dàiqīng Nuòyán of the Kā'ěrkā tribe;
Gǔlùgé and others of the Guīhuàchéng Tǔmètè tribe;
Dàiqīng Wēnbù Dá'ěrhàn Nángsū and Dálài Lǎmā, subjects of Yīlāgǔkèsān Hútúkètú, all came to pay tribute.
Cháoxiǎn and Kā'ěrkā Tǔxiètú Hán came again.
In the seventh year, spring, the first month, on the day *gēngshēn*,
the imperial army recovered Yǒngníng and Níngxiāng.
On the day *rénxū*,
the imperial army recovered Nánxióng.
On the day *guǐyǒu*,
Dāndá of the È'ěrdūosī tribe was enfeoffed as Bèilè,
and Shākèchá as Bèizi.
On the day *jiǎxū*,
the former Míng princes Zhū Cíyè, Prince Déhuà, and Zhū Yì (missing character), Prince Shíchéng, were trapped in Dàtián,
and the imperial army suppressed them.
On the day *dīngchǒu*,
Héshuò Zhèng Qīnwáng Jí'ěrhāláng's army returned.
In the second month, on the day *dīnghài*,
the empress dowager was posthumously honored with the canonized name Xiàoduān Zhèngjìng Rényì Zhuāngmǐn Fǔtiān Xiéshèng Wén Huánghòu.
On the day *jiǎwǔ*,
Liú Hóngyù was appointed Governor of Shānxī,
and Wáng Yīpǐn as Governor of Guǎngxī.
Lǐ Jiàntài occupied Tàipíng and rebelled;
the imperial army besieged him,
and he surrendered
and was executed.
The territories of Píngyáng, Lù'ān, and Zézhōu were all pacified.
In the third month, on the day *jǐwèi*,
the sun was crimson like blood.
Summer, fourth month, on the day *jiǎwǔ*,
Kǒng Yǒudé captured the former Míng generals Huáng Shùn and Lín Guóruì in Xīngníng,
and five tens of thousands of their troops surrendered.
On the day *bǐngshēn*,
Zhāng Jìlún, Bèilè of Kē'ěrqìn, was enfeoffed as Jùnwáng.
On the day *jiǎchén*,
Duōluó Qiān Jùnwáng Wǎkèdá's army returned.
Sixth month, on the day *yǐyǒu*,
the commoners of Bǎodé Zhōu, Cuī Yào and others, captured the former Míng general Niú Huàlín,
beheaded him,
and surrendered the city.
On the day *guǐmǎo*,
the imperial army recovered Níngdū and Shíchéng.
Autumn, seventh month, on the first day *rénzǐ*,
offerings were made at the Tàimiào.
On the day *yǐmǎo*,
the Regent Duō'ěrgǔn proposed building a border city for summer retreat,
and an additional levy of over 2.5 million taels of money and grain was imposed on nine provinces: Zhílì, Shānxī, Zhèjiāng, Shāndōng, Jiāngnán, Hénán, Húguǎng, Jiāngxī, and Shǎnxī.
On the day *xīnyǒu*,
the Emperor visited the residence of the Regent Duō'ěrgǔn.
Duō'ěrgǔn punished Bèizi Xíhàn and others for unauthorizedly requesting the imperial visit;
their offenses were investigated.
Bèizi Xíhàn was demoted to Zhèngguógōng,
and Lěngsēngjī, Áobài, and others were demoted and punished accordingly.
On the day *rénxū*,
Mǎ Zhīxiān was appointed Governor of Shǎnxī.
On the day *xīnwèi*,
the disaster tax for five years was remitted for the various fortresses and strongholds in Xīníng.
Eighth month, on the day *dīnghài*,
Héshuò Duānzhòng Qīnwáng Bóluò and Héshuò Jìngjǐn Qīnwáng Níkān were demoted to Duōluó Jùnwáng.
On the day *jǐchǒu*,
Sāibǔténg of the Bālín tribe and Bólúotè of the Hāoqítè tribe were enfeoffed as Duōluó Jùnwáng;
Gùmù of the Kē'ěrqìn kingdom and Gǔlùsī Xǐbù of the Kālāqìn tribe were enfeoffed as Duōluó Bèilè;
Chéngzé Qīnwáng Shuòsāi and Qīnwáng Láoqīn were changed to Duōluó Jùnwáng.
Ninth month, on the day *jiǎyín*,
the former Míng general Zhèng Chénggōng raided Cháozhōu,
and the General Officer Wáng Bāngjùn repelled him.
On the day *bǐngzǐ*,
the famine tax for the fifth and sixth years was remitted for seven prefectures and counties, including Qí and Máchéng.
Winter, tenth month, on the first day *xīnsì*,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day *jǐhài*,
the regulations for tea and horses in Shǎnxī were established.
On the day *gēngzǐ*,
the imperial army captured Shàowǔ,
seized the former Míng Grand Secretary Jiē Zhòngxī and others,
and beheaded them.
On the day *jǐyǒu*,
the famine tax for six counties including Tóngchéng was remitted.
Eleventh month, on the day *jiǎyín*,
the disaster tax for the previous year in Gānsù was remitted.
On the day *yǐmǎo*,
Wú Sānguì recovered Fǔgǔ,
beheaded the former Míng strategist Gāo Yǒucái and others,
and the remaining troops surrendered.
On the day *rénxū*,
the Regent Duō'ěrgǔn fell ill
while hunting outside the border.
On the day *yǐchǒu*,
Shàng Kěxǐ recovered Guǎngzhōu,
and the remaining troops surrendered.
On the day *wùyín*,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Yuánqiū.
Twelfth month, on the day *wùzǐ*,
the Regent Héshuò Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrgǔn passed away in Kālā Chéng.
On the day *rénchén*,
upon receiving the news,
the Emperor was deeply grieved,
and officials and commoners wore mourning attire.
On the day *bǐngshēn*,
when the funeral cortege arrived,
the Emperor personally offered sacrifices in the suburbs.
On the day *jǐhài*,
an edict stated:
"When Tàizōng Wén Huángdì passed away,
the princes and high officials urged the Regent to take the throne.
The King indeed humbly declined
and supported Our enthronement,
pacifying the Central Plains.
His supreme virtue and great accomplishments
are unparalleled through the ages.
Sadly, he has passed away,
and Our heart is deeply pained.
The mourning ceremonies, both inside and outside the court,
shall be conducted according to imperial rites."
On the day *gēngzǐ*,
the former Regent's seal of authority was collected
and stored in the imperial treasury.
On the day *jiǎchén*,
the former Regent was posthumously honored as Màodé Xiūdào Guǎngyè Dìnggōng Ānmín Lìzhèng Chéngjìng Yì Huángdì,
with the temple name Chéngzōng.
On the day *yǐsì*,
an edict stated:
"All state affairs
must be reported to Us.
As We are still young
and lack discernment regarding the worthy and the unworthy,
and there are vacancies for Shangshū,
let suitable and able individuals be jointly recommended for advancement.
As for minor affairs,
let the three administering princes manage them."
In this year,
Bāláng Hélúoqí, Dá'ěrhàn Nángsù, Péncuò Jiāncòu, and others from the Ká'ěrkā, Èlǔtè, and Wūsīzàng tribes came to court.
Cháoxiān,
Shuòléi Hàn, Zhásàkètú Hàn, Tǔxiètú Hàn, Chuòkètú Wèizhèng Nuòyán, Dàiqīng Nuòyán, Nàmùqí Wèizhèng Nuòyán, Cháhā'ěr Mò'ěrgēntáijí, Suǒnàmù from the Ká'ěrkā tribe;
Bātúlǔ Bèilè, Táijí Éqí'ěrtú, Gānbù Hútúkètú, Gāmùbù Hútúkètú, Shūhǔ'ěr Dàiqīng from the Èlǔtè tribe;
Chǎnhuà Wáng from the Wūsīzàng tribe;
the Suǒlún and Shǐlù tribes;
and Gǔlùgé from the Guīhuà Chéng Tǔmòtè tribe all came to pay tribute.
Cháoxiān came again.
Basic Annals V, Ancestral Annals II
In the eighth year, spring, first month, on the first day *jǐyǒu*,
Táijí Gá'ěrmǎsāwàng and Chǔhù'ěr of the Hāoqítè tribe led their followers to submit.
On the day *xīnhài*,
Bùdān was appointed Deliberative Minister.
On the day *jiǎyín*,
Héshuò Yīng Qīnwáng Ājígé plotted rebellion
and was imprisoned.
His associate, Jùnwáng Láoqīn, was demoted to Bèizi,
and Xítèkù and others were sentenced to death.
On the day *yǐmǎo*,
Sūkèsāhā and Zhāndài were appointed Deliberative Ministers.
On the day *bǐngchén*,
the annual tribute of oranges from Hànzhōng and tangerines from Jiāngnán, and pomegranates from Hénán was abolished.
On the day *wùwǔ*,
the officials supervising weaving and advancement in various places, and the annual tribute of felt, leather, and fur from Shǎnxī were abolished.
Duō'ěrbó, son of Héshuò Ruì Qīnwáng Duō'ěrgǔn, was ordered to inherit the title.
On the day *jǐwèi*,
the annual production of city bricks in Línqīng was abolished.
On the day *gēngshēn*,
the Emperor assumed personal rule,
held court to receive congratulations,
and granted a general amnesty.
An edict stated:
"We personally undertake major state affairs,
managing all the myriad duties.
Heaven and Earth, and the Ancestors, have entrusted Us with a heavy responsibility.
The people within the seas
eagerly hope for good governance.
We, considering Our meager virtue,
are reverent and fearful day and night.
The realm is vast,
and state affairs are numerous and complex,
not something We can manage alone.
Therefore, all Our princes, bèilè, and civil and military officials,
each must exert their loyalty and fulfill their duties,
maintain personal integrity and love the people,
report all advantages and disadvantages,
and ensure that Our intentions are understood by all below.
The common people should also understand Our heart,
focus on their fundamental occupations and enjoy their work,
and share in the blessings of peace and tranquility."
Kǒng Yǒudé captured Guìlín,
beheaded the former Míng Prince Jìngjiāng and 473 civil and military officials,
and all remaining partisans surrendered.
On the day *rénxū*,
the annual tribute of dragon bowls from Jiāngxī was abolished.
On the day *bǐngyín*,
Xià Yī'è was appointed Governor of Jiāngxī.
On the day *dīngmǎo*,
Empress Xiàoduān Wén Huánghòu was enshrined in the Tàimiào.
The former Regent Duō'ěrgǔn was posthumously honored as Chéngzōng Yì Huángdì
and enshrined in the Tàimiào.
The three Inner Courts were moved to the Forbidden City.
On the day *jǐsì*,
Yītú was appointed Deliberative Minister.
The tax on sesame and cotton in Ānzhōu was remitted.
On the day *dīngchǒu*,
Duānzhòng Jùnwáng Bóluò and Jìngjǐn Jùnwáng Níkān were re-enfeoffed as Héshuò Qīnwáng.
Gǒng'ādài and Áobài were appointed Deliberative Ministers.
On the day *wùyín*,
Bātúlǔ Zhān and Dù'ěrmǎ were appointed Deliberative Ministers.
On the Gēngchén day of the second month,
Mǎndáhǎi was promoted and enfeoffed as Hèshuò Xùn Qīnwáng;
Duōní as Hèshuò Xìn Qīnwáng;
Luókěduó as Duōluó Píng Jùnwáng;
Wǎkèdá as Duōluó Qiān Jùnwáng;
Jiéshū as Duōluó Kāng Jùnwáng.
The currency system was reformed;
every hundred cash were equivalent to one qián of silver.
On the Xīnsì day,
drought taxes were remitted for Shuòzhōu, Húnyuán, and Dàtóng.
On the Guǐwèi day,
Luóshí and Bó'ěrhuì were found guilty
and sentenced to death.
The Emperor wished to pardon their death sentence,
but his officials insisted that it was not permissible,
so they were executed.
On the Wùzǐ day,
the Emperor issued an edict on the honorary title of Zhāoshèng Císhòu Huáng Tàihòu.
On the Jǐchǒu day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
Calamity taxes for the sixth and seventh years were remitted for Wénshàng and five other counties.
On the Xīnmǎo day,
the corvée labor for building fortifications beyond the frontier was abolished.
The additional levies of money and grain were allowed to offset eight years of regular tax.
Officials who made donations were to be given appropriate consideration and exemption.
On the Guǐsì day,
Sūkèsàhā, Zhāndài, and Mùjìlún reported that the treasonous acts of the late Regent Prince Duō'ěrgǔn were all true.
His estate was confiscated,
and his partisans Héluòhuì and Húxī were executed.
On the Jiǎwǔ day,
drought taxes were remitted for Shānxī.
On the Wùxū day,
Bèilè Yuèlè was enfeoffed as Duōluó Ān Jùnwáng.
On the Jǐhài day,
Duō'ěrgǔn's crimes were exposed to both the court and the public.
His honorary title and the posthumous enfeoffments of his mother and wife were revoked,
and his temple offerings were withdrawn.
On the Gēngzǐ day,
Chén TàI was transferred to be Shàngshū of the Ministry of Personnel,
and Hán Dài was appointed Shàngshū of the Ministry of Punishments.
On the Xīnchǒu day,
the Emperor visited the Southern苑 (Nányuàn).
On the Rénwǔ day,
Kǒng Yǒudé was ordered to relocate and garrison Guìlín.
On the Guǐmǎo day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the Yǐsì day,
Fùshòu, son of Hèshuò Sù Qīnwáng Háogé, was enfeoffed as Hèshuò Xiǎn Qīnwáng.
On the Wùshēn day, the first day of the intercalary second month,
Niú Wàncái, a remaining rebel leader in Húnán, surrendered with his subordinates.
On the Gēngxū day,
Jìdù, son of Hèshuò Zhèng Qīnwáng Jí'ěrhālā, was enfeoffed as Duōluó Jiǎn Jùnwáng;
Lèdù as Duōluó Mǐn Jùnwáng.
On the Jiǎyín day,
an edict stated:
"The discipline of the state
first and foremost values honest officials.
Recently, officials have become accustomed to corruption,
causing the common people to suffer,
which greatly displeases Us.
Governors-General and Provincial Governors
bear great responsibility,
and it entirely depends on their accurate recommendations and impeachments
to make officials aware of encouragement and punishment.
Currently, many recommendations are unfounded,
and many impeachments are for minor officials,
while great corruption and evil are condoned.
How can this improve governance?
The Ministry of Personnel should thoroughly investigate and report."
Dǎng Chóngyǎ was transferred to be Shàngshū of the Ministry of Revenue,
Jīn Zhījùn as Shàngshū of the Ministry of War,
Liú Yúyòu as Shàngshū of the Ministry of Punishments,
and Xiè Qǐguāng as Shàngshū of the Ministry of Works.
Calamity taxes for the seventh year were remitted for Xiángfú and six other counties.
On the Yǐmǎo day,
Shuòsāi was promoted and enfeoffed as Hèshuò Chéngzé Qīnwáng.
An edict stated:
"The establishment of customs barriers
is for the state to facilitate commerce,
not to cause hardship.
Customs officials who harass the people and act selfishly
are no different from robbers.
We are clearly aware of the suffering of merchants and commoners.
Henceforth, one official shall be appointed for each customs barrier;
all superfluous and excessive positions shall be eliminated,
and no one shall presumptuously claim diligent service
for further appointments."
On the Bǐngchén day,
an edict instructed Governors-General and Provincial Governors to identify officials of superior talent and virtue, who were also proficient in literature, and promote them;
those who were illiterate, committed misdeeds, or engaged in corrupt practices were to be dismissed.
Officials appointed by the Ministry of Personnel who failed a literary examination were to be removed from their names.
On the Jǐwèi day,
Commander-in-Chief Xǔ Ěrxiǎn captured Zhàoqìng and Luódìng;
Xú Chénggōng captured Gāozhōu.
Lamas were prohibited from presenting Buddha statues, bronze stupas, and Tibetan dogs as tribute.
On the Rénxū day,
Ājìgé was imprisoned in a separate chamber;
his estate was confiscated;
Bèizǐ Láoqīn was stripped of his princely title and reduced to a commoner.
On the Yǐchǒu day,
Grand Secretary Féng Quán, Shàngshū Xiè Qǐguāng, and others were dismissed due to offenses.
An edict stated:
"When the state establishes officials,
they must vow to be public-spirited and loyal
to benefit the people
and collectively contribute to a flourishing reign.
Since We began personally governing,
We have repeatedly issued edicts,
encouraging a fresh start.
However, officials in the ministries and courts persist in old abuses,
clinging to their salaries and forming factions.
We shall personally carry out demotions and promotions,
showing the world.
From now on,
they must strive to correct past wrongs
and each fulfill their duties.
If they continue to deceive superiors and subordinates,
the law will show no mercy."
On the Bǐngyín day,
an edict stated:
"Local bandits in various provinces
are originally Our people,
driven to rebellion
by hunger and cold.
In recent years, they have been repeatedly suppressed,
but the generals and commanders in charge of troops
kill innocent people to claim merit,
fail to eliminate true bandits,
and instead inflict suffering on the people.
We deeply lament this.
Henceforth, Governors-General and Provincial Governors should employ both suppression and pacification,
and not harass the people under the pretext of arrests,
to fulfill Our intentions."
On the Dīngmǎo day,
Kǒng Yǒudé captured Wúzhōu and Liǔzhōu.
On the Wùchén day,
Grand Secretary Hóng Chéngchóu concurrently held the post of Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ of the Censorate;
Chén Zhīlín was appointed Shàngshū of the Ministry of Rites;
Zhāng Fèngxiáng as Shàngshū of the Ministry of Works.
On the Jǐsì day,
the Vice-Ministers overseeing military provisions in Jiāngnán and Shǎnxī were abolished,
as was the Vice-Minister in charge of grain transport in Huái'ān.
On the Gēngwǔ day,
Gùshān Ézhēn Ālāshàn and others suppressed bandits in Shāndōng.
On the Rénshēn day,
land enclosures were remitted for Zhuó, Liángxiāng, and thirteen other prefectures and counties.
On the Yǐhài day,
the crimes of officials who had aligned with Duō'ěrgǔn were determined;
Gānglín and Qíchōnggé were both found guilty.
On the Dīngchǒu day,
an edict stated:
"The imperial clan members of the late Míng dynasty
were previously executed in large numbers
for their unrestrained and illicit conduct.
We deeply pity them.
Henceforth, if there are any who have lost their homes and are willing to surrender,
officials shall respectfully send them to the capital,
where they will be given special grace and care.
Those below the rank of Zhènguó Jiāngjūn
shall be registered as commoners in their local areas
and each shall live peacefully in their occupations."
Calamity taxes for Wǎnpíng were remitted.
In the third month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Duānzhòng Qīnwáng Bóluò and Jìngjǐn Qīnwáng Níkān were degraded to Jùnwáng for their offenses.
On the day Guǐwèi,
an edict was issued for all princes (Wáng), Bèilè, and Bèizi to collectively manage the affairs of the Six Boards, the Court of Colonial Affairs (Lǐfānyuàn), and the Censorate (Dūcháyuàn).
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the local chieftains (tǔsī) from Bǎo, Jìng, Yǒngshùn, and other areas in Húnán submitted.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the disaster tax from the previous year in Wǔqiáng was remitted.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Xīfú was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hóngwényuàn,
and Chén Tài was appointed Grand Secretary of the Guóshǐyuàn.
Lǐ Shuàitài was reassigned as Grand Secretary of the Hóngwényuàn,
and Níng Wánwǒ as Grand Secretary of the Guóshǐyuàn.
Gádáhún was appointed Censor-in-Chief (Chéngzhèng) of the Dūcháyuàn,
Zhūmǎlǎ as Minister (Shàngshū) of the Board of Civil Office (Lìbù),
Yǎlàiyī as Minister of the Board of Revenue (Hùbù),
Tánbù as Minister of the Board of Works (Gōngbù),
and Lánbài as Gùshān Ézhēn of the Bordered Blue Banner Manchu.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the regulations for court attendance by princes and dukes (Wánggōng) were established.
On the day Rénchén,
the regulations for inheriting peerages were established.
On the day Guǐsì,
an edict stated:
"Imperial Censors (Yùshǐ) on circuit patrols
are tasked with ensuring the peace of the people and scrutinizing officials.
However, the Censors dispatched in the past
have accepted bribes and engaged in favoritism,
losing their own integrity.
How can they then scrutinize officials?
If officials cannot be scrutinized,
how can the people be at peace?
From now on, all should cleanse themselves and renew,
diligently fulfilling their duties.
Governors-general (Dūfǔ) are also permitted to impeach them,
and the Dūcháyuàn shall investigate and report on their performance."
On the day Guǐmǎo,
regulations for fasting and abstinence were established.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner (Hànjūn) youth were permitted to participate in the imperial examinations,
and appointments would be made according to their class and rank.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Gēngxū,
an imperial decree forbade officials from presenting tribute
where the imperial entourage passed.
Officials were dispatched to offer sacrifices at the sacred mountains, rivers, seas (Yuèzhèn Hǎidú), imperial mausoleums (Dìwáng Língqǐn), and the temple of Confucius (Xiānshī Kǒngzǐ Quèlǐ).
Bandits Luó Róng and others attacked Qiánzhōu,
and Vice-General (Fùjiàng) Yáng Yùmíng pursued and captured them.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the emperor traveled to Shāhé.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
he arrived at Chìchéng.
Wáng Wénkuí was appointed Governor-General of Grain Transport (Zǒngdū Cáoyùn).
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
he arrived at Shàngdū.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Duōléng Jùnwáng and others from the Wēngniútè tribe came to court.
On the day Jǐsì,
he arrived at É'ěrdòng.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the annual tribute of citrus, pomelo, and pomegranates from Cháoxiǎn (Korea) was remitted.
Gùlún Èfù Sèbùténg Jùnwáng and others from the Bālín tribe came to court.
It was ordered that the son of the late Jìngnán Wáng Gěng Zhòngmíng, Jìmào, should inherit the peerage.
On the day Xīnwèi,
he returned and arrived at Shàngdūhé.
On the day Rénshēn,
he arrived at É'ěrdònghé.
In the fifth month, on the first day, Dīngchǒu,
he arrived at Móhùlǐyīzhālǐhé.
Xià Yī'è attacked the former generals of the Ming Táng Wáng, Fù Dǐngquán and others,
pursued them into Fújiàn,
captured Dǐngquán and others, and executed them.
On the day Xīnsì,
he arrived at Kù'ěrqílèhé.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Bèilè Sèléng'é'ěrdéní and others from the Wūzhūmùqín tribe came to court.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
he arrived at Xīlātǎ.
Gádáhún was transferred to become Minister of the Board of Revenue (Hùbù Shàngshū).
Juéshàn was appointed Censor-in-Chief (Chéngzhèng) of the Dūcháyuàn,
and Chuòbèi as Gùshān Ézhēn of the Bordered White Banner Mongol.
On the day Rénchén,
he arrived at Sūnhé.
On the day Guǐsì,
he returned to the palace.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the outstanding land taxes from the famine years of five to seven in Yīngshān were remitted.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Bóluò and Níkān were reinstated as Qīnwáng.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Imperial Censor Zhāng Xuān was sentenced to death for impeaching Minister (Shàngshū) Chén Míngxià.
In the sixth month, on the first day, Bǐngwǔ,
the emperor visited Nányuàn.
Government troops defeated the Shǎnxī bandit Hé Cháishān and others at Luònán.
On the day Dīngsì,
Ālāshàn attacked and pacified the mountain bandits of Yínghé in Shāndōng.
On the day Rénxū,
the tribute of talismans (fúzhuàn) and solomon's seal (huángjīng) from Tàihé Shān was abolished.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the sacrificial rites for the imperial mausoleums, altars, and temples were established.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
an edict stated:
"I, for the corruption and cruelty of officials,
ordered governors-general to investigate and impeach.
Yet, after four or five months, no reports have been made.
Could it be that they have accepted bribes and acted selfishly,
controlled by the officials,
or are they pressured by powerful figures
and dare not impeach?
This is why banditry flourishes
and the common people see no improvement.
Let them immediately carry out the previous edict,
and report truthfully without concealment."
On the day Xīnwèi,
an edict declared that the mausoleum of the late Ming Shénzōng
should be treated like the Twelve Mausoleums (Shí'èr Líng),
with sacrifices offered at appropriate times,
and tomb-guarding households established.
Guǎngdōng government troops recaptured Liánzhōu and twelve other counties including Yǒng'ān.
On the day Rénshēn,
an order was issued to repair the imperial ancestral mausoleums (Zǔlíng),
establish guarding households,
determine sacrificial rites,
and restore the rituals of worshipping the sun at dawn and the moon at dusk.
In autumn, seventh month, on the first day, Bǐngzǐ,
an edict stated:
"Recently, Han people who have 'cast themselves into service' (tóuchōng Hànrén)
have caused trouble and harmed the people,
which I deeply resent.
Those who pay taxes and perform corvée are the common people (biānmáng),
while those who 'cast themselves into service' are slaves (núlì).
Now, the slaves are favored while the common people are treated lightly.
What will become of the national foundation and the laws?
From My own household (bāoyī niúlù)
down to the servants of princes and all officials who have 'cast themselves into service' (tóuchōng rén),
if they commit offenses,
their crimes shall be severely punished,
and those who knowingly abet them shall be implicated.
Previously, local officials who held 'tóuchōng rén' accountable
were themselves punished.
Henceforth, they shall be punished the same as ordinary citizens,
so there will be no differentiation.
Let all under heaven know My intent."
Another edict stated:
"All officials, great and small,
are officers of the court.
Treating them with courtesy
will further enhance the dignity of the court.
Currently, when Manchu and Han officials in the capital commit crimes,
some are arrested and interrogated without an imperial decree to dismiss them,
which is contrary to proper conduct.
Hereafter, when officials in any yamen commit offenses
or are accused,
an imperial decree to dismiss them must first be requested,
and then they shall be sent to the Board of Punishments (Xíngbù) for interrogation.
No one shall directly arrest and interrogate them.
This is hereby made law."
On the day Wùzǐ,
Grand Secretaries Chén Tài and Lǐ Shuàitài were dismissed for their offenses.
Yǎqín was appointed Grand Secretary of the Nèiguóshǐyuàn,
and Dù'ěrdé was appointed Deliberative Minister (Yìzhèng Dàchén).
On the day Yǐwèi,
the emperor visited Nányuàn.
On the day Jǐhài,
Chén Míngxià was appointed Grand Secretary of the Nèihóngwényuàn.
In the eighth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day, the first day of the month,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Qīn Wáng Zhuólìkètú Wúkèshàn of Kē'ěrqìn came to court.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Vice General Xǔ Wǔguāng requested to collect all gold hidden throughout the realm to fund military provisions.
The Emperor said:
"The way for emperors to generate wealth
lies in frugality and loving the people.
Digging the earth to seek gold
has never been done since ancient times."
He ordered him to be dismissed.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Zhào Kāixīn was appointed Zǔdōuyùshǐ.
It was decided that the Shùntiān provincial examination for Manchus and Mongols would be one榜 (list),
and for Han Chinese Bannermen and Han Chinese would be another 榜.
The metropolitan and palace examinations would follow this rule.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Bó'ěrjìjǐn Shì, daughter of Qīn Wáng Zhuólìkètú Wúkèshàn of Kē'ěrqìn, was formally enthroned as Empress.
On the *rénxū* day,
the regulations for cavalry and infantry were revised.
Lìbù Shàngshū Tán Tài was found guilty,
executed,
and his property confiscated.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the grand wedding ceremony was completed,
and the Empress Dowager was granted the honorary title Zhāoshèng Císhòu Gōngjiǎn Huángtàihòu.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Emperor presided over a court session to receive congratulations
and issued an imperial pardon.
On the *wùchén* day,
the title of Sù Qīn Wáng Háogé was posthumously restored.
On the *jǐsì* day,
an edict was issued to abolish all annual tribute goods from the realm that were inconvenient for the people.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Chén Jǐn, Jīn Lì, and others pursued the former Míng Prince Lǔ to Zhōushān,
and captured his general Ruǎn Jìn.
In the ninth month, on the *gēngchén* day,
court ceremonies were established.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Píngxī Wáng Wú Sānguì was ordered to conquer Sìchuān.
Chén Jǐn and Jīn Lì conquered Zhōushān,
and the former Míng Prince Lǔ fled.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Yǎlài, Tánbù, and Juéshàn were dismissed.
Zhuólúo was appointed Lìbù Shàngshū,
Chēkè Hùbù Shàngshū,
Lánbài Gōngbù Shàngshū,
Éluósàichén Dūcháyùan Zǔdōuyùshǐ,
and Zhào Guózuò Xiānghóngqí Hànjūn Gùshān Ézhēn.
Gá'ěr, the commander of the Ābàgāi department, was enfeoffed as Jùn Wáng.
Gùshān Ézhēn Gádáhún campaigned against Duō'ěrzhì of the È'ěrdūosī department.
On the *dīnghài* day,
taxes on barren lands in the four passes of Yǒngpíng were remitted.
On the *rénchén* day,
Chéngtiānmén was renamed Tiān'ānmén.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Emperor hunted in the near suburbs.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
he returned to the palace.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Tǔxiètú Hán, Chēchén Hán, Sàichén Hán, and others of the Kākèkǎ department came to offer tribute.
In the winter, tenth month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
Héshuò Chéngzé Qīn Wáng Shuòsài and Duōluó Qiān Jùn Wáng Wǎkèdá were appointed Yìzhèng Wáng.
On the *xīnhài* day,
disaster taxes in Xuānfǔ were remitted.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Èsèhēi was appointed Guóshǐyùan Dàxuéshì.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Ājìgé was granted death.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Lǐ Guóhàn joined Wú Sānguì in the campaign against Sìchuān.
Mǎ Guānghuī was appointed Zhílì Shāndōng Hénán Zǒngdū.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,

the annual tribute of pearls, sables, saddles, and horses from the various princes on the three major festivals, as well as the annual tribute of horses from the Yǎnshèng Gōng and the garrisons of Xuān and Dà, were remitted.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the mountains of Zàozǔ and Xīngzǔ's tombs were named Qǐyùn Shān.
The mountains of Jǐngzǔ and Xiǎnzǔ's tombs were named Jìqìng Shān.
The mountain of Fúlǐng was named Tiānzhù Shān.
The mountain of Zhāolíng was named Lóngyè Shān.
On this day,
auspicious clouds were seen on Qǐyùn Shān.
In the eleventh month, on the *yǐhài* day, the first day of the month,
the Emperor's first son, Niúniǔ, was born.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Yú Dàhǎi led his troops to Yílíng and surrendered.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Shàng Kěxǐ conquered Léizhōu.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
disaster taxes for the previous year were remitted in the two prefectures of Píngyáng and Lù'ān,
and the three departments of Zé, Liáo, and Qìn.
On the *wùxū* day,
Yī'ěrdé was appointed Zhènghuángqí Mǎnzhōu Gùshān Ézhēn,
and Tóng Túlái Zhènglánqí Hànjūn Gùshān Ézhēn.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
disaster taxes for the previous year were remitted in the four counties including Yángqǔ.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
barren land taxes in Níngjìn were remitted.
In the twelfth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
barren land taxes for the previous year were remitted in the four counties including Tóngchéng.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Zhōu Guózuǒ was appointed Jiāngníng Xúnfǔ.
In this year,
Cháoxiān,
È'ěrdénítáijí, Kūndūlún Wúbāshí, and Ābālāi of the Èlǔtè department,
Tǔxiètú Hán, Chēchén Hán, Sàichén Hán, Gùshí Hán, and Táijí Wúbāshí of the Kākèkǎ department,
and the Dàlái Lǎmā all came to offer tribute.
In the ninth year, spring, first month, on the *guǐyǒu* day, the first day of the month,
the Emperor visited Nányuàn.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Chén Tài was appointed Lǐbù Shàngshū.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Dàxuéshì Chén Míngxià was dismissed due to a crime.
Zhāng Xuān's injustice was redressed,
and the Lǐbù was ordered to deliberate on granting him posthumous honors.
There was an earthquake in the capital.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Chén Wéixīn was appointed Guǎngxī Xúnfǔ.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Emperor's first son, Niúniǔ, passed away.
In the second month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
Hùxībù was appointed Xiānghóngqí Mǎnzhōu Gùshān Ézhēn.
Gádáhún and others attacked Duō'ěrzhì of the È'ěrdūosī department at Hèlán Shān,
annihilating them.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Héshuò Xùn Qīn Wáng Mǎndáhǎi passed away,
and was posthumously enfeoffed as Héshuò Jiǎn Qīn Wáng.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Six Maxims inscribed on steles were promulgated throughout the realm.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Zhèng Qīn Wáng Jí'ěrhāláng was enfeoffed as Shú Héshuò Zhèng Qīn Wáng.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Chén Zhīlín was appointed Hóngwényuàn Dàxuéshì,
and Sūn Máolán Níngxià Xúnfǔ.
In the third month, on the *yǐhài* day,
Wáng Duó was appointed Lǐbù Shàngshū,
and Fáng Kězhuàng Zǔdōuyùshǐ.
Zhāng Xuān was posthumously granted the title Tàichángsì Qīng,
and his son was still recorded to receive an official position equal to his father's.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the regulations for posthumous enfeoffments and grants to officials were established.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the management of ministries by various princes, *bèilè*, and *bèizi* was abolished.
Héshuò Yù Qīn Wáng Duōduó was posthumously demoted to Duōluó Jùn Wáng.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Héshuò Duānzhòng Qīn Wáng Bóluò passed away,
and was posthumously enfeoffed as Héshuò Dìng Qīn Wáng.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Chén Tài was appointed Xiānghuángqí Mǎnzhōu Gùshān Ézhēn.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Èbìlóng, È'ěrkè Dàiqīng, Zhào Bùtài, Làitǎkù, and Suǒhóng were appointed Yìzhèng Dàchén.
Juéluó Lángqiú and Hú Shì'ān were appointed Lǐbù Shàngshū.
Gǒng'ādài, Xīhàn, Xīnnèbùkù, and Lěngsēngjī were executed for their crimes,
and their property was confiscated.
Bàiyīntú was spared death,
but imprisoned.
On the *wùxū* day,
Duōluó Shùnchéng Jùn Wáng Lèkèdéhún passed away,
and was posthumously enfeoffed as Duōluó Gōnghuì Jùn Wáng.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Mǎlèjí and other Manchu and Mongol tribute scholars,
and Zōu Zhōngyǐ and other Han Chinese Bannerman and Han tribute scholars were granted *jìnshì* degrees of varying ranks.
Summer, fourth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Cài Shìyīng was appointed Jiāngxī Xúnfǔ.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the positions of Dénglái and Xuānfǔ Xúnfǔ were abolished.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Hán Dài was appointed Lìbù Shàngshū,
Lánbài Xíngbù Shàngshū,
Xīngnè Gōngbù Shàngshū,
and Ālāshàn Dūcháyùan Zǔdōuyùshǐ.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Kǒng Yǒudé conquered Nánníng, Qìngyuǎn, and Sī'ēn in Guǎngxī.
Former Míng general Chén Bāngfù surrendered Xúnzhōu.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
prefectural and county officials were exempted from attending court audiences.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
regulations for official titles, carriages, and clothing for princes and below were established.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the proposal of the Lǐbù was approved:
three court audiences per month,
and one classical lecture in spring and autumn.
Officials for the Zōngrénfǔ were established.
Fifth month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
an edict declared that the *jīngchá* (capital review) would be held every six years.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
cattle taxes in Jiāngyīn and Qīngpǔ were remitted.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Kākāmù was appointed Ángbāng Zhāngjīng,
to guard and defend Jiāngníng.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the Emperor visited Nányuàn.
In the *dìngwèi* month of the sixth month,
the various garrisons (wèisuǒ) in Zhílì were merged.
On *wùshēn*,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On *gēngxū*,
Héshuò Jìngjǐn Qīnwáng Níkān was appointed to take charge of the Zōngrénfǔ (Court of the Imperial Clan),
and Bèilè Shàngshàn and Bèizi Wú Dáhǎi were made Left and Right Zōngzhèng (Directors of the Imperial Clan).
The imperial forces attacked the bandits in Zhàoqìng and Gāozhōu,
and pacified them.
On *dīngsì*,
an edict was issued that military reforms (jūnzheng) should be carried out every six years.
On *bǐngyín*,
officials of the Zhànshìfǔ (Grand Secretariat) were appointed.
Tú'ěrgé was posthumously granted the title of Zhōngyì Gōng,
and Túlái that of Zhāoxūn Gōng,
to be enshrined in the Tàimiào (Imperial Ancestral Temple).
In the seventh month of autumn, on *guǐyǒu*,
the former Míng general Sūn Kěwàng captured Guìlín,
and Dìngnán Wáng Kǒng Yǒudé died there.
On *bǐngzǐ*,
the north gate of the Imperial City was named Dì'ānmén.
The Governor-General of Zhè-Mǐn, Chén Jǐn, led an expedition against Zhèng Chénggōng,
and upon reaching Zhāngzhōu,
was killed by his own subordinates.
On *gēngchén*,
tax arrears from the brokerage firms in Huái'ān for the sixth and seventh years were remitted.
On *jiǎshēn*,
Héshuò Jìngjǐn Qīnwáng Níkān was appointed Dìngyuǎn Dàjiàngjūn,
to campaign in Húnán and Guìzhōu.
The mourning rituals for Manchu officials were revised.
On *dīnghài*,
Bā'ěrcùhún was made Xiānghóngqí Mǎnzhōu Gùshān Ézhēn.
The disaster taxes from the previous year for eight prefectures and counties, including Cí and Xiángfú, and Huáiqìng Wèi, were remitted.
Wú Sānguì and Lǐ Guóhàn pacified Zhānglà, Sōngpān, and Chóngqìng.
Mēilè Zhāngjīng Dài Dū was dispatched to besiege Chéngdū,
and the former Míng commander Liú Wénxiù surrendered the city.
On *jǐchǒu*,
famine taxes (huāngyáofù) for four counties in Línyì were remitted.
On *xīnmǎo*,
the local chieftains (tǔsī) of Tiānquán Liùfān, Wūsīzàng, and others surrendered.
On *wùxū*,
Zǔ Zéyuǎn was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng and Sìchuān.
In the eighth month, on *yǐsì*,
the marriage rituals for princes (wánggōng) and below were revised.
On *bǐngwǔ*,
Duōluó Qiān Jùnwáng Wǎkèdá passed away.
On *dīngsì*,
Níkān was ordered to redeploy his forces to suppress the remaining rebels in Guǎngxī.
In the ninth month, on *gēngwǔ* (the first day of the month),
Zhū Kǒnggé, Ājìlái, and Yībài were made Yìzhèng Dàchén (Grand Councillors).
On *xīnsì*,
the sacrificial and burial rituals for princes (wáng) and below were revised.
On *guǐwèi*,
Dáozhāngjīng Ā'ěrzīn was made Dìngnán Jiāngjūn,
to campaign with Mǎlāxī against the remaining rebels in Guǎngdōng.
On *jiǎshēn*,
Liú Qīngtài was appointed Governor-General of Zhèjiāng and Fújiàn,
and Wáng Láiyòng was made Shun'tiān Xúnfǔ (Patrolling Censor of Shun'tian).
On *xīnmǎo*,
the Emperor visited the Tàixué (Imperial Academy) to perform the *shìdiàn* ceremony.
On *guǐsì*,
the Yǎnshèng Gōng, the Wǔjīng Bóshì, descendants of the Four Surnames, the Jìjiǔ, Sīyè, and other officials were rewarded differently according to their ranks.
An imperial edict stated:
"The Way of the Sages
is like the sun at its zenith;
it is relied upon by the ruler above to achieve good governance,
and by the people below to serve their sovereign.
Officials of the Imperial Academy and students should all strive to uphold it."
In the tenth month of winter, on *gēngzǐ*,
disaster taxes for Pèixiàn from the sixth to the eighth year were remitted.
Shàng Kěxǐ and Gěng Jìmào captured Qīnzhōu and Língshān.
The former Míng Xīpíng Wáng Zhū Yùyú captured the bandit leader Lǐ Míngzhōng and came to surrender.
All the prefectures of Gāo, Léi, Lián, and Qióng were pacified.
On *rén'yín*,
the imperial forces recaptured Wúzhōu.
On *guǐmǎo*,
due to famine,
an edict was issued for all localities to accumulate grain,
prohibit grain hoarding (èdiáo),
and commend those who donated grain.
On *bǐngwǔ*,
disaster taxes for three counties, including Sānshuǐ, for the sixth year were remitted.
On *rénzǐ*,
Liú Yúyòu was appointed Hùbù Shàngshū (Minister of Revenue).
On *guǐchǒu*,
fallow land taxes (huāngfù) for Bàzhōu, Dōng'ān, and Wén'ān were remitted.
On *jiǎyín*,
Sūn Kěwàng attacked Bǎoníng,
and Wú Sānguì and Lǐ Guóhàn decisively defeated him.
Xīfú, Fàn Wénchéng, Éshèsī, Chēkè, Juéluó Lángqiú, Míng'āndálǐ, Jìxíhā, and Xīngnà were made Yìzhèng Dàchén (Grand Councillors);
Bāhànà was made Xíngbù Shàngshū (Minister of Punishments),
and Lánbài was dismissed.
On *wùwǔ*,
Héshuò Zhèng Qīnwáng Shìzi Jìdù,
Duōluó Xìn Jùnwáng Duōní,
Duōluó Ān Jùnwáng Yuèlè,
Duōluó Mǐn Jùnwáng Lèdū,
Bèilè Shàngshàn, Dù'ěrhù, and Dùlán were ordered to participate in deliberations (yìzhèng).
On *xīnyǒu*,
Ā'ěrzīn was made Ānxī Jiāngjūn,
and moved his garrison with Mǎlāxī to Hànzhōng.
On *bǐngyín*,
Lǐ Huàxī was appointed Xíngbù Shàngshū.
On *dīngmǎo*,
Tàizōng's Dàguìfēi was honored as Yìjìng Dàguìfēi,
and his Shūfēi as Kānghuì Shūfēi.
In the eleventh month, on *gēngwǔ*,
Zhuōluó was made Jìngnán Jiāngjūn,
to campaign with Lánbài and others against the remaining rebels in Guǎngxī.
On *jǐchǒu*,
sacrifices to Heaven were offered at the Yuánqiū.
On *gēngyín*,
the former Míng general Bái Wénxuǎn attacked Chénzhōu,
and Zǒngbīngguān Xú Yǒng, Cānyì Liú Shēngzuò, and Zhīfǔ Wáng Rènxī all died.
On *xīnmǎo*,
Níkān arrived at Xiāngtán.
The former Míng general Mǎ Jìnzhōng and others fled to Bǎoqìng.
Níkān pursued them to Héngshān,
defeated them there,
and then defeated them again at Héngzhōu.
Níkān died in the army.
Níkān was posthumously enfeoffed as Héshuò Zhuāng Qīnwáng.
On *yǐwèi*,
disaster taxes for Xīn, Lèpíng, and other prefectures and counties were remitted.
In the twelfth month, on *xīnchǒu*,
disaster taxes for Tàiyuán, Píngyáng, Fénzhōu, Liáo, Qìn, and Zé were remitted.
On *rén'yín*,
an edict ordered the return of land and people allocated to *tóuchōng* (Manchu bondservants) to over three hundred households in Qīngyuàn,
and their land rent was also remitted for one year.
The imperial forces recaptured Ānfú and Yǒngxīn.
On *bǐngwǔ*,
Zhuōluó's army and others were withdrawn to the capital.
On *gēngxū*,
the Emperor visited Nányuàn.
On *wùwǔ*,
he returned to the palace.
Bandits from Guǎngdōng attacked Xiāngshān,
and the imperial forces pacified them.
On *jǐwèi*,
Ā'ěrzīn was again appointed Dìngnán Jiāngjūn,
to campaign with Mǎlāxī and others against the remaining rebels in Chén and Cháng.
On *jiǎzǐ*,
disaster taxes for Chángwǔ were remitted.
In this year,
the Dalai Lama came to court.
Joseon,
the Örödt tribe's Gùshí Hàn and Bātúlǔ Nuòyán,
the Khalkha tribe's Tǔxiētú Hàn's subordinates Dàiqīng Nuòyán and Lāmá Dá'ěrdá'ěrhàn Nuòyán,
the Solon tribe's Suǒláng'ā Dá'ěrhàn, as well as the Bānchán Hútúkètú, Dìbā, and Bākā Hútúkètú Lāmá all came to offer tribute.
The Örödt Gùshí Hàn came three times.
In the tenth year, in the first month of spring, on *gēngwǔ*,
an imperial decree stated:
"Since I began to govern personally,
I have only seen Manchu ministers submitting memorials.
All officials, great and small,
are my trusted confidants.
Henceforth, for all memorials and documents,
Manchu and Han Shìláng and ministers of higher rank shall consult and present them together,
each avoiding shirking responsibility,
to demonstrate unity of purpose."
On *xīnwèi*,
an edict stated:
"Censors (yánguān) must not pick at trivial matters.
I handle myriad affairs every day;
how could there be nothing that fails to align with Heaven's will or human sentiment?
Let all ministers speak frankly and without concealment.
Those who are correct will surely be commended;
those who are blunt will not be punished."
On *guǐyǒu*,
disaster taxes for Zhuānglàng, Hóngchéngbǎo, and Táozhōu Wèi were remitted.
On *dīngchǒu*,
Hóng Chéngchóu was transferred to be Hóngwényuàn Dàxuéshì,
and Chén Míngxià to be Mìshūyuàn Dàxuéshì.
On *gēngchén*,
Bèilè Tūnqí was made Dìngyuǎn Dàjiàngjūn,
to command the army campaigning in Húnán,
and was given military strategies.
On *bǐngxū*,
Duōluó Èfù Nèiduó was made Yìzhèng Dàchén (Grand Councillor).
An edict ordered ministers of the third rank and above to recommend those they knew,
while strictly enforcing the law of collective responsibility (liánzuòfǎ).
On *gēngyín*,
Jīn Zhīyùn was transferred to be Zuǒ Dōu Yùshǐ (Left Censor-in-Chief),
and Liú Chāng was made Gōngbù Shàngshū (Minister of Works).
On *guǐsì*,
the annual stipends for Duōluó Bèilè and below were revised.
On *bǐngshēn*,
the Emperor visited the Nèiyuàn (Inner Garden),
and read the Tōngjiàn (Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government).
The Emperor asked who was superior among Hàn Gāozǔ, Wéndì, Guāngwǔ, and Táng Tàizōng, Sòng Tàizǔ, Míng Tàizǔ.
Chén Míngxià replied:
"Táng Tàizōng seems to surpass them."
The Emperor said:
"Not so.
Míng Tàizǔ's laws can endure permanently;
no ruler of any dynasty can compare."
In the second month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Gǎ'ěrmǎsàwàng of the Hāosqítè部 Táijí was enfeoffed as a Duōluó Jùnwáng.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Grand Secretary Chén Zhīlín was dismissed.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Chén Zhīlín was appointed as Hùbù Shàngshū.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Shěn Yǒngzhōng was appointed as Jiǎo fú Húnán Jiāngjūn,
to guard Húnán.
On the day Jǐwèi,
redundant Mǎn Shàngshū in various departments were abolished.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Gāo'ěr'yǎn was appointed as Hóngwén Yuàn Dàxuéshì,
and Fèiyánggǔ as Yìzhèng Dàchén.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Míng'āndálǐ and Liú Yúyòu were guilty
and dismissed.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Bēntǎ'ěr, Gǔnbù, Bēnbāshìxī, and Zāmùsū Táijí, under the Tǔxiètú Hàn of the Kā'ěrkā部, led their respective tribes to surrender.
In the third month, on the day Wùchén,
the emperor went to Nántái for an archery practice.
The emperor held a bow and said:
"Our dynasty established the realm with this [skill].
Whenever I go hunting,
I aim to practice horsemanship and archery.
Now I manage myriad affairs,
with no time to spare,
yet I never forget it."
Tāng Ruòwàng, the Tàicháng Sìqīng, was granted the title Tōngxuán Jiàoshī.
Six years of outstanding taxes for seventy-four prefectures and counties in Kělán and Bǎodé, Shānxī, were remitted,
and seven-tenths for the twelve prefectures and counties of Dài and Yúqì.
On the day Jǐsì,
Bēntǎ'ěr of the Kā'ěrkā部 was enfeoffed as Héshuò Dá'ěrhàn Qīnwáng,
Gǔnbù as Zhuólǐkètú Jùnwáng,
and Bēnbāshìxī as Gùshān Bèizǐ.
Nine years of disaster taxes for eleven prefectures and counties including Jì and Fēngrùn were remitted.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the emperor went to Nányuàn.
On the day Jiǎxū,
outstanding taxes for Wǔtái county and half of the regular taxes for eight years were remitted.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
six years of outstanding taxes on barren land in Jiāngxī were remitted.
On the day Xīnsì,
the Zōngxué was established.
Princes and Commandery Princes aged ten and above,
along with selected teachers, were instructed.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the emperor returned to the palace.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Jìxíhā was dismissed.
Gádáhún was appointed as Bīngbù Shàngshū.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Féng Quán was again appointed as Hóngwén Yuàn Dàxuéshì.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
the emperor personally tested the Hànlín officials Chéng Kègǒng and others.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the emperor held court in the Tàihé Diàn,
summoned the officials for an audience,
and issued edicts for their dispatch.
The edict said:
"When the state appoints officials,
those serving internally are familiar with the regulations,
while those serving externally are knowledgeable about local customs.
Only by serving both internally and externally
can true talent be seen.
Now that these literary officials have been personally tested,
those who are not retained
shall be reassigned as appropriate,
following the old custom for literary officials' external transfers,
to various Sī and Dào officials with generous provisions."
The Lìbù and Dūchá Yuàn were first ordered to conduct a Jīngchá.
On the day Jiǎchén,
outstanding taxes for six to nine years in Húnán, and barren land taxes for Xiàxiàn, Shānxī, were remitted.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Tóng Guóqì was appointed as Fújiàn Xúnfǔ.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Túhǎi was appointed as Hóngwén Yuàn Dàxuéshì.
On the day Rénzǐ,
due to drought,
an edict was issued to solicit frank criticism
and lighten punishments.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Tíxué Yùshǐ and Tíxué Dào were ordered to rectify educational administration.
Student quotas were set,
and abuse was prohibited.
The commutation of materials submitted by the common people was changed,
and the Yītiáobiān Fǎ was implemented.
On the day Dīngsì,
the regulation that Manchu officials observe three years of mourning after leaving office was established.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Chéng Kègǒng was appointed as Lìbù Shàngshū.
On the day Guǐhài,
one-third of the barren land taxes before the ninth year for six prefectures including Fúzhōu were remitted.
In the fifth month, on the day Jiǎxū,
the Yùshǐ's巡按直省 inspections were halted.
Nine years of disaster taxes for seven counties including Xiángfú, and eight years of disaster taxes for Miǎnyáng, Qiánjiāng, and Jǐnglíng, were remitted.
On the day Yǐhài,
Zhèng Zhīlóng was enfeoffed as Tóng'ān Hóu,
his son Chénggōng as Hǎichéng Gōng,
and his brother Hóngkuí as Fènghuà Bó.
Kākāmù was appointed as Jìngnán Jiāngjūn,
to suppress the remaining bandits in Guǎngdōng.
Eight and nine years of disaster taxes for sixty-nine prefectures and counties including Lìchéng were remitted.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the regulations for commending virtuous and loyal宗室 (imperial clan members) and chaste and valorous women were established.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
an imperial edict stated:
"The empire has just been settled,
its wounds not yet healed.
Frequent floods and droughts in recent years
have left the people struggling to survive.
Hunger and cold afflict them deeply,
forcing them into banditry.
Although there are many principal villains,
how can there be no innocent and wronged individuals?
Those coerced into banditry are trapped,
with no way to extricate themselves.
Considering these people,
who among them is not our child?
To destroy is extremely easy,
to nurture is exceedingly difficult.
To indiscriminately punish and eliminate them
is deeply regrettable and pitiable.
Now, a special grace is bestowed,
to extend leniency where appropriate.
If they can truly repent and reform,
all shall be given a chance for a new life.
Local officials
shall properly resettle them.
Soldiers shall return to their ranks,
and civilians shall return to farming.
If they do not wish to return to their hometowns,
allow them to reside wherever they are,
do not let them become homeless.
Let all hear and know this."
On the day Gēngchén,
the hot review system was established.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Shū'ěrhāqí was posthumously enfeoffed as Héshuò Qīnwáng,
and Ér'ěrgǔn, Jièkān, Yǎ'ěrhāqí, and Hùsāi as Duōluó Jùnwáng.
Nine years of disaster taxes for Wǔchāng, Hànyáng, Huángzhōu, Ānlù, Dé'ān, Jīngzhōu, and Yuèzhōu were remitted.
On the day Gēngyín,
Hóng Chéngchóu was granted the title Tàibǎo,
and was made Jīnglüè of Húguǎng, Guǎngdōng, Guǎngxī, Yúnnán, and Guìzhōu.
On the day Rénchén,
Zhāng Bǐngzhēn was appointed as Xíngbù Shàngshū.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
nine years of disaster taxes for thirty-one prefectures and counties including Bà and Bǎodìng were remitted.
On the *yǐwèi* day of the sixth month, the first day of the month,
Táshā Piāngǔ and Mù'ěrhāqí were posthumously enfeoffed as Duōluó Bèilè.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
an edict stated:
"Emperors transform the people with virtue
and regulate them with ritual.
It is only as a last resort that punishment is employed.
Law is the standard of the world;
it should not be swayed by likes or dislikes, making it light or heavy.
In the past, when subjects committed crimes,
their cases were always submitted to the ministries for deliberation,
as the duty of a judicial officer
lies in clarity and fairness.
Yet, some might speculate with personal biases.
When a case was brought up by the Emperor,
they would propose a severe penalty to await the Emperor's personal decision.
Citing old precedents,
they would also craft interpretations to make punishments excessively harsh.
I wish to protect all living beings
and rule with leniency.
For people who steal due to hunger and cold,
I still allow them to confess.
For those in distant regions who have not yet submitted,
I also offer to bring them in.
How can I bear to trap common people and court officials
in such wrongful excesses?
Henceforth, the judicial authorities must ascertain the true facts,
apply the original laws,
and eradicate all forms of forced implication and fabrication.
All these practices must be thoroughly reformed
to achieve a state where punishments are rarely needed."
Grand Secretary Gāo'ěryǎn was dismissed.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the practice of autumn assizes and court reviews was reinstated.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Zǔ Zéyuǎn was appointed to solely oversee Húguǎng,
and Méng Qiáofāng was concurrently appointed to oversee Sìchuān.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the disaster tax for eight years in Cíxī and five other counties was remitted.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the posthumous titles were granted to the sixteen individuals who died for the former Míng dynasty, including Grand Secretary Fàn Jǐngwén, Minister of Revenue Ní Yuánlù, and the eunuch Wáng Chéng'ēn,
and sacrificial fields were also granted.
Local officials in their respective areas were to offer sacrifices.
The method of converting tribute grain and silver in kind across the empire was changed,
and the *Yītiáobiān Fǎ* (Single Whip Law) was implemented.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Bèilè Tūnqí and others defeated Sūn Kěwàng at Bǎoqìng.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Lǐ Shuàitài was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng.
The Cíníng Gōng palace was completed.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the number of Hàn Grand Secretaries in the Three Inner Academies was increased,
with two for each academy.
On the *guǐhài* day,
an edict stated:
"In the eras of Táng, Yú, Xià, and Shāng, eunuchs were not used.
During the Zhōu dynasty, they merely held functional positions,
managing gates and sweeping, and relaying orders.
From the Qín and Hàn dynasties onward,
they began to usurp authority,
were granted titles and emoluments,
commanded troops, interfered in governance,
and brought calamity upon later generations.
With minor loyalty and minor trustworthiness,
they firmly won the ruler's heart;
with great wickedness and great treachery,
they secretly held the reins of the state.
The palace was deep and secluded,
and they lived in leisure within,
confusing right and wrong to obscure the worthy and the villainous,
and exploiting emotions to assert their power and influence.
Many changes arose from within,
and power gradually shifted downwards.
Reviewing past downfalls
serves as a warning.
I have considered ancient and modern practices
and decided on their appropriate establishment,
limiting their rank to no higher than the fourth grade.
Unless dispatched on official missions,
they are not allowed to leave the Imperial City without permission.
If any external officials are found to be colluding with them,
they will all be sentenced to death upon discovery."
On the *bǐngyín* day of the intercalary sixth month,
Chéng Kègǒng was appointed Grand Secretary of the Mìshū Yuàn,
Zhāng Duān was appointed Grand Secretary of the Guóshǐ Yuàn,
and Liú Zhèngzōng was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hóngwén Yuàn.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Jīn Zhījùn was appointed Minister of Personnel.
On the *gēngchén* day,
an edict stated:
"According to the Hóngfàn,
'being serious' is a sign for timely rain.
The interaction between Heaven and man
is truly unfailing.
I strive diligently from dawn to dusk,
hoping to receive Heaven's blessings.
However, the capital has suffered incessant rain for a month,
with accumulated water forming channels,
destroying people's homes,
and leaving the impoverished in distress and without food.
All this is due to my lack of virtue.
Now I intend to sincerely cultivate and examine myself,
revering Heaven's warnings.
All officials, great and small,
should likewise be vigilant and cease their faults."
On the *jiǎwǔ* day of the seventh month, the first day of the month,
the Emperor, following the Empress Dowager's instruction,
released eighty thousand *liǎng* of saved silver to relieve soldiers and common people suffering from flood disasters.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Yí Yǒngguì was appointed Circuit Inspector of Nángàn.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the second imperial son, Fúquán, was born.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Ān Jùnwáng Yuèlè was appointed General-in-Chief Xuānwēi,
to lead his troops and garrison Guīhuà Chéng.
On the *rénwǔ* day of the eighth month,
the fourteenth daughter of Tàizōng, Princess Héshuò, was married to Wú Sānguì's son, Yìngxíong, the Prince who Pacifies the West.
Shàng Kěxǐ captured Huàzhōu and Wúchuān.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the ranks of military officials were established.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Léi Xīng was appointed Circuit Inspector of Hénán.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Empress was demoted to Consort Jìng.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Lǐ Dìngguó attacked Pínglè.
Zhōu Yǒngxù, Surveillance Circuit of Fǔjiāng,
Yǐn Míngtíng, Prefect,
and Tú Qǐpéng and Huá Zhōng, County Magistrates, died there.
On the *rénzǐ* day of the ninth month,
the practice of triple review for cases by the Ministry of Justice was reinstated.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Gěng Jìmào and Kākāmù captured Cháozhōu.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Méng Qiáofāng pacified Zhū Jìng..., the former Míng King Yíchuān, at Zǐyáng.
It was pacified.
On the *guǐhài* day of the tenth month, the first day of the month,
Tián Xióng was ordered to relocate and garrison Dìnghǎi.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Mǎ Guānghuī and others attacked the rebellious general Hǎi Shíxíng at Yǒngchéng.
Hǎi Shíxíng was executed.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Jìxíhā was dispatched to suppress local bandits in Shāndōng.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
porridge kitchens were established to feed the starving people in the capital.
Disaster taxes for Tōng, Mìyún, and five other prefectures and counties were remitted.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Grand Secretaries and Academicians were ordered to take turns on duty inside the Tàihé Mén.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day of the eleventh month,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Yuánqiū.
On the *wùxū* day,
Zhèng Chénggōng refused the offered title,
and a gracious edict was sent in reply.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Kàng Déshí was appointed Circuit Inspector of Hénán.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the government army suppressed the rebellious Huí people in Xīníng,
and pacified them.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Zhū Mǎlā and Jīn Zhījùn were dismissed.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
disaster taxes in Jiāngnán were remitted.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Liú Qīngtài annihilated the bandits in Jiǔxiān Shān,
and pacified them.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
disaster taxes for fifty-four prefectures and counties in Jiāngxī were remitted.
On the *bǐngyín* day of the twelfth month,
Chén Tài was appointed Grand General Níngnán Jìngkòu,
and together with Lán Bài, garrisoned Húnán.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Lǚ Gōng was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hóngwén Yuàn,
Bóbó'ěrdài was appointed Deliberative Minister,
and Féng Shèngzhào was appointed Circuit Inspector of Piányuán.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Emperor visited Nányuàn.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
disaster taxes for nine years in eight counties of Jīnhuá were remitted.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
an official for supervising arrests was established in the Ministry of War.
Luó Bì was appointed Deliberative Minister.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
disaster taxes for the ninth and tenth years in Kāifēng, Zhāngdé, Wèihuī, Huáiqìng, and Rǔníng were remitted.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Zhèng Chénggōng attacked Wúsōng,
and the government army repelled him.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
That night,
there was an earthquake with sound.
In this year,
Cháoxiān,
Liúqiú,
Sōnuò'é'ěrdéní and É'ěrdéní Hātán Bātúlǔ from the Túshèntú Hàn's section of the Kā'ěrkā tribe,
Gùshí Hàn and Táijí Nuòmùqí from Gùshí Hàn's section of the Élǔtè tribe,
Bādákètú from the Suǒlún tribe,
Yíkùdá from Fùlā Cūn,
Wūmòtè and É'ěrduōkē from Hēilóngjiāng,
and Dálài Lǎma from Wūsī Zàng all came to pay tribute.
Cháoxiān came again.
In the eleventh year, spring, first month, on the day Xīnchǒu
the officials for weaving and manufacturing were dismissed.
On the day Wùshēn,
the disaster tax from the previous year was remitted for Jiāngníng, Ānhuī, Sūzhōu, Sōngjiāng, Chángzhōu, Zhènjiāng, Lúzhōu, Fèngyáng, Huáiyáng, Xúzhōu, and Chúzhōu.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Yuán Kuòyǔ was appointed Governor of Piānwán,
and Hú Quáncái was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Yún yáng.
On the day Gēngxū,
the bandits in Yuèdòng, Rénhuà, Guǎngdōng, were suppressed.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Zhèng Chénggōng attacked Chóngmíng, Jìngjiāng, and Tàixīng,
and the imperial army repelled him.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Jīn Lì was appointed Governor-General of the Three Borders of Chuānshǎn.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Zhèng Chénggōng attacked Jīnshān.
On the day Dīngsì,
the disaster tax from the previous year was remitted for Shùndé, Guǎngpíng, Dàmíng, Tiānjīn, and Jìzhōu.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the imperial army attacked the bandits in Táoyuán,
and executed the pseudo-General-in-chief Lǐ Yángchūn and others.
Second month, on the day Guǐhài,
the morning ceremony to the sun was held in the eastern suburbs.
On the day Bǐngyín,
an edict stated:
"Censors serve as the ears and eyes of the government.
