I have repeatedly sought frank advice,
hoping to receive it eagerly.
However, upon reviewing memorials,
few are truly devoted to the country,
while many are partisan and self-serving,
which I strongly disapprove of.
Therefore, cleanse your hearts and minds to renew governance."
Jīn Zhīzhùn was appointed Grand Academician of the Historiography Academy.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the Governors-General and Governors of the directly administered provinces were evaluated,
and there were dismissals and promotions accordingly.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
the ceremonial plowing of the imperial field began.
On the day Wùyín,
the deficient poll tax for Jiāngxī was remitted.
On the day Xīnsì,
Shàng Kěxǐ was ordered to specifically guard Guǎngdōng,
and Gěng Jìmào was transferred to station in Guìlín.
On the day Réngwǔ,
Mǎ Míngpèi was appointed Governor-General of Xuāndà and Shānxī,
Gěng Dūn was appointed Governor of Shāndōng,
Chén Yìngtài was appointed Governor of Shānxī,
Lín Tiānqíng was appointed Governor of Húguǎng,
and Huáng Tú'ān was appointed Governor of Níngxià.
On the day Guǐwèi,
the imperial army recaptured Píngyuǎn County.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
an edict stated:
"In recent years,
military campaigns have not ceased,
supplies have been very scarce,
and with floods and droughts in addition,
the common people have struggled for food,
while officials have failed to provide relief,
leaving many displaced on the roads.
My heart aches for them,
and I cannot rest.
I will immediately check the treasury reserves
and promptly plan for relief and pacification."
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the disaster tax for ten years was remitted for the prefectures, counties, and garrisons of Hénán.
On the day Gēngyín,
Lǐ Yìnzǔ was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì, Shāndōng, and Hénán.
Third month, on the day Rénchén,
the imperial army attacked the bandits in Guìdōng,
capturing their leader Lài Lóng.
On the day Wùxū,
the disaster tax for ten years was remitted for Xiāngyáng, Huángzhōu, Chángdé, Yuèzhōu, Yǒngzhōu, Jīngzhōu, Dé'ān, and the three garrisons of Chénzhōu, Chángzhōu, and Xiāngzhōu in Húguǎng,
and for Jǐnán and Dōngchāng in Shāndōng.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Níng Wánwǒ impeached Chén Míngxià for his crimes,
which were proven true,
and he was executed.
On the day Yǐsì,
Wáng Yǒngjí was appointed Censor-in-chief of the Left.
On the day Wùshēn,
the third imperial son Xuányè was born,
who became Shèngzǔ.
Jiǎng Hèdé was appointed Grand Academician of the Historiography Academy.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Duōluó Huìzhé Jùnwáng È'ěrgǔn, Duōluó Xuānxiàn Jùnwáng Jièkān, and Duōluó Tōngdá Jùnwáng Yǎ'ěrhāqí were enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
Mèng Míngfǔ was appointed Minister of War.
Summer, fourth month, on the day Rénxū,
the bandit leader Cáo Zhìpān attacked Ráozhōu,
the imperial army defeated him,
and Zhìpān surrendered.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the Sichuan bandit Wèi Yǒng attacked Shùnqìng,
the imperial army defeated him.
On the day Rénshēn,
there was an earthquake.
The imperial army attacked the former Míng generals Zhāng Míngzhèn and others at Chóngmíng,
and defeated them.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
one-third of the disaster tax from the previous year for Luònán was remitted.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the emperor visited Nányuàn,
and bestowed gold upon the farmers along the way.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the disaster tax for the previous year, affected by bandits, was remitted for Bǎokāng and three other counties.
On the day Dīnghài,
Wáng Yǒngjí was appointed Grand Academician of the Secretariat Academy,
and Qín Shìzhēn was appointed Governor of Zhèjiāng.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Jiangnan bandits Xú Kějìn and Zhū Yuán surrendered.
Fifth month, on the day Rénchén,
the emperor returned to the palace.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
he visited Xīyuàn,
and hosted a banquet for his ministers.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Hú Tú was appointed Deliberative Minister.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the disaster tax from the previous year for Píngliáng Garrison was remitted.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Dǎng Chóngyǎ was reinstated as Grand Academician of the Historiography Academy,
and Gōng Dǐngzī was appointed Censor-in-chief of the Left.
On the day Dīngwèi,
officials were dispatched to record prisoners in the directly administered provinces.
On the day Gēngxū,
the disaster tax from the previous year was remitted for Xīng'ān, Hànyīn, Pínglì and other prefectures and counties.
On the day Xīnhài,
Venus was visible during the day.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Yáng Qíxiáng was appointed Pacifying General of the South,
stationed in Hángzhōu.
Sixth month, on the first day Jǐwèi,
the river burst its banks at Dàwángmiào.
On the day Bǐngyín,
there was an earthquake in Shǎnxī.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Zhū Mǎlǎ was appointed General Quelling the South,
to campaign against the remaining bandits in Guǎngdōng.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the daughter of Kē'ěrqìn Zhènguógōng Chuò'ěrzhì, of the Bó'ěrjìjǐn clan, was established as Empress.
On the day Gēngchén,
there was a general amnesty.
Autumn, seventh month, on the first day Wùzǐ,
Shàng Zhì, the crown prince of Liúqiú, was enfeoffed as King of Zhōngshān.
On the day Rénchén,
the disaster tax for Qínzhōu, Cháoyì, and Āndìng was remitted.
On the day Wùshēn,
the disaster tax for Zhènyuán and Guǎngníng counties was remitted.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Tóng Dài was appointed Governor-General of Zhèfú.
Eighth month, on the first day Wùwǔ,
the barren land tax for Yán'ān Prefecture was remitted.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the imperial army annihilated the remaining bandits in Ruìjīn,
executing the pseudo-Commander Xǔ Shèngkě and others.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the officials for judicial relief in the directly administered provinces were dismissed,
and the Governors were ordered to review prisoners.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the disaster tax for ten years for Zhēnnìng County was remitted.
On the day Rénxū,
there was an audible earthquake in Púzhōu, Yánggǔ and other counties in Shāndōng.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Zhāng Zhōngyuán was appointed Governor of Jiāngníng.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Zhāng Bǐngzhēn was appointed Minister of War.
On the day Gēngchén,
Fù Yǐjiàn was appointed Grand Academician of the Secretariat Academy,
and Rèn Jùn was appointed Minister of Justice.
On the day Réngwǔ,
the former Míng Prince of Lè'ān, Zhū Yìpéng, plotted rebellion,
and was executed.
Ninth month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Fàn Wénchéng retired due to illness.
The disaster tax for ten years for Xī'ān, Píngliáng, and Fèngxiáng prefectures was remitted.
On the day Gēngyín,
Xiàn Guó'ān was enfeoffed as Third-rank Earl.
On the day Rénchén,
the prohibition against harboring fugitives was strictly reinforced.
On the day Guǐsì,
the disaster tax for Xuānfǔ and Wànquán Right Garrison was remitted.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Dǒng Tiānjī was appointed Governor of Zhílì.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Féng Shèngzhào was appointed Governor of Yánsuí.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *dìngsì* day which was the first day of the month,
a sacrificial ceremony was held at the Tàimiào.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the disaster levies for the four prefectures of Lú, Fèng, Huái, and Yáng,
and the three prefectures of Xú, Chú, and Hé were remitted.
On the *dìngchǒu* day,
it was ordered that cases of serious offenders, involving three judicial bodies, should be submitted for proposed verdicts,
and also that the deliberative princes (*yìzhèngwáng*), *bèilè*, and high officials should thoroughly discuss them.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
relief was provided to the counties and prefectures in the capital region (*jīfǔ*) affected by floods.
The outstanding taxes of Qíyáng and six other counties were remitted.
Lǐ Dìngguó captured Gāomíng
and besieged Xīnhuì.
Gěng Jìmào requested additional troops.
In the eleventh month, on the *dīnghài* day,
Chén Tài was appointed Minister of Personnel (*lìbù shàngshū*),
and Ā'ěrjīn was appointed *gùshān ézhēn* of the Bordered Blue Banner Manchu.
Shàng Kěxǐ sent his son to attend court.
On the *rényín* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"I have inherited the grand legacy
for eleven years,
but the effects of my governance have not yet been realized,
the borders have seen many troubles,
floods and droughts have appeared repeatedly,
and earthquakes have been frequently heard.
These are all due to my lack of virtue.
I, a humble person, am placed above the princes, dukes, officials, and common people,
but governance and instruction are not rectified,
and the wounds are not yet healed.
Yet, in memorials and documents,
I am often referred to as 'Sheng' (Saintly or Holy),
which further highlights my lack of virtue.
I am introspecting and restraining myself,
and all officials, great and small, should also diligently adhere to their duties
to collectively avert calamities and troubles.
In all memorials and official documents,
the term 'Sheng'
is not to be used.
A general amnesty is granted to the empire,
and all shall start anew."
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the emperor visited Nányuàn.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Gěng Jìmào sent his son to attend court.
In the twelfth month, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
Héshuò Chéngzé Qīnwáng Shuòsāi passed away.
On the *wùchén* day,
the disaster levies for Jīngmén, Zhōngxiáng, and six other counties and prefectures were remitted.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the disaster levies for Cí, Xiángfú, and thirty-four other counties and prefectures were remitted.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Jìdù was appointed Dìngyuǎn Dàjiāngjūn
to campaign against Zhèng Chénggōng.
Shàng Kěxǐ, Gěng Jìmào, and Zhūmǎlá defeated Lǐ Dìngguó at Xīnhuì,
and Dìngguó fled.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Zhèng Chénggōng captured Zhāngzhōu
and besieged Quánzhōu.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Míng'āndálǐ was ordered to campaign against the Luóshà.
The barren land taxes of the five guards of Xī'ān were remitted.
Huò Wǔ and other rebels from Jiāngxī led their followers to surrender.
In this year,
Cháoxiān,
Liúqiú,
the Érǔtè tribal leaders Ābālāinuòyán, Nuòménfú, and É'ěrdéNídáyúnchuò'ěrjì,
the Suǒlún tribal leader Suǒlánggádá'ěrhàn,
and the Tānggǔtè tribal leaders Dálàilǎmā and Dìbā Bānchán Hútúkètú all came to offer tribute.
In the first month of spring in the twelfth year, on the *wùzǐ* day,
the imperial army defeated the rebels at Yùbǎncháo
and also attacked the Fèngxiàn rebels,
defeating them.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the previous year's disaster levies for Dōngpíng, Jìyáng, and sixteen other counties and prefectures were remitted.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the previous year's disaster levies for eight prefectures in Zhílì,
and Zhāngdé, Wèihuī, and Huáiqìng in Hénán were remitted.
On the *wùxū* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Since I took personal charge of government,
it has been five years.
I have toiled and worried,
seeking good governance,
and hoped daily that my officials would present excellent strategies
to rectify my shortcomings.
However, the borders are not yet pacified,
floods and droughts are frequent,
official administration is corrupt,
and the people's lives are wretched.
Important advice for stabilizing the nation and governing is not heard.
All the princes and high officials have personally witnessed the difficulties of our ancestors in founding the dynasty.
Do they not have long-term strategies,
and yet none have directly presented criticisms or suggestions?
Is it that I am not open to listening,
or that my receptiveness to counsel is incomplete?
The empire is vast,
and administrative tasks are numerous;
the responsibility lies with one person,
but guidance is lacking.
Though I am not virtuous,
do I not remember the benevolent nurturing of our ancestors?
Therefore, express your utmost loyalty
to console my heart."
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Hán Dài was appointed Minister of Personnel (*lìbù shàngshū*),
and Yī'ěrdé and Ālàshàn were appointed Commanders (*dūtǒng*).
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Yú Shíyuè was appointed Governor of Guǎngxī.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
it was ordered that all officials in the capital of the seventh rank and above,
and all civil officials serving as prefects (*zhīfǔ*) and military officials serving as vice-generals (*fùjiàng*) and above in the provinces,
should each speak freely and without reservation
on matters of their duties and the suffering of soldiers and common people.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the Shùnzhì Dàxùn was revised.
In the second month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
imperial censors (*yùshǐ*) were again dispatched to inspect the direct provinces.
On the *rénxū* day,
Grand Secretary (*dàxuéshì*) Lǚ Gōng was dismissed due to illness.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the previous year's disaster levies for Chéng'ān and five other counties were remitted.
On the *jǐsì* day,
relief was provided to bannermen (*qídīng*).
The previous year's disaster levies for Píngliáng and Hànyīn counties were remitted.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Bómùbóguǒ'ěr was enfeoffed as Héshuò Xiāngqīnwáng.
The previous year's disaster levies for Bīn, Níngyáng, and nineteen other counties and prefectures were remitted.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the previous year's disaster levies for Chú and Hé prefectures were remitted.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Chén Zhīlín was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hóngwényuàn,
and Wáng Yǒngjí was appointed Grand Secretary of the Guóshǐyuàn.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Gěng Jìmào and Shàng Kěxǐ defeated Lǐ Dìngguó at Xīngyè.
The three prefectures of Gāo, Léi, and Lián in Guǎngdōng,
and Héngzhōu in Guǎngxī were pacified.
In the third month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
the previous year's disaster levies for Shímén county in Húguǎng were remitted.
Dài Míngshuō was appointed Minister of Revenue (*hùbù shàngshū*).
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Tóng Guóqì was appointed Governor of Nángàn,
and Yí Yǒngguì was appointed Governor of Fújiàn.
On the *rényín* day,
the previous year's taxes for land ravaged by bandits in Yúnyáng and Xiāngyáng prefectures were remitted.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Tú'ěrchen, Shǐ Dàchéng, and others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with differing ranks.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the title of Xùshùngōng Shěn Yǒngzhōng was stripped.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
an imperial decree stated:
"Since the disturbances at the end of the Míng dynasty,
there has been constant warfare,
and the pursuit of learning
has been neglected and not discussed.
Now that the empire is gradually stabilizing,
I intend to promote culture and education
and exalt Confucianism
to usher in an era of great peace.
Academic officials in the direct provinces
should instruct and supervise scholars
to be widely knowledgeable in ancient and modern times,
understanding the essence and applying it practically.
All officials, in their leisure from state affairs,
should also dedicate themselves to learning
to assist me in this cultural governance."
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
the position of lecturers for daily lessons (*rìjiǎngguān*) was established.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
the previous year's disaster levies for Shěnqiū and Huáiqìng Guard were remitted.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Nísīhā was further enfeoffed as Héshuò Jìngjǐn Qīnwáng,
and Qíkèxīn as Héshuò Duānzhòng Qīnwáng.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
an edict was issued to revise the sacred instructions of Tàizǔ and Tàizōng.
In the fifth month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
Túhǎi was concurrently appointed Minister of Justice (*xíngbù shàngshū*).
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Héshuò Zhèng Qīnwáng Jí'ěrhāláng passed away,
and court was suspended for seven days.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Shí Tíngzhù was appointed Zhènhǎi Jiāngjūn
and stationed at Jīngkǒu.
On the *wùxū* day,
Húshā was appointed *gùshān ézhēn* of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Juéluó Bāhānà was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hóngwényuàn.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Língqiū county experienced an audible earthquake.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Juéluó Lángqiú was appointed Minister of Revenue (*hùbù shàngshū*).
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Lǐ Jìqī was appointed Minister of War (*bīngbù shàngshū*).
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Ēngédé was appointed Minister of Rites (*lǐbù shàngshū*).
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Wèi Zhōuzuò was appointed Minister of Works (*gōngbù shàngshū*).
In the *jiǎyín* month of the sixth lunar month,
calamity taxes were remitted for Hángzhōu, Níngbō, Jīnhuá, Qúzhōu, and Táizhōu.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
an edict stated:
“I have observed the memorials from the judicial authorities,
which report five or six prisoners executed daily,
or sometimes more than ten.
I recall that these ignorant people,
after the disasters of war and pestilence,
are again caught in the net of the law;
this is deeply lamentable.
In the time of Yǒu Yú (Shùn),
the people did not transgress the law before the officials.
Emperor Wén of Hàn and Emperor Tàizōng of Táng almost brought about the suspension of punishments.
Now, offenders of the law are numerous.
Is it because customs are degenerating daily?
Or is it that the imperial court's virtue and teachings have not spread sufficiently,
or that those who judge cases have made errors in their decisions?
Hereafter, the judicial authorities must be clear and cautious in applying punishments,
and strive for fairness and impartiality.”
On the *wùchén* day,
calamity taxes for the previous year were remitted for Fángshān Xiàn.
Liú Wénxiù, a general of Prince Guì, raided Chángdé,
and sent his partisans to attack Yuèzhōu and Wǔchāng;
the government troops defeated and drove them away.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Bóguǒduó was enfeoffed as Héshuò Zhuāng Qīnwáng.
On the *xīnsì* day,
an iron plaque was ordered to be erected in the thirteen internal yamen.
An edict stated:
“The establishment of eunuchs
has never been abolished since ancient times.
If their appointments and deployment are improper,
they will bring calamity and disorder.
For instance, Wáng Zhèn, Wāng Zhí, Cáo Jíxiáng, Liú Jǐn, and Wèi Zhōngxián of the Míng Dynasty,
usurped power and controlled the government,
framed loyal and upright officials,
were dispatched to garrison frontiers and command troops,
poisoned the border regions,
instigated partisans to praise their achievements,
and plotted treason.
Their downfall followed one after another,
which serves as a profound warning.
I have prescribed the duties of the inner officials,
and the laws and regulations are very clear.
If anyone should usurp power, accept bribes,
collude with officials,
or make memorials beyond their authority,
they shall be put to death by slow slicing.
A special iron plaque is erected
for observance by future generations.”
In the seventh lunar month, autumn, on the first day, *guǐwèi* (new moon),
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *rénchén* day,
court officials were again dispatched to review punishments and show clemency.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the direct provinces were ordered to draw and submit maps.
In the eighth lunar month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
calamity taxes were remitted for Língqiū Xiàn.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Ā'ěrzīn was appointed Níngnán Jìngkòu Dàjiāngjūn,
to be stationed in Jīngzhōu with Zhuōluó,
and Zǔ Zérùn to defend Chángshā.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Duōluó Ān Jùnwáng Yuèlè was appointed Zuǒ Zōngzhèng,
and Bèilè Dùlán as Yòu Zōngzhèng.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
an edict stated:
“The capital region is the foundation of the empire.
The Board officials, due to a breach in the Grand Canal,
proposed collecting outstanding taxes.
I consider that the capital region has suffered consecutive floods and droughts,
and the people are in dire straits.
How can they bear
to pay the old taxes again?
Therefore, all are now remitted.
The cost of construction will be planned separately.”
Calamity taxes for the previous year were remitted for seven *zhōu* and *xiàn* including Cáo and Chéngwǔ, and for Línqīng Wèi and Qíhé Tún.
In the ninth lunar month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
calamity taxes were remitted for Fèngyáng.
On the *rénchén* day,
the military *huìshì* successful candidates, whose palace examination results were like civilian *jìnshì*, were decided.
Zhūmǎlǎ and Dūnbài returned after their campaigns.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the imperial compositions *Zīzhèng Yàolǎn*, *Fànxíng Yán*, *Quànshàn Yàoyán*, and *Jǐngxīnlù* were promulgated.
Each [official] from duke of different surname downwards,
and civilian officials of the third rank and above, received one set.
On the *wùshēn* day,
calamity taxes were remitted for Liǎngdāng and Níngyuǎn counties.
In the tenth lunar month, winter, on the first day, *xīnhài* (new moon),
officials of the Shàngbǎo Sì were established.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
calamity taxes were remitted for Wèizhōu and for Yánghé and Yánggāo *wèi*.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
calamity taxes were remitted for Gānzhōu, Sùzhōu, Liángzhōu, and Xīníng.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
it was ordered that prisoners be reviewed annually in the sixth lunar month,
and a report submitted in the seventh lunar month;
this was made into a regulation.
On the *guǐhài* day,
calamity taxes were remitted for eight *zhōu* and *xiàn* including Cí and Huòjiā.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
outstanding taxes before the eleventh year of Lóngpíng and calamity taxes for eight *xiàn* including Zīchuān were remitted.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
calamity taxes were remitted for Xuānfǔ and Dàtóng.
On the *wùchén* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“Emperors transform the people with virtue
and assist governance with punishment.
If laws and regulations are improperly severe or lenient,
and officials manipulate documents or make arbitrary decisions,
how can governance be equitable and disputes resolved?
I have reviewed memorials on judgments,
and the citations often fall short of satisfaction.
Let the current laws and regulations be transcribed and presented
so I may personally review and amend them.”
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Zhù Shìyǔn was appointed Xiānghóngqí Mǎnzhōu Gùshān Ézhēn.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Sūn Tíngquán was appointed Bīngbù Shàngshū.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the imperial genealogy (Yùdié) was revised.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Gōng Dǐngzī was dismissed due to offenses.
In the eleventh lunar month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
calamity taxes were remitted for thirteen *zhōu* and *xiàn* including Bīn and Tángyì.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Zhèng Chénggōng's general attacked Zhōushān.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Gu Rén, the Circuit Censor, was executed in the marketplace
for accepting bribes.
On the *dīnghài* day,
an edict stated:
“The state establishes governors, grand coordinators, and circuit censors
to uphold discipline, establish regulations,
eradicate abuses, and expose treachery,
intending them to supervise each other.
However, recent entrenched habits
have led to mutual concealment.
All those impeached are merely junior officials.
How can this fulfill the intent of establishing these offices?
Hereafter, those who show favoritism or indulge in self-interest
shall also be punished for their crimes.”
Zhèng Chénggōng's general captured Zhōushān,
and the Vice General Bǎ Chénggōng surrendered to the rebels.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the emperor visited Nányuàn.
Outstanding taxes for Yúnyáng and Xiāngyáng,
and calamity taxes for Jí, Qí, Zuòchéng and other counties were remitted.
On the *wùshēn* day,
calamity taxes were remitted for Línzhāng.
In the twelfth lunar month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
calamity taxes were remitted for Yàozhōu, Tóngguān, and Luònán.
On the *guǐhài* day,
calamity taxes were remitted for ten *zhōu* and *xiàn* including Ānjí and Rénhé,
and for the eight *wèi* of Xuānhuà.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the *Dàqīng Mǎnzì Lǜ* (Great Qing Manchu Script Laws) was promulgated.
Calamity taxes were remitted for ten *zhōu* and *xiàn* including Línqīng and Qíhé,
and for Dōngchāng Wèi.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Yú Shíyuè and Zǔ Zéyuǎn pacified 192 Yáo and Zhuàng villages in the Jiǔtuán and Liǎngdū areas.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Duōluó Mǐn Jùnwáng Lèdù passed away.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
calamity taxes were remitted for thirty-three *zhōu* and *xiàn* including Zhuó and Qìngyún,
and for Yǒngpíng Wèi.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Yí'ěrdé was appointed Nínghǎi Dàjiāngjūn
to suppress the Zhōushān rebels.
Qín Shìzhēn was appointed Ānhuī Xúnfǔ
and Tídū Cāojiāng;
Chén Yìngtài was appointed Zhèjiāng Xúnfǔ;
Bái Rúméi was appointed Shānxī Xúnfǔ.
Calamity taxes were remitted for eighteen counties including Línhǎi,
for Xiángfú and Lányáng counties,
and for Huáiqìng and Qúnmù *wèi*.
In this year,
É'ěrdéní Nuòmùqí Táijí, Ménzhāng Mé'ěrgēn Chǔhú'ěr Táijí, Yīshìxībù É'ěrdéní Táijí, and É'ěrkè Dàiqīng Táijí from the Kè'ěrkǎ (Khalkha) tribes came to court.
From Cháoxiǎn (Joseon),
Bìxīlè'ěrtú Hán, Éwùbù É'ěrdéní, Zébúzūn Dānbā Hútúkètú, Dānjīn Lǎmā, Chēchén Hán, Tǔxiètú Hán, and Lǎmā Tǎ'ěrdá'ěrhàn Nuòyán from under Tǔxiètú Hán of the Kè'ěrkǎ tribes;
Dùlā'ěrhúnjīn Táijí, Dūlā'ěrhúnjīn Ālìlùkèsāntuōyīn, Ābālāi Nuòyán, Èqí'ěrtú Táijí, and Gá'ěrdānbà from the Èlǔtè (Oirat) tribes;
Mǎlǔkǎi from the Suǒlún (Solon) tribe;
Yīkùdá, chief of the Nèmòlǐhé (Nemoli River);
Kùbài, chief of the Hēilóngjiāng (Amur River);
Bānchán Hútúkètú;
and envoys from Èluósī (Russia) Cágànhán (White Khan)
all came to pay tribute.
Cháoxiǎn came three times.
Ābālāi and Èqí'ěrtú Táijí of Èlǔtè came a second time.
In the spring of the thirteenth year, in the first month, on the *gēngchén* day, the first day of the month,
the Emperor toured the Southern Park.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
an edict was issued to revise the *Tōngjiàn Quánshū* and the *Xiàojīng Yǎnyì*.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
relief was granted from last year's disaster taxes in Hànzhōng, Fèngxiáng, and Xī'ān.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Zhèng Chénggōng was about to attack Táizhōu.
Vice-General Mǎ Xìn betrayed the city
and surrendered to the rebels.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
one-tenth of last year's disaster taxes in Guǎngdé was remitted.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
last year's disaster taxes in Fùyáng and six other counties were remitted.
On the *yǐsì* day,
arrears of taxes from the eighth year in Jiāngxī were remitted.
In the second month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
last year's disaster taxes in Jīngzhōu, Ānlù, Chángdé, Wǔchāng, and Huángzhōu were remitted.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
last year's disaster taxes in Guǎngpíng were remitted.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
last year's disaster taxes in Kělán and Wǔtái were remitted.
On the *wùchén* day,
the Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng was ordered to relocate to Wúzhōu.
The imperial army defeated Lǐ Dìngguó at Nánníng.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
regulations were established for the triennial evaluation of full officials in the Boards and Courts, and the sexennial *jīngchá* examination.
Lǐ Shuàitài was appointed Governor-General of Zhè-Mǐn,
and Wáng Guóguāng as Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Zhào Bùtài was appointed *gùshān ézhēn* of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the Emperor toured the Southern Park
and held an archery contest.
Last year's disaster taxes in Dōngpíng, Pú, and Chángshān were remitted.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Grand Secretary Féng Quán retired.
In the third month, on the *gēngchén* day,
the Emperor toured Yíngtái.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
last year's disaster taxes in Jǐnglín and nine other counties were remitted.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Fèiyǎsīhā was appointed deliberation minister,
and Mǎ Zhīxiān as Governor-General of the Three Borders of Chuān-Shǎn.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Chén Zhīlín was found guilty.
He was dismissed from his original post and sent to Shèngjīng to reside in idleness.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
an edict stated:
"The court appoints the virtuous without partiality.
Although many southerners have been dismissed or demoted recently,
all were rejected based on specific matters,
not due to any favoritism.
All officials should not discriminate by region,
nor form factions,
nor maliciously slander out of resentment,
nor harshly accuse based on perceived slights.
Thus, an even and fair governance can be restored."
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
an edict stated:
"Since I personally took charge of government,
I have worked diligently day and night,
always hoping to glorify the virtues of my ancestors,
and quickly achieve peace and order,
to align with Heaven's will,
and bring prosperity to the people.
When Prince Ruì acted as regent,
he dismissed loyalists and appointed villains,
causing the common people to grumble
and long for my personal rule.
However, there have been winter thunder and spring snow,
falling stones and raining soil,
reported from various places.
Within six years,
peace and order have not been achieved,
and disasters are frequently heard of.
This shows that I have failed the people.
Therefore, I am filled with trepidation and unease,
hoping to make a solemn declaration to Heaven and my ancestors,
and sincerely reflect and admonish myself.
The officials should select an auspicious day and report it to me."
In the summer, fourth month, on the *xīnhài* day,
Zhū Huáruán, the former Prince Yǒng'ān of the Ming dynasty in Guǎngxī, and various local chieftains surrendered.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
sacrifices were offered at the suburban altars and ancestral temples due to calamitous changes.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the imperial army defeated the rebel Yáo Huáng at Yílíng.
On the *rénxū* day,
an earthquake occurred in Tàiyuán and Yángqǔ.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Juéluó Kē'ěrkūn was appointed Minister of Personnel.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
wasteland taxes in Línyóu were remitted.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Liáng Qīngbiāo was appointed Minister of War.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Shàng Kěxǐ recaptured the three counties of Jiēyáng, Pǔníng, and Chénghǎi.
In the fifth month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
wasteland taxes in Dàníng were remitted.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Emperor toured the Southern Park.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Luōtuō was appointed Manchu *gùshān ézhēn* of the Bordered Blue Banner.
Juéluó Lángqiú was dismissed.
Míng'āndálǐ was appointed Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
Zhāng Xuánxī was appointed Governor-General of Xuān-Dà.
Last year's disaster taxes in Jīngmén, Jīngshān and eleven other prefectures and counties,
as well as Xiāngyáng Guard, were remitted.
In the intercalary fifth month, on the *wùshēn* day,
the Emperor toured Yíngtái.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
local officials from Dūkāng and other prefectures in Guǎngxī surrendered.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the Qiánqīnggōng, Kūnnínggōng, Jiāotàidiàn, and the Jǐngrén, Yǒngshòu, Chénggān, Yìkūn, Zhōngcuì, and Chǔxiù Palaces were completed.
Láng Tíngzuǒ was appointed Governor-General of Jiāngnán and Jiāngxī,
and Liú Hànzuò as Fujian Provincial Governor.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Zhāng Cháolín was appointed Jiangxi Provincial Governor.
In the sixth month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
an edict stated:
"Manchu bondservants were all acquired through conquest,
thus strict laws were established to deter escape.
In recent years, the chain of implication has been endless,
which grieves my heart.
These servants
are also children of others.
If bound by grace,
how could they not feel gratitude?
If they are abused at will,
what good are strict laws?
Henceforth, my intentions should be understood."
On the *rénchén* day,
an earthquake with sound occurred in Jǔzhōu.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
last year's wasteland taxes in Táoyuán were remitted.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Tián Jílín, the local chieftain of Róngměi, surrendered.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
*Gùshān Ézhēn* Lángsài was ordered to garrison Fújiàn.
Manchu officials assigned to supervise tax collection in the directly-administered provinces were withdrawn.
Huáng Sùhé, a rebel leader from Nínghuà, surrendered.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the *dīngwèi* day, the first day of the month,
a ceremony was held at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the imperial army defeated Lóng Tāo, a general of the Ming Prince Guì, in Guǎngxī,
and executed him.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Heshuò Xiāng Qīnwáng Bómùbóguǒ'ěr passed away.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Huáng Wú and other generals of Zhèng Chénggōng surrendered from Hǎichéng.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the Emperor first took his seat in the Qiánqīnggōng.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Tóng Yánnián was appointed Gansu Provincial Governor.
In the eighth month, on the *wùyín* day,
last year's disaster taxes in Guǎngxìn, Ráozhōu, and Ji'ān were remitted.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
disaster taxes for the eleventh and twelfth years in Pútián, Xiānyóu, and Xīngpíng Guard were remitted.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
relief was distributed in the capital region.
On the *rénchén* day,
Huáng Wú was enfeoffed as Hǎichéng Gōng.
The appointment of Manchu officials for customs duties was suspended.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Zhèng Chénggōng's army captured Mǐn'ānzhèn,
and advanced to besiege Fúzhōu;
the imperial army attacked and repelled them.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
disaster taxes for recent years in Shùntiān were remitted.
On the *jǐhài* day,
disaster taxes in Jìngyuǎn, Táomín, and other Guards were remitted.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
it was decreed that a grand review of troops be held every three years,
and this was made into a permanent regulation.
On the *yǐsì* day,
last year's disaster taxes in Dàtóng were remitted.
In the ninth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the imperial army defeated Zhèng Chénggōng's generals at Xiàguān,
and again defeated them at Héngshuǐyáng,
thereby recapturing Zhōushān.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Gu Gōng, an official under Zhèng Chénggōng, surrendered.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Heshuò Sù Qīnwáng Háogé was posthumously enfeoffed as Heshuò Wǔsù Qīnwáng.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
Jiǎng Guózhù was appointed Governor of Ānhuī,
and Tiánú Cāojiāng.
On the day Wùyín,
the Dengwen Drum was established.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the disaster tax for Xuānfǔ was remitted,
and three-tenths for Shénmù County in Yánsuī Town.
On the day Gēngchén,
the Sichuan bandit chiefs Dèng Xīmíng and Zhāng Yuánkǎi led their followers to surrender.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Hú Quáncái was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the emperor visited Nányuàn.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Zhāng Shàng was appointed to pacify Yúnnyáng.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the imperial army recaptured Chénzhōu.
On the day Rényín,
three-tenths of the disaster tax for Héshùn County was remitted.
Péng Hóngshù, the Tusi of Yǒngshùn, led his three zhou, six si, and 380 dong to surrender.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Chén Zhīlín was ordered to return to the capital.
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
the emperor returned to the palace.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the construction of Xīngjīng Mausoleum was completed.
On the day Gēngxū,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Yuánqiū.
On the day Xīnhài,
the emperor visited Nányuàn.
The prohibition against heterodox teachings was strictly reinforced.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the disaster tax for Qīngshuǐ County and Fèngxiáng Suǒ was remitted.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Zhāng Chánggēng was appointed Governor of Húguǎng.
The barren land tax for Hǎizhōu was remitted.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the disaster tax for Luòchuān was remitted.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Dǒng'è Shì, daughter of the Grand Minister Èshuò, was formally enfeoffed as Imperial Noble Consort,
and a general amnesty was granted.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the emperor returned to the palace.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Péncuò Jiāncā was enfeoffed as Chǎnhuà Wáng.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Lǐ Yìnzǔ was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the empress dowager's honorific title was augmented to Zhāoshèng Císhòu Gōngjiǎn Ānyì Zhāngqìng Huángtàihòu.
On the day Wùxū,
a general amnesty was granted.
In this year,
Tǔxiètú Qīnwáng Bādálǐ, Zhuólǐkètú Qīnwáng Wúkèshàn, Dá'ěrhàn Bātúlǔ Jùnwáng Mǎnjūxílí, and Gùlún Éfù Ābùnài Qīnwáng came to court.
Cháoxiǎn,
Hélán,
Tǔlǔfān,
the Chǎnhuà Wáng of Wūsīzàng,
from Kārkā Department Sùotèbá, Yí'ěrdēng Nuóyán, Lǎma Tǎ'ěrdúo'ěrdà Dā'ěrhàn Nuóyán, Chēchén Hàn, and Tǔxiètú Hàn,
from under Tǔxiètú Hàn, Dānijīn Lǎma, Dàiqīng, and É'ěrdéèní Lǎma,
from the Élǔtè Department Dálài Wúbāshí Tàijí, Nèmǔqí Tàijí, Ābālái Nuóyán, Cháhǎn Tàijí, Mǎlái Tàijí, Shíhǔ'ěr Dàiqīng, and É'ěrdéèní Tàijí, and from under Gùshí Hàn, Sèlèng Nuóyán,
and from the Suǒlún Department Dá'ěrbā, all came to present tribute.
Kārkā Tǔxiètú Hàn and Yí'ěrdēng Nuóyán came again.
In the fourteenth year, in spring, in the first month, on the day Xīnhài,
prayers for a good harvest were offered to Shàngdì,
with Tàizǔ Wǔhuángdì as co-sacrificer.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Wèi Yìjiè was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Yí'ěrdé Shī returned.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Zhāng Xuánxī was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì, Shāndōng, and Hénán.
The imperial army defeated Zhèng Chénggōng's general at Wūlóngjiāng,
and again defeated him at Huì'ān County.
On the day Wùwǔ,
an edict stated:
"The imperial examinations for selecting scholars,
and the recommendation of worthy officials by the Board of Civil Office,
are both public institutions of the court.
It is utterly meaningless for ministers and sons to use them to curry favor.
The title of 'teacher and student'
can only be genuinely earned when morality is mutually cultivated
and transmission has a clear origin.
How can one cling to power
and be arbitrarily intimate?
The examiners who select candidates
and officials who recommend subordinates
are always referred to as 'gate students'.
Bribery is openly practiced,
and numerous devious paths emerge.
Seeking connections and forming factions
are mutually encouraged and become a common practice.
I wish all officials, high and low, to put an end to these corrupt practices,
and diligently attend to their duties.
Violators will be punished."
The imperial tombs at Jīnlíng were repaired.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Lú Chóngjùn was appointed Governor-General of Xuāndà.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
an edict stated:
"The rise of Our dynasty
was due to well-regulated military training.
Now the people of the Eight Banners
are lazy in military matters,
resulting in a debilitated army
that is inferior to former times.
This is all because of fixed quotas based on age,
the examination of scholars and children,
who are selected for employment after both the provincial and metropolitan examinations,
as well as the examination by various yamen for 'Tāchìhāhāfān' and 'Bǐtiēshì',
who obtain office merely through literary skills
and are promoted very quickly.
Therefore, people are happy to pursue these paths.
All such practices are to be stopped."
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Měng'é and Tǎ'ěrnà were enfeoffed as Duōluó Jùnwáng,
Duō'ěrbó as Duōluó Bèilè,
and the Imperial Noble Consort's father Èshuò as Third Class Count.
In the second month, on the day Wùyín,
sacrifices were offered to the Gods of Earth and Grain.
The Confucian scholars were ordered to compile and edit the Yìjīng.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Zhū Yùnqián, the former Chóngyáng Wáng of the Ming dynasty, and others surrendered.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
sacrifices were offered at the Temple of Past Emperors.
On the day Jǐhài,
the law on harboring fugitives was relaxed.
Sàiyīndálǐ was appointed Manchu Gùshān Ézhēn of the Plain White Banner.
On the day Rényín,
there was an earthquake with sound in Yúnzhèn, Shānxī.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the previous year's disaster tax for Miǎnyáng and Yìyáng was remitted.
In the third month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
Tàizōng Wénhuángdì was enshrined as co-sacrificer at the Yuánqiū and the Qígǔ Tán.
Duōluó Jùnwáng Tǎ'ěrnà passed away.
On the day Rényín,
Tàizǔ Wǔhuángdì and Tàizōng Wénhuángdì were enshrined as co-sacrificers at the Fāngzé.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
as the co-sacrificial rites were completed,
a general amnesty was granted throughout the empire.
On the day Jiǎyín,
an edict was issued to seek lost books.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Kǒngzǐ's title was restored to Zhìshèng Xiānshī.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Dìngyuǎn Dàjiāngjūn Jìdù's army returned.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the day Jiǎxū,
Páng Guó'ān and other Yao officials of the twelve dong in Xīngníng County, affected by lightning, surrendered.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Zhèng Zhīlóng was exiled to Nínggǔtǎ.
On the day Guǐwèi,
there was a major earthquake in Wēi and Mào zhou, Bǎoníng Prefecture, Sìchuān.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Jìxíhā was appointed Manchu Dūtǒng of the Bordered Red Banner.
On the day Dīnghài,
due to prolonged drought,
leniency was shown in criminal cases.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
prayers for rain were offered at the suburban altar;
before returning to the palace,
there was heavy rain.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the emperor visited Nányuàn.
On the day Wùxū,
Shèngjīng Fèngtiān Fǔ was established.
In the fifth month, on the first day Guǐmǎo,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Dàolā was appointed Mongol Gùshān Ézhēn of the Bordered Red Banner.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Jìdù was enfeoffed as Héshuò Jiǎn Qīnwáng.
On the day Dīngsì,
Juéluó Yītú was appointed Minister of War.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the emperor returned to the palace.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnsì,
the previous year's disaster tax for Zhāngdé and Wèihuī prefectures was remitted.
On the day Réngwǔ,
the previous year's disaster tax for Wǔlíng County was remitted.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Hóng Chéngchóu resigned due to illness.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Bǐngchén,
Left Censor-in-Chief Wèi Yìjiè was stripped of his office,
but allowed to continue his duties under penalty.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Zhū Zhīxī was appointed Governor-General of River Conservancy.
In the eighth month, on the day Rénshēn,
Dūn was ordered to be appointed as Zǒngguǎn,
stationed in Shèngjīng.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the corvée and taxes for fugitive peasants on barren lands in Shānxī were remitted.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Zhèng Chénggōng attacked Táizhōu.
Cài Qióngzhī, Daò of Shàotái, rebelled
and surrendered to the bandits.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
aid was given to poor soldiers of the Eight Banners.
In the ninth month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
Kàng Déshí was appointed as Cáo Yùn Zǒngdū,
and Lǐ Guóyīng as Chuān-Shǎnxānbiān Zǒngdū.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the imperial lectures on the Classics were held for the first time.
Jiǎ Hànfù was appointed as Hénán Xúnfǔ.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Gāo Mínzhān was appointed as Sìchuān Xúnfǔ.
Autumn executions in the directly administered provinces were suspended.
On the day Bǐngyín,
the imperial army retook Mǐn'ānzhèn.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
there was an audible earthquake in the capital.
On the day Wùchén,
an edict stated:
"Since ancient times, changes do not occur without reason;
they are often due to human affairs.
I have personally governed for seven years,
and my administration has been amiss,
leading to heavenly chastisement as a warning,
with the audible earthquake.
I shall diligently examine myself,
and all civil and military officials should also work together to fulfill their duties.
If I have shortcomings,
my assisting ministers must report them without concealment."
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Rénshēn,
the start of daily lectures was announced by sacrificing to the Former Sage Kǒngzǐ in the Hóngdédiàn.
Disaster taxes from the previous year in Xīnlè were remitted.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Gùshān Érzhēn Zhào Bùtài was ordered to be stationed in Jiāngníng.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
the fourth imperial son was born.
The comprehensive book on taxes and corvée was revised.
On the day Xīnsì,
the emperor visited Nányuàn.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
military drills were reviewed.
On the day Dīnghài,
the Kǒngzǐ Temple was repaired.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the emperor returned to the palace.
On the day Gēngyín,
Liáng Huàfèng was redesignated as Shuǐshī Zǒngbīngguān,
stationed in Chóngmíng.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Lǐ Zhènyè, Zhāng Wǒpú, and other examiners from Shùntiān were executed in the marketplace for taking bribes.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the Zhāoshìdiàn and Fèngxiāndiàn were completed.
In the eleventh month, on the day Rénchén,
the emperor visited Nányuàn.
The fifth imperial son, Chángníng, was born.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Ān Jùnwáng Yuèlè was promoted to Qīnwáng.
On the day Gēngxū,
disaster taxes in Jíshuǐ and eight other counties were remitted.
On the day Wùwǔ,
disaster taxes in Bà, Bǎodǐ, and twenty-eight other prefectures and counties,
and in Bǎo'ān and four other garrisons were remitted.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Tián Guóqīn and other bandits from Jīngzhōu surrendered.
On the day Rénxū,
Sūn Kěwàng, a general of the Míng Guìwáng, surrendered.
Gùshān Bèizi Tūnqíkā was stripped of his title for his crimes.
In the twelfth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
Hóng Chéngchóu was again ordered to manage the five provinces,
and together with Luótuō and others, to take Guìzhōu.
Disaster taxes in Xīnjiàn and Fēngchéng were remitted.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Sūn Kěwàng was enfeoffed as Yìwáng.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Wú Sānguì was ordered to advance from Sìchuān,
Zhào Bùtài from Guǎngxī,
and Luótuō from Húnán to take Guìzhōu.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Tán Xīnchuán and other generals of the Míng Guìwáng surrendered.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
because the empress dowager's illness had recovered,
banner soldiers were rewarded,
and poor commoners were relieved.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn,
Bìxīlèrtú Hán of the Kā'ěrkǎ tribe, Bīngtútáijí, É'ěrdéníwéizhēngnuóyán, Wúbāshí Nàyán, Wánshūkè Nuóyán from under Tǔxiè Tútán,
Yīlāgǔkèsān, son of Àoqílèrtútáijí of the Èlǔtè tribe, Bāndì Dàhútúkètú, Chuòkètútáijí, Bātúlǔtáijí, Dálàiwūbāshítáijí,
Mǎlǔkà and Hǔ'ěrgéwú'ěrdáhàn of the Suǒlún tribe,
Tōukēluólè Shì and Nándí'ōu of the Dōngyí,
Dálàilāmǎ and Bānchán Hútúkètú all came to pay tribute.
Cháoxiǎn came three times.
In the fifteenth year, spring, the first month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
a great amnesty was declared.
An edict stated:
"For emperors and kings ruling the world with filiality,
there is no greater ritual than serving one's parents.
Recently, Her Majesty the Empress Dowager's sacred health was unwell,
and I was anxious day and night.
Thanks to Heaven's grace,
she is now fully recovered.
Encountering this great joy,
special favor should be extended.
From the princes and dukes downwards,
all civil and military officials within and outside the capital,
shall receive additional grants.
Arrears of taxes in the directly administered provinces
shall all be exempted.
All errors and mistakes of officials and commoners
shall be pardoned."
On the day Rénchén,
the sacrifices to the Tángzǐ were suspended.
Duōluó Xìnjùnwáng Duōní was appointed Ānyuǎnjìngkòu Dàjiāngjūn,
leading troops to conquer Yúnnán.
On the day Wùwǔ,
sacrifices were made at the Huánqiú.
On the day Jǐwèi,
sacrifices were made at the Fāngzé.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
sacrifices were made at the Tàimiào and Shèjì,
due to the empress dowager's recovery from illness.
The fourth imperial son died.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Zhōu Zhàonán was appointed Yánsuí Xúnfǔ.
In the second month, on the day Jiǎxū,
the Jīfǔ was relieved.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
disaster taxes from the previous year in Wǔqīng and Huò were remitted.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the tax quota for Liáoyáng was reduced.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Zhāng Jīng and other bandit leaders from Eastern Sìchuān surrendered.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
officials from the Six Boards and Censorate were ordered to submit proposals for affairs.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the imperial lectures on the Classics were held.
In the third month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
Yán Wéilóng and others of Lǐ Dìngguó's faction captured Héngzhōu,
but the imperial army attacked and drove them away.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the eunuch Wú Liángfǔ was executed for taking bribes.
On the day Rénzǐ,
barren land taxes in Xiāngyáng and Yúnyáng were remitted.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the daughter of the Kē'ěrqìn Bātúlǔwáng was posthumously enfeoffed as Dàofēi.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the fourth imperial son was posthumously enfeoffed as Héshuò Róngqīnwáng.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Sūn Chéng'ēn and other successful candidates received their various degrees.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
the imperial army defeated the bandits at Hézhōu,
and captured Chóngqìng.
On the day Guǐwèi,
disaster taxes for thirteen years in Jiāngxià and seven other counties were remitted.
On the day Bǐngxū,
an archery contest was held at Jǐngshān.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
barren land taxes in Chúnhuà were remitted.
Grand Secretary Wáng Yǒngjí was dismissed for his crimes.
On the day Rénchén,
Grand Secretary Chén Zhīlín was again exiled to Shèngjīng for his crimes.
In the fifth month, on the first day Dīngyǒu,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Wèi Zhōuzuò was transferred to be Lìbù Shàngshū.
On the day Wùshēn,
Liú Chāng was appointed Gōngbù Shàngshū.
The method of official selection was revised.
On the day Xīnhài,
Zhèng Chénggōng's general attacked Chénghǎi,
and guerrilla commander Liú Jìnzhōng rebelled with the city
and surrendered to Chénggōng.
On the day Rénzǐ,
arrears of salt tax from before the eleventh year in Shāndōng were remitted.
On the day Jǐwèi,
an archery contest was held at Jǐngshān.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
officials of the Zhānshìfǔ were reduced.
On the day Rénxū,
Hè Jiǔyí, a bandit general from Guǎngxī, attacked Bīnzhōu,
but the imperial troops attacked and defeated him.
On the day Guǐhài,
Hú Shì'ān, Wèi Zhōuzuò, and Lǐ Wèi were appointed Nèiyuàn Dàxuéshì.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the imperial army retook Yuánjìng,
and advanced to take Guìyáng, Píngyuè, Zhènyuǎn and other prefectures,
Nándān, Nàdì, Dúshān and other subprefectures,
and the native chieftain of Fǔníng all surrendered.
In the sixth month, on the day Wùchén,
Wú Sānguì and others defeated Lǐ Dìngguó's general Liú Zhèngguó at Sānpō,
conquered Zūnyì,
and captured Kāizhōu.
On Xīnwèi,
Zhào Tíngchén was appointed Governor of Guìzhōu.
On Rénshēn,
Tóng Guóqì was appointed Governor of Zhèjiāng,
and Sū Hóngzǔ was appointed Governor of Nángàn.
On Bǐngzǐ,
the government forces defeated sea pirates at Báishā.
On Xīnsì,
Lǐ Qīfèng was appointed Viceroy of Liǎngguǎng.
On Jiǎshēn,
Wáng Chóngjiǎn was appointed Minister of the Board of Rites.
On Rénchén,
the fixed taxes for fifteen prefectures and counties, including Jìng and Yuánlíng, and nine military garrisons (wèi suǒ) in Píngxī, were remitted.
On Guǐsì,
Zhèng Chénggōng attacked Wēnzhōu,
and captured Píngyáng and Ruì'ān.
In autumn, the seventh month, on Jǐhài,
the position of Viceroy of Xuāndà was abolished.
On Jǐyǒu,
Pān Cháoxuǎn was appointed Governor of Bǎodìng.
On Gēngxū,
Shā'ěrhǔdá attacked the Russians (Luóshà),
and defeated them.
The Grand Secretaries of the Three Inner Courts (Nèi Sān Yuàn Dàxuéshì) were renamed Grand Secretaries of the Palace Halls (Diàn Gé Dàxuéshì).
The Hànlín Yuàn and the official position of Chancellor (Zhǎng Yuàn Xuéshì) were established.
Thirty Censors (Yùshǐ) were added to each circuit (Dào).
On Jǐwèi,
the disaster taxes from the previous year for ten prefectures and counties, including Guìyáng and Héngyáng, were remitted.
On Jiǎzǐ,
Bāhā, Fèiyánggǔ, Guōmài, Túlùhuì, Mǎ'ěrjìhā, Èmòkètú, Kūnbātúlǔ, Wūbùgédémo'ěrgēnpáo, Kālán Tú, Èsāi, Bóluòsāilěng, Bātmǎ, and Bātài were all appointed Inner Ministers (Nèi Dàchén);
Zhào Guózuò was appointed Viceroy of Zhèjiāng;
and Lǐ Shuàitài was given sole command over Fújiàn.
In the eighth month, on Guǐyǒu,
Lǐ Xiǎnguì was appointed Gūsān Ézhēn of the Bordered White Banner Han Army.
On Bǐngzǐ,
Dūoní and others were issued imperial edicts,
granting them strategies.
Lǐ Dìngguó's general Wáng Xīng and the Pacification Commissioner (Xuānwèishǐ) of Shuǐxī, Ān Kūn, and others surrendered.
On Guǐsì,
the Imperial Lecture (Jīngyán) was held.
In the ninth month, on Dīngyǒu,
Sūn Tǎ was appointed Gūsān Ézhēn of the Bordered Blue Banner Mongol Army.
On Gēngxū,
the regulations for capital punishment in the Court of Colonial Affairs (Lǐfān Yuàn) were revised.
On Jǐyǒu,
Néngtú was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief (Zuǒ Dūyùshǐ).
On Rénzǐ,
gold was bestowed upon the officers and soldiers of the Bordered Yellow, Plain Yellow, and Plain White Banners.
On Jiǎyín,
the Grand Secretaries of the Inner Court (Nèi Yuàn Dàxuéshì), Juéluó Bāhāná and Jīn Zhījùn, were renamed Grand Secretaries of the Zhōnghé Hall;
Èsèhēi and Chéng Kègǒng were renamed Grand Secretaries of the Bǎohé Hall;
Jiǎng Hèdé and Liú Zhèngzōng were renamed Grand Secretaries of the Wénhuá Hall;
Hóng Chéngchóu, Fù Yǐjiàn, and Hú Shì'ān were renamed Grand Secretaries of the Wǔyīng Hall;
Wèi Zhōuzuò was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wényuān Pavilion;
and Lǐ Wèi was appointed Grand Secretary of the Dōnggé.
On Jǐwèi,
the famine taxes for the twelfth and thirteenth years for the three prefectures of Fúzhōu, Xīnghuà, and Jiànníng,
and Fúníng Prefecture, were remitted.
On Guǐhài,
funds were disbursed from the treasury to the families of soldiers on campaign.
In winter, the tenth month, on Rénwǔ,
Zǔ Zhòngguāng was appointed Governor of Shùntiān.
Jīngzhōu, Xiāngyáng, and Ānlù experienced continuous heavy rain,
the river overflowed,
and over ten thousand people were drowned.
In the eleventh month, on Jiǎwǔ, the first day of the month,
sea pirates attacked Luòyáng's inner harbor,
and the government forces defeated them.
On Yǐwèi,
famine taxes for Yúnnyáng and Xiāngyáng were remitted.
On Gēngzǐ,
the official ranks and grades for female officials in the palace were established.
On Xīnchǒu,
three-tenths of the disaster taxes for Lín Xiàn were remitted.
The Jiangnan Examination Officials Fāng Yóu, Qián Kāizōng, and others were executed for accepting bribes.
In the twelfth month, on Rénshēn,
Suǒhún was appointed Gūsān Ézhēn of the Bordered White Banner Manchu Army.
On Jiǎxū,
disaster taxes for Wǔtái were remitted.
On Rénwǔ,
the former Míng imperial family member Zhū Yìwěng led a crowd to surrender.
On Yǐyǒu,
Wūhè was appointed Minister of the Board of Rites.
Disaster taxes from the previous year for eight counties, including Shānyīn, were remitted.
On Wùzǐ,
Míng'āndálǐ was appointed General of Ānnán,
and commanded an army to garrison Guìzhōu.
On Jǐchǒu,
an imperial edict stated:
"The people of Chuān, Hú, Yún, and Guì [Sìchuān, Húguǎng, Yúnnán, Guìzhōu]
are all Our subjects.
Since the rebellions began,
they have long suffered through fire and water.
Now, wherever the great army reaches,
those who come to surrender
shall be treated with special care and comfort,
and allowed to settle.
Those who can exert themselves and achieve merit
will not be denied titles and rewards."
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn (Korea),
and from the Khalkha (Kā'ěrkǎ) tribe, Dò'ěrgéqí Nuòyán, Gá'ěrdāng Táijí, Tǔxiètú Hán, Bìxílè'ěrtú Hán, Dānjīn Lǎma;
from the Oirat (Èlǔtè) tribe, Ābālái Nuòyán;
under Chēchén Táijí, Chēchén Èmùbù and Èqílertú Táijí;
from the Solon (Suǒlún) tribe, Dábadài;
from the Khurkha (Kù'ěrkǎ) tribe, Tǎ'ěrshàn;
the chieftain of the 'Dog Kingdom' (Shǐ Quǎn Guó) Tì'ěrkù;
and the Dálài Lǎma all came to offer tribute.
Cháoxiǎn, Khalkha Tǔxiètú Hán, and Oirat Ābālái Nuòyán came again.
In the sixteenth year, spring, the first month, on Jiǎwǔ,
Guìwáng's general Tán Wén attacked Chóngqìng,
but his brother Tán Yì killed him,
and Tán Hóng and others surrendered.
On Dīngyǒu,
Xú Yǒngzhèng was appointed Governor of Fújiàn.
On Gēngzǐ,
Duōní conquered Yúnnán,
and reported the victory.
Originally,
Duōní, Wú Sānguì, and Zhào Bùtài combined their forces at Yánglǎobǎo in Píngyuè Prefecture,
and advanced to Yúnnán in three routes.
Duōní entered from Guìyáng,
crossed the Pán Jiāng to Sōnglíng Wèi,
and encountered Bái Wénxuǎn,
whom he greatly defeated.
Sānguì went from Zūnyì to Qīxīngguān,
but could not advance,
so he took a secret path through Shuǐxī to Wūsà.
Zhào Bùtài went from Dūyún to Luóyán Dù on the Pán Jiāng,
defeated the defending general Lǐ Chéngjué at Shāngǔkǒu,
and further defeated Lǐ Dìngguó at Shuānghékǒu.
All his advances were victorious,
and they all arrived in Yúnnán,
entering the provincial capital.
Lǐ Dìngguó and Bái Wénxuǎn escorted Guìwáng to Yǒngchāng.
On Guǐmǎo,
Lín Tiānqìng was appointed Governor of Yúnnán.
On Jiǎchén,
Bāhǎi was appointed Angban Janggin (Āngbāng Zhāngjūn),
stationed to guard Nínggǔtǎ.
On Xīnhài,
horses, cattle, and sheep were bestowed upon the impoverished princes of the Outer Mongol banners.
On Guǐchǒu,
Zhào Tíngchén was appointed Viceroy of Yúnguì,
and Biàn Sānyuán was appointed Governor of Guìzhōu.
In the second month, on Bǐngyín,
the disaster taxes from the previous year for the military colonies (tún) of Xīnzhuāng and others in Tóngguān Wèi were remitted.
On Dīngmǎo,
sea pirates attacked Wēnzhōu,
and the government forces defeated them.
On Gēngwǔ,
as Yúnnán and Guìzhōu were pacified,
it was ordered that the metropolitan examination (Huìshì) be held this autumn.
On Xīnwèi,
the disaster taxes from the previous year for nine prefectures and counties, including Jīngzhōu and Qiánjiāng, and the two military garrisons (wèi) of Miǎnyáng and Ānlù, were remitted.
On Bǐngzǐ,
Luōtuō and others were ordered to return to the capital,
and Míng'āndálǐ was to garrison Jīngzhōu.
On Rénwǔ,
Xǔ Wénxiù was appointed Governor of Shāndōng.
In the third month, on Bǐngshēn,
Jiǎng Guózhù was appointed Governor of Jiāngníng.
On Jǐhài,
Zhāng Zhòngdì was appointed Governor of Yánsuī.
On Wùshēn,
Zhū Yīzhù was appointed Governor of Ānhuī.
Zhèng Chénggōng attacked Tàipíng County in Zhèjiāng,
and the government forces defeated him.
On Jǐyǒu,
the Imperial Lecture (Jīngyán) was held.
On Jiǎyín,
Wú Sānguì was ordered to guard Yúnnán,
Shàng Kěxǐ to guard Guǎngdōng,
and Gěng Jìmào to guard Sìchuān.
On Dīngsì,
disaster taxes for six counties, including Xiāngyáng, were remitted.
In the intercalary third month, on Rénxū,
Grand Secretary Hú Shì'ān resigned due to illness.
On Dīngmǎo,
regulations for corruption offenses were established:
those who embezzled ten taels or more were exiled to the north,
and those who deserved a beating (zhàngzé) were not allowed to commute their punishment with a fine.
On Jiǎshēn,
the disaster taxes from the previous year for Zhōngxiáng County were remitted.
Túhǎi had committed a crime,
but was pardoned.
On Bǐngxū,
Tán Hóng was enfeoffed as Marquis Mùyì,
and Tán Yì as Marquis Xiànghuà.
On Dīnghài,
Zhāng Zìdé was appointed Governor of Shǎnxī.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *Jiǎyín* day,
Duōní and Wú Sānguì's forces captured Zhènnán Zhōu.
Bái Wénxuǎn set fire to the Láncāng Jiāng iron bridge and fled.
Our army advanced and captured Yǒngchāng.
Lǐ Dìngguó escorted Prince Guì to Téngyuè,
ambushing our forces at Mópán Shān.
Our army fought valiantly
and recaptured Téngyuè.
In the fifth month, on the *Rénxū* day,
Nánníng, Tàipíng, and Sī'ēn prefectures in Guǎngxī were pacified.
On the *Jǐsì* day,
Liú Bǐngzhèng was appointed Governor of Níngxià.
Mǎnzhūxílǐ was promoted and enfeoffed as Héshuò Dá'ěrhàn Bātúlǔ Qīnwáng.
On the *Wùyín* day,
government troops attacked Chénggōng at Dìngguān,
defeating him
and capturing or killing many.
On the *Xīnsì* day,
thirty thousand *liǎng* of silver from the imperial treasury were allocated,
half for relief of the poor commoners in Yúnnán and Guìzhōu,
and half for soldiers' pay.
In the sixth month, on the *Gēngzǐ* day,
Lǐ Hào, King of the Cháoxiǎn Kingdom, passed away.
On the *Rénzǐ* day,
Zhèng Chénggōng captured Zhènjiāng Fǔ.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *Dīngmǎo* day,
Dásù was appointed General of Ānnán,
and together with Suǒhóng, Láitǎ, and others, led troops to campaign against Zhèng Chénggōng.
On the *Bǐngzǐ* day,
Zhèng Chénggōng attacked Jiāngníng.
On the *Gēngchén* day,
the Emperor visited Nányuàn.
On the *Jiǎshēn* day,
he returned to the palace.
In the eighth month, on the *Jǐchǒu* new moon,
government forces in Jiāngnán defeated Zhèng Chénggōng at Gāoshān,
capturing Grand Coordinator Gān Huī and others,
and burning over five hundred enemy ships.
Chénggōng was defeated and fled.
Our army pursued to Guāzhōu,
where the enemy forces were utterly routed.
Previously,
Chénggōng, with an army of over one hundred thousand
and several thousand warships,
reached the outskirts of Jiāngníng city,
setting up eighty-three camps,
stretching continuously,
and deploying large cannons, landmines, scaling ladders, and wooden palisades
for a prolonged siege.
His military display was very impressive.
Our forces, led by Gáchǔhā, Mǎ'ěrsài, and others, came from Jīngzhōu with a naval fleet to reinforce,
meeting with Liáng Huàfèng, Commander-in-Chief of the Sūsōng naval forces, and Guerrilla Commander Xú Dēngdì, Participatory Commander Zhāng Guójùn, and others, who each arrived with their troops.
Governor-General Láng Tíngzuǒ united the forces for a combined battle,
advancing by both land and water,
and thus reported a victory.
On the *Gēngyín* day,
the Emperor attended the imperial lectures.
On the *Guǐsì* day,
the Emperor visited Nányuàn.
Liú Zhīyuán was appointed Grand General of Zhènhǎi,
stationed at Zhènjiāng with Meilè Zhāngjīng Zhāng Yuánxūn and others.
Cài Shìyīng was appointed Governor of Fèngyáng
and concurrently Governor-General of Grain Transport;
Yí Yǒngguì was appointed Governor of Ānhuī
and concurrently Grand Coordinator of Naval Affairs.
On the *Bǐngshēn* day,
Wǔ Gōngzì, a general of the Ānnán Kingdom, sent an envoy to offer submission to Hóng Chéngchóu's army.
On the *Wùxū* day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the *Jiǎchén* day,
Zhèng Chénggōng again attacked Chóngmíng,
and government forces defeated him.
On the *Yǐsì* day,
the Emperor visited Nányuàn.
On the *Bǐngwǔ* day,
he returned to the palace.
In the ninth month, on the *Gēngshēn* day,
taxes for Táizhōu from the fourth to the tenth year, affected by bandits, were remitted.
On the *Yǐhài* day,
Lù Yuánwén and others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with differing ranks.
On the *Dīngchǒu* day,
Dù Lìdé was appointed Minister of Punishments.
On the *Wùyín* day,
a posthumous title was granted to the late King Lǐ Hào of Cháoxiǎn,
and his heir apparent Yuān was enfeoffed as King.
On the *Gēngchén* day,
Hǎi'ěrtú was appointed *Gùshān Ézhēn* of the Bordered Blue Banner Han Army.
On the *Xīnsì* day,
the ancestral tombs in Xīngjīng were honored as Yǒnglíng.
On the *Jiǎshēn* day,
the Emperor visited Nányuàn.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *Gēngxū* day,
Hóng Chéngchóu resigned his post as Director-General due to illness.
On the *Jiǎyín* day,
Āhàn, the *Dá'ěrhàn* Prince of the Nàimàn tribe, was stripped of his title and reduced to a commoner for his crimes.
In the eleventh month, on the *Jǐwèi* day,
the former crimes of the late Prince Xùn Mǎndáhǎi, Prince Duānzhòng Bóluò, and Prince Jìngjǐn Níkān were discussed.
The titles of Prince Xùn and Prince Duānzhòng were abolished,
and their sons were demoted to *Duōluó Bèilè*.
Prince Jìngjǐn alone was exempted.
On the *Rénxū* day,
Gōng Wòhè and Gōng Pǔ'ěrbén were appointed Grand Ministers of the Interior.
On the *Bǐngyín* day,
the Emperor hunted in the imperial preserve.
On the *Rénshēn* day,
he reached Chāngpíng Zhōu.
The Emperor poured libations at the tomb of the Ming Chóngzhēn Emperor,
and dispatched Scholar Málèjí to sacrifice at Wáng Chéng'ēn's tomb.
On the *Jiǎxū* day,
officials were sent to sacrifice at the various Ming imperial tombs,
and the number of tomb households was increased,
repairs were enhanced,
and logging and gathering were prohibited.
On the *Wùyín* day,
the sixth imperial son Qíshòu was born.
On the *Jǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor stopped at Tāngquán.
On the *Jiǎshēn* day,
he stopped at Sāntúnyíng.
The Ming Chóngzhēn Emperor was posthumously granted the title Zhuāngliè Mǐn Huángdì.
On the *Bǐngxū* day,
Wú Sānguì captured Yuánjiāng.
In the twelfth month, on the *Wùxū* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *Yǐsì* day,
the regulations for the hereditary succession of official ranks were established.
On the *Gēngxū* day,
princesses' titles were augmented.
On the *Rénzǐ* day,
Gěng Jìmào was ordered to relocate and garrison Guǎngxī.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn;
Dānjīn Lǎma, Tǔxiètú Hàn, Chēchén Hàn, Bìxīlè'ěrtú Hàn, Lǔbùzāng Nuòyán, Chēchén Jìnóng, Kūndúlún Tuōyīn, and Duō'ěrjì Táijí under Tǔxiètú Hàn of the Kā'ěrkā tribe;
Ābùlái Nuòyán, Dálái Wúbàxī Nuòyán, and Éqí'ěrtú Táijí of the Èlǔtè tribe;
Hán Pīlǐ, the headman of Nángílètún in Hēilóngjiāng;
and Hú'ěrgé Wū'ěrdá'ěrhàn of the Suǒlún tribe, all came to offer tribute.
Cháoxiǎn,
and Tǔxiètú Hàn and Dānjīn Lǎma of the Kā'ěrkā tribe, came again.
In the seventeenth year, spring, the first month, on the *Bǐngyín* day,
Zhū Guózhì was appointed Governor of Jiāngníng.
On the *Gēngchén* day,
the Wen Miao (Confucian Temple) in the capital was completed.
Néngtú was appointed Minister of Punishments.
On the *Xīnsì* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“Since ancient times, emperors,
who rule the world,
if their governance has been effective,
then the joy is shared with the realm;
if their civilizing influence has not been achieved,
then the fault lies with Us.
Revering Heaven and diligently serving the people,
the Way does not go beyond this.
We, having continued the grand legacy of Our ancestors,
have striven for good governance
for seventeen years.
Yet, the people's lives are still not entirely fulfilled,
corrupt officials are still not entirely eliminated,
and hidden rebellions in Diān and Qián are not yet pacified,
with frequent reports of conscription.
Reflecting repeatedly,
We are truly without virtue,
failing the mandate bestowed by Heaven,
and unworthy of the trust placed by Our ancestors,
neglecting the grace of the Empress Dowager's education,
and disappointing the hopes of the myriad people within the Four Seas.
Whenever We consider this,
We dare not feel at ease.
Therefore, in the first month of this year,
We have offered sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the Altars of Land and Grain,
expressing Our sincere feelings and taking responsibility.
From now on,
all celebratory memorials and reports for New Year's Day, Winter Solstice, and Our birthday,
are hereby stopped.
A special general amnesty is granted:
for officials and commoners, except for the ten abominable crimes and capital offenses,
all sentences are reduced by one degree,
and those for military exile and below
are all pardoned.
Arrears of taxes in the provinces
are all remitted.
Those with merit shall be recorded,
and those with filial piety and righteousness shall be honored.
This is proclaimed to the entire realm,
so that all may know.”
Taxes for Táozhōu Wèi from the previous year, affected by disaster, were remitted.
On the *Jiǎshēn* day,
taxes for Jǔ and Níngyáng's twelve *zhōu* and *xiàn* from the previous year, affected by disaster, were remitted.
In the second month, on the day Wùzǐ,
an edict ordered the Grand Secretaries and Ministers of the capital to declare their own unworthiness.
Those from the third rank and below
were personally assessed and screened.
Wú Sānguì's army defeated the bandits at Pǔ'ěr.
General-in-chief Dingnán Zhào Bùtài's army returned.
On the day Rénchén,
Minister Liú Chāng declared himself old and
retired.
On the day Guǐsì,
the previous year's disaster taxes were remitted for Guìyáng and five other prefectures, and for the local chieftains.
The position of Fèngyáng巡撫 (Xúnfǔ) was re-established,
stationed at Tàizhōu.
On the day Wùxū,
the Governors-general and Governors of the directly-administered provinces and Han officials of the third rank and above in the capital were screened and assessed,
and Shí Shēn, Féng Pǔ, and others were recorded, dismissed, or demoted with varying degrees of punishment.
On the day Rényín,
Lín Qǐlóng was appointed Fèngyáng 巡撫 (Xúnfǔ).
The previous year's disaster taxes were remitted for the three prefectures of Huái, Yáng, and Fèng,
and for Xúzhōu.
It was decided that in the first month of each spring, the joint sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, Sun, Moon, and all gods would be held at the Dàxiǎngdiàn.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Board of Rites was instructed:
"Previously, the prayer for good harvest in the first month of spring was held at the Dàxiǎngdiàn.
Now that the joint sacrifice is held at the Dàxiǎngdiàn,
the prayer for good harvest will henceforth be held at the Huánqiū."
On the day Rénzǐ,
the previous year's disaster taxes for Liángchéngsuǒ were remitted.
In the third month, on the day Guǐhài,
the military system for the two principalities of Píngxī and Jìngnán was established.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Shǐ Jìgōng was appointed Zhèjiāng 巡撫 (Xúnfǔ).
On the day Xīnwèi,
the Board of Rites was instructed:
"I have examined the old regulations,
and besides the joint sacrifice at the end of the year,
there is the rite of joint sacrifice at the Fèngxiāndiàn.
Henceforth, on New Year's Day, the Empress Dowager's birthday, and My own birthday,
joint sacrifices shall be offered at the Fèngxiāndiàn.
Discuss the rites and rituals in detail and report."
For the crime of the fall of Zhènjiāng,
巡撫 (Xúnfǔ) Jiǎng Guózhù and Tídū Guǎn Xiàozhōng were dismissed from their posts,
spared from death but enslaved,
and Xiéliǎo Fèiyázhù and others were executed in the marketplace.
On the day Jiǎxū,
it was decided that the Han title for Gùshān Èzhēn would be Dūtǒng,
Mèilè Zhāngjīng would be Fùdūtǒng,
Jiǎlǎ Zhāngjīng would be Cānlǐng,
Niúlù Zhāngjīng would be Zuǒlǐng,
and Ángbāng Zhāngjīng would be Zǒngguǎn.
The Manchu titles remained as before.
Yuán Màogōng was appointed Yúnnán 巡撫 (Xúnfǔ).
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
the Emperor attended the Jīngyán lectures.
On the day Guǐwèi,
the titles for the wives and daughters of Princes, Bèilè, Bèizǐ, and Dukes were established.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the helmet and plume regulations for those from Míngōng, Hóu, Bó and below,
and Zhāngjīng and above were revised.
In the fourth month of summer, on the day Bǐngxū,
the previous year's disaster taxes for Bǎodǐ, Fēngrùn, and Wǔqīng were remitted.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Zhāng Chánggēng was appointed Húguǎng Zǒngdū.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Liú Zuòyuǎn was appointed Bǎodìng 巡撫 (Xúnfǔ),
and Zhāng Chūn was appointed Shǎnxī 巡撫 (Xúnfǔ).
On the day Xīnchǒu,
an edict established the punishment for concealing disasters and not reporting them.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Bái Bǐngzhēn was appointed to govern Yúnyáng.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the seventh imperial son, Lóngxǐ, was born.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
joint sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth at the Dàxiǎngdiàn.
On the first day of the fifth month, Ěrmǎo,
Juéluó Yītú was appointed Minister of Personnel.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the previous year's disaster taxes for the five prefectures and counties of Suídé and Fūshī were remitted.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Āsīhā was appointed Minister of War,
and Sūnàhǎi was appointed Minister of Works.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Tóng Zhuàngnián was appointed Dūtǒng of the Bordered Blue Banner Han Army,
and Guōěrtài was appointed Dūtǒng of the Bordered White Banner Mongol Army.
The previous year's disaster taxes for the two garrisons of Yuánzhōu and Zhènyuǎn were remitted.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
an edict stated:
"Previously, I repeatedly issued edicts taking blame and reproaching myself,
but thinking about it now,
they were all mere formalities with little real benefit.
Furthermore, between the twelfth and thirteenth years,
there were occasional errors,
which, although pointed out by censors and
met with punishment,
left this heart feeling uneasy and unresolved.
Now, Heaven has shown warnings,
with severe drought and plague,
and calamities occurring one after another.
Bandits have not ceased,
and the people's lives are distressed.
For this, I deeply reproach myself,
and have no peace day or night.
As for those who were previously punished for their words,
the Board of Personnel shall list their names and report.
As for the advantages and disadvantages concerning state affairs and the people's livelihood,
and My own shortcomings,
each shall speak frankly without concealment."
On the day Gēngchén,
Zhāng Tiānfú was appointed Dūtǒng of the Plain Yellow Banner Han Army.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Juéluó Bāhānà and others, citing the drought, declared their own unworthiness.
The Emperor said:
"Seeing the repeated droughts,
I issued an edict reproaching myself.
Your collective declaration of guilt
is still regarded as a mere formality,
and not My true intention to correct My errors.
Your duty is to draft proposals,
merely adhering to established rules,
unable to each express your own views
to assist Me in My deficiencies.
This is all My fault for not entrusting My ministers.
Henceforth, I shall give you special entrustment.
You should exert your full strength to assist Me,
uphold justice with impartiality,
to fulfill My expectations."
Duōluó Prince Xìn, Duōní's army returned.
On the day Guǐwèi,
the Yúnnán local chieftain Nàlún surrendered.
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
翰林 (Hànlín) officials were first ordered to begin their duties at the Jǐngyùnmén.
Āsīhā concurrently served as the Acting Left Censor-in-chief.
On the day Wùzǐ,
officials were dispatched to inspect prisons.
Yáng Màoxūn was appointed Húguǎng 巡撫 (Xúnfǔ).
The previous year's disaster taxes for the twelve prefectures and counties of Lǐ and Bālíng, and for Yuèzhōu and other garrisons, were remitted.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
additional sacrifices were offered to Shāng Zhōngzōng, Gāozōng, Zhōu Chéngwáng, Kāngwáng, Hàn Wéndì, Sòng Rénzōng, and Míng Xiàozōng at the Temple of Past Emperors.
The temple sacrifices for Liáo Tàizǔ, Jīn Tàizǔ, and Yuán Tàizǔ, and the accompanying sacrifices for Sòng ministers Pān Měi and Zhāng Jùn, were abolished.
Sūnàhǎi was appointed Minister of War.
On the day Guǐsì,
Mùlǐmǎ was appointed Minister of Works,
and Báisèchún was acting Governor-general of River Conservancy.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the Emperor walked to the southern suburbs for fasting and prayers for rain.
On this day,
there was heavy rain.
On the day Wùxū,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Huánqiū,
and it rained again.
On the day Jǐhài,
Grand Secretaries Liú Zhèngzōng, Chéng Kègǒng, and Wèi Yìjiè were dismissed due to their offenses.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
an order was given to review and establish the sacrificial rites for famous mountains, great rivers, and ancient emperors and sages throughout the realm.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the first day Jiǎyín,
Huò Dá concurrently served as the Acting Left Censor-in-chief.
Hèshuò Prince Jiǎn Jìdù passed away.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the surrendered soldiers were organized into ten battalions, including the Zhōngyǒng and Yìyǒng,
subordinate to Wú Sānguì,
and commanded by surrendered generals such as Mǎ Bǎo.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the sacrifice to the Northern Peak was moved to Húnyuánzhōu.
On the day Jǐsì,
the previous year's disaster taxes for the thirteen prefectures and counties of Jīngzhōu and Qíyáng, and for Héngzhōu and other garrisons, were remitted.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the previous year's famine taxes for the seven prefectures and counties of Jūn and Bǎokāng, and for Yún and Xiāng garrisons, were remitted.
Yáng Yì was appointed Minister of Works.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Gěng Jìmào was ordered to relocate to Fújiàn.
Nínggǔtǎ Zǒngguǎn Bāhǎi defeated the Russians in the land of the Shǐquǎnbù tribe,
and pacified and settled over 120 households from fifteen villages of Fèiyákā.
The criminals banished to Xībèiliú were relocated to Nínggǔtǎ.
On the day Gēngchén,
the dispatch of Imperial Censors to patrol directly-administered provinces was suspended.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Luótuō was appointed General Ānnán,
to lead an army to conquer Zhèng Chénggōng.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Néngtú was remitted.
On the *dìnghài* day of the eighth month,
Péng Yǒuyì was appointed Governor of Hénán.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the disaster tax from the previous year was remitted for Huàzhōu, Màomíng, and four other prefectures and counties, and for Gāozhōu Garrison.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the disaster tax from the previous year was remitted for Wǔgāng.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Dāo Mùdǎo, chieftain of Chēlǐ Tǔsī in Yúnnán, came to surrender.
On the *wùxū* day,
Shěn Yǒngzhōng was appointed Commissioner-General (guàyìnjiāngjūn),
to guard Guǎngdōng.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Àixīng'ā was appointed General Dingxi (dìngxījiāngjūn),
to campaign against Lǐ Dìngguó.
On the *rényín* day,
Imperial Noble Consort Dǒng'è Shì passed away,
and court was suspended for five days.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Dǒng'è Shì was posthumously enfeoffed as Empress.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the surrendered general Hǎo Chéngyì rebelled,
captured Qióngzhōu,
and besieged Jiādìng;
the government troops defeated him.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Mùlǐmǎ was appointed Manchu General Commandant (mǎnzhōudūtǒng) of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
On the *guǐchǒu* day, the first day of the ninth month,
Lí Wéiqí, King of the country of Ānnán, presented a memorial and surrendered.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Tóng Fèngcǎi was appointed Governor of Sìchuān.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the rebel general Dèng Yào occupied Hǎikāng;
the government troops attacked and drove him away.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Wáng Dēnglián was appointed Governor of Bǎodìng.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the disaster tax for the fourteenth year was remitted for Bǎochāng and six other counties, and for the two garrisons of Nánzhōu and Sháozhōu.
On the *wùyín* day,
the emperor visited Chāngpíng
to view the tombs of the former Míng dynasty.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
he returned to the palace.
In the winter, on the *dīnghài* day of the tenth month,
Juéluó Yǎbùlán was appointed Minister of Punishments.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the tribute of eagles from Cháoxiǎn was abolished.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the emperor visited the near suburbs.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
he returned to the palace.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Guō Kē was appointed Minister of Works.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the disaster tax from the previous year was remitted for Suīzhōu, Shāngqiū, and eleven other prefectures and counties, and for the two garrisons of Guīdé and Suīyáng.
On the *jiǎyín* day of the eleventh month,
the disaster tax from the previous year was remitted for Zhàozhōu, Bǎixiāng, and four other prefectures and counties, and for Zhēndìng Garrison.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the disaster tax from the previous year was remitted for Níngzhōu, Shàngráo, and forty-six other prefectures and counties.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the officials for inspecting punishments (xùxíngguān) in the directly administered provinces were abolished.
Míng'āndálǐ, general of Ānnán, returned with his army.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Grand Secretary Liú Zhèngzōng was dismissed due to an offense.
On the *rénxū* day,
Imperial Censors were again dispatched to patrol and inspect the directly administered provinces.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Prince Jìngjǐn Nísīhā passed away.
On the *wùyín* day,
the disaster tax was remitted for Suīzhōu, Yúchéng, and six other prefectures and counties.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the disaster tax from the previous year was remitted for Wǔhé and Āndōng.
On the *guǐsì* day of the twelfth month,
the disaster tax was remitted for Pīzhōu, Sùqiān, and four other prefectures and counties.
On the *wùxū* day,
the disaster tax was remitted for Qìngdū.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the eighth imperial son, Yǒnggàn, was born.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn,
Dānjīn Lǎma of the Khalkha tribe,
Wànshūkè Nòyán and the seven banners under Tǔxiētú Khan,
Èqílǐ Khan of the Oirat tribe,
the Dàlái Lǎma, Bānchán Hútúkètú,
Ālǐlùkèsān Tuōyīn,
Yínèkè of the Hurha tribe,
Cáhǎnhàn of the Russian (Èluósī) tribe,
and the chieftains Bùlēi, Sūdìnggá, and Sīláng'ā Dá'ěrhàn's son Zhāmùsū of the Shílù Suǒlún tribe came to offer tribute.
Cháoxiǎn came a second time.
In the spring, the first month, on the day of Rénzǐ of the eighteenth year,
the Emperor fell ill.
On the day of Bǐngchén,
his illness became critical.
A general amnesty was declared for all crimes down to capital offenses.
On the day of Dīngsì,
the Emperor passed away in the Yǎngxīn Diàn,
aged twenty-four.
His last will stated:
“I, with my meager virtue,
inherited this great imperial foundation,
and eighteen years have passed since then.
Since taking charge of government,
regarding the regulations and laws,
and the appointment of officials and administration,
I have been unable to emulate the grand achievements of Tàizǔ and Tàizōng.
I have been complacent and neglectful,
content with short-term solutions.
Furthermore, I gradually adopted Hàn customs,
and regarding the simple and traditional old systems,
daily changes were made.
This has resulted in the governance of the nation not reaching perfection,
and the livelihood of the people not being satisfactory.
This is my first fault.
Since my tender age,
I met with the passing of my Imperial Father, Emperor Tàizōng.
In instruction and upbringing,
I solely relied on the benevolent nurturing of the Holy Mother Empress Dowager.
Her immense grace is boundless,
her profound kindness cannot be repaid.
Morning and night, I attended to her,
hoping to fulfill my filial duties.
Now, I am unfortunately unable to complete my filial path,
and my sincere intentions are unfulfilled.
This is my second fault.
My Imperial Father passed away
when I was only six years old,
and I was unable to wear mourning clothes and observe the three-year mourning period,
a regret I will forever carry.
