I only served the Empress Dowager, complying with her wishes and pleasing her,
and hoped that after ten thousand years,
I might fulfill my duty as a son,
and somewhat relieve my past regret.
Now, I am forever separated from her side,
and instead cause the Holy Mother profound grief.
This is my third fault.
The imperial clansmen, various princes, Bèilè, and others,
are all descendants of Tàizǔ and Tàizōng,
and it is proper to treat them favorably,
to show familial closeness.
Yet, with the various princes and Bèilè,
my interactions have been sparse,
and my favors few.
Our affection and friendship have become distant,
and the way of brotherly love has not been perfected.
This is my fourth fault.
The Manchu officials,
some have been loyal for generations,
some have served diligently for years.
They should be relied upon more,
to fully exert their talents.
I, however, failed to trust them,
preventing those with talent from developing it.
Moreover, the loss of the nation in the late Míng dynasty
was largely due to the exclusive reliance on civil officials.
I did not take this as a warning,
and instead entrusted Hàn officials with responsibility.
Even the seals of the ministries and courts
were occasionally put under the charge of Hàn officials.
This caused Manchu officials to lose heart in their duties,
and their energy to slacken.
This is my fifth fault.
I was by nature proud,
and unable to humble myself to accept advice.
When appointing officials,
I always sought those whose virtue matched my own,
and failed to use individuals according to their talents,
which led me to constantly lament the lack of capable people.
If I had overlooked shortcomings and recorded strengths,
then even those with minor skills
would have been utilized.
How could it have come to pass that the whole world seemed devoid of talent?
This is my sixth fault.
Establishing offices and dividing responsibilities,
one should only use those with virtue;
advancing, demoting, dismissing, and promoting
must not be overlooked.
Regarding court officials,
even when I clearly knew of their unworthiness,
I did not immediately dismiss them,
but instead tolerated and indulged them.
For example, a person like Liú Zhèngzōng,
who was biased, impetuous, and jealous—
I fully understood this in my heart,
yet allowed him to long hold a position of power.
This can be described as seeing the worthy but being unable to promote them,
and seeing the unworthy but being unable to dismiss them.
This is my seventh fault.
National expenditures were vast,
and military provisions insufficient.
Yet, the funds from gold taxes and grain
were entirely allocated to palace expenses,
never having been saved or dispensed frugally.
When the treasury reported emptiness,
I often ordered the various princes and high officials to convene for discussions,
but they could not devise any special clever plans,
only proposing to cut salaries
to provide for military provisions.
Favoring myself and slighting others,
benefiting the high and harming the low.
This is my eighth fault.
Constructing palaces,
and manufacturing implements,
I always pursued extreme refinement and exquisite craftsmanship.
On unnecessary projects,
a great deal was wasted.
Yet I did not reflect upon myself,
nor considered the hardships of the people.
This is my ninth fault.
Empress Duānjìng perfectly fulfilled her filial duties to the Empress Dowager,
and assisted me,
bringing internal governance into good order.
I, revering the benevolent imperial edict,
and recalling her virtuous kindness,
made the funeral and sacrificial rites
excessively generous.
I was unable to restrain my emotions with propriety;
all matters were excessive,
extravagant and improper.
This is my tenth fault.
Our ancestors, when founding the enterprise,
never employed eunuchs.
Moreover, the Míng dynasty's fall
was also due to the entrustment of eunuchs.
I clearly knew of this drawback,
but did not take it as a warning.
I established the thirteen inner Yámén,
and entrusted them with duties,
no different from the Míng.
This led to private profiteering and corruption,
even more rampant than in previous times.
This is my eleventh fault.
My nature was fond of leisure and quiet,
and I often sought comfort and ease.
I resided in the deep palace,
and rarely held court.
This led to sparse contact with court officials,
and the feelings between high and low became obstructed.
This is my twelfth fault.
In human conduct,
who can be without error?
As for me, managing myriad affairs daily,
how could I be entirely without fault?
However, in listening to words and accepting admonitions,
one will know if there are faults.
I often relied on my own intelligence,
and was unable to listen and accept advice.
The ancients said: ‘A good merchant keeps his treasures hidden as if empty;
a gentleman of abundant virtue
appears foolish.’
I greatly contravened
these words.
This caused officials to remain silent,
unwilling to offer advice.
This is my thirteenth fault.
Since I knew I had faults,
I often reproached myself and felt regret.
Yet, I merely adhered to superficial forms,
and failed to truly reflect and change,
causing faults to accumulate daily,
and errors to multiply.
This is my fourteenth fault.
The foundation established by Tàizǔ and Tàizōng
is of utmost importance.
A principal heir to the throne
cannot be long absent.
My son Xuányè,
born of Consort Tóng,
is intelligent and sagacious,
and capable of inheriting the imperial lineage.
Therefore, he is hereby established as the Crown Prince.
He shall immediately observe the prescribed mourning rites for twenty-seven days,
and after removing mourning attire,
he shall ascend the imperial throne.
I specially appoint the Grand Ministers Sīní, Sūkèsāhā, Èbìlóng, and Áobài as regents.
They are all meritorious and venerable ministers,
whom I entrust with my heart.
They should strive to demonstrate loyalty,
assist the young ruler,
and manage governmental affairs.
This edict is to be proclaimed to all within and without the empire,
so that all may know.”
In the third month, on the day of Guǐyǒu,
the Emperor was posthumously granted the honorific title Tǐtiān Lóngyùn Yīngruì Qīnwén Dàdé Hónggōng Zhìrén Chúnxiào Zhāng Huángdì,
and his temple name was Shìzǔ.
He was buried in Xiàolíng.
Later, the full honorific title granted was Tǐtiān Lóngyùn Dìngtǒng Jiànjí Yīngruì Qīnwén Xiǎnwǔ Dàdé Hónggōng Zhìrén Chúnxiào Zhāng Huángdì.
A discussion states: At the beginning of the Shùnzhì reign,
Ruìwáng acted as regent.
He entered the pass, established the capital,
and occupied the whole of China.
However, as military affairs were still pressing,
he had no time
to attend to matters of rest and recuperation for the people.
It was not until the Emperor personally took charge of all state affairs
that he diligently governed and loved the people,
assiduously seeking good governance.
He clarified taxes and levies to abolish excessive demands,
and established laws and regulations to cleanse injustices and abuses.
Remissions of rent and tax deferrals
are ceaselessly recorded in history.
After he ascended the throne for eighteen years,
he brought people from dire straits to comfort.
Although his splendid destiny was not prolonged,
his great foundation was already consolidated.
As for the moment of his death,
he examined himself and took responsibility,
proclaiming it to his officials and people.
His self-reproach surpassed
that of Yǔ and Tāng.
The Shū Jīng says:
"Truly, the discerning and intelligent become the supreme ruler;
the supreme ruler is the parent of the people."
This refers to Shìzǔ.
Imperial Annals 6, Imperial Annals of Shèngzǔ 1
Shèngzǔ Hétiānhóngyùn Wǔwǔ Ruìzhé Gōngjiǎn Kuānyù Xiàojìng Chéngxìn Gōngdé Dàchéng Rén Huángdì,
whose personal name was Xuányè,
was Shìzǔ's third son.
His mother was Xiàokāngzhāng Huánghòu Tóngjiā Shì.
On the day Wùshēn in the third month of Shùnzhì 11, the Emperor was born in the Jǐngrén Gōng.
His appearance was handsome and distinguished,
his stature like a mountain, and his voice resonant.
At six years old,
he, along with his brothers, paid respects.
Shìzǔ asked what they desired.
The second imperial son Fúquán said:
"I wish to be a virtuous prince."
The Emperor said:
"I wish to emulate my imperial father."
Shìzǔ was astonished.
On the day Bǐngchén in the first month of Shùnzhì 18,
Shìzǔ passed away,
and the Emperor ascended the throne
at the age of eight,
changing the reign title to Kāngxī.
The imperial edict appointed Suǒní, Sūkèsāhā, Èbìlóng, and Áobài as the four Grand Ministers to assist in governance.
On the day Guǐwèi in the second month,
the Emperor put off his mourning clothes.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the guilty eunuch Wú Liángfǔ was executed,
and inner officials were dismissed.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Déesāi, son of the heir to Jiǎn Qīnwáng, Jìdù, inherited the title.
On the day Bǐngyín in the third month,
an edict stated:
"The laws and regulations of the state
have varied from generation to generation.
Tàizǔ and Tàizōng established systems and fixed laws,
leaving a rich legacy for future generations.
Now, some may differ between Manchu and Han,
or have been changed back and forth.
Let existing precedents be thoroughly examined,
compiled into codes and regulations,
and reported after collective deliberation."
In the fourth month,
attendant guard Fù Dáli, who died in the funeral, was granted a sacrificial burial.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the Governor-General of Húguǎng was ordered to be stationed in Jīngzhōu.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
General Xiàn Guó'ān was ordered to lead the Southern pacifying army to garrison Guǎngxī.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Lāhādá was appointed Minister of Works.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Límwìhkeī (Lí Wéiqí), King of the Annam state, sent envoys to present tribute.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Grand Secretary Hóng Chéngchóu requested retirement,
which was granted,
and he was given the hereditary position of Light Chariot Commandant, Third Class.
On the day Wùshēn,
Mǎ Shìjùn and three hundred eighty-three others were granted the Jinshì degree with different ranks.
In the fifth month,
the Provincial Surveillance Commissioners were abolished in various provinces.
On the day Jǐsì,
Gāo Jǐng was appointed Minister of Works,
and Liú Liángzuǒ was appointed Jiang-An Provincial Military Commander.
On the day Yǐhài,
Mò Jìngyào, a rebel minister from Annam, surrendered
and was enfeoffed as General Guīhuà.
On the day Jǐmǎo in the sixth month,
Zhū Guózhì, Governor of Jiāngsū, memorialized that there were 13,517 gentry and scholars in Sū province who had outstanding tax arrears;
the Ministry dismissed and demoted them with varying degrees of punishment.
On the day Xīnsì,
ten villages of the Fēiyákā tribe from Hēilóngjiāng surrendered.
On the day Gēngyín,
Èzhā, son of the heir to Xìn Jùnwáng, Duóní, inherited the title.
On the day Guǐsì,
Grand Secretary Fù Yǐjiàn requested retirement,
which was granted.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the Grand Secretariat was abolished,
and the Three Inner Courts were reinstated.
On the day Wùxū,
Wú Sānguì presented five trained elephants,
but they were rejected.
An edict was issued to stop tribute from the directly administered provinces.
On the day Gēngchén in the intercalary seventh month,
Chēkè was appointed Minister of Personnel,
and Āsīhā was appointed Minister of Revenue.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Fù Wéilín was appointed Minister of Works.
On the day Rényín,
Liáng Huàfèng, the Sū-Sōng Provincial Military Commander, was granted a baronetcy.
On the day Jiǎyín in the eighth month,
the Dalai Lama requested to open trade,
which was granted.
On the day Dīngwèi in the ninth month,
Biàn Sānyuán was appointed Governor-General of Yúnnán,
Lǐ Qīfèng was appointed Governor-General of Guǎngdōng,
Láng Tíngzuǒ was appointed Governor-General of Jiāngnán,
and Liáng Huàfèng was appointed Jiāngnán Provincial Military Commander.
On the day Jǐyǒu in the tenth month,
Lín Qǐlóng was appointed Governor-General of Canal Transport.
The surrendered general Zhèng Zhīlóng and his sons Shì'ēn and Shìyìn were executed.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the Shùntiān Provincial Surveillance Commissioner was abolished.
As the commoner Yú Qī caused rebellion in Shāndōng,
Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Xǔ Wénxiù,
and Regional Commanders Lǐ Yǒngshèng and Fàn Chéngzōng were arrested and interrogated.
General Jìshìhā was ordered to suppress it.
On the first day of the eleventh month, Bǐngzǐ,
the Emperor personally offered sacrifices to Heaven at the Altar of Heaven.
On the day Jǐhài,
Shìzǔ Zhāng Huángdì was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Wǔ Shàoxīn, the Hunan Provincial Censor, was executed in the marketplace for corruption.
On the day Bǐngwǔ in the twelfth month,
Píngxīwáng Wú Sānguì and Dìngxī Jiāngjūn Àixīng'ā jointly reported that the main army had entered Myanmar,
and the Burmese had captured Zhū Yóuláng, the Yǒnglì Emperor of the Ming, and presented him.
Ming General Bái Wénxuǎn surrendered.
The army returned.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the Imperial Clan Court presented the Imperial Genealogy.
This year, various prefectures and counties in Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Hénán, Zhèjiāng, Húguǎng, and Shǎnxī were granted partial exemptions from assessed taxes due to disasters.
Cháoxiǎn (Korea) sent envoys to offer incense and tribute.
Kāngxī First Year, Rén Yín, spring, first month, first day Yǐhài.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
sacrifices were offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the day Gēngyín,
Grand Secretary Fàn Wénchéng and others were rewarded for their meritorious service in assisting the founding of the dynasty,
and their sons, including Chéngmó, were all appointed as Academicians of the Inner Courts.
On the day Rényǐ in the second month,
it was the birthday of the Grand Empress Dowager,
and the Emperor led all officials in offering congratulations.
In the third month,
with the pacification of Diānnán,
an announcement was made to the temples and sacrifices were made at the imperial tombs,
and a general amnesty was granted to the empire.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
it was the birthday.
On the day Jǐhài,
officials were dispatched to pacify and settle the newly surrendered officials and commoners in Zhèjiāng, Fújiàn, and Guǎngdōng.
Summer, fourth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
honorary posthumous titles were conferred upon Tàizǔ and Tàizōng.
Fifth month, on the day Wùyín,
at the summer solstice,
the Emperor personally offered sacrifices to Earth at the Altar of the Earth.
On the day Dīngwèi in the sixth month,
the Ministry of Rites was ordered to determine ranks and distinctions for nobles and commoners.
Autumn, seventh month, first day Rényín,
Chēkè was appointed Grand Secretary,
Nínggǔlǐ was appointed Minister of Revenue,
Zhāng Jié was appointed Zhèjiāng Provincial Military Commander,
and Shī Láng was appointed Fújiàn Provincial Military Commander.
Eighth month, first day Xīnchǒu,
Grand Secretary Jīn Zhījùn was dismissed.
In the ninth month,
the Yánsuí Provincial Surveillance Commissioner was abolished.
Winter, tenth month, on the day Rényín,
Chéng Kègǒng was appointed Grand Secretary.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Empress Dowager was honored as the Grand Empress Dowager.
The Empress was honored as Rénxiàn Huáng Tàihòu,
and the Emperor's birth mother was honored as Cíhé Huáng Tàihòu.
On the day Xīnsì in the eleventh month,
at the winter solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Altar of Heaven,
and morning congratulations were waived.
On the day Xīnyǒu in the twelfth month,
Wú Sānguì was ordered to take overall charge of the two provinces of Yúnnán and Guìzhōu.
That year,
the number of households and adult males in the empire was nineteen million one hundred thirty-seven thousand six hundred fifty-two.
The silver tax collected amounted to twenty-five million seven hundred twenty-four thousand one hundred twenty-four taels and a fraction.
The salt tax silver was two million seven hundred twenty-one thousand two hundred twelve taels and a fraction.
Over two hundred ninety million coins were minted.
Disaster relief exemptions were granted for varying amounts of taxes in various prefectures and counties of Zhílì and Jiāngnán.
Cháoxiǎn offered tribute.
In the second year, the guǐmǎo year, in the spring, the first month, on the jǐhài day,
Lú Chóngjùn, the Grand Governor of Guǎngdōng, requested permission to requisition merchant ships to transport troops.
This was rejected.
In the second month, on the gēngxū day,
Empress Dowager Cíhé Tóngjiā Shì passed away.
In the third month,
the Kingdom of Hélán dispatched envoys to offer tribute,
requesting assistance for troops to attack Táiwān.
They were generously rewarded.
In the fifth month, on the bǐngzǐ day,
Sūn Tíngquán was appointed Grand Secretary.
On the yǐyǒu day,
Yúnnán established a minting bureau.
On the bǐngxū day,
an imperial edict decreed that all grain and silver taxes nationwide should be centrally managed by the Hùbù.
All funds required by the various ministries and courts
were to be obtained from the Hùbù.
This was established as a regulation.
On the wùzǐ day,
Wèi Yìjiè was appointed Shàngshū of the Lìbù.
On the jiǎwǔ day,
the posthumous honorific title bestowed upon the late Empress Dowager Cíhé was Xiàokāng Cíhé Zhuāngyì Gōnghuì Chóngtiān Yùshèng Huánghòu.
In the sixth month,
Shìzǔ Zhāng Huángdì was interred at Xiàolíng,
with Empress Xiàokāng and Empress Duānjìng entombed alongside him.
On the wùshēn day,
Gōng Dǐngzī was appointed Zuǒ Dūyùshǐ.
On the yǐmǎo day,
Lǐ Dìngguó's son, Sīxīng, a general from the former Míng dynasty, surrendered.
On the yǐchǒu day,
Hā'ěrkù was appointed Tídū of Zhèjiāng.
In the eighth month, on the guǐmǎo day,
an imperial edict suspended the eight-legged essay for the xiāngshì and huìshì examinations,
replacing it with policy essays (cèlùn).
The eight banners' Fānyì Xiāngshì was reinstated.
On the jiǎyín day,
Mùlǐmǎ was appointed Jìngxī Jiāngjūn,
and Túhǎi was appointed Dìngxī Jiāngjūn.
They were to lead the Imperial Guard to join the Grand Governors of Sìchuān, Húguǎng, and Shǎnxī to suppress the fugitive rebels Lǐ Láihēng and Hǎo Yáoqí and others in Yúnyáng.
In the winter, the tenth month, on the rényín day,
Gěng Jìmào and Shī Láng, with the assistance of Hélán warships, annihilated the sea bandits,
captured Xiàmén,
and seized the two islands of Wúyǔ and Jīnmén.
Zhèng Jǐn fled to Táiwān.
In the eleventh month,
an imperial edict exempted tribute envoys from various nations from taxes on their native products.
On the yǐyǒu day,
the winter solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Huánqiū Altar.
In the twelfth month, on the rénxū day,
a collective sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
That year,

disaster relief exemptions were granted for taxes in over two hundred seventy prefectures and counties in the provinces of Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Jiāngxī, Hénán, Shǎnxī, Zhèjiāng, Húguǎng, Sìchuān, Yúnnán, Guìzhōu, and others.
Cháoxiǎn offered tribute and presented incense.
In the third year, the jiǎchén year, in the spring, the first month,
silver, silk, saddles, and horses were bestowed upon the foreign vassal states attending the New Year's court.
In the second month, on the rényín day,
Zhāng Jíwǔ, the Salt Censor, requested an increase in the price of salt certificates for Chánglú.
This was rejected.
In the third month, on the bǐngzǐ day,
Gěng Jìmào and others captured Tóngshān.
On the bǐngxū day,
Yán Wǒsī and one hundred ninety-nine others were granted jinshì and other degrees with varying ranks.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the jǐhài day,
the Grand Secretaries falsely accused the Inner Grand Minister Fēiyánggǔ's son, the Imperial Guard Wōhè, of unauthorized riding of an imperial horse,
and Fēiyánggǔ of resentment and disloyalty.
Both were executed in the marketplace,
and their property was confiscated.
Áobài gave it to his younger brother Mùlǐmǎ.
Shàngshū Kāláníbù was dispatched to the forty-seven banners of Kē'ěrqìn to preside over the alliance.
On the wùshēn day,
the Yúnyáng Fǔzhì office was abolished.
In the fifth month, on the jiǎzǐ day,
an imperial edict declared that officials who condoned or concealed private levies by prefectures and counties that burdened the people
would also be punished.
In the sixth month, on the gēngshēn day,
an imperial edict remitted outstanding taxes from before the fifteenth year of Shùnzhì.
In the intercalary sixth month, on the yǐyǒu day,
Wáng Hóngzuò was appointed Shàngshū of the Xíngbù.
On the bǐngxū day,
Han Chinese京官 (metropolitan officials) were incorporated into the Han Chinese quota for promotions.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the dīngwèi day,
Shī Láng was appointed Jìnghǎi Jiāngjūn,
to conquer Táiwān.
In the eighth month, on the jiǎxū day,
Zhào Tíngchén, the Grand Governor of Zhèjiāng, submitted a memorial reporting the capture of the Míng official Zhāng Huángyán.
On the jǐmǎo day,
Mùlǐmǎ and Túhǎi submitted a memorial reporting their advance and suppression of Lǐ Láihēng and Hǎo Yáoqí at Máolùshān in Yúnyáng.
Both committed self-immolation,
and the rebels were pacified.
In the ninth month, on the guǐchǒu day,
granary grain was distributed to relieve the Eight Banners' manors.
On the yǐmǎo day,
Zhākèdàn was appointed Lǐngshìwèi Nèidàchén.
In the eleventh month, on the rénchén day,
the winter solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Huánqiū Altar.
On the dīngwèi day,
Wèi Yìjiè was appointed Grand Secretary,
Dù Lìdé was appointed Shàngshū of the Lìbù,
Wáng Hóngzuò was appointed Shàngshū of the Hùbù,
and Gōng Dǐngzī was appointed Shàngshū of the Xíngbù.
In the twelfth month, on the wùwǔ day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the bǐngxū day,
a collective sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
That month,
a comet was seen in the constellations Zhāngsù, Jǐngsù, Wèisù, and Kuísù.
Venus was seen.
Gěishìzhōng Yáng Yōngjiàn requested self-reflection and reform.
That year,

disaster relief exemptions were granted for varying amounts of assessed taxes in one hundred twenty-one prefectures and counties in the provinces of Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Jiāngxī, Shāndōng, Shǎnxī, Zhèjiāng, Fújiàn, Húguǎng, Guìzhōu, and others.
Cháoxiǎn offered tribute.
In the fourth year, the yǐsì year, in the spring, the first month, on the réndào day,
Hǎo Wéinà was appointed Zuǒ Dūyùshǐ.
On the jǐhài day,
the reward for excess revenue from customs duties was suspended.
On the xīncǎo day,
Bó'ōnguǒnuò, son of Prince Chéngzé Shuòsè, was enfeoffed as Huì Jùnwáng.
The retired Grand Secretary Hóng Chéngchóu passed away.
He was granted sacrificial rites and a burial,
and posthumously named Wénxiāng.
In the second month, on the yǐchǒu day,
on the occasion of the Grand Empress Dowager's birthday,
court congratulations were exempted.
On the jǐsì day,
Wú Sānguì submitted a memorial reporting the pacification of the Xīshuǐ Wūsà indigenous chieftains
and the capture of their leaders Ān Kūn and Ān Zhòngshèng.
On the bǐngxū day,
an imperial edict, prompted by celestial anomalies, commanded officials and workers to report shortcomings.
Yùshǐ Dǒng Wénjì submitted a memorial stating that the Grand Ministers were altering the institutions of the former emperor,
which was wrong,
and that everything should be restored to its previous state.
In the third month, on the wùzǐ day,
there was an earthquake in the capital with a rumble.
On the xīnmǎo day,
Venus was visible during the day.
Due to the celestial anomalies and earthquake, a general amnesty was declared,
and outstanding taxes were remitted.
Shānxī suffered a drought,
but the local officials failed to report it.
The matter was sent to the Lìbù for deliberation on punishment,
and their accumulated arrears and the current year's assessed taxes were remitted.
On the rénchén day,
an imperial edict prohibited prefectures and counties from pre-collecting next year's taxes.
On the bǐngshēn day,
an imperial edict stated:
"When prefectures and counties suffer from famine,
local officials memorialize to request tax exemptions,
but the common people have already paid beforehand,
meaning the benevolence does not reach them.
Henceforth, for those affected by disaster,
a three-tenths deferment of assessed taxes shall be granted in advance."
On the jiǎchén day,
the Emperor's birthday,
court congratulations were exempted.
On the bǐngwǔ day,
the Temple of Emperors of Past Dynasties was repaired.
Tàichángsì Shàowèi Qián Tíng requested that several elderly, virtuous, and widely learned scholars of classics and history
be selected to serve as attendants,
to be available for consultation.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the bǐngyín day,
an imperial edict decreed that all those granted tax exemptions due to disaster also be exempted from corvée labor.
On the wùchén day,
an imperial edict stated that vacancies for senior officials (Qīng'èr Dūfǔ)
should still be filled through court deliberation.
In the fifth month, on the dīngwèi day,
the office of Grand Governor of Zhílì was established,
also overseeing Shāndōng and Hénán.
The Grand Governor of Guìzhōu was abolished and merged with Yúnnán,
the Grand Governor of Guǎngxī with Guǎngdōng,
the Grand Governor of Jiāngxī with Jiāngnán,
the Grand Governor of Shānxī with Shǎnxī.
The Fǔyán, Níngxià, and Nángàn Patrol Inspectors were all abolished.
In the sixth month, on the yǐchǒu day,
an imperial edict decreed that if a father and son or brothers served in the same capacity,
they would be granted one year of exemption from duties.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the jǐyǒu day,
the Lìbù, citing that Shānxī had collected taxes as assessed,
requested deliberation.
The imperial edict stated:
"Previously, due to drought and famine in Tàiyuán and other places,
the Grand Governor failed to report it,
and punishment was deliberated.
By grace of an amnesty, he was pardoned.
How can collection be still reported as a top achievement?
Only local officials in areas not affected by disaster
shall still be given records of merit."
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
an edict was issued that corrupt officials who had been pardoned and acquitted of their crimes
would not be permitted to resume their posts.
In the ninth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
Hèshèlǐ-shì was installed as Empress.
She was the granddaughter of Assistant Minister Suǒní.
The honorary titles of the Grand Empress Dowager and the Empress Dowager were elevated,
and favors were extended to those within and outside the court.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Guǐhài,
the Emperor went to Nányuàn for archery practice and a hunting expedition.
On the day Jiǎxū,
he returned to the palace.
In the eleventh month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Yuánqiū.
In the twelfth month, on the day Gēngchén,
a joint sacrifice was performed at the Tàimiào.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted in varying degrees for 121 prefectures, counties, and garrisons in the provinces of Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Jiāngxī, Shāndōng, Hénán, Zhèjiāng, Guǎngdōng, and Guìzhōu.
Cháoxiǎn, Liúqiú, and Xiāmluó offered tribute.
The Suǒlún and Fēiyákā people came to submit.
In the fifth year, Bǐngwǔ, in spring, the first month, on the day Gēngyín,
due to drought in Guǎngdōng,
70,000 shí of grain from the granaries were distributed for relief.
Énkèbù, son of Prince Chéngzé Shuòsè, was made successor to the peerage.
In the second month, on the first day Rénzǐ,
the three prefectures of Píngyuǎn, Dàdìng, and Qiánxī were established.
On the day Dīngsì,
as the mid-month qi of the twelfth month did not correspond,
an edict was issued seeking those proficient in calendar calculation.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
an edict stipulated that from now on, if Han military officials experienced a mourning period for a parent,
they would be allowed to resign their posts and observe a three-year mourning period.
In the third month,
Hú Bài was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì.
In the fifth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
Sūn Yánlíng was appointed General of Guǎngxī,
taking command of the Dìngnán forces stationed in Guìlín.
In the sixth month, on the first day Gēngxū,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Fù Wéilín was dismissed due to illness,
and Hǎo Wéinè was appointed Minister of Works.
On the day Xīnwèi,
an edict announced the abolition of taxes on goods exiting the capital at Chóngwénmén.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day Gēngchén,
Zhū Zhībi was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
On the day Xīnsì,
Liúqiú offered tribute,
and also made up for previous tributes lost at sea.
The Emperor praised their reverence and obedience,
ordered their return,
and stipulated that from now on, products not native to their country should not be offered as tribute.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
Supervising Secretary Zhāng Wéichì submitted a memorial requesting the Emperor's personal rule.
In the ninth month, on the day Dīnghài,
the Emperor went on a hunting expedition in Nányuàn.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
he returned to the palace.
Minister of Rites Shā Chéng was dismissed.
Liáng Qīngbiāo was appointed Minister of Rites,
Gōng Dǐngzī Minister of War,
Hǎo Wéinè Minister of Punishments,
and Zhū Zhībi Minister of Works.
In winter, the tenth month,
an edict recalled Fàn Chéngmó to serve as Academician of the Secretariat.
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
Assistant Minister Áobài, citing the reallocation of enclosed lands,
falsely accused Grand Secretary and concurrently Minister of Revenue Sū Nàhǎi, Governor-General of Zhílì Zhū Chāngzuò, and Governor Wáng Dēnglián of crimes,
and had them arrested and imprisoned.
The four grandees, when assisting in governance,
were all chosen for their merits and long service.
Suǒní was old,
Èbìlóng was timid and weak,
Sūkèsāhā's prestige was shallow;
though they disagreed with Áobài's actions, they could not contend with him.
Áobài was tyrannical and overbearing,
and also a veteran general with many military achievements.
Though his rank was the lowest,
he was autocratic in all matters,
frequently initiating major imprisonments,
such that even his colleagues looked askance at him.
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
Áobài, by a forged imperial decree, killed Sū Nàhǎi, Zhū Chāngzuò, and Wáng Dēnglián.
On the day Jiǎxū,
a joint sacrifice was performed at the Tàimiào.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted in varying degrees for 86 prefectures and counties in the provinces of Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Jiāngxī, Hénán, Shǎnxī, Zhèjiāng, and Húguǎng.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú offered tribute.
In the sixth year, Dīngwèi, in spring, the first month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Fúquán, the second son of Shìzǔ, was enfeoffed as Yù Qīnwáng.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the Emperor went to Nányuàn for a hunting expedition.
Míng'āndálǐ was appointed Minister of Rites.
In the second month, on the day Guǐhài,
Prince Níkān's son, Bèilè Lánbù, was elevated to Jùnwáng.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Zōngshì Gōng Bānbù'ěrshàn was appointed Grand Secretary.
Tú Hǎi was recalled to serve again as Grand Secretary.
The late Governor-General Lǐ Shuàitài was posthumously granted the title of Earl of the First Class.
In the third month, on the day Jǐhài,
Miào Tóng and 150 others were granted the jinshi degree with varying ranks.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Jiǎxū,
Suǒní was elevated to First Class Duke.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
a commoner from Jiāngnán, Shěn Tiānfǔ, was executed for composing rebellious poetry and falsely accusing others.
All those who had been falsely accused were not prosecuted.
Censor Tián Liùshàn stated that cunning commoners would accuse people;
if from the south, they would say,
"colluding with pirates,"
or "rebellious writings;"
if from the north, they would say,
"part of Yú Qī's faction,"
or "a fugitive."
He requested that those who made false accusations be investigated and punished in return.
This was granted.
In the fifth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Wú Sānguì submitted a memorial resigning from the overall administration of the two provinces of Yúnnán and Guìzhōu.
This was granted.
In the sixth month, on the day Jǐhài,
officials and laborers collecting nanmu timber were prohibited from causing trouble and burdening the people.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
the Emperor began to rule personally,
holding court at the Tàihédiàn to receive congratulations.
Favors were extended both within and outside the court;
crimes not punishable by immediate death
were all pardoned.
On this day,
he first held court at the Qiánqīngmén.
On the day Jiǎyín,
it was ordered that all military officials be granted an audience.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Assistant Minister Áobài arbitrarily executed Assistant Minister Sūkèsāhā and his family.
On the day Guǐhài,
Assistant Ministers Èbìlóng and Áobài were granted an additional First Class Duke title.
In the ninth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
an order was given to compile the Veritable Records of Shìzǔ.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Shèngjīng experienced an earthquake with sound.
In the eleventh month, on the day Dīngwèi,
at the Winter Solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Yuánqiū.
Shìzǔ Zhāng Huángdì was enshrined as co-worshipper.
On the day Dīngsì,
the honorary titles of the Grand Empress Dowager and the Empress Dowager were elevated.
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐngxū,
Sàibáilǐ was appointed Naval Commander of Guǎngdōng.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Mǎ'ěrsài was appointed additional Minister of Revenue.
On the day Wùxū,
a joint sacrifice was performed at the Tàimiào.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted in varying degrees for 160 prefectures and counties in the provinces of Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Jiāngxī, Shāndōng, Shānxī, Shǎnxī, Gānsù, Zhèjiāng, Fújiàn, and Húguǎng.
Cháoxiǎn and Hélán offered tribute.
In the seventh year, Wùshēn, in spring, the first month, on the day Wùshēn,
Mòluò was appointed Governor-General of Shānxī and Shǎnxī,
and Liú Zhàoqí was appointed Governor-General of Sìchuān.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Áobài and Èbìlóng were elevated to Grand Tutor.
In the second month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
the Emperor went to Nányuàn.
In the third month, on the day Dīngwèi,
an edict stipulated that officials in ministries and courts with outstanding talent
should be promoted and transferred without adhering to usual regulations.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Gēngchén,
a commoner from Jiāshàn, Zhèjiāng, Yù Zhīzhāng, was found guilty and sent into exile;
his sons Bāo and Guǎng knocked on the palace gate requesting to take his place.
The Emperor pardoned both of them.
In the fifth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
due to unusual celestial phenomena and an earthquake,
an edict was issued for self-reflection and introspection,
instructing and warning officials.
In the sixth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
Venus was seen in broad daylight.
On the day Dīnghài,
Prince Píngnán Shàng Kěxǐ sent his son Zhīxìn to serve at court.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Wùwǔ,
former Grand Canal Transport Governor Wú Wéihuá requested to levy taxes on market stalls in towns
and to invite commoners to pay rent to cultivate marshland.
The Emperor disliked his emphasis on profit
and ordered the Ministry of Punishments to deliberate on his crime.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Kuādài was appointed Manchu General-in-Chief.
In the eighth month, on the day Rénshēn,
Minister of Revenue Wáng Hóngzuò was dismissed for failing to investigate clerks who forged seals and stole public funds.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Wúmǎhù was appointed General of Fèngtiān,
Échǔ General of Jiāngníng,
and Wǎ'ěrkā General of Xī'ān.
On the day Rén'yín,
the Emperor was about to inspect the border;
Academicians Xióng Cìlǚ and Supervising Secretary Zhào Zhīfú submitted memorials to dissuade him.
The Emperor consequently canceled his trip,
but still ordered them to speak frankly on matters when they arose.
In the tenth month of winter,
it was decreed that Manchu (Bāqí) military officials in mourning for one hundred days
should remove their mourning attire and resume their duties,
but still observe mourning for three years.
On the day *Gēngwǔ*,
the Emperor visited the Southern Park (Nányuàn).
On the day *Guǐchǒu* of the eleventh month,
it was the Winter Solstice (Dōngzhì),
and sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Altar of Heaven (Huánqiú).
On the day *Guǐyǒu* of the twelfth month,
Málèjí was appointed Governor-General (Zǒngdū) of Jiangnan (Jiāngnán),
Gān Wénkūn was appointed Governor-General of Yunnan (Yúnnán) and Guizhou (Guìzhōu),
and Fàn Chéngmó was appointed Provincial Governor (Xúnfǔ) of Zhejiang (Zhèjiāng).
On the day *Guǐsì*,
the joint sacrifice (Xiápjì) was performed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple (Tàimiào).
In this year,

the disaster taxes (Zāifù) of two hundred sixteen prefectures and counties in Fengtian (Fèngtiān), Zhili (Zhílì), Jiangnan (Jiāngnán), Shandong (Shāndōng), Henan (Hénán), Zhejiang (Zhèjiāng), Shaanxi (Shǎnxī), Gansu (Gānsù), and other provinces were remitted to varying degrees.
Joseon (Cháoxiān), Annam (Ānnán), and Siam (Xiāmluó) paid tribute.
In the spring of the eighth year, *Jǐyǒu*, on the day *Wùshēn* of the first month,
the Palace of Heavenly Purity (Qiánqīng Gōng) was repaired,
and the Emperor moved his residence to the Hall of Martial Valor (Wǔyīng Diàn).
On the day *Gēngwǔ* of the second month,
Nán Huáirén was ordered to calculate the calendar.
On the day *Gēngwǔ*,
the Emperor toured the vicinity of the capital (Jīnjī).
On the day *Xīnchǒu* of the third month,
the abandoned princely estates (Fān Tiándì) in Zhili (Zhílì) were granted to the common people.
In the summer of the fourth month, on the day *Guǐyǒu*,
Wèi Zhōuzuò was dismissed,
and Dù Lìdé was appointed Grand Secretary (Dàxuéshì).
On the day *Dīngchǒu*,
the Emperor visited the Imperial Academy (Tàixué),
offered sacrifices to the Former Sage Confucius (Xiānshī Kǒngzǐ),
and lectured on the *Zhouyi* (Zhōuyì) and *Shangshu* (Shàngshū).
On the day *Dīngsì*,
the Supervising Secretary (Gěishìzhōng) Liú Rúhàn requested the holding of imperial lectures (Jīngyán).
The Emperor praised and accepted this.
On the day *Yǐwèi* of the fifth month,
Huáng Jī was appointed Minister (Shàngshū) of the Ministry of Personnel (Lìbù),
Hǎo Wéinà was appointed Minister of the Ministry of Revenue (Hùbù),
Gōng Dǐngzī was appointed Minister of the Ministry of Rites (Lǐbù),
and Wáng Hóngzuò was reinstated as Minister of the Ministry of War (Bīngbù).
On the day *Wùshēn*,
an edict was issued to arrest the Auxiliary Minister (Fǔchén) Áobài and hand him over for trial (Tíngjū).
The Emperor had long known of Áobài's tyrannical usurpation of power and disruption of government,
and was particularly concerned about his great strength and difficulty to control.
Therefore, he selected young and strong imperial guards (Shìwèi) and imperial attendants (Bàitáng'ā) for wrestling practice.
On this day,
when Áobài came for an audience,
the imperial guards were immediately ordered to seize and bind him.
Thereupon, the system of the "Camp of Good Wrestlers" (Shànpū Yíng) was established,
led by close officials.
On the day *Gēngshēn*,
the princes (Wáng) and high officials (Dàchén) deliberated on Áobài's case and reported to the Emperor,
listing thirty major crimes,
and requested his execution along with his clan.
The edict stated:
"Áobài is foolish, perverse, and ignorant,
and indeed deserves to have his clan exterminated.
However, considering his long years of service
and repeated military achievements,
he is spared death,
his property is confiscated, and he is imprisoned."
His younger brothers Mùlǐmǎ and Sāiběndé,
his nephew Nèmó,
his partisans, Grand Secretary Bānbù'ěrshàn,
Ministers Āsīhā, Gáchǔhā, and Jìshì,
Vice Minister (Shìláng) Tàibìtú,
and Scholar (Xuéshì) Wúgésài, were all executed.
The rest were condemned and dismissed.
His younger brother Bāhā, who was a sincere and cautious imperial guard,
and Zhuóbùtài, who had military achievements,
were exempted from implication.
Subsequently, Prince of the First Rank (Qīnwáng) Lánbù, who had been respectful and cautious, was demoted to Duke Who Guards the State (Zhènguó Gōng).
Èbìlóng was stripped of his titles of Grand Tutor (Tàishī) and First-Class Duke (Yīděng Gōng).
In the sixth month, on the day *Dīngmǎo*,
an edict stated:
"Night and day, I strive for good governance,
with deep concern for the people's reliance.
In recent years, floods and droughts have been frequent,
and banditry has not ceased.
Coupled with corrupt officials' exploitation,
the people's strength is further exhausted,
which greatly grieves Me.
All officials of the ministries, bureaus, and supervisory offices
are hereby commanded to express their views
on how to alleviate the people's suffering
and report them."
On the day *Wùchén*,
an imperial decree was issued to remodel the instruments of the Imperial Observatory (Guānxiàngtái).
On the day *Rénshēn*,
an edict restored the Auxiliary Minister (Fǔchén) Sūkèsāhā's official post and hereditary rank,
and his nephew Bái'ěrtú, who had performed meritorious service at the border
and suffered particularly cruel injustice,
also had his hereditary rank restored,
both to be inherited by their sons.
On the day *Wùyín*,
an edict permanently prohibited Manchu (Mǎnbīng) soldiers from illegally occupying private houses and land,
and ordered that
they be returned to the people.
Mǐ Sīhàn was appointed Minister of the Ministry of Revenue (Hùbù).
On the day *Wùzǐ*,
an edict stated that to immediately sever the lineage records (Shǔjí) of imperial clansmen (Zōngrén) who committed crimes
was something I felt I could not bear.
Since the eighteenth year of Shunzhi (Shùnzhì),
the Imperial Clan Court (Zōngrénfǔ) was to investigate in detail those imperial clansmen whose lineage records had been removed
and report them.
In the autumn of the seventh month, on the first day (*Rénchén*),
the Governor-General (Zǒngdū) of Zhili (Zhílì), Shandong (Shāndōng), and Henan (Hénán) was abolished.
On the day *Rényín*,
an edict restored Grand Secretary Sūnàhǎi, Governor-General Zhū Chāngzuò, and Provincial Governor Wáng Dēnglián to their original offices,
and granted them posthumous titles (Shì).
In the eighth month, on the day *Jiǎshēn*,
Suǒ'étú was appointed Grand Secretary,
and Míngzhū was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left (Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ).
In the ninth month, on the day *Jiǎwǔ*,
there was an earthquake with sound in the capital (Jīngshī).
On the day *Dīngwèi*,
Lèbèi was appointed Manchu General-in-Chief (Mǎnzhōu Dūtǒng),
Sàibáilǐ was appointed Provincial Commander (Tídú) of Zhejiang (Zhèjiāng),
and Bìlìkètú was appointed Mongol General-in-Chief (Ménggǔ Dūtǒng).
In the tenth month of winter, on the day *Jiǎzǐ*,
the Emperor visited the Southern Park (Nányuàn),
and an edict prohibited the imperial entourage (Xíngzài) from borrowing civilian property.
The Lugou Bridge (Lúgōu Qiáo) was completed,
and the Emperor inscribed an essay on a stone tablet for it.
In the eleventh month, on the day *Jǐhài*,

previously, Mòluò, Governor-General (Zǒngdū) of Shanxi (Shānxī) and Shaanxi (Shǎnxī), and Bái Qīng'é, Provincial Governor (Xúnfǔ) of Shaanxi (Shǎnxī), were both dismissed for being part of Áobài's faction.
At this time,
the common people of Xi'an (Xī'ān) petitioned the court (Kòu Hūn), stating their honesty and integrity,
and begged for their reinstatement.
An edict specially granted this.
On the day *Rénzǐ*,
the Hall of Supreme Harmony (Tàihé Diàn) and the Palace of Heavenly Purity (Qiánqīng Gōng) were completed.
The Emperor ascended the Hall of Supreme Harmony to receive congratulations,
and took up residence in the Palace of Heavenly Purity.
In the twelfth month, on the day *Jǐmǎo*,
Prince Xiǎn Fúshòu passed away.
On the day *Dīnghài*,
the joint sacrifice (Xiápjì) was performed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple (Tàimiào).
In this year,

the disaster taxes (Zāifù) of forty-five prefectures and counties in Zhili (Zhílì), Jiangnan (Jiāngnán), Henan (Hénán), Shanxi (Shānxī), Shaanxi (Shǎnxī), Huguang (Húguǎng), and other provinces were remitted to varying degrees.
Joseon (Cháoxiān) and Ryukyu (Liúqiú) paid tribute.
In the spring of the ninth year, *Gēngxū*, on the day *Bǐngshēn* of the first month,
the descendants of the Song (Sòng) Confucians Chéng Hào and Chéng Yí were granted the title of Erudite of the Five Classics (Wǔjīng Bóshì).
On the day *Dīngyǒu*,
a feast was held at the Imperial Ancestral Temple (Tàimiào).
On the day *Xīnchǒu*,
prayers for a good harvest (Qígǔ) were offered to the Lord on High (Shàngdì),
with Emperor Tàizǔ Gāohuángdì, Emperor Tàizōng Wénhuángdì, and Emperor Shìzǔ Zhānghuángdì as co-sacrificers.
Èbìlóng was reinstated as Duke (Gōngjué)
and guarded within the inner court.
On the day *Jǐyǒu*,
an edict decreed that the land taxes of Ming (Míng) princely estates (Fān Tiánfù) should be paid in the same way as commoner's land.
On the day *Rénzǐ*,
the Emperor visited the Southern Park (Nányuàn).
In the second month, on the day *Guǐyǒu*,
Jīn Guāngzǔ was appointed Governor-General (Zǒngdū) of Guangdong (Guǎngdōng) and Guangxi (Guǎngxī),
and Mǎ Xióngzhèn was appointed Provincial Governor (Xúnfǔ) of Guangxi (Guǎngxī).
On the day *Guǐwèi*,
an edict decreed that the dispatch of criminals banished to Shangyangbao (Shàngyángbǎo) and Ningguta (Nínggǔtǎ)
be suspended between the tenth month and the first month inclusive.
In the third month, on the day *Xīnyǒu*,
Cài Qǐzūn and two hundred ninety-two others were granted the *Jinshi* (Jìnshì) degree and official ranks to varying degrees.
In the summer of the fourth month, on the day *Jǐchǒu*,
Cài Yùróng was appointed Governor-General (Zǒngdū) of Sichuan (Sìchuān) and Huguang (Húguǎng).
On the day *Jǐhài*,
the Emperor visited the Southern Park (Nányuàn).
On the first day (*Bǐngchén*) of the fifth month,
the honorable posthumous title (Zūnshì) of Empress Xiàokāng Zhānghuánghòu was further elevated,
and she was enshrined together in the Imperial Ancestral Temple (Tàimiào).
An imperial amnesty (Ēnzào) was issued,
seeking out recluses,
bestowing gifts upon the elderly,
and pardoning all crimes except for the most severe (Shúsǐ).
On the day *Bǐngzǐ*,
the comprehensive administrative statutes (Huìdiǎn) were compiled.
On the first day (*Bǐngxū*) of the sixth month,
Xí Bùchén was appointed Mongol General-in-Chief (Ménggǔ Dūtǒng).
On the day *Dīngyǒu*,
Dānzhēn, son of the late Prince Xiǎn Fúshòu, inherited the princely title.
On the day *Jǐyǒu*,
Grand Secretaries were ordered to assist the Ministry of Justice (Xíngbù) in reviewing prisoners.
In the autumn of the seventh month, on the day *Dīngsì*,
Wáng Fǔchén was appointed Provincial Commander (Tídú) of Shaanxi (Shǎnxī).
On the day *Dīngsì*,
Empress Xiàokāng Zhānghuánghòu was worshipped at the Hall for Worshipping Ancestors (Fèngxiān Diàn).
In the eighth month, on the day *wùzǐ*,
sacrifices were offered at the Altar of the Gods of Land and Grain (Shèjì Tán).

An imperial edict instructed the Censorate (Dūchá Yuàn) to investigate and rectify those princes, grandees, and ministers (wáng dàchén) who behaved improperly in their ranks while accompanying the sacrifices.
On the day *yǐwèi*,
the Grand Secretariat (Nèigé) was restored,
and the Hanlin Academy (Hànlín Yuàn) was restored.
On the day *dīngyǒu*,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Grand Empress Dowager (Tàihuang Tàihòu) and the Empress Dowager (Huang Tàihòu), offered sacrifices at Xiàolíng.
On the day *rénzǐ*,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
In the ninth month, on the day *gēngshēn*,
the son of Prince Jiǎnjiǎn Jìdù, Lābù, inherited the peerage.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day *gēngsì*,
the Sixteen Sacred Edicts (Shèngyù Shíliù Tiáo) were promulgated.
On the day *jiǎwǔ*,
the three Inner Courts (Nèi Sān Yuàn) were reorganized,
and the Grand Secretaries of the Zhōnghé Diàn, Bǎohé Diàn, and Wénhuá Diàn were reinstated.
On the day *dīngyǒu*,
an edict was issued to the Ministry of Rites (Lǐbù) to arrange the Imperial Lectures (Jīngyán).
In the eleventh month, on the day *guǐyǒu*,
Ài Yuánzhēng was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief (Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ).
On the day *rénwǔ*,
Wèi Yìjiè, Grand Secretary of the Zhōnghé Diàn, was concurrently appointed Minister of Rites (Lǐbù Shàngshū).
In the twelfth month, on the day *guǐmǎo*,
Mòluò was appointed Minister of Punishments (Xíngbù Shàngshū).
On the day *xīnhài*,
the combined ancestral sacrifice was performed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple (Tàimiào).
This year,

relief from disaster taxes (zāifù) was granted to 253 prefectures, counties, and garrisons (zhōuxiànwèi) in Hénán, Húguǎng, Jiāngnán, Fújiàn, Guǎngdōng, and Yúnnán provinces, with varying degrees of remission.
Cháoxiǎn offered tribute.
In the tenth year, on the *xīnhài* spring first month, on the day *dīngmǎo*,
the Sūnítè and Sìzǐ tribes of Měnggǔ suffered from heavy snow, hunger, and cold;
officials were dispatched to provide relief.
On the day *guǐyǒu*,
the fifth son of Shìzǔ, Chángníng, was enfeoffed as Prince Gōng (Gōng Qīnwáng).
On the day *gēngchén*,
Grand Secretary Wèi Yìjiè was dismissed.
Cáo Shēnjí was appointed Governor of Guìzhōu.
In the second month, on the day *dīngyǒu*,
Féng Pǔ was appointed Grand Secretary,
and Liáng Qīngbiāo was appointed Minister of Punishments.
On the day *yǐsì*,
four members of the Aisin Gioro (Zōngrén Juéluó) clan, including Zhào Bān, who were seventy years of age or older, were summoned for an audience,
and bestowed with court attire and silver coins.
On the day *wùshēn*,
an order was issued to compile the *Xiàojīng Yǎnyì*.
On the day *gēngxū*,
Níyǎhàn was appointed Manchu Grand Commander (Mǎmǎzhōu Dūtǒng).
In the third month, on the first day *rénzǐ*,
a solemn admonition was issued to young princes to study and practice horsemanship and archery,
and not to rely on their noble status to act dissolutely.
On the day *guǐchǒu*,
daily lecture officials (rìjiǎngguān) were appointed.
On the day *gēngwǔ*,
due to lack of rain, wind, and haze,
an imperial edict was issued to practice self-reflection and reform.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day *yǐyǒu*,
an order was issued to compile the Sacred Instructions (Shèngxùn) of Tàizǔ and Tàizōng.
An edict stated that idle members of the imperial clan (zōngrén xiánsǎn) and orphaned children
should be provided with appropriate sustenance,
and this was to be established as a regulation.
On the day *bǐngxū*,
an edict was issued to clarify common judicial cases,
reducing punishments by one degree for those that were questionable or deserving of clemency.
On the day *xīnmǎo*,
the daily lectures (rìjiǎng) officially began.
On the day *rénchén*,
the Emperor proceeded to the Temple of Heaven (Tiāntán) to pray for rain.
On the day *jiǎwǔ*,
it rained.
In the fifth month, on the day *gēngshēn*,
Kālán tú, Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs (Lǐfān Yuàn Shàngshū), requested retirement,
was granted the title of Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent (Tàizǐ Tàibǎo),
and appointed Inner Grandee (Nèi Dàchén) to attend court.
On the day *guǐyǒu*,
the Emperor visited the Southern Park (Nányuàn).
In the sixth month, on the day *dīnghài*,
Jìn Fǔ was appointed Governor of Ānhuī.
On the day *jiǎwǔ*,
Venus was seen during the day.
This month,
Prince Jìngnán Gěng Jìmào passed away,
and his son Jīngzhōng inherited the enfeoffment,
continuing to guard Fújiàn.
In the eighth month, on the first day *jǐmǎo*,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day *dīngwèi*,
the Emperor presided over the Imperial Lectures.
On the day *wùshēn*,
Wáng Zhīdǐng was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Jiāngnán.
In the ninth month, on the day *gēngxū*,
the Emperor announced the unification of the empire,
reporting its completion at the two imperial tombs.
On the day *xīnhài*,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Grand Empress Dowager and the Empress Dowager, departed in the imperial carriage.
Princes, *beile*, and dukes of the Měnggǔ Kēěrqìn, Kālāqìn, Tǔmòtè, and Áohàn tribes paid homage at the imperial traveling palace (xíngzài).
On the day *dīngmǎo*,
visits were made to Fúlíng and Zhāolíng.
On the day *wùchén*,
sacrifices were offered at Fúlíng,
and the ceremony of completion was performed.
On the day *gēngwǔ*,
sacrifices were offered at Zhāolíng,
and the ceremony of completion was performed.
On the day *xīnwèi*,
the Emperor visited Shèngjīng,
held court at Qīngníng Gōng,
bestowed a banquet upon all officials,
and summoned those eighty years and older to be personally offered wine.
Great rewards of silver were given to soldiers (jiǎshì) in Fèngtiān and Nínggǔtǎ, and to the wounded, disabled, old, and sick;
elderly people among the populace also received the same.
Death sentences were commuted by one degree,
and those exiled for military service or lesser crimes were released.
Along the imperial route outside Shānhǎiguān,
the land taxes for the current and next year were remitted.
Officials were dispatched to offer sacrifices at the tombs of various princes and ministers.
On the day *rénshēn*,
the Emperor made an eastern tour from Shèngjīng.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day *xīnsì*,
the Emperor stopped at Àixīn.
General Bāhǎi of Nínggǔtǎ was summoned,
and instructed to treat the newly attached Wǎěrkā and Hǔěrhā kindly.
On the day *jǐchǒu*,
the Emperor returned to Shèngjīng,
and again bestowed silver upon the elderly.
On the day *xīnmǎo*,
visits were made to Fúlíng and Zhāolíng.
Civil and military officials were ordered to hold archery competitions.
Outer vassals (wàifān) who came to court were ordered to hold archery competitions.
On the day *rénchén*,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Grand Empress Dowager and the Empress Dowager, returned in the imperial carriage.
In the eleventh month, on the day *gēngxū*,
they returned to the capital.
On the day *rénshēn*,
Míngzhū was appointed Minister of War (Bīngbù Shàngshū).
In the twelfth month, on the day *bǐngwǔ*,
the combined ancestral sacrifice was performed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
This year,

remission of disaster taxes and outstanding taxes (zāifù būfù) was granted to 302 prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Jiāngxī, Zhèjiāng, Shāndōng, Hénán, Shǎnxī, and Húguǎng provinces, with varying degrees of remission.
Cháoxiǎn and Líuqiú offered tribute.
In the eleventh year, on the *rénzǐ* spring first month, on the day *xīnwèi*,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Grand Empress Dowager, visited Chìchéng Tāngquán,
passing through Bādálǐng,
where he personally supported the imperial palanquin,
walking down the mountain.
In the second month, on the day *wùyín*,
the Grand Empress Dowager was escorted to Tāngquán.
On the day *xīnmǎo*,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day *bǐngshēn*,
he personally ploughed the sacred field (jítián).
On the day *dīngyǒu*,
he greeted the sun in the eastern suburbs.
On the day *wùxū*,
the Emperor proceeded to Chìchéng.
In the third month, on the day *wùchén*,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Grand Empress Dowager, returned to the palace.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day *yǐsì*,
Imperial Bodyguard (Shìwèi) Wú Dān and Academician (Xuéshì) Guō Tíngzuò were ordered to inspect river works.
In the fifth month, on the day *yǐchǒu*,
the *Veritable Records of Shìzǔ* (Shìzǔ Shílù) were completed.
On the day *bǐngyín*,
the Emperor went out of Déshèngmén to inspect the wheat.
In the sixth month, on the day *gēngyín*,
an order was issued to revise and compile the *Comprehensive Book of Land and Labor Taxes* (Fùyì Quánshū).
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day *jǐyǒu*,
rewards were granted for meritorious service in the campaigns against Miǎndiàn, Yúnnán, and Guìzhōu,
with hereditary official posts (shìzhí) bestowed upon 127 individuals, including Hé Jiànzhōng.
On the day *bǐngchén*,
the Emperor inspected the crops.
Censor Mèng Xióngfēi submitted a memorial stating that Sūn Kěwàng, having been in dire straits, surrendered
and was improperly granted a princely enfeoffment.
After his death,
the peerage had already been inherited twice.
Now that Sūn Zhēngchún has died,
it is appropriate to downgrade the inheritance.
An edict downgraded the inheritance to Prince Mùyì (Mùyì Gōng).
In the intercalary seventh month,
Shàng Shàn was again enfeoffed as *Beile*.
On the day *dīnghài*,
an edict was issued to judges not to use harsh torture leading to death in legal cases,
and offenders would be punished.
In the eighth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
the Emperor proceeded to the Southern Park for a hunt.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
an imperial edict stated:
"For emperors and kings to achieve good governance,
it is essential to uphold public morals
and distinguish ranks and statuses.
Recently, officials have been indulging in extravagant and unauthorized clothing and practices,
competing to imitate each other.
Let a ban on these practices be deliberated upon."
On the day Gēngshēn,
the Emperor attended the Imperial Lectures (Jīngyán).
On the day Rénxū,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, visited the Hot Springs in Zūnhuà.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
he reviewed the officials and soldiers of Jìzhōu in archery practice.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the Emperor paid homage at Xiàolíng.
In the ninth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
he reviewed the Zūnhuà troops and Sāntúnyíng troops.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, returned to the palace.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Fàn Chéngmó was appointed Governor-General of Fújiàn.
In the eleventh month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
the Emperor visited the Southern Park
and had a temporary palace built.
In the twelfth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
Yù Qīnwáng Fúquán, Zhuāng Qīnwáng Bóguǒduó, Huì Jùnwáng Bówēngguǒnuò, and Wēn Jùnwáng Mèng'é submitted memorials requesting to resign from deliberation on state affairs.
This was granted.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the Emperor summoned the lecturers and instructed them, saying:
"Someone has requested that censorial officials be permitted to speak on matters based on hearsay.
I believe that there is no lack of words that are truly pertinent to affairs.
However,
if one uses pretexts to stir up trouble,
to frame and disturb,
it is deeply detrimental to governance.
To allow the people to rest
lies in not disturbing them.
If the vital energy is wasted,
then the people's livelihood will be distressed."
On the day Jǐwèi,
Kāng Qīnwáng Jiéshū and Ān Qīnwáng Yuèlè submitted memorials requesting to resign from deliberation on state affairs.
This was not permitted.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
a joint sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple (Tàimiào).
In this year,

tax remissions were granted, varying in degree, for disaster-stricken areas in 141 prefectures, counties, and garrisons (wèi) in the provinces of Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Zhèjiāng, Shāndōng, Shānxī, Hénán, and Húguǎng.
Cháoxiǎn (Korea) presented tribute.
In the twelfth year, on the day Guǐchǒu, in spring, the first month, on the day Gēngyín,
the Emperor visited the Southern Park
for a grand review.
In the second month, on the day Xīnhài,
Wú Zhèngzhì was appointed Left Censor-in-chief (Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ).
On the day Rénzǐ,
the Emperor attended the Imperial Lectures (Jīngyán)
and ordered the lecturers to be on duty daily.
On the day Wùchén,
the *Dàxué Yǎnyì* (Elaboration of the Great Learning) was bestowed upon the Eight Banners official schools for translation.
In the third month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
the Emperor inspected the wheat fields.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Píngnánwáng Shàng Kěxǐ requested retirement,
which was granted;
he then requested that his son, Zhīxìn, inherit his title and command the forces in Yuè,
but this was not granted,
and he was ordered to dismantle his feudatory (fān) and return to Liaodong.
On the day Guǐsì,
Hán Tǎn and 166 others were granted the *Jìnshì Jíyì Chūshēn* degree, with varying ranks.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Dīngsì,
officials were dispatched to enfeoff the King of Xiāmluó (Siam).
In the fifth month, on the day Rénshēn,
Academician Fù Dálǐ and others requested to suspend lectures on the Summer Solstice.
The Emperor said:
"The path of learning
should have no interruptions.
Therefore, do not suspend them."
In the sixth month, on the day Rénwú,
Zhāng Cháozhēn was re-appointed Governor of Húguǎng,
and Lǐ Zhīfāng was appointed Governor-General of Zhèjiāng.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Emperor attended to affairs at Yíngtái,
summoned his ministers to view the lotus flowers, and bestowed a banquet upon them.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the practice of burying slaves alive with the deceased was banned for the Eight Banners.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Píngxīwáng Wú Sānguì submitted a memorial requesting the disbandment of his feudatory.
This was granted.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
heir to Jìngnánwáng Gěng Jīngzhōng submitted a memorial requesting the disbandment of his feudatory.
This was granted.
On the day Rénwǔ,
an order was issued to revise the Veritable Records of Taizong (Tàizōng Shílù).
In the eighth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
Han Chinese censorial officials (kēdào guān) were tested in the Bǎohé Diàn;
those found incompetent were dismissed.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Vice Minister Zhé'ěrkěn and Academician Fù Dálǐ were dispatched to Yúnnán,
Minister Liáng Qīngbiāo to Guǎngdōng,
and Vice Minister Chén Yībǐng to Fújiàn,
to manage the disbandment of the feudatories.
On the day Dīngsì,
an edict was issued to the Board of Rites:
"For major sacrificial ceremonies,
the rituals must be thoroughly complete and detailed
to invoke a response from the divine.
Therefore, consult ancient rites and ceremonies, deliberate, and report."
In the ninth month, on the day Wùchén,
Minister of Rites Gōng Dǐngzī requested retirement.
This was granted.
On the day Yǐhài,
an earthquake occurred in the capital,
and an imperial edict called for self-examination and reform.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Rénwú,
Wáng Zhīdǐng was appointed General of Jīngkǒu.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
the Emperor visited the Southern Park for a hunt.
In the eleventh month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
the former Ming imperial clansman Zhū Yìcóng was sentenced to death for growing his hair long.
An imperial decree granted him a reprieve from death and incorporation into a Banner,
along with a wife, house, and land.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
an imperial edict stated that private individuals who reclaimed barren land
would begin paying taxes after ten years.
In the twelfth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Yáo Wénrán was appointed Left Censor-in-chief.
Wú Sānguì rebelled,
killing Yúnnán Governor Zhū Guózhì.
Guìzhōu Provincial Military Commander Lǐ Běnshēn and Governor Cáo Shēnjí both surrendered to the rebels,
and Governor-General Gān Wénkūn died.
On the day Bǐngchén,
the news of the rebellion arrived,
and Front-rank Commander Shuòdài was ordered to lead the imperial guards to defend Jīngzhōu.
On the day Dīngsì,
Liáng Qīngbiāo and Chén Yībǐng were recalled,
and the disbandment of the two feudatories was halted.
Sūn Yánlíng was ordered to be promoted to General for Pacifying Barbarians (Fǔ Mán Jiāngjūn),
and Xiàn Guó'ān to Commandant (Dūtǒng),
to defend Guǎngxī.
Xi'ān General Wǎ'ěrkā was ordered to advance and defend Sìchuān.
In the capital, a commoner named Yáng Qǐlóng falsely claimed to be Zhū Sāntàizǐ (the Third Prince of Zhu),
planning an uprising.
The plot was discovered,
and Qǐlóng escaped.
His followers were arrested and executed.
An edict declared that the rebellion by wicked commoners had been suppressed,
and there should be no implication of others,
and the people should not be alarmed or flee.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Shùnchéng Jùnwáng Lè'ěrjǐn was appointed General-in-Chief for Pacifying Rebels in the South (Níngnán Jìngkòu Dàjiāngjūn)
to suppress Wú Sānguì.
Wú Sānguì's son, Fùmǎ Wú Yīngxióng, was seized and imprisoned.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Vice Commandant Mǎhādá was ordered to lead troops to station in Yǎnzhōu,
and Kuò'ěrkūn in Tàiyuán,
in readiness for deployment.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
an edict ordered that provincial governors (xúnfǔ) in the capital region and provinces (zhí shěng) would continue to manage military affairs.
On the day Rénxū,
an edict stripped Wú Sānguì of his noble title
and was promulgated throughout the empire.
Commandant Hèyè was appointed General for Pacifying the West (Ānxī Jiāngjūn)
to join Wǎ'ěrkā in defending Hànzhōng.
Wō Nèi was appointed General of Fèngtiān.
Wú Sānguì captured Chénzhōu.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
a joint sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In this year,
tax remissions were granted, varying in degree, for disaster-stricken areas in 26 prefectures, counties, and garrisons in the provinces of Zhílì, Shāndōng, Ānhuī, Zhèjiāng, and Húguǎng.
Cháoxiǎn and Ānnán (Annam) presented tribute.
In the thirteenth year, on the day Jiǎyín, in spring, the first month, on the day Yǐhài,
Lè'ěrjǐn's army set forth.
On the day Gēngchén,
Wú Sānguì captured Yuánzhōu.
On the day Dīnghài,
Piān-Yuán Governor Lú Zhèn abandoned Chángshā and fled.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Provincial Military Commander Tóng Guóyáo was ordered to defend Yúnxiáng.
Commander-in-chief Wú Zhīmào rebelled in Sìchuān,
and Governor Luó Sēn and Provincial Military Commander Zhèng Jiāolín surrendered to him.
Commander-in-chief Xú Zhìdū was ordered to return and defend Yílíng.
On the day Gēngyín,
the Seventh Son of Shìzǔ, Lóngxǐ, was enfeoffed as Chún Qīnwáng.
Xí Bùchén was appointed General for Pacifying the West (Zhènxī Jiāngjūn)
to defend Xī'ān.
On the *yǐwèi* day of the second month, the new moon.
The Grand Empress Dowager distributed funds from the Imperial Treasury to reward the troops.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the Qīntiān Jiān completed newly built astronomical instruments.
On the *rényín* day,
the rebels attacked Lǐzhōu.
The garrison troops betrayed the city,
and Commander-in-Chief Sāng É retreated to Jīngzhōu,
losing Chángdé.
Zhènnán Jiāngjūn Níyǎhàn was ordered to lead troops to defend Wǔchāng.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
the Emperor attended the Jīngyán lectures.
Zhào Lài was appointed Tídū of Guìzhōu.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Wú Sānguì captured Chángshā.
Vice General Huáng Zhèngqīng rebelled and joined him,
subsequently capturing Héngzhōu.
Dūtǒng Juéluó Zhūmǎn was ordered to defend Yuèzhōu.
Before he arrived,
Yuèzhōu was lost.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Mò Luò, Minister of the Board of Punishments, was granted the additional title of Grand Secretary
and appointed Administrator-in-Chief of Shǎnxī.
Sūn Yánlíng rebelled in Guǎngxī,
killing Dūtǒng Wáng Yǒngnián
and imprisoning Patrol Commissioner Mǎ Xióngzhèn.
On the *yǐchǒu* day of the third month,
an order was issued to reorganize the postal stations.
Every four hundred *lǐ*, a *bǐtiēshì* was to be stationed
to relay military dispatches
and send out urgent reports.
Zuǒdū Yùshǐ Duōnuò and others were ordered to supervise provisions at the front.
On the *wùchén* day,
Wú Sānguì's forces were about to attack Yílíng,
but Lèěrjǐn dispatched troops and defeated them.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the imperial son-in-law Huáshàn was appointed Ānnán Jiāngjūn
to guard Jīngkǒu.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Gěng Jīngzhōng revolted,
capturing and imprisoning Fújiàn Zǒngdū Fàn Chéngmó.
Patrol Commissioner Liú Bǐngzhèng surrendered to the rebels.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Yún Yáng Vice General Hóng Fú rebelled.
Commander-in-Chief Tóng Guóyáo defeated him.
On the *rénchén* day,
Xiāngyáng Zǒngbīng Yáng Láijiā rebelled with Gǔchéng.
Xīěrgēn was appointed Dìngnán Jiāngjūn,
with Minister Hāěrhāqí as his deputy.
Shūshù, Sāng'è, Gēntè, and Xíbù were ordered to lead troops to Jiāngxī.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Xī'ān Jiāngjūn Wǎěrkuākè guarded Yángpíng Guān.
In the summer, on the *guǐmǎo* day of the fourth month,
Xī'ān Vice Dūtǒng Déyèlì was transferred to guard Xiāngyáng.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Wú Sānguì's son Yìngxíong and grandson Shìlín were executed.
Initially,
Sānguì launched his rebellion hastily,
but his cause was not well-regarded,
and he later repented.
Upon reaching Lǐzhōu,
he hesitated.
At this point,
he heard the news while eating
and exclaimed in surprise:
"The young Emperor is capable of this?
The matter is settled!"
He pushed his food away and rose.
An edict was issued to dismiss Sūn Yánlíng from office.
Āmìdá was appointed Yángwēi Jiāngjūn
and stationed at Jiāngníng.
Lài Tǎ was appointed Píngnán Jiāngjūn
and dispatched to Hángzhōu.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Cháozhōu Zǒngbīng Liú Jìnzhōng rebelled with the city.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Gēntè was appointed Píngkòu Jiāngjūn
and dispatched to Guǎngxī to suppress Sūn Yánlíng.
Héběi Zǒngbīng Cài Lù plotted rebellion.
Āmìdá was ordered to ambush and execute him.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
an edict was issued to strip Gěng Jīngzhōng of his peerage.
On the *guǐhài* day,
an edict detailing the deployment of the Imperial Guards and the assignment of generals to various defenses was sent to Píngnán Wáng Shàng Kěxǐ.
On the *bǐngyín* day of the fifth month,
Imperial Prince Yìnrěng was born,
and Empress Hèshělǐshì passed away.
On the *wùyín* day,
Ānxī Jiāngjūn Hèyè and others defeated Wú Zhīmào at Zhágébǎo
and recaptured Cháotiān Guān.
On the *réngwǔ* day,
a military mutiny occurred in Píngyáng, Zhèjiāng.
Zǒngbīng Cài Cháozuǒ was seized,
and the mutineers joined Gěng Jīngzhōng's general Zēng Yǎngxìng,
besieging Ruì'ān.
Lài Tǎ was ordered to advance his troops and suppress them.
On the *rénchén* day,
Vice Dūtǒng Déyèlì defeated Hóng Fú at Wǔdāng.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day of the sixth month,
Bèilè Shàngshàn was appointed Ānyuǎn Jìngkòu Dàjiāngjūn
and ordered to lead troops to Yuèzhōu.
Bèizi Zhǔndá was dispatched to Jīngzhōu.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Zǒngbīng Zǔ Hóngxūn rebelled with Wēnzhōu.
Jīnhuá Vice General Móu Dàyín defeated Gěng Jīngzhōng's general at Chángshān.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Jiāngjūn Lāhādá was ordered to guard Hángzhōu.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Kāng Qīnwáng Jiéshū was appointed Fèngmìng Dàjiāngjūn and dispatched to Zhèjiāng.
Bèilè Dòng'è was appointed Dìngxī Dàjiāngjūn and dispatched to Sìchuān.
Wēnzhōu, Huángyán, and Tàipíng garrisons in Zhèjiāng rebelled one after another.
Lāhādá was ordered to guard Tái and Níng.
On the *xīnwèi* day of the seventh month,
Láng Tíngzuǒ was appointed Fújiàn Zǒngdū,
and Duàn Yìngjǔ was appointed Tídū.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Lài Tǎ defeated Gěng Jīngzhōng's general at Jīnhuá.
At this time, Jīngzhōng had dispatched his grand generals Mǎ Jiǔyù and Zēng Yǎngxìng to attack Zhèjiāng,
and Bái Xiǎnzhōng to attack Jiāngxī.
Bandits everywhere responded,
especially in Jiāngxī.
Nánruì Zǒngbīng Yáng Fù joined the rebels.
Dǒng Wèiguó executed him.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Bèilè Cháni fought a major battle against rebel general Wú Yìngqí at Qīlǐshān in Yuèzhōu,
defeating him.
On the *rényín* day of the eighth month,
Píngkòu Jiāngjūn Gēntè died in the army.
Hāěrhāqí was appointed to replace him.
Hǎichéng Gōng Huáng Wú died.
His son Fāngdù inherited the peerage
and guarded Zhāngzhōu.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Jīn Guāngzǔ reported that Sūn Yánlíng had captured Wúzhōu
and led troops to recapture it.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Emperor visited the Nányuàn.
On the *rénxū* day of the ninth month,
the Emperor attended the Jīngyán lectures,
ordering daily lectures to continue as usual.
Gěng Jīngzhōng's generals, with local bandits, captured Qīngxī and Huīzhōu.
Jiāngníng Jiāngjūn Échǔ and Tǒnglǐng Bāěrkān attacked and routed them,
fighting continuously into Jiāngxī,
and recaptured Lèpíng and other counties.
Shuòtǎ and others were ordered to be stationed at Ānqìng.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
local bandits Zōu Jūnshēng and others created disturbances in Máchéng.
Prefect Yú Chénglóng suppressed them.
Jiǎn Qīnwáng Lābù was appointed Yángwēi Dàjiāngjūn
and ordered to lead troops to Jiāngxī,
with Shìwèi Kūn as Zhènwǔ Jiāngjūn and his deputy.
Guǎngxī Tídū Mǎ Xióng rebelled.
Ān Qīnwáng Yuèlè was appointed Dìngyuǎn Píngkòu Dàjiāngjūn
and ordered to lead troops to Guǎngdōng,
with Zōngshì Wǎshān and Juéluó Huàtè as his deputies.
In the winter, on the *rénchén* day of the tenth month,
Lābù's army set forth.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Yuèlè's army set forth.
On the *rényín* day,
the Emperor accompanied the Grand Empress Dowager to the Nányuàn.
On the *xīnhài* day,
they returned to the palace.
On the *gēngshēn* day, the new moon of the eleventh month,
Mò Luò reported that Wú Zhīmào's forces had entered Cháotiān Guān,
obstructing the supply route,
and Dòng'è retreated to defend Xī'ān.
An order was issued to move the Xī'ān army to guard Hánzhōng,
and the Hénán army to guard Xī'ān.
On the *gēngyín* day, the new moon of the twelfth month,
Jiéshū greatly defeated Zēng Yǎngxìng at Qúzhōu,
and again defeated him at Táizhōu.
Wáng Fǔchén rebelled,
and Administrator-in-Chief Mò Luò died there.
The Emperor discussed leading a personal expedition.
However, the princes and high officials, considering the capital an essential foundation
and the Grand Empress Dowager's advanced age,
strongly advised against it, and he desisted.
Soldiers from Shèngjīng and Mongolian soldiers were summoned and dispatched to the front.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Shàng Kěxǐ was ordered to oversee military affairs in Guǎngdōng.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
a joint sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
In this year,
disaster relief was granted to seventy-eight prefectures and counties in Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Shāndōng, Hénán, and Shǎnxī provinces, varying in degree.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú paid tribute.
In the spring of the fourteenth year, *yǐmǎo*, on the *xīnyǒu* day of the first month,
Shàng Kěxǐ reported that rebels had attacked Liánzhōu,
and government troops defeated them.
On the *wùchén* day,
Shàng Kěxǐ was promoted to Píngnán Qīnwáng,
and his son Zhīxiào was ordered to bear the Grand General's seal and suppress the rebels.
In the second month, on the day *Guǐsì*,
an edict was issued severely reprimanding Bèi Lè Dòng'è for his retreat and loss of opportunity,
ordering him to swiftly secure Píngliáng and Qínzhōu to open up the plank road.
On the day *Yǐsì*,
Kāng Qīn Wáng Jiéshū dispatched troops to retake Chǔzhōu,
and advanced to retake Xiānjū.
Wáng Fǔchén captured Lánzhōu.
Xīníng General Soldier Wáng Jìnbǎo fought a great battle at Xīnchéng,
and besieged Lánzhōu.
Dòng'è retook Lǒngzhōu and Guānshānguān.
In the third month, on the first day *Jǐwèi*,
rebel general Yáng Láijiā attacked Nánzhāng,
General Soldier Liú Chénglóng repulsed him.
On the day *Wùchén*,
bandits from Ráozhōu attacked Qímén,
Patrol Inspector Zhāng Xíngjiàn was captured but refused to yield,
and died.
On the day *Dīngchǒu*,
Zhāng Yǒng was ordered to be Jìngnì Jiāngjūn (General who Quells Rebellion),
to join General Soldier Sūn Sīkè and others in suppressing Wáng Fǔchén.
Bandits captured Dìngbiānchéng,
and Commander Chén Fú was ordered to be stationed in Níngxià to suppress the bandits.
On the day *Dīnghài*,
Měnggǔ Bù'ěrní rebelled,
Xìn Jùnwáng Èzhā was ordered to be Fǔyuǎn Dàjiāngjūn (Generalissimo who Pacifies Afar),
Grand Secretary Túhǎi was made Vice-General,
to suppress and pacify them.
On the day *Wùzǐ*,
Xióng Cìlǚ was appointed Grand Secretary.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day *Jǐchǒu*,
Lèdéhóng was appointed Hùbù Shàngshū (Minister of Revenue).
Acting Commander of the Imperial Guards Lángsù and others suppressed Gěng's bandits at Wǔguìzhài,
beheading twenty thousand,
and retook Yúgàn.
On the day *Yǐwèi*,
Zhāng Yǒng was enfeoffed as Jìngnì Hóu (Marquis who Quells Rebellion),
Wáng Jìnbǎo as a first-class male.
On the day *Wùxū*,
Left Governor Xǔ Zhēn was appointed to govern Fúzhōu, Jiànchāng, and Guǎngxìn.
On the day *Wùshēn*,
Wáng Fǔchén dispatched troops to reinforce Qínzhōu,
but the government troops met and defeated them.
On the day *Xīnhài*,
the Emperor decreed:
"When court officials lecture,
I will lecture in return,
discussing with each other,
so that there may be enlightenment."
On the day *Guǐchǒu*,
Wáng Jìnbǎo retook Líntáo,
Sūn Sīkè retook Jìngyuǎn.
On the day *Wùwǔ*,
Shàoxīng Prefect Xǔ Hóngxūn recruited and pacified fifty thousand surrendered people.
In the fifth month, on the day *Gēngwǔ*,
the Four Banners of Cháhā'ěr Left Wing surrendered.
On the day *Gēngchén*,
Bìlìkètú was ordered to reinforce Yúlín.
Wáng Fǔchén's troops captured Yán'ān and Suídé.
On the day *Jiǎshēn*,
Zhāng Yǒng retook the two prefectures of Táo and Hé.
In the intercalary fifth month, on the day *Guǐsì*,
the Emperor visited Yùquánshān to observe the crops.
Yáng Láijiā and Hóng Fú captured Gǔchéng.
Vice General Mǎláng'ā, who failed to defend the city, was beheaded for public display,
General Soldier Jīn Shìxū was stripped of his position,
and ordered to serve with the army to atone.
On the day *Rénzǐ*,
Échǔ retook Guǎngxìn.
Lèpíng local bandits again captured Ráozhōu,
General Xī'ěrgēn attacked them,
and retook Ráozhōu.
In the sixth month,
Bìlìkètú retook Wúbǎo,
and retook Suídé.
On the day *Dīngchǒu*,
General Shūshù was ordered to reinforce Guǎngdōng.
On the day *Jǐmǎo*,
Zhènwǔ Jiāngjūn (General who Awe-Inspires Militancy) Fónílè was ordered to open up the plank road to reinforce Hànzhōng.
On the day *Gēngchén*,
the Emperor went to Nányuàn for a hunt.
On the day *Rénwǔ*,
Zhāng Yǒng attacked Gǒngchāng.
Jiāngxī government troops attacked Shíxiá,
suffered a defeat,
and Vice Deputy Commander Yǎlài died in battle.
On the day *Jiǎshēn*,
Lánzhōu was captured.
Bìlìkètú retook Yán'ān.
Due to the military campaign, the provincial examinations in Shǎnxī and Húguǎng were suspended.
In the seventh month, on the day *Yǐsì*,
Chén Fú suppressed Dìngbiān,
and beheaded bandit general Zhū Lóng.
On the day *Gēngxū*,
Jiāngxī government troops retook Fúliáng, Lèpíng, Yíhuáng, Chóngrén, and Lè'ān counties.
In the eighth month, on the day *Wùwǔ*,
the Emperor went to Nányuàn for a hunt.
Dòng'è, Bìlìkètú, and Āmìdá jointly attacked Wáng Fǔchén,
beheading bandit general Hǎo Tiānxiáng.
Fùlātǎ retook Huángyán.
On the day *Rénshēn*,
the Emperor accompanied the Grand Empress Dowager to Tāngquán.
On the day *Jiǎshēn*,
the Emperor returned to the capital,
and presided over the imperial lectures.
In the ninth month,
the Emperor stopped at Chāngpíng,
visited the Míng Tombs,
offered sacrifices at Chánglíng,
and dispatched officials to offer sacrifices at the other tombs.
On the day *Bǐngshēn*,
the Emperor accompanied the Grand Empress Dowager back to the palace.
On the day *Xīnchǒu*,
an edict decreed that executions be suspended in the first month of every year,
to be established as a permanent regulation.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day *Guǐhài*,
Kāng Qīn Wáng's troops retook Tàipíng, Lèqīng, and other counties.
On the day *Bǐngyín*,
the Emperor paid respects at Xiàolíng.
On the day *Wùchén*,
sacrifices were offered at Xiàolíng.
On the day *Yǐhài*,
returned to the palace.
Chén Fú and Wáng Fǔchén battled at Gùyuán,
but suffered a defeat,
and Vice General Tàibìtú died in battle.
For the merits in pacifying Bù'ěrní,
rewards and promotions were granted with variations,
and the Mongolian kings and Bèi Lès who assisted, such as Shājīn, were all advanced in rank,
while the Nàimàn and other tribes who aided the rebels were punished.
In the eleventh month, on the day *Guǐsì*,
Bèi Lè Chání retook Xìngshān.
On the day *Dīngyǒu*,
officials of the Zhànshìfǔ (Court of Imperial Stud) were re-established.
On the day *Rényín*,
rebel general Mǎ Xióng, in league with Wú Sānguì's troops, attacked Gāozhōu,
and successively captured Liánzhōu.
Jiǎn Qīn Wáng Lābù was ordered to reinforce Guǎngdōng from Jiāngxī.
In this month,
Zhèng Jǐn attacked and captured Zhāngzhōu,
Hǎichéng Gōng Huáng Fāngdù died,
and his family was murdered.
In the twelfth month, on the day *Bǐngyín*,
Imperial Prince Yìnrěng was established as Crown Prince,
an edict was issued to the country,
granting grace and general amnesty.
On the day *Yǐhài*,
as Lè'ěrjǐn's army had been campaigning for a long time without success,
the positions of his参赞 (cānzàn, counselor) Bā'ěrbù and others below him were stripped.
The Níngxià army mutinied,
and Commander Chén Fú died.
On the day *Rénwǔ*,
a combined sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted in varying degrees for seven prefectures and five sub-prefectures and counties in Húguǎng and Hénán.
Cháoxiǎn (Korea) paid tribute.
In the fifteenth year, *Bǐngchén*, spring, first month, on the day *Dīnghài*,
Wáng Jìnbǎo was appointed Shǎnxī Commander,
stationed at Qínzhōu.
On the day *Jiǎwǔ*,
