in celebration of the establishment of the heir, honorary titles were respectfully conferred upon the Grand Empress Dowager and Empress Dowager.
On the day *Yǐwèi*,
the position of Níngxià General Soldier was promoted to Commander,
and Zhào Liángdòng was appointed to it.
On the day *Xīnchǒu*,
the Emperor went to Nányuàn for a hunt.
In the second month, on the day *Dīngsì*,
an edict forbade killing and looting when capturing cities in the army.
On the day *Rénxū*,
Grand Secretary Túhǎi was appointed Fǔyuǎn Dàjiāngjūn (Generalissimo who Pacifies Afar),
to command all of Qín (Shaanxi),
and all from Bèi Lè Dòng'è downwards were subject to his control.
On the day *Guǐyǒu*,
the Emperor went to Gǒnghuá Chéng,
and instructed his entourage not to trample the spring fields.
On the day *Yǐhài*,
Wú Sānguì's general Gāo Dàjié captured Jí'ān.
On the day *Wùyín*,
Ān Qīn Wáng Yuèlè attacked Sānguì's general at Píngxiāng,
defeated him,
and retook Píngxiāng.
On the day *Xīnsì*,
the Emperor presided over the imperial lectures.
Deceased Vice General Zhāng Guóyàn was posthumously granted the title of Tàizǐ Tàibǎo (Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince),
and hereditary position.
On the *guǐwèi* day of the third month,
Huáng Fāngdù, Duke of Hǎichéng, was posthumously granted the title of prince.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Wáng Jìnbǎo and Fónílè greatly defeated Wú Zhīmào at Běishān.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Fùlātǎ besieged Wēnzhōu.
Zēng Yǎngxìng and Zǔ Hóngxūn led all their troops to attack.
Vice Commander-in-chief Jì'ěrtābù repelled them.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Yuèzhōu naval forces captured Jūnshān.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Lè'ěrjǐn crossed the river and fought against Sānguì's forces,
defeating them repeatedly.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Péng Dìngqiú and 208 others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with varying ranks.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Lè'ěrjǐn fought Sānguì's forces at Tàipíng Jiē,
suffered a disadvantage,
and retreated to defend Jīngzhōu.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Zhào Lài was transferred to be Provincial Commander of Jiāngxī.
In summer, on the *xīnchǒu* day of the fourth month,
Mǎ Xióng and Zǔ Zéqīng gathered Dīan rebels to attack Guǎngdōng.
Shàng Kěxǐ, old and ill, was unable to lead the army.
He repeatedly sent urgent memorials,
but reinforcements did not arrive in time.
By this time,
the rebels were pressing on Guǎngzhōu.
Shàng Zhīxìn seized his father and surrendered to the rebels.
Governor-general Jīn Guāngzǔ,
Provincial Governors Tóng Yǎngjù and Chén Hóngmíng,
and Provincial Commander Yán Zìmíng all surrendered with him.
Fújiàn Provincial Governor Yáng Xī and Commander-in-chief Bàiyīndá forced their way out.
Shūshù and Mǎngyītú retreated to Jiāngxī.
Upon hearing of the change in Guǎngdōng,
the Emperor ordered troops to reinforce Jiāngxī.
On the first day of the fifth month, *rénwǔ*,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Governorship of Yúnyáng was re-established,
with Yáng Màoxūn appointed to it.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
an envoy from Tsar Chaghan of Russia came to offer tribute.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Generalissimo Fǔyuǎn Túhǎi defeated Wáng Fǔchén at Píngliáng.
On the first day of the sixth month, *rénzǐ*,
Wáng Fǔchén surrendered,
and Túhǎi reported it.
An imperial edict reinstated his office,
appointed him General Jìngkòu,
and allowed him to prove himself through meritorious service.
All generals and officers were pardoned.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Gěng Jìshàn abandoned Jiànchāng and fled.
The Emperor issued an edict to Jiéshū, saying:
"Gěng Jīngzhōng has withdrawn his troops,
evidently compelled by the sea pirates.
Seize this opportunity and advance quickly."
On the first day of the seventh month, *xīnsì*,
the Russian envoy was bestowed with a saddle, horse, clothes, and other items.
Grand Secretary Xióng Cìlǚ was dismissed.
Mù Tiānyán was appointed Provincial Governor of Jiāngsū.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Yáo Wénrán was appointed Minister of Punishments,
and Láng Tíngxiāng was appointed Governor-general of Fújiàn.
General Zhènwǔ Fónílè, together with Zhāng Yǒng and Wáng Jìnbǎo, attacked Wú Zhīmào at Qínzhōu,
greatly defeating him.
The rebels fled during the night.
On the *jiǎyín* day of the eighth month,
Mùzhàn recovered Lǐxiàn.
On the *rénxū* day,
the Emperor escorted the Empress Dowager to Tāngquán.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Lài Tǎ attacked Mǎ Jiǔyù at Qúzhōu,
recovering Jiāngshān.
Mǎ Jiǔyù abandoned his army and fled.
On the first day of the ninth month, *gēngchén*,
Lài Tǎ advanced and attacked Mǎ Jiǔyù,
defeating him and
recovering Chángshān.
He then attacked Xiānxiá Pass.
Rebel general Jīn Yīnghǔ surrendered with the city,
recovering Púchéng,
and successively taking Jiànníng.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Zhāng Yǒng recovered Jiēzhōu.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Gěng Jīngzhōng murdered former Governor-general Fàn Chéngmó.
Shānxī Provincial Governor Dá'ěrbù was dismissed for a crime.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Mùzhàn was ordered to be General Zhēngnán,
and to move his troops to Húguǎng.
In winter, on the *xīnyǒu* day of the tenth month,
the Emperor escorted the Empress Dowager back to the palace.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Prince Kāng Jiéshū's army reached Yánpíng.
Rebel general Gěng Jìměi surrendered the city.
Gěng Jīngzhōng sent his son Xiǎnzuò to present his counterfeit seal and beg for surrender.
Jiéshū entered Fúzhōu,
and memorialized this.
The Emperor ordered his title reinstated,
and that he should prove himself by joining the campaign against the sea pirates.
His general Zēng Yǎngxìng and the rebellious general Zǔ Hóngxūn both surrendered.
The government troops and officials of Zhèjiāng recovered Wēnzhōu and Chǔzhōu prefectures.
The garrison troops at Yǎnzhōu were withdrawn.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the lecturers were ordered to lecture on the *Tōngjiàn*.
On the *bǐngxū* day of the eleventh month,
sea pirates attacked Fúzhōu.
Commander-in-chief Lāhādá defeated them.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the government army besieged Chángshā.
General Nínghǎi, Bèizi Fùlātǎ, died in the army.
On the *rénzǐ* day of the twelfth month,
Gěng Zhāozhōng was dispatched as General Zhènpíng,
stationed in Fúzhōu,
to command a portion of the Jìngnán vassal army.
Rebellious general Yán Zìmíng attacked Nánkāng.
Shūshù repelled him.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Shàng Zhīxìn sent an envoy to Prince Jiǎn's army to beg for surrender,
and also to request military aid.
This was reported in a memorial.
It was granted.
Wú Sānguì's general Wú Shìcóng killed Sūn Yánlíng
and occupied Guìlín.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Huáng Fāngshì, Duke of Hǎichéng, escaped from the rebels and returned.
The Emperor commended him,
added the title Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince,
and ordered him and his younger brother Huáng Lán to join Prince Kāng's grand army to suppress the rebels.
General Jiànwēi Wú Dān recovered Shānyáng.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
gold and silk were distributed as rewards to the soldiers of all armies.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
a joint sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
Gěng Jìshàn abandoned Shàowǔ,
and the sea pirates occupied it.
Vice Commander-in-chief Mùhèlín attacked them.
Rebel general Péng Shìxūn surrendered the city.
In this year,
tax exemptions of varying degrees were granted for disaster-stricken areas in 34 prefectures and counties across Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Jiāngxī, and Shǎnxī provinces.
Cháoxiǎn offered tribute.
In the sixteenth year, the spring of *dīngsì*, on the *bǐngshēn* day of the first month,
General Échǔ's attack on Jí'ān was unsuccessful.
Vice Minister Bāndí was ordered to rush to investigate the military situation.
On the *jǐwèi* day of the second month,
the Emperor went to Nányuàn for a hunt.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
a grand review was held at Nányuàn.
This year's rent and taxes for Fújiàn were remitted,
and scattered refugees were called to return.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Ènèi was appointed General Tǎonì,
and dispatched to Yuèzhōu.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Prince Kāng Jiéshū defeated Zhèng Jǐn at Xīng and Quán.
The rebels abandoned Zhāngzhōu and fled,
and Hǎichéng was recovered.
Director Lángzhōng Sèdù was sent to comfort the troops at Yuèzhōu
and inspect the military situation.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Jìn Fǔ was appointed Governor-general of Riverways.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
in recognition of the achievements in suppressing rebels at Huāmǎchí,
Mongolian Öljeyit Noyan Sonómu and others from the Ördös were promoted in rank to varying degrees.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the Emperor attended the imperial lectures (*jīngyán*).
In this month, the government forces of Jiāngxī recovered Ruìjīn and Qiānshān.
In the third month, on the day of Jiǎshēn,
Mǎngyītuó was appointed Commander-in-chief Pacifying the South,
to command troops in Guǎngdōng.
On Jǐchǒu,
an imperial edict was issued to the Ministry of Rites:
“Emperors must be diligent in observing Heaven’s warnings.
Whatever portents appear
are all related to governance.
Special officials are appointed
to diligently oversee astrological observations.
Now, the stars have encroached [upon other celestial bodies],
and frost and dew have appeared out of season.
The Qīn tiān jiān (Imperial Observatory) has not reported truthfully,
failing in its duties.
Investigate and deliberate on this, and then report.”
On Gēngyín,
members of the Hànlín Academy skilled in prose, poetry, and calligraphy
were ordered to present their works.
On Yǐwèi,
former commanders-in-chief Liú Jìnzhōng and Miáo Zhīxiù came to Prince Kāng Jíshū’s army and surrendered.
They were ordered to join the main army in suppressing the rebels.
On Kuǐwèi,
an imperial edict stated:
“Since the start of the war,
civil and military officials have sacrificed themselves for the frontier,
fully upholding their loyalty and integrity.
That some of their coffins cannot return [home]
and their wives and children cannot be supported
is deeply saddening.
Local frontier officials shall investigate clearly
and properly provide for their transportation and sustenance,
to manifest the utmost intention of commending loyalty.”
On Jiǎchén,
the star Hányù was seen,
and auspicious clouds appeared.
On Yǐsì,
Wú Sānguì gathered troops and defended Chángshā.
Lè'ěrjǐn was ordered to advance to Línjiāng,
Túhǎi to defend Hànzhōng,
Lābù to garrison Jí'ān,
Mǎngyītuó to advance to Sháozhōu,
Èchǔ to station at Yuánzhōu,
and Shūshù to guard Gànzhōu.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on Jǐwèi,
Prince Kāng Jíshū submitted a memorial stating that the common people Wú Chénrèn and others from Qìngyuán County, Chǔzhōu Prefecture, were unwilling to follow the rebels,
formed stockades to secure themselves,
upheld righteousness, and killed rebels,
which was truly commendable.
He had already instructed the Governor and Governor-General of Zhèjiāng
to employ those who rendered service
and reward those who returned to farming.
He also requested imperial favor and compassionate relief for those who died in battle, such as the commissioned守備 (Shǒubèi) Wú Shòunán.
This was granted.
On Xīnyǒu,
the Emperor went to Bàzhōu for a hunt.
Yīsāng'ā was appointed Minister of Works,
and Sòng Déyí was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
On Dīngmǎo,
Admiral Zhào Lài defeated local bandits at Tàihé,
capturing the bandit chief Xiāo Yuán.
On Wùchén,
officials such as Chén Dānchì, who died in the Wēnchǔ Circuit, were granted hereditary privileges.
On Xīnwèi,
the Emperor composed the "Ode to Great Virtue and Auspicious Fortune,"
inscribed it on a screen,
and presented it to the Grand Empress Dowager.
On Yǐhài,
Mǎngyītuó's army reached Nán'ān,
and Yán Zìmíng surrendered the city.
Consequently, Nánxióng was conquered,
and they entered Sháozhōu.
In the fifth month, on Jǐmǎo,
Shàng Zhīxìn surrendered.
He was ordered to have his title restored
and to join the main army in suppressing the rebels.
Fù Hóngliè, who had been banished to a military outpost as a prefect, was specially promoted to Governor of Guǎngxī.
Previously,
Hóngliè had been banished to Wúzhōu for reporting Wú Sānguì's rebellion.
When the war broke out,
Hóngliè submitted a memorial outlining strategies,
hence this appointment.
Soon after, he was additionally appointed General Pacifying Barbarians and Exterminating Bandits,
to plan the capture of Guǎngxī with Mǎngyītuó.
On Jiǎwǔ,
Èlǔtè Gá'ěrdān attacked and defeated Khalkha Chechen Khan
and came to offer military supplies,
which were refused.
In the sixth month, on Dīngsì,
Zǔ Zéqīng surrendered Gāozhōu.
In the autumn, in the seventh month, on Gēngzǐ,
Zhèng Jǐn's general Liú Guóxuān attacked Dōngguǎn from Huìzhōu.
Shàng Zhīxìn decisively defeated him,
and the rebel general Chén Lián surrendered Huìzhōu.
On Jiǎchén,
the Emperor attended the Biàndiàn (informal hall),
summoned Grand Secretaries and others, granted them seats,
and discussed classics and histories.
He then touched upon the evils of factionalism in previous dynasties
and issued a warning to be vigilant.
Míngzhū and Juéluó Lèdéhóng were appointed Grand Secretaries.
In the eighth month, on Dīngwèi,
Zhū Tǒngchàng, a descendant of the Míng imperial clan, raised an army and captured Guìxī and Lúxī.
On Jǐwèi,
the Emperor attended the Jīngyán (imperial lectures on classics).
On Bǐngyín,
Imperial Consort Niǔhùlù Shì was formally installed as Empress,
and Tóngjiā Shì as Imperial Consort.
On Wùchén,
Fù Hóngliè and others recaptured Wúzhōu.
In the ninth month, on Bǐngzǐ,
Prince Wēnqí of the imperial clan and Admiral Zhōu Bóshì were ordered to Húguǎng to assist in the suppression.
On Kuǐwèi,
the imperial son-in-law Huáshàn was ordered to lead troops to reinforce Prince Jiǎn's army,
and Kē'ěrkēdài was ordered to take over the garrison at Jiāngníng.
On Dīnghài,
the Emperor departed from Jīngshī (the capital),
paid respects at Xiàolíng,
and inspected the nearby frontier.
On Bǐngshēn,
he arrived at Kālāhétún.
On Gēngzǐ,
he arrived at Dáxīkābùqīn'áng'ā.
Zhámùsū and others from the Àohàn tribe of the nearby frontier Mongols paid respects at the Emperor's temporary residence,
offering camels and horses,
and were granted gold and silks.
Wú Sānguì's generals Hú Guózhù and Mǎ Bǎo raided Sháozhōu.
Generals Mǎngyītuó and Èchǔ attacked them from two sides and defeated them.
The rebels fled,
and were pursued past Lèchāng,
and Rénhuà was recaptured.
In the winter, in the tenth month, on Jiǎchén,
the Emperor arrived at Tāngquán.
On Kuǐchǒu,
he returned to the palace.
Fù Hóngliè defeated Wú Shìcóng at Zhāopíng,
and recaptured Xúnzhōu.
Wú Xīngzuò, the Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Fújiàn, defeated Zhū Tǒngchàng at Guāngzé,
and his followers captured Tǒngchàng and surrendered.
On Kuǐhài,
the Nánshūfáng (Southern Study) was first established,
and Lecturer of the Academy Zhāng Yīng and Secretary Gāo Shìqí were ordered to serve there.
In the eleventh month, on Jǐmǎo,
Wú Sānguì's general Hán Dàrèn captured Wàn'ān.
Commander of the Household Guard Hākèshān attacked and defeated him.
On Gēngzǐ,
the god of Chángbáishān was enfeoffed,
and officials were dispatched to offer sacrifices from a distance.
In this month,
government troops recaptured Chálíng and Yōuxiàn.
In the twelfth month, on Yǐsì,
sea pirates attacked Quánzhōu.
Admiral Duàn Yìngjǔ and others defended against them.
On Xīnhài,
sea pirates attacked Qīnzhōu.
Guerrilla Commander Liú Shìguì attacked and defeated them.
Advisor Lèbèi and General Èchǔ were ordered to advance and capture Chēnzhōu and Yǒngzhōu.
On Jǐsì,
Féng Sū was appointed Vice Minister of Justice.
On Xīnyǒu,
Venus was seen in daylight.
On Xīnwèi,
a grand joint sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In this year,
various disaster taxes in seventy prefectures and counties in Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Jiāngxī, Shǎnxī, and Húguǎng provinces were remitted.
Cháoxiǎn (Korea) sent tribute.
In the seventeenth year, the spring of Wùwǔ, in the first month, on Jǐchǒu,
Deputy Lieutenant-General Hādāng and Commander-in-Chief Xǔ Zhēn attacked Hán Dàrèn at Níngdū.
Dàrèn fled to Tīngzhōu
and came before Prince Kāng's army to surrender.
He was ordered to be captured and sent to the capital.
On Rénchén,
Guō Sìhǎi was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
On Yǐwèi,
an imperial edict stated:
“The rise of an era
must be accompanied by broadly learned and eminent scholars to revitalize the literary arts,
expound on the classics and histories,
and be available for consultation.
When We have leisure from Our myriad duties,
We wish to find broadly knowledgeable scholars
to assist in matters of scholarship.
Therefore, for those who possess both excellent scholarship and conduct, and outstanding literary talent,
regardless of whether they are already in office or not,
Our officials, both within and outside the capital, shall each recommend those they know.
We shall personally examine them.”
Thereupon, Grand Secretary Lǐ Wèi and others recommended seventy-one individuals, including Cáo Róng.
They were ordered to assemble in the capital and await imperial instructions.
In the second month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
Fù Hóngliè submitted a memorial stating that Wú Sānguì's troops had invaded Guǎngxī.
An imperial edict ordered Èchǔ and Lèbèi to defend Wúzhōu.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the Emperor attended the *jīngyán* (class on the Classics)
and composed a preface to the "Lectures and Expositions on the Four Books".
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Empress Niǔhùlùshì passed away
and was posthumously named Xiàozhāo Empress.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Mǎngyītuó and Wú Shìcóng fought at Pínglè,
suffered a defeat,
and retreated to defend Wúzhōu.
Shàng Zhīxìn and Commander Mǎ Jiǔyù were ordered to combine forces to defend Wúzhōu.
In the third month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Húguǎng government troops attacked Yáng Láijiā and Hóng Fú,
defeated them,
and retook Fángxiàn.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
sea pirates attacked Shímén,
and Huáng Fāngshì defeated them.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Zǔ Zéqīng again rebelled, aligning with Wú Sānguì.
In the intercalary third month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor toured the nearby suburbs.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Grand Minister of the Interior Kādài and Minister Mǎlā were ordered to go to the forty-nine banners of Kē'ěrqìn to preside over the alliance.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Wú Sānguì's general Lín Xīngzhū surrendered before the army of Ān Qīnwáng,
and an imperial edict enfeoffed him as Jiànyì Hóu
to follow the army in suppressing the rebels.
Vice Commander Gāndùhǎi and Ājìntài were arrested and interrogated
for missing a strategic opportunity in suppressing rebels in Jiāngxī.
In summer, fourth month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
sea pirate Cài Yín captured Pínghé
and advanced to threaten Cháozhōu.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Zǔ Zéqīng attacked Diànbái;
Shàng Zhīxìn and Èchǔ attacked him,
and Zéqīng fled.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the local bandit Yuán Běnxìu caused unrest in Qìngyáng,
and government troops attacked and beheaded him.
In the fifth month, on the first day, *gēngzǐ*,
the Duke of Hǎichéng, Huáng Fāngshì, died in the army,
and his brother Fāngtài was ordered to inherit the peerage.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the Governor-General of Fújiàn, Láng Tíngxiāng, the Governor Yáng Xī, and the Provincial Commander Duàn Yìngjǔ were all dismissed.
Yáo Qǐshèng was appointed Governor-General of Fújiàn,
Wú Xīngzuò was appointed Governor of Fújiàn,
and Yáng Jié was appointed Naval and Land Commander of Fújiàn.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the Emperor visited the western suburbs to inspect the crops.
The Jì nóng of the Èlǔtè tribe, pressured by Gá'ěrdān,
entered the border,
and Zhāng Yǒng drove them out.
In the sixth month, on the *rénshēn* day,
Shàng Shàn sent Lín Xīngzhū to defeat Wú Sānguì's navy at Jūnshān.
On the *dīnghài* day,
due to the severe drought in high summer,
the Emperor walked to the Temple of Heaven to pray.
On that day,
there was heavy rain.
On the *rénchén* day,
Wú Sānguì's general attacked Yǒngxīng;
Commander Bó Yílǐbù and Commander Hākèsān fought them,
suffered a defeat and died.
Sea pirates attacked Liánzhōu,
and Commander Bān Shàomíng and others attacked and drove them away.
Wú Sānguì's troops attacked Chénzhōu;
Vice Commander Shuòdài fought them,
was unsuccessful,
and fled to Yǒngxīng.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Since the outbreak of war,
officers and soldiers have endured armor and weapons,
extreme heat and severe cold,
and have suffered immensely.
I deeply commiserate with them.
Let the Ministry of War investigate those in the army who are in debt,
and the government shall repay it.
Those who die in battle or are wounded shall have their families comforted."
In the autumn, seventh month,
Zhèng Jǐn captured Hǎichéng;
Vanguard Commander Xīfó, Vice Commander Mùhèlín, and Provincial Commander Duàn Yìngjǔ died.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Zhèng Jǐn attacked Quánzhōu.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Ānzhùhù was appointed General of Fèngtiān.
On the *rénxū* day,
Wèi Xiàngshū was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Hanlin Academy Academician Chén Tíngjìng and Reader-Academician Yè Fāng'ǎi were summoned to serve in the Nánshūfáng (Southern Study).
In this month,
Wú Sānguì usurped the imperial title at Héngzhōu.
In the eighth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
Grand General for Suppressing Rebels and Bèilè Shàng Shàn died in the army;
Bèilè Cháni was ordered to replace him.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
an envoy from the Western country (Portugal), Āfēngsù (Afonso), entered with tribute.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the Emperor attended the *jīngyán*,
and bestowed his imperial poetry collection upon Chén Tíngjìng and others.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Wú Sānguì died,
and the siege of Yǒngxīng was lifted.
The Kāngxī Perpetual Calendar was promulgated.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"The rebel leader initiated rebellion,
and has now met with divine punishment.
Those who were mistakenly involved
should be treated with leniency.
Those who repent and return
shall all be pardoned."
In the ninth month,
the Emperor accompanied the Grand Empress Dowager to Tāngquán
and paid respects at Xiàolíng.
Yáo Qǐshèng and Lāhādá decisively defeated the sea pirates at Wúgōngshān;
Liú Guóxuān fled,
and the siege of Quánzhōu was lifted.
In winter, tenth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
the Emperor toured the border areas,
stopped at Luánhé,
and reviewed the troops at Sāntúnyíng.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
General Ènèi defeated Wú Yìngqí at Shíkǒu.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the Fourth Prince Yìnzhēn was born,
who would become Shìzōng;
his mother was Madam Wúyǎ.
In the eleventh month, on the *jǐhài* day,
Lāhādá submitted a memorial stating that the sea pirates had cut off the Jiāngdōng Bridge,
making it difficult for troop reinforcements to reach Quánzhōu.
Former Reader-Academician Lǐ Guāngdì served as a guide for the grand army,
repaired dangerous paths,
and supplied military provisions.
He requested deliberation on the matter.
The imperial rescript stated:
"Lǐ Guāngdì previously, at the beginning of the upheaval,
submitted a secret memorial with crucial suggestions.
Now he again welcomed the grand army
and prepared provisions.
This is highly commendable.
He is immediately promoted to Academician."
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the Emperor accompanied the Grand Empress Dowager back to the palace.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Fújiàn Land Commander Yáng Jié was ordered to be promoted to Zhāowǔ Jiāngjūn,
and Wáng Zhī'dǐng was appointed Fújiàn Naval Commander.
In the twelfth month, on the *dīnghài* day,
Èchǔ, Fù Hóngliè, and Wú Shìcóng fought at Téngxiàn,
were unsuccessful,
and retreated to defend Wúzhōu.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the joint ancestral sacrifice was held at the Tàimiào (Grand Ancestral Temple).
In this year,
tax exemptions were granted to various disaster-stricken prefectures and counties in Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Jiāngxī, and Húguǎng provinces.
Cháoxiǎn (Korea) and Xīyáng (Western countries) offered tribute.
In the eighteenth year, on the *jǐwèi* day, in the spring, first month, on the *wùshēn* day,
officials were dispatched to distribute relief in Shāndōng and Hénán.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Bèilè Cháni commanded the navy to besiege Yuèzhōu;
the rebel general Wú Yìngqí fled,
and Yuèzhōu was recovered.
The Emperor announced the victory at Wǔmén.
Commanders-in-Chief for Campaigns were established to accommodate surrendered generals,
but this was soon abolished.
On the *rénxū* day,
Liú Guóxuān attacked Chánglè;
Governor-General Yáo Qǐshèng, accompanied by Jì'ěrtābù and Wú Xīngzuò, defeated him.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Yuèlè retook Chángshā.
In the second month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
Fù Hóngliè fought Wú Shìcóng at Wúzhōu,
and the rebels fled.
On the *jǐsì* day,
an imperial edict enumerated the crimes of treacherous people in Jiāngxī for following the rebellion,
but still exempted them from outstanding taxes.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Shùnchéng Jùnwáng Lè'ěrjǐn led troops across the river,
and successively recovered Sōngzī, Zhījiāng, Yídū, and Lǐzhōu;
rebel general Hóng Fú surrendered with his fleet.
On the *wùyín* day,
Qīnwáng Lābù sent Vanguard Commander Xīfó to retake Héngzhōu;
rebel generals Wú Guóguì and Xià Guóxiāng fled.
On the *gēngchén* day,
an imperial edict ordered the princes and ministers at the front to discuss matters of advancing into Yúnnán and Guìzhōu.
Zhōu Yǒudé was appointed Governor-General of Yúnnán and Guìzhōu,
Sāng'é was appointed Provincial Commander of Yúnnán,
Zhào Lài was appointed Provincial Commander of Guìzhōu,
and they were all to follow the imperial army in the campaign.
Yáng Yōngjiàn was appointed Governor of Guìzhōu.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Kuāzhā was appointed Mongol Commander.
On the *bǐngshēn* day of the third month, the first day of the lunar month,
the Emperor personally examined the *bóxué hóngcí* (erudites of vast learning) at the Bǎohé Diàn.
Fifty people, including Péng Sūnyù, were appointed as Imperial Academicians, Lecturers, Compilers, and Revisers.
The compilation of the *Míng Shǐ* (History of the Ming Dynasty)
was entrusted to Grand Secretaries Xú Yuánwén and Yè Fāng'ǎi, and Junior Supervisor Zhāng Yùshū as chief compilers.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the Emperor went to Bǎodìng Xiàn for a hunting expedition.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Xú Zhìdū was appointed Grand Coordinator of Húguǎng.
General Mùzhàn attacked Wú Guóguì at Yǒngzhōu,
defeated him,
and recovered Yǒngzhōu, Dàozhōu, and Yǒngmíng.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Guī Yǔnsù and one hundred and fifty-one others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with different ranks.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
when the coffins of the generals who died in battle at Yuèzhōu arrived,
imperial bodyguards were dispatched to welcome and offer sacrifices.
The coffins of the generals and soldiers who died in battle in Fújiàn also received the same treatment.
In summer, on the *bǐngyín* day of the fourth month,
Yáng Màoxūn was appointed Governor-General of Sìchuān,
stationed at Yúnyáng.
On the *wùchén* day,
Wàn Zhèngsè was appointed Grand Coordinator of the Fújiàn Navy.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
due to severe drought,
the Emperor walked to the Tiāntán to pray.
On that day,
there was heavy rain.
Mǎngyītú attacked Wú Shìcóng at Xúnzhōu,
who fled in defeat.
On the *rényín* day,
the Emperor went out of Fùchéngmén to inspect the crops.
In the fifth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
Liú Guóxuān attacked Jiāngdōngqiáo,
and Lài Tǎ fought a great battle and defeated him.
In the sixth month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“In an era of great governance,
there is a surplus (of three years' harvest in nine, or one year's harvest in three).
Only when granaries are full and rites and education flourish,
can one be free from the worries of floods and droughts.
Recently, I have heard that the common people do not know how to save,
and when a lean year comes,
they often resort to migration.
To promote frugality and educate the people,
and to use rites in daily life,
relies solely on capable officials.
Governors-general and governors should select officials to instruct the people,
to fulfill My intention.”
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Xīfó was appointed Mongol Military Governor.
In autumn, on the *jiǎwǔ* day of the seventh month,
Jìn Fǔ reported in a memorial that the dikes at Huáiyáng were completed,
drying out fields,
and invited people to cultivate them.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the Emperor visited the ailing Qúnqīn Wáng Lóngxǐ.
Lóngxǐ passed away.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Échǔ defeated Wú Shìcóng at Nánníng,
and Shìcóng fled.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
An imperial edict ordered the release of one hundred thousand (taels) from the imperial treasury for relief,
and official repair of damaged houses.
On the *rénxū* day,
the Emperor summoned court officials and instructed them:
“I, being without virtue,
and my governance not yet harmonious,
have caused this earthquake as a warning.
I am anxious and uneasy,
and diligently seek the causes of this disaster.
Are the officials governing the people excessively extracting to curry favor?
Are ministers forming cliques and factions to promote private interests?
Are military commanders plundering and burning without being restrained?
Are tax remissions and relief not genuinely implemented?
Are judicial officials wrongly convicting innocent people when hearing cases?
Have princes and high ministers failed to restrain their subordinates, leading to encroachment on common people?
If any of these exists,
all are sufficient to cause disaster.
Only by upholding major laws and being lenient in minor matters,
with peaceful governance and just legal proceedings,
can we hope to move Heaven,
and avert calamities.
Therefore, I openly declare My heart,
and wish to strive together with all officials, great and small, inside and outside the court.”
In the eighth month, on the *guǐhài* day, the first day of the lunar month,
General Mùzhàn recovered Xīnníng.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Fù Hóngliè recovered Liǔchéng and Róngxiàn.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Grand Coordinator Zhào Guózuò and General Lín Xīngzhū decisively defeated Wú Guóguì at Wǔgāng,
Guóguì died,
and Wǔgāng Zhōu was recovered.
In the ninth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
prayers were offered at the Tiāntán due to the earthquake.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Qínqīn Wáng Lǎbù was ordered to guard Guìlín.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Jīn Guāngzǔ captured the rebellious commander Zǔ Zéqīng and sent him to the capital,
and his son Liángpián was executed by dismemberment.
In winter, on the *xīnwèi* day of the tenth month,
an imperial edict ordered Generals Zhāng Yǒng and Wáng Jìnbǎo,
and Grand Coordinators Zhào Liángdòng and Sūn Sīkè, to take Sìchuān.
Wáng Jìnbǎo and Zhào Liángdòng set off.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Wáng Jìnbǎo captured Wǔguān,
and recovered Fèngxiàn.
Zhào Liángdòng recovered Liǎngdāng.
In the eleventh month, on the *wùxū* day,
Wáng Jìnbǎo attacked the rebel general Wáng Píngfān,
who fled to Guǎngyuán,
and Hànzhōng was recovered.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Zhào Liángdòng recovered Lüèyáng,
and advanced to capture Yángpíngguān.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Xǔ Zhēn was appointed Grand Coordinator of Jiāngxī.
In the twelfth month, on the *rénxū* day,
Cài Yùróng was appointed Suíyuǎn General,
and tasked with pacifying Yúnnán and Guìzhōu.
Generals Fóníle and Wú Dān captured Liánghéguān,
the rebel general Hán Jìnqīng fled,
and Xīng'ān, Pínglì, Zǐyáng, Shíquán, Hànyīn, Xúnyáng, Báihé, and Zhúshān and Zhúxī of Yúnyáng were recovered.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor went to Nányuàn.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
an imperial edict ordered Ānqīn Wáng Yuèlè to lead Lín Xīngzhū's troops back to the capital.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Zhào Liángdòng was granted the title Yǒnglüè Jiāngjūn.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
joint sacrifices were offered at the Tàimiào.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted in part for two hundred and sixty-one prefectures and counties in the provinces of Shùntiān, Jiāngnán, Shāndōng, Shānxī, Hénán, Zhèjiāng, Húguǎng, etc.
Cháoxiǎn, Liúqiú, and Ānnán offered tribute.
In the nineteenth year, on the *jiǎwǔ* day of the first month of spring in the *gēngshēn* year,
Zhào Liángdòng recovered Lóng'ān Fǔ,
and advanced to Miánzhú.
The pseudo-governor Zhāng Wén and others surrendered,
and he then entered Chéngdū.
An imperial edict appointed Liángdòng as Governor-General of Yúnnán and Guìzhōu.
Wáng Jìnbǎo captured Cháotiān Guān,
recovered Guǎngyuán,
Wáng Píngfān hanged himself,
and Wú Zhīmào was captured alive.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the Emperor went to Gǒnghuá Chéng,
and dispatched a Grand Minister of the Interior to offer sacrifices at the tomb of Zhāoxūn Gōng Túlái.
In the second month, on the *xīnyǒu* day, the first day of the lunar month,
an imperial edict ordered Wú Dān to join Zhào Liángdòng in advancing to take Yúnnán,
Wáng Jìnbǎo to garrison Sìchuān,
Lè'ěrjǐn to take Chóngqìng,
and Xú Zhìdū to guard Jīngzhōu.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Fóníle recaptured Shùnqìng Fǔ,
and all counties including Tóngchuān, Zhōngjiāng, Nánbù, Péngxiàn, Guǎng'ān, and Xīchōng surrendered.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
an imperial edict ordered Mǎngyītú to oversee Mǎ Jiǔyù, Jīn Guāngzǔ, and Gāo Chéngyīn in advancing troops to Yúnnán.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Emperor went to Nányuàn.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
a grand review was held.
Yú Chénglóng was appointed Governor of Zhílì.
Xú Zhìdū decisively defeated the rebel general Yáng Láijiā,
recovered Wūshān,
and advanced to take Kuízhōu.
Yáng Màoxūn recovered Dàchāng and Dàníng.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Wàn Zhèngsè defeated sea pirates at Hǎitán.
In the third month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
Wú Dān recovered Chóngqìng.
Dázhōu, Fèngxiāng, and all other prefectures and counties were pacified.
Yáng Láijiā surrendered
and was sent to the capital.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Yī Pì was appointed Grand Coordinator of Yúnnán.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Prince Ānqīn, Yuèlè, returned with his army.
The Emperor met him at Lúgōuqíáo to reward him.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Mǎ Chéngyìn enticed and captured Fù Hóngliè.
Previously,
Mǎ Xióng had occupied Liǔzhōu.
Upon his death,
his son Chéngyìn surrendered Liǔzhōu.
By this time,
he rebelled again,
captured Hóngliè, and sent him to Guìyáng.
Hóngliè did not yield
and died.
General Píngnán, Lài Tǎ, recovered Tóngshān
and was ordered to garrison Cháozhōu to prepare for Chéngyìn.
Wàn Zhèngsè attacked the pirates at Pínghǎi Wù,
conquered it,
and then conquered Méizhōu, Nánrì, and Chóngwǔ Wù.
Zhū Tiānguì surrendered.
Lāhādá attacked Liú Guóxuān,
defeated him,
who then fled to Xiàmén.
The rebel general Sū Kān offered to surrender.
The army advanced and pacified nineteen camps including Yùzhōu, Shímǎ, Hǎichéng, and Mázhōu.
Then, together with Wú Xìngzuò, they retook Jīnmén.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Cháni took Chénlóngguān,
and Cài Yùróng recovered Tóngrén.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the first day Gēngshēn,
Lài Tǎ was appointed Manchu Commander-in-Chief.
On the day Guǐhài,
Mùzhàn and Dǒng Wèiguó defeated Wú Yìngqí,
recovered Yuánzhōu and Jìngzhōu,
and then recovered Lípíng.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the Emperor, noting that Academicians Zhāng Yīng and others served in the Inner Court
and were constantly consulted,
ordered the ministries to give them preferential treatment.
Gāo Shìqí and Dù Nà were both appointed Hanlin officials.
On the day Jǐsì,
it was ordered that the Hanlin of the Southern Study lecture on the Zīzhì Tōngjiàn every evening.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
the Emperor prayed for rain at the Temple of Heaven.
The next day,
it rained.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the lectures on the Shàngshū were promulgated.
Wáng Jìnbǎo returned to Gùyuán due to illness.
His son, Commander-in-Chief Yòngyǔ, was ordered to lead the army and garrison Bǎoníng.
On the day Gēngchén,
the Imperial Clan Court presented the Imperial Genealogy.
In the fifth month, on the day Rénchén,
the Grand Coordinator of Gānsù was ordered to govern Lánzhōu.
On the day Yǐsì,
Mǎngyītú joined forces to attack Mǎ Chéngyìn,
who surrendered again.
He was ordered to be captured and sent to the capital.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
a customs barrier was set up at Shānhǎiguān to collect taxes.
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
Cài Yùróng recovered Sīnán.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
it was ordered that the porridge kitchens in the five cities be extended for another three months,
and thirty imperial physicians were dispatched to treat the diseases and epidemics among the starving people.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Vice Commander-in-Chief Mǎěrhāqí and Camp Commander Mǎ Shùndé were condemned for allowing their soldiers to commit murder.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
the selection of Censorate officials from those who had purchased offices was suspended.
The Governor-General of Fújiàn, Fàn Chéngmó, and the Grand Coordinator of Guǎngxī, Mǎ Xióngzhèn, were commended and indemnified,
and posthumously granted official titles, honorary names, and hereditary privileges for their descendants.
On the day Yǐsì,
Zhéěrkěn was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Prince Shùnchéng-jùnwáng, Lèěrjǐn, was relieved of his position as Grand General
and recalled to the capital.
In the eighth month, on the day Wùchén,
the Emperor attended the Imperial Lectures.
On the day Jǐsì,
Lài Tǎ was ordered to move his garrison to Guǎngzhōu,
and Bójì's army was sent to reinforce him.
On the day Wùyín,
Grand Secretary Suǒ'étú was dismissed.
On the day Rénwǔ,
General Mǎngyītú died in the army.
Lèibèi was appointed to replace him.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Shàng Zhīxìn, because his subordinate Wáng Guóguāng accused him of crimes,
unilaterally executed him.
An imperial edict ordered Zhīxìn to die.
His younger brother Zhījié,
and his partisan Lǐ Tiānzhí,
were all executed.
Their families were escorted back to the capital.
In the intercalary eighth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
all generals and commanders were ordered to treat the Green Standard Army soldiers well.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Wáng Yǒngyù was appointed General of Guǎngdōng.
In the ninth month, on the day Guǐhài,
Wú Shìfán ordered his generals Xià Guózhù and Mǎ Bǎo to secretly invade Sìchuān.
Tán Hóng rebelled again in response,
successively capturing Lúzhōu and Yǒngníng.
Bandits in Kuízhōu also responded.
Generals Wú Dān and Gáěrhàn,
and Provincial Commanders Fàn Dálǐ and Xú Zhìdū, were ordered to attack them from different routes.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Lài Tǎ was appointed Grand General Píngnán
and led his army to advance into Yúnnán.
On the day Wùyín,
Wú Dān recovered Lúzhōu.
In winter, in the tenth month,
Rénhuái was lost.
Wú Dān was dismissed,
and Èkèjìhā was appointed to lead his army.
On the day Wùxū,
Āmìdá was appointed Mongol Commander-in-Chief.
Gáěrhàn recovered Wūshān.
On the day Rényín,
Grand General Prince Kāng, Jiéshū, returned with his army.
The Emperor met him in the suburbs to reward him.
On the day Wùshēn,
Zhāng Tái and Mùzhàn defeated Wú Shìfán at Zhènyuǎn.
Gáěrhàn attacked Tán Hóng at Tiěkāixiá
and defeated him.
This month,
the princes and ministers discussed the crimes of the princes, beile, and ministers who had been negligent in their military duties.
An imperial decree was issued:
Lèěrjǐn was stripped of his princely title,
his property confiscated, and he was imprisoned.
Shàngshàn and Cháni were both stripped of their beile titles.
Lánbù was stripped of his Zhènguógōng title.
Zhūmǎn was stripped of his Commander-in-Chief title
and immediately hanged.
The others were variously stripped of their offices, hereditary posts, flogged, and had their property confiscated.
In the eleventh month, on the first day Bǐngchén,
Winter Solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Round Mound.
A comet was seen,
and an edict was issued seeking frank advice.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Beizi Zhāng Tái advanced and recovered Píngyuè,
and then entered Guìyáng.
The rebel leader Wú Shìfán and Wú Yìngqí and others fled during the night.
The three prefectures of Ānshùn, Shíqiān, and Dōuyún all fell.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Dáhālǐ was appointed Mongol Commander-in-Chief.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Commander-in-Chief of Northern Sìchuān, Gāo Mèng, defeated Péng Shíhēng at Nánxīqiáo,
recovered Yíngshān,
and advanced to besiege Língjiùzhài,
beheading the rebel general Wèi Qīngwǔ.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Provincial Commander Zhōu Bóshì recovered Sīnán.
In the twelfth month, on the day Rénchén,
Xú Yuánwén was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Gāo Mèng recovered Qúxiàn.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Provincial Commander Sāng'é greatly defeated Wú Shìfán at Yǒngníng,
and pursued him to Tiěsuǒqiáo.
The rebels burned the bridge and fled.
Local officials Lóng Tiānyòu and Shā Qǐlóng built a pontoon bridge across the Pánjiāng River to aid the grand army.
On the day Rényín,
Gāo Mèng recovered Guǎng'ānzhōu.
On the day Gēngxū,
Hǎo Yù was appointed Grand Coordinator of Guǎngxī.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the comprehensive sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
This year,
taxes for disasters were remitted in 186 prefectures and counties across Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Shāndōng, Shānxī, Shǎnxī, Jiāngxī, Fújiàn, Húguǎng, and other provinces, with varying degrees of remission.
Cháoxiān and Liúqiú offered tribute.
In the twentieth year, Xīnyǒu, in the first month of spring, on the day Rénshēn,
the rebel general Lǐ Běnshēn surrendered
and was shackled and sent to the capital.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Commander-in-Chief Gāo Mèng recovered Dázhōu.
On the day Jiǎxū,
General Gáěrhàn recovered Yúnyáng.
Tán Hóng died.
He then recovered Zhōngzhōu, Wànxiàn, and Kāixiàn.
On the day Yǐhài,
Vice Minister Wēndài was ordered to manage the Tōngzhōu Grand Canal.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
General Mùzhàn and Provincial Commander Zhào Lài attacked Xià Guóxiàng and others,
drove them away,
and recovered Píngyuǎn.
On the day Xīnsì,
the number of lecturers was increased.
An edict ordered the judicial authorities to be careful in applying punishments.
This month,
Zhèng Jǐn died,
and his son Kèshuǎng succeeded him in leading his forces.
On the *jǐchǒu* day of the second month,
Bèizǐ Zhāngtài’s army arrived at Ānnán Wèi,
and attacked the rebel general Xiànwèi at Jiāngxī Pō.
The rebels arrayed elephant formations to resist.
The government troops divided into three teams and attacked fiercely,
greatly defeating them.
The rebels fled,
and Gōngtú and Dáhàntài pursued and attacked,
defeating them again,
and recovering Pǔ’ān Zhōu and Xīnxīng Suǒ.
On the *rénchén* day,
Vice Commander-in-chief Mǎngyìlù defeated the rebels Zhāngzúfǎ and others at Sānshān.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
an edict was issued to abolish all past offenses committed by the Three Feudatories that harmed the people.
The salt warrants of Fèngtiān were remitted.
Generalissimo Làitǎ’s army arrived in Guǎngxī,
greatly defeating the rebels at Huángcǎo Bà,
recovering Ānlóng,
and entering Qǔjìng.
Gāo Mèng recovered Dōngxiāng,
defeating Péng Shíhēng at Yuèchéng Zhài.
On the *wùxū* day,
one Manchu Vice Director was added to the Qīntiān Jiān.
Commanders Hīfú, Mǎ Jī, and Shuòtǎ recovered Mǎlóng Zhōu and Yánglín Chéng,
and entered Sōngmíng Zhōu,
where the rebels fled.
Mùzhàn recovered Qiánxī and Dàdìng,
executing their pseudo-general Zhāng Wéijiān.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Bèizǐ Zhāngtài, Generalissimo Làitǎ, and General Cài Yùróng successively entered Diān.
Rebel generals Hú Guóbǐng and Liú Qǐlóng met them in resistance,
but the government army divided its forces and defeated them,
executing Guóbǐng and Qǐlóng.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the Xiàolíng Mausoleum was visited.
On the *jiǎchén* day of the third month,
General Xuānwēi Èkèjìhā impeached himself for failing to relieve Jiànchāng.
An edict appointed Juéluó Jìhālǐ to replace him.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Empress Rénxiào and Empress Xiàozhāo were interred in the Chāngruìshān Mausoleum.
An edict ordered that memorials to the throne reviewed by the imperial carriage
be examined by the Grand Secretaries.
On the *rénxū* day,
Hú Guózhù attacked Jiànchāng,
and General Fónílè drove him away,
recovering Mǎhú.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Mǎ Bǎo abandoned Zūnyì,
and attacked Lú and Qú.
An edict ordered Fónílè and Zhào Liángdòng to swiftly attack the Diān rebels,
preventing them from returning to reinforce.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
officials such as Transport Commissioner Gāo Tiānjúe and Prefect Zhāng Ruìwǔ, who died in the service of Fújiàn, were posthumously granted compensation and hereditary official posts.
On the *wùchén* day,
the local chieftain Lù Dàoqīng surrendered Yǒngníng.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor, with the Grand Empress Dowager, visited the hot springs of Zūnhuà.
On the *jiǎchén* day, the first day of the fourth month in summer,
Wáng Yòngyǔ recovered Nàxī, Jiāng’ān, Rénhuái, and Héjiāng.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Bèizǐ Zhāngtài dispatched envoys to pacify various routes,
and Wǔdìng, Dàlǐ, Lín’ān, Yǒngshùn, and Yáo’ān all surrendered.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the Emperor, with the Grand Empress Dowager, returned to the palace.
On the *guǐchǒu* day, the first day of the fifth month,
Admiral Zhōu Bóshì captured Zūnyì,
received the surrender of pseudo-officials such as Jīn Shìjùn,
and recovered Zhēn’ān Zhōu, Rénhuái, Tóngzǐ, and Suīyáng counties.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
officials were dispatched to investigate the drought conditions in the Sūnítè and other banners of Mongolia.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
an edict ordered that those from prefectures and counties previously occupied by rebels should not be selected for Censorate and Supervising Censor positions.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Generalissimo Bèizǐ Zhāngtài reported his arrival at the provincial capital of Yúnnán,
and pseudo-general Lǐ Fāměi surrendered the prefectures of Hèqìng and Líjiāng.
On the *wùzǐ* day of the sixth month,
the housing tax (*fánghào yín*) in Shānxī and Shǎnxī was abolished.
On the *dīngsì* day of the seventh month in autumn,
Gāo Sìhǎi, Minister of Rites, was concurrently put in charge of the Board of Punishments.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
an edict ordered that private lands in Sìchuān occupied by officers and soldiers be investigated and returned to their owners.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Commander Hīfú and Admiral Sāng’é attacked Mǎ Bǎo at Wūmù Shān,
greatly defeating him.
Mǎ Bǎo surrendered,
was chained and sent to the capital for execution.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Zhào Liángdòng dispatched Brigade General Lǐ Fāngshù to defeat Hú Guózhù,
recovering Jiànchāng,
and entering Yúnnán.
On the *wùchén* day,
an edict ordered Túhǎi to lead Wáng Fǔchén back to the capital.
On the *rénshēn* day,
a banquet was held at Yíngtái,
attended by officials from Assistant Department Director (*yuánwàiláng*) and above,
and silk fabrics were bestowed.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Shī Láng was appointed Admiral of the Fújiàn Navy,
to plan the capture of Táiwān,
and Wàn Zhèngsè was appointed Admiral of the Land Forces.
On the *xīnsì* day, the first day of the eighth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Emperor attended the imperial lectures (*jīngyán*).
On the *xīnhài* day of the ninth month,
the Emperor made an imperial tour of the imperial domain (*jīdiàn*).
The funeral procession of the deceased Prince Píngnán, Shàng Kěxǐ, arrived at Tōngzhōu;
eight thousand taels of silver were bestowed,
and officials were dispatched to offer tea and fruit.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the Emperor stopped at Xióngxiàn,
summoned Magistrate Wú Jiàn,
and inquired about the residents affected by the flooding of the Húnhé River.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
An edict ordered the suspension of this year's autumn executions.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the silver for transport laborers (*yùn dīnggōng yín*) was reinstated.
On the *guǐwèi* day of the tenth month in winter,
Prefect of Piān Yuán, Hán Shìqí, defeated rebel general Huáng Míng at Gǔzhōu.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Gá’ěrdān of the Élǔtè offered tribute.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Grand Secretary Túhǎi's army returned,
and the Emperor praised and rewarded him.
On the *rénchén* day,
an edict ordered the withdrawal of officers and soldiers from the Píngnán and Jìngnán feudatories to the capital.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
an edict exempted Tǔlǔfān from offering tribute dogs and horses.
On the *xīnhài* day of the eleventh month,
an edict stated that all persons who followed the rebels,
except for those who clearly resisted the imperial army,
were to be stripped of their official posts and released.
Nuòmài was appointed Manchu Commander-in-chief.
On the *guǐhài* day,

Bèizǐ Zhāngtài, Grand General Dìngyuǎn Píngkòu; Làitǎ, Grand General Píngnán Commander-in-chief; Zhào Liángdòng, General Yǒnglüè Governor-general; and Cài Yùróng, General Suīyuǎn Governor-general, submitted memorials reporting that the imperial army entered Yúnnán city on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth month,
Wú Shìfán committed suicide,
his head was transmitted,
Wú Sānguì's bones were disinterred,
and displayed to the public at home and abroad,
the pseudo-chancellor Fāng Guāngchēn was executed,
the remaining rebels surrendered,
and Yúnnán was pacified.
On this day,
this was announced to Xiàolíng Mausoleum,
and the imperial carriage stopped at Jìzhōu.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
sacrifices were offered at Xiàolíng Mausoleum.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Bèizǐ Zhāngtài and General Zhào Liángdòng were summoned back to the capital.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the Emperor hunted in Nánshān,
and shot three tigers.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the imperial carriage returned.
On the *wùzǐ* day of the twelfth month,
a Manchu general was stationed at Jīngzhōu,
and a Han army general at Hànzhōng.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the ministers requested the conferment of an honorific title upon the Emperor.
An imperial edict stated:
"Since the rebellious traitors initiated chaos,
and wicked commoners responded,
the armies have been exhausted by levies and deployments,
and the populace afflicted by transportation duties.
Furthermore, floods and droughts have been frequent,
and calamities have appeared.
All this is due to My lack of virtue.
Relying on the spiritual power of the imperial ancestors and the state,
the various rebellious offshoots have been suppressed.
It is now appropriate to promote the worthy and virtuous,
and let the people rest;
how can I be so boastfully self-satisfied
as to accept meaningless embellishments?
How can I not feel ashamed?
Therefore, let it not be carried out."
The provincial examination of Guǎngxī was reinstated.
On the *wùxū* day,
Grand Secretary Túhǎi passed away.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Emperor received congratulations at the Tàihémén Gate,
and proclaimed the victory to all within and outside the capital.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
additional honorific titles were conferred upon the Grand Empress Dowager and the Empress Dowager,
an imperial amnesty was issued,
gifts were bestowed upon the imperial clan,
rewards were granted to the outer feudatories,
titles and enfeoffments were conferred,
the number of examination quotas was increased,
reclusive scholars were recommended,
filial piety and chastity were honored,
orphans and the solitary were given relief,
and all crimes not normally pardoned by extraordinary amnesty were forgiven.
Yú Chénglóng was appointed Governor-general of Jiāngnán and Jiāngxī,
and Wú Xīngzuò was appointed Governor-general of Guǎngdōng and Guǎngxī.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
a joint sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
That year,
the disaster tax was remitted, with variations, for seventy-five prefectures and counties in the provinces of Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Jiāngxī, Shāndōng, Shānxī, Zhèjiāng, and Fújiàn.
There were seventeen million seven hundred twenty-three thousand households.
Taxes collected in silver amounted to twenty-two million one hundred eighty-three thousand seven hundred sixty taels and a fraction.
Salt and tea taxes collected in silver amounted to two million three hundred ninety-nine thousand four hundred sixty-eight taels.
Twenty-three million one hundred thirty-nine thousand coins were minted.
Cháoxiǎn and Èlǔtè offered tribute.
Annals of the Holy Ancestor, Part 2, Volume Seven
Twenty-first year, Rénxū. Spring, first month, Rénxū
On the Yuánxiāo Festival,
a banquet was bestowed upon the court officials.
They watched the lanterns,
and composed poems in the Bóliáng style.
The Emperor sang the first line:
"The beautiful sun and gentle breeze cover myriad lands."
The court officials followed in sequence.
The Emperor wrote a preface to the "Shēngpíng Jiāyàn Shī Xù" (Preface to the Poem on the Auspicious Banquet of Peace and Prosperity)
and had it carved on stone at the Hànlín Yuàn.
Bǐngyín,
Cài Yùróng was transferred as Governor-General of Yún-Guì.
Wùchén,
the princes and high ministers memorialized, saying:
"Gěng Jīngzhōng, whose family has been enfeoffed as kings for generations,
willingly rebelled,
spreading disruption to Zhèjiang and Gàn,
and reaching as far as Wǎn and Huī.
If not for the might of the army and the strength of the ministers,
where would the spread have ended?
Lǐ Běnshēn, Liú Jìnzhōng and others have been high-ranking generals and commanders for many years,
enjoying high offices and generous emoluments,
yet they could not change their traitorous ways
and bowed their heads to the rebels.
What good were they?
They should all be severely punished
to set a great precedent
for the world's moral order and people's hearts.
We humbly propose this for your imperial decree."
An imperial decree was issued: Gěng Jīngzhōng, Zēng Yǎngxìng, Bái Xiǎnzhōng, Liú Jìnzhōng, and Lǐ Běnshēn are all to be dismembered and their heads displayed.
Gěng Jīngzhōng's son Gěng Jìzuò,
Lǐ Běnshēn's grandsons Lǐ Xiànggān and Lǐ Xiàngkūn,
his nephews Lǐ Jìxiáng and Lǐ Jìmín,
and Zǔ Hóngxūn and others are all to be executed by decapitation.
Chén Mènglěi, Lǐ Xuéshī, Jīn Jìng, and Tián Qǐjiāo, who were implicated by the rebels, are to have their death sentences reduced by one degree.
Jǐsì,
Yuè Xī, son of Ānqīn Wáng Yuèlè, was specially enfeoffed as Xī Jùnwáng.
Second month, Gēngchén,
Dádū was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
Guǐwèi,
officials were dispatched to offer sacrifices to the sacred mountains and rivers, ancient imperial mausoleums, and the temple of the First Teacher at Quèlǐ, to announce the pacification of Diān.
Jiǎshēn,
the Emperor attended the classic lecture.
Bǐngxū,
Tóng Guówéi was appointed Grand Minister of the Imperial Guard.
Xīnmǎo,
the Emperor observed a fast at Jǐngshān
to pray for blessings for the Grand Empress Dowager.
Guǐsì,
the Emperor embarked on an eastern tour,
the imperial procession started.
Crown Prince Yìnréng accompanied him.
The Mongolian princes and beile requested a venerable title for the Emperor,
which was not permitted.
Mùzhàn was appointed Mongolian Commander-in-Chief.
The sorcerer Zhū Fāngdàn was executed.
Wùxū,
arriving at Shānhǎiguān,
ministers were dispatched to offer sacrifices at the temple of Bóyí and Shūqí.
Third month, Rénzǐ,
the Emperor visited Fúlíng and Zhāolíng,
and stopped at Shèngjīng.
Jiǎyín,
sacrifices were offered at Fúlíng.
Bǐngchén,
sacrifices were offered at Zhāolíng.
Great rewards were bestowed upon generals and below,
down to tomb-guarding officials, retired elderly officials, and disabled or idle soldiers.
A partial amnesty was granted to Shèngjīng and Nínggǔtǎ.
Taxes along the imperial route were remitted.
Jǐwèi,
the Emperor visited Yǒnglíng,
and performed the sacrifice ceremony.
The Emperor personally presented silver carp and bream to the Grand Empress Dowager and Empress Dowager.
Gēngshēn,
the Emperor proceeded by a mountain path to Wūlā for a hunt.
Xīnyǒu,
a distant sacrifice was offered to Chángbáishān.
Yǐhài,
boating on the Sōnghuā Jiāng.
Summer, fourth month, Xīnsì,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
A banquet was bestowed upon the General and Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Nínggǔtǎ,
and gifts were given to retired officials and soldiers.
Yǐsì,
arriving at Zhōnghòusuǒ.
Wáng Tíngshì's son, Déyùn, a banished person, knocked at the palace gate to beg to take his father's place in exile.
The Board deliberated and disapproved.
The Emperor decreed:
"What Wáng Déyùn said is truly pitiable.
For him to encounter Our arrival here
is also a rare opportunity.
Since both father and son are educated,
they may both be released."
Fifth month, Xīnhài,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
Rénzǐ,
an edict stated that the Nínggǔtǎ region was too cold,
so banished persons were to be resettled in Liáoyáng.
Jǐwèi,
Grand Secretary Dù Lìdé requested retirement,
which was graciously granted.
Bǐngyín,
the tribute of eagles from Jílín was remitted,
and corvée labor was reduced.
Wùchén,
Wáng Xī was appointed Grand Secretary.
Sixth month, Yǐyǒu,
Tóng Guóyáo was appointed General of Fúzhōu.
Gēngyín,
Gōng Wōhè was appointed Mongolian Commander-in-Chief.
Jiǎchén,
Grand Secretary Féng Pǔ requested retirement,
which was graciously granted,
and an official was dispatched to escort him,
traveling by post-station to return to his hometown.
Autumn, seventh month, Gēngxū,
Háng'ài was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
Jiǎyín,
Wèi Xiàngshū, Minister of Justice, and Kē'ěr Kūn, Vice Minister of Personnel, were ordered to inspect Jīfǔ,
and those powerful bullies who oppressed the people were to be arrested and reported.
Yǐmǎo,
the pacification of the Three Feudatories was announced to Mongolia.
Eighth month, Bǐngzǐ,
an edict ordered Grand Secretaries of the Grand Secretariat to participate in state affairs.
Guǐmǎo,
Tán Hóng's sons Tán Tiānmì and Tán Tiānlún were executed.
Ninth month, Wùshēn,
Cài Shēngyuán and one hundred seventy-six others were granted the jinshì degree with various ranks.
Jiǎzǐ,
an edict ordered daily imperial audiences for governing,
in spring and summer at the beginning of chén,
and in autumn and winter at the middle of chén.
Winter, tenth month, Jiǎshēn,
Dìngyuǎn Dàjiāngjūn Beizi Zhāng Tài and Zhēngnán Dàjiāngjūn Dūtǒng Lài Tǎ returned triumphantly,
and the Emperor welcomed them outside the city.
Jǐchǒu,
Huáng Jī and Wú Zhèngzhì were appointed Grand Secretaries.
Xīnmǎo,
an edict ordered the revision of the Veritable Records of Taìzǔ,
and the compilation of the Sacred Instructions of Three Reigns and the "Píngdìng Sānnì Fānglüè" (Strategy for the Pacification of the Three Feudatories).
Eleventh month, Jiǎyín,
Lǐ Zhīfāng was appointed Minister of War,
Xīfú was appointed General of Xī'ān,
and Wǎdài was appointed General of Jiāngníng.
Wùwǔ,
an edict ordered the construction of the Shuāngzhōng Cí (Shrine of Double Loyalty) in Guǎngxī,
to commemorate Circuit Inspector Mǎ Xióngzhèn and Fù Hóngliè.
Gēngshēn,
Zhào Lài was appointed Han Army Commander-in-Chief.
Wùchén,
Shī Wéihàn was appointed Governor-General of Zhèjiāng,
and Gá'ěrhàn was appointed Manchu Commander-in-Chief.
Twelfth month, Jǐmǎo,
former Guǎngxī Circuit Inspector Chén Hóngqǐ, who was judged deserving of death for collaborating with rebels,
was ordered to be banished to Nínggǔtǎ.
Guǐwèi,
Xǔ Zhēn was appointed Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Guǎngdōng.
Wùzǐ,
Dá Hǎi's grandson Chén Bùlù was recorded as a bureau director in the Ministry of Justice.
Guǐsì,
for the crime of mismanagement during military campaigns,
Prince Jiǎn Lābù was stripped of his title,
and others were banished or demoted with varying degrees of punishment.
Gēngzǐ,
Lángtán returned from his mission to the Hēilóng Jiāng,
and reported on the Rōchà (Russians) encroaching on the border.
General Bāhǎi of Nínggǔtǎ and Deputy Commander-in-Chief Sàbùsù were ordered to lead troops to defend against them.
A wooden city was built at Hēilóng Jiāng and Hūmǎ'ěr,
and troops were distributed for garrison farming.
That year,
the assessed disaster tax was remitted, with variations, for seventy-eight prefectures, counties, and garrisons in the provinces of Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Jiāngxī, Shāndōng, Shānxī, Zhèjiāng, and Húguǎng.
Cháoxiǎn and Ānnán offered tribute.
Twenty-second year, Guǐhài. Spring, first month, Yǐmǎo,
a banquet was held and gifts bestowed upon court officials.
Jǐwèi,
the Emperor reviewed officials and cadets in archery practice.
Second month, Guǐyǒu,
Shuài Yánbǎo was dismissed;
Jièshān was appointed Minister of Rites,
and Kā'ěrtú was appointed Minister of Justice.
Jiǎshēn,
the Emperor visited Wǔtái Shān.
Third month, Wùshēn,
returned to the capital.
Wùwǔ,
Gá'ěrhàn was appointed General of Jīngzhōu,
and Péng Chūn was appointed Manchu Commander-in-Chief.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day `yǐhài`,
an order was issued for Tí Zhèn and other ministers to enter for an audience in sequence.
On the day `gēngchén`,
Bāhǎi was ordered to return and station at Wūlā.
Sàbùsù and Wǎlǐhù led their armies to station at Ésūlǐ to guard the border.
On the day `xīnmǎo`,
the Duke Pō'ěrběn was appointed Mongol Commander-in-Chief (`Dūtǒng`).
In the fifth month, on the day `bǐngwǔ`,
the Han Army Firearms Battalion was established.
On the day `jiǎzǐ`,
Shī Láng was ordered to conquer Táiwān.
In the sixth month, on the day `dīngchǒu`,
the Emperor inspected the imperial treasury
and bestowed currency and artifacts upon the court ministers.
On the day `wùyín`,
Yīsāng'ā was appointed Minister of Personnel (`Lìbù Shàngshū`),
and Háng'ài was appointed Minister of Revenue (`Hùbù Shàngshū`).
On the day `guǐwèi`,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, went to Gǔběikǒu to escape the summer heat.
In the intercalary sixth month, on the day `wùwǔ`,
Shī Láng captured Pénghú.
On the day `gēngshēn`,
an edict was issued to judicial officials, admonishing them not to unduly prolong cases.
In the autumn, seventh month,
the imperial carriage reached Hútúkètú.
Robes and hats were bestowed upon the Mongol princes and dukes who participated in the hunt,
and silver and currency upon the soldiers.
On the day `jiǎwǔ`,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, returned to the palace.
In the eighth month, on the day `gēngzǐ`,
the grand ceremony of the imperial lectures (`Jīngyán Dàdiǎn`) was commanded,
with Grand Secretaries (`Dàxuéshì`) and below attending.
On the day `wùshēn`,
Hāzhàn was appointed Minister of War (`Bīngbù Shàngshū`),
and Kē'ěrkun was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief (`Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ`).
On the day `wùchén`,
Shī Láng submitted a memorial reporting the army's entry into Táiwān.
Zhèng Kèshuǎng, along with his subordinates Liú Guóxuān and others, surrendered.
Táiwān was pacified.
An imperial edict granted titles of nobility to Kèshuǎng and Guóxuān,
conferred the title of Marquis Jìnghǎi upon Shī Láng,
and promoted and rewarded the generals and soldiers according to their achievements.
In the ninth month, on the day `guǐyǒu`,
Dīng Sīkǒng was appointed Circuit Inspector of Piān-Yuán (`Piān-Yuán Xúnfǔ`).
On the day `jǐmǎo`,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, visited Wǔtái Shān.
On the day `rénchén`,
upon reaching Chángchéng Líng,
the Empress Dowager turned back due to the dangerous road.
The Emperor proceeded to Wǔtái Shān.
The number of tribute envoys from the Èlǔtè was limited.
In the winter, tenth month,
the Emperor arrived at the Wǔlánghé temporary palace
and returned to the capital with the Empress Dowager.
On the day `dīngwèi`,
all ministers, noting the pacification of Táiwān,
requested the Emperor to accept an honorific title,
but he refused.
On the day `guǐhài`,
Sàbùsù was appointed the newly established General of Hēilóngjiāng.
On the day `yǐchǒu`,
an edict ordered coastal migrants to return to their fields and homes.
In the eleventh month, on the day `guǐwèi`,
the surrendered Russian Yíbān and others were granted official positions.
On the day `wùzǐ`,
the Emperor, noting the pacification of the pirates,
offered sacrifices to Xiàolíng.
On the day `guǐsì`,
the Emperor toured the border regions.
In the twelfth month, on the day `jiǎchén`,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day `dīngwèi`,
Lù Dàoqīng, a chieftain who had rebelled, was executed.
On the day `rénzǐ`,
Jì'ěrtābù was appointed Mongol Commander-in-Chief (`Dūtǒng`).
On the day `yǐmǎo`,
the daily lectures on the `Yìjīng` were completed,
and the Emperor composed a preface and had it promulgated.
Minister Zhū Zhībì and Left Censor-in-Chief Xú Yuánwén were dismissed for recommending unsuitable persons.
On the day `yǐchǒu`,
combined sacrifices were offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In this year,
disaster taxes were exempted, to varying degrees, in twenty prefectures and counties across the provinces of Shāndōng, Shānxī, Gānsù, Jiāngxī, Húguǎng, and Guǎngxī.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú offered tribute.
In the twenty-third year, `jiǎzǐ`, spring, first month, on the day `xīnsì`,
the Emperor visited Nányuàn for a hunt.
On the day `bǐngxū`,
Yuánduān, son of Prince Ān Qīnwáng Yuèlè, was additionally enfeoffed as Prince Qín Jùnwáng.
On the day `rénchén`,
an order was issued to rectify and solemnize court assembly rituals.
The Russians occupied the two cities of Yǎkèsà and Níbùcháo.
An order was issued to halt trade with them,
and Sàbùsù led troops to confront them.
In the second month, on the day `yǐsì`,
the Emperor presided over the imperial lectures (`Jīngyán`).
On the day `guǐchǒu`,
the Emperor toured the imperial domains (`Jīdiàn`).
On the day `bǐngyín`,
he returned to station at Nányuàn.
Grand Secretary Huáng Jī was dismissed.
On the day `yǐchǒu`,
Supervising Secretary Wáng Chéngzǔ memorialized requesting an eastern tour.
An order was given to investigate the ceremonial precedents and report back.
In the third month, on the day `rénshēn`,
Liú Guóxuān was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Tiānjīn (`Tiānjīn Zǒngbīngguān`).
Upon his farewell audience,
he was bestowed two hundred ounces of silver, thirty bolts of satin, and one imperial saddle horse.
On the day `dīnghài`,
the Emperor composed an inscription for the Wǔtái Shān monument
and summoned court ministers to view it.
He instructed them, saying:
"When a modern person produces an essay,
they dislike others altering it.
This is why their essays are not excellent."
In the summer, fourth month, on the day `jǐyǒu`,
officials for Táiwān Prefecture and counties were established,
subordinate to the Fújiàn province.
On the day `rénzǐ`,
Left Vice-Minister of Justice (`Xíngbù Zuǒ Shìláng`) Sòng Wényùn requested retirement.
He was granted the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent (`Tàizǐ Shàobǎo`) upon retirement.
On the day `gēngshēn`,
an edict was issued that for any matter involving two ministries,
they must jointly memorialize.
On the day `yǐchǒu`,
the Emperor instructed the lecturers:
"Lectures should prioritize precision, conciseness, and clarity.
Do not be verbose.
I have read Zhāng Jūzhèng's Minister's `Four Books Straightforward Explanations` (`Shàngshū, Sīshū Zhíjiě`).
The meanings are all precise and substantial,
without superfluous words.
This can serve as a model."
Yú Chénglóng, Governor-General of Jiāngnán and Jiāngxī, passed away.
Sacrifices and a funeral were granted,
and he was posthumously given the epithet Qīngduān.
In the fifth month, on the day `dīngmǎo`,
the post of Governor-General of Zhèjiāng was abolished.
The Duke Wǎshān was appointed Manchu Commander-in-Chief (`Mǎnzhōu Dūtǒng`).
On the day `jǐsì`,
the `Dà Qīng Huìdiǎn` (Collected Statutes of the Great Qing) was revised.
On the day `bǐngzǐ`,
Sūn Sīkè was appointed Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Gānsù (`Gānsù Tídū`).
On the day `xīnsì`,
ministers were ordered to investigate and recommend incorruptible officials.
The Nine Ministers recommended Gé'ěrgǔdé, Sūhè, Fàn Chéngxūn, Zhào Lún, Cuī Huá, Zhāng Pénghé, and Lù Lóngqí.
On the day `guǐwèi`,
Bāhǎi was reinstated as Mongol Commander-in-Chief (`Dūtǒng`).
On the day `jiǎshēn`,
the Emperor visited Gǔběikǒu,
and an edict forbade trampling crops along the imperial route.
On the day `yǐwèi`,
Prince Huì Jùnwáng Bówēngguǒnuò was stripped of his title for impropriety during a sacrificial ceremony.
Princes and high ministers deliberated and memorialized that Vice-Minister Yíchāng'ā and Circuit Inspector Jīn Jùn, while investigating Shàng Zhīxìn's family assets,
had secretly embezzled 890,000 taels of silver
and murdered the merchant Shěn Shàngdá.
They should be executed.
Director Sòng Ètuō, Assistant Director Zhuó'ěrtú, and Vice-Minister Chántǎhǎi, who conducted an unfaithful investigation, should be hanged.
This was approved.
An edict ordered that the recovered silver should not be deposited in the Imperial Household Department (`Nèiwùfǔ`)
but handed over to the Ministry of Revenue (`Hùbù`) for military provisions.
In the sixth month, on the day `dīngwèi`,
Liúqiú requested to send its sons and younger brothers to study at the Imperial Academy (`Guózǐjiān`).
This was permitted.
On the day `jiǎyín`,
King Sēlièpālàzhàogǔlóngpālàmahūlùkūnsīyóutíyàpú'āi of Xiānlúoguó sent his attendant ministers to report that tribute ships had arrived at Hǔtiàomén
but had been delayed for a long time,
often resulting in damage.
They humbly requested an edict to the officials of Yuè province to permit them
to enter the river, land early,
conduct trade and procurement,
and not be obstructed.
This was granted.
The Emperor instructed First-class Imperial Guard Ānánfán, saying:
"I regard the Mongols of the outer banners as one with the Eight Banners.
Now, during my tour,
I see their clothing and food are in distress,
which deeply saddens me.
You shall immediately convey my message to the Mongols in the areas we pass through who have no one to appeal to:
allow them to come and see me,
and I will inquire about their livelihoods."
Thereupon, the Mongols, supporting the elderly and leading the young,
prostrated themselves at the temporary palace gate.
The Emperor inquired in detail about their ages and livelihoods,
and granted them silver and cloth.
On the day `yǐmǎo`,
the Emperor inspected the herds
and bestowed horses upon his attending ministers.
Minister of Justice Wèi Xiàngshū again memorialized requesting retirement.
This was granted.
On the day `dīngsì`,
Tāng Bīn was appointed Circuit Inspector of Jiāngsū (`Jiāngsū Xúnfǔ`).
In the seventh month, on the day `yǐhài`,
Sòng Déyí was appointed Grand Secretary (`Dàxuéshì`).
On the day `xīnsì`,
the Emperor stationed at Yīngnítāngquán.
Tóngjiā was appointed Mongol Commander-in-Chief (`Dūtǒng`).
In the eighth month, on the day Wùshēn,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Grand Secretary Lǐ Wèi died.
Officials were dispatched to offer tea and wine,
and sacrifices and burial were bestowed,
with the posthumous title Wénqín.
Zhāng Yǒng, the Grand General of Gānsù and Marquis Jìngnì, died.
Sacrifices and burial were granted,
with the posthumous title Xiāngzhuàng.
In the ninth month, on the first day Jiǎzǐ,
this year's autumn executions were suspended.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Zhāng Shìzhēn was appointed Minister of Punishments,
and Bójì was appointed Manchu Grand Commander.
Due to the high cost of copper,
new coins were cast,
reducing the amount by one quarter.
The people were permitted to mine copper and lead,
without tax.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Liáng Qīngbiāo was reassigned as Minister of War,
and Yú Guózhù as Minister of Revenue.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Ālání, the Mongol Grand Commander, was concurrently put in charge of the Court of Colonial Affairs as Minister.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Chén Tíngjìng was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left,
and Mǎngyìlù was appointed Mongol Grand Commander.
On the day Dīnghài,
an imperial edict decreed that where the imperial retinue passed during the southern tour,
a one-year exemption from corvée labor and taxes would be granted.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the Emperor departed.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Rènyín,
the Emperor arrived at Tàí'ān,
ascended Mount Tài,
and offered sacrifices to the Eastern Peak.
On the day Xīnhài,
he arrived at Táoyuán,
inspected the river works,
comforted and rewarded the laborers,
and warned the river officials not to exploit them.
He personally inspected the Tiānfēi sluice gate.
He discussed strategies for river control with the river official Jìn Fǔ.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the Emperor crossed the Huái River.
On the day Jiǎyín,
he arrived at Gāoyóu Lake,
landed and traveled more than ten *lǐ*,
inquiring about the hardships of the elderly.
On the day Bǐngchén,
the Emperor visited Mount Jiāo and Mount Jīn,
crossed the Yángzǐ River,
and, in the boat, looked at his attendants and said:
"These are all warships.
Now they are used for imperial tours,
but the hardships must not be forgotten."
On the day Dīngsì,
the maritime prohibitions were lifted.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the Emperor stayed in Sūzhōu.
On the day Gēngshēn,
he visited Huìshān.
He instructed the Provincial Governor: "Many common people have traveled long distances to observe.
Those who cannot return should be provided with funds to travel."
In the eleventh month, on the first day Rénxū,
the Emperor stayed in Jiāngníng.
On the day Guǐhài,
he went to the Míng Mausoleum to offer sacrifices.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
he returned.
He moored his boat at Yànzǐjī,
and read until the third watch.
His attendant Gāo Shìqí requested:
"Your sacred health is overworked,
you should moderate your rest."
The Emperor said:
"Since I received my first books at the age of five,
I have always read until midnight,
I enjoy this and am not fatigued by it."
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Yīsāng'ā and Sāmǔhā were ordered to inspect the river mouth.
An edict stated:
"The river mouth has been silted up for many years,
resulting in blockage.
The waterway must be dredged and cleared,
only then can the flooding be avoided.
Even if it requires significant expenditure,
it is not to be spared."
On the day Xīnwèi,
he personally inspected Gāojiāyàn.
Next, he stayed overnight at Sùqiān.
Passing Báiyáng River,
he bestowed white silver upon the elderly.
On the day Wùyín,
the Emperor arrived at Qūfù.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the Emperor went to the Temple of the Former Sage,
entered the Dàchéng Gate,
and performed the nine kowtows.
He proceeded to the Shīlǐ Hall,
and lectured on the *Yìjīng*.
He ascended the Dàchéng Hall,
beheld the statue of the Former Sage,
and observed the ritual vessels.
He went to the Shèngjì Hall,
and viewed the maps and books.
He went to Xìngtán,
and observed the planted cypresses.
He entered the Chéngshèng Gate,
drew and tasted water from the Kǒng Well.
He inquired about the remains of the Lǔ Wall.
Doctor Kǒng Yùqí answered in great detail,
and was bestowed the official position of Assistant Instructor.
He went to Kǒnglín and poured wine before the tomb.
He inscribed the plaque
"Teacher of Ten Thousand Generations"
and presented it.
He left a bent-handled yellow parasol.
He bestowed upon the Duke Yǎnshèng Kǒng Yùxiān, and those next in rank, one copy of each of the Classics for lecturing the next day.
The taxes for Qūfù for the coming year were remitted.
On the day Gēngyín,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
Mǎhādá was appointed Manchu Grand Commander.
In the twelfth month, on the first day Rénchén,
Shí Wénbǐng was appointed Han Army Grand Commander.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Gōng Wǎshān was ordered to inspect the troops along the Hēilóng Jiāng,
with Tóng Bǎo and Fókětuō as his deputies,
to prepare for the Luocha (Russians).
On the day Jiǎchén,
Duke Zhèng Kèshuǎng, Earl Liú Guóxuān, and Fěng Xífàn were granted fields and residences,
and were assigned to the Han Army.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
it was ordered that exiles should serve during the winter months,
and be released after the severe cold season had passed.
On the day Bǐngchén,
the Emperor visited the imperial mausoleums,
and bestowed cattle and sheep upon the officers and soldiers guarding the mausoleums.
On the day Jǐwèi,
he returned to the palace.
In this year,
taxes were remitted to varying degrees for twenty-six prefectures and counties in the provinces of Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Jiāngxī, Hénán, Húguǎng, and others, due to disasters.
Cháoxiǎn (Korea) and Xiāmluó (Siam) offered tribute.
In the twenty-fourth year, on the day Yǐchǒu, in the spring, first month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
sacrifices were offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
An edict stated:
"When the Master of Ceremonies reads the prayer,
upon reading Our name,
his voice always drops,
which goes against the meaning of a son pronouncing his father's name.
From now on, all names shall be read out loud."
On the day Guǐwèi,
Duke Péngchūn was ordered to go to Hēilóng Jiāng to supervise military affairs.
Marquis Lín Xīngzhū was ordered to lead the Fújiàn rattan shield soldiers to accompany him.
Bāndá'ěrshā, Tóng Bǎo, and Mǎlǎ were appointed military advisors.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Hanlin and Censorate officials were tested in the Bǎohé Hall.
The Emperor personally graded them,
and those who were unsatisfactory were reassigned.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the cattle and sheep contributed by the ten banners of the Kē'ěrqìn Mongols were ordered to be sent to the troops at Hēilóng Jiāng.
In the second month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Dōngyě, a descendant of Duke Zhōu, was appointed Doctor of the Five Classics,
and was granted sacrificial land.
Èhènà was appointed Manchu Grand Commander.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Emperor attended the imperial lectures.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the Emperor toured the imperial domains.
On the day Gēngshēn,
he returned to the capital.
Liú Guóxuān was again granted a residence.
Fàn Chéngxūn was appointed Provincial Governor of Guǎngxī.
In the third month, on the day Rénxū,
the Emperor completed the inscription for the Confucius Temple stele,
and personally wrote and erected the stele.
The comprehensive book on labor service and taxation was revised.
On the day Xīnsì,
Lù Kěntáng and 121 others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with various ranks.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
the descendant of Zhōu Dūnyí, a scholar of the Sòng dynasty, was granted the title Doctor of the Five Classics.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Lǐ Zhīfāng was granted the hereditary position of Light Chariot Commandant.
On the day Wùxū,
Mǎlǎ presented the captured Luocha (Russians),
and it was ordered that they be released from the front.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
an edict stated that due to consecutive years of drought in Zhílì,
over 600,000 *liǎng* of outstanding taxes were entirely remitted,
and one-third of this year's regular tax was also remitted.
An edict ordered imperial physicians to broadly collect medical texts and records,
and compile them into one book.
On the day Gēngxū,
the Imperial Household Department School was established.
In the fifth month, on the *Guǐwèi* day,
an imperial edict was issued concerning the *Jìwáng* (济王) of the Öölöd, who had departed from his original部 (bù),
drawn by civilization,
and should be treated with kindness and care,
and given fields and residences.
Political governance and ethical instructions were to be revised.
On the *Jiǎshēn* day,
because the former Governor of Guǎngxī (广西), Hǎo Yù (郝浴), had been honest and incorruptible throughout his official career,
all the treasury funds he was supposed to repay were waived.
Péng Chūn (彭春) and others attacked the city of Yǎkèsà (雅克薩).
The Rōchà (羅刹) came to its aid.
Lín Xīngzhū (林興珠) led the rattan-shield soldiers to intercept them in the river,
defeated them,
sank their boats,
and their chieftain É'líkèshè (額里克舍) begged for surrender.
In the sixth month, on the first day, *Gēngyín* (庚寅),
the Emperor went on a tour outside the passes,
and the imperial procession departed.
On the *Wùxū* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *Guǐmǎo* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“The Èluósī (鄂羅斯) have encroached upon our borders,
harassed the people of Èlúnchūn (鄂倫春), Suǒlún (索倫), Hèzhé (赫哲), Fēiyákā (飛牙喀), and other places,
and occupied Yǎkèsà (雅克薩) for forty years.
Now that a successful achievement has been made,
the personnel involved
shall all be given generous rewards.
A meeting should be held to deliberate and memorialize on where permanent garrisons should be stationed.”
The Emperor personally tested the Hàn (漢) banner *bǐtiēshì* (筆帖式) and *jiānshēng* (監生).
Eight hundred people failed,
and were all dismissed,
ordered to study further and retake the examination.
On the *Yǐsì* day,
the Emperor toured outside the passes.
In the autumn, in the seventh month, on the *Rénshēn* day,
post roads were established for Jílín (吉林) and Hēilóngjiāng (黑龍江),
totaling nineteen relay stations.
In the eighth month, on the *Bǐngwǔ* day,
the Emperor stopped at Bàibāhā'áng'ā (拜巴哈昂阿),
and bestowed official robes and silver currency upon the Mongol princes and *bèi lè* (貝勒) who were in the imperial retinue.
In the ninth month, on the first day, *Wùwǔ* (戊午),
upon hearing that the Grand Empress Dowager was unwell,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *Jǐwèi* day,
the Emperor rushed back to the capital,
attended to her with medicine,
and she recovered soon after.
On the *Xīnsì* day,
