Wáng Jìnbǎo (王進寶), the Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Shǎnxī (陝西), passed away.
He was posthumously granted the title of Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince (*Tàizǐtàibǎo*, 太子太保),
given a state funeral,
and honored with the posthumous name Zhōngyǒng (忠勇).
On the *Jiǎshēn* day,
Deputy Commander-in-Chief Wēndài (溫代) and Nàqín (納秦) were ordered to garrison Hēilóngjiāng (黑龍江).
Bódìng (博定) was ordered to construct the city of Mò'ěrgēn (墨爾根),
with additional laborers provided,
and also instructed to establish military agricultural colonies.
On the *Yǐyǒu* day,
Wú Yīng (吳英) was appointed Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Sìchuān (四川).
In the winter, in the tenth month, on the *Jiǎwǔ* day,
the Emperor visited the Southern苑 (*Nányuàn*, 南苑).
On the *Wùxū* day,
Yītèmù (伊特木), an envoy from the Öölöd, was executed in the marketplace for murder.
On the *Jǐhài* day,
Wǎdài (瓦代) was appointed Manchu Grand Commander (*Mǎnzhōu Dūtǒng*, 滿洲都統).
On the *Gēngzǐ* day,
it was decreed that from the Outer Vassal Princes downwards,
they should present an annual tribute of one sheep and one bottle of wine.
On the *Bǐngwǔ* day,
auspicious clouds were observed.
On the *Jǐyǒu* day,
Jìn Fǔ (靳輔) requested that land exposed by the drying up of the lower reaches of the river be leased to tenant farmers
who would pay rent to cover the construction costs.
The Emperor said:
“This would burden the people.
Do not collect it.”
On the *Jiǎyín* day,
Bójì (博霽) was appointed General of Jiāngníng (江寧).
In the eleventh month, on the first day, *Dīngsì* (丁巳),
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *Gēngshēn* day,
Mǎngyìlù (莽奕祿) was appointed Manchu Grand Commander (*Mǎnzhōu Dūtǒng*, 滿洲都統),
and Tǎ'ěrdài (塔爾岱) was appointed Mongol Grand Commander (*Ménggǔ Dūtǒng*, 蒙古都統).
On the *Jiǎxū* day,
the Emperor conducted a grand review at Lúgōuqiáo (盧溝橋).
On the *Bǐngzǐ* day,
Jìn Fǔ (靳輔) and Yú Chénglóng (于成龍) arrived in the capital by imperial summons,
to deliberate on strategies for river management.
Jìn Fǔ (靳輔) proposed opening six rivers and constructing long dikes.
Yú Chénglóng (于成龍) requested dredging the old river channel at the river mouth.
The Grand Secretaries reported this.
The Emperor said:
“Both proposals have merit.
Inquire among the imperial officials from the seven prefectures and counties of Gāo (高) and Bǎo (寶) which would benefit the people more.”
Attendant Reader Qiáo Lái (喬萊) memorialized,
suggesting to follow Yú Chénglóng's (于成龍) proposal,
as the work would be easier to complete,
and the common people would benefit.
The Emperor ordered Yú Chénglóng (于成龍) to commence the work.
However, it was later halted due to inconvenience to the people.
On the *Jǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor bestowed upon Ènèi (鄂內) and Kūnbātúlǔ (坤巴圖魯) the title of Minister without Portfolio (*Sànzhí Dàchén*, 散秩大臣),
allowing them to reside at home,
as both were old officials from the reign of Emperor Tàizōng (太宗).
On the *Yǐyǒu* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“There was a solar eclipse on the first day of the month,
and sixteen days later, a lunar eclipse.
Within a single month,
eclipses of both sun and moon were seen.
The celestial phenomena warn us,
and we should earnestly examine ourselves and reform.
Let the court officials convene and deliberate on this.”
In the twelfth month, on the *Gēngyín* day,
Chání (察尼) was appointed General of Fèngtiān (奉天).
On the *Jǐhài* day,
the Emperor visited the Xiàolíng (孝陵) mausoleum.
On the *Guǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the *Jiǎyín* day,
a joint sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple (*Tàimiào*, 太廟).
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted in varying degrees for seventy-four prefectures, counties, and garrisons in provinces such as Jiāngnán (江南), Jiāngxī (江西), Shāndōng (山東), Shānxī (山西), and Húguǎng (湖廣).
Cháoxiǎn (朝鮮), Líuqiú (琉球), and Gá'ěrdān (噶爾丹) presented tribute.
In the twenty-fifth year, *Bǐngyín* (丙寅), in the spring, in the first month, on the *Bǐngshēn* day,
Mǎlā (馬喇) was ordered to oversee military agricultural colonies in Hēilóngjiāng (黑龍江).
The Èluósī (鄂羅斯) again occupied Yǎkèsà (雅克薩),
and Sàbùsù (薩布素) was ordered to lead troops to expel them.
In the second month, on the *Jiǎchén* day,
the revised Veritable Records of Emperor Tàizǔ (*Tàizǔ Shílù*, 太祖實錄) were completed.
On the *Dīngwèi* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“The state has suppressed rebellious villains
and pacified distant wildernesses,
and should now widely proclaim its benevolent intentions
to inspire awe and submission.
Recently, it has been observed that the high officials in Yúnnán (雲南), Guìzhōu (貴州), Sìchuān (四川), and Guǎngdōng (廣東)
are not good at conciliating and pacifying,
but rather inflict harsh abuses,
and are greedy and troublesome,
seeking credit under false pretenses.
I believe that since the native chieftains (*tǔsī*, 土司) and various *Miáo* (苗) tribes
have submitted to imperial rule,
why are there still disturbances
and ceaseless conflicts?
They must strive to demonstrate sincerity and trustworthiness,
to guide and pacify them,
thereby fulfilling my utmost desire to govern and manage distant lands.”
The transportation of timber from Sìchuān (四川) was halted.
On the *Jǐyǒu* day,
the Wénhuá Diàn (文華殿) was completed.
On the *Rénzǐ* day,
a sacrifice was offered to the Most Sacred Former Teacher (*Zhìshèng Xiānshī*, 至聖先師) at the Chuánxīn Diàn (傳心殿).
On the *Guǐchǒu* day,
the Emperor attended the Imperial Lecture (*Jīngyán*, 經筵).
Jīnjìn (津進) was appointed Grand Minister of the Imperial Guard (*Lǐngshìwèi Nèidàchén*, 領侍衞內大臣).
In the third month, on the *Wùwǔ* day,
the construction of the *Qīlíu Suǒ* (棲流所) was ordered.
On the *Jǐwèi* day,
the compilation of the *Yītǒng Zhì* (一統志) was ordered.
On the *Jiǎxū* day,
Tāng Bīn (湯斌) was appointed Minister of Rites (*Lǐbù Shàngshū*, 禮部尚書),
concurrently overseeing the Grand Secretariat of the Heir Apparent (*Zhānshì Fǔ*, 詹事府).
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the first day, *Yǐyǒu* (乙酉),
Ālāní (阿拉尼) was ordered to go to the seven banners of Khalkha (喀爾喀) to preside over their alliance.
On the *Gēngyín* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“Zhào Liángdòng (趙良棟), when the rebellious bandits occupied Hànzhōng (漢中),
was the first to enter Sìchuān (四川),
and his achievements were outstanding.
He then led troops directly to Yúnnán (雲南),
and after capturing the provincial capital,
he alone was able to strictly adhere to laws and regulations,
and maintain integrity,
which is highly commendable.
Now that he is old and has retired from his post,
his titles of Valiant General (*Yǒnglüè Jiāngjūn*, 勇略將軍), Minister of War (*Bīngbù Shàngshū*, 兵部尚書), and Governor-General (*Zǒngdū*, 總督) should be reinstated to show imperial favor.”
Lángtán (郎談), Bāndá'ěrshā (班達爾沙), and Mǎlā (馬喇) were ordered to Hēilóngjiāng (黑龍江) to assist in military affairs.
The hereditary posts of General Píngnì (平逆) Bìlìkètú (畢力克圖) and Counselor Ā'ěrhú (阿爾瑚), who died in service in Shǎnxī (陝西), were posthumously granted.
On the *Jiǎwǔ* day,
an imperial edict sought lost books.
On the *Wùshēn* day,
Wàn Zhèngsè (萬正色) was transferred as Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Yúnnán (雲南),
and Zhāng Yúnyì (張雲翼) was appointed Provincial Commander-in-Chief of the Land Forces of Fújiàn (福建).
On the *Xīnhài* day,
it was first ordered that the peasants and soldiers in the banner estates and agricultural colonies belonging to Shùntiān (順天) and other prefectures,
should be organized into *bǎojiǎ* (保甲) units,
the same as civilian households.
In the intercalary fourth month, on the *Xīnwèi* day,
Fàn Chéngxūn (范承勳) was appointed Governor-General of Yúnnán (雲南) and Guìzhōu (貴州).
In the fifth month, on the *Dīnghài* day,
an imperial edict ordered the destruction of all illicit shrines throughout the realm.
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐhài,
rewards were distributed for the merits of Píngnán Dàjiàngjūn Lài Tǎ, Dūtǒng Zhào Lài, and others.
Each was granted a hereditary position, with varying ranks.
On the day Wùyín,
Ālántài was appointed Zuǒdū Yùshǐ.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
King Johan Liánshì Gānbóshì of the Kingdom of Hélán was presented with patterned silk and white gold.
His envoys were ordered to deliver a letter to Èluósī.
The Lìbù memorialized a regulation that officials below the ranks of Shìdú and Shùzǐ who were found to be lacking in scholarship
should be transferred out as Tóngzhī or Yùnpàn.
This was approved.
On the day Xīnhài,
the Emperor toured outside the passes.
In the eighth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
the Emperor sojourned at Wū'ěrgésūtái.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
Suǒ'étú was appointed Lǐng Shìwèi Nèidàchén.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
an edict ordered Sàbùsù to besiege the city of Yǎkèsà,
blocking its relief forces,
with Bódìng participating in military affairs.
On the day Wùchén,
an edict ordered all academies in the realm to offer sacrifices to former Confucian scholars.
On the day Gēngchén,
an edict ordered an increase of over eleven qǐng of land for Kǒnglín,
at the request of Yǎnshèng Gōng Kǒng Yùshēn,
and its taxes were exempted.
In the ninth month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Bāndá'ěrshā was appointed Ménggǔ Dūtǒng.
On the day Yǐsì,
Túnà was appointed Sìchuān Shǎnxī Zǒngdū.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Chén Tíngjìng was appointed Gōngbù Shàngshū,
and Mǎ Qí was appointed Shānxī Xúnfǔ.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
an envoy from Èluósī Cháhàn Hàn came to request the lifting of the siege of Yǎkèsà.
This was granted.
In this month,
Nèidàchén Lāduòhù, by imperial edict, returned after having fixed the border with Luóbùzàng Jìnóng and Gá'ěrdān.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
Zhāng Shìzhēn was transferred to be Lǐbù Shàngshū,
and Hú Shēngyóu was appointed Xíngbù Shàngshū.
In the eleventh month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
the Emperor visited Xiàolíng.
Mongolian Kālāqìn soldiers who had rendered meritorious service in the campaigns in Zhèjiāng and Fújiàn were rewarded.
In the twelfth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Shìláng Sàhǎi was ordered to supervise the military colonies at Fènghuángchéng.
On the day Guǐhài,
an edict stated:
"The Jiūyí Yùshǐ must be strict in their supervision.
Even if I, the Emperor, am disrespectful,
they must still impeach me."
On the day Wùyín,
a joint sacrifice was offered at Tàimiào.
In this year,
taxes were remitted for varying amounts of the allotted tribute for 27 prefectures and counties in the provinces of Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Zhèjiāng, Húguǎng, and Gānsù that had suffered from disasters.
Cháoxiǎn, Ānnán, Hélán, and Tǔlúfān offered tribute.
In the twenty-sixth year, Dīngmǎo, in spring, the first month, on the day Wùzǐ,
medical officials were dispatched to treat the sick soldiers at Yǎkèsà,
and Russian soldiers who wished to receive medical treatment were also treated.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Tǔxiētú Hàn and Chēchén Hàn of Ménggǔ, along with the Jìnóng, jointly submitted a memorial requesting an honorable title for the Emperor.
This was not permitted.
On the day Yǐsì,
Dàxuéshì Wú Zhèngzhì requested retirement.
This was granted.
In the second month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
the Emperor conducted a grand review at Lúgōuqiáo.
Cài Yùróng, former Húguǎng Zǒngdū, had hidden Wú Sānguì's granddaughter as a concubine
and secretly taken rebellious wealth.
His death sentence was commuted to one hundred lashes,
three months in the cangue,
and confiscation of his property.
His son was also exiled to Hēilóngjiāng.
The original judges, Shàngshū Xǐfó and others, were found guilty of connivance
and were dismissed or demoted to varying degrees.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Yú Guózhù was appointed Dàxuéshì.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the Eight Banners Dūtǒng and Fùdūtǒng were ordered to take turns on duty at Zǐjìnchéng.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Zhāng Yùshū was appointed Xíngbù Shàngshū.
On the day Rénshēn,
the Hùbù reported that Sāng'é, the supervisor of Hǔshùguān, had excessively collected over twenty-one thousand liǎng of silver.
An imperial decree stated:
"The establishment of customs barriers
was originally to investigate malpractices.
Sāng'é not only collected excessive silver,
but also privately sealed off the Biànmínqiáo,
thereby disturbing and harming merchants and commoners.
He is to be severely investigated and dealt with.
Hereafter, if any customs official levies excessive charges,
the relevant ministry shall strictly admonish them."
In the third month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Dǒng Nà was appointed Jiāngnán Jiāngxī Zǒngdū.
On the day Guǐsì,
Wáng Hóngxù was appointed Zuǒdū Yùshǐ.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Emperor held court at Tàihémén,
and instructed the Dàxuéshì and others to thoroughly discuss any shortcomings in governance.
They all replied that there were no abuses to report.
The Emperor said:
"In the eras of Yáo and Shùn,
the government was well-managed and affairs were harmonious,
yet they were still cautious and diligent,
not daring to claim that all was well and settled.
Hàn Wéndì was also a wise ruler of antiquity,
yet Jiǎ Yì still pointed out successes and failures,
and offered frank and urgent remonstrances.
Now you merely say that the ruler is sagacious and the ministers are wise,
and that there are no shortcomings in governance.
Is it truly the case that there is nothing to be said about the state?
All officials, great and small,
should diligently attend to their duties,
regarding state affairs as their own household affairs.
Whatever they see or hear,
they should present without concealment."
Mǎ Shìjì was appointed Guìzhōu Xúnfǔ.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Jǐwèi,
the Emperor instructed the Dàxuéshì, saying:
"Have the officials compiling the Míng History
consulted the former Míng Shílù?
If they do not consult the Shílù,
how can they fully ascertain what is true and what is false?
When the Míng History is completed,
the Shílù should also be preserved,
so that future generations have something to verify with."
On the day Bǐngyín,
Tián Wén was appointed Jiāngsū Xúnfǔ.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the practice of Kēdào officials attending court was abolished.
In the fifth month, on the day Jǐhài,
the Zōngrénfǔ reported that Píng Jùnwáng Nà'ěrdū had beaten an innocent subordinate to death
and broken his hands and feet,
and requested his titles be revoked and he be imprisoned.
An imperial decree stated:
"Revoke his title,
but exempt him from imprisonment."
On the day Gēngchén,
an edict stated:
"This mid-summer,
with a prolonged drought and strong winds,
yin and yang are out of balance.
What greater disaster is there?
Therefore, I have reduced my meals and ceased entertainment,
residing in solitude and praying silently.
Although sweet rain has fallen,
it is not yet sufficient.
All this is due to my meager virtue,
unable to move Heaven's heart.
Any policies inconvenient to the people shall be changed.
All those whose crimes would not normally be pardoned by a general amnesty shall be pardoned and exempted."
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Emperor summoned Chén Tíngjìng, Tāng Bīn, and twelve others to each be tested on their writing.
He said:
"I often discuss classics and history with Xióng Cìlǚ,
always asking when in doubt.
Subsequently, Zhāng Yīng and Chén Tíngjìng, in turn, lectured,
which was greatly beneficial.
Dégélè always likes to comment on the scholarship of his contemporaries,
which I consider incorrect.
Therefore, I summoned them for this test,
and now it is clear."
On the day Rénchén,
the Emperor composed memorial inscriptions for the temples of Zhōugōng, Kǒngzǐ, and Mèngzǐ,
and personally inscribed them on stone.
In the sixth month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
the Emperor, in plain attire, walked
to the Tiāntán to pray for rain.
That night,
it rained.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the sacrifice to Běihǎi was moved to Húntóngjiāng.
Yáng Sùyùn was appointed Ānhuī Xúnfǔ.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Èluósī sent envoys to discuss peace,
and Sàbùsù was ordered to withdraw his troops.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Hùbù requested to cut public expenses for capital officials.
An imperial decree stated not to cut them.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
the Emperor toured outside the passes.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
he stopped at Bóluòhétún for a hunt.
On the day Jiǎxū,
silver and silk were bestowed upon the outer vassal states.
In the ninth month, on the Jǐmǎo day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the Xīnsì day,
Yú Chénglóng presented auspicious grain.
The Emperor said:
"This summer was dry,
and fortunately we received rain,
but it is not enough to be considered an auspicious omen."
On the Rénwǔ day,
Lǐ Zhīfāng was appointed Grand Secretary.
On the Yǐwèi day,
Tāng Bīn was transferred to be Minister of Public Works.
Xú Yuánwén was reinstated as Chief Censor of the Left.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the Guǐchǒu day,
the Emperor toured the imperial domain.
On the Jiǎzǐ day,
the Emperor returned to reside at the Chàngchūnyuán.
In the eleventh month, on the Jiǎshēn day,
Lǐ Zhèngzōng was appointed Gūshān Ején of the Han military banner.
On the Bǐngshēn day,
the Grand Empress Dowager became unwell.
The Emperor went to Cínínggōng to attend to her illness.
In the twelfth month, on the Yǐsì first day,
due to the Grand Empress Dowager's illness,
the Emperor personally composed a prayer text,
and walked to Tiāntán to pray.
On the Guǐhài day,
Wáng Yǒngyù was appointed Gūshān Ején of the Han military banner.
On the Yǐchǒu day,
Zhāng Wéi, the Governor of Húguǎng, was impeached by Censor Chén Zǐzhī for corruption and greed;
Assistant Minister Sèlèng’é's initial investigation found the charges untrue.
Thereupon,
Yú Chénglóng, Mǎ Qí, and Kāiyīnbù were ordered to hasten and apprehend him,
and after investigation, he was condemned to death.
Chén Zǐzhī was promoted internally.
On the Jǐsì day,
the Grand Empress Dowager passed away.
The Emperor wept and mourned, overseeing the encoffining,
cut his queue and wore mourning clothes,
residing in a mourning hut at Cínínggōng.
On New Year's Eve, Jiǎxū day,
all the officials requested the Emperor to return to the palace.
He did not permit it.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted in four prefectures and counties across Zhílì, Shāndōng, Shānxī, Jiāngxī, and other provinces, with varying amounts.
Cháoxiǎn offered tribute.
In the twenty-seventh year, Wùchén, in spring, in the first month, on the Wùzǐ day,
the Emperor resided in a side tent outside Qiánqīngmén.
On the Yǐwèi day, he shed his mourning clothes.
On the Dīngyǒu day, he resumed governing.
In the second month, on the Rénzǐ day,
Grand Secretaries Lèdéhóng, Míngzhū, and Yú Guózhù were dismissed for crimes;
Lǐ Zhīfāng was dismissed as Censor,
as Guō Xiù had submitted a memorial detailing their offenses.
Ministers Kē'ěrkūn, Fólún, and Xióng Yīxiāo were all dismissed.
On the Jiǎyín day,
Liáng Qīngbiāo and Yīsāng'ā were appointed Grand Secretaries,
Lǐ Tiānfù was appointed Minister of Public Works,
Zhāng Yùshū was appointed Minister of War,
and Xú Qiánxué was appointed Minister of Punishments.
The annual regulations for imperial clan members inheriting titles were established.
In the third month, on the Yǐhài day,
Mǎ Qí was appointed Chief Censor of the Left.
On the Xīnsì day,
the Emperor summoned the court officials, along with Dǒng Nà, Jìn Fǔ, Yú Chénglóng, Fólún, Xióng Yīxiāo, and others, to discuss river affairs.
The next day, it was the same.
On the Yǐyǒu day,
Sèlèng'é was condemned to death for his deceitful investigation of Zhāng Wéi's case.
Governor-General Xú Guóxiàng was dismissed for conniving,
and Assistant Minister Wáng Zūnxùn and others were dismissed for improper recommendations.
All were stripped of their official positions.
On the Jǐchǒu day,
Wáng Xīnmìng was appointed Director-General of River Conservancy.
On the Xīnmǎo day,
the post of Governor-General of Húguǎng was abolished.
On the Dīngyǒu day,
the officials involved in river works who had mutually impeached each other were punished.
Dǒng Nà, Xióng Yīxiāo, Jìn Fǔ, Mù Tiānyán, and Sūn Zàifēng were all stripped of their official positions,
and Zhào Jíshì and Chén Huáng were also punished.
On the Jǐhài day,
Zhāng Pénghé, a Director of the Board of Punishments overseeing arrests, and Chén Shì'ān, a Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for War, were dispatched
to meet with Inner Grand Secretary Suǒ'étú and Russia to negotiate and define boundaries.
On the Rényín day,
Shěn Tíngwén and one hundred forty-six others were granted the Jinshì degree with varying ranks.
Lǐ Guāngdì was subject to deliberation for his improper recommendation of Dégélè.
An imperial decree was issued:
"Lǐ Guāngdì rendered meritorious service during the campaign in Táiwān,
and shall continue to serve as a scholar."
In summer, in the fourth month, on the Guǐmǎo first day,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the Wùshēn day,
Fùlātǎ was appointed Governor-General of Jiāngnán and Jiāngxī.
On the Jǐyǒu day,
the Emperor personally escorted the Grand Empress Dowager's coffin to be temporarily enshrined in the Zàn'ānfèngdiàn.
Later, the mausoleum was built,
which is now known as Zhāoxīlíng.
He returned to Jìzhōu to cut his hair (mourning practice).
On the Jiǎyín day,
due to the Ölöd invasion of Khalkha,
an envoy was sent to admonish Gá'ěrdān.
On the Wùchén day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the Gēngwǔ day,
Assistant Ministers Chéng Qífàn and Xú Tíngxǐ were ordered to inspect the river works.
In the fifth month, on the Jǐmǎo day,
Minister of Personnel Chén Tíngjìng and Minister of Punishments Xú Qiánxué were dismissed due to illness.
On the Jiǎwǔ day,
Jì'ěrtābù was appointed Minister of War.
On the Bǐngshēn day,
the Emperor visited and offered sacrifices at the Zàn'ānfèngdiàn.
In the sixth month, on the Jiǎchén day,
Xià Fénglóng, a demobilized soldier from the Húguǎng Governor-General's command, rebelled,
occupying Wǔchāng.
Governor Kē Yǒngshēng threw himself into a well and died.
Acting Provincial Administration Commissioner and Grain Intendant Yè Yìngliú was killed after cursing the rebels.
Wǎdàipèi was ordered to lead the Zhènwǔ General seal to suppress him.
On the Gēngshēn day,
Ālànī reported that Gá'ěrdān had invaded E'ěrdénízhāo,
and Jébùzūndānbā and Tǔshēyú Hán had fled.
Troops were dispatched to defend the border.
On the Wùchén day,
Xióng Cìlǚ was reinstated as Minister of Rites,
and Xú Yuánwén as Chief Censor of the Left.
Wēng Shūyuán was appointed Minister of Public Works.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the Guǐyǒu day,
Fúguógōng Huàshàn was appointed Gūshān Ején of the Mongol banner.
On the Yǐyǒu day,
Húguǎng Commander-in-Chief Xú Zhìdū heavily defeated Xià Fénglóng at Yìngchéng,
burning the rebel boats at Lǐyútào.
The rebels fled to Huánggāng.
On the Bǐngxū day,
the Emperor toured beyond the Great Wall.
On the Wùzǐ day,
Nányáng Commander-in-Chief Shǐ Kǒnghuá recovered Hànyáng.
On the Gēngyín day,
Wǎdài recovered Huángzhōu,
captured Xià Fénglóng,
and executed him by dismemberment.
The rebellion was quelled.
On the Réngwǔ day,
Yúnnán Commander-in-Chief Wàn Zhèngsè was charged with embezzlement of military provisions
and condemned to death according to law.
The Emperor, remembering his defiant refusal to surrender when he was previously captured by rebels,
and his numerous merits from bloody battles on the front lines,
spared him from death,
stripped him of his Commander-in-Chief title,
but retained his hereditary office.
On the Rénchén day,
the Emperor stayed at Kǎ'ěrbìhāhādá.
There was a peak formerly named Nàhālǐ,
hundreds of tens of feet high.
The Emperor shot several arrows, all passing over the peak,
and bestowed its current name.
In the eighth month, on the Guǐmǎo day,
the Emperor stayed at Bāyángōu for a hunt.
Yè Yìngliú's posthumous memorial arrived.
He was posthumously granted the title of Assistant Minister of Public Works,
and the Ministry was ordered to provide generous compensation.
On the Yǐmǎo day,
Zhāng Yùshū reported on inspecting the river works,
mostly adopting Jìn Fǔ's former proposals.
In the ninth month, on the Rénshēn day,
Péngchūn and Nuòmǐn were dispatched to lead troops stationed at Guīhuàchéng to defend the border.
At this time, Khalkha had been conquered by Gá'ěrdān,
and its people had moved closer to the inner border.
Ālànī was dispatched to convey imperial instructions,
and also to transport rice for relief and pacification.
On the Xīnmǎo day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the Guǐsì day,
the post of Governor-General of Húguǎng was re-established,
with Dīng Sīkǒng appointed to it.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the Guǐmǎo day,
Yáng Sùyùn was transferred to be Governor of Húguǎng.
On the Gēngxū day,
Fúguógōng Chuòkètuō was appointed General of Fèngtiān.
On the Yǐmǎo day,
the Emperor granted the Grand Empress Dowager the posthumous title of Xiàozhuāngwén Huánghòu.
On the Xīnyǒu day,
she was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple,
and an imperial edict was issued to China and abroad.
In the eleventh month, on the Xīnmǎo day,
Jiāngzhōu General Gá'ěrhàn and others were stripped of their posts and
given one hundred lashes for delaying in suppressing the rebels.
Officials who sided with the rebels and accepted official positions were arrested and prosecuted,
while others were pardoned.
In the twelfth month, on the day *gēngzǐ*,
Xīfú was appointed Mongol Commander-in-chief.
On the day *jiǎchén*,
the Stele of Sacred Virtues and Divine Merits was erected for the Fúlíng Mausoleum and the Zhāolíng Mausoleum,
with the imperial inscription personally composed by the Emperor.
The Emperor visited the mountain mausoleum of Empress Xiàozhuāng.
On the day *yǐsì*,
Níyǎhàn was appointed Xi'ān General.
On the day *jǐyǒu*,
Zhāng Yùshū was promoted to Minister of Rites;
Xú Yuánwén, Minister of Justice,
was further promoted to Minister of Revenue.
On the day *bǐngyín*,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
The Ministry of War and the Ministry of Works jointly memorialized to reduce the cost of materials and silver for the previously constructed cannon ships in Fújiàn by over twenty thousand *liǎng*,
and that this sum should be recovered from the name of the deceased Governor-General, Yáo Qǐshèng.
The Emperor, considering Yáo Qǐshèng's significant achievements in managing the pacification of Táiwān,
ordered that no recovery was necessary.
In this year,
tax exemptions for disaster-stricken areas were granted, varying in degree, to thirty-three prefectures and counties in the provinces of Jiāngnán, Jiāngxī, Húguǎng, Yúnnán, and Guìzhōu.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú presented tribute.
In the twenty-eighth year, on the first month of spring, on the day *gēngwǔ* of the *jǐsì* year,
an imperial edict announced a southern tour to inspect river works.
The imperial retinue departed on the day *bǐngzǐ*.
An edict forbade the common people from repairing roads in the areas the Emperor passed through.
The common people of Xiànxiàn presented auspicious grain.
On the day *rénwǔ*,
an edict exempted Shāndōng from its land and poll tax quota.
On the day *jiǎshēn*,
the Emperor sojourned in Jǐnán.
On the day *yǐyǒu*,
a distant sacrifice was offered to Mount Tài.
On the day *gēngyín*,
the Emperor arrived at Shǎnchéng
and inspected the Middle River.
On the day *rénchén*,
the Emperor arrived at Qīnghé.
On the day *guǐsì*,
an edict exempted Jiāngnán from accumulated arrears of over two hundred thousand.
On the day *yǐwèi*,
the Emperor sojourned in Yángzhōu.
An edict stated:
"I observe customs and inquire about local conditions;
my imperial paraphernalia is not displayed,
and my retinue consists of only three hundred people.
Recently, when I sojourned in Yángzhōu,
the people adorned the streets with colorful decorations,
which, though stemming from sincere love and respect,
nonetheless caused some depletion of their resources.
Therefore, in the prefectures and counties along the route ahead,
all such activities should be stopped."
In the second month, on the day *xīnchǒu*,
the Emperor sojourned in Sūzhōu.
On the day *dīngwèi*,
the Emperor sojourned in Hángzhōu.
An edict expanded educational quotas,
bestowed gifts upon soldiers,
restored officials demoted for public service,
granted silver and silk to the princes, ministers, and others in the retinue,
and bestowed gold upon local elders.
On the day *xīnhài*,
the Emperor crossed the Qiántáng River
and arrived at the foot of Mount Kuàijī.
On the day *rénzǐ*,
a sacrifice was offered at Yǔlíng,
with a personal sacrificial text composed by the Emperor,
who wrote his name,
performed the nine prostrations,
composed an eulogy to be carved into stone,
and inscribed the title
"The Earth is Leveled, Heaven is Accomplished."
On the day *guǐchǒu*,
the Emperor returned to sojourn in Hángzhōu.
He inspected horsemanship and archery,
and granted a grand feast to the generals and officers.
On the day *dīngsì*,
the Emperor arrived at Sūzhōu.
Yè Fū, son of the deceased Húguǎng Grain Intendant Yè Yìngliú, welcomed the imperial retinue
and requested a posthumous title for his father.
The Emperor wrote the
two large characters "Zhōngjié"
and bestowed them upon him.
The common people of Sōngjiāng erected a stele to pray for the Emperor's longevity
and presented a stele inscription.
The common people of Jiāngnán appealed for the Emperor to prolong his stay
and presented local produce as imperial food,
which piled up on the riverbanks.
The Emperor ordered a pinch of rice
and one fruit to be taken,
and stayed for one more day.
Jīn Hóng, the Provincial Governor of Zhèjiāng, was found guilty,
stripped of his office, and exiled.
Zhāng Pénghé was appointed Provincial Governor of Zhèjiāng.
Naval forces were increased in Wǔchāng, Jīngzhōu, Chángdé, and Yuèzhōu.
On the day *guǐhài*,
the Emperor sojourned in Jiāngníng.
On the day *jiǎzǐ*,
a sacrifice was offered at the Míng Mausoleums.
White silver was bestowed upon elderly men and women of the garrisons in Jiāngníng and Jīngkǒu.
On the day *yǐchǒu*,
the Emperor inspected archery
and granted a feast.
The Emperor visited the Observatory
and discussed astronomical phenomena with Academician Lǐ Guāngdì, concluding that the Shēn constellation precedes the Zī constellation,
fixed stars move with the heavens,
and the Lǎorén star is seen in Jiāngnán,
it is not hidden or revealed.
The scholars and common people of Jiāngníng appealed for the imperial carriage to stay.
The Emperor stayed for two more days.
In the third month, on the first day *wùchén*,
the Emperor departed Jiāngníng.
On the day *jiǎxū*,
the Emperor inspected Gāojiāyàn
and personally gave instructions on river management strategies.
On the day *bǐngxū*,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
Upon hearing of the death of Prince Ān Yuèlè,
the Emperor first visited his residence to mourn him,
then returned to the palace.
On the day *dīnghài*,
it was ordered that the Eight Banners civil service examination should first test horsemanship and archery.
On the day *wùzǐ*,
an edict stated that Jìn Fǔ's achievements in river management were clearly outstanding,
and he should be reinstated to his original office.
On the day *dīngyǒu*,
the Eight Banners Artillery Corps was augmented,
with a Deputy Commander-in-chief in charge.
In the intercalary third month, on the day *rénzǐ*,
Prince Ān Yuèlè was granted a sacrificial burial and a stele erected,
with the posthumous title Hé.
On the day *jǐwèi*,
the Emperor visited the mausoleums.
On the day *bǐngwǔ*,
the Emperor visited the mountain mausoleum of Empress Xiàozhuāng
and the Xiàolíng Mausoleum.
On the day *xīnyǒu*,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the summer fourth month, on the first day *yǐhài*,
the Emperor composed "An Encomium for Confucius with a Preface" and encomiums for Yán, Zēng, Sī, and Mèng,
which were distributed to the educational academies.
On the day *rénchén*,
Sǒng'étú and others were again ordered to go to Níbùchǔ
to delimit the border with Éluósī.
The Khalkha Outer Mongols, having submitted, reported famine.
Inner Minister Bófēiyánggǔ was ordered to go and provide relief and comfort them.
It was ordered that coins be minted in Táiwān.
In the fifth month, on the day *yǐsì*,
Ālántài and Xú Yuánwén were appointed Grand Secretaries,
Gù Bādài was appointed Minister of Rites,
and Guō Xiù was appointed Censor-in-chief of the Left.
On the day *rénxū*,
the *Xiàojīng Yǎnyì* (Expanded Meaning of the Classic of Filial Piety) was promulgated.
On the day *guǐhài*,
it was ordered that troops be stationed in Guīhuàchéng to guard the frontier.
In the sixth month, on the day *yǐhài*,
Tóng Bǎo was appointed Nínggǔtǎ General.
Wú Xìngzuò, the Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng, was dismissed from office for irregularities in coinage.
In the autumn seventh month,
Shí Lín was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng.
On the day *guǐmǎo*,
Noble Consort Tóng Shì was formally installed as Empress.
On the day *jiǎchén*,
the Empress passed away,
and was posthumously titled Xiàoyì.
In the eighth month, on the day *guǐyǒu*,
the Emperor toured beyond the frontier.
On the day *wùyín*,
the Emperor sojourned in Bólòuhétún
and bestowed silver and rice upon the residents.
In the ninth month, on the day *guǐmǎo*,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day *wùwǔ*,
Wōhè was appointed Mongol Commander-in-chief,
and Princess's husband Mùhè was appointed Han Banner Commander-in-chief.
In the winter tenth month, on the day *bǐngyín*,
Láng Tán was appointed Manchu Commander-in-chief.
On the day *xīnwèi*,
two wings of Khalkha Zāsàk were added,
gathering refugees and defectors
and organizing them into banner units.
On the day *guǐyǒu*,
Censor-in-chief of the Left Guō Xiù was demoted for writing letters of recommendation to the provincial governor of his own province.
On the day *jiǎxū*,
Empress Xiàoyì was buried,
and the Emperor personally attended the funeral.
In this month,
the aboriginals of Mínzhōu submitted.
In the eleventh month, on the day *bǐngshēn*,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the day *xīnyǒu*,
Empress Xiàoyì was enshrined in the Fèngxiāndiàn Temple.
On the *yǐchǒu* day of the twelfth month,
an edict was issued to exempt Yunnan from outstanding taxes owed from the 21st to the 23rd years.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Emperor paid respects to the Empress Dowager in the new Cíníng Palace.
On the *wùchén* day,
Zhāng Yīng was appointed Minister of Works.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Grand Minister Sǒ Ér Tú submitted a memorial reporting the conclusion of a treaty with Ouluósī,
establishing Níbùchǔ as the border,
and erecting boundary markers,
with the text inscribed in five languages.
In this year,
disaster relief was granted, exempting 11 prefectures and counties in Zhílì, Zhèjiāng, Húběi, and other provinces from varying amounts of tax.
Cháoxiǎn offered tribute.
On the *guǐchǒu* day of the first month of spring in the 29th year, a *gēngwǔ* year,
the Emperor visited the Southern Park.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
officials were dispatched to provide relief to the Kǎěrkǎ Mongols.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day of the second month,
Yuè Lè's son, Mǎěrhún, was enfeoffed as Prince Ānjùn.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
ministers were dispatched to inspect the disaster-stricken areas and the displaced people in Zhílì.
The porridge kitchens in the Five Cities were extended in duration,
the silver and rice distributed were doubled,
and additional locations were established.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Emperor visited the Xiàozhuāng Mausoleum
and the Xiàolíng Mausoleum.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
there was heavy rain.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the Emperor presided over the imperial lecture (*jīngyán*).
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Chén Tíngjìng was reinstated as Censor-in-Chief on the Left.
On the *rénchén* day, the first day of the third month,
the newly increased salt tax of Chánglú was abolished.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
an edict was issued to compile the national histories of the three reigns.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Dūtǒng Èhènà, Hùjūn Tǒnglǐng Mǎlài, and Qiánfēng Tǒnglǐng Shuònài were ordered to lead troops to conquer Èlǔtè.
Previously,
Gáěrdān's forces had invaded Kǎěrkǎ,
repeated imperial edicts to persuade them to withdraw were disregarded,
and their troops approached the border.
At this point,
Èhènà and others were ordered to proceed to the border to defend against them.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the increased salt tax of Hēijǐng, Yúnnán, was abolished.
Zhāng Sīgōng was appointed General of Jīngkǒu.
On the *dīngchǒu* day of the fourth month in summer,
due to drought, a general amnesty was granted to prisoners sentenced to death or lesser punishments.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
a temple for Zǐ Sīzǐ was built in Quēlǐ.
The *Dà Qīng Huìdiǎn* was completed.
On the *xīnmǎo* day, the first day of the fifth month,
the Nine Ministers were ordered to recommend officials from prefectures and counties suitable for appointment as supervising censors (*kēdào*).
On the *guǐyǒu* day of the sixth month,
Grand Secretary Xú Yuánwén was relieved of his post.
On the *wùyín* day,
Gáěrdān pursued the Kǎěrkǎ and invaded the border.
Nèi Dàchén Sūěrdá was ordered to proceed to Kēěrqìn to levy Mongol troops for defense.
Kāng Qīnwáng Jiéshū and Kèshèn Jùnwáng Yuèxī were ordered to station troops at Guīhuà City.
On the *gēngyín* day, the first day of the seventh month in autumn,
Zhāng Yīng was appointed Minister of Rites,
and Dǒng Yuánqīng was appointed General of Jīngkǒu.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Gáěrdān invaded Wūzhūmùqín.
Yù Qīnwáng Fúquán was appointed Grand General Fúyuǎn,
with Imperial Prince Yìnzhī as his deputy,
to sally forth from Gǔběikǒu.
Gōng Qīnwáng Chángníng was appointed Grand General Ānyuǎn,
with Jiǎn Qīnwáng Lābù and Xìn Jùnwáng Èzhā as his deputies,
to sally forth from Xǐfēngkǒu.
Nèi Dàchén Tóng Guó Gāng, Sǒ Ér Tú, Míng Zhū, Péng Chūn, and others all joined the military council,
while Āmìdá, Ālānní, and Ānándá all gathered at the front.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Chén Tíngjìng was appointed Minister of Works,
and Yú Chénglóng was appointed Censor-in-Chief on the Left.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor personally led the expedition,
departing from the capital.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor stationed at Bóluòhétún,
but fell ill and returned to the capital.
On the *yǐwèi* day, the first day of the eighth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Grand General Fúyuǎn, Yù Qīnwáng Fúquán, decisively defeated Gáěrdān at Wūlánbùtōng.
Gáěrdān sent the lama Jílóng to sue for peace,
and Fúquán did not immediately advance his troops.
The Emperor severely reprimanded him.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Gáěrdān presented a sworn letter.
The Emperor said:
"This barbarian is not to be trusted.
Let the army be prepared to await him."
On the *guǐsì* day of the ninth month,
previously,
during the battle of Wūlánbùtōng,
Nèi Dàchén Gōng Tóng Guó Gāng was killed in action.
At this time,
his coffin returned,
and the Imperial Prince was ordered to lead ministers to welcome it.
All officials killed in battle were granted varying levels of sacrifices and pensions.
On the *wùshēn* day,
this year's autumn executions were suspended.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the ban on private horse breeding was relaxed.
On the *jǐwèi* day of the tenth month in winter,
the Emperor's illness slightly improved,
and he summoned the Grand Secretaries and other ministers to the Qiánqīng Palace for rotating audiences.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Èlúndài was appointed Dūtǒng of the Chinese Banners.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Zhāng Yīng, Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, failed to detect improprieties in the eulogy for Tóng Guó Gāng drafted by Compiler Yáng Xuān,
and was stripped of his position as Minister of Rites.
Yáng Xuān was dismissed from office, exiled to the frontier, and assigned to a banner.
On the *jǐhài* day of the eleventh month,
Xióng Cìlǚ was appointed Minister of Rites.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the Dálài Lǎmā requested the Emperor to accept an honorific title.
This was refused,
and his tribute was also rejected.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Yù Qīnwáng Fúquán and others arrived in the capital for interrogation.
The princely ministers deliberated and memorialized.
The Emperor deemed their offense minor,
and lightly punished them.
The merits of the generals and soldiers were still recognized.
On the *dīngchǒu* day of the twelfth month,
the Emperor visited the mausoleums,
performing the three-year sacrificial ceremony for Empress Xiàozhuāngwén.
On the *gēngchén* day, he returned to the capital.
In this year,
disaster relief was granted, exempting 32 prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Zhèjiāng, Gānsù, and other provinces from varying amounts of tax.
Cháoxiǎn offered tribute.
On the *wùshēn* day of the first month of spring in the 30th year, a *xīnwèi* year,
Ālùkēěrqìn Bèilè Chǔyī was enfeoffed as Prince Jùnwáng,
because he fought bravely against the Èlǔtè, was wounded and captured but remained unyielding, and eventually escaped and returned.
His twelve banner's fallen *táijí* were all posthumously granted the title of First-Rank *Táijí*,
and bestowed the honorific *Dáěrhàn*,
with their descendants inheriting the title.
Gáěrdān again plundered Kǎěrkǎ.
Wǎdài was appointed General Dìngběi,
stationed at Zhāngjiākǒu.
Lángtán was appointed General Ānběi,
stationed at Dàtóng.
The Governor-General of Chuān-Shǎǎn, along with the General of Xī'ān, stationed troops in Níngxià to guard against him.
The retired General Yǒnglǜe, Zhào Liángdòng, was ordered to join the military council.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Mǎ Qí was appointed Minister of War.
On the *dīngsì* day, the first day of the second month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Emperor presided over the imperial lecture (*jīngyán*).
The Commander of the Infantry was ordered to lead the three patrol battalions,
and concurrently oversee the police and arrest duties of the Five Cities.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
an envoy from Èlǔtè Cèwàng Ālābùtán arrived;
he was Gáěrdān's nephew.
His envoy was generously rewarded.
When he was about to return,
Lángzhōng Sāng'é was dispatched to escort him.
On the *wùzǐ* day of the third month,
the translation of *Tōngjiàn Gāngmù* was completed,
and the Emperor composed a preface.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Dài Yǒuqí and 147 others were granted the *Jìnshì Jíyǐ* degree and other equivalent ranks.
On the *wùwǔ* day of the fourth month in summer,
Censor-in-Chief on the Left, Xú Qiánxué, sent a private letter to the Governor of Shāndōng, Qián Yù.
When the incident was discovered,
both were dismissed from office.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor, due to the Kǎěrkǎ's allegiance,
personally traveled to the frontier to offer comfort and pacification.
On this day,
the imperial procession departed.
In the fifth month, on the day *bǐngxū*,
the Emperor resided at Duōluó'nuò'ěr.
The Khalkha came to pay tribute.
Previously,
Tǔxiètú Hán of Khalkha, instigated by Zhébozūndānbā,
killed his kinsman, Zāsàkètú Hán Dékédéihēimò'ěrgēn Āhǎi.
Internal strife arose repeatedly,
and the Èlǔtè took advantage of it.
At this point,
ministers were dispatched to investigate the matter.
Tǔxiètú Hán and Zhébozūndānbā both submitted memorials pleading guilty.
The Emperor pardoned them.
Regarding the Zāsàkètú Hán,
who was the leader of the seven banners,
His younger brother Cèwàngzhābù was ordered to succeed to the title of Hán,
and was enfeoffed as a *Qīnwáng*.
On the day *dīnghài*,
the Emperor attended court in his traveling tent.
Tǔxiètú Hán and Zhébozūndānbā came to pay their respects,
prostrating themselves and pleading guilty.
The minister proclaimed the pardon,
and they wept tears of gratitude.
They were granted tea, a banquet, and seats,
and grand music was played.
They performed the nine kowtows and then withdrew.
On the day *wùzǐ*,
Tǔxiètú Hán, Zhébozūndānbā, Cèwàngzhābù, Chēchén Hán, and thirty-five *Jìnóng*, *Wěizhēng*, *Nuòyán*, and *Āyùxī* grand *Táijí* from various Khalkha tribes were again invited to a banquet.
The Emperor declared:
"I wish to know you all well,
hence this renewed feast."
They were bestowed with caps and robes.
As Cèwàngzhābù was young,
he was given the clothes, hat, and prayer beads of an imperial prince.
Regarding Nàmǔzhā'ěr, the uncle of Chēchén Hán and *Zāsàkè Jìnóng*, who had previously encouraged Chēchén Hán to lead 100,000 people to surrender,
and had himself initiated the move,
and who had requested to be treated on par with the forty-nine banners,
this was deemed highly commendable.
He was allowed to retain his old *Zāsàkè* position,
but his title of *Jìnóng* was removed,
and he was enfeoffed as a *Jùnwáng*.
The others were enfeoffed with various noble ranks.
An edict was issued to the Khalkha, stating:
"You all were in extreme distress,
stealing and plundering from each other.
I have now rescued and cherished you.
Now, along with the forty-nine banners, *Zāsàkè* are to be established in various places,
to govern and inspect.
Each of you should comply.
If anyone acts recklessly again,
they will be punished by state law."
On the day *jǐchǒu*,
the Emperor, wearing armor and riding a horse,
inspected all the various tribes.
Dismounting, he personally shot arrows,
hitting the target nine out of ten times.
Next, a grand review was held for the Manchu soldiers, Han Chinese soldiers, and Gǔbèikǒu soldiers.
They formed ranks and sounded horns,
and the muskets fired in unison,
their sound shaking the valleys.
The assembled Khalkha looked around in astonishment and exclaimed:
"Truly divine power!"
The Khalkha and Kē'ěrqìn Mongol kings and *bèilè* requested that an honorific title be conferred upon the Emperor.
This was not granted.
On the day *gēngyín*,
the Emperor inspected the Khalkha encampments,
and bestowed cattle and sheep upon the impoverished among them.
On the day *xīnmǎo*,
officials were dispatched to organize the Khalkha into *zuǒlǐng* [companies]
and assign them pastures.
Regarding Chēgēn and other *Táijí* of Wūzhǔmùqín who had defected to the Èlǔtè,
they were tried and punished according to their actual crimes.
On the day *rénchén*,
the Emperor returned to his temporary palace.
On the day *guǐmǎo*,
he returned to the capital.
On the day *xīnhài*,
the *huìshì* (metropolitan examination) papers were divided into southern left, southern right, northern left, northern right, central left, and central right sections,
following the suggestion of the Censor Jiāng Fán.
On the day *rénzǐ*,
the assembled officials requested that an honorific title be conferred upon the Emperor.
This was not granted.
In the sixth month, on the day *yǐmǎo*,
Lǐ Tiānfù was appointed Minister of Personnel,
Chén Tíngjìng as Minister of Punishments,
and Gāo'ěrwèi as Minister of Public Works.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day *jiǎshēn*,
Níyǎhàn, the General of Xī'ān, received an imperial edict to lead troops to relocate Bātú'ěr'è'ěrkè Jìnóng to Cháhār.
The *Jìnóng*, fearing the relocation, fled.
Níyǎhàn pursued him but failed to catch him,
and was interrogated and sentenced to death.
The Governor-General Gěsītài was ordered to pursue and apprehend him.
The Korean envoy was accused of a crime in his country for purchasing the *Yītǒngzhì* (Comprehensive Gazetteer).
The retired Grand Secretary Dù Lìdé passed away;
he was granted sacrificial rites and a burial,
and posthumously given the epithet Wénduān.
In the intercalary seventh month, on the day *bǐngchén*,
Gěsītài reported in a memorial that Bójì, the younger brother of the *Jìnóng*, was at Chāngníng Hú.
He was attacked and defeated by troops dispatched by Commander Kē Cǎi,
who captured Bójì alive, along with Gélóng and others who had been previously banned.
All were executed.
On the day *yǐhài*,
the Emperor made a tour beyond the frontier.
In the ninth month, on the day *xīnyǒu*,
the Emperor returned to his temporary palace,
passing through Zūnhuà,
where he visited the Mausoleum of Xiàozhuāng,
and the Xiàolíng Mausoleum.
On the day *yǐchǒu*,
he returned to the capital.
On the day *gēngwǔ*,
Gōng Ālíng'ā was appointed Mongol Military Governor.
On the day *jiǎxū*,
Vice Ministers Bójì, Lǐ Guāngdì, and Xú Tíngxǐ were ordered to inspect the river together with Jìn Fǔ.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day *gēngyín*,
the Shè'ěrsù barbarians ambushed and killed Brigadier Zhū Zhèn.
Lǐ Fāngshù, the Commander-in-Chief of Xīníng, captured and executed the bandit leader Huámù'ěrjiā.
On the day *guǐsì*,
Bādéhún was appointed Manchu Military Governor,
and Hángyìlù as General of Jīngzhōu.
On the day *dīngwèi*,
Sūn Sīkè, the Provincial Commander of Gānsù, attacked Āqíluóbùzàng,
and executed him.
Previously,
Dáhǔ, a Supervising Secretary in the Hanlin Academy who had been sent as an envoy to the Èlǔtè, was returning and reached Jiāyù Guān
when he was murdered by Āqíluóbùzàng.
Sīkè was ordered to subjugate him.
At this time,
the victory was reported.
In the eleventh month, on the day *dīngsì*,
Suǒnuóhé and Lǐ Zhènyù were appointed Ministers of Public Works,
and Yīlèshèn as Manchu Military Governor.
On the day *jǐwèi*,
an imperial edict stated:
"I advocate virtue and education,
and alleviate burdensome strictures.
All officials, great and small,
have received grace and courtesy.
Even those dismissed due to various matters
are still allowed to live peacefully in their hometowns.
Recently, private feuds and disputes
have arisen incessantly,
and there is a tendency to form factions and attack those who differ.
Do they wish to brew the calamity of factional strife from the late Míng dynasty?
Let each of you set aside private grudges
and collectively vow loyalty and impartiality.
Should anyone persist,
I will thoroughly investigate and punish them."
At this time, Xú Yuánwén, Xú Qiánxué, and Wáng Hóngxù had been dismissed,
while Fùlàtǎ and others exposed minor hidden faults,
connecting them to instigate legal cases.
Therefore, this special edict was issued to warn and admonish them.
On the day *jiǎxū*,
an imperial edict stated:
"The Imperial Observatory reported that there will be a solar eclipse on the first day of the first month next year.
This celestial phenomenon serves as a warning,
and I am greatly fearful.
Therefore, the New Year's Day banquet and other ceremonies are to be canceled.
All officials should diligently perform their duties
and assist me in self-cultivation and reflection."
In the twelfth month, on the day *jiǎshēn*,
an imperial edict stated:
"In governing the realm,
I only think of cherishing and nurturing the common people,
to ensure their peace and prosperity.
In recent years, the *dìdīng* (land and poll tax) quota has been repeatedly exempted,
but the annual grain tribute transport
is still being collected,
which constantly troubles me.
Aside from Hénán, which has already received exemptions,
the grain tribute from Húguǎng, Jiāngsū, Zhèjiāng, Ānhuī, and Shāndōng
is to be successively exempted for one year each,
to alleviate the burden on the people."
On the day *dīnghài*,
the *Zhuàngdīng* (able-bodied men) from the banner estates were moved to Dá'ěrhé outside Gǔbèikǒu to cultivate land.
Vice Ministers Āshān, Dézhū, and others were dispatched to Shǎnxī to supervise disaster relief.
On the day *rénchén*,
Governors-General, Provincial Governors, Provincial Commanders, and Brigade-Generals were instructed to recommend competent military officials and those who had rendered meritorious service.
For banner officials of the Eight Banners within the capital,
the Military Governors were ordered to recommend them.
In this year,
disaster taxes in 188 prefectures and counties in provinces such as Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Jiāngxī, Hénán, Shāndōng, Shǎnxī, Húguǎng, and Yúnnán were exempted to varying degrees.
Cháoxiǎn, Ānnán, and Liúqiú offered tribute.
In the spring of the thirty-first year, Rénshēn, in the first month, on the day Xīnhài, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse,
and court celebrations were suspended.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Emperor presided over a court session at the Qiánqīngmén,
and displayed the Tàijítú, the Wǔyīn Bāshēng Bāfēngtú.
He then said:
"The method of 'one diameter and three circumferences' in the new book on pitch pipes [Lǜlǚ Xīnshū]
does not fit.
If the diameter is one chí, the circumference should be three chí, one cùn, four fēn, and one lí.
Accumulated to a hundred zhàng,
the difference would be over fourteen zhàng.
How can this be used?
Only the theory of 'generation every eight' [gébā xiāngshēng]
has been tested and found to be entirely consistent."
He also discussed the flow of water at the sluice gates of the river,
and how the daily and nightly volume
could be calculated.
He also displayed a sundial table,
showing by illustration the position of the sun's shadow at noon,
and it was verified to be accurate.
All the officials were impressed.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the Emperor went on a hunting expedition to Nányuàn.
In the second month, on the day Xīnsì,
Jìn Fǔ was appointed Grand Coordinator of Rivers [Hédào Zǒngdūdū].
On the day Yǐyǒu,
due to drought in Shǎnxī,
silver from the treasury of Shānxī and rice from Xiāngyáng were distributed for relief.
On the day Dīnghài,
the Emperor toured Jīdiàn.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Sàbì, the Provincial Governor of Shǎnxī, was dismissed from office for ineffective disaster relief.
On the day Wùxū,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Jǐhài,
the Emperor presided over a classics colloquium [Jīngyán].
On the day Yǐsì,
Mǎ Qí was appointed Minister of Revenue [Hùbù Shàngshū].
In the third month, on the day Bǐngchén,
Inner Minister Ā'ěrdí and President of the Court of Colonial Affairs [Lǐfānyuàn Shàngshū] Bāndí were dispatched to the frontier to establish Mongol post stations.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Xu Tíngxǐ, Vice-Minister of the Ministry of Works [Fǔchéng], was ordered to assist in river conservancy.
Sūn Sīkè, Provincial Military Commander [Tídū] of Gānsù, was granted the title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent [Tàizǐ Shàobǎo],
and hereditary office.
Féng Pǔ, Grand Secretary [Dàxuéshì] who had retired, passed away.
He was granted sacrificial rites and a burial,
and given the posthumous name Wénmǐn.
Āxītǎn was appointed Manchu General-in-chief [Mǎnzhōu Dūtǒng].
Yǒngběi Town was established in Yúnnán.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the day Gēngchén, the first day of the month,
Xī Fú was appointed Manchu General-in-chief,
and Hùbā was appointed Mongol General-in-chief.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
one million taels of silver from the treasury were issued for relief in Shǎnxī.
Ministers Wáng Zhì and Shā Mùhā went to inspect and provide additional relief.
On the day Wùxū,
the Emperor visited Yíngtái,
and summoned close officials to observe the paddy fields and the bamboo cultivation.
Jìn Fǔ, Grand Coordinator of Rivers, requested the construction of one sluice gate each at Xīnzhuāng and Zhòngjiāqiǎn.
The Ministry deliberated and approved it.
In the fifth month, on the day Gēngyín,
an edict was issued to the Ministry of Revenue, stating:
"Píngyáng in Shānxī has a bumper harvest,
officials can be sent to purchase grain to prepare for famine."
Wáng Wéizhēn was ordered to oversee this matter.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Khalkha [Kā'ěrkǎ] tribes were divided into three routes:
Tǔxiètú as the northern route,
Chēchén as the eastern route,
and Zhāsàkètú as the western route.
Their subordinate tribes were each divided into left and right wings according to their assigned territories.
In the sixth month, on the day Gēngchén,
Sòng Luò was appointed Provincial Governor of Jiāngníng.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the Khalkha [Kē'ěrqìn] Mongols presented over ten thousand households of Xībó, Guà'ěrcá, and Dǎhǔ'ěr.
Silver was given in return.
In the autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Yǐhài,
the Emperor toured beyond the Great Wall [Sàiwài].
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Wēng Shūyuán was appointed Minister of Justice [Xíngbù Shàngshū],
Bójì was appointed General of Xī'ān,
Lǐ Línlóng was appointed Provincial Military Commander [Tídū] of Gùyuán,
and Lǐ Fāngshù was appointed Provincial Military Commander [Tídū] of Guìzhōu.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùshēn,
a person belonging to Gá'ěrdān seized and murdered our envoy Mǎ Dí.
On the day Gēngxū,
the Emperor returned to Tāngquán.
On the day Jǐwèi,
he returned to the capital.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the Emperor presided over a classics colloquium [Jīngyán].
On the day Rénshēn,
the Emperor held a grand review at Yùquánshān.
In the winter, in the tenth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
an imperial edict stated:
"Qín Province has suffered consecutive years of famine,
compounded by epidemics,
and despite various relief efforts,
the accumulated distress has not been alleviated.
Therefore, all land and poll taxes [dìdīng shuìliáng] for the coming year
are hereby remitted.
All previous outstanding debts
are entirely waived.
This is to express Our utmost intention to benefit the common people."
On the day Gēngchén,
Lǐ Tiānfù was appointed Grand Secretary [Dàxuéshì].
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Emperor visited the imperial tombs [Líng].
A partial amnesty was granted to Shǎnxī:
those not guilty of the "ten heinous crimes" [shí'è] or who had not incurred punishment in military campaigns [jūnqián huòqiǎn]
were all granted a reprieve from death or had their sentences reduced by one degree.
Fólún was appointed Governor-General of Chuān-Shǎn [Chuān Shǎn Zǒngdūdū],
and Zōngshì Dǒng'é was appointed Manchu General-in-chief [Mǎnzhōu Dūtǒng].
On the day Gēngyín,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Guǐsì,
Xióng Cìlǚ was appointed Minister of Personnel [Lìbù Shàngshū],
and Zhāng Yīng was appointed Minister of Rites [Lǐbù Shàngshū].
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the sending of fresh tea and memorials [biǎojiān] from the direct provinces was suspended.
In the eleventh month, on the day Gēngxū,
Ālíng'ā was appointed Manchu General-in-chief [Mǎnzhōu Dūtǒng].
On the day Jiǎyín,
Xióng Cìlǚ was ordered to inspect the dried-up fields along the Huái and Yáng rivers.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Sūn Sīkè was promoted to Zhènwǔ General.
Juélúo Xítèkù was appointed Mongol General-in-chief [Ménggǔ Dūtǒng].
In the twelfth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Jìn Fǔ, Grand Coordinator of Rivers, passed away.
He was granted sacrificial rites and a burial,
and given the posthumous name Wénxiāng.
Yú Chénglóng was appointed Grand Coordinator of Rivers,
and Dǒng Nà was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left [Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ].
On the day Rénchén,
Láng Huàlín was appointed Han Banner General-in-chief [Hànjūn Dūtǒng].
On the day Xīnchǒu,
due to famine in Xī'ān,
rice from Xiāngyáng was transported for fair-price sale.
Xī Fú was promoted to Jiànwǔ General [Jiànwǔ Jiāngjūn],
and transferred to guard the Right Flank.
Shājīn, a Khalkha [Kē'ěrqìn] Mongol king, was summoned to the capital,
personally given strategic instructions,
and tasked with enticing Gá'ěrdān.
In this year,
tax remissions of varying degrees were granted to thirteen prefectures and counties in provinces such as Shǎnxī, Jiāngnán, and Sìchuān due to disasters.
Cháoxiǎn paid tribute.
In the thirty-second year, Guǐyǒu, in the first month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
an edict declared that Cháoxiǎn's annual tribute of gold and kapok would be permanently suspended.
In the second month, on the day Yǐhài, the first day of the month,
treasury funds were issued
to encourage merchants to transport rice to Xī'ān for fair-price sales.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Inner Minister Pō'ěrběn and others were dispatched to supervise the establishment of military agricultural colonies [túntián] in the three routes of Guīhuàchéng.
An edict ordered the repair of the Zhōuqíao embankment works in the Southern River.
These works had been surveyed by Jìn Fǔ and Chén Huáng in previous years.
At this time, the river inspection minister submitted a drawing,
and a special edict ordered its repair.
Cèwàng Ālābùtǎn sent envoys to pay tribute,
reporting on the murder of envoy Mǎ Dí and secret matters concerning Gá'ěrdān.
They were rewarded with colored silks.
On the day Guǐwèi,
the Emperor presided over a classics colloquium [Jīngyán].
Six departments [tīng] and ten guards [wèi] of Xuānfǔ were reorganized into one prefecture and eight counties.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Láng Tán was appointed Zhāowǔ General [Zhāowǔ Jiāngjūn],
and, along with Ānándá and Shuònài, led troops to Níngxià.
Generals Bójì and Sūn Sīkè participated in military affairs.
On the day Gēngyín,
the Emperor toured Jīdiàn,
inspected the Yuànjiākǒu embankment works in Bàzhōu,
and issued an edict to Provincial Governor Guō Shìlóng to repair them.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
Wèi Jìqí, Provincial Governor of Guìzhōu, memorialized falsely about suppressing local chieftains [tǔsī].
He was stripped of his office and exiled to Hēilóngjiāng.
In the third month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
Imperial Prince Yìnzhī was dispatched to offer sacrifices at Huàshān.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Ráozhōufǔ was moved to Jingdézhèn.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
a Transport Commissioner [Yùnsī] was established in Guǎngdōng, and a Co-Transport Commissioner [Yùntóng] in Cháozhōu.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
an edict stated that Zhào Liángdòng was an old official,
and could temporarily lead the Commander-in-Chief [Zǒngbīng] of Níngxià.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the day Bǐngxū,
Chēlínzhābù, a Khalkha [Kā'ěrkǎ] Taishī, returned from O'luósī (Russia).
He was rewarded with robes,
and granted pasturage at Kèlǔlún.
On the day Guǐsì,
an order was given to inspect ninety-nine items of materials sent from the direct provinces,
and forty items were exempted from being sent.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Xīnyù was appointed Mongol General-in-chief [Ménggǔ Dūtǒng].
In the fifth month, on the day Gēngxū,
Inner Minister Bófēiyánggǔ was appointed Ānběi General [Ānběi Jiāngjūn],
and stationed at Guīhuàchéng.
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐhài,
the quotas for the Bāqí Xiāngshì (Banner District Examinations) and Huìshì (Metropolitan Examinations) were expanded.
In the eighth month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
the land and poll tax for the provinces of Guǎngxī, Sìchuān, Guìzhōu, and Yúnnán for the coming year were remitted.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the Emperor went on a tour beyond the Great Wall for a hunting expedition.
The various tribes of Kē'ěrqìn Mongols came to court at the imperial encampment,
and were bestowed with robes, hats, silver, and silk.
In the ninth month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
the city of Shèngjīng was repaired.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Liúqiú came to present tribute,
and their hostage prince was sent back to his country.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the winter, tenth month, on the *rénshēn* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Censor Péng Péng impeached the examination officials of Shùntiān,
and requested that I personally interrogate them.
This implies that all high-ranking officials are not to be trusted.
To govern the empire, one should prioritize the broader principles.
If I were to personally attend to every matter,
how could the myriad affairs be properly managed?"
On the *rénchén* day,
the Emperor conducted a grand review at Yùquán Shān.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Ōluōsī Cháhàn Hàn came to present tribute.
The Emperor instructed the Grand Secretaries, saying:
"The tribute from foreign vassal states
is indeed a grand affair,
but when it is passed down to later generations,
it may not necessarily avoid causing trouble.
Only when China is peaceful
will external troubles not arise.
Therefore, cultivating the fundamental strength (yuánqì) should be the priority."
In the eleventh month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, visited Xiàozhuāng Shānlíng and Xiàolíng.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
they returned to the palace.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an edict remitted the grain tax for the coming year for the four prefectures of Shùntiān, Héjiān, Bǎodìng, and Yǒngpíng.
In the twelfth month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Yáng Dài, a princely relative of the imperial clan, was appointed Manchu Commander-in-Chief (Měnggǔ Dūtǒng).
On the *dīnghài* day,
the Emperor proceeded to Nányuàn for a hunting expedition.
An edict stated:
"The Manchu officers and soldiers have recently fallen short of their former prowess,
hence in recent years, I have personally conducted reviews
and interspersed them with hunting expeditions.
Recently, I observed that the ranks of the soldiers were orderly,
and their advances and retreats were skilled.
The military instructors concerned are to be rewarded with one month's salary and provisions,
and the supervising officials are to be rewarded with silk
to encourage military discipline."
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the joint ancestral sacrifices were offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple (Tàimiào).
This year,
disaster taxes were remitted to varying degrees for sixty-nine prefectures and counties in the provinces of Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Jiāngxī, Zhèjiāng, Shānxī, Húguǎng, and others.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú presented tribute.
In the thirty-third year, in the spring, first month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
there was a poor harvest in Shèngjīng.
Mǎ Qí was ordered to rush there
to distribute grain from the granaries to the soldiers,
and to transport grain from the Shandong granaries by sea to relieve the people's hunger.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the Director-General of Waterways (Hédào Zǒngdū), Yú Chénglóng, was summoned for an audience.
The Emperor asked:
"You previously said that the water-reducing dams should not be opened, and that Jìn Fǔ wasted money and grain.
How is it now?"
Yú Chénglóng replied:
"I was indeed presumptuous in my previous statement.
What is being done now follows Jìn Fǔ's methods."
The Emperor said:
"If that is the case, and what you said was wrong, and what Jìn Fǔ did was right,
why did you not clearly present this in your memorial,
but instead waited to undermine and entrap him?"
Then, he instructed the Grand Secretaries, saying:
"Yú Chénglóng previously memorialized that Jìn Fǔ had not planted willows along the river dikes.
When I made my southern tour,
I pointed to the willows along the riverbank and asked him,
and he had no words to reply.
He also memorialized that Jìn Fǔ released water to flood the people's fields.
I again visited the area and observed
that it would certainly not flood and damage the wheat fields.
And Wáng Zhì and Dǒng Nà also echoed Yú Chénglóng's words."
The matter was referred to the ministries for deliberation,
and Yú Chénglóng was to be dismissed from office and punished with the cangue.
The Emperor said:
"The projects he is overseeing are not yet complete,
so he should be dismissed from his current post but retained in office."
Wáng Zhì was allowed to retire,
and Dǒng Nà was dismissed from office.
In the second month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
the Emperor attended the imperial lectures (Jīngyán).
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Grand Secretaries requested that the Emperor hold court every three or four days.
The Emperor said:
"Yesterday, I issued an edict allowing officials aged sixty and above to memorialize every other day.
This was merely to show courtesy to elderly officials.
As for myself, how dare I indulge in leisure?
I shall hold court every day as usual."
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Nuòmùtú was appointed Han Banner Commander-in-Chief (Hànjūn Dūtǒng).
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Emperor toured the imperial environs (Jīdiàn).
An imperial order was issued to repair the dikes on both banks from Tōngzhōu to Xīgū.
In the third month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.

Shā Mùhā, Minister of Rites (Lǐbù Shàngshū), was dismissed from office for disrespect in his deliberation on the ritual for the Crown Prince's worship at the Hall for Ancestor Worship (Fèngxiāndiàn Yízhù).
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Hú Rènyú and one hundred sixty-eight others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with varying ranks.
Fàn Chéngxūn was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left (Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ).
In the summer, fourth month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Court of Colonial Affairs (Lǐfānyuàn) reported the census of 226,700 odd people in the forty-nine banners of the outer Mongol tribes.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Zhāmùyáng was appointed General of Hángzhōu.
In the fifth month, on the *wùyín* day,
Kǎiyīnbù, Commander of the Infantry (Bùjūn Tǒnglǐng), memorialized that the newly built road at the Temple of Heaven (Tiāntán) should not allow passersby.
The Emperor said:
"Roads are built for the people.
If they are not allowed to use them,
what is the benefit of building them?
If they are damaged later,
the infantry should be ordered to repair them at any time."
Lǐ Guāngdì, Education Commissioner of Shùntiān (Shùntiān Xuézhèng), mourned the death of his mother,
and was ordered to observe mourning in the capital.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the Hanlin Academy (Hànlín Yuàn), Grand Secretariat (Zhànshì Fǔ), and Imperial Academy (Guózǐ Jiān) were ordered to assign four officials daily to be on duty at the Southern Study (Nánshūfáng).
On the *xīnhài* day,
Jì'ěrtābù was appointed Manchu Commander-in-Chief (Mǎnzhōu Dūtǒng),
and Gá'ěrmǎ was appointed Mongol Commander-in-Chief (Měnggǔ Dūtǒng).
On the *jiǎyín* day,
an edict ordered the compilation of the *Lèihán*.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Emperor toured the imperial environs (Jīdiàn),
inspecting the river dikes.
He instructed the accompanying guards to march in single file,
not to trample the crops.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the Emperor inspected Lóngtánkǒu.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
he inspected Huàjiākǒu, Huángxūkǒu, Bābǎihùkǒu, Wángjiāfǔkǒu, Kuāng'érgǎngkǒu, Báiqūchǎngkǒu,
and ordered that weak sections
be reinforced and repaired.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
he inspected the new dikes at Táohuākǒu, Yǒng'ānkǒu, Lǐjiākǒu, Xìn'àikǒu, Liǔtānkǒu, and other places.
The Emperor said:
"The new dikes appear very sturdy,
and the common people will be spared from flood disasters for several years."
On the *rénxū* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the intercalary fifth month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Emperor examined officials who had entered service through the Hanlin Academy (Hànlín Chūshēn) at Fēngzé Yuán.
In the sixth month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
Xú Zhìdū, Regional Commander of Húguǎng (Húguǎng Tídū), was promoted to General Zhènpíng.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Fàn Chéngxūn was appointed Governor-General of Jiāngnán and Jiāngxī (Jiāngnán Jiāngxī Zǒngdū).
In the autumn, seventh month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
Jiǎng Hóngdào was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left (Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ),
Wáng Shìzhēn was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue of the Left (Hùbù Zuǒ Shìláng),
and Wáng Yǎn was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue of the Right (Hùbù Yòu Shìláng).
Bātú'ěr'é'ěrkèjìnóng memorialized that the surrendered person Qíqíkè had escaped,
and troops were dispatched to pursue and execute him.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the Emperor sought literary ministers.
The Grand Secretaries recommended Xú Qiánxué, Wáng Hóngxù, Gāo Shìqí, as well as Hán Tǎn and Táng Sūnhuá.
The Emperor said:
"Hán Tǎn is not a demoted official;
he should be summoned to fill his original post.
Xú Qiánxué, Wáng Hóngxù, and Gāo Shìqí can be appointed to compile books.
Also summon Xú Bǐngyì."
Another day, Táng Sūnhuá's poetry was tested and found excellent,
and he was appointed Secretary of the Board of Rites (Lǐbù Zhǔshì) and Hanlin Academy Probationer (Hànlín Yuàn Xíngzǒu).
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Fùlātǎ, Governor-General of Jiāngnán and Jiāngxī, died.
He was posthumously granted Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince (Tàizǐ Tàibǎo),
given sacrificial offerings and a burial,
and bestowed the posthumous title Qīngduān.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Emperor toured beyond the Great Wall.
In the eighth month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
the Emperor stopped at Bàibāhā'áng'ā.
Kā'ěrkā Zhébùzūndānbā came to court,
and was bestowed with robes and hats.
In the ninth month, on the *jǐsì* day,
the number of students admitted to schools for the Eight Banners was increased.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Shí Wénbǐng was appointed Han Banner Commander-in-Chief (Hànjūn Dūtǒng),
and Wáng Jìwén was appointed Governor-General of Yúnnán and Guìzhōu (Yúnnán Guìzhōu Zǒngdū).
In the winter, tenth month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
Wú Hè was appointed Governor-General of Sìchuān and Shǎnxī (Sìchuān Shǎnxī Zǒngdū).
On the *yǐsì* day,
Jīn Shìróng was appointed General of Fúzhōu.
In the eleventh month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
Empress Dǒngshàn Wēn Xī Guìfēi (溫僖貴妃) of the Niǔhùlù (鈕祜祿) clan passed away.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Zhāng Wàng (張旺) was appointed Grand Coordinator of Jiāngnán (江南).
On the *wùyín* day,
Chén Tíngjìng (陳廷敬) was reinstated as President of the Board of Revenue.
In the twelfth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
Juéluó Xítèkù (覺羅席特庫) was appointed Manchu General Commandant,
and Dùsīgá'ěr (杜思噶爾) was appointed Mongol General Commandant.
In this year,
the disaster tax exemption varied across twelve prefectures and counties in provinces such as Zhílì (直隸) and Shāndōng (山東).
Cháoxiǎn (朝鮮) presented tribute.
In the thirty-fourth year, *yǐhài*, in the spring, the first month, on the *dīnghài* day,
Hùbā (護巴) was appointed Manchu General Commandant.
In the second month, on the *jǐhài* day,
Guō Shìlóng (郭世隆) was appointed Governor-General of Zhèjiāng (浙江) and Fújiàn (福建).
On the *dīngsì* day,
the construction of the Tàihé Diàn (太和殿) was completed.
Li Zhīfāng (李之芳), the Grand Secretary who had retired, passed away.
Funeral rites and burial were granted,
and he was posthumously granted the epithet Wénxiāng (文襄).
In the third month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
Shí Wényīng (石文英) was appointed Han Bannerman General Commandant.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
there was an earthquake in Píngyáng Fǔ (平陽府).
On the *jiǎchén* day,
envoys were dispatched to enthrone the Bānchán Hútúkètú (班禪胡土克圖).
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
in recognition of Zhào Liángdòng’s (趙良棟) achievements in pacifying Shǔ (蜀) and Diān (滇),
he was granted the hereditary position of a first-class baron.
His subordinate generals received varying promotions and rewards.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Lǐ Huīzǔ (李輝祖) was appointed Governor of Hénán (河南).
In the fifth month, on the first day, *rényín*,
Minister Mǎ Qí (馬齊) was dispatched to inspect the relief efforts for earthquake victims.
Governor Gāshìtú (噶世圖) was dismissed for neglect during the disaster.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
an order was issued for each of the Eight Banners in the capital to build two thousand houses in their respective allocated areas to accommodate soldiers.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the Emperor toured the capital region,
inspecting new embankments and the waterway at the river mouth,
and ordered the construction of a temple for the Sea God.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
he returned to the capital.
In the sixth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
Shí (石) clan, the consort of Crown Prince Yìnréng (胤礽), was ceremonially enfeoffed.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
due to prolonged rain, an imperial edict commanded court officials to present criticisms,
and the Board of Rites performed rites to pray for clear weather.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Wáng Liáng (王樑), the Governor-General of Grain Transport, impeached Wei Qianzong (衞千總) Yáng Fèng (楊奉) for carrying goods on grain transport ships.
The edict stated:
"What harm is it to transport if merchants carry goods?
Wáng Liáng (王樑) searched out the goods and abandoned them on both banks;
his actions were extremely violent,
so he is immediately dismissed from office."
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
Juéluó Shūshù (覺羅舒恕) was appointed General of Níngxià (寧夏),
and Èluóshùn (鄂羅順) was appointed General of Jiāngníng (江寧).
Zhào Liángdòng (趙良棟) requested to go to Jiāngnán (江南) for medical treatment,
and he was granted the old imperial ships from the southern tour.
In the eighth month, on the *rénchén* day,
the Emperor toured beyond the Great Wall.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Bójì (博濟) reported that five hundred Muslims under Gá'ěrdān (噶爾丹) had trespassed into the Sānchàhé (三岔河) patrol area,
and Sùzhōu (肅州) Commander-in-Chief Pān Yùlóng (潘育龍) captured all of them,
detaining them in Sùzhōu (肅州).
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
they reached Kèlèhéluò (克勒和洛).
Imperial Prince Sūnú (蘇努) of the Imperial Clan, General Commandant Āxītán (阿席坦), and Hùbā (護巴) were ordered to lead troops to prepare for Gá'ěrdān (噶爾丹).
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
they reached Kèlèwūlǐyàsūtái (克勒烏理雅蘇台).
Dǒng Ānguó (董安國) was transferred to be Governor-General of River Conservancy,
and Sāng'é (桑額) was appointed Governor-General of Grain Transport.
In the ninth month, on the *xīnsì* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
an imperial edict was issued stating that due to flooding damaging crops in the four prefectures of Shùntiān (順天), Bǎodìng (保定), Héjiān (河間), and Yǒngpíng (永平),
next year's land and poll tax was exempted,
and forty thousand *dàn* of rice were still to be transported there for subsidized sale.
In the winter, the tenth month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
Grand Ministers Sā'étú (索額圖) and Míngzhū (明珠) were ordered to inspect Gá'ěrdān (噶爾丹).
In the eleventh month, on the first day, *jǐwèi*,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *rénxū* day,
the main army was ordered to divide into three routes to prepare for Gá'ěrdān (噶爾丹),
carrying eighty days' worth of provisions,
with the camel, horse, rice, and grain
supervised separately by Vice Minister Chén Rǔqì (陳汝器) and former Left Censor-in-Chief Yú Chénglóng (于成龍).
On the *bǐngyín* day,
this year's autumn executions were suspended.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Lǐ Tiānfù (李天馥) was ordered to resume his position as Grand Secretary.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Emperor conducted a grand review at the Nányuàn (南苑).
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Ānběi General (安北將軍) Bó Fēiyánggǔ (費揚古) was appointed Fǔyuǎn Grand General (撫遠大將軍).
Ministers were dispatched to Mongolia to mobilize troops,
announcing the campaign schedule.
In the twelfth month, on the *jǐhài* day,
Generals Bójì (博濟) and Sūn Sīkè (孫思克) were ordered to march out from Zhènyí (鎮彝).
On the *yǐsì* day,
there was an earthquake in Píngyáng (平陽).
An order was issued to remit this year's grain quota,
and also to exempt outstanding taxes in provinces such as Shānxī (山西), Shǎnxī (陝西), Jiāngnán (江南), Zhèjiāng (浙江), Jiāngxī (江西), Húguǎng (湖廣), Guǎngdōng (廣東), and Fújiàn (福建),
and to pardon those sentenced to death or lesser punishments.
Governors-General and Governors were ordered to report
any government policies inconvenient to the people.
Qí Shì (齊世) was appointed Manchu General Commandant.
In this year,
the disaster tax exemption varied across twelve prefectures and counties in provinces such as Zhílì (直隸), Shānxī (山西), Jiāngxī (江西), Fújiàn (福建), and Guǎngdōng (廣東).
Cháoxiǎn (朝鮮) and Liúqiú (琉球) presented tribute.
In the thirty-fifth year, *bǐngzǐ*, in the spring, the first month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
an imperial edict was issued for the Emperor to personally lead a campaign against Gá'ěrdān (噶爾丹).
Ministers and military officers accompanying the campaign were feasted.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Duke Péngchūn (彭春) was ordered to participate in military affairs of the western route army.
In the second month, on the first day, *dīnghài*,
the Emperor visited the imperial tombs.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *rénchén* day,
Shuònài (碩鼐) was appointed Mongol General Commandant.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
sacrifices were offered to the altars of Heaven and Earth, imperial ancestral temples, and the gods of land and grain.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Crown Prince Yìnréng (胤礽) was ordered to remain and guard the capital.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the Emperor personally led the six armies and set off.
In the third month, on the *wùchén* day,
the Emperor departed from his temporary palace to observe archery.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
they reached Gǔnnnō (滾諾),
where there was heavy rain and snow.
The Emperor stood exposed
until the soldiers finished pitching camp,
then he entered his imperial tent.
After the army had finished cooking,
he then ate his meal.
The tent, provisions, and firewood were left for those arriving later.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the deceased Governor Wáng Wéizhēn (王維珍) was granted funeral rites and burial,
and posthumously granted the epithet Mǐnsuì (敏[⿱⿰売⽎心]).
In the summer, the fourth month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Emperor reached Gédé'ěrkù (格德爾庫).
On the *rénchén* day,
the Emperor stationed at Tǎ'ěrqílā (塔爾奇拉).
An edict stated:
"Now that we have reached the border,
starting from tomorrow,
all will encamp in a circular formation."
