The vanguard reported that Gá'ěrdān (噶爾丹) was at Kèlúlán (克魯倫),
and the Mongol troops were ordered to advance and occupy the river.
On the *bǐngchén* day of the fifth month, the new moon,
the Emperor halted his imperial carriage at Tuōlíng Bùlākè.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
he reached Kūkùchē'ěr.
On the *rénxū* day,
having ascertained Gá'ěrdān's location,
the Emperor led the vanguard and set off first,
while all the armies advanced with two wings extended.
They encamped at Yàntúkùliètú.
The area was normally short of water,
but then mountain springs gushed forth,
which the Emperor personally inspected.
On the *guǐhài* day,
they reached the Kèlǔlún Hé.
The Emperor turned to his ministers and said:
"Gá'ěrdān does not know to take advantage of the river to resist battle;
he is incapable of achieving anything."
The vanguard's *zhōngshū* Ābìdá reported that Gá'ěrdān did not believe that the grand army had arrived suddenly.
He ascended Mount Mèngnà'ěr,
and seeing the yellow tents arranged like a city,
the vast army like clouds gathered,
boundless and without end,
he exclaimed in great surprise:
"How did they arrive so easily!"
He abandoned his yurts and fled that night.
Examining his horse droppings,
it seemed he had fled two days prior.
The Emperor led light cavalry in pursuit.
Along the way, many articles, camels, horses, women, and children were abandoned.
The Emperor turned to Kē'ěrqìn Wáng Shājīn and said:
"Why is the bandit so flustered?"
Shājīn replied:
"It is to escape with his life."
Kā'ěrkā Wáng Nàmùzhā'ěr said:
"When your servants fled during that time of trouble,
it was just like this."
The Emperor wrote a letter to the Huáng Tàihòu,
fully detailing the military situation,
and also setting a date for his return to the capital.
He pursued as far as Tuōnà'ālín and then returned,
ordering the Nèi Dàchén Mǎsīkā to continue the pursuit.
On the *wùchén* day,
the Emperor's army returned.
That morning,
five-colored clouds appeared.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
they reached Zhōng Tuōlíng.
The Fǔyuǎn Dàjiāngjūn Bó Fèiyánggǔ decisively defeated Gá'ěrdān at Zhāomòduō,
beheading three thousand enemies,
and slaying his wife Ānú in battle.
Gá'ěrdān fled with a few horsemen.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
they reached Cháhànnuò'ěr.
He summoned the various Mongolian kings,
and praised them for their efforts in repairing roads, digging wells, and supervising pastures,
bestowing silver upon each person.
On the *guǐsì* day of the sixth month,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In this campaign,
the central army, personally commanded by the Emperor, drove off Gá'ěrdān;
the western army, under Fèiyánggǔ, decisively defeated Gá'ěrdān;
only the eastern army, under Sàbùsù, due to the long distance, arrived late and achieved no merit.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Kā'ěrkā Jùnwáng Shànbā was rewarded for loaning all his horses to the army;
he was promoted to Qīnwáng.
Bèizi Pénchǔkè, who rendered meritorious service in enemy reconnaissance,
was enfeoffed as a Jùnwáng.
All the ministers performed the congratulatory ceremony.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Cháhā'ěr imperial guards were granted an additional *yueshǎng* of one gold coin,
and the Kā'ěrkā people six gold coins,
to be given for three years.
An edict was issued to suspend this year's autumn assizes.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Wú Diàn was appointed Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ,
Zhāng Wàng was transferred to be Fújiàn Shuǐshī Tídū,
and Zhāng Yúnyì to be Jiāngnán Tídū.
In autumn, on the *wùwǔ* day of the seventh month,
a stele commemorating the pacification of Shuòmò was erected at the Tàixué.
Lǐ Huīzǔ was appointed Húguǎng Zǒngdū.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the quotas for the provincial examinations in Guǎngzhíshěng were expanded.
On the *wùchén* day,
Wú Yīng was reassigned as Fújiàn Lùlù Tídū,
and Yuè Shēnglóng as Sìchuān Tídū.
In the eighth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
Suǒnuòhé was dismissed for lack of military supplies,
and Kǎiyīnbù was appointed Bīngbù Shàngshū.
On the *jiǎyín* day of the ninth month, the new moon,
the king of the Huíhuí kingdom, Ābùdūlǐshíkè, reported:
"Your servant, relying on celestial might,
was able to surrender.
I ask to be sent back to my country, Yè'ěrqīn,
and request an imperial decree to instruct Cèwàng Ālābùtǎn not to inflict harm."
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
officials, ranks, clothing, and provisions were bestowed upon the surrendered Èlǔtè people.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the Emperor made an inspection tour beyond the passes.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
he reached Shāchéng.
An edict stated:
"In recent years, Xuānhuà Prefecture,
which is responsible for pasturing army horses and providing numerous supplies,
has greatly burdened the people's strength.
Therefore, all its fixed taxes for the coming year shall be remitted."
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Deputy Commandant Zǔ Liángbì defeated Dānjìlā, a subordinate of Gá'ěrdān, at Wēngjīn.
In winter, on the *jiǎshēn* day of the tenth month, the new moon,
officials were dispatched to deliver clothing, furs, cattle, and sheep to the soldiers of the western army.
On the *dīnghài* day,
they reached Zhāohā.
Silver was bestowed upon the fallen soldiers of the Yòuwèi and Dàtóng.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Dàjiāngjūn Fèiyánggǔ presented his captives.
Silver was given for their redemption,
allowing them to reunite with their families.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the Emperor personally inspected the soldiers of the Yòuwèi,
and bestowed food upon them.
He issued a decree saying:
"In the battle of Zhāomòduō,
you, lacking provisions, marched on foot yet were able to repel the enemy.
Therefore, this food is specially bestowed upon you.
All outstanding loans from the imperial treasury are remitted.
The wounded and sick shall receive separate grants."
All prostrated themselves, expressing joyful gratitude.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Emperor halted his imperial carriage at Lìsū.
He wrote a letter to the Huáng Tàihòu,
thanking her for the gift of fur clothing.
In the eleventh month, on the *wùyín* day,
Gá'ěrdān sent an envoy to request surrender.
His envoy, Géléigūyīng, arrived,
apparently to subtly ascertain the Emperor's intention.
The Emperor told him:
"I will wait for you for seventy days;
after this, I will advance the army."
On the *gēngchén* day,
the imperial procession returned.
In the twelfth month, on the *rényín* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
Zōngshì Fèiyánggù was appointed Yòuwèi Jiāngjūn,
Qíbù as Mǎnzhōu Dūlǐng,
and Léi Jìzūn as Hànjūn Dūlǐng.
On the *gēngxū* day,
an edict stated:
"The prefectures, counties, and garrisons along the borders of Shǎnxī and Gānsù,
which lie on the main routes for army movements,
have had numerous provisions demanded of them,
causing hardship to the common people.
Therefore, their land and poll taxes for the coming year shall all be remitted."
In this year,
disaster taxes for thirty-two prefectures and counties in provinces like Jiāngnán and Jiāngxī were remitted to varying degrees.
Cháoxiǎn paid tribute.
In the thirty-sixth year, *dīngchǒu*, in spring, on the *bǐngchén* day of the first month,
the Emperor visited Nányuàn for a hunt.
On the *wùchén* day,
the Huíbù of Hāmì captured Gá'ěrdān's son, Sàibǔténgbā'ěrzhū'ěr, and presented him.
On the *jǐsì* day,
an official was sent to inquire about the well-being of Yǒnglüè Jiāngjūn Zhào Liángdòng,
bestowing ginseng and deer tails upon him.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
an edict stated:
"I have observed in the *Míng Shǐ*
that throughout that dynasty, there was no empress dowager who interfered in governance
and acted as a minister overpowering her sovereign.
In our dynasty's precedents,
many have followed this.
I do not, like previous people, casually ridicule a fallen state.
Now that the *Míng Shǐ* is being compiled,
let this edict be added to the imperial decrees."
In the second month, on the *dīnghài* day,
the Emperor personally led a campaign against Gá'ěrdān,
and the imperial carriage set forth.
On this day,
they reached Chāngpíng.
Ābìdá reported that Hāmì had captured Tǔkèqíhāshíhā, an Èlǔtè person,
who was the principal offender in harming the envoy Mǎdí.
He ordered his execution,
and his children to be given as slaves to Mǎdí's family.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Emperor halted at Dàtóng.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
they reached Lǐjiāgōu.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an edict remitted the fixed taxes for this year in the prefectures and counties of Kělán, Bǎodé, and Héqu,
which the army passed through.
On this day,
they reached Niǎnyān Cūn,
where mountain springs gushed forth from below,
providing ample water for men and horses.
On the *gēngxū* day,
an official was sent to offer sacrifices to the Spirit of the Huáng Hé.
In the third month, on the day Bǐngchén,
the Emperor's retinue stopped at Qūyě Hé.
The Ölöts Duōěrjì and Dálāshí, among others, successively came to surrender.
He bestowed gold, silks, robes, and hats upon the Uyghur King of Hāmì.
On the day Dīngsì,
Zhào Liángdòng passed away.
When the Emperor heard of it,
he sighed and grieved for a long time,
saying to his close officials:
"Zhào Liángdòng
was a great man!"
On the day Xīnyǒu,
he reached Yúlín.
On the day Wùchén,
he reached Ānbiān Chéng.
The General of Níngxià, Wáng Huàxíng, requested the Emperor to hunt at Huāmǎ Chí.
The Emperor said:
"How about resting the horses' strength to hunt Gáěrdān instead?"
On the day Xīnwèi,
he reached Huāmǎ Chí.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
the Emperor crossed the river from Héngchéng.
He dispatched the eldest prince, Yìnzhī, to offer sacrifices to Zhào Liángdòng and the former Provincial Commander Chén Fú.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the Emperor's retinue stopped at Níngxià.
He provided relief to the officers and soldiers who died in battle at Zhāomòduō and Wēngjīn.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
he offered sacrifices to Hèlán Shān.
On the day Gēngchén,
the Emperor reviewed the troops.
He ordered his imperial guards to distribute imperial food to the warriors.
In the intercalary third month, on the first day Xīnsì,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Gēngyín,
Kāng Qīnwáng Jiéshū passed away.
Upon hearing that the Emperor was about to depart,
the common people of Níngxià earnestly begged him to stay for a few more days.
The Emperor said:
"The borderlands are barren and desolate;
staying one more day
would mean one more day of disturbance.
Your sincerity
is already known."
In summer, fourth month, on the day Xīnhài,
the Emperor reached Lángjūxū Shān.
On the day Jiǎyín,
he returned to the capital.
On the day Gēngshēn,
he ordered the directly-administered provinces to select scholars of both excellent character and conduct to be 'bágòngshēng' (tribute students),
and send them to the Guózǐjiān (Imperial Academy).
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Fèi Yánggǔ reported by memorial that on the thirteenth day of the intercalary third month, Gáěrdān had died by taking poison,
and his daughter Zhōngqíhǎi, leading three hundred households, had come to surrender.
The Emperor, with all his officials, performed the ceremony of 'bàitiān' (worshipping Heaven).
He issued an edict for all armies to return to their garrisons.
On that day,
there was heavy rain.
The surrendered Ölöts requested a celebration.
He stopped them.
Prior to this,
the Emperor was going to inspect the Yellow River in Níngxià.
He traveled by boat from Héngchéng,
reaching Hútān Héshuò.
He disembarked and walked,
leading his imperial guards on a hunt,
catching fish and shooting wild ducks for food,
and met his chariots and cavalry at Bāotóu Zhèn.
In the fifth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Fù Lātǎ was appointed Minister of Justice (Xíngbù Shàngshū),
Xíěrdá as Censors-in-Chief (Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ);
Wēng Shūyuán was dismissed;
Wú Diān was appointed Minister of Justice (Xíngbù Shàngshū),
Zhāng Pénghé as Censors-in-Chief (Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ).
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Ministry of Rites requested to confer an honorific title upon the Emperor.
This was not permitted.
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
the Ministry of Rites requested to inscribe a record of achievements on famous mountains along the route of the army.
This was granted.
A sacrificial burial was granted to the late Brave and Resourceful General, First-Class Viscount Zhào Liángdòng,
and he was posthumously given the title Xiāngzhōng.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Guǐwèi,
the ministers requested to confer an honorific title on the Empress Dowager.
They requested three times,
but it was not granted.
On the day Yǐwèi,
as the northern deserts were pacified,
officials were dispatched to offer sacrifices at the suburban altars, ancestral temples, imperial tombs, and to the former teachers.
Lǐ Pán and one hundred and fifty others were granted the status of 'jìnshì jí dì' (successful candidates in the highest imperial examination) with varying ranks.
Grand General of the First Class, Earl Fèi Yánggǔ, was promoted to First-Class Duke;
all below the rank of counselor were granted hereditary posts.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the flag soldiers' loan debts were remitted.
On the day Yǐsì,
officials were dispatched to grant rewards to the troops of the forty-nine Outer Mongol banners.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Emperor toured beyond the Great Wall.
In the eighth month, on the day Yǐhài,
the Emperor stayed at Bātúshèlǐ,
bestowing silver and silks upon the Mongolian kings, princes, and taijis.
In the ninth month, on the day Guǐwèi,
the Ölöt Dānjílā returned and submitted.
The Emperor received him alone in a felt tent.
When Dānjílā emerged, he said to others:
"I am a sinner,
yet the Emperor did not doubt me.
He is truly a divine man."
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Commandant Kǎiyīnbù was concurrently appointed Commander of the Infantry.
On the day Rényín,
the Emperor attended the imperial lecture (Jīngyán).
On the day Yǐsì,
General Zhèn Píng and Provincial Commander of Húguǎng, Xú Zhìdū, passed away.
He was posthumously granted the title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent,
and a sacrificial burial was granted,
with the posthumous title Xiāngyì.
Relief was provided to residents of Hēilóng Jiāng affected by floods.
Xíěrdá was appointed Minister of War (Bīngbù Shàngshū),
and Hāyǎěr as Censors-in-Chief (Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ).
In winter, tenth month, on the day Jǐsì,
it was first ordered that imperial clan members could sit for the provincial and metropolitan examinations.
On the day Réngxū,
an imperial edict stated:
"In recent years, military campaigns have repeatedly passed through
the territory of Shānxī,
which has borne the burden of providing provisions and lodging.
Therefore, Shānxī's regular tax for next year is remitted."
Zhènhuógōng Sūnú, who participated in the campaign, was promoted to Bèizǐ.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the Emperor visited the imperial tombs.
On the day Jiǎxū,
eunuch Liú Jìncháo was sentenced to death for extortion.
In the eleventh month, on the day Xīnsì,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Princess Héshuò Kèjìng was married to the Khalkha Prince Dūnduōbùduōěrjì.
On the day Wùxū,
Joseon requested to purchase grain;
it was ordered that thirty thousand piculs of rice be transported for relief.
On the day Jiǎchén,
an edict ordered that reports of disasters from directly-administered provinces should be immediately investigated and reported.
In the twelfth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
the imperial clan member Dǒng'é was changed to Manchu Commandant.
On the day Yǐhài,
the grand sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In this year,
disaster taxes for fifty-nine prefectures and counties in Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Ānhuī, Jiāngxī, and other provinces were remitted with varying degrees.
Joseon, Ryukyu, and Annan presented tribute.
In the thirty-seventh year, Wùyín, spring, first month, on the day Gēngyín,
Cèwàng Ālābùtán memorialized about the death of the Dalai Lama, hidden by the Desi (Dìbā),
repudiating the Panchen Lama and exalting himself,
earnestly requesting imperial judgment.
The Emperor replied:
"I have already issued an edict rebuking the Desi to truthfully report and confess his guilt.
If he stubbornly refuses to repent,
I will not easily pardon him."
He also dispatched Academician of the Hanlin Academy, Yīdào, and others with an edict.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Emperor toured Wǔtái Shān.
On the day Jiǎchén,
he reached Zhuōzhōu.
He ordered the eldest prince, Yìnzhī, and Grand Secretary Yīsāng'ā to offer sacrifices at the tombs of Emperor Tàizǔ and Shìzōng of Jīn.
In the second month, on the day Xīnhài,
an edict remitted Shānxī's outstanding taxes for the thirty-sixth year.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Emperor's retinue stopped at Púsà Dǐng.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
officials were dispatched to provide disaster relief in Shāndōng.
On the day Wùchén,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the third month, on the first day Bǐngzǐ,
the Emperor attended the imperial lecture (Jīngyán).
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the eldest prince, Yìnzhī, was enfeoffed as Zhí Jùnwáng;
the third prince, Yìnzhǐ, as Chéng Jùnwáng;
the fourth prince, Yìnzhēn; the fifth prince, Yìnqí; the seventh prince, Yìnyòu; and the eighth prince, Yìnsì, were all enfeoffed as Bèilè.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the distillation of liquor was prohibited.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the Governor of Zhílì, Yú Chénglóng, memorialized that he, together with the Westerner Ānduō and others, had surveyed the Húnhé River,
assisted in dredging and deepening it,
and presented a map.
An imperial decree was received:
"The work is to be completed by the sixth month."
In summer, fourth month, on the day Guǐhài,
the customs duties in Guǎngdōng were reduced.
On the day Jǐsì,
an edict stated that Wēn Jùnwáng Yánshòu's conduct was improper,
and he was demoted to Bèilè;
Bèizǐ Yuánduān was stripped of his title.
On the day Réngshēn,
Bèizǐ Sūnú was put in charge of the General of Shèngjīng.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the Emperor inspected the Grand Canal (Cáohé).
In the fifth month, on the day of Jiǎxū,
the people of Wǔqīng requested to build an outer dike.
The Emperor said:
"Building an outer dike might damage people's fields."
The people said:
"The harm from the river bursting its banks
is even worse than damaging fields."
The Emperor said:
"As floods are about to descend,
temporarily erect wooden piles to protect the dike,
and dig a small river to drain the water.
I will have it completed for you before the spring rains next year."
On the day of Guǐwèi,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day of Rénshēn,
the Shànglínyuàn was abolished.
Lǐ Línshèng was appointed Tídū of Shǎnxī,
and Zhāng Wàng was appointed Tídū of Guǎngxī.
That month,
Cèwàng Ālābùtǎn reported on engaging in war with the Hāsàkè,
and the reasons for detaining Dānjīn Èmùbù.
It was ordered to show this to the Yìzhèng Dàchén.
In the sixth month, on the day of Xīnhài,
Wú Yīng was transferred to be Fújiàn Shuǐshī Tídū.
On the day of Dīngsì,
the Liángwànyíng in Sìchuān was renamed Huàlínyíng,
and officials from Cānjīang downwards were appointed.
On the day of Jǐwèi,
Shí Wénchéng, the Xúnfǔ of Yúnnán, memorialized that those of the Sānfān adherents who were granted immunity from pursuit by imperial decree
should be permitted to reclaim land and take examinations.
This was approved.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day of Guǐyǒu,
Zhāng Yùshū left office due to his mother's death.
Wú Diān was appointed Dàxuéshì,
and Wáng Shìzhēn was appointed Zuǒ Dūyùshǐ.
On the day of Xīnmǎo,
the Lìbù was ordered to select Tóng, Tōng, Zhōu, and Xiàn officials monthly for imperial audience.
On the day of Guǐsì,
the new river at Bàzhōu was completed,
and named Yǒngdìng Hé.
A temple to the River God was built.
On the day of Jǐhài,
Lú Chóngyào was appointed Guǎngzhōu Jiāngjūn,
and Yīn Huàxíng was appointed Guǎngdōng Tídū.
On the day of Gēngzǐ,
Sūěrfā was appointed Mǎnzhōu Dūtǒng.
On the day of Xīnchǒu,
the Emperor escorted the Empress Dowager on an eastern tour,
taking the route beyond the Great Wall.
In the eighth month, on the day of Guǐchǒu,
the Emperor escorted the Empress Dowager to the residence of Kālāqìn Duānjìng Gōngzhǔ,
and bestowed gold and silk upon her and her Èfù Gáěrzàng.
On the day of Jiǎzǐ,
the Empress Dowager offered a distant sacrifice to her parents at Fākù Shān.
On the day of Jǐsì,
Duānmǐn Gōngzhǔ and her Èfù Dárhàn Qīnwáng Bāndì were bestowed gold and silk.
The mountain bandit Huáng Míng from Húnán attacked Jìngzhōu,
and Chén Dānshū attacked Chálíngzhōu.
The government troops suppressed them.
In the ninth month, on the day of Rénshēn,
the Emperor arrived at Kèěrsū,
and personally offered wine before the tomb of the late Qīnwáng Mǎnzhūxíyǐ of Kēěrqìn,
who was the father of Xiàozhuāng Huánghòu.
On the day of Guǐsì,
the Emperor stationed at Xīng'ā.
Sàbùsù, the Hēilóngjiāng Jiāngjūn, and others were bestowed gold, silk, official robes, and hats.
On the day of Gēngzǐ,
the execution of prisoners in Shèngjīng and Wūlā was suspended for this year.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day of Guǐmǎo,
the Emperor went hunting,
and shot dead two tigers.
One of them,
he shot across a ravine,
piercing its flank.
On the day of Dīngwèi,
the Emperor went hunting,
and shot dead two bears with a gun.
On that day,
he made a temporary imperial residence at Huīfā.
On the day of Jǐyǒu,
Yǒngníng Fǔ in Yúnnán was abolished,
and Yǒngběi Fǔ was established.
On the day of Guǐsì,
the Emperor made a temporary imperial residence at Xīngjīng.
On the day of Jiǎyín,
the Emperor visited Yǒnglíng.
An official was dispatched to offer sacrifice at the tomb of Wǔgōng Jùnwáng Lǐdūn.
The Shuǐxī Tǔsī in Guìzhōu was reformed,
and Dàdìng, Píngyuǎn, and Qiánxī Sānliúguān were established.
On the day of Dīngsì,
the Emperor visited Fúlíng and Zhāolíng,
and personally offered sacrifice at the tombs of Wǔxūn Wáng Yánggǔlì, Zhíyì Gōng Fèiyīngdōng, and Hóngyì Gōng Èyìdōu.
Taxes on rice and beans in Fèngtiān were exempted for this year.
On the day of Rénxū,
the Emperor escorted the Empress Dowager back to the capital.
In the eleventh month, on the day of Guǐwèi,
the Emperor escorted the Empress Dowager back to the palace.
On the day of Bǐngxū,
an imperial edict stated:
"During My inspection tour,
the pastures of the various Mongol tribes of Áohàn, Nàimàn, Ālùkēěrqìn, and Zhālǔtè were excellent,
yet their livelihoods were difficult,
due to livestock theft,
preventing night grazing.
I have immediately dispatched Lángzhōng Lǐ Xuéshèng and others to manage this,
and the theft has significantly reduced.
Other Mongol areas should also have similar dispatches.
Banner officials who wish to go to Mongolia to teach
are permitted to do so.
The various cases of theft
shall be heard and decided jointly."
On the day of Gēngyín,
Zhāng Pénghè was appointed Jiāngnán Jiāngxī Zǒngdū.
In the twelfth month, on the first day of Xīnchǒu,
Xú Tíngxǐ was ordered to assist in river management,
and Shàngshū Mǎ Qí,
together with Shìláng Yù Chénglóng and Cháng Shòu, were ordered to inspect the river works.
On the day of Gēngxū,
the Zōngrén Fǔ was instructed:
"For idle imperial clansmen
who are capable and resourceful,
skilled in horsemanship and archery,
as well as those who are poor and without a livelihood,
investigate thoroughly and report."
An edict stated that wives and daughters of officials and commoners involved in incidents
should not be detained for interrogation,
and this was established as a regulation.
The Dōngchuān Tǔsī in Sìchuān was reformed into Dōngchuān Fǔ,
and officials from Zhīfǔ downwards were appointed.
On the day of Wùwǔ,
an edict ordered the Eight Banners to investigate filial sons and chaste women.
On the day of Jǐwèi,
Bāxī was appointed Yúnnán Guìzhōu Zǒngdū,
and Mǎ Zìdé was appointed Jīngkǒu Jiāngjūn.
On the day of Jǐsì,
a grand sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
This year,
disaster relief taxes were exempted for thirty-five prefectures and counties in Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Fújiàn, Zhèjiāng, Húguǎng, and other provinces, with varying amounts.
Cháoxiǎn offered tribute.
In the thirty-eighth year, on the day of Jǐmǎo, in spring, the first month, on the day of Xīnmǎo,
an edict stated:
"I will embark on a southern tour to inspect river works.
All supplies
shall be prepared by the capital.
Officials shall be strictly instructed in advance
not to burden the common people."
In the second month, on the day of Rényín,
Zhānshì Yǐn Tài was dismissed from office due to incompetence.
On the day of Guǐmǎo,
the Emperor, escorting the Empress Dowager, set off on the southern tour.
On the day of Wùshēn,
Tiānjīn Zǒngbīng Pān Yùlóng was bestowed imperial robes and sable fur for his effective training.
In the third month, on the day of Gēngwǔ,
the Emperor arrived at Qīngkǒu,
and escorted the Empress Dowager across the river.
On the day of Xīnwèi,
the Emperor boarded a small boat
and personally inspected the works at Gāojiāyàn, Guīrén Dī, Lànníqiǎn, and other places.
One hundred thousand dàn of grain transported by canal were intercepted
and distributed for fair-price sale in Gāoyóu, Bǎoyìng, and twelve other prefectures and counties.
On the day of Réngzǐ,
the Emperor inspected the Yellow River dikes.
On the day of Bǐngzǐ,
the imperial carriage was stationed at Yángzhōu.
The accompanying soldiers were instructed not to trample wheat crops.
On the day of Rénwǔ,
an edict exempted outstanding taxes in Shāndōng and Hénán,
and granted a partial pardon to those sentenced to death or lesser punishments.
On the day of Guǐwèi,
the imperial carriage arrived at Sūzhōu.
On the day of Xīnmǎo,
the imperial carriage was stationed at Hángzhōu.
On the day of Bǐngshēn,
the Emperor reviewed troops and conducted shooting drills.
On the day of Wùxū,
the Emperor escorted the Empress Dowager back to the capital.
In summer, the fourth month, on the first day of Gēngzǐ,
the return journey reached Sūzhōu.
An edict exempted the additional silver amounts on salt taxes and customs duties,
and specifically increased the student quotas for the two provinces of Jiāngnán and Zhèjiāng.
On the day of Yǐsì,
Dāndài was appointed Hángzhōu Jiāngjūn.
On the day of Jǐyǒu,
the imperial carriage arrived at Jiāngníng.
The Emperor reviewed troops.
On the day of Gēngshēn,
it arrived at Yángzhōu.
On the day of Xīnyǒu,
Péng Péng was appointed Guǎngxī Xúnfǔ.
On the day of Bǐngyín,
after crossing the Yellow River,
the Emperor boarded a small boat
and inspected the new embankments.
In the fifth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
he arrived at Cìzhòngjiāzhá.
He wrote
the plaque "Sage's Gate of Wisdom"
and
hung it at the temple of the late worthy, Zǐlù.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the Emperor returned to the palace after attending to the Empress Dowager.
On the day Dīnghài,
Mǎ'ěrhàn was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left,
and Wáng Hóngxù was appointed Minister of Works.
In the sixth month, on the first day, Wùxū,
Guō Xiù was recalled to serve as Governor-General of Húguǎng,
and Zhèn Guógōng Yīngqí was appointed Tūtǒng of the Mongols.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
the river breached its banks in Huái and Yáng.
In the intercalary seventh month, on the day Wùxū,
Consort Mǐn, of the Zhāngjiā clan, passed away.
Chéng Jùnwáng Yìnzhǐ, who was her son,
had his hair shaved before one hundred days had passed,
and was demoted to Bèilè.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
previously,
the Miao bandit Huáng Míng had been repeatedly reported as captured or dead,
yet still reported as committing offenses.
At this time,
officials were dispatched to investigate and try the case,
and he and his associates, Chén Dānshū, Wú Sīxiān, and over thirty others, were executed.
The governors and governors-general, such as Málèjí, who submitted false reports, were demoted or dismissed with varying degrees of punishment.
The Emperor went on an inspection tour beyond the frontier.
In the ninth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Bǐngchén,
the Emperor presided over the Imperial Lectures.
Yáng Dài was transferred to be Tūtǒng of the Manchus,
and Lǔ Bóhè, Tuōlún, and Chónggǔlǐ were all appointed Tūtǒng of the Mongols.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Grand Secretary Ālántài passed away.
The Emperor mourned and cherished him,
sent his eldest son, Yìnzhī, to visit him during his illness,
bestowed offerings and additional sacrifices,
and posthumously granted him the title Wénqīng.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
the Emperor inspected the Yongding River works.
On the day Gēngchén,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
Grand Secretary Lǐ Tiānfù passed away,
and was granted sacrifices and burial,
and posthumously granted the title Wéndìng.
In the eleventh month, on the day Yǐsì,
the Emperor visited the imperial tombs.
On the day Rénchén,
Mǎqí, Fólún, Xióng Cìlǚ, and Zhāng Yīng were appointed Grand Secretaries;
Chén Tíngjìng was appointed Minister of Personnel;
Lǐ Zhènyù was appointed Minister of Revenue;
Dù Zhēn was appointed Minister of Rites;
Mǎ'ěrhàn and Fàn Chéngxūn were appointed Ministers of War;
and Wáng Shìzhēn was appointed Minister of Punishments.
On the day Rényín,
four Manchu and four Han investigating censors were ordered to attend court.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Baoyuán Bureau was ordered to purchase discarded coins.
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùchén,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Guǐsì,
joint sacrifices were offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In this year,

disaster relief exemptions for taxes and levies were granted to seventy-three prefectures and counties in the provinces of Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Jiāngxī, Zhèjiāng, Fújiàn, Shǎnxī, and Húguǎng, with varying degrees of relief.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú presented tribute.
In the thirty-ninth year, Gēngchén, in spring, the first month, on the day Jǐwèi,
King Lǐ Tūn of Cháoxiǎn offered local products for the return of refugees,
and the Emperor sent them back.
On the day Guǐhài,
the Emperor inspected the Yongding River works.
In the second month, on the day Jiǎxū,
the Emperor traveled by boat to inspect the waterways of Lángchéng and Liǔchà.
As the water was shallow,
he changed to a smaller boat and proceeded,
giving instructions on the strategy for river repair.
On the day Réngwǔ,
he returned to the capital.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Grand Ministers Fèiyánggǔ and Yīsāng'ā were ordered to test the equestrian and archery skills of imperial clan members' children.
In the third month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Emperor presided over the Imperial Lectures.
The Ministry of Personnel reported on the case of the Anhuī Provincial Governor Lǐ Bǐng, who had been impeached,
and requested that it be handed over to the general and admiral for investigation.
The Emperor said:
"Generals and admirals are not involved in civilian affairs.
The Ministry's deliberation is inappropriate."
He severely reprimanded them.
Minister Kùlènà was subsequently dismissed.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Zhāng Pénghé was appointed Director-General of River Conservancy.
Pénghé requested the removal of assistant officials and temporary personnel,
and the ministerial officials relaxed the regulations,
to ensure success.
This was granted.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Imperial Clan member Tèkèxīn was appointed Tūtǒng of the Mongols.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Wāng Yì and three hundred and one others were granted the Jinshi degree with varying ranks.
Sìchuān Provincial Governor Yú Yǎngzhì and Admiral Yuè Shēnglóng mutually impeached each other,
and officials were dispatched to investigate.
Both were stripped of their positions.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Gēngchén,
the Emperor inspected the Yongding River.
Eight Banner soldiers were ordered to assist in opening the river,
led by Zhí Jùnwáng Yìnzhī,
with Xī Jùnwáng Yuèxī and five others accompanying him.
On the day Réngwǔ,
the Emperor inspected the Zǐyá River.
On the day Rénchén,
he returned to the capital.
In the fifth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
Āshān was appointed Governor-General of Jiāngnán and Jiāngxī.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Ālíng'ā was appointed Tūtǒng of the Mongols.
In the sixth month, on the day Guǐhài,
Zhāng Pénghé reported the completion of the dredging of the river mouth,
and the river flowed smoothly.
The Lánhuáng Dam was renamed Dàtōngkǒu,
and a Temple of the Sea God was built.
Dù Zhēn was dismissed,
Wáng Zéhóng was appointed Minister of Rites,
and Lǐ Nán was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the day Dīnghài,
the imperial examinations for imperial clan members were suspended.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Court of Colonial Affairs deliberated and replied that there was no need to discuss the lama Shāngnánduō'ěrzhǐ's memorial concerning Cèwàng Ālābùtǎn's dispatch of troops to Qīnghǎi.
There was no need to discuss it.
The Emperor said:
"This matter seems very minor at present,
but in the future, it will have great significance.
The said ministry proposes no discussion;
if Qīnghǎi were to ask Shāngnánduō'ěrzhǐ,
how would he respond?
Cèwàng Ālābùtǎn is cunning,
and has always acted wickedly.
All the neighboring tribes
are his enemies.
His claim of going to conquer Dìbā,
with its long and dangerous route,
might be a mere show of force to intimidate Qīnghǎi,
which is unknown.
It is essential to ensure that they dare not instigate conflict."
On the day Yǐsì,
it was stipulated that Hanlin officials, including compilers, revisers, and probationary bachelors, would receive a monthly stipend of three taels of silver.
When a position of Education Intendant became vacant,
officials would be selected based on their salary ranks.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the late General Zhènwǔ, Sūn Sīkè, passed away.
The Emperor ordered his eldest son, Yìnzhī, to pour libations,
bestowed two saddled horses,
one thousand taels of silver,
and posthumously granted him the title Xiāngwǔ.
On the day Dīngsì,
the Emperor went on an inspection tour beyond the frontier.
Lǐ Guāngdì, Zhāng Pénghé, Guō Xiù, and Péng Péng were ordered to deliberate in detail on matters concerning the examination halls.
In the eighth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
the Emperor arrived at Qíláotú.
In the ninth month, on the day Guǐsì,
this year's autumn executions were suspended.
An edict ordered Zhāng Pénghé to solely manage river works,
and Fàn Chéngxūn and nine others were recalled.
Investigating Censor Mùhélún requested a ban on luxurious attire,
and the Grand Secretaries drafted a response of reprimand.
The Emperor said:
"The role of censorial officials is to be the eyes and ears;
if they are punished for their words,
who will speak again?
However, his statement that luxury was prevalent after the tenth year of Kāngxī is incorrect;
it was only during the time of the auxiliary ministers.
Now it has subsided somewhat."
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
on the Empress Dowager's sixtieth birthday,
the Emperor composed the "Ode of Boundless Longevity,"
and personally wrote it on a folding screen as a presentation.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the Emperor inspected the Yongding River.
On the day Wùyín,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
it was ordered that officials selected for censorial posts this year who had not yet been appointed
should serve as supernumerary censors,
participating in deliberations with the regular court.
In the eleventh month, on the day Gēngyín,
Qīnghǎi's È'ěrbùtú Hātān Bātú'ěr was ordered to relocate to Níngxià.
An edict ordered Vice Minister Wēndá to inspect the post stations in Shǎn and Gān.
Wáng Zéhóng was dismissed,
and Hán Tǎn was appointed Minister of Rites.
It was ordered that the children of high ministers and officials of integrity who took the examinations
be categorized as "official candidates,"
with a limited quota for selection.
On the day Xīnhài,
the Emperor went on an inspection tour beyond the frontier.
Distinguished officials, like those selected by imperial decree, were ordered to be granted an audience.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the local tribes of Dǎjiànlú in Sìchuān rebelled,
and Vice Minister Mǎnpī was dispatched with Admiral Táng Xīshùn to suppress them.
On the *jǐwèi* day of the twelfth month, which was the first day of the month,
the Emperor halted his imperial equipage at Nuǎnquán.
He bestowed white gold upon outer vassal kings down to officers and soldiers.
On the *wùchén* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Xiāo Yǒngzǎo was transferred to be the Governor of Guǎngxī,
and Péng Péng was appointed Governor of Guǎngdōng.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the late Prince Ānqīn, Yuèlè, was found to have made an error in the previous trial concerning Bèilè Nuóní's case.
His title was posthumously reduced to Jùnwáng.
His son, Prince Xī Jùnwáng Yuèxī, and Bèizi Wú'ěrzhàn were both demoted to Zhènguógōng.
On the *dīnghài* day,
a grand sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted in varying degrees for fifty-seven prefectures and counties in the provinces of Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Ānhuī, Shǎnxī, and Zhèjiāng.
Cháoxiǎn offered tribute.
In the spring of the forty-first year, *xīnsì*, on the *xīnhài* day of the first month,
because the River God displayed spiritual efficacy,
Jīnlóng Sīdàwáng was ennobled.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Xīnyù was appointed Manchu Dūtǒng.
On the *jǐwèi* day of the second month, which was the first day of the month,
the Emperor inspected the Yǒngdìng Hé.
He instructed Lǐ Guāngdì, saying:
“When river water dries up, it will inevitably become blocked by silt.
This is very difficult to manage.
We should deliberate on it slowly.”
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Mǎnpī and Táng Xīshùn pacified the aboriginal barbarians of Dǎjiànlú,
and twelve thousand households of barbarian people submitted.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the *wùzǐ* day of the third month,
the Emperor attended the Imperial Lecture.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Zhāng Pénghé requested to compile a book on river management strategies.
The Emperor reprimanded him, saying:
“I have
read every book on river affairs.
Broadly speaking, it is easy to speak about,
but difficult to put into practice.
The nature of rivers is unpredictable;
how can one apply a single method to regulate them?
Compiling it into a book
would not only make it difficult for future generations to follow,
but even when I consider it myself,
I find it hard to be confident.
Zhāng Pénghé, you may try to compile it!”
Censor Mǎ Shìfāng impeached the Guǎngxī Provincial Administration Commissioner Rèn Fēnghòu for old age.
He was summoned for an audience,
and his age was not yet in decline.
The Emperor then decreed, saying:
“For sitting positions,
one must have experienced and astute individuals to be appropriate.
However,
this is not suitable for prefectural and county officials.”
In the summer of the fourth month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
Lǐ Línshèng was transferred to be the Grand Coordinator of Gānsù,
Pān Yùlóng was promoted to be the Grand Coordinator of Gùyuán,
Lán Lǐ was moved to be the Commander-in-Chief of Tiānjīn,
and Cáo Bǐnghuán was appointed Manchu Dūtǒng.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the Minister of Justice Wáng Shìzhēn requested leave to return to his hometown.
The Emperor instructed the Grand Secretaries, saying:
“The people of Shāndōng are generally stubborn,
fond of winning and seeking revenge.
Only Wáng Shìzhēn is not like this.
His poetry is excellent,
and at home, he only reads books.
If he were to return to his hometown,
it would be a great pity.
Grant him five months' leave,
without vacating his position.”
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Emperor inspected the Yǒngdìng Hé.
He instructed Lǐ Guāngdì:
“In deep winter when ice forms,
the release [of water] can proceed as normal.
The clear water flows beneath the ice,
and being compressed by the ice,
it scours the riverbed even deeper.”
Upon inspecting Dàwānkǒu,
he decreed:
“The stone embankment has not yet begun construction.
Southern fir wood can be used for piling.
Do not neglect this.”
He inspected the Zǐyá Hé.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the fifth month, on the *guǐsì* day,
there was a vacancy for an official managing boatmen in Hēilóngjiāng.
The ministers of the board proposed the banished Circuit Intendant Zhōu Chāng for the position.
The Emperor said:
“Since Zhōu Chāng has already been banished,
appointing him an official in Wūlā
would mean he would never be able to return home.
This can be given to an Eight Banners official willing to serve.”
On the *wùshēn* day,
Censor Zhāng Yuàn requested the destruction of the tomb of Wèi Zhōngxián, an imperial eunuch of the former Míng dynasty.
This was granted.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the Emperor traveled to beyond the Great Wall.
In the sixth month, on the *gēngchén* day,
the descendants of the Sòng dynasty scholar Shào Yōng were granted the title of Wǔjīng Bóshì.
In the autumn of the seventh month, on the *dīnghài* day,
the Grand Minister of the Imperial Guard, Duke Fèiyánggǔ, fell ill while accompanying the Emperor.
The Emperor halted his imperial carriage for a day
and personally visited him.
When news came that he had passed away,
three saddled horses,
four unsaddled horses,
and five thousand taels of silver were bestowed.
A minister was dispatched to escort his remains back to the capital.
Sacrifices and a funeral were granted,
and he was posthumously given the epithet Xiāngzhuàng.
In the eighth month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Emperor visited Suǒyuè'ěrjì Shān.
He said:
“The topography of this mountain is majestic and towering,
truly worthy of being called a famous scenic spot.
Henceforth, hunting is forbidden here.”
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Emperor hunted at Mǎnítú,
piercing two yellow sheep with one arrow
and also severing Lāhā Lìmù.
The Mongols were all astonished.
In the ninth month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
Prince Jiǎn, Yǎbù, passed away while accompanying the Emperor.
Ministers were ordered to escort his remains back to the capital.
The Emperor's eldest son, Yìnzhī, and third son, Yìnzhǐ, went out to meet them.
Officials were dispatched to manage the funeral.
Four thousand taels of silver were bestowed,
and the imperial princes collectively contributed three thousand taels of silver.
At the time of the funeral procession,
the imperial princes and imperial guards went to send him off.
Sacrifices, a funeral, and a stele were granted,
and he was posthumously given the epithet Xiū.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Emperor attended the Imperial Lecture.
Grand Secretary Wáng Xī requested retirement due to old age and illness.
A compassionate imperial decree expressed consolation,
and he was promoted to Shàofù and allowed to retire.
Gá'ěrdān's daughter, Zhōngqíhǎi, arrived in the capital.
She was ordered to live with her elder brother, First-Class Imperial Guard Sèbùténgbā'ěrzhǔ'ěr,
and married to Second-Class Imperial Guard Měnggǔ Shākèdǔ'ěr.
In the winter of the tenth month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
Imperial Clansman Tèkèxīn was appointed Manchu Dūtǒng,
and Yàtúbù'ěrsài was appointed Mongol Dūtǒng.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Grand Secretary Zhāng Yùshū was recalled to court.
An imperial edict remitted Gānsù's scheduled taxes for the coming year.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Liáng Nài was appointed General-in-Chief of the Land Forces of Fújiàn.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Jiāngsū's scheduled taxes for next year were remitted.
Yuè Shēnglóng was reinstated as Grand Coordinator of Sìchuān.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Pǔqí was transferred to be Manchu Dūtǒng,
Sūn Zhāqí was appointed Mongol Dūtǒng,
and Huáxiǎn was appointed Governor-General of Sìchuān and Shǎnxī.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Grand Secretary Zhāng Yīng requested retirement.
A compassionate imperial decree expressed consolation and permitted him to retire.
Censor Jìn Ràng memorialized, stating that for prefectural and county officials,
they must ensure that households have sufficient provisions and people are well-fed
to be considered good officials.
Jìn Ràng was ordered to be reassigned as the Magistrate of Tōngzhōu.
An imperial edict ordered Governors-General Guō Xiù, Zhāng Pénghé, Sāng'é, and Huáxiǎn,
and Governors Lǐ Guāngdì, Péng Péng, and Xú Cháo to each recommend worthy and capable individuals.
Prince Píngdào, Nè'ěrfú, passed away.
His son, Nè'ěrsù, succeeded to the title.
In the eleventh month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“I have carefully reviewed the major cases of the autumn assizes,
and there are many errors in wording.
The court officials have not even noticed one or two.
The Ministry of Justice has been particularly careless.
Let them be punished.”
In the twelfth month, on the *rénshēn* day,
the Yao bandits of Liánshān, Guǎngdōng, rebelled.
Dūtǒng Sōngzhù was ordered to suppress them.
On the *xīnsì* day,
a grand sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted in varying degrees for forty-two prefectures and counties in the provinces of Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Hénán, Shǎnxī, and Guǎngdōng.
Cháoxiǎn and Líuqiú offered tribute.
Basic Annals Eight: Basic Annals of Shèngzǔ, Part Three
In the spring of the forty-first year, *rénwǔ*, on the *rénzǐ* day of the first month,
an imperial edict ordered the repair of the Guózǐjiān.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
an imperial edict decreed that prisoners whose executions had been repeatedly delayed should have their sentences reduced by one degree.
Yǎ'ěrjiāng'ā inherited the title of Prince Jiǎn.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Emperor traveled to Wǔtái Shān.
On the *gēngshēn* day of the second month,
[the Emperor] arrived at Shèhǔchuān.
The officials and people requested to build a Wànshòu Pavilion on Bódàsàdǐng to pray for blessings.
[The Emperor] did not permit it.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor inspected the Zǐyá River.
On the *rénwǔ* day of the third month,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
Wǎěrdài was appointed as Mǎnzhōu *Dū Tǒng*,
and Wúdáchán, Mǎsīhā, and Mǎnpī were appointed as Ménggǔ *Dū Tǒng*.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the Emperor attended the Imperial Lectures (*jīngyán*).
On the *jiǎxū* day of the fourth month in summer,
the retired Grand Secretary Wáng Xī was bestowed with an imperial inscription plaque and couplet.
An imperial edict stated:
"You are an old minister from the previous reign.
Please eat heartily,
be careful with medicine,
to console Our thoughts."
On the *guǐsì* day of the fifth month,
it was decreed that criminals sentenced to exile should be assigned to their native places.
If an exiled criminal died in exile,
their wife and children were permitted to return to their hometown.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Xiǎn Qīnwáng Dānzhēn passed away.
Imperial princes and ministers were dispatched to manage the funeral,
and ten thousand taels of silver were bestowed.
He was posthumously granted the title Mì.
His son Yǎnhuáng succeeded him.
On the *rénchén* day,
previously,
the Yáo people of Liánshān in Liánzhōu Prefecture had rebelled.
An Imperial Censor impeached them,
and *Dū Tǒng* Sōngzhù was ordered to lead the imperial guards to suppress them,
and *Shàngshū* Fàn Chéngxūn was ordered to investigate the situation.
By this time,
Sōngzhù reported that as soon as the government troops arrived,
the Yáo people pleaded for surrender,
with over nineteen thousand Yáo people surrendering successively.
Nine individuals, including Lí Guì, who had killed officials, were handed over
and immediately executed before the army.
The surrendered Yáo people were resettled
and handed over to the Governor-General for management.
Fàn Chéngxūn reported that the Yáo people had caused trouble,
Vice-General Dù Fāng had been wounded and died,
and Commander Liú Hǔ had retreated prematurely,
and should be sentenced to decapitation.
General Yīn Huàxíng should be dismissed from office.
An imperial edict was received:
"Yīn Huàxíng has military merits;
he shall be retired with his original rank.
Liú Hǔ shall be spared death."
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
court officials were summoned to the Bǎohé Hall,
and imperial writings were bestowed.
On the *rénzǐ* day of the sixth month,
the Miáo people of Géyí Village in Guìzhōu rebelled.
Government troops suppressed them.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the Emperor composed a text to admonish scholars and students,
promulgated it throughout the provinces,
and had it engraved on stone at academic institutions.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, departed for Rèhé.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Yuè Shēnglóng, Commander of Sìchuān, reported in a memorial that the chieftain Mǎbǐbì of the Luǒ people in Dàliángshān had led his followers to submit.
He requested to appoint him as a native commander (*tǔ qiānhù*)
and grant him seals.
On the *xīnchǒu* day of the intercalary sixth month,
over nineteen thousand households of Mùyā Fan people submitted.
It was requested to establish positions such as Pacification Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, and native hundred-household head (*tǔ bǎihù*).
All were approved.
On the *gēngchén* day, the first day of the eighth month,
the quota for provincial examinations in Shùntiān, Zhèjiāng, and Húguǎng was increased.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, returned to the palace.
On the *xīnhài* day of the ninth month,
Lǐ Zhèngzōng, Lú Chóngyào, and Féng Guóxiàng were appointed as Hànjūn *Dū Tǒng*.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the regulations for passing the Five Classics examination were established.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
the autumn executions for this year were suspended.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Qí Shì and Sōngzhù were appointed as Mǎnzhōu *Dū Tǒng*,
Mǎngkā was appointed as Hànjūn *Dū Tǒng*,
and Chēnàfú was appointed as Ménggǔ *Dū Tǒng*.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an edict stated:
"During the Southern Tour to inspect the rivers,
lodging provisions along the route are to be stopped,
and extortions prohibited.
Officials are not to exchange gifts,
and the common people are to each attend to their own occupations.
The Governors-General and Governors shall announce this
so that Our intention is clearly understood."
On the *jǐsì* day,
Xíhānà was appointed as Grand Secretary,
Dūnbài as Minister of Personnel (*Lìbù Shàngshū*),
Xīěrdá as Minister of Rites (*Lǐbù Shàngshū*),
Wēndá as Censor-in-Chief of the Left (*Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ*),
and Guǎn Yuánzhōng as General of Guǎngzhōu.
Lǐ Fēng and other scholars from Zhènggān knocked at the palace gate, stating that the Hóng Miáo people were committing murder,
but the local authorities were not investigating.
The Emperor ordered Vice-Ministers Fù Jìzǔ and Gān Guóshū,
and Governor Zhào Shēnqiáo to travel by express post to investigate.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor set off on his Southern Tour.
On the *rénwǔ* day of the tenth month in winter,
[the Emperor] arrived at Dézhōu.
Crown Prince Yìnréng fell ill,
and the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Guō Shìlóng was appointed Governor-General of Guǎngdōng and Guǎngxī,
and Jīn Shìróng was appointed Governor-General of Zhèjiāng and Fújiàn.
On the *bǐngchén* day of the eleventh month,
an edict waived the regular taxes for Shǎnxī and Ānhuī for the next year.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Grand Secretary Yīsāngā requested to retire,
and was ordered to do so.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Xiāo Yǒngzǎo, Governor of Guǎngxī, impeached the Provincial Administration Commissioner Jiào Huàxīn for embezzling grain from the granaries,
and stated that he should be ordered to compensate.
The Emperor said:
"Grain must have a storage place
to last a long time.
If there are no granaries,
and it is piled in open fields,
it is difficult to avoid spoilage,
especially in the low and humid southern regions.
A separate regulation should be set and reported."
It was ordered to repair Yǔlíng.
On the *rénchén* day of the twelfth month,
court officials requested to bestow an honorific title upon the Emperor
for his fiftieth birthday, which would be next year.
The Emperor did not permit it.
The Board of Revenue (*Hùbù*) deliberated on rejecting the disaster report from Fèngtiān.
The Emperor said:
"Rain and shine are originally not fixed.
It is common for there to be harmonious rainfall at first,
and then for a disaster to occur later.
This is a normal occurrence.
Their report can be approved."
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Zhào Shēnqiáo was reassigned as Governor of Piānwán,
Zhào Hóngcàn was appointed Commander of Guǎngdōng,
Wáng Shìchén as Commander of Zhèjiāng,
and Sūn Zhēnghào as Hànjūn *Dū Tǒng*.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Èlǔtè Dānjīnalābùtǎn came to pay respects,
was generously rewarded,
ennobled as a Prince of a Commandery (*Jùnwáng*),
and granted land for pasturage.
In this year,
disaster taxes were exempted, to varying degrees, in ten prefectures and counties across provinces such as Jiāngnán, Hénán, Zhèjiāng, Húguǎng, and Gānsù.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú offered tribute.
On the *rénzǐ* day of the first month in the spring of the forty-second year (1703),
Grand Secretaries and other ministers offered congratulations for the Emperor's fiftieth birthday,
respectfully presenting
a screen with "Wànshòu Wújiāng" (Boundless Longevity).
[The Emperor] refused it
but accepted their written memorial.
On the *rénxū* day,
the Emperor went on a Southern Tour to inspect the rivers.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Yú Yìmó was appointed Commander of Húguǎng.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
[the Emperor] arrived at Jǐnán,
viewed the Zhēnzhū Spring,
and composed a poem "Three Crossings of the Qí River."
On the *rénshēn* day,
[the Emperor] arrived at Tài'ān
and ascended Mount Tài.
An edict waived last year's outstanding taxes for areas along the imperial route and those with poor harvests.
On the *dīngchǒu* day of the second month,
forty thousand *shí* of tribute grain were transported to relieve Jìníng and Tài'ān.
[The Emperor] inspected the dyke work at Táoyuán.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
[the Emperor] boarded a boat from Táoyuán
and thoroughly inspected the river dikes.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
[the Emperor] crossed the river and ascended Jīnshān.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
[the Emperor] arrived at Sūzhōu.
An official was dispatched to offer sacrifices at the tomb of Grand Secretary Sòng Déyí.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Emperor stayed in Hángzhōu and reviewed archery.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
[the Emperor] arrived at Jiāngníng.
In the third month, on the day Wùshēn,
the Emperor inspected the dike works at Gāojiāyàn and Zháijiābà.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
the Emperor inspected the dikes south of the Yellow River at Lóngwō, Yāndūn, and other places.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Guǐhài,
it was the Wànshòujié (Emperor's birthday).
The Emperor paid respects at the Empress Dowager's palace,
and exempted court officials from offering congratulations.
An edict of grace was issued,
bestowing favors upon the aged,
remitting outstanding taxes,
investigating filial piety and righteousness,
aiding the poor and distressed,
recommending recluses of talent,
and pardoning all those whose crimes were not otherwise excusable by extraordinary amnesties.
All such were pardoned.
Gifts were bestowed upon Imperial Princes, Commandery Princes, and civil and military officials below them, with different grades of gifts.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Dòng'è was granted the inherited title of Qínwáng (Prince of the First Rank) of Xìn.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the Emperor presided over the Jīngyán (Imperial Lectures).
Wāng Hào, Hé Zhuó, and Jiǎng Tíngxī, who were Jǔrén (recommended men) serving in the Imperial Academy for compiling books, were granted the status of Jìnshì (presented scholars),
and were to participate uniformly in the Diànshì (palace examination).
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Xīnsì,
Wáng Shìdān and 163 others were granted the status of Jìnshì Jíyǐ (Metropolitan Graduate of the First Class) and other ranks.
The "raw barbarians" of eighteen villages in Lóngxī, Wēizhōu, Sìchuān province, submitted and paid tribute grain.
On the day Dīnghài,
Grand Secretary Xióng Cìlǚ requested retirement,
and was ordered to relinquish his office but retain his salary,
remaining available for consultation.
Fù Jìzǔ and others investigated the case of red Miao banditry in Húguǎng.
An imperial decree was issued, stating:
"Governor-General Guō Xiù and Provincial Commander Dù Běnzhí concealed the matter and failed to report it,
and are both dismissed from office.
Provincial Governor Jīn Xǐ is demoted."
Yù Chénglóng was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng.
On the day Guǐsì,
retired Grand Secretary Wáng Xī passed away.
Sacrificial rites and burial were granted,
and he was posthumously granted the name Wénjìng.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Chén Tíngjìng was appointed Grand Secretary and concurrently Minister of Personnel.
On the day Wùxū,
an edict stated that former Vice-Minister Rèn Kèpǔ, being over ninety years old,
was truly a venerable elder,
and was granted the additional title of Minister.
Lǐ Guāngdì was appointed Minister of Personnel,
and was to continue as Provincial Governor of Zhílì.
Mǎngkā was appointed General of Jīngzhōu,
Nuóluóbù as General of Hángzhōu,
Imperial Clansman Àiyīntú as Manchu Commander-in-Chief,
and Sūn Zhāqí and Wēng'élǐ as Mongol Commanders-in-Chief.
On the day Jǐhài,
an edict was issued to the people of the Eight Banners:
"I spared millions of taels of treasury funds to pay off debts and redeem land for banner soldiers,
and to plan for their livelihoods.
If each of you can sincerely uphold filial piety and fraternal duty,
and diligently and frugally carry out your affairs,
then you will fully comfort My heart.
If you do not cherish this,
and continue to idle about, drink, and gamble as before,
you will certainly be dealt with according to strict laws.
This proclamation is personally written;
let all respectfully comply!"
In the fifth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Yù Qínwáng Fúquán was ill,
and the Emperor visited him for several consecutive days.
On the day Guǐhài,
Imperial Grand Minister Suǒ'étú was found guilty of a crime,
and was imprisoned in the Imperial Clan Court.
On the day Jǐsì,
the Emperor went on an inspection tour beyond the passes.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnsì,
Gōng Qínwáng Chángníng passed away.
The Imperial Princes were ordered to assemble daily,
ten thousand taels of silver were bestowed,
and officials were dispatched to construct his tomb and erect a stele.
On the day Rén'yín,
Yù Qínwáng Fúquán passed away.
Upon hearing this,
the Emperor hastened back to the capital.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day, Yǐsì,
the Emperor went to the funeral of Yù Qínwáng,
and wept bitterly.
He entered through the Cāngzhènmén and took residence in the Jǐngrén Gōng.
The princes and high ministers requested that he return to the Qiánqīng Gōng,
but the Emperor said:
"Residing in a temporary palace is in compliance with established precedent."
After residing there for five days,
the Emperor ordered the First Imperial Prince and others to observe mourning rites,
and ordered Censor Luó Zhàn to construct the tomb and erect the stele,
with the posthumous name Xiàn.
His son Bǎotài inherited the princely title.
On the day Wùshēn,
due to heavy rains in Shāndōng,
officials were dispatched to distribute relief.
On the day Gēngxū,
the Emperor went on an inspection tour beyond the passes.
On the day Jǐsì,
three hundred thousand taels of treasury funds were allocated,
and fifty thousand dàn of grain transport was diverted to relieve Shāndōng.
Officials in Shāndōng who failed to manage the famine relief
were suspended from promotion and transfer.
In the eighth month, on the day Guǐsì,
the autumn judicial review for this year was suspended.
In the ninth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
sacrificial rites and burial were granted to the late Vice-Ministers Gāo Shìqí and Lì Dùnà.
On the day Jǐsì,
Minister Xí'ěrdá was ordered to oversee the suppression of the red Miao.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Guǐwèi,
the Emperor began his western tour.
Grand Secretary Mǎnpǔ and Censor Gù Sù were ordered to follow behind,
to investigate servants who caused trouble,
and immediately arrest them.
On the day Gēngyín,
Lamas requested to expand the temple in Táozhōu Wèi,
but the Emperor said:
"Taking people's land to expand temples
harms the livelihood of the people.
This should be permanently prohibited."
On the day Guǐsì,
he passed through Jǐngxíng,
and stopped at the Bǎijǐng post station.
The station had previously lacked springs,
but now the well water overflowed.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
he stopped in Tàiyuán.
On the day Wùxū,
an edict remitted outstanding taxes in Shānxī.
The common people gathered before the temporary palace, pleading for the imperial carriage to stay,
and the Emperor stayed for one more day.
In the eleventh month, on the day Yǐsì,
he stopped at Hóngdòng.
Officials were dispatched to offer sacrifices at the tomb of Nǚwā.
On the day Rénzǐ,
he crossed the Yellow River,
and stopped at Tóngguān.
Officials were dispatched to offer sacrifices to the Western Peak.
One hundred-year-old elders who welcomed the imperial carriage were granted silver.
On the day Jiǎyín,
he stopped at Wèinán.
He reviewed the archery of the Gùyuán garrison soldiers,
and granted Provincial Commander Pān Yùlóng and those below him an additional rank.
On the day Bǐngchén,
the Emperor resided in Xī'ān.
On the day Dīngsì,
he reviewed the archery of the banner garrison officials and soldiers.
Officials were dispatched to offer sacrifices to King Wén of Zhōu and King Wǔ of Zhōu,
with the imperial name personally inscribed on the sacrificial texts.
Officials were dispatched to offer libations at the tombs of Provincial Commanders Zhāng Yǒng and Liáng Huàfèng.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the Emperor conducted a grand review in Xī'ān,
and bestowed his personal bow and arrows upon General Bójì.
A banquet was given for the officials and soldiers.
The military and common people gathered before the temporary palace, pleading for him to stay,
and the Emperor stayed for one more day.
The recluse Lǐ Yǒng of Zhōuzhì was granted an imperial calligraphic plaque
with the inscription "Pure in aspiration and conduct."
Outstanding taxes in Shǎnxī and Gānsù were remitted.
Outstanding taxes in Shǎnxī and Gānsù were remitted.
On the day Guǐhài,
the Emperor returned.
On the day Jǐsì,
he stopped at Shǎnzhōu.
The Third Imperial Prince Yìnzhǐ was ordered to go and inspect the Sānmén Dǐzhù.
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐhài,
he stopped at Xiūwǔ.
Upon reviewing the disorganized state of the Huáiqìng camp,
Commander-in-Chief Wáng Yìngtǒng was arrested and brought to the capital for judgment with a death sentence.
On the day Gēngchén,
he stopped at Cízhōu.
An imperial calligraphic plaque
with the inscription "Enduring legacy of sages and worthies"
was hung at the tomb of the ancient worthy Zǐgòng.
On the day Gēngyín,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
it was decreed that officials serving in external posts must recuse themselves if their native place was within five hundred *lǐ*.
Chángníng's son Hǎishàn was enfeoffed as Bèilè.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted for ninety-one prefectures and counties in the provinces of Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Shāndōng, Hénán, Shǎnxī, Zhèjiāng, Húguǎng, and others, with varying degrees of remission.
Cháoxiǎn (Korea), Liúqiú (Ryukyu), and Ānnán (Vietnam) sent tribute.
In the spring of the 43rd year, *jiǎshēn*, in the first month, *xīnyǒu* day,
an edict stated:
"I have consulted on the sufferings of the people,
and deeply understand the hardships of labor.
Those who cultivate thirty *mǔ* of land,
after paying rent and taxes,
have approximately twenty *dàn* remaining.
Food, clothing, and labor service
are provided from this.
If they are fortunate enough to encounter an honest official,
there may still be a surplus.
But if there is endless extortion,
then the people will have nothing to live on.
Therefore, scrutinizing officials is how the people are brought peace,
and it fundamentally requires high officials to genuinely sympathize."
On the *wùchén* day,
an edict was issued that Han bannermen whose entire family was serving outside the capital
should be considered for reassignment as capital officials.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Emperor visited the imperial tombs.
In the second month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
the Huái River god was enfeoffed as the Great Huái God of Chángyuán Yòushùn,
and the Emperor's calligraphy
"Língdú Ānlán" (Divine River, Peaceful Waves)
was hung as a plaque.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
Lǐ Jīhé was appointed Governor of Jiāngxī,
and Néng Tái was appointed Governor of Sìchuān.
In the third month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Emperor attended the Imperial Lectures.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
an edict suspended the "hot review" (judicial process for urgent cases).
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Wú Hóng was appointed Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Gānsù.
Famine victims from Shāndōng were provided with funds to return to their native places.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Wēn Dá was appointed Minister of Works.
In the summer, fourth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
Imperial Bodyguard Lāxī was ordered to inspect the source of the river.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor visited Móujì Shān,
and subsequently inspected the Yǒngdìng Hé and Zǐyá Hé rivers.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the fifth month, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
Yú Zhǔn was appointed Governor of Guìzhōu.
In the sixth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
the Emperor went on an inspection tour beyond the passes.
In the autumn, ninth month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
an edict stated that governors-general and governors who transferred officials in violation of regulations would be punished.
Vice Minister Cháng Shòu pacified 237 Gŭangdōng pirates, including Ā Bǎowèi,
and they were integrated into the army.
On the *wùmǎo* day,
Minister of Justice Wáng Shìzhēn was demoted for mishandling a case.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Imperial Bodyguard Lāxī, who had inspected the river source,
returned from Xīngxiù Hǎi,
presenting a map.
In the winter, tenth month, on the *wùchén* day, the first day of the month,
the old channel of Yángcūn was dredged.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
an edict exempted Shùntiān and Héjiān prefectures, and Shāndōng and Zhèjiāng provinces, from next year's land tax.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Lǐ Zhènyù was appointed Minister of Rites,
Xú Cháo was appointed Minister of Revenue,
Tú Cuìzhōng was appointed Minister of War,
Wáng Yǎn was appointed Minister of Justice,
and Wú Hán was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
imperial-made copper *dǒu* and copper *shēng* measures were issued to the Ministry of Revenue,
with orders to make iron ones for general circulation.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Zhào Hóngxiè was appointed Governor of Hénán.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
orders were given to dredge the Fén, Wèi, and Jiǎlǔ rivers.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Emperor inspected the Yǒngdìng Hé.
In the eleventh month, on the *dīngyǒu* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
The Emperor returned to the palace.
The Emperor, noting that instrumental measurements did not match the Qīzhèng calendar,
pardoned the officials of the Imperial Astronomy Bureau who requested punishment.
Lángzhōng Fèi Yǎnggǔ was executed in the marketplace for corruption.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the regulations for the Ministry of Personnel's selection of county magistrates for promotion were established,
and recommendations by governors-general and governors were suspended.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Húguǎng Governor Liú Diànhéng built an imperial calligraphy pavilion.
The Emperor reprimanded him for the extravagance,
and strictly prohibited using construction as a pretext to embezzle funds or burden the people.
Sìchuān-Shǎnxī Governor-General Bó Jì submitted a memorial impeaching Liángzhōu General Wèi Xūn for old age.
The Emperor said:
"Wèi Xūn previously rendered military service,
and is loved by both soldiers and people.
He, along with Shī Dìbīn, Mài Liángxǐ, and Pān Yùlóng, are all veteran officials,
and are difficult to find;
how can they be impeached?"
On the *rénxū* day,
instructions were given to the historians compiling the Míng History to verify public opinion
and clarify right and wrong,
in order to complete a trustworthy history.
In the twelfth month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
Tiānjīn General Lán Lǐ requested coastal military agricultural colonies,
which was approved.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the imperial poetry collection was bestowed upon court officials.
That year,
disaster taxes were differentially remitted for 109 prefectures and counties in Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Shāndōng, Húguǎng, Guǎngdōng, and other provinces.
Cháoxiǎn (Korea) paid tribute.
In the spring of the 44th year, *yǐyǒu*, in the first month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
the *Gǔwén Yuānjìan* (Mirror of Ancient Literature) was completed,
and bestowed upon court officials
and government schools.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Emperor visited Tāngquán.
In the second month, on the *yǐchǒu* day, the first day of the month,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor embarked on a southern inspection tour to examine the rivers.
An edict stated:
"I pay close attention to river defense,
and have repeatedly conducted inspections,
achieving success reports.
Now the Yellow River flows smoothly,
but its topography still needs to be examined,
so I will follow the river south.
No temporary palaces should be built wherever I go,
and those who levy exactions to burden the people
shall be punished by military law."
On the *rénwǔ* day,
he arrived at Jìnghǎi.
An official was sent to offer sacrifices at the tomb of the late Vice Minister Lì Dùnà,
who was granted the posthumous name Wénkè.
In the third month, on the *jǐhài* day,
an imperial instruction was given to the Shāndōng governor, stating:
"Hundreds of thousands of common people welcome me along the roadside daily.
Counting the days for my return,
it will be precisely during the wheat harvest.
They should each attend to farming,
so as not to impede agricultural work."
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Emperor resided in Yángzhōu.
River official Zhāng Pénghé was given strategies.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the Emperor resided in Sūzhōu.
Orders were given to select skilled calligraphers from among the *jǔ*, *gòng*, *shēng*, and *jiàn* students of Jiāngnán and Zhèjiāng to enter the capital to compile books.
Gōng Fúshàn,
Grand Secretaries Zhāng Yùshū and Chén Tíngjìng,
Grand Secretary-in-retirement Zhāng Yīng,
and Commander-in-Chief Àiyīntú were granted silver.
Grand Secretary Mǎ Qí and others were granted the *Huángyú Biǎo*.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
he arrived at Sōngjiāng to review archery.
The plaque with the imperial calligraphy
"Shèngjì Yíhuī" (Glorious Traces of the Sagely Deeds)
was bestowed upon the Kǒng clan of Qīngpǔ.
The late Vice Minister Gāo Shìqí was granted the posthumous name Wénkè.
In the summer, fourth month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
the Emperor resided in Hángzhōu to review archery.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
an edict pardoned death sentences by one degree in Shāndōng, Jiāngsū, Zhèjiāng, and Fújiàn.
On the *wùyín* day,
the plaque with the imperial calligraphy
"Zhìdé Wúmíng" (Supreme Virtue is Nameless)
was hung at the Wú Tàibó Ancestral Temple,
and plaques with the names Jì Zhá, Dǒng Zhòngshū, Jiāo Xiān, Zhōu Dūnyí, Fàn Zhòngyān, Sū Shì, Ōuyáng Xiū, Hú Ānguó, Mǐ Fú, Zōng Zé, and Lù Xiùfū were also hung in their respective temples.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor resided in Jiāngníng.
In the intercalary fourth month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor inspected the dike works at Gāojiāyàn.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the fifth month, on the *wùyín* day,
the Emperor personally tried the case of Lángzhōng Chén Rǔbì,
and acquitted Rǔbì.
Minister of Justice Ānbùlù and Censor-in-Chief of the Left Shūlù were dismissed for mishandling the case.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Bèi Hénuò was appointed Governor-General of Yúnnán and Guìzhōu.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Emperor went on an inspection tour beyond the passes.
In the sixth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
an order was issued that county magistrates selected for promotion could not be chosen for Censorate or Supervising Censor positions unless they were serving a second term.
On the *gēngxū* day,
mining in Guǎngdōng was suspended.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the Emperor sojourned in Rèhé.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the *rénshēn* day,
the river breached at Qīngshuǐgōu and Hánzhuāng,
and river officials were ordered to investigate the residents' fields and houses and report.
In the eighth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Seventy *wàn* *liǎng* of silver, advanced as military provisions to the Eight Banners, were remitted.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Yù Chénglóng was dismissed,
and Shí Wénshèng was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
The Emperor departed for Bólōhé Tún,
to inspect the herds.
In the ninth month, on the *jǐsì* day,
He arrived at Zhāngjiākǒu.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day, he returned to the capital.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Xīfúnà was appointed Grand Censor of the Left,
and Dájiā was appointed General of Jiāngníng.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *xīnmǎo* day (the first day of the month),
The reconstruction of the Huáyīn Xīyuè Miào was completed,
and the Emperor composed the stele inscription.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Fùníng'ān was appointed Manchu Commander of the Han Army.
In the eleventh month, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
Mongolian Duke Dānjílā was ordered to prepare troops at Tuīhé,
to observe Cèwàng Ālābùtǎn.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Lǐ Guāngdì was appointed Grand Secretary,
Sòng Luò was appointed Minister of Personnel,
and Zhào Hóngxiè was transferred to be Governor of Zhílì.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
An imperial edict remitted Húguǎng's regular taxes for the following year and all previous arrears.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
The Guózǐ Jiān was completed,
and the Emperor personally inscribed
"Lúntáng"
on the plaque.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Wāng Hào was appointed Governor of Hénán.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
The Emperor visited the imperial tombs.
He also made a tour of inspection near the frontier.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
School officials were established for the two prefectures of Guǎngnán and Líjiāng in Yúnnán,
and local people were permitted to take examinations.
In the twelfth month, on the *rén'yín* day,
The Emperor attended the funeral of Yù Qīnwáng Fúquán.
Ālíng'ā was appointed concurrent Minister of the Lǐfān Yuàn.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
The Emperor returned to the palace.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Zǔ Liángbì was appointed General of Fúzhōu.
In this year,
Taxes for disaster-stricken areas in forty-six prefectures and counties across provinces like Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Húguǎng, and Guǎngdōng were remitted to varying degrees.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú paid tribute.
In the forty-fifth year, *bǐngxū*, in spring, in the first month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
Sūn Zhāqí and Xú Cháo were ordered to supervise the dredging of the Huái-Yáng diversion river.
The Shùntiān examiners, Minister of Revenue Wāng Pín and Zànshàn Yáo Shìlěi, were stripped of their posts for unfair selection of scholars.
In the second month, on the *guǐsì* day,
The Emperor toured the imperial domains.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
He arrived at Jìnghǎi,
and inspected the Zǐyá Hé.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
He returned to reside at Nányuàn.
Zhū Mǎn was appointed General of Jiāngníng.
Wáng Rán was appointed Governor of Zhèjiāng.
The Governor-General of Jiāngnán and Jiāngxī, Ā Shān, impeached Chén Péngnián, the Prefect of Jiāngníng, for disrespect in implementing imperial decrees.
The Board recommended beheading.
Previously,
during the Southern Tour in the *yǐyǒu* year,
Chén Péngnián, following the imperial decree, did not build a temporary palace.
Ā Shān then used other pretexts to impeach him.
The Emperor ordered him to enter the capital to compile books.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
The Emperor returned to the palace.
In the third month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
The Emperor presided over the Jīngyán lectures.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Shī Yúnjǐn and 289 others were granted *jìnshì* degrees of various ranks.
An imperial edict ordered the establishment of infant care halls in all provinces.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *wùzǐ* day (the first day of the month),
There was a solar eclipse.
Lǐ Fāngshù, the Provincial Commander of Guìzhōu, was promoted to General Zhènyuǎn.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Wú Hán was dismissed,
and Méi Xuān was appointed Grand Censor of the Left.
In the fifth month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
Jīn Shìróng was appointed Minister of War.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
An imperial edict remitted tax arrears in Zhílì and Shāndōng.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Liáng Nài was appointed Governor-General of Fújiàn and Zhèjiāng.
On the *wùyín* day,
The Emperor toured beyond the Great Wall.
In the sixth month, on the *dīnghài* day (the first day of the month),
An imperial edict ordered the compilation of biographies of meritorious officials.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Méi Xuān and Èrgé were ordered to re-examine the case of Tǔsī Tián Shùnnián of Róngměi.
On the *rén'yín* day,
It was decreed that for all money and grain requested by ministries and courts not by imperial petition,
The Ministry of Revenue should report the total monthly sum.
Lán Lǐ was appointed Provincial Commander of the Army in Fújiàn.
On the *xīnhài* day,
The Governor of Sìchuān, Néng Tài, reported that the Ānlè iron chain bridge was completed,
and a thousand-commander from the Huàlín battalion was moved to guard it.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
The Emperor stopped at Rèhé.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Dézhāo inherited the title of Qīnwáng Xìn.
In the eighth month, on the *rénchén* day,
The river embankment at Gāojiāyàn Chēluóbà Jiàn Hé was completed.
In the ninth month, on the *jǐhài* day,
The Emperor returned to the capital.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *yǐyǒu* day (the first day of the month),
Dūnbài was dismissed,
and Wēndá was appointed Minister of Personnel,
Xīfúnà was appointed Minister of Works.
On the *gēngyín* day,
The martial palace examination was held.
An edict stated:
"Today, the realm has been at peace for a long time.
Ministers who have experienced battle are few,
and those who understand naval warfare are even fewer.
In the future, there may be concerns regarding Táiwān.
When I went on the Southern Tour in the *jiǎzǐ* year,
I boarded a boat from Jiāngníng,
and when I reached Huángtiāndàng,
a strong wind rose on the river.
I stood alone at the bow of the boat, shooting river dolphins,
and felt no concern at all.
Later, when crossing the river,
I gradually felt my heart stir.
Last year, when crossing the river,
I felt palpitations.
This is all due to age.
Asking veteran generals, it is the same for them.
How can one expect older men to bravely exert themselves and serve now? "
On the *rén'yín* day,
Grand Secretary Xíhānà, Vice Minister Zhāng Tíngshū, and Xiāo Yǒngzǎo were ordered to re-examine the case of Tǔsī Tián Shùnnián.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Yàtú was appointed Manchu Commander.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
An imperial edict remitted tax arrears in ten provinces: Shānxī, Shǎnxī, Jiāngsū, Ānhuī, Jiāngxī, Zhèjiāng, Fújiàn, Húběi, Húnán, and Guǎngdōng.
In the eleventh month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
Minister Jīn Shìróng, Vice Ministers Bāxí and Fàn Chéngliè were ordered to supervise the dredging of the Qīnghé.
Over 3,956,600 *liǎng* of silver borrowed by officials and soldiers of the Eight Banners and not yet repaid to the government were remitted.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Ā Shān was appointed Minister of Justice.
On the *gēngchén* day,
The Emperor visited the imperial tombs.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Shào Mùbù was appointed Governor-General of Jiāngnán and Jiāngxī.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Because of widespread private coining in Shāndōng,
it was permitted to pay regular taxes with small coins,
and officials were charged with transporting them to the capital for minting.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
The Emperor toured beyond the Great Wall.
The Dálài Lǎma of Xīzàng died,
and his subordinate Dìbā concealed it,
and also installed a false Dálài Lǎma.
Lāzàng Hàn killed the Dìbā and presented the false Lǎma.
Lǎma Shāngnánduōěrjì of Xīníng reported this.
In the twelfth month, on the *rén'yín* day,
The Emperor returned to the palace.
An imperial edict reduced sentences by one degree for criminals whose executions had been deferred for three to four years.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Guō Shìlóng was dismissed,
and Zhào Hóngcàn was appointed Governor-General of Guǎngdōng and Guǎngxī.
In this year,
