Taxes for disaster-stricken areas in thirty-two prefectures and counties across provinces like Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Fújiàn, Jiāngxī, and Húguǎng were remitted to varying degrees.
Cháoxiǎn paid tribute.
In the forty-sixth year, *dīnghài*, in spring, in the first month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
An imperial edict stated:
"During the Southern Tour to inspect the rivers,
I will travel by boat both ways,
and will not reside in imperial lodging.
No provisions are to be offered in the places I pass through."
On the *dīngsì* day,
Méi Xuān was dismissed,
and Xiāo Yǒngzǎo was appointed Grand Censor of the Left.
In the second month, on the *wùxū* day,
He arrived at Táizhuāng,
where the common people offered food.
He summoned the elders,
inquired in detail about agricultural matters and livelihoods,
and departed after a long time.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
The Emperor inspected Liūhuái Tào,
landed at Qīngkǒu,
and went to Cáojiā Miào.
Seeing that the terrain was contiguous with mountains,
it could not be dredged,
and the path of the river,
would directly destroy people's homes, dwellings, and ancestral tombs.
All would be ruined.
He admonished Zhāng Pénghé and others,
and consequently, the project was halted,
and the residents along the road cheered "Long live!"
He ordered a separate survey of the river channel below the Tiānrán Bà.
In the third month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
the Emperor resided in Jiāngníng.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Emperor resided in Sūzhōu.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Emperor resided in Hángzhōu.
An edict stated:
“Recently, while inspecting the river,
朕 stayed on the Huái River.
Officials and common people of the Jiāngnán and Zhèjiāng provinces entreated 朕 to visit,
and 朕 reluctantly yielded to the public sentiment,
crossing the Jiāng River and heading south.
Currently, the two wheat crops are almost ripe,
and the common people gather along the river to watch,
unavoidably trampling the crops.
Therefore, let welcoming and seeing-off ceremonies be suspended,
to demonstrate 朕's profound intention of valuing agriculture and loving the people.”
On the *wùshēn* day,
Èkèsùn was appointed General of Jiāngníng,
and Yīntài was appointed Grand Coordinator of Gānsù.
In the fifth month, on the *rénzǐ* day, the first day of the month,
the Emperor arrived at Shānyáng,
and revealed the strategy to the river officials.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Āshān was relieved of his post as Minister,
and Zhāng Pénghé's rank of Palace Guardian was revoked.
On the *wùyín* day,
the late Director-General of River Conservancy, Jìn Fǔ, was posthumously granted the title of Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince,
and his hereditary rank was bestowed.
The Grand Coordinator of Fújiàn, Wú Yīng, was promoted to General of Awesome Strategy.
Gāo Tiānjué, a Salt Commissioner who died in the rebellion, was posthumously granted an official rank,
and given the posthumous epithet Zhōngliè.
Dáěrzhàn was appointed General of Jīngzhōu.
In the sixth month, on the *dīnghài* day,
the Emperor toured beyond the frontier.
Cháo Kětuō was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left,
and Guō Shìlóng was reinstated as Governor-General of Húguǎng.
In the seventh month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
the Emperor resided in Rèhé.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the imperial carriage departed Kālāhétún,
to tour various Měnggǔ tribes.
The outer vassal states came to court,
and each was bestowed clothing and silk.
In the eighth month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
the Emperor arrived at Táobìlā,
and bestowed silver and silk upon the Solon commanders Sèyīnchákè and Dùlātú, and the hunters, who welcomed the imperial carriage.
The Miáo people of Sānjiāng in Guìzhōu rebelled,
and they were suppressed.
In the ninth month, on the *guǐhài* day,
the Emperor resided in HéěrbóTúgáchà.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Emperor reviewed the archery of the Cháhāěr and Bāěrhǔ soldiers.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *xīnsì* day,
due to drought in Jiāngsū and Zhèjiāng,
treasury funds were allocated to purchase and stabilize grain prices,
grain tribute was diverted for famine relief,
and outstanding taxes were remitted.
Outer vassal states offered camels and horses,
but these were declined.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Ministry of Revenue discussed increasing the mining tax in Yúnnán,
but it was ordered to remain at the old rate.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Jīn Shìróng was dismissed,
and Xiāo Yǒngzǎo was appointed Minister of War.
In the eleventh month, on the *jǐyǒu* day, the first day of the month,
an edict stated:
“Recently, due to drought disasters in Jiāngnán and Zhèjiāng,
朕 immediately ordered tax reductions, remission of arrears, and diversion of grain tribute.
All poll taxes due from the two provinces of Jiāngnán and Zhèjiāng next year
shall be completely remitted.
In the affected areas,
the main land tax shall also be remitted.
Thus, within one year,
the common people shall have no need to appear in public courts,
and may live and work in peace,
fulfilling 朕's profound intention of loving and benefiting the populace.”
On the *jǐwèi* day,
an edict stated that people from Táiwān lacking food,
who wished to return, were permitted to cross on public ships.
Wāng Wùlǐ was appointed Manchu General.
On the *jǐhài* day,
an edict ordered the various prefectures and counties of Jiāngnán and Zhèjiāng to undertake water conservancy projects to prepare for droughts and floods.
In the twelfth month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
Wēndá was appointed Grand Secretary,
Mǎěrhàn was appointed Minister of Personnel,
Gěngé was appointed Minister of War,
Cháo Kětuō was appointed Minister of Punishments,
Fùníngān and Wáng Jiǔlíng were appointed Censors-in-Chief of the Left.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
princes, ministers, and imperial guards were granted varying amounts of silver.
In this year,
the disaster taxes of thirty-two prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Jiāngxī, Fújiàn, Húguǎng, and other provinces were remitted to varying degrees.
Cháoxiǎn and Líuqiú offered tribute.
In the forty-seventh year, *wùzǐ* year, in spring, the first month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
the bandits Zhāng Niànyī and Zhū Sān from Dàlán Shān in Zhèjiāng raided Cíxī, Shàngyú, and Shèngxiàn;
government troops captured and pacified them.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the reconstruction of Nányuè Temple was completed,
and the Emperor personally composed the inscription.
Juéluó Mèngélò was appointed General of Fèngtiān.
On the *yǐhài* day,
an edict ordered the retention of four hundred thousand *shí* of grain tribute from Húguǎng and Jiāngxī,
to be used for stabilizing grain prices in the six prefectures of Jiāngnán.
In the second month, on the *gēngyín* day,
the Emperor attended the Imperial Lectures.
On the *rénchén* day,
Secretary Mùdān was dispatched to investigate the Dàlán Shān case,
and academician È'gé was dispatched to investigate the Hóngmiáo case.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Emperor toured the imperial domains.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
an edict stated that Siāmluó envoys carrying local products
were permitted to trade anywhere,
and their taxes were remitted.
In the third month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
the Emperor returned to reside at Chàngchūnyuán.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Xīsīhā and Lǐ Shéngzōng were appointed Manchu Generals.
In the intercalary third month, on the *wùyín* day, the first day of the month,
the reconstruction of Běizhèn Temple was completed,
and the Emperor personally composed the inscription.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Shī Shìbiāo was appointed Grand Coordinator of Guǎngdōng,
and Xí Zhù was appointed General of Xī'ān.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
Sòng Luò was dismissed,
Xú Cháo was appointed Minister of Personnel,
and Qí Shìwǔ was appointed Governor-General of Sìchuān and Shǎnxī.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Zhào Shìxiǎn, the Provincial Governor of Shāndōng, reported the capture of Zhū Sān and his son,
and they were sent to Zhèjiāng.
The Emperor said:
“Zhū Sān and his son traveled around teaching and
lived off others.
If they are arrested on this account,
too many people would be implicated,
so this order should be conveyed.”
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Yú Yìmó, the Grand Coordinator of Húguǎng, secretly requested to suppress the Hóngmiáo.
The Emperor did not allow it,
as the Hóngmiáo had committed no major crimes.
Ālànà was appointed Měnggǔ General,
and Lǐ Línsheng was appointed Manchu General.
Inner Grand Secretary Míngzhū died,
and the Third Prince Yìnzhǐ was ordered to offer tea and wine,
and four horses were bestowed.
In the fifth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
Wáng Hóngxù was appointed Minister of Revenue,
Fùníngān was appointed Minister of Rites,
and Mùhélún was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Emperor toured beyond the frontier.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
an edict remitted the crime of implication for Wáng Zhāojùn and his uncles, brothers, and nephews, natives of Tàicāng, who were members of the Dàlán Shān bandit group.
In the sixth month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
the Emperor resided in Rèhé.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Nine Ministers discussed and reported on the Dàlán Shān case,
and received the imperial decree:
“Those who were the principal culprits shall be executed.
Zhū Sān and his son are unforgivable,
but those implicated can have their sentences changed to exile.
Provincial Governor Wáng Rán and Grand Coordinator Wáng Shìchén shall both remain in their posts,
and injured officers and soldiers shall all be compensated.”
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the *Qīngwén Jiàn* was completed,
and the Emperor personally composed the preface.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Ministry of Punishments was ordered
to exempt from execution those who had committed crimes while in exile for capital offenses.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the *Píngdìng Shuòmò Fānglüè* was completed,
and the Emperor personally composed the preface.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Emperor went on a hunting expedition.
È'gé reported that Liáo Lǎozǎi and others who had killed people in the Hóngmiáo case were to be beheaded and their heads displayed,
and Guard Commander Wáng Yìngruì, who had unauthorizedly dispatched troops to the Miáo village, was to be exiled;
this was approved.
In the eighth month, on the *jiǎchén* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *rénxū* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital,
residing in Yǒng'ānbàiyáng'ā.
In the ninth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
the Emperor resided at Bù'ěrhāsūtái.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
he summoned his court officials to the temporary imperial residence,
proclaimed the crimes of Crown Prince Yìnréng,
ordered his arrest and detention,
and sent him to the capital for imprisonment.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Crown Prince Yìnréng was deposed,
and an edict was issued to the empire.
In the winter, tenth month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
Bèilè Yìnsì was stripped of his title.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Wáng Shàn was appointed Minister of Works (*Gōngbù Shàngshū*),
and Zhāng Pénghé was appointed Minister of Punishments (*Xíngbù Shàngshū*).
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the Emperor went to the Southern Park for a hunt.
Xīn Tài was appointed Mongol commander-in-chief (*Ménggǔ Dūlǒng*).
In the eleventh month, on the first day, *guǐyǒu*,
Zhíjùnwáng Yìnzhī was stripped of his title
and imprisoned.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Grand Secretary (*Dàxuéshì*) Zhāng Yīng, who had retired, died.
Sacrificial rites and a burial were granted,
and he was posthumously granted the title Wénduān.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Vice Censor-in-Chief (*Fù Dūyùshǐ*) Láo Zhībiàn memorialized, requesting the reinstatement of the deposed Crown Prince.
He was stripped of his office and flogged.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
court officials were summoned to discuss the establishment of a successor.
Ālíng'ā, Èlúndài, Kuí, Wáng Hóngxù, and other high officials requested the Eighth Prince Yìnsì.
The Emperor did not approve.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the deposed Crown Prince Yìnréng was released.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
princes and high officials requested the re-establishment of Yìnréng as Crown Prince.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Fā Dù, a member of the imperial clan, was appointed General of Hēilóngjiāng.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Yìnsì was reinstated as Bèilè.
In the twelfth month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
sacrificial stipends were given to the deceased scholars Jī Yǒngrén, Wáng Lóngguāng, Shěn Tiānchéng, and Fàn Chéngpǔ, who had died in hardship.
They were to be venerated in Fàn Chéngmó's ancestral shrine,
as requested by Fàn Chéngmó's son, Governor Fàn Shíchóng.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Chén Shēn was appointed Governor of Húguǎng,
Jiǎng Chénxī as Governor of Shāndōng,
Huáng Bǐngzhōng as Governor of Zhèjiāng,
and Liú Yìnshū as Governor of Guìzhōu.
That year,
tax exemptions of varying degrees were granted to sixty prefectures and counties in disaster-stricken provinces such as Shāndōng, Fújiàn, and Húguǎng.
Cháoxiǎn offered tribute.
In the 48th year, the *jǐchǒu* year, in spring, the first month, on the *guǐsì* day,
court officials were summoned and questioned about who had initiated the proposal to establish Yìnsì.
The officials were terrified and dared not answer.
Then Grand Secretary Zhāng Yùshū was brought forward and questioned,
to which he replied:
"I first heard of it from Mǎ Qí."
The Emperor severely reprimanded him.
The next day,
Mǎ Qí's crimes were listed,
and he was pardoned from death but detained.
Later, the Emperor gradually investigated and found him to have been slandered,
and released him.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the Emperor went to the Southern Park.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Vice Minister (*Shìláng*) Hè Shòu was ordered to reside in Zàng,
to assist in Tibetan affairs.
Initially, Lāzàng Hán and Qīnghǎi disputed the establishment of the Dálài Lǎma.
The matter remained unresolved,
so special ministers were sent to supervise it.
Wáng Hóngxù and Lǐ Zhènyù were exempted.
In the second month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor toured the imperial environs.
Yáng Fú, a member of the imperial clan, was appointed General of Hēilóngjiāng,
Juéluó Méng'éluò as General of Nínggǔtǎ,
and Wáng Wényì as Provincial Military Commander (*Tídū*) of Guìzhōu.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Sōng Zhù was appointed acting General of Fèngtiān.
On the *wùchén* day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Zhāng Pénghé was appointed Minister of Revenue (*Hùbù Shàngshū*),
and Zhāng Tíngshū as Minister of Punishments (*Xíngbù Shàngshū*).
In the third month, on the *xīnsì* day,
Yìnréng was re-established as Crown Prince,
announced to the imperial ancestral temple,
and an edict was issued to the empire.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Zhào Xióngzhào and 292 others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with varying ranks.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
Fùníng'ān was appointed Minister of Personnel (*Lìbù Shàngshū*),
Mùhélún as Minister of Rites (*Lǐbù Shàngshū*),
and Mùdān as Left Censor-in-Chief (*Zuǒ Dūyùshǐ*).
Yìnzhī was transferred to a public office for imprisonment,
and officials were dispatched with troops to guard him.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor toured outside the passes.
In the fifth month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
the Emperor stayed at Rèhé.
In the sixth month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
Kāngqīnwáng Chūntài died.
He was posthumously granted the title Dào.
His son Chóng'ān inherited the title.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *gēngyín* day,
Yīn Tài was appointed Governor-General (*Zǒngdū*) of Sìchuān and Shǎnxī,
Gálǐ as Governor-General of Jiāngnán and Jiāngxī,
Jiāng Qí as Provincial Military Commander (*Tídū*) of Gānsù,
and Shī Yìdé as Provincial Military Commander of Jiāngnán.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Emperor went hunting.
In the eighth month, on the first day, *jǐhài*,
there was a solar eclipse.
Pān Yùlóng, Provincial Military Commander of Shǎnxī, was granted the title Zhènsuí Jiāngjūn.
In the ninth month, on the *gēngyín* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
Nián Gēngyáo was appointed Governor of Sìchuān.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *rényín* day,
an edict was issued for the Governors-General and Governors of Fújiàn and Guǎngdōng to recommend those deeply knowledgeable in water skills and familiar with naval affairs.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the Third Prince Yìnzhǐ was enfeoffed as Chéngqīnwáng,
the Fourth Prince Yìnzhēn as Yōngqīnwáng,
the Fifth Prince Yìnqí as Héngqīnwáng,
the Seventh Prince Yìnyòu as Chúnjùnwáng,
the Tenth Prince Yìn'è as Dūnjùnwáng,
and the Ninth Prince Yìnchén, Twelfth Prince Yìntáo, and Fourteenth Prince Yìntí were all enfeoffed as Bèilè.
On the *rénxū* day,
an edict exempted Huái, Yáng, and Xú in disaster-stricken Jiāngsū,
Yǎnzhōu in Shāndōng,
and Guīdé in Hénán from the land and poll taxes for the following year.
In the eleventh month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
an edict stated that if the funds remitted by various provinces to the Board were excessive,
a suitable portion could be retained
for urgent needs.
Ānjùnwáng Mǎ'ěrhún died.
He was posthumously granted the title Huī,
and his son Huá inherited.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Sāng'é, Governor-General of Grain Transport (*Cáoyùn Zǒngdū*), was granted the title Tàizǐ Tàibǎo.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Emperor discussed with Grand Secretary Lǐ Guāngdì about water veins and sources,
mentioning that Mount Tài, Mount Dài, and other mountains originated from Mount Chángbái.
The Jǐ River flowed underground,
and the Yellow River also flowed underground before reaching Jīshí,
which Mongolians had written about in great detail.
The source of the Jiāng River also came from Kūnlún,
but it did not flow underground once it reached Mínshān.
Zhāng Pénghé and Gámǐntú were dispatched to investigate Yí Sīgōng's case of embezzlement in Jiāngnán.
In the twelfth month, on the *jǐhài* day,
the Emperor visited the imperial tombs.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
Mǎ Qí was ordered to manage the trade with Èluósī.
Minister of Punishments (*Xíngbù Shàngshū*) Cháo Kětuō was dismissed.
That year,
tax exemptions of varying degrees were granted to fifty-three prefectures and counties in disaster-stricken provinces such as Zhílì, Jiāngsū, Ānhuī, Shāndōng, Hénán, and Húguǎng.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú offered tribute.
In the 49th year, the *gēngyín* year, in spring, the first month, on the *gēngyín* day,
an order was given to compile the Mǎn-Méng Hébì Qīngwénjiàn.
In the second month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
the Emperor toured Mount Wǔtái.
Minister of Personnel (*Lìbù Shàngshū*) Xú Cháo requested retirement,
which was granted.
In the third month, on the *jǐsì* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *yǐhài* day,
an order was given to compile a dictionary.

An edict promoted Lǐ Mǐnqǐ, the legitimate grandson of the late Grand Secretary Lǐ Wèi and a director (*Zhǔshì*), to be Assistant Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices (*Tàichángsì Shàoshēng*).
On the *wùyín* day,
an imperial decree enfeoffed Húbì'ěrhán Bōkètǎ of Xīzàng as the Sixth Dálài Lǎma.
On the *xīnsì* day,
an edict exempted the two prefectures of Háng and Hú in Zhèjiāng from unpaid grain tribute of over 39,000 *shí*.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *yǐsì* day,
Xiāo Yǒngzǎo was transferred to be Minister of Personnel (*Lìbù Shàngshū*),
and Wáng Shàn was transferred to be Minister of War (*Bīngbù Shàngshū*).
In the fifth month, on the first day, *jǐyǒu*,
the Emperor toured outside the passes.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
he stopped at Huāyùgōu.
He reviewed the officials and soldiers of Jílín and Hēilóngjiāng.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Emperor resided at Rèhé.
In the sixth month, on the *jǐhài* day,
the imperial princes were ordered to respectfully welcome the Empress Dowager to Rèhé for summer retreat.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Minister of Punishments (*Xíngbù Shàngshū*) Zhāng Tíngshū was dismissed.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
Xiāo Yǒngzǎo, Minister investigating affairs in Húnán, and others reported on the mutual impeachment case between the Governor and Provincial Military Commander.
The investigation confirmed the facts.
An imperial edict was issued:
"Yú Yìmó is to retire,
Zhào Shēnqiáo is to be dismissed from office but retained in his post."
In the intercalary seventh month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
the Emperor went hunting.
In the eighth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
an edict was issued concerning the drought in Fújiàn’s Zhāng and Quán prefectures.
Thirty *wàn* *shí* of grain were transported from the Jiāng and Zhè regions to relieve them,
and the outstanding taxes for the current year were all remitted.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Emperor returned to reside at Rèhé.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Fàn Shíchóng was appointed Governor-General of Fújiàn and Zhèjiāng,
and Élúntè was appointed Provincial Military Commander of Húnán.
In the ninth month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, returned to the palace.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Xīfúnà was dismissed.
At this time, it was discovered that the Board of Revenue had suffered a deficit in the purchase of fodder for over ten years.
Over a period of ten years,
one hundred and twenty successive Ministers and Vice Ministers were involved,
with the deficit amounting to over forty *wàn*.
The Emperor leniently waived arrest and interrogation,
setting a deadline for repayment.
Xīfúnà, being the current Minister,
was specifically reprimanded.
Mùhélún was appointed Minister of the Board of Revenue,
and Bèihénuò was appointed Minister of the Board of Rites.
In the tenth month of winter, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an edict stated:
“I have ruled the realm for nearly fifty years,
sincerely believing that the people are the foundation of the state,
and governance lies in nurturing the people.
I have repeatedly remitted hundreds of millions in taxes,
using the savings from frugality
to provide vast relief.
However, upon observing the people’s livelihood,
it is not yet entirely prosperous,
largely due to the daily increase in population,
while the land does not expand.
It is fitting to bestow great benevolence
to cultivate the people’s strength.
Starting from the 50th year of Kāngxī,
all land and poll taxes throughout the realm shall be universally remitted,
to be completed over three years.
The land and poll taxes of Zhílì, Fèngtiān, Zhèjiāng, Fújiàn, Guǎngdōng, Guǎngxī, Sìchuān, Yúnnán, and Guìzhōu—nine provinces in total—
shall be fully remitted after investigation.
All accumulated arrears from past years
shall be uniformly waived.
For the provinces due for remission in the 51st and 52nd years,
edicts will be issued at the appropriate time.
Great officials in the provinces, as well as prefects and magistrates, must embody my desire to protect and govern,
and genuinely cherish and nurture the people,
so that peace and prosperity may truly be manifested.”
“Upon receipt of this document,
it shall be engraved and promulgated,
making it known to all.”
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
an imperial instruction was issued that as the outer vassal states had already paid their respects at the traveling palace,
there was no need for them to attend the formal court.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Guō Lì was appointed Governor-General of Yúnnán and Guìzhōu,
Guō Shìlóng was appointed Minister of the Board of Punishments,
and Èhǎi was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the Emperor instructed the Grand Secretaries:
“The deficit in land and poll taxes in Jiāngnán amounts to several hundred thousand *liǎng*.
This may be due to my several southern tours,
where funds were diverted by local authorities.
Zhāng Pénghé suggested that salaries and construction funds could make up the difference.
However, if local officials have no salaries,
it will still burden the people.
It would be better to remit these.
Discuss this and report back.”
In the eleventh month, on the *xīnmǎo* day (the first day of the month),
an edict stipulated that in years of tax remission,
seven-tenths should be remitted for landowners,
and three-tenths for tenants.
This was to be established as a permanent regulation.
Grand Secretary Chén Tíngjìng requested retirement due to old age.
A warm imperial decree offered comfort and instruction,
ordering him to retire.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Emperor visited the imperial tombs.
Xiāo Yǒngzǎo was appointed Grand Secretary,
Wáng Yàn was appointed Minister of the Board of Rites,
and Xú Yuánzhèng was appointed Minister of the Board of Works.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Sūn Zhēnghào was appointed Minister of the Board of War.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Sāng’é was appointed Minister of the Board of Civil Office.
In the twelfth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
Hèshòu was appointed Governor-General of Grand Canal Transport.
On the *wùyín* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *xīnsì* day,
an edict stated:
“As the old officials in the court gradually decline,
there are not many *jìnshì* from the Shùnzhì reign who have retired from office and returned to their native places.
Wáng Shìzhēn, Jiāng Gāo, Zhōu Mǐnzhèng, Yè Jiǎorán, and Xú Shújiā, all of whom were dismissed due to public misconduct,
are hereby reinstated to their original official positions.”
Zhào Shēnjiáo was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
This year,
the disaster taxes in seven prefectures and counties in Zhílì, Jiāngnán, and other provinces were remitted by varying amounts.
Cháoxiǎn and Ānnán paid tribute.
In the first month, on the *guǐchǒu* day of spring in the 50th year,
the Emperor toured the imperial demesne
to inspect the river dikes at Tōngzhōu.
In the second month, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
Bāndí was appointed Manchu Grand Commander,
and Shàndān was appointed Mongol Grand Commander.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
he inspected Kuāng’érgǎng
and ordered the construction of a water-diverting dam.
Upon arriving at Héxīwù,
the Emperor disembarked and walked for about two *lǐ*,
personally placing instruments,
determining directions,
and driving in stakes
to mark the measurement points.
He issued an instruction saying:
“Using this method, one can measure heaven and earth, and solar and lunar eclipses.
The calculation method originated from the *Yì*.
When using the odd numbers seven and nine,
if they are insufficient,
use the even numbers twelve and twenty-four to complete it,
which symbolizes the twelve hours and twenty-four solar terms.”
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the Emperor presided over the Imperial Lecture.
In the third month, on the *gēngyín* day,
the princes and high ministers requested an honorific title for the Emperor on his birthday.
Since the pacification of Diān,
this was the fourth such request.
The Emperor, being humble by nature,
never consented.
In the fourth month of summer, on the *gēngshēn* day,
Xú Yuánzhèng returned to his hometown to care for his parents,
and Chén Shēn was appointed Minister of the Board of Works.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, went to Rèhé to escape the summer heat.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Board of Rites was ordered to pray for rain.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
there was heavy rain.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Grand Secretary Zhāng Yùshū, who remained in the capital, passed away.
The Emperor lamented and grieved,
composed a poem,
dispatched officials to oversee the funeral,
bestowed one thousand *liǎng* of silver,
added rituals for sacrifice and burial,
and granted the posthumous title Wénzhēn.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
an edict remitted over one hundred thousand *liǎng* of unaccounted silver in Jiāngsū.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
retired Grand Secretary Chén Tíngjìng was summoned to the cabinet to handle affairs.
The quota for the Five Classics in the provincial and metropolitan examinations was increased.
In the sixth month, on the *wùchén* day,
a Confucian instructor was established for Xīlóng Zhōu in Guǎngxī.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *bǐngchén* day,
the Emperor went on a hunting expedition.
In the eighth month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
Gāozōng Chún Huángdì was born.
Wáng Yuánqí was appointed President of the Hanlin Academy.
A Five Classics Scholar position was established for the descendants of the worthy sage Zǐyóu.
In the ninth month, on the *wùshēn* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, returned to the palace.
Lán Lǐ was dismissed for wrongdoing.
Yáng Lín was appointed Provincial Military Commander of Fújiàn (land forces),
and Mǎ Jìbó was appointed Provincial Military Commander of Sìchuān.
This year's autumn executions were suspended.
In the tenth month of winter, on the *bǐngchén* day,
an edict remitted the rice taxes due in Táiwān for the 51st year.
Bèihénuò was dismissed,
and Sōngzhù was appointed Minister of the Board of Rites.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
an edict reiterated the previous decree for universal remission of land and poll taxes.
In the 51st year, this was to be extended to the six provinces of Shānxī, Hénán, Shǎnxī, Gānsù, Húběi, and Húnán.
Their land and poll taxes and all arrears were to be remitted.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Shuònài was appointed Manchu Grand Commander,
and Húshìbā and Mǎ’ěrsài were appointed Mongol Grand Commanders.
On the *wùyín* day,
the annual tribute of white gold and leopard skins from Cháoxiǎn was waived.
On the *gēngchén* day,
an edict was issued to commend filial piety and righteousness.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Zhāng Pénghé was ordered to preside over a court case in Yángzhōu
to investigate the Jiāngnán examination scandal.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
È Shàn, Gěng É, Qí Shìwǔ, Wùlǐ, and others were found guilty
and stripped of their posts and imprisoned.
Zhào Shēnjiáo submitted a memorial impeaching Dài Míngshì, a newly appointed compiler, for being arrogant and unrestrained due to his talent,
and for uttering many rebellious remarks.
The case was sent to the Board for strict interrogation.
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngxū,
Yīn Tèbù was appointed Governor-General of the Hàn Army,
Lóng Kēduō was appointed Commander of the Infantry,
and Zhāng Gǔzhēn was appointed Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Yúnnán.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Emperor visited the imperial tombs,
and bestowed horses and silver upon the officials and servants guarding them.
In the twelfth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the day Guǐwèi,
a grand ancestral sacrifice was held at the Tàimiào.
This year,
tax exemptions, varying in degree, were granted to eight prefectures and counties in the calamity-stricken provinces of Zhílì, Ānhuī, and others.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú paid tribute.
The number of households was 24,621,324.
The amount of land was 6,930,344 qǐng and 34 mù.
The silver collected in taxes amounted to 29,904,652 liǎng and 8 qián.
The salt tax silver was 3,729,228 liǎng.
The number of coins minted was 37,493,340,000 and some odd.
In the fifty-first year, on the day Rénchén, in the spring, first month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
Compiler Zhāng Yìshào was promoted to Academician-in-waiting of the Hànlín Academy.
He was the son of the late Grand Secretary Zhāng Yùshū.
On the day Rénzǐ,
ministers both inside and outside the court were ordered to submit memorials detailing affairs.
The practice of submitting memorials (zhé zòu) began from this point.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Emperor went on an inspection tour of the Jīdiàn region.
An edict stated that Fèi Yánggǔ, a prince of the imperial clan and General of the Right Guard, handled affairs with sincerity,
had served for many years,
and moreover, being a prince,
could be ennobled as Fǔguó Gōng.
In the second month, on the day Dīngsì,
an edict ordered that the Sòng scholar Zhūzǐ be accorded a shared sacrifice at the Kǒng Temple,
ranking next to the Ten Sages.
Zhāng Bóxíng, Governor of Jiāngsū, and Gǎ Lǐ, Governor-General, mutually impeached each other,
were both dismissed from their posts,
and handed over to Zhāng Pénghé and Hè Shòu for investigation and trial.
Fàn Shíchóng, Governor-General of Fújiàn and Zhèjiāng, memorialized that coastal fishing boats
should only be allowed to have a single mast,
and should not be permitted to travel across provinces,
and that local civil and military officials should control them.
The Emperor said:
"This matter is impractical.
If fishing households are incorporated into the naval camps,
then military personnel will exploit them.
How can all bandits be eliminated?
Where are there no occasional outbreaks of theft?
Only implement what benefits the people;
one should not use legal provisions as tools for oppression."
On the day Wùyín,
outstanding military officials were ordered to be introduced for an audience in the same manner as civil officials.
On the day Gēngchén,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Rénwǔ,
an edict stated:
"Peace has prevailed for a long time,
and the population has grown daily.
Henceforth, newly born individuals
need not pay additional poll tax;
the number of adult males this year shall be set as the fixed quota,
and this shall be made law."
In the third month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
the Grand Secretaries were instructed:
"The translation of memorials
is of great importance.
Yesterday, I saw the two characters 'jiǎ guān' (false official)
within a memorial,
translated as 'wěi guān' (traitorous official),
which is a serious error.
Strictly admonish them."
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the Emperor attended the Jīngyán lecture.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Dīngsì,
Wáng Shìchēn and 177 others were granted the jinshì degree, varying in rank.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Kāng Tàipíng was appointed Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Sìchuān.
The rule for the provincial allocation of successful candidates in the metropolitan examination was established.
On the day Rénshēn,
an imperial decree stated:
"The late Grand Secretary Xióng Cìlǚ was a scholar of profound learning and an old minister.
Since his death,
he has often been remembered.
Hearing that his son has grown to adulthood,
he may be ordered to come to the capital for employment."
On the day Rénxū,
the late First Class Imperial Guard Hǎi Qīng was granted the title of Deputy Lieutenant-General,
and was given offerings and burial,
with the posthumous title Guǒyì.
The retired Grand Secretary Chén Tíngjìng passed away.
The third imperial son was ordered to offer tea and wine,
the Emperor composed an elegy,
and ordered the Hànlín scholars Lì Tíngyí and Zhāng Tíngyù from the Nánshūfáng to burn it as an offering.
One thousand liǎng of silver were granted for the funeral expenses,
and he was given the posthumous title Wénzhēn.
An edict announced that for the Emperor's 60th birthday next year,
a special provincial examination would be held in the second month,
and a metropolitan examination in the eighth month.
Sōng Zhù was appointed Grand Secretary,
Hēi Shuòzī was appointed Minister of Rites,
Mǎn Dù was appointed Minister of Works.
Wáng Zhǎn was appointed Grand Secretary,
Chén Shēn was appointed Minister of Rites,
and Zhāng Tíngshū was reinstated as Minister of Works.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, departed for Rèhé to escape the summer heat.
The imperial procession set out.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Emperor resided at Rèhé.
In the fifth month, on the day Rénchén,
officials were ordered to investigate migrants who moved to the frontier to cultivate land.
Mù Dān was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left,
and È Dài was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Mongol Banner Forces.
In the sixth month, on the first day Guǐchǒu,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Dīngsì,
Mù Hélún and Zhāng Tíngshū were ordered to re-examine the case of mutual impeachment between the Governor-General and Governor of Jiāngnán.
Wú Lǎohuà, the leader of the Red Miáo in Zhènggān, Húguǎng, along with 52 villages including Máodū Táng, submitted to allegiance.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Zhāng Cháowǔ was appointed Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Guǎngxī.
In the autumn, eighth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
the Emperor went on an imperial hunt.
On the day Wùyín,
an edict allowed Cháoxiǎn, if Chinese fishing boats violated prohibitions and entered their border waters,
to detain them and report the matter.
Eighty-three more Miáo villages in Zhènggān submitted to allegiance.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngxū,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, returned to the palace.
Crown Prince Yìnréng was again deposed due to his crimes,
and imprisoned in the Xián'ān Palace.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Rénxū,
Mù Hélún and others reported on the re-examination of the Jiāngnán case.
The Emperor ordered the dismissal of Gǎ Lǐ,
and Zhāng Bóxíng was reinstated.
Kuí was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left,
and Hè Shòu was appointed Governor-General of Jiāngnán and Jiāngxī.
In the eleventh month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
the case of former Fújiàn Provincial Commander-in-Chief Lán Lǐ was concluded,
and he was sentenced to death.
The Emperor, remembering his meritorious service in the conquest of Táiwān,
specifically pardoned him.
On the day Jǐhài,
ministers requested to confer an honorable title upon the Emperor for his 60th birthday,
but he refused.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the re-deposition of Crown Prince Yìnréng was announced at the ancestral temple,
and declared throughout the realm.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
the Emperor visited the imperial tombs,
and bestowed silver upon the ministers guarding them.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎxū,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
This year,
tax exemptions, varying in degree, were granted to 23 prefectures and counties in the calamity-stricken provinces of Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Shāndōng, Zhèjiāng, and others.
Cháoxiǎn paid tribute.
In the fifty-second year, on the day Guǐsì, in the spring, first month, on the day Wùshēn,
an edict enfeoffed the Bānchán Hútúkètú Lama of Hòucáng as Bānchán É'ěrdéní.
In the second month, on the day Gēngxū,
Zhào Shēnqiáo memorialized that the Crown Prince was the foundation of the state,
and should be formally enthroned.
The Emperor, considering the establishment of an heir a momentous affair not to be decided lightly,
issued an imperial instruction to the court ministers,
and returned the original memorial to him.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the Emperor went on an inspection tour of the Jīdiàn region.
Compiler Dài Míngshì was executed in the marketplace for his madly rebellious writings.
Jinshì Fāng Bāo, implicated for writing a preface,
was spared death and enrolled in a Banner,
then later pardoned and released.
On the day Yǐhài,
the Emperor returned and resided at the Chàngchūnyuán.
On the *wùyín* day of the third month, the first day of the lunar month,
an edict was issued to the princes and high ministers:
"Yesterday, when Zhèn returned to the capital,
I saw countless people praying for Zhèn's protection and blessings
in various places,
which truly made me feel ashamed and embarrassed.
The peace of all nations
is Zhèn's peace;
the happiness of all under Heaven
is Zhèn's happiness.
Those who pray for longevity should prioritize this.
Zhèn is old now,
and the thought of 'standing on the edge of a deep abyss and treading on thin ice'
grows day by day.
How dare I become complacent?"
Another edict said:
"There are extremely many elderly people in the various provinces who are celebrating longevity.
Should one or two of them be unwell,
imperial physicians may be sent to treat them.
Zhèn will enter the palace's Buddhist pavilion on the seventeenth,
and the elders have already been able to respectfully observe and pay respects at their leisure.
On the eighteenth, the rites will be performed at Zhèngyángmén;
there is no need to come again to the Imperial Pavilion.
Let officials of Hàn ethnicity in the various provinces be informed of this edict."
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
Officials and common people from the various provinces prostrated themselves along the roads to welcome him.
The Emperor stopped his carriage to comfort them.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Longevity Festival,
the Emperor held court at Cínínggōng,
and presided over Tàihédiàn to receive congratulations.
He issued an imperial edict extending grace,
bestowing gifts upon the aged,
exalting recluses,
honoring filial piety and righteousness,
remitting overdue taxes and debts,
providing for widows, widowers, orphans, and the helpless,
with officials arranging their support.
Crimes not meriting capital punishment
were all pardoned.
On the *rényín* day,
officials, scholars, and commoners aged sixty-five and above from the direct provinces were summoned
to a banquet at Chàngchūnyuán.
The Imperial Princes supervised the meals,
and Imperial Clansmen served drinks.
Elders aged eighty and above were assisted to the front,
and the Emperor personally watched them drink.
He instructed them, saying:
"In ancient times, providing for the aged and honoring the virtuous was paramount.
If everyone knows filial piety and fraternity,
then customs will be wholesome.
You elders should convey this sentiment to your villages.
Yesterday, there was heavy rain,
and the fields are sufficiently watered.
You should return quickly,
without delaying agricultural work."
On that day,
thirty-three people aged ninety and above,
and five hundred thirty-eight people aged eighty and above,
were each granted silver.
The elderly ministers Sòng Luò and Tián Zhǒngyù were additionally blessed with titles: Sòng Luò as Tàizǐ Shǎoshī,
and Tián Zhǒngyù as Tàizǐ Shǎofù.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
officials, soldiers, and idle personnel of the Eight Banners were banqueted at Chàngchūnyuán,
with the supervision of meals, serving of drinks, and granting of silver for drinks being the same as before.
On that day,
there were seven people aged ninety and above,
and one hundred ninety-two people aged eighty and above.
In the summer, on the *jiǎyín* day of the fourth month,
È Hǎi was appointed Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Sìchuān,
Élúntè was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng,
and Gāo Qíwèi was appointed Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Húguǎng.
Yuè Shēnglóng, Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Sìchuān, requested to be registered as a native of Sìchuān,
which was granted.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
officials were dispatched to offer sacrifices to mountains and rivers, ancient imperial tombs, and Quèlǐ.
In the fifth month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, went to Rèhé to escape the summer heat.
Zhāng Tíngshū was transferred to be President of the Board of Punishments,
and Wáng Xùlíng was appointed President of the Board of Works.
Silver was bestowed upon Mongolian elders.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
an edict ordered the suspension of this year's autumn assizes.
In the intercalary fifth month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
silver was bestowed upon elders in Rèhé.
Censor Chén Rǔxián recruited and brought the sea pirate Chén Shàngyì for an audience.
He was questioned about the maritime situation and the design of foreign ships,
and was ordered to be settled in Jīnzhōu,
where a naval camp was established.
In the sixth month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
mathematical treatises on temperament were revised.
In the autumn, on the *rénzǐ* day of the seventh month,
an edict commanded that the descendants of imperial clan members who had been expelled from the imperial genealogy
be distinguished by wearing red or purple sashes,
and their names recorded in the Imperial Genealogy (Yùdié).
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Emperor went hunting.
In the eighth month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
Sōng'ālābù, the Prince of the Mongolian È'ěrdūs, requested to graze his herds at Cháhàntuōhuī.
This was not permitted.
It was ordered that grazing be bounded by the Yellow River,
following the request of Commander-in-Chief Fàn Shíjié.
In the ninth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, returned to the palace.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
one hundred thousand *shí* of grain tribute from Jiāngnán was allocated for transport to Guǎngdōng and Fújiàn for sale at stable prices.
In the winter, on the *bǐngzǐ* day of the tenth month,
Zhāng Pénghé was appointed President of the Board of Civil Office.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Wáng Jìngmíng and one hundred forty-three other individuals were granted the *jìnshì jíde chūshēn* (various ranks of *jìnshì* degree).
In the eleventh month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
an edict exempted twenty-one prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Guǎngdōng, Fújiàn, and Gānsù from next year's land tax.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Emperor visited the imperial tombs.
In the twelfth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
Hèyì was appointed President of the Board of Works.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
those who wished to take both the civil and military examinations
were permitted to change to one examination.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Wǔgé was appointed Mongolian Military Governor.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the combined ancestral sacrifice was held at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
This year,
calamity taxes were variously remitted in ten prefectures and counties of Zhèjiāng.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú presented tribute.
In the spring of the fifty-third year, *jiǎwǔ*, on the *jǐwèi* day of the first month,
an order was given to repair the musical instruments in the altars, temples, and palace halls.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Board of Revenue requested a ban on small coins.
The Emperor said:
"All matters must aim to benefit the people.
If it does not benefit the people,
and only speaks of enforcing the law,
what good is a severe prohibition?"
On the *wùchén* day,
the Emperor toured the imperial domains.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Hé Tiānpéi was appointed General of Jīngkǒu.
In the second month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
an edict ordered the suspension of this year's autumn assizes.
Suspects whose cases were doubtful
were to be investigated and reported,
and those sentenced to exile or lighter punishments
were to have their sentences reduced.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Vice Minister Cháng Tài and Minor Minister Chén Rǔxián were ordered to Gānsù to provide relief and pacify disaster victims.
On the *dīngsì* day,
former President Wáng Hóngxù presented two hundred eighty volumes of *Míngshǐ Lièzhuàn* (Biographies from the History of the Ming Dynasty),
and it was ordered to be placed in the Imperial Historiography Institute.
In the summer, on the *wùzǐ* day of the fourth month,
Shī Yìdé was appointed Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Gānsù.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, went to Rèhé to escape the summer heat.
In the sixth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
an edict stated:
"Lāzàng Hàn is nearly sixty years old,
and his two sons are abroad.
He should guard against foreign threats
and plan carefully for himself."
On the *guǐwèi* day,
due to the intense heat, the attendance of ministers at evening court was excused.
In the autumn, on the *xīnmǎo* day of the seventh month,
an edict was issued that due to drought in Jiāngnán,
high rice prices in Zhèjiāng,
and poor harvests in Hénán,
three hundred thousand *shí* of grain tribute would be diverted
and transported to the three provinces for sale at stable prices.
In the eighth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
the Emperor went hunting.
In the ninth month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, returned to the palace.
In the winter, on the *jǐsì* day of the tenth month, the first day of the lunar month,
Zhāng Pénghé and Āxī’nài were ordered to investigate the Mǒu Qīnyuán case in Jiāngnán.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Grand Secretaries and Hanlin academicians of the Southern Study were ordered to review and finalize musical scores.
In the eleventh month,
the Board of Revenue was ordered to divert over three hundred thousand *shí* of grain tribute
for famine relief in Jiāngnán and Zhèjiāng.
On the *wùshēn* day,
twenty-eight prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Jìngbiān, Gānsù, were exempted from next year's regular taxes.
Qínwáng Yìnzhǐ and others presented the Emperor's work, *Lǜlǚ Zhèngyì* (Orthodox Meaning of Temperament and Pitch).
An imperial decree was issued:
"The three books on temperament (*lǜlǚ*), calendrical calculations (*lìfǎ*), and arithmetic (*suànfǎ*) will be combined into one work,
named *Lǜlì Yuānyuán* (Origins of Temperament and Calendrical Calculations)."
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Winter Solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Altar of Heaven (Huánqiū),
and new music was played.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the Emperor toured beyond the frontier.
Yǎqíbù, a subordinate of Bèilè Yìn Sì, was executed for his crimes.
Hé Guódòng was dispatched to measure the elevation of the North Star and sun's shadow in provinces such as Guǎngdōng and Yúnnán.
On the *Guǐyǒu* day of the twelfth month,
the Emperor halted at Tèbùkè,
and bestowed silver coins upon the accompanying Mongolian soldiers.
On the *Jǐchǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *Xīnmǎo* day,
nineteen tribes of "raw" *Lāzi* barbarians from beyond the borders of Táo and Mín submitted.
In this year,
taxes were remitted in varying degrees for 122 prefectures and counties in the provinces of Jiāngnán, Hénán, Gānsù, Zhèjiāng, and Húguǎng due to disasters.
Cháoxiān offered tribute.
In the first month, *Jiǎzǐ* day, of the spring of the 54th year, *Yǐwèi*,
the system of passing the imperial examinations based on the Five Classics was suspended.
Àbāgāi Tái jí Démùchǔkè was enfeoffed as Fǔguó Gōng.
An edict declared Bèi Lè Yìn Sī and Yánshòu negligent in their duties,
and their stipends were suspended.
On the *Wùchén* first day of the second month,
Zhāng Bóxíng was dismissed from his post due to an incident,
and the case was handed over to Zhāng Pénghé for investigation.
On the *Jǐsì* day,
Shī Shìlún was appointed Grand Canal Governor.
On the *Xīnwèi* day,
the Emperor toured the imperial environs,
and instructed Governor Zhào Hóngxiè, saying:
"Last year's winter snow was abundant,
and this year's spring rain arrived seasonably,
so the people's fields must have been sown early.
However, I fear the growth might be too vigorous,
which could lead to a 'double blight'.
Inform the farmers that weeding and tilling should be sparse,
to prevent wind and dust."
He further instructed:
"When I tour the imperial environs,
I see that the people's lives are somewhat better than before.
However, there are few who read aloud,
which affects customs.
It is appropriate to establish more charity schools in poor and remote villages,
and encourage reading.
You officials should pay attention to this."
On the *Jiǎwǔ* day,
Dù Chéngsì was appointed Jiāngnán Provincial Commander-in-chief,
and Mù Tíngshì was appointed Fújiàn Land Forces Provincial Commander-in-chief.
On the *Jǐhài* day of the third month,
due to snow disasters in the fourteen banners of the Mongolian Wūlāt and other tribes,
Minister Mùhélún was ordered to transport rice for relief,
and teach them to fish for food.
On the *Gēngzǐ* day,
Zhào Hóngxiè was appointed Zhílì Governor-General,
and concurrently held the post of Governor.
Mùsēn was appointed Nínggǔtǎ General.
On the *Gēngwǔ* day of the fourth month of summer,
Xú Táozhāng and 190 others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with varying ranks.
On the *Jǐmǎo* day,
Shī Yìdé reported that Céwàng Ālābùtǎn's troops had plundered Hāmì,
and Patrol Commander Pān Zhìshàn defeated them.
Ministers Fùníng'ān and General Xízhù were ordered to lead troops to reinforce and suppress,
Qí Lǐdé was sent to Tuīhé,
and Kārkā and others were instructed to prepare troops.
On the *Gēngchén* day,
outer vassal troops were conscripted and gathered at Guīhuà Chéng,
and *Dǎshēng Suǒlún* soldiers were dispatched to Tuīhé.
On the *Jǐchǒu* day,
the Emperor instructed the Council of Grand Ministers:
"I have personally led expeditions beyond the Great Wall,
and am fully aware of the strategic points.
Now, there are three routes for advancing against Céwàng Ālābùtǎn: one directly from Gásī to the source of the Yīlǐ River,
approaching his lair;
one crossing Hāmì and Tǔlǔfān,
deeply penetrating enemy territory;
and one via Kārkā,
to Bókédá Érún Hābì'ěrhàn,
crossing the mountains and securing the passes.
Advancing on all three routes simultaneously,
great success is assured."
On the *Rénwǔ* day,
Grand Canal Governor Láng Tíngjí passed away.
The Emperor praised him for comforting and assisting the transport laborers,
and for ensuring unimpeded transport throughout his tenure.
He was granted sacrifices and a burial,
and posthumously given the epithet Wēnqín.
On the *Xīnmǎo* day,
the Emperor escorted the Empress Dowager to escape the summer heat at Rèhé.
On the *Yǐwèi* day,
Fùníng'ān was ordered to divide his troops to garrison Gásīkǒu,
and Commander-in-chief Lù Zhènyīn was stationed at Hāmì.
On the *Bǐngwǔ* day of the fifth month,
Hēilóngjiāng General Zōngshì Yángfú passed away.
One thousand taels of silver were bestowed,
and Imperial Guard Shàng Chóngyì and Fùsēn were ordered to rush by post to offer sacrifices.
He was posthumously given the epithet Xiāngyì,
and his son Sānguānbǎo was ordered to temporarily assume his father's post.
On the *Wùwǔ* day,
Grand Secretariat Reader Túlǐchēn was sent on an envoy mission to Èluósī,
to prepare troops.
On the *Rénshēn* day of the sixth month,
Commander Túshāi and others were ordered to go to Hútānhéshuò to transport grain.
On the *Jiǎxū* day,
Fùníng'ān and Xízhù submitted a memorial reporting their strategy for advancing troops.
An imperial decree was received,
stating that troops would advance next year.
On the *Dīnghài* day,
Minister of War Sūn Zhēnghào passed away.
Two saddled horses, two unsaddled horses, and five hundred taels of silver were bestowed,
and he was posthumously given the epithet Qīngduān.
On the *Jiǎwǔ* first day of the seventh month of autumn,
Prince Hétuītuī Bóbèi was ordered to pacify Wūliánghǎi.
On the *Xīnyǒu* day,
Prince Fù'ěrdān was ordered to go to Wūlángǔ and other places to establish military agricultural colonies.
On the *Xīnwèi* day of the eighth month,
Grand Secretary Lǐ Guāngdì requested leave to return home,
and the Emperor composed a poem to see him off.
On the *Guǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor went hunting.
On the *Rénchén* day,
the garrison troops at Gásīkǒu were withdrawn to Sùzhōu.
On the *Jǐyǒu* day of the ninth month,
Bóbèi pacified the Wūliánghǎi tribe, and they submitted.
On the *Bǐngyín* day of the tenth month of winter,
the Emperor instructed the Grand Secretaries:
"My right hand is ill and cannot write,
so I use my left hand to hold the brush and endorse memorials,
to ensure no leaks."
On the *Xīnsì* day,
the Emperor escorted the Empress Dowager back to the palace.
An edict stated that Shùntiān, Bǎodìng, Héjiān, Yǒngpíng, and Xuānhuà prefectures suffered from excessive rain this year,
resulting in damaged crops and poor harvests,
so all taxes for the 55th year owed by these five prefectures
were completely remitted.
On the *Jiǎwǔ* day of the eleventh month,
Fàn Shíchóng was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief,
Juéluó Mǎnbǎo was appointed Zhèjiāng and Fújiàn Governor-General,
and Zōngshì Bāsāi was appointed Mongolian Commander.
On the *Gēngzǐ* day,
executions of prisoners in the capital were suspended.
On the *Xīnchǒu* day,
Sòng Dynasty official Fàn Zhòngyān was enshrined in the Temple of Confucius.
On the *Jǐwèi* day,
the Winter Solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Altar of Heaven,
using the imperial-approved ritual music for the first time.
On the *Jǐsì* day of the twelfth month,
Tǎbài was appointed Hángzhōu General.
Imperial Guard Commander Yànbù was ordered to lead troops and be stationed at Xīníng.
On the *Jiǎshēn* day,
Zhāng Bóxíng was accused of embezzlement, found guilty, and sentenced to death,
but the Emperor pardoned him,
and reinstated him as Storage and Granary Vice Minister.
In this year,
taxes were remitted in varying degrees for 24 prefectures, counties, and garrisons in the provinces of Jiāngnán and Húnán due to disasters.
Cháoxiān and Liúqiú offered tribute.
On the *Rénzǐ* day of the first month of the spring of the 55th year, *Bǐngshēn*,
the Emperor visited Tāngquán.
On the *Yǐchǒu* day of the second month,
Vice Commander Sū'ěrdé was ordered to manage military agricultural colonies at Túhūlǔkè and other places.
On the *Guǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to reside at Chàngchūnyuán.
On the *Bǐngzǐ* day,
an edict remitted the annual tribute of rhinoceros horns and ivory from Ānnán.
On the *Jǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor toured the imperial environs.
On the *Gēngyín* day,
the regulation for *dīng* (poll tax) based on land ownership was established.
On the *Dīngyǒu* day of the third month,
Assistant General Wáng Qǐyún, who was wounded or killed in the suppression of the Yáo in Guǎngxī's Yòujiāng, was posthumously compensated with an official rank and hereditary privilege.
On the *Gēngzǐ* day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the *Yǐsì* day,
Xízhù was recalled,
Yànbù replaced him,
and Lù Zhènyīn joined the military affairs.
On the *Guǐchǒu* day,
Mongolian Tú'ěrhútè Bèizi Ālābùzhū'ěr requested to join the army.
He was ordered to lead Mongolian troops to garrison Gásīkǒu.
Guìzhōu Governor Liú Yīnshū submitted a memorial requesting the cessation of military action,
and was ordered to travel by post to inspect the army and submit a report.
On the *Guǐhài* day of the intercalary third month,
Élúntè was appointed acting Xī'ān General,
and Mǎnpī was appointed acting Húguǎng Governor-General.
On the *Dīngchǒu* day,
Zuǒ Shìyǒng was appointed Guǎngxī Provincial Commander-in-chief.
On the *Rénwǔ* day,
two hundred thousand *shí* of rice from the imperial granaries were distributed for relief in Shùntiān and Yǒngpíng.
The gruel kitchens in the five cities were extended until autumn.
The Ministry of Rites was ordered to pray for rain.
On the *Guǐmǎo* day of the fourth month of summer,
the Emperor escorted the Empress Dowager to escape the summer heat at Rèhé.
In the fifth month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
the Emperor resided in Rèhé,
and fasted and prayed for rain.
Mǎ Qí was appointed Grand Secretary,
and Mùhélún was appointed Minister of Revenue.
On the *rénxū* day,
granary rice was released for sale at a stable price.
Rations for the Eight Banners' soldiers were advanced.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
it rained.
The Emperor said:
"Song scholars said: 'When one prays for rain and gets rain,
how can drought be without cause?'
This statement is worth pondering."
On the *jǐsì* day,
as rain was sufficient near and far in the capital,
the Emperor resumed his normal diet.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Hèyì was dismissed,
and Sūnzhāqí was appointed Minister of Works.
In the sixth month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
the Emperor visited Tāngquán.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
an order was given to move the garrison at Gégāsī mouth, dividing the troops to be stationed at Cháhǎnwūsū and Gáshùn.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the Emperor went hunting.
In the eighth month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
Dǒng Hóngyì, former Prefect of Fèngtiān Fu, was impeached for having converted the rice and beans from Chéngdé and other nine prefectures and counties into silver levies,
leading to a shortage in granary reserves,
and was dismissed from office.
In the ninth month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
Jiǎng Chénxī was appointed Governor-General of Yúnnán and Guìzhōu.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Emperor escorted the Empress Dowager back to the palace.
In winter, the tenth month, on the first day (*dīnghài shuò*),
an imperial edict ordered the Ministry of Punishments to distinguish and reduce the sentences of those who had been long-term prisoners with deferred judgments for years.
This year's autumn executions were suspended.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Tuōliú was appointed General of Hēilóngjiāng,
and Zhào Hóngcàn was appointed Minister of War.
On the *guǐsì* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Recently, due to Cèwàng Ālābùtǎn's invasion of Hāmì,
troops were conscripted for border defense,
and all provisions transported rapidly by land and water through the border regions
could not avoid drawing upon the people's resources.

Therefore, all outstanding silver, rice, grain, and fodder taxes for the coming year, as well as accumulated arrears, from the forty-eight prefectures, counties, and garrisons of Shānxī, Shǎnxī, and Gānsù,
are hereby exempted."
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
an imperial edict ordered the recruitment of settlers to cultivate land in the areas of Xījí Mù, Dálǐtú, and Jīntǎ Sì, which are adjacent to Sùzhōu and Bùlóngjílěr to the north.
Yáng Lín was appointed Governor-General of Guǎngdōng and Guǎngxī.
Zōngshì Bāsài was appointed Manchu General of the Banner,
and Yànbù was appointed Mongol General of the Banner.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Cèwàng Ālābùtǎn captured Luóbuzàng Dānjìbù, a *tàijí* of Qīnghǎi,
and attacked Gásī Kǒu.
The imperial troops repelled him.
Élúntè was ordered to station troops in Xīníng,
to dispatch troops to garrison Gásī Kǒu,
and Ālànà, a minister without portfolio from Bùlóngjílěr, was ordered to Bā'ěrkù'ěr to assist in military affairs.
In the eleventh month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
Fù'ěrdān and É'ěrjǐn were appointed Grand Ministers of the Imperial Guard.
On the *wùchén* day,
the Emperor paid respects at the imperial tombs.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Emperor toured beyond the Great Wall.
A tomb of the Míng Dynasty was robbed.
An order was given to prosecute the perpetrators according to the law.
In the twelfth month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
An imperial edict exempted Shùntiān and Yǒngpíng's thirty-five prefectures and counties from land and poll taxes for the coming year,
and all accumulated arrears were also remitted.
In this year,
taxes for disasters were remitted in sixty-three prefectures and counties of Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Shāndōng, Zhèjiāng, Jiāngxī, Húguǎng and other provinces, with varying amounts.
Cháoxiǎn and Ānnán offered tribute.
In the fifty-sixth year, the *dīngyǒu* year, in spring, the first month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
the *Zhōuyì Zhézhōng* was completed,
and distributed to academic institutions.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Xú Yuánmèng was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left,
and Zhū Shì was appointed Governor of Zhèjiāng.
In the second month, on the first day (*bǐngxū shuò*),
the Emperor toured the imperial domains.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
troops from Fèngtiān and Jílín were conscripted to reinforce Qíyìdé's army.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor returned to reside at Chàngchūnyuán.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
a regulation was established for cases of robbery where the law allowed no leniency, but the circumstances could be considered for clemency.
Nuóluóbù, Prince of Shùnchéng Commandery, passed away.
He was posthumously given the epithet Zhōng,
and his son Xībǎo inherited the title.
Kuí, Censor-in-Chief of the Left, passed away.
Sacrificial offerings and burial were granted,
and he was posthumously given the epithet Wénduān.
In the third month, on the *dīngsì* day,
the Emperor attended the imperial lectures (*jīngyán*).
On the *wùyín* day,
Fùníng'ān was appointed General Jìngnì,
Fù'ěrdān was appointed General Zhènwǔ,
and Qíyìdé was appointed Assistant General,
to inspect and guard the borders.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Emperor inspected the dikes at Héxīwù.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to reside at Chàngchūnyuán.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
rice from Tōngzhōu granary was distributed to various prefectures and counties in Zhílì for disaster relief.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Chén Áng, General-in-Chief of Jiéshí Garrison, memorialized that Catholic churches were springing up in various provinces,
and suggested they be prohibited.
This was followed.
Sūn Zhù and Fàn Shíchóng were appointed Ministers of War.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Emperor escorted the Empress Dowager to Rèhé to escape the summer heat.
In the fifth month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
the Nine Ministers deliberated that if princes and *bèilè* sent agents out
without proper credentials,
they should be investigated immediately.
In the sixth month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
Fù'ěrdān launched a surprise attack on the Öelüt Bóluóbù'ěrhāsū,
beheading and capturing them before returning.
Zhào Hóngcàn, Minister of War, passed away.
Sacrificial offerings and burial were granted,
and he was posthumously given the epithet Qīngduān.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
Cèwàng Ālābùtǎn dispatched his general Cèlíng Dūnduōbù to invade and plunder Lāzàng.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Fùníng'ān launched a surprise attack on the Öelüt at Tōng'ébāxī,
advanced to Wūlǔmùqí,
destroyed their crops,
and on his return journey encountered the bandit Bìliútú,
whom he defeated.
Huītè *tàijí* Zhámùbì was killed in action
and posthumously ennobled as *Fǔguó Gōng*.
In the eighth month, on the first day (*rénwǔ shuò*),
the Emperor went hunting.
In the ninth month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Lù Zhènyáng was appointed acting Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Sìchuān.
Kàng Tǐng, a treacherous civilian from Hénán, caused disturbances.
Imperial troops captured him,
and Tǐng fled and died.
Minister Zhāng Tíngshū and Scholar Lèshíbù were ordered to investigate,
and reported that former Governor Lǐ Xī's greed and cruelty had provoked the uprising.
Lǐ Xī was stripped of his office and sentenced to death,
and the bandit leaders were executed.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
Vice Minister Liáng Shìxūn and Hǎishòu were ordered to supervise farming colonies in Bā'ěrkù'ěr.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the Emperor escorted the Empress Dowager back to the palace.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Grand Minister of the Interior, Duke Cèwàng Nuò'ěrbù, General Élúntè, Imperial Guard Āqítú, and others were ordered to lead troops to garrison Qīnghǎi.
Zōngshì Gōng Tūnzhū was appointed Minister of Rites,
and Cài Shēngyuán was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
In the eleventh month, on the day of Rénzǐ,
an order was given to halt prisoner executions.
On the day of Yǐchǒu,
the Empress Dowager became unwell.
The Emperor visited her in the Cínínggōng Palace to inquire about her illness.
On the day of Xīnwèi,
an imperial edict stated:
“The rule of emperors and kings
must be rooted in revering Heaven and emulating ancestors.
To make the hearts of all under Heaven one's own heart,
to make the benefits of the four seas one's own benefit,
to establish order before chaos arises,
to secure the state before danger looms—
this diligent vigilance day and night
is how enduring stability is planned.
I ascended the throne at the age of eight,
and have reigned for over fifty years,
now approaching seventy years of age.
When I was twenty,
I dared not project reaching thirty.
When I was thirty,
I dared not project reaching forty.
By the grace of the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain,
it has now been fifty-seven years,
which is not something my meager virtue could have achieved.
I have reached a venerable age,
and have numerous descendants.
The empire is harmonious and joyful,
and the four seas are peaceful and secure.
Though I dare not claim that every family is self-sufficient and every person well-provided,
or that customs have easily changed and habits transformed,
my desire to enable the people to live in peace and for goods to flourish
has remained consistent from beginning to end.
To exhaust my thoughts
and deplete my energy
can scarcely be described by the words ‘toil and hardship.’
Ancient emperors did not enjoy long lives,
and scholars often criticized them for it.
They did not realize that the myriad affairs of the world are burdensome,
and one cannot bear the mental strain.
A minister, if he can serve, serves;
if he can stop, he stops.
When he is old, he retires and returns home,
still able to hold his children and play with his grandchildren,
living a life of leisure and ease.
An emperor's burden cannot be entrusted to others.
Shùn died in Cāngwú,
Yǔ passed away in Kuàijī;
they never had a moment of peace,
and ultimately found no rest.
The Five Blessings in the Hóngfàn
conclude with 'a peaceful end,'
because longevity is hard to come by.
The six lines of the Dùn hexagram in the Yìjīng
do not include the ruler,
because a monarch has no place to retreat and hide.
How can one compare the ease of a ruler with that of ministers and common people!
From my youth, I studied books,
seeking the principles of governance.
When I was in the prime of my strength,
I drew powerful bows and shot arrows.
The pacification of the Three Feudatories
and the appeasement of Mòběi
were all conceived in my mind;
I never wantonly killed a single person.
The gold in the imperial treasury
was never wantonly spent, unless for military expeditions or famine relief.
My imperial lodges during tours
were not adorned with colorful paintings.
From a young age, I knew that sensual pleasures should be avoided,
and sycophants should be kept at a distance.
Fortunately, I have managed to achieve a rough peace.
This spring, I have suffered considerably from dizziness,
and my body has gradually become emaciated.
During the hunting expedition beyond the passes,
the water and climate were better,
and my health somewhat improved;
I rode and shot arrows daily,
yet did not feel fatigued.
However, with the Empress Dowager's discomfort,
my dizziness has recurred,
and walking is difficult.
Should I suddenly pass away,
my deepest feelings might not be fully known.
Death is the natural course for humans,
but it is essential, when one's mind is clear,
to articulate all one's lifelong concerns
—only then will it be satisfactory.
People of the past often said that emperors should grasp the main principles,
and need not concern themselves with minor details.
I do not agree with this;
one careless act
can cause distress throughout the empire;
one careless thought
can lead to a century of trouble.
I have always approached matters, whether great or small,
with the utmost caution.
However, now that I am old and infirm,
I only fear that the diligence, concern, and vigilance of these fifty-seven years
might slacken at the end of my path.
The great matter of appointing an heir
is certainly on my mind.
But the supreme power of the empire
must be unified;
the sacred vessel is immensely important,
and finding the right person for the empire is exceedingly difficult.
That is why I, in my old age, continue tirelessly.
If all my officials, great and small, can understand my heart,
then the task of my peaceful end will be complete.
I have specifically summoned my sons and all ministers to discuss this in detail.
My future imperial testament
is contained herein.”
On the day of Jiǎxū,
two million taels of silver in outstanding loans from the Eight Banners were remitted.
On the day of Bǐngzǐ,
an imperial edict remitted accumulated back taxes for the provinces of Zhílì, Ānhuī, Jiāngsū, Zhèjiāng, Húguǎng, Shǎnxī, and Gānsù.
For Jiāngsū and Ānhuī, five-tenths of the grain transport silver and rice taxes were also remitted.
In the twelfth month, on the day of Jiǎshēn,
the Empress Dowager's illness worsened.
The Emperor had been ill for over seventy days,
his feet swollen,
and he needed assistance to attend court daily at Níngshòugōng Palace.
On the day of Bǐngxū,
the Empress Dowager passed away.
An imperial edict was issued,
and the Emperor wore mourning clothes, cut his queue,
and moved to a separate palace.
On the day of Jǐyǒu,
the Emperor returned to his palace.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn paid tribute.
In the spring of the fifty-seventh year, Wùxū, in the first month, on the day of Yǐmǎo,
the Emperor was ill
and went to Tāngquán.
On the day of Wùyín,
twenty thousand suits of clothing were bestowed upon the border defense troops.
In the second month, on the day of Gēngyín,
Lāzàng requested military aid.
The Emperor ordered imperial bodyguard Sèlèng to join the Qīnghǎi troops and go to his aid.
On the day of Guǐmǎo,
Lù Zhènshēng was appointed Provincial Military Commander of Gānsù.
Investigating Censor Zhū Tiānbǎo submitted a memorial requesting the reinstatement of Yìnréng as Crown Prince.
The Emperor personally interrogated him at the imperial traveling palace, saying:
“What do you know that you dare to defy the imperial decree and submit this memorial?”
Zhū Tiānbǎo replied:
“I heard it from my father,
and my father ordered me to say it.”
The Emperor said:
“This is a disloyal and unfilial person.”
He ordered his execution.
On the day of Dīngwèi,
the Emperor returned to his palace.
Chén Áng, of Jiéshízhèn, submitted a memorial requesting that foreign ships entering port
first be inspected for large cannons
before being allowed to enter for trade.
The Board discussed it and did not implement it.
In the third month, on the day of Guǐchǒu,
the taxes on factory workshops in Dàxīng and Wǎnpíng were reduced.
On the day of Xīnyǒu,
the Emperor bestowed the posthumous title Xiàohuì Rénxiàn Duānyì Chúndé Shùntiān Yìshèng Zhāng Huánghòu upon the late Empress.
On the day of Bǐngyín,
Yán Shòu was appointed General of the Right Guard,
and Huáng Bǐngyuè was appointed General of Fúzhōu.
On the day of Wùchén,
the position of Official for Recording Daily Life was abolished.
Seven education administrators, including Cóng Shù, found to be incompetent,
were all dismissed from office.
On the day of Dīngchǒu,
it was ordered that the north and south customs duties in Zhèjiāng be managed by the Tóngzhī.
On the day of Wùyín,
Zhū Shì, the Governor of Zhèjiāng, requested the repair of the Hǎiníng seawall.
This was granted.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day of Yǐyǒu,
Empress Xiàohuìzhāng was buried in Xiàodōnglíng.
On the day of Dīnghài,
Wāng Yìngquán and one hundred seventy-one others were granted the Jinshì degree and various ranks.
On the day of Xīnmǎo,
the Emperor visited Rèhé.
Mùhélún was dismissed,
and Sūn Zhāqí was appointed Minister of Revenue.
In the fifth month, on the day of Guǐchǒu,
Xú Yuánmèng was appointed Minister of Public Works.
On the day of Dīngsì,
Élúntè reported that Lāzàng Hán had been ambushed and killed,
his two sons murdered,
and the Dàlái and Bānchán both detained.
On the day of Jǐwèi,
Mǎn Bǎo, the Governor-General of Zhèjiāng and Fújiàn, memorialized that Táiwān Commandery had nine major strategic ports
and fifteen secondary strategic ports.
He requested sending people to build fortifications,
appropriately relocating officers and officials,
and establishing a garrison commander in Dànshuǐ Camp.
This was granted.
In the sixth month, on the day Rénchén,
an envoy was dispatched to invest Shàng Jì (尚敬), the great-grandson of the former king of Liúqiú (琉球), as Zhōngshān Wáng (中山王).
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Grand Secretary Lǐ Guāngdì (李光地) passed away.
The fifth imperial son, Héng Qīnwáng Yìnqí (恆親王胤祺), was ordered to offer tea and wine at the funeral.
One thousand taels of silver were bestowed.
Xú Yuánmèng (徐元夢) returned to the capital to handle the funeral arrangements.
He was posthumously granted the title Wénzhēn (文貞).
On the day Dīngwèi,
four hundred suits of clothing were bestowed upon the soldiers in Hāmì (哈密).
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Jǐwèi,
the Mòní (墨𩹉) Lạtma (喇嘛) from outside Dǎjiànlú (打箭爐) submitted.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the grand ceremony of Xiūshěng Fāng (修省方) was revised.
In the eighth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
there was a flood in Suǒlún (索倫),
and an official was sent to provide relief.
Mèng Guāngzǔ (孟光祖) was executed.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Emperor went on a hunting expedition.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Tūnzhū (吞珠), the Minister of Rites, passed away.
He was granted imperial sacrifices and burial.
He was posthumously granted the title Kèmǐn (恪敏).
Commander-in-chief Chóu Jī (仇機) was found guilty and executed.
In the intercalary eighth month, on the day Wùchén,
an imperial edict stated:
"The barbarians are causing trouble,
and our great army is stationed far in the west.
All military campaigns and preparations
have caused great toil to the people of Qín (秦).
Therefore, all land and poll taxes for Shǎnxī (陝西) and Gānsù (甘肅) for the coming year are hereby remitted,
and all accumulated arrears from previous years are also completely cancelled."
In the ninth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Tǒngtǒng Ā'ěrnà (都統阿爾納) and Zǒngbīng Lǐ Yào (總兵李耀) were ordered to lead troops to Gásīkǒu (噶斯口) and Cháidànmù (柴旦木) to garrison.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Wáng Xùlíng (王頊齡) was appointed Grand Secretary,
and Chén Yuánlóng (陳元龍) was appointed Minister of Works.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
Jiāngjūn Éléntè (將軍額倫特) and Shìwèi Sèlèng (侍衞色楞) joined forces at Kālāwūsū (喀喇烏蘇),
repeatedly defeating the bandits.
As the bandits advanced further,
the army had no reinforcements.
They fought until their arrows were exhausted,
and perished in battle.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
the execution of prisoners for this year was suspended.
On the day Bǐngchén,
the fourteenth imperial son, Bàizǐ Yìnzhì (貝子胤禵), was appointed Fúyuǎn Dàjiàngjūn (撫遠大將軍),
to oversee the army in Qīnghǎi (青海).
The deceased Gānmén Kūn (甘文焜), Governor-general, and Huáng Tíngbǎi (黃庭柏), Prefect, who died in the line of duty, were ordered to have shrines built and be included in the sacrifices.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
an imperial edict was issued to Nián Gēngyáo (年羹堯), Governor of Sìchuān (四川), stating
that since the start of the military campaign,
he had handled affairs with clarity and keenness,
and was therefore promoted to Governor-general.
The Hànlín (翰林) and Kēdào (科道) officials were ordered to serve in shifts.
On the day Wùchén,
the Emperor resided at Tāngquán (湯泉).

The seventh imperial son Yìnyòu (胤祐), the tenth imperial son Yìntáng (胤●), and the twelfth imperial son Yìntáo (胤祹) were ordered to separately manage the affairs of the Zhènghuáng (正黃), Zhèngbái (正白), and Zhènglán (正藍) Banners for the Manchu, Mongol, and Han peoples.
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
the Emperor returned to reside at Chàngchūnyuán (暢春園).
Chén Bīn (陳璸), Governor of Fújiàn (福建), passed away.
He was posthumously granted the title Minister of Rites
and given the posthumous name Qīngduān (清端).
Yí Zhàoxióng (宜兆熊) was appointed Hànjūn Dūtǒng (漢軍都統).
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
the Emperor visited the imperial mausoleums.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Empress Xiàohuì Zhāng (孝惠章皇后) was interred in the Tàimiào (太廟),
located to the left of Empress Xiàokāng Zhāng (孝康章皇后).
An imperial edict was promulgated throughout the empire.
The Miáo (苗) people of Sǎdiàn (撒甸) in Yúnnán (雲南) submitted.
On the day Jǐsì,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
In this year,
calamity taxes were remitted in varying degrees for twenty-six prefectures, counties, and garrisons in provinces such as Jiāngnán (江南), Fújiàn (福建), Gānsù (甘肅), and Húguǎng (湖廣).
Cháoxiǎn (朝鮮), Liúqiú (琉球), and Ānnán (安南) paid tribute.
In the fifty-eighth year, Jǐhài (己亥), in spring, on the first day of the first month, Jiǎxū (甲戌),
there was a solar eclipse.
An imperial edict stated:
"The solar eclipse, occurring three times,
is a clear celestial omen.
It is fitting to mend human affairs
to heed the warning from Heaven.
Let my officials report any shortcomings in governance."
On the day Yǐwèi,
the Emperor went to Tāngquán (湯泉).
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the Emperor returned to reside at Chàngchūnyuán (暢春園).
On the day Xīnchǒu,
an imperial edict decreed that officials who had achieved merit could retire,
and their hereditary positions could be passed on to their sons and younger brothers.
If there were no suitable heirs,
they would be granted a stipend for life.
On the day Rènyín,
430,000 shí (石) of tribute grain were ordered to be intercepted
and kept in Jiāngsū (江蘇) and Ānhuī (安徽) for famine relief.
In the second month, on the day Jǐsì,
the Emperor toured the capital region (Jīdiàn 畿甸).
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Xuéshì Jiǎng Tíngxī (學士蔣廷錫) presented the *Huángyú Quánlǎntú* (皇輿全覽圖, "Complete Map of the Imperial Domain"),
which was distributed to court officials.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the Emperor returned to reside at Chàngchūnyuán (暢春園).
On the day Xīnwèi,
Tǒngtǒng Fǎlǎ (都統法喇) was ordered to pacify and organize Mòtáng (墨𩹉塘) and Bātáng (巴塘).
Hùjūn Tǒnglǐng Gé'ěrbì (護軍統領噶爾弼) was to manage military affairs concurrently.
In the third month, on the day Yǐwèi,
Shìláng Sè'ěrtú (侍郎色爾圖) was dismissed due to delays in grain transport.
Governor Géshítú (噶什圖) was ordered to take over.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the day Yǐsì,
