Fúyuǎn Dàjiàngjūn Yìnzhì (撫遠大將軍胤禵) was ordered to station his army in Xīníng (西寧).
On the day Kuǐchǒu,
the Emperor toured Rèhé (熱河).
In the fifth month, on the day Wùyín,
due to a bountiful wheat harvest,
the people were ordered to store it in a timely manner.
On the day Gēngchén,
Yángdū (揚都) was appointed Mongol Dūtǒng (都統).
Suǒtài (索泰), the chief examiner for Zhèjiāng (浙江), was bribed to sell examination favors.
Chén Xún (陳恂), a scholar living at home, brokered the deal.
Chén Fèngchí (陳鳳墀) used connections to pass the examination.
All were sentenced to death,
and those who recommended Suǒtài as examiner were also punished.
The Nányáng (南陽) garrison soldiers seized and insulted Prefect Shěn Yuān (沈淵).
Zǒngbīng Gāo Chéng (總兵高成) was dismissed from office.
Yóují Wáng Hóngdào (游擊王洪道) was sentenced to death.
The soldiers were executed.
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
Bèilè Mǎndùhù (貝勒滿篤祜) was appointed Manchu Dūtǒng (都統).
On the day Dīngwèi,
Nián Gēngyáo (年羹堯), Gé'ěrbì (噶爾弼), and Fǎlǎ (法喇) successively reported that Fùjiàng Yuè Zhōngqí (副將岳鍾琪) had recruited and pacified the Mòtáng (墨𩹉塘) and Bātáng (巴塘) people.
Fǎlǎ (法喇) was ordered to advance and station in Bātáng (巴塘),
and Nián Gēngyáo (年羹堯) was to dispatch troops to provide support.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Mǎ Jiànbó (馬見伯) was appointed Gùyuán Tídū (固原提督).
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Kuǐwèi,
Zōngchámù (宗查木) was appointed Xī'ān Jiāngjūn (西安將軍).
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngxū,
the Emperor went on a hunting expedition.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Zhènwēi Jiāngjūn Fù'ěrdān (振威將軍傅爾丹) reported that two cities and stations were built at È'ěrzhài Tú (鄂爾齋圖).
Shàngshū Fàn Shíchóng (尚書范時崇) was ordered to oversee the project.
In the ninth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
an edict stated that the new Húbìlèhǎn (胡畢勒罕) currently in Xīníng (西寧)
was indeed the reincarnation of the Dálài (達賴),
and ordered the Grand General to send an official with troops to Xīzàng (西藏) to install him in the monastery.
On the day Wùxū,
Ān Jùnwáng Huá (安郡王華) passed away.
He was posthumously granted the title Jié (節).
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Wáng Lánshēng (王蘭生), a Jǔrén (舉人) from Měngyǎngzhāi (蒙養齋), was ordered to revise the Yīnyùn Tú (音韻圖).
On the day Jiǎyín,
Gùyuán Tídū Pān Yùlóng (固原提督潘育龍) passed away.
He was posthumously granted the title Tàizǐ Shàobǎo (太子少保),
and granted imperial sacrifices and burial.
He was posthumously granted the title Xiāngyǒng (襄勇).
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
Chén Shēn (陳詵), Minister of Rites, retired.
On the day Gēngyín,
the quota for Jiāngxī (江西) for sending grain was increased.
In the twelfth month, on the day Rènyín,
Cài Shēngyuán (蔡升元) was appointed Minister of Rites,
and Tián Cóngdiǎn (田從典) was appointed Zuǒ Dūyùshǐ (左都御史).
On the day Wùshēn,
the coffin of Xī'ān Jiāngjūn Éléntè (西安將軍額倫特) arrived in the capital.
The fifth imperial son, Héng Qīnwáng Yìnqí (恆親王胤祺), and the twelfth imperial son, Bàizǐ Yìntáo (貝子胤祹), were ordered to meet and offer sacrifices.
On the day Gēngshēn,
100,000 shí (石) of tribute grain from Húguǎng (湖廣) were ordered to be intercepted and kept in that province for famine relief.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
an imperial edict stated:
"In recent years, troops have been sent on a western expedition,
traveling far to the frontiers.
The people have endured hardship in providing sustenance and provisions.
Therefore, the people's resources are exhausted.
All silver and grain taxes levied for the coming year in the sixty-six prefectures, counties, and garrisons along the border
are hereby remitted."
In this year,
calamity taxes were remitted in varying degrees for thirteen prefectures and counties in provinces such as Jiāngsū (江蘇) and Ānhuī (安徽).
Cháoxiǎn (朝鮮) and Liúqiú (琉球) paid tribute.
In the fifty-ninth year, Gēngzǐ (庚子), in spring, in the first month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
Fúyuǎn Dàjiàngjūn Yìnzhì (撫遠大將軍胤禵) was ordered to move his army to Mùlúsīwūsū (穆魯斯烏蘇).
Zōngshì Yánxìn (宗室延信) was appointed Píngnì Jiāngjūn (平逆將軍),
leading troops to advance into Xīzàng (西藏),
with Gōng Cèwàng Nuò'ěrbù (公策旺諾爾布) assisting in military affairs.
Xī'ān Jiāngjūn Zōngchámù (西安將軍宗查木) was ordered to garrison Xīníng (西寧),
and Píng Jùnwáng Nà'ěrsù (平郡王訥爾素) was to garrison Gǔmù (古木).
In the second month, on the *Jiǎchén* day,
the Emperor toured the imperial domain.
On the *Guǐchǒu* day,
Gá'ěrbì was appointed General Dingxi,
to lead Sichuan and Yunnan troops into Tibet,
and to enthrone the new Húbìlèhǎn as the Sixth Dalai Lama.
On the *Xīnyǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to reside at Chàngchūnyuán.
In the third month, on the *Jǐchǒu* day,
Zhāng Gǔzhēn, the Provincial Commander of Yunnan, was ordered to garrison Lìjiāng and Zhōngdiàn.
On the *Bǐngshēn* day,
Fùníng'ān, General Jingni, was ordered to advance his army to Wūlǔmùqí;
Ālànà, an official without fixed duties, to advance his army to Tǔlǔfān;
Qí Lǐdé to lead seven thousand troops from Bùlóu'ěr;
and Fù'ěrdān to lead eight thousand troops from Bùlāhǎn.
They were to simultaneously attack the Zhǔngá'ěr.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *Wùshēn* day,
the Emperor toured Rèhé.
In the fifth month, on the *Xīnsì* day,
prayers were offered for rain, and requests for advice were made due to drought.
On the *Rénwǔ* day,
it rained.
In the sixth month, on the *Jǐhài* day,
Shaanxi experienced famine,
and stored grain from the south of the river was transported there for relief.
On the *Bǐngchén* day,
Bǎo'ān and Huáilái experienced earthquakes,
and officials were dispatched to provide relief.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the first day, *Bǐngyín*,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *Guǐyǒu* day,
Fùníng'ān attacked the rebels at Ākètǎsī, Yī'ěrbù'ěrhésháo,
defeated them,
and captured their *tàijí* Chuímùpā'ěr.
Ālànà's army reached Qíkètǎmù,
encountered the rebels,
defeated them,
and captured all their forces.
They advanced to attack Píchán City,
and it surrendered.
When the army reached Tǔlǔfān,
the local chieftain Ākèsū'ěrtǎn led his people to welcome them and surrender.
On the *Bǐngxū* day,
Fù'ěrdān attacked the rebels at Gé'ě'ěrgé,
killing and capturing six hundred,
capturing Zàisāng Bèikěn on the battlefield,
burning their stockpiles, and then returning.
Bèikěn was sent to the capital.
Qí Lǐdé defeated the rebels at Kēng'é'ěrhé,
and accepted the surrender of their *zàisāng* Sèbùténg and over two thousand others.
In the eighth month, on the *Wùxū* day,
the Emperor went hunting.
On the *Gēngzǐ* day,
Liúqiú requested permission for their accompanying officials' children and younger brothers to study at the Guózǐjiān,
which was granted.
On the *Guǐchǒu* day,
Yánxìn, General Pingni, repeatedly defeated the rebel forces at Bǔkèhé.
On the *Dīngsì* day,
he again defeated the rebel forces at Chuōmǎlā,
and the rebel general Cèlíng Dūnduōbù fled.
Gá'ěrbì, General Dingxi, led Vice General Yuè Zhōngqí to advance troops from Lālǐ.
On the *Wùwǔ* day,
they conquered Xīzàng,
captured over a hundred lamas who had sided with the rebels,
executed five of their leaders,
and pacified the Tánggǔtè and Tǔbótè.
Xīzàng was pacified.
Gāo Qízhuó was appointed Governor of Guǎngxī.
In the ninth month, on the *Rénshēn* day,
Yánxìn, General Pingni, escorted the Dalai Lama with troops into Xīzàng to take his seat.
Fùníng'ān's army entered Wūlǔmùqí,
where the Háxīhā Hui people welcomed them and surrendered.
The army then returned to Wūlánwūsū.
On the *Wùyín* day,
Jiǎng Chénxī, Governor-General of Yún-Guì, and Gān Guóbì, Governor, were stripped of their posts for the late delivery of provisions,
but were still ordered to transport rice into Tibet.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *Guǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
An edict ordered that stored grain from Hénán be again transported to Shǎnxī for relief.
Next year,
the grain transport quota for Hénán would be fully reimbursed with stored grain,
and the remaining transport grain would be stored in Hénán.
On the *Jiǎchén* day,
Lǐ Dūn, King of Cháoxiǎn, died.
The edict stated:
"Lǐ Dūn held the enfeoffment for fifty years,
served his vassal state with reverence and caution,
and governed his people with kindness and love.
Hearing of his sudden demise,
We feel profound sorrow and grief.
His son, Lǐ Yún, is immediately ordered to inherit the enfeoffment.
All tribute items presented are to be returned,
and the customary compassionate rites are to be investigated and reported."
An edict granted a total exemption of 1,880,000 *liǎng* of land and poll tax for the 60th year of Kāngxī in Shǎnxī and Gānsù provinces.
This was to be universally implemented.
Due to poor harvests along the border,
rice prices were high,
and military resources were strained,
so this year's military provisions were to be distributed in advance.
Rewards were also given to the officers and soldiers who entered Tibet.
On the *Jiǎyín* day,
Zhào Shēnjiāo, President of the Board of Revenue, died.
He was granted sacrificial rites and a funeral,
and posthumously named Gōngyì.
On the *Dīngsì* day,
an edict ordered Yìnzhí, Grand General Fǔyuǎn, to convene a meeting regarding next year's campaign schedule.
On the *Wùwǔ* day,
due to poor harvests in Shǎnxī and Gānsù,
it was ordered that both silver and grain be distributed as relief,
until the wheat harvest.
In the eleventh month, on the *Xīnwèi* day,
an official was dispatched to offer sacrifices to Lǐ Dūn, King of Cháoxiǎn.
He was specially granted the posthumous name Xīshùn,
and his heir apparent, Lǐ Yún, was enfeoffed as King of Cháoxiǎn.
On the *Wùyín* day,
Tián Cóngdiǎn was appointed President of the Board of Revenue,
Zhū Shì as Censor-in-Chief of the Left,
and Yáng Míngshí as Governor of Yúnnán.
On the *Xīnsì* day,
an edict stated:
"With the grand army's entry into Tibet,
that territory has now been incorporated into the imperial domain.
The names of its mountains and rivers differ between the indigenous and Han languages;
these should be immediately investigated and clarified,
to be truthfully passed down to future generations."
The Emperor then discussed with the Grand Secretaries the sources of the Yellow River and the Yangtze River,
and the Sānwēi in the *Yǔgòng*.
On the *Gēngyín* day,
Lóngkēduō was appointed President of the Court of Colonial Affairs,
still concurrently holding the position of Commander of the Gendarmerie.
In the twelfth month, on the *Jiǎchén* day,
court officials again requested to hold the celebration ceremony for the sixtieth year.
This was not granted.
On the *Rénzǐ* day,
the descendant of the ancient sage Zǐ Xià was granted the title of Wǔjīng Bóshì.
On the *Jiǎyín* day,
Hóngshèng, son of Chéng Qīnwáng Yìnzhǐ, and Hóngshēng, son of Héng Qīnwáng Yìnqí, were made heirs apparent.
On the *Xīnyǒu* day,
the comprehensive ancestral sacrifice was held at the Tàimiào.
In this year,
tax exemptions were granted to varying degrees for disaster-stricken areas in fifty-six prefectures, counties, and guards in Zhílì, Jiāngsū, Shǎnxī, Zhèjiāng, and Sìchuān provinces.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú paid tribute.
In the spring of the first month, *Yǐhài*, of the 60th year, *Xīnchǒu*,
the Emperor, having reigned for sixty years,
dispatched his fourth son Yìnzhēn, twelfth son Yìntáo, and heir apparent Hóngshèng to offer sacrifices at Yǒnglíng, Fúlìng, and Zhāolíng.
In the second month, on the *Yǐwèi* day,
the Emperor visited Xiàozhuāng Shānlíng, Xiàolíng, and Xiàodōnglíng,
and performed sacrificial rites.
Officials were dispatched to offer sacrifices at the suburban altars, temples, and altars of soil and grain.
On the *Yǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
Wáng Měigōng and other salt workers in Shāndōng rebelled and were captured and executed.
On the *Jǐwèi* day,
Gōng Cèwàngnuò'ěrbù was ordered to garrison Xīzàng.
For their achievements in conquering Tibet,
Dìbā Ā'ěrbùbā and Kāngjìnài were enfeoffed as *Bèizǐ*,
and Dìbā Lóngbùnài as Fǔguó Gōng.
In the third month, on the *Yǐchǒu* day,
the ministers requested the Emperor to accept an honorific title for his birthday (*Wànshòu Jié*).
The Emperor did not permit it,
saying:
"Adding honorific titles
is merely a deeply ingrained bad habit,
nothing more than changing the wording slightly
to deceive ignorant rulers.
Our dynasty's family tradition
is only to care for the people,
not to regard auspicious stars, propitious clouds, magical herbs, or sweet dew as omens of good fortune,
nor to carry out *Fēngshàn* rituals or change era names.
Currently, military campaigns are underway in the western frontier,
soldiers have been exposed to hardships for a long time,
and the people suffer from transportation.
I am already too busy with self-reflection and governance,
what is there to celebrate?"
On the *Gēngwǔ* day,
Jǔrén Wáng Lánshēng and Liú Bǎo were granted the status of *Jìnshì*,
and were to participate in the palace examination together.
On the *Jiǎxū* day,
previously,
Grand Secretary Wáng Yàn had secretly submitted a memorial proposing the restoration of the heir apparent.

Now, censors Táo Yí, Rèn Píng, Fàn Chángfā, Zōu Túyún, Chén Jiāyóu, Wáng Yǔnjìn, Lǐ Yǔnfú, Fàn Yǔn [missing character], Gāo Bīn, Gāo Yí, Zhào Chéng [missing character], and Sūn Shàozēng submitted memorials requesting the establishment of an heir apparent.
The Emperor was displeased,
and severely reprimanded Wáng Yàn as well,
ordering his son, Academician Wáng Yìqīng, and Táo Yí and twelve others to serve as supernumerary *Zhāngjīng*,
to exert themselves at the front.
In the summer, fourth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Lǐ Lín was appointed Grand Protector of Gùyuán.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Dèng Zhōngyuè and 162 others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with various ranks.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
an imperial edict ordered the rectification and establishment of the rites for worshipping successive emperors at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Zhāng Pénghé and Chén Péngnián were dispatched to Shāndōng to inspect the rivers.
Lài Dū was made Minister of Rites,
and Tuō Lài was made Minister of Punishments.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Emperor visited Rèhé.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Gá'ěrbì, General Who Pacifies the West, was ordered to station in Zàng.
In the fifth month, on the *rénxū* day,
Yìn Tí, Grand General Who Pacifies the Distant, was ordered to move his troops to Gānzhōu.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Zhu Yīguì, a treacherous commoner in Táiwān, rebelled,
killing Commander-in-Chief Ōuyáng Kǎi.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Yuè Zhōngqí, acting Brigade General of Yǒngníng and serving as Vice-General, was appointed Grand Protector of Sìchuān.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the native prefecture of Sīmíng was transferred to Tàipíng Prefecture in Guǎngxī.
On the *wùyín* day,
an imperial edict ordered the cessation of military advances for the current year.
Cháng Shòu was appointed Supernumerary Vice-Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs,
to manage affairs in Xīníng.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Nián Gēngyáo was appointed Governor-General of Sìchuān and Shǎnxī,
and granted bows and arrows.
Fifty thousand taels of silver from the imperial treasury were allocated to relieve Shānxī and Shǎnxī,
and Zhū Shì and Lú Xún were ordered to oversee the matter.
In the sixth month, on the *rénchén* day,
Gāo Qíwèi was transferred to be Grand Protector of Jiāngnán,
and Wèi Jīngguó was made Grand Protector of Húguǎng.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Yán Xìn, General Who Pacifies Rebels,
is Our nephew.
Leading troops, he traversed treacherous and miasmatic lands never before reached,
annihilated the great captives,
and pacified the Zàng region.
Truly, he has not disgraced his lineage.
He may be enfeoffed as Fǔguó Gōng."
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Huí people of Tǔlǔfān, Tuōkètuōmámùkè and others, submitted.
Ālànà, a minister without specific duties, was ordered to lead troops to escort them.
Shī Shìbiāo, Naval Grand Protector of Fújiàn, pacified Táiwān,
captured Zhū Yīguì and sent him to the capital.
An imperial edict praised Chén Cè, commander of Dànshuǐ battalion, for his meritorious defense,
and promoted him exceptionally to Commander-in-Chief of Táiwān.
In the intercalary sixth month, on the *gēngshēn* new moon,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Board of Punishments was ordered to release those lightly imprisoned.
On the *wùchén* day,
Gá'ěrbì was made Mongol Commander-in-Chief.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor went on a hunting expedition.
In the eighth month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
Deputy Commander-in-Chief Zhuāng Tú was ordered to lead 2,000 troops to station in Tǔlǔfān,
reinforcing Ālànà's army.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the river burst its banks in Wǔzhì, flowing into the Qìn River.
In the ninth month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
Deputy Commander-in-Chief Mùkèdéng was ordered to lead 2,000 troops to Tǔlǔfān.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Gá'ěrbì was dismissed due to illness.
Duke Cèwàngnuò'ěrbù was ordered to serve as acting General Who Pacifies the West,
stationed in Zàng,
with Ābǎo and Wǔgé participating in military affairs.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Cèwàng Ālābùtǎn attacked Tǔlǔfān,
and Ālànà defeated and repelled him.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
relief was provided for flood-stricken Hénán, Shāndōng, and Zhílì.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Deputy Censor-in-Chief Niú Niǔ, Expositor Qí Sūlè, and Director Mǎ Tài were ordered to build up the Yellow River breach,
diverting the Qìn River into the Grand Canal.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Ālànà was made Assistant General.
The Emperor composed an inscription for the Stele of the Pacification of Xīzàng.
In the winter, tenth month, on the *rénxū* day,
Surveillance Censors for Táiwān were established.
An imperial edict stated:
"All autumn reviews of cases this year have been thoroughly examined.
For cases in the provinces proposed for delayed execution,
the Nine Ministers have already reviewed and confirmed them.
We cannot bear to review them again,
lest the reconsideration lead to a heavier sentence."
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Yìn Tí, Grand General Who Pacifies the Distant, was summoned to the capital.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Grand Secretary Xióng Cìlǚ served his office with integrity and uprightness,
with extensive and profound scholarship.
We have not forgotten him for a long time,
and have often ordered his family to be cared for.
Now his two sons have come to the capital.
Observing their temperament,
they are still capable of studying.
They should be nurtured further.
This should be conveyed to the Nine Ministers."
Zhōng Shìchén was appointed Grand Protector of Zhèjiāng,
Yáo Táng was appointed Naval Grand Protector of Fújiàn,
and Féng Yì was appointed acting Grand Protector of Guǎngdōng.
In the eleventh month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
Chén Péngnián was appointed acting Governor-General of Waterways.
On the *wùxū* day,
Mǎ Wǔ and Yī'ěrhādài were made Mongol Commanders-in-Chief.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor visited Nányuàn.
An imperial edict granted posthumous honors to General ÉrLúntè, Imperial Bodyguard Sèlèng, Deputy Commander-in-Chief Chá Lǐhún, Grand Protector Kāng Tài, and others,
who died in battle for the country.
All were granted compassionate relief.
In the twelfth month, on the *rénshēn* day,
Yuè Zhōngqí, Grand Protector of Sìchuān, campaigned against the Guōluòkè barbarians,
and pacified them.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to reside at Chàngchūnyuán.
È Hǎi and Yǒng Tài were dispatched to inspect the agricultural garrisons in Tǔlǔfān.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted in varying degrees for 123 prefectures and counties in provinces such as Jiāngnán, Hénán, Shǎnxī, Gānsù, Fújiàn, Zhèjiāng, and Húguǎng.
Cháoxiǎn, Liúqiú, and Ānnán offered tribute.
The number of registered households was 29,148,359,
plus 467,850 additional *dīng* (taxable males) born after the permanent tax exemption.
The silver collected was 28,790,000.
Salt tax silver was 3,772,363 taels and a fraction.
The number of coins minted was 437,325,800 and odd.
In the sixty-first year, on the *rén'yín* spring first month *wùzǐ* day,
680 civil and military officials of the Eight Banners aged 65 or above were summoned.
Those who had retired were also invited to a banquet,
and imperial clansmen were granted titles and encouraged to drink.
Three days later,
a banquet was held for 340 Han officials aged 65 or above, likewise.
The Emperor composed a poem,
and the officials harmonized with it,
titled "Poem of the Banquet of a Thousand Elders."
On the *wùshēn* day,
the Emperor toured the imperial domains.
In the second month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
Gāo Qízhuó was appointed acting Governor-General of Yúnnán and Guìzhōu.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the Emperor returned to reside at Chàngchūnyuán.
In the third month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
Ā Lǔ was made General of Jīngzhōu.
In the summer, fourth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
envoys were dispatched to enfeoff Lǐ Yún's younger brother, Qǐn, as Heir Apparent of Cháoxiǎn.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor toured Rèhé.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Yìn Tí, Grand General Who Pacifies the Distant, resumed command of the army.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the Fúzhōu garrison soldiers mutinied.
General Huáng Bǐngyuè was unable to restrain them,
so he was stripped of his office,
and the ringleaders were executed.
In the fifth month, on the *wùxū* day,
Shī Shìlún died.
Zhāng Dàyǒu was appointed acting Governor-General of Grain Transport.
In the sixth month,
due to successive years of abundant harvests in Fèngtiān,
the maritime prohibitions were lifted.
As rice from Xiāmluó was cheap,
its entry into the interior was permitted,
and its tax was remitted.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Zhílì was ordered to divert 200,000 *shi* of grain transport for disaster relief.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Zhào Hóngxiè died.
His nephew, Langzhong Zhào Zhīyuán, was granted the title of Assistant Censor-in-Chief,
and appointed acting Governor of Zhílì.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
Qí Lǐdé, General Who Campaigns in the West, reported on matters concerning agricultural garrisons in Wūlángǔmù.
He requested additional troops for defense.
Commander-in-Chief Tú Lā was ordered to lead troops there.
On the *rén'yín* day,
Sè'ěrtú was ordered to go to Xīzàng to command the Sìchuān defense troops.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Cài Tǐng was appointed Governor of Sìchuān.
The late Governor-General of Zhílì, Zhào Hóngxiè, was granted sacrificial burial,
and given the posthumous title Sùmǐn.
In the eighth month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
the annual executions were suspended.
The wife and children of the late Grand Protector Lán Lǐ had previously been assigned to the banner system due to a crime.
At this time,
the Emperor, remembering his merit in pacifying Táiwān,
pardoned them and returned them to their original hometown,
and exempted them from being pursued for debts.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor resided at Hàntèmù'ěrdábāhàn'áng'ā.
Silver currency, saddles, and horses were bestowed upon the foreign vassal states who came to court,
and silver currency upon the soldiers accompanying the hunt.
In the ninth month, on the *Jiǎshēn* day,
the Emperor resided at Rèhé.
On the *Yǐyǒu* day,
an imperial edict was issued to the Grand Secretaries, stating:
“Some people say that My hunting expeditions beyond the Great Wall
cause hardship to the soldiers.
They do not know that after a long period of peace,
how can We completely forget military preparedness?
Numerous military campaigns have been launched,
strengthening the military and the efforts of the officials,
which have successfully led to achievements.
This is all due to diligent training.”
On the *Jiǎwǔ* day,
Nián Gēngyáo and Gáshítú requested to incrementally increase the *huǒhào* (meltage fee)
to compensate for the deficit in the prefectural treasuries.
The Emperor said:
“The *huǒhào* should only be discussed for reduction,
how can it be increased?
This current deficit
is mostly due to military expeditions.
When officials and soldiers passed through,
there might have been some aid provided.
Initially, public funds were misappropriated,
and over time, this led to deficits.
In past years, there was an imperial edict granting remission.
Currently, military provisions are urgently needed,
so funds from the Board of Revenue's treasury will be immediately allocated to Xī'ān for备用 (emergency use).”
On the *Wùxū* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *Dīngwèi* day,
he stopped at Mìyún
to inspect the river dikes.
On the *Gēngxū* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the winter, tenth month, on the *Xīnyǒu* day,
Yōng Qīnwáng Yìnzhēn, Hóngshēng, Yánxìn, Sūn Zhāqí, Lóngkēduō, Chábìnà, and Wú'ěrzhàn were ordered to inspect the granaries.
On the *Rénxū* day,
Juéluó Dé'ěrjīn was appointed as the Mongol General-in-Chief,
and Āntái as the General of Hángzhōu.
On the *Xīnwèi* day,
Chábìnà was appointed as the Governor-General of Jiāngnán and Jiāngxī.
On the *Guǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor went to Nányuàn for a hunting expedition.
Lǐ Shùdé was appointed as the General of Fúzhōu,
and Huáng Guócái as the Provincial Governor of Fújiàn.
In the eleventh month, on the *Wùzǐ* day,
the Emperor fell ill
and returned to reside at Chàngchūnyuán.
Bèizi Yìntáo and Fǔguógōng Wú'ěrzhàn were appointed as the Manchu General-in-Chiefs.
On the *Gēngyín* day,
the Fourth Prince Yìnzhēn was commanded to respectfully deputize in the sacrifice to Heaven.
On the *Jiǎwǔ* day,
the Emperor's illness worsened greatly.
At the hour of *Xū* (7-9 PM),
the Emperor passed away,
aged sixty-nine.
That evening, the body was moved into the Forbidden City for the funeral.
In the second month of Yōngzhèng's first year,
a respectful posthumous title was bestowed.
In the ninth month, on the *Dīngchǒu* day,
he was buried in Jǐnglíng.
A commentary states: The Sagely Ancestor's (Kāngxī) benevolence and filial piety were innate,
his wisdom and courage heaven-bestowed.
He assumed great responsibilities early,
diligently governed and loved the people.
He brought order through culture and military prowess,
unifying the realm.
Though it is said he preserved the inheritance,
he was effectively a founder.
His sagely learning was profound,
he honored Confucianism and esteemed the Dao.
During his leisure, he investigated phenomena,
comprehending the relationship between Heaven and man,
which is particularly unseen throughout history.
And through long-term moral transformation,
customs shifted and habits changed,
the world was harmonious and joyful,
achieving great peace.
His prosperous and tranquil era
makes later generations long for and dwell on it,
even to this day without ceasing.
The *Chuán* (Commentary) says:
“As a ruler,
one should rest in benevolence.”
It also says:
“When the Dao is flourishing and virtue is supreme,
the people cannot forget it.”
Alas,
how magnificent it was!
Annals of Shìzōng, Ninth Reign
Shìzōng Jìngtiānchāngyùn Jiànzhōngbiǎozhèng Wǔwǔ Yīngmíng Kuānrén Xìnyì Ruìshèng Dàxiào Zhìchéng Xiàn Huángdì, personal name Yìnzhēn,
was the fourth son of the Sagely Ancestor.
His mother was Empress Xiàogōngrén, of the Wūyǎ clan.
He was born with extraordinary signs,
of imposing stature and majestic appearance,
his demeanor was dignified and composed.
In the 37th year of Kāngxī, he was enfeoffed as *Bèilè*.
In the 48th year, he was enfeoffed as Yōng Qīnwáng.
In the eleventh month of the 61st year,
the Sagely Ancestor fell ill at Chàngchūnyuán
and ordered him to deputize in the sacrifice at the Altar of Heaven.
On the *Jiǎwǔ* day,
the Sagely Ancestor's illness worsened greatly.
He was summoned to the fasting palace,
where an imperial edict proclaimed his succession to the throne.
The Sagely Ancestor passed away.
On the *Xīnchǒu* day,
the Emperor ascended the throne,
designating the following year as the first year of Yōngzhèng.
*Bèilè* Yìnshì, the Thirteenth Imperial Brother Yìnxiáng, Grand Secretary Mǎqí, and President Lóngkēduō were ordered to manage state affairs.
Fǔyuǎn Dàjiāngjūn Yìntí was summoned to the capital.
President of the Board of War Bái Huáng was ordered to assist the Grand Secretaries.
Yáng Zōngrén was appointed as Governor-General of Húguǎng,
and Nián Xīyáo was provisionally appointed as Provincial Governor of Guǎngdōng.
In the twelfth month, on the *Wùwǔ* day,
the practice of offering local products from the provinces was abolished.
On the *Rénxū* day,
*Bèilè* Yìnshì was enfeoffed as Lián Qīnwáng,
Yìnxiáng as Yí Qīnwáng,
Yìntáo as Lǚ Jùnwáng,
and Hóngxī, son of the deposed Crown Prince Yìnréng, as Lǐ Jùnwáng.
The sacrificial rites for emperors of past dynasties were revised.
On the *Guǐhài* day,
an imperial edict stated that the compilation of the *Gǔjīn Túshū Jíchéng* was not yet completed,
and that scholars of profound knowledge should be quickly appointed to edit it into a book.
Fǔguógōng Yánxìn was appointed as the General of Xī'ān
and provisionally held the position of Fǔyuǎn Dàjiāngjūn.
On the *Jiǎzǐ* day,
an imperial edict stated that provincial and departmental treasury deficits
must be made up within three years,
and those who exceeded the deadline would be punished.
Fùníng'ān was appointed as Grand Secretary,
Lóngkēduō as President of the Board of Civil Office,
and Lián Qīnwáng Yìnshì was put in charge of the Board of Colonial Affairs.
On the *Rénshēn* day,
Zhāng Tíngyù was appointed as President of the Board of Rites.
Grand Secretary Mǎqí was granted the title of Earl of the Second Rank
and given the name Dūnhuì.
In the first month, *Xīnsì* day, the first day of the Yōngzhèng first year, spring,
imperial edicts were issued instructing Governor-Generals, Provincial Governors, Provincial Commanders-in-Chief, and Brigade-Generals,
civil officials down to Prefects and Magistrates,
and military generals down to Colonels and Majors,
a total of eleven edicts.
On the *Bǐngxū* day,
a seasonal sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the *Xīnmǎo* day,
prayers for grain were offered to Shangdì (God).
On the *Rényín* day,
bows, arrows, quivers, and arrow cases, mementos of the late Emperor, were bestowed upon Provincial Commanders-in-Chief, Brigade-Generals, and Lieutenant-Generals.
Presidents of the Board of Punishments Táo Lài and Zhāng Tíngshū were demoted for acquitting two sons in the case of Chén Mènglěi during their interrogation.
They were demoted from their official positions.
On the *Jiǎchén* day,
Hóngshǔ, son of Chún Jùnwáng, was enfeoffed as his eldest son, and Hóngchūn as *Bèizi*.
On the *Yǐsì* day,
Grand Secretary Wáng Yǎn requested retirement,
which was granted.
In the second month, *Xīnhài* day, the first day,
Fógé and Lì Tíngyí were appointed as Presidents of the Board of Punishments.
On the *Rénzǐ* day,
Zhāng Pénghé was appointed as Grand Secretary.
On the *Yǐmǎo* day,
the Sixteenth Imperial Brother Yìnlù was adopted as the heir of Zhuāng Qīnwáng Bóguǒduó,
succeeding to his title.
Qiúlín, Bóguǒduó's nephew, was enfeoffed as *Bèilè*.
On the *Gēngshēn* day,
*Bèizi* Yìntáng was disciplined.
On the *Yǐchǒu* day,
Fǔguógōng Yánxìn was enfeoffed as *Bèizi*.
Regulations were established for the examination and selection of clerks in the Boards and offices after their terms were completed and they returned to their hometowns.
An imperial edict ordered one Censor from the Censorate to submit a memorial daily.
On the *Xīnwèi* day,
Yízhàoxióng was appointed as the General of Fúzhōu.
Zhào Zhīyuán was dismissed,
and Lǐ Wéijūn was appointed as Provincial Governor of Zhílì.
On the *Jǐmǎo* day,
Deputy General Ālànà reported that the Uighurs of Luóbùnǎo'ér had submitted.
In the third month, on the *Jiǎshēn* day,
the defensive troops in Xīzàng garrisoned in Chámùduō were withdrawn.
Lóngkēduō, Mǎqí, and Nián Gēngyáo were promoted to Grand Preceptor (*Tàibǎo*).
Governor-Generals and Provincial Governors were ordered to recommend their private secretaries.
Nián Gēngyáo was enfeoffed as a Duke of the Third Rank.
On the *Rénchén* day,
Wú'ěrzhàn, Sèhéngtú, Jīngxī, and their sons, grandsons of the late Ānhé Qīnwáng Yuèlè, were ordered to relocate to Shèngjīng
and their affiliation with the imperial clan was removed.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Xīnhài,
the coffin of the Great Departed was solemnly placed in the Hall of Offerings.
Bèizi Yìnzhēn was ordered to guard it.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Yí Qīnwáng Yìnxiáng was ordered to oversee the Board of Revenue,
and his son Hóngchāng was enfeoffed as Bèizi.
Departments for translation were established for the provincial and metropolitan examinations.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the post of officials for the Diaries of Activity and Repose was reinstated.
The Seventeenth Imperial Younger Brother, Yìnlǐ, was enfeoffed as Guǒ Jùnwáng.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the Emperor first held court at the Qiánqīngmén.
Three edicts were issued, instructing and admonishing the Grand Secretaries, the Grand Ministers of the Imperial Guard, and the civil and military ministers.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Chún Jùnwáng Yìnyòu was promoted to Qīnwáng.
General-in-chiefs were ordered to submit memorials directly concerning state affairs.
In the fifth month, on the day Gēngchén,
an edict exempted soldiers dispatched from Yúnnán to Tibet from having to replace deceased horses.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Emperor held court in the Tài Hé Diàn.
Lǐ Wéijūn requested that accumulated deficits be compensated from the annual revenues of prefectures and counties.
The Emperor said:
"Officials in prefectures and counties should be given some leniency
before they can be held accountable for diligently promoting prosperity.
How can they be forced to make up for the shortfalls of others?!"
On the day Yǐyǒu,
an edict ordered Lǐ Jùnwáng Hóngyí to move to Zhèngjiāzhuāng.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Shàngshū Xú Yuánmèng was ordered to serve as acting Grand Secretary.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Empress Dowager Rénshòu passed away.
She was the Emperor's birth mother.
Her coffin was solemnly placed in the Níngshòu Gōng.
Bèizi Yìnzhēn was enfeoffed as Xún Jùnwáng.
In the sixth month, on the day Dīngsì,
Zuǒ Shìyǒng was appointed Hànjūn Dūtǒng.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Kǒngzǐ was posthumously granted the title of king for five generations of his ancestors.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the eight banners personnel without permanent property were ordered to relocate to Rèhé to reclaim land for cultivation.
On the day Rénxū,
Qīnghǎi Jùnwáng É'ěrdéní, having been defeated by Luóbùzàng Dānjīn,
led his subordinates to surrender.
Officials were dispatched to pacify them.
His nephew Gá'ěrdān Dáxī subsequently came to pledge allegiance,
and was ordered to reside together at Sūyóu.
On the day Rénshēn,
an edict was issued to Lǐ Wéijūn:
"Within the Gīdiàn,
banners people and commoners live intermixed.
The arrogance and tyranny of the banners people
cause considerable suffering to the common folk.
You must rectify this,
without avoiding distinctions between banners people and Hàn people,
and without fearing princes, dukes, meritorious subjects, or imperial relatives.
Report everything secretly."
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
an edict permitted members of the Eight Banners who were harassed or extorted by their banner's Dūtǒng or their supervising princes and dukes
to lodge complaints.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Shìláng Chángshòu was ordered to negotiate peace with Luóbùzàng Dānjīn.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
officials were dispatched to Shèngjīng, Jiāngxī, and Húguǎng to sell rice and transport it to the capital.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
an edict exempted those in Jiāngxī from mistakenly levied transport fees for grain tribute.
On the day Rénchén,
the Manchu title "Gùshān É'zhēn" was changed to "Gùshān Ángbāng",
and "Yīdū É'zhēn" to "Yīdū Zhāngjīng".
On the day Xīnsì,
this year's autumn executions were suspended.
The beggar registers for lazy people in Shàoxīng were abolished.
The Xiàojīng Yǎnyì was promulgated.
On the day Rényín,
Lóngkēduō and Wáng Xùlíng were ordered to supervise the compilation of the Míng Shǐ,
with Xú Yuánmèng and Zhāng Tíngyù as chief compilers.
In the eighth month, on the day Dīngsì,
Yáng Lín was appointed Governor-General of Guǎngdōng,
and Kǒng Yùxún was appointed Governor-General of Guǎngxī.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Emperor summoned the princes, grand ministers, and nine ministers, and personally declared to them:
"The matter of establishing an heir
should ideally be settled early.
The incident of last November
was decided suddenly,
with a single word.
Shèngzǔ was a divine sage,
beyond what I can achieve.
Now, I have personally written and sealed it,
placed it in a brocade box,
and hidden it behind the 'Zhèng Dà Guāng Míng' plaque.
All you ministers, be aware of this."
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Chángshòu reported in a memorial that he had arrived in Qīnghǎi,
and negotiated peace with Luóbùzàng Dānjīn,
but it was rejected.
An edict ordered Nián Gēngyáo to prepare troops.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the Emperor visited the imperial tombs.
In the ninth month, on the first day Dīngchǒu,
Shèngzǔ Rén Huángdì was interred in Jǐnglín,
and Xiàogōng Huánghòu was interred with him.
On this day,
five-colored clouds were seen.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Xīnsì,
Hǎo Yùlín was appointed Tídū of Yúnnán.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Zhāng Tíngyù was appointed Shàngshū of the Board of Revenue,
and Zhāng Bóháng was appointed Shàngshū of the Board of Rites.
On the day Guǐsì,
Yù Qīnwáng Bǎotài was placed in charge of the Bordered Yellow Banner affairs.
The compilation of laws and regulations was ordered.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Ālànà was appointed Měnggǔ Dūtǒng.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Wùshēn,
Nián Gēngyáo was granted the title of Fǔyuǎn Dà Jiāngjūn by imperial edict,
and Yánxìn was renamed Píngnì Jiāngjūn.
On the day Guǐhài,
Luóbùzàng Dānjīn seized our envoy Chángshòu,
and Bǐtiēshì Duō'ěrjì died.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Ā'ěrsōng'ā was appointed Shàngshū of the Board of Rites,
and Yǐntài was appointed Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ.
In the eleventh month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
Yú Zhèn and two hundred forty-six others were granted the Jinshì and various other degrees.
On the day Wùyín,
Luóbùzàng Dānjīn invaded Xīníng.
The Prefectural Commander Mǎ Yǒurén and the Assistant General Sòng Kějìn defeated him at Shēnzhōngbǎo,
and the bandits fled.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Nián Gēngyáo reported in a memorial that General-in-chief Yáng Jìnxìn had attacked the Tibetan bandits at Zhuānglàng Yǐzishān,
beheading several hundred bandits.
He received an imperial edict of commendation.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
on the Winter Solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Yuánqiū,
with Shèngzǔ Rén Huángdì honored as co-sacrificer.
In the twelfth month, on the first day Bǐngwǔ,
due to the resentment and dissatisfaction of Wú'ěrzhàn and others,
they were not permitted to inherit the title of Ān Jùnwáng,
and their affiliated companies were also dissolved.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Nián Gēngyáo reported in a memorial that bandits had launched an attack,
and Assistant General Sūn Jìzōng defeated them.
Foreigners were settled in Àomén,
the Catholic church was repurposed as a public office,
and conversion to Catholicism was strictly prohibited.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the primary consort Nàlāshì was formally invested as Empress,
Lady Niánshì was enfeoffed as Guìfēi,
Lady Niǔhùlùshì as Xīfēi,
and Lady Gěngshì as Yùpín.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the Grand Imperial Ancestral Temple held a collective sacrifice.
In this year,
disaster taxes were partially exempted for forty-nine prefectures and counties in Zhílì, Jiāngnán, and other provinces.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú paid tribute.
There were 25,326,270 registered households,
plus an additional 480,557 persons born after the permanent exemption from additional taxes.
Land tax collected amounted to 30,223,943 taels of silver and a fraction.
Salt tax amounted to 4,261,933 taels of silver and a fraction.
499,200 coins and a fraction were minted.
In the second year, on the first month, on the day Xīnsì,
prayers for good harvest were offered to Shàngdì,
with Shèngzǔ Rén Huángdì honored as co-sacrificer.
An edict ordered Grand Secretary Túhǎi to be honored in the Tàimiào.
Chángshòu returned from Luóbùzàng Dānjīn's territory
and was ordered to be imprisoned in Xī'ān.
On the day Dīnghài,
Yuè Zhōngqí was appointed Fènwēi Jiāngjūn,
exclusively commanding the campaign against Qīnghǎi.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Gāo Qípeì was appointed Hànjūn Dūtǒng.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
a Kǒngzǐ temple was built in Guīhuàchéng.
In the second month, on the day of bǐngwǔ,
the Emperor's personally composed Shèngyù Guǎngxùn
was promulgated throughout the empire.
On the day of wùwǔ,
Yuè Zhōngqí's troops reached Qīnghǎi,
capturing Ā'ěrbùtǎn Wēnbù and two other rebels,
and pacifying scattered tribes.
An imperial edict declared that the military campaign in Qīnghǎi was nearing completion,
and that Cèwàng Ālābùtǎn was submissive,
thus dismissing the troops at Ā'ěrtài and Wūlángǔmù.
On the day of xīnyǒu,
an imperial edict regarding the grand ceremony of entering the Imperial Academy
changed "visiting the academy" (xìng xué) to "proceeding to the academy" (yì xué).
On the day of guǐhài,
the Emperor plowed the sacrificial field.
After three passes were completed,
an additional pass was made.
On the day of jiǎzǐ,
an imperial decree ordered prefectures and counties to recommend elderly farmers
and grant them official insignia.
Nián Gēngyáo memorialized that Jiǎng Jiǒng, the Dao Commissioner of Liángzhuāng, had pacified the Āgāng tribe,
and was granted the title of Surveillance Commissioner.
On the day of bǐngyín,
Gāo Qízhuō memorialized that the Tibetan barbarians of Zhōngdiàn had submitted.
On the day of gēngwǔ,
the Emperor prayed for rain at Hēilóngtán.
In the third month, on the first day of the month, yǐhài,
the Emperor proceeded to the Imperial Academy to offer sacrifices to Confucius,
and gave a lecture on the Shàngshū and Dàxué in the Yílúntáng,
increasing the quota for the provincial examinations at the Imperial Academy.
On the day of dīngchǒu,
sacrifices were offered at the Temple of Past Emperors.
On the day of gēngchén,
the Emperor visited the imperial tombs.
Yuè Zhōngqí's army reached the rebel stronghold,
Luóbùzàng Dānjīn fled,
his mother Ā'ěrtài Kātún was captured,
and Qīnghǎi was pacified.
Nián Gēngyáo was enfeoffed as a first-class Duke,
Yuè Zhōngqí as a third-class Duke,
and 200,000 taels of silver were disbursed from the treasury to reward the army.
On the day of yǐyǒu,
on the Qīngmíng Festival,
the Emperor proceeded to the Jǐnglín Mausoleum to perform the earth-tending ritual.
On the day of dīnghài,
he returned to the palace.
In summer, fourth month, on the day of dīngwèi,
Kǒng Yùxún was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng,
and Lǐ Fú was appointed Governor of Guǎngxī.
On the day of gēngxū,
the Emperor summoned imperial princes and ministers to admonish Qīnwáng Yìn Sì (Lián Qīnwáng),
ordering him to reform his conduct,
and also commanded the imperial princes and ministers to observe his good and bad deeds,
and report them truthfully.
On the day of jǐsì,
Dūn Jùnwáng Yìn Táng was found guilty,
deprived of his title and imprisoned.
In the intercalary fourth month, on the day of dīngchǒu,
the compilation of the Collected Statutes was resumed.
On the day of bǐngxū,
Jī Zēngyún was appointed Vice Governor-General of River Conservancy.
On the day of dīngyǒu,
Sūdān was appointed Mongol Military Governor.
On the day of guǐwèi,
the Qīnghǎi rebel captives Ā'ěrbùtǎn Wēnbù, Chuīlākè Nuòmùqí, and Zàngbāzhābù were brought in chains to the capital,
and the Emperor personally received the captives at the Wǔmén Gate.
In the fifth month, on the first day of the month, guǐmǎo,
it was the Summer Solstice,
and sacrifices were offered to Earth at Fāngzé,
with Shèngzǔ Rén Huángdì honored as co-sacrificed.
Bèilè Ābùlán was again demoted to Fǔguó Gōng.
On the day of bǐngchén,
Bèizi Sūnǔ was impeached for being a partisan of Lián Qīnwáng and stripped of his title,
and he and his sons were all exiled to Yòuwèi.
On the day of xīnyǒu,
an imperial edict was issued to the Governors-General, Governors, Provincial Military Commanders, and Brigade Commanders of Sìchuān, Shǎnxī, Húguǎng, Yúnnán, and Guìzhōu:
"We have heard that the native chieftains in various places
seldom know the laws and regulations,
treating their subordinates harshly,
and exercising power over life and death arbitrarily.
While the whole realm now enjoys peace and prosperity,
the native people alone suffer deeply,
which Our heart cannot bear.
It is fitting to strictly admonish the native chieftains
not to act with wanton cruelty,
so as to fulfill Our ultimate intention of benefiting the common people."
On the day of rénxū,
Nàmǐn was appointed Manchu Military Governor.
On the day of wùchén,
Bèizi Hóngchūn was stripped of his title.
In the sixth month, on the day of guǐwèi,
an imperial decree forbade the Eight Banners from arbitrarily beating family members to death.
On the day of yǐyǒu,
with the pacification of Qīnghǎi,
a stone tablet was erected at the Imperial Academy.
On the day of wùxū,
the Emperor, due to the fire at Quēlǐ Temple,
offered sacrifices to the Former Master,
and dispatched officials to oversee its repair.
Bèizi Yìn Táo was demoted to Zhènguó Gōng.
Lǐ Guāngfù was dismissed,
and Lǐ Yǒngshào was appointed Minister of Works.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day of dīngsì,
the Emperor's personally composed Pángdǎng Lùn (On Factions)
was promulgated to all ministers.
On the day of rénxū,
Dīng Shòu was appointed Garrison General of Ā'ěrtài.
On the day of guǐhài,
Vice General Ālànà died in the military campaign,
and the Emperor, mindful of his long service in the field,
granted him a hereditary position.
In the eighth month, on the day of jiǎxū,
it was decreed that candidates who had to avoid certain examiners for the provincial and metropolitan examinations should be examined together,
with other ministers specially appointed to review their papers.
On the day of rénwǔ,
the autumn executions for this year were suspended.
On the day of gēngyín,
Tián Wénjìng was appointed Acting Governor of Hénán.
In the ninth month, on the first day of the month, xīncǒu,
Dīng Shòu was granted a hereditary position for his military service in Ā'ěrtài.
The practice of donating for official positions to the Board of Revenue was suspended.
On the day of jiǎyín,
it was ordered that the dīngyín tax in Shānxī be incorporated into the land tax for collection,
and subsequently this was gradually implemented in other provinces.
In winter, tenth month, on the day of yǐhài,
Chén Déhuá and 299 others were granted the jinshì degree with various ranks.
On the day of wùyín,
Zhū Zhīlián, a descendant of the Míng dynasty, was enfeoffed as a first-class Marquis,
to perpetually oversee the Míng sacrifices.
On the day of guǐwèi,
an imperial edict ordered the construction of a Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness in the capital.
On the day of yǐwèi,
an imperial edict granted the E'lǔtè Jùnwáng, E'fù Ābǎo, permission to graze his herds in Qīnghǎi.
A garrison was established at Níngxià.
On the day of bǐngshēn,
Ā'ěrsōng'ā, Minister of Justice, was stripped of his office and title
for lacking sincerity in his service,
and exiled to Shèngjīng,
with his elder cousin Yīndé inheriting the title of Guǒyì Gōng.
The Kingdom of Xiānluó presented tribute of rice seeds and fruit trees.
A Provincial Administration Commission and a Provincial Surveillance Commission were established in Zhílì,
and Governor Lǐ Wéijūn was appointed Governor-General.
On the day of gēngzǐ,
Yīndé and Kuādài were both appointed Grand Ministers of the Imperial Guard.
On the day of dīngwèi,
Sūdān was appointed General of Níngxià.
In the eleventh month, on the day of gēngxū,
Hóngshèng was stripped of his title for his crimes.
On the day of yǐmǎo,
Chuòqí was appointed Mongol Military Governor,
and Gá'ěrbì was appointed Han Military Governor.
On the day of dīngsì,
Gāo Qízhuō memorialized that the government troops had advanced and pacified the Zhòng Miáo.
It was pacified.
On the day of xīnyǒu,
the mausoleum of Empress Xiàozhuāng Wén was designated Zhāoxī Líng.
In the twelfth month, on the day of guǐyǒu,
it was ordered that a tablet bearing the names of jinshì be erected at the Imperial Academy.
On the day of guǐwèi,
the deposed Crown Prince Yìn Rěng died,
and was posthumously enfeoffed as Lǐ Qīnwáng,
with the posthumous title Mì.
Chuòqí was appointed General of Fèngtiān.
On the day of jǐchǒu,
Yù Qīnwáng Bǎotài was stripped of his title for his crimes,
and his nephew Guǎngníng inherited the title of Yù Qīnwáng.
An Education Commissioner was established for Húnán.
On the day of wùxū,
the grand seasonal sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In this year,
various amounts of disaster relief were granted for taxes in 57 prefectures, counties, and garrisons in provinces such as Jiāngnán and Zhèjiāng.
Cháoxiǎn, Ānnán, and Xiānluó paid tribute.
In the third year, yǐsì, spring, first month, on the day of guǐchǒu,
an imperial edict allocated 200 qǐng of state land in Gù'ān as jǐngtián,
and dispatched idle Eight Banner members to cultivate it.
On the day of rénxū,
Cài Tǐng was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the day of guǐhài,
Āqítú was appointed Commander of the Gendarmerie.
In the second month, on the day of gēngwǔ,
the sun and moon were conjoined,
and the five planets formed a conjunction.
On the day of gēngchén,
the Emperor, having completed the three-year mourning period,
performed the grand seasonal sacrifice.
On the day of dīnghài,
an imperial edict reprimanded Nián Gēngyáo for failing to pacify and care for the remnants of the Qīnghǎi tribes,
stating that if even one or two individuals escaped into Zhǔngá'ěr,
he would be severely punished.
On the day of yǐwèi,
Èlúndài was stripped of his office and title for being a partisan of Lián Qīnwáng,
and exiled to Shèngjīng,
with his younger brother Kuādài inheriting the title of first-class Duke.
On the day of dīngyǒu,
the Emperor summoned court officials to declare the crimes of Yìn Táng,
also implicating Yìn Sì, Yìn Táng, and Yìn Tí.
In the third month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
Mǎ Huìbó was appointed Grand Protector (Tídū) of Guìzhōu.
Cèwàng Ālābùtǎn sent envoys to offer tribute.
An Education Commissioner (Xuézhèng) for Ānhuī was established.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Grand Secretary Zhāng Pénghé passed away.
Minister of Rites (Lǐbù Shàngshū) Zhāng Bóxíng passed away.
On the *dīngsì* day,
450,000 taels of floating grain tax were remitted for Sūzhōu and Sōngjiāng.
Mǎn Bǎo reported that seventy-four communities of uncivilized aboriginals (shēngfān) in Táiwān had assimilated.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Nián Gēngyáo submitted a congratulatory memorial for the conjunction of the sun and moon (rìyuè hébì)
and the alignment of five planets (wǔxīng liánzhū),
but
wrote "cháo gān xī tì" (diligent day and night)
as
"xī tì cháo gān" (diligent night and day).
An imperial edict severely rebuked him, saying:
"Nián Gēngyáo is not a careless person.
This directly implies that he does not consider 'cháo gān xī tì' to apply to Us.
In that case, Nián Gēngyáo's achievements in Qīnghǎi
are also subject to Our approval or disapproval,
which is uncertain.
This is clearly disrespectful.
He must reply clearly."
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Grand Minister (Zǒnglǐ Wáng Dàchén) and Prince Yí Yìnxiáng was granted one son as a Commandery Prince (Jùnwáng);
Lóngkēduō and Mǎ Qí were given additional hereditary posts (shìzhí).
Prince Lián Yìnshì was not included,
and was severely admonished by imperial edict.
In summer, fourth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
Nián Gēngyáo was transferred to be General (Jiāngjūn) of Hángzhōu.
Yuè Zhōngqí was appointed Governor-General (Zǒngdū) of Sìchuān and Shǎnxī.
Scholar Zhòng Fóbǎo and Deputy Commander (Fù Dūtǒng) Zhā Shǐ were dispatched to Zhǔngá'ěr to demarcate the border.
Dǒng Jínà was appointed General of Jiāngníng.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Tián Cóngdiǎn was appointed Grand Secretary.
In the fifth month, on the *guǐhài* day,
Left Censor-in-Chief (Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ) Yǐn Tài was appointed Vice Minister of Rites (Lǐbù Shìláng) for Shèngjīng,
concurrently managing the Prefect (Fǔyǐn) of Fèngtiān.
In the sixth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
an edict ordered that Nián Gēngyáo's sons Nián Fù and Nián Xīng,
and Lóngkēduō's son Yù Zhù, all be stripped of their offices.
On the *yǐhài* day,
it was ordered that sons of hereditary officials of the Upper Three Banners (shàng sān qí shìzhí) and those who scaled city walls (dēngchéng bátúlǔ),
who were twenty years old or younger,
and fourteen years old or older,
be selected, granted audience, and appointed.
Nián Gēngyáo was stripped of his Grand Tutor (Tàibǎo) title.
Soon after, he was stripped of his First Class Duke (Yīděng Gōng) title.
In autumn, seventh month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
Lóngkēduō was stripped of his Grand Tutor title.
On the *rénxū* day,
Grand Secretary Bái Huáng was dismissed.
Gāo Qíwèi was appointed Grand Secretary,
and Zhāng Tíngyù was made Acting Grand Secretary.
Lóngkēduō was ordered to go to Ālánshàn Mountain to repair fortifications.
On the *rénxū* day,
General of Hángzhōu Nián Gēngyáo was demoted to an idle banner member (xiánsǎn qíyuán).
On the *guǐhài* day,
Bèizi Yìn táng, having committed crimes, was stripped of his princely title.
In the eighth month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Lǐ Wéijūn was arrested and interrogated for factionalism with Nián Gēngyáo.
Lǐ Fú was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Emperor resided at Yuánmíngyuán.
Prince Yí Yìnxiáng's stipend was increased.
Prince Guǒ Yìn Lǐ was granted imperial guard duty.
In the ninth month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
Zhū Shì was appointed Grand Secretary.
Cài Tǐng was transferred to be Minister of Personnel (Lìbù Shàngshū),
still concurrently managing the Board of War (Bīngbù) and the Censorate (Dūcháyuàn).
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Nián Gēngyáo was arrested and sent to the Board of Punishments (Xíngbù).
In winter, tenth month, on the *wùchén* day,
it was decreed that provincial governors (xúnfǔ) who did not reside in the same city as the governor-general (zǒngdū)
could impeach their subordinate officials
and personally conclude the trials.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Héng Qīnwáng Yìnqí's son Hóngzhì was enfeoffed as an Auxiliary Duke (Fǔguó Gōng).
On the *gēngyín* day,
Yáng Míngshí was appointed Governor-General of Yúnnán and Guìzhōu,
managing affairs of the provincial governor.
È'ěrtài was appointed Provincial Governor of Yúnnán,
managing affairs of the governor-general.
In the eleventh month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
the Emperor visited the imperial tombs (yèlǐng).
On the *wùshēn* day,
he returned to the palace.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Gá'ěrbì was appointed General of Fèngtiān.
In the twelfth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
Commandery Prince Yìn tí was demoted to Bèizi.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
court officials debated Nián Gēngyáo's ninety-two crimes.
An imperial decree was received:
"Nián Gēngyáo is granted death by suicide.
His son Nián Fù shall be immediately beheaded.
His other sons shall be exiled to the military frontiers.
Their father and elder brothers are exempt from implication."
On the *xīnsì* day,
Wāng Jǐngqí was executed by beheading for slander.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Juéluó Bāyándé was appointed Commander (Dūtǒng) of the Tiānjīn Naval Camp.
On the *rénchén* day,
the grand sacrifice (jiáp jì) was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple (Tàimiào).
In this year,
disaster relief taxes were remitted to varying degrees in twenty-seven prefectures and counties across provinces such as Zhílì, Jiāngsū, Hénán, Zhèjiāng, and Guǎngdōng.
Cháoxiǎn, Liúqiú, and Xīyáng (Western countries) offered tribute.
Fourth year, on the *bǐngwǔ* day in spring, first month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Emperor presided over the Taìhé Diàn to receive court congratulations.
Outer vassals (wàifān) presented their respects for the New Year,
and according to the precedent of previous dynasties,
were bestowed with silver and silk.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
an edict denouncing the crimes of Imperial Ninth Brother Yìn táng was proclaimed.
On the *wùxū* day,
court officials were assembled to proclaim an edict denouncing the crimes of Imperial Eighth Brother Yìnshì.
His princely title was changed to Commoner Prince (Mínwáng).
He was stripped of his yellow girdle,
and his name was removed from the imperial genealogy.
His wife, Fùjìn of the Wūyǎ clan, was dismissed,
and sent back to her maternal family.
Then, he was stripped of his Commoner Prince title again,
and imprisoned in the Imperial Clan Court (Zōngrénfǔ).
An imperial decree ordered his name to be changed to Āqínà,
and his son Hóngwàng's name to Púsàbǎo.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Lóngkēduō was stripped of his office,
but still ordered to go to Russia to negotiate the border.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the deceased Minister Gù Bādài was posthumously granted the title of Grand Tutor (Tàifù)
and posthumously named Wénduān,
for he was the Emperor's teacher (shòudú shī).
In the second month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Sūn Zhù was appointed Minister of Personnel,
concurrently managing the Board of War.
Fǎ Hǎi was appointed Minister of War,
and Fú Mǐn was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
Bèizi Lǔ Bīn and Duke of the State Protector (Zhèngguógōng) Yǒngqiān were both stripped of their princely titles for equivocating in the trial of Yìnshì.
Soon after, Lǔ Bīn was reinstated as an Auxiliary Duke.
Grand Secretary Zhū Shì's mother passed away,
and he was granted four thousand *pǐ* of silver for funeral expenses.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Prince Jiǎn Yǎ'ěrjiāng'ā was stripped of his princely title.
His younger brother Shénbǎozhù inherited the title.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Zhāng Tíngyù was appointed Grand Secretary.
Jiǎng Tíngxí was appointed Minister of Revenue (Hùbù Shàngshū).
Shēn Mùdé was appointed Right Guard General (Yòuwèi Jiāngjūn).
In the third month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
Dīng Shòu was ordered to station troops at Tèsī
in preparation for Cèwàng Ālābùtǎn.
On the *rénxū* day,
the incident of Court Lecturer (Shìjiǎng) Qián Míngshì sending poems to Nián Gēngyáo came to light.
He was stripped of his official titles.
The Emperor personally wrote
the four characters "Míngjiào Zuìrén" (sinner against moral teachings)
and hung them on his gate,
and also ordered civil officials to write essays and poems condemning his wickedness.
In summer, fourth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
Fàn Shíyì was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng.
In the fifth month, on the *guǐsì* day,
Imperial Fourteenth Brother Yìn tí and his son Bái Qǐ were imprisoned next to the Shòuhuáng Diàn.
His son Bái Dūn was enfeoffed as a Duke of the State Protector.
Èlúndài and Ā'ěrsōng'ā were executed at their places of exile.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Yìn táng's name was changed to Sàisīhēi,
and he was imprisoned in Bǎodìng.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Prince Shùnchéng Xībǎo was ordered to receive the stipend of a Prince of the First Rank (Qīnwáng).
Imperial Fifteenth Brother Yìn● was enfeoffed as a Bèilè,
and Imperial Twentieth Brother Yìn Yǐ as a Bèizi.
In the sixth month, on the *guǐhài* day,
Auxiliary Duke Bāsài was appointed General Zhènwǔ
to guard the border.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Zhā Bìnà was appointed Minister of War.
In autumn, seventh month, on the *guǐsì* day,
thirteen people, including Court Censor (Yùshǐ) Táo Yí, were released from military custody.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Cài Tǐng was ordered to exclusively manage the Commander (Dūtǒng) office.
Zhā Bìnà and Yáng Míngshí were appointed Ministers of Personnel.
Prince Píng Nà'ěrsù, having committed crimes, was stripped of his princely title.
His son Fú Péng inherited the title.
In the eighth month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
the autumn executions for this year were suspended.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Lǐ Fú reported that Sàisīhēi had died in Bǎodìng.
In the ninth month, on the day Rénchén,
Yí Zhàoxióng was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng.
Soon after, Fú Mǐn was ordered to replace him.
Cài Liáng was appointed General of Fúzhōu.
Bèizi Mǎndūhù was demoted to Fǔguó Gōng [Duke Who Assists the State],
and his banner company was withdrawn.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Fǔguó Gōng Ābùlán was stripped of his title for violating regulations in expressing gratitude,
and his banner company was withdrawn.
On the day Wùxū,
the Double Ninth Festival,
the Emperor attended at the Qiánqīng Gōng,
bestowed a banquet upon the court officials,
and composed a Bǎiliáng-style poem.
On the day Jǐhài,
Xībǎo reported that Āqínà had died in custody.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Grand Secretary Zhū Shì was reinstated to serve in the Grand Secretariat.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Vice Minister Zhā Sìtíng was imprisoned for slander.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
a Commissioner for Observing Customs and Rectifying Morals was established in Zhèjiāng.
It was ordered that those who passed the provincial examinations as 'alternate candidates' (fùbǎng) based on the Five Classics, and those who passed as 'alternate candidates' twice,
would be granted the status of jǔrén.
On the day Wùchén,
an edict was issued to the court officials:
"My august father reigned for over sixty years,
personally practicing frugality and moderation.
The palace carpets were used for thirty to forty years,
yet they remained clean and tidy.
His clothes and personal effects
were always plain and simple,
rarely precious or rare.
Yesterday, when I inspected the old artifacts
and took out the furnishings from the Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng [Mountain Resort for Escaping the Heat],
my thoughts of his splendid virtues
were truly endless.
Therefore, I specially wrote this
to instruct my sons and grandsons."
On the day Xīnsì,
Yù Qīnwáng Guǎngníng was stripped of his title
and perpetually imprisoned in the Zōngrén Fǔ [Imperial Clan Court].
On the day Jiǎshēn,
due to the Miao territory of Pǔxióng
bordering Sìchuān and Diān [Yúnnán],
the Governor-General of Chuān-Shǎn [Sìchuān and Shǎnxī] was ordered to relocate his residence to Chéngdū.
È'ěrtài was appointed Governor-General of Yún-Guì,
and Xiàndé was appointed Governor of Húběi.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the Kingdom of Liúqiú expressed gratitude for the bestowed plaque
and offered tribute.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jǐhài,
Grand Secretary Gāo Qíwèi was dismissed.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Fùníng'ān was granted the title of First-Class Marquis
for his long service in guarding the frontier.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
an edict stated that the scholarly customs in Zhèjiāng were corrupt
and that cheating was prevalent;
therefore, its provincial and metropolitan examinations were suspended.
In the twelfth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
the princes and high ministers requested that the wives of Āqínà and Sàisīhēi be executed.
The imperial decree stated:
"Although Āqínà and Sàisīhēi were extremely rebellious and disloyal,
their acts of rebellion have not been clearly demonstrated,
so their families are exempted from implication.
Sàisīhēi's wife shall be sent back to her maternal home and confined.
Their other family members
shall be supported by the Nèi Wù Fǔ [Imperial Household Department]."
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Hénán, Shǎnxī, and Sìchuān were ordered to uniformly distribute the poll tax (dīngyín) into the land tax for collection.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Censor Xiè Jìshì memorialized to impeach Tián Wénjìng on ten charges.
An edict stripped Tián Wénjìng of his office and banished him.
On the day Rénshēn,
È'ěrtài reported that twenty-one villages of the Zhòng Miao who had submitted were pacified,
and over thirty thousand mu of cultivated and uncultivated land were found.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Lǐ Fú was appointed Right Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works.
Yí Zhàoxióng was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì.
Liú Shīshù was to assist him.
Máo Wénquán was appointed General of Jīngkǒu.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the collective sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào [Imperial Ancestral Temple].
In this year,
disaster relief was granted by exempting taxes in sixty-three prefectures, counties, and garrisons in provinces such as Zhílì, Shāndōng, Ānhuī, Jiāngxī, and Húguǎng, with varying degrees.
Cháoxiǎn [Korea], Liúqiú, and Sūlù offered tribute.
In the fifth year, Dīngwèi, spring, first month, on the first day, Wùzǐ,
the seasonal sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
On the day Rényín,
the sons of Nián Gēngyáo who had been banished to the frontier were pardoned.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the princes and high ministers reported that the Yellow River had cleared [itself of sediment]
and requested a congratulatory court audience.
The Emperor did not permit it.
All civil and military officials were promoted one rank.
An imperial decree ordered the Eight Banners to hand over copper articles.
Those who concealed them after the three-year deadline
would be punished.
On the day Yǐsì,
Sūn Zhù was appointed Acting Grand Secretary.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Shěn Jìnsī was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
In the second month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
the Emperor visited the imperial tombs.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the garrison soldiers in Guǎngzhōu caused trouble.
General Lǐ Dì was sentenced to death for condoning and shielding them.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the Emperor attended the imperial lectures.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Lǐ Fú was ordered to go to Guǎngxī to apprehend the escaped criminal Luó Wéngāng.
Wéngāng surrendered himself.
In the third month, on the day Gēngyín,
an imperial decree ordered that this year's metropolitan examination be held in the third month,
and ginger soup and charcoal be provided.
Guǎnglù succeeded to the title of Yù Qīnwáng.
On the day Wùxū,
the Emperor publicly declared the crimes of Cài Tǐng
and had him imprisoned and interrogated by the Ministry of Justice.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the maritime prohibition in Mǐnshěng [Fújiàn province] was lifted.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the envoy Sàwǎ from Luóluósī Cháhàn [Russia's Tsar] offered congratulations on the Emperor's ascension to the throne,
presented tribute,
and was granted rewards according to precedent.
Grand Minister Mǎ Wǔ died.
Grand Secretary Gāo Qíwèi died.
In the intercalary third month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
unsuccessful jǔrén candidates were selected
and dispatched to the direct provinces
to serve as prefectural and county officials.
On the day Wùchén,
Yí Zhàoxióng was appointed Minister of Personnel.
Mài Zhù was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the two native prefectures of Wūméng and Zhènxíóng were reorganized with appointed officials.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Juéluó Yīlǐbù was appointed General of Fèngtiān.
Chángshòu was appointed General of Jiāngníng.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Hóngshēng was stripped of his title for committing a crime.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
the Hui chieftain of Tǔlǔfān requested to offer tribute.
This was not permitted,
as the troops had already been withdrawn,
and because the territory had been promised to Cèwàng Ālābùtǎn.
Fú Mǐn was appointed Minister of Personnel.
Huáng Guócái was appointed Acting Minister of War.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Péng Qǐfēng and two hundred twenty-six others were granted the status of jìnshì, with varying degrees.
On the day Guǐsì,
prefectural and county officials were ordered to recommend outstanding students in conjunction with school officials.
On the day Yǐsì,
two Censors from the Imperial Clan were appointed.
In the fifth month, on the day Wùwǔ,
Lāxī was appointed Manchu Grand Commander.
Zhā Sìtíng died in prison,
and his corpse was desecrated.
On the day Yǐhài,
for his achievements in Wūméng and Zhènxíóng,
È'ěrtài was granted a hereditary position.
In the sixth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
one Deputy Grand Commander from Shèngjīng was moved to Jinzhōu.
A Deputy Grand Commander of Xióngyuè was established.
Hóngjǐng, son of Chéng Qīnwáng Yìněnzhǐ, was enfeoffed as Zhèngguó Gōng [Duke Who Guards the State].
Lóngkēduō was stripped of his title for a crime.
His younger brother, Qìngfù, succeeded to the title of First-Class Duke.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day *Yǐmǎo*
Fùníng'ān was appointed Han Army Grand Commandant.
On the day *Jǐwèi*,
Lǐ Yǒngshào was dismissed,
and Huáng Guócái was appointed Minister of Works.
Tián Wénjìng was promoted to Minister
and made Governor-General of Hénán.
On the day *Jǐsì*,
Kuādài was appointed Minister of Works.
On the day *Bǐngzǐ*,
Fǔguógōng Hóngzhì, Èqí, and Xīliáng were promoted to Zhènguógōng.
The deposed Bèilè Sūnú had smeared the imperial vermilion edicts of Shèngzǔ.
This was impeached by the princes, ministers, and the Ministry of Justice.
An imperial decree was issued:
“Sūnú, entrenched in his wickedness, is incorrigible.
He even allowed his sons Sūěrjīn, Kùěrchen, and Wūěrchen to follow the Western religion.
When ordered to repent and change,
he defiantly declared: ‘I am willing to suffer the correct punishment;
I cannot change my religion.’
Now it has also been discovered that on a memorial of Shèngzǔ from years past,
he dared to scribble and smear,
a sight that makes one’s hair stand on end.
He should immediately be executed according to the law for high treason.
However, as he has as many as forty descendants,
to execute them all
would be unbearable.
If we were to distinguish who should live and who should die,
how would one even make such a distinction?
For now, he is spared death,
and is to remain imprisoned as before.”
In the eighth month, on the day *Jǐchǒu*,
the emperor attended the imperial lectures.
On the day *Gēngyín*,
Làidōu was dismissed,
and Chángshòu was appointed Minister of Rites.
On the day *Guǐmǎo*,
the late Píngnán Dàjiāngjūn Lài Tǎ was posthumously ennobled as a first-class *Gōng*,
and his grandson Bóěrtún inherited the title.
On the day *Yǐsì*,
Kāěrkā Jùnwáng Ěfù Cèlíng and the Russian envoy Sàwǎ defined the border,
making Qiàkètú a place for trade,
with the Lǐfānyuàn dispatching officials to manage it.
In the ninth month, on the day *Bǐngyín*,
the system for officials' hats and insignia was established.
Sūn Zhù was appointed Grand Secretary,
and Zhā Bìnà was appointed Minister of War.
On the day *Jǐsì*,
Èěrtài reported that the Huāmiáo had submitted,
and that the Làngqú were suppressed and pacified.
The Wēiyuǎn Luǒmiáo also submitted.
On the day *Wùyín*,
the Ministry of Justice deliberated on the case of Cài Tǐng,
finding eighteen major crimes,
for which he should be immediately beheaded,
and his wife and children enslaved in the *Xīnhzhěkù*.
An imperial decree was issued
to change the sentence to delayed execution.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day *Yǐyǒu*,
it was ordered that Censorate officials and Ministry of Personnel department officials need not exclusively be selected from examination graduates.
On the day *Dīnghài*,
the princes and ministers jointly reviewed the case of Lóngkēduō,
finding fifty major crimes,
for which he should be immediately beheaded,
his wife and children enslaved in the *Xīnhzhěkù*,
and his property confiscated.
An imperial decree was issued
that Lóngkēduō be imprisoned.
Bóěrtún was appointed Mongolian Grand Commandant.
In the eleventh month, on the day *Guǐchǒu*,
Zhā Lángā and Mài Lù were ordered to defend the border.
On the day *Dīngsì*,
Lǐ Wèi, Governor of Zhèjiāng, was promoted to Governor-General.
On the day *Dīngmǎo*,
Áobài was posthumously restored to first-class *Gōng*,
and his grandson Dá Fú was ordered to inherit the title.
An imperial edict ordered the compilation of the *Zhízhōng Chéngxiàn*.
On the day *Wùchén*,
Èěrtài reported that 184 villages of raw Miao, including Kèměng and others, in the rear road of Chángzhài in Guìzhōu had submitted.
On the day *Yǐhài*,
Xiāo Yǒngzǎo, Grand Secretary guarding the Jǐnglín, was impeached for failing to supervise Gǔanshàn, a titled official, who overstepped his bounds in offering salutations.
He was stripped of his office,
but remained guarding the mausoleum as before.
On the day *Gēngchén*,
officials were dispatched to survey land in Sìchuān.
Shùnchéng Jùnwáng Xībǎo was stripped of his princely stipend for shielding Yánxìn and seizing his relative,
and his *Jùnwáng* stipend was also suspended for three years.
In the twelfth month, on the new moon day *Rénwǔ*,
Nàsūtú was appointed General of Hēilóngjiāng.
On the day *Yǐyǒu*,
it was ordered that provincial education commissioners select students once every six years.
The princes and ministers deliberated on Bèilè Yánxìn’s twenty major crimes,
for which he should be executed.
An imperial decree was issued
that Yánxìn be spared death
and imprisoned with Lóngkēduō.
On the day *Xīnchǒu*,
Fàn Shíyì reported that the people of Qīpǔ in Tàicāngzhōu wished to repair and dredge waterways themselves.
The emperor did not permit it,
saying:
“The livelihood of the people
is the national livelihood.
When national expenditures are insufficient,
we must rely on the people’s strength.
However, as national expenditures are currently ample,
we shall still issue silver from the treasury for this.”
On the day *Wùxū*,
Shěn Jìnsī, Left Censor-in-Chief, passed away.
On the day *Rényín*,
Táng Zhíyù was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
On the day *Gēngxū*,
the ancestral temple was collectively worshipped.
In this year,
tax exemptions for disasters were granted to varying degrees in thirty-four prefectures and counties in Zhílì, Jiāngsū, Jiāngxī, Zhèjiāng, Fújiàn, Húguǎng, and Guǎngdōng provinces.
Cháoxiǎn and Éluósī offered tribute.
In the sixth year, *Wùshēn*, spring, the first month, on the day *Jǐwèi*,
Gāo Qízhuō submitted a memorial detailing the state of armed conflicts in the Mǐn province.
An imperial decree was issued:
“In such places, one must encourage subordinate officials to exert themselves genuinely and diligently,
only then can there be success.
Should one or two capable individuals emerge,
as soon as they wish to bring order,
they are immediately labeled as meddlesome.
When subordinate officials observe this hidden dynamic,
who would be willing to face resentment and move forward?
It is necessary to understand the difficulty and yet persevere,
only after two or three years will there be results.”
On the day *Yǐchǒu*,
Bèilè Qiúlín was promoted to Huì Jùnwáng,
and Zhènguógōng Hóngchūn to Bèizǐ.
On the day *Jǐmǎo*,
Háng Yìlù and Rèn Lánzhī were ordered to be envoys to Ānnán.
In the second month, on the day *Bǐngxū*,
Guǒ Jùnwáng Yìnlǐ was promoted to Qīnwáng.
On the day *Guǐsì*,
the emperor attended the imperial lectures.
On the day *Gēngzǐ*,
Lái Wén was appointed General of Jiāngníng.
On the day *Rényín*,
Péng Zhàohuái, the chieftain of Yǒngshùn who had submitted, was granted a hereditary position,
along with ten thousand *liǎng* of white gold.
On the day *Gēngxū*,
Jī Zēngyún was appointed Minister of War,
and continued to manage river conservancy.
In the third month, on the day *Dīngsì*,
Grand Secretary Tián Cóngdiǎn was dismissed,
and Jiǎng Tíngxī was appointed Grand Secretary.
On the day *Gēngwǔ*,
with the imperial troops entering Zàng stationed in Xīníng,
Governor Háng Yìlù was ordered to supervise them.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day *Jiǎshēn*,
Chén Tài was appointed Manchu Grand Commandant.
The retired Grand Secretary Tián Cóngdiǎn passed away.
On the day *Guǐmǎo*,
Zhā Lángā and Jī Zēngyún were appointed Ministers of Personnel.
On the day *Rényín*,
an imperial edict stated:
“Local officials privately levying surcharges on taxes
are difficult to eliminate.
It is solely up to the governors-general and governors to prudently use them,
but they must not be converted to public funds.
If they are converted to public funds,
then local officials will again exploit the people.”
In the fifth month, on the day *Guǐchǒu*,
Guō Hóng was appointed Governor of Guǎngxī.
Èěrtài reported the suppression of the rebellious Miao Lù Tiānyòu and Lù Shìháo in Dōngchuān,
and their pacification.
On the day *Rénxū*,
an imperial edict stated:
“Among the eight provisions [for leniency], the clause regarding old age
is not entirely clear in its meaning.
Any elderly person who is still capable of handling affairs
should not be included in the eight provisions.”
On the day *Dīngmǎo*,
Fùníng'ān’s marquisate was revoked,
but he remained Grand Secretary.
Mǎěrsài was ordered to work within the Grand Secretariat.
On the day *Yǐhài*,
Tián Wénjìng was appointed Governor-General of Hédōng,
also overseeing Shāndōng.
Gěng Huàzuò was appointed Han Army Grand Commandant.
In the sixth month, on the day *Gēngchén*,
an imperial edict ordered that the *yuánwàiláng* and *zhǔshì* of the Six Boards be treated as common vacancies,
and not be promoted based on banners.
On the day *Guǐwèi*,
a Five Classics Erudite was established for the descendants of the Former Worthy Zhònggōng.
On the day *Bǐngxū*,
Cài Liáng was appointed General of Guǎngzhōu,
Shílǐhā was appointed General of Fúzhōu,
and Yǐn Jìshàn was assigned to assist in the river conservancy work in Jiāngnán.
On the day *Guǐsì*,
Zhāng Guǎngsì was appointed Governor of Guìzhōu,
and Yuè Jùn was acting Governor of Shāndōng.
On the day *Jǐhài*,
Chéng Qīnwáng Yìněr Zhǐ was demoted to *Jùnwáng* due to offenses,
and his son Hóngshèng was detained in the Zōngrénfǔ.
Lǐmì Qīnwáng’s son Hóngyàn was ennobled as Fǔguógōng.
In the autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Xīnhài,
Lǐ Wèi was ordered to concurrently manage the detective affairs of Jiāngsū.
On the day Wǔwǔ,
È'ěrtài reported that troops had been dispatched to suppress and pacify the Mǐtiē rebel Miao in Chuān territory.
It was ordered that this matter be assigned to the Sichuan Tídū Huáng Tíngguì.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Yuè Zhōngqí reported that Pōluónài's troops had arrived in Xīzàng,
and the Lamas had captured and presented Ā'ěrbùbā, Lóngbùnài, Zhā'ěrnài, and others.
Xīzàng was pacified.
On the day Wùchén,
Jì Chéngbīn was appointed Gùyuán Tídū.
On the day Rénshēn,
Grand Secretary Fùníng'ān passed away.
Níng Lán, a third-generation descendant of the late Grand Secretary Níng Wánwǒ, was bestowed the title of Xiāoqíxiào,
a residence,
and five hundred silver taels.
Níng Bāngxǐ, a fourth-generation descendant, was appointed Bàitáng'ā.
In the eighth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
His Majesty attended the Classics Mat Lecture.
Yǐn Jìshàn was appointed acting Jiāngsū Xúnfǔ.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the two Tǔsī of Sāngzhí and Bǎojìng in Húguǎng were converted to permanent official administration.
Mǎ'ěrsài was appointed Grand Secretary.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Zǔ Bǐnghéng was appointed Jīngkǒu Jiāngjūn.
On the day Dīngwèi,
an edict was issued to reinstate the provincial and metropolitan examinations in Zhèjiāng.
In the ninth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
it was ordered that descendants of meritorious officials and old families of the Eight Banners who had committed crimes or embezzled funds
be thoroughly investigated and reported.
Descendants of Han officials who died in battle, devoted themselves to duty, or held office with integrity,
were to be investigated and reported in the same manner.
Gōng Èqí, Dūtǒng of the Tiānjīn Naval Camp, was stripped of his rank for failing to supervise his soldiers, resulting in injury to an official,
and demoted to a third-class imperial guard.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Zhā Láng'ā reported that he had led troops to Xīzàng,
and together with Fùdūtǒng Mǎlā and Xuéshì Sēnggé, had interrogated and confirmed the rebel leaders Ā'ěrbùbā and others.
They were immediately executed,
and the rest of the rebels were dealt with.
In the winter, in the tenth month, on the day Dīnghài,
È'ěrtài, having suppressed and pacified the Bādázhài rebel Miao in Guǎngxī,
was concurrently appointed supervisor of the three provinces of Yúnnán, Guìzhōu, and Guǎngxī.
One hundred thousand taels of silver from the imperial treasury were allocated to reward the soldiers of Diān and Qián.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
nine hundred and forty thousand taels from the imperial treasury were disbursed to compensate the Western Expeditionary soldiers for outstanding payments.
Shí Wénzhuō was appointed Lǐbù Shàngshū,
and Lù Zhènyáng was appointed Bīngbù Shàngshū.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Yuè Zhōngqí reported that the Lārǔwō indigenous rebels in Jiànchāng had caused disturbances,
and he had suppressed them.
An edict stated:
"There are many Tǔsī in Húguǎng;
they perform their duties and contribute resources,
no different from permanent officials.
