The Gāidū Fǔ should not lightly discuss converting them to permanent official administration."
Cài Shìshān was appointed Zhèjiāng Guānfēng Zhěngsúshǐ.
On the day Guǐsì,
an imperial decree ordered the cessation of management of Banner affairs by the various princes.
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngchén,
the Xián'āngōng Guānxué was established,
where children of the Bāoyī studied.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the execution of prisoners for this year was suspended.
On the day Wùchén,
Jiāngxī Xúnfǔ Bùlántài was dismissed for incompetence.
An additional Westerner was appointed Jiānfù in the Qīntiānjiān.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
the seven-year quota tax of Chóngqìng Zhōu, Sìchuān, was remitted.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the "Dàqīng Lǜ Jíjiě Fùlì" was completed.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Pōluónài was enfeoffed as Bèizi for his meritorious service in pacifying Xīzàng,
and tasked with managing the affairs of Hòuzàng.
Two Gālóng were selected to manage the affairs of Qiánzàng.
His soldiers were rewarded with thirty thousand taels of silver.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Shìláng Wáng Jī and Péng Wéixīn were ordered to go to Jiāngnán to investigate outstanding taxes.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the collective sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted to varying degrees in twenty-six prefectures and counties in provinces such as Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Shǎnxī, and Sìchuān.
Cháoxiǎn paid tribute.
In the seventh year, on the day Xīnhài of the first month of spring, Yǐyǒu,
È'ěrtài reported that on the occasion of the Longevity Festival,
auspicious clouds were seen in Yúnnán.
It was ordered to be recorded in the Imperial Archives.
On the day Dīngsì,
Chén Yuánlóng and Yǐn Tài were appointed Grand Secretaries.
On the day Rénshēn,
the Mongol Marquis Ēngédé'ěr's title was restored as a third-class Duke,
to be inherited by his great-grandson Gá'ěrsà.
The Mongol second-class Earl Míng'ān was promoted to first-class Marquis,
to be inherited by his grandson Mǎlántài.
Dūtǒng Earl Sìgé was imprisoned for crimes;
His Majesty, remembering the merits of his grandfather Mǎnggù'ěrdài,
released him.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Shìláng Fǎbǎo and others were ordered to inspect and repair the main road from Zhílì to Jiāngnán.
In the second month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
it was ordered that officers and soldiers on expedition be given "sitting rations" in addition to "travel rations."
Yǐn Jìshàn was appointed Hédào Zǒngdū.
On the day Wùyín,
Duōsuǒlǐ was appointed Fèngtiān Jiāngjūn.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
His Majesty visited the imperial tombs.
On the day Gēngyín,
he returned to the capital.
An Agricultural Censor for Zhílì was established.
On the day Jǐhài,
Yíqīnwáng and others were ordered to investigate instances where hereditary positions of the Eight Banners had been abolished due to lack of heirs;
it was permitted for clan members to inherit the enfeoffment.
On the day Yǐwèi,
His Majesty attended the Classics Mat Lecture.
Lǐ Dié was appointed Hànjūn Dūtǒng.
Sixty thousand taels of Zhèjiāng's quota tax for this year were remitted.
On the first day of the third month, Yǐsì,
Kǒng Yùkē was appointed Jiāngnán Hédào Zǒngdū,
and Hǎo Yùlín was appointed Guǎngdōng Zǒngdū.
Yuè Zhōngqí reported the suppression and pacification of over one hundred rebel Miao villages in Léibō.
On the day Wùshēn,
È'ěrtài reported the suppression and pacification of the wild Miao in Dānjiāng, Jiǔgǔ, and other places.
Four hundred thousand taels of Hénán's quota tax for this year were remitted.
On the day Xīnhài,
Jī Zēngjūn was appointed Hénán Shāndōng Zǒngdū.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
His Majesty, believing that Zhǔngá'ěr's Gá'ěrdān Cèlíng had accumulated evil and harbored deceit,
and would eventually become a border threat,
appointed Fù'ěrdān as Jìngbiān Dàjiāngjūn,
to lead an army on the northern route,
and Yuè Zhōngqí as Níngyuǎn Dàjiāngjūn,
to lead an army on the western route,
to conquer Zhǔngá'ěr.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Èshàn and Mǎnghúlí were both appointed Měnggǔ Dūtǒng.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
an edict appointed Duke Bāsài as Fùjiāngjūn,
Shùnchéng Jùnwáng Xībǎo as Zhènwǔ Jiāngjūn,
Chén Tài, Gǔntài, Shílǐhā, Dàiháo, Dáfú, and Hǎilán as Cāncàn.
Six thousand Banner soldiers,
eight thousand soldiers from three provinces,
and eight hundred Mongol soldiers
were assigned to the northern route,
stationed at Ā'ěrtài.
Zǒngbīngguān Wèi Lín and Shǎn Wénxiù led eight thousand soldiers from the Chēqí Camp
to Bù'ěrkù on the western route.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
Zhā Láng'ā was appointed acting Chuānshǎn Zǒngdū,
and Shǐ Yízhí was appointed acting Fújiàn Zǒngdū.
Edicts were issued for the construction of altars and temples for Yun, Yu, Feng, and Lei.
The Tiānquán Tǔsī of Sìchuān was converted to permanent official administration and a prefecture was established.
Gāo Qízhuō impeached Hǎichéng Gōng Huáng Yìngzǎn for bribery in inheriting his title,
and recommended his dismissal.
An edict granted him leniency.
In the fifth month, on the day Wùwǔ,
the three Tǔsī of Bǎojìng, Sāngzhí, and Yǒngshùn in Húnán were converted to permanent official administration and prefectures and counties were established.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
it was ordered that grain transport boats could carry commercial goods,
allowing up to one hundred shí beyond the old limit of sixty shí.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
earlier,
Yuè Zhōngqí had reported that a Húnán native, Zhāng Xī, had delivered seditious writings,
and interrogation revealed he was instigated by his teacher Zēng Jìng.
It was ordered that Zēng Jìng and Zhāng Xī be brought to the capital.
The Nine Ministers interrogated them,
and Zēng Jìng confessed that he had been led astray and became fanatical
by reading the writings of the late Lǚ Liúliáng.
At this point,
a clear imperial edict denounced Lǚ Liúliáng,
and ordered officials both inside and outside the court to deliberate on his crimes.
In the sixth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Táng Zhíyù was appointed acting Zhílì Zǒngdū.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
due to the arduous and costly transport in Gānsù, Sìchuān, Yúnnán, Guìzhōu, and Guǎngxī,
the entire quota tax for the year Gēngxū was remitted.
Shǎnxī's tax was remitted by three-tenths.
In the autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
the wild Miao of Dūyùn, as well as the Nóng and Zhòng wild Miao, in Guìzhōu pledged allegiance.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Guǒqīnwáng Yìn Lǐ was put in charge of the Gōngbù,
and Zhuāngqīnwáng Yìn Lù was put in charge of the Mǎnzhōu Dūtǒng.
On the day Jǐsì,
the tribute from the Kingdom of Xiāmluó was reduced.
In the intercalary seventh month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Ālǐgùn was appointed Hángzhōu Jiāngjūn.
In the eighth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Wáng Yì was appointed Jīngkǒu Jiāngjūn.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
His Majesty attended the Classics Mat Lecture.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Zhèn'ān in Guǎngxī was converted to permanent official administration.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
thirteen sons of Han ministers, including Jiǎng Pǔ, were granted the title of *jǔrén*.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an edict stated:
“Regarding the case of clearing outstanding taxes in Jiāngnán,
previous edicts have been very clear,
emphasizing the distinction between official embezzlement and arrears owed by the people.
However, the officials dispatched to handle the matter have performed poorly,
with some designating funds collected by gentry and scholars as official embezzlement,
and others decreeing that funds embezzled by clerks be apportioned among wealthy households for compensation.
There are also those who have increased the *huǒhào* (surcharge) on collected grain and money,
and even those who have ordered the collection of items that were suspended from collection.
Policies intended to benefit the people
have instead disturbed them.
Is this not the fault of those in charge of these affairs?
They must strictly adhere to previous edicts and handle matters appropriately.
Should these malpractices occur again,
severe punishment will be meted out.”
On the *wùchén* day,
due to the diligent and cautious service of officials inside and outside the court,
Yí Qīnwáng's ceremonial guard was doubled,
Zhāng Tíngyù was made Shàobǎo,
Jiǎng Tíngxī was made Tàizǐ Tàifù,
Lì Tíngyí was made Tàizǐ Shàofù,
Fù'ěrdān, Yuè Zhōngqí, and È'ěrtài were all made Shàobǎo,
Tián Wénjìng was made Tàizǐ Tàibǎo,
Lǐ Wèi, Zhā Láng'ā, and Xí Bó were all made Tàizǐ Shàobǎo.
In the eleventh month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
a million *liǎng* of treasury silver was issued to repair the stone works of Gāojiāyàn.
Mǎ Huìbó was appointed Bīngbù Shàngshū,
but remained at the front lines.
On the *wùyín* day,
the arrears of over 500,000 *liǎng* of silver owed by the descendants of meritorious officials, such as Shī Shìhuá, were waived,
and the sum was covered by funds from the imperial treasury.
Their deserved punishments, such as banishment, confiscation of assets, and their wives and children being made government property,
were all pardoned.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
executions scheduled for this year were suspended.
In the twelfth month, on the *wùshēn* day,
a Guānfēng Zhěngsú Shǐ for Guǎngdōng and an Xuézhèng for Zhàogāo were established.
On the *wùchén* day,
a *xiápjì* (combined ancestral sacrifice) was performed at the Tàimiào.
This year,

disaster relief was granted, waiving taxes in twenty-four prefectures and counties across provinces such as Jiāngnán, Jiāngxī, Zhèjiāng, Fújiàn, Húnán, Yúnnán, and Gānsù, with varying degrees of relief.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú presented tribute.
In the eighth year, *gēngxū*, spring, in the first month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
Shàng Chóngyì, who was the Zǒnglǐ Língqǐn Shìwù Lǐng Shìwèi Nèi Dàchén, was made Shèngjīng Wǔbù Shàngshū.
Nàsūtú was appointed Fèngtiān Jiāngjūn,
Chángdé was appointed Nínggǔtǎ Jiāngjūn,
Zhuó'ěrhǎi was appointed Hēilóngjiāng Jiāngjūn.
Qìngfù was appointed Hànjūn Dūlǒng.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
auspicious *zhī* (a type of fungus) appeared at Jǐnglíng.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Táng Zhíyù reported that on the twentieth day of the first month, a phoenix was seen at Fángshān.
The imperial decree stated:
“This matter has already been reported by Fǔyǐn Sūn Jiāgàn.
Furthermore, Shàng Chóngyì reported seeing a divine bird on Tiāntái Shān,
five or six *chǐ* tall,
with feathers like brocade,
surrounded by other birds,
flying north.
My own virtue is meager,
insufficient to cause such a supreme auspicious omen.”
Six thousand *liǎng* of silver for lamp oil was issued to Guózǐjiān,
to be a regular annual allocation.
In the second month, on the *gēngzǐ* day, the first day of the month,
the title of Chéng'ēn Gōng was set for imperial relatives through marriage.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the Emperor attended the Jīngyán lectures.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Lài Shìgōng's ducal title was restored.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Chéng Jùnwáng Yìnzhǐ was restored as Chéng Qīnwáng,
Bèilè Yìn'è was made Yú Jùnwáng,
Bèizǐ Yìnyī was made Bèilè,
the twenty-first imperial brother Yìnxǐ and the twenty-second imperial brother Yìnhù were made Bèizǐ,
and the twenty-third imperial brother Yìnqí was made Zhènguó Gōng.
On the *wùchén* day,
the country of Nánzhǎng sent envoys to present tribute,
requesting a fixed tribute schedule.
The Emperor responded with a generous edict,
decreeing tribute every five years.
In the third month, on the *dīnghài* day,
Zhāng Tíngyù and Jiǎng Tíngxī were ordered to manage the affairs of the Sānkù.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Shǐ Yízhí was appointed acting Liǎngjiāng Zǒngdū,
the Sānzǔ Yùzuǎn Shūjīng Chuánshuō was promulgated,
and the Emperor composed a preface for it.
In summer, in the fourth month,
Chún Qīnwáng Yìnyòu passed away,
and was posthumously named Dù.
His son Hóngjǐng inherited the title of Jùnwáng.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Zhōu Shù and 399 others were granted the *jìnshì jíyǐ chūshēn* (various degrees of *jìnshì*).
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Dàxuéshì was set as Zhèng Yīpǐn (Senior First Rank),
and Zuǒ Dūyùshǐ as Cóng Yīpǐn (Junior First Rank).
On the *guǐhài* day,
Jī Céngyún was appointed acting Jiāngnán Hédào Zǒngdū,
and Tián Wénjìng concurrently managed Dōnghé Zǒngdū.
In the fifth month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Yí Qīnwáng Yìnxiáng passed away.
The Emperor mourned deeply,
personally attended his funeral,
and he was posthumously named Xián,
and his spirit tablet was placed in the Tàimiào.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Gá'ěrdān Cèlíng sent envoys to inquire about relations.
The Emperor ordered a temporary delay in military action,
and summoned Fù'ěrdān and Yuè Zhōngqí to the capital.
Gāo Qízhuó was transferred to be Liǎngjiāng Zǒngdū,
and Liú Shìmíng was made Fújiàn Zǒngdū.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Emperor again attended the funeral of Yíxián Qīnwáng.
An edict stated:
“The names of all my brothers
were bestowed by the late Emperor.
At the beginning of my reign,
Yìnzhǐ, following precedent, petitioned to change the first character of his name.
Having reported it to the Empress Dowager,
it was reluctantly carried out.
Now that Yí Qīnwáng has passed away,
his name shall still be written with the original character,
to mark my remembrance of him.”
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
previously,
Chéng Qīnwáng Yìnzhǐ, attending the funeral of Yíxián Qīnwáng,
arrived late and left early,
and showed no sign of grief.
He was referred to the Zōngrénfǔ for deliberation and punishment.
By this day,
the deliberation was submitted,
requesting his demotion and execution.
The imperial decree ordered
his demotion and imprisonment.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Yuè Chāolóng was appointed Húguǎng Tídū.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Bèizǐ Yìnxǐ was promoted to Bèilè,
Jùnwáng Hóngzhòu was promoted to Qīnwáng,
Gōng Hóngjǐng was made Bèizǐ.
Yìntáo's Jùnwáng title was restored.
In the sixth month, on the *wùxū* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *rén'yín* day,
eight characters,
“Zhōngjìng Chéngzhí Qínshèn Liánmíng” (loyal, reverent, sincere, upright, diligent, cautious, incorruptible, discerning),
were added to Yíxián Qīnwáng's posthumous name.
On the *wùshēn* day,
È'ěrtài reported that the *shēngmiáo* (unassimilated Miao) of Lípíng and Dōuyún had submitted.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Mǎ Huìbó was removed from office.
Táng Zhíyù was appointed Bīngbù Shàngshū,
and Shǐ Yízhí was appointed Zuǒ Dūyùshǐ.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the *wùyín* day,
it was ordered to establish Xiánliáng Cí.
On the *rénchén* day,
officials were dispatched to provide disaster relief to flood victims in places such as Jiāngnán, Húnán, Zhílì, and Shāndōng.
On the *guǐsì* day,
it was ordered that the ranking of Xúnfǔ be above that of Fù Dūtǒng.
In the eighth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
as Shāndōng was more severely affected by floods,
the entire province's grain tribute was specifically waived.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Yíxián Qīnwáng's son Hóngxiǎo was ordered to inherit the title of Qīnwáng,
and Hóngjǐng was separately enfeoffed as Jùnwáng,
both titles to be hereditary.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
an earthquake occurred in the capital.
Kāng Qīnwáng Chóng'ān was relieved of his duties managing the Zōngrénfǔ,
and Yù Qīnwáng Guǎnglù was appointed to manage the Zōngrénfǔ.
In the ninth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
due to the earthquake in the capital,
officials were granted half pay,
and each of the Eight Banners was granted 30,000 *liǎng* of silver.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Gāo Qízhuó was granted a hereditary position for surveying the auspicious site of Tàipíngyù.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
È'ěrtài reported that the Báishì of Měnglòng, and Mènglián and Nùzǐ, had submitted.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
the hat finials for all civil and military officials were re-regulated.
First-rank officials had a coral finial;
second-rank officials had a carved coral finial;
third-rank officials had a translucent blue glass finial;
fourth-rank officials had a lapis lazuli finial;
fifth-rank officials had a crystal finial;
sixth-rank officials had a tridacna finial;
seventh-rank officials had a plain gold finial;
eighth-rank officials had a carved gold finial;
ninth-rank officials and those not in the regular stream had a carved silver finial.
On the day Xīnhài,
Zhā Bìnà was appointed Deputy General
and sent to the northern route army camp.
On the day Rénzǐ,
È'ěrtài reported the recovery of Wūméng Fǔchéng,
and that the Miáo rebels were pacified.
On the day Jiǎyín,
because Mǎ'ěrsài, Zhāng Tíngyù, and Jiǎng Tíngxī had long participated in state affairs,
they were each granted the hereditary title of Earl.
The Wénmiào in Quèlǐ was completed,
and the Fifth Imperial Prince, Hóngzhòu, and Jùn Wáng Hóngjǐng were ordered to go and offer sacrifices.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jǐsì,
officials for the administration of the Kǒngmiào were established.
On the day Yǐhài,
an order was issued that land tax and deed tax in all provinces should not be exacted harshly or excessively.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
a clear imperial edict admonished the Han Chinese military meritorious descendants who had fallen into disgrace: high officials Fàn Shíyì, Shàng Chóngyì, Lǐ Yǒngshēng, and others.
On the day Wùzǐ,
an imperial decree ordered that of the silver remitted to the Board from various provinces,
half should be retained for public use.
In the twelfth month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
Fù'ěrdān and Yuè Zhōngqí were each ordered to return to their respective armies.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Jì Chéngbīn reported that Qí Wáng'ěr's bandits had attacked Kuòshètú Kǎlún,
and Grand General Fán Tíng defeated them.
Fán Tíng was granted a hereditary office
and ten thousand taels of silver.
Zhāng Cháozuǒ and others were also granted hereditary offices,
with varying amounts of silver awards.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted for eighteen prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Shānxī, Húnán, Guìzhōu, and other provinces.
Additionally, varying amounts of grain tribute were remitted for Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Shāndōng, and Hénán.
Cháoxiǎn, Ānnán, and Nánzhǎng presented tribute.
In the ninth year, the spring, first month, on the day Gēngyín,
an imperial edict allocated two hundred thousand *shi* of accumulated grain from the Yángzhōu salt granary
to further relieve the flood victims of Pī and Sù from the previous year.
In the second month, on the day Yǐwèi,
Yú Jùn Wáng Yìn● passed away.
His posthumous title was Kè,
and his son Hóngqìng inherited the title of Jùn Wáng.
One hundred fifty thousand *shi* of rice from the Tōngcāng granary,
two hundred thousand *shi* of rice from Fèngtiān,
and fifty thousand *shi* of purchased rice
were transported to Shāndōng for disaster relief.
On the day Wùxū,
Cháng Lài was appointed Zhèn'ān Jiāngjūn,
leading Gān and Liáng soldiers to be stationed at Ānxī.
On the day Wùwǔ,
due to Tián Wénjìng's old age and frequent illness,
Assistant Minister Wáng Guódòng was ordered to Hénán to relieve the flood victims.
On the day Rénxū,
a special Governor-General for Sìchuān was established,
and Huáng Tíngguì was appointed to the post.
In the third month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Sāntài was appointed Minister of Rites,
and È'ěrqí was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
On the day Wùzǐ,
two thousand household retainers from the Eight Banners were ordered to be selected,
and Yīlǐbù was appointed to command them
as Deputy General of the Western Route.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Shǐ Yízhí and Háng Yìlù were ordered to Shǎnxī to issue proclamations and guide the people.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Èmídá reported that the indigenous Lì people of Qióngshān and Dānzhōu had pledged allegiance.
In the fifth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
Shí Yúnzhuō was appointed Deputy General of the Western Route.
Zhào Zhīyuán and Mǎ Lóng were ordered to oversee the transport of provisions for the Western Route.
In the sixth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
Fù'ěrdān reported that the Qí Wáng'ěr had invaded Zháksài Hé,
and he led troops to engage them.
On the day Xīnhài,
Yuè Zhōngqí reported that the Qí Wáng'ěr had attacked Túlǔfān,
and he led troops to reinforce,
whereupon the bandits fled.
Troops were left to garrison the area.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Emperor prayed for rain,
and on that very day,
it rained.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
È'ěrtài was summoned to the capital.
Gāo Qízhuō was appointed Governor-General of Yún-Guì,
and Yǐn Jìshàn was appointed Governor-General of Liǎng-Jiāng.
On the day Jǐsì,
Huáng Tíngguì reported that the Fān rebels of Zhānduì were in revolt,
and troops were dispatched to suppress them.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Fù'ěrdān reported that the imperial troops' attack on the Qí Wáng'ěr was unfavorable,
and they retreated to Kēbùduō.
In this engagement,
they advanced lightly and fell into an ambush.
Fù'ěrdān abandoned the main army and retreated first,
leading to a crushing defeat.
Deputy General Zhā Bìnà, Duke Bāsài, and Counselor-in-Chief Dá Fú, among others, all died.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Mǎ'ěrsài was appointed Fǔyuǎn Dàjiāngjūn,
and Xībǎo was ordered to firmly defend Cháhàn Shòué'ěr.
Yuè Zhōngqí reported leading troops to advance to Wūlǔmùqí.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐhài,
Èmídá was appointed Qīngzhōu Jiāngjūn.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Kēbùduō troops were moved to be stationed at Cháhàn Shòué'ěr.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Xībǎo was promoted to Shùnchéng Qīnwáng.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Yuè Zhōngqí reported that his troops had reached Nàlín Hé,
two days' journey from Wūlǔmùqí,
and learned that the bandits had fled,
so the main army immediately returned.
An order was given for a generous discussion of awards.
In the ninth month, on the day Yǐhài,
Kāng Qīnwáng Chóng'ān was ordered to the army camp,
and ten thousand taels of silver were provided for his equipment.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Liú Yúyì was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì,
Shěn Tíngyù was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì waterways,
and Zhū Zǎo was appointed Governor-General of Hédōng waterways.
On the day Jǐsì,
Empress Nàlā Shì passed away,
and was posthumously titled Xiàojìng Huánghòu.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
Qián Yǐkǎi requested retirement,
and Wèi Tíngzhēn was appointed Minister of Rites.
The Qí Wáng'ěr invaded Kèlúlún,
plundering pastoral areas.
Qīnwáng Dānjīnduō'ěrzì and Èfù Jùn Wáng Cèlíng combined forces and attacked them,
capturing and executing countless numbers.
The Emperor commended them,
each granting ten thousand taels of silver,
and promoting Cèlíng to Qīnwáng.
In the eleventh month, on the day Guǐhài,
Shùnchéng Qīnwáng Xībǎo was appointed Jìngbiān Dàjiāngjūn.
Fù'ěrdān was demoted to Zhènwǔ Jiāngjūn,
and Mǎ'ěrsài was demoted to Suíyuǎn Jiāngjūn.
Kāng Qīnwáng Chóng'ān was ordered to act as Fǔyuǎn Dàjiāngjūn.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Shǐ Yízhí was appointed Minister of War,
and Péng Wéixīn was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
In the twelfth month, on the first day Gēngyín,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
the *Shèngzǔ Shílù* and *Shèngxùn* were completed.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Mǎ Shìjié was appointed acting Guǎngzhōu Jiāngjūn,
and Zhǔntài was appointed acting Fúzhōu Jiāngjūn.
On the day Dīngsì,
the ancestral temple was jointly sacrificed to.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted for ninety-three prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Hénán, Fújiàn, Shǎnxī, Húnán, Guǎngxī, Gānsù, and other provinces, with varying amounts.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú presented tribute.
In the tenth year, the Rén'yín spring, first month, on the day Guǐhài,
the Grand Ancestral Temple was offered sacrifices to in the first month of spring,
and the Fourth Imperial Prince, Hónglì, performed the rites.
On the day Rénwǔ,
È'ěrtài was appointed Grand Secretary.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Commander Dál'ěrzì at the front was appointed Jiànxūn Jiāngjūn,
and stationed troops at Báigé'ěr.
In the second month,
Wáng Cháo'ēn was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì waterways,
and Wèi Tíngzhēn was appointed Governor-General of Grain Transport.
On the day Jǐhài,
È'ěrtài was enfeoffed as a First-Class Earl,
a hereditary title.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Yuè Zhōngqí reported that the Qí Wáng'ěr had attacked Hāmì,
and Grand General Cáo Xiáng was dispatched to reinforce,
defeating them,
whereupon the bandits fled via Wúkèkè Lǐng.
Deputy General Shí Yúnzhuō was arrested and interrogated
for failing to intercept them.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Zhāng Guǎngsì was appointed Deputy General of the Western Route,
and Liú Shìmíng was appointed Military Counselor.
In the third month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
the Grand Secretaries and others impeached Yuè Zhōngqí for making false reports,
with conflicting statements.
The matter was referred to the appropriate Board for strict deliberation.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
one Grand Commander (Zǒngbīng) each was established for Guìzhōu's Gǔzhōu Garrison and Qīngjiāng Garrison.
On the day Yǐsì,
Hǎi Shòu was appointed Minister (Shàngshū) of the Board of Revenue (Hùbù),
and Xìng Guì was appointed Minister of the Board of Punishments (Xíngbù).
The third-class Duke (Sānděng Gōng) Yuè Zhōngqí was demoted to third-class Marquis (Sānděng Hóu),
but still commanded as Grand General (Dàjiāngjūn).
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Zhāng Dàyǒu was appointed Minister of the Board of Rites (Lǐbù),
and Fàn Shíyì was appointed Minister of the Board of Works (Gōngbù).
On the day Yǐmǎo,
an imperial edict ordered the repair of water conservancy works in Sōngmíng Zhōu and Xúndiàn Zhōu in Yúnnán.
In the fifth month, on the day Wùchén,
Wǔ Gé was appointed General Who Manifests Military Might (Yángwǔ Jiāngjūn),
with Liú Shìmíng as his deputy.
In the intercalary fifth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
Prince Héng, Yìnqí, passed away.
He was posthumously granted the epithet Wēn.
His son, Hóngzhì, inherited the title of Prince Héng.
The former Prince Chéng, Yìnzhǐ, died in confinement at Jǐngshān.
He was granted five thousand taels of silver
and buried according to the rites for a Prince of the Commandery (Jùnwáng).
The Minister of the Board of Civil Office (Lìbù Shàngshū), Lì Tíngyí, passed away.
On the day Gēngxū,
aboriginal people (Xīfān) in the northern circuit of Táiwān caused trouble,
and government troops suppressed them.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Lǐ Wèi was appointed acting Minister of the Board of Punishments.
In the sixth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
Mǎng Húli was appointed Manchu Grand Commander (Hànjūn Dūtǒng).
On the day Rénshēn,
Gāo Qízhuō reported that the indigenous people (Tǔyí) of Sīmáo in Yúnnán colluded with the indigenous people of Yuánjiāng to raid Pǔ'ěr Commandery city.
Grand Commander Dǒng Fāng was dispatched to lead troops to suppress them.
On the day Xīnsì,
the Grand Ministers of the Military Affairs Office (Bànlǐ Jūnjī Dàchén) deliberated and proposed a special posthumous grant to Tselek, a Bulwark Duke (Fǔguógōng) of Khalkha, who died in battle.
His son, Mishke, inherited the title.
The establishment of the Grand Ministers of the Military Affairs Office began at this time.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Bǐngxū,
Mǎ Lǎ was dismissed.
Wǔ Gé was appointed Minister of the Board of Works.
On the day Dīnghài,
a bull in Jùyě, Shāndōng, gave birth to an auspicious qílín.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the descendants of Gù Bādài were granted ten thousand taels of silver.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
È'ěrtài was ordered to manage military affairs as Governor-General (Jīnglüè).
Yuè Zhōngqí was summoned to the capital.
Liú Yúyì was appointed Governor-General of Shǎnxī,
and Lǐ Wèi was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the Zǔngá'ěr invaded Wūsūnzhu'ěr.
Fù'ěrdān engaged them but was defeated.
The Grand General (Dàjiāngjūn) Xībǎo was ordered to investigate the circumstances of the defeat and report.
On the day Yǐsì,
Grand Secretary (Dàxuéshì) Jiǎng Tíngxí passed away.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Fú Mǐn was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary (Xiélǐ Dàxuéshì),
and Táng Zhíyù concurrently managed the Board of Punishments as Minister.
In the eighth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
the original princely title of Hǎishàn Bèi Lè, son of Prince Gōng, was restored.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the three Khans (Hàn) Yamu, Yeleng, and Kukumu of Bā'ěrbù Kingdom, outside the border of Xīzàng, sent envoys to present tribute.
They were courteously rewarded with imperial edicts.
On the day Rénshēn,
the Northern Route Deputy General (Běilù Fùjiāngjūn) Prince Dānjīnduō'ěrzì and the imperial son-in-law (Éfù) Prince Cèlíng reported pursuing the Zǔngá'ěr barbarians to È'ěrdéwú Zhāo,
killing over ten thousand enemy troops.
The enemy fled towards Tuīhé.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
two million taels of imperial silver were allocated and sent to the northern army front for rewards.
In the ninth month, on the first day Yǐyǒu,
for their merits in attacking the Zǔngá'ěr barbarians,
Dānjīnduō'ěrzì was granted the honorific title Zhìyǒng,
Cèlíng was granted the honorific title Chāoyǒng,
his son Chēbùdēngzhābù was enfeoffed as Bulwark Duke (Fǔguógōng),
and others were promoted or appointed with varying ranks.
Mǎ'ěrsài was stripped of his rank and office and executed for letting the enemy escape and missing the opportunity.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Fù'ěrdān was stripped of his rank and office.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Rénxū,
the execution of prisoners for this year was suspended.
Yuè Zhōngqí was stripped of his rank and office,
arrested and sent to the capital for detention by the Board of War (Bīngbù).
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngxū,
Cháng Dé was appointed Deputy General (Fùjiāngjūn) of the Left for Pacifying the Border (Jìngbiān Zuǒfùjiāngjūn).
On the day Yǐwèi,
Émǐnhézhuó of Túlǔfān was enfeoffed as Bulwark Duke (Fǔguógōng).
The student (Shēngyuán) Qiáo Jīn, whose family had lived together for seven generations in Yuánjiāng County, Húnán, was granted an imperial plaque with calligraphy.
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
posthumous grants were bestowed upon Zhābìnà, Mǎ'ěrsà, Hǎilán, Dá fú, and other officials who died in battle on the northern route, with varying amounts.
Vice Minister (Shìláng) Sūn Jiāgàn was condemned to death for his crimes,
but was ordered to work in the Imperial Silver Treasury (Yínkù).
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Lǚ Liúliáng was punished for his crimes.
His corpse, along with those of Lǚ Bǎozhōng and Yán Hóngkuí, were dismembered.
Lǚ Yìzhōng and Shěn Zàikuān were beheaded.
His grandsons were exiled to remote areas as slaves.
Zhū Yǔcǎi and others were released.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Wǔ Gé was arrested and interrogated for fabricating rumors to withdraw troops.
On the day Xīnsì,
a combined sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple (Tàimiào).
This year,
disaster taxes were remitted for seventy-five prefectures and counties in Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Shāndōng, Húnán, and other provinces, with varying amounts.
The number of tax households (Dīnghù) was twenty-five million four hundred twelve thousand two hundred eighty-nine.
The number of people born after the permanent abolition of additional taxes (Yǒngbù Jiāfù Hòuzīshēng Réndīng) was nine hundred thirty-six thousand four hundred eighty-six.
The total area of cultivated land (Tiándì) was eight hundred ninety thousand four hundred sixteen qǐng and forty mù.
The silver collected as tax was twenty-nine million eight hundred seventy-two thousand three hundred thirty-two taels and six qián.
Three hundred forty-two thousand three hundred fifty-one tea permits (Yǐn) were issued.
The salt tax (Yánkè) amounted to three million nine hundred eighty-eight thousand eight hundred fifty-one taels of silver.
The number of coins minted was over sixty-eight million four hundred thirty-six thousand two hundred.
Cháoxiǎn and Bā'ěrbù Kingdom offered tribute.
In the eleventh year, in spring, the first month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Hǎi Wàng and Lǐ Wèi were ordered to inspect the seawalls in Zhèjiāng.
The Fàn Gōng Dī was repaired.
On the day Rénchén,
one thousand taels of oil-lamp silver (Gāohuǒ Yín) each were distributed to academies (Shūyuàn) in the direct provinces (Zhíshěng).
Gāo Qízhuō was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
and Yǐn Jìshàn was appointed Governor-General of Yún-Guì.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
È'ěrtài was ordered to inspect the military affairs of the northern route.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Emperor visited the imperial mausoleum (Líng).
In the second month, on the day Rénzǐ,
the Emperor observed water jars (Shuǐgāng) placed along the road,
storing water for sprinkling the path.
The Emperor admonished them, saying:
"Even if there is fine dust on the imperial route,
what harm is there?
Local officials should prioritize nurturing the common people.
If the devotion shown to me were transferred to cherishing the populace,
would that not be excellent?"
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Bǎomíng, Chá'ěrtài, and Yīlèshèn were all appointed Manchu Grand Commanders (Mǎnzhōu Dūtǒng).
On the day Jǐwèi,
the Emperor attended the imperial lectures (Jīngyán).
The Emperor's twenty-fourth brother, Yìn Mì, was enfeoffed as Prince Chéng (Chéngqīnwáng).
The Emperor's fourth son, Hónglì, was enfeoffed as Prince Bǎo (Bǎoqīnwáng).
The Emperor's fifth son, Hóngzhòu, was enfeoffed as Prince Hé (Héqīnwáng).
Bèi Lè Hóngchūn was promoted to Prince of the Commandery Tàijùnwáng.
On the day Rénxū,
Péng Wéixīn was ordered to assist in managing the Grand Secretariat (Nèigé).
Wú Shìyù was appointed Minister of the Board of Rites,
and Tú Tiānxiāng was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief (Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ).
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Rèn Qǐyùn was specially granted the Hanlin academic title (Hànlín)
and assigned to work in the imperial princes' study (Āgē Shūfáng).
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Chén Tán and three hundred twenty-eight others were granted the Jinshi degree with varying ranks.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Jī Zēngyún was appointed Grand Secretary,
still overseeing the Yellow River as Governor (Hédū).
Liú Yúyì was appointed Minister of the Board of Civil Office,
Tú Tiānxiāng was appointed Minister of the Board of Punishments,
and Zhāng Zhào was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
On the day Jǐwèi,
scholars with extensive knowledge and literary talent (Bóxué Hóngcí) were summoned and recommended.
In the fifth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
Gāo Qízhuō reported that the Miaoren (Miáorén) of Pǔsī, Diāo Xīngguó, had rebelled,
and they were suppressed.
Compiler (Biānxiū) Zhāng Ruò'ài,
and probationers (Shùjíshì) Èróng'ān and Èlún were all ordered to work in the Military Affairs Office.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the imperial son-in-law (Éfù) Cèlíng was appointed Deputy General of the Left for Pacifying the Border (Jìngbiān Zuǒfùjiāngjūn),
with Cháng Dé as his deputy.
Tǎ'ěrdài was appointed Deputy General of the Right for Pacifying the Border (Jìngbiān Yòufùjiāngjūn),
with Yǒng Fú as his deputy,
and they were jointly stationed at Kēbùduō.
The revised collection of statutes (Huìdiǎn) was completed.
On the day Rén'yín,
the General (Jiāngjūn) of Hēilóngjiāng, Dù Lài, reported that six clans of Chuòmǐn from the island of Tèméng and Qítúshān and other places had submitted,
paying tribute in sable furs annually.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
the former Provincial Military Commander (Tídū) Jì Chéngbīn was executed.
In the sixth month, on the day Wùwǔ,
the King of the Sulu Kingdom, Wú Hàn Wèi Wú Lā Lǜ Lín, reported that his distant ancestor, the Eastern King, came to court during the Yǒnglè reign of the Míng dynasty.
On his return, he fell ill and died in Dézhōu, Shāndōng.
His eldest son returned to his kingdom to succeed him as king.
His second son, Āndūlù,
and third son, Wēnhālà, remained to guard the tomb.
Their descendants divided into the two surnames Ān and Wēn,
receiving an annual fixed allowance of eight taels of silver for sacrifices.
He requested that their descendants be appointed as sacrificial students (Fèngsì Shēng).
This was approved.
On the day Wùyín,
Hā Yuánshēng reported the suppression of the rebellious Jiǔgǔ Miaoren.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Grand Secretary Chén Yuánlóng requested retirement due to being over eighty years old,
and was granted the title of Tàizǐ Tàifù before retiring.
Lǐ Huī was dismissed from his post for overstepping his authority in speaking on affairs.
The office of the Húnán Guānfēng Zhěngsú Shǐ was abolished.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Shùnchéng Qīnwáng Xībǎo was stripped of his princely title,
but his son Xīliáng still inherited the title of Jùnwáng.
Píng Jùnwáng Fúpéng was appointed as Dìngbiān Dàjiàngjūn.
Qīnwáng Dānjīnduōěrjì was demoted to Jùnwáng,
and his honorable epithet (yǒng hào) was removed.
In the eighth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Gù Cóng was appointed Zhílì Hédào Zǒngdū,
Zhào Hóngēn was appointed Liǎngjiāng Zǒngdū,
and Gāo Qízhuō was appointed Jiāngsū Xúnfǔ.
On the day Jǐsì,
four patrol and bandit-catching assistant magistrates were established in Shùntiān Fǔ.
In the ninth month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
Èěrqí was dismissed from office and investigated.
Qìngfù was appointed Hùbù Shàngshū,
and Ècháng was appointed acting Bùjūn Tǒnglǐng.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Kòulóu was appointed Ménggǔ Dūtǒng,
and Zhōngdá Gōng Mǎ Lǐshàn was appointed Xíngbù Shàngshū.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎchén,
Guǒyì Gōng Nèqīn was ordered to serve in the Bànlǐ Jūnjī Chù.
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùwǔ,
an imperial edict stated:
"Previously, Èmídá submitted a memorial proposing the construction of a city in Táiwān.
Hǎo Yùlín reported that the thorny bamboo in Táiwān
could be planted to form a city.
The unrest in Táiwān
often arises from within.
If the rebels have no city to occupy,
it will be easy to suppress them.
Only Lùěrmén is the gateway to Tái Jùn;
building artillery forts there
is sufficient for defense.
Planting thorny bamboo
will serve as a barrier.
The artillery forts in places like Dànshuǐ
should also be constructed
and regularly repaired."
On the day Jǐwèi,
Shǐ Yízhí was appointed Hùbù Shàngshū,
Zhāng Zhào was appointed Xíngbù Shàngshū,
and Xú Běn was appointed Zuǒ Dūyùshǐ.
On the day Rénxū,
Gāo Bīn was appointed Jiāngnán Hédào Zǒngdū.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
the grand ancestral temple was jointly sacrificed to.
In this year,
the disaster taxes for twenty prefectures, departments, counties, and garrisons in Zhílì, Jiāngsū, Ānhuī, Jiāngxī, Shāndōng, and other provinces were remitted,
and the salt taxes for twenty-five salt permits in Jiāngsū salt fields were also remitted, with varying amounts.
Cháoxiǎn, Ānnán, and Sūlù paid tribute.
In the twelfth year, Jiǎyín, spring, first month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
Píng Jùnwáng Fúpéng presented five hundred horses,
to be used for military preparations.
On the day Rényín,
Assistant Minister Zhā Kèdàn handled the affairs of the Chēchén Hán tribe appropriately,
was granted the rank of Shàngshū,
bestowed five thousand taels of silver,
and had the confiscated land, houses, and population returned to him.
In the second month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
the Emperor attended the Jīngyán lecture.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Bèizi Yīnhù was promoted to Bèilè.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Attendant Reader Chūnshān and Remonstrance Official Lǐ Xuéyù were ordered to enfeoff the King of Ānnán.
On the day Rénshēn,
Éfù Cèlíng was ordered to take overall charge of frontline military affairs.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Yuán Zhǎnchéng reported that one hundred and sixty Miáo villages from Pōdōng and Pōxī had submitted.
The centenarian Lǎo Mín from Xīngníng County, Guǎngdōng, who was 102 years old and enjoying prosperous years, was commended,
and because his five sons
were all seventy or eighty years old,
a family of long-lived individuals,
he was specially granted a piece of imperial satin.
In the third month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
Gōngbù Shàngshū Fàn Shíyì was dismissed.
On the day Wùxū,
Hénán Xuézhèng Yú Hóngtú was executed for corruption and embezzlement,
and his father, Assistant Minister Yú Zhàoshèng, was dismissed from office.
Yǐn Jìshàn reported the suppression of the rebellious Miáo in Pǔsī,
and the pacification and enlistment of those who surrendered.
An imperial edict stated:
"Everything tends to slacken when nearing completion,
and to be neglected once settled.
Exert yourselves!"
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
if there were any crimes or dismissals among the tǔsī (native chieftain) and commoners of Róngměi in Húguǎng,
the native chieftain system was to be replaced by regular officials.
Kāng Qīnwáng Chóng'ān passed away,
and his uncle Bāěrtú inherited the title,
while his son Yǒng'ēn was enfeoffed as Bèilè.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the sale of ivory mats in Guǎngdōng was prohibited,
and their private purchase and use by the populace were also forbidden.
In the fifth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
the Xuānfǔ Sī of Shīnán was replaced by regular officials.
On the day Guǐsì,
Lǐ Xǐ was appointed Hànjūn Dūtǒng.
On the day Yǐwèi,
due to the arrival of the Zhǔngáěr envoys,
the military advance was halted.
On the day Jǐhài,
Láibǎo, the Zǒngguǎn of the Nèiwù Fǔ, was ordered to proceed to the Chēchén Hán tribe
to assist Zhā Kèdàn in his duties.
In the sixth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
fifteen tǔsī in Húguǎng, including Zhōngdòng, were replaced by regular officials.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Guǐsì,
Guǒ Qīnwáng Yìnlǐ was ordered to manage the residence of the Dálài Lǎma in Zàng (Tibet),
and also to inspect troops in Zhílì, Shānxī, Shǎnxī, and Sìchuān.
An imperial edict stated that since the military campaigns in the northwest had been ongoing for many years,
whether to take advantage of this military strength to advance directly into enemy territory,
or to send envoys there to explain the advantages and disadvantages,
the court officials should convene and deliberate upon it and report.
Kāng Qīnwáng Bāěrtú and others proposed advancing troops,
while Grand Secretary Zhāng Tíngyù and others proposed sending envoys.
The Emperor then announced the beginning and end of the military campaign,
and followed the latter proposal of sending envoys.
In the eighth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
Fù Nài and Ākèdūn were dispatched to Zhǔngáěr to deliver the imperial message.
On the day Rénxū,
Bèizi Yīnyī was demoted to Gōng,
and Tàijùnwáng Hóngchūn was demoted to Bèizi.
In the ninth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
Assistant Minister Lǚ Yàozēng and Minister Qīng Défú were ordered to Guìzhōu to deliver the imperial message to the Miáomán.
Yúnnán was ordered to open furnaces for minting coins.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
Guǒ Qīnwáng Yìnlǐ submitted a memorial stating:
"When officials submit memorials,
they should present the facts truthfully,
and not merely pick up scraps to fulfill their duty."
An imperial edict stated:
"What is said is very true,
let the rotating memorial-submitting officials be informed of this."
On the day Dīngwèi,
Èmídá was appointed acting Tiānjīn Dūtǒng,
Ālǐgùn was appointed Qīngzhōu Jiāngjūn,
and Fù Sēn was appointed Hángzhōu Jiāngjūn.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Hǎo Yùlín was appointed Zhè-Mǐn Zǒngdū.
Sāntài and Xú Běn both assisted in the affairs of the Nèigé.
On the day Jǐsì,
auspicious ganoderma appeared at Jǐnglín.
In the eleventh month, on the first day Rénshēn,
the former Zhí Jùnwáng Yīntí passed away,
and he was ordered to be buried with the rites of a Bèizi,
and his son Hóngfǎng was enfeoffed as Zhènguó Gōng.
On the day Bǐngyín,
an imperial decree ordered the continued compilation of the Huáng Qīng Wényǐng.
On the day Rényǔ,
a special imperial edict was issued to Zhāng and Quán prefectures in Fújiàn,
to civilize their strong and fierce ways,
and prevent further clan feuds.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Lǐmì Qīnwáng's son Hóngxiào was enfeoffed as Fǔguó Gōng.
In the twelfth month, on the first day Guǐchǒu,
an imperial decree ordered Guǎngxī to remain under the concurrent jurisdiction of the Guǎngdōng Zǒngdū.
On the day Dīngsì,
Wèi Tíngzhēn was appointed Bīngbù Shàngshū,
Gù Cóng was appointed Cáoyùn Zǒngdū,
Zhū Zǎo was appointed Zhílì Hédào Zǒngdū,
Bái Zhōngshān was appointed Hédōng Hédào Zǒngdū,
and Gāo Bīn was appointed Jiāngnán Hédào Zǒngdū.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the grand ancestral temple was jointly sacrificed to.
In this year,
the disaster taxes for fourteen prefectures and counties in Zhílì, Ānhuī, and other provinces were remitted,
and the salt taxes for fourteen salt permits in Zhílì salt fields were also remitted, with varying amounts.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú paid tribute.
In the thirteenth year, Yǐmǎo, spring, first month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Juéluó Bóxiū was appointed Shèngjīng Jiāngjūn,
Nàsūtú was appointed Hēilóngjiāng Jiāngjūn,
and Hèxīng was appointed Níngxià Jiāngjūn.
In the second month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
the Emperor attended the Jīngyán lecture.
On the day Gēngxū,
Wèi Tíngzhēn was appointed Lǐbù Shàngshū.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Emperor visited the imperial tombs.
On the day Jǐwèi,
he returned to the capital.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Bātài assisted as Grand Secretary.
In the third month, on the Dīngsì day,
the Emperor personally ploughed the sacrificial field.
On the Wùzǐ day,
an imperial edict stated:
"When establishing bǎojiǎ (local militia) in various regions,
it is essential to comply with public sentiment
and guide them gently.
If it is overly strict and urgent,
then good people will suffer.
The essence of governance is to obtain the right people.
If one does not obtain the right people,
even with good laws and noble intentions,
they merely serve as a beautiful spectacle
and do not benefit the people."
In summer, the fourth month, on the Yǐsì day,
the collected works of Shèngzǔ (the Kangxi Emperor) were printed,
and distributed to court officials.
On the Dīngsì day,
mining operations in Guǎngdōng were halted.
In the intercalary fourth month, on the Dīngyǒu day,
the Dzungars sent their envoy, Nàmùkā, to present a memorial and tribute.
An imperial decree ordered the delimitation of the border.
On the Jǐhài day,
the Xiāncán Tán (Altar of the First Silkworm) was built in the northern suburbs.
In the fifth month, on the Wùshēn day,
provisions of silver were given to the Eight Banners soldiers and commoners in Sānxìng.
On the Dīngsì day,
because rebellious Miaó in Gǔzhōu and Táigǒng, Guìzhōu, were causing trouble,
Hā Yuánshēng was appointed Yángwēi Jiāngjūn (General Who Manifests Awe)
to lead the officials and soldiers from four provinces to suppress them.
On the Jiǎzǐ day,
Guǒ Qīnwáng (Prince Guo), the Fourth Imperial Son, and the Fifth Imperial Son,
Grand Secretaries È'ěrtài and Zhāng Tíngyù, were ordered to handle Miaó border affairs.
Bātài, the Minister of Works, was dismissed from his post.
Zhāng Zhào, the Minister of Justice, and Déxīshòu, the Vice Censor-in-Chief, were ordered to investigate Miaó border affairs.
On the Dīngmǎo day,
Hā Yuánshēng reported that the rebellious Miaó had been suppressed,
and Huángpíng and Shībǐng were entirely pacified.
In the sixth month, on the Yǐhài day,
the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to audit the hàoxiàn (wastage and deficit surcharges) in all provinces.
On the Guǐwèi day,
Chá Kèdàn was appointed Minister of Works.
On the Jiǎshēn day,
it was permitted for Tǔsī (hereditary native chieftains) who were graduates of shēngyuán (Imperial College students) to participate in examinations.
On the Xīnmǎo day,
the tribute of local products from various provinces was reduced.
Lǚsòng (Luzon) suffered from famine
and requested to purchase grain.
This was granted.
On the Bǐngshēn day,
Dǒng Fāng was appointed Vice General
to assist in suppressing the Miaó bandits.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the Yǐmǎo day,
È'ěrtài requested to resign his earldom and position as Grand Secretary.
This was granted,
and he was given leave to recuperate from illness,
while still receiving his salary.
Liú Shìmíng, acting Gānzhōu Tídú (Provincial Commander of Ganzhou), was sentenced to beheading for failing to prevent soldiers from looting.
On the Bǐngchén day,
Zhū Shì was ordered to investigate the seawall in Zhèjiāng.
On the Xīnyǒu day,
Màizhù and Chá Láng'ā were appointed Grand Secretaries,
and Zhāng Guǎngsì was appointed Húguǎng Zǒngdū (Governor-General of Huguang).
In the eighth month, on the Jǐsì day,
an imperial edict stated:
"The previous management of Miaó border regions
was originally intended to pacify the lives of the people.
However, the mismanagement
led to the rampant emergence of rebellious Miaó,
who colluded with pacified Miaó
to plunder residents.
Thus, the intention of pacifying the people
resulted in a policy of oppressing them.
Reflecting on the original intention,
how can one not feel ashamed?
Therefore, all the land tax and grain tribute of Guìzhōu for this year
are universally remitted.
For the prefectures and counties attacked by bandits,
the remission will be for three years,
to demonstrate the intention of pacification, relief, and compassion."
On the Dīnghài day,
the Emperor became unwell.
On the Wùzǐ day,
the Emperor's illness worsened dramatically,
and an imperial decree was issued to pass the throne to the Fourth Imperial Son, Bǎo Qīnwáng (Prince Bao), Hónglì.
On the Jǐchǒu day,
the Emperor passed away,
aged fifty-eight.
In the eleventh month of that year, on the Dīngwèi day,
the honorary posthumous title Jìngtiān Chāngyùn Jiànzhōng Biǎozhèng Wǔwǔ Yīngmíng Kuānré Rènyì Ruìshèng Dàxiào Zhìchéng Xiàn Huángdì was respectfully conferred,
and the temple name Shìzōng.
In the third month of Qiánlóng's second year,
he was buried in the Tàilíng Mausoleum.
The historian comments: Shèngzǔ's governance favored leniency and benevolence,
while Shìzōng succeeded him with severity and clarity.
Commentators compare this to Emperor Wén and Emperor Jǐng of Hàn.
However, the fraternal affection
is doubted to have been firm.
Yet, Huáinán's tyranny and arrogance
were self-inflicted faults,
not entirely due to Emperor Wén's lack of kindness.
The Emperor thoroughly researched the art of governance,
especially concerned about the fatigue and hardship of lower officials.
A close minister once said that the income of prefectures and counties was excessive,
and should be rectified.
He retorted:
"You have never been a prefect or county magistrate;
how do you know the difficulties of prefectures and counties?"
How profound these words,
one could say he understood the essentials of governance!
Annals Ten: Annals of Gāozōng I
Gāozōng Fǎtiān Lóngyùn Zhìchéng Xiānjú Tǐyuán Lìjí Fūwén Fènwǔ Qīnmíng Xiàocí Shénshèng Chún Huángdì,
whose given name was Hónglì,
was Shìzōng's fourth son,
his mother being Empress Xiàoshèngxiàn.
He was born on the thirteenth day of the eighth month of Kāngxī's fiftieth year in the mansion of Yōng Qīnwáng (Prince Yong).
He had a prominent nose and a tall stature.
Shèngzǔ saw him and doted on him,
ordering him to study in the palace,
receiving instruction from the Shùjíshì (compiler) Fúmǐn,
and could recite after a single reading.
He also learned archery from Bèilè Yǔnxǐ,
and firearms from Zhuāng Qīnwáng (Prince Zhuang) Yǔnlù.
During the Mùlán hunt,
he was ordered by the imperial guards to shoot a bear.
As soon as he mounted his horse,
the bear suddenly sprang up.
The Emperor controlled his reins with composure.
Shèngzǔ used his imperial musket to kill the bear.
Entering the military tent,
he looked at Wēnhuì Huáng Tàifēi (Imperial Concubine Wenhui) and said:
"This person's destiny is noble;
his good fortune will surpass mine."
In the eighth month of Yōngzhèng's first year,
Shìzōng, in the Qiánqīng Gōng (Palace of Heavenly Purity),
secretly wrote his name
and sealed it behind the plaque inscribed with "Zhèngdà Guāngmíng" (Upright and Open) written by Shìzǔ (the Shunzhi Emperor).
In the fifth year,
he married Empress Xiàoxián, of the Fùchá clan.
In the eleventh year,
he was enfeoffed as Héshuò Bǎo Qīnwáng (Prince Bao of the First Rank).
At that time, the Dzungar campaign was not yet concluded,
and there were also military affairs concerning the Qián Miaó.
He was ordered to oversee military affairs
and consult on major policies.
In the eighth month of the thirteenth year, on the Dīnghài day,
Shìzōng became unwell.
At that time, he was residing at the Yuánmíng Yuán (Old Summer Palace).
He (Hónglì) and Hé Qīnwáng (Prince He) Hóngzhòu diligently attended him day and night.
On the Wùzǐ day,
Shìzōng's illness worsened dramatically.
Zhuāng Qīnwáng Yǔnlù,
Guǒ Qīnwáng Yǔnlǐ,
Grand Secretaries È'ěrtài and Zhāng Tíngyù,
the Imperial Bodyguard Minister Fēngshèng'é and Nèqīn,
and the Inner Minister and Vice Minister of Revenue Hǎiwàng were summoned to receive the Emperor's dying instructions.
On the Jǐchǒu day,
he passed away.
The princes and ministers requested to escort the deceased Emperor back to the palace.
Zhuāng Qīnwáng Yǔnlù and others opened the sealed imperial edict for the establishment of the Crown Prince from Yōngzhèng's first year
and proclaimed the edict for him (Hónglì) to ascend the imperial throne.
Soon after, an edict was issued, in accordance with the deceased Emperor's last will,
appointing Zhuāng Qīnwáng Yǔnlù, Guǒ Qīnwáng Yǔnlǐ, È'ěrtài, and Zhāng Tíngyù as regents,
and also ordering È'ěrtài to resume his post,
as È'ěrtài had previously requested leave due to illness.
By the last will, his imperial concubine mother was honored as Empress Dowager,
and further by imperial decree, the former imperial concubine was honored as Empress.
Grand Secretary Zhū Shì was summoned back to the capital.
Grand Secretary Jī Zēngyún was ordered to oversee the seawall project in Zhèjiāng,
and Zhào Hóng'ēn was appointed acting Governor-General of Riverways in Jiāngnán.
For the grand encoffinment of the deceased Emperor,
it was ordered that the southern corridor of the Qiánqīng Gōng be used as the mourning hall.
On the Gēngyín day,
the princes and ministers overseeing affairs were ordered to discuss the implementation of the three-year mourning period.
Lǚ Jùnwáng (Prince Lü) Yǔntáo was ordered to temporarily manage the affairs of the Ministry of Rites.
Zhāng Zhào was summoned back to the capital.
Zhāng Guǎngsì was appointed to oversee Miaó border affairs,
and Grand Secretary Màizhù was appointed acting Governor-General of Húguǎng.
It was decreed that Great General Chá Láng'ā be stationed in Sùzhōu,
to jointly manage military affairs with Liú Yúyì,
and that the Northern Route Great General, Píng Jùnwáng (Prince Ping) Fú Pēng, should hold his position firmly.
Yángwēi Jiāngjūn Hā Yuánshēng and others were instructed to suppress and pacify the Miaó border regions.
On the Guǐsì day,
the deceased Emperor's last will and testament were promulgated.
In the ninth month, on the *dìngyǒu* day of the first quarter,
there was a solar eclipse.
Gāo Qǐ and Xiàn Dé were both dismissed,
but retained their titles as Grand Secretaries.
È'ěrtài was appointed to oversee the Ministry of War,
Qīn Wáng Yǔnlǐ of the Guǒ-rank to oversee the Ministry of Punishments,
Qīn Wáng Yǔnlù of the Zhuāng-rank to oversee the Ministry of Public Works.
Gān Rǔlái was made Han Minister of War,
and Fù Nài was acting Manchu Minister of War.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Emperor ascended the throne in the Tàihé Diàn,
designating the following year as the first year of Qiánlóng.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the three-year mourning period was fixed,
and the request from the assembled officials to shorten it to one month per year was rejected.
Grand Secretary Zhū Shì was ordered to assist the princely ministers who were overseeing affairs.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Shǐ Yízhí was summoned to the capital.
On the *rényín* day,
the presentation of local products as tribute was halted.
Monks circulating within the inner court were forbidden from soliciting ostentatiously.
The *Shíxiàn Shū* for the first year of Qiánlóng was issued.
Qiánlóng Tōngbǎo coins were cast.
Officials were dispatched to Korea to promulgate the imperial edict.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
relief was provided for the drought in Lánzhōu, Píngliáng and other areas of Gānsù.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Qìng Fù was ordered to the northern military camp,
to replace Huí Fú Péng.
A handwritten decree was sent to the *Èfù* Cèlíng, ordering him not to leave the military camp.
On the *dìngwèi* day,
the coffin of the late Emperor was respectfully placed in the Yōnghé Gōng.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the Emperor went to the Yōnghé Gōng to perform rites.
From this day until the *yǐmǎo* day, this became a regular practice.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Qīn Wáng Yǔnlù of the Zhuāng-rank and Qīn Wáng Yǔnlǐ of the Guǒ-rank were awarded double stipends.
È'ěrtài and Zhāng Tíngyù were granted hereditary titles of First-Class Light Chariot Commandant.
Zhū Shì was granted the hereditary title of Cavalry Commandant.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Yáng Míngshí was summoned to the capital.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Hǎi Wàng was appointed acting Minister of Revenue,
and Fù Nài acting Minister of Punishments.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor went to the Yōnghé Gōng to perform a grand sacrifice.
The Empress Dowager was moved to reside in the Yǒngrén Gōng.
On this day,
the Emperor moved to reside in the Yǎngxīn Diàn.
Court officials were ordered to submit memorials in rotation,
each presenting what they knew.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Lǐ Fú was awarded the title of Vice Minister,
and put in charge of the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the Emperor went to the Yōnghé Gōng to perform the monthly sacrifice before the late Emperor's coffin.
From this point until the coffin's relocation,
this was done every month.
The arrears of *dìngfù* (poll tax) owed by the people were again remitted,
and it was also decreed that officials who had embezzled funds would also be pardoned.
Fù'ěrdān was arrested and imprisoned.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
an *Enke* (special examination) for the provincial and metropolitan examinations was opened.
The regular taxes of counties in Guìzhōu affected by unrest were remitted,
while those unaffected had their collection suspended.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the Emperor went to Tián Cūn to offer sacrifices before the coffin of Empress Xiàojìng.
Due to numerous irregularities in this year's provincial examinations,
the examiners Gù Zǔzhèn and Dài Hàn were arrested for investigation.
Grand Secretary Mǎ Qí requested retirement,
which was granted.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Sūn Jiāgàn, acting Salt Commissioner for Hédōng, was summoned to the capital
to be appointed as a Vice Minister.
In the tenth month, on the *bǐngyín* day of the first quarter,
a sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào,
with Qīn Wáng Guǎngbǎo of the Yù-rank deputizing.
Vice General Cháng Dé was ordered to the northern military camp.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the prohibition on tribute from the provinces was reiterated.
Zhāng Guǎngsì was appointed as the Commissioner for the suppression of the Miao,
and General Yángwēi Hā Yuánshēng, Vice General Dǒng Fāng, and all below them were placed under his command.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Jùn Wáng Yǔntáo of the Lǚ-rank was ordered to manage the Ministry of Rites.
The former Minister Tú Tiānxiāng was summoned to the capital.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Rèn Lánzhī was appointed Minister of Rites.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the grain transport arrears, reed taxes, and school rents and miscellaneous taxes in Jiāngnán and other provinces were remitted.
An order was issued to prosecute Zēng Jìng and Zhāng Xī.
Fú Mǐn, Left Censor-in-chief, was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
Because the princely ministers handling affairs were slow and lax,
an edict was issued to strictly instruct them to be resolute and active,
and not to contradict the intention of leniency.
Xú Běn was transferred to be Minister of Punishments,
and Tú Tiānxiāng Minister of Public Works.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Liú Xiǎng was appointed Governor-General of Waterways for Zhílì.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Péng Wéixīn was reinstated as Left Censor-in-chief.
Xú Běn was ordered to serve in the Grand Council.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
princes were forbidden from concurrently managing ministry or court affairs.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Hǎi Wàng was appointed Minister of Revenue.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Lái Bǎo was appointed acting Minister of Public Works,
and concurrently managed the Imperial Household Department.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Fù'ěrdān, Yuè Zhōngqí, Shí Yúnzhuō, and Mǎ Lántài were sentenced to beheading.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Nàqīn, Hǎi Wàng, and Xú Běn were redesignated as Assistant Ministers for General Affairs,
and Nàyántài was appointed to serve,
following the precedent of Bāndì and others.
Fēngshèng'é and Mǎnghú Lì were dismissed.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Zhāng Zhào was imprisoned for interrogation.
On the *rényín* day,
fifteen Tusi (native chieftains) in Zhōngyǒng and other areas of Húběi were reformed,
and one prefecture and five counties were established.
The prefectural seat was established in Ēnshī County,
named Shīnán Fǔ.
The county seats were separately established,
named Xuān'ēn, Láifèng, Xiánfēng, and Lìchuān.
On the *yǐsì* day,
an edict was reiterated to recommend scholars of profound learning and extensive literary skill.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the Emperor bestowed the posthumous title on the late Emperor as Jìng Tiān Chāng Yùn Jiàn Zhōng Biǎo Zhèng Wén Wǔ Yīng Míng Kuān Rén Xìn Yì Dà Xiào Zhì Chéng Xiàn Huángdì,
with the temple name Shìzōng.
The next day, an edict of widespread grace was promulgated with various provisions.
The regular taxes for drought-stricken Bā Xiàn and other counties in Sìchuān were remitted.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Mài Zhù was summoned to the capital,
and Shǐ Yízhí was appointed acting Governor-General of Húguǎng.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Sūn Jiāgàn was appointed Left Censor-in-chief.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Qìng Fù was appointed Commander-in-chief of Dìngbiān,
to proceed to the northern military camp.
Sūn Jiāgàn was ordered to continue concurrently managing the Ministry of Personnel.
An edict was issued to pardon the crimes of the surrendered Miao.
The *hàoxiàn* (wastage and deficit levies) for Guìzhōu for three years were remitted.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the Emperor went to Tián Cūn to bestow the posthumous title on Empress Xiàojìng Xiàn as Xiàojìng Gōng Hé Yì Shùn Zhāo Huì Yòu Tiān Yì Shèng Xiàn Huánghòu.
The next day, an edict of widespread grace was promulgated with various provisions.
The Governor-General of Hédōng was changed back to Governor of Hénán,
and Fù Dé was appointed to this post.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Zhōng Bǎo was appointed Governor of Húnán,
and Yú Zhàoyuè Governor of Jiāngxī.
Dài Línbù was appointed Right Wing General.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Jùn Wáng Fú Péng of the Píng-rank was appointed Assistant Minister for General Affairs.
Dǒng Fāng, Yuán Zhǎnchéng, and Dé Xīshòu were stripped of their positions and arrested for questioning.
Hā Yuánshēng was stripped of his title of General Yángwēi.
Commissioner Zhāng Guǎngsì was ordered to concurrently serve as Governor of Guìzhōu.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the descendants of Āqínà and Sàisīhēi were granted red sashes,
and their names were entered into the Imperial Genealogy.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the princely ministers collaborated with the Ministry of Punishments to interrogate Lǐ Xǐ and Gěng Tāo,
and the interrogating ministers were ordered to observe the general principle.
In the twelfth month, on the *bǐngyín* day of the first quarter,
Bódì was appointed General of Jílín,
and Wú Lǐbù General of Hēilóngjiāng.
The Governor-General of Chuānxí was re-established,
and the Governor-General of Sìchuān was abolished.
On the *wùchén* day,
relief was provided for the flood in Sìzhōu, Ānhuī and Qiánjiāng, Húběi.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
arrears of salt tax for salt fields in Zhèjiāng, Shāndōng, Fújiàn, and Guǎngdōng were remitted.
On the *wùyín* day,
the Empress Dowager was granted the honorific title Chóngqìng Huángtàihòu.
The next day, an edict of widespread grace was promulgated with various provisions.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
as the Zūnggǎr sent envoys to request peace,
the Khalkha Zhasak and others were ordered to discuss and determine border matters in detail.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Fù Nài was transferred to be Minister of Punishments,
and continued concurrently managing the Ministry of War.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Zēng Jìng and Zhāng Xī were publicly executed by dismemberment.
Commandant Lǐ Xǐ for corruption,
and Minister Gāo Qǐ for deception and fraud,
were both sentenced to beheading.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Jī Zēngyún was ordered to concurrently manage the governorship of Zhèjiāng.
Gāo Bīn was appointed Governor-General of Waterways for Jiāngnán.
A General and a Vice Commandant were established for Guīhuà Chéng.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Nàqīn was promoted to First-Class Duke,
with hereditary succession.
In the spring of the first year of Qiánlóng, on the day bǐngshēn of the first month,
the Emperor proceeded to the Tángzǐ to perform rites.
Upon reaching the Guāndédiàn, he changed into plain attire,
and after performing rites at the Yōnghémén,
he led the various princes and high officials to the Cínínggōng to perform rites.
He presided over the Grand Audience at the Tàihédiàn,
without music
and without reading memorials.
On the day wùxū,
Sāmǔhā, the assistant minister for the northern route, was ordered to return to the capital.
On the day xīncǎo,
the Emperor personally proceeded to perform rites
to the Heavenly Lord for a good harvest.
From then on, this was done annually.
On the day guǐmǎo,
the Xiāncántán was established in the capital.
Gá'ěrdāncèlíng, the Tàijí of the Zhǔngá'ěr, sent envoys to present local products as tribute.
On the day dīngwèi,
Chuīnnàmùkē, an envoy from the Zhǔngá'ěr, was received in audience.
General Qìngfù was recalled to the capital.
Yīlèshen, Āchéng'ā, and Hādài were appointed assistant ministers,
to work with the Éfù Cèlíng,
stationed at È'ěrkun.
Dūtǒng Wáng Cháng and Shìláng Bǎixiū were ordered to È'ěrkun to survey military colonies.
On the day bǐngchén,
Gù Cóng was appointed acting governor of Jiāngsū.
On the day jǐwèi,
Cuī Qǐqián, the acting general-in-chief of the Yǒngzhōu Garrison in Húnán, was impeached for falsely accusing È'ěrtài and Zhāng Guǎngsì,
stripped of his position, and arrested for trial.
Nánzhǎng offered tribute.
On the day gēngchén,
the Emperor began his journey to visit the imperial tombs.
On the day guǐhài,
the Emperor visited the Zhāoxīlíng, Xiàolíng, Xiàodōnglíng, and Jǐnglíng.
Relief was provided to earthquake victims in Zhūluó County, Táiwān.
Relief was provided to drought victims in Gùyuán, Gānsù, and Zhōngzhōu, Sìchuān, and other prefectures and counties.
In the second month, on the day bǐngyín,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day wùchén,
the Emperor personally proceeded to perform rites
at the Grand Altar of the Earth and the Grand Altar of Grain.
From then on, this was done annually.
Bǔ Xī was appointed acting governor-general of grain transport.
On the day jiǎxū,
the Zhǔngá'ěr envoys were sent back,
and an imperial edict was issued, in accordance with the late Emperor's decree,
to delimit the border,
and sent to Gá'ěrdāncèlíng.
On the day yǐmǎo,
an imperial rescript was granted to Gá'ěrdāncèlíng, the Tàijí of the Zhǔngá'ěr,
rejecting his request to use Zhé'ěrgéxīlāhūlǔsū as the border,
and to exclusively resettle the Khalkha people internally.
On the day gēngchén,
Mài Zhù was appointed concurrently in charge of the Ministry of Works.
Xiè Jìshì, Lǐ Huī, Chén Shìguān, and others were sternly reprimanded for their erroneous and absurd memorials.
Yáng Míngshí was granted the title of Minister of Rites
and concurrently managed the affairs of the Guózǐjiàn Jìjiǔ.
On the day xīnyǒu,
Lǐ Yǐn, King of Cháoxiǎn, sent envoys to offer incense,
and was bestowed gifts according to custom.
On the day jiǎshēn,
Jī Zēngyún was ordered to be reassigned as governor-general of Zhèjiāng,
concurrently managing the salt administration of the two Zhè regions.
Hǎo Yùlín, as governor-general of Fújiàn and Zhèjiāng, was to exclusively manage affairs in Fújiàn.
On the day wùzǐ,
the imperial tomb of Shìzōng was named Tàilíng.
On the day jǐchǒu,
the Dálài Lǎmā and Bèilè Pōluónài sent envoys to present local products as tribute.
On the day xīnmǎo,
Chéng Yuánzhāng was appointed governor-general of grain transport.
On the day guǐsì,
Yǐn Jìshàn reported the capture of the stockades of Kèkōngbài and Táixióng.
Zhāng Guǎngsì reported the capture of the greater and lesser Dānjiāng and other places.
In the third month, on the day gēngzǐ,
the relatives of Wāng Jǐngqí and Zhā Sìtíng were released to return to their hometowns.
On the day yǐsì,
additional honorific titles were conferred upon Tàizǔ as Tàizǔ Chéngtiān Guǎngyùn Shèngdé Shéngōng Zhàojì Lìjí Rénxiào Ruìwǔ Duānyì Qīn'ān Hóngwén Dìngyè Gāohuángdì,
and upon Empress Xiàocí as Xiàocí Zhāoxiàn Jìngshùn Rénhuī Yìdé Qìngxiǎn Chéngtiān Fǔshèng Gāohuánghòu;
upon Tàizōng as Tàizōng Yìngtiān Xìngguó Hóngdé Zhāngwǔ Kuānwēn Rénshèng Ruìxiào Jìngmǐn Zhāodìng Lóngdào Xiǎngōng Wénhuángdì,
and upon Empress Xiàoduān as Xiàoduān Zhèngjìng Rényì Zhéshùn Cíxī Zhuāngmǐn Fǔtiān Xiéshèng Wénhuánghòu,
and upon Empress Xiàozhuāng as Xiàozhuāng Rénxuān Chéngxiàn Gōngyì Zhìdé Chúnhuī Yìtiān Qǐshèng Wénhuánghòu;
upon Shìzǔ as Shìzǔ Tǐtiān Lóngyùn Dìngtǒng Jiànjí Yīngruì Qīnwén Xiǎnwǔ Dàdé Hónggōng Zhìrén Chúnxiào Zhānghuángdì,
and upon Empress Xiàohuì as Xiàohuì Rénxiàn Duānyì Císhū Gōng'ān Chúndé Shùntiān Yìshèng Zhānghuánghòu,
and upon Empress Xiàokāng as Xiàokāng Cíhé Zhuāngyì Gōnghuì Wēnmù Duānjìng Chóngtiān Yùshèng Zhānghuánghòu;
upon Shèngzǔ as Shèngzǔ Hétiān Hóngyùn Wénwǔ Ruìzhé Gōngjiǎn Kuānyù Xiàojìng Chéngxìn Zhōnghé Gōngdé Dàchéng Rénhuángdì,
and upon Empress Xiàochéng as Xiàochéng Gōngsù Zhènghuì Ānhé Shūyì Lìtiān Xiāngshèng Rénhuánghòu,
and upon Empress Xiàozhāo as Xiàozhāo Jìngshū Mínghuì Zhènghé Ānyù Qīntiān Shùnshèng Rénhuánghòu,
and upon Empress Xiàogōng as Xiàogōng Xuānhuì Wēnsù Dìngyù Cíchún Zàntiān Chéngshèng Rénhuánghòu.
On the day dīngwèi,
the additional levies on the indigenous people in Liángshān, Sìchuān, and other places were remitted.
On the day jǐyǒu,
old debts owed by Muslim residents of Wēilǔbǎo, Sùzhōu, were remitted.
On the day gēngxū,
Fán Tíng, the Tídū of Gùyuán, was appointed governor-general stationed at Hāmì.
On the day yǐmǎo,
the increased fishing tax and outstanding arrears for Guīshàn and three other counties in Guǎngdōng, and the entire province, were remitted.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day bǐngyín,
the deferred collection of grain tribute in Fùníng and other prefectures and counties in Jiāngnán was remitted.
On the day rénshēn,
Wáng Cháng and Hǎi Lán were appointed assistant ministers,
to work with the Éfù Cèlíng.
Gāo Qízhuó was appointed governor of Húběi,
and temporarily acting governor of Húnán.
On the day wùyín,
Wáng Shìjùn was appointed governor of Sìchuān.
On the day xīnsì,
Hā Yuánshēng, the Tídū of Guìzhōu, was stripped of his position and arrested for questioning.
The position of vice director-general of rivers for Zhílì was abolished,
with the governor-general concurrently managing river affairs.
On the day wùzǐ,
Jīn Déyīng and 334 other successful candidates in the imperial examination were granted the degree of Jìnshì and related ranks.
On the day rénchén,
Línqìnqíléi Lābùjì, Noyan of the Bùlǔkèbā Department, arrived in Xīzàng to inquire about the Emperor's well-being,
and presented local products as tribute.
In the fifth month, on the day dīngwèi,
relief was provided for flood victims in Yǒngchéng County, Hénán.
On the day rénzǐ,
the vice director-general of rivers for Jiāngnán was ordered to relocate to Xúzhōu.
On the day jiǎyín,
the additional levies on account of damage from wind and hail in Nánxī and other prefectures and counties in Sìchuān were remitted.
On the day yǐmǎo,
Lǐ Yǐn, King of Cháoxiǎn, presented a memorial congratulating the Emperor on his accession and on honoring the Empress Dowager,
and also presented local products.
On the day yǐsì,
Cān Lì Pāizhào Guǎng Pāimǎ Hū Liù Kūn Sī Yóutíyà Pú Āi, King of Xiāmluó, presented a memorial of thanks for the bestowed plaque,
and also presented local products.
On the day gēngchén,
the shortfall in Dīngyín due to deaths and injuries from earthquakes in Fúqiáng and other prefectures and counties in Gānsù was remitted.
In the sixth month, on the day wùchén,
relief was provided for flood victims in Xiāo County and other prefectures and counties in Jiāngsū.
On the day jǐsì,
Qìngfù was appointed acting Minister of Personnel,
and continued to concurrently act as Minister of Revenue.
On the day guǐyǒu,
Zhāng Guǎngsì was appointed governor-general of Guìzhōu,
and concurrently managed the affairs of the governor.
Yǐn Jìshàn was appointed governor-general of Yúnnán.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day guǐsì,
as many displaced people from Guìzhōu had sought refuge in Yuánzhōu,
the additional levies for Yuánzhōu were remitted.
On the day jiǎwǔ,
the Grand Ministers of the Imperial Secretariat and the Nine Chief Ministers were summoned,
and the secret decree for establishing the heir apparent was proclaimed,
to be stored above the "Zhèngdà Guāngmíng" plaque in the Qiánqīnggōng.
On the day jǐhài,
the additional levies for the entire province of Guìzhōu for that year were remitted.
On the day xīncǎo,
the Miao levies in Gǔzhōu and other places were abolished.
On the day jiǎchén,
Cuī Qǐqián's punishment was remitted.
On the day bǐngwǔ,
relief was provided for flood victims in Ānfú, Jiāngxī.
On the day xīnhài,
posthumous titles were conferred upon Emperor Jiànwén of Míng as Gōngmǐn Huìhuángdì.
Relief was provided for flood victims in Xiāo, Dàng, and other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Jiāngnán.
On the day dīngsì,
relief was provided for flood and hail victims in Lǒngxī and other prefectures and counties in Gānsù.
On the day wùwǔ,
Zhōng Bǎo was reassigned as governor of Húběi,
and Gāo Qízhuó as governor of Húnán.
Relief was provided for flood victims in Hànchuān and five other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Húběi.
On the day guǐyǒu,
Wáng Shìjùn was arrested for questioning,
and subsequently condemned to be beheaded.
Relief was provided for flood victims in Nánhǎi, Cháoyáng, and other counties in Guǎngdōng.
In the eighth month, on the day wùchén,
the Emperor personally proceeded to perform rites
at the Grand Altar of Grain and the Grand Altar of the Earth.
From then on, this was done annually.
Mèngkè, a person from the Zhǔngá'ěr tribe, surrendered.
On the day gēngwǔ,
Shàngshū Fù Nài was dismissed due to offenses.
On the day yǐmǎo,
relief was provided for flood victims in Nányáng and five other counties in Hénán.
On the day yǐyǒu,
relief was provided for the hungry in Kālāqìn.
On the day dīnghài,
Tōng Zhì, Minister of War, was dismissed,
and replaced by Nàsūtú, General of Fèngtiān.
Bódì was reassigned as General of Fèngtiān.
Jí'ěrdǎng'ā was appointed General of Nínggǔtǎ.
Relief was provided for hail victims in Shénmù and Fǔgǔ, Shǎnxī.
On the day xīnmǎo,

relief was provided for flood victims in Lánxī and six other counties in Zhèjiāng, Lìshuǐ and twenty-four other prefectures and counties in Jiāngnán, and Qiánjiāng and nine other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Húběi.
In the ninth month, on the day Rénshēn,
Zhāng Zhào, Hā Yuánshēng, Dǒng Fāng, Yuán Zhǎnchéng, and Déxīshòu were dismissed for offenses that misled the Miáojiāng region.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Yáng Míngshí, President of the Board of Rites, passed away.
On the day Wùxū,
Qìngfù was appointed President of the Board of Punishments,
also overseeing the Board of Civil Office.
Fù Nài was ordered to temporarily act as President of the Board of War.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
this year's autumn executions were suspended.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
relief was provided for flood victims in Ānjí and three other counties in Zhèjiāng.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Emperor visited Grand Secretary Zhū Shì at his residence to inquire about his illness.
The regular land tax for flood-affected areas in Ānfú, Jiāngxī, was remitted.
On the day Gēngxū,
Grand Secretary Zhū Shì passed away.
The Emperor personally attended and offered sacrifices.
On the day Rénzǐ,
relief was provided for flood victims in Sùzhōu and twenty other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Ānhuī.
Chén Yuánlóng, a retired Grand Secretary, passed away.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
relief was provided for flood victims in Xiāoxiàn and three other prefectures and counties in Jiāngsū.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the imperial examination for Scholars of Broad Learning and Extensive Vocabulary was held for one hundred seventy-six candidates in the Hall of Preserving Harmony.
Liú Lún and others were appointed to official positions.
Relief was provided for flood victims in Wúxī and thirteen other prefectures and garrisons in Jiāngsū.
The Zǔngāěr táijí Chēlín and others surrendered.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Rénxū,
Shào Jī was appointed Governor of Jiāngsū.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the regular land tax for flood-affected areas in Ránhé and other prefectures and counties in Zhèjiāng was remitted.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Yuè Jùn was transferred to be Governor of Jiāngxī,
and Fǎ Mǐn was appointed Governor of Shāndōng.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, escorted Shìzōng's coffin to the Tàilíng mausoleum.
On the day Gēngchén,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, returned to the capital.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Emperor began holding court at the Qiánqīng Gate.
Jī Zēngyún was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
Xú Běn was appointed Grand Secretary of the Dōnggé,
continuing to oversee the Board of Punishments.
Sūn Jiāgàn was appointed President of the Board of Punishments,
and Yáng Rǔgǔ was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
Értú was appointed General of Hēilóngjiāng.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the regular land tax for Chǔxióng and four other prefectures, departments, and counties in Yúnnán was remitted.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
relief was provided for flood victims in Huòqiū and three other counties and garrisons in Ānhuī, and Hánchuān and thirteen other counties and garrisons in Húběi.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
on the Winter Solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Yuánqiú Altar,
and the Emperor personally went to perform the rites.
From then on, this was done annually.
On the day Jǐwèi,
relief was provided for hail victims in Dìngbiān, Shǎnxī,
and flood victims in Chángzhōu and twelve other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Jiāngnán.
In the twelfth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
relief was provided for drought victims in the four banners of Báolín Jùnwáng and others.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
relief was provided for flood victims in Lóu, Lìshuǐ, and thirteen other prefectures and counties in Jiāngsū.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the Shòuchūn Commandery in Jiāngnán was reorganized into a鎮 (zhèn, military division),
and a Commander-in-Chief was established.
On the day Jǐsì,
the regular land tax for hail-affected areas in Fǔgǔ and Shénmù, Shǎnxī, for this year was remitted.
The Deputy Grand River Director of the Southern River was relocated to Xúzhōu.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the regular land tax for flood-affected areas in Sīzhōuwèi's Tún Tián (military colony farms), Chánglú, and Guǎngyún Zàodì in Ānhuī was remitted.
On the day Dīnghài,
Dàilín Bù was reassigned as General of Jiāngníng.
Wáng Cháng was appointed General Jiànwēi,
and Yǎěrtú was appointed Counselor Minister.
The regular land tax for flood-affected areas in Guǎndú and three other salt fields in Liǎnghuái was remitted.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn, Nánzhǎng, Xiānluó, and Ānnán paid tribute.
In the second year, spring, in the first month, on the first day Gēngyín,
the morning audience was canceled.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Zhào Hóngēn was summoned to the capital.
Qìngfù was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng.
Nàsūtú was transferred to be President of the Board of Punishments.
Nàqīn was appointed President of the Board of War.
On the day Yǐsì,
Yáng Cháozēng was appointed Governor of Guǎngxī.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Wáng Shìjùn was released.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Lǐ Wèi impeached the guards of Chéngqīnwáng's residence for favoritism.
The Emperor praised him
and bestowed upon him a four-dragon official robe.
In the second month, on the day Bǐngyín,
Lí Wéihù, King of Ānnán, passed away.
His heir, Lí Wéiyī, sent an envoy to announce the mourning
and present local tribute.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
relief was provided for flood victims in Gāoyóu, Jiāngsū.
On the day Wùyín,
Sōngshòu, Reader of the Hanlin Academy, and Chén Tán, Compiler, were dispatched to enfeoff Lí Wéiyī as King of Ānnán.
On the day Gēngchén,
Empress Xiàojìng Xiàn Hòú's funeral procession began.
