during the selection of Censors,
Háng Shìjùn's policy statement about "Manchu within, Han outside"
offended the Emperor and led to his dismissal.
Liú Yúyì was transferred to be Governor of Shānxī.
Sūn Jiāgàn was ordered to act as Governor of Fújiàn.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Yǐn Jìshàn was ordered to act as Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
to assist Bái Zhōngshān in managing river affairs.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Dèng Shímǐn, Lecturer, and Ní Guólián, Supervising Secretary, were appointed as Envoys for Propaganda and Guidance for Fèng, Yǐng, and Sì.
Tú Féngzhèn, Compiler, and Xú Yǐshēng, Censor, were appointed as Envoys for Propaganda and Guidance for Huái, Xú, Yáng, and Hǎi.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the extra tax from flood-stricken areas in Hánchuān and eleven other *zhōu*, *xiàn*, and *wèi* in Húběi was remitted.
Zhào Guólín was permitted to return to his native place.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Qīn Wáng Hóngzhòu was dispatched to offer sacrifices at the Altar of Agriculture (*Xiānnóngtán*) in place of the Emperor, using the *Zhōnghé Sháoyuè* music,
which was equivalent to the Emperor's personal sacrifice,
and this was established as a precedent.
Famine relief was distributed in Téngxiàn and six other *zhōu* and *xiàn* in Shāndōng.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Kā'ěrjǐshàn was transferred to be Governor of Shāndōng,
Yàn Sīshèng as Governor of Húběi,
and Fàn Càn as Governor of Ānhuī.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the Emperor visited the palace of Empress Dowager Shòuqí to inquire about her illness.
In the fourth month of summer, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
Empress Dowager Shòuqí passed away,
and court was suspended for ten days.
The Emperor wished to observe mourning,
but Qìng Wáng and others pleaded for him to be excused.
An edict was issued to instruct the Nine Chief Ministers to be diligent in their duties.
Another edict ordered all Governors-General and Governors to report on the competence of their subordinates.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor visited the palace of Empress Dowager Shòuqí to offer condolences.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Imperial Household Department (*Fèngchén Yuàn*) was ordered to experiment with the *qūtián* cultivation method.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
famine relief was distributed to the flood-stricken people in the six prefectures and *zhōu* under Fèngyáng in Ānhuī.
The extra tax from flood-stricken areas in Xiāngyáng and three other *xiàn* in Húběi was remitted.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the Coastal Defense Circuit (*Hǎifángdào*) of Jiāngsū was abolished.
The Huái-Xú Sea Circuit (*Huáixú Hǎidào*) was established,
stationed at Xúzhōu Fǔ.
The Sū-Sōng Inspection Circuit (*Sūsōng Xúndào*) concurrently managed dike works.
Yángzhōu Fǔ was placed under the Cháng-Zhèn Circuit (*Chángzhèndào*).
The formerly established Huái-Xú and Huái-Yáng two circuits exclusively managed river works.
On the *jiǎyín* day of the intercalary fourth month,
Ryūkyū paid tribute.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Emperor personally examined Hanlin and Imperial Tutors (*Zhànshì*) and other officials,
promoting Wáng Huìfén and two others to the first rank,
while the rest were promoted or demoted accordingly.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the extra tax for this year's flood-stricken areas in Zhèngzhōu and thirteen other *zhōu* and *xiàn* in Hénán was remitted.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the land tax for collapsed and submerged fields in Wújiāng and two other *xiàn* in Jiāngsū was abolished.
On the *guǐwèi* day of the fifth month,
an edict stated that during imperial tours,
the escorting guards and others should be strictly disciplined,
and not be allowed to trample crops.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Censor Shěn Màohuá was summoned for an audience to present his lecture notes on classics and history.
After he had left,
the matter was sent to the relevant board for severe deliberation.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Hénán was ordered to suspend the collection of money and grain taxes in areas affected by last year's floods.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the brokerage tax (*yáshuì*) in Shānyáng and thirteen other *zhōu* and *xiàn* in Jiāngsū was remitted.
The shipping fees for tax grain and the copper compensation for merchants in Línqīng were remitted.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
famine relief was distributed in Lìchéng and eighteen other *zhōu*, *xiàn*, and *wèi* in Shāndōng.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Shuòsè was appointed Governor of Hénán,
and Jìshān as Governor of Sìchuān.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Qìngfù was transferred to be Governor-General of Chuānshǎn.
Mǎ'ěrtài was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng.
Zhāng Yǔnsuí was appointed Governor-General of Yúnnán,
concurrently managing gubernatorial affairs.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
King Mahāma Ariban Níng of Sūlù memorialized to request tribute be paid every three years.
The Emperor ordered the old custom of five years to be followed.
On the *rénzǐ* day of the sixth month,
Censor Chén Rén requested that Hanlin and Imperial Tutors be examined in classics and history,
and that poetry and prose should not be used.
The Emperor commended him.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Nánzhǎng's tribute was changed to once every ten years.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the land tax for submerged land in Pèixiàn, Jiāngsū, was abolished.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
appeals for advice were sought due to drought.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Ālǐgǔn was ordered to temporarily act as Governor of Hénán.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
regarding the case where Censor Hú Dìng impeached Xǔ Róng, Governor of Húnán,
it was found that the Governor-General and Governor had colluded in false accusations,
and punishment was meted out.
On the *rénshēn* day,
an edict instructed Governors-General and Governors to lead their subordinates in emphasizing agriculture.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
the Emperor visited the palace of Shùnyì Mì Tàifēi to inquire about her illness.
On the day Bǐngxū,
due to unrest in Ānnán,
which disturbed the Kǎihuà Dūchǎng in Yúnnán,
Zhāng Yǔnsuí and others were ordered to strictly guard against it.
Sài Dū, the commander-in-chief of Kǎihuà Town, requested to suppress Ānnán,
but this was not permitted.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, traveled from Rèhé to Shèngjīng to visit the imperial tombs.
The taxes and grain of the areas of Zhílì and Fèngtiān through which they passed were exempted.
Four hundred thousand shí of grain from the public granaries were allocated to relieve the drought disaster in Zhílì.
On the day Rénchén,
the additional taxes for drought-stricken areas in Lìchéng and sixteen other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Shāndōng were exempted.
On the day Yǐwèi,
this year's capital punishment reviews were suspended.
The Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, resided at the Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the land tax for flood-affected areas in Liánjiāng and two other counties in Fújiàn was abolished.
On the day Jǐhài,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, proceeded to Shèngjīng.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Emperor went hunting at Yǒng'ān Mǎngkā.
On the day Yǐsì,
the Emperor went hunting at Àilǐ.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Emperor went hunting at Xīlānuòhǎi.
Orders were given to strictly eliminate the abuses of prefectures and counties levying grain taxes and holding grain in storage.
On the day Wùshēn,
the additional taxes for households affected by hail in Cāngzhōu, Zhílì, were exempted.
The Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, resided at Māmātǎlā.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
the Emperor went hunting.
This continued until the day Jǐmǎo.
The leakage of secret memorials by governors and other officials was strictly prohibited.
Relief was provided for flood disasters in Xīngguó and three other prefectures and counties in Húběi,
and their additional taxes were also exempted.
On the day Guǐhài,
the Emperor's birthday (Wànshòu Jié) was celebrated.
The Emperor proceeded to the Empress Dowager's imperial tent to perform the ceremony.
At the imperial tent,
the accompanying princes, ministers, officials, and Mongolian princes and other officials offered congratulations.
Princes, ministers, and Mongolian princes were granted a banquet.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Emperor resided at Bāyá'ěrtútālá.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the Emperor went hunting.
On the day Wùchén,
the Emperor went hunting.
On the day Rénshēn,
the Emperor resided at Yīkè Nà'ěr,
and went hunting.
This continued until the day Bǐngzǐ.
On the day Jiǎxū,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Xīchāng, Sìchuān.
Matters regarding disaster relief for drought-stricken prefectures and counties in Zhílì were settled.
Relief was provided for flood disasters in Shǐxīng and sixteen other prefectures and counties in Guǎngdōng.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the Emperor went hunting at Bāyàn,
and personally shot and killed a tiger.
In the ninth month, on the first day Gēngchén,
the Emperor went hunting at Wǔshíháng'ā,
and personally shot and killed a tiger.
On the day Xīnsì,
the Emperor went hunting at Wēizhǔn.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Emperor went hunting at Huángkē.
On the day Guǐwèi,
the Emperor went hunting at Ālán.
Because the Jebtsundamba Khutuktu did not memorialize about going to É'ěrdění Zhāolǐbài,
both the Tǔxiètú Hàn Dùndānduō'ěrzǐ were referred to the Lǐfānyuàn for deliberation and punishment.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
relief was provided for flood and famine in Shāngzhōu, Shǎnxī.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the Emperor went hunting at Shèlǐ.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the Emperor went hunting at Shànyán Wōhè.
On the day Dīnghài,
the Emperor went hunting at Bāyàn.
Èmǐdá was reassigned as the Jiāngjūn of Jīngzhōu.
Bódì was transferred to be the Jiāngjūn of Jílín,
and Fùsēn was transferred to be the Jiāngjūn of Hēilóngjiāng.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Emperor went hunting at Níyǎmǎnhū.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the Emperor went hunting at Zhūdùn.
On the day Gēngyín,
the Emperor went hunting outside the Yīng'é Biānmén.
On this day,
he resided at Wūsū Hé.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Xǔ Róng, whose impeachment of Xiè Jìshì for corruption and indulgence was found to be entirely baseless,
and Sūn Jiāgàn, who colluded in settling the case,
were both dismissed from their posts.
The acting grain intendant Cāng Dé, whose involvement in the disclosure was confirmed by interrogation,
was given to [be executed].
The Emperor resided at Mùqí Cūn.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, visited Yǒnglíng.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the grand sacrificial rites were performed.
It was ordered to halt Gù Cóng's proposal to limit private land.
Relief was provided for drought disasters in Xiángfú and twenty-one other prefectures and counties in Hénán, and Qídōng and eighteen other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Shāndōng,
and their additional taxes were exempted to varying degrees.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Fúlíng was visited.
On the day Rényín,
the grand sacrificial rites were performed.
Zhāolíng was visited.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the grand sacrificial rites were performed.
The Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, resided at Shèngjīng.
Lǐ Qǐn, the King of Joseon, sent his attendant ministers to Shèngjīng to present tribute.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the Emperor led his assembled officials to the Empress Dowager's palace to perform the congratulatory ceremony.
He ascended the Chóngzhèng Diàn to receive congratulations.
A banquet was granted to the assembled officials and the Joseon envoys.
He ascended the Dàzhèng Diàn to grant a general amnesty.
An edict was issued to extend grace to varying degrees.
On the day Yǐsì,
the Emperor proceeded to the Wénmiào to offer sacrifices to Confucius.
He visited the Jiǎngwǔ Tái for a grand review.
He instructed the princes, dukes, imperial clan members, and ministers to purify ceremonial observances,
to instruct soldiers and commoners,
and not to forget the pure and simple old customs.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Emperor personally offered sacrifices at the tombs of Prince Kèqín Yuètào and Wǔxūn Wáng Yánggǔlì.
Officials were dispatched to offer distant sacrifices to Mount Chángbái, Mount Yīwūlǘ of the Northern March, and the tomb of Liáo Tàizǔ.
On the day Wùshēn,
the Emperor personally offered sacrifices at the tombs of Hóngyì Gōng Éyídū and Zhíyì Gōng Fèiyīngdōng.
The collection of people's arrears in Hénán from before the seventh year of Qiánlóng was exempted.
In winter, the tenth month, on the first day Gēngxū,
the Emperor ascended the Dàzhèng Diàn,
and granted a banquet to the accompanying princes and ministers in front of the Fènghuáng Lóu.
He instructed the princes, dukes, and imperial clan members to eliminate bad practices
and strictly adhere to old regulations.
The additional taxes for this year and the arrears from the seventh year of Qiánlóng for the banner lands in Shèngjīng, Xīngjīng, and fifteen other locations were exempted.
The Emperor's imperial composition, the "Shèngjīng Fù," was created.
On the day Xīnhài,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, returned to the imperial residence.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Nánhǎi and seven other counties in Guǎngdōng.
On this day,
the Emperor ascended the Wànghǎi Lóu,
and resided at Wénshū Ān.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
it was ordered that distressed areas in Zhílì should sell grain at reduced prices.
On the day Jǐsì,
ministers of the Six Boards and Censorate were ordered to each recommend worthy individuals during the annual京察 (Jīngchá) review to replace themselves.
Liú Yúyì was appointed as Hùbù Shàngshū,
and Ālǐgǔn as Shānxī Xúnfǔ.
Xú Běn was ordered to continue concurrently managing the Hùbù.
Chén Hóngmóu was transferred to be Shǎnxī Xúnfǔ,
and Sàiléng'é was transferred to be Jiāngxī Xúnfǔ.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
relief was provided for drought disasters in Xiángfú and fourteen other prefectures and counties in Hénán.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, returned to the capital.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the Emperor, after the completion of the tomb-visiting ceremony,
led his assembled officials to the Empress Dowager's palace to perform the congratulatory ceremony.
He ascended the Tàihé Diàn,
and the princes, ministers, and various officials presented their memorials and offered congratulations.
In the eleventh month,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Wúwéi, Ānhuī,
and their additional taxes were also exempted.
On the day Rénwǔ,
relief was provided for flood, insect, wind, and hail disasters in Dí Dào and twenty-four other prefectures and counties in Gānsù.
On the day Gēngyín,
Lí Wéiyī, the King of Ānnán, submitted a memorial expressing gratitude for the bestowed sacrifice and the grace of succession to his title,
and presented tribute.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Wànzhōu and fourteen other prefectures and counties in Guǎngdōng,
and for drought disasters in Táiwān and three other counties in Fújiàn.
On the day Rényín,
grain from granaries was loaned to soldiers and others affected by drought and frost in Hēilóngjiāng.
Relief was provided for drought disasters in Qǔwò and eleven other prefectures in Shānxī.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
relief was provided for drought disasters in Tiānjīn and two other counties in Zhílì.
On the day Dīngwèi,
relief was provided for drought disasters in Shòuzhōu and nine other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Ānhuī.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
three-tenths of the additional taxes for the areas passed through during the tomb visit were exempted.
In the twelfth month, on the *gēngxū* day, the new moon,
relief was provided for the drought in Wúchuān County, Guǎngdōng.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Shǐ Yízhí was appointed to assist as a Grand Secretary.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
relief was provided for the drought in Líng County and twelve other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Shāndōng.
Duānhuì Huáng Tàizǐ was interred in the mausoleum at Zhūhuáshān.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Grand Secretary Fúmǐn requested retirement.
A warm imperial edict was issued to persuade him to stay.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Zǔngé'ěr envoys, including Tú'ěrdū, arrived in the capital,
expressing gratitude for allowing the Tibetans to travel via the Gásī road,
and for the imperial favor of providing livestock assistance,
and presenting local products as tribute.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
regarding Chén Déhuá's secret memorial concealing the defense of his younger brother, Shǎnxī Surveillance Commissioner Chén Dézhèng, in a corruption case,
it was submitted to the Board for strict deliberation.
Dézhèng was stripped of his office and subjected to interrogation.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
in response to an anomalous celestial phenomenon as a warning,
an imperial edict was issued to encourage self-reflection and reform.
In the ninth year, spring, the first month, on the *xīnsì* day,
due to Xú Běn's illness,
Shǐ Yízhí was appointed as a Grand Secretary.
Liú Yúyì was appointed as Minister of Personnel and Assistant Grand Secretary,
and Zhāng Kǎi as Minister of Revenue.
Chén Déhuá was dismissed,
and Wáng Ānguó was appointed as Minister of War.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Emperor visited Yíngtái.
Presiding from the grand tent,
a banquet was bestowed upon the Zǔngé'ěr envoy Tú'ěrdū,
and he was ordered to sit at the end of the first row of ministers.
Given Gá'ěrdāncèlǐng's obedience and reverence,
and Tú'ěrdū's sincerity and commendable respect,
Tú'ěrdū was summoned forward,
granted three cups of wine,
and given additional rewards.
Instructions were issued to all provinces, prefectures, and counties to implement both education and care.
On the *dīnghài* day,
relief was provided for the disaster in Tiānjīn and eleven other prefectures and counties in Zhílì.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Wáng Ānguó was relieved of his duties due to mourning,
and Péng Wéixīn was appointed as Minister of War.
Xǔ Róng was appointed acting Governor of Húběi.
Shǐ Yízhí was appointed Wényuāngé Grand Secretary.
Cháoxiǎn presented tribute.
Nèqīn was issued the seal for the Imperial Commissioner.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor escorted the Empress Dowager to Tàilíng.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Emperor visited Tàilíng.
On this day,
the Empress Dowager's imperial carriage returned.
In the second month,
the Emperor escorted the Empress Dowager to Nányuàn.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
based on the memorial from Censor Chén Dàjiè and others,
the appointment of Xǔ Róng as acting Governor of Húběi was rescinded,
Yàn Sīshèng was retained in his post,
and censors were further warned to collectively censure.
The previous year's land tax quota for Tóngchéng and eight other prefectures and counties in Ānhuī, affected by floods, was remitted.
The land tax quota for Táiwān and two other counties in Fújiàn, affected by drought, was remitted,
and relief was also provided.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Chén Déhuá was demoted.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
relief was provided for the floods in Zhān and Yì, two prefectures and counties in Yúnnán.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Minister of Revenue Zhāng Kǎi passed away.
Ā'ěrsài was appointed to succeed him,
and Èmǐdá was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng.
In the third month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
Wāng Yóudūn was appointed Minister of Works.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the land tax quota for Pèixiàn in Jiāngsū, Zhōngmóu in Hénán, and four other counties, affected by drought, was remitted.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Bódì was transferred to be General of Xī'ān.
Bālíng'ā was appointed General of Nínggǔtǎ.
On the *yǐsì* day,
relief was provided for the drought in Dézhōu and four other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Shāndōng.
Regarding Nèqīn's memorial reporting on the dilapidation of military encampments in Hénán and Jiāngnán,
the Emperor said:
"It is clear that not a single high official in the outer provinces is not deceiving Us.
We must punish one to warn a hundred."
In the fourth month, on the *wùshēn* day, the new moon,
the Altar to the First Silkworm was completed.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor proceeded to the Yuánqiú to perform the great rain-praying ceremony,
and specifically issued an edict to reduce the grandeur of the rituals
to demonstrate pious prayer.
Due to the drought, an order was given to lighten punishments and relax prohibitions.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
relief was provided for the drought in Dépíng and seven other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Throughout this spring,
rainfall has been scarce.
The Empress Dowager, due to the prolonged drought,
showed anxiety in her expression,
and today walked from her sleeping quarters to the Dragon God Temple in the garden to pray devoutly.
We were filled with trepidation,
and immediately went to inquire about her health,
earnestly expressed our apologies,
and specifically inform all civil and military officials, both inside and outside the capital, of this."
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the sacrifice to Earth was performed at Fāngzé,
without using the imperial sedan,
and without setting up imperial paraphernalia.
On the *gēngyín* day,
it rained.
On the *rényín* day,
the Grand Secretaries and Nine Ministers deliberated on Censor Chái Cháoshēng's request to repair the water conservancy in Zhílì,
and ordered Assistant Grand Secretary Liú Yúyì to go to Bǎodìng to consult with Gāo Bīn and make plans.
In the sixth month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
Grand Secretary Xú Běn requested retirement due to illness,
which was granted.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
relief was provided for the drought in Lìchéng and thirty-one other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng,
and for hail damage in Lánshān and five other prefectures and counties.
Autumn, seventh month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day, the new moon,
an edict was issued that the collection of new and old land taxes for the current year would be suspended
in Tiānjīn and fifteen other prefectures and counties in Zhílì heavily affected by disaster.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
arrears from the thirteenth year of Yōngzhèng in Jiāngsū and Ānhuī were remitted.
On the *rénchén* day,
É'ěrtú was dismissed for incompetence,
and Dálèdǎng'ā was appointed General of Fèngtiān.
Eighth month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
aid was provided for the floods in Shèxiàn and nineteen other prefectures and counties in Ānhuī.
On the *wùshēn* day,
arrears from the thirteenth year of Yōngzhèng in Huái'ān, Jiāngsū, and Fèngyáng, Ānhuī, two prefectures, were remitted.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
relief was provided for the floods in Chéngdū and other prefectures and counties in Sìchuān.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the retired Grand Secretary Xú Běn returned to his hometown.
The Emperor bestowed a poem to honor his departure,
gave additional rewards,
and further stated that on the day of the imperial tour to Nányuàn,
he would personally visit and offer comfort.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the previous year's arrears for Tiānjīn and thirty other prefectures and counties in Zhílì were remitted.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Emperor escorted the Empress Dowager to Nányuàn,
and the Emperor went hunting.
On the *jǐhài* day in the ninth month, which was the first day of the lunar month,
due to Hànlínyuàn editor Huáng Tǐmíng's presentation of his lecture notes,
which touched upon the excessive strictness of searches,
and implicitly contained satire,
the appropriate department was ordered to strictly deliberate his dismissal from office.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the current year's *é fù* (fixed tax quota) for hailstorm-stricken Qīngshuǐhé (清水河) in Shānxī (山西) was remitted.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
drought relief was provided to Bóxīng (博興) and other counties in Shāndōng (山東).
On the *dīngwèi* day,
it was decided to change the upcoming year's metropolitan examination (*huìshì*) to be held in the third month.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
as Chén Shìguān's (陳世倌) leave had expired,
he was ordered to enter the Grand Secretariat (*génèi*) to handle affairs.
Flood relief was provided to Wénshuǐ (文水) and other counties in Shānxī.
On the *gēngxū* day,
because Jiǎng Wèi (蔣蔚), the Education Commissioner (*xuézhèng*) of Sìchuān (四川), had diligently instructed scholars,
he was ordered to remain in office.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, visited Tāngshān (湯山).
There was a locust plague in Jiāngnán (江南), Hénán (河南), and Shāndōng.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Emperor visited Pánshān (盤山).
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, returned to the palace.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the reconstruction of the Hànlínyuàn was completed.
The Emperor visited the Hànlínyuàn and bestowed a banquet,
where he assigned rhymes for composing poems.
He then personally composed the opening line of a *Bǎiliángtǐ* (柏梁體) poem,
and the assembled officials continued it in sequence.
Grand Secretaries È'ěrtài (鄂爾泰) and Zhāng Tíngyù (張廷yù), who were in charge of the Hànlínyuàn, were bestowed with imperial calligraphic plaques,
and other Hànlín (翰林) and Zhànshì (詹事) officials received calligraphic works and silks, varying by rank.
On the same day,
he visited the examination hall (*gòngyuàn*),
and bestowed imperial calligraphic couplet plaques.
He then visited the Zǐwēidiàn (紫微殿) and the Guānxiàngtái (觀象臺).
Relief was provided for floods, insect plagues, hailstorms, and other disasters in Bǎodìng (保定) and eighteen other prefectures and counties in Zhílì (直隸).
Relief was provided for tidal disasters in Jìngjiāng (靖江) and twelve other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Jiāngsū (江蘇),
and for floods in Shèxiàn (歙縣) and twenty-one other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Ānhuī (安徽).
On the *gēngchén* day,
Sūn Jiāgàn (孫嘉淦) was reinstated as the Administrator (*fǔchéng*) of the Zōngrénfǔ (宗人府).
On the *xīnsì* day,
the land tax for land washed away by floods in Zhuōzhōu (涿州) and three other prefectures and counties in Zhílì was remitted.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Mǎ Shìlóng (馬世龍), the General-in-Chief (*zǒngbīng*) of Dēngzhōu (登州) Garrison in Shāndōng, was
found guilty of illegally levying on soldiers and sentenced to strangulation.
Relief was provided for various hailstorm and flood disasters in Hézhōu (河州) and thirty-five other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Gānsù (甘肅).
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
because Jīn Déyīng (金德瑛), the Education Commissioner of Jiāngxī (江西), was fair in selecting scholars,
he was ordered to remain in office.
On the *jǐhài* day,
because Tóng Bǎoshǒu (佟保守), the Education Commissioner of Guìzhōu (貴州), was clean and uncorrupted in his official conduct,
he was ordered to remain in office.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
È'ěrtài reported on Liú Yúyì's (劉於義) memorial regarding the investigation of water conservancy in Zhílì,
and an allocation of 500,000 *liǎng* of silver was ordered for its construction.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the *é fù* for drought-stricken Rénhé (仁和) and thirty-one other prefectures and counties in Zhèjiāng (浙江) was remitted,
and relief was also provided.
On the *xīnhài* day,
flood relief was provided to Chéngdū (成都) and thirty other prefectures and counties.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
permission was granted for the Dzungar envoys, Hā Liǔ (哈柳) and others, to trade cattle, sheep, and other goods they brought with them in Sùzhōu (肅州).
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the current year's *é fù* for drought, hailstorms, and other disasters in Lìchéng (歷城) and thirty-two other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Shāndōng was remitted.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the current year's *é fù* for floods, droughts, insect plagues, and hailstorms in Bǎodìng and eleven other prefectures, counties, and sub-prefectures in Zhílì was remitted.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Léi Hóng (雷鋐) was awarded the supernumerary title of Yùdé (諭德),
and received a stipend.
On the *wùchén* day,
Zhāng Zhào (張照) went into mourning.
Wāng Yóudūn (汪由敦) was transferred to be Minister (*shàngshū*) of the Board of Punishments (*Xíngbù*),
and Zhào Hóng'ēn (趙弘恩) was made Minister of the Board of Works (*Gōngbù*).
The *é fù* for floods in Shèxiàn and twenty-one other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Ānhuī was remitted.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
due to fires in Mǐnxiàn (閩縣) and other counties in Fújiàn (福建),
an edict was issued reprimanding border officials for not strictly preparing for fires.
Luóbǔzàng Dānzěn (羅卜藏丹怎) was captured.
In the first month of spring in the tenth year, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Grand Secretaries and Hànlín (翰lín) officials of the inner court were summoned to the Chónghuá Gōng (重華宮) to compose linked verses.
The metropolitan examination (*huìshì*) was changed to the third month,
and this was established as a rule.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Grand Secretary È'ěrtài requested to resign due to illness,
but an imperial edict graciously comforted and retained him.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Dzungars sent an envoy, Hā Liǔ, to present local products as tribute.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Gāo Bīn (高斌) was summoned to the capital,
and Liú Yúyì was appointed acting Governor-General (*zǒngdū*) of Zhílì.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
relief was provided for the previous year's floods in Chún'ān (淳安) and four other counties in Zhèjiāng.
Cháoxiān (朝鮮) presented tribute.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the Emperor visited È'ěrtài's residence by the Nèiyòumén (內右門) straight corridor to inquire about his illness.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the Emperor visited the Zhāoxī Líng (昭西陵), Xiàolíng (孝陵), Xiàodōng Líng (孝東陵), and Jǐnglíng (景陵).
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the previous year's *é fù* for floods in Hǎiyáng (海陽) and two other counties in Guǎngdōng (廣東) was remitted.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the previous year's *é fù* for floods in Dāntú (丹徒) and ten other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Jiāngsū was remitted.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the *é fù* for the ninth year of Qiánlóng's (乾隆) drought in Bóxīng and two other counties in Shāndōng was remitted.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Gāo Bīn returned to his post as Governor-General of Zhílì.
On the *guǐyǒu* day in the third month, which was the first day of the lunar month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the palace examination (*diànshì*) was changed to the fourth month,
and this was established as a rule.
Flood relief was provided to Báiyánjǐng (白鹽井) in Yúnnán (雲南).
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Emperor visited È'ěrtài's residence to inquire about his illness.
On the *xīnsì* day,
È'ěrtài was promoted to Grand Mentor (*Tàifù*).
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Assistant Grand Secretary and Minister of the Board of Rites (*Lǐbù Shàngshū*) Sāntài (三泰) requested to retire,
which was granted.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Nèqīn (訥親) was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary.
Láibǎo (來保) was transferred to be Minister of the Board of Rites,
and Shèng'ān (盛安) was made Minister of the Board of Punishments.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the previous year's *é fù* for drought in Rénhé and thirty other prefectures and counties in Zhèjiāng was remitted.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
due to Mò Kāngwǔ's (莫康武) rebellion in Ānnán (安南),
which captured Tàiyuán (太原), Gāopíng (高平), and other places,
Nàsūtú (那蘇圖) and others were ordered to strictly guard the border passes.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Shǐ Yízhí (史貽直), Chén Shìguān, Láibǎo, and Gāo Bīn were promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent (*Tàizǐ Tàibǎo*).
Liú Yúyì, Zhāng Yǔnsuí (張允隨), and Zhāng Guǎngsì (張廣泗) were promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent (*Tàizǐ Shǎobǎo*).
In the fourth month of summer, on the *guǐmǎo* day, which was the first day of the lunar month,
560,000 *liǎng* of silver from the Jiāngnán treasury were allocated for dredging river channels.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the additional hearth tax (*zàokè*) levied due to drought in Hǎifēng (海豐) and two other counties in Shāndōng was remitted.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Grand Secretary È'ěrtài passed away.
The Emperor personally attended the mourning ceremony,
and suspended court for two days.
He ordered that, in accordance with the last will of Shìzōng (世宗),
he should be enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple (*Tàimiào*).
Nàsūtú was summoned to the capital.
Cèléng (策楞) was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng (兩廣).
Zhǔntài (準泰) was transferred to be Governor (*xúnfǔ*) of Guǎngdōng (廣東).
Wèi Dìngguó (魏定國) was made Governor of Ānhuī.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Jiǎng Pǔ (蔣溥) was summoned to the capital.
Yáng Xífú (楊錫紱) was made Governor of Húnán (湖南).
On the *rénxū* day,
coastal provinces were ordered to train their naval forces.
On the *guǐhài* day,
due to the drought, the Board of Punishments was ordered to clear up minor legal cases.
On the *wùchén* day,
the examination of tribute scholars (*gòngshì*) was conducted,
and an imperial edict stated that those who could deeply understand current political affairs and offer frank and strong remonstrances would be listened to.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Qìngfù (慶復) and Jìshān (紀山) reported on the suppression of the Zānduì (瞻對) barbarians.
In the fifth month, on the *rénshēn* day, which was the first day of the lunar month,
Qián Wéichéng (錢維城) and 333 others were bestowed with the *jìnshì jíyǐ chūshēn* (進士及第出身) degrees, varying by rank.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the reed tax for collapsed or submerged land in Sūzhōu (蘇州) and nine other prefectures in Jiāngsū was remitted.
The imperial composition "Exhortations to Scholars of the Imperial Academy" (*Yùzhì Tàixué Xùnshì Shìzǐ Wén*) was promulgated to all provincial academies,

to be proclaimed on the first and fifteenth days of each lunar month, along with Shìzǔ's (世祖) "Inscribed Stele" (*Wòbēiwén*), Shèngzǔ's (聖祖) "Amplified Instructions" (*Shèngyù Guǎngxùn*), and Shìzōng's (世宗) "Treatise on Factionalism" (*Péngdǎng Lùn*).
Nèqīn was appointed Grand Secretary of the Bǎohé Diàn (保和殿).
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Minister of the Board of Revenue (*Hùbù Shàngshū*) Ā'ěrsài (阿爾賽) was murdered by his domestic slave,
and the domestic slave was publicly executed by dismemberment.
Gāo Bīn was made Minister of the Board of Civil Office (*Lìbù Shàngshū*).
Nàsūtú was made Governor-General of Zhílì.
Gāo Bīn and Liú Yúyì were ordered to continue managing the Zhílì water conservancy and river affairs.
Liáng Shīzhèng (梁詩正) was made Minister of the Board of Revenue.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Liú Yúyì was ordered to concurrently manage the affairs of the Board of Revenue.
On the *dīngwèi* day of the sixth month,
a general remission of land and poll taxes was declared nationwide.
An imperial edict stated:
“I have ruled the realm
for ten years now.
In nurturing the populace,
I have personally practiced frugality,
lightened taxes and reduced corvée,
and diligently worked to maintain peace,
not daring to indulge in the slightest ease or idleness.
Now the empire is pacified,
the imperial treasury has a surplus,
and in maintaining prosperity and preserving peace,
nothing is more important than satisfying the people.
The wealth of the world
is only a fixed amount;
if it does not gather above,
it will disperse below.
My August Ancestor reigned for sixty-one years,
and edicts remitting taxes and bestowing复 (or复)
were continuously recorded in history,
once granting a universal remission of land and poll taxes.
My August Father issued decrees almost daily to reduce levies and lighten collections.
For example, in Gānsù province alone,
the regular tax was entirely remitted for over ten years.
I, with the intention of continuing their aspirations and fulfilling their deeds,
and having succeeded to an era of cumulative prosperity and widespread harmony,
desire to ensure that all corners of the sea and remote mountain areas
may partake in this great beneficence.
Therefore, I specially issue this edict,
that the land and poll taxes due for collection in the directly governed provinces in the *bǐngyín* year
shall be entirely remitted.”
On the *gēngxū* day,
the *hàoxiàn* (customary surcharge) was remitted for consecutive years of disaster-stricken areas in Fèngyáng and other prefectures and departments of Ānhuī.
Fùhéng, Vice Minister of the Board of Revenue, was ordered to serve in the Grand Council.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Censor Hètài requested the recall of the imperial decree for the general remission of land and poll taxes.
The Emperor rebuked him for his perverse absurdity,
and stripped him of his office.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Emperor went to Hēilóngtán to pray for rain.
On the *xīnwèi* day, the first day of the seventh month of autumn,
arrears of taxes were remitted for Níngxià and two other counties in Gānsù.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
due to drought in Wǎnpíng and sixty-three other departments, prefectures, and counties in the directly governed area,
collection of land and poll taxes was ordered to be suspended.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Gāo Bīn was ordered to continue concurrently serving as Governor-General of River Conservancy for Zhílì.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
relief was distributed for floods and hail disasters in Shòuzhōu and seventeen other departments, counties, and garrisons in Ānhuī.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, visited Duōlúnnuòěr.
Four-tenths of the allocated taxes for the passing prefectures and counties were remitted.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, resided at Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng.
Relief was distributed for flood disasters in Sùzhōu and other departments, counties, and garrisons in Ānhuī.
On the *guǐmǎo* day of the eighth month,
relief was distributed for flood disasters in Guǎndú and two other salt fields in Liǎnghuái.
Collection of allocated taxes was suspended for flood disasters in Hànchuān and seventeen other departments and counties in Húběi, and for hail disasters in Guānghuà and two other counties,
and relief was also distributed.
The Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, went on a hunting expedition to Mùlán.
On the *jiáchén* day,
the Emperor resided at Bōluóhétún.
A banquet was bestowed upon the Mongol princes and dukes of Qīnghǎi,
and gifts were also given.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the Emperor went hunting at Yǒng'ānmángkā.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the Emperor went hunting at Bìyǎkālā.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor went hunting at Wēndūlǐhuá.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the Emperor went hunting at É'ěrgǔn'guō.
A banquet was bestowed upon Mongol princes, *èfù*, *tàijí*, and others.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
the Emperor went hunting at Bù'ěrgásūtái.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the Emperor went hunting at Bāyàngōu.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor went hunting at Wūlǐyàsūtái.
A banquet was bestowed upon princes, ministers, Mongol princes, *èfù*, *tàijí*, and others.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the Emperor went hunting at Bìtúshè'ěr.
Relief was distributed for drought disasters in the prefecture of Xuānhuàfǔ in Zhílì.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Emperor went hunting at Ājígējiūhèluò.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the Emperor went hunting at Sēngjītú.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the Emperor went hunting at Yǒng'ānpài.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the Emperor went hunting at Yīngtúhèluò.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the Emperor went hunting at Sàdákètúkǒu.
On the *rénxū* day,
relief was distributed for flood disasters in Yíchéng and two other departments, counties, and garrisons in Húběi.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Emperor went hunting at Lǎotúbólèqí'ěr.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Emperor went hunting at Kù'ěrqílè.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
relief was distributed for drought disasters in Āndìng and two other counties in Gānsù, and Diànbái and two other counties in Guǎngdōng,
insect plagues in Hǎifēng,
and wind disasters in Nán'ào.
The Emperor resided at Duōlúnnuòěr.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
a banquet was bestowed upon princes, ministers, Mongol princes, *èfù*, *tàijí*, and others.
Relief was distributed for flood disasters in Qǔwò and twelve other departments and counties in Shānxī.
On the *gēngwǔ* day, the first day of the ninth month,
the Emperor went hunting at É'ěrtuō'ángsèqīn.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Emperor went hunting at Duōlúnébótú.
On the *rénshēn* day,
an envoy was sent to offer sacrifices at the Míng Tombs.
The Emperor went hunting at Gǔzhénuòěr.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Zhāng Yǔnsuí reported that the native chieftains of Měngmiǎn, such as Fèngtíngzhēng, were colluding with Mianmang,
and requested to replace native rule with appointed officials;
this was ordered to be deliberated in detail.
The Emperor went hunting at Tǎbēntuóluóhǎi.
On the *yǐhài* day,
relief was distributed for flood disasters in Yǒngchéng and five other counties in Hénán.
The Emperor went hunting at Zhámàkètú.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the Emperor went hunting at Èrhū.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
relief was distributed for drought disasters in Gùchéng and fifteen other departments, counties, and garrisons in Zhílì.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the Emperor resided at Xuānhuàfǔ.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Emperor reviewed the troops of Xuānhuàzhen.
On the *dīnghài* day,
relief was distributed for flood disasters in Jìníng and six other departments, counties, and garrisons in Shāndōng,
and drought disasters in Hǎifēng.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, returned to the capital, Jīngshī.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Èmǐdá was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng.
Relief was distributed for flood disasters at Miàowāncháng in Liǎnghuái.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
due to the general remission of land and poll taxes,
an order was issued to investigate the accumulated silver surplus in each province over the years,
to offset annual expenditures.
On the *wùxū* day,
Yǐn Jìshàn was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng.
An order was issued to repair the tomb of Míng Mǐndì.
Relief was distributed for disaster-stricken departments and counties in Huái, Xú, and Hǎi in Jiāngsū.
Qìngfù reported the pacification and taking control of Shàngzhānduì,
and the advance against Xiàzhānduì Bāngǔn,
capturing Jiāshèyā and other passes, as well as various stockades on the southern route.
Relief was distributed for flood disasters in Cháng'ān and six other counties in Shǎnxī.
On the *dīngwèi* day of the tenth month of winter,
the Gānshāndào in Gānsù was merged into Sùzhōudào.
On the *wùshēn* day,
relief was distributed for flood disasters in Shāngqiū and five other counties in Hénán.
On the *xīnhài* day,
one Han Right Vice Minister of the Court of Transmission was abolished.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
an order was issued to block the breach at Chénjiāpǔ.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
an order was issued to strictly investigate *guōfěi* (bandits) in Sìchuān.
Rèn Lánzhī, Minister of Rites, requested retirement,
which was granted.
On the *guǐhài* day,
grain transport taxes were remitted for Hǎizhōu and seven other departments and counties in Jiāngsū.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
silver for repairing houses was given to disaster victims in Jiāngnán.
Relief was distributed for flood disasters in Jiāngpǔ and twenty-one other departments, counties, and garrisons in Jiāngsū.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
relief was distributed for drought disasters in Xiāngyīn and three other counties in Húnán, and Hànchuān and twenty-one other departments, counties, and garrisons in Húběi.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
land taxes for water-damaged fields were exempted for Dāngyáng and two other departments and counties in Húběi.
In the eleventh month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
relief was granted for drought disasters in Xianghé and 47 other zhōu, tīng, and xiàn in Shùnzhí.
Relief was also granted for flood disasters in Xīngpíng and five other xiàn in Shǎnxī.
On the day Xīnwèi,
relief was granted for flood disasters in Téngxiàn and six other zhōu, xiàn, and wèi in Shāndōng.
On the day Rénshēn,
Wáng Ānguó was appointed as Minister of Rites (Lǐbù Shàngshū).
On the day Jiǎxū,
relief was granted for flood disasters in Miàowān and other salt fields in Liǎnghuái.
On the day Yǐhài,
Fù Qīng reported that the Dzungar (Zhǔngá'ěr) taisha (tàijí) Gá'ěrdān Cèlíng was engaging in hostilities with Ābùdū'ěrgālǐmù Hàn.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
relief was granted for drought, frost, and hail disasters in Dàtóng and 17 other zhōu and xiàn in Shānxī.
Yàn Sīshèng, the Governor of Húběi, requested to retire,
and Kāitài was appointed to replace him.
On the day Xīnsì,
relief was granted for drought disasters in Sī'ēn and other xiàn in Guǎngxī.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Dzungar taisha Gá'ěrdān Cèlíng passed away.
Orders were issued to prepare border defenses for the northwest and west routes.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
relief was granted for wind disasters in Hǎicuó and three other salt fields in Guǎngdōng.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the grain tax (cáoliáng) was remitted for areas affected by flood disasters in Sùzhōu and four other zhōu and xiàn in Ānhuī.
On the day Gēngyín,
the breach at Chénjiāpǔ was closed.
On the day Guǐsì,
relief was granted for drought disasters in areas belonging to Xuānhuà Fǔ and in Qìngyún Xiàn in Zhílì.
In the twelfth month, on the day Xīnhài,
Grand Secretary (Dàxuéshì) Fúmǐn requested to retire,
and his request was granted with a generous imperial edict,
and he was promoted to Grand Tutor (Tàifù).
On the day Rénzǐ,
Qìngfù was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wénhuá Hall,
but remained in his post as Governor-General of Chuānshǎn.
Gāo Bīn was ordered to assist the Grand Secretaries.
Relief was granted for drought disasters in Lǒngxī and other zhōu and xiàn in Shǎnxī.
Relief was granted for flood disasters in Bǎnpǔ and other salt fields in Huáiběi.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Assistant Grand Secretary (Xiéyàn Dàxuéshì) Gāo Bīn and Vice Minister (Shìláng) Jiǎng Pǔ were both ordered to serve in the Grand Council (Jūnjī Chù).
Annals, Volume 11, Gaozong Annals 2
In the eleventh year, spring, first month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
to commemorate the commencement of the new era (jìnián kāizhuì),
an order was issued to reduce punishments.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Qìngfù was ordered to advance and suppress Zhānduì,
to provide support for Lǐ Zhìcuì.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
relief was granted for famine in Tóngshān, Jiāngsū, and Sùzhōu, Ānhuī, and other zhōu and xiàn.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Cháoxiǎn (Korea) presented tribute.
Lǐ Zhìcuì attacked Língdá.
Bāngǔn's mother came to the camp to beg for her son's life,
and was allowed to return.
The emperor reprimanded him for missing an opportunity.
Qìngfù was instructed to lead the troops forward.
In the second month, on the day Wùxū,
relief was granted for famine in Dàtóng and eleven other zhōu and xiàn in Shānxī.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Assistant Ministers (Cānzàn Dàchén) Lābùdūn and Wūlè of the Northern Route military camp were summoned to the capital,
and Tǎ'ěrmǎshàn and Nǔdēng were appointed to replace them.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Emperor went to the Southern Park (Nányuàn) for a hunt.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the extra tax (éfù) for areas affected by floods in Xīnníng and other zhōu and xiàn in Guǎngdōng, and Hèqìng Fǔ in Yúnnán, was remitted.
On the day Xīnhài,
due to a solar eclipse on the first day of the third month,
an imperial edict was issued to practice self-reflection with sincerity.
It was decreed that in years when the Empress did not personally perform the silkworm rite, a consort would be sent to perform it instead.
On the day Bǐngchén,
the extra tax for areas affected by floods in Yǒngchéng and four other xiàn in Hénán was remitted.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Lěngzōngnài, a taisha from Xīzàng (Tibet), was sentenced to execution for unauthorized withdrawal of troops while attacking Zhānduì.
He was sentenced to execution.
An imperial edict pardoned him from death.
In the third month, on the day Jǐsì,
the extra tax for areas affected by floods in Yánshān and seven other zhōu and xiàn in Zhílì was remitted.
On the day Jiǎxū,
relief was granted for flood disasters in Báiyánjǐng, Yúnnán.
On the day Yǐhài,
the Dzungar taisha Cèwàngduō'ěrjǐ Nàmzhálè, being newly installed,
sent an envoy, Hālyǔ, to present local products,
and requested to dispatch personnel to Xīzàng to prepare tea.
On the day Wùyín,
Qìngfù arrived at Dǎjiànlú,
and impeached Lǐ Zhìcuì and others for having delayed the troops and overlooked the enemy (lǎoshī wánkòu),
requesting further deployment of government troops for suppression,
which was approved.
On the day Xīnsì,
Inner Grand Minister (Nèi Dàchén) Bāndì and others were dispatched to the Zhānduì military camp.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Hālyǔ and others were given a banquet.
They were granted an audience,
and their request to go to Xīzàng to prepare tea was granted,
and they were bestowed with ruyi scepters.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
an imperial edict was issued to the Dzungar taisha Cèwàngduō'ěrjǐ Nàmzhálè.
Alms were given to the late taisha Gá'ěrdān Cèlíng.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the extra tax for areas affected by last year's floods in Qiánjiāng and other zhōu and xiàn in Húběi was remitted.
Qìngfù reported that he had advanced and stationed at Língquè.
In the intercalary third month, on the first day Dīngyǒu,
Shǎnxī was ordered to repair the imperial tombs (Dàilíng mù).
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Bái Zhōngshān was summoned to the capital.
Gù Cóng was appointed acting Governor-General of River Affairs for Jiangnan,
and Gāo Bīn was temporarily in charge.
Liú Tǒngxūn was appointed acting Governor-General of Grain Transport (Cáoyùn Zǒngdūdū).
Relief was granted for famine in Xuānhuà Fǔ, Zhílì.
Relief was granted for flood, drought, hail, and frost disasters in Lǒngxī and eleven other zhōu and xiàn in Gānsù.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Wāng Yóudūn was appointed acting Censor-in-Chief (Zuǒ Dūyùshǐ).
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Censor-in-Chief Háng Yìlù retired,
and Ākèdūn was appointed to replace him.
Summer, fourth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
Bái Zhōngshān was dismissed from office
and sent to serve at the Southern River (Nánhé).
The Grand Council was warned against leaking confidential information.
È Chāng was appointed acting Governor of Guǎngxī.
On the day Dīnghài,
the extra tax for areas affected by floods in Xiāngyīn and four other xiàn in Húnán was remitted.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the extra tax for areas affected by floods in Xīnníng and three other zhōu and xiàn in Guǎngdōng was remitted.
In the fifth month, on the first day Bǐngshēn,
Shèng'ān was appointed Censor-in-Chief,
and Ākèdūn was appointed Minister of Punishments (Xíngbù Shàngshū).
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Gù Cóng was ordered to investigate the wasteful expenditures at the Southern River,
and Bái Zhōngshān was ordered to make restitution.
On the day Rén'yín,
the extra tax for last year's drought and frost disasters in Dàtóng and seventeen other zhōu and xiàn in Shānxī was remitted.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Qìngfù reported that he had attacked Zhānduì,
and the barbarian chieftain Bāngǔn would soon be captured.
Qìngfù was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent (Tàizǐ Tàibǎo).
On the day Wùshēn,
the extra tax for last year's drought disasters in Jìngyuǎn and two other xiàn in Gānsù was remitted.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
three tenths of the annual extra tax for Qìngyún Xiàn, Zhílì, was permanently abolished.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the Dalai Lama (Dálài Lǎmā) and others requested clemency for Bāngǔn,
which was not granted.
Fù Qīng was ordered to convey the report,
and was severely reprimanded.
In the sixth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
Qìngfù, Bāndì, and others jointly attacked Yālǔnírì Stronghold,
and captured it.
Bāngǔn committed suicide by self-immolation.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
because the native tribes (fān) from inside and outside Dǎjiànlú participated in the campaign effectively,
their tribute (gòngfù) was again remitted for two years.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
an earthquake occurred in the capital.
On the day Rénchén,
orders were issued to return Russian fugitives to Qiàkètú.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day Bǐngshēn,
Jiānàsūtú and Cèléng were granted the title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
Zhōu Xuéjiàn was granted the title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Gāo Bīn was ordered to Jiāngsū to inspect the Yellow River and Grand Canal projects.
Liú Yúyì was appointed acting Governor-General of Riverways for Zhílì.
On the day Rényín,
Liú Qí, the leader of the Dàchéng Jiào in Sìchuān, was executed by dismemberment in the marketplace
for fabricating seditious writings.
On the day Gēngxū,
Zhōu Xuéjiàn reported the arrest of over two thousand Catholics.
The Emperor, considering that this went against the intention of pacification,
pardoned them.
On the day Rénxū,
relief was provided to seven counties in Húběi, including Hànchuān, suffering from floods.
On the day Guǐhài,
regarding Zhāng Bǎotài of Yúnnán spreading a heterodox sect,
which had spread to several provinces,
an edict was issued to set a deadline for those who had been lured to surrender themselves.
Those who continued to maintain churches were to be arrested and punished.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Bālíng'ā, the General of Jílín, was summoned to the capital.
Ālántài was appointed to replace him.
Relief was provided to seven counties and camps in Zhílì, including Qìngyún, suffering from drought.
On the day Jǐsì,
Lǐ Zhìcuì, the Provincial Commander of Sìchuān, was dismissed
for deceit and embellishment in his report on the suppression of Zhānduì.
Flood taxes were remitted for banner lands in Guǎngníng and other areas.
On the day Xīnwèi,
relief was provided to four prefectures and counties in Húnán, including Yìyáng, suffering from floods.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
an additional award of silver for repairing houses was granted to flood victims in Jiāngsū and Ānhuī.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
relief was provided to eleven prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Shāndōng, including Jīnxiāng, suffering from floods.
On the day Gēngyín,
the Emperor presided over a banquet at Yíngtái,
for imperial princes and nobles.
Chóngyǎ Diàn was renamed Dūn Diàn.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the Emperor presided over a banquet at Yíngtái,
for Grand Secretaries, Nine Chief Ministers, Hanlin academics, and censors,
and publicly recited four seven-character regulated verses.
On the day Rénchén,
the people of Shàngháng County in Fújiàn, including Luó Rìguāng, incited a crowd to demand equal tenant rents, causing disturbances.
They were arrested and punished.
On the day Guǐsì,
the request of the King of Cháoxiǎn (Joseon) was granted,
to suspend the patrolling cavalry outposts (●niúshàoxùnbīng) established in Fèngtiān.
On the first day of the ninth month, Jiǎwǔ,
land taxes were remitted for accumulated sand and collapsed land in three counties in Zhèjiāng, including Guī'ān.
On the day Wùxū,
instructions were given to governors and viceroys to govern with sincerity.
Relief was provided to three prefectures and counties in Shāndōng, including Téngxiàn, and six camps in Liǎnghuái, including Bǎnpǔ, suffering from floods.
On the day Jǐhài,
Gāo Bīn was ordered to Fèngtiān to dredge river channels.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
this year's autumn executions were suspended.
Zhōu Xuéjiàn was appointed Governor-General of Riverways for Jiāngnán.
Chén Dàshòu was transferred to be Governor of Fújiàn,
and Ānníng was appointed acting Governor of Jiāngsū.
Regulations were established for Imperial Commissioners inspecting the military garrisons in various provinces.
Relief was provided to three prefectures and counties in Hénán, including Zhèngzhōu, suffering from floods.
On the day Rényín,
Nàqīn was ordered to concurrently manage the Board of Revenue.
Flood surtaxes were remitted for nine prefectures and counties in Gānsù, including Lǒngxī.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, set out for Tàilíng,
and also toured Wǔtái Shān.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Emperor visited Tàilíng.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Ālǐgǔn fell ill,
and Bāndì was appointed acting Governor of Shānxī.
On the day Gēngxū,
gifts were bestowed upon elders and common people in the Zhílì prefectures and counties that were passed through.
On the day Jiǎyín,
relief was provided to three prefectures and counties in Jiāngsū, including Fēngxiàn, suffering from hail disasters.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the Emperor halted at Wǔtái Shān to hunt tigers.
Considering the honest and simple customs of Shānxī,
an edict was issued to provincial officials to apply both teaching and nurturing,
so that the common people would revere and practice civility and deference.
On the day Bǐngchén,
three-tenths of the regular tax for Wǔtái County in Shānxī was remitted for the next year.
On the day Dīngsì,
Mǎěrtài was summoned to the capital.
Kāěrjīshàn was appointed Governor-General of Mǐnzhè.
Sàiléng'é was transferred to be Governor of Shāndōng,
Chén Hóngmóu to be Governor of Jiāngxī,
and Xú Qǐ to be Governor of Shǎnxī.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, returned.
On the day Rénxū,
Èmídá was summoned to the capital.
Sàiléng'é was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng.
Ālǐgǔn was transferred to be Governor of Shāndōng,
and Àibìdá to be Governor of Shānxī.
Relief was provided to twenty-six prefectures and counties in Hénán, including Yānlíng, suffering from floods.
In the tenth month of winter, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
relief was provided to twenty-two prefectures and counties in Shānxī, including Yángqǔ, suffering from floods and hail.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the Emperor inspected the Hútú Hé dikes.
Relief was provided to nine prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Húběi, including Hànchuān, suffering from floods.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, halted at Bǎodìng Fǔ.
On the day Réngshēn,
the Emperor reviewed the troops,
and bestowed varying amounts of silver and silk.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Zhāng Guǎngsì was given an award
for apprehending the rebels Wèi Wángshì and Liú Qí.
It was decided to add the title of Military Preparedness Commissioner to the Guīsuī Circuit in Shānxī,
to supervise the Jìngyuǎn camp.
On the day Wùyín,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, returned to the capital.
Kāitài was transferred to be Governor of Jiāngxī,
and Chén Hóngmóu to be Governor of Húběi.
On the day Gēngchén,
Zhāng Tíngyù was exempted from leading in audiences,
and was further enjoined not to enter court early in the morning or to force himself to enter the palace.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Wāng Yóudūn was ordered to serve in the Grand Council.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Censor Wàn Niánmào was dismissed from office
for falsely impeaching Grand Secretary Chén Bāngyàn and others for flattering Fùhéng.
On the day Wùzǐ,
flood surtaxes were remitted for twenty-three prefectures and counties in Ānhuī, including Shòuzhōu.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
a special allocation of over two million two hundred thousand taels of silver and piculs of grain was made to disaster victims in the Huái, Yáng, Xú, and Hǎi prefectures of Jiāngsū.
In the eleventh month, on the day Guǐsì,
the order for selecting censors and compilers was rescinded.
Censor Lǐ Zhàoyù was handed over to the appropriate board for deliberation and punishment.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Wāng Shìhuáng, the Provincial Education Commissioner of Hénán, was dismissed from office
for partiality in examinations.
Flood surtaxes were remitted for twenty-four prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Jiāngsū, including Shānyáng,
and grain transport taxes were cancelled or delayed to varying degrees.
On the day Yǐsì,
land taxes were remitted for land crushed and damaged in two counties in Fèngtiān, including Jǐnxiàn.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
mourning silver was granted to the late Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, Zhāng Ruò'ǎi,
and Zhāng Tíngyù was enjoined to moderate his grief and take care of himself.
On the day Xīnhài,
Lǐ Zhìcuì was sent to serve at the front.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Qìngfù reported that the Tǔsī (local chieftain) Shāluóbēn of Dàjīnchuān was harassing Xiǎojīnchuān.
He stated that if Shāluóbēn did not comply with the judgment,
the only way to achieve success would be to use aboriginal forces.
The Emperor approved of this.
In the twelfth month, on the day Guǐhài,
Bāndì was summoned to the capital.
Táo Zhèngzhōng was appointed acting Governor of Shānxī.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
relief was provided to seven prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Húběi, including Qiánjiāng, suffering from floods.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
regarding Fù Qīng's report that the Lama Suīběng of Dálài Lǎma's tea-viewing monastery was suppressing Prince Quánluónài (Pholhanas),
an imperial handwritten letter was bestowed to comfort and reconcile them,
and an edict was issued to work together with Dálài Lǎma
to ensure local security.
On the day Wùchén,
Húbǎo was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Hāmì garrison.
On the day Jiǎxū,
insect disaster surtaxes were remitted for Jìnghǎi in Zhílì,
and relief was also provided.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
due to Zhāng Tíngyù's old age,
his son, the Shùjíshì (compiler) Zhāng Ruòchéng, was ordered to serve in the Southern Study,
to provide support.
On the day Wùyín,
relief was provided to prefectures and counties in Gānsù, including Āndìng, suffering from drought.
Flood surtaxes were remitted for eight prefectures and counties in Shāndōng, including Jīnxiāng.
On the day Gēngchén,
land taxes were remitted for flood-damaged land in Yǒngfú, Guǎngxī.
On the day Guǐwèi,
the Zūnggáěr Tàijí Cèwàngduōěrdì Nàmzhálè sent envoys, including Mǎmùtè, to appear at court.
They were granted an audience at Tàihé Zhāi.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
relief was provided to banners in Sūnítè, Ābāgá, and other areas suffering from disasters.
Chén Dàshòu reported that
the Sūlù (Sulu) state had sent aboriginal officials carrying two memorial forms of gratitude, one in aboriginal script and one in Chinese characters,
which did not conform to precedent.
This was rejected,
but the aboriginal officials were still generously provided for and ordered to return to their country.
The Emperor praised this as appropriate.
In the first month of spring of the twelfth year, on the day Rénhén,
Yùbǎo was ordered to handle the Zūnggáěr envoy's affairs for their trip to Zàng (Tibet).
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
three-tenths of the regular tax in kind was remitted for six prefectures and eight states in Shānxī, including Tàiyuán, and Guīhuà Chéng.
The two prefectures of Dàtóng and Shuòpíng were entirely remitted.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Mǎmùtè was granted a banquet at Fēngzé Yuán.
On the day Wùxū,
old arrears were remitted for the people's kilns in three prefectures and counties in Jiāngsū, including Hǎizhōu, and six camps including Bǎnpǔ.
On the day Dīngwèi,
relief was provided to thirteen prefectures and counties in Shāndōng, including Shòuguāng, suffering from famine.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
an imperial edict was granted to the Zūnggáěr Tàijí Cèwàngduōěrdì Nàmzhálè,
allowing his dispatched Tibetan prayer-reciters to winter and trade in Hājíěrdé Bùtèěrqù (Khajirdebter).
On the *xīnyǒu* day of the second month, the first day of the lunar month,
taxes in kind for the previous year's drought disaster in Jílín were remitted.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the Emperor paid respects at Zhāoxīlíng, Xiàolíng, Xiàodōnglíng, and Jǐnglíng.
Jì Shān reported that the *tǔsī* of Dàjīnchuān had encroached upon the *tǔsī* of Géshíbùzhá,
and had deceitfully seized the seal of Zéwàng, the *tǔsī* of Xiǎojīnchuān.
An edict was issued to order the repair of defenses,
and to avoid rash actions.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the Emperor visited Pán Shān.
On the *gēngchén* day,
relief was provided for the famine in Lánshān, Shāndōng.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the assessed tax for land in Méngxiàn, Hénán, that had been washed away was remitted.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Dīng Zàobǎo, former Minister of the Imperial Household Department, reached the age of one hundred,
and was granted an imperial calligraphy plaque, court robes, and colored silks.
Assessed taxes for the previous year's flood disaster in Zǎoyáng, Húběi, were remitted.
In the third month,
assessed taxes for the previous year's flood disaster in Yángqǔ and one other county in Shānxī were remitted.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Qìngfù was summoned to join the Grand Council to handle affairs,
and Zhāng Guǎngsì was transferred to be the Governor-General of Chuān-Shǎn.
The post of Governor-General of Yún-Guì was re-established,
with Zhāng Yǔnsuí appointed to it.
Tú'ěrbǐng'ā was appointed Governor of Yúnnán,
and Sūn Shàowǔ as Governor of Guìzhōu.
Relief was provided for the flood disaster in Hénán.
Because the *tǔsī* of Dàjīnchuān had plundered the *tǔsī* of Géshíbùzhá and Míngzhèng,
and had disturbed military outposts,
Qìngfù was ordered to remain in Sìchuān,
and discuss with Zhāng Guǎngsì a plan for advance and suppression.
Zhāng Guǎngsì was also instructed to pacify and control the various tribes of Guōluōkè, Qǔqǔwū, Zhānduì, and Bātáng.
Assessed taxes for the previous year's flood disaster in Huái'ān and three other prefectures and departments in Jiāngsū were remitted.
Grand Secretary Zhā Láng'ā requested to retire,
and his request was granted.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Prince (Jùnwáng) of Xīzàng, Pōluónài, died,
and Zhū'ěrmòtènámzhále inherited the title of Prince (Jùnwáng).
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Gāo Bīn was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wényuāngé,
and Lái Bǎo as Minister of Personnel.
Hǎi Wàng was transferred to be Minister of Rites,
and Fù Héng as Minister of Revenue.
Suǒ Bài was ordered to be stationed in Xīzàng,
to assist Fù Qīng in handling affairs.
Assessed taxes for the previous year's flood disaster in Shòuzhōu and twenty-two other departments, counties, and military garrisons in Ānhuī were remitted.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Deputy Commander-in-Chief Luó Shān was ordered to manage the military post of Ā'ěrtài with his original rank,
and also to discuss affairs concerning the horse ranches of Shāngdōu and Dábsùnnuò'ěr.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Zhāng Guǎngsì was ordered to advance and suppress Shāluóbēn, the *tǔsī* of Dàjīnchuān.
Bǎo Dé, Adviser to the Western Route Army Camp, whose term had expired,
was replaced by Nàlántài.
On the *gēngxū* day,
assessed taxes for the previous year's flood disaster in Jìzhōu and thirteen other prefectures, counties, and departments in Zhílì were remitted.
On the *wùchén* day,
Gāo Bīn was ordered to Jiāngnán to join Zhōu Xuéjiàn in inspecting river works,
and to clear up accumulated abuses in money and grain.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Nà Sūtú was provisionally appointed Governor-General of Riverways for Zhílì.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Nè Qīn was given the seal of Imperial Commissioner,
and ordered to Shānxī to join Ài Bìdá in reviewing the case of crowd gathering in Ānyì and one other county.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Yǎ'ěrtú was recalled to the capital.
On the *xīnmǎo* day of the fifth month,
Zhǔntài was summoned to the capital,
and Cèléng was concurrently appointed Governor of Guǎngdōng.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
relief was provided for the famine in Ānqiū and one other county in Shāndōng.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
sacrifices were offered to the Earth at Fāngzé,
and the imperial insignia was withheld due to drought.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Ministry of Justice was ordered to clear up general prisons,
and to reduce sentences below penal servitude.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor visited Hēilóngtán to pray for rain.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Ài Bìdá was dismissed,
and Zhǔntài was transferred to be Governor of Shānxī.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
because of repeated cases of coercion of officials in Fújiàn, Shāndōng, Jiāngnán, Guǎngdōng, and Shānxī,
an edict stated:
"When stubborn commoners gather crowds
and violate criminal laws,
We cannot but take it as Our own fault.
Let the various governors-general and governors earnestly guide and educate,
so that ignorant people know to respect and revere officials,
and obey orders."
On the *gēngshēn* day of the sixth month, the first day of the lunar month,
an edict stated that in the coming spring, the Empress Dowager's imperial carriage would make an eastern tour,
and personally offer sacrifices at Kǒnglín,
and ordered all government offices to prepare accordingly.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Governor of Guìzhōu was ordered to command the military affairs of the entire province.
Huò Bèi was dismissed from office for failing to investigate and impeach officials for embezzlement,
and sent to the military frontier post for service.
On the *rénshēn* day,
relief was provided for the famine in Yìdōu and six other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Zéwàng, the *tǔsī* of Xiǎojīnchuān, led his followers to surrender,
and also returned the three fortified villages of Wōrì.
Government troops advanced to suppress Dàjīnchuān,
attacking the fortified villages of Máoniú and Mǎsāng, etc.,
and captured them.
Qìngfù was recalled to the capital.
On the *jǐchǒu* day of the seventh month of autumn, the first day of the lunar month,
relief and aid were provided for the various water and hail disasters in Lìchéng and nineteen other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Shāndōng.
Gāo Bīn and others were ordered to dredge the Liùtáng and other rivers in Jiāngsū.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Nàyántài was ordered to provide relief for the drought disaster in the six banners of Sūnítè, etc.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Liú Yúyì's concurrent management of the Ministry of Revenue was suspended,
and Nè Qīn was appointed in his place.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
relief was provided for the water, drought, and hail disasters in Gù'ān and seventy-four other departments, prefectures, and counties in Shùnzhílì.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the Emperor, with the Empress Dowager, visited the Mountain Resort.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Zhāng Guǎngsì advanced to and stationed in Měinuò village of Xiǎojīnchuān,
divided his forces to attack and suppress,
and accepted the surrender of Xiǎojīnchuān.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor and the Empress Dowager stayed at the Mountain Resort.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
relief was provided for the salt-producing households affected by drought disaster in Chánglú, Yǒnglì, and one other salt field.
On the *xīnyǒu* day of the eighth month,
the Emperor and the Empress Dowager visited Mùlán for the autumn hunt.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
relief was provided for the salt-producing households in Chánglú and Hǎifēng, and one other county.
On the *wùchén* day,
the Emperor hunted at Wēndū'ěrhūa.
A banquet was granted to the Mongol princes, dukes, and *tàijí*.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
rice was purchased from Bāgōu and other places in Rèhé,
to provide relief for the drought disaster in the six banners of Sūnítè.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
relief was provided for the tidal disaster in Sūzhōu, Sōngjiāng, and other prefectures in Jiāngsū.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
silver was ordered to be distributed as relief to the six banners of Sūnítè,
all to be taken from the imperial treasury,
without deducting the stipends of princes and *bèilè*.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Qìngfù reported on the attack on Guā'ěryá,
and consecutive battles resulted in victories.
An edict stated:
"How can minor victories in breaking down fortifications and capturing villages
console Us?"
On the *rénwǔ* day,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Shòuchāng and two other counties in Zhèjiāng.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Bàzhōu and fourteen other prefectures, counties, and departments in Shùnzhílì.
Relief was provided for the flood disaster in Lěiyáng and eight other counties in Húnán, Cháoyì in Shǎnxī, and Shùndé and two other counties in Guǎngdōng.
On the *wùzǐ* day of the ninth month, the first day of the lunar month,
three-tenths of the assessed taxes in passing areas were remitted.
Relief was provided for the drought disaster in Fúqiāng and nine other counties in Gānsù, and Ānníng and two other prefectures and counties in Yúnnán.
The Emperor, with the Empress Dowager, returned to stay at the Mountain Resort.
On the *guǐsì* day,
due to the tidal disaster in Chóngmíng, Jiāngsū,
which drowned over 12,000 people,
the assessed taxes for the following year were remitted,
and relief was still provided.
On the *yǐsì* day,

relief was provided for the flood disaster in Shèxiàn and seven other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Ānhuī, Tōngxǔ and twenty-six other prefectures and counties in Hénán, and Qíhé and eighty-six other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the Emperor, with the Empress Dowager, returned.
On the *yǐsì* day,
one hundred thousand *shí* of grain from Fèngtiān were allocated to provide relief for Shāndōng.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the retired Grand Secretary Zhā Láng'ā died.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an edict ordered Jiāngsū to investigate accumulated arrears,
and because Chén Wéixīn and Secretary Chén Déhuá had evaded responsibility,
both were dismissed from office.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Xǔzhōu, Hénán.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Gù Cóng was appointed Governor of Zhèjiāng,
and Yùn Zhù as Governor-General of Grain Transport.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Lǚtián and nineteen other salt fields of Liǎnghuái.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Chén Dàshòu was appointed Minister of War,
Pān Sīqǔ was transferred to be Governor of Fújiàn,
and Nà Mǐn was appointed Governor of Ānhuī.
Winter, 10th month, Xīnyǒu (21st day).
Because Sūlù again dispatched foreign envoys to Fújiàn to repeatedly appeal regarding the incident where the Lǚsòng foreign leader plundered tribute envoys,
an edict stated:
“If island barbarians dispute among themselves,
they may be allowed to handle it themselves;
there is no need to show partiality.”
Yǐchǒu (25th day).
The Emperor, due to the Empress Dowager's illness,
went to Cíníng Gōng to inquire about her well-being and administer medicine.
On this day,
he stayed overnight at Cíníng Gōng.
He administered medicine three times daily,
and continued to do so until Xīnwèi (31st day).
Gēngwǔ (5th day).
Relief was distributed to the flood-stricken areas of Fùníng and twenty other zhōu, xiàn, and wèi in Jiāngsū.
Dīngchǒu (12th day).
The fixed tax for flood-affected areas in Jílín was remitted.
Wùyín (13th day).
Relief was distributed to the flood-stricken areas of Hǎiníng and eleven other xiàn in Zhèjiāng.
Jǐmǎo (14th day).
As Zhǔngá'ěr envoys were going to Tibet to boil tea,
and Zǎisāng Bāyǎsīhúláng and others arrived at Débùtè'ěr for trade,
Qìngfù was recalled to the capital.
Rénwǔ (27th day).
Relief was distributed to the tide-stricken areas of Chángshú and nineteen other zhōu, xiàn, and wèi in Jiāngsū,
and to the drought-stricken areas of Shàngyuán and fifteen other zhōu, xiàn, and wèi.
Jiāngsū was ordered to again intercept 400,000 shí of next year's grain tribute for relief.
Guǐwèi (28th day).
Zhāng Guǎngsì was instructed not to accept Shāluóbēn's surrender.
11th month, Dīnghài (1st day)朔.
The Emperor went to the Empress Dowager to administer medicine,
three times daily,
and continued to do so until Jǐchǒu (3rd day).
Ālǐgǔn was summoned to the capital,
and Hèhèhù was appointed Governor of Shāndōng.
Guǐsì (7th day).
Relief was distributed to the famine-stricken areas of Shòuchāng and three other xiàn in Zhèjiāng,
and disaster-affected fixed taxes were exempted.
Jǐyǒu (13th day).
Èfù Cèlíng had an audience with the Emperor,
and Tǎ'ěrmǎshàn was temporarily appointed Acting Deputy General of Dìngbiān.
Gēngxū (14th day).
Relief was distributed to the disaster-stricken people of Chóngmíng and other xiàn in Jiāngsū, with different amounts.
Guǐchǒu (17th day).
Relief was distributed to the disaster-stricken people of Dōngpíng and other zhōu, xiàn, and wèi in Shāndōng.
Xīnyǒu (25th day).
Relief was distributed to the flood-stricken areas of Shèxiàn and other zhōu, xiàn, and wèi in Ānhuī.
Jǐsì (3rd day).
Xú Qǐ was summoned to the capital,
Chén Hóngmóu was transferred to be Governor of Shǎnxī,
and Péng Shùkuí was appointed Acting Governor of Húběi.
Relief was distributed to the flood-stricken areas of Qíhé and eighty-five other zhōu and xiàn in Shāndōng.
Xīnwèi (5th day).
The retired Grand Secretary Xú Běn passed away.
Yǐhài (9th day).
As Zhāng Guǎngsì was advancing to suppress Dàjīnchuān,
Huáng Tíngguì was appointed Acting Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù.
Relief was distributed to the flood-stricken areas of Tiānjīn and six other zhōu and xiàn in Zhílì.
Zhāng Guǎngsì reported that Shāluóbēn requested surrender,
and was told that this military campaign
would not cease until the enemy was annihilated.
The Emperor
encouraged him by saying,
“I have chosen the right person in you.”
Jǐmǎo (13th day).
As Grand Secretary Qìngfù, who was advancing to suppress Zhānduì,
falsely reported that Bāngǔn had self-immolated,
he was ordered to be stripped of his office and await punishment.
As Bāndì and Nú Sān both reported Bāngǔn's self-immolation,
they were dismissed from their duties as Imperial Guards.
Gēngchén (14th day).
Láibǎo was appointed Grand Secretary of Wǔyīng Diàn.
13th year, Spring, 1st month, Rénchén (7th day).
Relief was distributed to the flood-stricken areas of Fùníng and other xiàn in Jiāngsū, and Sùzhōu and five other zhōu and xiàn in Ānhuī.
Gēngzǐ (15th day).
Fùhéng was ordered to concurrently manage the affairs of the Minister of War.
Xīnchǒu (16th day).
Nàqīn was ordered to go to Zhèjiāng to jointly interrogate Governor Cháng'ān with Gāo Bīn.
Yǐsì (20th day).
Ākèdūn was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary,
and Fùhéng was appointed Assistant Minister for Imperial Tours and Cabinet Affairs.
Wùshēn (23rd day).
The Emperor arrived at Cáobātún.
Jiǎyín (29th day).
Grand Secretary Zhāng Tíngyù requested retirement,
but was kindly consoled and persuaded to stay,
and his concurrent management of the Ministry of Personnel was suspended,
with Láibǎo replacing him.
2nd month, Wùwǔ (4th day).
The Emperor embarked on an Eastern Tour,
leading the Empress Dowager and the Empress on the imperial carriage.
Guǐhài (9th day).
The Emperor resided at Zhàoběikǒu,
and accompanied the Empress Dowager to inspect the water conservancy project.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú presented tribute.
Jiǎzǐ (10th day).
Relief was distributed to the flood-stricken areas of Tiānjīn and fifteen other zhōu and xiàn in Zhílì.
Bǐngyín (12th day).
Cháng'ān was stripped of his office for corruptly accepting bribes.
Rénshēn (18th day).
Bandits formed a rebellion in Ōuníng, Fújiàn,
and General Liú Qǐzōng suppressed them.
Guǐyǒu (19th day).
An additional month of relief was given to the disaster-stricken zhōu and xiàn passed through in Shāndōng.
Qítōng'ā was dismissed as Commander of the Imperial Bodyguard,
and Ālǐgǔn replaced him.
Yǐhài (21st day).
Three-tenths of the fixed tax was remitted for the zhōu and xiàn passed through in Zhílì and Shāndōng.
Wùyín (24th day).
The Emperor resided at Qūfù Xiàn,
and remitted the fixed tax for the Yǐsì year for Qūfù, Tài'ān, and Lìchéng three xiàn in Shāndōng, where he resided.
Jǐmǎo (25th day).
The Emperor completed the ceremony of offerings to Confucius,
and visited the Kǒnglín.
He went to the mausoleum of Shàohào and the temple of Zhōugōng to offer sacrifices.
He ordered a yellow parasol with a curved handle to be left for the Dàchéng Diàn,
and bestowed a banquet upon Yǎnshèng Gōng Kǒng Zhāohuàn and the doctoral scholars.
Rénwǔ (28th day).
The Emperor resided at Tài'ān Fǔ.
Guǐwèi (29th day).
The Emperor offered sacrifices at Dàiyuè Miào,
and accompanied the Empress Dowager to ascend Dài.
In the third month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
sentences of surveillance pending review, suspended execution, military exile, and lesser crimes were reduced in Zhílì and Shāndōng.
On the day Dīnghài,
Bāndì was ordered to the Jīnchuān military camp to deliberate on military affairs.
Zhāng Guǎngsì and Bāndì were instructed to transfer Yuè Zhōngqí to the military camp,
to be employed as a Zǒngbīng.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Emperor arrived at Jǐnán Fǔ,
and visited Bāotū Quán.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, reviewed troops,
and paid respects at the Dì Shùn Temple.
On the day Gēngyín,
the Emperor inspected the city,
and visited Lìxià Tíng.
This year's grain tribute was exempted for five counties in Zhèjiāng, including Yúyáo, due to tidal disasters.
On the day Rénchén,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager and the Empress, returned to the capital.
On the day Guǐsì,
last year's taxed land quota was exempted for seven prefectures and counties in Ānhuī, including Shèxiàn, due to flooding.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the Emperor arrived in Dézhōu and boarded a boat.
The Empress passed away.
Zhūang Qīnwáng Yǔnlù and Hé Qīnwáng Hóngzhòu were ordered to escort the Empress Dowager back to the capital.
The Emperor stayed in Dézhōu.
Wányán Wěi was recalled to the capital.
Gù Cóng was appointed Hédōng Hédào Zǒngdūd.
Àibìdá was appointed Zhèjiāng Xúnfǔ.
Xiébàn Dàxuéshì and Lìbù Shàngshū Liú Yúyì passed away.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
The coffin of the deceased Empress arrived in the capital,
and was interred at Chángchūn Gōng.
The Emperor suspended court for nine days.
On the day Rényín,
