an earthquake occurred in twenty-three prefectures, counties, and departments in Sìchuān, including Chéngdū.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the Empress Dowager arrived in the capital,
and the Emperor welcomed her back to Shòukāng Gōng.
On the day Yǐsì,
the Emperor went to Chángchūn Gōng to offer sacrifices before the coffin of the deceased Empress.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Emperor personally conferred the posthumous title Xiàoxián Huánghòu upon the deceased Empress.
As the First Prince was unable to perform all mourning rites due to his age,
his tutors and supervisors (āndá) were penalized with differentiated salary deductions.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Emperor went to Chángchūn Gōng to perform the Yīndiàn ritual before the coffin of the deceased Empress.
Gāo Bīn and Liú Tǒngxūn were ordered to investigate disaster relief in Shāndōng.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
the coffin of the deceased Empress was moved to Guāndé Diàn.
The imperial edict regarding the deceased Empress was issued to all provinces.
Officials were dispatched with the edict to Cháoxiǎn, as well as Nèi Zhásàkè, Kā'ěrkā, Hāmì, Qīnghǎi, and other places.
On the day Xīnhài,
Àibìdá was transferred to be Guìzhōu Xúnfǔ.
Fāng Guānchéng was appointed Zhèjiāng Xúnfǔ.
On the day Dīngsì,
Fù Héng, Nàsūtú, Zhāng Guǎngsì, and Bāndì were promoted to Tàizǐ Tàibǎo.
Kā'ěrjīshàn was promoted to Tàizǐ Shàobǎo.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Zhùzàng Fù Dūtǒng Fù Qīng was recalled to the capital.
Lābùdùn was appointed in his place.
Zhèngbái Qí Lǐng Shìwèi Nèi Dàchén Yīlèshèn passed away.
Nàsūtú and Wàngzhále were appointed acting officials.
Láibǎo was relieved from concurrently serving as Lǐng Shìwèi Nèi Dàchén.
Fēng'ān was appointed in his place.
On the day Réngxū,
the Emperor went to Guāndé Diàn to offer sacrifices to the deceased Empress.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Nèqīn was ordered to manage military affairs in Sìchuān.
Xiébàn Dàxuéshì Ākèdūn was dismissed.
Fù Héng was appointed in his place,
and also concurrently managed the Lìbù Shàngshū.
Hādáhā was appointed acting Bīngbù Shàngshū.

Last year's taxed land quota was exempted for sixteen prefectures, counties, and guards in Jiāngsū, including Chángshú, due to tidal disasters, and for fourteen prefectures, counties, and guards, including Shàngyuán, due to drought disasters.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Liáng Shīzhèng was transferred to be Bīngbù Shàngshū.
Jiǎng Pǔ was appointed Hùbù Shàngshū.
Last year's taxed land quota was exempted for eighteen prefectures, counties, and guards in Jiāngsū, including Shānyáng, due to disasters.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Jūnjī Dàchén Jiǎng Pǔ was dismissed.
Chén Dàshòu was appointed in his place.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Chén Dàshòu was appointed Xiébàn Dàxuéshì.
Dálèdāng'ā was appointed Xíngbù Shàngshū.
On the day Yǐhài,
the former Chuānshǎn Zǒngdūd Yuè Zhōngqí was recalled to the Jīnchuān military camp,
and awarded the rank of Tídū.
Ālántài was transferred to be Shèngjīng Jiāngjūn.
Suǒbài was appointed Nínggǔtǎ Jiāngjūn.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Fù'ěrdān was recalled to be Nèi Dàchén,
and sent to the Jīnchuān military camp.
Additional relief was provided for drought disasters in two counties in Fújiàn, including Táiwān.
On the day Wùyín,
the First-Class Marquis Fù Wén was promoted to First-Class Duke.
On the day Gēngchén,

one Han position each for Qiān Dūyùshǐ of the Dūchá Yuàn, Yòu Tōngzhèng of the Tōngzhèng Sī, Shàōqīng of Dàlǐ Sì, Shào Zhānshì of Zhānshì Fǔ, Shàoqīng of Tàipú Sì, and Sīyè of Guózǐ Jiān were abolished.
One Man councilor position in the Tōngzhèng Sī was changed to Yòu.
The Man and Han Zuǒ Tōngzhèng were changed to Tōngzhèng Fùshǐ.
In the fifth month, on the first day Jiǎshēn,
two hundred and sixty-four individuals, including Liáng Guózhì, were granted the Jinshì Jídì and other degrees.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
last year's taxed land quota was exempted for thirty-two prefectures, counties, and departments in Zhílì, including Wén'ān, due to flooding.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Fù Héng was ordered to oversee the three treasuries of the Hùbù.
On the day Gēngyín,
Ākèdūn was sentenced to beheading.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Zhāng Guǎngsì reported a victory at Róngbùzhài.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
last year's taxed land quota was exempted for twenty-eight prefectures and counties in Hénán, including Tōngxǔ, due to flooding.
On the day Rényín,
last year's taxed land quota was exempted for seven prefectures, counties, and guards in Ānhuī, including Jīngdé, due to drought.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the Emperor went to Guāndé Diàn to formally confer the posthumous title Xiàoxián Huánghòu upon the deceased Empress,
and issued an imperial edict.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Ākèdūn was released from prison,
and ordered to serve as acting Gōngbù Shìláng.
On the day Wùshēn,
last year's taxed land quota was exempted for eight fields in Shāndōng, including Yǒnglì, due to flooding.
On the day Rénzǐ,
last year's taxed land quota was exempted for twelve prefectures and counties in Shānxī, including Yǒngjì, due to flooding and hail disasters.
In the sixth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
Lǐ Tǎn was stripped of his earldom for long-term absence from duties regarding ancestral sacrifices.
Banner officials were warned.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the Emperor personally tested officials of the Hànlín and Zhānshì academies,
promoting three officials, including Qí Zhàonán, to the first class,
with others promoted or demoted differentially.
The Emperor personally tested officials entering the Hànlín and Zhānshì academies from ministries and bureaus,
promoting Shào Zhānshì Shì Guì and marking him for promotion in Sìchuān.
On the day Guǐhài,
drought relief was provided for twenty-two prefectures and counties in Shǎnxī, including Yàozhōu.
On the day Wùchén,
Xiè Yìnglóng, the Diǎnshǐ of Wènchuān County in Sìchuān, stationed in Wòrì Tǔsī,
obstructed a general from moving camp.
The Emperor praised him,
and awarded him the rank of Zhōu Tóng.
On the day Jǐsì,
Zhào Huì was ordered to concurrently manage affairs of the Hùbù.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the Zuǒ Yòu Yì Fù Dūtǒng of Guīhuàchéng Tǔmòtè were abolished.
On the day Jiǎxū,
an edict was issued prohibiting court officials from requesting the establishment of a Crown Prince,
and the First Prince was reprimanded for showing no sorrow or reverence during the Empress's grand rites.
The Emperor went to Guāndé Diàn to offer wine before the coffin of Empress Xiàoxián,
and performed the hundred-day memorial ceremony.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day Guǐwèi,
the Empress Dowager issued an imperial decree:
"Xián Guìfēi Nàlā Shì will succeed the Queen Consort.
She will first be conferred the title of Huáng Guìfēi,
and temporarily manage the affairs of the Six Palaces."
On the day Dīnghài,
last year's taxed land quota was exempted for two counties in Fújiàn, including Chánglè, due to drought.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Nèqīn and others were instructed to promptly report strategies for advancing troops.
On the day Réchén,
silver for seeds was lent to farmers in Shāndōng.
Last year's taxed land quota was exempted for Sùqiān in Jiāngsū due to flooding.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Gāo Bīn was ordered to meet Zhōu Xuéjiàn to inspect matters concerning river and lake dredging.
On the day Yǐwèi,
as five counties in Shānxī, including Yǒngjì, suffered from poor harvests,
they were provided with relief.
On the day Wùxū,
Dépèi was dismissed.
Dálèdāng'ā was transferred to be Lìbù Shàngshū.
Shèng'ān was appointed Xíngbù Shàngshū.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
drought relief was provided for twenty-nine prefectures and counties in Zhílì, including Qīngxiàn.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Ālǐgùn requested a reduction in punishment for starving people who committed plunder.
The Emperor issued an edict reprimanding this as lenient and nurturing wickedness,
and disallowed it.
Relief was provided for water and hail disasters in twenty-nine prefectures and counties in Shāndōng, including Lìchéng.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Cháng'ān was sentenced to strangulation.
On the *guǐchǒu* day, the first day of the intercalary seventh month,
Àkèdūn was appointed acting Minister of Personnel (Xíngbù Shàngshū),
and Dètōng was made Censor-in-Chief of the Left (Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ).
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the annual land tax (éfù) was remitted for Bázhōu and Gù'ān in Zhílì due to flood disaster.
Relief was provided for flood victims in Yìyáng and eight other prefectures and counties in Húnán.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Péng Shùkuí was appointed Governor of Húběi (Húběi Xúnfǔ).
On the *wùchén* day,
Zhōu Xuéjiàn was arrested and imprisoned
for unauthorized shaving of his head, in violation of regulations.
Gāo Bīn was ordered to manage the Southern River (Nánhé Zǒngdū) affairs.
Yǐn Jìshàn was stripped of his office but retained in his post
for favoritism.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Emperor visited Pánshān.
Xīnzhù was appointed acting Governor-General of Húguǎng (Húguǎng Zǒngdū).
Ānníng was summoned to the capital.
Yǐn Jìshàn was ordered to concurrently manage the duties of Governor of Jiāngsū (Jiāngsū Xúnfǔ).
Sǒubài, the General of Nínggǔtǎ, was transferred to be the Grand Commandant of Gǔběikǒu (Gǔběikǒu Tídū).
Yǒngxìng replaced him.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
an edict reprimanded Nàqīn for his indecisive recommendations regarding the campaign in Jīnchuān,
and also admonished Fùěrdān, Yuè Zhōngqí, and Bāndì.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the Emperor resided at Pánshān.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Zhǔntài was transferred to be Governor of Shānxī (Shānxī Xúnfǔ),
Ālǐgǔn to be Governor of Shāndōng (Shāndōng Xúnfǔ),
Èchāng to be Governor of Jiāngsū (Jiāngsū Xúnfǔ),
and Shūlù to be Governor of Guǎngxī (Guǎngxī Xúnfǔ).
Sèléng'é was arrested and imprisoned
for unauthorized shaving of his head, in violation of regulations.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Kūnyáng and other prefectures and counties in Yúnnán.
On the *wùyín* day,
Ālǐgǔn was summoned to the capital.
Táng Suíxǔ was appointed acting Governor of Shāndōng (Shāndōng Xúnfǔ).
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the annual land tax (éfù) was remitted for Yuánhé and ten other counties in Jiāngsū for the current year due to hail disaster.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the *jiǎshēn* day of the eighth month,
Bāndì was appointed acting Governor of Sìchuān (Sìchuān Xúnfǔ).
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
for the visit to the Tàilíng mausoleum,
Qīn Wáng Yǔnlù and others were ordered to take overall charge of affairs in the capital.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the crime of falsely reporting on the campaign against Zhānduì was re-evaluated.
Qìngfù was imprisoned.
Xǔ Yìnghǔ was sentenced to decapitation.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
an edict commanded that relief be given to the earthquake victims in Dǎjiànlú, Sìchuān.
Láibǎo was ordered to concurrently manage the Ministry of Works (Gōngbù Shàngshū).
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Emperor proceeded to the Tàilíng mausoleum.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Ānníng was summoned to the capital.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Emperor paid respects at the Tàilíng mausoleum.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
nine years of outstanding tax arrears were remitted for Qìngyún and two other counties in Zhílì.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Zhàohuì, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue (Hùbù Shìláng), was ordered to proceed to the Sìchuān military camp to supervise provisions transport.
Nàqīn requested to deploy thirty thousand troops for the campaign,
but this was not permitted.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Zhāng Shīzǎi, Vice Minister of Granaries (Cāngchǎng Shìláng), was ordered to go to Jiāngnán to learn river conservancy from Gāo Bīn.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital (Jīngshī).
On the *rénzǐ* day, the first day of the ninth month,
Èchāng was transferred to be Governor of Sìchuān (Sìchuān Xúnfǔ).
Cèlèng and Gāo Bīn were ordered to jointly interrogate Zhōu Xuéjiàn.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Sèléng'é was granted permission to commit suicide.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Tǎěrmǎshàn and Nǔsān, Advising Ministers of the Northern Route (Běilù Cānzàn Dàchén), were summoned to the capital.
Mùkèdēng'é and Sàbùhāshàn replaced them.
Nàqīn and others reported the capture of Shēnjiá and Shēndá cities.
Cèlèng was transferred to be Governor-General of the Two Jiāngs (Liǎngjiāng Zǒngdū).
Yǐn Jìshàn was transferred to be Governor-General of the Two Guǎngs (Liǎngguǎng Zǒngdū).
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Nàqīn and Zhāng Guǎngsì were summoned to the capital.
Fùěrdān was ordered to be acting Governor-General of Sìchuān (Sìchuān Zǒngdū),
and to consult with Yuè Zhōngqí to advance the campaign as circumstances dictated.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Dǒng Bāngdá was reinstated to serve in the Inner Court (Nèitíng).
Minister Bāndì was ordered to proceed to the military camp
and manage military affairs jointly with Fùěrdān and Yuè Zhōngqí.
All officials in the military camp, from大臣 downwards, were to be subject to Fùěrdān's command.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Huáng Tíngguì was summoned to the capital.
Húbǎo was appointed acting Governor of Gānsù (Gānsù Xúnfǔ),
and concurrently managed the affairs of Governor-General of Shǎnxī-Gānsù (Shǎnxī-Gānsù Zǒngdū).
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Emperor visited the Jìngyí Yuán to review troops.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Jiǎn Qīn Wáng Shénbǎozhù was stripped of his princely title
for abusing his brother's daughter.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Dépèi was ordered to inherit the title of Jiǎn Qīn Wáng.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
an edict reprimanded Nàqīn and Zhāng Guǎngsì for wasting military resources due to their incompetence,
and ordered Nàqīn to surrender his seal as Commissioner (Jīnglüè).
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Fùhéng was ordered to temporarily manage the affairs of Governor-General of Sìchuān and Shǎnxī (Chuānshǎnzǒngdū),
and to proceed to the military camp.
Shūhèdé, Vice Minister (Shìláng), was ordered to serve in the Grand Council (Jūnjīchù).
On the *gēngchén* day,
Nàqīn and Zhāng Guǎngsì were stripped of their offices and arrested for questioning
due to errors in military planning.
Zhāng Guǎngsì was summoned to the capital.
Nàqīn was sent to serve in the Northern Route military camp.
Fùhéng was appointed Commissioner (Jīnglüè)
to command the Jīnchuān military affairs.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Láibǎo was ordered to temporarily manage the Ministry of Revenue (Hùbù).
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Rénwǔ, the first day of the month,
5,000 Manchu soldiers were dispatched to the military camp at Jīnchuān.
The princes and high ministers requested that Nèqīn be punished.
An imperial edict rebuked Nèqīn for betraying the country and its grace,
and stated that a further decree would be issued after his reply was received.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Yǐn Jìshàn was summoned to the capital.
Shuòsè was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng,
and Èróng'ān was appointed acting Provincial Governor of Hénán.
Relief was provided for the flood disaster in Xīnníng County, Húnán.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Bāndì was demoted for not impeaching Nèqīn.
He was downgraded.
Shūhèdé was appointed Minister of War.
On the day Dīnghài,
Fùhéng was appointed Grand Secretary of the Bǎohé Hall,
and concurrently managed the Board of Revenue.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the coffin of Empress Xiàoxián was moved to Jìng'ān Zhuāng.
The Emperor went to Jìng'ān Zhuāng to offer libations.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Zōupíng and thirty other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Shāndōng.
Yǐn Jìshàn was appointed Minister of Revenue.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the Emperor visited Fēngzégård,
and hosted a banquet for the Commander-in-Chief Fùhéng and the generals and soldiers who participated in the campaign.
Yuè Zhōngqí reported the victory at Gēnzá.
On the day Rénchén,
Kāitài was appointed Provincial Governor of Húnán,
and Táng Suíyǔ was appointed Provincial Governor of Jiāngxī.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
relief was provided for the drought disaster in Yángqǔ and fifteen other prefectures and counties in Shānxī.
On the day Wùxū,
the Emperor visited Bǎodì Temple
and reviewed the Eight Banners' practice of cloud-ladder warfare.
On the day Dīngwèi,
relief was provided for the disaster in Fùyáng and other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Ānhuī.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Yǐn Jìshàn was ordered to assist as Grand Secretary.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the Emperor visited Chónghuá Palace
and hosted a banquet for the Commander-in-Chief Fùhéng.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Emperor went to the Tángzǐ to perform sacrificial rites
and to sacrifice to Jí'ěrdān's banner.
On the day Jiǎyín,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Tóngshān County, Jiāngsū, and Hànchuān and eight other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Húběi.
On the day Bǐngchén,
it was ordered that all provincial governors should concurrently hold the title of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
On the day Dīngsì,
the Emperor went to the Southern Park for a hunt.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the Emperor reviewed the troops.
On the day Wùchén,
Zhōu Xuéjiàn was granted permission to commit suicide.
Prince Píng Fúppéng died,
and court was suspended for two days.
On the day Jǐsì,
Yǐn Jìshàn was ordered to serve in the Grand Council.
Relief was provided for drought, tidal, and other disasters in Jìnjiāng and fourteen other counties in Fújiàn.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
land rent was remitted for the flood disaster in Wén'ān and three other counties in Zhílì.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the Emperor visited Fēngzégård
and hosted a banquet for the troops of the Three Eastern Provinces,
and bestowed various rewards.
Cèlèng was appointed Governor-General of Chuānshǎn,
and Yǎ'ěrhāsàn was appointed acting Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng.
Fùhéng was commended
for traveling over two hundred *lǐ* daily.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Yǐn Jìshàn was given the seal of Imperial Commissioner
and appointed acting Governor-General of Chuānshǎn.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Nèqīn's request to order Zhāng Guǎngsì and Yuè Zhōngqí to advance on separate routes
was rebuked as contradictory.
He was arrested for trial.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
due to the heavy expenditure on the Jīnchuān campaign,
a secret edict instructed Fùhéng to resolve the matter peacefully.
On the day Gēngchén,
the posts of Governor-General of Sìchuān and Governor-General of Shǎnxī-Gānsù were separately established.
Yǐn Jìshàn was appointed Governor-General of Shǎnxī-Gānsù,
Cèlèng was appointed Governor-General of Sìchuān,
managing the affairs of the provincial governor,
and Èchāng was appointed Provincial Governor of Gānsù.
Shūhèdé was transferred to Minister of Revenue,
and Húbǎo was appointed Minister of War.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
it was decreed that the Grand Secretaries of the Grand Secretariat would be two Manchu and two Han,
the Assistant Grand Secretaries would be one or two Manchu and one or two Han,
and the four Halls and two Pavilions that they concurrently managed were changed to three Halls and three Pavilions.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Fùhéng was promoted to Grand Guardian.
Ākèdūn was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary.
On the day Dīnghài,
Huáng Tíngguì was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng.
The Emperor ascended the Yíngtái
and personally interrogated Zhāng Guǎngsì.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Shūhèdé was dispatched to arrest Nèqīn and take him to the military camp
to be severely interrogated by Fùhéng.
Hǎiwàng was appointed acting Minister of Revenue,
and Hādáhā was appointed acting Minister of War and Commander of the Infantry.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Qìngfù and Lǐ Zhìcuì were sentenced to beheading.
Grand Secretary Chén Shìguān was dismissed.
On the day Rénchén,
Zhāng Guǎngsì was executed by beheading.
On the day Bǐngyín,
a secret edict instructed Fùhéng that
if he could not achieve success by the third month of next year,
he should accept surrender and withdraw the troops.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
it was ordered that the Governors-General and Provincial Governors of Sìchuān and Shǎnxī should all be subject to Fùhéng's command.
Bāndì was to exclusively handle provincial governor affairs,
and Zhàohuì was to exclusively handle grain transport.
Gāo Bīn was exempted from the post of Grand Secretary,
but remained in his post as Governor-General of the Southern River.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Fùhéng and others were ordered to thoroughly interrogate Nèqīn
and execute him at the military front with his grandfather Èbìlóng's sword.
On the day Jiǎchén,
relief was provided for the drought disaster in Yàozhōu and twenty-five other prefectures and counties in Shǎnxī.
In the fourteenth year, in spring, in the first month, on the day Xīnhài,
an edict instructed Fùhéng and Yuè Zhōngqí to advance and suppress from Dǎngbà,
while Fù'ěrdān handled the Kǎsà route.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
due to Grand Secretary Zhāng Tíngyù's old age,
he was ordered to enter the palace every five days for consultation.
Fùhéng was instructed that the fourth month was the deadline
for accepting surrender and withdrawing the army.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
relief was provided for the disaster in Jīnxiāng and other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng.
On the day Dīngsì,
Fù'ěrdān, Dálèdǎng'ā, Shūhèdé, Yǐn Jìshàn, and Cèlèng were ordered to assist in the military affairs of Dàjīnchuān.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Húbǎo was appointed acting Governor-General of Shǎnxī-Gānsù.
Attendant Bāndì was stripped of his office,
but remained acting Provincial Governor of Sìchuān.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Fùhéng was summoned back to the capital.
Ministers Dálèdǎng'ā, Shūhèdé, and Yǐn Jìshàn were all ordered to return to their posts.
Cèlèng and Yuè Zhōngqí were to manage the military affairs of Dàjīnchuān.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Fù'ěrdān was severely reprimanded
for requesting to advance deeper.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
as Shāluóbēn and Lángkǎ of Dàjīnchuān requested to surrender,
Fùhéng was ordered to withdraw the army
and was specially enfeoffed as Zhōngyǒng Gōng (Duke of Loyalty and Valor).
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Fùhéng was instructed to accept the surrender of Shāluóbēn and others.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Dǎosūn, King of the country of Nánzhǎng, presented ivory.
In the second month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Táng Suíyǔ requested to lead his subordinates in donating their allowances to aid the military provisions.
The Emperor severely rebuked him
for not understanding the system of governance.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Láibǎo was promoted to Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
Chén Dàshòu, Shūhèdé, Cèlèng, and Yǐn Jìshàn were promoted to Grand Guardian to the Crown Prince.
Wāng Yóudūn and Liáng Shīzhèng were promoted to Grand Preceptor to the Crown Prince.
Dálèdǎng'ā, Nàyántài, Ākèdūn, and Hādáhā were promoted to Junior Preceptor to the Crown Prince.
On the day Rénchén,
Fùhéng reported that
on the fifth day of the second month, an altar was set up and the road cleared,
and the imperial edict was proclaimed to accept the surrender of the native chieftain Shāluóbēn and the native officer Lángkǎ of Dàjīnchuān.
Fùhéng was bestowed with a four-dragon embroidered robe,
and additionally two leopard-tail spears and two imperial guards.
Yuè Zhōngqí was promoted to Junior Guardian to the Crown Prince.
On the day Guǐsì,
the Emperor issued an edict specifically commending Yuè Zhōngqí
for personally going to Lèwūwéi to persuade Shāluóbēn and others to surrender.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Lābùdūn and Zhòngfóbǎo were summoned to the capital.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Shūhèdé was ordered to inspect the military camps in Yúnnán and other provinces
and jointly inspect the Jīnshā River project with Xīnzhù.
Húbǎo was appointed acting Governor-General of Húguǎng.
On the day Yǐsì,
the Emperor visited Fēngzégård to demonstrate plowing.
Shāluóbēn presented ten barbarian boys and ten barbarian girls, but the Emperor declined them by edict.
In the third month, on the day *Guǐchǒu*,
the Emperor ordered the eldest imperial son and Prince Yù, among others, to welcome Fùhéng in the suburbs.
On the day *Yǐmǎo*,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, went to Jìng'ānzhuāng to offer libations before the coffin of Empress Xiàoxián.
On the day *Dīngsì*,
the Emperor led the Grand Secretary and Duke Fùhéng to the Empress Dowager's palace to inquire about her health.
Yuè Zhōngqí was enfeoffed as a third-rank Duke
and granted the title of Minister of War.
On the day *Jǐwèi*,
Fùhéng was ordered to concurrently manage the Court of Colonial Affairs,
and Láibǎo to concurrently manage the Ministry of War.
Nàmùzhálè and Débǎo were ordered to remain as Grand Ministers of the Imperial Household Department.
On the day *Xīnyǒu*,
the Emperor visited the Eastern Mausoleums.
On the day *Jiǎzǐ*,
the Emperor paid respects at Zāoxīlíng, Xiàolíng, Xiàodōnglíng, and Jǐnglíng.
On the day *Dīngmǎo*,
the Emperor went to the Southern Park for a hunt.
On the day *Guǐyǒu*,
the Emperor paid respects at Tàilíng.
On the day *Jiǎxū*,
relief was provided for flood victims in six prefectures and counties, including Hànchuān in Húběi.
On the day *Yǐhài*,
taxes were remitted for drought-stricken areas in ten prefectures, counties, and departments, including Bǎo'ān in Zhílì.
On the day *Dīngchǒu*,
the post of Governor-General of Riverways in Zhílì was abolished,
and the concurrent management of the official seal and imperial edicts was included.
Fùsēn was transferred to be General of Xī'ān.
Fù'ěrdān was appointed General of Hēilóngjiāng.
In the fourth month, on the day *Rénwǔ*,
the Emperor presided at the Tàihédian,
and by order of the Empress Dowager,
Consort Gāotiān Nàlāshì was invested as Imperial Noble Consort,
and given charge of the six palaces.
On the day *Jiǎshēn*,
Láibǎo's concurrent management was changed to the Ministry of Justice.
Yùnzhe was summoned to the capital,
and Gùcóng was made acting Governor-General of Grain Transport.
Nàyántài and others were ordered to investigate the disaster in Hā'ěr.
On the day *Yǐyǒu*,
the Empress Dowager's honorary title was augmented to Chóngqìng Cíxuān Kānghuì Huángtàihòu.
The next day, an edict was issued granting varying degrees of imperial benevolence.
On the day *Xīnmǎo*,

taxes were remitted for flood-stricken areas in twenty prefectures and counties, including Zōupíng in Shāndōng, and for hail-stricken areas in twelve departments, prefectures, and counties, including Lán in Gānsù.
Péng Shùkuí was summoned to the capital.
Táng Suí'zǔ was transferred to be Governor of Húběi,
and Āsīhā was appointed Governor of Jiāngxī.
Zhāng Shīzài, the Vice Minister of Granaries, was ordered to assist in managing river affairs in Jiāngnán with his original title.
On the day *Wùxū*,
Húbǎo was appointed Governor-General of Grain Transport.
Táng Suí'zǔ was ordered to be acting Governor-General of Húguǎng.
Hādáhā was transferred to be Minister of War,
and Sānhé was appointed Minister of Works.
Taxes were remitted for four granaries, including Wángjiāgāng in Shāndōng.
On the day *Jǐhài*,
the Governor of Jiāngxī was ordered to concurrently hold the title of Commander-in-Chief.
On the day *Gēngzǐ*,
Nàmǐn was summoned to the capital,
and Wèi Zhézhì was appointed Governor of Ānhuī.
On the day *Yǐsì*,
relief was provided for disaster-stricken areas in three counties, including Táiwān in Fújiàn.
Taxes were remitted for last year's flood-stricken areas in Xīnníng, Húnán.
In the fifth month, on the day *Yǐmǎo*,
taxes were remitted for drought-stricken areas in thirteen departments, prefectures, and counties, including Lán in Gānsù.
On the day *Bǐngchén*,
taxes were remitted for last year's drought-stricken areas in thirteen prefectures, counties, and garrisons, including Fùyáng in Ānhuī.
On the day *Xīnyǒu*,
the Emperor went to Hēilóngtán to pray for rain.
In the sixth month, on the day *Bǐngshēn*,
relief was provided for drought-stricken areas in Wèiyuán and other prefectures and counties in Gānsù.
On the day *Jǐhài*,
Hú Zhōngzǎo, the Education Commissioner of Guǎngxī, expressed resentment about the abolition of his post.
He was ordered to come to the capital for re-appointment,
and his case was still referred to the board for severe deliberation.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day *Wùshēn*,
relief was provided for flood-stricken areas in two counties, including Guāngzé in Fújiàn.
On the day *Gēngxū*,
taxes were remitted for last year's flood-stricken areas in six prefectures and counties, including Hànchuān in Húběi.
On the day *Xīnhài*,
Nàsūtú, the Governor-General of Zhílì, died.
Taxes were remitted for tidal disaster-stricken areas in nine counties, including Jìnjiāng in Fújiàn.
On the day *Rénzǐ*,
Fāng Guānchéng was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì,
Chén Dàshòu was made acting Governor-General,
and Yǒngguì was made acting Governor of Shāndōng.
Láibǎo was ordered to concurrently manage the Ministries of Personnel and Revenue,
and Ākèdūn was made acting Commander of the Infantry.
On the day *Gēngshēn*,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, stayed at the Summer Resort.
On the day *Xīnyǒu*,
Fùhéng and Chén Dàshòu were ordered to translate foreign books from Western and other countries.
On the day *Dīngmǎo*,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, went hunting in Mùlán.
On the day *Yǐhài*,
remissions and exemptions were granted for disaster-stricken areas in six prefectures and counties, including Yǒngjì in Shānxī.
In the eighth month, on the day *Gēngchén*,
the Emperor hunted at Bāyángōu,
and the Mongol princes and others offered a feast.
On the day *Rénwǔ*,
relief was provided for flood-stricken areas in two counties, including Luótián in Húběi.
On the day *Guǐmǎo*,
relief was provided for flood-stricken areas in seven counties, including Yánjīn in Hénán.
On the day *Jiǎchén*,
relief was provided for flood-stricken areas in thirteen prefectures and counties, including Qiánjiāng in Húběi.
In the ninth month, on the day *Yǐmǎo*,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, returned to the capital.
On the day *Yǐchǒu*,
Èróng'ān was appointed Governor of Hénán.
On the day *Bǐngyín*,
Bāngǔn, the chieftain of Zhāndiào, surrendered.
Qìngfù was granted permission to commit suicide.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day *Jiǎwǔ*,
relief was provided for flood-stricken areas in twenty-two prefectures, counties, and departments, including Qiántáng in Zhèjiāng, and eighteen granaries, including Bàoláng.
Fùqīng was awarded the title of Commander-in-Chief,
and stationed in Tibet with Jìshān,
in charge of the official seal of the Imperial Commissioner.
On the day *Dīngyǒu*,
Bāshíwǔ was summoned to the capital,
and Zhuónài was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Guīhuàchéng.
On the day *Wùxū*,
Sìchuān was ordered to strictly arrest "guō" bandits.
Because Zhū'ěrmòtènàmùzhálè was dissolute,
Cèléng, Yuè Zhōngqí, Fùqīng, and Jìshān were instructed to guard against him.
Wàngbùduō'ěrjì, son of Prince Èlínqìn of Khalkha, captured an Èlǔtè escapee.
The Emperor commended and rewarded him.
Varying degrees of grain tribute were remitted for twenty-three prefectures and counties, including Fùníng in Jiāngsū.
On the day *Jǐhài*,
taxes were remitted for flood-stricken areas in eighteen prefectures, counties, and departments, including Jìzhōu in Zhílì,
and relief was also provided.
On the day *Jiǎchén*,
Sūn Jiāgàn, the former Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, was summoned to the capital.
In the eleventh month, on the day *Dīngwèi*,
Liáng Shīzhèng was ordered to concurrently manage the Ministry of Personnel.
On the day *Guǐhài*,
Wāng Yóudūn, the Minister of Justice, was ordered to be acting Assistant Grand Secretary.
On the day *Wùchén*,
Grand Secretary Zhāng Tíngyù requested retirement,
which was granted.
On the day *Gēngchén*,
Liú Tǒngxūn was appointed Minister of Works.
On the day *Xīnsì*,
Péng Wéixīn was reinstated as Left Censor-in-Chief.
On the day *Guǐwèi*,
poetry was bestowed upon Zhāng Tíngyù,
and the order for him to be enshrined in the imperial ancestral temple was reaffirmed.
On the day *Dīnghài*,
due to Wāng Yóudūn's leakage of imperial decrees,
he was relieved of his post as Assistant Grand Secretary,
but remained in his post as Minister.
Liáng Shīzhèng was made Assistant Grand Secretary.
On the day *Xīnmǎo*,
Zhāng Tíngyù, the retired Grand Secretary, was stripped of his title of Earl Xuānqín,
and retired with his original title of Grand Secretary,
but was still permitted to be enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
Hādáhā was transferred to be Minister of Works,
Shūhèdé to be Minister of War,
and Hǎiwàng to be Minister of Revenue.
Mùhélán was appointed Minister of Rites,
Xīnzhù was appointed General of Jílín,
and Yǒngxìng was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng.
On the day *Yǐwèi*,
Wèi Zhézhì was summoned to the capital.
Tú'ěrbǐng'ā was transferred to be Governor of Ānhuī,
and Yuè Jùn to be Governor of Yúnnán.
Sūchāng was appointed Governor of Guǎngdōng.
In the fifteenth year, spring, first month, on the day *Bǐngwǔ*,
outstanding "haoxian" surcharges were remitted for Zhílì, Shānxī, Hénán, and Zhèjiāng.
Six-tenths of the "haoxian" surcharges were remitted for Jiāngsū, Ānhuī, and Shāndōng.
On the day *Dīngwèi*,
Zhāng Yǔnsuí was appointed Grand Secretary of the Dōnggé,
Shuòsè was appointed Governor-General of Yún-Guì,
Chén Dàshòu was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng,
Liáng Shīzhèng was appointed Minister of Personnel,
and Lǐ Yuánliàng was appointed Minister of War.
On the day *Jiǎyín*,
the Emperor visited Yíngtái and Zǐguānggé,
and granted a banquet to Nímǎ, the envoy from Zhǔngá'ěr.
On the day *Yǐmǎo*,
Jìshān was summoned back to the capital,
and Lābùdùn was ordered to work in Tibet with Fùqīng.
On the day *Rénxū*,
Liú Lún, Vice Minister of Works, was ordered to serve in the Grand Council.
Lǐ Zhìcuì was executed by decapitation,
and Wáng Shìtài and Luó Yúcháo were sentenced to execution by decapitation.
In the second month, on the *yǐhài* day,
the Emperor, respectfully accompanying the Empress Dowager, toured Wǔtái to the west.
One-third of the regular taxes of the passing through areas were remitted.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Cháoxiǎn offered tribute.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Emperor, respectfully accompanying the Empress Dowager, stayed at Púsàdǐng on Wǔtáishān.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Cèlíng, Prince Chāoyǒng of Khalkha, the Assistant Commander-in-Chief of Dìngbiān Left, passed away.
Bèilè Luóbùzàng was ordered to act as the Assistant Commander-in-Chief of Dìngbiān Left.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the previous year's regular taxes of Púxiàn and two other counties in Shānxī, which had suffered disasters, were again remitted by three-tenths.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Emperor stayed at Zhàoběikǒu for a hunting expedition.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
classical texts were sought out from private collections.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor inspected the dikes of the Yǒngdìnghé.
In the third month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Zhāng Yǔnsuí was promoted to Tàizǐ Tàibǎo.
Jiǎng Pǔ, Fāng Guānchéng, and Huáng Tíngguì were promoted to Tàizǐ Shàobǎo.
Three-tenths of the regular taxes of Jìzhōu and seventeen other prefectures and counties in Zhílì were again remitted.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor, respectfully accompanying the Empress Dowager, returned to Jīngshī.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
on the second anniversary of Empress Xiàoxián's passing,
the Emperor went to Jìng'ānzhuāng to offer sacrifices.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the retired Grand Secretary Zhāng Tíngyù returned to his hometown.
He was generously bestowed with gifts,
and ten imperial guards led by a Sànzhì Dàchén were ordered to escort him.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the regular taxes for the fourteenth year's flood disaster of Guìchí and thirty other prefectures and counties in Ānhuī were remitted,
and relief was also provided.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the regular taxes for the fourteenth year's flood disaster of Qiánjiāng and four other prefectures and counties in Húběi were remitted.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the regular taxes for the fourteenth year's flood disaster of Zōupíng and twenty-seven other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Shāndōng were remitted.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
there was a disaster at the gunpowder bureau in the provincial capital of Yúnnán.
On the *rénchén* day,
Ā Guì was appointed to serve as *yuánwàiláng* in the Lìbù.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the retired Grand Secretary Zhāng Tíngyù was stripped of the privilege of being commemorated in the imperial ancestral temple alongside the emperors.
The regular taxes for the fourteenth year's flood disaster of Guìchí and thirty other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Ānhuī were remitted.
On the *wùxū* day,
Lābùdūn was summoned to the capital.
Bāndì was ordered to be stationed in Xīzàng,
and Jìshān was stationed in Qīnghǎi.
In the fifth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
the Emperor went to Hēilóngtán to pray for rain.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the Xíngbù was ordered to clear minor cases,
reducing sentences below penal servitude and caning.
Zhílì also followed suit.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
the Jiǔ Qīng and Kē Dào were instructed to directly point out deficiencies.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Xīnzhù was summoned to the capital.
Zhuō Nài was appointed as the General of Jílín,
and Zhòngfóbǎo as the Governor of Guīhuàchéng.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Emperor went to Hēilóngtán to pray for rain.
In the sixth month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Chénggǔnzhábù, Prince of Khalkha, was appointed as the Assistant Commander-in-Chief of Dìngbiān Left.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Lètíng, Zhílì.
Bǎodé was appointed as the Advisory Minister for the Northern Military Camps.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Yuè Jùn, the Provincial Governor of Guǎngdōng, was dismissed from his post.
Tú'ěrbǐng'ā and Wèi Zhézhì were ordered to remain in their posts as Provincial Governors of Yúnnán and Ānhuī, respectively.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Liú Tǒngxūn was ordered to go to Guǎngdōng to investigate abuses related to converting rice into cash and grain storage.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Wāng Yóudūn was demoted to Vice Minister of the Bīngbù.
Liú Tǒngxūn was appointed as Minister of the Bīngbù,
and Sūn Jiāgàn as Minister of the Gōngbù.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Miǎndiàn offered tribute.
In the eighth month, on the *rénshēn* day,
the Emperor ascended the Tàihédiàn,
and with the imperial decree of the Empress Dowager,
the Imperial Noble Consort Nàlā Shì was formally established as Empress.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
for the establishment of the Empress,
the Emperor, leading the princes and high officials, respectfully accompanied the Empress Dowager to the Cínínggōng to perform the congratulatory ceremony,
and the Empress Dowager's honorific title was augmented to Chóngqìng Cíxuān Kānghuì Dūnhé Huángtàihòu.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the Emperor, respectfully accompanying the Empress Dowager and leading the Empress, visited the imperial tombs,
and also toured Sōng and Luò.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Jìshān was ordered to go to Xīníng to handle affairs.
Bāndì was ordered to go to Zàng to handle affairs,
replacing Lābùdūn who returned to the capital.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Emperor, respectfully accompanying the Empress Dowager, visited Zhāoxīlíng, Xiàolíng, Xiàodōnglíng, and Jǐnglíng.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Dé Tōng and Péng Wéixīn, Censors-in-Chief of the Left,
and Mǎ Líng'ā, Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Left, were all deliberated for punishment due to their favoritism towards Fù Héng,
and were demoted or dismissed to varying degrees.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Yìxiàn and seven other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng.
In the ninth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day, the first day of the month,
Méi Juéchéng was appointed as Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the *rényín* day,
the Emperor, respectfully accompanying the Empress Dowager and leading the Empress, visited Tàilíng.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Censor Suǒ Lù and others impeached Jiǎng Bǐng for hypocrisy.
The Emperor issued an edict rebuking them for deliberately disturbing governance,
and they were dismissed from their posts.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Lìbù reported that the former Grand Secretary Zhāng Tíngyù had formed a faction with his protégés,
and had also married into Zhū Quán's family.
He should be dismissed and punished.
The Emperor specially pardoned him.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor stayed at Zhèngdìngfǔ to review troops.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Lābùdūn was appointed as Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
three-tenths of the regular taxes of the passing through areas in Hénán were remitted.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Emperor stayed at Zhāngdéfǔ,
and visited the Jīngzhōngmiào.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the Emperor stayed at Bǎiquán,
and respectfully accompanied the Empress Dowager to Báilùyuán.
Cèwàngduō'ěrzhǐ Nàmzhálè, Taiji of Dzungaria, was assassinated by his own people.
His elder brother, Lama Dá'ěrzá, was enthroned.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
five-tenths of the regular taxes of the poor harvest areas in Hénán were again remitted.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Mǐnxiàn and nine other counties in Fújiàn.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the regular taxes for the coming year of Xiángfú and other counties in Hénán were remitted.
An earthquake occurred in Héyáng, Yúnnán.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
the Emperor visited Sōngshān.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the Emperor, respectfully accompanying the Empress Dowager, stayed at Kāifēngfǔ.
On the *wùyín* day,
the Emperor visited Gǔchuítái.
Èróng'ān was promoted to Nèi Dàchén.
Relief was provided for the flood disaster in Chún'ān, Zhèjiāng.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Àibìdá was transferred to be Provincial Governor of Yúnnán, KāitàI to be Provincial Governor of Guìzhōu,
and Yáng Xīfú to be Provincial Governor of Húnán.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the regular taxes for the flood disaster of Qīnghé and nine other prefectures and counties in Jiāngsū were remitted.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the regular taxes for the flood disaster of Yìngzhōu and three other prefectures and counties in Shānxī were remitted.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the regular taxes for various flood and hail disasters in Gù'ān and forty-six other departments, prefectures, and counties in Shùnzhí were remitted,
and relief loans were still provided to varying degrees.
On the *wùxū* day,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Lìyáng and other prefectures and counties in Jiāngsū.
In the eleventh month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
the Emperor, respectfully escorting the Empress Dowager and accompanied by the Empress, returned to the capital.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
relief was provided to twenty-eight departments and prefectures in Gānsù and Píngliáng suffering from hail and drought.
On the day Rénzǐ,
tribute taxes were remitted for drought-stricken Lánshān and other counties in Shāndōng,
and relief was also provided.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Zhū'ěrmòtè Nàmzhálè plotted rebellion,
and Fùqīng, the Resident Amban of Tibet, and Lābùdūn, the Left Censor-in-Chief, lured and executed him.
His confederates, Zhuóní Luóbùzàng Zhāshí and others, led a revolt,
and Fùqīng and Lābùdūn were killed.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Cèlèng and Yuè Zhōngqí were ordered to lead troops to Tibet,
Yǐn Jìshàn was transferred to Sìchuān to manage provisions and supplies,
and Grand Secretary Nàmzhálè was ordered to reside in Tibet with Bāndì.
Jìshān was arrested and brought to the capital,
Shūmíng was ordered to reside in Qīnghǎi,
and Zhòng Fóbǎo was appointed acting [Grand Secretary].
On the day Yǐmǎo,
an edict was issued proclaiming Zhū'ěrmòtè Nàmzhálè's crime of murdering his brother Chēbùdēng and other rebellious acts.
Fùqīng and Lābùdūn were posthumously granted the title of first-class Earl,
Fùqīng's son Míngrén and Lābùdūn's son Gēndūn were enfeoffed as first-class Viscounts,
with hereditary succession.
Grand Secretary Zhàohuì was ordered to go to Tibet
to assist Cèlèng in handling post-rebellion affairs.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Shūhèdé was ordered to remain serving in the Grand Council.
Mùhélín was transferred to become Left Censor-in-Chief,
and Wǔlíng'ān was appointed Minister of Rites.
Yǎ'ěrhāsàn was summoned to the capital,
and Wáng Shī was appointed Governor of Jiāngsū.
On the day Dīngsì,
Cèlèng was ordered to select Tibetan chiefs to assist Bāndì in the affairs of the Kǎbùlún.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Ālǐgǔn was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng,
Āsīhā was transferred to become Governor of Shānxī,
Wèi Zhézhì was appointed Governor of Guǎngxī,
and Dìngcháng was appointed Governor of Ānhuī.
On the day Wùchén,
with the capture of Zhuóní Luóbùzàng Zhāshí and others,
the rebellion was pacified.
Yuè Zhōngqí's advance into Tibet was halted,
and he was ordered to be stationed at Dǎjiànlú.
In the twelfth month, on the first day Gēngwǔ,
relief was provided for flood disasters in six stations including Gāolípiáo in Shèngjīng.
On the day Rénshēn,
Han officials such as Liáng Shīzhèng were first permitted to gain experience in various ministries through the grace of imperial patronage.
On the day Wùyín,
relief was provided for flood disasters in three salt fields including Guǎndú in Liǎnghuái.
On the day Gēngchén,
Shūhèdé was ordered to inspect the sea walls in Zhèjiāng.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Sābùhā, the Assistant Amban of Wūlǐyàsūtái, was dismissed from his post,
and Bǎodé replaced him.
On the day Wùzǐ,
relief was provided for flood disasters in seven cities including Liáoyáng and six prefectures and counties including Chéngdé in Shèngjīng,
and tribute taxes were remitted or deferred to varying degrees.
On the day Guǐsì,
Táng Suízǔ was impeached and dismissed,
and Yán Ruìlóng was appointed acting Governor of Húběi.
In the sixteenth year, in the spring, first month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
due to the first Southern Tour,
arrears of tribute taxes from the first to the thirteenth year in Jiāngsū and Ānhuī were remitted,
tribute taxes for the current year in Zhèjiāng were remitted,
and the sentences of criminals in Zhí Shěng whose cases had been deferred three or more times were reduced.
Due to the previous year's tour to Sōng and Luò,
arrears of tribute taxes in Hénán from before the fourteenth year were remitted.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Sùzhōu and other prefectures and counties in Ānhuī from the previous year.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
an edict was issued to reform the accumulated abuses in tax collection, as the arrears in Jiāngsū had reached over 2.2 million.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
arrears of tribute taxes from the first to the tenth year in Gānsù were remitted.
Yán Ruìlóng was appointed acting Governor of Húběi.
On the day Xīnhài,
the Emperor, respectfully escorting the Empress Dowager, embarked on a Southern Tour.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
three-tenths of the current year's tribute taxes in the areas of Zhílì and Shāndōng traversed [by the tour] were remitted.
From then on, all Southern Tours followed this precedent.
On the day Rénxū,
Zhuóní Luóbùzàng Zhāshí and others were executed.
On the day Guǐhài,
relief was provided for drought disasters in Shèxiàn and fifteen other prefectures and counties in Ānhuī.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
arrears of tribute taxes and granary grain in Zōupíng and other counties in Shāndōng were remitted.
In the second month, on the day Xīnwèi,
relief was provided for drought disasters in Lánshān and seven other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
arrears of tribute taxes for salt households in Liǎnghuái were remitted.
On the day Yǐhài,
Dèqìnzhābù, a Qā'ěrkā prince, was appointed Qā'ěrkā Deputy General,
and Duke Chēbùdēngzhābù was appointed Assistant Amban.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
the Emperor, respectfully escorting the Empress Dowager, crossed the river
and inspected the Tiānfēi floodgate.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the Gāojiāyàn embankment was inspected.
On the day Xīnsì,
tribute taxes for flood disasters in Yìxiàn and seven other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng were remitted to varying degrees.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the Emperor visited Jiāoshān.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Dìngcháng was transferred to become Governor of Guǎngxī.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the Emperor stayed in Sūzhōu,
and issued an edict to the scholars and common people of Sānwú,
exhorting them
to uphold their fundamental occupations
and strive to shun extravagance.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Zhū'ěrmòtè Nàmzhálè's crimes of rebellion were proclaimed
and punished according to the law.
Yán Ruìlóng was dismissed from his post,
and Ālǐgǔn was ordered to concurrently hold the post of Governor of Húběi.
On the day Rénchén,
old and new land taxes in Wǔjìn and other counties in Jiāngsū were remitted,
and arrears of tribute taxes from the first to the eighth year in Xīnghuà county were remitted.
On the day Guǐsì,
the Dzhungar envoys È'ěr qīn and others were received at the imperial temporary palace in Sūzhōu.
In the third month, on the first day Wùxū,
the Emperor, respectfully escorting the Empress Dowager, visited Hángzhōu Prefecture.
Loans were granted to banner people and commoners affected by floods in Hūlán, Hēilóngjiāng,
and tribute taxes for the current year from official estates were remitted.
Tribute grain for the current year due to floods in Chún'ān county, Zhèjiāng, was remitted.
On the day Jǐhài,
Zhāng Shīzài was appointed Governor of Ānhuī.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the Emperor visited the Fūwén Academy
and the Guāncháolóu (Tidal View Tower) to review troops.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the Han Military Deputy Lieutenant-General of Hángzhōu was abolished.
On the day Yǐsì,
the Emperor offered sacrifices at Yǔlíng (the Tomb of Yu).
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Emperor, respectfully escorting the Empress Dowager, returned to stay in Hángzhōu Prefecture.
On the day Dīngwèi,
troops were reviewed.
On the day Wùshēn,
Gāo Bīn was ordered to continue to manage the Grand Canal Director-General affairs with the title of Grand Secretary.
On the day Gēngxū,
an edict exhorted the scholars and common people of Zhèjiāng to value sincerity and humility
and for their sons to diligently work the land.
Bāndì was ordered to take charge of the seal of the Imperial Commissioner Resident in Tibet.
On the day Xīnhài,
Zhāng Yǔnsuí, Grand Secretary of the East Pavilion, passed away.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Emperor, respectfully escorting the Empress Dowager, stayed in Sūzhōu Prefecture.
On the day Jiǎyín,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Hǎikāng and other counties in Guǎngdōng.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the Emperor visited the ancestral temple of the Sòng minister Fàn Zhòngyān,
bestowed the garden the name Gāoyì (High Righteousness),
and rewarded his descendants, Fàn Hóngxīng and others, with sable furs and silk.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the Emperor, respectfully escorting the Empress Dowager, visited Jiāngníng Prefecture.
On the day Rénxū,
the Emperor offered sacrifices at Míng Tàizǔlíng (the Tomb of Emperor Tàizǔ of Míng).
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Jìshān was granted the order to commit suicide.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Chén Shìguān was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wényuāngé.
Tribute taxes for disaster-stricken areas in Jiāngpǔ and fifteen other prefectures and counties in Jiāngsū were remitted to varying degrees.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Zhuónài, the General of Jílín, was transferred to be General of Hángzhōu,
and Yǒngxīng replaced him.
Tribute taxes for disaster-stricken areas from the thirteenth year in Lán and nine other departments and counties in Gānsù were remitted.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the Emperor inspected Jiǎngjiābà.
Arrears of tribute taxes from before the ninth year in Pèixiàn, Jiāngnán, were remitted.
On the day Jiǎxū,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Yǒngjiā and ten other prefectures, counties, salt fields, and garrisons in Zhèjiāng.
Relief was provided for flood disasters from the fifteenth year in Lóngchuān and twelve other prefectures and counties in Guǎngdōng.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
relief was provided for flood disasters from the fifteenth year in Shānyáng and twenty-four other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Jiāngsū.
On the day Jǐmǎo,

tribute taxes for disaster-stricken areas from the fourteenth year in Dí Dào and twenty other departments and counties in Gānsù, affected by floods, droughts, hail, and frost, were remitted to varying degrees.
Héngwén was appointed Governor of Húběi.
On the day Guǐwèi,
tribute taxes for flood disasters from the fourteenth year in Yānlíng and sixteen other prefectures and counties in Hénán were remitted.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Yǒngxīng was dismissed from his post and arrested for questioning,
Zhuónài, the General of Jílín, was demoted,
and Fùsēn replaced him.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the Emperor stayed in Tàiaān Prefecture
and offered sacrifices to the Eastern Peak.
On the day Wùzǐ,
an imperial edict declared that due to the solar eclipse on the first day of the fifth month,
all decorations in the imperial temporary palace were to be removed, and a fast was to be observed.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Prince Lǚ Yǔntáo was sent to offer the Chángyú sacrifice in place of the Emperor.
In the fifth month, on the *dìngyǒu* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *dìngwèi* day,
His Majesty personally presided over the memorial ceremony for Grand Commander Fù Qīng and Left Censor-in-Chief Lābùdūn.
On the *wùshēn* day,
due to Yǒngxīng and others falsely impeaching Táng Suīzǔ,
his registered property was returned,
and he was summoned back to the capital.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Wú Hóng and 243 others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with varying ranks.
On the *dìngsì* day,
the quota tax for wind disaster in eleven prefectures and counties, including Hǎikāng in Guǎngdōng, was remitted for fifteen years.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Yán Ruìlóng was sentenced to beheading
for falsely accusing Táng Suīzǔ.
On the *guǐhài* day,
relief was provided for tidal disasters in six prefectures and counties, including Yèxiàn in Shāndōng.
In the intercalary fifth month, on the *wùyín* day,
Huáng Tíngguì was transferred to be the Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù,
and Yǐn Jìshàn was made the Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Yǒngguì was appointed as the Provincial Governor of Zhèjiāng.
On the *rénchén* day,
an imperial order commanded Chén Zǔfàn, Wú Dǐng, Liáng Xīyú, and Gù Dònggāo, who were recommended for their classical scholarship, to present their writings,
and those who wished to report to the board for an audience were permitted to do so.
On the *guǐsì* day,
locusts plagued prefectures and counties including Héjiān in Zhílì.
In this month,
the quota tax for water and hail disasters from the previous year in nineteen prefectures and counties, including Tàiyuán in Shānxī, was remitted with varying amounts.
Relief was provided for water disasters in six counties, including Shòuguāng in Shāndōng, and three salt fields, including Guāntái,
for water disasters in two counties, including Nínghuà in Fújiàn,
and for earthquake disasters in seven prefectures and counties, including Jiànchuān in Yúnnán.
In the sixth month, on the *jǐhài* day,
Táng Suīzǔ was reinstated as the Surveillance Commissioner of Shānxī.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
relief was provided for hail disaster in Jìngjiāng County in Jiāngsū.
Relief was provided for water disasters in four prefectures and counties, including Yīngdé in Guǎngdōng.
Relief was provided for water disasters in Fèngtái and Gāopíng in Shānxī.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the quota tax for water disaster in Pèixiàn in Jiāngsū from the previous year was remitted.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the quota tax for drought disaster in seven departments, prefectures, and garrisons, including Yǒngjiā in Zhèjiāng, from the previous year was remitted.
Relief was provided for water disasters in counties including Nínghuà in Fújiàn.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Myanmar sent tribute.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the quota tax for water disaster in twenty-five prefectures and counties, including Shòuzhōu in Ānhuī, was remitted.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Bùtúxùnlíntègūsī, a person from the Zǔngé'ěr tribe, surrendered.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
relief was provided for water disasters in counties including Guīhuà in Fújiàn.
On the *rénshēn* day,
His Majesty escorted the Empress Dowager on the autumn hunt in Mùlán.
On the *wùyín* day,
His Majesty escorted the Empress Dowager to stay at the Summer Resort.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Yellow River burst its banks at thirteen forts in Yángwǔ, Hénán.
On the *gēngchén* day,
His Majesty escorted the Empress Dowager on a tour to Mùlán,
and held a hunting expedition.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the quota tax for hail disaster in Qīngshuǐhé Department in Shānxī was remitted.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
relief was provided for water disaster in Cháoyì County in Shǎnxī.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
relief was provided for water disasters in prefectures and counties including Píngdù in Shāndōng.
On the *rénchén* day,
relief was provided for water disasters in nine counties, including Fèngtái in Shānxī.
In the eighth month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
relief was provided for drought disasters in sixty-five prefectures, counties, and garrisons, including Hǎiníng in Zhèjiāng, and salt fields including Dàsōng.
Relief was provided for seven counties, including Shàngráo in Jiāngxī, which suffered drought.
Relief was provided for drought disaster in Tiānmén, Húběi.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Chén Zǔfàn and Gù Dònggāo were granted the title of Director of Studies of the Guózǐjiān.
On the *wùxū* day,
due to Shuòsè exposing the fabricated memorial draft of Sūn Jiāgàn
and the forged vermilion endorsements,
an imperial edict commanded Fāng Guānchéng and others to secretly investigate and apprehend the culprits.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
His Majesty escorted the Empress Dowager back to stay at the Summer Resort.
On the *xīnhài* day,
an imperial order commanded the renovation of the tombs of Jīn Tàizǔ and Shìzōng in Fángshān County.
On the *dìngsì* day,
His Majesty escorted the Empress Dowager back to the capital.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
relief was provided for water disasters in fourteen counties, including Shāngqiū in Hénán.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Zhǔntài was stripped of his office and arrested for investigation
due to his connivance in concealing and falsely reporting.
Èróng'ān was transferred to be the Provincial Governor of Shāndōng, Shū Lù as the Provincial Governor of Hénán, È Chāng as the Provincial Governor of Jiāngxī,
and Yáng Yìngjū was appointed as the Provincial Governor of Gānsù.
Gāo Bīn was ordered to Hénán to manage the Yángwǔ River project.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Zhuāng Yǒugōng was appointed as the Provincial Governor of Jiāngsū.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the large tax for hail disaster in five prefectures and counties, including Píngliáng in Gānsù, was remitted.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
it was decided that the provincial *xiāngshì* (provincial examinations) for the special *ēn kē* (grace examination) would be held in the second month of the following year.
An imperial edict ordered the suspension of this year's autumn executions.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
relief was provided for water disasters in fifty-three prefectures and counties, including Zōupíng in Shāndōng.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
His Majesty escorted the Empress Dowager to Tàilíng.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
relief was provided for water disasters in two counties, including Fú'ān in Fújiàn.
On the *gēngchén* day,
His Majesty escorted the Empress Dowager to visit Tàilíng.
On this day,
they returned.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Shū Hèdé was ordered to Jiāngnán to investigate the matter of the fabricated memorial draft of Sūn Jiāgàn.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Chén Shìguān was ordered to concurrently manage the Ministry of Rites.
Chén Dàshòu, the Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng, passed away.
Ālǐgùn was transferred to replace him,
and Yǒngcháng was appointed as the Governor-General of Húguǎng.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
relief was provided for water disasters in prefectures and counties including Shàngcài in Hénán.
On the *guǐsì* day,
relief was provided for tidal disasters in four counties, including Xiápǔ in Fújiàn.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *wùxū* day,
Fàn Shíshòu was appointed acting Provincial Governor of Húnán.
On the *rén'yín* day,
relief was provided for water disasters in seven salt fields, including Fùguó, belonging to Chánglú, and three salt fields, including Wángjiāgāng in Shāndōng.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
relief was provided for drought disasters in eighteen prefectures and garrisons, including Shèxiàn in Ānhuī.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
relief was provided for water disasters in eight prefectures and counties, including Tóngshān in Jiāngsū.
Chén Hóngmóu was transferred to be the Provincial Governor of Hénán,
and Shū Lù as the Provincial Governor of Shǎnxī.
Relief was provided for this year's water disasters in seven prefectures and counties, including Qídōng in Shāndōng, and hail disaster in Róngchéng County.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
relief was provided for water and hail disasters in twenty-six prefectures and counties, including Wǔqīng in Zhílì.
On the *guǐhài* day,
relief was provided for tidal disasters in the two salt fields of Guāntái in Shāndōng.
In the eleventh month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
relief was provided for water disasters in five counties, including Xiángfú in Hénán.
On the *yǐhài* day,
relief was provided for this year's water disasters in three prefectures and counties, including Dōngmíng in Zhílì.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the breach at Yángwǔ was closed.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
to celebrate the Empress Dowager's sixtieth birthday,
His Majesty conferred the honorary title of Chóngqìng Cíxuān Kānghuì Dūnhé Yùshòu Huángtàihòu,
and issued an imperial edict granting widespread favors with varying degrees.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Gāo Bīn and Wāng Yóudūn were ordered to jointly inspect the Tianjin river works.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the Empress Dowager's birthday,
His Majesty escorted the Empress Dowager to the Cíníng Palace,
and led the princes, dukes, and ministers in a celebratory ceremony.
In the twelfth month, on the *guǐsì* day, the first day of the month,
Wū'ěrdēng was appointed Minister-Counselor of the Northern Route Army Camp.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the diversion channel of the Yǒngdìng River was dredged.
On the *wùxū* day,
relief was provided for this year's water disaster in Húnchūn area in Jílín.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
relief was provided for water disasters in fifty-five prefectures and counties, including Zōupíng in Shāndōng.
On the *rén'yín* day,
Yǎ'ěrhāsàn was appointed as the Provincial Governor of Zhèjiāng.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the northern and southern reduction channels of the Grand Canal in Zhílì were dredged.
Duō'ěrzhì was ordered to replace Bāndì in handling affairs in Tibet.
On the *xīnhài* day,
relief was provided for drought and insect disasters in sixty prefectures, counties, departments, and garrisons, including Yínxiàn in Zhèjiāng, and eight salt fields, including Dàsōng.
In the spring of the seventeenth year, the first month, on the *yǐhài* day,
the Zǔngé'ěr envoys, Túbǔqí'ěrhāláng and others, were granted a banquet.
On the *gēngxū* day,
a Minister of the General Affairs of the Internal Affairs Bureau of Shèngjīng was established,
to be concurrently managed by the General.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
due to internal strife between Zǔngé'ěr's Dáwǎqí and Āmù'ěrsānà,
troops were reinforced at the Ā'ěrtài border pass.
Shū Hèdé and Yù Bǎo were ordered to inspect the Northern Route Army Camp.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Ābāqí and Dáqīng'ā were appointed Minister-Counselors of the Northern Route.
On the *dīnghài* day,
relief was provided for disaster-stricken poor people in six prefectures and counties, including Tóngshān in Jiāngsū, and nine prefectures and counties, including Shèxiàn in Ānhuī.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the lower mouth of the Yǒngdìng River and the Fèng Embankment in Zhílì were repaired.
In the second month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
Zhōng Yīn was appointed as the Provincial Governor of Shǎnxī.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Zhǔntài was released.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
His Majesty proceeded to the Eastern Mausoleums.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
È'ěrdénì Dìbā of Bùlǔkèbā offered local products as tribute.
On the *dīngsì* day,
His Majesty visited the Zhaoxī Mausoleum, Xiào Mausoleum, Xiàodōng Mausoleum, and Jǐng Mausoleum.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
His Majesty stayed at Pánshān.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
relief was provided for disaster-stricken poor people in Shānyīn and Yúxiāng in Shānxī.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the tombs of Jīn Tàizǔ and Shìzōng in Fángshān County were repaired.
In the third month, on the day Wùchén,
due to the severe disaster in Zhèdōng,
an imperial edict instructed Yǎ'ěrhāshàn to increase relief,
preventing displacement.
On Gēngwǔ,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On Rénshēn,
Mò'ěrhuan was appointed as the Dūtǒng of Guīhuàchéng.
On Wùyín,
Pān Sīqǔ, the Provincial Governor of Fújiàn, passed away.
Chén Hóngmóu was transferred to become the Provincial Governor of Fújiàn,
and Jiǎng Bǐng was appointed as the Provincial Governor of Hénán.
In summer, the fourth month, on Jiǎwǔ,
taxes were remitted for the twelve prefectures, counties, and garrisons including Qídōng in Shāndōng that suffered from floods the previous year.
On Yǐsì,
taxes were remitted for the twenty-three sub-prefectures, prefectures, and counties including Wǔqīng in Zhílì that suffered from floods the previous year.
On Gēngxū,
taxes were remitted for the seventy-three prefectures, counties, and garrisons including Hǎiníng in Zhèjiāng and the thirteen salt fields including Dàsōng that suffered from floods the previous year.
On Dīngsì,
taxes were remitted for the four salt fields including Yǒnglì in Zhílì and counties including Shānyīn in Shānxī that suffered from floods the previous year.
In the fifth month, on Xīnwèi,
forty-three prefectures and counties including Dōngguāng and Wǔqīng in Zhílì suffered from locust infestations.
On Gēngchén,
relief was provided for the fourteen counties including Xiángfú in Hénán that suffered from floods.
On Jǐchǒu,
relief was provided for the fourteen prefectures and counties including Dídao in Gānsù that suffered from floods the previous year.
Eight prefectures including Jǐnán in Shāndōng suffered from locust infestations,
and twelve prefectures and counties including Shàngyuán in Jiāngnán experienced locust nymph outbreaks.
In the sixth month, on Jiǎwǔ,
Níyǎsī, a person from the Zhǔngá'ěr (Dzungar) tribe, surrendered.
On Dīngwèi,
an imperial examination was held for officials of the Hánlín Academy and the Zhànshì Office.
Wāng Tíngyú and two other officials were promoted to the first rank,
while others were promoted or demoted according to their performance.
An examination was held for Manchu officials transferred from various ministries and courts to the Hánlín Academy and the Zhànshì Office.
Dé'ěrtài was promoted to the first rank,
while others were demoted or appointed to lower positions according to their performance.
On Bǐngchén,
Èlèshùn was appointed as the Provincial Governor of Gānsù.
In autumn, the seventh month, on Dīngchǒu,
the Emperor accompanied the Empress Dowager on the autumn hunt in Mùlán.
On Jǐmǎo,
three-tenths of the money and grain taxes were remitted for the prefectures and counties they passed through.
On Guǐwèi,
the Emperor accompanied the Empress Dowager to stay at the Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng.
On Dīnghài,
relief was provided for counties including Tóngshān in Jiāngsū that suffered from floods.
In the eighth month, on Bǐngshēn,
Cài Shítián, an imperial censor serving in the inner bureau of the Shùntiān provincial examination, and the recommended scholar Cáo Yǒngzǔ, were executed
for colluding and engaging in illicit activities.
On Rényín,
relief was provided for the prefectures and counties including Jìnjiāng in Fújiàn that suffered from wind disasters.
On Jiǎchén,
the Emperor accompanied the Empress Dowager on an inspection tour to Mùlán,
where they held a hunting expedition.
On Bǐngwǔ,
Huáng Tíngguì was ordered to investigate and handle disaster relief in Shǎnxī.
On Yǐmǎo,
relief was provided for the twenty-one prefectures and counties including Xiánníng in Shǎnxī that suffered from drought.
In the ninth month, on Xīnyǒu,
the kingdom of Portugália in the West sent envoys to pay tribute.
Cāngwàng, the local chieftain of Zágǔ in Sìchuān, rebelled.
Yuè Zhōngqí was ordered to lead troops to suppress him.
On Gēngwǔ,
the letter of credence brought by the Sūlù chieftain as tribute was found to be unsatisfactory.
Kā'ěrjīshàn and others were ordered to send him back to his country.
On Jiǎxū,
the imperial army in Sìchuān captured Zágǔnǎo,
and one hundred and six barbarian strongholds surrendered.
Cèlèng and Yuè Zhōngqí were highly commended.
On Wùyín,
the excessively heavy taxes were reduced for the five counties including Zhāngyè in Gānsù.
Relief was provided for the famine victims in Hénán.
On Jǐmǎo,
the Emperor accompanied the Empress Dowager back to the capital.
On Gēngchén,
Liáng Shīzhèng, Grand Secretary concurrently Minister of the Board of Civil Office, requested to retire to care for his parents,
which was granted.
Sūn Jiāgàn was appointed Minister of the Board of Civil Office and Grand Secretary,
and Wāng Yóudùn was appointed Minister of the Board of Works.
On Xīnsì,
the Dzungar lamas Gēndūn Línqìn and others surrendered.
On Dīnghài,
Yǐn Jìshàn was summoned to the capital.
Zhuāng Yǒugōng was appointed acting Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng.
Cāngwàng was executed.
In winter, the tenth month, on Wùzǐ (the first day of the month),
one hundred and forty-one individuals including Qín Dàshì were granted the degree of Jìnshì of varying ranks.
Èchāng was summoned to the capital.
È Róng'ān was appointed acting Provincial Governor of Jiāngxī,
and Yáng Yìngjū was appointed acting Provincial Governor of Shāndōng.
On Rényín,
Āsīhā reported that the gentry and common people of Píngyáng had donated silver for disaster relief.
An edict stated that it was undesirable to compel wealthy commoners in disaster areas to contribute,
and ordered the return of the donations.
Dìngcháng was transferred to become Provincial Governor of Shānxī,
and Lǐ Xītài was appointed Provincial Governor of Guǎngxī.
On Jǐyǒu,
the Emperor visited the Eastern Tombs,
and also escorted Empress Xiàoxián to her burial chamber.
On Rénzǐ,
the Emperor paid respects at Zhāoxīlíng, Xiàolíng, Xiàodōnglíng, and Jǐnglíng.
On Dīngsì,

relief was provided for nineteen prefectures and counties including Shàngyuán in Jiāngsū, ten prefectures and counties including Línjìn in Shānxī, and twenty-five prefectures, counties, and garrisons including Zhōngxiáng in Húběi, all suffering from drought.
The Zágǔ and Hēishuǐ tribes, lower and upper villages, in Sìchuān surrendered.
In the eleventh month, on Gēngshēn,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On Jiǎzǐ,
Liú Tǒngxūn, Minister of the Board of Punishments, was ordered to serve in the Jūnjī Chù.
On Wùchén,
relief was provided for the five prefectures and counties including Wénxǐ in Shānxī that suffered from drought.
On Gēngchén,
È Róng'ān was appointed Provincial Governor of Jiāngxī.
In the twelfth month, on Wùzǐ,
relief was provided for the twenty-one sub-prefectures, prefectures, and counties in Lánzhōu, Gānsù, that suffered from floods and hail.
On Jǐchǒu,
the city walls of nine counties including Yǒngshòu in Shǎnxī were repaired,
with labor serving as relief.
Relief was provided for Wǔzhì County in Hénán that suffered from floods.
Fù'ěrdān, General of Hēilóngjiāng, passed away,
and Chuò'ěrdō was appointed to replace him.
On Yǐsì,
Yúshǐ Shūchéng requested the release of the person who circulated a counterfeit memorial, which displeased the Emperor,
and he was dismissed from office.
An edict instructed Chén Hóngmóu not to pursue and arrest Catholic followers.
In the eighteenth year, spring, the first month, on Wùwǔ,
relief was provided for thirty-seven prefectures and counties including Yàozhōu in Shǎnxī, and eleven prefectures and counties including Yǒngjì in Shānxī, all suffering from drought.
On Bǐngyín,
bandits Mò Xìnfēng and others in Dōngguǎn County, Guǎngdōng, and bandits Cài Róngzǔ and others in Pínghé County, Fújiàn, rebelled.
They were captured and punished.
On Wùyín,
Huáng Tíngguì was transferred to be acting Governor-General of Sìchuān,
Yǐn Jìshàn was appointed acting Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù,
È Róng'ān was concurrently acting Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
and Bāndì was appointed acting Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng.
On Xīnsì,
Èchāng and others were dismissed from office and interrogated.
On Yǐyǒu,
arrears of taxes from previous years were remitted for thirty-one prefectures, counties, and garrisons including Zhāngqiū in Shāndōng.
In the second month, on Dīnghài (the first day of the month),
regarding Yuè Zhōngqí's request to use military force against Guōluòkè,
an imperial edict instructed Huáng Tíngguì to deliberate and report.
On Bǐngshēn,
the Emperor paid respects at Tàilíng.
On Dīngyǒu,
the Emperor offered sacrifices at the tombs of Emperor Tàizǔ and Emperor Shìzōng of Jīn.
Lú Lǔshēng, a Qiānzǒng in Jiāngnán, was executed by dismemberment in the marketplace
for forging a memorial by Sūn Jiāgàn.
On Jǐhài,
the Empress Dowager departed from Chàngchūnyuán and traveled to Zhuōzhōu.
The Emperor went to the temporary palace to pay his respects.
On Rényín,
the Emperor accompanied the Empress Dowager on a boat to Liánhuādiàn to inspect the water hunt.
On Bǐngwǔ,
the land tax for the sixteenth year, suffered from floods, was remitted for the five counties including Xiàyì in Hénán.
On Dīngwèi,
Zhàohuì was ordered to handle affairs in Tibet.
On Wùshēn,
the Emperor inspected the Yongding River works.
On Gēngxū,
the Emperor went to Nányuàn for a hunting expedition.
On Xīnhài,
the land tax for the seventeenth year, suffered from floods, was remitted for the ten prefectures and counties including Shàngyuán in Jiāngsū.
In the third month, on Guǐhài,
regarding Yǎ'ěrhāshàn's failure to thoroughly investigate the forged memorial,
the case was sent to the ministry for severe deliberation.
On Wùyín,
relief was provided for the famine victims in the eleven prefectures, counties, and garrisons including Shòuzhōu in Ānhuī that suffered from drought the previous year.
On Jǐmǎo,
Kāitài was appointed acting Governor-General of Húguǎng,
and Dìngcháng was appointed acting Provincial Governor of Guìzhōu.
On Xīnsì,
relief was provided for the nineteen prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Húběi that suffered from drought the previous year.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Dīnghài,
Qián Chénqún remonstrated concerning the investigation and handling of a forged memorial draft.
The Emperor rebuked him for seeking fame,
and ordered him not to keep drafts,
admonishing him
with the words, “Your descendants will not preserve their heads.”
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Portugal (Bóěrdūgálìyǎ) sent envoys to offer tribute of local products,
and was answered with an excellent imperial edict.
Héngwén was appointed Acting Governor-General of Húguǎng.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
a banquet was bestowed upon the tribute envoys from Portugal (Bóěrgádūlǐyǎ).
On the day Yǐwèi,
the stipulated tax for Yúnnán's Jiànchuānzhōu, affected by earthquakes and floods in the 16th and 17th years, was partially remitted,
and relief was provided.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
an imperial edict was bestowed upon the King of Portugal (Bóěrdūgálìyǎ),
and additional gifts of fine silk and precious objects were granted.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
due to drought, the Ministry of Justice (Xíngbù) was ordered to clear minor prison cases,
reducing sentences for crimes below penal servitude,
and Zhílì followed suit.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Emperor went to Hēilóngtán to pray for rain.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Yǒngcháng and Nǔsān were ordered to Ánxī,
and were given seals as Imperial Commissioners.
In the fifth month, on the day Guǐhài,
sentences for crimes delayed three times or more in autumn and court reviews were reduced.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
locusts appeared in Shāndōng's Jìníng, Wénshàng and other prefectures and counties.
The stipulated tax for Guǎngdōng's Fēngshùn and two other counties, affected by floods last year, was remitted.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the stipulated tax for Zhèjiāng's Rénhé and five other counties, and Rénhé Field, affected by floods last year, was remitted,
and relief was provided.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the Zunghar Taiji Lǎma Dáěrzhá and Dawachi attacked each other, and Lǎma Dáěrzhá was captured.
Dawachi made himself Taiji.
In the sixth month, on the day Guǐsì,
Cèlèng was appointed Acting Minister of War (Bīngbù Shàngshū).
On the day Yǐwèi,
Dīng Wénbīn, a native of Shàngyú, Zhèjiāng, was proven guilty of having the Duke Yǎnshèng, Kǒng Zhāohuàn, produce rebellious writings.
Having been tried and found guilty,
he was executed by dismemberment.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
locusts appeared in Tiānjīn and other prefectures and counties.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
thirty-two prefectures, counties, and garrisons including Shùntiān and Wǎnpíng controlled locusts.
On the day Rénshēn,
two sluice gates of Jiāngnán's Shàobóhú and the Gāoyóu chēlúo dam burst simultaneously.
Cèlèng and Liú Tǒngxūn were ordered to investigate the flood disaster together with Gāo Bīn.
Relief was provided for flood-stricken Xī and Tàihú and other counties in Ānhuī.
On the day Gēngchén,
Zhuāng Yǒugōng was ordered to provide relief for Gāoyóu and Báoyìng, affected by floods.
On the day Rénwǔ,

the practice of provincial circuit intendants concurrently holding titles such as Policy Councillor (Cānzhèng) and Policy Advisor (Cānyì) of theàng Provincial Administration Commission, Vice Commissioner (Fùshǐ) and Assistant Commissioner (Qiānshì) of the Provincial Surveillance Commission,
and promotion to Vice Minister (Shàokīng) of the Court of State Ceremonials (Hónglúsì) was abolished.
In the eighth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Lǚ Qīnwáng Yǔntáo was ordered to offer sacrifices on behalf of the Emperor to the Grand Altars of Soil and Grain.
Relief was provided for flood-stricken Bǎnpǔ and other salt fields in Liǎnghuái.
On the day Wùxū,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, hunted in Mùlán in autumn.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Gāo Bīn was dismissed,
and Cèlèng was appointed Acting Governor-General of the Southern River (Nánhé Hédào Zǒngdū),
to investigate various malpractices and embezzlements in river works with Liú Tǒngxūn.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Yǒngcháng and Kāitài were ordered to return to their respective posts.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, stopped at the Imperial Summer Resort.
On the day Yǐsì,
one hundred thousand shi of rice from Jiāngxī and Húběi respectively were allocated for disaster relief in Jiāngnán.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, made an imperial tour to Mùlán,
and conducted a hunt.
On the day Gēngxū,
Gāo Bīn and Zhāng Shīzài were stripped of their posts,
and retained to render service in river works.
Wèi Zhézhì was appointed Governor of Ānhuī.
On the day Xīnhài,
relief was provided for flood-stricken Tóngshān and twelve other prefectures and counties in Jiāngsū, and Lánshān and other counties in Shāndōng.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
relief was provided for flood-stricken Qiánjiāng and two other counties in Húběi.
On the day Rénxū,
a dike burst in the thirteen forts of Yángwǔ, Hénán.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
due to fear and hesitation in advancing during the imperial hunt escort,
Fēng'ān Gōngjué and Tián Guó'ēn Hóujué were stripped of their titles,
and Ālǐgùn was dismissed as Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard (Lǐngshìwèi Nèidàchén).
Hóngshēng was appointed Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard of the Bordered White Banner.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
as the Empress was going to Pánshān,
Shūhèdé was ordered to accompany her as Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard and Minister in charge of the Imperial Household Department (Nèiwùfǔ Dàchén).
The Tóngshān river in Jiāngsū burst its banks.
On the day Rénshēn,
Shūhèdé was ordered to assist in the Jiāngnán river works.
Ālǐgùn was appointed Acting Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard,
and accompanied the Empress to Pánshān.
Yǐn Jìshàn was appointed Governor-General of Riverways in Jiāngnán (Jiāngnán Hédào Zǒngdū),
È Róng'ān as Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
Yǒngcháng was transferred to be Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù,
Kāitài as Governor-General of Húguǎng,
Huáng Tíngguì as Governor-General of Sìchuān,
Dìngcháng as Governor of Guìzhōu,
Hú Báochuán as Governor of Shānxī,
Fàn Shíshòu as Governor of Jiāngxī,
Yáng Xífú as Governor of Húnán.
Bāndì was summoned to the capital,
and Cèlèng was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
