and walked to offer earnest prayers.
Yáng Yìngjū was appointed Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù.
Wú Dáshàn held the title of Governor-General while managing the affairs of a Provincial Governor.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Yáng Tíngzhāng was appointed Governor-General of Mǐnzhè,
and Zhuāng Yǒugōng was appointed Provincial Governor of Zhèjiāng.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the land tax quota for the previous year's wind disaster in Qiántáng and sixteen other counties in Zhèjiāng was remitted.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
famine relief for the drought in Hézhōu and other places in Gānsù was extended.
The Ministry of Justice was ordered to clear prisons and reduce sentences.
Gānsù was also to do the same.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
famine relief was provided for the drought and hail disaster in Dídào and twenty-three other departments, prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Gānsù.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the Emperor personally attended the funeral of the former Grand Secretary Huáng Tíngguì.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the land tax quota for the previous year's flood and hail disaster in Yángqǔ and five other prefectures and counties in Shānxī was remitted.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the weaving and production of exquisite silk fabrics and embroidery for tribute was prohibited.
Shūhèdé was ordered to return to garrison Ākèsū.
In the fifth month, on the day Xīnsì,
this year's land tax quota for Tóngguān and sixty-five other departments, prefectures, and counties in Shǎnxī was remitted with variations.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the Emperor went to Hēilóngtán to pray for rain.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
famine relief was provided for the drought in Xiánníng and other prefectures and counties in Shǎnxī.
On the day Jǐhài,
an edict was issued to all officials to reflect and reform,
and to continue to speak frankly about successes and failures.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the Emperor, in plain attire, went to the Shèjìtán to pray for rain.
On the day Dīngwèi,
as the rain was not abundant,
the Emperor did not use the imperial carriage
and had no imperial procession,
walking from Jǐngyùnmén to sacrifice at Fāngzé.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
famine relief was provided for drought-stricken people in Gāolán and other prefectures and counties in Gānsù.
In the sixth month, on the day Gēngxū,
the execution of common offenders who had been submitted for approval was postponed.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Hénglù was appointed General of Suīyuǎnchéng.
On the day Wùwǔ,
famine relief was provided for the drought in Yúlín and eleven other prefectures and counties in Shǎnxī.
On the day Gēngshēn,
due to the prolonged drought, the Emperor
walked to the Huánqiú to perform the great Yú sacrifice.
On this day,
there was heavy rain.
Zhàohuì was ordered to advance his troops to Kāshígáěr,
and Fùdé to advance his troops to Yèěrqiāng.
On the day Jiǎxū,
locusts appeared in Hǎizhōu and other prefectures and counties in Jiāngsū, and Lánshān and other counties in Shāndōng.
Qiú Yuēxiū and Hǎimíng were instructed to eradicate the locusts.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
when English merchant ships came to Níngbō for trade,
Zhuāng Yǒugōng memorialized to refuse them.
Lǐ Shìyáo was instructed to gather foreign merchants
and present them with the prohibitions.
In the intercalary sixth month, on the day Bǐngxū,
the land tax quota for the previous year's wind disaster in Táiwān and three other counties in Fújiàn was remitted.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
famine relief was provided for the drought in Gāolán and other prefectures and counties in Gānsù.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Bùlānídūn abandoned Kāshígáěr and fled.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Huòjízhan abandoned Yèěrqiāng and fled.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Liú Lún was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the day Wùshēn,
due to the drought in Gānsù,
the dispatch of convicted criminals to Bālǐkūn and other places this year was suspended.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the first day Jǐyǒu,
Zhàohuì and others reported that the Muslim populace of Kāshígáěr and Yèěrqiāng welcomed their surrender.
Bùlānídūn and Huòjízhan fled to Bādákèshān.
Ālǐgùn and others were ordered to lead troops to attack Bāěrqǔkè.
On the day Gēngxū,
Zhàohuì and others were instructed to pursue and capture Bùlānídūn and Huòjízhan.
Chēbùdēngzhābù was ordered to garrison Yīlí
to prevent Huòjízhan and others from entering Russia.
On the day Xīnhài,
due to ineffective locust eradication,
Chén Hóngmóu was deprived of his Governor-General title.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, set out
for the autumn hunt in Mùlán.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, stayed at the Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng.
The land tax quota for the drought in Yángqǔ and thirty-nine other departments, prefectures, and counties in Shānxī was suspended.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the Governor-General of Xī’ān was changed to Governor-General of Chuānshǎn,
the Governor-General of Sìchuān to Provincial Governor of Sìchuān,
and the Provincial Governor of Gānsù to Governor-General of Gānsù managing the affairs of a Provincial Governor.
Kāitài was appointed Governor-General of Chuānshǎn,
and Yáng Yìngjū was appointed Governor-General of Gānsù.
Locusts appeared in Píngdìng and other prefectures and counties in Shānxī.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Míngruì pursued and annihilated Huòjízhan and others at Huòsīkùlǔkè Líng,
decisively defeating them.
On the day Rénwǔ,
famine relief was provided for this year's drought in Gāolán and forty other departments, prefectures, and counties in Gānsù.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the prohibition against English merchant ships lingering in Níngbō was reiterated.
On the day Rénchén,
Fùdé and others reported pursuing and annihilating Huòjízhan at Ālèchǔěr,
decisively defeating him.
On the day Guǐsì,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, went to Mùlán
for a hunt.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Fùdé reported that his troops reached Yèshílkùlènuòěr,
and Huòjízhan fled to Bādákèshān.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngxū,
famine relief was provided for the flood in Jiāngshān and other counties in Zhèjiāng.
Rewards were given for meritorious service in suppressing the rebels.
The Muslim leader Èduì was promoted to Bèizi,
Āshímòtè and Hādàimòtè were promoted to Gōng,
and Mǐnzhūěrdōěrjì's ducal title was restored.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the sacrificial rites for the Western Regions were established.
Āguì was ordered to go to Ākèsū to handle affairs.
Yùsùbù was promoted to Bèilè.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Ānxī Garrison in Gānsù was changed to Ānxī Prefecture.
The Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, returned to the capital.
Sūchāng was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng.
The oppressive levies of Huòjízhan and others in the Muslim cities were abolished.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Āguì was granted the seal of an Imperial Commissioner.
On the day Guǐwèi,
famine relief was provided for the drought in Yángqǔ and fifty-six other departments, prefectures, and counties in Shānxī.
On the day Dīnghài,
Hāníngā was granted the right to commit suicide.
On the day Wùzǐ,
county and prefectural officials were prohibited from imposing burdens on the populace when eradicating locusts.
On the day Guǐsì,
seven-tenths of this year's land tax quota for drought-stricken horse-feeding households and village heads in Shānxī was remitted.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Èbì was appointed Provincial Governor of Shānxī.
Famine relief was provided for the drought in Kāiyuán and other cities in Shèngjīng, and Chéngdé and seven other prefectures and counties;
relief and compensation were provided for salt-producing households affected by flood in Cāngzhōu and six other prefectures and counties in Chánglú, and Yánzhèn and five other salt-producing areas;
all had their land tax quotas remitted with variations.
The land tax quota for the previous year's flood and hail disaster in Dídào and twenty-two other departments, prefectures, and counties in Gānsù was remitted.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
famine relief was provided for the floods, frost, hail, and insect disasters in Gù'ān and forty-seven other prefectures, counties, and departments in Shùntiān Zhílì,
and their land tax quotas were also remitted with variations.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
an edict stated:
"For a hundred years, the nation has enjoyed peace,
recuperating and thriving,
and the population has gradually increased.
Now, fortunately, the frontiers have been extended by over ten thousand *lǐ*,
and the newly opened territories
supplement the cultivation of the central plains,
transforming the treacherous and wicked into upright and industrious people.
This single endeavor achieves several good outcomes.
All Governors-General and Provincial Governors are to instruct their subordinates
to settle the criminals sent to the various cities of Bālǐkūn,
punishing them individually,
and not to consider releasing the guilty as an act of benevolence,
which would render good laws ineffective."
On the day Jǐhài,
famine relief was provided for the flood, insect, wind, and tidal disasters in Shàngyuán and nineteen other prefectures, counties, departments, and garrisons in Jiāngsū.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Fùdé reported that Sùlètǎshā of Bādákèshān presented the head of Huòjízhan,
and the entire force surrendered.
An edict was issued to proclaim this domestically and abroad.
General Zhàohuì was further awarded an imperial clan ducal rank saddle and bridle.
General Fùdé was promoted to Marquess,
and also awarded a double-eyed peacock feather.
Grand Ministers-Assistant, Duke Míngruì and Duke Ālǐgùn, were awarded double-eyed peacock feathers.
All from Shūhèdé downwards
were rewarded generously according to assessment.
Èmínhézhuó was promoted to Prince of a Commandery,
and Yùsùbù was awarded the rank of Prince of a Commandery.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
regarding the beginning and end of the military campaigns to pacify the Dzungar and Muslim tribes,
the "Kāihuò Lùn" (Disquisition on Dispelling Delusion) was compiled
and promulgated domestically and abroad.
Famine relief was provided for the flood and insect disasters in Jiāxīng and twenty other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Zhèjiāng, and Shuāngsuì and nine other salt-producing areas.
On the day Rén Yín,
the request from various princes and high officials to bestow an honorary title upon the Emperor was refused.
Famine relief was provided for the drought, hail, and frost disasters in Dìngbiān and nine other counties in Shǎnxī.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Khans, princes, and dukes of the Khalkha and Dörbet tribes were summoned to Tàipíng for a grand banquet.
In the 11th month, on the day *Xīnhài*
— for the pacification of the Huí 部,
the Emperor led the various princes and high officials to the Shòukāng Palace of the Empress Dowager to offer congratulations.
He held court in the Tàihé Hall to receive congratulations.
An imperial edict was promulgated to the capital and the provinces,
extending imperial grace with various degrees of remission.
On the day *Xīnsī*,
Yáng Yìngjū was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
On the day *Yǐchǒu*,
taxes were remitted for lands flooded in Jìníng Prefecture and Yútái County, Shāndōng.
On the day *Guǐyǒu*,
it was ordered that the Bèikè of the various Huí cities should enter court in rotating shifts.
The Khaltagīn Burūt submitted.
In the 12th month, on the day *Jiǎzǐ*,
relief was provided for the current year's drought in 14 prefectures, departments, and counties including Gāolán in Gānsù, and in the jurisdiction of the Magistrate of Dōnglè County.
On the day *Guǐsì*,
seven-tenths of the payable commutation price for disaster-stricken areas in seven salt fields, including Dīngxī in Liǎnghuái, was remitted.
On the day *Jiǎwǔ*,
relief was provided for the current year's flood and tidal disasters in 16 prefectures, counties, and garrisons including Hǎifēng in Shāndōng, and in three salt fields including Yǒngfù.
On the day *Dīngyǒu*,
the regular taxes for the current year's flood disaster in three counties, including Jiāngshān in Zhèjiāng, were remitted.
In the 25th year, spring, 1st month, on the day *Wùshēn*
— for the triumphant return of the western army,
the regular taxes for Gānsù for the coming year were again remitted.
On the day *Jǐyǒu*,
relief was provided for the drought in prefectures and counties including Gāolán in Gānsù.
On the day *Gēngxū*,
colonization for farming was ordered in Wūlǔmùqí.
On the day *Yǐmǎo*,
the Ěrdéní Bèikè of Huòkǎn dispatched envoys, including Tuókètǎmǎtè, to enter court.
On the day *Bǐngchén*,
Sùlètǎn Shā of Bādákèshān dispatched envoys, including Émù'ěr Bèikè, and envoys from Qílǐkè and Bóluólěi, to enter court.
The General stabilizing the borders, Zhào Huì, and others, brought the head of Huò Jízhàn to the Emperor,
and also brought the captive chief Ménduōsuǒpī and others to the capital.
On the day *Dīngsì*,
the Emperor presided over the ritual of presenting captives at the Wǔmén Gate.
He ordered that Huò Jízhàn's head be displayed in public thoroughfares,
and pardoned Ménduōsuǒpī and others.
On the day *Jǐwèi*,
Ājíbǐ of Bùlǔtè dispatched envoys, including Xīlágāsī, to enter court.
2nd month, on the day *Dīngchǒu*,
it was ordered that Chancellor Qiú Yuēxiū and Yīlùshùn should investigate the handling of military supplies in the various prefectures and counties of Gānsù.
Relief was provided for the famine of the four tribal banners, including Zāshāyīkètú Khān.
On the day *Guǐwèi*,
the Emperor set out on his imperial tour to the Eastern Mausoleums.
On the day *Yǐyǒu*,
relief was provided for last year's drought in prefectures and counties including Yángqǔ in Shānxī.
On the day *Bǐngxū*,
the Emperor visited the Zhāoxī Mausoleum, Xiào Mausoleum, Xiàodōng Mausoleum, and Jǐng Mausoleum.
On the day *Dīnghài*,
for Qīngfù's procrastination and concealment,
he was ordered to be executed.
On the day *Xīnmǎo*,
the regular taxes for drought in 19 postal stations, including Shèngjīng, were remitted,
and relief was also provided.
On the day *Guǐsì*,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day *Bǐngshēn*,
Chēbùdēng Zābù was ordered to lead troops as Deputy General to suppress and capture Bālǔkè Bātúlǔ of Hāsàkè,
with Mǎ Chāng and Chēwùchǔkè Zābù as Advising Ministers.
The Emperor proceeded to the Tàilíng Mausoleum.
On the day *Jǐhài*,
the Emperor visited the Tàilíng Mausoleum.
Zhào Huì and Fù Dé were appointed Imperial Front Ministers.
On the day *Rényín*,
Zhào Huì and others returned triumphantly,
and the Emperor went to the outskirts of Liángxiāng to comfort them.
On the day *Guǐmǎo*,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day *Jiǎchén*,
the Zásàkè Commandery Prince of Hāmì, Bèilè Yùsùbù, and others were granted caps and robes of various grades.
3rd month, on the day *Bǐngwǔ*, the new moon
— the Emperor held court in the Tàihé Hall to receive congratulations for the triumphant return.
On the day *Dīngwèi*,
colonization for farming was initiated as a trial in Yīlí, Hǎinúkè, and other places.
Farming villages were established from Wūlǔmùqí to Luókèlún.
The regular taxes for last year's floods and insect plagues in 17 prefectures, counties, and garrisons, including Huáiníng in Ānhuī, were remitted.
On the day *Rénzǐ*,
Ābùdūlā was appointed Āqímù Bèikè of Wūshí,
Āshímòtè was appointed Āqímù Bèikè of Hétián,
Gádàimòtè was appointed Āqímù Bèikè of Kāshígá'ěr,
and Èduì was appointed Āqímù Bèikè of Yè'ěrqiāng.
On the day *Jiǎyín*,
Ā Guì was granted an official seal,
to be stationed in Yīlí to handle affairs,
with Cháng Liàng and others assisting in the work.
On the day *Dīngsì*,
the regular taxes for last year's floods and insect plagues in 10 prefectures, counties, and garrisons, including Rénhé in Zhèjiāng, and in nine salt fields, including Shuāngsuì, were remitted.
On the day *Xīnyǒu*,
relief was provided for last year's floods in 55 prefectures, counties, and garrisons, including Shàngyuán in Jiāngsū.
On the day *Jiǎzǐ*,
the Emperor attended the funeral of Princess Héshuò Héwǎn,
and offered sacrifices.
On the day *Bǐngyín*,
the Emperor visited the residence of the Sixth Imperial Son, Yǒngróng.
On the day *Wùchén*,
Xīn Zhù was ordered to go to Yè'ěrqiāng to handle affairs.
On the day *Jǐsì*,
Consort Chún was promoted to Imperial Noble Consort.
Bātú Jí'ěrgálè was appointed Inner Minister.
On the day *Gēngwǔ*,
the regular taxes for last year's tidal and water disasters in 16 prefectures and counties, including Hǎifēng in Shāndōng, and in three salt fields, including Yǒngfù, were remitted.
Summer, 4th month, on the day *Wùzǐ*
— as locust nymphs emerged in counties including Lánshān in Shāndōng,
Zhílì was ordered to take preventative measures.
On the day *Jǐhài*,
Inner Minister Sālálè died.
5th month, on the day *Jiǎchén*, the new moon
— there was a solar eclipse,
and an edict was issued for self-reflection and rectification.
On the day *Bǐngwǔ*,
it was decreed that the jurisdiction of the Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù would extend only to Wūlǔmùqí,
and Yáng Yìngjū was ordered to return to the interior.
On the day *Rénzǐ*,
an edict stated:
"To prohibit people from the interior from going to the 48 Bù of Měnggǔ to farm
is to cause hardship to the people.
Now, the colonization for farming in various places in Wūlǔmùqí is flourishing,
and visiting commoners are going there,
forming various settlements.
Wastelands are opened up, and many find food,
greatly benefiting the state's original plan for the people.
The ignorant still suspect it causes hardship to the people.
A special proclamation is therefore made."
On the day *Guǐchǒu*,
Bì Yuán and 164 others were granted the *Jìnshì Jídì* and other degrees with varying distinctions.
On the day *Dīngsì*,
the regular taxes for last year's floods and insect damage in 17 prefectures, counties, and garrisons, including Huáiníng in Ānhuī, were remitted.
On the day *Yǐchǒu*,
the Yújiā Circuit of Shǎnxī was abolished,
and the Yánsuī Circuit was reorganized as the Yányúsūi Circuit,
with its station moved to Yúlín Prefecture.
Fū Prefecture was subordinated to the Director of Grain Transport Circuit.
On the day *Jǐsì*,
Ābùlèbāmùbǐtè of Hāsàkè dispatched envoys to enter court.
An imperial letter was granted,
but their request to graze in Yīlí
and reside in Bā'ěrlǔkè and other places was refused.
Bālǔkè Bātúlǔ, who had previously plundered Wūliánghǎi, confessed his crime,
returned what he had seized,
and was still granted gifts.
6th month, on the day *Yǐhài*,
the surcharges for the current year and the coming year in Gānsù were remitted.
On the day *Dīngyǒu*,
Ālǐgǔn was recalled to the capital.
Hǎimíng was ordered to go to Kāshígá'ěr to handle affairs.
Autumn, 7th month, on the day *Guǐmǎo*, the new moon
— an edict was issued to capture locusts in Rèhé.
On the day *Jiǎchén*,
locusts appeared in departments including Níngyuǎn in Shānxī, and in prefectures and counties including Guǎngchāng in Zhílì.
On the day *Jiǎyín*,
the Huí people of Bóshíkèlèmù and other villages, Mài Lǎmùníyǎsī, rebelled,
and Ālǐgǔn pacified them.
Āsīhā was appointed Governor of Jiāngxī.
On the day *Yǐmǎo*,
relief was provided for flood disasters in prefectures and counties including Gāoyóu in Jiāngsū.
On the day *Wùchén*,
Yáng Níng was appointed Admiral of Kāshígá'ěr.
On the day *Jǐsì*,
as Russia stationed troops in the four routes of Hénínglǐng, Kātúnhé, É'ěrqísī, and Ālètánnuò'ěr,
and declared an intention to delineate the border,
Ā Guì, Chēbùdēng Zābù, and others were instructed to expel them with troops in the coming year.
8th month, on the day *Bǐngxū*,
the Ministers stationed in Wūlǔmùqí, Āntài, Dìngcháng, and Yǒngdé, were appointed as general administrators,
and their names were listed in reports to the throne.
Other ministers and imperial guards
were all to follow the precedent of leading ministers,
each specializing in one matter,
and submitting their reports through Āntài and others.
On the day *Jǐchǒu*,
the Emperor accompanied the Empress Dowager on the autumn hunt in Mùlán.
On the day *Rénchén*,
Ā Guì was appointed to oversee Yīlí affairs,
and granted the title of Commandant.
On the day *Bǐngshēn*,
the Emperor accompanied the Empress Dowager to stay at the Mountain Resort.
On the day *Wùxū*,
the Emperor accompanied the Empress Dowager to Mùlán,
and conducted a hunt.
On the day *Jǐhài*,
the office of Jiāngníng Provincial Governor of Jiāngsū was newly established,
stationed in Jiāngníng Prefecture,
to administer the six prefectures and departments of Jiāng, Huái, Yáng, Xú, Tōng, and Hǎi.
The Sūzhōu Provincial Governor would administer the five prefectures and departments of Sū, Sōng, Cháng, Zhèn, and Tài,
and the Ānhuī Provincial Governor returned to be stationed in Ānqìng.
Tuō Yōng was ordered to be transferred to fill the post of Jiāngníng Provincial Governor.
Minister of the Board of Revenue Yú Mǐnzhōng was ordered to serve in the Grand Council.
In the ninth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Qā'ěrkā Chēchén Hán Zhāsàkè Wàngqìnzhābù,
for failing to control his subordinates,
was stripped of his Zásàkè title,
and demoted from Bèizǐ to Zhènguógōng.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Hénglù was granted an audience.
Shūmíng was appointed acting General of Suīyuǎnchéng.
On the day Dīngsì,
Bādài, Deputy Commander of Sānxìng, for allowing people digging ginseng to cause trouble,
and failing to arrest and punish them,
but instead issuing them permits,
was criticized by the Emperor for his cowardice,
and ordered to be executed according to the law.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Dé'ěrgé was ordered to be stationed in Pìzhǎn to manage affairs.
On the day Guǐhài,
Dūlètèkèlè, envoy of the Kazakh Khan Ābùlái, entered the court for an audience.
In winter, on the first day of the tenth month, Rénshēn,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, returned to reside at the Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng.
On the day Yǐhài,
Sūchóng'ā, Provincial Administrator of Sūzhōu, for torturing clerks
and falsely accusing them of embezzling over 700,000 (taels),
which Liú Tǒngxūn and others found to be baseless after investigation,
was dismissed and exiled to Yīlí.
On the day Wùyín,
Hénglù was appointed General of Jílín,
and RúSōng as General of Suīyuǎnchéng.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
relief was granted to Sùzhōu and thirteen other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Ānhuī for this year's flood disaster.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, returned to the capital, Jīngshī.
Ālǐgùn was appointed Chief Imperial Bodyguard (Lǐng Shìwèi Nèidàchén).
On the day Guǐsì,
tax exemptions were granted to Xuānhuà and seven other prefectures and counties in Zhílì for this year's flood and hail disasters.
On the day Jǐhài,
relief was granted to Chángníng and twelve other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Húnán for drought disaster.
In the eleventh month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
tax exemptions were granted, with some variations, to Shānyáng and twenty-five other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Jiāngsū for this year's flood disaster.
On the day Dīngwèi,
land tax was remitted for Yǒnglì and two other salt fields in Shāndōng, and for the tidal-impacted salt pans in Hǎifēng county.
On the day Gēngshēn,
relief was granted to Táozhōu and twenty-seven other administrative divisions (tīng, zhōu, xiàn, wèi) in Gānsù for this year's flood disaster.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Chángjūn was appointed acting Governor of Jiāngxī.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
permission was granted to reclaim barren land adjacent to Sùzhōu,
and to dig canals to irrigate fields.
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐngxū,
Sōng'ālǐ, General of Xī'ān, for accepting bribes from his subordinates,
was dismissed from office and sentenced to strangulation.
The post of Governor-General of Gānsù was reinstated as Governor-General of Shǎnxī-Gānsù.
Since high officials (Dàchén) were stationed in Yīlí, Yè'ěrqiāng and other places,
there was no need to replace the circuit intendants (Dàoyuán);
they were placed under the jurisdiction of the Governor-General.
The Governor-General of Sìchuān ceased to concurrently manage Shǎnxī.
Hú Bǎochuán was transferred to be Governor of Jiāngxī,
Wú Dáshàn to be Governor of Hénán,
and Míngdé to be Governor of Gānsù.
On the day Dīnghài,
Grand Secretary Jiǎng Pǔ requested retirement due to illness,
but was kindly persuaded by the Emperor to stay.
On the day Rénchén,
the Emperor visited Yíngtái,
and bestowed a banquet upon the Bèikè Sàlǐ and others from various cities of Yè'ěrqiāng who came for an audience.
He then granted them tea and fruit at Chónghuá Gōng.
On the day Rénchén,
Āsīhā was sentenced to strangulation.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Démǐn was promoted to General of Jīngzhōu.
Yǒngguì was appointed Censor-in-Chief (Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ),
and ordered to go to Kāshígá'ěr to manage affairs,
replacing Shūhèdé who was to return to the capital.
That year,
Cháoxiǎn and Nánzhǎng sent tribute.
In the spring of the 26th year, in the first month, on the day Rényín,
the Zǐguāng Gé was completed.
A banquet was given to meritorious officials whose portraits were displayed, and to civil and military officials,
Mongolian princes and dukes.
Relief was granted to Línglíng and seven other prefectures and counties in Húnán, and Qīnghé and six other prefectures and counties in Jiāngsū for flood disasters.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
for Àibìdá and Liú Zǎo having identical performance evaluations of their subordinates for two consecutive years,
the matter was sent to the board for severe deliberation.
Mǎ Lóngtú, Provincial Military Commander of Zhèjiāng, for misappropriating public funds,
was relieved of his post and investigated.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Yǐn Jìshàn was granted an imperial audience.
Gāo Jìn was appointed acting Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng.
Hǎimíng was transferred to Ākèsū to manage affairs.
Shūhèdé was ordered to Kāshígá'ěr to manage affairs,
and Yǒngguì to Yè'ěrqāng to manage affairs.
On the day Guǐhài,
Fùsēn was appointed acting Censor-in-Chief.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the Emperor visited the residence of Grand Secretary Jiǎng Pǔ to check on his illness.
Èbǎo, for protecting the case of releasing bandits in Lùchuān county,
was sent to the board for severe deliberation.
Tuōyōng was appointed Governor of Guǎngxī,
and Yǒngtài acting Governor of Húnán.
On the day Gēngchén,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, embarked on a western tour to Wǔtái.
On the day Réngwǔ,
a three-tenths exemption from regular taxes was granted to the prefectures and counties passed through.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, visited Tàilíng.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Lí Wéiyī, King of Ānnán, died.
His nephew Lí Wéikū was enfeoffed as King of Ānnán.
On the day Dīnghài,
arrears from the 8th to 18th years of Qiánlóng were remitted for Xuānhuà, Wànquán, and eight other prefectures and counties in Zhílì.
On the day Guǐsì,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, stayed at Táilù Sì.
On the day Jǐhài,
tax exemptions were granted to Jìníng and three other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng for last year's flood disaster.
Pea seeds were loaned to farmers in Yuānquán and three other counties in Gānsù,
for trial planting.
In the third month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Èmù'ěrbǐ of Xībùchàkè Bùlǔtè defected from Ānjíyán,
and sent an envoy for an audience.
On the day Yǐsì,
the Emperor visited Zhèngdìng Fǔ to review the troops.
On the day Wùshēn,
Bái Zhōngshān, Governor-General of Riverways in Jiāngnán, died.
Gāo Jìn was appointed to succeed him.
Tuōyōng was transferred to be Governor of Ānhuī,
and Xióng Xuépéng as Governor of Guǎngxī.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
an Imperial Resident Minister was established in Kāshígá'ěr,
and Yīlètú was ordered to assist Yǒngguì in managing affairs.
On the day Gēngxū,
relief was granted to Sùzhōu and thirteen other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Ānhuī for flood disaster.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the Emperor visited Píngyáng Diàn for a hunt.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
tax exemptions were granted to Xuānhuà and two other counties in Zhílì for last year's hail disaster.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Āguì was appointed Grand Minister of the Interior (Nèidàchén).
The title of Jiànwēi General of Suīyuǎnchéng was changed to General of Suīyuǎnchéng.
On the day Jǐsì,
Sūmǎlāsātīlá Zhǔndìjiàgōngmǎn, King of Nánzhǎng, sent envoys to congratulate the Empress Dowager on her sacred longevity and the Emperor on his eternal longevity,
and offered local products as tribute.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
the Emperor visited the residences of Prince Zhuāng and Grand Secretary Jiǎng Pǔ to check on their illnesses.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Zhuāng Yǒugōng impeached Participatory Commander Ān Tíngzhāo,
not for recommending him previously,
but for condoning him later.
The Emperor issued an edict praising Zhuāng Yǒugōng.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Grand Secretary Jiǎng Pǔ died.
Jīng'érlǐ and Āsīhā were ordered to Ūlǔmùqí to manage affairs,
and Dásāng'ā to Ākèsū to manage affairs,
replacing Āntài, Dìngcháng, and Nàshìtōng who were to return to the capital.
On the day Wùzǐ,
tax exemptions were granted, with some variations, to Chángníng and twelve other prefectures and counties in Húnán for last year's drought disaster.
On the day Gēngyín,
the Emperor reviewed the troops of the Jiànruì Battalion.
On the day Rénchén,
Lǐ Shìyáo was appointed Minister of Revenue (Hùbù Shàngshū),
Sūchāng was transferred to be Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng,
and Àibìdá as Governor-General of Húguǎng.
Wú Dáshàn was appointed Governor-General of Yún-Guì,
and Chángjūn as Governor of Hénán.
On the day Guǐsì,
Liú Zǎo was ordered to temporarily act as Governor-General of Yún-Guì.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Wáng Jié and 217 other individuals were granted the status of Jìnshì and other degrees, with some variations.
In the fifth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
Liú Tǒngxūn was appointed Grand Secretary of Dōnggé,
and concurrently managed affairs of the Ministry of Rites.
Liáng Shīzhèng was appointed Minister of Personnel (Lìbù Shàngshū) and Associate Grand Secretary,
Liú Lún as Minister of War (Bīngbù Shàngshū),
and Jīn Déyīng as Censor-in-Chief.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Dìngcháng was appointed Governor of Fújiàn,
with Yáng Tíngzhāng concurrently acting in the role.
In the sixth month, on the day Guǐwèi,
relief was granted to Xīnxīng and two other prefectures and counties in Yúnnán for earthquake disaster.
On the day Rénchén,
land tax was remitted for submerged land in Jùróng and eighteen other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Jiāngsū.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
Èmǐdá, Associate Grand Secretary, died.
Zhàohuì was ordered to serve as Associate Grand Secretary.
Shūhèdé was transferred to be Minister of Punishments (Xíngbù Shàngshū),
and Zhàohuì acted in the role.
Āguì was appointed Minister of Public Works (Gōngbù Shàngshū),
and Ālǐgùn acted in the role.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Emperor departed,
for the autumn hunt at Dàlán.
Qínwáng Yǔnmì was ordered to accompany the Empress Dowager.
On the day Rénxū,
the Emperor resided at Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng.
For the Empress Dowager's tour to Mùlán,
civil and military officials along the route in Zhílì were negligent and evasive.
An order was issued to the board for severe deliberation.
On the day Bǐngyín,
rivers overflowed in Xiángfú and other prefectures and counties in Hénán.
In the eighth month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
relief was provided for the victims of floods in Húběi's Hànchuān and other thirteen prefectures, counties, and garrisons.
On the *wùyín* day,
Tāng Pìn was appointed as the Governor of Húběi,
Hú Bǎochuán as the Governor of Hénán,
and Cháng Jūn as the Governor of Jiāngxī.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Gāo Jìn was ordered to Hénán to assist in river works.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, visited Mùlán.
On the *rénchén* day,
Mèngkè and Yǎmùgǔěrqí, the nephews of the *bèikè* of the Chágāěr and Sàěrbāgāshén tribes, were granted an audience.
In the ninth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
this year's capital punishment reviews were suspended.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Míngruì was ordered to Yīlí to handle affairs,
replacing Āguì who returned to the capital.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
all breaches in the Yellow River and Grand Canal in the twenty fortifications of Cáo County, Shāndōng, were closed.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Húnán's Wǔlíng and other prefectures and counties.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the Dān and Qìn Rivers in Huáiqìng Prefecture, Hénán, overflowed into the city,
drowning over 1,300 people.
Relief was provided for the affected people.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Húběi's Miǎnyáng and other eleven prefectures, counties, and garrisons.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Dòu Guāngnài was severely reprimanded by the Board [of Punishments]
for his clamor and abusive language during the grand judicial review.
He was handed over to the Board for strict deliberation.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Sùchéng was ordered to Wūshí to handle affairs,
replacing Yǒngqìng who returned to the capital.
Zhálāfēng'ā was appointed as the Assistant Amban of Wūlǐyǎsūtái.
Yǎláng'ā was sent to Kēbùduō to handle affairs,
replacing Zhálóng'ā and Fúlù who returned to the capital.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Fù Jǐng was ordered to Xīzàng to handle affairs,
replacing Jífú who returned to the capital.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Shāndōng's Jìhé and other forty-five prefectures and counties,
and for this year's flood victims in Hénán's Xiángfú and other fifty-four prefectures and counties.
In the tenth month of winter, on the *wùchén* day,
the land tax for flood-damaged fields in Gānsù's Gāolán and other thirty-two sub-prefectures, prefectures, and counties was remitted,
and the transport grain for flood-damaged areas in Shāndān and other five counties was also exempted.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, returned to the capital.
On the *rénchén* day,
Qiú Yuēxiū was summoned back to the capital.
Relief was provided for flood victims in Jiāngsū's Tóngshān and other counties.
Zhōu Rénjì reported on the trial weaving of pongee silk in Rénhuái and other places,
and the Emperor praised him for the imitation across various prefectures.
The Emperor praised him.
On the first day of the eleventh month, *yǐwèi*,
relief was provided for this year's flood victims in Shùnzhí's Gù'ān and other sixty-nine prefectures and counties.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Yīnglián was appointed as the Minister of the Imperial Household Department.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Yángqiáo breach in Hénán was closed.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Sōngchūn was transferred to be the General of Cháhār,
and Shūmíng was appointed as the General of Suīyuǎrchéng.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,

the attached collection of silver for damage caused by floods over twenty-four years was remitted for Shānxī's Yángqǔ and other thirty-eight prefectures and counties, and for the fourteen sub-prefectures managing grain in Dàtóng.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the grain transport tax and other related items were remitted for Hénán's Xiángfú and other forty-three prefectures and counties, with differing amounts.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the land tax for submerged lands in Jiāngsū's Shānyáng and other twenty-one prefectures, counties, and garrisons was reduced,
and the land tax for civilian farms, school fields, lakes, and reedy marshes was also remitted.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Wǔlíng'ān, the Minister of Rites, was dismissed from his post
for errors in reading memorials.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, visited Cíníng Palace.
An additional honorary title was conferred upon her, namely Chóngqìng Cíxuān Kānghuì Dūnhé Yùshòu Chúnxī Gōngyì Huángtàihòu.
The next day, an imperial edict was issued, granting various favors.
Yǒngguì was appointed as the Minister of Rites,
with Ālǐgǔn acting in his stead.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, visited Cíníng Palace,
and led the princes and ministers in a celebratory ceremony.
A string of pearls was presented for the Empress Dowager's seventieth birthday,
but by imperial decree from the Empress Dowager,
the presentation was halted.
Lèěrsēn was appointed as the Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
In the twelfth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
due to earthquake damage in Yúnnán's Jiāngchuān and other two prefectures and counties,
it was ordered that relief be doubled,
and this year's land tax be remitted.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the land tax for Jiāngsū's Nánhuì and other six prefectures and counties affected by floods and droughts in the twenty-third year was remitted.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Shānxī's Wénshuǐ and other thirteen prefectures and counties.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Húběi's Hànchuān and other two counties and garrisons.
In the first month of spring of the twenty-seventh year, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
due to the Empress Dowager's tour of Jiāngsū and Zhèjiāng,
an imperial edict remitted outstanding taxes in Jiāngsū, Ānhuī, and Zhèjiāng.
Relief was provided to disaster victims in Hénán's Xiángfú and other prefectures and counties, with differing amounts.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
due to disaster in Kēěrqìn Mǐnzhūrduōěrdì Banner,
granary grain was lent for relief.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, began the Southern Tour,
departing from the capital.
Three-tenths of this year's money and grain taxes were remitted for the passing areas in Zhílì and Shāndōng,
and five-tenths for areas affected by disaster last year.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Jīn Déyīng, the Censor-in-Chief of the Left, passed away.
Dǒng Bāngdá was appointed to replace him.
Relief was provided for last year's flood victims in Shùnzhí's Wén'ān and other twenty-eight prefectures and counties.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Shāndōng's Cáo and Qíhé and other two counties, with differing amounts.
Duōěrdì was summoned back to the capital,
and Róngbǎo was ordered to reside in Xīníng to handle affairs.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Shūmíng, the General of Suīyuǎrchéng, passed away.
Yùnzhe was transferred to replace him.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
arrears of grain silver from previous years were remitted for Shāndōng's Huìmín and other fifteen prefectures, counties, and garrisons.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Zhōu Rénjì was dismissed
for his stubborn insistence on opening the Nánmíng River,
which ruined agriculture and burdened the people.
Qiáo Guāngliè was appointed as the Governor of Guìzhōu.
On the *guǐhài* day,
an order was given to thoroughly investigate the border with Russia.
In the second month, on the *jǐsì* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Jiāngsū's Gāoyóu and other eleven prefectures and counties, and Ānhuī's Tàihé and other five prefectures and counties.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Yǐn Jìshàn was appointed as a Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, crossed the river,
and inspected the Qīngkǒu East Dam and Huìjì Sluice.
Ālǐgǔn was appointed as a Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard,
and Gāo Jìn as a Grand Minister of the Interior.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Cháoxiǎn paid tribute.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Kazakh envoy Cèbókè and others were granted an audience at the imperial temporary residence,
and were bestowed with various robes and caps.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, crossed the Yangtze River,
and reviewed the troops at Jīngkǒu.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the Emperor visited Jiāoshān.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, visited Sūzhōufǔ.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
last year's land tax for flood victims in Hénán's Xiángfú and other forty-three prefectures and counties was remitted.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the Emperor visited the Temple of Confucius.
On the first day of the third month, *jiǎwǔ*,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, visited Hángzhōufǔ.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Emperor visited Hǎiníng to inspect the sea dike.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Húběi's Qiánjiāng and other nine prefectures, counties, and garrisons.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Emperor reviewed the troops.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
outstanding land and poll tax, military provisions, and grain transport taxes for successive years in Jiāngsū and Zhèjiāng were remitted,
as well as the salt tax in waterside areas.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
relief was provided for last year's flood victims in Shāndōng's Qíhé and other five prefectures and counties.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Emperor visited Guāncháo Pavilion.
Shěn Chū and another person, *gòngshēng* who had been specially tested in Zhèjiāng, were granted the *jǔrén* degree,
and were both appointed Grand Secretaries of the Grand Secretariat, along with Sūn Shìyì and another person who had obtained the *jìnshì* degree.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, inspected the weaving workshops.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the imperial procession returned.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Qián Chénqún was given the title of Minister of Justice.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, crossed the Yangtze River.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
orders were given to dredge and construct dikes for various rivers in Zhílì,
using public works as a form of relief.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the Guīsuī Circuit of Shānxī was moved to Suīyuǎrchéng.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the Emperor offered sacrifices at the Mausoleum of Míng Tàizǔ,
reviewed the troops,
and visited the residence of Yǐn Jìshàn, the Governor-General of the two Jiāng provinces.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
this year's land tax was remitted for Jiāngsū's Jiāngníng and Sūzhōu,
and for the counties attached to Hángzhōu.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Chéng Jìnfāng and four other *shēngyuán* who had been specially tested in Jiāngnán were granted the *jǔrén* degree,
and were both appointed Grand Secretaries of the Grand Secretariat, along with Wú Tàilái and two other people who had obtained the *jìnshì* degree.
On the *rénxū* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, crossed the Yangtze River.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day of Gēngwǔ,
the Emperor inspected Gāojiāyàn (Gaojia Embankment).
An imperial edict was issued to construct brickwork from Jìyùn Dàbà to the Yùnkǒu (Grand Canal entrance).
The Emperor accompanied the Empress Dowager across the river.
Gù Rǔxiū, the Senior Deputy Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, was dispatched as an envoy to Ānnán (Annam).
He presumptuously sent a letter to question and reprimand the king,
and was stripped of his office.
On the day of Guǐyǒu,
Prince Zhuāng Yǔnlù and others were ordered to escort the Empress Dowager back to the capital by water.
The Emperor landed and inspected the river from Xúzhōu (Xuzhou).
On the day of Jiǎxū,

the previous year's flood-damaged tax quotas were remitted for Rénché (Renhe) and ten other counties in Zhèjiāng (Zhejiang), one prefecture in Húzhōu (Huzhou), and Rénché (Renhe) and five other salt fields.
On the day of Gēngchén,
the Emperor offered sacrifices at the temple of Mèngzǐ (Mencius),
and paid respects at the temple of the Former Sage (Confucius).
On the day of Xīnsì,
the Emperor visited Kǒnglín (Confucius Forest).
Relief was provided for the previous year's hail disaster in Āndìng (Anding) and ten other prefectures and counties in Gānsù (Gansu).
On the day of Rénwǔ,
the previous year's flood-damaged tax quotas were remitted for Qíhé (Qihe) and forty-four other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Shāndōng (Shandong).
On the day of Wùzǐ,
the Empress Dowager disembarked,
and resided at the traveling palace in Dézhōu (Dezhou).
On the day of Jǐchǒu,
the Emperor saw the Empress Dowager off onto the boat.
On the day of Gēngyín,
Liú Tǒngxūn was ordered to jointly investigate matters related to dredging and constructing defenses in Jǐngzhōu (Jingzhou).
On the day of Xīnmǎo,
arrears of taxes were remitted for Dàxīng (Daxing) and ten other prefectures, counties, and departments in Shùnzhí (Shunzhi).
In the fifth month, on the day of Jiǎwǔ,
Èlǔtè È'ěrqídásùn, an attendant at the Qiánqīngmén (Gate of Heavenly Purity), was awarded
the title of third-class Earl for his diligent and courageous conduct.
Relief was provided for the previous year's flood in Shòuzhōu (Shouzhou) and ten other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Ānhuī (Anhui).
On the day of Yǐwèi,
the Emperor arrived at Zhuōzhōu (Zhuozhou).
The Khazakh tributary envoys Ātǎhǎi and others were granted an audience,
and bestowed with varying caps and robes.

Relief was provided for the previous year's flood-affected households in Cāngzhōu (Cangzhou) and seven other prefectures and counties belonging to Chánglú (Changlu), and Yánzhèn (Yanzhen) and seven other salt fields,
with varying tax remissions.
On the day of Xīnchǒu,
the Emperor went to Huángxīnzhuāng (Huangxinzhuang) to welcome the Empress Dowager to reside at Chàngchūnyuán (Changchun Garden).
Relief was provided for the previous year's flood in Wǔlíng (Wuling) and four other prefectures and counties in Húnán (Hunan),
with varying remissions of tax quotas.
On the day of Guǐmǎo,
tax quotas for waterlogged wasteland in Hóngxiàn (Hongxian) and four other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Ānhuī (Anhui) were abolished.
On the day of Wùshēn,
Èbì was transferred to become the Governor of Shǎnxī (Shaanxi).
Zhālāfēng'ā was appointed as the Senior Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard of the Bordered White Banner.
On the day of Guǐchǒu,
Wōhé was appointed as the Grand Minister of the Imperial Household Department.
In the intercalary fifth month, on the first day, Guǐhài,
Qīngbǎo (Qingbao) was summoned to the capital
due to his old age.
Géshètú (Geshetu) was transferred to become the General of Shèngjīng (Shengjing),
with Cháoquán (Chaoquan) acting in his stead.
On the day of Dīngmǎo,
the previous year's flood-damaged tax quotas were remitted for Qiánjiāng (Qianjiang) and nine other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Húběi (Hubei).
On the day of Xīnsì,
Nàyántài's (Nayantai's) property was confiscated.
On the day of Xīnmǎo,
Rúsōng (Rusong), the General of Xī'ān (Xi'an), was ordered to inherit the title of Prince Xìnjùn (Xinjün).
Xiūlíng (Xiuling), the son of Dézhāo (Dezhao), inherited Rúsōng's (Rusong's) ducal title.
Sōngchūn (Songchun), the Commander of Cháhā'ěr (Chahar), was transferred to become the General of Xī'ān (Xi'an),
and Bā'ěrpǐn (Barpin) replaced him.
In the sixth month, on the day of Dīngyǒu,
the previous year's flood-damaged tax quotas were remitted for Gù'ān (Guan) and seventy-four other prefectures, counties, and departments in Zhílì (Zhili).
On the day of Rén'yín,
Shěn Qílǐ (Shen Qili), a compiler who had retired after assisting with the recent Southern Tour, was summoned to the capital,
and Fēng Hào (Feng Hao) and thirteen other officials who had been demoted or dismissed for various reasons were granted an audience.
On the day of Yǐsì,
in response to the tribute from Kù'ěrlè Bókè (Kuerle Beg) and others,
an edict was issued to grant rewards based on their value.
It was also generally announced to all cities
that all forms of tribute from outside major ceremonies should be stopped.
On the day of Jǐyǒu,
in recognition of the former General Bāndì (Bandi) and Grand Councillor Èróng'ān's (Erong'an's) loyal and complete devotion in Yīlí (Yili),
it was ordered that a memorial tablet be set up behind the Guāndì Miào (Guan Di Temple) in Yīlí (Yili) for offerings.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day of Rénxū,
as fugitives from the Sānshuǐ Fǔ (Sanshui Prefecture) in Cháoxiǎn (Joseon) had crossed the border and caused trouble,
Hénglù (Henglu) and others were ordered to investigate the border area.
On the day of Guǐhài,
the previous year's flood-damaged tax quotas were remitted for Shòuzhōu (Shouzhou) and sixteen other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Ānhuī (Anhui).
On the day of Wùchén,
the Emperor accompanied the Empress Dowager on an inspection tour to Mùlán (Mulan),
and five-tenths of the current year's grain and money taxes were remitted for the areas passed through.
On the day of Yǐhài,
as Huòhàn (Kokand) had invaded and occupied Èdégēnè Ājìbǐbùlǔtè (Edegen’e Ajibibuluote) and other places like Èsī (Esi),
Yǒngguì (Yonggui) was ordered to issue a proclamation to Huòhàn (Kokand) to return them.
In the eighth month, on the day of Gēngzǐ,
Gùlèzhá (Gulezha) and Wūhā'ěrlǐkè (Uharlike) were built in Yīlí (Yili),
and named Suídìng (Suiding) and Ānyuǎn (Anyuan).
The Emperor accompanied the Empress Dowager back to reside at the Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng (Mountain Resort).
On the day of Jiǎchén,
Tuō'ēnduō (Tu'endo) observed mourning leave.
Míngshān (Mingshan) was transferred to act as Governor of Guǎngdōng (Guangdong),
Sūchāng (Suchang) concurrently acted in his stead,
Tāngpìn (Tangpin) became Governor of Jiāngxī (Jiangxi),
Sòng Bāngsuí (Song Bangsui) became Governor of Húběi (Hubei),
and Àibìdá (Aibida) concurrently acted in his stead.
On the day of Rénzǐ,

arrears of taxes were remitted for Wén'ān (Wen'an) and seventeen other prefectures, counties, and departments in Shùnzhí (Shunzhi), and the current year's flood-damaged tax quotas for Nínghé (Ninghe) and five other counties.
On the day of Bǐngchén,
an imperial rescript was granted to the Commander of Cháhā'ěr (Chahar).
Chuòlèduō (Chuoleduo), the General of Hēilóngjiāng (Heilongjiang), died,
and Guóduōhuān (Guoduohuan) was transferred to replace him.
In the ninth month, on the day of Guǐhài,
Tǎ'ěrbāhāqìn Èlǔtè Bāsāng (Tarbakhchin Elute Basang), who had come to defect from the Khazakhs, was awarded silver brocade.
On the day of Gēngwǔ,
the Emperor accompanied the Empress Dowager on their return journey.
On the day of Xīnwèi,
Sùlètǎnshā (Suletansha) of Bādákèshān (Badakshan) sent envoys to pay tribute.
On the day of Dīngchǒu,
Míngrén (Mingren), a bodyguard of the Qiánqīngmén (Gate of Heavenly Purity), was ordered to take an imperial physician to attend to Hú Bǎozhuàn's (Hu Baozhuan's) illness.
Relief was provided for the flood in Qíhé (Qihe) and thirty-five other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Shāndōng (Shandong),
and tax quotas were remitted.
On the day of Jiǎshēn,
a castle was built in Wūlǔmùqí (Urumqi).
The cities were named Níngbiān (Ningbian) and Jíhuái (Jihuai),
and the forts were named Xuānrén (Xuanren), Huáiyì (Huaiyi), Lèquán (Lequan), Bǎochāng (Baochang), Huìlái (Huilai), and Lǚfēng (Lvfeng).
On the day of Wùzǐ,
Fùdé (Fude), President of the Court of Colonial Affairs and Senior Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard, was
stripped of his office and arrested for extorting horses and livestock from Mongol princes and dukes.
On the day of Jǐchǒu,
Xīnzhù (Xinzhu) was appointed President of the Court of Colonial Affairs,
and Míngruì (Mingrui) was appointed Senior Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard of the Bordered White Banner.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day of Xīnmǎo,
Chén Hóngmóu (Chen Hongmou) was transferred to become Governor of Húnán (Hunan),
Sòng Bāngsuí (Song Bangsui) acted in his stead,
Zhuāng Yǒugōng (Zhuang Yonggong) became Governor of Jiāngsū (Jiangsu),
Xióng Xuépéng (Xiong Xuepeng) became Governor of Zhèjiāng (Zhejiang),
Féng Qián (Feng Qian) became Governor of Guǎngxī (Guangxi),
and Gù Jìměi (Gu Jimei) protected him.
On the day of Guǐsì,
because Miǎnmù Gōngxián Yàn (Mianmu Gongxian Yan) had burned and killed the entire family of Dāo Pàichūn (Dao Paichun), the tǔsī (native chieftain) of Mènglián (Menglian),
he was ordered to be executed by beheading,
and his head was displayed to the public.
On the day of Guǐmǎo,
as Āi Wūhàn Hán Āihāmòtèshā (Ai Wuxan Khan Aihamotesha) sent envoys to pay tribute,
governors-general and governors along the route were ordered to prepare banquets,
and Èlèdēng'é (Eledeng'e) was ordered to escort them.
On the day of Yǐsì,
a General for Yīlí (Yili) and other places was established,
with Míngruì (Mingrui) as the appointee.
It was ordered that a city be built in Kēbùduō (Kobdo).
On the day of Jǐyǒu,
relief was provided for the flood, hail, and frost disasters in Bàzhōu (Bazhou) and sixty-three other prefectures, counties, and departments in Shùnzhí (Shunzhi),
and the current year's flood-damaged tax quotas were remitted for Qīnghé (Qinghe) and seventeen other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Jiāngsū (Jiangsu).
On the day of Jiǎyín,
relief was provided for the flood in Rénché (Renhe) and twenty-eight other prefectures, counties, garrisons, and salt fields in Zhèjiāng (Zhejiang).
On the day of Dīngsì,
Tōng Fúshòu (Tong Fushou), the Magistrate of Fèngtiān Fǔ (Fengtian Prefecture), was
dismissed from office and prosecuted for conniving with the Chief Magistrate Gāo Jǐn (Gao Jin) to extort merchants.
In the eleventh month, on the first day, Jǐwèi,
the Grand Canal in Dézhōu (Dezhou), Shāndōng (Shandong) was dredged.
On the day of Gēngshēn,
Counselor Ministers for Yīlí (Yili) were established,
with Àilóng'ā (Ailong'a) and Yīlètú (Yiletu) as the appointees.
On the day of Xīnyǒu,
Commandant Ministers for Yīlí (Yili) were established.

Míngruì (Mingrui) and others were ordered to lead troops to expel the Khazakhs who were grazing across the border in Hālàbāhā (Halabaha) and other places on the south side of Mount Tǎ'ěrbāhātái (Tarbagatai).
On the day of Wùchén,
as Shābātú (Shabatu), the leader of the Sàlǔbùlǔtè (Sarubulute), returned the horses and other goods plundered from Huòhàn (Kokand) traders,
Yǒngguì (Yonggui) and others were ordered to appropriately reward him.
The Hūshíqíbùlǔtè (Hushiqibulute), who had been invaded by Huòhàn (Kokand), came to defect,
and were ordered to move to Ālākètú Hūlè (Alaktu Hule) and other places to graze.
On the day of Gēngwǔ,
Bósīhélè (Bosihele) was appointed the Alliance Leader of the Dù'ěrbótè (Dörbet),
and two Deputy Generals were established,
with Chēlìng Wūbāshí (Cheling Ubashi) as the Right Wing Deputy General,
and Bāsāng (Basang) as the Left Wing Deputy General.
On the day of Xīnwèi,
a new city was built in Kāshígá'ěr (Kashgar).
On the day of Rénshēn,
the Assistant Commander of the Pínglǔ Yíng (Pinglu Camp) in Shānxī (Shanxi) was changed to a Commander,
and the previously established Garrison Commander of the Central Army and the Commander of Jǐngpíng Yíng (Jingping Camp) were abolished.
On the day of Bǐngzǐ,
Nú'ěrlái (Nurlei) of Khazakh and Hāyǎkè (Hayake) of Wū'ěrgēnqí (Urgench) sent envoys to pay tribute.
On the day of Jiǎshēn,
Fāng Guānchéng (Fang Guancheng) was ordered to emulate Hénán (Henan) in dredging roads and ditches.
Relief was provided for the current year's ice, hail, frost, and snow disasters in Gāolán (Gaolan) and twenty other departments, prefectures, and counties in Gānsù (Gansu).
On the day of Wùzǐ,
river channels and ditches in Shòuzhāng (Shouzhang) and other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng (Shandong) were dredged.
In the twelfth month, on the *gēngyín* day,
Grand Secretary Shǐ Yízhí (史貽直) requested retirement due to old age and illness.
An exceptional imperial edict expressed solace and requested him to remain,
ordering that he need not concurrently oversee the Ministry of Public Works (Gōngbù),
to show compassion.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Neyaz Beg (呢雅斯伯克) of Kashmir (Kèshénmǐěr) requested an imperial audience,
which was granted.
Khoqand (Huòhǎn) submitted a letter,
claiming the former territory of the Burut (Bùlǔtè) Os (鄂斯) as its own.
An imperial edict instructed Yǒngguì (永貴) and others to issue a stern dispatch ordering its return.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
regarding the Beg (Bókè) of Khoqand's (Huòhǎn) reply to Yǒngguì (永貴) and others, stating that a previous envoy, by imperial decree, had called him a Khan (Hán),
and wishing to make Kashgar (Kāshígáěr) the border,
an imperial edict ordered a stern dispatch to refute and reject this.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Guī Xuānguāng (歸宣光), Minister of Public Works (Gōngbù Shàngshū), passed away.
Dǒng Bāngdá (董邦達) was appointed in his place.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Nàshìtōng (納世通) was ordered to go to Kashgar (Kāshígáěr) to handle affairs,
replacing Yǒngguì (永貴) who was to return to the capital.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Badakhshan (Bādákèshān) invaded and besieged Bolor (Bólóěr).
An imperial edict instructed Xīnzhù (新柱) and others to issue a stern dispatch ordering them to cease hostilities,
and to demand the surrender of Bùlánídūn's (布拉尼敦) wife and children.
In the twenty-eighth year, spring, first month, on the *gēngshēn* day,

relief was provided to the thirty-five prefectures and counties, including Bàzhōu (霸州), in the Zhílì (直隸) province, and the thirty prefectures, counties, and garrisons, including Qíhé (齊河), in Shāndōng (山東) province, for flood disasters, with varying amounts.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Emperor proceeded to the Zǐguāng Gé (紫光閣),
and hosted a banquet for envoys from the various tribes of Afghan (Ài wū hǎn), Badakhshan (Bādákèshān), Khoqand (Huòhǎn), and Kazakh (Hāsàkè).
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor conducted a grand review at the Xīchǎng (西廠) of the Chàngchūnyuán (暢春園),
ordering the envoys from various tribes to observe.
Fǎqǐ (法起) was appointed as the General-in-Chief (Dūtǒng) of Guīhuàchéng (歸化城).
On the *rénshēn* day,
Àguì (阿桂) was ordered to serve in the Grand Council (Jūnjīchù).
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Hú Bǎochuán (胡寶瑔), Governor (Xúnfǔ) of Hénán (河南), passed away.
Yè Cúnrén (葉存仁) was appointed as Governor (Xúnfǔ) of Hénán (河南).
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Nàshìtōng (納世通) was appointed as Councillor Minister (Cānzàn Dàchén),
stationed in Kashgar (Kāshígáěr),
to oversee all affairs in Huíjiāng (回疆).
On the *rénchén* day,
Fāng Guānchéng (方觀承) was ordered to Hénán (河南) to jointly inspect the Zhānghé (漳河) river engineering project.
On the *wùxū* day,

the Assistant General-in-Chief (Fù Dūtǒng) for Manchu (Mǎnzhōu) and Han (Hàn) Banner forces in Xī'ān (西安) was reformed into Assistant General-in-Chief of the Left and Right Wings (Zuǒ Yòuyì Fù Dūtǒng).
On the *rén'yín* day,
the Minister for Sīníng (Xīníng) Affairs was abolished.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Emperor visited Zhāoxī Líng (昭西陵), Xiào Líng (孝陵), Xiàodōng Líng (孝東陵), and Jǐng Líng (景陵).
On this day,
the imperial carriage returned.
The Deputy General (Fùjiàng) of Ürümqi (Wūlǔmùqí) was changed to Commander-in-Chief (Zǒngbīng).
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Vice Minister (Shìláng) Qiú Yuēxiū (裘曰修) was ordered to supervise water conservancy in Zhílì (直隸).
In the third month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *rénxū* day,
the assessed taxes for flood disasters in thirty-one prefectures, counties, and garrisons, including Qíhé (齊河) in Shāndōng (Shāndōng), were remitted.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor visited Tài Líng (泰陵).
On this day,
the imperial carriage returned.
Lǐ Yǒuyì (李友益), a centenarian of one hundred and three years from Níngjīn (寧津) county, and his sons, nephews, and grandsons were rewarded with silver medals and silk fabrics, with varying amounts.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
three Superintendents (Zǒngguǎn) for the Ili (Yīlí) Oirat (Élǔtè) were established,
with varying numbers of Assistant Superintendents (Fù Zǒngguǎn) and other positions.
On the *wùyín* day,
Fúdé (福德) was ordered to Kūlún (庫倫)
to work with Sāngzhāi Duōěrzì (桑齋多爾濟).
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the assessed taxes for flood disasters in fourteen prefectures, counties, and garrisons, including Qīnghé (清河) in Jiāngsū (江蘇), were remitted.
In summer, fourth month, on the *rénchén* day,
relief was provided for last year's flood disasters in seventeen prefectures, counties, and districts, including Qiántáng (錢塘) in Zhèjiāng (浙江).
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor went to Hēilóngtán (黑龍潭) to pray for rain.
On the *yǐsì* day,
it rained.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Fǎqǐ (法起) was dismissed due to corruption.
Fùliáng (傅良) was appointed as General-in-Chief (Dūtǒng) of Guīhuàchéng (歸化城).
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Qín Dàchéng (秦大成) and one hundred and eighty-eight others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with varying ranks.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the General-in-Chief (Dūtǒng) of Guīhuàchéng (歸化城) was abolished.
In the fifth month, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
Yuánmíng Yuán (圓明園) caught fire.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Minister (Shàngshū) Àguì (阿桂) was ordered to places like Bàzhōu (霸州) in Zhílì (直隸),
to jointly supervise dredging operations with Vice Minister (Shìláng) Qiú Yuēxiū (裘曰xiū) and Governor-General (Zǒngdū) Fāng Guānchéng (方觀承).
Shūhèdé (舒赫德) was appointed acting Minister of Public Works (Gōngbù Shàngshū).
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Lǐ Hé (李●), the grandson of the King of Joseon (Cháoxiān), was enfeoffed as Heir Apparent (Shìsūn).
On the *jǐsì* day,
Prince Guǒ Qīn Wáng Hóngyàn (果親王弘●) was stripped of his princely title for interfering in state affairs,
but was still granted the title of Bèilè (貝勒).
Prince Hé Qīn Wáng Hóngzhòu (和親王弘晝) was fined three years' salary for ceremonial transgressions and extravagance.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Grand Secretary Shǐ Yízhí (史貽直) passed away.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the Emperor tested officials of the Hanlin (Hànlín) Academy and Grand Secretariat (Zhànshì),
promoting Wáng Wénzhì (王文治) and two others to the first rank,
while others were promoted or demoted with varying degrees.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, went on an autumn hunt at Mùlán (木蘭).
Lǐ Shìyáo (李侍堯) was appointed Governor-General (Zǒngdū) of Húguǎng (湖廣),
Fǔdé (輔德) as Governor (Xúnfǔ) of Húběi (湖北),
with Chén Hóngmóu (陳宏謀) concurrently acting in this role.
Liú Lún (劉綸) was transferred to Minister of Revenue (Hùbù Shàngshū),
still concurrently acting as Minister of War (Bīngbù).
Chén Hóngmóu (陳宏謀) was appointed Minister of War (Bīngbù Shàngshū).
Qiáo Guāngliè (喬光烈) was transferred to Governor (Xúnfǔ) of Húnán (Húnán),
with Láicháo (來朝) acting in this role.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Cuī Yīngjiē (崔應階) was appointed Governor (Xúnfǔ) of Guìzhōu (貴州).
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Míngdé (明德) was transferred to Governor (Xúnfǔ) of Jiāngxī (江西).
Hé Qízhōng (和其衷) was appointed Governor (Xúnfǔ) of Shānxī (Shānxī).
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Fúdé (福德) was ordered to Kūlún (庫倫) to handle affairs,
still holding the acting title of Vice Minister (Shìláng) of the Court of Colonial Affairs (Lǐfànyuàn).
É'ěrjǐng'é (額爾景額) was appointed Councillor Minister (Cānzàn Dàchén),
to go to Yarkant (Yè'ěrqiāng) to handle affairs.
In the sixth month, on the *gēngyín* day,
locusts appeared in prefectures and counties, including Lìchéng (歷城) in Shāndōng (Shāndōng).
On the *rénchén* day,
relief was provided for flood, drought, frost, and hail disasters in thirty prefectures, departments, and counties, including Dídao (狄道) in Gānsù (Gānsù).
On the *wùxū* day,
Kāità (開泰) was dismissed for cowardice and evasion.
Èbì (鄂弼) was appointed Governor-General (Zǒngdū) of Sìchuān (四川),
Míngshān (明山) as Governor (Xúnfǔ) of Shǎnxī (Shǎnxī),
with Ālǐgǔn (阿里袞) acting in this role.
Āsīhā (阿思哈) as Governor (Xúnfǔ) of Guǎngdōng (廣東),
with Sūchāng (蘇昌) concurrently acting.
Āsīhā (阿思哈) was first ordered to act as Governor (Xúnfǔ) of Guǎngxī (Guǎngxī).
On the *rén'yín* day,
Èbì (鄂弼), Governor-General (Zǒngdū) of Sìchuān (四川), passed away.
Ā'ěrtài (阿爾泰) was appointed Governor-General (Zǒngdū) of Sìchuān (四川),
Cuī Yīngjiē (崔應階) as Governor (Xúnfǔ) of Shāndōng (Shāndōng),
Túlèbǐng'ā (圖勒炳阿) as Governor (Xúnfǔ) of Guìzhōu (貴州),
and Wú Dáshàn (吳達善) concurrently acting as Governor (Xúnfǔ) of Yúnnán (Yúnnán).
Liáng Shīzhèng (梁詩正) was appointed Grand Secretary (Dàxuéshì) of the Dōnggé (東閣),
and Liú Lún (劉綸) as Associate Grand Secretary (Xiébàn Dàxuéshì).
Chén Hóngmóu (陳宏謀) was transferred to Minister of Personnel (Lìbù Shàngshū),
Péng Qǐfēng (彭啟豐) as Minister of War (Bīngbù Shàngshū),
and Zhāng Tàikāi (張泰開) as Censor-in-Chief of the Left (Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ).
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the Emperor visited Prince Jiǎn Qīn Wáng's (簡親王) residence to inquire about his illness.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Prince Jiǎn Qīn Wáng Qítōng'ā (奇通阿) passed away.
Autumn, seventh month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
Yīnglián (英廉) observed mourning leave.
Shūhèdé (舒赫德) was ordered to concurrently act as Minister of Revenue (Hùbù Shàngshū),
and Liú Lún (劉綸) remained in the ministry to manage affairs.
On the *wùchén* day,
the Minister for Xīníng (西寧) Affairs was re-established,
with Qīshíwǔ (七十五) appointed to the post.
On the *jǐsì* day,
locusts appeared in prefectures and counties, including Dàchéng (大城) and Cāngzhōu (滄州) in Zhílì (直隸).
On the *gēngchén* day,
Prince Lǚ Qīn Wáng Yǔntáo (允祹) passed away.
Eighth month, on the *guǐsì* day,
the city of Ürümqi (Wūlǔmùqí) was named Díhuà (迪化),
and the city of Tènègé'ěr (特訥格爾) was named Fùkāng (阜康).
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, went to Mùlán (木蘭)
to conduct a hunt.
Ninth month, on the first day, *yǐmǎo*,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, returned and resided at the Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng (避暑山莊).
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, returned to the imperial carriage.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Líntáo (臨洮) Circuit (Dào) of Gānsù (Gānsù) was changed to the Post Road Circuit (Yìchuándào),
also inspecting Lánzhōu (蘭州) Prefecture.
The Táomín (洮岷) Circuit (Dào) was changed to the Gǒngqínjiē (鞏秦階) Sub-circuit (Fēnxún Dào).
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, returned to the capital.
Winter, tenth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
Liáng Shīzhèng (梁詩正) and Gāo Jìn (高晉) were promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent (Tàizǐ Tàifù).

Zhàohuì (兆惠), Liú Lún (劉綸), Ālǐgǔn (阿里袞), Shūhèdé (舒赫dé), Qín Huìtián (秦蕙田), Àguì (阿桂), Chén Hóngmóu (陳宏謀), Yáng Xí fú (楊錫紱), Yáng Tíngzhāng (楊廷璋), Lǐ Shìyáo (李侍堯), Sūchāng (蘇昌), and Ā'ěrtài (阿爾泰) were promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent (Tàizǐ Tàibǎo).
Zhuāng Yǒugōng (莊有恭) and Liú Zǎo (劉藻) were promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent (Tàizǐ Shàobǎo).
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Emperor personally offered sacrifices to Prince Lǚ Qīn Wáng Yǔntáo (允祹).
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the assessed taxes for flood disasters in nine prefectures and counties, including Tóngshān (銅山) in Jiāngsū (Jiāngsū), were remitted.
In the eleventh month, on the *jiǎyín* day, the first day of the month,
Chénggǔn Zhābù was summoned to the capital.
Zhālāfēng'ā was appointed acting General of Wūlǐyǎsūtái,
and Yǎláng'ā remained in Kēbùduō.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Zhāng Shīzài, Governor-General of Riverways for Hédōng, passed away.
Yè Cúnrén was appointed in his place.
Āsīhā was transferred to be Governor of Hénán,
Míngshān to be Governor of Guǎngdōng,
Míngdé to be Governor of Shǎnxī,
Fǔdé to be Governor of Jiāngxī,
and Cháng Jūn to be Governor of Húběi.
Yáng Yìngjū was concurrently appointed acting Governor of Gānsù.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Grand Secretary Liáng Shīzhèng passed away.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Yáng Tíngzhāng was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tǐrén Pavilion,
but remained in his post as Governor-General of Mǐnzhè.
In the twelfth month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
the outstanding land tax due to hail and drought in ten prefectures and counties, including Yánqìng in Zhílì, was remitted.
On the *dīnghài* day,
famine victims of drought in twelve departments and counties, including Gāolán in Gānsù, were relieved.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
flood victims in eight prefectures, counties, and garrisons, including Jìníng in Shāndōng, were relieved.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Guóduōhuān was summoned to the capital.
Fùsēng'ā was transferred to be General of Hēilóngjiāng.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Méi Juéchéng, retired Censor-in-chief of the Left, passed away.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Chuòkètú was ordered to go to Wūlǔmùqí for duty,
replacing Jīng'élǐ, who returned to the capital.
In the twenty-ninth year, in spring, the first month, on the *guǐchǒu* day, the first day of the month,
disaster victims in seven prefectures, counties, and garrisons, including Jìníng in Shāndōng, and twenty-four departments, prefectures, and counties, including Yǒngchāng in Gānsù, were relieved.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
additional relief was provided to earthquake victims in five prefectures and counties, including Jiāngchuān in Yúnnán,
and their outstanding land tax was remitted.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Cháoxiǎn paid tribute.
In the second month, on the *dīnghài* day,
Āmǐn'ěrtú was ordered to be stationed in Zàng for duty,
replacing Fúnài, who returned to the capital.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Emperor visited the Tàilíng Mausoleum.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Guānyīnbǎo was ordered to go to Yīlí,
replacing Àilóng'ā, who returned to the capital.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the outstanding land tax due to hail in Wèizhōu and drought in Wànquán county in Zhílì from the previous year was remitted.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the outstanding land tax due to floods in three prefectures, counties, and garrisons, including Miǎnyáng in Húběi, from the previous year was remitted.
In the third month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince and Grand Secretary Lái Bǎo passed away.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù was moved to be stationed in Lánzhōu,
concurrently managing the affairs of the Governor of Gānsù.
The post of Governor of Gānsù was abolished.
The Regional Commander of Gùyuán was moved back to be stationed in Xī'ān.
The Brigade General of Hézhōuzhèn was changed to Brigade General of Gùyuánzhèn.
The outstanding land tax due to floods in seven prefectures, counties, and garrisons, including Jìníng in Shāndōng, from the previous year was remitted.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the Emperor visited the residence of the late Grand Secretary Lái Bǎo to offer sacrifices.
The outstanding land tax due to floods in twenty-eight prefectures, counties, and garrisons, including Tóngshān in Jiāngsū, from the previous year was remitted.
On the *rénxū* day,
Zhàohuì was appointed acting Minister of Public Works.
Āguì was ordered to go to Xīníng to jointly select Gēluōkè tribal chiefs with Qīshíwǔ and Zhāngjiā Hútúkètú.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
drought victims in counties, including Jīn county in Gānsù, were relieved.
In the fifth month, on the *rénzǐ* day, the first day of the month,
an imperial edict forbade customs officials and tribute envoys from Guǎnghǎi from presenting pearls and similar items.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Tuō'ēnduō was appointed acting Minister of War.
In the sixth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
flood victims in prefectures and counties, including Wǔgāng in Húnán, were relieved.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Yùguì was ordered to go to the Northern Route,
replacing Zhālāfēng'ā, who returned to the capital.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Yè Cúnrén, Governor-General of Riverways for Hédōng, passed away.
Lǐ Hóng was appointed in his place.
On the *gēngyín* day,
locusts plagued prefectures and counties, including Níngyuǎn in Fèngtiān.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
flood victims in counties, including Yīngdé in Guǎngdōng, were relieved.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Sūchāng was transferred to be Governor-General of Mǐnzhè,
Lǐ Shìyáo to be Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng,
with Míngshān acting in his stead.
Wú Dáshàn was transferred to be Governor-General of Húguǎng.
Liú Zǎo was appointed Governor-General of Yúnguì.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Cháng Jūn was transferred to be Governor of Yúnnán.
Wáng Jiǎn was appointed Governor of Húběi.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Ā'ěrtài was ordered to return to Sīchuān as Governor-General.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *xīnhài* day, the first day of the month,
Yáng Yìngjū was appointed Grand Secretary,
remaining in his post as Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù.
Chén Hóngmóu was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Cháng Jūn was temporarily appointed acting Governor-General of Húguǎng,
and Liú Zǎo concurrently acting Governor of Yúnnán.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the river overflowed in prefectures and counties, including Huángméi in Húběi.
Orders were given to comfort and relieve the disaster victims.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
lake water overflowed in prefectures and counties, including Xiāngyīn in Húnán.
Orders were given to relieve and comfort the disaster victims.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor, with the Empress Dowager, hunted in Mùlán in autumn.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor, with the Empress Dowager, stayed at the Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng (Mountain Resort for Avoiding the Heat).
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
flood victims in prefectures and counties, including Dāngtú in Ānhuī, were relieved.
In the eighth month, on the *xīnsì* day,
the outstanding land tax due to drought this year in thirty-two prefectures, counties, and departments, including Gāolán in Gānsù, was remitted.
On the *rénchén* day,
Ā'ěrtài and others were instructed to inform the nine *tǔsī* (native chieftains) of Chuòsījiǎbù to jointly attack Jīnchuān.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Emperor, with the Empress Dowager, toured Mùlán,
and held a hunt.
Qín Huìtián resigned due to illness.
Liú Lún was appointed acting Minister of Rites.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
two additional Chief Commanders were added for Yīlí, Yǎ'ěr and other places.
Chuòkètú was appointed Councillor-Minister of Tǎ'ěrbāhātái.
Wǔmǐtài and others were ordered to remain in Wūlǔmùqí for duty.
In the ninth month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
Āyǒng'ā, Vice Minister of Justice, was ordered to jointly adjudicate with Wú Dáshàn the case of the strike organized by commoners distributing leaflets in Xīnníng county, Húnán.
On the *guǐhài* day,
flood victims in eight counties, including Nánchāng in Jiāngxī, were relieved,
and their outstanding land tax was remitted.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Qín Huìtián, Minister of Justice, passed away.
Zhuāng Yǒugōng was appointed in his place,
temporarily remaining in his post as Governor of Jiāngsū.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Emperor, with the Empress Dowager, returned to be stationed at Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *guǐsì* day,
Qiáo Guāngliè was dismissed from office due to the Xīnníng strike case.
Túlèbǐng'ā was transferred to be Governor of Húnán.
Fāng Shìjùn was appointed Governor of Guìzhōu.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Tuō'ēnduō was appointed Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Shāndōng presented peonies.
On the *rényín* day,
disaster victims in six prefectures and counties, including Shàngyuán in Jiāngsū, were relieved.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Zhōngyīn was summoned back to the capital.
Fùmíng'ān was transferred to Yè'ěrqiāng for duty.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
flood victims in nineteen prefectures, counties, and garrisons, including Huáiníng in Ānhuī, were relieved.
In the eleventh month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
drought victims in twenty departments, prefectures, and counties, including Gāolán in Gānsù, were relieved.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
the city of Hūtúbì was completed,
and bestowed the name Jǐnghuà.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the outstanding land tax due to floods in two prefectures and counties, including Wǔgāng in Húnán, was remitted.
Flood and hail victims in fifteen departments, prefectures, and counties, including Gāolán in Gānsù, were relieved.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Zhàohuì, Assistant Grand Secretary and Minister of Revenue, passed away.
The Emperor personally offered sacrifices.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Ālǐgǔn was appointed Minister of Revenue and Assistant Grand Secretary.
Tuō'ēnduō was transferred to be Minister of War.
Wǔjí was appointed Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs,
and Zhàodé was appointed Imperial Bodyguard of the Front Gate for the Bordered Yellow Banner.
In the twelfth month, on the *wùyín* day, the first day of the month,
Chángfù was appointed Councillor-Minister of Wūlǐyǎsūtái.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
flood victims in prefectures and counties, including Huángméi in Húběi, were relieved.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Chén Déhuá, Minister of Rites, resigned due to illness.
Dǒng Bāngdá was transferred to replace him.
Yáng Tíngzhāng was appointed Minister of Public Works.
In the thirtieth year, in spring, the first month, on the *wùshēn* day,
due to the Empress Dowager's fourth tour of Jiāngnán and Zhèjiāng,
all outstanding poll tax and grain tribute due to past disasters in Jiāngsū, Ānhuī, and Zhèjiāng were remitted.
Drought victims in twenty-nine departments, prefectures, and counties, including Gāolán in Gānsù, and flood victims in four counties, including Jiānlì in Húběi, received varying degrees of relief.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Liú Lún observed mourning.
Zhuāng Yǒugōng was ordered to be Minister of Justice and Assistant Grand Secretary.
Yú Mǐnzhōng was appointed Minister of Revenue.
Míngdé was transferred to be Governor of Jiāngsū,
Hé Qízhōng to be Governor of Shǎnxī.
Zhāngbǎo was appointed Governor of Shānxī,
with Wénshòu acting in his stead.
On the *rénxū* day,
the Emperor, with the Empress Dowager, departed on the Southern Tour.
On the *guǐhài* day,
three-tenths of the outstanding land tax in the prefectures and counties of Zhílì and Shāndōng along the route were remitted.
In the second month, on the day Wùzǐ,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, crossed the Yellow River.
He inspected the wooden dragon and the Huìjì Gate at the east dam of Qīngkǒu.
Āguì was ordered to proceed to Yīlí to manage affairs.
On the day Rénchén,
outstanding arrears of land tax and miscellaneous levies on cultivated fields from Jiāngsū Prefecture and counties before the 28th year of Qiánlóng were remitted,
along with half of the current year's regular tax for the prefectures and counties traversed.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, crossed the Yangtze River.
On the day Jǐhài,
Cháoxiǎn sent tribute.
In the intercalary second month, on the first day Bǐngwǔ,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, visited Sūzhōufǔ.
The Emperor paid respects at the Confucian Temple.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
the head tax for the current year was remitted for the prefectures and counties attached to Jiāngníng, Sūzhōu, and Hángzhōu.
Half of the current year's regular tax was remitted for the prefectures and counties of Zhèjiāng traversed.
On the day Xīnhài,
Chǒudá was transferred to manage affairs in Yèěrqiāng.
Suǒlín was ordered to proceed to Kùlún to manage affairs.
Éěrjǐngé was appointed Assistant Grand Minister of Kèshígáěr.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, visited Hángzhōufǔ.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the Huí people of Wūshí rebelled,
killing the Grand Minister managing affairs, Sùchéng.
On the day Dīngsì,
Shěn Déqián and Qián Chénqún were promoted to Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
Míngruì was ordered to advance and suppress Wūshí.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Míngruì and Éěrjǐngé were appointed to oversee the military affairs of Wūshí,
with Míngruì commanding all armies.
Āguì and Míngliàng were ordered to proceed to Yīlí to manage affairs.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Shūhèdé was retained in the capital to manage affairs.
Tuō'ēnduō was appointed acting Minister of Public Works.
On the day Wùchén,
Míngshān was transferred to be Governor of Jiāngxī,
Wáng Jiǎn to be Governor of Guǎngdōng,
with Lǐ Shìyáo also acting in that capacity.
Lǐ Yīnpéi was appointed Governor of Húběi.
On the day Jǐsì,
the newly built garrison city in Yīlí was bestowed the name Huìyuǎn,
and the Huí city of Hāshí the name Huáishùn.
On the day Yǐhài,
regular taxes for the previous year's flood and drought disasters were remitted for five counties including Shàngyuán in Jiāngsū.
In the third month, on the first day Bǐngzǐ,
relief was granted for the previous year's flood disaster in seven prefectures and counties including Hànyáng in Húběi.
The Emperor visited Jiāoshān.
On the day Wùyín,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, stayed in Jiāngníngfǔ.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Emperor went to the tomb of Míng Tàizǔ to offer libations.
He visited the residence of Yǐn Jìshàn.
Guānyīnbǎo's campaign against the rebel Huí of Wūshí was unsuccessful.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Féng Qián was appointed Governor of Húnán,
Sòng Bāngsuí Governor of Guǎngxī.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, crossed the Yangtze River.
On the day Dīnghài,
Guǒ Jùnwáng Hóngzhòu died.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Grand Secretary Fùhéng and others were granted rewards from the capital's evaluations.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the Emperor inspected the Gāojiāyàn embankment,
and, accompanying the Empress Dowager, crossed the Yellow River.
