He issued an edict regarding Wǔlānáchá's abuses in over-collecting grain tax in Zhèjiāng.
On the day *Jǐwèi*,
Grand Secretary Jī Huáng was again granted an honorary banquet,
and the Emperor bestowed upon him self-composed poems.
On the day *Xīnyǒu*,
Jíqìng was ordered to jointly inspect with Sōngchūn the border from Yīng'é to Àiyáng.
On the day *Yǐchǒu*,
the regular taxes for the previous year's flood disaster in Ānhuī's Sùzhōu, Língbì, and eight other prefectures, counties, and garrisons were remitted.
The Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day *Bǐngyín*,
the Emperor visited Hēilóngtán to pray for rain.
Mǐn Éyuán was dismissed.
Fú Sōng was transferred to be Governor of Jiāngsū.
Hé Yùchéng was made Governor of Ānhuī.
On the day *Gēngwǔ*,
due to Shūlín's deceptive second memorial,
he was submitted to the board for severe deliberation,
but retained in his position.
Mǐn Éyuán was stripped of his post and arrested for questioning.
On the day *Rénshēn*,
the regular taxes for the fifty-fourth year's flood disaster in Hénán's Yǒngchéng were remitted.
On the day *Guǐyǒu*,
Sūn Shìyì was made Governor-General of Sìchuān,
and Lǐ Shìjié was made Minister of War.
On the day *Yǐhài*,
Shí Yùnyù and ninety-six others were bestowed with varying degrees of the *Jìnshì* examination degree.
On the day *Jǐmǎo*,
three-tenths of the regular taxes for Shānxī's Tàiyuán, Liáozhōu, and sixteen other prefectures and departments, as well as Guīhuàchéng and other areas, were remitted.
In the fifth month, on the day *Gēngyín*,
the Emperor visited the Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng.
On the day *Gēngzǐ*,
Lí Wéiqí was bestowed with an official title of the third rank.
On the day *Rényín*,
taxes and levies for thirty-nine tribes belonging to Xīzàng were remitted.
On the day *Jǐyǒu*,
Shūlín was stripped of his post and arrested for questioning.
Fú Sōng concurrently served as acting Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng.
Hán Hóng went to Jiāngnán to assist in river works.
In the sixth month, on the day *Rénzǐ*,
Sūn Shìyì was transferred to be Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng.
Bǎoníng was appointed acting Governor-General of Sìchuān.
Yǒngbǎo was appointed acting General of Yīlí.
On the day *Yǐmǎo*,
Chén Yòngfū was made Governor of Guǎngxī.
Mǐn Éyuán was sentenced to decapitation.
On the day *Dīngsì*,
the regular taxes for the previous year's flood disaster in Zhílì's Bàzhōu and fifty-three other departments, prefectures, and counties, as well as banner lands in various prefectures, were remitted.
On the day *Wùwǔ*,
miscellaneous grain taxes for the Miáo people in Húnán's Qiánzhōu and four other departments and counties were abolished.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day *Jǐchǒu*,
the King of Ānnán, Ruǎn Guāngpíng, had an imperial audience.
On the day *Gēngyín*,
Zhū Guī was made Governor of Ānhuī.
On the day *Jiǎwǔ*,
relief was provided for flood victims in Zhílì's Cháoyáng and Tiānjīn.
On the day *Bǐngshēn*,
relief was provided for flood victims in Fèngtiān's Jǐnzhōu Jiǔguāntái,
and Shāndōng's Píngyuán, Yǔchéng, and other counties.
On the day *Dīngyǒu*,
Minister of War Lǐ Shìjié retired due to his failure to investigate his clerks.
On the day *Jǐhài*,
Liú was reinstated as Minister of War.
On the day *Wùshēn*,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
Relief was provided for flood victims in Jiāngsū's Dàngshān and other counties,
Ānhuī's Sùzhōu,
and Hénán's Yǒngchéng and Xiàyì.
The river at Wángpíngzhuāng in Jiāngsū's Dàngshān breached its banks.
Fú Sōng was ordered to go to Sùzhōu to manage the river works.
On the day *Dīngwèi*,
relief was provided for flood victims in Shāndōng's Línqīng.
In the eighth month, on the day *Gēngxū*,
Zhèng Huá, the King of Xiāmluó, presented a memorial congratulating the Emperor on his birthday,
and offered local products as tribute.
Lánggān impeached himself for failing to investigate the grain tax,
and was dismissed.
Hǎiníng was transferred to be Governor of Zhèjiāng.
Shūlín was made Governor of Shānxī.
On the day *Xīnyǒu*,
on the Emperor's eightieth birthday,
he presided over the Tàihédiàn.
Kings, *Bèilè*, *Bèizǐ*, Dukes, civil and military ministers,
Mongolian Khans, Kings, *Bèilè*, *Bèizǐ*, Dukes, *Éfù*, *Táijí*,
Huíbù Kings, Dukes, *Táijí*, *Bókè*,
Kazakhs, the King of Ānnán, Cháoxiān, Miǎndiàn, Nánzhǎng tribute envoys,
local chieftains from various provinces,
and Taiwanese indigenous people performed celebratory rituals.
After the ceremony,
banquets were held at the Níngshòugōng and Qiánqīnggōng as usual.
On the day *Jǐsì*,
Minister of Justice Kāníng'ā died.
Míngliàng replaced him.
Shūcháng was ordered to concurrently serve as acting minister.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùyín,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Sìzhōu, Ānhuī.
On the day Guǐwèi,
King Nguyễn Quang Bình of Annan was ordered to return the relatives of Lê Duy Kỳ and his former officials who were in his country.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the Emperor reviewed the soldiers of the Jiànruì Battalion.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Píngyuán and twenty-seven other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Chánglín was dismissed from his post for factual inaccuracies in judicial reviews.
Huìlíng was transferred to be the Governor of Shāndōng,
Fúníng was appointed Governor of Húběi,
and Bì Yuán concurrently served as acting governor.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Píngyuán and twenty-seven other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Bǎoníng was ordered to return to be the General of Yīlí,
and Èhuī was appointed Governor-General of Sìchuān.
On the day Rénshēn,
Fúsōng was appointed Governor of Zhèjiāng,
and Chánglín was recalled to act as Governor of Jiāngsū.
Relief was provided for the frost disaster in Gāolán and three other counties in Gānsù.
The eleventh month, on the day Dīngchǒu (the first day of the lunar month),
Pǔlín was appointed Governor of Fújiàn,
and Féng Guāngxióng was appointed Governor of Húnán.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Grand Secretary Wáng Jié was granted the title of Tàizǐ Tàibǎo,
and Ministers Péng Yuánruì, Dǒng Gào, Hú Jìtáng, Fú Cháng'ān, and General Bǎoníng were granted the title of Tàizǐ Shàobǎo.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Fùlèhún and Yǎdé were released.
On the day Wùxū,
Qìngchéng was ordered to go with Yǐn Zhuàngtú to Shānxī to audit the granaries.
On the day Rénxū,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Jǐnxiàn and three other prefectures and counties in Fèngtiān.
On the day Wùchén,
Péng Yuánruì, Minister of Personnel, was ordered to assist in the affairs of the Grand Secretariat.
In the spring of the 56th year, the first month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
relief was provided for the previous year's flood disaster in Xiāoxiàn and three other counties in Jiāngsū, and Sùzhōu and three other prefectures and counties in Ānhuī.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Wén'ān and thirty other prefectures and counties in Zhílì, and Píngyuán and twenty-seven other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Yǐn Zhuàngtú was dismissed from his post and punished for making a deceitful report.
On the day Wùxū,
Yuán Fèngmíng was executed by beheading.
Cháoxiǎn, Xiāmluó, and Miǎndiàn all sent envoys to express gratitude
and present tribute.
Rewards and banquets were given as usual.
On the day Jǐhài,
Bǎoníng was appointed Grand Minister of the Imperial Guard.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Liú Yōng was transferred to be Minister of Rites,
and Jì Yún was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
In the second month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
an edict stated:
"I diligently seek good governance
and always remain cautious.
Yǐn Zhuàngtú's presumptuous remarks,
I should take as criticism.
As an act of grace, Yǐn Zhuàngtú is exempted from punishment,
and appointed as Reader in the Grand Secretariat."
On the day Wùwǔ,
imperial examinations were held for officials such as Hanlin academicians and Grand Supervisors.
Ruǎn Yuán and two other officials were promoted to the first rank,
while others were promoted or demoted according to their performance.
In the third month, on the day Yǐhài,
relief was provided for the previous year's flood disaster victims and their banner lands in Jǐnzhōu and other places in Fèngtiān,
and taxes were remitted according to their situation.
On the day Wùyín,
the Emperor toured Pánshān.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the previous year's frost disaster taxes in Gāolán and three other counties in Gānsù were remitted.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Yǒngbǎo was appointed Grand Minister.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
the previous year's flood disaster taxes in Línqīng and thirty other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Shāndōng were remitted.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Péng Yuánruì was demoted to Vice Minister due to favoritism.
Sūn Shìyì was appointed Minister of Personnel.
Shūlín was appointed Governor-General of the Liangjiāng,
with Chánglín temporarily acting.
Féng Guāngxióng was transferred to be Governor of Shānxī.
Jiāng Shèng was appointed Governor of Húnán.
In the fifth month, on the day Gēngyín,
Chánglín was appointed Governor of Jiāngsū.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the Emperor went on an autumn hunt at Mùlán.
On the day Xīnc丑,
the Emperor sojourned at the Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng (Mountain Resort).
The sixth month, on the day Jiǎchén (the first day of the lunar month),
the previous year's flood disaster taxes in Bāzhōu and sixty-nine other departments, prefectures, and counties in Zhílì were remitted.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Gēngchén,
half of the accumulated arrears of taxes in Jiāngníng and five other prefectures and departments in Jiāngsū were remitted due to disaster.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
King Méng Yǔn of Miǎndiàn was rewarded
for sending back people from the interior who had been detained.
On the day Jǐhài,
the previous year's flood disaster taxes in Sùzhōu and nineteen other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Ānhuī were remitted.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
arrears of taxes in Cháoyì and two other counties in Shǎnxī were remitted.
In the eighth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
Lātènàxīdì was appointed Jìsàkè First-Rank Tábùnáng of Kālāqìn.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the Emperor went on an imperial hunt at Mùlán.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Emperor went on an imperial hunt.
The Gurkhas, having lured and surrounded lamas and gabluns with outstanding debts,
disturbed Xīzàng.
Èhuī, Governor-General of Sìchuān, and General Chéngdé were ordered to suppress them.
Sūn Shìyì was ordered to act as Governor-General of Sìchuān.
On the day Jǐsì,
Fúkāng'ān was ordered to come to the capital to celebrate his mother's birthday,
and Guō Shìxūn acted as Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng.
The Gurkhas captured various strongholds in Dìngrì, Xīzàng,
and occupied Jìlóng.
In the ninth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
the Emperor returned to sojourn at the Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng.
On the day Gēngchén,
Sōngchūn was recalled to the capital,
Línníng was appointed General of Shèngjīng,
and Héngxiù was transferred to be General of Jílín.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the Emperor returned.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Dánggǔtè troops and Dámù Ménggǔ troops were defeated in resisting the Gurkhas.
Gōng Zhāshénàmùzhálè of Dánggǔtè and Xiélǐng Zébājié of Dámù died.
Èlèdēngbǎo and other Imperial Bodyguards of the Qiánqīng Gate were ordered to go to the military camp in Xīzàng.
On the day Rénchén,
Bǎotài was dismissed from his post for cowardice.
Kuílín was ordered to go to Xīzàng to manage affairs.
Shūlián was granted the title of Vice Commandant,
to assist in the management.
The Dálài Lǎma and others were commended
for firmly defending the Bùdálā Palace.
Liú Yōng was ordered to act as Minister of Personnel.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
with the Gurkhas besieging Zhāshílúnbù,
Èhuī and others were ordered to advance and suppress them.
On the day Xīnc丑,
arrears of taxes in Guǎngníng County, Fèngtiān, were remitted.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Yǐsì,
Mǐn Èyuán was pardoned of his crime.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Gurkhas entered Zhāshílúnbù,
and then fled.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Bāyánsān, Minister of Revenue, was dismissed from his post for overestimating the cost of city construction.
Fú Cháng'ān was transferred to replace him.
Jīn Jiǎn and Péng Yuánruì were appointed Manchu and Han Ministers of Works, respectively.
On the day Bǐngchén,
with Annan opening its borders for trade,
the Tongpan (Assistant Prefect) of Lóngzhōu, Guǎngxī, was changed to Tongzhi (Assistant Prefect).
On the day Yǐchǒu,
an edict stated that princes and high officials need not hold the honorary title of Yi Zheng (Deliberative Minister).
The eleventh month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
Fúkāng'ān was granted the title of General,
and Hǎilánchá and Kuílín were appointed Counselors,
to campaign against the Gurkhas.
On the day Xīnsì,
Èhuī and Chéngdé were dismissed from their posts.
Huìlíng was appointed Governor-General of Sìchuān,
Kuílín was appointed General of Chéngdū,
and Jíqìng was appointed Governor of Shāndōng.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Chén Huái was appointed Governor of Guìzhōu.
The twelfth month, on the day Xīnhài,
Hǎilánchá and others, as well as the Suǒlún and Dáhú'ěr troops, were ordered to proceed to Xīzàng via Xīníng.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Dū'ěrjiā was recalled to the capital.
Míngliàng was appointed General of Hēilóngjiāng,
and Míngxīng was appointed Counselor Minister of Kāshígá'ěr.
In the spring of the 57th year, the first month, on the day Rénshēn,
Lǐ Zhìyǐng, a retired Court Chamberlain of the Imperial Stud, who had served seven generations, was awarded an imperial calligraphy plaque.
Arrears of taxes in Fèngtiān, Zhílì, Ānhuī, Húnán, and Guǎngdōng were remitted.
On the day Yǐhài,
the Dálài Lǎma again sent Dānjīnbānzhū'ěr and others to secretly negotiate peace with the Gurkhas,
and an edict was issued to stop them.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Bā Zhōng was posthumously criticized for unauthorized peace negotiations with the Gurkhas and promising annual silver payments.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Sū Líng'ā was appointed Minister of Justice.
In the second month, on the day Rén Yín,
Chéngdé reported a victory against the bandits at Pāijiǎlǐng.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Grand Secretary Āguì and others, Ministers Fú Cháng'ān and others, Vice Ministers Démíng and others, Governor-General Fúkāng'ān and others, and Governor Chánglín and others were given rewards.
The offices of Hedong Salt Commissioner and Salt Transport Commissioner were abolished.
The Hedong Circuit of Shānxī was relocated to Yùnchéng.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Fifteenth Prince, Jiāqīn Wáng, was ordered to offer sacrifices to the Former Teacher Kǒngzǐ.
The previous year's drought disaster taxes in Jǐnzhōufǔ, Fèngtiān, were remitted.
On the day Jǐsì,
Vice Minister Hélín was ordered to manage Xīzàng affairs.
Èhuī and others reported the recapture of Nièlāmù,
but an edict criticized them for their delay.
In the third month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
the Emperor went to Xīlíng
and toured Wǔtái Shān.
The passing regions were exempted from three-tenths of their money and grain taxes for the current year.
On the day Wùyín,
the request of Yǔnjì Lónghūtúkètú
for the dharma name "Huìtōng Chánshī"
was granted.
Pàkèlǐ, the battalion officer (yíngguān), and his Tibetan troops, having recovered Zhémèngxióng and Zōngmù,
were rewarded.
On the day Xīnsì,
the Emperor paid homage at Tàilíng and Tàidōnglíng.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the accumulated arrears of rice and grain from Dàxīng and eight other zhou and xian in Zhílì were remitted.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Fúkāng'ān was promoted to Grand General (dàjiāngjūn).
On the day Gēngyín,
Wǔtái was exempted from five-tenths of its money and grain taxes for the current year,
and the outstanding arrears from Dàtóng and Shuòpíng prefectures (fǔ) were remitted.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the Emperor sojourned at Wǔtái Shān.
In summer, the fourth month, on the first day Jǐhài,
Lǐ Shìzhèng, the Amban (bànshì dàchén) of Hétián, was found to have failed to detect Màimǎtènízá'ěr's (Muhammad Nizam) actions,
and was sent to the board (bù) for strict deliberation.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the Emperor inspected the Hūtú Hé (Hutuo River).
Gòngchǔkèzhábù was appointed Counselor Amban (cānzàn dàchén) of Wūlǐyǎsūtái.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Emperor offered sacrifices at the temple of Dì Yáo.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Emperor returned to the capital (jīngshī).
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the Emperor went to Hēilóngtán to pray for rain.
The Ministry of Justice (Xíngbù) was ordered to clear minor cases in prisons,
reducing sentences for crimes below penal servitude.
In the intercalary fourth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
due to the prolonged drought,
an edict was issued to Táiwān and coastal provinces to thoroughly investigate cases of murder and robbery,
without intentionally being overly severe.
The extra taxes from the previous year's drought in Tāngyīn and five other xian in Hénán were remitted.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
due to the prolonged drought,
an edict was issued to seek criticism.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
it rained.
For the loss of Zháshílúnbù (Tashilhunpo),
Zhòngbā Hūtúkètú and Zīzhòng Lǎmā and others were punished.
Hé Lín and È Huī were ordered to convey the imperial decree to the Dálài Lǎmā and others.
In the fifth month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
it was decided that the kingdom of Ānnán would pay tribute once every two years,
and send envoys to court once every six years.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Emperor visited Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng,
and the passing regions were exempted from five-tenths of their money and grain taxes.
On the day Wùshēn,
Chánglín was transferred to be Governor (xúnfǔ) of Shānxī,
and Qífēng'é was appointed Governor of Jiāngsū.
On the day Xīnhài,
the request of Huòhǎn Érdéníbóké Nà'ěrbātú (Alikhan Erdeni Bakhadur) to send envoys to pay tribute was granted.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Emperor sojourned at Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng.
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎxū,
Fúkāng'ān reported the capture of Cāmshuǎ Āi, an strategic pass occupied by the Guō'ěrkā (Gorkhas).
On the day Dīngchǒu,
disaster relief was provided for flood victims in Nánfēng and Guǎngchāng, Jiāngxī.
Fúkāng'ān reported the annihilation of the bandits at Mǎgá'ěrxìlǚjiǎ Shānliáng.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Fúkāng'ān and others reported the capture of Jìlóng.
On the day Xīnsì,
Chén Huái was transferred to be Governor of Jiāngxī,
and Féng Guāngxióng was appointed Governor of Guìzhōu.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Fúkāng'ān and others reported the capture of Rèsuǒ Qiáo.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Fúkāng'ān and others reported the capture of Xiébùlǔ Zhài.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Jiǎchén,
disaster relief was provided for drought victims in Héjiān and other places in Zhílì,
and for locust infestations in Wǎnpíng, Yùtián and other zhou and xian in Shùnzhí.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Fúkāng'ān and others captured the Guō'ěrkā Eastern Jué Shānliáng,
and encampments and checkpoints in Yǎ'ěrsàilā and other places;
Chéng Dé and others captured Zhámù, Tiěsuǒ Qiáo and other places.
In the eighth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Chéng Dé captured Duōluòkǎ, Lónggāng and other places.
Sūn Shìyì was ordered to be stationed in Qiánzàng (Ü-Tsang) to supervise grain transport.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Fúkāng'ān was appointed Grand Secretary (dàxuéshì) of Wǔyīng Diàn,
and Sūn Shìyì was appointed Grand Secretary of Wényuān Gé.
Jīn Jiǎn and Liú Yǒng were transferred to be Ministers (shàngshū) of the Ministry of Personnel (Lìbù),
Hé Lín was appointed Minister of the Ministry of Public Works (Gōngbù),
Jì Yún was appointed Minister of the Ministry of Rites (Lǐbù),
and Dòu Guāngnài was appointed Censor-in-Chief (zuǒdōuyùshǐ).
On the day Gēngchén,
Bóxīng was appointed Amban of Kùlún.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Fúkāng'ān and others reported the capture of Gálèlā, Duībùmù city and checkpoints,
with Āmàntài and Mò'ěrgēnbǎo dying in battle.
Chéng Dé and others captured Lìdǐ and Dàshān bandit strongholds.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Fúkāng'ān reported that the Guō'ěrkā chief Lātènàbādù'ěr (Rana Bahadur) and others had sought surrender.
The Emperor, considering their repentance and plea for surrender,
granted it,
and ordered the army to return.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
disaster relief was provided for drought victims in Xiánníng and six other zhou and xian in Shǎnxī.
In the ninth month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Jǐhài,
the merits of the campaign against Guō'ěrkā were discussed.
Fúkāng'ān was awarded the First Class Light Chariot Commandant (yīděng qīngchē dūwèi);
Hǎilánchá's peerage was promoted from Second Class Duke (èrděng gōng) to First Class;
the rewards for Sūn Shìyì and others were deliberated and varied.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Emperor ordered Fúkāng'ān, Sūn Shìyì and others to consult on the aftermath of Xīzàng (Tibet).
Imperial Bodyguard (yùqián shìwèi) Huìlún and others were ordered to carry the Golden Urn (jīnbēnbābíng) to Xīzàng,
to contain the names of the Hūbìlèhǎn (Hübileγan),
which would be drawn by the Dálài Lǎmā and others in public.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the titles and ranks of the Guō'ěrkā kings and nobles were restored,
and it was decreed that tribute would be paid once every five years.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Wùchén,
Guō'ěrkā tribute envoys arrived for an audience.
On the day Jǐsì,
disaster relief was provided for victims in Ānyáng and sixteen other xian in Hénán,
and old and new extra taxes were remitted or deferred with varying degrees.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Jī Huáng and Ā Guì were dismissed as Chancellors of the Hanlin Academy (hànlín yuàn zhǎngyuàn xuéshì),
and Hé Shēn and Péng Yuánruì replaced them.
On the day Rénwǔ,
disaster relief was provided for drought victims in Héjiān, Rènqiū and five other zhou and xian in Zhílì,
and the extra taxes for afflicted bannermen and commoners in Shùntiān and thirteen other prefectures (fǔ) and zhou were remitted.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Guō Shìdào reported that Yīngjílì (England) had sent envoys
requesting to pay tribute via Tiānjīn,
which was granted.
On the day Dīnghài,
È Huī was stripped of his position for concealing the Guō'ěrkā's memorial of gratitude and tribute,
and handed over to Fúkāng'ān and others for strict interrogation.
Disaster relief was provided for drought victims in Xiányáng and fourteen other zhou and xian in Shǎnxī.
On the day Guǐsì,
Túsāng'ā was transferred to be General (jiāngjūn) of Suíyuǎn Chéng.
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
disaster relief was provided for drought victims in Dézhōu and twenty other zhou and xian in Shāndōng.
In the twelfth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
regulations for the training of Tánggǔtè (Tangut) Tibetan soldiers were established.
Silver was cast into coins,
with the inscription
"Qiánlóng Bǎozàng".
On the day Jiǎxū,
the extra taxes on salt fields in Chánglú Xīngguó and five other salt pans (chǎng), and Cāngzhōu and seven other zhou and xian, affected by disaster, were remitted.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Chánglín was appointed Governor of Zhèjiāng,
and Jiǎng Zhàokuí was appointed Governor of Shānxī.
Due to snow disaster on the farmlands of the Huímin (Muslims) in Yīlí,
the grain taxes for the current year were remitted.
On the day Guǐwèi,
disaster relief was provided for drought victims in Ānyáng and twenty-five other xian in Hénán.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
È Huī and others were ordered to be permanently shackled in Xīzàng.
In the first month of spring, fifty-eighth year, on the day Bǐngshēn,
disaster relief was provided for drought victims in Línxiàn and five other xian in Hénán, and Xiánníng and three other zhou and xian in Shǎnxī.
On the day Jǐhài,
disaster relief was provided for drought victims in Bǎodìng and twenty-one other zhou and xian in Zhílì.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the Hángzhōu Textile Office (zhīzào) was changed to Salt Commissioner (yánzhèng) concurrently managing textile affairs;
the Salt Intendant (yándào) was changed to Salt Transport Commissioner (yùnsī);
the customs duties of the northern and southern passes were placed under the management of the Governor.
Quándé was appointed Salt Commissioner for both Zhè (Zhèjiāng) regions.
Héngxiù returned to be General of Jílín.
On the day Yǐsì,
an imperial edict was issued to Nguyễn Quang Bình, the King of Ānnán, urging friendly relations with neighbors,
and careful guarding of the borders,
and he was bestowed with silk fabrics.
On the day Bǐngchén,
King Nguyễn Quang Bình of Ānnán died,
and his heir apparent Nguyễn Quang Toản succeeded him.
On the day Yǐhài,
the extra taxes for the previous year's drought in Ānyáng and twenty-five other xian in Hénán were remitted.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Āqímù Bóké of Kāshígé'ěr (Kashgar) was appointed Assistant Minister (xiébàn dàchén) of Kāshígé'ěr.
In the third month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
the Emperor visited Pánshān.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the Emperor sojourned at Pánshān.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Cháng Qīng, Minister of the Ministry of Rites, died,
and Démíng replaced him.
On the day Wùshēn,
an edict was issued to set up the Golden Urn at Yōnghé Gōng,
and ordered the directors (tángguān) of the Lifan Yuan (Lǐfān Yuàn) and the Zasak Lamas (zhǎngyìn zhásàkè lǎmā)
to jointly draw the Hübileγan originating from Měnggǔ (Mongolia).
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Emperor returned.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Féng Guāngxióng was transferred to be Governor of Yúnnán,
and Yīng Shàn was appointed Governor of Guìzhōu.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Hǎilánchá, the Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard (lǐng shìwèi nèi dàchén), died.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Rénshēn,
Shōngyún was appointed Grand Minister of the Imperial Household Department,
to serve as an Imperial Bodyguard.
On the day Xīnsì,
an edict was issued to establish the Jīn Bēnbā Píng (Golden Urn) at the Dàzhāo Temple in Anterior Tibet and at the Yōnghé Gōng (Lama Temple),
for the public drawing to select Hūbìlèhǎn (Living Buddhas),
in order to eradicate the corrupt practice of princes and sons of nobles privately creating Hūbìlèhǎn.
On the day Yǐyǒu,

the titles of Grand Secretary concurrently Minister, Academy Chancellor of the Hànlín Yuàn concurrently Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites, and Prefect of Shùntiān Fǔ concurrently Education Intendant were abolished.
On the day Dīnghài,
Pān Shì'ēn and eighty-one others were granted the Jinshì degree with various ranks.
On the day Wùzǐ,
it was decreed that a special grace examination (Xiāngshì Ēnkē) for the provincial level be held in the autumn of the 59th year of Qiánlóng,
and a grace examination (Huìshì Ēnkē) for the metropolitan level in the spring of the 60th year.
On the day Gēngyín,
Gūo'ěrkā returned the Dǐmǎ'ěr Zōng (Dimar Jong) area to Xīzàng.
The two places of Lājié (Lhaje) and Sādǎng (Sardang) outside the Xīzàng Card were assigned to Gūo'ěrkā.
In the fifth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
Chénglín, the Judicial Commissioner of Guǎngxī, was ordered to go to Shēnglóng Chéng (Thăng Long, Hanoi) in Ānnán,
to bestow offerings and confer investiture.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Emperor visited the Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng (Summer Resort).
On the day Jǐyǒu,
as Míngxīng had not reported on dispatching Huí (Muslim) people to Huòhàn (Kokand) and other places to manage foreign vassal affairs,
he was dismissed as Counselor Minister of Kāshígā'ěr (Kashgar),
and Yǒngbǎo was transferred to replace him.
Wǔmíwǔxùn was appointed Counselor Minister of Tǎ'ěrbāhātái (Tarbagatai),
and Gòngchǔkè Zhábù as Counselor Minister of Kēbùduō (Kobdo).
Tèchéng'é was appointed Counselor Minister of Wūlǐyǎsūtái (Uliastai).
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Fúkāng'ān was additionally enfeoffed as a First-Class Zhōngruì Jiāyǒng Gōng (Duke of Loyalty, Sharpness, Gallantry, and Bravery).
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Emperor resided at the Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng.
In the sixth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
relief was provided for earthquake victims in Tàiníng, Sìchuān.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the English tribute ships arrived in Tiānjīn.
On the day Wùzǐ,
they disembarked at Tōngzhōu.
It was ordered that a banquet be held for them in Tiānjīn.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Guǐsì,
Hélín was ordered to audit the entry and exit of Tibetan merchants.
On the day Rényín,
the English envoys were ordered to stay at Hóngyǎ Yuán,
and Jīnjiǎn and Yīlíng'ā were to arrange the tribute items separately at Yuánmíng Yuán.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
due to drought, the Ministry of Justice was ordered to clear minor cases in prisons,
reducing sentences below penal servitude.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the Emperor was in the large tent at Wànshù Yuán,
where the English chief envoy Mǎjiā'ěrnì (Macartney) and deputy envoy Sīdāngdōng (Staunton) and others were received in audience.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Fúkāng'ān was transferred to be Governor-General of Sìchuān,
and Huìlíng temporarily replaced him;
Chánglín was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng (Guangdong and Guangxi),
Jíqìng was transferred to be Governor of Zhèjiāng,
and Huìlíng was appointed Governor of Shāndōng.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the fixed tax on salt-field land affected by tidal disasters in Chánglú Guāntái and two other salt yards was remitted.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the Emperor returned to Jīngshī (the capital).
On the day Wùzǐ,
Qìngguì was appointed Minister of War.
On the day Gēngyín,
an edict was issued for the English envoys to return to their country by boat from Àomén (Macau) in Guǎngdōng via the inland waterways.
In the ninth month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
Chánglín was additionally granted the title of Tàizǐ Shàobǎo (Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent).
Shōngyún was ordered to escort the English envoys to Dìnghǎi, Zhèjiāng.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Fúníng was transferred to be Governor of Shāndōng,
and Huìlíng to be Governor of Húběi.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
due to flood disasters in Wúwéi and two other prefectures and counties in Ānhuī,
differing amounts of rations were awarded.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Guǐhài,
Ruan Guāngzǎn (Nguyễn Quang Toản), King of Ānnán, submitted a memorial to express gratitude,
offering two parts of tribute items,
of which one was accepted.
On the day Wùzǐ,
regarding Chánglín's report that the English envoy wished to submit another memorial and tribute items,
and had presented it to the Governor-General for memorialization,
an edict stated:
"This is in accordance with precedent,
and there is no other intention.
The King can be at ease.
If tribute is offered again,
there will also be no fixed annual limit."
In the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
Héníng was ordered to go to Xīzàng to assist Hélín in handling affairs.
On the day Wùwǔ,
regarding the total reported population of over 37,046,000 for all provinces in the previous year,
which was fifteen times greater than that in the 49th year of Kāngxī,
an edict stated:
"Those who produce are few,
and those who consume are many,
which will inevitably lead to increasing hardship.
Governors-general and governors of all provinces, and those responsible for caring for the people,
must earnestly admonish and guide them,
so that all cultivate a habit of frugality,
diligently engage in farming,
cherish resources, make the most of the land,
and share in the blessings of peace."
On the day Jǐwèi,
as many elephants had been offered by Ānnán and other countries,
an edict was issued to the Governors-General of Yún-Guì and Liǎngguǎng to send dispatches declining elephant tribute.
In the twelfth month, on the day Guǐwèi,
Wǔlānà was granted an audience,
and Jíqìng was appointed acting Governor-General of Mǐn-Zhè (Fujian and Zhejiang).
In the spring of the 59th year, first month, on the day Gēngyín,
three-tenths of the outstanding taxes in Zhílì, Shāndōng, and Hénán were remitted.
On the day Gēngxū,
Guǎn Gànzhēn resigned due to illness,
and Shūlín was appointed acting Governor-General of Grain Transport concurrently.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Héngxiù was stripped of his position for embezzling funds,
Bǎolín was transferred to be General of Jílín,
and Shōngyún acted in his stead.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Límízhì (Lê Duy Trị), a person from Ānnán who had sought asylum, was settled in Jiāngnán.
In the second month, on the day Gēngshēn,
as the New Year's Day and the Lantern Festival of the next year would coincide with a solar and lunar eclipse,
an edict was issued for self-reflection and cultivation,
and not to hold celebratory ceremonies.
On the day Guǐhài,
Gūo'ěrkā sent envoys to present a memorial and tribute.
On the day Dīnghài,
the construction of naval warships in Guǎngdōng was increased.
In the third month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Héngxiù was sentenced to strangulation.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the Emperor made an inspection tour to Tiānjīn,
remitting three-tenths of the fixed taxes in the areas passed through and those belonging to Tiānjīn Fǔ,
remitting outstanding taxes in Tiānjīn Fǔ,
and remitting four-tenths of outstanding taxes in Dàxīng and thirteen other prefectures and counties.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the Emperor resided in Tiānjīn Fǔ.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Réngxū,
during the seasonal prayer for rain (chángyú),
the Eighth Prince, Yí Jùnwáng Yǒngxuán, was ordered to perform the ceremony on behalf of the Emperor.
On the day Guǐhài,
the Emperor returned to Jīngshī.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the Emperor went to Hēilóngtán (Black Dragon Pool) to pray for rain.
In the fifth month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
it rained in Jīngshī.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Guō Shìxūn resigned due to illness,
Zhū Guī was transferred to be Governor of Guǎngdōng,
and Chén Yòngfū was appointed Governor of Ānhuī.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
due to drought in Bǎodìng and eighty-three other prefectures and counties in Zhílì,
one month's rations were ordered to be awarded.
The transit taxes on merchant goods like beans and wheat from Fèngtiān passing through Zhílì and Shāndōng customs were reduced.
On the day Xīnhài,
the Emperor visited the Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng,
remitting differing amounts of money and grain taxes in the areas passed through.
In the sixth month, on the new moon day Bǐngchén,
due to drought in Lìchéng Shānzhuāng and fifty-one other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng,
one month's rations were given to the poor,
and land tax on fields damaged by flood in Línqīng Zhōu, Shāndōng, was remitted.
On the day Dīngsì,
the Emperor resided at the Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
cairns (èbó) were set up at the borders of the southwestern foreign tribes of Tánggǔtè (Tangut), Bùlǔkèbā (Bhutan), Zhéméngxíong (Sikkim), Zuòmùláng (Mustang), and Gūo'ěrkā.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Wùzǐ,
the Yǒngdìng Hé (River) breached its banks.
On the day Gēngyín,
the Dān and Qìn rivers in Hénán breached their banks.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
relief was provided for flood victims in Píngdìng and other places in Shānxī.
On the day Jǐhài,
relief was provided for flood victims in Línqīng and other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
relief was provided for flood victims in Tiānjīn and other places in Zhílì.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Qǔjiāzhuāng River in Fēngběi Tīng, Hénán, breached its banks.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Shūlín was stripped of his position for conniving in the association of the salt official Bānìng'ā with merchants,
Fùgāng was transferred to be Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng (Jiangnan and Jiangxi),
and Sūlíng'ā was appointed acting.
Fúkāng'ān was transferred to be Governor-General of Yún-Guì (Yunnan and Guizhou).
Hélín was appointed Governor-General of Sìchuān,
and Sūn Shìyì acted in his stead.
Shōngyún, who was managing affairs in Xīzàng, was appointed Minister of Works.
On the day Yǐsì,
Féng Guāngxióng was appointed acting Governor-General of Yún-Guì.
Grand Secretary Jī Huáng died,
and Sūn Shìyì was summoned to join the Grand Secretariat to manage affairs.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Mùlán hunting expedition for this year and next year was suspended.

Fixed taxes on areas under Bǎodìng and other prefectures in Zhílì, Wèihuī and other prefectures in Hénán, Línqīng and five other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng, and Dàizhōu and three other prefectures and counties in Shānxī that were affected by floods were remitted.
In the eighth month, on the *dìngsì* day,
due to severe flooding in the prefectures of Tiānjīn and Héjiān in Zhílì,
the collection of assessed taxes was exempted for those affected by the disaster.
On the *wǔwǔ* day,
the breach in the southern section of the Yǒngdìng Hé was closed.
On the *jǐsì* day,
as the next year would mark the sixtieth year of the Emperor's reign,
a universal exemption of one year's grain tribute was granted to all provinces.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
Fúníng was transferred to be the Governor of Hénán,
Mùhélín was appointed Governor of Shāndōng,
with Jiāng Lán serving as acting governor.
Fúkāng'ān reported that the sectarian rebels Xiè Tiānxiù and others in Dàníng, Sìchuān, were spreading heterodox teachings,
which had extended to Shǎnxī, Húběi, and Hénán,
and an edict was issued to rigorously pursue and suppress them.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
arrears of taxes were remitted for Tōngzhōu and twenty-three other *zhōu* and *xiàn* in Zhílì.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Bì Yuán was demoted to Governor of Shāndōng,
and fined by having to surrender five years of his *yǎnglián* allowance as Governor-General of Húguǎng.
Fúníng was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng,
and Mùhélín remained as Governor of Hénán.
In the ninth month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Miǎnyáng and other *zhōu* and *xiàn* in Húběi.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Xiùlín was appointed General of Jílín.
On the *jǐhài* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Zhāng and Quán prefectures in Fújiàn.
The rent on official lands of the Imperial Household Department in Zūnhuà, Zhílì, was reduced.
Fúníng was ordered to be stationed in Xiāngyáng,
to supervise the pursuit and arrest of sectarian criminals.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
for correcting the stone classics,
Péng Yuánruì was granted the title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Gāoyào and other *xiàn* in Guǎngdōng.
Because the sectarian rebels Duàn Hànróng and others in Láifèng Xiàn, Húběi, had gathered a crowd to resist arrest,
an edict was issued criticizing Bì Yuán for his laxity.
On the *wùshēn* day,
arrears of taxes due to flooding were remitted for Qíqíhā'ěr and two other cities.
In the winter, tenth month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
arrears of taxes were remitted for Jí Xiàn and eight other *xiàn* in Hénán, and Línqīng and nine other *zhōu* and *xiàn* in Shāndōng.
On the *rénxū* day,
Lèbǎo reported the capture of the sectarian leader Liú Sōng.
Ānhuī was ordered to strictly pursue his follower Liú Zhīxié.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Netherlands presented tribute.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
this year's assessed taxes were remitted for the four *tīng*, *zhōu*, and *xiàn* under Zhāngzhōu Fǔ in Fújiàn due to flooding.
On the *wùchén* day,
seven border posts including Kēbùduōwēihuò'ěr were ordered to be moved back to their original locations on the northern boundary;
the remaining land was granted to Dù'ěrbótè Hán Mǎkèsuǒ'ěrzhábù and others for grazing.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Chén Yòngfū was transferred to be Governor of Húběi,
and Huìlíng was appointed Governor of Ānhuī.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Héngxiù's crime was pardoned.
In the eleventh month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
because Liú Qīngnǎi, the Magistrate of Fúgōu Xiàn, Hénán, had been negligent in preventing Liú Zhīxié's escape,
he was dismissed from office and arrested,
and Mùhélín was handed over to the appropriate board for severe deliberation.
On the *rénchén* day,
this year's grain tribute was remitted for Línqīng and other *zhōu* and *xiàn* in Shāndōng.
On the *rényín* day,
Fùgāng was ordered to be acting President of the Board of Punishments.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Mùhélín was stripped of his office
and sent to perform meritorious service in Wūlǔmùqí.
Ājīng'ā was appointed Governor of Hénán.
In the twelfth month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
arrears of taxes from previous years were universally remitted for all provinces.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Jīn Jiǎn, President of the Board of Civil Office, died,
and Bǎoníng was appointed to replace him.
Míngliàng was appointed General of Yīlí.
On the *wùyín* day,
Shūliàng was appointed General of Hēilóngjiāng.
Túsāng'ā, General of Suīyuǎn Chéng, was transferred to be General of Xī'ān,
and Yǒngkūn was appointed to replace him.
In the sixtieth year, spring, first month, on the *jiǎshēn* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse,
and morning congratulations were exempted.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,

relief was provided to varying degrees for impoverished commoners affected by flooding in Tiānjīn and twenty other *zhōu* and *xiàn* in Zhílì, Jí Xiàn and fourteen other *xiàn* in Hénán, and Línqīng and ten other *zhōu* and *xiàn* in Shāndōng during the previous year.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Sūlíng'ā was summoned to the capital,
Fúníng was transferred to be Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
Bì Yuán was reinstated as Governor-General of Húguǎng,
and Yùdé was appointed Governor of Shāndōng.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Chén Yòngfū was transferred to be Governor of Guìzhōu,
Yīngshàn was appointed Governor of Húběi,
and Bì Yuán concurrently served as acting governor.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Gùlún Èfù Fēngshēn Yīndé was appointed Minister of the Imperial Household Department.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
arrears of taxes from previous years were remitted for Shāndōng.
On the *gēngxū* day,
arrears of taxes from previous years were remitted for Jiāngsū.
The collection of silver and grain that had been suspended was remitted for Jiāngxī.
In the second month, on the *guǐchǒu* day, the first day of the month,
arrears of taxes from previous years were remitted for Guǎngdōng.
Chén Yòngfū was dismissed from office and arrested for mishandling the investigation and arrest of the key criminal Liú Zhīxié.
Yáo Fēn was transferred to be Governor of Guìzhōu,
and Chéng Lín was appointed Governor of Guǎngxī.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
arrears of taxes from previous years were remitted for Shǎnxī.
The Miáo rebels Shí Liǔdèng and others in Sōngtáo Tīng, Guìzhōu, and Shí Sānbǎo and others in Yǒngsuí, Húnán, revolted.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the Húnán Miáo rebels captured Qiánzhōu Tīng,
and Assistant Prefect Sòng Rúchūn and others died.
Fúkāng'ān was ordered to suppress them,
and Bì Yuán was stationed in Chángdé to prepare provisions and supplies.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
because Grand Secretary Āguì and others could not express the imperial edicts to the Emperor's satisfaction,
their promotion reviews were suspended,
and Vice Minister Chéngcè and others were handed over to the appropriate board for disciplinary action.
A deliberation was granted to Governor-General Fúkāng'ān and others.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the Guìzhōu Miáo rebels besieged Zhūlóng'ā, the Brigade-General of Zhènyuǎn Garrison, at Zhèngdàyíng.
Arrears of taxes on banner lands in Guǎngníng and Jǐnzhōu, Fèngtiān, were remitted.
Arrears of taxes from previous years were remitted for Gāolán and forty-four other *zhōu* and *xiàn* in Gānsù.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Hélín, Governor-General of Sìchuān, was ordered to go to Yǒuyáng Zhōu to prepare for the Miáo rebels,
while Sūn Shìyì remained in Sìchuān to handle accounts.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
arrears of taxes from previous years on civilian land and salt-field land were remitted for Zhèjiāng.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Miáo rebels captured Yāyǒuzhài in Yǒngsuí Tīng,
and Brigade-General Míng'āntú of Zhènggān Garrison and others died.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Húnán Yǒngshùn Miáo rebels Zhāng Tíngzhòng and others revolted,
harassing Bǎojìng and Lúxī.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
arrears of taxes from previous years were remitted for Ānhuī.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Guìzhōu Miáo rebels harassed the area around Sīnán and Yìnjiāng,
and fled into Xiùshān, Sìchuān.
Fúkāng'ān went to Tóngrén to supervise the suppression.
Délèngtài was ordered to lead the *bātúlǔ* imperial guards and others to the Guìzhōu military camp.
In the intercalary second month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
Fúkāng'ān reported lifting the siege of Zhèngdàyíng.
On the *rénchén* day,
Féng Guāngxióng remained as Governor of Guìzhōu,
and Yáo Fēn was transferred to be Governor of Yúnnán.
Due to the Miáo rebel uprising,
assessed taxes were remitted for Sōngtáo, Zhèngdà, and other places under Tóngrén Fǔ in Guìzhōu.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Emperor went to the Eastern Tombs,
and three-tenths of the grain and silver taxes in the areas he passed through were remitted.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Emperor paid respects at the Zhaoxī Líng, Xiào Líng, Xiàodōng Líng, and Jǐng Líng.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Fúkāng'ān reported lifting the siege of Xiùnǎo.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Fúkāng'ān reported capturing Shíchéng,
and eradicating the Miáo rebels in the caves.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the Emperor paid respects at the Tài Líng and Tàidōng Líng,
and honored the tomb of Empress Xiàoxián.
Accumulated arrears in the salt fields of Liǎnghuái were remitted.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Fúkāng'ān reported lifting the siege of Sōngtáo.
In the third month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
Hélín reported clearing the rear route in Xiùshān,
and was ordered to go to Sōngtáo to join Fúkāng'ān in the suppression.
Sūn Shìyì was appointed acting Governor-General of Sìchuān.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Fúkāng'ān reported annihilating the Miáo rebels in Chángchōng and Kǎluò,
and advancing troops into the Chǔ territory.
Èlèdéngbǎo was ordered to quickly proceed to Fúkāng'ān's military camp.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Fúkāng'ān reported lifting the rebel siege of Yǒngsuí, Húnán.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
bandits led by Chén Zhō quán in Zhānghuà, Táiwān, revolted,
and captured the county seat.
Soon after, it was recovered.
On the day Guǐsì,
Dòu Guāngnài was demoted
for mishandling the grading of papers in the metropolitan examination.
Zhū Guī was made Left Censor-in-Chief
but remained in his post as Governor of Guǎngdōng.
On the day Jǐhài,
as Kuílún impeached the rampant piracy,
Pǔ Lín was ordered to come to the capital to await further instructions.
Yáo Fēn was transferred to be Governor of Fújiàn,
and Kuílún was appointed acting governor.
Jiāng Lán was made Governor of Yúnnán.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Wáng Yǐxián and 110 others were granted the degree of Jìnshì and corresponding official ranks.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Xú Xīn, Fù Gàn, and Lǐ Duān, Jǔrén whose recommended papers in the metropolitan examination were deemed superior in literary quality, were rewarded with positions as Cabinet Secretaries.
On the day Wùshēn,
the Emperor went to the Guǎng rùn Temple to pray for rain.
That night,
it rained.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the current year's taxes in areas passed through by Guìzhōu officials and soldiers were partially remitted.
Fúkāng'ān and others reported the capture of Huángguāzhài.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
as Fúníng and Huìlíng had not yet completed managing the military affairs in Húnán,
Sū Líng'ā was ordered to remain acting Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
and Fèi Chún was made Governor of Ānhuī.
On the day Gēngxū,
the previous year's taxes in Lóngxī and three other counties in Fújiàn, affected by floods, were partially remitted.
Bandit leader Chén Zhō quán and others were executed.
In the fifth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
the Emperor visited the Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng.
Wǔ Lānà and Pǔ Lín were dismissed from their posts and subjected to judicial inquiry
for mismanagement of disaster relief.
Kuílún was ordered to concurrently hold the acting position of Governor-General of Mǐnzhè.
Three-tenths of the current year's taxes in areas passed through were remitted.
On the day Dīngsì,
Fèi Chún was transferred to be Governor of Jiāngsū,
and Huìlíng remained Governor of Ānhuī.
Fúkāng'ān and others reported the capture of Gòupízhài, Sūpízhài, and other places.
Fúkāng'ān was transferred to be Governor-General of Mǐnzhè,
and Lè Bǎo was made Governor-General of Sìchuān.
Yí Mián was made Governor-General of Shǎnxī-Gānsù.
On the day Rénxū,
the Emperor resided at the Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
as it was confirmed that Fújiàn's treasuries were deficient,
the Censors and Supervising Secretaries were reprimanded for not reporting it.
They were also ordered
not to shirk their responsibility for speech when submitting memorials on major local events in the future.
Ājīng'ā was summoned to the capital,
and Jǐng'ān was made Governor of Hénán.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Huìlíng was summoned to the capital,
and Wāng Xīn was made Governor of Ānhuī.
On the day Wùchén,
Sū Líng'ā was ordered to be stationed at Qīngjiāngpǔ,
concurrently acting as Governor of Jiāngsū.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Yú Mǐnzhōng was stripped of his hereditary rank of Light Chariot Commandant
for engaging in corrupt practices and disgracing his office.
In the sixth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
as Miáo bandits in Húnán harassed the rear route of Zhèngān,
Fúníng was admonished for cowardice,
and Liú Jūnfǔ for passively holding his ground.
Huìlíng was ordered to remain acting Governor of Húběi.
On the day Wùzǐ,
due to drought, the Board of Punishments was ordered to clear minor cases,
reducing punishments for crimes less than penal servitude.
Chéngdé Prefecture followed suit.
On the day Gēngyín,
Fúkāng'ān and others reported the capture of the Miáo villages of Shādōu, Duōxǐ, and other places.
On the day Yǐwèi,
relief was provided for flood victims in Nánhǎi and other counties in Guǎngdōng.
On the day Wùshēn,
Yáo Fēn was dismissed from his post for being interrogated and investigated.
Kuílún was ordered to concurrently act as Governor of Fújiàn,
and Cháng Lín as Governor-General of Mǐnzhè.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Gēngshēn,
Démíng was sentenced to strangulation
for implicating Chén Zhào, the Zhīxiàn of Zīyáng County, in suicide.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the previous year's taxes in Jiānglíng and eleven other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Húběi, affected by floods, were remitted.
On the day Bǐngyín,
as Fúkāng'ān and others reported continuous victories over Miáo villages
and crossing the Dàwūcǎo River,
they were bestowed with precious gifts.
On the day Rénshēn,
Jébozūndānbā Hútúkètú and others came for an audience,
were granted an audience and bestowed with tea.
In the eighth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Yǒngkūn was transferred to be General of Wūlǐyàsūtái,
and Héngruì was made General of Suīyuǎnchéng.
On the day Guǐwèi,
the King of Nánzhǎng, Zhàowēnměng, and the King of Miǎndiàn, Mèngyǔn, were granted imperial edicts,
both receiving embroidered silks.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the request for retirement by Liú, the Minister of War, was granted.
Zhū Guī replaced him,
remaining in his post as Governor of Guǎngdōng.
Jīn Shìsōng was made Left Censor-in-Chief.
On the day Dīngwèi,
accumulated arrears of banner rent in Tōngzhōu and fifty-one other prefectures and counties in Zhílì were remitted.
Fúkāng'ān and others advanced and stationed at Yángliǔpíng.
In the ninth month, on the day Xīnhài,
the Emperor held court in the Qínzhèng Hall,
summoning the imperial princes, imperial grandsons, princes, dukes, and high ministers to an audience.
It was announced that the fifteenth imperial son, Prince Jiāqīn, was established as Crown Prince,
and the following year would be the first year of Jiāqìng of the succeeding emperor.
Relief was provided for flood victims in Hǎizhōu and six other prefectures and counties in Jiāngsū.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the Crown Prince, princes, dukes, internal and external civil and military ministers,
and Mongol princes and dukes all submitted memorials requesting that the ceremony of abdication be held
only after the Emperor reached the age of one hundred.
This was not granted.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Fùlèhún and Yǎdé were both dismissed from their posts
and sent to Réhé and Yīlí respectively to perform meritorious service,
due to the previous Governor-General's corruption.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the Emperor reviewed the troops of the Jiànruì Battalion.
Fúkāng'ān was promoted to the rank of Zhōngruì Jiāyǒng Bèizi,
and Hélín to First-Class Xuānyǒng Bó.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the Emperor ordered the Crown Prince to visit the Eastern Tombs and Western Tombs.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Shū Liàng, the General of Hēilóngjiāng, was dismissed from his post and subjected to judicial inquiry
for extortion.
Yǒngkūn was transferred to replace him.
Túsāng'ā was made General of Wūlǐyàsūtái.
Héngruì was reassigned as General of Xī'ān,
and Wū'ěrtúnàxùn replaced him.
Bóxīng was made Commandant of Cháhā'ěr.
Tèkèshen was transferred to be Minister for Affairs in Kùlún,
and Cèbākè was made Minister for Affairs in Xīníng.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Míngliàng was dismissed from his post for embezzling sable furs during his tenure as General of Hēilóngjiāng.
Bǎoníng was made General of Yīlí.
On the day Jǐsì,
Shū Liàng was sentenced to strangulation.
Míngliàng was retained in Wūlǔmùqí to perform meritorious service.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
as Fèngtiān, Shānxī, Sìchuān, Húnán, Guìzhōu, and Guǎngxī had no tax arrears,
two-tenths of the next year's main taxes were remitted.
On the day Yǐhài,
the previous year's taxes in Lóngxī and five other counties in Fújiàn,
and Huáfēng and Luóxī two counties, affected by floods, were remitted.
In winter, the tenth month, on the new moon day Wùyín,
the calendar for the first year of Jiāqìng was promulgated.
On the day Gēngchén,
Fúkāng'ān and others reported the capture of bandit leader Wú Bànshēng.
Fúkāng'ān's son, Délín, was granted the rank of Vice Commander-in-Chief,
Hélín a yellow belt,
and others received various rewards as deliberated.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
due to Wǔ Lānà and others' greed and corruption,
their sons were exiled to Yīlí.
Cháng Lín was dismissed from his post for sheltering Wǔ Lānà and Pǔ Lín,
and ordered to come to the capital.
Kuílún was appointed acting Governor-General of Mǐnzhè,
and Yáo Fēn acting Governor of Fújiàn.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
all land and poll taxes for the first year of Jiāqìng throughout the empire were generally remitted.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Wǔ Lānà and Pǔ Lín were executed by beheading.
On the day Rénchén,
Élèdéngbǎo and Délèngtài were appointed Grand Ministers of the Imperial Household
for their bravery in suppressing and capturing Miáo bandits.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the ceremony for the transfer of the throne in the year Bǐngchén was ordered to be set.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
it was ordered that in the first lunar month of the next year,
the Thousand Elders Banquet would be grandly held again.
In the eleventh month, on the day Dīngsì,
Fúkāng'ān and others reported the capture of Tiānxīngzhài and other places.
Hélín was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent,
and Fúkāng'ān and Hélín were each bestowed with a dark sable fur imperial coat.
On the day Gēngshēn,
relief was provided for banner people and commoners affected by drought in the three cities of Jīnzhōu, Xióngyuè, and Jǐnzhōu in Fèngtiān,
and the three prefectures and counties of Nínghǎi and others.
Taxes were partially remitted.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the Emperor ordered the Crown Prince to reside in the Yùqìng Palace.
On the *wùyín* day of the twelfth month, the first day of the lunar month,
an edict stated:
"After I relinquish power next year,
all memorials and reports
shall be addressed to the Tàishàng Huángdì.
When responding to an audience, address him as Tàishàng Huáng."
On the *wùzǐ* day,
relief was provided to the distressed refugees of Tóngrén, Guìzhōu.
Fúkāng'ān and others reported the capture of Tiānxīng and other Miáo stockades.
On the *rényín* day,
Zhū Guī was permitted to accept the tribute memorial from the King of Yīngjílì (England).
An imperial edict of commendation and reward was bestowed,
and it was sent back via the English merchant Bōláng (Brouwer).
Regarding the King's suggestion in his memorial to persuade the Guō'ěrkā (Gurkhas) to submit,
the edict informed him that British military assistance was unnecessary.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
an imperial edict was bestowed upon Shàng Wēn, King of the Liúqiú (Ryukyu) Kingdom.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
it was decreed that on the New Year's Day of the coming year,
the imperial throne would be passed to the Crown Prince as the heir Emperor.
Officials were dispatched in advance to offer sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the Imperial Ancestral Temples.
In this year,
Miǎndiàn (Myanmar), Nánzhǎng (Laos), Xiāmluó (Siam), Ānnán (Annam), Yīngjílì (England), Liúqiú (Ryukyu), and Guō'ěrkā (Gurkhas) came to pay tribute.
On the *wùshēn* day, the first day of the lunar month of the first year of Jiāqìng,
the grand ceremony of abdication and succession was held.
The Crown Prince was enthroned as Emperor.
The former Emperor was honored as the Tàishàng Huángdì.
Important military and state affairs were still to be reported to him,
who would deliberate and make decisions.
Major decrees and edicts were issued by him.
The almanac used in the palace continued to bear the Qiánlóng reign title.
In the winter of the third year,
the Emperor fell ill.
On the *rénxū* day of the first month of the fourth year, he passed away,
at the age of eighty-nine.
In this year,
on the *yǐwèi* day of the fourth month,
the Emperor was posthumously honored with the full title Fǎtiān Lóngyùn Zhìchéng Xiānjú Tǐyuán Lìjí Fūwén Fènwǔ Xiàocí Shénshèng Chún Huángdì,
and his temple name was Gāozōng.
On the *gēngwǔ* day of the ninth month,
he was interred in the Yùlíng mausoleum.
Commentary states: Gāozōng's reign was one of extreme prosperity.
He diligently strived for good governance,
expanded the territory,
and campaigned against the disobedient in all four directions.
His achievements in both civil administration and military prowess
were most splendid.
His long reign
matched that of the Shèngzǔ,
and his longevity surpassed it.
Since the Three Dynasties,
such a phenomenon had not occurred.
However, in his old age, being weary of duties,
he was misled by powerful favorites,
which obscured the brilliance of his reign.
This is indeed lamentable.
Annals Sixteen: Annals of Rénzōng

Rénzōng, who received the mandate of Heaven, initiated prosperity, propagated transformation, appeased the righteous, revered literature, disciplined the military, was filial, respectful, diligent, frugal, upright, keen, heroic, sagacious, and astute, the Ruì Huángdì,
his given name was Yǒngyǎn,
the fifteenth son of Gāozōng.
His mother was the Wèi Jiā Shì,
posthumously honored as Xiàoyí Huánghòu.
He was born on the sixth day of the tenth month of the twenty-fifth year of Qiánlóng.
In the fifty-fourth year,
he was enfeoffed as Jiā Qīnwáng.
In the ninth month of the sixtieth year,
he was officially designated Crown Prince.
Gāozōng intended to abdicate in his favor,
designating the following year as the first year of Jiāqìng.
On the *wùchén* day, the first day of the lunar month in the spring of the *bǐngchén* year, the first year of Jiāqìng,
the internal abdication ceremony was held.
The Emperor attended Gāozōng in performing comprehensive rites at the Tángzǐ, Fèngxiān Diàn, and Shòuhuáng Diàn.
Gāozōng ascended the Tàihé Diàn
and conferred the imperial seal.
The Emperor ascended the throne,
honored Gāozōng as Tàishàng Huángdì,
and received his instruction in governance.
An imperial edict was issued to the empire,
and a banquet was given to the imperial clan and vassals.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Empress Xǐtǎlā Shì was established.
A "Thousand Elders Banquet" was held at the Níngshòu Gōng,
attended by the Tàishàng Huángdì.
Those aged ninety and above
were summoned to the imperial seat
and bestowed cups of wine, following custom.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
prayers for harvest were offered to Shàngdì.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Tàishàng Huángdì, hosted a banquet for court officials at the Zhèngdà Guāngmíng Diàn.
All banquets followed this protocol.
Grand Secretary Fúkāng'ān and others, managing affairs in Miáojiāng, reported the capture of Lángpō
and the advance on Pínglǒng.
Rebels of the White Lotus sect arose in Zhījiāng and Yídū, Húběi.
On the *dīngchǒu* day, the first day of the second lunar month,
sacrifices were offered to the foremost teacher Kǒngzǐ.
On the *wùyín* day,
sacrifices were offered to the gods of grain and soil.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the imperial lectures (jīngyán) were held for the first time.
On the *xīnsì* day,
an edict ordered the construction of a Confucian temple in Guìdé Tīng, Gānsù.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the vernal equinox,
sacrifices were made to the sun in the eastern suburbs.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Emperor held court at the Qiánqīng Mén;
when in the gardens, he held court at the Qínzhèng Diàn,
making it a regular practice.
On the *jǐhài* day,
White Lotus rebels rose in Dāngyáng, Húběi,
killing officials.
Xi'ān General Héngruì led two thousand troops to suppress them.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
sacrifices were offered at the Temple of Successive Emperors.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Húběi Governor Huìlíng reported the capture of the White Lotus rebel Niè Jiérén.
On the *gēngxū* day of the third month,
the continued levy of military funds in Sìchuān was suspended.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the Emperor personally ploughed the ceremonial field,
making four passes.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the Emperor accompanied the Tàishàng Huángdì to visit the imperial mausoleums.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the imperial carriage returned to the capital.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Empress sacrificed to the First Silkworm Goddess.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Héngruì reported the recapture of Zhúshān, Húběi.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Liú Bǎozhù was exempted.
Wú'ěrtú Nàxùn was appointed President of the Court of Colonial Affairs,
Fùruì was appointed General of Suīyuǎn Chéng,
and Yǒngqìng was appointed Military Governor of Měnggǔ.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day, the first day of the fourth lunar month of summer,
the seasonal sacrifices were offered at the Tàimiào.
Yímíán, Yǒngbǎo, Héngruì, Sūn Shìyì, and others were ordered to suppress the Húběi White Lotus rebels in separate campaigns.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the regular sacrifice for rain (chángyú)
was offered to Heaven at the Huányū.
For his achievement in suppressing Láifèng,
Sìchuān Governor-General Sūn Shìyì was promoted to third-class baron.
An edict ordered that horses from Yīlí for tribute should travel via the grasslands.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the Emperor accompanied the Tàishàng Huángdì to pray for rain at the Hēilóngtán.
On this day,
it rained.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Zhào Wénkǎi and one hundred others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with various ranks.
On the *wùshēn* day of the fifth month,
an edict stated that if Élǔtè (Oirat) people arriving in the capital had smallpox,
they should henceforth proceed via the grasslands to Rèhé for an audience.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
sacrifices were offered to Earth at the Fāngzé.
On the *rénxū* day,
the Emperor accompanied the Tàishàng Huángdì to避暑 Mùlán (Mulan).
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Fù Gāng was appointed Grand Canal Governor.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Grand Secretary and Bèizi Fúkāng'ān died in the military campaign.
On the *yǐhài* day, the first day of the sixth lunar month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Kuílún was appointed Governor-General of Mǐnzhè,
and Zhū Guī was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng.
Jì Yún was appointed Minister of War,
Jīn Shìsōng was appointed Minister of Rites,
and Shěn Chū was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Fúchāng was transferred to be General of Fúzhōu.
Míngliàng was appointed acting General of Guǎngzhōu.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
land tax for fields flooded in Dàizhōu and three counties of Shānxī was remitted.
On the *wùyín* day,
Hélín reported the capture of the Miáo rebel Shí Sānbǎo,
who was sent to the capital and executed.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Fēngxùn River in Jiāngnán breached its banks.
On the *xīnhài* day of the seventh month of autumn,
Míngliàng reported the suppression of the White Lotus rebels in Xiàogǎn County.
Grand Secretary, Sìchuān Governor-General, and third-class baron Sūn Shìyì died in the military campaign.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day of the eighth month,
the autumn hunt was suspended due to rain.
On the *rényín* day,
Hélín died in the military campaign.
Míngliàng and Èhuī were ordered to take over command of the troops.
On the *yǐsì* day of the ninth month,
the imperial carriage returned to the capital.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day of Wùyín,
it was the Emperor's (Jiāqìng's) birthday (Wànshòu Jié).
He went to the Grand Supreme Emperor (Gāozōng/Qiánlóng) to perform the ritual.
After the ritual was completed,
he received congratulations from the court officials.
On the day of Jǐmǎo,
Dǒng Gào was appointed Grand Secretary.
Wáng Jié, due to a foot ailment, submitted a memorial declining his duties in the Grand Council (Jūnjī Chù), Southern Study (Nánshū Fáng), and Ministry of Rites (Lǐbù).
This was granted.
Shěn Chū was appointed Grand Councillor (Jūnjī Dàchén).
On the day of Xīnsì,

Huā Liánbù, the Provincial Commander (Tídū) who died in battle during the suppression of the Miáo rebellion, was posthumously granted the title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent (Tàizǐ Shàobǎo).
His descendants were granted a hereditary post.
On the day of Bǐngxū,
Shěn Chū was transferred to be Minister of War (Bīngbù Shàngshū),
and Jì Yún was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left (Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ).
In the eleventh month, on the day of Gēngxū,
the Héfù embankment construction on the Fēngxùn River closed, but then reopened.
Wáng Yìsūn, a Patrol Inspector (Xúnjiǎn) from Húběi who died in the line of duty, Gān Dù, an Instructor (Xùndǎo), and Pǔ Bǎoguāng, a Judicial Officer (Diǎnshǐ), were granted hereditary posts.
On the day of Jiǎzǐ,
it was the Winter Solstice (Dōngzhì).
Sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Altar of Heaven (Huánqiū).
On the day of Yǐchǒu,
Chén Huái, the Provincial Governor (Xúnfǔ) of Jiāngxī, was found guilty,
arrested for questioning, and exiled to a military frontier post.
On the day of Jǐsì,
because the sectarians (Jiàofěi) from Húběi secretly crossed the Gǔnhé River into Qín (Shǎnxī),
Yǒng Bǎo was stripped of his position, arrested for questioning,
and Huì Líng was appointed to command his troops.
In the twelfth month, on the day of Wùzǐ,
the Miáo rebels in Húnán were pacified.
Míng Liàng was enfeoffed as an Earl (Bójué),
Élèdēngbǎo as a Marquis (Hóujué),
and Délèngtài and others were granted various hereditary posts.
On the day of Gēngzǐ,
the comprehensive ancestral sacrifice (Xiájì) was performed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple (Tàimiào).
On the day of Xīnchǒu,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Grand Supreme Emperor, held court in the Tàihé Hall,
hosting a banquet for the tribute envoys from the outer vassal states.
In this year,

taxes (zāifù) and overdue taxes (bùgè fù) were remitted to varying degrees for thirty-nine departments, prefectures, and counties in provinces such as Shùntiān, Jiāngsū, Shānxī, Húnán, and Fújiàn, which had suffered from disasters.
The census counted 275,662,044 people nationwide,
and 37,206,539 *shí*, 1 *shēng*, 2 *hé*, 7 *sháo* of grain.
Cháoxiǎn (Korea) sent tribute.
In the second year (1797), in spring, the first month, on the day of Dīngmǎo,
Wáng Nángxiān, a woman of the Zhòng Miáo Yi tribe from Nánlóng, Guìzhōu, started a rebellion.
The Governor-General (Zǒngdū) Lè Bǎo was ordered to suppress it.
On the day of Gēngwǔ,
Guān Chéng reported that the sectarian leader (Jiàofěi) Xú Tiāndé in Sìchuān was harassing Dázhōu and Dōngxiāng.
The Brigade-General (Zǒngbīng) Zhū Shèdòu and others were ordered to suppress them.
In the second month, on the day of Guǐyǒu,
the Emperor presided over the Imperial Lecture (Jīngyán).
The Héfù embankment construction in Jiāngnán was again reported to be closed.
On the day of Wùyín,
the Empress died.
Following the edict of the Grand Supreme Emperor,
the Emperor wore plain clothes for seven days
and did not remove his hat plume.
Court officials did likewise,
and close officials wore their ordinary attire without pearl necklaces.
On the day of Xīnsì,
Jǐng Ān was promoted to Third-Class Earl for his功 (gōng - meritorious service) in suppressing and capturing sectarians.
On the day of Wùxū,
the deceased Empress was posthumously granted the title of Xiàoshū Empress.
Huì Líng reported the capture of the rebel leaders Liú Qǐ and others,
who were sent to the capital and executed.
In the third month, on the day of Wùshēn,
the Emperor visited the Western Mausoleum (Xīlíng).
On the day of Dīngsì,
he returned to the capital.
On the day of Guǐhài,
Liú Yōng was appointed Grand Secretary,
Shěn Chū was transferred to be Minister of Personnel (Lìbù Shàngshū),
and Zhū Guī was appointed Minister of War.
Fú Cháng'ān and Qìng Guì were appointed Manchu Generals-in-Chief (Mǎnzhōu Dūtǒng),
and Délèngtài was appointed Han Banner General-in-Chief (Hànjūn Dūtǒng).
Bā Kètǎnbù and Qìng Chéng reported
pursuing the rebels from Yìngshān into Yù (Hénán),
and it was confirmed that the rebel leaders Lǐ Quán, Wáng Tíngzhào, and Yáo Zhīfù were all among them.
An imperial edict ordered their capture.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day of Rénshēn,
a Brigade-General (Zǒngbīng) was established for the Zhèn Gān Garrison in Húnán,
and Bǎojìng *tǔxiàn* (native county) was changed to a *liúguān* (regularly appointed official) county.
On the day of Xīnsì,
the late Vice Minister (Shìláng) Fèng Kuān was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Tutor (Tàishī) and Minister of Rites,
as he had been the Emperor's teacher.
In the fifth month, on the day of Wùchén,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Grand Supreme Emperor, went to Mùlán for summer retreat.
On the day of Jǐsì,
Huì Líng reported that the sectarian leaders Yáo Zhīfù and others had forcibly crossed the Hànjiāng River from Báimǎshí into Chuān (Sìchuān).
An imperial edict dismissed the Commander-in-Chief (Zǒngtǒng) Qìng Chéng, Héng Ruì, and others,
demoting each official,
and appointed Yí Mián as Commander-in-Chief,
with Míng Liàng and Délèngtài as Deputy Commanders.
In the sixth month, on the day of Guǐyǒu,
Lè Bǎo reported
suppressing the Zhòng Miáo rebels in Nánlóng,
repeatedly capturing places like Shuǐyānpíng and Kǎzǐhé.
An imperial decree was issued: "Quickly capture the Miáo leaders Xiāngū and others."
In the intercalary sixth month, on the day of Gēngzǐ,
Jí Qìng reported capturing the Yàgǎo Miáo stronghold in Xīlóng Prefecture.
On the day of Bǐngwǔ,
Lè Bǎo reported advancing and capturing Pǔpíng,
killing the rebel leader in battle,
and lifting the siege of Nánlóng.
An imperial edict commended the gentry and common people for their steadfast defense of the imperiled city,
showing a deep understanding of justice,
and renamed Nánlóng Prefecture to Xīngyì Prefecture.
Lè Bǎo subsequently reported lifting the siege of Huángcǎobà,
opening the road between Diān (Yúnnán) and Qián (Guìzhōu).
On the day of Rénxū,
the Grand Council Secretaries (Jūnjī Zhāngjīng) Wú Xióngguāng and Dài Qūhéng were both promoted to Third-Rank Minister (Sānpǐn Qīng Xián),
and, along with Vice Minister Fù Sēn, were to learn and act as Assistant Grand Councillors.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day of Jǐsì,
the Yǒngdìnghé River burst its banks.
On the day of Jǐmǎo,
Kāshígā'ěr and Yīngjíshā'ěr, two Hui cities, were ordered to store grain in preparation for famine.
On the day of Guǐwèi,
General-in-Chief Bā Kètǎnbù died in the army.
On the day of Yǐyǒu,
the annual regular taxes for the next year were remitted for the six prefectures and counties of Fèngjié in Sìchuān, which had transported military provisions.
In the eighth month, on the day of Jiǎchén,
the Yǒngdìnghé River was closed.
On the day of Bǐngchén,
Fàn Yíhéng died.
Shěn Chū was transferred to be Minister of Revenue (Hùbù Shàngshū),
and Jì Yún was appointed Minister of Rites.
On the day of Jǐwèi,
Grand Secretary, Courageous Duke (Chéngmóu Yǒnggōng) Āguì died.
On the day of Bǐngyín,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Grand Supreme Emperor, returned to the capital.
In the ninth month, on the day of Wùchén,
Lè Bǎo reported attacking and capturing the Zhòng Miáo rebel lair,
capturing the rebel leader Wáng Nángxiān and others,
who were sent to the capital and executed.
Lè Bǎo was enfeoffed as a Third-Class Marquis.
On the day of Dīngchǒu,
the Emperor personally offered sacrifices to the late Grand Secretary Āguì.
On the day of Jiǎshēn,
Sū Líng'ā was appointed Grand Secretary,
and Lǐ Fènghàn was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng.
On the day of Gēngyín,
an imperial edict ordered Yí Mián, Lè Bǎo, Fèng Chéng'ēn, Jǐng Ān, and others to separately recruit local militias (Xiāngyǒng) to join the army and suppress the rebels.
On the day of Guǐsì,
an imperial edict stated:
"It is heard that the rebels often force common people to join their ranks
and resist the imperial army.
When the imperial army reports victories,
the 'rebels killed' they mention
are mostly common people,
not true rebels.
Thus, little progress has been made over a long time.
The high-ranking officers leading the troops should find ways to disperse them,
and not let jade and stone be burned together."
On the day of Jiǎwǔ,
because the gentry and common people of Ēnshī and Lìchuān in Húběi,
and Fèngjié in Sìchuān, bravely killed rebels,
their money and grain taxes were remitted for another year.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day of Wùxū,
Míng Liàng and Délèngtài requested extensive construction of civilian forts (Mínbǎo)
to weaken the rebels' power.
An imperial edict rebuked this as slow and impractical.
On the day of Bǐngchén,
the Qiánqīnggōng and Jiāotàidiàn suffered a fire.
On the day of Xīnyǒu,
Lè Bǎo was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Sìchuān military affairs.
In the eleventh month, on the first day of Bǐngyín,
Fó Zhù, a Minister without specific duties (Sànzhí Dàchén) who died in battle, and Ā'ěrsàláng, a Commander of the Imperial Guards (Hùjūn Tǒnglǐng), were granted hereditary posts.
In the twelfth month, on the day of Wùshēn,
Kāng Jītián was appointed Governor-General of Riverways in Jiāngnán,
and Sīmǎ Táo was appointed Governor-General of Riverways in the Eastern River (Dōnghé).
Míng'āntú, a Brigade-General who died in battle, Zēng Pānkuì, a Deputy General (Fùjiàng), and Yīsà Nà and others were granted hereditary posts.
On the day of Jiǎzǐ,
the comprehensive ancestral sacrifice was performed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In this year,
taxes (zāifù) were remitted to varying degrees for fifty-seven prefectures and counties in provinces such as Shùntiān, Húguǎng, Shǎnxī, Yúnnán, and Gānsù, which had suffered from disasters.
Cháoxiǎn, Liúqiú, and Xiāmluó (Siam) sent tribute.
In the third year (1798), in spring, the first month, on the day of Gēngwǔ,
Liáng Kěntáng was appointed Minister of War,
and Hú Jìtáng was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì.
On the day of Jiǎshēn,
Lè Bǎo was transferred to be Governor-General of Sìchuān.
On the day of Yǐchǒu,
Élèdēngbǎo reported capturing the rebel leader Tán Jiāyào.
The Emperor criticized him for the delay,
and stripped Élèdēngbǎo of his noble title and position.
Míng Liàng and Délèngtài were also stripped of their noble titles and positions for lax defense,
and Shū Liàng and Mùkèdēng'ā were stripped of their positions,
their families' properties confiscated,
and they were all ordered to serve in the army to atone for their mistakes.
In the second month, on the day Dīngwèi,
the Emperor performed the ancestral rites at the Wénmiào (Confucian Temple)
and lectured at the Yōngdian (Imperial Academy).
Èqítài was appointed as the Jiāngjūn of Hēilóngjiāng,
and Qìnglín as the Jiāngjūn of Jiāngníng.
On the day Xīnhài,
Kēfān and Wūěrtúnàxùn were removed from their posts for having allowed Shǎnxī bandits to enter Chǔ.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Wú Shěngqīn was appointed as Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
it was ordered that Nàyànchéng, a Grand Secretary of the Nèigé, learn and act in the Jūnjīchù.
In the third month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
Délèngtài reported that
the bandit chiefs Qíwángshì and Yáo Zhīfù were pursued and annihilated,
and died by falling off a cliff.
Míngliàng was granted the title of Fù Dū Tǒng.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Guānchéng and Liú Jūnfǔ were dismissed from their posts
due to delays in bandit suppression.
Fùchéng was appointed as the Jiāngjūn of Chéngdū.
In summer, the fifth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
old arrears of taxes for the entire province of Fújiàn were remitted.
On the day Jǐsì,
the grain tribute from Jiāngxī was intercepted
to provide relief for flood victims in Cáo Xiàn and thirteen other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the Emperor, accompanying the Tàishàng Huángdì, went to Mùlán for summer retreat.
In the sixth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
Délèngtài was stripped of all his noble titles and ranks
due to delays in bandit suppression,
and was ordered to serve under the title of Fù Dū Tǒng to prove his worth.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Èhuī, the Zǒngdū of Yún-Guì and a Third Class Nán, passed away.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Fùléngtài passed away.
Délègélèngguì was appointed as the Jiāngjūn of Níngxià.
The autumn hunt was suspended due to rain.
In the eighth month,
for the achievement of capturing the sectarian bandit Wáng Sānhuái,
Lèbǎo and Héshēn were promoted to Gōngjué,
and Fúchángān to Hóujué.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Zhāng Chéngjī reported that sectarian bandits were causing trouble in Xīníng Zhōu, Jiāngxī,
and they were suppressed.
In the ninth month, on the day Guǐhài,
the Emperor, accompanying the Tàishàng Huángdì, returned to the capital.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Yuán Chónghuàn, the Ming Dynasty's Grand Coordinator, was honored with a sacrifice at the Xiánliáng Cí.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
the newly built Qiánqīng Gōng and Jiāotài Diàn were completed.
In the eleventh month, on the day Dīnghài,
Shūcháng, the Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ, passed away.
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐsì,
Huìlíng reported the capture of the bandit chiefs Luó Qīqīng and Luó Qīshū.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the comprehensive ancestral rites were performed at the Tàimiào.
This year,
relief was granted for disaster taxes in forty-eight departments, prefectures, and counties in Shǎnxī, Guìzhōu, and other provinces, varying by degree.
Cháoxiǎn, Liúqiú, and Xiāmluó paid tribute.
In the fourth year, the Jǐwèi spring, the first month, on the day Rénxū,
the Tàishàng Huángdì passed away,
and the Emperor began to rule personally.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Héshēn, a Grand Secretary, was found guilty,
and he, along with Shàngshū Fúchángān, were imprisoned and interrogated.
Yíjùnwáng Yǒngxuán was promoted to Qīnwáng,
Bèilè Yǒnglín was enfeoffed as Qìngjùnwáng,
Miányì was enfeoffed as Lǚjùnwáng,
Yìlún and Yìshēn studied in the Shàngshūfáng,
and Miánzhì and others were rewarded differently.
An edict stated:
"Memorials from inside and outside the court should be submitted directly to Us;
no copies are allowed to be sent to the Jūnjīchù."
It was ordered that Chéngqīnwáng Yǒngxīng, Grand Secretary Dǒnggào, and Shàngshū Qìngguì serve in the Jūnjīchù.
Shěnchū was relieved of his duties.
Chéngqīnwáng Yǒngxīng took charge of the Hùbù.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Héshēn was granted death in prison,
and Fúchángān was sentenced to beheading.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
a special edict reiterated military discipline.
Lèbǎo was appointed as Jīnglüè,
and Míngliàng and Élèdēngbǎo as Cāncàn,
and an inquiry was ordered into Liúqīng's conduct in office,
with a factual report to be submitted.
Wú Shěngqīn was dismissed,
and Liú Quánzhī was appointed as Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ.
Bǎoníng was appointed as Grand Secretary,
and continued to manage the Jiāngjūn of Yīlí;
Qìngguì assisted as Grand Secretary;
Shūlín was appointed as the Shàngshū of the Lìbù;
Sōngyún was appointed as the Shàngshū of the Hùbù.
For the achievement of beheading the bandit chief Rǎn Wénchóu,
Huìlíng and Délèngtài were commended.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Yímián was relieved of his post,
and Héngruì was appointed as the Zǒngdū of Shǎn-Gān.
On the day Dīnghài,
Cáo Xībǎo, the former Yùshǐ, was posthumously granted the title of Fù Dū Yùshǐ,
and one of his sons was granted an imperial protection position.
Yǐn Zhuàngtú, former Grand Secretary of the Nèigé, was summoned to the capital.
In the second month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Sōngyún was appointed as the Zǒngdū of Shǎn-Gān,
and Bùyàndálài as the Shàngshū of the Hùbù.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
an edict stated:
"Since the sectarian bandits started their troubles,
they have coerced good people and
burned down fields and houses.
The people do not willingly follow the bandits;
they wish to flee but have nowhere to go,
