and even if they return, they have no food.
It is urgent to offer amnesty and disband them,
but this cannot be achieved with empty words.
How should they be appeased, resettled,
and Lèbǎo should inquire with Liúqīng and other good officials,
to devise good methods,
so that they can be implemented,
and report back quickly."
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the prohibition on the private sale of Hétián jade was lifted.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Qín Chéngēn was stripped of his post and arrested for questioning
for military blunders.
Lǐ Fènghàn passed away,
and Fèi Chún was appointed as the Zǒngdū of Liǎng-Jiāng.
On the day Yǐsì,
the imperial clan members' participation in the Xiāngshì and Huìshì examinations was reinstated,
and the quota for imperial clan members in the ranks of Lángguān in the various boards and academies was increased.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the descendants of Xú Shùkuí and Wáng Xīhóu, who had been exiled due to guilt by association, were released and allowed to return.
On the day Dīngsì,
the descendants of the late Grand Secretaries Zhū Shì and Sūn Jiāgàn were employed.
In the third month, on the first day Jǐwèi,
Sūlíng'ā was dismissed,
Qìngguì was appointed as Grand Secretary,
Chéngdé as Shàngshū of the Xíngbù,
and Fùsēn as Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Shěnchū, the Shàngshū of the Hùbù, passed away,
and Fàn Jiànzhōng was appointed as the Shàngshū of the Hùbù.
On the day Guǐhài,
Shūlín was appointed as the Zǒngdū of Mǐn-Zhè and assisted as Grand Secretary.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Qìnglín was transferred to become the Jiāngjūn of Fúzhōu,
and Fúchāng was appointed as the Jiāngjūn of Jiāngníng.
On the day Wùchén,
Daoyuan officials in the direct provinces were permitted to submit secret memorials.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Jǐng'ān was relieved of his post,
Wōshíbù was appointed as the Zǒngdū of Húguǎng,
and Wú Xióngguāng as the Xúnfǔ of Hénán.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Élèdēngbǎo reported the suppression and extermination of the sectarian bandits Xiāo Zhànguó and Zhāng Chánggēng,
which the Emperor commended,
and granted him the title of Èrděng Nán.
Commanders Zhū Shèdǒu and Yáng Yùchūn, among others, were commended.
On the day Wùyín,
regulations for the Imperial Guard were established.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the fourth imperial brother Lǚduān Jùnwáng Yǒngchéng was posthumously granted the title of Qīnwáng,
the seventh imperial brother Dàomǐn Huángzǐ Yǒngcóng was granted the title of Zhéqīnwáng,
and the twelfth imperial brother Yǒngjī was granted the title of Bèilè.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Lèbǎo reported the suppression and extermination of the sectarian bandit Lěng Tiānlù.
An imperial decree stated:
"To have eliminated three chiefs in less than ten days
is deeply commendable.
Élèdēngbǎo is promoted to Yīděng Nán."
New and old fixed taxes for Dèng Zhōu and twenty counties in Hénán affected by bandits were remitted.
Guǎnghòu, the Bùzhèngshǐ of Gānsù, reported the killing of the bandit leader Zhāng Shìlóng.
In summer, the fourth month, on the first day Jǐchǒu,
the Qīntiān Jiān reported that on the first day of the fourth month,
the sun and moon would be in conjunction (hébì),
and five planets would be aligned (liánzhū).
The Emperor said:
"Such an alignment is a chance occurrence;
with warfare not yet ceased,
how can it be considered an auspicious sign?"
Yǐn Zhuàngtú was granted the position of Gěishìzhōng,
and allowed to return to his hometown to care for his parents.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the posthumous honorific title was respectfully conferred upon the deceased Emperor.
After the ceremony,
an edict was issued, extending imperial grace.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
new and old fixed taxes for Xiàoyì and thirty-five other departments, prefectures, and counties in Shǎnxī affected by bandits were remitted.
On the day Jǐhài,
new and old fixed taxes for Fèngjié and thirty-six other departments, prefectures, and counties in Sìchuān affected by bandits were remitted.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
an edict ordered adherence to the late Emperor's decree
to hold the Xiāngshì and Huìshì Enkē examinations in the Gēngshēn and Xīnyǒu years.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Yáo Wéntián and two hundred twenty others were granted the Jinshì Jídì degree, with varying ranks.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Qìngchéng was appointed as the Jiāngjūn of Chéngdū.
On the *wǔwǔ* day of the fifth month, the first day of the lunar month,
this year's autumn executions were suspended.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the old and new quotas of land tax for Húběi's Xiàogǎn and forty-six other prefectures, counties, and garrisons that had been attacked by rebels were remitted.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Jiāng Lán was dismissed,
and Chū Pénglíng was appointed Governor of Yúnnán.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Fù Sēn was appointed Minister of War,
and Ādísī was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Qèqín Jùnwáng Héngjǐn was stripped of his peerage for being disrespectful.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Dǒng Gào was appointed Grand Secretary.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Fèi Chún was ordered to investigate and impeach corrupt officials.
An edict remitted the additional gold and silver and the converted price of grapes for the Huí people of Bódéérgē.
On the *jǐchǒu* day of the sixth month,
additional Brigade Generals for the Left and Right Wings of the Infantry Commander were established.
On the *gēngyín* day,
an edict stated:
"I have heard that Suízhōu in Húběi has not been disturbed by rebels.
Because the people dug ditches and piled up mountains,
it provided sufficient defense.
Village forts among the people
can all be handled in the same way.
Lèbǎo, Sōngjūn, and Wú Xióngguāng are to immediately inform the common people."
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Wú Xióngguāng and Wú Diān requested an increase in the shipping fee for straw materials for river works.
They received an imperial rebuke,
and the matter was referred to the board for discussion and resolution.
On the *gēngxū* day,
hereditary posts were granted to console Bǎoxīng, the Brigade General of Shǎnxī, and others who died in battle.
In autumn, on the *xīnyǒu* day of the seventh month,
three thousand Shānxī troops were dispatched to Húběi,
and two thousand Shèngjīng troops,
commanded by Élèhēng'é,
were dispatched to Sìchuān to suppress the rebels.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Lèbǎo reported the capture of rebel leader Bāo Zhènghóng,
and Zhū Shèdǒu was granted a hereditary post as Commandant of Cavalry.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Lèbǎo, the Generalissimo, was stripped of his post and arrested for questioning due to negligence in military affairs;
Míngliàng was appointed Generalissimo,
and KuíLún was appointed Governor-General of Sìchuān.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Jǐng'ān was stripped of his earldom
and banished to Yīlí.
The old and new quotas of land tax for Gānsù's Lǒngxī and forty-seven other prefectures and counties that had been attacked by rebels were remitted.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the Mid-Autumn tribute was suspended.
On the *jǐchǒu* day of the eighth month,
Fùjùn was dismissed,
and Xīngkuí was appointed Military Governor of Wūlǔmùqí.
On the *rénchén* day,
two thousand Shèngjīng troops,
and one thousand Jílín and Hēilóngjiāng troops each,
were dispatched to Húběi to suppress the rebels.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Chánglín was appointed Governor-General of Yún-Guì.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Lèbǎo reported that Délèngtài had captured rebel leader Gōng Wènyù alive,
and Délèngtài was granted a hereditary post as Commandant of Cavalry.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Míngliàng was dismissed as Generalissimo,
and Élèdēngbǎo was ordered to serve as Generalissimo with the rank of Military Governor.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Zhào Wénkǎi, a compiler, and Lǐ Dǐngyuán, a secretary, were ordered to enfeoff Shàng Wēn as King of the Liúqiú Kingdom.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Qìngchéng and Yǒngbǎo were arrested for questioning for ineffective supervision of troops,
and Nà Yànchéng was ordered to Shǎnxī to oversee affairs.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Hóng Liàngjí, a compiler, privately discussed state affairs in a letter to Chéng Qīnwáng,
and was banished to Yīlí.
On the *bǐngchén* day of the ninth month, the first day of the lunar month,
a hereditary post was granted to console Sūn Dàyóu, the Deputy General of Guìzhōu, who died in battle.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Yí Qīnwáng Yǒngláng passed away.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Grand Coffin departed,
and the Emperor respectfully saw off the imperial cortege.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Emperor Gāozōng Chún was interred in the Yùlíng mausoleum.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Emperor Gāozōng Chún, Empress Xiàoxián Chún, and Empress Xiàoyí Chún were enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple,
and an edict granting widespread imperial favor was issued.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the late Bì Yuán, Governor-General of Húguǎng, was stripped of his hereditary post for abusing military funds,
and his official privilege of 'Yǐnguān' was revoked.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Míngliàng was dismissed as Counselor-in-Chief for ineffective suppression of rebels,
stripped of his rank as Military Governor,
and granted the rank of Deputy Military Governor to suppress rebels.
In winter, on the *rénchén* day of the tenth month,
Zhū Guī was transferred to Minister of Revenue,
Liú Quánzhī to Minister of Personnel,
and Fàn Jiànzhōng to Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Míngliàng reported the capture of rebel leader Zhāng Háncháo.
Hú Qílún, a circuit intendant in Húběi, was executed for embezzlement of money and grain.
On the *rényín* day,
Délèngtài reported the capture of rebel leaders Gāo Jūndé and Gāo Èr.
Délèngtài was granted the title of Second Class Baron.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Chéng Qīnwáng Yǒngxīng was exempted from serving in the Grand Council.
Fù Sēn was ordered to resume his position as Grand Councilor.
On the *xīnhài* day,
court officials were ordered to recommend virtuous and capable individuals.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Lèbǎo was condemned to beheading,
and sent to the capital for supervision pending execution.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day of the eleventh month,
Gōng Ānlù, son of the late Duke Chāoyǒng Hǎilánchá, died in battle suppressing rebels in Sìchuān;
an edict granted generous consolation,
his son was named Ēntèhèmèizhālāfēn,
and inherited the title of Duke Chāoyǒng.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
long-standing accumulated arrears of taxes in Zhílì were remitted.
On the *wùyín* day,
Xīngzhào and Qìngchéng were banished for ineffective troop leadership.
Élèdēngbǎo was rewarded with ten thousand taels of silver,
and Délèngtài with five thousand taels of silver.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Winter Solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Altar of Heaven,
with Emperor Gāozōng Chún sharing the offerings,
and an edict granting widespread imperial favor was issued.
On the *rénchén* day of the twelfth month,
Jiǎng Zhàokuí, Governor-General of Grain Transport, was dismissed for unilaterally requesting increased taxes to aid transport.
Hereditary posts were granted to console Deputy Generals Dīng Yǒuchéng, Délìang, and others who died in battle.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Fúníng was stripped of his post and arrested for questioning for reporting victory after killing surrendered rebels,
and Jǐng'ān for allowing rebels to harm the people.
Both were stripped of their posts and arrested for questioning.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Élèdēngbǎo reported the capture of cult leader Wáng Dēngtíng.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Jiāng Shèng reported the capture of Miáo bandit Wú Chénshòu in Húnán.
An imperial decree commended him,
and he was granted the title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
a joint sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In this year,
the old and new quotas of land tax for Hénán and Húběi's sixty-seven prefectures and counties that had suffered from military conflict were remitted,
and land taxes for Zhílì, Hénán, and Húběi through which troops passed were collected.
Furthermore, the land tax quotas for one county each in Jiāngsū and Húběi due to collapsed land were remitted,
and disaster taxes for Sānxìng in Jílín, Hēilóngjiāng, and Shípíngzhōu in Yúnnán were remitted.
All accumulated arrears of taxes throughout the empire were generally remitted.
Cháoxiǎn and Xiānmó came to pay tribute.
In the spring, on the *jiǎyín* day of the first month, the first day of the lunar month of the *wǔwǔ gēngshēn* year,
the Emperor visited the imperial mausoleum.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
he went to Yùlíng to perform the initial memorial ceremony.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
Élèdēngbǎo was ordered to suppress cult rebels in Shǎnxī,
and Délèngtài and KuíLún were ordered to suppress cult rebels in Sìchuān.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Sōngjūn was appointed General of Yīlí,
but remained in Shǎnxī to suppress rebels.
Chánglín was transferred to Governor-General of Shǎn-Gān,
Yùdé was appointed Governor-General of Mǐn-Zhè,
and Ruǎn Yuán was appointed Governor of Jiāngsū.
On the *rénxū* day,
an edict ordered a clear-up of treasury discrepancies,
to be gradually made up,
without causing hardship to the people due to severity or urgency.
Jīn Shìsōng passed away,
and Zhāng Ruòtíng was appointed Minister of War.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
prayers for grain were offered to Shangdì,
with Emperor Gāozōng Chún sharing the offerings.
Wōshíbù was relieved of his post,
Jiāng Shèng was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng,
and Sōngjūn was transferred to suppress rebels in Húběi.
On the *wùyín* day,
Jǐngyì was appointed General of Hēilóngjiāng.
On the *dīnghài* day of the second month,
Nà Yànchéng was ordered to serve as Counselor-in-Chief for military affairs in Gānsù.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Wāng Chéngpèi was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the *guǐsì* day,
an imperial decree ordered the minting of Qiánlóng coins in Xīnjiāng.
On the *rényín* day,
hereditary posts were granted to console Guān Liánshēng, the Deputy General of Sìchuān, and others who died in battle.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
previous lenient officials who allowed rebels to escape were reviewed;
Qín Chéng'ēn and Yímán were banished to Yīlí.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the retired Grand Secretary Cài Xīn passed away.
In the third month, on *gēngshēn* day,
the Emperor paid respects at the Imperial Mausoleum.
On *xīnyǒu* day,
seventy-five officials were dismissed from their posts,
and Jīng was arrested and punished.
On *jiǎzǐ* day,
Qīngmíng Festival,
the Emperor performed the earth-spreading ceremony.
On *yǐchǒu* day,
Ādísī was arrested and interrogated for hoarding troops and causing delays;
Lèbǎo was appointed as General of Chéngdū to protect the city.
On *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor visited the Southern Park.
Délèngtài reported on intercepting and suppressing the sectarian rebels crossing the Jiāng,
capturing the rebel leader Rǎn Tiānyuán,
and was promoted to a third-class viscount.
On *rénshēn* day,
the Emperor paid respects at the Western Mausoleum.
On *yǐhài* day,
he returned to the capital.
On *xīnsì* day,
descendants of ministers in the Hall of Worthies were selected and recorded.
For allowing rebels to cross the Jiālíng Jiāng
and then the Tónghé,
Kuílún was stripped of his office and arrested for interrogation.
Lèbǎo was appointed acting Governor-General of Sìchuān,
and Míngliàng was appointed a blue-feathered imperial guard to join the army.
In summer, the fourth month, on *guǐwèi* day, the new moon,
there was a solar eclipse.
On *yǐyǒu* day,
Ādísī was exiled to Yīlí,
and Délèngtài was made General of Chéngdū.
On *gēngzǐ* day,
the Luǒ Yí in Yúnnán were pacified,
and Shūlín was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
In the intercalary fourth month, on *jiǎyín* day,

the Ministry of Justice was ordered to investigate officials and criminals long imprisoned, as well as their children and grandchildren under house arrest, and those long exiled, for leniency and reduction of sentences.
On *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Emperor walked and prayed for rain.
On *yǐmǎo* day,
Hóngliàngjí was released and returned to his hometown.
On *bǐngchén* day,
the Annanese Límǔ and others were released from prison,
settled in the Firearm Division,
and given monthly rations.
On this day,
it rained.
On *bǐngyín* day,
the hereditary post of Dásāntài, the Provincial Commander of Sìchuān who died in battle, was compensated.
On *wùchén* day,
Nàyànchéng was dismissed from his post in the Grand Council
for being incompetent in military affairs,
and recalled to the capital.
In the fifth month, on *rénxū* day, the new moon,
it was the summer solstice,
and sacrifices were offered to the earth at Fāngzé,
with Gāozōng Chún Huángdì honored as co-sacrificed.
On *jǐchǒu* day,
for his meritorious service in suppressing rebel leaders such as Liú Yǔngōng, the Grand Minister Ѐlèdēngbǎo
was promoted to a third-class viscount.
On *bǐngwǔ* day,
Nàyànchéng arrived in the capital,
and his report was unsatisfactory;
he was demoted to Reader of the Hànlín Academy.
In the sixth month, on *rénxū* day,
Ѐlèdēngbǎo reported the capture of rebel leader Yáng Kāijiǎ.
On *dīngmǎo* day,
Zhāng Ruòtíng was appointed Minister of Justice,
Wāng Chéngpèi as Minister of War,
and Féng Guāngxióng as Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On *jiǎxū* day,
Kuílún was granted permission to commit suicide,
and his son Zhāláfēn was exiled to Yīlí.
In autumn, the seventh month, on *xīnmǎo* day,
Chánglíng, Commander-in-Chief of the Right Wing, was ordered to lead troops from Jílín and Hēilóngjiāng to Húběi to assist in suppressing the sectarian rebels.
Lánggān reported that the Qīngmiáo (Green Shoots) Yáng Wéntài was stirring up rebellion,
and pacified it.
Mǎ Huìyù reported the capture of the chief perpetrator of spreading heresy, Liú Zhīxié,
who was sent to the capital and executed.
On *bǐngshēn* day,
Démíng, Minister of Rites, died;
Dáchūn was appointed Minister of Rites.
On *jǐyǒu* day,
Ѐlèdēngbǎo reported the capture of rebel leader Chén Jié.
In the eighth month, on *bǐngchén* day,
Wáng Wénxióng, Provincial Commander of Gùyuán, died in battle suppressing rebels;
he was granted a third-class viscountcy.
In the ninth month, on *rénwǔ* day,
the Emperor paid respects at the Eastern Mausoleum.
On *wùzǐ* day,
he returned to the capital.
On *dīngwèi* day,
the hereditary post of Lǐ Xīmìng, a Vice-General of Sìchuān who died in battle, was compensated.
In winter, the tenth month, on *wùchén* day,
Hú Jìtáng died;
Jiāng Shèng was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì,
Shūlín as Governor-General of Húguǎng,
and Lánggān as Governor-General of Yún-Guì.
In the eleventh month, on *yǐyǒu* day,
Prince Ruì Chúnyǐng passed away.
On *jǐhài* day,
the hereditary posts of Fùchéng and other generals who died in battle or were dismissed from office were compensated.
In the twelfth month, on *jiǎyín* day,
the Shǎnxī sectarian rebel Xú Tiāndé fled to Húběi,
and the Húběi sectarian rebel Rǎn Xuéshèng fled to Shǎnxī;
Délèngtài, Lèbǎo, and others were demoted and reprimanded.
On *dīngsì* day,
Délèngtài reported the capture of sectarian rebels such as Yáng Kāidì.
On *bǐngzǐ* day,
a grand sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In this year,
the disaster taxes in seventy prefectures, sub-prefectures, and counties in provinces such as Shùntiān, Jiāngsū, Sìchuān, Yúnnán, and Gānsù were remitted,
as were various portions of land taxes due to troop movements and collapsed fields.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú offered tribute.
In the sixth year, *xīnyǒu* year, spring, the first month, on *rénwǔ* day,
Fùsēn was appointed Minister of Revenue,
and Míng'ān as Commandant of the Gendarmerie.
On *xīnmǎo* day,
Assistant Minister Wōxīng'ā and Qíu Xíngjiǎn were dispatched to reward the armies of Ѐlèdēngbǎo and Délèngtài.
On *dīngyǒu* day,
for his meritorious service in suppressing the Shānyáng sectarian rebels, Délèngtài
was reinstated as a first-class viscount.
On *jiǎchén* day,
Délèngtài reported the capture of rebel leaders Gāo Èr and Wáng Rú.
On *yǐsì* day,
Lèbǎo reported the capture of rebel leaders Xú Wànfù and others, identified by their yellow, blue, and white banners.
In the second month, on *yǐmǎo* day,
Lèbǎo reported the capture of rebel leader Wáng Shìhǔ.
On *bǐngchén* day,
Shūlín reported that Míngliàng had captured rebel leader Bǔ Xīng'áng.
On *wùwǔ* day,

Yù, the sixth-generation grandson of Minister Wèi Xiàngshū, Jǐngzéng, the great-grandson of Minister Yáng Míngshí, and Cóngxù, the grandson of Provincial Governor Xú Shìlín, all descendants of worthies, were granted the *jǔrén* degree.
On *wùchén* day,
the Emperor paid respects at the Imperial Mausoleum
and performed the earth-spreading ceremony.
On *rénshēn* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
The Provincial Commander of Húguǎng was renamed Provincial Commander of Húnán.
A Provincial Commander of Húběi was established,
stationed in Xiāngyáng.
The Commander-in-Chief of Xiāngyáng Garrison was renamed Commander-in-Chief of Yúnyáng Garrison.
On *guǐyǒu* day,
Fùsēn died;
Chéngdé was appointed Minister of Revenue and Grand Councilor.
On *yǐhài* day,
Ѐlèdēngbǎo reported the capture of rebel leader Wáng Tíngzhào.
In the third month, on *gēngchén* day,
an edict stated:
"Many bandits coerced by rebels are actually good people.
All who surrender will be pardoned from death.
The ministers at the front lines are to understand Our intention
and widely publicize this,
ensuring everyone knows."
The hereditary posts of Duō'ěrjìzābù, Lǐ Shàozǔ, and other commanders-in-chief who died in battle were compensated.
On *dīngyǒu* day,
Wéihàn, the fourth-generation grandson of Grand Secretary Lǐ Guāngdì, Niànzéng, the fourth-generation grandson of Minister Tāng Bīn, both descendants of worthies, were granted the *jǔrén* degree;
Zhēnglóng, the sixth-generation grandson of Provincial Governor Fù Hóngliè and a county assistant magistrate, was granted the *zhīxiàn* (county magistrate) degree.
On *jǐhài* day,
an edict stated:
"We are about to visit the Imperial Mausoleum.
The spring seedlings are thriving.
Ministers are ordered to supervise the people's fields,
not allowing them to be trampled."
For their meritorious service in assisting in suppressing the sectarian rebel Liú Liándēng, the scholars and common people of Jiāngxī
had Jiāngxī Níngzhōu renamed Yìníngzhōu.
On *xīnchǒu* day,
the Emperor paid respects at the Imperial Mausoleum.
On *yǐsì* day,
the ceremony for removal of mourning clothes was performed.
In summer, the fourth month, on *dīngwèi* day, the new moon,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On *jǐwèi* day,
because the people of Sìchuān contributed funds for public service,
the regular taxes for the coming year were remitted for Suìníng and eighty-six other prefectures, sub-prefectures, and counties.
On *xīnyǒu* day,
Empress Niǔhùlùshì was formally enthroned.
On *rénxū* day,
Shūlín, Assistant Grand Secretary and Governor-General of Húguǎng, died;
Wú Xióngguāng was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng.
Délèngtài reported the capture of rebel leader Zhāng Yǔnshòu.
On *bǐngyín* day,
for their merits in capturing Wáng Tíngzhào, Gāo Èr, and Mǎ Wǔ,
Ѐlèdēngbǎo was promoted to a second-class viscount,
and Yáng Yùchūn to a Knight Commander of Cavalry.
On *wùchén* day,
Jíqìng, Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng, was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary.
On *xīnwèi* day,
Gù Gāo and 275 others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with varying distinctions.
In the fifth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
the descendant of a worthy and virtuous Grand Secretary, Wáng Xī, his great-grandson Yuánhóng, was granted the title of jǔrén.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the Emperor offered sacrifices at the Wénchāng Temple,
and it was then that it was ordered to be included in the canon of sacrifices.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Zhū Shèdǒu, the Commander-in-Chief of Sìchuān who died in battle, was posthumously recognized as a Provincial Commander-in-Chief [Tídū],
and his family was granted a hereditary position.
On the day Bǐngxū,
it was ordered that commanders-in-chief take turns presenting themselves at court.
The Prefectural Administrator [Fǔchéng] of Fèngtiān was put in charge of academic affairs [xuézheng],
and his term was for three years.
On the day Yǐsì,
Èlèdēngbǎo was appointed President of the Court of Colonial Affairs [Lǐfān Yuàn Shàngshū].
In the sixth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
there was heavy rain.
The Yǒngdìng River overflowed its banks.
Court officials [Qīngyuán] were dispatched to provide relief to the flood victims.
Due to the flood, this year's autumn hunt [qiūmiǎn] was suspended.
Jiāng Shèng was dismissed [from his post]
and sent to render service on the Yǒngdìng River.
Chén Dàwén was reinstated to act as Governor-General of Zhílì.
On the day Bǐngchén,
it rained again.
Héngruì, the General of Xī'ān, passed away.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the Emperor walked barefoot to the Altar of Land and Grain [Shèjì Tán] to pray for clear weather.
On that day,
it cleared up.
Lèbǎo reported that all the Qīng and Lán bandit gangs in Dōngxiāng had been annihilated.
In the seventh month, on the day Gēngchén,
a special one-month ration of grain was issued to soldiers in the capital.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Nàyànbǎo and Bāníng'ā were ordered to repair the Yǒngdìng River works.
Lèbǎo reported the capture of bandit leaders Xú Tiānshòu and Wáng Dēnggāo.
On the day Wùxū,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Rèhé.
In the eighth month, on the day Dīngsì,
Èlèdēngbǎo reported the capture of bandit chiefs Wáng Shìhǔ and Rǎn Tiānsì.
Lèbǎo reported that Qīshíwǔ had captured bandit leaders Liú Qīngxuǎn, Tāng Bùwǔ, and others.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Lèbǎo reported the capture of bandit chiefs Rǎn Xuéshèng and others,
and was enfeoffed as a third-class baron [nán].
In the ninth month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
the Comprehensive Statutes of the Great Qīng [Dà Qīng Huìdiǎn] continued to be revised.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Yǒngdìng River was closed [i.e., its breaches were repaired].
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Èlèdēngbǎo reported the capture of bandit chief Xīn Dǒu.
Délèngtài reported the killing of bandit chief Lóng Shàozhōu.
On the day Guǐhài,
an imperial edict commended the military achievements in Sìchuān and Shǎnxī,
promoting Èlèdēngbǎo to third-class earl [bó],
Délèngtài to second-class earl,
Sàichōng'ā to commandant of cavalry [qí dūwèi],
and Wēnchūnyún to cavalry guard [qíwèi].
In the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
Yīsāng'ā, the Governor of Guìzhōu, was granted death for his arrogance, corruption, deception, and fraud.
On the day Guǐsì,
an imperial edict stated:
"The military campaign will conclude shortly.
The resettlement of the local militia [xiāngyǒng] is an important matter for post-conflict management.
A detailed plan should be submitted for consideration."
On the day Yǐwèi,
Èlèdēngbǎo reported the capture of bandit chief Gāo Jiànqí.
On the day Wùxū,
Qīshíwǔ was stripped of his office and arrested for questioning
for letting bandits escape.
On the day Jǐhài,
Dázhōu in Sìchuān was promoted to Suídìng Prefecture [Suídìng Fǔ],
and Tàipíng Camp [Tàipíng Yíng] was promoted to Tàipíng Brigade [Tàipíng Xié].
In the twelfth month, on the first day, Guǐmǎo,
Qìngchéng reported the capture of Gǒu Wénmíng's bandit faction.
On the day Dīngwèi,
an imperial edict stated:
"Previously, by special decree of the late Emperor,
an investigation was conducted into officials of this dynasty who died for their country but had not received hereditary positions.
Over 140 officials have already been identified,
and their families have been granted the hereditary position of Grace Cavalry Guard [Ēnqíwèi Shìzhí].
Now, over 990 more officials have been identified in a subsequent investigation.
A list has been presented for review,
all of whom were loyal officials who resisted [the enemy] unto death.
Their descendants shall all be granted the hereditary position of Grace Cavalry Guard [Ēnqíwèi Shìzhí],
and be provided with salaries and provisions.
Apart from those who volunteer for service,
those who wish to take examinations
are permitted to take them as civil or military students,
and participate in the examinations equally."
On the day Guǐhài,
an imperial edict commended Liú Qīng,
and he was specially appointed as the Intendant of Jiànchāng, Sìchuān.
On the day Rénshēn,
Èlèdēngbǎo reported the suppression of bandits in Tōngjiāng,
killing bandit leader Gǒu Cháoxiàn.
On the day Xīnwèi,
a collective sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple [Tàimiào].
In this year,
land taxes were remitted in varying degrees for 231 prefectures, departments, counties, and garrisons in provinces such as Zhílì, Shānxī, Zhèjiāng, Ānhuī, Sìchuān, Yúnnán, and Gānsù.
Cháoxiǎn [Korea] and Xiāmluó [Siam] paid tribute.
In the seventh year, Rénxū, spring, first month, on the first day, Guǐyǒu,
the Emperor visited Yùlíng [Mausoleum]
and performed the three-period sacrificial rites.
Cotton clothes were bestowed upon the poor people along his route.
On the day Jiǎxū,
it was decreed that the sacrifice at the Altar of Land and Grain [Shèjì Tán] should be held on the day Shàngwù.
On the day Wùyín,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Sōngyún was appointed General of Yīlí.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Èlèdēngbǎo reported the capture of the chief rebel Xīn Cōng,
and the remaining rebels were all pacified.
Wú Xióngguāng reported the capture of bandit chief Zhāng Yǔnshòu's son, Déguì,
and the annihilation of the Lán bandit faction.
Míng'ān was stripped of his office for greed and corruption
and exiled to Yīlí.
Lùkāng was appointed Commander of the Gendarmerie [Bùjūn Tǒnglǐng],
and relieved of his position as President of the Board of Punishments [Xíngbù Shàngshū].
Èlèdēngbǎo was demoted to baron [nán]
for his lax defense which allowed Gǒu Wénmíng to escape across the Hàn Jiāng.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the Emperor presided over the Imperial Lectures [Jīngyán].
In the second month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
as Gǒu Wénmíng had fled to the old forests of Nánshān,
commanding ministers were ordered to blockade and suppress him,
and local officials were to strictly investigate and apprehend him,
not allowing the rebellion to spread.
On the day Dīngwèi,
sacrifices were offered to Confucius, the First Teacher [Xiānshī Kǒngzǐ].
On the day Rénxū,
exceptional compassion was shown to the families of Deputy Commander Hán Zìchāng and his younger brother, Deputy Commander Hán Jiāyè, who died in battle.
Local officials were ordered to construct a Double Martyrs' Shrine for them,
and their mother was given 300 liǎng of silver.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Èlèdēngbǎo reported that Liú Qīng had captured bandit chiefs Lǐ Bīn and Xīn Wén,
and Liú Qīng was granted the title of Surveillance Commissioner [Ànchásǐ Xián] and a peacock feather [huālíng].
In the third month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
Lèbǎo reported the capture of bandit chiefs Zhāng Tiānlún, Wèi Xuéshèng, and Chén Guózhū.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Délèngtài reported the capture of bandit chiefs Gōng Qíyáo, Lǐ Shìhàn, and Lǐ Guózhēn,
and the remaining rebels were all pacified.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Emperor visited Tàilíng [Mausoleum].
On the day Gēngyín,
he returned to the capital.
On the day Rénchén,
Chéngdé passed away,
and Lùkāng was appointed President of the Board of Revenue [Hùbù Shàngshū].
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Wùshēn,
Yán Jiǎn was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Wú Tíngchēn and 247 others were granted the jinshì degree, with varying ranks.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Qìngchéng reported the capture of bandit chiefs Wèi Hóngshēng, Zhāng Xǐ, and Bái Yōng.
In the fifth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Ruì Qīnwáng Bǎo'ēn passed away.
Lánggān reported the capture of the chief Luǒ bandit, Làyěbù.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Lèbǎo reported the capture of bandit chiefs Tuǒ Xiàngyáo, Xú Tiānpéi, and Zhāng Sīcóng.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Qìngchéng reported searching for and apprehending remaining bandits,
capturing Kāng Èrmá and Zhāng Chāngyuán,
and was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince [Tàizǐ Tàibǎo].
In the sixth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
Délèngtài reported that the Sectarian bandit Fán Rénjié had drowned,
his wife and children were captured,
and the remaining bandits were all annihilated.
Délèngtài was promoted to third-class marquis [hóu].
On the day Jiǎyín,
Liú Quánzhī and Déyīng were appointed Grand Councilors [Jūnjī Dàchén].
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Dáchūn passed away,
and Chánglín was appointed President of the Board of Rites [Lǐbù Shàngshū].
Bǎoníng was ordered to manage the Board of War [Bīngbù].
Lùkāng and Gōng'ālā were appointed Manchu Banners Lieutenant-Generals [Hànjūn Dūtǒng].
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day Xīnwèi,
Lèbǎo reported the suppression and annihilation of the bandits of the Yellow, White, Green, and Blue banners,
and was promoted to first-class male.
On Gēngchén,
Hé Tài, a gòngshēng from Shǎnxī, submitted a memorial advocating for the suppression of extravagance and promotion of frugality,
to rectify social customs.
An imperial edict stated his proposals were acceptable,
and he was rewarded with two bolts of fine silk.
On Jiǎshēn,
Grand Secretary Wáng Jié retired,
was granted the title of Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince,
and received his stipend while residing at home.
On Wùzǐ,
the Emperor went on the autumn hunt at Mùlán.
On Guǐsì,
an imperial edict stated:
"Regarding the escape of prisoners from Bóluó in Guǎngdōng,
after I issued a vermilion edict for inquiry,
the said governor and governor-general truthfully reported the facts.
Then, there must be many unrevealed matters in the empire,
which is truly regrettable
and even more deeply alarming.
Besides punishing those involved individually,
may they uphold the great laws and minor probity,
to fulfill the earnest intention of purifying officialdom."
Xīngkuí was appointed General of Xī'ān,
and Míngliàng was appointed Military Governor of Wūlǔmùqí.
On Jiǎwǔ,
Èlèdéngbǎo reported the capture of the rebel leader Gǒu Wénmíng.
An edict stated:
"Upon arriving at Mùlán,
I immediately heard the news of victory.
Among all the culprits of the sectarian rebellion,
only this bandit remained.
Now that he has been captured,
it will not be difficult to thoroughly suppress the rebellion.
Èlèdéngbǎo is promoted to first-class count,
and Yáng Yùchūn and others below him
shall all be generously rewarded."
Zhāng Ruòtíng died,
and Xióng Méi was appointed Minister of Punishments.
Wāng Chéngpèi was transferred to be Censor-in-Chief of the Left,
and Dài Qúhēng was appointed Minister of War.
In the eighth month, on the first day Jǐhài,
there was a solar eclipse.
An imperial edict stated:
"A solar eclipse on the first day of the month and a lunar eclipse on the full moon
are heavenly portents of warning,
deeply urging caution and vigilance.
Are there any shortcomings in my person?
In suppressing and apprehending the evil bandits,
their remnants are not yet completely eradicated.
Should they be pacified with military might,
or guided by moral transformation?
Are there any government policies inconvenient for the people,
which, though implemented for a time,
might lead to prolonged abuses?
Let all speak candidly without reservation.
As for reforming punishments during a lunar eclipse,
it is imperative to clarify laws and strictly enforce penalties,
striving for meticulousness and prudence,
which should be diligently pursued by myself and all officials, both inside and outside the court."
Zhū Guī was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary.
On Guǐmǎo,
Jī Chéngzhì was appointed Governor-General of the Yellow River in the East,
and Liú Qīng was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Sìchuān.
On Yǐmǎo,
the Emperor went on a hunt.
Nóng Nài and Ruǎn Fúyìng of Yuènán,
with their subordinates, pledged allegiance and submitted to the court,
surrendering the former vassal's imperial seal.
An edict permitted them to offer tribute.
On Xīnyǒu,
Délèngtài reported the capture of the bandit leader Pú Tiānbǎo.
In the ninth month, on Gēngchén,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On Wùzǐ,
the Emperor paid respects at the imperial tombs.
On Xīnmǎo,
he returned to the capital.
On Bǐngshēn,
Wú Xióngguāng reported the death of Huáng-banner bandit leader Táng Míngwàn.
In the tenth month of winter, on Jǐyǒu,
Hóngfēng, General of Hángzhōu, died,
and Zhāng Chéngxūn was appointed General of Hángzhōu.
On Rénzǐ,
Lèbǎo reported the capture of White-banner bandit leader Zhāng Jiǎn and Blue-banner bandit leader Tāng Sījiāo.
On Dīngsì,
Délèngtài reported the death of bandit leader Dài Sì,
and the capture of bandit chief Zhào Jiàn.
In the eleventh month, on the first day Wùchén,
Délèngtài reported the capture of bandit leader Chén Chuánxué.
On Gēngwǔ,
an imperial edict stated that Jíqìng, in handling the Fúluó sect bandits,
had submitted inaccurate reports,
and was relieved of his position as Assistant Grand Secretary.
Nà Yànchéng was ordered to investigate the matter.
Soon after, Jíqìng was dismissed as Governor-General,
and Hú túlí was ordered to act in his stead.
On Bǐngxū,
Èlèdéngbǎo reported the capture of bandit leader Jǐng Yīng,
and was promoted to third-class marquis.
In the twelfth month, on the first day Wùxū,
bandits caused unrest in Sùzhōu, Ānhuī,
and Fèi Chún and others suppressed them.
On Guǐchǒu,
an imperial edict announced that Èlèdéngbǎo, Délèngtài, Lèbǎo, Huìlíng, and Wú Xióngguāng jointly reported the complete suppression of the sect bandits in Sìchuān, Shǎnxī, and Chǔ.
Èlèdéngbǎo and Délèngtài were ennobled as first-class marquises,
Lèbǎo as first-class count,
Míngliàng as first-class male.
Sài Chōng'ā, Yáng Yùchūn, and others were ennobled and rewarded accordingly.
Favors were also extended to Chéng Qīnwáng Yǒngxīng and others, and to Grand Secretaries of the Military Council Qìng Guì, Dǒng Gào, and others.
On Yǐchǒu,
the combined ancestral sacrifice was performed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted for fifty-six prefectures, departments, and counties in provinces such as Zhílì, Shǎnxī, Jiāngxī, and Sìchuān.
Land collapse taxes were exempted for ten counties and garrisons in Jiāngsū, Fújiàn, and Shāndōng.
Cháoxiǎn offered tribute.
In the eighth year, Guǐhài, in the first month of spring, on Gēngwǔ,
Wōshíbù was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng.
On Dīngchǒu,
Yīlí was ordered to extensively open up civilian fields.
Zhāng Chéngjī was condemned to strangulation for submitting inaccurate reports regarding the suppression of local bandits in Yìníng Zhōu.
On Yǐyǒu,
cotton clothes were bestowed upon the poor.
On Jiǎwǔ,
the Emperor attended the imperial lecture.
In the second month, on Jǐwèi,
the Emperor paid respects at the Eastern Mausoleums.
In the intercalary second month, on Wùyín,
the Emperor returned and resided at Yuánmíng Yuán.
On Yǐyǒu,
he returned to the palace.
Upon entering the Shùnzhēn Gate,
the traitor Chén Dé suddenly attacked the imperial carriage.
Dìng Qīnwáng Mián'ēn, Èfù Lāwàngduō'ěrjì, and Dānbāduō'ěrjì and others captured him,
and he was handed over to court officials for strict interrogation.
Mián'ēn and others were rewarded differently.
On Dīnghài,
a sacrifice was offered to the God of Agriculture,
and the Emperor personally plowed the sacrificial field.
On Jǐchǒu,
an imperial edict stated:
"Chén Dé's act
should be viewed as that of a rabid dog,
and there is no need for exhaustive interrogation.
What I am ashamed of
is that moral transformation has not been clearly manifested,
hence this warning to me.
Let judgment be made according to the law."
On this day,
Chén Dé and his two sons were executed.
Retired Grand Secretary Wáng Jié took his leave,
was bestowed a jade dove staff,
imperial poems,
and returned to his hometown by imperial post station.
On Gēngyín,
gate regulations were strictly reinforced.
In the third month, on Bǐngshēn,
the Emperor personally tested the Hanlin scholars.
On Jiǎchén,
Mùkèdéngbù, Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Gānsù, died in battle while suppressing remaining bandits,
and was posthumously granted the title of second-class male.
Royal favors were extended to Wáng Màoshǎng, Commander-in-Chief of Húběi, and others who died in battle,
granting hereditary ranks.
On Gēngshēn,
the Empress performed the ceremony of personally gathering mulberry leaves.
In the fourth month, on Bǐngxū,
the Emperor prayed for rain.
On Dīnghài,
it rained.
In the fifth month, on Yǐwèi,
residences for imperial clan members and collateral imperial relatives were built.
On Guǐchǒu,
Fùjùn was appointed General of Jílín.
In the sixth month, on Wùzǐ,
Minister Péng Yuánruì requested retirement,
which was granted,
and he continued to preside over the compilation of the Veritable Records of Gāozōng.
Fèi Chún was appointed Minister of War,
and Chén Dàwén was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng.
On Jǐchǒu,
Ruǎn Fúyìng was enfeoffed as King of Yuènán.
In the seventh month of autumn, on Yǐsì,
Nà Yànchéng was appointed Minister of Rites.
On Dīngwèi,
due to the complete suppression of remaining bandits in the three provinces,
Èlèdéngbǎo, Délèngtài, and the Grand Secretaries of the Military Council were generously rewarded.
On Rénshēn,
the Emperor went on an inspection tour to Mùlán.
In the eighth month, on Rénwǔ,
Fùjùn was transferred to be General of Shèngjīng.
The hunting excursion was halted, and the Emperor returned to the capital.
On Xīnmǎo,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the ninth month, on Wùshēn,
the retired Minister and former Assistant Grand Secretary Péng Yuánruì died.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Rénshēn,
Lánggān reported the capture of the chief perpetrator, Héng Zhàgāng,
but the Xiélì bandits were not yet pacified.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Empress Xiàoshū was interred in the imperial mausoleum.
In the eleventh month, on the day Wùxū,
Zhū Guī and others requested to erase the Míng dynasty inscription on the Jìngyī Pavilion,
but the Emperor disallowed it.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
the grand ancestral sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
In this year,

the collection of disaster taxes and arrears was partially remitted for four hundred eighteen prefectures, departments, counties, and garrisons in the provinces of Zhílì, Shāndōng, Hénán, Jiāngsū, Ānhuī, Shǎnxī, Húběi, Sìchuān, Yúnnán, and Gānsù.
Cháoxiǎn and Yuènán paid tribute.
In the ninth year, Jiǎzǐ, in the spring, first month, on the day Dīngwèi,
Xīngkuí was transferred to be the General of Níngxià,
and Sài Chōng'é became the General of Xī'ān.
In the second month, on the day Rénxū,
the Emperor presided over the Jīngyán lectures.
On the day Guǐhài,
the Emperor visited the Hànlín Yuàn,
bestowed a banquet,
and composed a poem in Bǎiliáng style.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Emperor visited the Dōnglíng.
In the third month, on the day Rénchén,
he toured Pánshān.
On the day Rényín,
he visited the Mínglíng,
and offered wine at Chánglíng.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Jǐsì,
the Emperor reviewed the soldiers of the Jiànruìyíng.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Jī Chéngzhì was summoned to the capital,
and Xú Duān was made acting Grand Governor of River Management for Hédōng.
In the fifth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Emperor prayed for rain at Hēilóngtán.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
it rained.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Tiě Bǎo presented one hundred thirty-four volumes of Eight Banners poetry,
which were granted the title Xīcháo Yǎsòng Jí.
In the sixth month, on the day Rényīn,
Yù Dé and others reported that the pirate Cài Qiān had disturbed Lù'ěrmén
and suddenly entered Shāndàzhài.
An imperial decree was issued: "Pursue and capture him, ensuring success."
On the day Wùchén,
Lù Kāng was made Associate Grand Secretary,
Míngliàng was appointed Minister of Works,
Chánglín as Minister of Justice,
and Fèi Chún as Minister of Personnel.
Déyīng was dismissed from his post in the Grand Council,
and Nà Yànchéng and Yīng Hé were made Grand Councilors.
On the day Yǐhài,
Huìlíng passed away,
and Nà Yànchéng was appointed Grand Governor of Shǎnxī and Gānsù.
The Grand Commander Hú Zhènshēng, who died in action while suppressing pirates, was posthumously honored,
granted the title of Tiādū,
given a hereditary position,
and his son was employed.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Emperor toured Mùlán.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Chū Pénglíng was dismissed from his post for falsely impeaching Wú Xióngguāng.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
due to the completion of a full cycle of the sexagenary calendar,
the execution of prisoners was suspended for the current year.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐwèi,
an investigation into the excessive military expenditures in Húběi was conducted,
and Fúkāng'ān, the son of Hélín, and Bì Yuán and others were held accountable and punished.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the Emperor returned to the capital and visited the imperial mausoleums.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngyín,
the Emperor visited Nányuàn for a hunt.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
due to the complete eradication of the remaining bandits in the three provinces,
Ělèdēngbǎo and others were rewarded in varying degrees.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
Sūn Tíngbiāo, the magistrate of Wǔyuán county in Guǎngxī, concealed injuries and released a murderer.
An imperial decree ordered his execution by strangulation,
and the judicial commissioner was dispatched to exile him to Wūlǔmùqí.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the Emperor presided at Dūndiàn,
and hosted a banquet for imperial clansmen and princes.
In the eleventh month, on the day Wùshēn,
Nà Yànchéng was transferred to be Grand Governor of Liǎngguǎng,
and Wōshíbù became Grand Governor of Shǎnxī and Gānsù.
In the twelfth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Xú Duān was transferred to be Grand Governor of River Management for Jiāngnán.
On the day Gēngchén,
Grand Secretary Liú Yōng passed away.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the grand ancestral sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
In this year,
the collection of disaster taxes was partially remitted for twenty-one prefectures, departments, and counties in the provinces of Zhílì, Húběi, and Sìchuān.
Cháoxiǎn and Xiāmluó paid tribute.
In the tenth year, Yǐchǒu, in the spring, first month, on the day Yǐwèi,
the retired Grand Secretary Wáng Jié died while in the capital for a longevity celebration,
and a generous imperial edict was issued for his posthumous honors.
On the day Xīnhài,
Zhū Guī was made Grand Secretary,
Jǐ Yún Associate Grand Secretary,
and Tiě Bǎo Grand Governor of Liǎngjiāng.
An edict commanded the Ministers of the Imperial Household Department to strictly control the eunuchs,
monitor their comings and goings,
compile this into the court history,
and establish it as a regulation.
In the second month, on the day Jǐwèi,
the Emperor presided over the Jīngyán lectures.
On the day Jǐsì,
Prince Lǐ Yǒng'ēn passed away,
and his son Zhāo Lián succeeded him.
Associate Grand Secretary Jǐ Yún passed away,
and Liú Quánzhī was transferred to be Minister of Rites and Associate Grand Secretary.
In the third month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
the Emperor visited Nányuàn for a hunt.
On the day Jǐhài,
the Emperor visited the Tàilíng.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
he returned to the capital
and reviewed the soldiers of the Jiànruìyíng.
On the day Wùshēn,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
Hóng Kāng was made General of Guǎngzhōu.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Xīnsì,
Cài Wéiyù, a censor, submitted a memorial requesting a ban on Westerners printing books and spreading their religion.
An imperial decree was issued: "Investigate and ban them uniformly."
On the day Wùyín,
Péng Jùn and two hundred forty-three others were granted the Jinshì degree with varying ranks.
In the fifth month, on the first day Jiǎshēn,
an edict stated that the Ministers of the Imperial Household Department, who managed the Western churches,
had failed to strictly supervise them
and allowed them to spread their religion,
and thus they were referred to the appropriate ministry for deliberation on punishment.
Their scriptures were to be inspected and destroyed,
and Tóng Lán and others who practiced the religion were to be punished.
On the day Wùshēn,
the merit for pacifying the Píngjiàofěi and clearing the countryside was posthumously awarded,
Jiā Lèbǎo was granted Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince,
and Míngliàng was granted a First-Class Viscountcy.
In the sixth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
Yán Jiǎn was dismissed from his post for failing to detect a deficit,
Wú Xióngguāng was transferred to be Grand Governor of Zhílì,
and Bǎilíng became Grand Governor of Húguǎng.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the Yǒngdìng River burst its banks.
In the intercalary sixth month, on the day Guǐwèi,
Liú Quánzhī was dismissed,
Fèi Chún became Associate Grand Secretary,
and Qín Chéng'ēn became Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the day Wùxū,
the breach in the Yǒngdìng River was closed.
On the day Yǐsì,
Qīng Āntài was appointed Governor of Zhèjiāng.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Rénchén,
the Emperor departed for Shèngjīng to visit the imperial mausoleums.
In the eighth month, on the day Bǐngxū,
the Emperor offered sacrifices at the Běizhèn Temple.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the Emperor visited the Yǒnglíng.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the Grand Sacrifice was performed.
He reviewed the archery of the Jílín officials and soldiers.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the Emperor visited the Fúlíng,
and performed the Grand Sacrifice.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the Emperor visited the Zhāolíng,
and performed the Grand Sacrifice.
He paid respects at the tombs of Prince Kèqín Yuètuō, Prince Wǔxūn Yánggǔlì, Duke Hóngyì Éyìdōu, and Duke Zhíyì Fèi Yīngdōng.
The Emperor resided in Shèngjīng,
and paid respects before the precious registers.
On the day Jiǎchén,
he paid respects at the Tiāntán and Dìtán.
On the day Yǐsì,
the Emperor presided at the Chóngzhèng Diàn to receive congratulations.
Grand Minister of the Imperial Presence, Third-Class Duke Ělèdēngbǎo passed away,
and a memorial temple was built for him in the capital.
Qìng Chéng was made General of Chéngdū.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Emperor presided at the Dàzhèng Diàn,
and hosted a banquet for the accompanying princes, ministers, and Cháoxiǎn envoys.
He personally composed eight chapters of the Shèngjīng Sòng.
A personally inscribed plaque was bestowed upon King Lǐ Sōng of Cháoxiǎn.
On the day Wùshēn,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the ninth month, on the day Jǐsì,
the Emperor visited the Dōnglíng.
On the day Rénshēn,
he returned to the capital.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
he personally offered sacrifices to Ělèdēngbǎo.
In winter, 10th month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
an order was issued for Dài Jūnyuán to hasten to Nánhé to inspect the construction work.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the King of Yīngjílì (England) offered tribute,
and was bestowed with an imperial edict and patterned silks.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Nà Yànchéng was dismissed.
Wú Xióngguāng was transferred to be Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng,
and Qiú Xíngjiǎn was appointed Acting Governor-General of Zhílì.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Sài Chōng'ā was appointed General of Guǎngzhōu.
In the 11th month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
Bǎilíng was dismissed,
and Quán Bǎo was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Qìng Pǔ was appointed Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Húběi.
In the 12th month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
a joint sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In this year,
disaster taxes and special levies for eleven salt fields in Liǎnghuái were remitted for thirty-four prefectures and counties in Zhílì, Shānxī, Shǎnxī and other provinces, with variations.
The total population of the empire was counted as 33,218,143 people,
and the grain yield was 29,411,999 *shí*, 7 *shēng*, 3 *hé*, 2 *sháo*.
Cháoxiǎn (Korea) and Yīngjílì (England) offered tribute.
In the 11th year, *bǐngyín*, spring, 1st month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
the pirate Cài Qiān captured Fèngshān County.
Yù Dé was ordered to suppress them,
and Sài Chōng'ā, General of Guǎngzhōu, was transferred to supervise the suppression.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Nà Yànchéng was stripped of his office
and exiled to Yīlí
for putting on plays in his yamen
and indiscriminately accepting pirates.
In the 2nd month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
the Emperor attended the Imperial Lectures (Jīngyán).
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Emperor visited the Eastern Mausoleums.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the Emperor went to the Southern Park for a hunt.
On the *wùshēn* day,
he returned to the capital.
In the 3rd month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
Àixīntài, Commander-in-Chief of Táiwān, recaptured Fèngshān County,
and was granted a hereditary position.
In summer, 4th month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Emperor reviewed the troops of the Jiànruì Battalion.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Lǐ Hēngtè was dismissed,
and Wú Jìng was appointed Governor-General of River Conservancy for Hédōng.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the *Huángqīng Wényǐng* was continued and compiled.
In the 5th month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
Yù Dé was dismissed,
and Ālínǎo was appointed Governor-General of Mǐnzhè.
In the 6th month, on the *wùyín* day,
Jiāng Shèng was transferred to be Minister of Public Works,
and Qín Chéng'ēn was transferred to be Minister of Justice.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Qìng Chéng was stripped of his office
and exiled to Hēilóngjiāng
for making inaccurate responses in an audience.
Tèqīng'é was appointed General of Chéngdū.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Dài Jūnyuán was appointed Governor-General of River Conservancy for Jiāngnán,
and Xú Duān was appointed Deputy River Supervisor.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Dé Lèngtài was ordered to manage the Board of War.
In autumn, 7th month, on the *guǐhài* day,
Chén Féngshùn, a new soldier of Níngshǎn Garrison, gathered a gang to murder officials,
captured Yáng County,
and disturbed Níngqiāng.
Dé Lèngtài was ordered to lead Bātúlǔ Imperial Guards and Suǒlún soldiers to suppress them.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor toured Mùlán.
In the 8th month, on the *gēngyín* day,
the Emperor went hunting.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Lǐ Chánggēng reported having suppressed and annihilated many of Cài Qiān's bandit followers,
but Cài Qiān escaped.
In the 9th month, on the *yǐsì* day,
Bātúlǔ Imperial Guards, Suǒlún and other soldiers were dispatched to Shǎnxī.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
a judgment was made on the case of uninvestigated embezzlement in Zhílì.
Yán Jiǎn was exiled to Wūlǔmùqí.
Jiāng Shèng, Chén Dàwén, and Xióng Méi were demoted to Fourth Grade Capital Officials.
Péng Líng was reinstated as Provincial Governor of Ānhuī.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Liú Quánzhī was reinstated as Censor-in-Chief.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In winter, 10th month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
Dé Lèngtài reported having suppressed the rebellious soldiers in Yáng County.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Quán Bǎo was appointed Governor-General of Shǎnxī-Gānsù,
Wāng Zhìyī was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng,
and Cáo Zhènyōng was appointed Minister of Public Works.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Wēn Chénghuì was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì.
Ruǎn Yuán was reinstated as Acting Provincial Governor of Fújiàn,
but declined due to illness.
Zhāng Shīchéng was transferred to be Provincial Governor of Fújiàn,
and Jīn Guāngtì was transferred to be Provincial Governor of Jiāngxī.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Hé Níng was appointed Military Governor of Wūlǔmùqí.
Grand Secretary Bǎo Níng requested retirement,
and was honorably granted retirement with an imperial edict,
receiving his public salary.
In the 11th month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
Lù Kāng was appointed Grand Secretary,
Cháng Lín Assistant Grand Secretary,
and Wén Níng Commander of the Gendarmerie.
An imperial edict sternly reproached Dé Lèngtài
for his leniency in accepting the surrender of rebellious soldiers
during the suppression.
Yáng Yùchūn was demoted to Commander-in-Chief of Níngshǎn Garrison,
and Yáng Fāng was exiled to Yīlí,
immediately escorting the surrendered soldiers to their exile.
In the 12th month, on the *wùyín* day,
Grand Secretary Zhū Guī passed away.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor visited his residence to offer condolences.
On the *gēngchén* day,
a special imperial edict commanded both Manchu and Han people to strive for frugality.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
a joint sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted for thirty-five departments, prefectures, and counties in Zhílì, Sìchuān and other provinces, with variations.
Cháoxiǎn (Korea) and Liúqiú (Ryukyu) offered tribute.
In the 12th year, *dīngmǎo*, spring, 1st month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Fèi Chún was appointed Grand Secretary,
and Dài Qúhēng Assistant Grand Secretary.
On the *guǐhài* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Previously, during the suppression of evil bandits,
too many local militia were employed.
When peace was restored, it was difficult to disband them,
so many were ordered to enlist as regular soldiers.
Now, reports from Níngshǎn in Shǎnxī
and Suídìng in Sìchuān
repeatedly indicate new soldiers causing trouble,
which is suppressed in due course.
These fierce and unruly individuals
must be punished and reformed as soon as possible,
to prevent them from causing further incidents."
On the *wùchén* day,
new soldiers caused trouble at Wǎshípíng in Shǎnxī,
and they were suppressed.
In the 2nd month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
the Emperor attended the Imperial Lectures (Jīngyán).
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Jīlākān was dismissed
and stripped of his noble rank.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Emperor visited the Eastern Mausoleums.
In the 3rd month, on the *rénchén* day,
the Emperor went to the Southern Park for a hunt.
On the *xīnhài* day,
he visited the Western Mausoleums.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
he returned to the capital.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the *Gāozōng Shílù* and *Shèngxùn* were completed.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the Emperor prayed for rain.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
it rained.
In summer, 4th month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
the Emperor reviewed the troops of the Jiànruì Battalion.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the Emperor prayed for rain.
In the 5th month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
it rained.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Cháng Líng was appointed Governor-General of Shǎnxī-Gānsù,
and Sàbīntú was appointed Grand Canal Governor.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the prices for river conservancy materials were increased.
Since the Yōngzhèng reign,
the annual cost of river works was usually 600,000,
but from this point, it gradually increased to 1,600,000.
In the 6th month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
private advisors (*mùyǒu*) of governors-general and governors were forbidden from obtaining official positions through recommendation.
In autumn, 7th month, on the *yǐsì* day,
Xi Qún, compiler, and Fèi Xīzhāng, supervising secretary, were ordered to confer the title of King upon the King of Liúqiú.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the Emperor toured Mùlán.
In the 8th month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor went hunting.
In the 9th month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Emperor returned to reside at Mùlán.
Xiānluó (Siam) privately recruited merchants for trade;
an imperial edict was issued to instruct them to stop.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
he reviewed the troops at Gǔběikǒu.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
he returned to the capital.
In winter, 10th month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
it was ordered that the policy questions (*cèlùn*) be abolished from the civil service examinations for military officials (*wǔxiāng*) and the metropolitan military examinations (*huìshì nèichǎng*),
and replaced with memorized recitation of military classics.
In the eleventh month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
the dam entrance at Chénjiāpǔ was blocked,
directing the Yellow River to flow through its old course into the sea.
In the twelfth month, on the day Guǐwèi,
Qīng'āntài was transferred to be the Governor of Hénán,
and Ruǎn Yuán was appointed Governor of Zhèjiāng.
On the day Guǐsì,
the ancestral spirits were collectively sacrificed at the Tàimiào.
This year,
the disaster tax and salt gabelle were remitted for forty-seven prefectures and counties in the provinces of Zhílì, Jiāngsū, Sìchuān, Gānsù, and others.
The fixed land tax for fields washed away in five counties in Jiāngsū, Fújiàn, and Shānxī was abolished.
Cháoxiǎn, Liúqiú, and Nánzhǎng sent tribute.
In the thirteenth year (1798), on the day Wùwǔ of the first month of spring (Wùchén year),
Lǐ Chánggēng, the Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Zhèjiāng, died
in battle while pursuing pirates,
and was posthumously granted the title of Earl.
His subordinate Wáng Délù was appointed Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Zhèjiāng.
In the second month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
the Second Prince was ordered to offer sacrifices to the Former Master Kǒngzǐ.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the Emperor attended the Jīngyán lectures.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Bǎo Níng, who had been granted retirement as a Grand Secretary, passed away.
On the day Wùyín,
an imperial edict specially commended Fù Nài, the Dàoshǐ of Chényuán-Yǒngjìng in Húnán,
and added to his title that of Surveillance Commissioner.
In the third month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
the Emperor visited the Dōnglíng mausoleum.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Emperor inspected the long embankment at Tiānjīn.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Xú Duān was appointed Grand Canal Governor of Nánhé.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the Emperor reviewed the troops of Tiānjīn Garrison.
On the day Bǐngyín,
the Emperor went to the Nányuàn for a hunt.
Chánglín and Dài Qúhéng were ordered to inspect Nánhé.
In the fourth month of summer, on the day Wùchén,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Wú Xìnzhōng and 260 others were granted the Jinshì degree with various ranks.
In the fifth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Chánglín and Dài Qúhéng reported on their inspection of the river works,
requesting to use an old man named Zhāng, over 130 years old, who pointed out that Jìn Fǔ had previously built two sluices east of the Tiānrán Sluice,
and upon verification, dam foundations were found.
They proposed to repair them.
An imperial decree approved this,
and the old man was rewarded with silver and silk.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the Kǒngmiào temple at Quèlǐ was repaired.
In the intercalary fifth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Xiānhèlíng, the Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Húnán, was dismissed
for using improper language in his congratulatory memorial on the birth of the Eldest Imperial Grandson.
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
the Emperor's own poem "Gēngzhītú" was composed
and published in the Shòushí Tōngkǎo.
On the day Yǐsì,
Qín Chéng'ēn was dismissed,
and Wú Jìng was appointed Minister of Punishments.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day Gēngchén,
the Emperor made an imperial tour to Mùlán.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
the Emperor went hunting.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the hereditary official title of Lín Guóliáng, the Brigade-General of Guǎngdōng who was killed while apprehending bandits, was continued.
In the ninth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the tenth month of winter, on the first day Guǐsì,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the eleventh month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Wú Xióngguāng was dismissed,
and Yǒngbǎo was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng.
On the day Gēngyín,
Xīngzhào was appointed General of Hángzhōu.
In the twelfth month, on the first day Rénchén,
the Second Prince was ordered to go to the Dàgāodiàn to pray for snow.
On the day Jǐhài,
the Emperor prayed for snow.
On the day Yǐsì,
it snowed.
Zhōu Xīngdài was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the ancestral spirits were collectively sacrificed at the Tàimiào.
This year,
disaster taxes and uncollected taxes were remitted for thirteen prefectures, departments, and counties in Zhílì, Sìchuān, and other provinces.
The fixed land tax for fields washed away in eleven prefectures, departments, and counties in Zhílì, Jiāngsū, Zhèjiāng, Fújiàn, Yúnnán, Gānsù, and other provinces was abolished,
as were the fixed taxes on collapsed land in two salt fields in Zhèjiāng and Fújiàn.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú sent tribute.
In the fourteenth year (1799), on the first day Xīnyǒu of the first month of spring (Jǐsì year),
the Emperor's fiftieth birthday was celebrated,
and an imperial edict granting extensive favors was issued.
Miánzhì, son of Yǒngxuán, Prince Yíqīn, and Yìlún, grandson of Yǒngxīng, Prince Chéngqīn, were promoted to Bèilè,
and various favors were granted to princes and court officials.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Bǎilíng was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng.
On the day Rénshēn,
Guǎngxīng was found guilty and executed;
his son Yùnxiù was exiled to Jílín,
and his property confiscated.
Many others were demoted due to this case;
Chánglíng was exiled to Yīlí.
Hé Níng was appointed Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù.
In the second month, on the day Rénchén,
the Emperor attended the Jīngyán lectures.
On the day Rényín,
the Emperor composed the poem "Chóngjiǎn Shī" and the "Yìlì Biàn" (Discourse on Righteousness and Profit),
and distributed them to court officials.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Emperor visited the Dōnglíng mausoleum.
On the day Dīngsì,
Xǔ Sōngnián, the Brigade-General of Fújiàn, annihilated the pirate Zhū Fén,
and was granted a hereditary official title.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the third month, on the day Guǐhài,
the Emperor visited the Xīlíng mausoleum.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
he returned to the capital.
Delěngtài, General of Xī'ān and a Third-Class Duke, passed away.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Sōngyún reported that over a hundred exiled rebel soldiers, including Pú Dàfāng and Mǎ Yǒuyuán, were behaving unlawfully in exile,
and had all been executed separately.
The Emperor chastised him for indiscriminate killing
and stripped him of his office.
Jìnchāng was appointed General of Yīlí,
and Xīngzhào was appointed General of Jīngzhōu.
In the fourth month of summer, on the day Jiǎyín,
Hóng Yíng and 240 others were granted the Jinshì degree with various ranks.
Wú Xióngguāng was exiled to Yīlí;
this was due to Bǎilíng's impeachment.
Sūn Yùtíng was dismissed.
In the fifth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
a special imperial edict sternly criticized court officials for their laziness and negligence.
On the day Wùyín,
Yīnglún, the Censor for Grain Transport, was executed by strangulation for corruption and immorality.
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
the case of grain theft from the secret records of the granaries was uncovered,
and various former Vice Ministers were censured and demoted.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Sōngyún was appointed Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day Wùchén,
an edict ordered the suspension of this year's autumn executions.
Lǐ Yùchāng, the Zhīxiàn of Shānyáng, who was investigating relief efforts in Jiāngsū, was poisoned to death by Wáng Shēnhàn, the Zhīxiàn of Shānyáng.
The case was submitted to the ministry for investigation and verified.
Wáng Shēnhàn was immediately beheaded,
Wáng Gǔ, the Zhīfǔ, was immediately strangled,
and his household servants, including Lǐ Xiáng, received the severest punishments.
Tiě Bǎo, the Governor-General, was stripped of his office and exiled,
and Wāng Rìzhāng, the Governor, was stripped of his office.
The Emperor composed the poem "Mǐnzhōng Shī" (Lament for the Loyal),
and granted Lǐ Xīzuǒ, the adopted son of Lǐ Yùchāng, the title of Jǔrén, and Lǐ Qīngtài, the martial student who brought the complaint, the title of Wǔjǔ.
Álínbǎo was transferred to be Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
and Fāng Wéidiàn was appointed Governor-General of Mǐnzhè.
On the day Rénshēn,
Huā Jié, a Supervising Censor, was demoted for his unsubstantiated impeachment of Dài Qúhéng, a Grand Councillor, for favoritism.
On the day Yǐhài,
an edict stated:
"I am deeply troubled in my heart,
and whenever disaster is reported from any province,
I immediately bestow favors
and provide relief in many ways.
However, Governors-General and Governors fail to investigate carefully,
leading to cases of fraudulent relief.
For example, in the recent cases of Bǎochí and Shānyáng,
an upright investigating official was actually murdered.
How can this not be punished?
It is not that I begrudge anything.
Censor Zhōu Yuè therefore requested that for places reporting disaster,
separate Dao-Fu officials be appointed for detailed investigation.
But who knows if the Dao-Fu officials would also be capable and virtuous?
In the current Bǎochí case,
Guī Ēnyàn, the Tongzhī of the Eastern Circuit who had jurisdiction, indeed extorted three thousand liǎng of silver.
In the Shānyáng case,
Wáng Gǔ, the Zhīfǔ who had jurisdiction, received two thousand liǎng of silver.
If such Dao-Fu officials are encountered,
can they be trusted?
Dao-Fu officials also cannot visit every village,
and would still delegate to investigating officials,
making them even less trustworthy.
The key truly lies in Governors-General and Governors finding the right people.
As for considering disaster investigation difficult
and consequently collectively concealing disasters,
their fault would be even greater.
Let this be universally proclaimed."
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Emperor made an imperial tour to Mùlán.
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngxū,
Liú Fènggào, the Education Commissioner and Vice Minister of Zhèjiāng, was stripped of his office and
exiled to Hēilóngjiāng for malpractices in supervision.
Ruǎn Yuán, the Governor, was stripped of his office for concealment.
In the ninth month, on the day *jǐwèi*,
Qìngchéng was made Fúzhōu General.
On the day *gēngshēn*,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day *jǐsì*,
Zhāng Shīchéng reported in a memorial that Wáng Délù and Qiū Liánggōng had jointly attacked the pirate Cài Qiān,
pressing hard on the pirate ships,
breaking off a ship's stern,
whereupon Cài Qiān fell into the sea and drowned.
Wáng Délù was granted the title of Viscount,
and Qiū Liánggōng, Baron.
On the day *rénshēn*,
Bǎilíng petitioned to change the transport of salt from Yuè to overland,
which was granted.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day *guǐsì*,
it was the Emperor's birthday (*wànshòujié*).
He personally attended the Tàihé Diàn to receive congratulations
and bestowed a banquet.
On the day *gēngxū*,
Ālínbǎo petitioned to increase the conversion rate for grain tribute to silver,
but the Emperor sternly reprimanded him.
In the eleventh month, on the day *rénchén*,
Sōngyún was made Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
and Nàyànchéng, Governor-General of Shǎnxī-Gānsù.
In the twelfth month, on the day *wùxū*,
for failing to detect clerks in the Board of Works fraudulently claiming silver from the Board of Revenue and the Imperial Household Department,
Lùkāng and Fèichún, among others, were demoted and dismissed.
On the day *jiǎyín*,
a joint ancestral sacrifice was held at the Tàimiào.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted for twenty-four prefectures and counties in provinces such as Zhílì and Jiāngsū.
Land taxes were abolished for the low-lying areas of Wén'ān in Shùntiān, Qiánqīng Farm in Zhèjiāng, and collapsed land in Cházhōu, Húnán.
Cháoxiān, Liúqiú, Xiāmluó, Yuènán, and Nánzhǎng paid tribute.
In the fifteenth year, *gēngwǔ*, spring, the first month, on the day *bǐngzǐ*,
Liú Quánzhī was made Assistant Grand Secretary.
In the second month, on the day *jǐchǒu*,
the Emperor attended the imperial lecture (*jīngyán*).
On the day *rénchén*,
Chánglín was dismissed due to illness.
Hútúlǐ was made President of the Board of Punishments,
and Tuōjīn, President of the Board of Works.
On the day *bǐngshēn*,
Lèbǎo was summoned to the capital,
and Chángmíng was made Governor-General of Sìchuān.
On the day *bǐngzǐ*,
an edict was issued stating that opium injures life,
and all governors-general and governors were ordered to cut off its source.
In the third month, on the day *jiǎzǐ*,
the Emperor visited the Dōnglíng.
On the day *wùyín*,
the Emperor traveled to Nányuàn for a hunt.
On the day *guǐwèi*,
he returned to the capital.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day *dīngyǒu*,
the Emperor reviewed the soldiers of the Jiànruì Battalion.
In the fifth month, on the day *guǐhài*,
Lèbǎo was dismissed from Grand Secretary
for failing to report an anonymous letter,
and demoted to President of the Board of Works.
Lùkāng was reinstated as Grand Secretary,
and Míngliàng as Assistant Grand Secretary.
Dài Qúhēng was made Grand Secretary,
and Fèichún, President of the Board of Works.
In the sixth month, on the day *wùxū*,
the Vice Military Governor of Rèhé was changed to Military Governor,
and Jīlākān was appointed to fill the position.
On the day *rénzǐ*,
Bǎilíng was granted a hereditary rank of light cavalry commander (*qīngchē dūwèi shìzhí*)
for his功捕獲並押解海盜烏石二功.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day *jiǎyín*,
the Yǒngdìng Hé overflowed.
On the day *rénshēn*,
the Emperor toured Mùlán.
On the day *xīnsì*,
Xú Duān was made Governor-General of River Conservancy of the Southern River.
The Yúntī Guān estuary was modified,
and Mǎ Huìyù was ordered to supervise the work.
In the eighth month, on the day *wùxū*,
the Emperor went hunting.
On the day *rénzǐ*,
Zàobǎo was made Mongol Military Governor.
A Grand Commander of the Guǎngdōng Navy was established,
and a Brigade-General of the Yángjiāng Town Navy.
In the ninth month, on the day *jǐwèi*,
Wāng Zhìyī was made Governor-General of Mǐn-Zhè,
Mǎ Huìyù, Governor-General of Húguǎng,
and Gōng'ālā, President of the Board of Works.
On the day *jiǎzǐ*,
the breach in the Yǒngdìng Hé was closed.
On the day *jǐsì*,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day *yǐhài*,
the price of straw for the Southern River was increased.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day *jiǎwǔ*,
the Gāoyàn and Shānxū dikes in Jiāngnán breached.
On the day *dīngyǒu*,
the daily duty regulations for the Boards and Court were set.
In the eleventh month, on the day *rénxū*,
the former Jílín General Xiùlín was granted death
for embezzling ginseng silver.
In the twelfth month, on the day *bǐngshēn*,
Guǎngxī reported in a memorial that the centenarian Lán Xiáng was one hundred and forty-two years old,
and was specially granted imperial poems, an imperial calligraphic plaque, a sixth-rank cap button, and fifty taels of silver.
On the day *dīngyǒu*,
Mǎ Huìyù reported in a memorial that the great work at Yúntī Guān had been completed and closed,
and the river had returned to its proper course to the sea.
An imperial edict of commendation was received.
On the day *jǐhài*,
Chén Fèngxiáng was made Governor-General of River Conservancy of Jiāngnán.
On the day *rénchén*,
Xīngzhào was transferred to Cháhā'ěr Military Governor.
On the day *jǐyǒu*,
a joint ancestral sacrifice was held at the Tàimiào.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted for seven prefectures and counties in Zhílì.
Land taxes were abolished for collapsed fields in Dāntú and Shànghǎi, Jiāngsū,
and廢田 in Wúwéizhōu, Ānhuī.
Cháoxiān and Xiāmluó paid tribute.
In the sixteenth year, *xīnwèi*, spring, the first month, on the day *wùwǔ*,
due to the newly constructed long dike at Mǎgǎng, Yúntī Guān,
the Huáihǎi Circuit was added,
and two Assistant Prefects (*tóngzhī*) for Hǎi'ān and Hǎifù Departments.
On the day *guǐyǒu*,
Bǎilíng was made President of the Board of Punishments,
Sōngyún was transferred to Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng,
and Lèbǎo was made Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng.
In the second month, on the day *rénwǔ*,
the Emperor attended the imperial lecture (*jīngyán*).
On the day *dīnghài*,
a sacrifice was made to the former teacher Kǒngzǐ.
An imperial edict stated:
"Because of the excessive expenditure on river works in the Southern River for consecutive years, amounting to over forty million,
We specially ordered Tuōjīn and Chū Pénglíng to investigate.
According to their report,
the accounts for silver receipts and expenditures for the works appear to be consistent,
but the projects are not entirely solid.
This is indeed the fault of successive river officials.
Wú Jǐng and Xú Duān are both demoted and dismissed in varying degrees.
All personnel involved in the works are also dismissed.
The sixty thousand taels of silver that have not yet been disbursed
are also to be withheld."
In the third month, on the day *bǐngyín*,
the Emperor visited the Xīlíng.
On the day *rénwǔ*,
after the completion of the visit to the mausoleum,
he made a western tour to Wǔtái Shān.
On the day *yǐhài*,
President of the Board of Works Fèi Chún died,
and was posthumously granted Grand Secretary.
Prince Sù Yǒngxī was made Mongol Military Governor.
In the intercalary third month, on the day *gēngchén*,
the Emperor stayed at Wǔtái Shān.
On the day *yǐyǒu*,
the Emperor returned.
On the day *bǐngshēn*,
the Emperor paid respects and performed rites at Yáo Mǔ Líng and Dì Yáo Miào.
On the day *wùxū*,
the Emperor reviewed the Green Standard Army in Zhílì,
visited Liánchí Shūyuàn,
and sent an official to offer sacrifices at the shrine of Míng minister Yáng Jìshèng.
On the day *guǐmǎo*,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day *wùshēn*,
Grand Secretary Dài Qúhēng died.
On the day *jiǎzǐ*,
the Emperor prayed for rain.
The retired Assistant Grand Secretary Chánglín died.
On the day *rénshēn*,
Jiǎng Lìyōng and two hundred and thirty-seven others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with varying ranks.
Fúqìng was made Manchu Military Governor,
and Chónglù, Mongol Military Governor.
In the fifth month, on the day *xīnsì*,
Liú Quánzhī was made Grand Secretary,
Zōu Bǐngtài, Assistant Grand Secretary,
and Liú Huánzhī, President of the Board of War.
On the day *dīnghài*,
the Emperor again went to the Altar of Heavenly Spirits to pray for rain.
On the day *gēngyín*,
it rained.
In the sixth month, on the day *rénwǔ*,
Míngliàng was demoted to Vice Military Governor
for an untrue report.
Sōngyún was made Assistant Grand Secretary.
On the day *guǐchǒu*,
Lùkāng was demoted to Vice Military Governor
for an untrue report.
Lèbǎo was made Grand Secretary
and was put in charge of the Board of Civil Appointments.
Jílún was made President of the Board of Works and Commander of the Infantry.
On the day *yǐchǒu*,
Fù Nài, Surveillance Commissioner of Húnán, died,
and was posthumously granted Governor
and permitted to have a dedicated shrine built.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day Wùyín,
Lú Yìnpǔ, a Junior Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments (Guānglù Sì Shàocīng), was ordered to serve in the Grand Council (Jūnjī Chù),
and granted the honorary title of a Fourth-Rank Minister (Sìpǐn Qīng Xián).
On the day Rénchén,
Westerners were forbidden from secretly residing in the interior.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the Emperor made an imperial tour to Mùlán.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Lǐjiālóu River in Jiāngnán burst its banks.
On the day Yǐsì,
Xīngzhào was relieved of his duties due to old age,
and Gòngchǔkèzhābù was appointed as Cháhā'ěr Dutǒng.
In the eighth month, on the day Rénxū,
the Emperor went on a hunting expedition.
In the ninth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
a shrine for the spirit of the Dàlǐng Mountain in Xìng'ān was built,
with sacrifices offered in spring and autumn.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Sōngjūn was appointed Minister of Personnel (Lìbù Shàngshū),
and Jiǎng Yōuxiǎn was appointed Governor-General of Guǎngdōng and Guǎngxī (Liǎngguǎng Zǒngdū).
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the Emperor visited the imperial mausoleums.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the Yí people of Shí'èr zhīlǐng in Sìchuān assimilated,
and their native administration (tǔguān) was replaced by regular administrative officials (liúguān).
In the eleventh month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
an imperial edict ordered that the management of the Pī and Sù sections of the Grand Canal engineering projects be returned to river officials.
In the twelfth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
Héyǒuníng was appointed General of Shèngjīng.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the collective sacrifice (xiápjì) was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple (Tàimiào).
In this year,
disaster relief taxes were remitted for eight prefectures and counties in Shùntiān, Jiāngsū, Hénán, and other provinces.
Arrears of taxes in Gānsù were remitted,
and also land taxes for the Huí (Muslim) agricultural estates in Kāshígá'ěr were remitted.
Cháoxiǎn, Liúqiú, Xiāmluó, and Miǎndiàn paid tribute.
In the first month of spring of the seventeenth year, Rénshēn, on the day Rénwǔ,
the seasonal sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple,
