and the second imperial son was commanded to perform the ceremony.
In the second month, on the first day, Jiǎchén,
the Emperor presided over the imperial lectures (Jīngyán).
In the third month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
the Emperor visited the Eastern Mausoleums (Dōnglíng).
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the Emperor made an imperial tour to Nányuàn for a hunting expedition.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Míngliàng was appointed General of Xī'ān.
On the day Rénchén,
the Emperor ascended Liàngyīngtái,
and held a grand review of the officials and soldiers of the Eight Banners.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the fourth month of summer, on the day Jiǎchén,
an imperial edict stated:
"The population of the Eight Banners is increasing daily,
and it is urgently necessary to devise extensive plans for their livelihood.
I have heard that the fertile land of Jílín is vast and sparsely populated.
Beyond the Liǔtiáobiān (Willow Palisade),
the ginseng fields have moved far away,
and the open spaces in between,
no less than over a thousand li,
are mostly rich soil.
Migrant people occasionally go there to cultivate.
It is appropriate to follow the precedent of Lālín established during the Qiánlóng reign,
to send idle banner members to Jílín,
allocate land to them,
either for cultivation or tenancy,
to provide for their sustenance.
During agricultural slack seasons, they can still practice horsemanship and archery,
to be ready for service,
thus benefiting both their livelihood and military training.
The generals and others concerned should carefully plan and devise arrangements for their settlement,
and report in detail."
On the day Bǐngchén,
the Emperor reviewed the soldiers of the Jiànruìyíng.
On the day Guǐhài,
Zhākètǎ'ěr, commander of the Imperial Guards (Hùjūn Tǒnglǐng), passed away,
and was granted three hundred taels of silver.
In the fifth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Wēn Chénghuì reported the arrest of Dǒng Huáixìn and others belonging to the evil cults of Jīndān and Bāguà in Luánzhōu.
An imperial decree ordered their severe punishment.
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐsì,
idle imperial clansmen (zōngshì) were relocated to Shèngjīng to reside,
and houses, land, and silver were provided.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day Wùzǐ,
the Emperor made an imperial tour to Mùlán.
In the eighth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Chén Fèngxiáng was dismissed for incompetence,
and Lí Shìxù was appointed Governor-General of Riverways in Jiāngnán (Jiāngnán Hédào Zǒngdū).
On the day Jiǎyín,
Ruǎn Yuán was appointed Governor-General of Grain Transport (Cáoyùn Zǒngdū).
On the day Bǐngchén,
the Emperor went on a hunting expedition.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Qìngguì was dismissed due to old age,
and Sōngjūn was appointed Grand Councilor (Jūnjī Dàchén).
In the tenth month of winter, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Gōng'ālā was appointed Minister of Rites (Lǐbù Shàngshū).
In the eleventh month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Jǐng'ān was appointed Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs (Lǐfānyuàn Shàngshū) concurrently as Hánjūn Dūtǒng.
In the twelfth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Tiěbǎo was appointed Minister of Rites (Lǐbù Shàngshū),
and Pān Shì'ēn was appointed Minister of Works (Gōngbù Shàngshū).
On the day Jiǎyín,
Xīngzhào was appointed General of Jiāngníng.
In this year,
disaster relief taxes, tax arrears, and banner rent were remitted for twenty-seven prefectures and counties in Shùntiān, Fèngtiān, Zhílì, Hénán, Ānhuī, and other provinces,
and the land tax in Gámǎlán, Táiwān, which was washed away by floods.
Cháoxiǎn and Xiāmluó paid tribute.
In the first month of spring of the eighteenth year, Guǐyǒu, on the day Yǐhài,
Grand Councilor Sōngjūn was dismissed and appointed Imperial Bodyguard (Yùqián Dàchén),
and Lèbǎo was appointed Grand Councilor.
In the second month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
the Emperor presided over the imperial lectures (Jīngyán).
In the third month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
the Emperor made an imperial tour to Nányuàn for a hunting expedition.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the Emperor visited the Western Mausoleums (Xīlíng).
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the fourth month of summer, on the day Jǐhài,
Míngliàng was appointed Mongolian Dutǒng.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Emperor prayed for rain.
On the day Guǐhài,
Fùjùn was appointed General of Hēilóngjiāng.
In the fifth month, on the day Gēngchén,
the Emperor prayed for rain.
On the day Rénchén,
it rained.
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Bāo Tíngbó, a student who submitted books, was granted the title of Jǔrén.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Sōngjūn was appointed General of Yīlí.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day Jiǎxū,
the laws against trafficking and selling opium were strictly enforced,
and users were also punished.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Censor Féng Dàzhōng submitted a memorial stating that officials both inside and outside the capital were slow and negligent in their duties,
and requested an imperial edict for investigation and review.
The Emperor approved it.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Emperor made an imperial tour to Mùlán.
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngxū,
the Emperor went on a hunting expedition.
In the ninth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Emperor, due to continuous rain, reduced the siege.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to his imperial residence.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the Hé'nán Suīzhōu River overflowed.
In Huáxiàn, Hé'nán, Lǐ Wénchéng, a leader of the Bāguà Jiàofěi, gathered a multitude to plot rebellion.
The county magistrate, Qiáng Kèjié, arrested and imprisoned him.
His confederates, Féng Kèshàn and Niú Liàngchén, captured the county seat,
and Qiáng Kèjié died.
The rebel factions in Chángyuán, Zhílì, and Cáoxiàn, Shāndōng, all responded.
The Emperor ordered Gāo Shí and Tóng Xīng to defend and block,
and Wēn Chénghuì, bearing the seal of an Imperial Commissioner, to suppress them.
Yáng Yùchūn was summoned to lead troops north.
The rebel faction led by Xú Ānguó captured Chángyuán,
and killed the county magistrate Zhào Lún.
The Jīnxiāng county magistrate, Wú Jiē, arrested the rebels Cuī Shìjùn and others.
On the *wùyín* day,
the Emperor's procession passed Bāojìshān.
On this day,
dozens of traitors led by Chén Shuǎng suddenly broke into the Zǐjìnchéng,
and attempted to force their way into the inner palace.
The Emperor's second son shot and killed one of them with a gun.
One rebel climbed the wall of Yuèhuámén,
holding a flag and directing others.
The Emperor's second son again shot him, causing him to fall,
and Bèilè Miánzhì subsequently killed another.
The princes and high ministers led the Jiànruì and Huǒqìyíng soldiers in,
and captured and beheaded all of them.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
an imperial edict enfeoffed the Emperor's second son as Zhìqīnwáng,
and Miánzhì with the title of Jùnwáng.
For their meritorious service in capturing the rebels,
each was rewarded.
Jí Lún was stripped of his office,
and Yīng Hé was appointed Commander of the Infantry.
On the *gēngchén* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"I have inherited the great lineage,
and dare not indulge in leisure,
nor commit acts of tyranny against the people.
Since the suppression of the Jiàofěi in Chuān and Chǔ,
I had hoped to share the blessings of peace with my people.
Yet, yesterday, on the fifteenth day of the ninth month,
an extraordinary event occurred within the Great Inner Palace.
Such a thing was unheard of in the Hàn, Táng, Sòng, or Míng dynasties,
and I am truly ashamed.
However, though the change occurred in a single morning,
the disaster had been accumulating for a long time.
The greatest current affliction
lies solely in procrastination and idleness.
Although I have repeatedly warned and admonished,
to the point of wearing out my tongue and dulling my brush,
it has ultimately been insufficient to move my officials to listen.
I can only reflect upon myself and make amends.
May my officials who wish to be loyal and good
devote their full effort,
rectify my faults,
and correct the will of the people.
Do not continue to hold office idly as before,
thereby increasing my shortcomings.
Let this be universally known."
Nà Yànchéng was appointed Imperial Commissioner
to suppress the rebels in Hé'nán.
Tídū Yáng Yùchūn, Fùdūtǒng Fùsēngdé, and Zǒngbīng Yáng Fāng were ordered to lead troops to assist in the suppression.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the chief rebel Lín Qīng was captured.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Sōngyún and Cáo Zhènyōng were appointed Grand Secretaries,
Tuō Jīn and Bǎilíng as Assistant Grand Secretaries,
and Tiě Bǎo and Zhāng Xù as Ministers of Personnel.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the chief rebel Lín Qīng, the collaborating inner eunuch Liú Jìnhēng, and others were executed.
In the winter, tenth month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
Zǔ Zhīwàng was dismissed,
and Hán Fēng was appointed Minister of Justice.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Liú Qīng, Salt Commissioner of Shāndōng, greatly defeated the rebels at Hùjiājí.
Shìwèi Sū'ěrshèn recaptured Dìngtáo and Cáoxiàn.
Censor Zhāng Péngzhǎn submitted a memorial, stating
that the common people dared not report wicked bandits
because local officials evaded punishment
and refused to handle such cases,
or even falsely accused the informers.
The Emperor approved of this.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Nà Yànchéng memorialized, proposing to gather troops from various routes
and launch another attack.
The Emperor sternly reprimanded him.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Tuō Jīn was ordered to oversee military affairs in Hé'nán,
and Guì Fāng entered the Jūnjīchù.
On the *dīngsì* day,
hereditary posts were granted to the Imperial Guards such as Nàlún who were wounded or killed resisting the rebels in the Forbidden City.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Lù Kāng and Yù Ruì, for failing to detect their subordinates' participation in the rebellion,
were sent to Shèngjīng for imprisonment.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
officials of the Han banner and Zhílì籍 among the Kedao officials were demoted.
On the *rénxū* day,
Míng Liàng was appointed Minister of War.
In the eleventh month, on the first day, *jiǎzǐ*,
Nà Yànchéng memorialized, reporting the capture of the Dàokǒu rebel stronghold
and the commencement of the siege of Huáichéng.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
an imperial decree ordered the deletion and reduction of public offense regulations.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the collaborating Dūsi Cáo Lún was executed.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Nà Yànchéng memorialized, reporting that Yáng Fāng and others had captured the Sīzhàishān rebel stronghold
and killed the chief culprit Lǐ Wénchéng.
In the twelfth month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
Sōngyún and Chánglíng were ordered to deliberate on the expenses for Xīnjiāng.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Nà Yànchéng memorialized, reporting the capture of Huáichéng,
the execution of rebel leaders Sòng Yuánchéng and others,
and the capture of Niú Liàngchén and others.
Nà Yànchéng was granted the title of Earl of the Third Rank,
and Yáng Yùchūn and others were rewarded in descending order of merit.
Tuō Jīn was ordered to remain and handle the rebel bandits in Chángyuán.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted for twenty-six prefectures and counties in Zhílì, Hé'nán, Húnán, and other provinces.
Land taxes on abandoned fields in Jiāngsū, Hé'nán, and Húnán were abolished.
Cháoxiǎn, Liúqiú, Yuènán, and Xiāmluó paid tribute.
In the nineteenth year, *jiǎxū*, in spring, the first month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
Wú Jìng was appointed Governor-General of River Conservancy for Hédōng.
In the second month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Emperor presided over the Jīngyán lectures.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Jìn Chāng was appointed General of Shèngjīng.
On the *rénvín* day,
Chéngdū General Sài Chōng'ē, for suppressing the Shǎnxī rebels Miáo Xiǎoyī and others,
was granted the title of Earl of the Third Rank.
Chánglíng was granted the title of Qīngjū Dūwèi,
and Yáng Yùchūn was promoted to Earl of the First Rank.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Fù Jùn was appointed General of Jílín,
and Tèyīshùnbǎo was appointed General of Hēilóngjiāng.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Tiě Bǎo was dismissed,
and Yīng Hé was appointed Minister of Personnel.
Yì Shào was appointed Hānjūn Dūtǒng.
Dài Jūnyuán was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
In the intercalary second month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Hé Níng was appointed Minister of Rites.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
hereditary posts were granted to the deceased county magistrate of Huáxiàn, Qiáng Kèjié, the instructor Lǚ Bǐngjūn, the patrol inspector Liú Bīn, and others, who died in service.
In the fourth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
the Emperor reviewed the Jiànruìyíng troops.
Yùqīnwáng Yùfēng, for failing to detect his subordinate Zhù Xiàn joining the sect
and plotting rebellion, which was discovered
but not reported to the throne,
was stripped of his princely title.
His younger brother Yù Xīng inherited the title.
Xīng Zhào was appointed Hānjūn Dūtǒng.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Grand Canal Governor Guì Fāng died.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Lóng Rǔyán and two hundred twenty-six others were granted the *jìnshì* degree in various ranks.
In the fifth month, on the *guǐhài* day,
Hé Níng was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Rèhé.
In the sixth month, on the first day, *gēngshēn*,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Liú Huánzhī was appointed Minister of Revenue,
and Chū Pénglíng was appointed Minister of War.
He was concurrently acting Governor of Jiāngsū.
In the eighth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Emperor presided over the Jīngyán lectures.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Grand Secretary, Count of Wēiqín, Lè Bǎo, again requested retirement,
which was granted,
and he was ordered to continue receiving his count's stipend.
Tuō Jīn was appointed Grand Secretary,
and Míng Liàng was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary.
On the *wùyín* day,
the Emperor visited the imperial tombs.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the ninth month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
Jǐng Ān was appointed Minister of Revenue.
In winter, tenth month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
Qìng Pǔ was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Ruǎn Yuán, Governor of Jiāngxī, for capturing local bandits,
was given the additional title of Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
In the eleventh month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
orders were given to reclaim barren land in Yīlí and Jílín.
In the twelfth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
Bǎilíng was dismissed as Assistant Grand Secretary,
and Zhāng Xù was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
a collective sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted for two counties in Zhílì, two counties in Hé'nán, and various cities in Hēilóngjiāng.
Land taxes on abandoned fields in Xiùyán, Fèngtiān, and four counties in Xī'ān, Zhèjiāng, were abolished.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú paid tribute.
In the spring, the first month, jiǎwǔ day, of the 20th year, the yīhài year,
a seasonal offering was made at the Tàimiào,
and Zhì Qīnwáng was ordered to perform the rites.
In the second month, jǐwèi day,
the Emperor attended the Jīngyán lectures.
In the third month, gēngyín day,
the Emperor visited the Dōnglíng.
On wùshēn day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On jiǎwǔ day,
Chū Pénglíng was demoted
for his unsubstantiated impeachment of Bǎilíng and for interceding on behalf of Máo Yù, who feigned illness.
He was demoted.
Subsequently, after Bǎilíng's investigation and counter-impeachment,
Chū Pénglíng was dismissed from office.
On jǐyǒu day,
Jiǎng Yōuxiān, Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng, submitted a memorial outlining regulations for prohibiting opium.
An imperial edict was issued:
"When foreign ships arrive at Àomén,
they are to be searched according to the vessel to
cut off the source.
Officials who connive in its release and commoners who privately traffic it
shall be punished separately."
In the summer, the fourth month, jǐsì day,
the Emperor reviewed the Jiànruìyíng troops.
On rénwǔ day,
the Emperor composed "Guānzhēn" (Admonitions for Officials) in twenty-six chapters,
which he promulgated to his ministers and officials.
In the fifth month, dīnghài day,
the Ministry of Justice memorialized,
having clarified that Zhīfǔ Wáng Shùxūn was in fact the monk Míngxīn,
who had fraudulently obtained official positions through donation and guarantee.
An imperial edict was issued: he was to be caged for two months
and banished to Hēilóngjiāng.
Jiǎng Yǔpú, the Shìláng who had joined a sect, was dismissed from office.
In the sixth month, wùchén day,
the Emperor composed "Qínzhèng Àimín Lùn" (On Diligent Governance and Loving the People),
which he promulgated to all within and without the court.
On jǐmǎo day,
Cháng Míng reported that Luòbù Qīlì, a native chieftain in Zhānduì, was causing trouble.
General Rō Sījǔ was re-appointed to proceed from Xià Zhānduì to suppress him.
General Luó Shēnggāo, who had been ineffective in the suppression, and Dūshī Tú Táng'ā, who had reported the matter, were both dismissed from office and arrested for questioning.
In the autumn, the seventh month, jiǎwǔ day,
General Luó Sījǔ completed the suppression of the native chieftain Luòbù Qīlì in Zhānduì.
The matter was submitted to the ministries for deliberation.
On guǐmǎo day,
the Emperor made an imperial tour to Mùlán.
In the eighth month, wùchén day,
the Emperor went hunting.
Bǎilíng was promoted to a third-class Nán
for his achievement in capturing Fāng Róngshēng, the principal offender who had compiled rebellious writings.
In the ninth month, jǐhài day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the winter, the tenth month, gēngshēn day,
Sōngyún was summoned to the capital,
and Chánglíng was appointed General of Yīlí.
On guǐhài day,
Shìláng Nàyànbǎo was ordered to investigate the earthquake disaster in Shānxī.
In the eleventh month, dīnghài day,
Lǐ Qīnwáng Zhāolián was stripped of his title and imprisoned
for using torture in a case involving a tenant's unpaid rent,
and Línzhǐ succeeded him.
In the twelfth month, jǐmǎo day,
a collective sacrifice was made at the Tàimiào.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted for Níngjìn and two other counties in Zhílì.
Land taxes were abolished for wasteland in Bǎoshān and Jìngjiāng in Jiāngsū,
and Jìnglè in Shānxī.
The total population of the empire was counted as 326,574,895 people,
and the grain stored in granaries amounted to 30,802,869 dàn, 9 dòu, 1 shēng, 7 hé, 5 sháo.
Cháoxiǎn, Liúqiú, and Xiānmó came to pay tribute.
In the spring, the first month, bǐngxū day, of the 21st year, the bǐngzǐ year,
a special edict commanded all Qīnwáng and Jùnwáng not to allow eunuchs to memorialize on their behalf,
lest it lead to collusion.
In the second month, rénzǐ day,
the Emperor attended the Jīngyán lectures.
On jiǎxū day,
the Emperor visited the Dōnglíng.
On gēngchén day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the third month, gēngyín day,
the Emperor visited the Xīlíng.
On xīntǐ day,
the Emperor visited the tomb of the late Grand Secretary Zhū Guī to offer condolences.
On dīngwèi day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
In the summer, the fourth month, bǐngzǐ day,
Zhāng Shīchéng was dismissed
for returning to his hometown without awaiting an imperial edict
after submitting a memorial concerning his father's illness.
Hú Kèjiā was appointed Governor of Jiāngsū.
In the fifth month, xīnmǎo day,
Mǎ Huìyù was appointed Left Dū Yùshǐ,
and Sūn Yùtíng was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng.
On dīngwèi day,
Èlèzhéyītú was appointed Yùqián Dàchén.
In the sixth month, dīngchǒu day,
the retired Grand Secretary Qìngguì died.
On wùyín day,
Nàyànchéng was dismissed from office and arrested for questioning due to an incident,
and Fāng Shòuchóu was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì.
In the intercalary sixth month, wùxū day,
Zhāolián was released from confinement.
On rénzǐ day,
Dài Jūnyuán was appointed Shàngshū of the Ministry of Personnel.
In the autumn, the seventh month, yǐmǎo day,
Hé Shìtài, Mùkèdēng'é, and Sūlèng'é were all demoted
for their unfamiliarity with proper procedures
in leading the British envoy,
which prevented his audience.
Sōngyún was appointed Mǎnzhōu Dūtǒng,
and Héníng was appointed Shàngshū of the Ministry of Works.
On yǐchǒu day,
the Emperor made an imperial tour to Mùlán.
In the eighth month, rénchén day,
the Emperor went hunting.
In the ninth month, wùwǔ day,
the Emperor returned to the capital,
reviewing troops at Gǔběikǒu.
On rénxū day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the winter, the tenth month, wùzǐ day,
Sōngyún was ordered to act as Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
and Zhāng Xù was appointed Jūnjī Dàchén.
In the eleventh month, rénzǐ day,
Bǎilíng died.
Sūn Yùtíng was transferred to be Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
and Ruǎn Yuán was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng.
On bǐngchén day,
Miánzhì was appointed Lǐngshìwèi Nèidàchén.
In the twelfth month, guǐmǎo day,
a collective sacrifice was made at the Tàimiào.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted in varying degrees for fifty-six zhou and xian in provinces such as Zhílì, Hénán, Zhèjiāng, and Húnán.
Cháoxiǎn, Liúqiú, and Yīngjílì came to pay tribute.
In the spring, the first month, rénshēn day, of the 22nd year, the dīngchǒu year,
the Emperor attended the Jīngyán lectures.
In the second month, dīngchǒu day,
a sacrifice was offered to the Former Master Kǒngzǐ.
On guǐwèi day,
Chánglíng was appointed Governor-General of Shǎnxī-Gānsù,
Jìnchāng was appointed General of Yīlí,
and Fùjùn was appointed General of Shèngjīng.
In the third month, the first day, jiǎchén,
Dǒng Jiàozēng was appointed Governor-General of Mǐn-Zhè.
On wùshēn day,
a new Commander-in-Chief (Zǒngbīngguān) was established for the Tiānjīn Naval Camp,
specifically overseeing two naval battalions.
On rénzǐ day,
the Emperor visited the Dōnglíng.
On jǐsì day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On xīnwèi day,
Zhāng Xù was dismissed.
Dài Jūnyuán was appointed to assist the Grand Secretaries,
Lú Yìnpǔ was appointed Shàngshū of the Ministry of War,
and Wāng Tíngzhēn was appointed Left Dū Yùshǐ.
In the summer, the fourth month, dīnghài day,
the Emperor reviewed the Jiànruìyíng troops.
On gēngyín day,
the midsummer horse tribute from Yīlí was suspended.
On xīnmǎo day,
the Yi bandits in Yúnnán were pacified,
and Bólín was granted the title of Tàizǐ Shàobǎo.
On wùxū day,
Wú Qíjùn and 255 others were granted the Jinshì Jídì and other degrees.
In the fifth month, xīnyǒu day,
the Emperor prayed for rain.
On rénxū day,
it rained.
Yùlín was appointed Resident Minister in Tibet.
On dīngmǎo day,
Lǐ Gēngyún, the Financial Commissioner of Fújiàn, was falsely accused and committed suicide.
Xīchāng and Wáng Yǐnzhī were dispatched to investigate the matter,
and the truth was ascertained.
An imperial decree ordered: Governor-General Wāng Zhìyī and Governor Wáng Shàolán were both dismissed from office.
On rénshēn day,
the Emperor composed "Wàngyǔ Xǐngqiān Shuō" (On Looking at the Rain and Reflecting on One's Faults).
In the sixth month, jiǎxū day,
Sōngyún memorialized requesting the cessation of the imperial visit to the ancestral tombs next year.
An imperial decree sternly rebuked him,
dismissed him as Grand Secretary,
and demoted him to Dūtǒng of Cháhā'ěr.
Míngliàng was appointed Grand Secretary,
Bólín was appointed to assist the Grand Secretaries,
and Héníng was appointed Shàngshū of the Ministry of War.
Sàichōng'ā was appointed Yùqián Dàchén,
and Déníng'ā was appointed General of Chéngdū.
In the autumn, the seventh month, gēngshēn day,
the Emperor made an imperial tour to Mùlán.
Sūlèng'é was appointed Shàngshū of the Ministry of Works,
and Hé Shìtài was appointed Shàngshū of the Lǐfānyuàn.
In the eighth month, dīnghài day,
the Emperor went hunting.
On rénchén day,
Jīlākān was dismissed,
and Yùxiù was appointed General of Hángzhōu.
In the ninth month, on the day _Guǐchǒu_ (the 20th day of the 60-day cycle),
Chángmíng died.
Jiǎng Yōuxiān was appointed Governor-General of Sìchuān,
Ruǎn Yuán was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng,
and Qìngbǎo was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng.
On the day _Gēngshēn_ (the 57th day),
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day _Gēngwǔ_ (the 7th day),
the Emperor composed "A Treatise on Admonishing Ministers"
and distributed it to the Dūcháyuàn.
In winter, on the first day of the tenth month, _Xīnwèi_ (the 8th day),
there was a solar eclipse.
In the eleventh month, on the day _Yǐchǒu_ (the 2nd day),
Yīchōng'ā was appointed General of Rèhé.
In the twelfth month, on the day _Jiǎxū_ (the 11th day),
arrears of silver from the copper mines in Yúnnán were remitted.
On the day _Dīngyǒu_ (the 34th day),
the combined sacrifice was performed at the Tàimiào.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted for eight counties in Zhílì and three cities in Hēilóngjiāng.
Land taxes that had been washed away by floods or covered by rivers were remitted for Chéngdé in Fèngtiān,
Dìngzhōu in Zhílì,
Dāntú and Jiāngyīn in Jiāngsū,
Fēngchéng in Jiāngxī,
Mèngxiàn in Hénán,
and Hóuguān in Fújiàn, among other counties.
Cháoxiǎn, Liúqiú, and Yuènán paid tribute.
In the twenty-third year, _Wùyín_ (the 15th year of the cycle), in the spring, in the first month, on the day _Wùshēn_ (the 45th day),
a special imperial edict ordered Sōngyún not to seek fame or favor,
to preserve his remaining years.
On the day _Jiǎyín_ (the 51st day),
an imperial edict stated that Míngliàng, being over eighty years old,
should conserve his energy and rest,
and was no longer required to report for duty regularly,
nor to lead audiences or receive imperial decrees.
In the second month, on the day _Gēngwǔ_ (the 7th day),
Dài Jūnyuán and Héníng were appointed Grand Councilors.
Grand Secretary Dǒng Gào retired,
and was granted his full salary.
On the day _Gēngchén_ (the 17th day),
the Emperor attended the imperial lecture.
On the day _Jǐchǒu_ (the 26th day),
the Emperor reviewed the Firearms Division troops.
In the third month, on the day _Gēngzǐ_ (the 37th day),
the Emperor visited the Xīlíng.
On the day _Gēngxū_ (the 47th day),
Zhāng Xù was appointed Grand Secretary,
Wāng Tíngzhēn was appointed President of the Board of Rites,
and Wú Fāngpéi was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
On the day _Wùwǔ_ (the 55th day),
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the fourth month, on the first day, _Wùchén_ (the 5th day),
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day _Yǐhài_ (the 12th day),
there was a windstorm with haze.
On the day _Bǐngzǐ_ (the 13th day),
an imperial edict stated:
"Yesterday, at the third _kè_ of the beginning of the _yǒu_ hour (around 5:45 PM),
a violent wind came from the southeast,
and dust and haze filled all four directions.
It was only by lighting candles that colors could be distinguished.
This phenomenon is extremely unusual.
My heart is filled with awe and trepidation,
and I ponder the reason for the warning from Heaven above.
Referring to the 'Prohibitions of the Great Plan' and its ominous omens,
and understanding the meaning of 'constant wind and alike' (referring to unusual winds),
all these are due to my lack of clarity in governance and improper use of personnel.
Those who have the responsibility to speak out,
understanding my fear in the face of disaster,
should present their arguments earnestly
without concealing anything.
Even if there are common people who have grievances,
they may also directly present them based on facts,
to fulfill my intention of cultivating virtue and averting disaster."
Censor Lú Zhè submitted a memorial, stating
that the wind and sand were a warning,
and requested that officials be prohibited from seeking credit through indiscriminate arrests,
which harasses innocent people.
An imperial decree was issued:
"What has been reported is very true.
After the fugitives from the Lín Qīng case were ordered to be pursued,
the officers responsible for the pursuit often made arrests of other offenders to fulfill their duty.
Runners and soldiers,
taking advantage of the opportunity, indulged in tyranny,
making false accusations and extorting captives,
stopping at nothing.
By the time they are brought to official judgment,
they are already skin and bones,
their wealth completely squandered,
and some even die as a result.
Their grievances are beyond appeal,
which is certainly the cause of this disaster.
All the secondary fifty-odd offenders
are to be generally suspended from pursuit.
Even the six offenders, such as Zhù Xiàn,
are only to be registered by the Board of Punishments,
and dealt with upon capture.
Henceforth, if arresting officers commit the aforementioned offenses,
the responsible officials shall severely punish them,
and their family property shall be given to the families of those falsely accused,
so that evil practices may be deterred and the good and weak be made secure."
On the day _Jǐmǎo_ (the 16th day),
the Imperial Observatory submitted a memorial, stating:
"Respectfully, according to the 'Correct Meaning of Astronomy,'
when the heavens and earth are obscured in all four directions,
as if rain of dust is falling,
it is called _mái_ (haze).
Therefore, it is said that when heaven and earth are hazy,
the ruler and ministers are at odds,
there will be great drought,
and also that rice prices will be high."
An imperial decree was issued:
"The event on the eighth day
is indeed consistent with the phenomenon described in the 'Correct Meaning.'
However, I conscientiously follow established precedents,
daily summoning my officials for audience,
consulting them extensively from the front of the mat,
so it seems unlikely that there would be discord.
But this is merely the outward appearance;
in reality, how many are there who share my heart's desire for good governance!
How many indeed!
Not daring to admonish me directly,
but speaking behind my back after withdrawing,
appearing united but disunited in sentiment –
this is indeed discord.
Among their colleagues,
not acting with the harmony of a gentleman but with the conformity of a petty person –
this is also discord.
May our ruler and ministers both take this as a warning."
On the day _Gēngchén_ (the 17th day),
the Emperor prayed for rain.
On the day _Wùzǐ_ (the 25th day),
the Emperor prayed for rain again.
On the day _Xīnmǎo_ (the 28th day),
it rained.
In the fifth month, on the day _Wùxū_ (the 35th day),
an imperial edict stated:
"The academicians presented the imperially commissioned _Míngjiàn_,
which, for the Wànlì and Tiānqǐ eras, included matters of the previous dynasty's founding,
and also added commentary in praise,
which is inappropriate in terms of style and precedent.
The Vice-President, Assistant Minister Xiùníng, is demoted to Imperial Bodyguard,
and sent to Xīnjiāng for rotation.
The President, Cáo Zhènyōng, and others are each given minor penalties,
and a new compilation is to be undertaken."
In the sixth month, on the day _Rénshēn_ (the 9th day),
the Qìn River overflowed at Wǔzhì,
but a report of its closure was soon received.
In the seventh month, on the day _Jiǎzǐ_ (the 1st day),
the Emperor's eastern tour commenced.
In the eighth month, on the first day, _Dīngmǎo_ (the 4th day),
an imperial edict remitted the regular taxes for four prefectures and counties in Fèngtiān and Chéngdé, as the imperial route passed through common fields.
On the day _Wùzǐ_ (the 25th day),
the _Huángcháo Tōnglǐ_ was promulgated.
On the day _Rénwǔ_ (the 19th day),
the Emperor sacrificed at the Northern Marchmount.
On the day _Xīnmǎo_ (the 28th day),
he visited the Yǒnglíng,
and performed the Grand Feast ritual.
In the ninth month, on the first day, _Bǐngshēn_ (the 33rd day),
he visited the Fúlíng.
On the day _Dīngyǒu_ (the 34th day),
he visited the Zhāolíng,
and performed the Grand Feast ritual at both,
and bowed before the imperial records.
The Emperor composed "A Record of the Celebration of the Second Eastern Tour."
He personally offered libations at the tombs of Prince Kèqín Yuètūo, Prince Wǔxūn Yánggǔlì, Grand Duke Hóngyì Éyìdōu, and Grand Duke Zhíyì Fèiyīngdōng.
Five descendants of Éyìdōu and
one descendant of Fèiyīngdōng received imperial favor.
On the day _Gēngzǐ_ (the 37th day),
the Emperor went to the Tiāntán and the Tángzǐ to perform rituals.
On the day _Xīnhài_ (the 48th day),
the Emperor returned.
On the day _Dīngsì_ (the 54th day),
Fùjùn was appointed Military Governor of Jílín,
and Sàichōng'ā was appointed Military Governor of Shèngjīng.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day _Gēngwǔ_ (the 7th day),
the Emperor stayed at Xīnglóng Temple.
On the day _Xīnwèi_ (the 8th day),
it was the Emperor's birthday,
and he received congratulations at the temporary palace.
On the day _Guǐyǒu_ (the 10th day),
the Emperor visited the Dōnglíng.
On the day _Bǐngzǐ_ (the 13th day),
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day _Xīnsì_ (the 18th day),
retired Grand Secretary Dǒng Gào died,
and the Emperor personally visited his residence to offer libations.
In the eleventh month, on the day Wùshēn,
Yīhào was appointed as the Měnggǔ Dū tǒng.
On the day Xīnhài,
an imperial edict stated:
"The state has governed for many years,
and attention should be given to the hearts of the people and their customs.
The rectitude of the people's hearts
and the purity of their customs
depend on the success or failure of government and education.
The subtle influence of these matters is profound,
and it deeply affects the destiny of the nation,
not to be regarded as a distant or impractical plan.
There are myriad affairs in the world,
but their principle ultimately returns to one.
Whether to be strict or lenient,
it must be based on reason.
Only when implementation is effective
can it inspire great reverence among the people.
When the people's will is stable,
their hearts will be upright.
All of us, rulers and ministers,
should act with a spirit of concern for prosperity and awareness of danger,
not pursuing temporary convenience and comfort.
Regarding the purity or corruption of customs,
it is particularly important to constantly observe,
subtly influence and transform,
rectify institutions and discipline,
and correct the people's hearts to correct their customs.
To achieve great and brilliant accomplishments,
nothing is more important than this.
We expect all officials, both inside and outside the court, to strive together."
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùchén,
the Emperor prayed for snow.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Bāshíliù was appointed as Guǎngzhōu Jiāngjūn,
Sōngyún as Lǐbù Shàngshū,
and Liú Huánzhī as Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ.
On the day Rénchén,
a combined sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
In this year,
disaster taxes were remitted in part for seventy-nine prefectures and counties in the provinces of Shùntiān, Zhílì, Shāndōng, Ānhuī, Gānsù, and Yúnnán.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú offered tribute.
In the twenty-fourth year, on the first day of spring, Jiǎwǔ (the new moon),
the Emperor's sixtieth birthday was celebrated,
and an imperial edict proclaimed a general amnesty,
and a banquet was bestowed upon court officials.
The Emperor's third son, Miánkǎi, was enfeoffed as Dūn Qīnwáng,
his fourth son, Miánxīn, as Ruì Qīnwáng,
and his eldest imperial grandson, Yìwěi, as Bèilè.
Miánzhì, Yìshào, and others were promoted in rank in various degrees.
On the day Dīngsì,
Hé níng was relieved from his duties in the Jūnjī (Grand Council),
and Shìláng Wénfú was appointed as Jūnjī Dàchén.
In the second month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Emperor attended the Jīngyán (Imperial Lectures).
In the third month, on the day Jǐhài,
the Emperor visited the Dōnglíng.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the Emperor went to Nányuàn for a hunt.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the Emperor visited the Xīlíng.
In summer, fourth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Gēngchén,
the Emperor reviewed the Jiànruìyíng troops.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Chén Hàng and 224 others were granted the Jinshì and Jídì ranks, and other titles in varying degrees.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the supervisors of the Fèngyáng and Jiǔjiāng customs houses were dismissed,
and their duties were concurrently managed by the Xúndào.
On the day Jǐsì,
the Emperor prayed for rain.
On the day Gēngyín,
Sōngyún was appointed as Nèi Dàchén.
In the intercalary fourth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
the Emperor went to the Tiānshén Tán to pray for rain.
On that day,
it rained.
In the fifth month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Chéng Qīnwáng Yǒngxīng was dismissed from his post, had his salary revoked, and returned to his residence due to an impropriety in the sacrificial ceremony.
Yīnghé and Héshìtài were both appointed as Mǎnzhōu Dū tǒng.
In the sixth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Sōngyún was transferred to be Gōngbù Shàngshū.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Rénxū,
Zhèng Qīnwáng Wū'ěrgōng'ā was appointed as Hànjūn Dū tǒng.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the Emperor made an imperial tour to Mùlán.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Yǒngdìng Hé burst its banks,
and Wú Jìng and Nàyànbǎo were ordered to survey and construct repairs.
In the eighth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
the Hé in Lányáng, Hénán, overflowed on its north bank.
The retired Grand Secretary and Wēiqín Bó Lèbǎo passed away,
and was posthumously granted the title of Yīděng Hóu.
In the ninth month, on the day Rénxū,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Sōngyún was dismissed as Yùqián Dàchén and appointed as Shèngjīng Jiāngjūn.
In winter, tenth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
on the Emperor's birthday (Wànshòu Jié),
the Emperor held court in the Tàihé Diàn to receive congratulations.
Shìláng Zhōu Xìyīng was dismissed from office
for impeaching Húnán commoners for arson and murder, and for sending a private letter;
his son, a Jǔrén, was also expelled.
In the eleventh month, on the day Yǐsì,
Míngliàng was promoted to Sānděng Hóu.
In the twelfth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Wú Bāngqìng was demoted for providing an untruthful report on the Húnán commoners' arson and murder case.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Dǒng Jiàozēng submitted a memorial requesting permission for foreign ships to trade tea,
but the imperial decree rejected it.
On the day Bǐngchén,
a combined sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
In this year,
disaster taxes and flag rents were remitted in part for thirty-nine prefectures, counties, and garrisons in the provinces of Zhílì, Zhèjiāng, and Húnán.
The land tax on abandoned land in Chuānshā Tīng and Bǎoshān Xiàn in Jiāngsū was abolished.
Cháoxiǎn, Liúqiú, Yuènán, Xiāmluó, and Nánzhǎng offered tribute.
In the twenty-fifth year, on the first day of spring, Rénshēn,
an imperial edict showed special solicitude for elder statesmen Míngliàng, Hé níng, and others,
exempting them from having to come to the garden for imperial audience.
In the second month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
the Emperor attended the Jīngyán.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Zhāng Xù retired due to illness,
and Dài Jūnyuán was appointed as Dàxuéshì,
Wú Jìng as Xiébàn Dàxuéshì.
On the day Wùshēn,
the Emperor reviewed the Huǒqìyíng troops.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Qìng Jùnwáng Yǒnglín fell ill,
the Emperor personally visited him,
and promoted him to Qīnwáng.
In the third month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Emperor visited the Dōnglíng.
The Bīngbù lost an official seal,
and when the matter was reported,
Míngliàng and others were penalized and demoted in varying degrees.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the Emperor went to the mausoleums of Míng Chéngzǔ, Xuānzōng, and Xiàozōng to offer wine.
On the day Jǐsì,
Qìng Qīnwáng Yǒnglín passed away.
On the day Wùyín,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
He personally visited the residence of the late Qìng Qīnwáng to offer sacrifices,
and ordered his son Miánmǐn to inherit the title of Jùnwáng.
In summer, fourth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Emperor went to Bālǐzhuāng, to the Qìngxī Qīnwáng's funeral place, to offer sacrifices.
On the day Gēngxū,
Chén Jìchāng and 246 others were granted the Jinshì and Jídì ranks, and other titles in varying degrees.
In the sixth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
princes and nobles were forbidden from privately employing Àndá and from buying common women as concubines.
Sōngyún was demoted to Xiāoqíjiao.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Rénshēn,
the Emperor made an imperial tour to Mùlán.
Fāng Shòuchóu and others presented auspicious grain (Jiāhé).
On the day Wùyín,
the Emperor resided at the Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the Emperor was unwell,
and by evening his condition worsened considerably.
An imperial edict was issued to enthrone his second imperial son, Zhì Qīnwáng, as Crown Prince.
As the day entered the Xū hour,
the Emperor passed away at the traveling palace,
at the age of sixty-one.
In the eighth month, on the day Yǐsì,
the imperial coffin was escorted back to the capital.
In the tenth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
the posthumous title was respectfully conferred as Shòutiān Xīngyùn Fūhuà Suīyóu Chóngwén Jīngwǔ Xiàogōng Qínjiǎn Duānmǐn Yīngzhé Ruì Huángdì,
and his temple name was Rénzōng.
In the first year of Dàoguāng, in the third month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
he was buried in Chānglíng.
Commentary: Rénzōng, in the beginning, encountered the regency and was
respectful and obedient.
When he personally took charge of all affairs,
he eliminated villains and promoted the virtuous.
He suppressed rebellious bandits,
captured and punished pirates,
firmly held the crucial power,
advocated frugality and diligence in governance,
and opened up land for settlement.
These were all great foundations for good governance.
He issued numerous edicts,
earnestly seeking honest advice.
However, the tradition of frank remonstrance
was not immediately apparent,
which is regrettable.
Main Annals Seventeen, Main Annals of Xuānzōng One
Xuānzōng Xiào Tiānfúyùn Lì Zhōngtǐzhèng Zhìwénshèngwǔ Zhìyǒngréncí Jiǎnqín Xiàomǐn Kuāndìng Chéng Huángdì,
whose taboo name was Mínníng,
was the second son of Rénzōng.
His mother was Empress Xiàoshūrùiruì.
On the tenth day of the eighth month of the forty-seventh year of Qiánlóng,
the Emperor was born in the Jiéfāng Hall.
As a child, he was fond of learning.
He successively studied under the Supervising Editor Qín Chéngyè and the Reviewer Wàn Chéngfēng.
He also discussed matters morning and evening with Wāng Tíngzhēn, the Right Vice Minister of the Board of Rites, and Xú Tíng, a Reader of the Hanlin Academy.
In the eighth month of the fifty-sixth year of Qiánlóng,
Gāozōng went on a hunting expedition to Wēixùngé'ěr.
The Emperor drew his bow and captured a deer.
Gāozōng was greatly pleased
and bestowed upon him a yellow jacket and a peacock feather.
In the first year of Jiāqìng,
he married Empress Xiàomùchéng.
On the wùxū day of the fourth month of the fourth year,
Rénzōng, following the imperial household law for establishing a crown prince,
personally wrote the Emperor's name
and sealed it in a locked box.
In the first month of the thirteenth year,
Empress Xiàomùchéng passed away.
He then married Empress Xiàoshènchéng.
In the ninth month of the eighteenth year,
he accompanied the emperor on the autumn hunt at Mùlán.
The Emperor returned to the capital earlier,
and the rebellion of the bandit Lín Qīng's party attacking the palace broke out.
In that month,
on the wùyín day,
the rebels entered the Right Inner Gate,
reached south of the Yǎngxīm Hall,
and intended to flee north.
The Emperor personally shot two rebels with his gun,
the remaining rebels scattered,
and the disturbance was quelled.
A speedy report was sent to the emperor.
Rénzōng was greatly relieved,
and enfeoffed the Emperor as Zhì Qīnwáng,
naming the gun he used
"Wēiliè" (Awesome and Fierce).
An imperial edict was issued to the Grand Secretariat, saying:
"With both loyalty and filial piety,
how can we withhold a generous bestowal of grace?"
The Emperor was humble and not self-congratulatory.
In his memorial thanking the emperor, he stated:
"The event was sudden,
and there was no one to defend against the rebels.
The situation was beyond my control,
and the more I think about it afterward, the more frightened I become."
Such was his modesty and lack of self-praise.
In the seventh month of the autumn of the twenty-fifth year,
Rénzōng went on an autumn hunt at Rèhé,
and the Emperor accompanied him.
On the wùyín day,
Rénzōng became unwell.
On the jǐmǎo day,
he was critically ill.
The Imperial Ministers Sài Chōng'ā and Suǒtènàmùduōbùzhāi,
the Grand Councilors Tuōjīn, Dài Jūnyuán, Lú Yìnpǔ, and Wénfú,
and the Directors-General of the Imperial Household Department Xǐ'ēn and Hé Shìtài jointly opened the locked box
and revealed the imperial decree written in the fourth year of Jiāqìng,
establishing the Emperor as the Crown Prince.
Rénzōng passed away.
On the same day, the Emperor escorted the coffin of the late Emperor back to the capital.
On the xīnsì day,
he honored his birth mother as Empress Dowager,
promoted Dūn Jùnwáng Miánkǎi to Dūn Qīnwáng,
and Miányú to Huì Jùnwáng.
On the guǐwèi day,
an imperial decree from the Empress Dowager stated:
"The great departed Emperor has ascended to the heavens.
The second Imperial Son, Zhì Qīnwáng, is filial, intelligent,
heroic, upright, and pure.
He was with the Emperor on his travels,
and it is proper for him to accept the mandate
and govern the people.
However, I fear that in the haste,
the great departed Emperor did not have time to issue a clear decree,
and the second Imperial Son's nature is humble and retiring,
which I know well.
Therefore, I issue this imperial decree,
to be conveyed to the princes and ministers remaining in the capital,
to be urgently sent to the second Imperial Son,
that he should immediately ascend the throne."
The Emperor, upon receiving the imperial decree,
respectfully submitted a memorial in reply,
and also presented the imperial decree of the fourth month of the fourth year of Jiāqìng establishing the Crown Prince, which was stored in the locked box opened by the Imperial Ministers.
He summoned Qín Chéngyè, an academician of the Hanlin Academy currently out of office, to the capital.
On the yǐyǒu day of the eighth month,
he ordered that the three-year mourning period be observed according to ancient custom,
while officials and commoners would still wear mourning attire according to established regulations.

He exempted the prefectures and counties under Chéngdé Prefecture in Zhílì, and the five prefectures and counties including Wǎnshì that he passed through, from their regular taxes for the following year.
On the guǐsì day,
he assented to the request of the princes and ministers
to observe mourning for one hundred days.
On the yǐwèi day,
the coffin of the great departed Emperor returned to the capital.
Censor Yuán Xiǎn submitted a memorial proposing seven matters concerning establishing principles and correcting likes and dislikes.
The Emperor graciously accepted them with a benevolent edict.
Fāng Shòuchóu was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
On the wùshēn day,

the Grand Scholars and Nine Ministers submitted a memorial proposing the temple name and posthumous title for the great departed Emperor as Rénzōng Shòutiānxīngyùn Fūhuàsuíyóu Chóngwénjīngwǔ Xiàogōngqínjiǎn Duānmǐn Yīngzhé Ruì Huángdì.
The will of the great departed Emperor was promulgated to the nations of Cháoxiǎn, Liúqiú, Xiāmluó, Yuènán, and Miǎndiàn.
On the gēngxū day,
the Emperor ascended the imperial throne in the Tàihé Hall,
offered sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the Altars of Land and Grain,
and issued an imperial edict to the entire realm,
designating the following year as the first year of Dàoguāng.
He bestowed favors upon officials and commoners,
and those not pardoned by ordinary amnesties
were all pardoned.
Huáng Yuè, Liú Huánzhī, Sài Chōng'ā, Sūn Yùtíng, and Jiǎng Yōuxiān were promoted to Junior Protector of the Crown Prince.
On the xīnhài day,
this year's autumn executions were suspended.
In that month,
relief was provided for the earthquake disaster in Xǔzhōu, Hénán.
A year's worth of money and grain was loaned to soldiers affected by flooding at Zhāngwǔtái Biānmén and other places in Shèngjīng,
and funds for house repairs were also provided.
A month's rations were loaned at Jùliúhé and other places.
On the jǐwèi day of the ninth month,
the mausoleum of the great departed Emperor was named Chānglíng.
On the gēngshēn day,
the Grand Councilors were severely reprimanded
for errors in drafting the imperial will.
Tuōjīn and Dài Jūnyuán were dismissed as Grand Councilors.
Wénfú and Lú Yìnpǔ remained Grand Councilors,
but all were handed over to the appropriate board for severe deliberation.
Bīnjìng reported that Zhāng Gé'ěr, son of Chōngbāgáshí Àimànbùlǔtè Bǐsūlánqí Jiūsāmùsàkè, was stirring up rebellion.
Qìngxiáng was ordered to proceed at full speed to Kāshígá'ěr to suppress him.
Grand Scholar Cáo Zhènyōng,
Ministers Huáng Yuè and Yīnghé were ordered to serve as Grand Councilors.
On the rénxū day,
Nàyànchéng was appointed Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
The Minister of Personnel and concurrently Associate Grand Scholar Wú Jìng was ordered to supervise the river works at Yífēng, Hénán.
Liú Huánzhī was transferred to Minister of Personnel,
Rú Fēn to Minister of War,
Lú Yìnpǔ to Minister of Works,
Huáng Yuè to Minister of Revenue,
Wāng Tíngzhēn to Minister of Rites,
and Gù Déqìng to Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
Sōngyún was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the wùchén day,
Qín Chéngyè was appointed Reader of the Hanlin Academy,
and ordered to serve in the Imperial Study.
On the gēngwǔ day,
the Emperor first took his seat in the tent at Xīchǎng
to grant audiences to court officials.
An edict was issued to open special examinations for the provincial and metropolitan levels.
Officials were ordered to speak truthfully on matters.
On the dīngchǒu day,
Yù Qīnwáng Yùxīng was stripped of his title and imprisoned for his crimes.
On the rénwǔ day,
Governor-General Yáng Yùchūn was promoted to Junior Protector of the Crown Prince
and awarded a double-eyed peacock feather.
In that month,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Suīzhōu and six other prefectures and counties in Hénán,
and a month's rations were also provided for Suīzhōu and three other prefectures and counties.
On the wùzǐ day of the tenth month in winter,
Yīnghé was transferred to Minister of Revenue,
Nàyànchéng to Minister of Personnel,
Mùkèdēng'é to Minister of Works,
Pǔgōng to Minister of Rites,
Hé Shìtài to Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs,
and Sōngyún to Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the xīncǒu day,
the posthumous title and temple name of the great departed Emperor were bestowed.
The next day,
an imperial edict was promulgated to the entire realm,
bestowing different degrees of grace.
On the jiǎchén day,

relief was provided for the flooded eight prefectures and counties including Jiāngníng in Jiāngsū, and the prefectures and counties under Fèngyáng and other prefectures in Ānhuī that were affected by floods.
On the wùshēn day,
Déyīng'ā was appointed Governor-General of Wūlǔmùqí.
In that month,
relief was provided for the flood and drought disasters in Hǎizhōu in Jiāngnán, Sīzhōu in Ānhuī, and seven other prefectures and counties, as well as military colonies.
Rations were provided to the poor in Xiāoshān and thirty-two other counties in Zhèjiāng.
On the bǐngchén day of the eleventh month,
the Emperor escorted the Empress Dowager to reside in the Shòukāng Palace.
On the wùchén day,
Wèi Yuánwèi was appointed Governor of Jiāngsū,
and Zuǒ Fǔ as Governor of Húnán.
On the gēngwǔ day,
on the winter solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Yuánqiú Altar.
Thereafter, this was done annually.
On the guǐyǒu day,
Chéng'ān was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left,
and Sōngyún was appointed Governor-General of Rèhé.
On the jiǎxū day,
Chéng'ān was transferred to Governor-General of the Bordered Yellow Banner Chinese Army.
Wénfú was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the dīngchǒu day,
Gù Chún, a Reader of the Hanlin Academy, memorialized that Sōngyún should be kept close to the Emperor.
This displeased the Emperor,
and he was handed over to the appropriate board for severe deliberation.
On the jiǎshēn day of the twelfth month,
the Emperor promoted the Empress Dowager's honorary title to Gōngcí Huáng Tàihòu.
The next day,
an imperial edict was issued to the empire,
granting grace with distinctions.
An imperial decree, by the will of the Empress Dowager,
established the Emperor's secondary consort, the Tóngjiā clan, as Empress.
On the bǐngxū day,
Héshìtài was reassigned as Fúzhōu General.
Jìnchāng was appointed as President of the Lǐfānyuàn.
Qìngbǎo was transferred to be Governor-General of Mǐnzhè.
Shǐ Zhìguāng was appointed as Governor-General of Yún Guì,
Hán Kèjūn as Governor of Yúnnán,
and Yán Jiǎn as Governor of Fújiàn.
On the gēngyín day,
the breach at Yífēng in Hénán was closed.
On the guǐsì day,
additional honorary posthumous titles were bestowed upon Empress Xiàojìngxiàn, Empress Xiàoshèngxiàn, Emperor Gāozōngchún, Empress Xiàoxiánchún, and Empress Xiàoyíchún.
Yīnghé was dismissed as Grand Councillor,
and continued to serve in his former posts as President, etc.
On the bǐngshēn day,
Wāng Tíngzhēn, Tāng Jīnzhāo, Fāng Shòuchóu, and Jiǎng Yōuxiān's proposals to investigate "corrupt practices" were deemed inconvenient to discuss,
while Sūn Yùtíng's memorial was particularly incisive,
and he was commended with a gentle decree.
Lǐ Hóngbīn was recalled to serve as Governor of Ānhuī.
Zhāng Yìnghàn was summoned to the capital,
Chén Ruòlín was appointed as Governor-General of Húguǎng,
and Shuài Chéngyíng as Governor of Zhèjiāng.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú presented tribute.
In the spring of the first year of Dàoguāng, on the guǐchǒu day of the first month,
the Emperor held court in the Tàihé Hall,
with music prepared but not played,
and the congratulatory memorials not read.
On the bǐngchén day,
Chū Pénglíng, an Assistant Department Director of the Board of Punishments, was granted the rank of Vice Minister of the Board of Rites.
The Zhèjiāng Salt Administration was abolished,
and its duties were concurrently managed by the Governor.
On the jǐwèi day,
Wén Fú was appointed as President of the Board of Rites,
and Nà Qīng'ān as Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the dīngmǎo day,
Yuènán sent incense,
presented a congratulatory memorial,
and offered local products as tribute;
an edict ordered them to cease.
On the bǐngzǐ day,
King Lǐ Gōng of Cháoxiǎn presented a memorial of condolence;
King Rèzūndá'ěrbìgá'ěrmǎsàyě of Guō'ěrkā reported the passing of Rénzōng and the wearing of mourning attire,
and offered gold brocade as tribute.
He was awarded an imperial rescript of commendation and gifts.
On the rénwǔ day, the first day of the second month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Bānchán È'ěrdéní presented tribute,
and was awarded an imperial rescript of commendation and gifts.
On the wùxū day,
Assistant Grand Secretary Wú Jìng retired due to illness.
On the gēngzǐ day,
Sūn Yùtíng was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary,
while remaining Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng.
Zhǎnglín, Governor-General of Shǎnxī-Gānsù, was given the title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
On the jiǎchén day,
the outstanding grain loans for seeds and rations of the people in Féngchéng and five other counties in Jiāngxī were remitted.
On the xīnhài day, the first day of the third month,
the Imperial Astronomy Bureau reported
that on the first day of the fourth month of this year,
the sun and moon would be in conjunction,
and five planets would be aligned.
An edict stated:
"We shall redouble Our diligence and reverence,
and work with Our inner and outer officials to achieve optimal governance;
there is no need to announce this to the Imperial Historiography Office."
On the rénzǐ day,
due to the escort of Emperor Rénzōng Ruì's coffin to the imperial tomb,
Qīn Wáng Miánkè of Zhuāng and others were ordered to remain in the capital to handle affairs.
On the guǐchǒu day,
the banner rents for this year in the passing-through areas were again remitted,
and wheat seeds were provided.
On the xīnyǒu day,
Emperor Rénzōng Ruì's funeral procession departed,
and the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, saw it off to Chānglíng.
On the rénxū day,
Guō'ěrkā presented a memorial and tribute for the Emperor's ascension to the throne;
it was ordered that this be presented together with the regular tribute of the second year of Dàoguāng.
On the bǐngyín day,
the Emperor visited Tàilíng, Tàidōnglíng, Chānglíng, and the Lóng'ēn Hall,
and bestowed the honorary posthumous title Xiàoshū Duānhé Rénzhuāng Cíyì Guāngtiān Yòushèng Ruì Huánghòu upon Empress Xiàoshū Ruì.
On the dīngmǎo day,
Nímáshàn, General of Chéngdū, was ordered to Yúnnán to assist in military affairs.
On the guǐyǒu day,
Emperor Rénzōng Ruì was interred at Chānglíng.
Tuōjīn and Cáo Zhènyōng were promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
On the dīngchǒu day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, returned to the capital.
On the wùyín day,
Emperor Rénzōng Ruì and Empress Xiàoshū Ruì were enshrined in the Tàimiào.
On the jǐmǎo day,
with the enshrinement ceremony completed,
an imperial edict was issued to the empire,
granting grace with distinctions.
Luó Sījǔ, Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Guìzhōu, was ordered to the Yúnnán military camp to assist in suppression.
This month,

grain rations from granaries were loaned to disaster victims of the previous year in Kělán and nine other prefectures and counties in Shānxī, and Dídào and four other prefectures and counties in Gānsù.
In the summer, on the bǐngxū day of the fourth month,
the regular rainy season sacrifice was performed,
offering sacrifice to Heaven at the Yuánqiū,
with Emperor Rénzōng Ruì accompanying in the sacrifice;
this became a regular practice from this year onwards.
On the gēngyín day,
Nímáshàn was appointed Imperial Commissioner,
to supervise military affairs in Yǒngběi, Yúnnán.
Nà Qīng'ān was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
Grand Secretary and Third-Class Marquis Míngliàng retired.
Dài Jūnyuán, Mùkèdéng'é, and Ākèdāng'ā were ordered to survey a suitable site for the imperial tomb.
On the jiǎchén day,
the rebellion of the Lāgǔ bandits in Dàyáo, Yúnnán, was suppressed.
On the dīngwèi day,
the Emperor went to the Dàgāo Hall to pray for rain.
On the wùwǔ day,
456,000 taels of relief silver were allocated to Hǎizhōu and other prefectures and counties in Jiāngsū.
Bólín was appointed Grand Secretary concurrently in charge of the Board of War.
Zhǎnglín was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary,
while remaining in his post as Governor-General of Shǎnxī-Gānsù.
On the guǐhài day,
an edict ordered the suspension of this year's autumn executions.
On the jiǎzǐ day,
Bólín was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tǐrén Pavilion,
and Cáo Zhènyōng Grand Secretary of the Wǔyīng Hall.
On the bǐngyín day,
Nguyễn Phúc Ánh was enfeoffed as King of Yuènán.
Sōngyún was appointed President of the Board of War,
and Qìnghuì as General-in-Chief of Rèhé.
On the rénshēn day,
at the summer solstice,
sacrifice was offered to Earth at Fāngzé,
with Emperor Rénzōng Ruì accompanying in the sacrifice;
this became a regular practice from this year onwards.
On the guǐyǒu day,
the rebellion of the Yǒngběi Dàyáo bandits in Yúnnán was suppressed.
On the xīnsì day of the sixth month,
Zhāng Shīchéng was appointed Governor of Guǎngdōng.
On the jiǎshēn day,
Āndìngmén suffered a disaster.
On the gēngyín day,
the Emperor attended the Tàihé Gate,

and ordered Qīn Wáng Wū'ěrgōng'ā of Zhèng and Jùn Wáng Lúnzhù of Shùnchéng to carry the imperial seal and patent to Empress Xiàomù's funeral palace to perform the ceremony of conferring her posthumous title.
On the wùxū day,
Chénglíng was summoned to the capital,
Lǐ Hóngbīn was appointed Governor-General of Caoyun,
and Sūn Ěrzhǔn as Governor of Ānhuī.
Land taxes in Xīnxiāng County, Hénán, were abolished.
Qíshàn was appointed Governor of Shāndōng.
In the autumn, on the gēngxū day of the seventh month,
Héyīng, President of the Board of Punishments, died.
Nàyànchéng was transferred to be President of the Board of Punishments,
Sōngyún as President of the Board of Civil Office,
and Jìnchāng as President of the Board of War.
Mùkèdéngbù was appointed President of the Lǐfānyuàn.
On the jǐwèi day,
Yán Lǎng, with a third-rank button, provisionally served as Governor-General of the Hédōng Riverways.
On the dīngmǎo day,
Yùdài was transferred to be Governor of Jiāngxī.
Yáng Màotián was appointed Governor of Húběi.
On the gēngwǔ day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, visited the Xīlíng,
and one-third of the regular taxes in the passing-through areas were remitted.
On the rénshēn day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, returned to the capital.
This month,
relief was provided for flood and drought disasters in Níngxià and three other counties in Gānsù,
and the previous year's regular taxes were remitted.
On the gēngchén day of the eighth month,
the Shùntiān provincial examination was postponed to the ninth month.
On the dīnghài day,
Sōngyún was ordered to serve as Grand Councillor.
Tèyīshùnbǎo was appointed General of Wūlǐyásūtái.
On the guǐsì day,
Rúfēn, President of the Board of War, died,
and Chū Pénglíng was appointed in his place.
On the yǐwèi day,
Khokhānd sent envoys requesting an audience,
but was refused.
On the bǐngwǔ day,
Zhāng Shīchéng was transferred to be Governor of Ānhuī,
and Sūn Ěrzhǔn as Governor of Guǎngdōng.
On the wùchén day of the ninth month,
King Zhèng Fó of Xiāmluó sent envoys to offer incense and tribute local products,
and was gently decreed to cease.
On the jǐsì day,
Zhǎnglín was summoned to the capital,
and Zhū Xūn provisionally served as Governor-General of Shǎnxī-Gānsù.
This month,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Sùzhōu and two other prefectures and counties in Ānhuī.
In the winter, on the jǐmǎo day of the tenth month,
the Emperor held court at the Qiánqīng Gate;
this became a regular practice from this year onwards.
On the dīnghài day,
Sūn Ěrzhǔn was transferred to be Governor of Ānhuī,
and Sōngfú as Governor of Guǎngdōng.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jǐwèi,
Chén Ruòlín, the Grand Coordinator of Guìzhōu, memorialized to request a reduction of 22,000 shí of land rent for commoners and Miáo people annually.
He also requested travel expenses for Jǔrén from the Miáo border region attending the triennial provincial examinations.
This was granted.
On the day Rénxū,
Lí Shìxù was awarded the title of Tàizǐ Tàibǎo for his achievements in river conservancy.
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Qiū Shùtáng was appointed Grand Coordinator of Shānxī.
On the day Guǐsì,
Liú Huánzhī, Minister of the Board of Civil Office, passed away.
Lú Yìnpǔ was transferred to be Minister of the Board of Civil Office,
and was relieved of his duties as Grand Councillor.
Chū Pénglíng was transferred to be Minister of the Board of Works.
Dài Liánkuí was appointed Minister of the Board of War.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn, Yuènán, and Liúqiú sent tribute.
In the second year, spring, the first month, on the day Dīngwèi, which was the first day of the lunar month,
Fāng Shòuchóu was excused due to illness.
Yán Jiǎn was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì,
and Chánglíng acted in his stead.
Yè Shìzhuó was appointed Grand Coordinator of Fújiàn.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
prayers for harvest were offered to Shàngdì.
Rénzōng Ruì Huángdì was honored in the sacrifice as a co-recipient,
and from then on, this was done annually.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Tèyīshùnbǎo was summoned to the capital.
Yìhào was transferred to be General of Wūlǐyǎsūtái,
and Sōngyún was transferred to be General of Hēilóngjiāng.
Jìnchāng was appointed General of Shèngjīng.
Nàqīng'ān acted as Minister of the Board of War.
On the day Xīnwèi,
based on the three-year performance review,
the recommendations of Cáo Zhènyōng and others were accepted.
Vice-Ministers Nàyànbǎo, Shànqìng, and Wú Fāngpéi were dismissed.
Gu Gédéqìng, Censor-in-Chief of the Left, was demoted.
Wáng Dǐng was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
Chánglíng was ordered to return to be Governor-General of Shǎnxī-Gānsù.
Sōngyún was appointed to act as Governor-General of Zhílì.
Nàyánchéng was appointed to act as Minister of the Board of Civil Office.
In the second month, on the day Dīnghài,
Zhuāng Qīnwáng Miánkè and others were ordered to remain in the capital to handle affairs, as the Emperor was to visit the imperial tombs.
On the day Guǐsì,
Dài Liánkuí, Minister of the Board of War, passed away.
Wáng Zōngchéng replaced him.
In the third month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
540,000 liǎng of relief silver were allocated to twenty prefectures and counties, including Shàngyuán in Jiāngsū.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Emperor visited the Eastern Mausoleums.
Three-tenths of the regular taxes were remitted for the areas passed through.
On the day Gēngxū,
the Emperor visited the Zhāoxī Mausoleum, Xiàodōng Mausoleum, Jǐng Mausoleum, and Yù Mausoleum.
He offered sacrifices at the garden tomb of Duānhuì Huáng Tàizǐ.
Mùkèdēng'é was transferred to be Minister of the Board of Rites.
Wénfú was transferred to be Minister of the Board of Works.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, visited the Western Mausoleums.
Three-tenths of the regular taxes were remitted for the areas passed through.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
due to carelessness in the Yù Mausoleum project,
Zhuāng Qīnwáng Miánkè was demoted to Jùnwáng.
Dài Jūnyuán was relieved of his Tàizǐ Tàibǎo title and his management of the Board of Punishments.
Sūlèng'é was stripped of his office,
and ordered to serve as a messenger at the construction site,
and was still to pay varying amounts in compensation.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the Emperor visited the Tài Mausoleum, Tàidōng Mausoleum, and Chāng Mausoleum.
On the day Jǐwèi,
on the Qīngmíng Festival,
the Emperor performed the earth-laying ceremony at the Chāng Mausoleum.
On the day Rénxū,
the Emperor offered sacrifices before the coffin chamber of Xiàomù Huánghòu.
He returned to the capital with the Empress Dowager.
In the intercalary third month, on the day Wùyín,
Mùkèdēngbù was relieved of his duties as Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Xǐ'ēn was appointed Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Dài Lánfēn and 222 others were awarded Jìnshì degrees of varying ranks.
In this month,
regular taxes for three prefectures and departments, including Níngyuǎn in Fèngtiān, were exempted or deferred.
Summer, fourth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
the Emperor bestowed honorary posthumous titles upon Xiàojìng Xiàn Huánghòu, Xiàoshèng Xiàn Huánghòu, Gāozōng Chún Huángdì, Xiàoxián Chún Huánghòu, and Xiàoyí Chún Huánghòu.
The imperial seals and records were deposited in the Tàimiào and the Shèngjīng Tàimiào.
Additionally, the seals and records of Rénzōng Ruì Huángdì and Xiàoshú Ruì Huánghòu were deposited in the Shèngjīng Tàimiào.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Tibetan bandits in Qīnghǎi were suppressed.
Ālín was appointed Grand Coordinator of Jiāngxī.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
because Mò Jìn, Vice-Minister of the Granary and Stud, made presumptuous remarks in a memorial,
the Emperor issued a vermilion rescript rebuking and dismissing him.
He was demoted to Grand Academician of the Grand Secretariat.
In this month,
land taxes for sixteen prefectures, departments, and counties, including Suīzhōu in Hénán, affected by sand burial, dike occupation, and water occupation, were exempted or deferred.
Also, flood taxes for five prefectures and counties, including Cāngzhōu in Zhílì, and the two salt fields of Yánzhèn and Hǎifēng, were exempted or deferred.
In the sixth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
Grand Secretary Bólín retired with his original rank.
Dài Jūnyuán was ordered to continue managing the Board of Punishments.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Nàyánchéng was ordered to act as Grand Coordinator of Shǎnxī.
Sōngfú was transferred to be Grand Coordinator of Guìzhōu.
Luó Hánzhāng was appointed Grand Coordinator of Guǎngdōng.
Nàqīng'ān was appointed to act as Minister of the Board of Punishments.
On the day Rénxū,
Sōngyún was stripped of his titles as Minister of the Board of Civil Office and Grand Councillor,
and ordered to await appointment as an Assistant Director in one of the Six Boards.
On the day Wùchén,
Chánglíng was appointed Grand Secretary and concurrently manager of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
Yīnghé was appointed Associate Grand Secretary.
Wénfú was transferred to be Minister of the Board of Civil Office.
Xǐ'ēn was transferred to be Minister of the Board of Works.
Nàqīng'ān was appointed Minister of the Board of War.
Yùlín was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the day Jǐsì,
Fùjùn was appointed Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
Sōnglín was appointed General of Jílín.
Déyīng'ā was appointed General of Hēilóngjiāng.
Yīnghuì was appointed Commandant of Wūlǔmùqí.
In this month,
relief was provided for flood victims in Xīngxiàn, Shānxī.
Autumn, seventh month,
Chéng Zǔluò was appointed Grand Coordinator of Hénán.
Wáng Dǐng acted in his stead.
Chéng Guórén was appointed Grand Coordinator of Shǎnxī.
In this month,
relief was provided for flood victims in twenty-one prefectures and counties, including Bàzhōu in Zhílì.
Eighth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Shǐ Zhìguāng, Governor-General of Yúnnán-Guìzhōu, was summoned to the capital.
Míngshān replaced him.
The sectarian bandit Zhū Mázi revolted in Xīncài County, Hénán.
Chéng Zǔluò was ordered to capture and execute him.
On the day Wùshēn,
Qìngbǎo was summoned to the capital.
Zhào Shènzhěn was appointed Governor-General of Mǐn-Zhè.
Lú Kūn was appointed Grand Coordinator of Guǎngxī.
On the day Gēngxū,
Lú Kūn was appointed to act as Grand Coordinator of Shǎnxī.
On the day Wùchén,
the King of Guō'ěrkā was awarded a jeweled hat-button.
Gājībìmùxīngtǎbā was awarded a third-rank hat-button.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Chánglíng and Sōngtíng were summoned to the capital.
Nàyánchéng was appointed to act as Governor-General of Shǎnxī-Gānsù.
In this month,
relief grain was provided to three counties including Ānyáng in Hénán,
twelve prefectures and counties including Bàzhōu in Zhílì,
two departments, Guīhuàchéng and Sàlāqí, in Shānxī,
and three counties including Ēnxiàn in Shāndōng, all affected by floods.
Loaned relief grain to the flood-affected Mongols of Tǔmòtè.
Taxes were exempted or deferred for forty-one prefectures, counties, and garrisons, including Gāotáng in Shāndōng,
and for the two prefectures of Hèqìng and Jiànchuān in Yúnnán, which suffered from crop failure.
Ninth month, on the day Rénshēn, which was the first day of the lunar month,
Siāmluó's regular annual tribute was accepted.
On the day Jiǎxū,
100,000 shí of grain from the public granary were allocated to relieve flood victims in Zhílì.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the Guǒluòkè Tibetan bandits in Sìchuān were suppressed.
Yán Lǎng was appointed Governor-General of Rivers for Hédōng.
On the day Gēngyín,
Jiǎng Yōuxiān was appointed to act as Minister of the Board of Punishments.
Chén Ruòlín was transferred to be Governor-General of Sìchuān.
Lǐ Hóngbīn was transferred to be Governor-General of Húguǎng.
Wèi Yuánzēng was appointed Governor-General of Grain Transport.
Hán Wénqǐ was appointed Grand Coordinator of Jiāngsū.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Lú Kūn was transferred to be Grand Coordinator of Shǎnxī.
Chénggé was appointed Grand Coordinator of Guǎngxī.
In this month,
relief grain was provided to Ruìchāng County in Jiāngxī,
and Wǔzhì and Yuánwǔ counties in Hénán, all affected by disaster.
Winter, tenth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ, the Emperor visited the imperial tombs.
Zhuāng Qīnwáng Miánkè and others were ordered to remain in the capital to handle affairs.
Nàyánchéng was appointed Governor-General of Shǎnxī-Gānsù.
Jiǎng Yōuxiān was appointed Minister of the Board of Punishments.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the Emperor, having changed from mourning attire, accompanied the Empress Dowager to visit the Western Mausoleums.
Three-tenths of the regular taxes were remitted for the areas passed through.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the Emperor visited the Tài Mausoleum, Tàidōng Mausoleum, and Chāng Mausoleum.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the Emperor performed the ceremony of removing mourning attire at the Chāng Mausoleum.
On the day Guǐhài,
the Emperor returned to the capital with the Empress Dowager.
In this month,
relief was provided for flood victims in forty-three prefectures and counties, including Hézhōu in Gānsù, Sùzhōu in Ānhuī, and Bàzhōu in Zhílì,
and in Hǎizhōu in Jiāngsū and Tiānmén County in Húběi.
Loaned relief grain to flood victims in Guǎngníng County in Shèngjīng,
five prefectures and counties including Púzhōu in Shāndōng,
and two stations including Kùxīmù'ěr in Hēilóngjiāng.

Old and new regular taxes affected by flood were exempted or deferred for six prefectures and counties including Jìngníng in Gānsù, twenty-three departments and counties including Yífēng in Hénán, thirteen prefectures and counties including Miǎnyáng in Húběi, fifty-one prefectures, counties, and garrisons including Púzhōu in Shāndōng, eighteen prefectures and counties including Tōngzhōu in Zhílì, and thirty-four departments, prefectures, counties, and garrisons including Hǎizhōu in Jiāngsū.
Old arrears of grain were exempted or deferred for Mò'ěrgēn and Bùtèhā.
Regular and excess salt taxes of Chánglú and Sōngjiāng Prefecture in Jiāngsū were exempted or deferred.
On the *xīnwèi* (辛未) day of the eleventh month,
Yùlín (玉麟) was appointed Minister of the Board of Rites.
On the *guǐwèi* (癸未) day,
relief was provided to the poor egg-sellers affected by the fire in the provincial capital of Guǎngdōng (廣東).
On the *yǐyǒu* (乙酉) day,
Yùlín (玉麟) was appointed Minister of the Board of Rites,
and Qìngbǎo (慶保) was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the *bǐngxū* (丙戌) day,
the Consort Tóngjiā (佟佳) was established as Empress.
The next day,
an imperial edict was promulgated throughout the empire.
A general pardon was granted with varying degrees of favor.
On the *wùzǐ* (戊子) day,
Sōngjūn (松筠) was reinstated as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
On the *rénchén* (壬辰) day,
the Emperor proceeded to the Dàgāo (大高) Temple to pray for snow.
On the *dīngyǒu* (丁酉) day,
with the ceremonies for the establishment of the Empress completed,
the Grand Empress Dowager was honored with the auspicious title Gōngcí Kāngyù Huáng Tàihòu (恭慈康豫皇太后).
The next day,
an imperial edict was promulgated throughout the empire,
and a general pardon was granted with varying degrees of favor.
In this month,

relief was provided for flood and drought disasters in Sùzhōu (宿州) and seven other prefectures and counties in Ānhuī (安徽) province, as well as various garrisons, and Wǔzhì (武陟) county in Hénán (河南) province.

Food provisions were distributed to disaster victims in Sìzhōu (泗州) and eight other prefectures and counties in Ānhuī (安徽), and Hézhōu (河州) and eleven other prefectures, departments, and counties in Gānsù (甘肅).
Old and new taxes were remitted and deferred for Sùzhōu (宿州) and seventeen other prefectures and counties in Ānhuī (安徽), as well as various garrisons,
Wǔzhì (武陟) and Yángwǔ (陽武) two counties in Hénán (河南),
Dídào (狄道) and six other prefectures, departments, and counties in Gānsù (甘肅),
Nánchāng (南昌) and seven other counties, and Nánchāng (南昌) and Jiǔjiāng (九江) two garrisons in Jiāngxī (江西),
Lǐzhōu (澧州) in Húnán (湖南) and Hǎiníng (海寧) and four other prefectures and counties in Zhèjiāng (浙江) affected by disaster,
and the old and new taxes for Lánglú (長蘆) flooded areas, and Bǎnpǔ (板浦) and nine other salt fields in Liǎnghuái (兩淮) affected by flood.
On the *bǐngwǔ* (丙午) day of the twelfth month,
the Emperor proceeded to the Dàgāo (大高) Temple to pray for snow.
On the *guǐchǒu* (癸丑) day,
as the Emperor's prayers for snow had not been answered,
he commanded a further seven days of prayer.
Chéngdé (成德), the General of Rèhé (熱河), died,
and Qìngbǎo (慶保) was appointed in his place.
Sōngjūn (松筠) was awarded a second-rank button and appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
Chéng Hánzhāng (程含章) was transferred to be Governor of Shāndōng (山東).
Chén Zhōngfú (陳中孚) was appointed Governor of Guǎngdōng (廣東).
On the *jiǎyín* (甲寅) day,
bandits such as Lú Zhàocháng (盧照常) in Yúchéng (虞城) county, Hénán (河南), rebelled,
and they were captured and executed.
On the *gēngshēn* (庚申) day,
arrears of the *tānzhēng* (攤徵) silver tax owed by commoners in Jiāngsū (江蘇) and Ānhuī (安徽) prior to the 23rd year of Jiāqìng (嘉慶) were remitted.
Déyīng'ē (德英阿) was transferred to be General of Suīyuǎncchéng (綏遠城),
and Lùchéng (祿成) was appointed General of Hēilóngjiāng (黑龍江).
On the *yǐchǒu* (乙丑) day,
the Han Memorial Processing Office of the Grand Secretariat caught fire.
In this month,
food provisions were distributed for the flood disaster in Dàchéng (大城) county, Zhílì (直隸).
Silver rations were loaned to soldiers stationed in disaster areas in Zhílì (直隸).
Old and new taxes were remitted and deferred for Lóngpíng (隆平) and three other counties in Zhílì (直隸), and Shānyáng (山陽) and four other counties in Jiāngsū (江蘇), affected by flood and drought.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn (朝鮮), Xiāmluó (暹羅), and Liúqiú (琉球) came to offer tribute.
In the spring of the third year, on the *rénshēn* (壬申) day of the first month,
the Emperor presided at the Chónghuá (重華) Palace,
hosting a banquet for ministers and the Hanlin (翰林) academicians of the inner court.
Sūn Ěrzhǔn (孫爾準) was transferred to be Governor of Fújiàn (福建).
Táo Shù (陶澍) was appointed Governor of Ānhuī (安徽).
As the King of Guō'ěrkā (廓爾喀), É'ěrdéní (額爾德尼), sent Gājī Dánàpéngzàbānglǐ (噶箕達納彭咱邦禮) and others to congratulate the Emperor on his accession and present a memorial and tribute,
an edict was bestowed to commend and encourage them,
and they were also generously rewarded.
On the *rénwǔ* (壬午) day,
the Emperor visited the Yuánmíng (圓明) Garden.
On the *yǐwèi* (乙未) day,
Grand Secretary Chánglíng (長齡) was ordered to serve among the Grand Councilors.
Shǐ Zhìguāng (史致光) was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
In this month,

relief was provided for the flood disaster in Xiǎohēishān Báiqíbǎo (小黑山白旗堡) Manchu Banner households in Fèngtiān (奉天), Bàzhōu (霸州) and thirty-six other prefectures and counties in Zhílì (直隸), and Hǎizhōu (海州) in Jiāngsū (江蘇).

One month's food provisions were distributed to disaster victims in Pīzhōu (邳州) and eight other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Jiāngsū (江蘇) affected by flood, Sùzhōu (宿州) and twelve other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Ānhuī (安徽) affected by flood and drought, Wǔzhì (武陟) county in Hénán (河南) affected by flood, and Púzhōu (濮州) and six other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng (山東).
Loans were granted for drought disasters in Hǎiyán (海鹽) and Chángxīng (長興) two counties in Zhèjiāng (浙江),
hail and flood disasters in Liúbà (留壩) and eleven other departments, prefectures, and counties in Shǎnxī (陝西),
earthquake disasters in Jìngníng (靜寧) and seventeen other prefectures and counties in Gānsù (甘肅),
flood disasters in Bǎnpǔ (板浦) and nine other salt fields in Liǎnghuái (兩淮),
Wǔzhì (武陟) and three other counties in Hénán (河南),
and flood-affected seeds and grain were loaned to Manchu Bannermen in Qíqíhā'ěr (齊齊哈爾) and Mò'ěrgēnchéng (墨爾根城) in Hēilóngjiāng (黑龍江).
On the *xīnchǒu* (辛丑) day, the first day of the second month,
it was ordered that the former Grand Secretary Āguì (阿桂) be enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
Sōngfú (嵩孚) was transferred to be Governor of Húnán (湖南).
Chéng Guórén (程國仁) was appointed Governor of Guìzhōu (貴州).
On the *dīngwèi* (丁未) day,
sacrifices were offered to the Former Master Kǒngzǐ (孔子).
On the *xīnhài* (辛亥) day,
the former Minister Tāng Bīn (湯斌) was ordered to be honored in the Confucian Temple.
On the *guǐchǒu* (癸丑) day,
the Emperor proceeded to the Confucian Temple to offer sacrifices,
and lectured at the Bìyōng (辟雍) Imperial Academy,
and Minister of the Board of Rites Wāng Tíngzhēn (汪廷珍) was granted the title of Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
In this month,
additional food provisions were distributed to Dàchéng (大城) county, Zhílì (直隸).
On the *rénshēn* (壬申) day of the third month,
the Emperor presided at the Qínzhèng (勤政) Palace to attend to government affairs.
On the *yǐhài* (乙亥) day,
the Emperor personally plowed the sacrificial field,
adding one furrow.
On the *bǐngzǐ* (丙子) day,
