Rations were provided to the military and civilians in Dōngliú and Hánshān counties in Ānhuī.
Loans of rations were provided for flood victims in Báiqíbǎo and Xiǎohēishān in Fèngtiān.

New and old regular and miscellaneous taxes were exempted or deferred for Cāngzhōu and thirty-three other prefectures and counties in Zhílì, and Miǎnyáng and eight other prefectures and counties under the jurisdiction of the Weǐ in Húběi, which were affected by floods.
In the 11th month, on the day Gēngyín,
the Emperor visited the Western Mausoleums,
and five-tenths of the taxes in the areas passed through were remitted.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Emperor visited the Tàilíng, Tàidōnglíng, and Chānglíng mausoleums,
and also offered wine at the mausoleums of Empress Xiàomù and Empress Xiàoshèn,
and performed the preliminary relocation ceremony before Empress Xiàoquán's coffin.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Empress Xiàoquán's coffin was interred in the underground palace,
the Emperor personally supervised,
and ordered the imperial princes to perform the rituals.
On the day Jǐhài,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Lùpǔ was transferred to be General of Jīngzhōu,
and Yìxiāng was transferred to be General of Wūlǐyàsūtái.
The British captured Dìnghǎi.
On the day Wùshēn,
Wūěrgōngé was sentenced to strangulation.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Yīlǐbù reported that the British were demanding trade at Àomén and Dìnghǎi.
An imperial edict instructed Qíshàn to order the British to return Dìnghǎi.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Zhōu Tiānjúe was stripped of his post
for unauthorized use of illegal torture,
and exiled to Yīlí.
Yùtài was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng,
and Wú Qíjùn was appointed Provincial Governor of Húnán.
That month,
relief was provided to the flood and drought-stricken people in Shàngyuán and sixteen other counties in Jiāngsū, and Tiānjīn County in Zhílì.

Loans were provided for military pay to the Jiāngníng garrison and the various camps under the Governor-General and Provincial Military Commander stationed in disaster areas in Jiāngsū, and for rations and housing funds for agricultural soldiers in the flood-stricken city of Mòěrgēn in Hēilóngjiāng.
New and old taxes were exempted or deferred for Tàizhōu and seventy-two other prefectures and counties under the Weǐ in Jiāngsū, Tiānjīn County in Zhílì, and Héquǔ County in Shānxī.
In the 12th month,
with Empress Xiàoquán enshrined in the Fèngxiāndiàn,
the Emperor personally went to offer sacrifices.
The next day,
the Fourth Imperial Prince was ordered to perform the rituals.
On the day Wùchén,
Yú Bùyún was transferred to be Admiral of Zhèjiāng.
Tiělín was appointed General of Cháhāěr,
and Ēnguì was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
Bìchāng was appointed Assistant Minister of Yīlí.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Wú Wénróng was transferred to be Provincial Governor of Húběi,
and Liú Hóngáo was appointed Provincial Governor of Fújiàn.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Hú Sōngé was summoned to the capital,
and Ēntèhéngé was appointed Acting Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù.
That month,
rations and housing funds were provided to the flood-stricken people in Lóngxī and Nánjìng counties in Fújiàn.
Loans were provided for military pay to the three battalions including Jiāngyīn in Jiāngsū.
New and old regular and miscellaneous taxes were exempted or deferred for Chángxīng and four other counties in Zhèjiāng, which were affected by floods and droughts.
That year,
Cháoxiǎn offered tribute.
Imperial Annals 19: Annals of Xuānzōng (3)
In the 21st year, spring, 1st month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
the British attacked Hǔmén in Guǎngdōng,
and Vice-Admiral Chén Liánbì and his son Jǔpéng died there.
On the day Gēngyín,
Yìshān was appointed Minister of the Imperial Presence.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Qíshàn was handed over to the Board for severe deliberation
for the fall of Hǔmén,
and Admiral Guān Tiānpéi was stripped of his button.
Yìshān was appointed General Jìngnì,
Lóngwén and Yáng Fāng were appointed Assistant Ministers,
to oversee the coastal defense of Guǎngdōng.
Sàishàng'ā was ordered to serve among the Grand Councilors.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Nèěrjīngé was ordered to be stationed in Tiānjīn,
to oversee coastal defense.
Hāliǎng'ā was ordered to proceed to Shānhǎiguān,
to oversee coastal defense.
Qíyīng and others were ordered to be diligent in scouting.
On the day Jǐsì,
Yīlǐbù was ordered to return to his post as Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
and Yùqiān was appointed Imperial Commissioner
to manage military affairs in Zhèjiāng.
On the day Xīnhài,
Qíshàn was stripped of his Grand Secretary title,
and still handed over to the Board for severe deliberation.
That month,
relief was provided to the banner households affected by flood in Báiqíbǎo, Fèngtiān.
Granary grain was provided to the flood-stricken people in Jiāngdū and Dāntú counties in Jiāngsū,
station soldiers in Xiǎohēishān, Fèngtiān,
salt workers at Miàowān saltworks, Jiāngsū,
and rations to the flood and drought-stricken people in Dōngliú and Fánchāng counties in Ānhuī.

Loans of seeds were provided to the flood-stricken people in Miǎnyáng and eight other prefectures and counties under the Weǐ in Húběi, Wǔlíng County in Húnán, and Jīnzhōu and five other prefectures, departments, and counties in Gānsù;
rations for flood-stricken people in Shàngyuán and eleven other counties in Jiāngsū, and Gāolán County in Gānsù;
and granary grain for hail-stricken people in Héquǔ County in Shānxī.
On the Gēngshēn day of the second month,
due to Yīlǐbù's procrastination and failure to advance,
the Board was ordered to deliberate severely.
On the Xīnyǒu day,
Qíshàn was arrested for questioning,
and his property was still confiscated.
Qíshì was appointed Governor-General of Guǎngdōng and Guǎngxī,
Yíliáng concurrently acted in the position,
Lǐ Zhènhù acted as Minister of Justice (Xíngbù Shàngshū),
Nè'ěrjīng'é was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì,
and Ēntèhéng'é was appointed Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù.
On the Bǐngyín day,
the King of Yuènán, Ruǎn Fútián, died,
and an imperial edict suspended the tribute of local products.
On the Wùchén day,
the British left Dìnghǎi.
Because Yīlǐbù was incompetent and cowardly,
he was stripped of his title of Assistant Grand Secretary (Xiébàn Dàxuéshì),
but remained in his post as Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng.
Bǎoxìng was appointed Grand Secretary (Dàxuéshì),
but remained in his post as Governor-General of Sìchuān.
Yìjīng was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary.
On the Wùyín day,
Qíshèn was appointed Minister-Counselor (Cānzàn Dàchén),
to proceed to Guǎngdōng to assist in the suppression.
On the Rénwǔ day,
the British captured the Hǔmén fort and Wūyǒng checkpoint in Guǎngdōng.
Guān Tiānpéi, the Admiral of the Guǎngdōng navy, and Xiángfú, the acting Admiral of Húnán, died.
This month,
relief was extended to disaster victims in Jiāngsū's Jiāngníng and Tōngzhōu prefectures and departments.
On the Bǐngxū day, the first day of the third month,
Zhōu Tiānjúe was released to proceed to the military camp in Guǎngdōng.
On the Jiǎwǔ day,
the Emperor visited the Xīlíng tombs,
and three-tenths of the regular taxes were remitted for the areas passed through.
On the Yǐwèi day,
Wénfú, the retired Grand Secretary, died.
On the Bǐngshēn day,
British warships entered the inner harbor of Guǎngdōng,
and Yáng Fāng and others repelled them.
On the Wùxū day,
the Emperor visited the Tàilíng, Tàidōnglíng, and Chānglíng tombs,
and offered libations at the mausoleums of Empress Xiàomù, Empress Xiàoshèn, and Empress Xiàoquán in Lóngquányù.
On the Jǐhài day,
the Emperor revisited the Chānglíng tomb,
and performed the ceremony of laying earth.
He proceeded to the Lóng'ēn Diàn to perform the grand sacrificial ceremony.
On the Rényín day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the Bǐngwǔ day,
the Emperor visited the residence of the late Grand Secretary Wénfú to offer libations.
On the Wùshēn day,
trade with Mǐlǐjiān (America) and other nations was permitted.
On the Gēngxū day,
based on Yùqiān's memorial,
it was ordered that trade by merchants and civilians at coastal trading ports should continue as before.
On the Rénzǐ day,
Yáng Fāng and others requested that British merchant ships still be allowed to trade in Guǎngdōng.
This was not granted,
and Yáng Fāng and Yíliáng were ordered to be severely deliberated upon.
On the Yǐmǎo day, the first day of the intercalary third month,
Yáng Fāng and Yíliáng were stripped of their posts,
but remained in office.
On the Bǐngyín day,
Tāng Jīnzhāo was demoted,
Zhuó Bǐngtián was transferred to Minister of Personnel (Lìbù Shàngshū) and Assistant Grand Secretary,
Qí Jùnzǎo was made Minister of Revenue (Hùbù Shàngshū),
and Xǔ Nǎipǔ was appointed Minister of War (Bīngbù Shàngshū).
On the Dīngmǎo day,
Yīlǐbù was summoned to the capital,
Yùqiān was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
and Liú Yùnkē was ordered to manage the Dìnghǎi defenses.
Liáng Zhāngjù was transferred to Governor of Jiāngsū,
and Zhōu Zhīqí was appointed Governor of Guǎngxī.
On the Yǐhài day,
an edict was issued to Yìshān and others to console and offer relief to foreign merchants from various countries.
This month,
grain from the granaries for last year's poor harvest was lent to Jízhōu and ten other departments and counties, as well as Hélín'gé'ěr Ting, in Shānxī.
Water-affected land rents in Sùqiān county, Jiāngsū, were remitted and deferred.
On the Jǐchǒu day of the fourth month in summer,
Yùqiān was still appointed Imperial Commissioner (Qīnchāi Dàchén),
to supervise the coastal defense of Zhèjiāng.
The British captured the forts outside Guǎngdōng city.
On the Jiǎchén day,
Kuízhào, the Minister of Rites (Lǐbù Shàngshū), resigned due to illness,
and Sèkèjīng'é was appointed Minister of Rites.
Lóng Qǐruì and 202 others were granted the Jinshi degree with differing ranks.
On the Xīnhài day,
Ruì Qīnwáng and others, the Grand Secretaries, Grand Councilors (Jūnjī Dàchén), and Ministers of various Boards were ordered to jointly interrogate Yīlǐbù with the Ministry of Justice.
On the Guǐchǒu day,
as the provincial capital of Guǎngdōng was in urgent siege,
Yìshān and others' memorial was approved,
allowing the British to trade.
This month,
arrears of taxes in Shuòzhōu and six other departments, prefectures, and counties in Shānxī were deferred.
On the Bǐngchén day of the fifth month,
British ships entered the waters of Zhèjiāng,
and Yùqiān was ordered to strictly reinforce military preparations at all seaports.
On the Guǐhài day,
Dèng Tíngzhēn and Lín Zéxú were banished to Yīlí.
On the Guǐyǒu day,
British ships left Hǔmén, Guǎngdōng.
Mùzhāng'ā was relieved of managing the Court of Colonial Affairs (Fānyuàn),
and Sàishàng'ā was ordered to replace him.
Lóngwén, Minister-Counselor and Minister of Revenue, died in the army.
On the Gēngchén day,
Jìngzhēng was transferred to Minister of Revenue,
Sàishàng'ā to Minister of Public Works (Gōngbù Shàngshū),
and Ēnguì to Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
On the Rénwǔ day,
Wú Wénróng was transferred to Governor of Jiāngxī,
and Qián Bǎochēn to Governor of Húnán.
Yìxīng was appointed General of Suīyuǎn City.
In the sixth month,
Qíshì and others' memorial establishing regulations for merchant ships going to Tiānjīn and other places was approved.
On the Gēngyín day,
Yīlǐbù was stripped of his post,
and sent to a military post for penal servitude to atone for his crimes.
Yìshān and others' memorial to withdraw troops in phases was approved.
On the Wùxū day,
Qíshàn was sentenced to beheading.
On the Guǐmǎo day,
the river burst its banks in Xiànán Ting, Hénán.
On the Xīnmǎo day,
Wénchōng was stripped of his post,
but remained in his position as Governor-General of River Affairs for Hédōng.
Niújiàn was ordered to be severely deliberated upon by the Board.
On the Bǐngchén day of the seventh month,
Wáng Dǐng and others were ordered to proceed to Hédōng to supervise the work.
On the Réngxū day,
Lǐ Zhènhù was appointed Minister of Justice.
On the Dīngmǎo day,
as the Dálài Lǎma had been enthroned in the fourth month,
an imperial rescript was issued.
On the Wùchén day,
Tèyīshùn, the former General of Níngxià, was appointed Minister-Counselor,
to proceed to Guǎngdōng.
On the Xīnwèi day,
due to river flooding,
Niújiàn was ordered to relocate and provide relief to the affected population.
On the Jǐmǎo day,
Nánzhǎng paid tribute.
On the Gēngchén day,
the British captured Xiàmén, Fújiàn,
and Jiāng Jìyún, the Brigade-General, died.
Ruǎn Fútián, the son of the late King Ruǎn Fútián of Yuènán, was appointed King of Yuènán,
and Bǎoqīng, the Surveillance Commissioner (Ànchásǐ) of Guǎngxī, was ordered to go and confer the title.
On the Guǐwèi day of the eighth month,
Guìlún was appointed General-in-chief of Rèhé.
On the Dīnghài day,
the British invaded Zhèjiāng.
On the Gēngyín day,
Zhū Xiāng was appointed Governor-General of River Affairs for Hédōng.
On the Xīnmǎo day,
on the Emperor's birthday (Wànshòujié),
the Emperor proceeded to the Empress Dowager's palace to perform the rites.
At the Zhèngdàguāngmíng Diàn,
the Imperial Princes, and civil and military officials below the rank of Prince,
Mongolian envoys, and outer vassal princes performed the congratulatory rites.
Wénchōng was stripped of his post,
and put in a cangue by the river.
Wáng Dǐng acted as Governor-General of River Affairs for Hédōng.
The British left Xiàmén.
On the Dīngyǒu day,
the British attacked Shuāng'ào, Shípǔ, and other places in Zhèjiāng.
Yùqiān commanded troops to repel them.
Yíliáng was ordered to Fújiàn to investigate and handle military affairs.
Liáng Bǎocháng acted as Governor of Guǎngdōng.
On the Gēngzǐ day,
Zhào Bǐngyán was appointed Governor of Húběi.
On the Xīnchǒu day,
the British launched another major invasion of Zhèjiāng.
On the Wùshēn day,
the British recaptured Dìnghǎi,
and Wáng Xīpéng, Zhèng Guóhóng, Gé Yúnfēi, and other Brigade-Generals died.
Yùqiān and Yú Bùyún were ordered to be severely deliberated upon by the Board.
This month,
the regular taxes for flood-affected areas in Huázhōu, Dà'èr prefectures and counties in Shǎnxī,
and Suīzhōu and eight other departments, prefectures, and counties in Hénán were remitted.
In the ninth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
the British captured Zhènhǎi.
Imperial Commissioner Yùqiān died there,
and Commander Yú Bùyún fled.
Yìjīng was appointed General Wēiyáng,
Hālānga and Hú Chāo were appointed Grand Councilors,
to supervise coastal defense in Zhèjiāng.
Yíliáng was appointed Imperial Commissioner,
to jointly supervise coastal defense in Zhèjiāng with Yán Bǎotáo and Liú Hóng'áo.
Niú Jiàn was appointed acting Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
and Èshùn'ān was appointed acting Governor of Hénán.
On the day Dīngsì,
Wénwèi was appointed Grand Councilor
and sent to Zhèjiāng,
while Hú Chāo remained stationed in Tiānjīn.
Tèyīshùn was appointed Grand Councilor
and sent to Zhèjiāng,
while Hālānga remained stationed at Shānhǎi Pass.
Qí Jùnzǎo was ordered to serve as a Grand Councilor.
Niú Jiàn was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the British captured Níngbō Prefecture in Zhèjiāng.
On the day Jǐsì,
the Emperor reviewed the Firearm Battalion soldiers.
That month,
relief was provided for flood victims in Liáoyáng and other six prefectures and counties in Fèngtiān.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Sēnggélínqìn and others were ordered to inspect the Tiānjīn estuary.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
British ships entered the Táiwān estuary,
and Dáhóng'ā and others repelled them.
Wáng Délù was ordered to go to Táiwān to assist in the suppression.
That month,
relief was provided for Huáróng County and Yuèzhōu衛 in Húnán,
and Déhuà and other ten counties in Jiāngxī suffering from floods.

Additional relief was provided for disaster victims in Miǎnyáng and other nine prefectures and counties in Húběi, Sàlāqí Hall in Shānxī, and Shàngyuán and other fifteen counties and guards in Jiāngsū,
and their regular taxes were remitted.
Grain rations and housing expenses were provided for flood victims in Wúwéi and other twelve prefectures and counties in Ānhuī,
and their regular taxes were remitted.
In the eleventh month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Chéng Yùcǎi was appointed acting Governor of Jiāngsū.
Due to snow disaster among the Yùshù Tibetan tribes in Qīnghǎi,
their silver tribute was remitted for two years.
On the day Wùyín,
the British captured Yúyáo County in Zhèjiāng,
and re-entered Cíxī.
That month,
relief was provided for disaster victims in Shàngyuán and Jiāngníng counties in Jiāngsū.
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Yán Bǎotáo was stripped of his office,
and Yáng Guózhēn was appointed Governor-General of Mǐnzhè.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Liáng Èhán was appointed Governor of Shānxī.
On the day Guǐsì,
the British captured Fènghuà County in Zhèjiāng.
On the day Rènyín,
bandits led by Zhōng Rénjié revolted in Chóngyáng County, Húběi,
and captured the county seat.
Yùtài and others were ordered to lead troops to suppress them.
Chéng Yùcǎi was appointed Governor of Jiāngsū.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
British ships attacked Zhàpǔ in Zhèjiāng.
On the day Wùshēn,
British ships attacked Dànshuǐ and Jīlóng in Táiwān,
and Dáhóng'ā and others repelled them.
That month,
relief was provided for disaster victims in Xīnyáng County in Jiāngsū.
Relief was extended to disaster victims in Xiángfú and other six counties in Hénán, and Shàngyuán and other ten counties in Jiāngsū.
Seeds and grain rations were loaned to poor people in Suīzhōu and Zhéchéng counties in Hénán,
and granary grain in Huáiníng County was sold at a stable price.
Arrears of taxes in Nánchāng and other twenty-two counties in Jiāngxī,
and salt duties in Hěngpǔ and Pǔdōng two salt fields in Zhèjiāng were deferred.
That year,
Cháoxiǎn, Liúqiú, and Nánzhǎng presented tribute.
In the twenty-second year, spring, the first month, on the day Bǐngchén,
Yáng Guózhēn was relieved due to illness,
and Yíliáng was appointed Governor-General of Mǐnzhè,
and Liáng Bǎocháng was appointed Governor of Guǎngdōng.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
General Qíyīng of Shèngjīng was transferred to be General of Guǎngzhōu,
and Xī'ēn was appointed acting general.
On the day Jǐsì,
the bandits of Chóngyáng in Húběi captured Tōngshān,
and Yùtài sent troops to defeat them.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Chóngyáng County in Húběi was retaken,
and the bandit leader Zhōng Rénjié was captured.
That month,
relief was provided for Wúwéi and other twelve prefectures, counties, and guards in Ānhuī,
and disaster victims in Liáoyáng and other six places, and Xīnmín and other four halls and counties in Fèngtiān.
Grain rations were provided for flood victims in Sīzhōu and other twenty-two prefectures, counties, and guards in Ānhuī, and Hǎiníng and other seven prefectures and counties in Zhèjiāng.

Seeds and grain rations for flood victims were loaned to Déhuà and other seven counties in Jiāngxī, Wǔlíng County in Húnán, Jiāyú and other nine counties and guards in Húběi, and Jiāzhōu and other five prefectures and counties in Shǎnxī,
granary grain for poor harvest in Sàlāqí Hall in Shānxī,
and soldiers' pay for Jīngyòu and other battalions in Jiāngsū disaster areas.
Old and new regular taxes in Hǎiníng and other nine prefectures, counties, and guards in Zhèjiāng affected by floods were remitted and deferred.
In the second month, on the day Bǐngxū,
Lín Zéxú was ordered to remain exiled in Yīlí.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Yìjīng and others failed in their attack on Níngbō.
Yīlǐbù was released and sent to the Zhèjiāng military camp.
Qíyīng was appointed acting General of Hángzhōu.
Wáng Dǐng requested leave.
Qí Shèn was ordered to remain Grand Councilor,
to manage military affairs in Zhèjiāng.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Qíyīng was appointed Imperial Commissioner,
to jointly defend the Zhèjiāng provincial capital with Tèyīshùn,
and Liú Yùnkē was ordered to jointly manage defense affairs,
while Yìjīng and others were tasked with defending various coastal ports.
That month,
relief was provided for disaster victims in Liáoyáng and other places in Shèngjīng, and Shàngyuán and other eight counties in Jiāngsū.
In the third month, on the day Rénzǐ,
the Emperor visited Nányuàn.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Emperor went hunting,
and did so again the next day.
On the day Dīngsì,
the Emperor returned to Yuánmíngyuán.
Ēntèhēng'é died,
and Fùníyáng'ā was appointed Governor-General of Shǎnxī-Gānsù,
Bìchāng was appointed Governor of Shǎnxī.
Qìngchāng was appointed Grand Councilor of Yīlí.
That month,
arrears of taxes on waterlogged land in Zhèngzhōu, Hénán were remitted and deferred.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Guǐwèi,
the British again attacked Táiwān,
and Dáhóng'ā and others repelled them.
Dáhóng'ā was promoted to Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the British left Níngbō Prefecture.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Emperor went to the Black Dragon Pool Temple to pray for rain.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the British captured Zhàpǔ in Zhèjiāng,
and Tongzhi Wéi Fēngjiǎ died there.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Yú Bùyún was stripped of his office and arrested for questioning.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Zhōng Rénjié was executed.
That month,
seeds and grain rations were loaned to frontier soldiers and Miao tenants in Fènghuáng and other five halls and counties in Húnán,
and granary grain in Jízhōu and other fourteen prefectures and counties in Shānxī.
Arrears of grain taxes in Yángqǔ County and Sàlāqí Hall in Shānxī were deferred.
In the fifth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
Grand Secretary Wáng Dǐng died suddenly.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Tāng Jīnzhāo was demoted to Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
On the day Dīngsì,
Tāng Jīnzhāo requested retirement,
which was granted.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Yìshān was stripped of his Censor-in-Chief of the Left for submitting an untrue report,
and Qí ● and Liáng Bǎocháng were stripped of their offices but retained in their positions.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Minister of Rites Sèkèjīng'é died,
and Ēnguì was appointed to replace him.
Jílúntài was appointed Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
Kuízhào was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the day Rénxū,
the British captured Bǎoshān County in Jiāngsū,
and Commander Chén Huàchéng died there.
Qíyīng and Yīlǐbù were ordered to go to Jiāngsū,
to jointly defend and suppress with Niú Jiàn.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the British captured Shànghǎi County,
and County Clerk Yáng Qìng'ēn died there.
Sàishàng'ā was appointed Imperial Commissioner,
to jointly defend and suppress with Nè'ěrjīng'é.
That month,
seeds for poor harvest were loaned to Shānyáng County and Huái'ān and other two counties and guards in Jiāngsū.
In the sixth month, on the first day Wùyín,
there was a solar eclipse.
Old and new regular taxes in Chóngyáng and other five counties and guards in Húběi disturbed by bandits were remitted and deferred.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Wénqìng was appointed Minister for Kulun Affairs.
On the day Rénchén,
old and new regular taxes in Dìnghǎi and other twelve counties in Zhèjiāng disturbed by the British were remitted and deferred.
On the day Guǐsì,
British ships attacked Jīngkǒu.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
British ships attacked Zhènjiāng,
and Qí Shèn and others fled.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the British captured Zhènjiāng,
and Deputy Commander Hǎilíng died there.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
British ships invaded the provincial capital of Jiāngníng.
Yīlǐbù and others were ordered to negotiate a settlement.
Yìjīng was ordered to advance and garrison Chángzhōu.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Qíyīng reported that he had discussed with the British military officer Mǎlìxùn (Morrison) and others to cease hostilities.
An edict stated,
“I prioritize the lives of the people,”
and ordered a proper and decisive agreement to be made.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Qíyīng and others requested to finalize a treaty with the British military officer,
and affix the imperial seal.
An edict stated,
“Because it concerns the lives of millions of people,”
and granted the request.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the river burst its banks in the Táoběi Sub-prefecture of Jiāngnán.
In this month,
relief was provided for the earthquake disaster in Bālǐkūn.
In the eighth month, on the *wùyín* day,
Qíyīng reported that Guǎngzhōu, Fúzhōu, Xiàmén, Níngbō, and Shànghǎi ports
had agreed with Great Britain to open for trade.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Línqìng was
stripped of his post but retained in office for negligence in river defense.
Jìngzhēng and Liáo Hóngquán were ordered to Jiāngnán to inspect river works.
In this month,
loans were provided for house repair costs for the earthquake disaster in Bālǐkūn.
In the ninth month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
Shěn Qí requested to retire to care for his parents,
which was granted.
Lǐ Zōngfǎng was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Xī'ēn was appointed General of Shèngjīng.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Zhū Shù requested to retire to care for his parents,
which was granted.
Zhōu Tiānjúe was ordered to serve as acting Governor-General of Grain Transport with a second-rank button.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Niú Jiàn, Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng, was stripped of his post and arrested for questioning;
Qíyīng was ordered to replace him.
Yìshān was summoned to the capital.
Yīlǐbù was appointed Imperial Commissioner and General of Guǎngzhōu,
to handle post-war affairs.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Zhū Xiāng, Governor-General of Riverways of Hédōng, died;
Huìchéng was appointed to act in his place.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Yìjīng and Wénwèi were summoned to the capital.
Qí Shèn was ordered to return as Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Sìchuān.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Yīlǐbù was ordered to discuss matters of commercial taxation.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Bìchāng was transferred to General of Fúzhōu;
Lǐ Xīngyuán was appointed Governor of Shǎnxī.
In the winter, tenth month, on the *gēngchén* day,
the Emperor reviewed the Eight Banners musketeers at Yuánmíngyuán.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Yìshān, Yìjīng, and Wénwèi were handed over to the Board of Punishments for trial;
Tèyīshùn and Qí Shèn were sent to the Board for severe deliberation.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the old and new tax quotas for the forty prefectures, departments, counties, and garrisons including Tàicāng in the coastal areas of Jiāngsū affected by warfare were reduced or remitted differently.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Yìshān, Yìjīng, and Wénwèi were all stripped of their posts and condemned to decapitation;
Tèyīshùn and Qí Shèn were stripped of their posts but retained in office.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Jìngzhēng, Minister of the Board of Revenue, was ordered to assist as Grand Secretary;
Ēnguì was transferred to Minister of the Board of Civil Office;
Línkuí was appointed acting Minister of the Board of Rites.
On the *wùxū* day,
Yìcǎi, Prince Qìnjùn, was stripped of his princely title due to an incident;
Miánxìng, a Fǔguógōng of the Unranked Eight Divisions, was stripped of his title and banished to Shèngjīng.
In this month,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Táoyuán and Shùyáng counties of Jiāngsū.
Rations were distributed to disaster victims in four counties including Jiānglíng in Húběi, and three prefectures/departments/counties including Bǎodé in Shānxī.
Rations were loaned to disaster victims in places such as Niúzhuāng in Fèngtiān.
The old and new tax quotas for five prefectures/counties including Hǎizhōu in Jiāngsū, and eight prefectures/counties/garrisons including Lǐzhōu in Húnán were remitted or deferred.
In the eleventh month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
Gùqìng, Assistant Amban of Kēbùduō, was summoned to the capital;
Guǒlèmíng'ā was appointed to replace him.
Shèngguì, Assistant Amban of Wūlǐyàsūtái, was summoned to the capital;
Lèbīn was appointed to replace him.
Méngbǎo, Amban Resident in Tibet, was summoned to the capital;
Hǎipú was appointed to replace him.
Pān Xī'ēn was appointed Governor-General of Riverways of Jiāngnán.
Huìchéng was appointed Governor-General of Riverways of Hédōng.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Zhōu Tiānjúe's request to return home for mourning was granted;
Liáo Hóngquán was appointed acting Governor-General of Grain Transport.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Yíliáng was ordered to investigate Dáhóng'ā and others for the unauthorized killing of shipwrecked foreigners.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Niú Jiàn was condemned to decapitation.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
poor people in six counties including Dāntú in the riverside areas of Jiāngsū affected by warfare were given rations and house repair funds,
and the tax quotas for thirteen prefectures/departments/counties including Tōngzhōu were remitted differently.
In this month,
rations were distributed for flood disaster in Xiāoxiàn and Xúzhōu Garrison of Jiāngsū.
The old and new tax quotas for three counties including Chún'ān in Zhèjiāng were remitted or deferred.
In the twelfth month, on the *xīnsì* day,
Liáo Hóngquán was summoned to the capital;
Lǐ Xiāngfēn was appointed acting Governor-General of Grain Transport.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
a Brigade-General of Tōngyǒng Garrison was established,
stationed at Lútái;
Xiàng Róng was appointed Brigade-General of Tōngyǒng Garrison.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Chéng Yùcǎi was summoned to the capital;
Sūn Shànbǎo was appointed Governor of Jiāngsū.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Tuōhúnbù was dismissed due to illness;
Chéng Yùcǎi was appointed Governor of Shāndōng.
On the *wùxū* day,
Grand Secretaries, the Nine Ministers, and Censors were further ordered to deliberate Yu Bùyún's crime,
and he was condemned to decapitation.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Liáng Bǎocháng was transferred to Governor of Shāndōng;
Chéng Yùcǎi was transferred to Governor of Guǎngdōng.
In this month,
rations and house repair funds were distributed for flood disaster in three counties/departments including Fēngshì in Fújiàn.
In this year,
Gurkha, Cháoxiǎn, and Liúqiú paid tribute.
In the twenty-third year, spring, first month, on the *xīnhài* day,
Lǐ Huì and Chéng Gāng were ordered to Nánhé,
to supervise the works jointly with Pān Xī'ēn.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the British military officer Pǔdǐngchá (Pottinger) returned to Hong Kong,
leaving Mǎlìxùn and others to await treaty negotiations.
Yīlǐbù and others were ordered to prepare for trade matters.
Lǐ Xiāngfēn was ordered to prepare for post-war affairs north of the Jiāng with Qíyīng.
In this month,
relief was provided for disasters in Xiāoxiàn and Táoyuán counties of Jiāngsū,
and rations were distributed to six counties/garrisons including Shùyáng.
Seeds and rations were loaned for flood disaster to three counties/garrisons including Jiānglíng in Húběi,
and Lǐzhōu and Dòngtíng garrisons in Húnán.
In the second month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
Yīlǐbù, Imperial Commissioner and General of Guǎngzhōu, died;
Qíshàn was ordered to take over the administration of commercial tariffs.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Yìxiāng, General of Wūlǐyàsūtái, was transferred to General of Guǎngzhōu;
Lùpǔ was appointed to replace him.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Yìxīng was transferred to General of Wūlǐyàsūtái;
Lùpǔ was transferred to General of Suīyuǎnchéng.
In this month,
granary grain was loaned to garrison troops in Jīngzhōu, Húběi, affected by flood.
In the third month, on the *gēngxū* day,
Qíyīng was appointed Imperial Commissioner,
to handle trade matters in Jiāngsū and Zhèjiāng.
Bìchāng was appointed acting Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Emperor personally examined Hanlin and Court officials;
Wàn Qīnglí and five others were promoted to the first class,
while others were promoted or demoted differently.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Lùpǔ was transferred to Mongol Commandant of the Bordered Red Banner;
Yìxīng was transferred to General of Suīyuǎnchéng;
Guìlún was appointed General of Wūlǐyàsūtái;
Qíshàn was reinstated as Commandant of Rèhé.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Wénwèi was reinstated as Minister Leading Troops at Gǔchéng.
Yìjīng was reinstated as Assistant Minister at Yè'ěrqiāng.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Yíliáng reported that Dáhóng'ā and Yáo Yíng had no military achievements;
they were ordered to be stripped of their posts and arrested for questioning.
Subsequently, Dáhóng'ā and Yáo Yíng were acquitted of punishment.
In this month,
granary grain was loaned to six prefectures/counties including Jiàngzhōu in Shānxī, and garrison troops in Jīngzhōu, Húběi, affected by disaster;
silver was loaned to garrison troops in Jiāngníng and various supervisory/assistant garrisons affected by disaster and poor harvests;
seeds and rations were loaned to Miáo tenants and Tún soldiers in five prefectures/counties including Fènghuáng in Húnán.
In the summer, fourth month, on the *jiǎxū* day, the first of the month,
Wéiqín was appointed Commandant of Wūlǔmùqí.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Línkuí was appointed Minister of the Board of Rites.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
following the impeachment by Censor Chén Qìngyōng,
Qíshàn, Wénwèi, and Yìjīng were again stripped of their posts.
Kuízhào was dismissed due to illness;
Tèdēng'é was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left;
Sàyíng'ā was appointed Commandant of Rèhé.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Qíyīng was ordered to meet with the British to discuss trade.
On the *wùchén* day,
Yíliáng was dismissed due to illness;
Liú Yùnkē was appointed Governor-General of Mǐnzhè;
Wú Qíjùn was transferred to Governor of Zhèjiāng;
Lùfèi Zhuán was appointed Governor of Húnán.
In the sixth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
the bandit Zēng Rúzhù rebelled in Wǔgāng Prefecture, Húnán,
and assassinated the Prefect Xú Guāngbì;
Wú Qíjùn was ordered to suppress him.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Zēng Rúzhù was executed.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Yǐsì,
the Hé [Yellow River] breached its banks in Dōnghé, Mùfǔ, at nine forts.
Huìchéng's subordinate departments debated stringently.
Qíyīng's memorial was approved,
establishing regulations for commercial tariffs,
initially to be implemented in Guǎngzhōu.
Jìngzhēng and Hé Rǔlín were reassigned to Dōnghé to investigate.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
È Shùn'ān was ordered to provide disaster relief to flood victims along the river.
In the intercalary seventh month, on the day Wùyín,
the Yǒngdìng Hé in Zhílì breached its banks.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
as the Mùfǔ breach remained unsealed,
Huìchéng was ordered to be put in a cangue at the river bank.
Zhōngxiáng was appointed Governor-General of Riverways for Hédōnghé.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Fǎfēng'ē was summoned to the capital.
Déxīng was appointed Minister Resident in Xīníng.
On the day Dīnghài,
Liáo Hóngquán was ordered to Hénán
to jointly supervise the river works.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Línqìng was appointed to Dōnghé to supervise the river works.
On the day Gēngyín,
Jìngzhēng and others were ordered to deliberate on the production of paper currency.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Wú Qíjùn was transferred to be Governor of Yúnnán,
and Guǎn Yùqún was appointed Governor of Zhèjiāng.
In the eighth month, on the day Yǐsì,
Chéng Màocǎi was admonished to provide relief and comfort to the flood victims in the affected prefectures and counties of Ānhuī.
This month,
disaster relief was provided for flood and hail damage in Miǎn Xiàn and two other counties in Shǎnxī.
In the ninth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
Lǐ Xiāngfēn was appointed acting Grand Canal Governor-General with a third-rank button.
This month,
disaster relief was provided for flood damage in Fúshān Xiàn, Shāndōng.
Taxes and miscellaneous levies for flood and hail disasters were remitted and deferred in Jǐng Zhōu and twenty-six other prefectures and counties in Zhílì, and Fúshān Xiàn in Shāndōng.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
Qíyīng memorialized that commercial affairs were completed,
and was ordered to return to his post as Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
to handle post-settlement and Shanghai commercial affairs.
Qíshàn and others were to handle the remaining affairs of Yuè Shěng [Guǎngdōng Province].
On the day Gēngxū,
Qíshàn was appointed Minister Resident in Zàng [Tibet].
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Dáhóng'ē was appointed Minister Resident in Hāmì.
This month,
disaster relief was provided for flood and hail damage in Tàihé and two other counties in Ānhuī, and Kělán Zhōu in Shānxī.
Grain rations were loaned for poor harvests in Tàihé and three other counties in Ānhuī, and four localities including Qíqíhā'ěr.
New and old principal and miscellaneous taxes and levies were remitted and deferred in Liáoyáng and five other prefectures, departments, and counties in Fèngtiān; Shěnyáng and two other localities;
Qíqíhā'ěr and three other localities;
Línqīng and twenty-six other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Shāndōng;
Sī Zhōu and thirty-six other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Ānhuī;
Kělán and six other prefectures and counties in Shānxī;
Lǐ Zhōu and five other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Húnán.
In the eleventh month, on the first day Jǐsì,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Wáng Zhí was appointed Governor of Zhèjiāng.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Chéng Màocǎi was transferred to be Governor of Zhèjiāng,
and Wáng Zhí was appointed Governor of Ānhuī.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the Emperor went to Dàgāo Diàn to pray for snow.
This month,
disaster relief was provided to the victims in Shùyáng Xiàn, Jiāngsū, and Dàhé Wèi.
Seeds, grain rations, and granary grain were loaned to Nánchāng and fourteen other counties in Jiāngxī, and Suídé and eight other prefectures and counties in Shǎnxī.

New and old taxes and levies for flood and drought disasters were remitted and deferred in Xīnhé and three other counties in Zhílì, and Gāoyóu and sixty-seven other prefectures, departments, counties, and garrisons in Jiāngsū.
In the twelfth month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
trade regulations with the Kingdom of Italy were agreed upon.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Liáng Bǎocháng was transferred to be Governor of Zhèjiāng,
and Chóng'ēn was appointed Governor of Shāndōng.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
it snowed.
On the day Dīngsì,
Liú Yùnkē was ordered to handle Níngbō trade affairs.
Gōng Shǒuzhèng, Minister of Rites, resigned due to illness,
and Chén Guānjùn was appointed to replace him.
This month,
new and old principal and miscellaneous taxes and levies for flood damage were remitted and deferred in Suī Zhōu and fifteen other prefectures and counties in Hénán.
This year,
Cháoxiǎn [Korea], Miǎndiàn [Burma], and Xiānmó [Siam] offered tribute.
In the twenty-fourth year, spring, first month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
seeds were loaned for flood and hail disasters in Jiā Zhōu and three other prefectures and counties in Shǎnxī, and Dàtóng and two other counties in Shānxī.
In the second month, on the first day Wùxū,
Qíshàn resigned due to illness.
Qíyīng was transferred to be Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng,
and Bìchāng was appointed acting Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Jìngmǐn, Prince Sù, and others were ordered to remain in the capital to handle affairs during the Emperor's visit to the Eastern Mausoleum.
On the day Gēngxū,
as the Mùfǔ dam works had again stagnated,
Línkuí and Liáo Hóngquán were dismissed from their posts,
granted seventh-rank buttons,
and retained for river works.
Zhōngxiáng was dismissed from his post,
but retained as Governor-General of Dōnghé.
È Shùn'ān was demoted by three ranks.
Tèdēng'é was appointed Minister of Rites,
Wénqìng was appointed Censor-in-chief of the Left,
Chén Guānjùn was transferred to be Minister of Works,
Lǐ Zōngfǎng was appointed Minister of Rites,
and Dù Shòutián was appointed Censor-in-chief of the Left.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Mùzhāng'ā was ordered to remain in the capital to handle affairs.
As Chéng Yùcǎi memorialized that the American envoy wished to come to Tiānjīn for an audience
and to discuss trade regulations,
Qíyīng was ordered to Guǎngdōng
to jointly with Chéng Yùcǎi appropriately handle trade affairs with America and other nations.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
three-tenths of the land tax in transit areas was remitted.
This month,
grain rations were provided to the people and military colonists in Hǎizhōu and two other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Jiāngsū.
In the third month, on the day Rénshēn,
Qíyīng was appointed Imperial Commissioner
to handle post-settlement trade affairs.
Chéng Yùcǎi was again ordered to instruct the American envoy to desist from coming to the capital.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Zhōngxiáng and others memorialized on post-settlement river works,
and the Emperor issued an edict:
"If even one man is displaced,
the fault lies with Us.
You, ministers, should manage it well."
This month,
granary grain was loaned for poor harvests in Píngdìng and ten other prefectures, departments, and counties in Shānxī.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
the inner sea forts at Hǔmén, Guǎngdōng, were repaired.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the bandits in Táiwān were pacified.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Sūn Yùjìn and two hundred nine other individuals were granted the degree of Jìnshì and various official ranks.
This month,
three months of grain rations were additionally provided for flood damage in Suī Zhōu and fourteen other prefectures and counties in Hénán.
In the sixth month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
the Yǒngdìng Hé in Zhílì breached its banks.
On the day Rén'yín,
the bandits Yáng Dàpéng and others rebelled in Lèiyáng Xiàn, Húnán.
Lùfèi Quán and others were ordered to suppress them.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
the trade treaty with America was concluded.
This month,

new and old taxes and levies for disaster-stricken areas were deferred in Línqīng and twenty-one other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng, and the two garrisons of Dé Zhōu and Dōngchāng, with varying amounts.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Xīnsì,
Fùníyáng'ā and Admiral Zhōu Yuèshèng were subjected to stringent departmental deliberation.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the bandits in Lèiyáng Xiàn, Húnán, were pacified,
and the bandit leader Yáng Dàpéng was executed.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Wànchéng Dī dike in Jīngzhōu, Húběi, breached.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Yìxīng was summoned to the capital.
Tiělín was appointed acting General of Suīyuǎn Chéng,
and Āyàntài was appointed acting Military Governor of Cháhā'ěr.
This month,
three months of grain rations were additionally provided for flood damage in Zhōngmóu and eight other counties in Hénán.
Seeds were loaned for hail damage in Jiā Zhōu, Shǎnxī.
In the eighth month,
disaster relief was provided for flood and hail damage in Fényáng Xiàn, Shānxī,
and taxes and levies were remitted and deferred in Fényáng and two other counties.
In the ninth month,
three months of grain rations were provided for flood damage in Huáiníng and two other counties in Hénán.
In the winter, tenth month, on the first day Jiǎwǔ,
Burut Āxīm was permitted to inherit a fourth-rank peacock feather.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Yìjīng, Assistant Military Governor of Yè'ěrqiāng, was transferred to be Commander of the Cavalry at Yīlí,
and Línkuí was appointed to replace him.
On the day Rénxū,
Dáhóng'ē, Assistant Military Governor of Yīlí, resigned due to illness.
Lín Zéxú was ordered to Ākèsū, Wūshí, Kùchē, Hétián, and other places to investigate and deliberate on reclamation affairs.
On the day Guǐhài,
Shūxīng'ā was appointed Assistant Military Governor of Yīlí.
This month,
disaster relief was provided to the banner people of Bà Zhōu and Yǒngqīng and two other prefectures and counties in Zhílì.
Grain rations were provided for flood damage in Jǐn Zhōu and seven other prefectures, departments, and counties in Fèngtiān.

New and old taxes and levies for flood, drought, and hail disasters were remitted and deferred in Bà Zhōu and thirty-six other prefectures and counties in Zhílì; Jīn Zhōu and seven other prefectures, counties, and departments in Fèngtiān; and Miǎnyáng and twenty-eight other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Húběi.
In the eleventh month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
Guìliáng was permitted to come for an audience.
Wú Qíjùn was concurrently appointed acting Governor-General of Yúnguì.
Former Vice Minister of Punishments Huáng Juézī was appointed to official posts such as Supernumerary Secretary.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the Emperor went to Dàgāo Diàn to pray for snow.
This month,
grain rations were loaned for poor harvests at the Jīn Zhōu naval camp in Shèngjīng.
In the twelfth month, on the first day Guǐsì,
the Emperor again went to Dàgāo Diàn to pray for snow.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Lín Zéxú was further ordered to Kāshígá'ěr to investigate reclamation.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the Emperor went to Dàgāo Diàn to pray for snow.
Zhuó Bǐngtián was appointed Grand Secretary.
Chén Guānjùn was appointed Minister of Rites and concurrently Associate Grand Secretary.
Dù Shòutián was appointed Minister of Works.
Zhù Qìngfān was appointed Censor-in-chief of the Left.
This month,
additional grain rations were provided for disaster-stricken areas in Suī Zhōu and fourteen other prefectures and counties in Hénán,
and seeds and granary grain were loaned.
Silver and rice were loaned to the garrison soldiers in Jiāngníng and the various camp soldiers and artisans in Jiāngsū.
This year,
Cháoxiǎn [Korea] and Xiānmó [Siam] offered tribute.
In the spring, in the first month, on the day Yǐchǒu of the twenty-fifth year,
the river works at Zhōngmóu, Hénán, were completed (lit. "the dragons were joined").
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Lǐ Xīngyuán was transferred to be the Governor of Jiāngsū;
Huìjí was appointed Governor of Shǎnxī;
Chéng Yùcǎi was made Governor-General of Grain Transport;
and Huáng Éntóng was appointed Governor of Guǎngdōng.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Róngzhào was summoned to the capital;
Línqìng was made the Minister Resident at Kùlún (Ulaanbaatar).
In this month,
grain rations were distributed to disaster victims in the two prefectures and counties of Bàzhōu and Yǒngqīng in Zhílì.
Loans of seeds were provided to five counties, including Déhuà, in Jiāngxī;
six counties and garrisons, including Jiānglíng, in Húběi;
and military and civilian populations in the two counties of Yuánjiāng and Ānxiāng in Húnán.
On the day Gēngxū,
Fújí was appointed Minister of the Imperial Household Department.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Ruì Qīnwáng Rénshòu was punished for improperly recommending Hǎipú:
he was stripped of his titles as Zǒngzhèng of the Zōngrénfǔ, Leader of the Imperial Guards, and Grand Minister of the Imperial Presence.
Jìngzhēng was punished for improperly recommending Mèngbǎo:
he was stripped of his titles as Assistant Grand Secretary and Minister of the Board of Revenue.
Qíyīng, the Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng, was ordered to serve as Assistant Grand Secretary.
Sàishàng'ā was transferred to be Minister of the Board of Revenue;
Yùchéng was made Minister of the Board of Works.
Wénqìng was appointed Minister of the Board of War;
Chénggāng was made Censor-in-Chief on the Left.
Sēnggélínqìn was transferred to be Leader of the Imperial Guards of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
Chēdēngbāzā'ěr was made Leader of the Imperial Guards of the Plain Yellow Banner.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Huìjí was transferred to be Governor of Fújiàn;
Dèng Tíngzhēn was appointed Governor of Shǎnxī.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
regulations for trade at the five treaty ports were promulgated.
On the day Jǐsì,
the Emperor reviewed the Eight Banner musketeers at Yuánmíngyuán.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Línqìng was dismissed due to illness;
Chéngkǎi was appointed Minister Resident at Kùlún.
In this month,
loans of granary grain were provided to seventeen prefectures, counties, and departments, including Xīnzhōu, in Shānxī, due to poor harvests.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Guìliáng remained in the capital;
Hè Chánglíng was appointed Governor-General of Yúnguì.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Wú Qíjùn was transferred to be Governor of Fújiàn;
Huìjí was made Governor of Yúnnán;
Qíao Yòngqiān was appointed Governor of Guìzhōu.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Emperor proceeded to Hēilóngtán to pray for rain.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Fùníyáng'ā passed away;
Huìjí was appointed Governor of Shǎnxī;
Dèng Tíngzhēn acted in his stead;
Zhèng Zǔchēn was appointed Governor of Yúnnán.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Xiāo Jǐnzhōng and 217 others were granted the Jinshì degree with various distinctions.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Yùchéng and Xǔ Nǎipǔ were demoted;
Jìngzhēng was appointed Minister of the Board of Works;
Hé Rǔlín was made Minister of the Board of War.
In the fifth month, on the day Bǐngxū,
it rained.
On the day Dīnghài,
the Emperor again proceeded to Hēilóngtán to pray for rain.
In this month,
grain rations were distributed to flood victims in six counties, including Yuè'ān, in Shāndōng.
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
Belgium was granted permission to trade.
An imperial edict ordered the suspension of autumn executions for this year.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Chóng'ēn was ordered to suppress the Niǎn bandits in places such as Púzhōu and Yùnchéng.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
earthquake victims in Zhānghuà County, Táiwān, were provided with relief.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Jíruì, the Minister Resident at Ākèsù, was
stripped of his position for initiating reclamation work without prior imperial approval.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the river at Táoyuán Xùn, Jiāngsū Zhōnghé Tīng, burst its banks.
Qìnghé, the Brigade General of Xīníng Zhèn, Gānsù, encountered Tibetan bandits at Jīnyánglǐng
and died.
Huìjí was ordered to suppress the Tibetan bandits.
In this month,
the collection of outstanding taxes from forty-two prefectures, counties, and garrisons, including Bīnzhōu, in Shāndōng, which were affected by disasters, was deferred.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Denmark was granted permission to trade.
Grand Secretary Zhuō Bǐngtián was ordered to oversee the Board of War.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Dáhóng'ā was ordered to proceed to Gānsù to investigate and deal with the Tibetan bandits.
In the eighth month, on the day Rénchén,
an imperial edict announced the celebration of the Empress Dowager's seventieth birthday,
and exempted all outstanding principal and miscellaneous land taxes from before Dàoguāng's twentieth year.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Zhèng Zǔchēn was transferred to be Governor of Fújiàn;
Liáng Èhán was made Governor of Yúnnán;
Wú Qíjùn was transferred to be Governor of Shānxī.
Jìngzhēng was dismissed due to illness;
Tèdēng'é was transferred to be Minister of the Board of Works;
Bǎochāng was appointed Minister of the Board of Rites.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Lín Zéxú was recalled to the capital
to serve as a probationary official of the fourth or fifth rank in the capital.
Xǐ'ēn was dismissed due to illness;
Yìxiāng was transferred to be the General of Shèngjīng.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
additional honorific titles were bestowed upon the Empress Dowager: Gōngcí Kāngyù Ānchéng Zhuānghuì Shòuxǐ Chóngqí Huángtàihòu.
The Emperor presented the imperial seal and tablet,
and led the imperial princes, princes, dukes, and ministers in a celebratory ceremony.
On the day Wùxū,
on the Empress Dowager's seventieth sacred birthday,
the Emperor led the imperial princes, princes, dukes, and ministers in a celebratory ceremony.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Lǐ Zōngfǎng was dismissed due to illness;
Zhù Qìngfán was appointed Minister of the Board of Rites;
Wèi Yuánlǎng was made Censor-in-Chief on the Left.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
following the completion of the ceremony for bestowing honorific titles upon the Empress Dowager,
an imperial edict was issued, granting varying degrees of special imperial favor.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
all outstanding banner rent owed by the populace in Zhílì before Dàoguāng's twentieth year was remitted.
In this month,
disaster victims in four counties, including Bǎochí, in Zhílì, were provided with relief.
In the eleventh month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Huìjí, the Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù, passed away;
Bùyàntài was appointed Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù;
Lín Zéxú acted in his stead;
Sàyíng'ā was made the General of Yīlí;
Guìliáng was appointed the Military Governor of Rèhé.
On the day Guǐhài,
Censor Chén Qìngyōng was demoted.
In this month,
silver loans were provided to soldiers in the hunting grounds of Rèhé due to poor harvests.
In the twelfth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
the Emperor proceeded to Dàgāodiàn to pray for snow.
On the day Wùxū,
outstanding rent, grain, and rice owed by the populace in Táiwān before Dàoguāng's twentieth year were remitted.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Emperor again proceeded to Dàgāodiàn to pray for snow.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Emperor once more proceeded to Dàgāodiàn to pray for snow.
In this year,
Cháoxiān (Korea) and Yuènán (Vietnam) sent tribute.
In the spring, in the first month, on the day Gēngchén of the twenty-sixth year,
Sàishàng'ā and Zhōu Zǔpéi were ordered to inspect the river defenses.
On the day Xīnsì,
the prohibition on Catholicism was lifted.
Lù Jiànyíng was appointed Governor of Yúnnán.
In this month,
flag-bearers and common people in Fènghuángchéng and Xiùyán Tīng, Fèngtiān,
and four counties, including Bǎochí, in Zhílì, were given grain rations.
Seed loans were provided to disaster victims in thirteen counties, including Jìngníng, in Gānsù.
In the second month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Muslim bandits rebelled in Yǒngchāng, Yúnnán;
Admiral Zhāng Bìlù was ordered to suppress them.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Dìng Jùnwáng Zàiquán and others were ordered to remain in the capital to handle affairs during the Emperor's visit to the imperial tombs.
In the third month, on the day Guǐhài,
the Emperor visited the Western Tombs,
and remitted three-tenths of the extra taxes in the areas he passed through.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the Emperor visited Táilíng, Tàidōnglíng, Chānglíng, and the tombs of Zhìxiào Mùhuánghòu, Xiàoshèn Huánghòu, and Xiàoquán Huánghòu to offer libations.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the Emperor proceeded to Nányuàn for a hunt.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the Emperor went hunting;
he did the same the next day.
On the day Yǐhài,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
The Xīngpíng Granary caught fire.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the Emperor proceeded to Hēilóngtán to pray for rain.
Lín Zéxú was appointed Governor of Shǎnxī.
In this month,
loans of granary grain were provided to nine prefectures and counties, including Píngdìng, in Shānxī, due to poor harvests.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
due to the Yǒngchāng Muslims creating trouble under false pretenses,
Hè Chánglíng was ordered to investigate and deal with them.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Emperor proceeded to Hēilóngtán to pray for rain.
On the day Gēngxū,
Ruìyuán was appointed Assistant Minister Resident at Kēbùduō (Khovd).
In the fifth month, on the day Rénxū,
the Emperor proceeded to Hēilóngtán to pray for rain.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Zhāng Bìlù defeated the Muslim bandits at Yǒngchāng.
Hè Chánglíng was
referred to the appropriate ministry for deliberation due to the excessive killing of sympathetic Muslims in Yǒngchāng in the previous year.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the Emperor again proceeded to Hēilóngtán to pray for rain.
The British withdrew from Zhōushān.
In the intercalary fifth month, on the new moon day Yǐyǒu,
Tibetan bandits rebelled in Hēicuò Sìgōu, Qīnghǎi;
Bùyàntài was ordered to suppress them.
On the day Guǐsì,
the Yǒngchāng Muslim bandits fled into Měngtíng;
Hè Chánglíng led troops to suppress them.
On the day Wùshēn,
Línkuí was appointed Assistant Minister Resident at Wūlǐyǎsūtái (Uliastai).
On the *wùwǔ* day of the sixth month,
Qí Jùnzǎo and Wénqìng were ordered to investigate the salt administration in Tiānjīn.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Ruǎn Yuán, a Grand Secretary who had been granted retirement, was honored for his repeated success in the provincial examinations.
He was promoted to Grand Tutor (*Tàifù*)
and granted a full stipend.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Dá Hóng'ā attacked and routed the Fān bandits who had taken refuge in Guǒchà.
He defeated them.
In the autumn, on the *xīnmǎo* day of the seventh month,
Xǐ'ēn was stripped of his dukedom
for failing to detect treacherous commoners
and demoted to Duke of the State Protector (*Zhènguó Jiāngjūn*).
On the *rényín* day,
the Emperor reviewed the mounted and archery skills of the officials and soldiers of Jílín and Hēilóngjiāng.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
because the accumulated animosity between the Han and Huí peoples in Yúnnán remained unresolved,
Hè Chánglíng was ordered to handle the matter impartially
without differentiating between factions.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the palace gates were strictly secured.
That month,
relief was provided for flood victims in Sānxìng and Nínggǔtǎ and other areas.
On the *rénshēn* day of the eighth month,

the generals, governors-general, and governors of the seven provinces of Shèngjīng, Zhílì, Jiāngnán, Zhèjiāng, Fújiàn, Shāndōng, and Guǎngdōng were ordered to prepare for training troops and storing provisions.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor reviewed the soldiers of the Artillery Battalion.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Hè Chánglíng was demoted to Financial Commissioner (*Bùzhèngshǐ*) of Hénán
for his failure in defense and suppression.
Lǐ Xīngyuán was appointed Governor-General of Yúnguì,
Lù Jiànyíng was transferred to be Governor of Jiāngsū,
and Zhāng Rìzhǐng was appointed Governor of Yúnnán.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Burut bandits entered the Kālún outpost of Kāshígá'ěr,
and Sàishīyǎlètài was ordered to suppress them.
On the *jǐhài* day of the ninth month,
bandits Wáng Zōngxiàn and others rebelled in Xīntián County, Húnán;
they were captured and executed.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Yáng Diànbāng was appointed acting Governor-General of Grain Transport.
On the *xīnhài* day,
bandits Jīn Déshùn and others rebelled in Zhāowén County, Jiāngsū;
they were captured and executed.
That month,
relief was provided for disaster victims in Dōngpíng and Láiwú Prefectures and Counties in Shāndōng.
Relief was provided for Banner people and commoners affected by floods in Sānxìng and Húnchūn.
Food rations were distributed to disaster victims in Wènshàng and four other counties in Shāndōng.

New and old regular taxes were remitted or deferred for disaster and famine-stricken areas in Liáoyáng and thirteen other prefectures, departments, and counties in Fèngtiān; Bāzhōu and thirty-five other prefectures and counties in Zhílì; and Dōngpíng and four other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng.
On the *dīngsì* day of the tenth month,
the regular taxes of the Fān people in Hēicuò Sìgōu were remitted.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Xú Jìyú was appointed Governor of Guǎngxī.
That month,
food rations were distributed to disaster victims in Jíxiàn and eight other counties in Hénán,
and Fǔgǔ and Shénmù two counties in Shǎnxī.
Regular taxes for disaster-affected areas in Lǐzhōu and five other prefectures and counties, as well as Yuèzhōu Military Guard, in Húnán were remitted or deferred.
On the *yǐyǒu* day of the eleventh month,
Guìlún was transferred to be the General of Jīngzhōu,
and Tèyīshùn was appointed General of Wūlǐyǎsūtái.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Emperor went to the Dàgāo Hall to pray for snow.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Bìchāng and others were ordered to deliberate on the possibility of transporting a portion of Jiāngsū's grain tribute by sea.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Huáng Éntóng was referred to the appropriate ministry for severe deliberation
for his request to grant official titles to elderly martial students taking examinations.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Shāndōng was ordered to strictly apprehend bandits who kidnapped people for ransom.
That month,
relief was provided for disaster victims in Yuánqǔ County, Shānxī.

New and old regular taxes for disaster-affected areas in Bǎodé and six other prefectures and counties, as well as Guīhuàchéng and three other places in Shānxī; Yúháng and forty-four other counties and military guards in Zhèjiāng; and Ānzhōu and six other prefectures and counties in Zhílì were remitted or deferred.
On the *guǐchǒu* day of the twelfth month,
Huáng Éntóng was dismissed from office,
Xú Guǎngjìn was transferred to be Governor of Guǎngdōng,
Chéng Yùcǎi was appointed Governor of Yúnnán,
and Yáng Diànbāng was appointed Governor-General of Grain Transport.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Huí bandits from Měngtǒng, Yúnnán, intruded into Miǎnníng,
and Lù Jiànyíng was ordered to investigate the matter.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Dá Hóng'ā, the Minister for Affairs in Xīníng, was relieved of his post due to illness,
and Hālèjínà was appointed to replace him.
On the *wùchén* day,
Wáng Zhàochēn was appointed Governor of Shānxī.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
orders were given to clarify cases in the Board of Punishments and in the various prisons of Zhílì, Shāndōng, Shānxī, Hénán, Shǎnxī, and Gānsù provinces.
Bǎo Xìng was ordered to remain in the capital to manage the Board of Punishments.
Qí Shàn was awarded a second-rank button
and appointed Governor-General of Sìzhōu.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Zhèng Zǔchēn was transferred to be Governor of Guǎngxī,
and Xú Jìyú was transferred to be Governor of Fújiàn.
That month,
food rations were distributed to flood victims in Jìnyún and Xuānpíng two counties in Zhèjiāng.
That year,
Cháoxiǎn (Korea) and Liúqiú paid tribute.
In the spring of the twenty-seventh year, on the *guǐwèi* day of the first month,
Chéng Kǎi was transferred to be Assistant Grand Minister (*Cāncàn Dàchén*) of Tǎ'ěrbāhātái.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Tiě Lín was promoted to General of Jīngzhōu,
and Yùchéng was appointed Military Governor (*Dūtǒng*) of Cháhā'ěr.
That month,

food rations for last year's disasters and famines were distributed to Fùyáng and six other counties and military guards in Zhèjiāng; Wǔhé and three other counties in Ānhuī; and Táoyuán and five other counties and military guards in Jiāngsū.
Food rations and seeds for flood and drought disasters were distributed to Hénéi and thirteen other counties in Hénán,
and granary grain was loaned to Huīxiàn and eight other counties.

Seeds, food rations, and granary grain for disaster and famine were loaned to Jiāzhōu and three other prefectures and counties in Shǎnxī, and Bāzhōu and thirty-nine other prefectures and counties in Zhílì.
On the *jǐwèi* day of the second month,
Huí bandits rebelled in Yúnzhōu, Yúnnán,
and Lǐ Xīngyuán was ordered to suppress them.
On the *guǐhài* day,
for the imperial tomb visit,
Zài Quán and others were ordered to remain in the capital to handle affairs.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
due to sea pirates in Fújiàn robbing and killing foreign merchants,
Liú Yùnkē and others were ordered to search for and apprehend them.
On the *wùyín* day,
the Emperor visited the Eastern Tombs,
and three-tenths of the regular taxes in the passing areas were remitted.
That month,
food rations were distributed to disaster-affected people in Jíxiàn and five other counties in Hénán.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Bìchāng was promoted to Grand Minister of the Interior,
Lǐ Xīngyuán was transferred to be Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
Lín Zéxú was appointed Governor-General of Yúnguì,
and Yáng Yǐzēng was appointed Governor of Shǎnxī.
On the *wùxū* day,
British ships withdrew from Hǔmén.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Wèi Yuánlǎng was appointed Minister of Rites,
and Jiǎ Zhēn was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
In the summer, on the *wùwǔ* day of the fourth month,
Burut bandits again attacked Sèlèkùlè,
and Bókèbāshí and others repelled them.
Sàishīyǎlètài and others reported that the English had occupied Yīndǐ and Nǔpǔ'ěr,
and all tribes were submitting to them.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
arrears of taxes and Banner rent silver in Fēngníng County, Rèhé, were remitted.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Zhāng Zhīwàn and 230 other individuals were granted the *Jìnshì Jídì Chūshēn* (Metropolitan Graduate and First Class) degrees, with varying distinctions.
That month,
seeds and food rations were loaned to military colonists' tenants and Miao tenants in Shànggāo and Xīnchāng two counties in Jiāngxī,
and Fènghuáng and five other departments and counties in Húnán.
On the *bǐngxū* day of the fifth month,
the Emperor personally examined Hanlin and supervisory officials,
promoting Wáng Qìngyún and three others to the first rank,
with others promoted or demoted according to their performance.
Hé Rǔlín was excused due to mourning.
Wèi Yuánlǎng was transferred to be Minister of War,
Jiǎ Zhēn was appointed Minister of Rites,
and Sūn Ruìzhēn was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Wénqìng and Chén Fú'ēn were ordered to serve above the Grand Councilors.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
because the public sentiment in Guǎngdōng was prone to conflict with foreigners,
gentry members were selected to assist in managing negotiation affairs.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Zēng Guófān was promoted to Academician of the Grand Secretariat.
In the sixth month,
the Court of Colonial Affairs reported that a Russian Dalai Lama requested to trade in Tǎ'ěrbāhātái, Yīlí, and Kāshígá'ěr;
this was not permitted.
In the autumn, on the *jǐmǎo* day of the seventh month,
Lín Zéxú was ordered to try the case of Huí people in Yúnnán accusing incense bandits of killing over ten thousand innocents.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Lín Zéxú was ordered to try the case of Dù Wénxiù, a Huí person from Yúnnán, who accused others of falsely implicating him in rebellion.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
due to drought in Hénán,
one hundred thousand taels of silver were issued from the treasury,
and two hundred thousand taels of silver were allocated from neighboring provinces for relief.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
Andíyán (Andijan) bandits attacked Kāshígáěr (Kashgar).
Jímíng and others repelled them.
Sàishìyǎlèntài (Sayishiyarlantai) committed suicide.
Yìshān (Yishan) was transferred to be Yèěrqiāng (Yarkand) Assistant Imperial Resident.
On the day Guǐhài,
Bùyàntài (Buyantai) was dispatched to Sùzhōu (Suzhou) to manage affairs,
Yáng Yǐzēng (Yang Yizeng) was appointed acting Shǎnxī-Gānsù (Shaanxi-Gansu) Governor-General,
and Héngchūn (Hengchun) acting Shǎnxī (Shaanxi) Provincial Governor.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
due to the rebellion of the Bùlǔtè (Burut) people outside the Kāshígáěr (Kashgar) checkpoints and the Andíyán (Andijan) bandits,
Bùyàntài (Buyantai) was appointed General of Dìngxī (Dingxi),
and Yìshān (Yishan) Assistant Imperial Resident,
to suppress them.
Shàntáo (Shantao) was appointed Wūlǐyǎsūtái (Uliyasutai) Assistant Imperial Resident.
Jímíng (Jiming) was appointed acting Yèěrqāng (Yarkand) Assistant Imperial Resident.
On the day Wùchén,
Yìxiāng (Yixiang) was transferred to be Hángzhōu (Hangzhou) General,
Yìxīng (Yixing) was transferred to be Shèngjīng (Shengjing) General,
and Yīnglóng (Yinglong) was appointed Suíyuǎrchéng (Suiyuan City) General.
Due to widespread disaster in Hénán (Henan),
an additional 300,000 taels of silver were allocated from the privy purse,
and the Board of Revenue was ordered to allocate 300,000 taels of silver for relief.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Andíyán (Andijan) bandits besieged Yīngjíshāěr (Yingjishar) city.
Bùyàntài (Buyantai) was ordered to station in Sùzhōu (Suzhou),
and troops were dispatched to suppress them.
In this month,
relief was provided for flood victims in Xīníng (Xining) county, Gānsù (Gansu).
Collection of outstanding taxes was deferred for six flood-affected counties including Lè’ān (Le'an) in Shāndōng (Shandong),
as well as the salt tax from four salt fields including Yǒnglì (Yongli).
In the ninth month, on Dīngchǒu (dingchou), the first day of the lunar month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Wùyín,
Wénqìng (Wenqing) and Zhāng Lǐzhōng (Zhang Lizhong) were ordered to Hénán (Henan) to investigate relief efforts.
On the day Xīnsì,
Jímíng (Jiming) and others dispatched troops to reinforce Kāshígáěr (Kashgar),
attacked the Andíyán (Andijan) bandits,
and greatly defeated them.
On the day Yǐsì,
as French warships entered Cháoxiǎn (Joseon),
Qíyīng (Qiying) was ordered to speak to the French envoy
to have their troops withdraw.
In this month,
rations were distributed to drought victims in forty-one prefectures and counties including Yǔzhōu (Yuzhou) in Hénán (Henan).
New and old outstanding taxes for thirty-six prefectures and counties including Ānzhōu (Anzhou) in Zhílì (Zhili), affected by floods, droughts, and hail, were remitted or deferred.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Yáo (Yao) people, led by Léi Zàihào (Lei Zaihao) and others, rebelled in Xīnníng (Xinning) county, Húnán (Hunan).
Lùfèi Qún (Lüfei Qun) and others pursued and suppressed them.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the Emperor reviewed the Jiànruìyíng (Jianrui Battalion) troops.
On the day Wùchén,
Yìshān (Yishan) and others annihilated the Andíyán (Andijan) bandits at Kēkēréyīwàtè (Kekoreyiwate) in Yèěrqiāng (Yarkand),
and greatly defeated them.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
they were again defeated at Yīngjíshāěr (Yingjishar).
On the day Rénshēn,
the Andíyán (Andijan) bandits fled.
Kāimíngā (Kaiming'a) and other officials leading the Kāshígáěr (Kashgar) office were stripped of their positions and arrested for questioning.
In this month,
new and old outstanding taxes for thirty-nine prefectures and counties including Sīzhōu (Sizhou) in Ānhuī (Anhui), affected by floods and droughts, were remitted or deferred.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
Yīnglóng (Yinglong) was transferred to be Hēilóngjiāng (Heilongjiang) General,
and Chéngyù (Chengyu) to be Suíyuǎrchéng (Suiyuan City) General.
On the day Rénchén,
Zhāng Lǐzhōng (Zhang Lizhong) was appointed Shāndōng (Shandong) Provincial Governor.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the rebels in Xīnníng (Xinning), Húnán (Hunan) were pacified.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
bandits from Dàozhōu (Daozhou), Húnán (Hunan) escaped to Guànyáng (Guanyang) county, Guǎngxī (Guangxi).
Zhèng Zǔchēn (Zheng Zuchen) was ordered to suppress and capture them.
In this month,
rations were distributed to eleven prefectures, departments, and counties including Jiàngzhōu (Jiangzhou) in Shānxī (Shanxi).

New and old regular and miscellaneous outstanding taxes for three prefectures and counties including Ānzhōu (Anzhou) in Zhílì (Zhili), eleven prefectures, departments, and counties including Jiàngzhōu (Jiangzhou) in Shānxī (Shanxi), and sixty-four prefectures and counties including Yǔzhōu (Yuzhou) in Hénán (Henan), affected by disaster, were remitted or deferred.
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùwǔ,
Miáo (Miao) bandits rebelled in Qiánzhōutīng (Qianzhou Department), Húnán (Húnán).
Yùtài (Yutai) and others were ordered to suppress and capture them.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Qíyīng (Qiying) was recalled.
Xú Guǎngjìn (Xu Guangjin) was appointed acting Liǎngguǎng (Liangguang) Governor-General and Imperial Commissioner,
to manage trade.
In this month,
rations were distributed to flood victims in seventeen counties including Xiángfú (Xiangfu) in Hénán (Henan),
and grain was loaned from storehouses in Zhèngzhōu (Zhengzhou) and other places.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn (Joseon) and Liúqiú (Ryukyu) brought tribute.
In the spring of the twenty-eighth year, in the first month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
Pān Shì'ēn (Pan Shi'en) was promoted to Grand Tutor,
Bǎoxìng (Baoxing) to Grand Guardian,
and Bǎochāng (Baochang), Ālèqīngā (Aleqing'a), Lǐ Zhènhù (Li Zhenhu), Chénggāng (Chenggang) to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the Miáo (Miao) bandits in Qiánzhōutīng (Qianzhou Department), Húnán (Hunan) surrendered.
Yùtài (Yutai) was ordered to mete out punishments accordingly,
and continue to search for remaining bandits.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the Gurkha envoy was ordered to attend a banquet with the envoys from Cháoxiǎn (Joseon) and Xiāmluó (Siam).
On the day Wùxū,
Nguyễn Phúc Tuyền (Nguyễn Phúc Tuyên), King of Yuènán (Vietnam), passed away.
The customary tribute for this year was suspended.
Outstanding regular and miscellaneous taxes for both Han and Muslim households in Kāshígáěr (Kashgar) were remitted.
In this month,
relief efforts were extended for disaster victims in five counties including Yánshān (Yanshan) in Zhílì (Zhili).
Rations were distributed to flood and drought victims in three counties including Fèngyáng (Fengyang) in Ānhuī (Anhui).

Rations and seeds were loaned to disaster victims in Ānxiāng (Anxiang) county, Húnán (Hunan), four departments and counties including Níngyuǎn (Ningyuan) in Shānxī (Shanxi), and seven counties including Gāolán (Gaolan) in Gānsù (Gansu).
In the second month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Ēnguì (Engui), President of the Board of Civil Office, passed away.
Wénqìng (Wenqing) was dismissed as Grand Councillor,
and transferred to be President of the Board of Civil Office.
Línkuí (Linkui) was appointed President of the Board of Rites.
Guìliáng (Guiliang) was made General Commandant of the Plain White Banner Manchu Army.
Huìfēng (Huifeng) was appointed acting Rèhé (Rehe) General Commandant.
Bǎochāng (Baochang) was appointed President of the Board of War.
On the day Rénxū,
bandits rebelled in Chángníng (Changning) and Chóngyì (Chongyi) counties, Jiāngxī (Jiangxi).
Wú Wénróng (Wu Wenrong) was ordered to suppress and capture them.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
for the imperial mausoleum visit, Ruìqīnwáng Rénshòu (Prince Rui Renshou) and others were ordered to remain in the capital to manage affairs.
In the third month, on the day Wùyín,
bandits rebelled in Zhàozhōu (Zhao prefecture), Yúnnán (Yunnan).
Lín Zéxú (Lin Zexu) was ordered to suppress and capture them.
Yìshān (Yishan) was appointed Yīlí (Ili) Assistant Imperial Resident,
and Jímíng (Jiming) Yèěrqiāng (Yarkand) Assistant Imperial Resident.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Emperor visited the Western Mausoleums,
and remitted three-tenths of the outstanding taxes in the passing regions.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the Emperor visited the Tàilíng (Tailing) mausoleum, Tàidōnglíng (Taidongling) mausoleum, and Chānglíng (Changling) mausoleum,
and offered wine at the tombs of Empress Xiàomù (Xiaomu), Empress Xiàoshèn (Xiaoshen), and Empress Xiàoquán (Xiaoquan).
On the day Gēngyín,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Yùchéng (Yucheng) was transferred to Jīngzhōu (Jingzhou) General,
and Shuāngdé (Shuangde) was appointed Cháhāěr (Chahar) General Commandant.
In this month,
storehouse grain was loaned for poor harvests in seven prefectures and counties including Jízhōu (Jizhou) in Shānxī (Shanxi).
In summer, in the fourth month, on the day Wùchén,
the bandits in Bǎoshān (Baoshan), Yúnnán (Yunnan) were pacified.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the bandits in Guànyáng (Guanyang), Pínglè (Pingle), Yángshuò (Yangshuo) and other counties in Guǎngxī (Guangxi) were pacified.
In the sixth month, on Guǐmǎo (guimao), the first day of the lunar month,
Xú Zéchún (Xu Zechun) was appointed Shāndōng (Shandong) Provincial Governor.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Qíyīng (Qiying) was ordered to remain in the capital to manage the Board of Rites.
Xú Guǎngjìn (Xu Guangjin) was appointed Liǎngguǎng (Liangguang) Governor-General and Imperial Commissioner,
to manage trade.
Yè Míngchēn (Ye Mingchen) was appointed Guǎngdōng (Guangdong) Provincial Governor.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Qíyīng (Qiying) was transferred to manage the Board of War.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Emperor visited Hēilóngtán (Black Dragon Pool) to pray for rain.
On the day Wùchén,
Fù Shéngxūn (Fu Shengxun) was appointed Jiāngxī (Jiangxi) Provincial Governor.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Wú Wénróng (Wu Wenrong) was transferred to be Zhèjiāng (Zhejiang) Provincial Governor.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Gēngyín,
Lín Zéxú (Lin Zexu) was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent,
and awarded the peacock feather.
In the eighth month, on the day Dīngsì,
Èshùn'ān (Eshun'an), Hénán (Henan) Provincial Governor, was stripped of his position.
Pān Duó (Pan Duo) was appointed to replace him.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Russian merchant ships requested to trade in Shànghǎi (Shanghai),
but were refused.
In the ninth month, on the day Jiǎxū,
Pān Xī'ēn (Pan Xi'en) was dismissed.
Yáng Yǐzēng (Yang Yizeng) was appointed Jiāngnán (Jiangnan) Riverways Governor-General,
and Chén Shìméi (Chen Shimei) Shǎnxī (Shaanxi) Provincial Governor.
Chéngyù (Chengyu) was recalled to the capital.
Shèngxún (Shengxun) was appointed acting Suíyuǎrchéng (Suiyuan City) General.
Relief was provided for flood victims in three prefectures including Jiāngníng (Jiangning).
On the day Yǐyǒu,
relief was provided for flood victims in Húběi (Hubei).
On the day Guǐsì,
Qiáo Yòngqiān (Qiao Yongqian) was recalled to the capital.
Luó Ràodiǎn (Luo Raodian) was appointed acting Guìzhōu (Guizhou) Provincial Governor.
In this month,
rations and housing expenses were provided to flood victims in four counties including Wǔlíng (Wuling) in Húnán (Hunan).
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
Bǎoxìng (Baoxing), Grand Secretary of the Wénhuà (Wenhua) Hall, passed away.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Bāěrtèchùkè (Barchuk) city was repaired.
In this month,
relief was provided for flood victims in seven prefectures and counties including Tōngzhōu (Tongzhou) in Zhílì (Zhili) and sixteen prefectures and counties including Wúwéi (Wuwei) in Ānhuī (Anhui).
Rations were distributed to disaster victims in fourteen prefectures and counties including Hézhōu (Hezhou) in Ānhuī (Anhui),
Huáróng (Huarong) county, and Yuèzhōuwèi (Yuezhou Guard) in Húnán (Hunan).
Seeds were loaned to disaster victims in Ānxiāng (Anxiang) county and Lǐzhōu (Lizhou) in Húnán (Hunan).

New and old outstanding taxes for fifty-two prefectures and counties including Tōngzhōu (Tongzhou) in Zhílì (Zhili), thirty-nine prefectures, counties, and guards including Miǎnyáng (Mianyang) in Húběi (Hubei), nine prefectures and counties including Lǐzhōu (Lizhou) in Húnán (Hunan), and twenty-four prefectures and counties including Sīzhōu (Sizhou) in Ānhuī (Anhui), affected by disaster, were remitted or deferred.
In the eleventh month, on the day Yǐhài,
the son of the late King of Yuènán, Ruǎn Fú--- Fúshí, was enfeoffed as the King of Yuènán.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Qíyīng was appointed Grand Secretary
Qíshàn was made Associate Grand Secretary,
and remained in his post as Governor-General of Sìchuān.
Ruìyuán was summoned to the capital,
and Huìchéng was appointed Amban of Kēbùduō.
Censor Zhāng Hóngshēng requested the casting of large coins,
which was referred to the ministry for deliberation.
On the day Xīnsì,
Prince Dìng Jùnwáng Zǎiquán and Vice Minister Jì Zhīchāng were ordered to investigate salt affairs in Zhílì;
Grand Secretary Qíyīng and Vice Minister Zhū Fèngbiāo were ordered to investigate salt affairs in Shāndōng.
On the day Dīnghài,
Qíyīng was appointed Grand Secretary of Wényuān Pavilion.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Tuōmíng'ā was appointed General of Suīyuǎn City.
That month,
relief grain was provided to twenty counties in Jiāngxī, including Déhuà, affected by floods.
Military stipends were loaned to the Hunan Tíbìao and Changdé camp areas affected by disaster.

New and old fixed taxes were remitted and deferred in seventy-seven prefectures, departments, counties, and garrisons in Jiāngsū, including Tàizhōu; twenty salt fields in Liǎnghuái, including Lǚsì; twenty-two counties in Jiāngxī, including Déhuà; and six prefectures and counties in Zhílì, including Ānzhōu, all affected by floods.
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Emperor went to the Dàgāo Hall to pray for snow.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Emperor went to the Dàgāo Hall to pray for snow.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the Emperor went to the Temple of Heaven to pray for snow.
On the day Rénxū,
Vice Minister Chén Fú'ēn, for not accepting public funds during his previous tenure as Acting Governor of Shāndōng,
was awarded a first-rank button
and an imperial inscription plaque.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Wōshénà was appointed General of Jílín,
Chénggāng was appointed Minister of Rites,
and Bǎijùn was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Zhāng Xiánghé was appointed Governor of Shǎnxī.
That month,
disaster relief was provided to the victims in fourteen prefectures and counties in Zhílì, including Tōngzhōu.
That year,
Cháoxiān, Liúqiú, Xiāmluó, and Yuènán paid tribute.
In the spring of the twenty-ninth year, in the first month, on the day Guǐwèi,
Yìgé was appointed General of Wūlǐyǎsūtái.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Qíyīng and Jì Zhīchāng were ordered to inspect military camps and granaries in Zhèjiāng.
That month,
additional flood relief was provided to fourteen prefectures, departments, counties, and garrisons in Ānhuī, including Wúwéi.
Relief grain was provided to six prefectures and counties in Húnán, including Lǐzhōu, and thirteen prefectures and counties in Ānhuī, including Hézhōu, affected by floods.
Seeds were loaned to twelve counties in Jiāngxī, including Nánchāng, and six prefectures and counties in Húnán, including Lǐzhōu, affected by floods.
