In the second month, on the first day Gēngzǐ,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Liú Yùnkē was ordered to provide relief and comfort to those affected by floods and earthquakes in the northern route of Táiwān.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Lǐ Xīngyuán was instructed to manage relief efforts in Jiāngsū.
On the day Xīnhài,
Mùzhāng'ā, Pān Shì'ēn, and Chén Guānjùn were relieved from their posts as Chief Imperial Tutors in the Shàngshūfáng.
Qí Jùnzǎo and Dù Shòutián were appointed Chief Imperial Tutors in the Shàngshūfáng,
and Dù Shòutián continued to teach the Fourth Prince.
On the day Bǐngchén,
the Tibetan laborers of Zhōngzhānduì in Sìchuān, Bùlángjié, rebelled,
and Qíshàn was ordered to suppress them.
Yùchéng was concurrently appointed Acting Governor-General of Sìchuān.
That month,
military stipends for one season were loaned to the eight camps in Jiāngsū disaster areas, including Jīngzuǒ.
In the third month, on the day Gēngyín,
Xú Guǎngjìn and others memorialized, saying:
"The soldiers and people are mutually protecting each other.
Regarding the inner rivers and outer seas,
strict defenses have been ordered.
The matter of the English entering the provincial capital
is absolutely not permissible."
An edict was issued, approving of this.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the day Rényín,
Lǐ Xīngyuán was relieved due to illness,
Lù Jiànyíng was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
Fù Shéngxūn was transferred to be Governor of Jiāngsū,
and Fèi Kāishòu was appointed Governor of Jiāngxī.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Lù Jiànyíng and others memorialized that the southern grain transport need not be converted to cash,
and this was followed.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Xú Guǎngjìn memorialized that the English had ceased discussions about entering the city.
Xú Guǎngjìn was ennobled as Viscount and Yè Míngchēn as Baron,
both with first-class hereditary succession.
An edict praised the people of Yuè for their deep understanding of the greater good.
In the intercalary fourth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Yán Yǐyù was appointed Acting Governor-General of River Conservancy for Héshuǐ.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Zhào Bǐngyán was transferred to be Governor of Húnán,
and Luó Ràodiǎn was appointed Governor of Húběi.
On the day Xīnsì,
Qíshàn suppressed the Zhōngzhānduì Tibetans
and defeated them.
On the day Rényǐ,
Délíng was appointed Amban of Yè'ěrqiāng.
In the fifth month, on the day Yǐsì,
the customs office in Àomén, Guǎngdōng, was moved to Huángpǔ.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
wild barbarians in Téngyuè Department, Yúnnán, rebelled,
and Lín Zéxú suppressed them.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Wáng Zhàochēn, Governor of Shānxī, was dismissed from his post and arrested for accepting bribes;
Jì Zhīchāng was appointed Governor of Shānxī.
That month,
granary grain was loaned due to hail disaster in Téngxiàn, Shāndōng.
In the sixth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
bandits in Yángshān and Yīngdé counties of Guǎngdōng were suppressed.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Chénggāng, Minister of Rites, passed away.
On the day Gēngyín,
Yùshū was transferred to be Military Governor of Wūlǔmùqí,
and Wéiqín was appointed Military Governor of Rèhé.
In the autumn, in the seventh month, on the first day Bǐngshēn,
bandits, including Lín Shì, in Mǐnxiàn, Fújiàn, rebelled,
and were captured and executed.
On the day Wùxū,
Chén Guānjùn, Associate Grand Secretary and Minister of Personnel, passed away;
Jiǎ Zhēn was transferred to be Minister of Personnel.
Sūn Ruìzhēn was appointed Minister of Rites,
and Wáng Guǎngyìn was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
Féng Déxīn was appointed Governor of Húnán.
On the day Jǐhài,
Qí Jùnzǎo was appointed Associate Grand Secretary.
On the day Xīnhài,
Wàn Gòngzhēn, Financial Commissioner of Húnán, was ordered to provide relief to flood victims in Wǔlíng and other counties.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Wáng Zhàochēn was exiled to Xīnjiāng.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Lín Zéxú was relieved due to illness;
Chéng Yùcǎi was appointed Governor-General of Yún-Guì,
and Zhāng Rìzhěng was appointed Governor of Yúnnán.
Vice Minister Dài Xī was demoted to a third-rank button and retired.
That month,
relief grain was provided to five counties in Jiāngxī, including Déhuà, and nine prefectures, departments, counties, and garrisons in Húnán, including Lǐzhōu, affected by floods.
New and old fixed taxes were remitted and deferred in twenty-two departments and counties in Jiāngsū, including Chuānshā.
In the eighth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
Lù Jiànyíng memorialized on relief efforts and the situation after the floodwaters receded.
An edict stated:
"The well-being of the officials and people
is also Our well-being."
On the day Bǐngxū,
Jì Zhīchāng was summoned to the capital,
and Gōng Yù was appointed Acting Governor of Shānxī.
That month,

relief grain was provided to banner people of Jǐnzhōu in Fèngtiān, nine counties in Jiāngxī including Póyáng, and ten prefectures, departments, counties, and garrisons in Húnán including Lǐzhōu, affected by floods.
In the ninth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
Bùyàntài was relieved due to illness;
Qíshàn was appointed Acting Governor-General of Shǎn-Gān,
and Yùchéng was appointed Acting Governor-General of Sìchuān.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Yán Yǐyù was appointed Governor-General of River Conservancy for Héshuǐ.
On the day Wùshēn,
Jì Zhīchāng, Acting Vice Minister of Personnel, was ordered to serve concurrently in the Grand Council.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Qíshàn was appointed Governor-General of Shǎn-Gān.
Xú Zéchún was appointed Governor-General of Sìchuān,
and Chén Qìngxié was appointed Governor of Shāndōng.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
wild barbarians in Xiǎoyǔjiāng and other places outside Baoshān Prefecture, Yúnnán, rebelled,
and Chéng Yùcǎi suppressed them.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Hé Rǔlín, Minister whose mourning period was over, was ordered to continue serving in the Grand Council.
That month,
relief grain was provided to Tóngzǐ County, Guìzhōu, affected by floods,
and fixed taxes were remitted and deferred.
In the winter, in the tenth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
the son of the late King of Cháoxiān, Lǐ---, inherited the title,
and Ruìcháng and Hésèběn were ordered to go and confer the title.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Grand Secretary Pān Shì'ēn requested to be relieved of his duties,
and was ordered to be exempted from the Grand Council.
On the day Gēngyín,
Gēngfú was appointed Acting Military Governor of Rèhé.
That month,
relief grain was provided to seven prefectures and counties in Húnán, including Lǐzhōu, and Xúgōu County in Shānxī, affected by disaster.

New and old fixed taxes were remitted and deferred in thirty-seven prefectures and counties in Zhílì, including Jìzhōu; twenty-one counties in Zhèjiāng, including Fùyáng; and three departments and counties in Shānxī, including Sàlāqí, affected by disaster.
In the eleventh month, on the first day Jiǎwǔ,
bandits, including Lǐ Yuánfā, in Xīnníng County, Húnán, rebelled,
and Féng Déxīn was ordered to suppress them.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Rùan Yuán, Grand Tutor and former Grand Secretary, passed away.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Gōng Yù was transferred to be Governor of Húběi,
and Zhàonàsūtú was appointed Governor of Shānxī.
On the day Yǐsì,
the princes' residence caught fire.
On the day Gēngxū,
bandits, including Wú Shǔn, in Jiāyì County, Táiwān, rebelled,
and were captured and executed.
That month,
flood relief was provided to fourteen counties in Jiāngxī, including Déhuà.
Relief grain was provided to banner people in six cities, including Qíqíhā'ěr, and salt workers in eight salt fields in Zhèjiāng, including Rénhé.

New and old fixed taxes were remitted and deferred in seventy-three prefectures, departments, counties, and garrisons in Jiāngsū, including Tàizhōu, and twenty-one counties in Jiāngxī, including Déhuà, affected by disaster,
and salt taxes in fourteen salt fields in Zhèjiāng, including Hǎishā.
In the twelfth month, on the day of Gēngwǔ,
rebels led by Huáng Sān in Dàozhōu, Húnán province, caused disturbances.
Yùtài was ordered to suppress them.
Zālāfēntài was appointed Assistant Military Governor of Tǎ'ěrbāhātái.
On the day of Xīnwèi,
the Empress Dowager fell ill.
The Emperor visited Cínínggōng to inquire after her health,
and thereafter did so daily.
On the day of Jiǎxū,
the Empress Dowager passed away.
On the day of Yǐhài,
the coffin of the late Empress Dowager was placed for repose in Cínínggōng.
The Emperor resided in a mourning hut,
sleeping on the ground on a mat of straw.
All the princes and high officials requested him to return to the palace,
but he refused.
On the day of Jiǎshēn,
the Empress Dowager's coffin was moved to Yínghuīdiàn in Qǐchūnyuán.
From then on, the Emperor resided in the mourning hut at Shèndétáng.
On the day of Yǐyǒu,
Lǐ Zhènhù retired due to illness,
and Chén Fū'ēn was appointed Minister of Punishments.
On the day of Dīnghài,
rebels from Xīnníng, Húnán province, scattered into Guǎngxī province.
Zhèng Zǔchēn dispatched troops to defend against and suppress them.
In this year,
Cháoxiān, Liúqiú, and Yuènán paid tribute.
In the thirtieth year, in the first month, on the first day of Jiǎwǔ,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day of Bǐngshēn,
Qí Jùnzǎo and others reported that Bùyántài, the Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù, had been negligent in his inspection of border defenses.
The matter was referred to the relevant board for severe deliberation.
On the day of Dīngyǒu,
when the princes and high officials again requested to stop the personal escort of the late Empress Dowager's coffin,
an imperial edict allowed it.
On the day of Wùxū,
the late Empress Dowager was posthumously honored with the title Xiàohégōngcí Kāngyù'ānchéng Xīshèng Ruìhuánghòu.
On the day of Gēngzǐ,
the Emperor proceeded to Yínghuīdiàn, before the coffin of Empress Xiàohé Ruì, to perform a grand sacrifice.
On the day of Jiǎchén,
the Emperor proceeded before the coffin to perform the monthly sacrifice.
On the day of Yǐsì,
Empress Xiàohé Ruì's mausoleum was designated Chāngxīlíng.
On the day of Bǐngwǔ,
the Emperor fell ill.
On the day of Dīngwèi,
the Emperor's illness worsened critically.
Zàiquán, the head of the Imperial Clan Court;
Zàiyuán, Duānhuá, and Sēnggélínqìn, the Grand Ministers of the Imperial Guard;
Mùzhāng'ā, Sàishàng'ā, Hé Rúlín, Chén Fū'ēn, and Jì Zhīchāng, the Grand Councilors;
and Wénqìng, the Grand Minister of the Imperial Household Department, were summoned to jointly open the sealed casket
and declare the imperial handwritten decree:
"The fourth imperial son is established as the Crown Prince."
On this day,
the Emperor passed away in the mourning hut at Shèndétáng in Yuánmíngyuán.
An imperial rescript declared:
"The sixth imperial son, Yìxīn, is enfeoffed as a qīnwáng."
In the fourth month, on the day of Jiǎxū,
the Emperor was posthumously honored with the title Xiàotiānfúyùn Lìzhōngtǐzhèng Zhìwénshèngwǔ Zhìyǒngréncí Jiǎnqín Xiàomǐnchéng Huángdì,
and his temple name was Xuānzōng.
In the second month of the second year of Xiánfēng, on the day of Rénzǐ,
he was interred in Mùlíng.
A commentary states: Xuānzōng's virtue of respect and frugality,
and his magnanimity and benevolence,
were excellent qualities for maintaining the established order.
Yet, distant peoples engaging in trade
provoked conflicts and warfare.
Their threat, compared to the barbarian troubles of earlier dynasties,
was not comparable.
The ministers in charge initially acted with haste and severity,
then with fear and hesitation,
thus leaving the Emperor with worries day and night.
This is what is called having an emperor but no ministers,
being able to comply and follow but unable to advise and rescue.
The nation's impending crisis
began here.
Alas,
how regrettable!
Annals 20: Annals of Wénzōng
Wénzōng Xiétiānyìyùn Zhízhōngchuímóu Màodézhènwǔ Shèngxiàoyuāngōng Duānrénkuānmǐn Xiǎnhuángdì,
whose personal name was Yìzhǔ,
was Xuānzōng's fourth son.
His mother was Empress Xiàoquánchéng Níuhùlùshì,
and he was born on the ninth day of the sixth month of the eleventh year of Dàoguāng.
In the twenty-sixth year,
following the ancestral law for establishing an heir,
his name was written down and sealed away.
In the first month, on the day of Dīngwèi, of the thirtieth year,
Xuānzōng fell ill,
summoned his ministers, and showed them his vermillion decree,
establishing him as Crown Prince.
Upon Xuānzōng's demise,
on the day of Jǐwèi,
the Emperor ascended the throne,
issued a proclamation bestowing widespread grace,
and designated the following year as the first year of Xiánfēng.
He honored the Imperial Noble Consort as Empress Xiàocí.
His elder brothers, Bèilè Yìwěi, Yìgāng, and Yìyì, were posthumously granted the title of Jùnwáng.
His younger brothers, Yìxīn, was enfeoffed as Gōngqīnwáng;
Yìxuǎn as Chúnjùnwáng;
Yìhé as Zhōngjùnwáng;
and Yìhuì as Fújùnwáng.
One hundred days of white mourning and twenty-seven months of plain clothes were decreed.
In the second month, on the day of Wùchén,
Bóyùn, the Left Censor-in-Chief, and Jīpǔ, the Minister of the Imperial Household Department, were ordered to construct Chāngxīlíng
as the mausoleum for Empress Xiàohé.
Initially, Xuānzōng's last will
stipulated that there was no need for the Empress to be elevated to the imperial ancestral temple or share in the imperial ancestral worship.
This was submitted to the court officials for deliberation.
They deliberated and submitted their opinion.
An edict stated:
"The late Emperor's humility
is something we dare not follow.
To appropriately respect his sentiments,
a limit should be set.
Let the practice be discontinued after the Three Ancestors and Five Sovereigns,
and it shall not be performed again thereafter."
The Húnán bandit Lǐ Yuánfā caused disturbances.
An edict stated:
"Huìqīnwáng is Our uncle,
and is exempted from the kowtow ceremony,
to show respect for elders and close relatives."
On the day of Gēngchén,
an imperial decree ordered the coastal areas to reorganize the navy
and conduct diligent patrols and investigations.
On the day of Rénchén,
Wōrén, the Grand Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, responded to the imperial summons and offered advice.
The Emperor praised his frank remonstrance.
In the third month, on the first day of Guǐsì,
Bǎochāng passed away.
Bóyùn was appointed Minister of War,
and Huāshānà was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
On the day of Rényín,
Luó Dūnyǎn, the Commissioner of the Office of Transmission, responded to the imperial summons and offered advice.
The Emperor responded with a gracious edict.
On the day of Guǐmǎo,
Wénruì, the Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, submitted a memorial outlining four matters,
and also included a copy of the former Grand Secretary Sūn Jiāgàn's memorial from the first year of Qiánlóng on "Three Habits and One Vice."
Zēng Guófān, the Vice Minister of Rites, submitted a memorial outlining three matters regarding the appointment of officials.
All were graciously accepted.
On the day of Xīnhài,
the Báimáo River in Jiāngsū was dredged,
and the stone sluice gate at the river mouth was relocated to Lǎozhágqiáo.
On the day of Rénxū,
Qùánlíng, the Prince Lǐ, passed away.
His son Shìduó inherited the title.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the day of Yǐchǒu,
Russia requested to open trade at Tǎ'ěrbāhātái,
which was granted.
On the day of Jǐsì,
Chē Kèshèn, a Grand Academician of the Grand Secretariat, submitted a memorial outlining ten articles on revering Heaven, continuing imperial aspirations, appointing officials, and governing.
The Emperor responded with a gracious edict.
On the day of Guǐyǒu,
the Board of Revenue submitted a memorial outlining financial reforms,
listing various malpractices.
An imperial decree ordered: "Implement vigorous reforms."
On the day of Gēngchén,
British ships arrived at the Hǎikǒu of Jiāngsū to deliver official documents,
but were rejected.
On the day of Yǐyǒu,
the ships reached Tiānjīn.
In the fifth month, on the day of Bǐngshēn,
they weighed anchor and sailed south.
On the day of Dīngyǒu,
an imperial edict stated:
"Officials responsible for the common people in zhōu and xiàn bear extremely heavy responsibilities.
In recent years, advancements have been arbitrary and undeserved,
and the ranks of officials are diverse and disorderly,
many relying on yamen runners and squeezing the common people.
On whom can the people's livelihood depend?
The Governors-General and Governors, the high officials, should pay close attention to examination,
recommending those who are honest and fair,
and eradicating the greedy and corrupt,
so that the people's hardships may gradually be relieved,
to fulfill Our expectations."
Lǐ Yuánfā, the rebel leader from Húnán, was captured
and sent to the capital to be executed.
Zhèng Zǔchēn was instructed by edict:
"Society bandits are rising everywhere in Guǎngxī;
they should be suppressed immediately.
Do not conceal or embellish reports."
On the day of Xīnhài,
the Déngzhōuzhèn in Shāndōng was changed to a Water Army Commander-in-Chief,
also overseeing land forces.
On the day of Guǐchǒu,
an edict ordered the survey and planning of civilian weirs along the Southeast and Two Rivers.
On the day of Jiǎyín,
Gùqìng was appointed General of Jílín.
On the Guǐhài day of the sixth month,
the Yǒngdìng Hé overflowed.
Grand Secretary Pān Shì'ēn retired,
receiving his full stipend.
Qí Jùnzǎo was appointed Grand Secretary,
Dù Shòutián was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary,
Sūn Ruìzhēn was appointed Minister of the Board of Revenue,
Wáng Guǎngyìn was appointed Minister of the Board of War,
and Jì Zhīchāng was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the Jiǎxū day,
the land tax on fractional plots (jīlíngdìyín) for commoners and aboriginals in Gānsù was abolished.
On the Jiǎshēn day,
an imperial edict commanded governors-general and governors to impeach and evaluate their subordinates
by listing facts in detail,
not by empty words.
This month,
Hóng Xiùquán, a native of Huā Xiàn, Guǎngdōng, launched an uprising in Jīntián, Guìpíng Xiàn, Guǎngxī.
In the autumn, on the Xīnmǎo day of the seventh month,
an imperial edict commanded coastal governors-general and governors to prepare defenses for maritime ports.
On the Bǐngchén day,
Minister Wénqìng was dismissed for inviting the sorcerer Xuē Zhízhōng to treat an illness.
He was dismissed.
On the Dīngmǎo day of the eighth month,
Hóng Xiùquán fled to Xiūrén and Lìpǔ.
Zhèng Zǔchēn was commanded to suppress him.
Xiàng Róng was transferred to be Admiral of Guǎngxī to suppress the rebels.
On the Jiǎshēn day,
an imperial edict stated:
"In various provinces, cases of people gathering to cause trouble,
especially grave cases, are occurring repeatedly.
What are the local officials responsible for?
Take, for instance, the Niǎn bandits in Hénán who have formed gangs,
even disturbing neighboring provinces,
and engaging in rampant robbery.
They should be jointly captured and suppressed,
and their roots completely eradicated.
If high-ranking provincial officials are negligent at first,
and then conceal the facts afterwards,
leading to the brewing of major disasters,
We will severely punish those governors-general and governors.
Beware!"
On the Bǐngshēn day of the ninth month,
due to the spread of the rebel forces in Guǎngxī,
two thousand troops each from Húnán, Yúnnán, and Guìzhōu were dispatched for suppression,
and gentry and commoners were encouraged to organize local militias (tuánliàn).
On the Xīnchǒu day,
Lín Zéxú was appointed Imperial Commissioner
to suppress the rebels in Guǎngxī.
On the Jiǎchén day,
due to marauding bandits causing trouble in Guǎngdōng,
Xú Guǎngjìn was ordered to suppress them.
On the Bǐngwǔ day,
the grand procession for the coffin of the late emperor departed.
On the Xīnhài day,
Emperor Xuānzōng Chéng was temporarily interred in the Lóng'ēn Diàn.
In winter, on the Rénwǔ day of the tenth month,
due to covering up and causing trouble,
Zhèng Zǔchēn was dismissed from his post.
Lín Zéxú was appointed acting Governor of Guǎngxī.
On the Jiǎzǐ day,
the breach in the Yǒngdìng Hé was closed.
On the Bǐngxū day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Grand Secretary Mùzhāng'ā, being cunning and servile, usurped his position,
ousted those who differed from him,
obstructed military affairs,
and disregarded national interests.
He is hereby stripped of his office.
Assistant Grand Secretary Qíyīng, being shameless and incompetent,
is demoted to Yuanwailang.
This is promulgated to all within and without the empire."
Sàishàng'ā was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary.
On the Wùxū day of the eleventh month,
Yìshān was appointed General of Yīlí.
On the Gēngzǐ day,
Imperial Commissioner Lín Zéxú died en route.
Zhōu Tiānjúe was appointed acting Governor of Guǎngxī.
The former Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng, Lǐ Xīngyuán, was appointed Imperial Commissioner
to proceed to Guǎngxī to suppress the rebels.
On the Yǐsì day,
an imperial edict ordered that miscellaneous funds accumulated in provincial treasuries
be allocated for military expenses,
and charitable donations (kāijuān) be temporarily suspended.
Liú Yùnkē was dismissed.
Yùtài was appointed Governor-General of Mǐnzhè,
Chéng Yǔcǎi was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng,
and Wú Wénróng was appointed Governor-General of Yúnguì.
The Guǎngxī bandit leader Zhōng Yàchūn was captured
and executed.
On the Jǐsì day of the twelfth month,
the ceremony for posthumous titles and canonization of Empress Xiàodé was completed.
The empress's father, Fùtài, was posthumously enfeoffed as a third-rank duke.
Yìshān was commanded to consult and determine trade regulations with Russia and report them.
On the Gēngwǔ day,
an imperial edict ordered that the grain tribute from the four prefectures of Jiāngsū be temporarily transported by sea.
On the Jiǎxū day,
Xiàng Róng suppressed the rebels in Héngzhōu,
defeating them.
On the Jǐmǎo day,
hereditary ranks were granted to Sub-General Yīkètānbù and others who died in battle in Guǎngxī.
On the Bǐngxū day,
a collective sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
This year,
land taxes in sixty-seven prefectures and counties in Zhílì, Zhèjiāng, Húnán, and other provinces were exempted to varying degrees due to disaster.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú offered tribute.
In the spring of the first year of Xiánfēng, on the Wùzǐ day, the first day of the first month,
the Emperor held court in the Tàihé Diàn to receive congratulations.
An imperial edict ordered all direct provinces to investigate outstanding principal and surtax grain arrears owed by the people prior to the thirtieth year of Dàoguāng
and submit a list for imperial instruction.
Sàishàng'ā was appointed Grand Secretary.
On the Rényín day,
the Emperor visited the Mùlíng
and performed the grand annual sacrificial rites.
On the Gēngxū day,
he returned to the capital.
On the Xīnhài day,
an imperial edict commanded officials of the Hànlín Academy and the Imperial Clan Court to separately compile commentaries and present them.
Supervising Censor Sū Tíngkuí submitted a memorial requesting sincerity in appointing the virtuous
and careful planning from beginning to end.
The Emperor praised and accepted it.
On the Yǐchǒu day of the second month,
an imperial edict exempted the people of direct provinces from grain arrears that had already been reported for cancellation,
as well as the people of Jiāngsū from grain tribute arrears,
all of which were to be remitted.
Dù Shòutián submitted a memorial detailing four matters: rectifying military discipline, recruiting elite brave soldiers, encouraging local militias, and surveying terrain.
These were sent to the ministers at the front.
On the Gēngwǔ day,
Lǐ Xīngyuán reported a victory in suppressing rebels in Jīntián.
On the Jǐmǎo day,
an imperial edict stated:
"This year, the season has passed the spring equinox,
yet the cold has not abated.
We reflect internally,
having failed to move Heaven's harmony.
We recall that last winter, the Board of Rites compiled a memorial concerning chaste women,
and the Grand Secretariat drafted a double slip,
consequently issuing a slip stating that 'no commendation is necessary.'
These chaste women sacrificed their lives for righteousness,
sufficient to inspire a declining morality and uphold the cardinal virtues.
Therefore, all thirty-seven chaste women, including Madam Péng,
are permitted to be universally commended,
to comfort their chaste souls."
Deputy Commander-in-Chief Wūlántài of Guǎngzhōu was ordered to take the military equipment he had manufactured to Guǎngxī to suppress the rebels.
On the Bǐngshēn day of the third month,
Grand Secretary Sàishàng'ā was ordered to carry the Imperial Commissioner's seal,
and rush to Húnán to manage defenses.
Commander Bāqīngdé and Deputy Commander Dáhóng'ā accompanied him.
On the Gēngzǐ day,
the Emperor reviewed archery at the Zǐguāng Gé.
On the Xīnchǒu day,
he practiced archery on foot at the Gǒngchén Diàn
and reviewed the archery of ministers and imperial bodyguards.
On the Jǐyǒu day,
Hénán Governor Pān Duó reported the capture of over two hundred Niǎn bandits, including Yáo Jīngnián.
On the Gēngxū day,
troops from Guǎngdōng, Húnán, and Sìchuān were transferred to Guǎngxī to assist in the suppression.
On the Rényǐ day,
one million taels of silver from the imperial treasury were allocated for military provisions in Guǎngxī,
and grain from Sìchuān granaries was milled and transported to Húnán.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day *wùwǔ*,
Sài Shàng'ā was ordered to proceed to Guǎngxī to take over military affairs.
On the day *jǐwèi*,
Shūxīng'ā, Assistant Minister of the Board of Revenue, was appointed Grand Councillor.
On the day *gēngshēn*,
the Emperor attended to government affairs at the Qiánqīng Gate.
Hereditary ranks were granted in commiseration for Qíqīng'ā, a Brigadier-General, and others who died in an ambush in Guǎngxī.
An imperial edict severely reprimanded Lǐ Xīngyuán and others
for having no viable plans,
and falling into the rebels' trap.
Zhèng Zǔchēn was banished to Yīlí
for nourishing a carbuncle that caused harm.
On the day *bǐngyín*,
Zhōu Tiānjúe reported that Hóng Xiùquán's followers were scattered,
and due to the treacherous mountains and familiar paths,
they would clash when opportunities arose.
Even if defeated, they could not be utterly crushed.
At this time, the military strength was insufficient,
so he advised focusing on defense.
Only when there were surplus troops
could a continuous encampment be established to press for extermination.
The imperial decree stated:
"You must guard strictly,
and not allow them to escape."
When Sài Shàng'ā's army set off,
he was granted the Èbìlóng sword.
Cháng Ruì, Commander-in-Chief of the Tiānjīn Garrison, and Cháng Shòu, Commander-in-Chief of the Liángzhōu Garrison, were ordered to join the expedition.
On the day *gēngwǔ*,
the outstanding land tax from the thirtieth year of Dàoguāng in Zhílì was remitted.
Zhōu Tiānjúe impeached Huìqìng, Commander-in-Chief of the Yòujiāng Garrison, and Qìngjí, Yòujiāng Circuit Intendant, for ineffective suppression of rebels,
and both were stripped of their posts.
On the day *bǐngzǐ*,
Lǐ Xīngyuán reported the extermination of the secret society bandits at Shànglín Xū.
On the day *guǐwèi*,
Lǐ Xīngyuán died.
Wūlántài reported that
on the third day of the fourth month,
he arrived at the Wǔxuān military camp.
Upon investigating the rebel situation,
it appeared they were largely an unorganized rabble.
However, the secret society bandits in Wǔxuān Dōngxiāng numbered over ten thousand,
with long hair and changed clothing,
and had titles of "pseudo-kings" and "pseudo-officials,"
posing a real threat to the heartland of Guǎngxī.
The imperial decree stated:
"The rebel situation is cunning and treacherous;
you must act with prudence."
In the fifth month, on the day *wùzǐ*,
Zhōu Tiānjúe reported
that the escaped rebels from Wǔxuān Dōngxiāng had fled into Xiàngzhōu.
An imperial edict severely reprimanded them,
and each was lightly censured.
Yú Wànqīng, Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Húnán, was ordered by imperial edict to assist in blocking and suppressing them.
On the day *gēngyín*,
Zhuó Bǐngtián submitted a memorial requesting the implementation of the "strengthen fortifications and clear the fields" strategy,
which was conveyed to Sài Shàng'ā and the Governors-General and Governors.
On the day *jiǎwǔ*,
Zhōu Tiānjúe reported the pacification of the Sǐchéng bandits,
with Chén Yà and others surrendering,
and pursuing the rebels into Hépǔ.
On the day *dīngyǒu*,
Wūlántài reported that
on the seventeenth day of the fourth month,
he rushed to Xiàngzhōu
to intercept the escaped rebels.
On the day *jiǎchén*,
Qíshàn, Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù, was stripped of his post and arrested for questioning
for arbitrarily and recklessly killing
while suppressing aboriginal tribes.
On the day *yǐsì*,
Jì Zhīchāng was appointed Governor-General of Fújiàn and Zhèjiāng,
and Yùchéng, Minister of the Board of Revenue, was appointed Associate Grand Secretary.
On the day *jǐyǒu*,
an imperial edict halted all construction projects throughout the empire.
Péng Yùnzhāng, Assistant Minister of the Board of Works, was appointed Grand Councillor.
On the day *yǐmǎo*,
the Emperor went to the Dàgāo Hall to pray for rain.
In the sixth month, on the day *dīngsì*,
Sài Shàng'ā reported his arrival in Chángshā.
The imperial edict stated:
"The rebels in Xiàngzhōu
should be heavily surrounded.
The rebels who have scattered to Nánníng and Tàipíng
should be pursued and suppressed by detached forces.
You should carefully assess the terrain and available personnel,
and coordinate your arrangements.
Logistics stations are especially crucial;
they should also be separately established
to facilitate transport."
On the day *bǐngyín*,
Wūlántài reported that
on the tenth day of the fifth month,
rebels captured a Guìzhōu military camp,
but it was recaptured on the same day.
The rebels gathered at Nánshān
were also engaged and driven south.
Fifteen officers and
over two hundred soldiers died in battle;
a list was attached requesting compensation.
Tóng Pānméi, a Guìzhōu Battalion Commander, and others who first retreated were stripped of their ranks.
On the day *xīnwèi*,
one hundred and fifty thousand *liǎng* of customs duty silver from Jiānghǎi
were allocated for soldiers and couriers passing through Húběi.
On the day *yǐhài*,
Sài Shàng'ā reported that
on the fourth day of the sixth month,
he rushed to Guìlín
to formulate an overall plan.
The Emperor praised him for his appropriate actions.
On the day *dīngchǒu*,
the Niǎn bandits in Nányáng, Hénán, were causing widespread disturbances;
the imperial edict ordered the relevant authorities to capture them.
On the day *xīnsì*,
aboriginal bandits in Xīníng engaged in looting;
Sàyíng'ā was ordered to dispatch generals to suppress and capture them.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day *bǐngxū*,
Sài Shàng'ā reported that
rebels had retreated from Xiàngzhōu back to Dōngxiāng,
and troops were dispatched to block and suppress them.
On the day *gēngyín*,
Cáo Yǒuyíng, a Censor, memorialized that official administration was stagnant,
and urged a comprehensive review of names and realities.
The imperial decree stated:
"If officials were competent,
how could villains secretly gather
and cause such great trouble?
Henceforth, if similar situations arise,
the Governors-General and Governors alone will be held accountable."
On the day *gēngzǐ*,
Sài Shàng'ā reported that
he advanced to suppress the rebel lair at Xīnxū,
achieving victory in all seven battles.
Wūlántài and Qín Dìngsān were reinstated with their peacock feathers.
The Governors-General and Governors of Húguǎng and Sìchuān were ordered to strictly investigate secret society bandits and sectarian bandits.
On the day *dīngwèi*,
an imperial order set the annual repair project for the Southern River
at a rate of three million.
On the day *jǐyǒu*,
Sài Shàng'ā reported:
"Upon investigating the merits and demerits of the military commanders,
Wūlántài's initial victory followed by defeat
was due to a vigorous pursuit falling into an ambush.
The rebels blocked the river and set an ambush,
resulting in over a hundred deaths among the rear army from the swift current.
When Xiàng Róng first arrived in Guì,
he achieved successive victories,
and after each victory, soldiers were rewarded one *liǎng* of silver each.
When Lǐ Xīngyuán arrived,
this was reduced to three *qián*.
The soldiers were enraged,
swearing not to fight.
These have now been separately removed and eliminated;
it is crucial to act with prudence."
Jiǎng Wénqìng, Governor of Ānhuī, reported that
Chéng Liùmá, a bandit from Shòuzhōu, and Gāo Sìbā, a Niǎn bandit from Héféi, were causing unrest.
On the day *gēngxū*,
Bāo Qǐbào was transferred to be Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Húnán,
Róng Yùcái to be Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Yúnnán,
and Zhòng Lún to be Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Guìzhōu.
In the eighth month, on the day *yǐmǎo*,
Sài Shàng'ā reported that
he advanced to suppress the rebel stronghold at Xīnxū,
capturing Zhūjí Xiá and Shuāngjì Shān.
He received an imperial commendation.
On the day *yǐchǒu*,
Chén Qìngxié, Governor of Shāndōng, reported that
the Dēngzhōu naval ships were captured by rebels,
and a Brigadier-General fell into the water.
The imperial decree stated:
"Proceed quickly to pursue and suppress them."
Yìxīng and Nè'ěrjīng'é were also ordered to strictly guard the seaports.
Huìfēng, Minister of the Board of Rites, died.
On the *jiǎshēn* day of the intercalary eighth month,
Hóng Xiùquán (洪秀全), the leader of the Xīnxū (新墟) multitude, captured Yǒng'ān Zhōu (永安州).
He occupied it
and usurped the title Tàipíng Tiānguó (太平天國).
Lù Jiànyíng (陸建瀛) memorialized, requesting a prohibition on Catholicism.
An imperial decree was issued:
"In foreign relations,
one must be cautious from the outset.
Those [rights] stipulated in the original treaty
should still be observed according to old regulations."
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Chéng Yùcǎi (程矞采) memorialized that
bandits from Yángshān (陽山) had fled and attacked Yízhāng (宜章) and Rǔyuán (乳源).
Orders were given to General Sūn Yìngzhào (孫應照) to suppress them.
Féng Yuánjí (馮元吉), a patrol inspector who died for the country in Guǎngxī (廣西), was granted a hereditary position
and a memorial shrine was built for him;
his son, Shùpǔ (澍溥), was included in the sacrifices.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Héběi (河北) section of Nánhé (南河) burst at Sānbǎo (三堡).
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
regulations for the examination of *jūnjī zhāngjīng* (軍機章京) were established.
On the *rényín* day,
Sài Shàng'ā (賽尚阿) memorialized that the Xīnxū (新墟) rebels had crossed the mountains
and captured Yǒng'ān Zhōu (永安州).
An edict severely reprimanded him
and referred the matter to the board for deliberation and punishment.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
orders were given to Dǒng Guāngjiǎ (董光甲), General of Héběi (河北) Garrison, and Shào Hèlǐng (邵鶴齡), General of Yún Yáng (鄖陽) Garrison, to hasten to Guǎngxī (廣西) to suppress the rebels.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Cháng Dàchún (常大淳) memorialized that pirate ships were openly plundering at Shípǔ (石浦),
and Prefect Luó Yōng (羅鏞) repelled them.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Shū Xīng'ā (舒興阿) was appointed Governor-General of Shǎnxī-Gānsù (陝甘總督).
In the ninth month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
Sài Shàng'ā (賽尚阿) memorialized that Bā Qīngdé (巴清德) and Xiàng Róng (向榮) feigned illness to shirk responsibility,
delaying the advance of troops.
An imperial decree was issued,
stripping both of their posts for them to prove themselves.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
an edict was issued to deliberate on regulations for the combined river and sea transport of tribute grain.
In the winter tenth month, on the *wùxū* day,
special shrines were ordered to be built for Gě Yúnfēi (葛雲飛) and Zhèng Guóhóng (鄭國鴻), the generals who died in battle at Dìnghǎi (定海).
In the eleventh month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
Yè Míngchén (葉名琛) memorialized
that the Yīngdé (英德) bandits had been completely suppressed.
He was granted the additional title of *tàizǐ shàobǎo* (太子少保).
In the twelfth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
Sài Shàng'ā (賽尚阿) memorialized that
Xiàng Róng (向榮) had stationed his troops at Lóngyǎntáng (龍眼塘).
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Lù Jiànyíng (陸建瀛) memorialized that
the pirate Bù Xīngyǒu (布興有) had surrendered his weapons and pledged allegiance,
and arrangements were made for his resettlement in the barracks.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the general ancestral sacrifices were offered at the Tàimiào (太廟).
This year,
all civil arrears of money and grain from before the *Dàoguāng* (道光) thirtieth year were universally remitted.
Furthermore, civil arrears of banner rent in sixty-one departments and counties of Zhílì (直隸),
and silver and grain collected in fifty-one departments and counties of Zhèjiāng (浙江) were remitted.
Additionally, disaster taxes in fifteen circuits, departments, and counties of Fèngtiān (奉天),
four cities of Jílín (吉林),
one city of Hēilóngjiāng (黑龍江),
and seven circuits, departments, and counties of Húnán (湖南) were remitted.
Arrears of salt duties in salt fields of Zhèjiāng (浙江) and Fújiàn (福建) were also remitted.
Furthermore, the regular taxes for eighty-six departments and counties in Guǎngxī (廣西) affected by rebels were remitted.
Cháoxiǎn (朝鮮) and Liúqiú (琉球) sent tribute.
In the second year, the *rénzǐ* year, in spring, the first month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
Yìkuāng (奕劻) was enfeoffed as a *Bèizi* (貝子)
to carry on the sacrificial offerings of Qìng Qīnwáng Yǒnglín (慶親王永璘).
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Yùchéng (裕誠) was appointed Grand Secretary (*Dàxuéshì*),
Nè'ěr Jīng'é (訥爾經額) Assistant Grand Secretary (*Xié bàn Dàxuéshì*),
and Xǐ'ēn (禧恩) Minister of the Board of Revenue (*Hùbù Shàngshū*).
On the *rénxū* day,
Sài Shàng'ā (賽尚阿) memorialized that
he had encamped three *lǐ* from Yǒng'ān Zhōu (永安州) city to oversee the battle.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
attendant-minister Quánqìng (全慶) and deputy commander Lóngqìng (隆慶) were ordered to enthrone the King of Cháoxiǎn's (朝鮮) consort.
In the second month, on the *dīnghài* day,
Chén Qìngjiē (陳慶偕) was dismissed due to illness,
and Lǐ Huì (李僡) was appointed Governor of Shāndōng (山東).
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Emperor visited the Xīlíng (西陵).
In the third month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
Emperor Xuānzōng Chénghuángdì (宣宗成皇帝) was grandly interred in Mùlíng (慕陵).
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital,
reverently escorting the spirit tablets of Emperor Xuānzōng Chénghuángdì (宣宗成皇帝)
and the three Empresses Xiàomù (孝穆), Xiàoshèn (孝慎), and Xiàoquán (孝全) to be enshrined in the Tàimiào (太廟),
and an imperial edict granting widespread grace was issued.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Zōu Mínghè (鄒鳴鶴) memorialized that all the rebels entrenched in Yǒng'ān (永安) had fled eastward,
and Wūlántài (烏蘭泰) was unsuccessful in pursuing the rebels.
Generals Cháng Ruì (長瑞), Cháng Shòu (長壽), Dǒng Guāngjiǎ (董光甲), and Shào Hèlǐng (邵鶴齡) all died.
An imperial decree was issued,
referring Sài Shàng'ā (賽尚阿) and others to the board for deliberation and punishment,
and ordering Chéng Yùcǎi (程矞采) to dispatch troops to guard Húnán (湖南).
The four generals, Cháng Ruì (長瑞) and the others, were posthumously granted hereditary positions
and shrines were built for them.
Wūlántài (烏蘭ài), Deputy Commander of Guǎngzhōu (廣州), died in the army,
was posthumously granted the title of Commander,
and awarded compassionate relief according to the precedent for those killed in battle.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the deputy general Ā'ěrjīng'ā (阿爾精阿) and others who died in service in Guǎngxī (廣西) were posthumously granted hereditary positions.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Shèng Bǎo (勝保), Grand Academician of the Grand Secretariat (*Nèigé Xuéshì*), memorialized:
"The pleasure grounds [have been]
completely renovated and shine anew.
The common people secretly murmur,
which detracts from the Emperor's virtue."
The Emperor treated him with indulgence.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
the regular rain sacrifice was performed,
sacrificing to Heaven at the Yuánqiū (圜丘),
with Emperor Xuānzōng Chénghuángdì (宣宗成皇帝) respectfully honored as co-sacrificed.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Prefect Wáng Qìngyún (王慶雲) memorialized on the salt administration of Hédōng (河東),
proposing to permanently prohibit solicited merchants,
which could raise a large sum of money.
The matter was referred to the board for deliberation and implementation.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Emperor visited Mùlíng (慕陵)
and performed the ceremony of doffing mourning attire.
Xú Guǎngjìn (徐廣縉) was appointed Imperial Commissioner (*Qīnchāi Dàchén*)
to take over military affairs in Guǎngxī (廣西).
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Chéng Yùcǎi (程矞采) memorialized that bandits in Chénzhōu (郴州) led by Liú Dàiwěi (劉代偉) had rebelled,
and Participating General Jīlāmíng (積拉明) captured and executed him.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Cháng Dàchún (常大淳) memorialized that
salt smugglers resisted arrest,
killing Deputy General Zhāng Huì (張蕙) and County Magistrate Déchéng (德成).
General Shànlù (善祿) and Prefect Bì Chéngzhāo (畢承昭) dispatched troops to attack them,
beheading and capturing over a hundred,
while the remaining bandits scattered.
Zhāng Huì (張蕙) and Déchéng (德成) were granted hereditary positions.
Xú Jìyú (徐繼畬), Junior Supervisor of the Court of the Imperial Stud (*Tàipúsì Shà qīng*), memorialized after the doffing of mourning attire,
that three gradual declines should be guarded against: one, the decline into excessive building;
two, the decline into excessive ease;
and three, the decline into obstruction of information.
An imperial decree was issued:
"Place this by my seat,
to be reviewed constantly."
On the *jǐhài* day,
more than 66,000 nominal grain transport soldiers, added during the Qiánlóng (乾隆) era, were reduced.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Chéng Yùcǎi (程矞采) memorialized that
Hóng Xiùquán (洪秀全) had attacked Quánzhōu (全州),
then advanced to attack Yǒngzhōu (永州),
and split into contingents to escape to Yǒngfú (永福) and Yìníng (義寧).
Generals Bāo Qǐbào (鮑起豹) and Liú Chángqīng (劉長清) were ordered by dispatch to separately defend against them,
and Sài Shàng'ā (賽尚阿) was also consulted to jointly block and defend.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Tèdēng'é (特登額) was dismissed,
and Guìliáng (桂良) was appointed Minister of War (*Bīngbù Shàngshū*).
On the *yǐsì* day,
Zhāng Yún (章鋆) and 239 others were granted the *jìnshì jí dì* (進士及第) degree, with varying ranks.
Qí Shàn (琦善) was exiled to Jílín (吉林).
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Zōu Mínghè (鄒鳴鶴) was stripped of his post
for keeping troops to guard the city
and not allowing pursuit of the rebels.
Láo Chóngguāng (勞崇光) was appointed Governor of Guǎngxī (廣西).
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
an order was issued to retain 600,000 *shí* of tribute grain
to be transported to Jiāngsū (江蘇) and Shāndōng (山東) for disaster relief.
In the fifth month, on the *xīnhài* day,
Bù Yàntài (布彥泰) memorialized that
400,000 bolts of Hui (回) cloth were in storage,
and requested a flexible system of commuted payment.
This was granted.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
at the Summer Solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Earth at Fāngzé (方澤),
with Emperor Xuānzōng Chénghuángdì (宣宗成皇帝) respectfully honored as co-sacrificed.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
rebels captured Dàozhōu (道州) in Húnán (湖南).
Sài Shàng'ā (賽尚阿) remained to guard Guìlín (桂林),
and dispatched Jiāng Zhōngyuán (江忠源) and Zhāng Guóliáng (張國樑) to move their troops to Húnán (湖南).
In the sixth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
the disaster relief efforts in Shāndōng (山東) were investigated and handled.
Dù Shòutián (杜受田) and Yíliáng (怡良) memorialized that when grain boats enter the east,
unloading should be carried out first
to facilitate distribution.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Sài Shàng'ā (賽尚阿) was ordered to go to Húnán (湖南) to oversee military affairs,
and Xú Guǎngjìn (徐廣jìn) took over military affairs in Guǎngxī (廣西).
On the *dīnghài* day,
Empress Niǔhùlù Shì (鈕祜祿氏) was formally enthroned.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Sēnggé Línqìn (僧格林沁) impeached Grand Minister of the Presence Zhèng Qīnwáng Duānhuá (鄭親王端華) for altering the examination paper of the grand examination *shìjiǎng xuéshì* (侍講學士) Bǎo Qīng (保清),
and obstructing [his actions] without listening,
being arrogant and stubborn,
and difficult to work with.
An edict ordered Duānhuá (端華) to withdraw from the Grand Ministers of the Presence,
and Bǎo Qīng (保清) was stripped of his post.
On the *wùxū* day,
Huìchéng (慧成) was appointed Director-General of River Conservancy for Hédōng (河東).
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Jǐwèi,
the bandit force of Lóu Rójìng Líng Shíbā Gǔ in Guǎngdōng was suppressed.
The Emperor bestowed commendations.
Chūn Xī, the minister managing affairs in Wūshén, reported that
the Hui bandit Tiěwánkùlǐ Huòzhuó had infiltrated and harassed Wūshén,
but the government troops repelled them.
An edict commanded the chancellor-examiner to thoroughly investigate and report.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
an edict stated that military affairs were not yet concluded,
and there was an urgent need for talent.
Therefore, those who knew military strategy,
wherever they were, should be recommended and appointed.
An edict commanded the direct provinces to repair their city walls.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Du Shòutián, the Assistant Grand Secretary, passed away.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Luó Ràodiǎn reported that
upon reaching Chángshā,
he learned that the rebels had escaped from Dàozhōu into Jiānghuá, Yǒngmíng, Guìyáng, and Jiāhé.
He feared that the Hēngjùn district might be lost,
and the provincial capital should also take preventive measures.
An imperial decree ordered
that proper plans be immediately made and executed.
On the day Wùchén,
Yuán Jiǎsān, a Supervising Secretary, impeached Jùnwáng Zàiquán, Shàngshū Héngchūn, and Shìláng Shūyuán.
Repeated investigations found evidence,
and each was reprimanded.
Regarding the officials who composed poems and odes for Zàiquán's "Xi Xíjiān Tú" (Taking a Rest from Affairs),
they were also referred to the ministry for deliberation and punishment.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Yìshān and Bùyàntài reported that
the Hui bandit Wōlǐhǎn had colluded with the Bùlǔtè to break into the kǎlún (frontier post),
but the government troops repelled them.
On the day Rénshēn,
Hóng Xiùquán captured Chénzhōu.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Cháng Dàchún reported that Yuèzhōu should prepare defenses.
An edict commanded Xú Guǎngjìn to dispatch troops there.
Línkuí was appointed Minister of Punishments.
In the eighth month, on the first day Jǐmǎo,
Xiàng Róng was stripped of his position for feigning illness to evade duty,
and sent to Xīnjiāng for exile.
Later, he was retained in the army to serve.
Fúxìng was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Guǎngxī.
On the day Guǐwèi,
the imperial lectures were held for the first time.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
an edict was issued to the Governors-General and Governors of Húguǎng:
"The Dòngtíng Hú of Húnán and the Great River of Húběi
both have thousands of fishing boats and large merchant ships.
They should be urgently collected
to prevent them from being used by the rebels.
Their boatmen are accustomed to wind and waves
and are suitable as naval recruits.
Attention should be immediately paid to recruiting them."
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Luó Ràodiǎn and Luò Bǐngzhāng reported that
the rebel bandits had captured Ānrén and Yōuxiàn,
and were advancing towards the provincial capital.
An imperial order commanded Sài Shàng'ā to quickly relieve the siege of the capital.
On the day Gēngyín,
ministers of the court were ordered to jointly plan for military provisions.
Cháng Dàchún was transferred to be Governor of Shānxī.
Luó Ràodiǎn was appointed Governor of Húběi.
Zhāng Fèi was appointed Acting Governor of Jiāngxī.
On the day Jiǎchén,
an order temporarily exempted merchants transporting rice from Sìchuān and Jiāngxī to Húběi from taxes.
One thousand troops from Fújiàn and Zhèjiāng were transferred to Jiāngxī for defense.
In the ninth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
an edict stated that Sài Shàng'ā had failed in his command,
mismanaging the frontier.
He was stripped of his post and arrested for questioning,
and his property confiscated.
On the day Xīnhài,
Zàiquán was appointed Commander of the Gendarmerie.
Nè'ěrjīng'é was appointed Grand Secretary.
Xǐ'ēn was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Xīníng Tibetan bandit Ālǐkè Gōngzhù was captured
and executed.
Luò Bǐngzhāng was ordered to temporarily remain in Húnán to assist in affairs.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the Emperor visited the Eastern Mausoleums.
Fúchéng, the General who died in battle in Húnán, and others were granted hereditary ranks.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Cháng Dàchún reported that the rebels intended to move north,
and the defense forces were insufficient.
Xú Guǎngjìn was ordered to dispatch troops to Yuèzhōu to assist in the defense.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Xīnsì,
the Emperor visited the residence of Grand Secretary Du Shòutián to offer condolences,
and posthumously awarded his father, Dù È, the title of Minister of Rites.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Huáng Zōnghàn petitioned for the new grain tribute from Zhèjiāng to be transported by sea.
This was approved.
On the day Rénchén,
Jì Zhīchāng was dismissed.
Wú Wénróng was appointed Governor-General of Mǐnzhè.
In the eleventh month, on the first day Dīngwèi,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Dīngsì,
the rebels captured Yuèzhōu.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Qí Shàn was reinstated as Acting Governor of Hénán.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
an edict commanded Xú Guǎngjìn to divide his troops to defend Wǔchāng, Hànyáng, and Jīngzhōu.
Lù Jiànyīng and Jiǎng Wénqìng were each to strictly defend strategic points according to the terrain.
On the day Guǐhài,
as the rebels were approaching Húběi,
Qí Shàn was ordered to strictly defend the Hénán border.
Zhāng Fèi was commanded to strictly defend the vital passes along the river.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Wénqìng was appointed Minister of Revenue.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the rebels captured Hànyáng.
Lù Jiànyīng was ordered to hasten to the upper reaches of the river to defend.
On the day Yǐhài,
Xiàng Róng's title of Commander-in-Chief was restored.
An edict commanded Zēng Guófān, a former imperial censor living at home, to oversee the organization of local militia.
Fúzhūhóng'ā was transferred to be Commander-in-Chief of Jiāngnán.
In the twelfth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
an imperial order commanded gentry and scholars in each province to organize local militia.
Shèng Bǎo, a fourth-rank metropolitan official, was ordered to join the army in Hénán.
On the day Guǐsì,
the rebels captured Wǔchāng,
and Governor Cháng Dàchún died.
The Emperor severely reprimanded the commanding ministers for not considering the overall situation,
and hoarding troops for their own defense.
Xú Guǎngjìn was arrested for punishment.
Xiàng Róng was appointed Imperial Commissioner
to oversee military affairs.
Zhāng Liàngjī was appointed Acting Governor-General of Húguǎng.
Yè Míngchēn was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng.
Bǎi Guì was appointed Governor of Guǎngdōng.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Xiàng Róng reported that the rebels had successively captured Wǔ and Hàn,
and had built pontoon bridges.
It was necessary to prepare more cannon boats
to burn the bridges
before an attack could be launched.
An imperial decree was issued:
"The cannon boats led by Lú Yìngxiáng, a Department Director of the Board of Punishments,
had previously attacked rebels in Chángshā.
He should immediately hasten to the front."
On the day Jiǎchén,
troops levied from Jílín and Hēilóngjiāng arrived in the capital.
An imperial decree stated:
"Each detachment should set out every two days.
Commanding officers must strictly adhere to discipline,
and not demand extra vehicles,
or harass relay stations."
A grand sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
This year,
the disaster taxes in 42 prefectures and counties in Zhílì and one prefecture in Shānxī were remitted.
The collection of silver and rice taxes was delayed in 48 prefectures and counties in Zhèjiāng to varying degrees.
Cháoxiǎn and Xiāmluó paid tribute.
In the third year, Guǐchǒu, spring, first month, on the day Dīngwèi,
Cháng Qīng, the Deputy Lieutenant-General of Qīngzhōu, was ordered to move his troops to Yù and Chǔ for defense.
On the day Wùshēn,
Zhāng Liàngjī reported that
the rebel leader Xiāo Cháoguì had indeed been killed by cannon fire outside the city of Chángshā.
His body was recovered,
identified, decapitated, and displayed.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Jiǎng Wénqìng reported that the city walls were weak and troops scarce,
and requested that soldiers from the East and West Liáng Shān be transferred to the city for defense.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Xiàng Róng reported that
the rebels occupying Wǔchāng were moving their cannons onto boats,
intending to flee.
Lù Yìnggǔ reported that
intelligence indicated the rebels planned to move east to Ānqìng and Jiāngníng at the start of the new year.
Xiàng Róng was commanded to diligently scout and prepare
to intercept and suppress them.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Commander of the Gendarmerie and the Commander of the Vanguard were ordered to prepare military supplies
and interrogate traitors.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the rebels captured Jiǔjiāng.
Lù Jiànyīng retreated to defend Jiāngníng.
Sài Shàng'ā was sentenced to execution.
His son Chóngqǐ and others were stripped of their official positions.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Lǚ Xiánjī, Vice Minister of Works, was ordered to return to Ānhuī to manage defenses.
Zhōu Tiānjúe was granted the title of Vice Minister
to assist in defense affairs.
On the day Rénshēn,
Lù Jiànyīng was stripped of his post and arrested for questioning.
Xiáng Hòu was appointed Imperial Commissioner.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
as the gentry and commoners of Shānxī, Shǎnxī, and Sìchuān provinces had donated military provisions,
the quotas for provincial examinations and scholar candidates were increased.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the rebels captured Ānqìng,
and Jiǎng Wénqìng died.
Zhōu Tiānjúe was appointed Acting Governor of Ānhuī.
Ēncháng, the General who died in battle in Jiāngxī, was granted a hereditary rank.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day of the second month, which was the first day of the month,
an edict stated:
“The fifteen myriad banner soldiers in the capital's camps
should be diligently trained by their supervising ministers.”
Féng Péiyuán (馮培元), the education commissioner of Húběi who died as a martyr, was posthumously promoted to Assistant Minister (Shìláng 侍郎),
and given the posthumous name Wénjiè (文介).
Liáng Xīngyuán (梁星源), the financial commissioner (Bùzhèngshǐ 布政使), was given the posthumous name Mǐnsù (敏肅).
Ruìyuán (瑞元), the judicial commissioner (Ànchásǐ 按察使), was given the posthumous name Duānjié (端節).
Officials from prefect down were all granted hereditary ranks and dedicated shrines.
Duānfú (雙福), the commander-in-chief (Tídū 提督), and Wáng Jǐnxiù (王錦繡), the brigade-general (Zǒngbīngguān 總兵官), were included in the shrine of Cháng Dàchún (常大淳).
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
a sacrifice was offered to the former teacher Kǒngzǐ (孔子).
Assistant Minister (Shàqīng 少卿) Léi Yǐxián (雷以諴) and Academician Expositor-in-waiting (Shìjiǎng Xuéshì 侍講學士) Jìnkāng (晉康) were dispatched to Nánhé (南河),
and Junior Compiler (Shàozhànshì 少詹事) Wáng Lǚqiān (王履謙) to Dōnghé (東河),
to assist in defense matters.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the Emperor gave a lecture at the Imperial Academy (Yǒngyōng 雍).
Kǒng Fánhào (孔繁灝), the Duke Yǎnshèng (Yǎnshèng Gōng 衍聖公), was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent (Tàizǐ Tàibǎo 太子太保).
On the *dīnghài* day,

an imperial decree ordered that 40% of the integrity allowance (yǎnglǐan 養廉) for civil officials of the third rank and above, and 20% for military officials of the second rank and above, be allocated to military provisions.
The Ministry of Revenue (Hùbù 戶部) requested to implement commercial donations and household levies,
but the Emperor disallowed it.
On the *rénchén* day,
the rebels captured Jiāngníng (江寧).
General Xiánghòu (祥厚), Commander-in-chief Fúzhūhóng'ā (福珠洪阿), and others died.
Yíliáng (怡良) was appointed Governor-General of the Two Jiāngs (Liǎng Jiāng Zǒngdū 兩江總督),
and Huìchéng (慧成) was ordered to hasten to Jiāngnán (江南) for defense and suppression.
Tuōmíng'ā (托明阿) was transferred to be General of Jiāngníng (Jiāngníng Jiāngjūn 江寧將軍).
Wénbīn (文斌) was made General of Suíyuǎn Chéng (Suíyuǎn Chéng Jiāngjūn 綏遠城將軍).
Ruìchāng (瑞昌) was made General of Hángzhōu (Hángzhōu Jiāngjūn 杭州將軍).
Dèng Shàoliáng (鄧紹良) was made Commander-in-chief of Jiāngnán (Jiāngnán Tídū 江南提督).
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Qíshàn (琦善) was ordered to assist in the defense of Huái-Yáng (淮揚).
An imperial decree ordered that Húběi temporarily use two thousand *yǐn* (引) of salt from Sìchuān (四川) for its salt trade.
An imperial decree ordered Lǐ Huì (李僡) to investigate and apprehend Niǎnfěi (捻匪) in the three prefectures of Yǎn (兗), Yí (沂), and Cáo (曹) in Shāndōng (山東).
Academician of the Grand Secretariat (Nèigé Xuéshì 內閣學士) Shèngbǎo (勝保) was ordered to assist in the defense of Jiāngběi (江北).
On the *yǐsì* day of the third month,
the rebels captured Zhènjiāng (鎮江) and Yángzhōu (揚州).
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Empress Xiàohé Ruì (孝和睿皇后) was interred in the Imperial Ancestral Temple (Tàimiào 太廟).
On the *xīnhài* day,
the Emperor plowed the ceremonial field (Jìtián 耤田).
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Jiāng Zhōngyuán (江忠源), the judicial commissioner of Húběi, was ordered to assist in military affairs in Jiāngnán.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
an imperial decree ordered Assistant Minister Yìjīng (奕經) to lead the Mìyún (密雲) troops to Shāndōng for joint defense.
On the *dīngsì* day,
an imperial decree stated that local militia (tuánliàn 團練) in all provinces were permitted to kill bandits without consequence.
Luò Bǐngzhāng (駱秉章) was reinstated as Governor of Húnán (Húnán Xúnfǔ 湖南巡撫).
An imperial decree ordered Chén Qǐmài (陳啟邁), the financial commissioner of Jiāngníng, to establish a grain depot in Xúzhōu (徐州).
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Xiàng Róng (向榮) engaged the rebels at Jiāngníng
and defeated them.
Shī Dégāo (施得高) was appointed Commander-in-chief of the Fújiàn (福建) Naval Forces (Shuǐshī Tídū 水師提督).
On the *rénxū* day,
Lúzhōu (廬州) was designated as the provincial capital of Ānhuī (安徽).
Zhōu Tiānjúe (周天爵) suppressed the rebels quickly and effectively,
and Qíshàn (琦善) achieved consecutive victories in his attacks.
Both were commended and rewarded.
An imperial decree ordered Zhílì (直隸) and Fèngtiān (奉天) to prepare defenses for their seaports.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Xiàng Róng reported repeated victories against the city rebels
and occupying Zhōngshān (鍾山).
The Emperor greatly praised him.
Yìjīng and Tuōmíng'ā were ordered to Qīngjiāng (清江) for defense and suppression.
Ruìchāng (瑞chāng) was ordered to lead Shèngjīng (盛京) troops to Huái (淮) and Xú (徐) for joint defense.
Ēnhuá (恩華) was ordered to lead Jílín (吉林) troops to garrison Zhílì.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
an imperial decree ordered Guǎngdōng (廣東) to recruit "red-boat" (hóngdānchuán 紅單船) vessels
and select generals to lead them to Jiāngnán to suppress the rebels.
Fúji (福濟) was appointed Governor-General of Grain Transport (Cáoyùn Zǒngdū 漕運總督).
On the *gēngchén* day of the fourth month in summer,
a black halo was seen around the sun.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the rebels captured Pǔkǒu (浦口) and Chúzhōu (滁州).
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Qíshàn was ordered to command all armies in Jiāngběi.
Yáng Wéndìng (楊文定) was arrested and prosecuted.
The Jebtsundamba Khutuktu (Zhébùzūndānbā Lǎma 哲布尊丹巴喇嘛) of the Khalkha Mongols (Kùlún Kā'ěrkā Měnggǔ 庫倫喀爾喀蒙古) offered three thousand horses,
and the Xīlín (西林) league leader also offered horses,
but both were warmly declined by imperial decree.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Sūn Rújǐn (孫如僅) and 222 others were granted the *jìnshì jíyì* (進士及第) degree with varying ranks.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the rebels captured Fèngyáng (鳳陽).
The Ānhuī Niǎnfěi marauded Měngchéng (蒙城).
On the *wùshēn* day of the fifth month,
silver notes (yínchāo 銀鈔) were first produced.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Wáng Yìdé (王懿德) reported that the Huìfěi (會匪) of Hǎichéng (海澄) had captured Tóng'ān (同安), Ānxī (安谿), and Xiàmén (廈門).
He was severely reprimanded.
Zhōu Tiānjúe reported the recapture of Fèngyáng.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Lǐ Jiāduān (李嘉端) reported that the Nánlíng (南陵) rebel boats had advanced upstream.
An imperial edict stated
that this report differed from Xiàng Róng's memorial,
and ordered a thorough investigation.
Luò Bǐngzhāng reported
that Liú Hóngyì (劉洪義), a bandit leader in Shàngyóu County (Shàngyóu Xiàn 上猶縣) of Jiāngxī (江西), had gathered a crowd and was causing disturbance in Guìdōng (桂東),
bordering Guǎngdōng and Húnán.
An imperial edict stated
that the three provinces should jointly suppress them.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Lù Yìnggǔ (陸應穀) reported the fall of Bózhōu (亳州)
and that the rebels were attacking Biànliáng (汴梁).
An imperial decree ordered Jiāng Zhōngyuán to hasten to Hénán (河南) to suppress the rebels.
Wáng Yìdé reported that the commander (zhèn 鎮) and intendant (dào 道) of Zhāngzhōu (漳州) had been killed by rebels,
and that Yǒng'ān (永安) and Shāxiàn (沙縣) had fallen one after another.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Shèngbǎo was ordered to lead troops to Hénán.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Sàishàng'ā (賽尚阿) and Xú Guǎngjìn (徐廣縉) were released from prison
to serve in the army and prove their worth.
Yáng Diànbāng (楊殿邦) and Dàn Mínglún (但明倫) were both retained at Qīngjiāngpǔ (清江浦) to manage defenses.
Zhōu Tiānjúe reported that escaped bandits from Fèngyáng were marauding westward,
and he would immediately go to their aid.
An imperial edict stated:
“Zhōu Tiānjúe has always been known for his bravery,
and the trained volunteers (liànyǒng 練勇) he recommended, Zāng Yúqīng (臧紆青), can hold their own on one front.
Is he truly unable to fight the rebels to the death?”
Lù Yìnggǔ and Ēnhuá reported that the marauding rebels had forded the Cáo River (Cáohé 曹河)
and invaded Shāndōng.
An imperial edict stated
that Shǎnxī (陝西) troops should be dispatched for reinforcement,
and ordered them to firmly guard the gateway of Tóngguān (潼關).
The rebels captured Guīdé (歸德).
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the rebels recaptured Ānqìng (安慶).
An edict ordered Jiāng Zhōngyuán to defend Jiǔjiāng (九江).
Mongolian troops and their five thousand horses were summoned to gather at Rèhé (熱河).
On the *rénxū* day,
an edict stated that due to the rebels' northward advance,
gentry and commoners in the north were encouraged to form militias for self-defense.
Those who contributed to killing rebels
would be rewarded for their achievements.
Sēnggélínqìn (僧格林沁), Huāshānà (花紗納), Dáhóng'ā (達洪阿), and Mùyìn (穆蔭) were ordered to supervise the patrols and defenses of the capital.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Xǔ Nǎipǔ (許乃普) was appointed Minister of Justice (Xíngbù Shàngshū 刑部尚書),
and Wēng Xīncún (翁心存) was appointed Minister of Works (Gōngbù Shàngshū 工部尚書).
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Hénán soldiers and commoners were praised with an imperial edict
for their firm defense of the provincial capital.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Nè'ěrjīng'é (訥爾經額) was ordered to defend Héběi (河北).
Guìliáng (桂良) went to Bǎodìng (保定) to manage defenses.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Kāifēng (開封) was relieved,
and the rebels marauded southward to Zhōngmóu (中牟) and Zhūxiānzhèn (朱仙鎮).
An imperial decree ordered Tuōmíng'ā and others to pursue them.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the "Ten-Cash" (dāngshídàqián 當十大錢) coin was first minted.
On the *yǐhài* day of the sixth month,
the gentry and merchants of Fújiàn recaptured Zhāngzhōu.
They were praised with an imperial edict
and would be investigated for rewards.
On the *wùyín* day,
Hénán rebels attacked Sìshuǐ (汜水),
and a detachment crossed the river and captured Wēnxiàn (溫縣).
Tuōmíng'ā attacked them
and recaptured Sìshuǐ.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Nánlíng rebel boats advanced upstream and captured Nánkāng (南康),
then proceeded to besiege Nánchāng (南昌).
On the *xīnsì* day,
the gentry and brave men of Wēnxiàn defeated the rebels
and recaptured their city.
They then joined the government army and defeated the rebels at Wǔzhì (武陟).
Nè'ěrjīng'é was appointed Imperial Commissioner (Qīnchāi Dàchén 欽差大臣)
to supervise military affairs in Hénán and Héběi.
Ēnhuá and Tuōmíng'ā were his deputies.
The Yellow River (Huánghé 黃河) again breached its banks north of Fēng (Fēngběi 豐北).
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Muslim rebels (Huífěi 回匪) in Dōngchuān (東川) of Yúnnán (雲南) revolted.
Indigenous bandits (tǔfěi 土匪) in Táiwān (臺灣) of Fújiàn revolted.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
an American envoy requested an audience,
but an imperial edict declined it.
Hénán rebels besieged Huáiqìng (懷慶).
The government army lifted the siege of Xǔzhōu (許州),
and the rebels fled to Luóshān (羅山).
Fújiàn government troops recaptured Yǒng'ān and Shāxiàn.
Tuōmíng'ā and others defeated the rebels at Huáiqìng.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Zhènjiāng government army suffered a defeat.
Commander-in-chief Dèng Shàoliáng was stripped of his post.
Hé Chūn (和春) was appointed acting Commander-in-chief of Jiāngnán.
On the *wùxū* day,
Commander-in-chief Shuānglái (雙來), who was wounded and killed during the siege of Yángzhōu, was granted generous posthumous honors, hereditary rank, and silver.
Indigenous bandits in Quánzhōu (全州) of Guǎngxī (廣西) revolted.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day *jiǎchén*, the first day of the lunar month,
bandits in Guǎngxī captured Xīng'ān and Língchuān,
then spread out to attack Guìlín.
The government forces defeated them,
and recovered Língchuān and Xīng'ān.
On the day *bǐngwǔ*,
an imperial decree ordered Huìchéng to return to Qīngjiāngpǔ to guard against and suppress bandits.
On the day *dīngwèi*,
Shèngbǎo was appointed to assist in military affairs in Hénán.
On the day *bǐngchén*,
an imperial decree ordered the river officials in the Southeast to remove ferry boats
to prevent bandits from secretly crossing.
A hereditary position was granted in remembrance of Mǎ Jìměi, the General-in-chief who died in battle in Jiāngxī.
On the day *dīngsì*,
an imperial edict ordered that the new grain tribute from Jiāngxī and Húguǎng be commuted to silver and sent to the capital.
On the day *xīnyǒu*,
bandits escaped to Húběi and Ānhuī.
An imperial decree ordered Yíliáng to establish a customs house in Shànghǎi to collect taxes.
On the day *guǐhài*,
a hereditary position was granted in remembrance of Admiral Fúzhūhóng'ā.
On the day *jiǎzǐ*,
an imperial edict decreed that gentry and scholars who organized militias to resist bandits and died in the process
should all be granted special remembrance and pensions.
On the day *yǐchǒu*,
government forces in Fújiàn recovered Yóuxī.
In the eighth month, on the day *bǐngzǐ*,
government forces lifted the siege of Huáiqìng,
and the bandits escaped to Shānxī.
On the day *wùyín*,
Wú Wénróng was transferred to be Governor-General of Húguǎng,
Yùruì was made Governor-General of Sìchuān,
and Lèbīn was made General of Chéngdū.
On the day *gēngchén*,
bandits captured Yuánqǔ.
On the day *guǐwèi*,
Lǐ Huì died.
Zhāng Liàngjī was appointed Governor of Shāndōng,
and Luò Bǐngzhāng was appointed Governor of Húnán.
On the day *jiǎshēn*,
bandits in Jiāngxī captured Ráozhōu Prefecture,
and local bandits in Jí'ān responded remotely.
On the day *bǐngxū*,
bandits captured Jiàngxiàn and Qǔwò,
and advanced to besiege Píngyáng.
Hāfēn was dismissed,
and Héngchūn was appointed Governor of Shānxī.
On the day *gēngyín*,
bandits captured Píngyáng.
Shèngbǎo's troops arrived,
defeated them,
and recovered Píngyáng.
The bandits fled east from Hóngdòng.
On the day *guǐsì*,
Shèngbǎo was appointed Imperial Commissioner,
granted the "Divine Sparrow Blade,"
with Ēnhuá and Tuōmíng'ā as his deputies.
On the day *dīngyǒu*,
Tuōmíng'ā defeated bandits at Chénliú.
In the ninth month, on the day *guǐmǎo*, the first day of the lunar month,
they were again defeated at Lùchéng and Líchéng.
The bandits fled to Zhílì,
entering Línmíngguān.
Nè'ěrjīng'é was stripped of his position and interrogated.
Guìliáng was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì.
On the day *bǐngwǔ*,
bandits captured Bǎixiāng.
The siege of Nánchāng in Jiāngxī was lifted,
and the bandits again fled to occupy Ānqìng.
On the day *dīngwèi*,
Kuíqín was transferred to be Minister of Rites,
Huāshānà was made Minister of Public Works,
and Shèngbǎo was appointed Manchu Commander of the Eight Banners.
Local bandits in Jiāngsū captured Qīngpǔ and Bǎoshān,
which government forces recovered.
On the day *wùshēn*,
an order was issued to retain grain tribute for disaster relief in Shāndōng.
Due to the urgency of military affairs,
repairs to the Fēngběi River project were postponed.
On the day *xīnhài*,
Huìqīnwáng was appointed Commander-in-Chief by Imperial Order,
granted the "Sharp and Agile Blade."
Jùnwáng Sēnggélínqìn of Kē'ěrqìn was appointed Adviser,
granted the "Nèkùnísù Blade."
Gōngqīnwáng Yìxīn, Dìngjùnwáng Zàiquán, and Inner Grand Minister Bìchāng were to jointly manage patrol and defense.
On the day *yǐmǎo*,
bandits passed through Zhàozhōu and captured Shēnzhōu.
Orders were given to set up defenses at Héjiān, Zhuōzhōu, and Tōngzhōu.
On the day *xīnyǒu*,
Lǐ Jiāduān was dismissed.
Jiāng Zhōngyuán was appointed Governor of Ānhuī.
On the day *jiǎzǐ*,
Sēnggélínqìn recovered Shēnzhōu.
On the day *bǐngyín*,
Lù Yìnggǔ was dismissed.
Yīngguì was appointed Governor of Hénán.
On the day *jǐsì*,
Zhōu Tiānjué died in the army.
On the day *xīnwèi*,
bandits captured Xiànxiàn, Jiāohé, and Cāngzhōu,
then advanced to attack Tiānjīn.
Magistrate Xiè Zǐchéng led and supervised trained militia to intercept them,
and died.
His unit defeated the bandits for thirty *lǐ*.
Xiè Zǐchéng was posthumously granted the title of Provincial Administration Commissioner,
a shrine was built for him,
and the trained militia were highly commended.
Upon hearing the alarm,
the capital was put on alert.
Sēnggélínqìn stationed troops in Wǔqīng.
In the tenth month of winter, on the day *jiǎxū*,
Zēng Guófān was ordered to lead trained militia to Húběi to suppress bandits.
On the day *bǐngzǐ*,
bandits captured Huángzhōu.
Xú Fēngyù, Circuit Intendant of Hàn-Huáng-Dé, died.
They consecutively captured Hànyáng,
and advanced to besiege Wǔchāng.
On the day *dīngchǒu*,
bandits occupied Dúliúzhèn.
Shèngbǎo led his troops there,
and defeated them in consecutive battles.
On the day *wùyín*,
Gōngqīnwáng Yìxīn was appointed to serve in the Grand Council.
Línkuí was dismissed as Grand Councillor.
Ruìlín and Mùyìn were appointed Grand Councillors.
On the day *yǐmǎo*,
Yúán Jiǎsān, a Supervising Secretary, was granted the third-rank official title of Minister,
to suppress the Niǎn bandits in Ānhuī.
On the day *rénchén*,
the siege of Wǔchāng was lifted.
Jiāng Zhōngyuán proceeded to Ānhuī.
Acting Judicial Commissioner Táng Shùyì was ordered to suppress bandits on the river in Jiāngxī.
On the day *guǐsì*,
bandits captured Tóngchéng.
On the day *wùxū*,
an advance collection of land tax from the three provinces of Shānxī, Shǎnxī, and Sìchuān was ordered,
but later stopped.
In the eleventh month, on the day *rénzǐ*, the first day of the lunar month,
Wáng Qìngyún was appointed Governor of Shǎnxī.
On the day *bǐngwǔ*,
government forces in Fújiàn recaptured Xiàmén.
Bandits in Ānhuī captured Shūchéng.
Vice Minister Lǚ Xiánjī, who was in charge of organizing militias, died.
On the day *gēngxū*,
bandits captured Yízhēng.
On the day *guǐchǒu*,
Vice Minister Zēng Guófān was ordered to lead naval forces to suppress bandits in Ānhuī.
On the day *dīngmǎo*,
Shèngbǎo suppressed bandits at Dúliú,
but was unsuccessful.
Deputy Commander Tóng Jiàn died in battle,
and was posthumously granted the title of General and a pension.
In the twelfth month, on the day *jiǎxū*,
bandits in Yángzhōu broke out of the siege,
but government forces recovered the city.
Qíshàn, Huìchéng, and others were all stripped of their positions and sent to serve in the army.
On the day *yǐhài*,
an imperial edict stated that bandits in Huángzhōu were congregating,
and ordered Wú Wénróng to leave the province to suppress them.
On the day *wùzǐ*,
Qíshàn recovered Yízhēng.
On the day *jǐchǒu*,
bandits captured Lúzhōu.
Jiāng Zhōngyuán died.
Fúyì was appointed Governor of Ānhuī,
and Shào Càn was appointed Governor-General of Grain Transport.
On the day *bǐngshēn*,
Vice Minister Dù Hàn was appointed Grand Councillor.
Wēng Xīncún was dismissed.
Zhào Guāng was appointed Minister of Public Works.
On the day *jǐhài*,
the imperial ancestral temple held a joint sacrifice.
In this year,

disaster taxes were remitted for three hundred and forty-four prefectures, departments, counties, and garrisons in Fèngtiān, Zhílì, Shāndōng, Shānxī, Zhèjiāng, Húběi, Húnán, Guǎngxī, Yúnnán, and Gānsù provinces.
In addition, earthquake silver and grain, and fodder bundles in Gānsù Zhōngwèi were also remitted, with varying amounts.
Cháoxiǎn, Liúqiú, Xiāmluó, Yuènán, Miǎndiàn, and Nánzhǎng paid tribute.
In the fourth year, *Jiǎyín*, in the spring, on the *Xīnchǒu* day of the first month, the new moon occurred.
The *qīnwáng* and *jùnwáng* who were leaders of various Mongolian leagues repeatedly offered silver for military provisions.
An imperial decree warmly commended them,
but all were declined and returned.
On the *Yǐsì* day,
three hundred thousand taels of silver from the imperial treasury were allocated and dispatched to Shèngbǎo's army camp.
On the *Gēngxū* day,
the government troops recaptured Dúliúzhèn,
and the entrenched bandits fled back.
On the *Rénzǐ* day,
Zhāng Fèi was dismissed,
and Chén Qǐmài was appointed *Jiāngxī Xúnfǔ*.
Wáng Lǚqiān memorialized, stating that the administration in Hénán was lax and corrupt,
military expenditures were fraudulently inflated,
and river conservancy projects were wasteful.
The matter was sent to Yīngguì for investigation and report.
On the *Bǐngchén* day,
the sea transport of tribute grain from Zhèjiāng was rerouted to sail from Liúhékǒu,
and Jiāngsū was ordered to dispatch officials to establish an office.
On the *Jǐwèi* day,
Fújì was ordered to manage the salt affairs north of the Huái River (*Huáiběi*).
Wáng Yìdé was appointed *Mǐnzhè Zǒngdū*,
and Lǚ Quánsūn was appointed *Fújiàn Xúnfǔ*.
On the *Xīnyǒu* day,
Yuán Jiǎsān memorialized, requesting that matters related to food provisions
be directly handed over by the *Jūnjīchù* to the relevant ministries,
and not be sent to the *Nèigé*.
This was granted.
On the *Yǐchǒu* day,
Guǎngdōng was ordered to purchase foreign cannons and transport them to Wǔchāng.
On the *Bǐngyín* day,
the bandits occupied Shùchéngcūn.
A stern imperial edict commanded Sēnggélínqìn and Shèngbǎo to swiftly suppress and capture them.
On the *Dīngmǎo* day,
the Húběi forces attacking Huángzhōu suffered a defeat.
Governor-General Wú Wénróng,
and Táng Shùyì, acting *Ànchásǐ* and former *Bùzhèngsǐ*, died.
The *Hùbù* deliberated and reported on Hé Shàojī, *Sìchuān Xuézhèng*, whose memorial regarding his donation of personal funds used *piánwén* (parallel prose), which violated the prescribed style.
The Emperor rebuked Qí Jùnzǎo, saying:
"When you reviewed Hé Shàojī's memorial,
you also criticized its pedantic and rigid style.
Why then did you imitate it, despite finding fault with it?
As a *Dàxuéshì* overseeing the ministry,
can you not even change a single word in an official's draft?!"
The bandits fled to Dōngchéngzhuāng in Xiànxiàn.
Sēnggélínqìn and Shèngbǎo's combined forces attacked them.
The bandits fled and captured Fùchéng,
then split into groups and fled into Shāndōng.
On the *Jǐsì* day,
the gentry and militia of Lùhéxiàn, Jiāngsū, exerted great effort to protect the endangered city.
An imperial edict commended them,
and exempted them from one year's land tax.
In the second month, on the *Dīngchǒu* day,
the Emperor attended the Imperial Lectures (*jīngyán*).
On the *Jǐmǎo* day,
Xǔ Nǎipǔ was dismissed from serving in the *Nánshūfáng*,
and demoted to *Nèigé Xuéshì*.
Zhū Fèngbiāo was appointed *Xíngbù Shàngshū*,
and Zhōu Zǔpéi was appointed *Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ*.
Wēng Xīncún was reinstated as *Lìbù Zuǒ Shìláng*.
On the *Xīnsì* day,
Tái Yǒng was appointed *Húguǎng Zǒngdū*.
On the *Rénwǔ* day,
Zēng Guófān memorialized that he would lead seventeen thousand land and naval troops.
He would depart from Héngzhōu and rush to Húběi.
On the *Guǐsì* day,
Yìxīng was dismissed,
and Yīnglóng was appointed *Shèngjīng Jiāngjūn*.
Zēng Guófān memorialized, requesting that since Yáng Jiāng, grandson of former Governor Yáng Jiàn, had donated twenty thousand taels of silver,
Yáng Jiàn be permitted to be enshrined in the Temple of Local Worthies (*Xiāngxián Cí*).
An imperial decree stated:
"Yáng Jiàn was a retired official.
Enshrinement in the Temple of Local Worthies is a great honor
that cannot be obtained through donations.
Zēng Guófān should not have made such a request so hastily.
The Board is to deliberate on his punishment."
Since the outbreak of military campaigns,
the treasury was empty and matters were critical,
yet the Emperor was still so cautious with honors and appointments.
The hereditary position was granted to Liú Yùzhěn, *Ānhuī Bùzhèngsǐ*, who died as a martyr.
He was posthumously named *Qínzhuàng*.
On the *Guǐwèi* day,
former Associate Grand Secretary Tāng Jīnzhāo and Minister of War Tèdēng'é were again entertained at the Lùmíng banquet,
granted palace titles
and bestowed with imperial calligraphy on plaques.
On the *Bǐngxū* day,
Zhāng Liàngjī memorialized that the bandit leader Wáng Xiǎoyǒng, who had murdered high-ranking officials, had been captured.
His heart was extracted for a remote sacrificial offering.
An imperial decree ordered that
the families of Tóng Jiàn and Xiè Zǐchéng be immediately informed to perform the sacrificial rites.
Tuōmíng'ā was ordered to assist Sēnggélínqìn with military affairs.
On the *Guǐsì* day,
Qīnglín was appointed *Húběi Xúnfǔ*.
Chónglún was in mourning (*dīngyōu*),
but was still ordered to jointly defend the city.
On the *Wùxū* day,
Zhāng Liàngjī memorialized that the *Niǎn Zéi* had crossed the river, fled from Fēngxiàn into Shànxiàn.
Government troops engaged and won a victory,
but the rebels later captured Jīnxiāng.
In the third month, on the *Gēngzǐ* day, the new moon occurred.
Zhāng Liàngjī memorialized that the rebels had captured Jùyě and Yùnchéng.
On the *Xīnchǒu* day,
Zàilíng was ordered to lead one thousand troops to garrison Héjiān.
Guìlíng and Táilù were to lead fifteen hundred cavalry and infantry to garrison Dézhōu.
Luò Bǐngzhāng memorialized that the rebels had captured Yuèzhōu.
Zēng Guófān returned to the provincial capital to defend and block.
Expectant *dao* official Hú Línyì was left to suppress the rebels in southern Húguǎng (*Chǔnán*).
On the *Rényín* day,
the rebels captured Yánggǔ.
Magistrate Wén Yǐng, who had been in office for five days,
died there.
He was given generous posthumous honors, and a shrine was built for him.
On the *Jiǎchén* day,
the rebels fled from Yánggǔ and Guànxiàn to Xiǎotān in Qīnghé.
They then split up and fled to Lǐguānzhuāng in Línqīng.
On the *Yǐsì* day,
Shèngbǎo was ordered to intercept and attack the rebels fleeing into Shāndōng.
*Bùzhèngsǐ* Chóng'ēn memorialized that he would lead troops to guard Línqīngzhōu.
On the *Xīnhài* day,
the Emperor plowed the sacred field (*jìtián*).
On the *Dīngsì* day,
the rebels captured Línqīng.
Ten days later,
government troops recaptured it.
The routed rebels fled south.
Shèngbǎo pursued them.
Zēng Guófān memorialized that the suppression of rebels in Yuèzhōu had failed.
He returned to defend Chángshā.
The Board was ordered to deliberate on his punishment.
In the summer, on the *Gēngchén* day of the fourth month,
*Shùnchéng Jùnwáng* Chūnshān passed away.
The rebels from Fùchéng fled to Liánzhèn.
Sēnggélínqìn pursued and surrounded them.
On the *Rénwǔ* day,
Shèngbǎo memorialized that his cavalry had pursued and
completely annihilated the routed rebels from Línqīng.
An imperial decree commended him,
and he was given the title of *Tàizǐ Shàobǎo*.
Délèkèsèlèng and Shànlù were granted yellow jackets (*huángmǎguà*).
On the *Jǐchǒu* day,
Retired Grand Secretary Pān Shì'ēn passed away.
Grand Minister of the Imperial Household Bìchāng passed away.
On the *Xīnmǎo* day,
Bào Qǐbào was dismissed,
and Tǎqíbù was appointed acting *Húnán Tídū*.
Zēng Guófān was stripped of his official post to suppress the rebels.
Zēng Guófān recaptured Xiāngtán.
Tǎqíbù, Péng Yùlín, and Yáng Zǎifú achieved a great victory in suppressing the rebels.
