The rebels in Jìnggǎng retreated.
In the fifth month, on the *Jǐhài* day, the new moon occurred.
The temple for Gě Yúnfēi was completed,
and an imperial calligraphy plaque was bestowed.
The King of Kuò'ěrkā (Gurkhas) memorialized, requesting to send troops to suppress the rebels.
A warm imperial edict instructed him to desist.
On the *Xīnchǒu* day,
Sūn Ruìzhēn was dismissed.
Zhū Fèngbiāo was appointed *Hùbù Shàngshū*,
Zhào Guāng was appointed *Xíngbù Shàngshū*,
and Péng Yùnzhāng was appointed *Gōngbù Shàngshū*.
Deputy Lieutenant-General Miánxún pursued the rebels in Fēngxiàn.
He defeated them.
He was bestowed the heroic title of *Bātúlǔ*.
On the *Yǐsì* day,
Lǐ Kāifāng, the rebel leader from Liánzhèn, fled and captured Gāotángzhōu.
Shèngbǎo personally led troops to pursue him.
On the *Rénshēn* day,
the Emperor prayed for rain at Dàgāodiàn.
On the *Dīngsì* day,
he prayed for rain at the Altar of Heavenly Spirits (*Tiānshéntán*).
On the *Gēngshēn* day,
Guān Wén, *Jīngzhōu Jiāngjūn*, memorialized that government troops had recaptured Jiānlìxiàn and the city of Yíchāngfǔ.
An imperial edict commanded Tǎqíbù to lead his army to Húběi to suppress the rebels.
Former *Húběi Xúnfǔ* Chónglún was dismissed from office for feigning illness.
On the *Rénxū* day,
it rained.
On the *Guǐhài* day,
Héchūn and Fújì memorialized that they had recaptured the city of Lù'ānzhōu in Ānhuī.
In the sixth month, on the day Wùchén at the new moon,
rations for one month were granted to the refugees in Línqīng and Guānxiàn who had suffered from the rebels.
The Jiāngxī rebels fled to Dé'ān, Húběi.
On the day Gēngchén,
Xǔ Nǎizhāo was dismissed,
and Jí'ěrháng'ā was appointed as the Governor of Jiāngsū.
An imperial edict stated:
"Chinese seaports,
apart from the five treaty ports,
have always been off-limits to foreign ships.
Recently, however, there have been unauthorized entries into Jīnlíng and Zhènjiāng.
What is their intention?
Yè Míngchēn is hereby ordered to immediately speak to the foreign chiefs and prevent this."
On the day Xīnsì,
an edict ordered that in the directly administered provinces, those in the local militia who killed rebels
should have grand commemorative arches erected,
and be enshrined in the Zhōngyì Cí (Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness);
women who died defending themselves in times of difficulty
should be enshrined in the Jiéxiào Cí (Shrine of Chastity and Filial Piety).
On the day Guǐwèi,
the rebels captured Wǔchāng.
Tái Yǒng was dismissed,
and Yáng Pèi was appointed as the Governor of Húběi,
and acting Governor-General.
Zēng Guófān was ordered to advance from Yuèzhōu to suppress the rebels,
and Yīng Guì to go to Xìnyáng to defend.
Vice Commander-in-chief Dáhóng'ā died in the army
and was posthumously granted the title of Commander-in-chief.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Yè Míngchēn was commanded to suppress and capture the bandit boats of the Huìfěi in Guǎngdōng.
Iron coins and lead coins were minted.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
the Húběi rebels captured Yuèzhōu,
and subsequently Chángdé.
On the day Rénzǐ,
an edict stated:
"Qīnglín abandoned the city and fled,
going far to Chángshā.
Guān Wén is hereby ordered to convey the imperial decree for his execution."
Vice Commander-in-chief Tè'ěrqīng'é died in the army.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the Húnán navy recaptured Yuèzhōu,
and Zēng Guófān, who had been dismissed as a Vice Minister, was granted a third-rank title.
Circuit Intendant Hú Línyì was ordered to attack and suppress the rebels in Chángdé.
On the day Réngxū,
Yáng Pèi reported the recapture of Miǎnyáng;
the rebels captured Ānlù.
In the intercalary seventh month, on the day Wùchén,
the Húběi imperial army recaptured Ānlù.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Imperial Commissioner Qí Shàn died in the army,
and Tuōmíng'ā was appointed Imperial Commissioner,
to supervise military affairs in Yángzhōu.
On the day Gēngchén,
Yáng Pèi reported the recapture of Jīngshān, Xiàogǎn, Tiānmén, Huángpí, Máchéng, and other cities.
Xiàng Róng reported the imperial army's recovery of Gāochún.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Hé Chūn reported the recapture of Tàipíng.
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Guān Wén reported the continuous recapture of Jiāyú and Púqí.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Guǎngdōng local bandits captured Zhàoqìng,
and troops from Húnán and Fújiàn were dispatched to suppress them.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Húnán imperial army advanced from Chénglíngjī to attack Tōngchéng.
On the day Guǐhài,
British and American warships arrived at the Tiānjīn seaport,
and Guìliáng was ordered to handle the matter.
In the ninth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
the Húběi and Húnán imperial armies captured Wǔchāng and Hànyáng.
Yáng Pèi was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng;
Zēng Guófān was granted a second-rank title and appointed acting Governor of Húběi;
Tǎqíbù was granted a yellow riding jacket;
Lǐ Mèngqún, Luó Zénán, and Lǐ Xùbīn were all promoted accordingly.
Yuè Xīng, the Provincial Administration Commissioner who died in the line of duty, and Lǐ Qīnggǔ, the acting Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, were both granted posthumous titles and enshrined.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Húběi imperial army recaptured Huángzhōu.
Zēng Guófān, with the title of Vice Minister of War, was ordered to lead the army with Tǎqíbù eastward.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Yù Ruì was dismissed,
and Huáng Zōnghàn was appointed Governor-General of Sìchuān,
Hé Guìqīng as Governor of Zhèjiāng.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Ānhuī imperial army recovered Lújiāng.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Wèi Yuánlàng died,
and Wēng Xīncún was appointed Minister of War.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
Huāshānà was appointed Minister of Personnel,
Quán Qìng as Minister of Public Works,
and concurrently Administrator of the Guózǐjiān (Imperial Academy).
Wén Qìng was transferred to be Manchu Commander-in-chief,
Yì Xīng as Han Banner Commander-in-chief,
and Yì Shān as Grand Minister of the Interior.
On the day Dīngsì,
Zēng Guófān reported that the naval and land forces attacked the rebels at Bànbìshān,
killing over ten thousand rebels.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Zālāfēntài was appointed General of Yīlí.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Zēng Guófān and others reported the capture of Tiánjiāzhèn;
Yáng Zàifú and Péng Yùlín were promoted.
The Húběi army recovered Qízhōu.
In the eleventh month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
the Emperor went to the Dàgāodiàn to pray for snow.
On the day Gēngchén,
Yáng Pèi reported the recapture of Guǎngjì and Huángméi.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Luó Ràodiǎn died,
and Héngchūn was appointed Governor-General of Yún-Guì,
Wáng Qìngyún as Governor of Shānxī,
Wú Zhènyù as Governor of Shǎnxī.
Shànlù, the General of Suīyuǎnchéng, died in the army.
On the day Gēngyín,
Grand Secretary and Grand Councilor Qí Jùnzǎo retired.
Jiǎ Zhēn was appointed Grand Secretary,
Wēng Xīncún as Minister of Personnel,
Zhōu Zǔpéi as Minister of War,
Xǔ Nǎipǔ as Left Censor-in-chief.
On the day Guǐsì,
the Húběi rebels captured Yīngshān, Ānhuī.
The Ānqìng rebels fled to Jiǔjiāng and Húkǒu,
and reached Wúchéng.
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
Zēng Guófān reported the capture of Xiǎochíkǒu;
the Emperor praised him highly,
and bestowed a yellow riding jacket trimmed with fox fur.
On the day Wùxū,
Hé Chūn reported the recapture of Yīngshān.
Because the recapture of both Yīng and Huò counties relied on the efforts of the people,
the grain tribute for three years was remitted.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Yuán Jiǎsān reported that the Jǔrén Zāng Yūqīng attacked Tóngchéng
and died in battle after exhausting his strength;
he was posthumously granted a third-rank title
and hereditary office.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Yìjì's son Zàizhōng was enfeoffed as Bèilè,
succeeding to the Yǐnzhì Jùnwáng,
and his name was changed to Zàizhì.
Guìzhōu imperial troops attacked the rebels,
defeated them,
and lifted the siege of Xīngyì city.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the Ānhuī imperial army recaptured Hánshān.
Sēnggélínqìn reported the destruction of the rebel stronghold at Xīliánzhèn.
On the day Guǐhài,
a joint sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
In this year,
calamity taxes were remitted in 129 prefectures and counties in provinces such as Hénán, Shāndōng, Shānxī, Fújiàn, Húnán, and Guǎngxī,
as well as in twelve native prefectures and counties in Guǎngxī, with varying degrees of remission.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú paid tribute.
In the fifth year, on the day Jǐsì in spring, the first month of Yǐmǎo,
the Sìchuān imperial army recaptured Tóngzǐ, Guìzhōu.
On the day Rénshēn,
the Guìzhōu imperial army suppressed bandits at Léitáishān,
capturing the bandit chief Chén Liángmó.
On the day Jiǎxū,
as the grain tribute from Jiāng and Zhè was insufficient for the capital's granaries,
Yíliáng was ordered to organize the collection of grain donations for transport to the capital.
On the day Wùyín,
Jí'ěrháng'ā reported the recapture of Shànghǎi county town.
An edict praised him.
On the day Xīnsì,
the Húběi rebels turned back from Huángméi to Hànkǒu;
Yáng Pèi retreated to Dé'ān,
was stripped of his office,
but remained in his post.
On the day Guǐwèi,
the Jiāngxī imperial army recaptured Wǔníng.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Sēnggélínqìn reported the capture of Liánzhèn,
and the chief rebel Lín Fèngxiáng was apprehended.
Sēnggélínqìn was enfeoffed as a Qīnwáng (Prince of the First Rank),
and his army was moved to Shāndōng
to suppress the bandits occupying Gāotáng.
Imperial Commissioner Shèngbǎo's army had been long without success,
so he was stripped of his office and arrested for questioning.
On the day Bǐngxū,
local bandits caused trouble in Yuèqīng, Zhèjiāng,
and they were suppressed.
For the merit at Liánzhèn,
Xīlíng'ā, Ruìlín, Qìngqí, Miánxún, Lāmùgùnbùzhābù, and Gùnchǔkèlínqìn were all granted generous rewards.
Second month, jiǎwǔ (day 1 of the month).
Wáng Yìdé memorialized that foreign merchants were coming to Mǐn to trade tea,
renting private houses for long stays.
To levy tea tax,
this was permitted.

Regarding the French general Láciní's (presumably meaning Charles Montauban or another French military figure, though the pinyin for 'Láciní' is not standard for a known French name, it's transliterated as given) assistance in attacking Shànghǎi,
four pieces of silk and ten thousand taels of silver were bestowed,
following Jí'ěrháng'ā's request.
Jǐhài.
The Emperor attended the Classics Mat Lectures (Jīngyán).
Sēnggélínqìn memorialized that Gāotáng Zhōu had been recaptured,
and the remaining rebels had fled into Féngguāntún.
Xīnchǒu.
Bandits in Fújiàn revolted;
they were suppressed.
Wùwǔ.
The Ě (Húběi) rebels fled north.
Sēnggélínqìn was ordered to dispatch three to four thousand cavalry and infantry to Hénán to assist in defense.
Third month, jiǎzǐ.
Guǎngdōng government troops recaptured Hǎifēng.
The Wǎn (Ānhuī) rebels captured Huīzhōu.
Yǐchǒu.
The Emperor visited Xīlíng.
The rebels captured Wǔchāng.
Governor Táo Ēnpéi died there.
Hú Línyì was appointed acting Húběi Governor.
Xīnwèi.
The Emperor returned to the capital.
Xīnmǎo.
Yáng Fèng, a bandit leader in Guìzhōu, was captured and executed.
The remaining bandits were pacified.
Summer, fourth month, yǐwèi.
Ānhuī government troops recaptured Wùyuán.
The Emperor's son-in-law Jǐngshòu was appointed Imperial Bodyguard (Yùqián Dàchén).
Dīngwèi.
Jiāngxī rebels captured Guǎngxìn.
Gēngxū.
Sēnggélínqìn and others memorialized that the rebel stronghold at Féngguāntún had been captured,
and the chief rebel Lǐ Kāifāng had been apprehended.
All remaining rebels were annihilated.
An imperial decree stated: "Greatly pleased!"
Sēnggélínqìn was immediately granted the hereditary title of Qīnwáng,
and permitted to ride in a sedan chair.
Délèkèsèlèng was granted the title of Béilè.
Others were promoted.
Jiāngxī government troops recaptured Yìyáng.
Zhèjiāng rebels captured Kāihuà.
Jǐwèi.
Zhālāfēn, the Xi'ān General, died in battle while suppressing rebels in Húběi.
He was given generous posthumous honors.
Yáng Pèi was dismissed from his post.
Guānwén was appointed Húguǎng Governor-General.
Miánxún was appointed Jīngzhōu General.
Ruìlín was appointed Xi'ān General.
Xīlíng'ā was appointed Imperial Commissioner
to Húběi to suppress rebels.
Gēngshēn.
Jiāngxī government troops recaptured Ráozhōu, Guǎngxìn, and Xīng'ān.
Xīnyǒu.
Guǎngdōng government troops won a victory against bandits;
all land and water bandits were pacified.
Fifth month, bǐngyín.
Fújiàn Magistrate Gāo Hóngfēi, who died in battle, was honored.
He was enshrined in the Zhāozhōng Cí in the capital,
and a shrine was also built in Táiwān.
Dīngmǎo.
Xiàng Róng memorialized that rebels at Sānshān had been suppressed;
victory was achieved.
Wùchén.
Guǎngdōng government troops recaptured Héyuán and other counties,
annihilating rebels at Sānshuǐ.
Xīnwèi.
The Emperor held court at Qiánqīngmén.
By imperial command, Grand General Huì Qīnwáng Miányú and Councillor Minister Qīnwáng Sēnggélínqìn respectfully returned the Grand General's seal and the Councillor's seal.
Rénshēn.
An imperial edict stated:
"The establishment of Tuánliàn (local militia)
was originally for defending local communities.
However, Hénán has repeatedly seen incidents of resisting grain levies and resisting officials.
Such widespread emulation
has extremely serious consequences.
All Governors-General and Governors should pay more attention to rectification,
and not allow it to fester into trouble over time."
At this time,
the problem of "Black Tuán" (Hēituán) already existed in Shāndōng,
but had not yet been reported to the Emperor.
It was later finally suppressed by military force.
Yǐhài.
Bǎijùn was appointed Rèhé Dutǒng.
Wùyín.
Yáng Pèi's army recaptured Suízhōu.
Guǐwèi.
Hénán troops recaptured Guāngshān.
Dīnghài.
Hú Línyì memorialized that he had divided command of land and water forces to vigorously attack Wǔ and Hàn (Wǔchāng and Hànyáng),
winning four battles out of four.
An imperial decree ordered
swift recapture.
An imperial edict stated:
"We hear that Huímín in Yúnnán are prone to causing trouble,
and have repeatedly gathered to resist grain levies.
Héngchūn and Shūxīng'ā must punish the principal offenders,
and not allow it to spread over time."
Lǐ Jūn was appointed Dōnghé Hédào Zǒngdū (Grand Canal Governor of the Eastern River).
Sixth month, yǐwèi.
Jiāngxī rebels captured Yìníng.
Dīngyǒu.
Admiral Dèng Shàoliáng recaptured Xiūníng.
Yǐsì.
Guǎngdōng government troops recaptured Fēngchuān,
annihilating rebels off Hǔmén.
Bǐngchén.
The Lányáng River in Hénán overflowed.
Jǐwèi.
It was decreed that the Huīníngchíguǎng Dào of Ānhuī should report on affairs by special memorial, like the Táiwān Dào.
Xīnyǒu.
Guānwén memorialized that government troops had recaptured Yúnmèng and Yìngchéng.
Autumn, seventh month, rénxū (day 1 of the month).
The Imperial Noble Consort Dowager was honored as Kāngcí Huáng Tàihòu.
Guǎngdōng rebels captured Chénzhōu and Yízhāng in Húnán.
Guǐhài.
Chén Qǐmài was stripped of his position.
Wénjùn was appointed Jiāngxī Governor.
Jǐsì.
Xiàng Róng memorialized that Wúhú had been recaptured.
Gēngwǔ.
The Empress Dowager passed away.
Dīngchǒu.
Xīlíng'ā's campaign against the Dérán rebels was unsuccessful;
he retreated to Suízhōu.
Dūxīng'ā was ordered to move his troops from Féngguāntún to suppress them.
Xīnsì.
Gōng Qīnwáng Yìxīn was dismissed from his duties in the Grand Council
and returned to the Upper Study Room (Shàngshūfáng) to study.
Wénqìng was appointed Grand Councillor.
Guǐwèi.
Guǎngdōng government troops recaptured Zhàoqìng Fǔ and Déqìng Zhōu.
Jiǎshēn.
Local bandits caused trouble in Yángchéng, Shānxī;
they were suppressed.
Dīnghài.
Guānwén memorialized that Hànchuān had been recaptured.
Eighth month, xīnmǎo (day 1 of the month).
Hú Línyì led his army to capture Hánzhèn (Hànkǒu),
then laid siege to Hànyáng.
Jiǎwǔ.
Yīngguì memorialized that Qiū Lián'ēn had captured the Niǎn leaders Yì Tiānfù and Wáng Dǎng, and executed them.
Jǐhài.
Húnán Admiral Tǎqíbù died in the army.
He was posthumously granted the title of General.
Gēngzǐ.
The Emperor bestowed the posthumous honorary title Xiàojìng Kāngcí Huánghòu upon the late Grand Empress Dowager.
Huí rebels from Kāshígé'ěr entered the pass.
Wōshíhúnbù dispatched troops to drive them out.
Wùshēn.
Guǎngdōng government troops successively recaptured Liánzhōu, Sānjiāng, and Liánshān,
and lifted the siege of Yǒng'ān City.
Ninth month, jiǎzǐ.
Grand Secretary Zhuō Bǐngtián passed away.
Yǐchǒu.
Liú Zhēng was appointed Hànjūn Dutǒng.
Gēngwǔ.
Wénqìng and Yè Míngchēn were ordered to assist in Grand Secretary duties.
Guǐyǒu.
One hundred thousand taels from the imperial treasury were allocated to continue relief efforts for disaster victims in Zhílì and Shāndōng.
Rénwǔ.
Yí (non-Han ethnic group) bandits caused trouble in Mǎbiāntīng, Sìchuān;
government troops suppressed them.
Guǐwèi.
Niǎn leader Zhāng Luòxíng fled south from Guīdé.
Admiral Wǔ Lóng'é was ordered to suppress him.
Yǐyǒu.
Guānwén was appointed Imperial Commissioner
to supervise military affairs in Húběi.
Zhè (Zhèjiāng) troops recaptured Xiūníng and Shídài in Ānhuī.
Wùzǐ.
Dèng Shàoliáng was transferred to be Gùyuán Tídú.
Winter, tenth month, dīngyǒu.
Hé Chūn and Fú Jì memorialized that Lúzhōu Fǔ City had been recaptured.
An imperial decree praised and rewarded them.
Hé Chūn was bestowed a yellow jacket (huángmǎguà).
Fú Jì was granted the title Tàizǐ Shàobǎo (Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent).
Héféi's quota tax (é fù) was remitted for three years.
Xīnchǒu.
Miáo rebels in Guìzhōu captured Dūjiāng.
Rényín.
Guānwén memorialized that Dé'ān had been recaptured.
Wùshēn.
Shí Dákāi fled back to Húběi.
Hú Línyì intercepted and suppressed him.
Rénzǐ.
The additional forty thousand taels of silver levied for river conservancy work in Hénán were permanently remitted.
In the eleventh month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Hú Lín-yì奏 (presented a memorial),
saying that Luó Zé-nán and Lǐ Xù-bīn engaged Shí Dá-kāi and Wéi Jùn at Yánglóu Cave
and defeated them.
He requested the purchase of Western cannons to strike the rebels.
An imperial edict ordered Yè Míng-chēn to procure six hundred Western cannons
to be transported by water from Húnán to Húběi for use.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Gorkha barbarians occupied Jìlóng in Ü-Tsang.
Dé-xīng died.
Lín-kuí was transferred to be Minister of the Board of Punishments,
and Ruì-lín was made Minister of the Board of Rites.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Guān Wén reported the recapture of Xiánníng and Jīnkǒu,
and also reported that rebels in Jiāngxī had captured Yìníng.
He dispatched an order for Luó Zé-nán to return and suppress them.
The imperial rescript stated:
"Luó Zé-nán is currently engaged in suppression efforts,
and Wǔhàn is in a critical situation;
he cannot return to suppress them."
An imperial edict ordered Zēng Guó-fān and others to send Zhōu Rǔ-yún to Chóng and Tōng
to provide support for Luó Zé-nán's rear.
Hé Chūn and others reported that the Niǎn rebels under Lǐ Zhào-shòu had fled to and occupied Yīngshān.
Circuit intendant Hé Guì-zhēn secretly plotted to join forces and capture them,
but failed
and died.
In the twelfth month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Emperor went to the Dàgāo Hall to pray for snow.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Jiāngxī rebels captured Línjiāng and Ruìzhōu.
An imperial edict ordered Zēng Guó-fān to dispatch troops to suppress them.
On the *wùxū* day,
two hundred thousand *shí* of grain from Jiāngsū's grain tribute were retained to aid the Jiāngnán army.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Guǎngxī government troops recaptured Xīng'ān.
Guìzhōu rebel Xú Tíng-jié captured Zhèngān,
and then part of Sīnán.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Wén-qìng and Yè Míng-chēn were appointed Grand Secretaries,
Guì-liáng and Péng Yùn-zhāng Assistant Grand Secretaries,
Bǎi-jùn Minister of the Board of Revenue,
Yì-xiāng General-in-chief of Shèngjīng,
and Yīng-lóng Military Governor of Rèhé.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Zhèng Qīn-wáng Duān-huá was made Manchu Military Governor,
and Yì-shān General-in-chief of Hēilóngjiāng.
Xī Líng-ā was ordered to go to Hénán to defend and suppress rebels.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Niǎn rebel Zhāng Luò-xíng fled back to Guīdé.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Yīng-guì was ordered to supervise the suppression of Niǎn rebels in the three provinces of Hénán, Shāndōng, and Ānhuī.
Jǐng-chún submitted a memorial detailing the defense situation against the barbarians;
the Emperor praised and rewarded him.
The Amban residing in Tibet, Hè-tè-hè, reported that he had swiftly arrived in Ü-Tsang to plan a general strategy for defense.
The imperial rescript stated:
"Jiāngzī, Dìngrì Canton, Mǎbùjiā, and other places
are all vital strategic points along the central route;
they should be immediately held.
Among the *kābúlún* (Tibetan ministers), select those who are trusted by the barbarians,
and have them assist in handling affairs
to supplement the inadequacy of military strength.
Captured barbarians
shall be temporarily kept in the camp
and allowed to communicate back and forth
to demonstrate a policy of conciliation.
The six proposals drafted by Lè Bīn and others
are to be conveyed to the said Amban."
On the *dīngsì* day,
the ancestral rites were performed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In this year,
taxes were remitted for two prefectures and one hundred fifty-eight departments and counties in Zhílì, Shāndōng, Húběi, Guǎngxī, Guìzhōu, and other provinces,
and for thirty-eight native departments and counties in Guǎngxī due to disaster;
salt field taxes in Jiāngsū varied.
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú offered tribute.
In the sixth year, the spring of *bǐngchén*, on the first day of the first month, *jǐwèi*,
Dūn Jùn-wáng Yì-zōng was reinstated as a Prince of the First Rank.
Yì-shān was made a Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard,
and Bèi-lè Zǎi-zhì was appointed to serve before the Emperor.
On the *rénxū* day,
Yáng Yǐ-zēng died.
Gēng-cháng was made Governor-General of River Affairs in Jiāngnán.
On the *rénshēn* day,
rebels harassed Huàngzhōu and Máyáng in Húnán.
Government troops repelled them,
and beheaded rebel leader Hé Lù.
On the *yǐhài* day,
an imperial edict ordered Luò Bǐng-zhāng to dispatch Prefect Liú Cháng-yòu to Jiāngxī to suppress rebels.
On the *wùyín* day,
Guǎngdōng Provincial Military Commander Kūn-shòu suppressed the Guīshàn rebels
and pacified them.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Provincial Military Commander Qín Dìng-sān captured Shūchéng.
In the second month, on the *rénchén* day,
an imperial edict allowed Miao officers who had performed meritoriously in suppressing bandits in Húnán
to remain in the army and be promoted based on seniority.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Emperor attended the Imperial Lecture.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Shùntiān Prefect Jiǎng Qí-chún presented two admonitions, "Self-Restraint" and "Return to Propriety."
The Emperor praised and accepted them.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the two nations of Britain and America requested treaty revisions.
The matter was referred to Yè Míng-chēn for his information.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
troops from Jílín, Hēilóngjiāng, Cháhā'ěr, and Suíyuǎn City were transferred to Shāndōng and Hénán to suppress rebels.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the "reduced stipend for integrity" for civil officials in directly administered provinces was appropriately increased.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Fú-xīng was ordered to assist in military affairs in Jiāngnán.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Gorkha requested a cessation of hostilities.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Guìzhōu government troops captured Tóngrén.
In the third month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
Guāzhōu rebels fled out onto the Grand Canal.
Tuō Míng-ā pursued and suppressed them.
Yì-xiāng was dismissed,
and Qìng-qí was made General-in-chief of Shèngjīng.
On the *rénxū* day,
Húnán government troops recaptured Yǒngmíng and Jiānghuá.
Liú Cháng-yòu's army entered Jiāngxī
and recaptured Píngxiāng.
Jiāngxī rebels captured Jí'ān.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Emperor performed the plowing ceremony at the imperial field.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Jiāngnán rebels again captured Yángzhōu.
Tuō Míng-ā and Léi Yǐ-chén were stripped of their positions.
Dé-xīng-ā was appointed Imperial Commissioner,
with Junior Compiler Wēng Tóng-shū as his deputy.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Shí Dá-kāi captured Ruìzhōu.
An imperial edict ordered Guǎngdōng to block and suppress them.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Sài Shàng-ā and Nè'ěr Jīng-é were released from their places of exile.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Provincial Military Commander Dèng Shào-liáng vigorously attacked Yángzhōu
and captured it.
Dé-xīng-ā was ordered to assist in military affairs.
The rebels fled to Jiāngpǔ.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Luó Zé-nán vigorously attacked Wǔchāng
and died in battle.
He was posthumously granted the title of巡撫 (Governor),
awarded a pension, and given a posthumous epithet.
On the *wùyín* day,
rebels captured Jiànchāng in Jiāngxī.
Wàn Qīng-lí, Education Commissioner of Zhèjiāng, and Yàn Duān-shū, Provincial Administration Commissioner, were ordered to supervise the defense of Sānqú.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Mùzōng's birth mother, Yì Pín Nālā Shì, was promoted to Yì Fēi.
Zēng Guó-fān suffered a defeat while attacking rebels at Zhāngshù;
the matter was referred to the Board for deliberation on punishment.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Héng-chūn memorialized on military affairs and the provincial Governors-General and Governors,
requesting permission for them to memorialize with a single signature.
This was approved.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Zhāng Guó-liáng's army captured Pǔkǒu.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
the Yue rebels again captured Yízhēng.
Government troops soon recaptured it.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Guìzhōu troops recaptured Lángdài.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Hàn and Huí (Muslim) people in Chǔxióng, Yúnnán, came into conflict.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Jiāngxī troops recaptured Jìnxián.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
an earthquake occurred in Jīnzhōu, Fèngtiān.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Ānhuī rebels captured Níngguó.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
former Assistant Grand Secretary and retired Supervisor of the Imperial Banquets Tāng Jīn-zhāo died;
he was posthumously granted the title of Minister.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Wēng Tóng-hé and two hundred sixteen others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with varying ranks.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Dé-xīng-ā reported that government troops attacked rebels at Sānchàhé
and destroyed their stronghold.
In the fifth month, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
Mù-kè-dé-nà was appointed General-in-chief of Guǎngzhōu,
and Dū-xīng-ā General-in-chief of Jiāngníng.
On the *rénxū* day,
Húběi government troops suffered a defeat at Tōngchéng;
Circuit Intendant Jiāng Zhōng-jì died.
Jiāngsū Governor Jí'ěr Háng-ā engaged rebels at Huángnízhōu near Zhènjiāng,
was defeated
and died.
He was posthumously granted the title of Governor-General.
Zhào Dé-zhé was appointed acting Jiāngsū Governor.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Jiāngnán rebels attacked the camp at Jiǔhuá Mountain
and captured it.
Hénán troops recaptured Guāngzhōu.
Xī Líng-ā was reinstated as Military Governor.
Yuán Jiǎ-sān was reinstated as a third-rank minister.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
rebels captured Lìshuǐ.
On the *bǐngxū* day of the sixth month,
the Jinlíng [Nánjīng] rebels attacked and captured the grand encampment.
The imperial forces retreated to defend Dānyáng,
and Xiàng Róng and Fúxìng were dismissed from their posts.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Xú Zōnggàn, the Surveillance Commissioner, was appointed to assist in the defense of Ānhuī.
Yíliáng was ordered to hire steamships to enter the river and suppress the rebels.
An imperial edict was issued to Henán and Guǎngdōng to dispatch troops,
and Hé Chūn and Fù Zhènbāng were to go to reinforce Jiāngnán.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Yè Míngchēn reported that the envoys from England, America, and France, having fixed the treaty for twelve years,
requested to proceed to the capital to revise the treaty.
An imperial edict conditionally agreed to modifications,
but forbade their coming to the capital.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the Yǒngdìng Hé overflowed.
Rebels in Jiāngxī captured Ráozhōu.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
Guǎngdōng reinforcements successively recovered Shàngyóu and Yúdū in Jiāngxī,
lifting the siege of Gànzhōu city.
Wáng Yìdé presented the American national letter,
and received an imperial decree stating:
"It is difficult to approve a change of treaty;
they are still ordered to return to Guǎngdōng to discuss and finalize it."
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Commander-in-chief Zhāng Guóliáng was ordered to assist Xiàng Róng in military affairs.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the imperial forces in Jiāngxī successively recovered Nánkāng and Ráozhōu.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Imperial Commissioner Xiàng Róng died in the army.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Salars in Gānsù caused trouble,
and the imperial forces suppressed them.
Hé Chūn was ordered to hasten to the Dānyáng military camp to suppress the rebels,
and Zhèng Kuíshì was to take over the military affairs of Ānhuī.
Húběi reinforcements recovered Xīnchāng and Shànggāo in Jiāngxī.
Hètèhè reported that Gurkhas and Tanggūte had made peace,
and withdrew the garrison troops.
In the eighth month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
Huáng Zōnghàn was dismissed,
Wú Zhènyù was made Governor-General of Sìchuān,
and Tán Tíngxiāng was made Governor of Shǎnxī.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Shūxīng'ā was ordered to strictly deal with the Muslim rebels [Huí Fěi]
and organize local militia.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Guǎngxī imperial forces recovered Shàngsīzhōu and Guìxiàn.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Guìzhōu rebels captured Dūyún and Shībǐng,
then went on to capture Gǔzhōu.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Ānhuī imperial forces attacked and captured Sānhé.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
secret society rebels in Jiāngxī attacked and captured Guǎngchāng, Nánfēng, Xīnchāng, and Lúxī.
In the ninth month, on the *yǐmǎo* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
rice was expensive in the capital,
so five public kitchens were opened,
and grain from granaries and copper cash were allocated to relieve the famine victims in the six prefectures and counties of Gù'ān.
On the *jǐsì* day,
local bandits in Yúnnán captured Làngqióng.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Jiāngnán imperial forces attacked Gāochún
and captured it.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Ānhuī imperial forces recovered Wúwéizhōu.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Wénqìng and others submitted Méng Bǎo's translation of the *Dàxué Yǎnyì*,
and it was ordered to be collated, printed, and promulgated.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Heifans in Xīníng caused trouble,
and Commander-in-chief Suǒ Wén suppressed them.
Yì Táng was relieved due to illness,
Lè Bīn was appointed Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù,
Yǒu Fèng was appointed General of Chéngdū,
and Dōngchún was appointed General of Fúzhōu.
In the tenth month of winter, on the *bǐngxū* day,
Guìzhōu rebels captured Táigǒng and Huángpíng.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Guān Wén suppressed the bandits in Xiāngyáng
and pacified the area.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Yīng Guì and Qín Dìngsān were ordered to jointly suppress the Nian rebels in Wōhé and Méngchéng.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Ānhuī imperial forces recovered Hézhōu.
Muslim rebels in Dàlǐ, Yúnnán, murdered officials and occupied the city.
On the *rényín* day,
Xiāngfán rebels attacked Dèngzhōu.
Henán rebels moved from Xiàyì to harass Xúzhōu.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Zhèjiāng imperial forces recaptured Xiūníng.
Former Governor Zhāng Fèi was granted the rank of Third Grade Minister.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the Right River garrison in Guǎngxī mutinied,
and Láo Chóngguāng suppressed them.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Hé Guìqīng reported that Zhèjiāng troops advanced and captured Yīxiàn,
and Huīzhōu was cleared.
Shào Càn reported that imperial forces repelled Nian rebels,
and Xúzhōu was relieved of siege.
Cháng Qīng was appointed General of Yīlí.
In the eleventh month, on the *yǐmǎo* day, the first day of the month,
the *Xuānzōng Shílù* was completed.
Péng Yùnzhāng was appointed Grand Secretary,
Wēng Xīncún was appointed Associate Grand Secretary,
Xǔ Nǎipǔ was appointed Minister of Works,
and Zhū Zūn was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Yúnnán imperial forces recovered Yáozhōu.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Wénchāng was promoted to be worshipped in the middle sacrifice.
Zhèng Kuíshì was ordered to move his army to join Yīng Guì in suppressing the Nian rebels,
and Qín Dìngsān was to join Fú Jì in suppressing the Ānhuī rebels.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Shèng Bǎo was ordered to proceed to the Ānhuī military camp.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Grand Secretary Wénqìng died.
The British in Guǎngdōng instigated conflict by inspecting a ship,
and shelled the city.
The gentry and local militia angrily counterattacked them,
killing several hundred people.
Yè Míngchēn was ordered to handle the situation as circumstances required.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Bó Jùn was appointed Grand Councillor.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Jiāngxī rebels captured Fǔzhōu.
On the *wùyín* day,
Liú Chángyòu, a circuit intendant of the Chǔ Army, successively recovered Yuánzhōu and Fēnyí in Jiāngxī.
He was granted the title of Surveillance Commissioner,
his parents were granted enfeoffment of the third rank,
and Governor Luò Bǐngzhāng was granted a peacock feather.
Yīng Guì reported breaking the rebel stronghold at Zhìhéjí.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Emperor visited Grand Secretary Wénqìng's residence to offer condolences.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Hú Línyì recovered Wǔchāng.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Guān Wén recovered Hànyáng.
Both received imperial praise.
Guìzhōu forces attacked and captured Dūyún.
In the twelfth month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
Húběi imperial forces attacked and captured Lǎohékǒu.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Emperor prayed for snow.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Prince Sù Huáfēng was appointed Grand Minister of the Interior.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Húběi has been repeatedly occupied by rebels,
and the common people who survived the devastation of war
are in a pitiable state.
Now that Wǔchāng and Hànyáng are recovered,
it is urgent to relieve the suffering of the people.
Regarding money and grain, remission and deferment should be distinguished.
How should disaster victims be consoled and cared for?
Quickly deliberate and report."
Húběi imperial forces successively recovered Wǔchāng Xiàn and Huángzhōu Fǔ city.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Hú Línyì reported on military and administrative governance in Húběi.
He received an imperial decree stating:
"Since you have indeed clear insights,
you should implement them with actual effort."
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Guān Wén reported on suppressing local bandits in Suízhōu,
and the bandit chief was captured.
Later reports confirmed that imperial forces successively recovered Xìngguó, Dàyě, Qíshuǐ, Qízhōu, and Guǎngjì.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Ānhuī and Zhèjiāng imperial forces recovered Níngguó,
and Hé Guìqīng was granted a peacock feather.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
due to Húnán imperial forces suppressing the rebels in Chóngyáng and Tōngchéng, Húběi,
the expectant Daoist Wáng Zhēn was granted the title of Surveillance Commissioner.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Guān Wén reported that imperial forces burned rebel ships in Jiǔjiāng.
An imperial edict ordered Zēng Guófān to encourage his officers and soldiers
to move from Húběi down the river
for a joint suppression.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Shāndōng imperial forces killed Nian rebel leader Wáng Fāngyún.
Húběi imperial forces recovered Huángméi.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Guì Liáng was appointed Grand Secretary,
and Bó Jùn was appointed Associate Grand Secretary.
Tán Tíngxiāng was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì,
and Zēng Wàngyán was appointed Governor of Shǎnxī.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the seasonal sacrifice was performed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In this year,
the regular taxes for 165 prefectures and counties in Zhílì, Jiāngsū, Shāndōng, Shānxī, Hénán, Húnán, and Guìzhōu provinces that suffered from disasters or rebels were remitted,
and the salt tax for six saltworks in Jiāngsū was also remitted to varying degrees.
Cháoxiǎn [Korea] paid tribute.
In the seventh year, *dìngsì*, spring, first month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
Yíliáng reported that Fù Zhènbāng had recovered Gāochún,
and Zhāng Guóliáng had advanced to Qùróng.
Hé Guìqīng reported on the relief and suppression efforts in Zhèjiāng Province,
defending its own borders internally
and protecting neighboring territories externally.
An imperial decree expressed commendation.
Quánqìng was appointed Minister of War (Bīngbù Shàngshū),
Wéncǎi as Minister of Works (Gōngbù Shàngshū),
and Sùshùn as Left Censor-in-Chief (Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ).
Bandits in Tàipíng Prefecture, Guǎngxī, were suppressed.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Xīlíng'ā and Chóng'ān were recalled to the capital.
Shèngbǎo was given the rank of Deputy Lieutenant-General (Fù Dūtǒng)
to assist in bandit suppression matters.
Wáng Lǚqiān returned to his hometown,
and Lǐ Jūn was ordered to take over river defense.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Yè Míngchēn reported a victory in defending against and suppressing the English barbarians.
The imperial decree stated:
"Controlling foreign barbarians
is not comparable to internal affairs.
The former events at Dìnghǎi
can be taken as a warning.
Therefore, it is essential to manage the situation appropriately,
lest regrets arise later.
I will not control from afar.
Let all Governors and Governors-General of Sūzhōu, Zhílì, Mǐn, and Zhè know this."
Second month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
Zēng Guófān reported the recovery of Jiànchāng.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Emperor attended the imperial lecture (Jīngyán).
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Húběi government troops recovered Yíchāng.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Húi bandits rebelled in Bīnchuān, Yúnnán.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Húběi rebels captured Yuǎn'ān and Jīngmén,
but government troops defeated and drove them away.
On the *dìngwèi* day,
Ānhuī bandits attacked Huángméi,
and Dūxīng'ā defeated them.
Ānhuī bandits captured Lù'ān.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Yīngguì and Shèngbǎo reported suppressing the Niǎn bandits,
recapturing Wūlóngjí,
and advancing towards Gùshǐ.
Third month, on the *guǐsì* day (first day of the month),
Zēng Guófān observed mourning for his father.
He was granted leave for the funeral,
and Yáng Zàifú was ordered to temporarily command the navy,
with Péng Yùlín as his deputy.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Húběi government troops under Táng Xùnfāng and Bāyáng'ā suppressed bandits in Nánzhāng,
defeating them,
and the bandit leader Liú Shàngyì surrendered.
Xiàoshùn, the Provincial Commander-in-Chief (Tídú) of Guìzhōu, was routed at Dūyún
and died.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Xiāngfán rebels captured NèiXiāng, Hénán,
but government troops recovered it.
An imperial edict instructed Yíliáng
"to secretly investigate whether Zhāng Guóliáng and Héchūn are in disagreement.
The key for a commander in the army
is to win the hearts of the people.
If one fails to control properly,
causing capable generals to be unwilling to exert themselves,
the consequences will be severe."
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Emperor plowed the sacrificial field (*jìtián*).
On the *dìngmǎo* day,
Qílíng was appointed Governor (Xúnfǔ) of Jiāngxī.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
for the achievement of recovering Wǔchāng and Hànyáng,
Assistant Commander Duōlóng'ā was employed as a Deputy Lieutenant-General.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Héngchūn reported that Húi bandits were causing disturbances,
and there was a shortage of generals.
He requested that Wáng Guócaí, the General-in-Chief (Zǒngbīng) of Yúnyáng Garrison, be transferred to Yúnnán to assist in suppression,
which was granted.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Jiāngxī government troops attacked Jǐngdézhèn,
but were unsuccessful.
Dūshī Bì Jīnkē died in battle,
and Liú Chángyòu was again defeated at Xīnyù.
On the *xīnsì* day,
bandits in Héngzhōu, Guǎngxī, caused trouble,
and Guǎngdōng government troops suppressed them.
Yè Míngchēn reported that English ships had withdrawn from the provincial river.
The imperial decree stated:
"It is always best to put an end to this conflict
and prevent border troubles from arising."
Summer, fourth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
Héngchūn reported the surrender of Húi bandits in western Yúnnán.
Délèkè Duōěrjì reported that Russia requested to send an envoy to the capital,
and an edict ordered them to be stopped.
On the *dìnghài* day,
Jiāngxī rebels fled into Fújiàn,
capturing Shàowǔ and Guāngzé.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Yíliáng was dismissed due to illness,
and Hé Guìqīng was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Guìzhōu rebels captured Yǒngcóng.
On the *dìngyǒu* day,
Húnán reinforcements under Liú Chángyòu captured Xīnyù, Jiāngxī.
Fifth month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
Sàyíng'ā died,
and Liú Zhēng was appointed acting General-in-Chief of Xī'ān.
Húběi government troops recovered Fèngxīn, Jìng'ān, and Ānyì in Jiāngxī.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Lǐ Mèngqún reported going to relieve Lúzhōu
and recovering Yīngshān.
Fújiàn rebels captured Tīngzhōu.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Délèkè Duōěrjì reported that the Russian envoy had arrived in the capital via Tiānjīn,
and Tán Tíngxiāng was ordered to appease him.
Intercalary fifth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
Héchūn reported the recovery of Lìshuǐ.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Zēng Guófān requested to complete his mourning period,
but an imperial edict graciously retained him,
still ordering him to quickly proceed to Jiāngxī to oversee the army.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Húi bandits caused trouble in Wǔdìng Prefecture, Yúnnán,
and government troops suppressed them.
Lǐ Mèngqún reported defeating the fleeing rebels from Huòqiū,
receiving imperial commendation.
On the *dìngyǒu* day,
Shèngbǎo attacked Zhèngyángguān,
but was unsuccessful.
Circuit Intendant (Dàoyuan) Jīn Guāngzhù died,
and was posthumously awarded the title of Provincial Administration Commissioner (Bùzhèngshǐ).
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Russians arrived at Hǎilánpào with troops,
built camps and mounted cannons,
demanding trade.
Yìshān was ordered to refuse them.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Hé Guìqīng requested that Prefect (Zhīfǔ) Wēn Shàoyuán be reinstated,
to manage the Lùhé local militia.
An edict ordered that troops from Jílín and Hēilóngjiāng, who had been serving abroad for a long time,
be gradually withdrawn.
On the *rényín* day,
Qìngyīng reported that Khokand was colluding with Húi bandits,
occupying Yīngjíshā'ěr city,
and troops were assembled to suppress them.
Zhāng Guóliáng was appointed Provincial Commander-in-Chief (Tídú) of Húnán.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Fújiàn government troops recovered Guāngzé and Tīngzhōu,
and the occupying bandits fled to Liánchéng,
where they were defeated.
Sixth month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
Shūxīng'ā was summoned to the capital,
and Sāng Chūnróng was appointed Governor (Xúnfǔ) of Yúnnán.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Fújiàn government troops recovered Shàowǔ.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Jiāngnán government troops recovered Qùróng,
Héchūn was granted the title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent (Tàizǐ Shàobǎo),
and Zhāng Guóliáng was awarded a yellow riding jacket (huángmǎguà).
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Wáng Zhēn reinforced Jí'ān, Jiāngxī,
winning consecutive battles,
and was awarded the heroic title Bātúlǔ.
On the *dìngmǎo* day,
bandits in Nányáng, Hénán, were suppressed.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Fújiàn government troops recovered Tàiníng and Jiànníng.
Russian barbarians arrived in Tiānjīn to present a national letter,
and Wénqiān was ordered to refuse it.
The Yǒngdìng River overflowed.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Húi bandits attacked the provincial capital of Yúnnán,
and Héngchūn committed suicide.
Upon hearing of the event,
Wú Zhènyù was appointed Governor-General of Yúnguì,
Wáng Qìngyún as Governor-General of Sìchuān,
and Héngfú as Governor of Shānxī.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Jiāngxī government troops recovered Lóngquán.
On the *wùyín* day,
Xǔ Nǎizhāo was ordered to assist in military affairs in Jiāngnán,
and Zhāng Liàngjī was given a fifth-rank title
to assist in bandit suppression matters in Yúnnán.
Autumn, seventh month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
Lǐ Mèngqún reported the recovery of Huòshān.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Hénán government troops recovered Dèngzhōu.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Yìshān was ordered to meet with the Russian envoy to survey and demarcate the borders on both banks of the Hēilóng River.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Guìzhōu government troops recovered Jǐnpíng.
Húběi government troops achieved a great victory in attacking and suppressing Huángméi,
but General-in-Chief Wáng Guócaí died bravely in battle,
and was posthumously awarded the title of Provincial Commander-in-Chief (Tídú),
with a pension and an ancestral shrine built for him.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Dūxīng'ā was ordered to assist in Guānwén's military affairs.
On the *jǐyǒu* day of the eighth month, the first day of the lunar month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the government forces in Fújiàn recovered Nínghuà.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
the government forces in Jiāngxī recaptured Ruìzhōu.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Fǎfúlǐ reported the recapture of Yīngjíshāěr (Kashgar) Muslim City,
and the lifting of the siege of Hànchéng.
On the *wùyín* day,
Guān Wén and Hú Línyì reported that Húběi Province was completely pacified.
An imperial decree was issued:
"Hú Línyì shall personally lead his troops to attack and capture the rebel city of Xiǎochíkǒu,
and then, taking advantage of this prestige, proceed to recover Jiǔjiāng,
to revitalize the entire situation."
Previously,
Lín Yì had secretly memorialized that to protect È Province and recover Jīnlíng,
the only way was to first take Jiǔjiāng,
then recover Ānqìng,
only then could the strategic points be grasped.
Therefore, the imperial edict followed his suggestion.
On the *gēngchén* day of the ninth month,
Wáng Zhēn, the circuit intendant of Húnán assisting Gàn, died in the army.
He was posthumously granted the title of Provincial Administration Commissioner (Bùzhèngshǐ).
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Shèng Bǎo reported the recapture of Zhèngyángguān,
and also reported that Miáo Pèilín, a student from Fèngtái, was gathering a militia.
An imperial decree was issued:
"It is proper to show him trust,
to dispel any rebellious tendencies."
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Fǎfúlǐ reported the recovery of Kāshígáěr (Kashgar) Muslim City.
On the *gēngyín* day,
rebels in Húběi captured Shūchéng.
Niǎn bandits in Hénán captured Nányáng.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the government forces in Jiāngxī recaptured Dōngxiāng.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the Húnán government forces assisting Qián (Guìzhōu) recaptured Lípíng.
In the tenth month of winter, on the *wùshēn* day, the first day of the lunar month,
Guān Wén and Hú Línyì reported that
Lǐ Xùbīn and others, advancing by both land and water,
had captured Húkǒuxiàn City in Jiāngxī.
Shèng Bǎo and Yuán Jiǎsān reported that
General Zōngbīng Zhū Liántài, Shǐ Róngchūn, and others had attacked and suppressed the Niǎn bandits,
and destroyed the rebel stronghold of Hánwéi.
Jiǎng Wèiyuǎn and Tóng Pānméi reported that
they had suppressed the Miáo and Sectarian bandits,
killing and capturing many,
and the Dūyún rebels had retreated.
The government forces in Hénán defeated the rebels in Nánzhāo,
and proceeded to suppress the remaining bandits in Yùzhōu and Bìyáng.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Lǐ Mèngqún suppressed the Niǎn bandits in Dúshān,
but was unsuccessful,
and his army collapsed.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Húběi reinforcements, Lǐ Xùbīn and others, captured Péngzé.
The government forces in Guǎngxī recovered Nánníng.
On the *wùchén* day,
Hú Línyì memorialized on the accumulated abuses of the grain transport system,
requesting a reform of the regulations for collection
to meet military expenses.
This was granted.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Hénán rebels entered Wǔshèngguān,
and directly assaulted Shāngnán.
The Shǎnxī government forces repelled them.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Yáng Zàifú was appointed Provincial Military Commander (Lùlù Tídū) of Fújiàn.
Lǐ Xùbīn was appointed Provincial Administration Commissioner (Bùzhèngshǐ) of Zhèjiāng.
On the *wùyín* day of the eleventh month, the first day of the lunar month,
Yīng Guì reported that Délèngtài had defeated the rebels in Lúshì,
and Qiū Lián'ēn had defeated the rebels in Xīchuān.
Ānhuī rebels captured Hézhōu and Huòshān.
Yáng Zàifú recaptured Wàngjiāng, Dōngliú, and Tónglíng.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Luò Bǐngzhāng reported that Jiǎng Yìlǐ and Jiāng Zhōngjùn, while assisting in suppressing rebels in Guǎngxī,
won consecutive battles,
and proceeded to besiege Pínglè.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Hú Línyì recommended commoners Wàn Húquán, Sòng Dǐng, Zōu Jīnsù, and others.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Guōěrkā (Gurkhas) submitted a memorial expressing loyalty,
and precious gifts were bestowed upon them.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Déxīng'ā and others reported the recapture of Guāzhōu.
An imperial decree expressed commendation and encouragement,
and granted them double-eyed peacock feathers (shuāngyǎn huālíng) and the hereditary post of Cavalry Commander (qí dūwèi shìzhí).
Wēng Tóngshū was employed as a Vice-Minister (Shìláng).
Jū Diànhuá was given the additional title of Provincial Military Commander (Tídū).
On the *wùxū* day,
Hé Chūn reported that together with Zhāng Guóliáng, they had recaptured Zhènjiāng.
Hé Chūn was granted double-eyed peacock feathers (shuāngyǎn huālíng) and the hereditary post of Light Chariot Commander (qīngchē dūwèi shìzhí).
Zhāng Guóliáng was granted the hereditary post of Cavalry Commander (qí dūwèi shìzhí).
Hé Guìqīng was granted the title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent (Tàizǐ Tàibǎo).
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Yīng Guì reported defeating the rebels in Rǔzhōu,
and that western Yù (Hénán) was pacified.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Yǒngdìng Hé River was successfully closed (dike repair completed).
On the *xīnhài* day of the twelfth month,
Qí Líng reported that Zēng Guóquán had captured Jíshuǐ.
Luò Bǐngzhāng and Láo Chóngguāng jointly reported that the government forces had captured Pínglè.
Guǎngxī rebels captured Qìngyuǎn.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Shèng Bǎo, the Deputy Commander-in-Chief (Fù Dūtǒng) overseeing the suppression of bandits in three provinces, requested that all troops in Wǎn (Ānhuī) be placed under his command.
An imperial decree was issued:
"Shèng Bǎo is still brave,
if he can curb his impulsiveness
and rein in his arrogance,
he can be a useful talent.
Why need he make such a request himself?"
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the British entered the provincial capital of Guǎngdōng,
and abducted Governor-General Yè Míngchén.
An imperial edict dismissed Míngchén from his post,
appointed Huáng Zōnghàn as Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng,
and Bó Guì as acting Governor-General.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Lǐ Mèngqún reported that Cantonese and Niǎn bandits had combined forces and moved eastward,
approaching Shāng and Gù.
Shèng Bǎo was ordered to guard against them strictly.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the joint ancestral sacrifice was performed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple (Tàimiào).
In this year,
taxes were remitted for two hundred and thirty-five prefectures, sub-prefectures, counties, and garrisons in provinces such as Zhílì, Jiāngsū, Shāndōng, Shānxī, Hénán, Shǎnxī, Húnán, and Guǎngxī.
The assigned taxes (éfù) for four indigenous counties in Guǎngxī that suffered from disaster and rebel attacks were differentiated.
Cháoxiān (Joseon) and Liúqiú (Ryukyu) paid tribute.
In the spring of the eighth year, on the *jǐmǎo* day of the first month,
Tóng Pānméi was dismissed,
and Jiǎng Yùlóng was appointed Provincial Military Commander (Tídū) of Guìzhōu.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
an imperial edict instructed Wáng Yìdé to prepare for coastal defense.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the government forces in Jiāngxī recovered Línjiāng.
On the *gēngwǔ* day of the second month,
the government forces recaptured Língguān,
and advanced to besiege Jīnlíng.
Hé Chūn was granted the additional title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent (Tàizǐ Tàibǎo),
Zhāng Guóliáng was granted double-eyed peacock feathers (shuāngyǎn huālíng).
General Zōngbīng Hǔ Kūnyuán, who died in battle, was given generous posthumous benefits and a hereditary post (shìzhí).
On the *dīngchǒu* day of the third month, the first day of the lunar month,
Shèng Bǎo reported success in suppressing rebels,
and the siege of Gùshǐ was lifted.
An imperial decree expressed commendation.
On the *wùyín* day,
Russian ships arrived in Tiānjīn.
An imperial edict instructed Tán Tíngxiāng to defend and block them.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the government forces north of the Jiāng (Yangtze) River recaptured Jiāngpǔ.
Circuit Intendant (Dàoyuán) Wēn Shàoyuán was reinstated.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Fú Jì reported the recovery of Hézhōu.
Guìzhōu rebels captured Dūyún,
and former Provincial Military Commander (Tídū) Tóng Pānméi died there.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day bǐngwǔ, the first day of the month,
Tán Tíngxiāng reported that the Russians were not abiding by the old agreement of Xīng'ān,
and requested to use the Wūsūlǐ Hé and Suīfēn Hé as the boundary.
The envoy still requested to proceed to the capital.
An imperial decree was issued, stating:
"Boundary demarcation has already been assigned to high-ranking officials for joint investigation.
Envoys are not permitted to enter the capital at this time.
Reject them."
On the day dīngwèi,
rebels from Jiāngxī infiltrated Fújiàn,
capturing Zhènghé and Sōngxī.
On the day wùshēn,
the Russians requested land route travel,
and the British and French requested to enter the capital once every few years.
An imperial edict forbade this.
Shèng Bǎo reported that the Niǎn rebel leader Lǐ Zhàoshòu had surrendered,
which was permitted.
On the day jǐyǒu,
rebels in Ānhuī captured Máchéng,
and another contingent captured Méng, Bó, Huái, and Sù.
An imperial edict ordered Yuán Jiǎsān to suppress them.
An imperial edict permitted Russian trade,
but forbade their entry to the capital.
On the day gēngxū,
rebels captured Hézhōu.
Muslim rebels from Dàlǐ in Yúnnán captured Shùnníng.
On the day wùshēn,
an imperial edict instructed Tán Tíngxiāng to inform the British and French
that tax reductions and increased market access
would await the conclusion of the Guǎngdōng affairs.
At that time, their request to come to the capital would be discussed again.
On the day gēngxū,
rebels from Jiāngxī captured Chángshān and Kāihuà.
Commander-in-chief Zhōu Tiānshòu was ordered to be granted the title of Tídū
to exclusively manage Zhèjiāng's defense,
and circuit intendant Ráo Tíngxuǎn was to defend Qúzhōu.
On the day xīnhài,
Tán Tíngxiāng presented the credentials from the United States.
An imperial edict permitted reduced tax rates and increased ports,
but still forbade entry to the capital.
On the day yǐmǎo,
British and French warships entered Dàgū,
and the government forces retreated.
Sēnggélínqìn was ordered to prepare troops in Tōngzhōu.
On the day wùwǔ,
Jiāngxī government forces recaptured Yúdū, Lè'ān, Chónghuà, and Yíhuáng.
On the day xīnyǒu,
British and French ships arrived at Jīnguān.
Grand Secretary Guìliáng and Minister Huāshānà were ordered to handle foreign affairs.
Jiāngxī rebels infiltrated Zhèjiāng,
capturing Chǔzhōu and Yǒngkāng.
On the day rénxū,
Húběi government forces recaptured Jiǔjiāng.
Guān Wén and Hú Línyì were promoted to Tàizǐ Shǎobǎo,
and Lǐ Xùbīn was granted the title of Xúnfǔ.
On the day yǐchǒu,
British and French troops retreated to Sānchàhé.
They sent a communication with the Russians and Americans,
requesting that the negotiating ministers must have full powers to act expediently
before discussions could begin.
Guìliáng and others reported this,
and an imperial edict permitted acting expediently.
On the day bǐngyín,
Sēnggélínqìn was ordered to carry the seal of an Imperial Commissioner
to manage defense affairs.
On the day wùchén,
Shèng Bǎo reported the recapture of Lù'ān.
On the day yǐsì,
an imperial decree ordered military camps in all provinces to train cavalry.
On the day gēngwǔ,
Hé Chūn was ordered to concurrently manage Zhèjiāng military affairs.
British ships departed Dàgū.
Guìliáng and others reported that the British treaty involved trade in Zhènjiāng and Hànkǒu,
steamship navigation on the Cháng Jiāng,
the selection of sites for consulates,
and an ambassador stationed in the capital.
The Emperor hesitated for a long time but then permitted it.
In the fifth month, on the day bǐngzǐ,
Ānhuī rebels captured Huáng'ān in Húběi.
Guìliáng and Huāshānà reported
that the British envoy was pressing hard for a treaty
and refused to see Qíyīng.
Qíyīng requested to return to the capital,
but an imperial edict stopped him.
On the day wùyín,
Niǎn rebels captured Huáiyuǎn.
On the day jǐmǎo,
Yìshān requested to cede the vacant land on the left bank of the Hēilóng Jiāng to the Russians.
On the day jiǎshēn,
Guìliáng and others reported that Russia had agreed to mediate,
and permission was first granted for Russians to travel by land.
On the day dīnghài,
court officials were ordered to gather and discuss war and peace,
choosing the lesser of two evils.
On the day wùzǐ,
Guìliáng and others reported that the British said China was merely procrastinating,
and they would abandon peace for war.
Grand Secretary Yùchéng died,
and the Emperor personally attended to offer condolences.
On the day gēngyín,
Guìliáng and others presented fifty-one articles of treaties concluded with Britain and France,
and also requested to first conclude treaties with Russia and America.
On the day rénchén,
Húběi government forces recaptured Huáng'ān and Máchéng.
Fújiàn government forces recaptured Guāngzé.
Guǎngdōng government forces recaptured Wúzhōu in Guǎngxī.
Qílíng was ordered to dispatch Xiāo Qǐjiāng, Zhāng Yùnlán, and Wáng Kāihuà's forces from Qímén to reinforce Zhèjiāng.
On the day guǐsì,
Qíyīng returned to the capital without permission
and was granted death by suicide.
Grand Tutor Dù È died,
and the Emperor personally attended to offer condolences.
On the day yǐwèi,
Zēng Guófān was ordered to manage Zhèjiāng military affairs.
On the day dīngyǒu,
Guìliáng and Huāshānà presented the treaties with Russia, America, Britain, and France.
An imperial decree was issued, stating:
"Since the official seal has already been affixed,
and now a vermilion endorsement agrees with the proposals,
the four nations should be informed to proceed accordingly.
As for the commercial tariff,
it shall be discussed in Shànghǎi."
On the day gēngzǐ,
Jiāngběi government forces recaptured Jiāngpǔ and Lái'ān.
On the day jiǎchén,
all foreign ships completely withdrew from the inland rivers.
Assistant Minister of Personnel Kuāng Yuán and Grand Academician of the Grand Secretariat Wén Xiáng were ordered to serve as acting Grand Councilors.
In the sixth month, on the day jǐyǒu,
Guìliáng, Huāshānà, Assistant Minister Jī Pǔ, and Director of the Department of Armaments Míng Shàn were ordered to go to Jiāngsū to discuss commercial tariffs.
Jiāngxī government forces recaptured Xīnchéng and Jīnxī.
On the day guǐchǒu,
rebels in Fújiàn captured Jiànníng.
Fúxīng was dismissed,
and Zhōu Tiānshòu was made to command his troops to reinforce Fújiàn.
Sāng Chūnróng was summoned to the capital,
and Zhāng Liàngjī was appointed Governor of Yúnnán.
On the day jiǎyín,
Guǎngxī forces recaptured Xiàngzhōu.
On the day dīngsì,
rebels in Zhèjiāng captured Shòuchāng,
but government forces quickly recaptured it.
Fú Jì was dismissed for incompetence,
deprived of his official title,
and relieved of his post.
Wēng Tóngshū was appointed Governor of Ānhuī.
On the day gēngshēn,
regarding the incident at Tiānjīn,
Tán Tíngxiāng was dismissed,
and Tídū Zhāng Diànyuán was exiled.
Qìng Qí was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì,
and Yù Míng was appointed General of Shèngjīng.
On the day dīngmǎo,
Circuit Intendant Zhào Yìnchuān of Fújiàn died
while suppressing rebels.
Zhèjiāng government forces recaptured Chángshān and Kāihuà.
Jiāngxī reinforcement troops recaptured Wǔyì, Yǒngkāng, and Qúzhōu in Zhèjiāng,
and the siege of Shàoxīng city was lifted.
Ruì Lín requested funds to repair and build the Tiānjīn barracks, ramparts, and artillery forts.
Sēnggélínqìn was ordered to handle this.
On the day xīnwèi,
the Russians requested to stop the provision of sheep for the postal stations.
An imperial edict instructed the Kùlún Minister to cite old precedents and refuse.
On the day rénshēn,
Duàn Chéngshí, a Director in the Board of Punishments, was granted the Fifth-Rank Minister title
to assist in tariff discussions.
Zēng Guófān reported landing at Jiǔjiāng and proceeding to Zhèjiāng,
and an imperial edict commended him.
Zhèjiāng forces recaptured Jìnyún.
In the autumn, in the seventh month, on the *Jiǎxū* day, the first day of the month,
Yìshān and Jǐngchún reported that Russian men had trespassed at Hēihékǒu,
intending to enter the Sōnghuā Jiāng,
and were building houses and installing cannons at Wūsūlǐ.
An imperial edict ordered an investigation into the boundaries between Jílínsheng and Hēilóngjiāngsheng,
and to logically refuse their demands.
On the *Yǐhài* day,
Lǐ Mèngqún was appointed acting Governor of Ānhuī.
On the *Dīngchǒu* day,
following Fǎfúlǐ's request,
the Kashíjiāěr Battalion Commander was promoted to Affairs Minister.
Zhōu Tiānshòu attacked and recovered Chǔzhōu in Zhèjiāng,
and then moved his army to Fújiàn.
On the *Guǐwèi* day,
an imperial edict instructed Zēng Guófān to clear Qúzhōu and Yánzhōu,
and then redirect to reinforce Fújiàn.
On the *Yǐyǒu* day,
Yáng Zàifú recovered Jiàndé in Ānhuī.
On the *Guǐsì* day,
Hú Línyì, Governor of Húběi, mourned his mother's death.
An imperial edict ordered him to observe the mourning period in office,
and granted leave and money for the funeral.
On the *Bǐngshēn* day,
the rebels captured Lúzhōu.
Lǐ Mèngqún was stripped of his office but retained in the army.
Shèngbǎo was appointed Imperial Commissioner
to oversee military affairs in Ānhuī,
and Yuán Jiǎsān was to lead troops to suppress the Niǎn bandits in the three provinces.
On the *Dīngyǒu* day,
the Fújiàn army recovered Jiànyáng and Guāngzé,
while the rebels captured Nínghuà.
On the *Gēngzǐ* day,
Yàn Duānshū was summoned to the capital,
and Hú Xīngrén was appointed Governor of Zhèjiāng.
On the *Rényín* day,
Zhāng Fú's army recovered Lóngquán,
and he was granted a peacock feather.
In the eighth month, on the *Guǐmǎo* day, the first day of the month,
the Tiānjīn navy was re-established.
On the *Jiǎchén* day,
the Fújiàn army recovered Zhènghé and Sōngxī.
Shèngbǎo reported that the Taiping rebels' self-proclaimed King Yīng, Chén Yùchéng, had fled to Diànbù and Liángyuán,
and was directly pressing towards Dìngyuǎn.
On the *Gēngxū* day,
Lǐ Dìngtài suppressed the rebels at Yùshān,
won a victory,
and lifted their siege.
On the *Xīnhài* day,
Jiǎng Yìlǐ's relief army recovered Qìngyuǎn in Guǎngxī,
and he was promoted to Judicial Commissioner.
On the *Bǐngchén* day,
Zhōu Tiānshòu reinforced Fújiàn,
captured Pǔchéng,
and advanced to capture Nínghuà.
The Niǎn bandits captured Fēngxiàn.
On the *Xīnyǒu* day,
the Niǎn bandits fled into Shāndōng,
and captured Shànxiàn.
Yīngguì was transferred to be Governor of Shānxī,
and Héngfú to be Governor of Hénán.
On the *Yǐchǒu* day,
the government army recovered Fēngxiàn.
The Niǎn bandits captured Cáoxiàn,
but it was soon recovered.
Hé Guìqīng requested that the customs surplus be used to supplement military provisions,
which was granted.
On the *Rénshēn* day,
the army north of the Yangtze suffered a defeat at Pǔkǒu,
and Déxīng'ā and Jú Diànhuá were stripped of their posts.
Héchūn reported:
"The defeat at Pǔkǒu has led to the immediate deployment of troops originally sent to reinforce Zhèjiāng directly to Liùhé.
Information suggests that rebels fleeing back from Fújiàn province
will pass through Nínguó and Tàipíng to reinforce Jīnlíng,
which clearly means the city rebels are in dire straits,
and are ordering their forces to cause disturbances everywhere
to divide our military strength.
I request that all routes be ordered to reinforce and suppress on their own,
so as not to disrupt the overall situation."
The Emperor approved this.
In the ninth month, on the *Guǐyǒu* day, the first day of the month,
the Húběi government army under Duōlóng'ā recovered Tàihú.
On the *Yǐhài* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Tiāncháng and Yízhēng have successively fallen,
and Liùhé is in danger.
Although Wēn Shàoyuán has always enjoyed public support,
it is feared he may not be able to hold out for long.
One division of Zhōu Tiānpéi's army is to be immediately dispatched to reinforce Liùhé and Dé'ān,
and another division to go and assist."
On the *Xīnsì* day,
Guānwén and Hú Línyì reported that Lǐ Xùbīn and Dū Xīng'ā had successfully recovered Tóngchéng and Qiánshān by separate routes,
Duōlóng'ā was attacking Shípái,
and Bào Chāo was vigorously attacking Léigōngbù,
all achieving success.
An imperial edict ordered them to coordinate with the navy to advance on Ānqìng.
The Húnán government army recovered Jí'ān,
and officials like the Prefectural Magistrate Zēng Guóquán were promoted according to their merits.
On the *Rénwǔ* day,
Míngyì reported that the Russian case had been resolved through negotiations,
diplomatic credentials exchanged,
and trade initiated.
The rebels captured Yángzhōu,
and Déxīng'ā was stripped of his hereditary rank.
Bǎijùn and Wēng Xīncún were appointed Grand Secretaries,
Guānwén and Zhōu Zǔpéi were appointed Assistant Grand Secretaries.
Ruìlín was transferred to be Minister of the Board of Revenue,
Sùshùn to be Minister of the Board of Rites,
Zhū Fèngbiāo to be Minister of the Board of Revenue,
Chén Fú'ēn to be Minister of the Board of War,
Ruìcháng to be Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs,
and Miánsēn to be Censor-in-chief of the Left.
An imperial decree ordered General Máosānyuán and Chéngmíng to assist Déxīng'ā in military affairs.
On the *Jiǎwǔ* day,
Zhāng Guóliáng captured Yángzhōu,
and then recovered Yízhēng.
Qìngduān reported the capture of Shàowǔ,
and that Fújiàn province was pacified.
On the *Wùxū* day,
Miánxún, the General of Jīngzhōu, died.
Dū Xīng'ā was transferred to be General of Jīngzhōu,
Héchūn to be General of Jiāngníng,
and Zhāng Guóliáng to be Provincial Commander-in-chief of Jiāngnán.
On the *Jǐhài* day,
the rebels captured Liùhé,
and the county magistrate Wēn Shàoyuán died there.
Shàoyuán had defended the precarious city alone,
fighting over a hundred battles for several years,
until his strength was exhausted and it fell.
The Emperor mourned and regretted him,
granted him the posthumous title of Provincial Administration Commissioner,
bestowed generous pensions,
and ordered a memorial shrine built and a posthumous name conferred.
In the winter, in the tenth month, on the *Guǐmǎo* day, the first day of the month,
local bandits caused trouble in Nínghǎi, Zhèjiāng.
Admiral Ālínbǎo suppressed them.
On the *Yǐsì* day,
Shèngbǎo reported the recovery of Tiāncháng,
and that Lǐ Zhàoshòu had exerted effort in the matter.
An imperial edict was issued:
"Lǐ Zhàoshòu is granted the name Lǐ Shìzhōng,
a third-rank title, a peacock feather,
and is to be employed as an Assistant Commander."
On the *Jǐyǒu* day,
Censor Mèng Chuánjīn impeached the *jǔrén* Píng Líng for discrepancies in his examination papers.
Zàiyuán and Duānhuá were assigned to seriously investigate.
On the *Dīngsì* day,
Sēnggélínqìn reported the completion of the Tiānjīn fortresses.
The Emperor praised him
and bestowed an imperial robe.
On the *Jǐwèi* day,
the Jiāngnán government army recovered Lìshuǐ.
On the *Rénxū* day,
Lǐ Xùbīn was ordered to assist Shèngbǎo in handling military affairs in Ānhuī.
On the *Wùchén* day,
an imperial edict stated that the chief examiners and associate examiners for this year's provincial examinations were utterly preposterous.
Upon re-examination of the disputed papers,
there were as many as fifty such cases.
The chief examiner Bǎijùn was immediately dismissed from office,
and the associate examiners Zhū Fèngbiāo and Chéng Tíngguì were temporarily relieved of their duties
pending investigation.
The Emperor ordered Prince Zhuāng Yìrén to learn to serve among the imperial ministers.
In the eleventh month, on the *Rénshēn* day, the first day of the month,
Jílín cavalry was moved to reinforce Yuán Jiǎsān's army.
On the *Yǐhài* day,
Yuán Jiǎsān requested to levy taxes in the three eastern prefectures of Shāndōng to aid military provisions,
which was granted.
On the *Jǐmǎo* day,
Xú Zéchún died.
Zhū Zūn was appointed Minister of the Board of Rites,
and Zhāng Xiánghé was appointed Censor-in-chief of the Left.
On the *Yǐyǒu* day,
the armies reinforcing Fújiàn and Zhèjiāng recovered Pǔchéng and Shùnchāng.
Zhōu Tiānpéi was granted the title of Admiral.
On the *Bǐngxū* day,
Héngfú reported a great victory by the government army against the Niǎn,
and that Hénán province was pacified.
General Fù Zhènbāng was promoted to Admiral,
and Compiler Yuán Bǎocì was granted the valiant title *Bātúlǔ*.
On the *Dīngyǒu* day,
the secondary archive of the Grand Secretariat was robbed.
On the *Jǐhài* day,
Wú Zhènyù was dismissed due to illness.
Zhāng Liàngjī was appointed Governor-General of Yúnnán and Guìzhōu,
and Xú Zhīmíng was appointed Governor of Yúnnán.
On the *Gēngzǐ* day,
the fallen Admiral Dèng Shàoliáng was granted generous pensions and a memorial shrine.
In the twelfth month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
Sòng丞相 Lù Xiùfū was assigned to be worshipped alongside Confucius in the Wénmiào.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Tídū Lǐ Cháobīn recovered Dōngliú and Jiàndé in Ānhuī.
He was granted the *Bātúlǔ* brave title.
Yǒngzhōu Zhèn Zǒngbīng Fán Xiè was impeached and dismissed for riding in a sedan chair.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Zhèng Kuíshì was appointed Zhèjiāng Tídū.
He was put in charge of military affairs in Níngguó.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Lǐ Xùbīn advanced to suppress the rebels in Ānhuī,
but suffered a defeat at Sānhéjí.
He died there.
He was posthumously granted the title of Zǒngdū,
and a shrine was built for him, and he was given a posthumous epithet.
Tóngzhī Zēng Guóhuá was posthumously granted the title of Dàoyuán,
and given a posthumous epithet.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Hé Guìqīng was appointed Qīnchāi Dàchén [Imperial Commissioner]
to manage commercial treaty affairs.
Zhào Dézhé was dismissed,
and Xú Yǒurén was appointed Jiāngsū Xúnfǔ.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Ruìlín was appointed Dàxuéshì.
Sùshùn was transferred to Hùbù Shàngshū,
Línkuí to Lǐbù Shàngshū,
and Ruìcháng to Xíngbù Shàngshū.
A grand sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
In this year,
the land tax quotas for 92 prefectures, departments, and counties in the provinces of Zhílì, Ānhuī, Fújiàn, Húběi, and Guìzhōu that suffered from natural disasters or banditry were remitted.
Additionally, the salt tax for six salt fields in Jiāngsū was remitted with varying degrees.
Cháoxiǎn and Líuqiú presented tribute.
In the ninth year, the spring first month, on the *rénshēn* day, which was the first day of the month,
Guìliáng and others reported that the British, using the pretext of disturbances in Guǎngdōng,
had suspended negotiations and returned to Yuè.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Yuán Jiǎsān was summoned to the capital.
Fù Zhènbāng was appointed to suppress the Niǎn bandits in the three provinces,
with Yīxīng'ā as his deputy.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Jiāngxī government troops recovered Ruìjīn,
and lifted the siege of Ānyuǎn.
Other bandits captured Nán'ān.
Guìliáng and others reported on four articles of the peace treaty.
An imperial decree stated that discussions should be held appropriately after the British envoy returned to Hù.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Fújiàn bandits Zhōu Hóngxī and others surrendered,
and Liánchéng was subsequently recovered.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Ānhuī government troops recovered Jiàndé.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
an imperial decree ordered Húběi to purchase horses and train cavalry.
On the *wùxū* day,
Guìliáng and others reported that the British envoy insisted on proceeding to the capital.
An imperial decree ordered Sēnggélínqìn to strictly guard the seaports.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Dūxīng'ā requested leave.
Duōlóng'ā was appointed to take command of his troops.
An imperial edict ordered sea transport grain boats to avoid barbarian ships.
In the second month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
the Niǎn bandit Xuē Zhīyuán surrendered Jiāngpǔ.
He joined Lǐ Shìzhōng to capture Púkǒu.
He was granted the name Xuē Chéngliáng,
awarded a peacock feather and a third-rank title,
and Lǐ Shìzhōng was promoted to Fùjiàng.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
coastal artillery forts were constructed in Fèngtiān.
Zhèng Kuíshì captured the bandit strongholds at Wānzhǐ and Huángchí.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the Emperor summoned court officials to announce the crimes of corruption in the *wùwǔ* imperial examinations.
According to the proposal by Zàiyuán and Duānhuá,
the chief examiner, Dàxuéshì Bǎi Jùn, was implicated because his household servants swapped endorsed examination papers.
He was sentenced to beheading.
The associate examiner Pú Ān, who was complicit in accepting bribes from Lǐ Hèlíng,
and Luó Hóngyì, who secured a passing grade through bribery,
were both sentenced to beheading.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Zhāng Fú reported that government troops had captured Wùyuán,
and the bandit leaders Zhāng Cóngxiàng and others had pleaded for surrender.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Wēng Tóngshū reported that bandits had captured Liù'ān.
Qìngqí died.
Héngfú was appointed Zhílì Zǒngdū,
and Yīngqǐ was appointed Hénán Xúnfǔ.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Zhāng Guóliáng reported the capture of Yángzhōu and Yízhēng,
and that his returning army subsequently captured Lìshuǐ.
An imperial edict specially commended them,
granting a hereditary post of Qīngchē Dūwèi.
Lǐ Ruòzhū was awarded a yellow riding jacket.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Zēng Guófān reported that his army had reached Nánkāng.
Xiāo Qǐjiāng recovered Nán'ān.
An imperial decree of commendation was received,
and Xiāo Qǐjiāng was granted the *Bātúlǔ* brave title.
An imperial edict assigned compiler Lǐ Hóngzhāng to Yīxīng'ā's command.
In the third month, on the *xīnwèi* day, which was the first day of the month,
former Bùzhèngshǐ Lǐ Mèngqún's troops were routed at Guāntíng.
He died there.
He was posthumously restored to office and given relief.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Yìshān and Jǐngchún reported that Russians had directly reached the Wūsūlǐ Jiāng and Suífēn Hé to select sites for building houses,
and requested a joint survey.
An imperial edict denied this.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Niǎn bandits attacked Xīhuá and Wǔyīn in Hénán.
Former Zǒngbīng Qīu Lián'ēn died there.
He was posthumously granted the title of Tídū,
and given relief.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Guìliáng and others reported that British warships were sailing north,
and that attempts to stop them were unsuccessful.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Tángtóu people in Sìchuān revolted.
Ēnqìng suppressed them,
executing their barbarian leader Dèng Zhū.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Emperor prayed for rain.
On the *gēngyín* day,
due to drought, advice was sought.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Lǐ Jūn died.
Huáng Zàntāng was appointed Dōnghé Hédào Zǒngdū.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Russians were trading on the Hēilóng Jiāng.
They were permitted to be exempt from taxes,
but not to enter Wūsūlǐ or Suífēn without permission.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *xīnchǒu* day, which was the first day of the month,
Shèngbǎo reported the recovery of Liù'ān.
Yīxīng'ā was relieved as assistant,
and Guānbǎo was appointed to assist Fù Zhènbāng in military affairs.
On the *rénchén* day,
Wáng Qìngyún was transferred to Liǎngguǎng Zǒngdū,
and Huáng Zōnghàn to Sìchuān Zǒngdū.
Jiāngxī bandits fled to Chēnzhōu and Guìyáng in Húnán.
Líu Chángyòu defeated and drove them away.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Shèngbǎo reported the surrender of the Niǎn bandit Zhāng Yuánlóng,
and the recovery of Fèngyáng Prefecture and counties,
as well as the recovery of Línhuái Guān.
Nínghé artillery forts were constructed.
On the *wùshēn* day,
local bandits in Yúyáo, Zhèjiāng, revolted.
They were suppressed.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the Russian envoy Sàishànyóu entered the capital by land through Cháhār.
He requested assistance with guns and cannons,
to be delivered to Qiàkètú.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the Emperor prayed for rain again.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Shào Càn was dismissed due to illness.
Yuán Jiǎsān was provisionally appointed Cáoyùn Zǒngdū.
Láo Chóngguāng was transferred to Guǎngdōng Xúnfǔ,
and concurrently held the provisional title of Zǒngdū.
Bandits captured Tiāncháng.
Former Tídū Dé'ān died there.
He was posthumously restored to office and given relief.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Yìshān reported that Russian ships had entered the Sōnghuā Jiāng from the Hēilóng Jiāng, sailing east into the sea.
An imperial decree stated
that they were not allowed to enter Suífēn,
and ordered Tèpǔqīn to send officials to obstruct them.
On the *rénxū* day,
Wáng Yìdé was dismissed.
Qìngduān was appointed Mǐnzhè Zǒngdū,
and Luó Zūndiàn was appointed Fújiàn Xúnfǔ.
On the *guǐhài* day,
it rained.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Sūn Jiānài and 180 others were granted the *jìnshì jíyǐ chūshēn* title with varying ranks.
On the *wùchén* day,
Guǎngdōng government troops recovered Jiāyìng.
Fleeing bandits harassed Liánpíng,
and captured Lèchāng.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day of the fifth month,
an imperial edict commanded Luò Bǐngzhāng to retain Tián Xīngshù, ordering him to return to reinforce Guìzhōu.
Zhào Chēn's army was withdrawn.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
an imperial decree ordered Yìshān to rectify the treaty with the Russians.
On the *xīnsì* day,
an imperial decree ordered Qìngyún to secretly investigate Russians residing in Zhāngjiākǒu and Báichéng.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Zhōu Tiānshòu was made acting Superintendent of Military Affairs for Níngguó.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Russians requested to trade in Sānxìng.
An imperial edict reprimanded Yìshān for handling affairs weakly,
stripped Vice Commander-in-Chief Jílamíng'ā of his post,
and ordered him to be paraded in a cangue in the Wūsùlǐ region.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Guān Wén reported hearing that Shí Dákāi intended to invade Sìchuān.
An imperial edict commanded Zēng Guófān to move his army to Kuízhōu.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Guì Liáng and Huā Shānà reported that the English chieftain had anchored near the capital on the thirteenth day of this month.
Guì Liáng and others immediately galloped back to the capital by post-horse.
Grand Secretary Wēng Xīncún requested retirement,
which was granted.
Jiǎ Zhēn was again appointed Grand Secretary.
Xǔ Nǎipǔ was transferred to be Minister of Personnel,
Zhāng Xiánghé was made Minister of Works,
and Shěn Zhàolín was made Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Luò Bǐngzhāng reported that Shí Dákāi had fled into Húnán.
Liú Chángyòu, Jiāng Zhōngyì, Tián Xīngshù, and other armies attacked and repulsed him.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Sēnggélínqìn reported that English ships, firing cannons, had forced their way into Dàgū.
Our army opened fire and bombarded them,
sinking many ships.
Infantry also landed and challenged for battle.
Our army bravely advanced and attacked,
killing several hundred men.
Their commander, surnamed Hè, was also wounded by cannon fire.
Our army also suffered casualties, including Commander Shǐ Róngchūn and Vice General Lóng Rǔyuán.
The foreign ships immediately exited.
An imperial decree was issued:
"The generals and officers, with concerted effort
and extraordinary bravery,
are first awarded 5,000 *liǎng* of silver,
and further investigation shall be made for commendation."
On the *wùxū* day,
an imperial edict stated that although the foreigners had been punished and deterred,
measures should still be devised to pacify and control them.
Héngfú was immediately appointed to specifically handle pacification,
while Sēnggélínqìn would continue to manage defense.
On the first day of the sixth month, *jǐhài*,
Sēnggélínqìn was bestowed with imperial garments and precious items.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the Niǎn bandits captured Xūyí.
Government troops soon recaptured it.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Tèpǔqīn reported that the Russians in Sānxìng
were stubborn and refused to withdraw.
Jǐngchún was ordered to investigate and handle the matter.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Guǎngxī government troops recaptured Shànglín.
Bandits captured Bīnzhōu.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Zhāng Liàngjī reported that the Muslim bandit Mǎ Línghàn had been executed.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Héngfú reported that American envoys were coming to the capital to exchange treaties,
which was permitted.
On the *guǐsì* day,
all British and French warships departed.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
