Lǐ Ruòzhū was appointed Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Fújiàn Land Forces.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Hé Guìqīng reported that the British and French were successively returning to Shànghǎi.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Chén Yùchéng captured Dìngyuǎn.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Hé Chūn reported a victory of the navy in suppressing bandits.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
Zēng Guófān reported the capture of Jǐngdézhèn
and the recapture of Fúliáng.
On the *wùyín* day,
Shèng Bǎo reported the details of Wēng Tóngshū's defeat.
An imperial decree was issued:
"You, as commander,
only know how to display your own strengths,
and are unwilling to aid others in their failures.
Daily wrangling,
what good does it do!"
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
American envoy Huá Ruòhàn presented his national letter,
and the treaty was sealed
and exchanged in Běitáng.
On the *gēngchén* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"We hear that Shèng Bǎo makes recruiting surrenders his sole achievement.
The surrendered troops have not all shaved their heads,
and Zhāng Yuánméng is even foraging everywhere.
He also reported the recapture of Xūyí,
but that county has no city walls.
The bandits withdrew due to lack of provisions,
so this was a false report to claim credit.
This time, We will not investigate deeply.
You must restrain the wayward
and diligently correct your past wrongs.
Beware!"
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Censor Zhào Yuánmó reported that the Yellow River, flowing north,
had dried up and exposed three to four thousand *qǐng* of riverside farmland.
He requested the establishment of屯田 (túntián) (military colonies),
stationing soldiers among farmers,
which would be more effective than local militias.
The Emperor approved this,
and instructed Yuán Jiǎsān and Gēng Cháng to deliberate and report.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"The princes and grand ministers have continued to clarify and propose punishments for the high officials and their sons involved in the examination fraud case,
and for the officials who facilitated the connections.
In this case, Chéng Bǐngcǎi, after his father Chéng Tíngguì entered the examination hall,
received the connections,
and had his family member transfer them into the hall.
Chéng Tíngguì did not report it.
Chéng Bǐngcǎi is to be executed.
Chéng Tíngguì is spared from death
and exiled to a military post.
Xiè Sēnchí, Pān Zǔtóng, Pān Dūnyǎn, and others are all spared from death
and exiled to Xīnjiāng."
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Luò Bǐngzhāng reported that Shí Dákāi was besieging Bǎoqìng.
Lǐ Xùyí relieved it,
immediately lifting the siege.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Lǐ Ruòzhū was ordered to assist in military affairs in Jiāngnán.
On the first day of the eighth month, *wùxū*,
Chóng'ēn was dismissed.
Wén Yù was made Governor of Shāndōng.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Emperor presided over the Imperial Lectures.
On the *yǐsì* day,
an imperial decree ordered Héng Qí to remain and manage trade affairs in Guǎngdōng.
Shèng Bǎo reported Lǐ Shìzhōng's victory in suppressing bandits,
relieving the sieges of Dìngyuǎn and Chúzhōu.
An imperial edict promoted Lǐ Shìzhōng to Provincial Commander-in-Chief.
Guǎngdōng government troops recaptured Liánshān and Kāijiàn.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Zēng Guófān was ordered to station his troops at Húkǒu.
Dū Xīng'ā was ordered to assume the post of General of Jiāngníng.
Duō Lóng'ā was to take command of his former troops,
overseeing all frontline affairs.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Jǐngchún reported that Russian ships in Sānxìng
had now been ordered to withdraw.
Those in Wūsùlǐ
had not yet complied.
An imperial edict commanded to observe public sentiment
and handle the matter appropriately.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the Americans requested to open trade first,
but because the British and French treaties were not yet settled,
it was rejected.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Luò Bǐngzhāng reported that Shí Dákāi had moved south, capturing Jiānghuá and Yǒngmén,
and was about to enter Guǎngxī.
Liú Chángyòu was now ordered to lead his troops in pursuit and suppression.
An imperial decree was issued,
stating that Tián Xīngshù's army should reinforce Qián (Guìzhōu),
and Lǐ Xùyí's army should return to Húběi to await deployment.
On the *rénxū* day,
the long-haired rebels and Niǎn bandits jointly attacked Shòuzhōu.
Government troops repulsed them.
Censor Chén Qìngsōng reported that the redemption of crimes for sons of high officials involved in the examination case, such as Chén Jǐngyàn, was too hasty.
He requested they still be exiled.
A stern edict rebuked him.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Guǎngdōng government troops recaptured Língshān.
In the ninth month, on the *wùchén* day,
Anhuī bandits captured Huòshān and Xūyí.
Shèng Bǎo repelled them.
Shèng Bǎo was observing mourning for his mother,
but remained in camp to oversee military affairs.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Hú Xìngrén was dismissed.
Luó Zūndiàn was transferred to be Governor of Zhèjiāng.
On the *wùyín* day,
Wáng Qìngyún was dismissed due to illness.
Láo Chóngguāng was made Governor-General of Guǎngdōng and Guǎngxī.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Guān Wén and Hú Línyì reported that Duō Lóng'ā had broken through Shípái in Ānhuī,
defeated the reinforcing bandits,
and captured bandit leaders Huò Tiānyàn and Shí Tíngyù.
An imperial decree conveyed commendation.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Fù Zhènbāng reported pursuing and suppressing Niǎn bandits,
defeating them.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Cáo Shùzhōng reported that Shí Dákāi was besieging the provincial capital of Guǎngxī.
Xiāo Qǐjiāng and Sū Fèngwén, combined with Jiǎng Yìlǐ, attacked in separate routes,
defeating them
and immediately lifting the siege.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *dìngyǒu* day of the first quarter,
the imperial ancestral temple was offered seasonal sacrifices,
and the Emperor personally attended to perform the rites.
Luò Bǐngzhāng memorialized that refugees escaping from the rebels
should be given passports exempting them from capital punishment
and be sent back to their native places.
Those who wished to offer their services
should be allowed to remain in the camps.
An imperial decree was issued,
stating that all provinces could follow this practice.
On the *wùxū* day,
the imperial forces in Yúnnán recaptured Sōngmíng,
and rebel leader Sūn Hàndǐng was killed in battle.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Zēng Wàngyán was appointed acting Governor-General of Sìchuān,
and Tán Tíngxiāng was appointed acting Provincial Governor of Shǎnxī.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Yuán Jiǎsān was appointed Imperial Commissioner
to oversee military affairs in Ānhuī.
Kūang Yuán, a Vice Minister, and Wénxiáng, a Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, were appointed Grand Councilors.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Niǎn bandits in Hénán captured Lányí,
besieged Kǎochéng and Tōngxǔ,
harassed Wèishì,
and scattered into Zhílì and Shāndōng.
On the *wùshēn* day,
General Tián Zàitián was ordered to assist Fù Zhènbāng in military affairs.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Yuán Jiǎsān was appointed Governor-General of Grand Canal Transport.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Shèng Bǎo recaptured Huáiyuǎn.
The imperial forces in Jiāngsū suffered a defeat in suppressing the rebels at Lùhé,
and Lǐ Ruòzhū was dismissed from his post.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the American envoy requested the opening of Cháozhōu and Táiwān as treaty ports.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the imperial forces in Hénán suppressed the Niǎn bandits at Yānlíng,
and the western route was cleared.
On the *rénxū* day,
Míngyì was appointed General of Ùliǎsūtái,
Jǐnglián was appointed Assistant Military Governor of Yīlí,
and Chóngshí was appointed Amban in Tibet.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Guānwén, Zēng Guófān, and Hú Línyì were ordered to make proper plans for the four routes to recover Ānwēi.
In the eleventh month, on the *wùchén* day,
Dian bandits attacked a prefecture,
Wànfú was dismissed from his post,
and Zàoshēng was promoted to Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Sìchuān.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Hé Guìqīng memorialized
that he had learned that England and France would certainly come to provoke trouble next spring.
Héngqí memorialized that British troops were continuing to arrive in Guǎngdōng.
An imperial edict ordered Sēnggélínqìn to pay special attention to the defense of Tiānjīn.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the rebels captured Pǔkǒu,
and General Zhōu Tiānpéi died there,
for which he was granted a hereditary post.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Tèpǔqīn memorialized that Russians had occupied more than fifty settlements on the left bank of the Hēilóngjiāng,
and requested that troops from Xīdānmòěrgēn and Bùtèhā be transferred for Nàěrhúshàn to train,
to organize banner people and conscripted laborers,
and to resist in case of trouble.
This was granted.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Zhāng Fèi was ordered to oversee military affairs in southern Ānhuī.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Zēng Guófān memorialized that Wèi Zhìjùn had surrendered at Chízhōu.
Dian bandits captured a prefecture,
and another band captured Yǒuyáng and Xiùshān.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the imperial forces in Sìchuān recovered Yúnlián, Qìngfú, and Gāoxiàn.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Board of Revenue suffered a disaster (a fire).
In the twelfth month, on the *bǐngshēn* day of the first quarter,
Jiǎng Wěiyuǎn memorialized that Shí Dákāi had gathered over one hundred thousand partisans and invaded Qián from Guì,
intending to spy on Shǔ.
An imperial edict ordered Tián Xīngshù to suppress them.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Emperor went to the Dàgāo Hall to pray for snow.
Bandits in Qiūběi, Yúnnán, caused trouble and killed officials,
and the imperial forces suppressed them.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Hé Chūn memorialized that the imperial forces had broken through the rebel stronghold at Jiāngpǔ,
and the western border of Yángzhōu was cleared.
On the *rényín* day,
Huāshānà, Minister of the Board of Civil Office, passed away.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Hé Guìqīng reported that British and French warships had arrived in Hù.
Tián Xīngshù was appointed Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Guìzhōu.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Xiāng Army reinforcing Qián recaptured Zhènyuǎn.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Jǐngchún memorialized requesting to recruit displaced people and conscripted laborers,
grant them land and establish outposts,
to aid in border defense.
This was granted.
On the *rénxū* day,
Yuán Jiǎsān memorialized that Línhuáiguān had been captured.
An imperial decree expressed commendation,
and it was referred to the Board for discussion.
Mùténg'ā was granted the title of Commander.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
a grand sacrifice was offered at the imperial ancestral temple.
In this year,
the land tax for 157 prefectures and counties in Zhílì, Hénán, Shāndōng, Zhèjiāng, Guìzhōu, and other provinces, which had suffered from disasters or rebels, was remitted to varying degrees.
Cháoxiǎn and Líuqíu paid tribute.
In the spring of the tenth year, *gēngshēn*, in the first month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
the Emperor's thirtieth birthday was celebrated,
and an imperial edict granting extensive favors was issued.
The edict stated that although previous emperors' birthdays involved sacrificial ceremonies
and court audiences,
they should not be held this year.
Foreign officials and foreign vassal states were also suspended from coming to the capital to offer congratulations.
Favors were bestowed upon imperial princes:
Dūn Qùnwáng Yìzōng was promoted to Qīnwáng,
Bèizǐ Yìkuāng was promoted to Bèilè,
and others were granted titles and rewards,
including court officials and provincial officials.
On the *wùchén* day,
former General of Níngxià, Tuōyúnbǎo, passed away.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Shèng Bǎo was relieved of his post as Imperial Commissioner,
to focus solely on suppressing bandits in Hénán,
and Yuán Jiǎsān focused solely on Ānhuī.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Yīngqǐ was demoted for delaying the transport of imperial provisions to the capital,
and Qìnglián was appointed Provincial Governor of Hénán.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Hé Qiūtāo, a secretary in the Board of Punishments, presented his compilation, the *Běijiǎo Huìbiān* in eighty volumes.
The Emperor praised and accepted it,
bestowed the name *Shuòfāng Bèichéng*,
and appointed him to serve in the Màoqín Hall.
On the *rénchén* day,
Yǒufèng was dismissed,
and Quánliàng was appointed General of Chéngdū,
and Zhàntài was appointed Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Sìchuān.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Censor Bái Ēnyòu stated that the defense of Tiānjīn was of great importance,
and requested that backup routes be planned in advance
to ensure complete safety.
An imperial decree stated:
"What you have memorialized is indeed correct,
but stationing troops and planning provisions
is very difficult.
Currently, the defense of Tiānjīn is thorough,
so there is no need to discuss this."
Tèpǔqīn memorialized requesting to recruit Òlúnchūn people into the army.
This was granted.
Zhālāfēntài memorialized requesting to ally with Russia and Gurkha to attack India.
The Emperor said:
"Russia is not friendly.
How can Gurkha be an enemy of England?"
In the second month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
the Emperor attended the imperial lectures.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Liú Yuánhào was appointed Provincial Governor of Guìzhōu.
Yuán Jiǎsān memorialized that Fèngyáng had been recaptured,
and he was bestowed a yellow jacket.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Hé Guìqīng memorialized that the British in Shànghǎi, guided by Chinese merchants,
demanded one million for military expenses.
The Tiānjīn treaty could not be altered,
and they would enter the capital to exchange the treaty.
If not permitted,
they would sail north.
An imperial edict ordered Sēnggélínqìn to strictly prepare the Tiānjīn defense and its backup routes.
The sea transport of grain tribute
was temporarily postponed.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the imperial forces in Húnán recaptured Zhènyuǎn, Guìzhōu.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Niǎn bandits captured Táoyuán,
then went north to Qīngjiāng,
and Gēngcháng retreated to guard Huái'ān.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the Xiāng Army reinforcing Guì recaptured Liǔzhōu and Liǔchéng,
and Daoyuan Liú Kūnyī was granted the title of Judicial Commissioner.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Zhāng Fèi memorialized that the imperial forces had recovered Jiàndé,
but bandits had captured Jīngxiàn and Jīngdé,
and then captured Tàipíng consecutively.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Wōshíhúnbù was appointed Minister of the Board of Rites,
and Chūnyòu was appointed Military Governor of Rèhé.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
an imperial edict ordered Hé Chūn to divide his troops to reinforce Zhèjiāng.
On the *yǐchǒu* day of the third month, the new moon,
Yuán Jiǎsān reported that the imperial army had recovered Qīngjiāng.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Tídū Zhāng Yùliáng was ordered to command troops to reinforce Zhèjiāng.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the rebels captured Hángzhōu,
and Xúnfǔ Luó Zūndiàn died there.
Six days later,
Jiāngjūn Ruìchāng recovered the city.
Ruìchāng, Zhāng Yùliáng, and others were heavily rewarded.
Wáng Yǒulíng was appointed Zhèjiāng Xúnfǔ.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the Emperor tilled the sacrificial field.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Zhèjiāng imperial army recovered Chángxīng, Lín'ān, and Xiàofēng.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Hé Guìqīng reported that foreign ships were invading the north.
On the *guǐmǎo* day of the intercalary third month,
the Sìchuān imperial army recovered Pújiāng,
and the rebels captured Míngshān.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Cáo Shùzhōng was ordered to supervise the army in Sìchuān,
and Liú Chángyòu was appointed Guǎngxī Xúnfǔ.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the rebels captured Lìshuǐ,
and subsequently captured Jùróng.
Zhāng Yùliáng was appointed Guǎngxī Tídū,
and was kept in Sūzhōu to supervise the army,
but was soon ordered to return to Hángzhōu.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Hé Chūn and others reported that Chén Yùchéng led his followers to suddenly attack the main camp,
and the city rebels sallied forth to join the attack.
The imperial army could not resist,
and retreated to defend Zhènjiāng.
On the *rénxū* day,
Wáng Mènglín was appointed Cáo Yùn Zǒngdū.
In the summer, on the *bǐngyín* day of the fourth month,
the Míng dynasty scholar Cáo Duān was enshrined in the Confucius Temple.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the rebels captured Dānyáng,
Zhāng Guóliáng died there,
and Hé Chūn fled to Chángzhōu.
On the *wùyín* day,
an imperial edict ordered all provinces to organize local militias (*tuánliàn*).
Dū Xīng'ē was ordered to supervise military affairs north of the Jiāng River.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
an imperial edict stated that Liǎngjiāng Zǒngdū Hé Guìqīng had repeatedly lost cities,
and ordered his dismissal and arrest for questioning.
Zēng Guófān was appointed acting Liǎngjiāng Zǒngdū.
Bīngbù Lángzhōng Zuǒ Zōngtáng was promoted to a fourth-rank京堂(*jīngtáng*) official,
to assist Zēng Guófān with military affairs.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the rebels attacked Chángzhōu.
Hé Chūn was wounded in battle while resisting,
and died.
Kuí Yù was appointed acting Jiāngníng Jiāngjūn,
to join Bā Dòng'ē in holding Zhènjiāng.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the rebels captured Jiànpíng,
and Zhāng Yùliáng's troops were routed at Wúxī.
On the *rénchén* day,
Zhōng Jùnshēng and 183 others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with various ranks.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the rebels captured Sūzhōu,
and Xúnfǔ Xú Yǒurén died there.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day of the fifth month, the new moon,
Xuē Huàn was appointed Jiāngsū Xúnfǔ,
and temporarily acting Zǒngdū.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Zhōu Mùrùn, the Zhīxiàn of Chángshú County, Jiāngsū, recruited local brave men (*shāyǒng*),
and recovered Jiāngyīn.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the rebels captured Chángxīng, Zhèjiāng,
and besieged Húzhōu.
Xiāo Hànqìng's attempt to relieve the city failed,
and he died.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Zēng Guófān reported on advancing in three columns,
planning to protect Sūzhōu and defend Zhèjiāng,
and also requested the deployment of Shěn Bǎozhēn.
The Emperor praised and approved it.
Dōng Chún was also appointed acting Sìchuān Zǒngdū.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the rebels captured Wújiāng, Kūnshān, and Jiāxīng in Zhèjiāng.
Yùmíng reported that over sixty foreign ships were anchored at the seaports of Jīnzhōu and Xiùyán,
plundering livestock.
On the *gēngxū* day,
an imperial decree ordered Wáng Mènglín to supervise, together with Qiáo Sōngnián, the establishment of the grain supply office (*liángtái*) north of the Jiāng River.
On the *xīnhài* day,
relief was granted to the deceased retired Shìláng Dài Xī,
who was posthumously promoted to Shàngshū,
given a hereditary official position,
had a dedicated ancestral temple built,
and was given the posthumous title Wénjié.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Máo Chǎngxī was ordered to organize *tuánliàn* in Hénán,
and Dù Chuò was ordered to organize *tuánliàn* in Shāndōng.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Lǐ Ruòzhū reported that Xuē Chéngliáng had surrendered and then revolted again,
and had been captured and executed.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Zēng Guófān reported that Bào Chāo and Zhū Pǐnlóng had been dispatched to Qímén,
and that the Húběi army should not be redeployed.
This was accepted.
Yùmíng reported over one hundred foreign ships at the Jīnzhōu sea surface.
Wén Yù reported that approximately ten thousand British and French soldiers had arrived at Yāntái,
and intelligence suggested they might invade north from Dàshān in Hǎifēng.
These reports were all sent to Sēnggélínqìn for his information.
On the *guǐhài* day of the sixth month, the new moon,
an imperial decree approved that Bā'ěrhǔ banner people be allowed to take examinations like others.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
British ships sailed into Běitáng.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the rebels captured Qīngpǔ and Sōngjiāng.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Liú Chángyòu reported the recovery of Qìngyuǎn,
and Shí Dákāi's flight south.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Ruìchāng reported the recovery of Guǎngdé.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Emperor's birthday (*wànshòujié*),
he received congratulations in the main hall.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Dàxuéshì Péng Yùnzhāng was dismissed from duty in the Grand Council.
Shào Càn, Liú Yì, Yàn Duānshū, and Páng Zhōnglù were each ordered to organize *tuánliàn* in their native places.
On the *wùyín* day,
Wáng Yǒulíng reported that retired Dáoyuán Zhào Jǐngxián had recovered Húzhōu.
Xuē Huàn reported the recovery of Sōngjiāng.
On the *gēngchén* day,
British and French troops landed,
and then occupied Běitáng.
The positions of Nánhé Hédào Zǒngdū and all officials of the Huáihǎi Circuit were abolished.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Sēnggélínqìn reported that the British and French forces were strong and arrogant,
making peace talks unlikely.
An imperial edict was received,
entrusting the peace negotiations to Héng Fú,
in consideration of the larger situation.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Zēng Guófān was appointed Qīnchāi Dàchén,
and formally confirmed as Liǎngjiāng Zǒngdū.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
foreigners attacked Xīnhé,
and the imperial army retreated to defend Tánggū.
Luò Bǐngzhāng was ordered to rush to Sìchuān to supervise military affairs.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
a handwritten edict to Sēnggélínqìn stated:
"It has been over half a year since we parted with a handshake.
The situation on both banks of Dàgū is critical.
I presume your heart is burning with worry.
However, the nation's foundation lies in the capital, not at the seaports.
If there is any setback,
you must always retreat to defend Jīn [Tiānjīn] and Tōng [Tōngzhōu],
and absolutely must not stake your life on the forts,
making it a matter of personal gain.
My hand trembles as I write this,
you must strive to obey!"
Xīlíng'ā was ordered to firmly defend Tiānjīn,
and Ruì Lín and Yīlèdōng'ā were to proceed to Tōngzhōu to set up defenses.
In autumn, on the *guǐsì* day of the seventh month,
Bā Dòng'ē was ordered to reinforce Jīntán.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Dàgū forts fell,
and Tídū Lèshàn died there,
for whom generous relief was granted and a shrine was built.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Sēnggélínqìn retreated to defend Tōngzhōu.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the British captured Tiānjīn.
The Zhèjiāng rebels captured Lín'ān and Yúháng.
The Sìchuān rebels captured Qióng [Qióngzhōu], Pú [Pújiāng], and Xīnjīn.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the Jiāngsū rebels re-captured Sōngjiāng.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Chóngshí was appointed acting Sìchuān Zǒngdū.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Yùruì reported that Khokand requested to resume trade as before,
which was granted.
Cháng Qīng was appointed Yīlí Jiāngjūn.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Jīntán fell.
Zhīxiàn Lǐ Huái had defended it for three years,
but no reinforcements arrived.
He died from exhaustion,
and over a thousand gentry and common people died with him.
Shèng Bǎo was ordered to lead the cavalry to defend Tōngzhōu.
In the eighth month, on the day *Guǐhài*,
foreign troops arrived at Tōngzhōu.
Zàiyuán (載垣) lured and captured the British envoy Bāxiàlǐ (巴夏禮) and sent him to the capital.
On the day *Wùchén*,
Ruìlín (瑞麟) and others fought against foreign troops at Bālǐqiáo (八里橋),
but were unsuccessful.
Gōng Qīnwáng Yìxīn (恭親王奕訢) was appointed Imperial Commissioner
to manage the peace negotiations.
On the day *Jǐsì*,
the Emperor proceeded to Mùlán (木蘭),
departing from Yuánmíngyuán (圓明園).
On the day *Dīngchǒu*,
the Emperor stopped at Bìshǔ Shānzhuāng (避暑山莊).
Lǐ Shìzhōng (李世忠) was promoted to Gāngnán Tídū (江南提督) for capturing the rebel general Xuē Chéngliáng (薛成良).
On the day *Wùyín*,
an imperial edict stated:
"The Gāngnán Tídū Zhāng Guóliáng (張國樑) possessed both strategy and courage,
and was full of loyalty and drive.
In the army for ten years,
his military achievements were outstanding,
and he was relied upon as a great wall
for half of the southeast.
This year, the grand encampment scattered,
and he returned to aid and strike the bandits,
but was wounded and drowned.
After successive reports,
We still hoped they were inaccurate.
Now, after several months,
there is no doubt that he sacrificed his life.
If Zhāng Guóliáng were still alive,
how could the area of Sū (蘇) and Cháng (常)
have become so devastated?
Recalling his ultimate service,
Our sorrow deepens.
He is posthumously granted the title of Tàizǐ Tàibǎo (太子太保),
enshrined in Zhāozhōng Cí (昭忠祠),
and a special shrine shall be built for him.
His sons, however many,
shall be sent to the Board for employment."
On the day *Jǐmǎo*,
Dūxīng'ā (都興阿) was ordered to lead troops to the capital's defense,
as requested by Guānwén (官文).
Yùmíng (玉明), Chéngkǎi (成凱), Lèbīn (樂斌), Wényù (文煜), and Yīngguì (英桂) were ordered to lead troops to the capital's defense.
On the day *Xīnsì*,
Héngfú (恆福) was ordered to garrison Gǔběikǒu (古北口) for defense,
and Wú Tíngdòng (吳廷棟) was to manage the transfer of official dispatches.
On the day *Rénwǔ*,
Zhèjiāng (浙江) government troops recaptured Pínghú (平湖) and Jiāshàn (嘉善).
Guǎngdōng (廣東) government troops recaptured Lèchāng (樂昌) and Rénhuà (仁化).
On the day *Wèǐ*,
bandits in Jiāngsū (江蘇) captured Chángshú (常熟).
Yuánmíngyuán (圓明園) suffered a disaster,
Cháng Pín (常嬪) passed away,
and Nèiwùfǔ Dàchén (內務府大臣) Shàngshū Wénfēng (文豐) died by suicide.
On the day *Gēngyín*,
Gōng Qīnwáng (恭親王) presented a memorial requesting the return of Bāxiàlǐ (巴夏禮) to the British army.
Xuē Huàn (薛煥) impeached Féng Zǐcái (馮子材) for going to aid Jīntán (金壇),
but holding back his troops,
leading to the fall of the city.
An edict mildly reprimanded him.
In the ninth month, on the day *Rénchén*,
Shèngbǎo (勝保) was appointed Imperial Commissioner
to command the reinforcing armies.
An imperial decree ordered Gōng Qīnwáng Yìxīn (恭親王奕訢) to notify the British
not to repair the fortifications north of the city
and to proceed quickly with the treaty negotiations.
On the day *Jiǎwǔ*,
the British and French envoys entered the city.
Dàxuéshì Péng Yùnzhāng (彭蘊章) and Shàngshū Xǔ Nǎipǔ (許乃普) requested to be relieved due to illness,
which was granted.
On the day *Jǐhài*,
Qìnglián (慶廉) and Yīngguì (英桂) were ordered to station their troops for deployment.
On the day *Xīnchǒu*,
bandits captured Níngguó (寧國),
and Zhōu Tiānshòu (周天受) died there.
On the day *Jiǎchén*,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng (左宗棠) was ordered to oversee military affairs in Zhèjiāng (浙江).
On the day *Yǐsì*,
the peace negotiations were concluded.
Gōng Qīnwáng Yìxīn (恭親王奕訢) memorialized requesting that the agreement be promulgated domestically and internationally,
and that it be strictly adhered to as agreed.
The Russians were permitted to station troops in Wūsūlǐ (烏蘇里) and Suífēn (綏芬).
Aid troops from various provinces were halted.
An imperial decree ordered Yīngguì (英桂) to return to the capital.
A western tour was discussed.
On the day *Wùshēn*,
Lǐ Ruòzhū (李若珠) reported the recapture of Jiāngyīn (江陰).
On the day *Xīnhài*,
bandits captured Huīzhōu (徽州),
and the city-defending Dàoyuán Lǐ Yuándù (李元度) abandoned the city and fled.
On the day *Guǐchǒu*,
bandits in Zhílì (直隸), Shāndōng (山東), and Hénán (河南) rose simultaneously,
and Sēnggélínqìn (僧格林沁) was ordered to suppress them.
On the day *Gēngshēn*,
Gōng Qīnwáng Yìxīn (恭親王奕訢) reported that the foreigners had retreated to Tiānjīn (天津),
and appealed for the Emperor's return to the capital.
In the tenth month, on the first day *Xīnyǒu*,
an edict stated that as the weather was getting colder,
the return to the capital would be temporarily postponed.
Tián Xìngshù (田興恕) was appointed Guìzhōu Tídū (貴州提督).
The deceased Tídū Zhōu Tiānshòu (周天受) and Zhōu Tiānpéi (周天培) were granted hereditary posts,
shrines were built for them, and posthumous titles were conferred;
Dàoyuán Fúxián (福咸) and others were enshrined alongside them.
On the day *Rénxū*,
Liú Yuánhào (劉源灝) was appointed Yún-Guì Zǒngdū (雲貴總督),
and Dèng Érhéng (鄧爾héng) was appointed Guìzhōu Xúnfǔ (貴州巡撫).
On the day *Jiǎzǐ*,
an imperial decree ordered Wénqiān (文謙) and Héngqí (恆祺) to manage trade affairs,
and Wú Tíngdòng (吳廷棟) to oversee defense matters.
Wén'ān (文安) was appointed Húnán Tídū (湖南提督).
Féng Zǐcái (馮子材) was appointed to oversee military affairs in Zhènjiāng (鎮江).
On the day *Bǐngyín*,
Gōng Qīnwáng Yìxīn (恭親王奕訢) memorialized requesting the exchange of the Russian treaty,
and asked for the use of the imperial seal,
which was granted.
On the day *Xīnwèi*,
Russia presented firearms and cannons.
On the day *Guǐyǒu*,
an imperial decree ordered Lèbīn (樂斌) and Yīngguì (英桂) to return to their posts.
On the day *Gēngchén*,
Yán Shùsēn (嚴樹森) was appointed Hénán Xúnfǔ (河南巡撫),
and Máochàngxī (毛昶熙) was appointed to oversee the Nian bandits in Hénán (河南).
On the day *Xīnsì*,
Dūxīng'ā (都興阿) was ordered to oversee military affairs north of the Jiāng (江),
with Lǐ Ruòzhū (李若珠) as his deputy.
Zǒngbīng Tián Zàitián (田在田) was appointed to take over the suppression of bandits in Xú (徐) and Sù (宿),
with Huái-Xú Dào Wú Táng (吳棠) assisting in the management.
In the eleventh month, on the day *Xīnmǎo*,
Shèngbǎo (勝保) memorialized requesting that Dàshùn-Guǎng Dào Liányīng (大順廣道聯英) be solely responsible for river defense,
and that his reports be approved,
which was granted.
On the day *Guǐsì*,
Wēng Tóngshū (翁同書) presented a memorial outlining the need to heed Heaven's warnings,
strengthen the national foundation,
recruit talented individuals,
train the capital garrisons,
and contest strategic positions.
An imperial rescript stated:
"The proposal to recruit talented individuals,
has more disadvantages than advantages.
The rest have been perused."
On the day *Jiǎwǔ*,
bandits in Zhèjiāng (浙江) captured Xīnchéng (新城), Lín'ān (臨安), and Fùyáng (富陽).
On the day *Yǐwèi*,
Wáng Mènglín (王夢齡) memorialized reporting victory in bandit suppression,
with Sānhé (三河) cleared,
and requested control over Huáng Kāibǎng's (黃開榜) naval forces,
which was granted.
On the day *Gēngzǐ*,
Zēng Guófān (曾國藩) memorialized that Bào Chāo (鮑超) and others had recaptured Yīxiàn (黟縣).
On the day *Xīnchǒu*,
Lǐ Ruòzhū (李若zhū) requested to retire to care for his parents,
and Zēng Bǐngzhōng (曾秉忠) was appointed in his place.
On the day *Guǐmǎo*,
as Hángzhōu (杭州) was relieved of its siege,
Ruìchāng (瑞昌), Wáng Yǒulíng (王有齡) and others were generously rewarded.
Ruìchāng (瑞chāng) memorialized that Qìngduān (慶端) had exerted himself to protect the borders of Zhèjiāng (浙江),
and requested generous awards.
An imperial rescript stated:
"Without distinction of region,
these are all duties within your responsibilities as a high official.
The selection of governors-general and governors
comes from the imperial court's decree,
not something you can presumptuously request."
On the day *Wùshēn*,
Chéngqí (成琦) was ordered to jointly investigate the eastern border of Russia with Jǐngdūn (景惇).
On the day *Guǐmǎo*,
Zhèjiāng (浙江) army's Zhāng Yùliáng (張玉良) recaptured Yánzhōu (嚴州).
On the day *Jiǎyín*,
Guānwén (官文) and Hú Línyì (胡林翼) memorialized that Chén Yùchéng (陳玉成) intended to invade Huái (懷) and Tóng (桐),
and Duōlóng'ā (多隆阿) combined forces with Lǐ Xùyí (李續宜) to intercept and suppress them,
defeating them soundly,
killing over ten thousand bandits.
Duōlóng'ā (多隆阿) was bestowed with a Yellow Jacket,
and Lǐ Xùyí (李續宜) was promoted to the second rank.
In the twelfth month, on the day *Xīnyǒu*,
Xīlíng'ā (西凌阿) and Guóruì (國瑞) were ordered to assist Sēnggélínqìn's (僧格林沁) military affairs.
On the day *Bǐngyín*,
Zhāng Liàngjī (張亮基) was ordered to remain and manage military affairs in Yúnnán (雲南).
On the day *Jǐsì*,
the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Tōngshāng Shìwù Yámén (總理各國通商事務衙門) was first established,
and Gōng Qīnwáng Yìxīn (恭親王奕訢), Guìliáng (桂良), and Wénxiáng (文祥) were appointed to manage it.
Chónghòu (崇厚) was appointed Sānkǒu Tōngshāng Dàchén (三口通商大臣),
and Xuē Huàn (薛煥) concurrently managed trade affairs in Shànghǎi (上海) and other places.
Bannermen were permitted to learn foreign languages and scripts.
On the day *Jǐsì*,
Tián Xìngshù (田興恕) was appointed Imperial Commissioner
to oversee military affairs in Guìzhōu (貴州).
On the day *Bǐngzǐ*,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng (左宗棠) memorialized that his supervising army had recaptured Déxīng (德興) in Jiāngxī (江西) and Wùyuán (婺源) in Ānhuī (安徽),
and he was granted the third rank of Jīngqīng (京卿).
On the day *Yǐyǒu*,
Guānwén (官文) and Zhōu Zǔpéi (周祖培) were appointed Dàxuéshì (大學士),
Sùshùn (肅順) Assistant Dàxuéshì (大學士),
Shěn Zhàolín (沈兆霖) Hùbù Shàngshū (戶部尚書),
and Zhū Fèngbiāo (朱鳳標) Bīngbù Shàngshū (兵部尚書).
On the day *Wùzǐ*,
a joint sacrifice was offered at Tàimiào (太廟).
That year,
the regular and outstanding tax levies of the three provinces of Jiāngsū, Zhèjiāng, and Ānhuī were remitted.

Additionally, the regular tax levies of four hundred and one prefectures, counties, and garrisons in provinces such as Zhílì, Shāndōng, Hénán, Jiāngxī, Húběi, Húnán, Fújiàn, and Guǎngxī, which had suffered from disasters or banditry, were adjusted accordingly.
The total population of the empire was counted as 262,092,4675 individuals.
The grain stored in granaries amounted to 5,231,920 *dàn*, 4 *dǒu*, 6 *shēng*, 5 *hé*, and 1 *sháo*.
Cháoxiǎn paid tribute.
In the eleventh year, *xīnyǒu* (1861),
His Majesty was at Mùlán.
On the *gēngyín* (1st) day of the first month of spring,
His Majesty held court at the Suīchéng Diàn to receive congratulations.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
an imperial edict announced that the imperial procession would return on the thirteenth day of the second month.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Zēng Guófān reported that Yáng Zàifú had suppressed the rebels,
recaptured Dūchāng,
and lifted the siege of Nánlíng.
Tián Zàitián reported that the Niǎn bandits had attacked Dàngshān,
were repelled,
and he was promoted to the rank of Tídū.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Wēng Tóngshū was summoned to the capital,
and Lǐ Xùyí was appointed Governor of Ānhuī.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Fú Jì was appointed General of Chéngdū.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
rebels captured Xiàofēng,
and Hángzhōu declared martial law.
On the *rényín* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Since the beginning of the reign,
a special amnesty should be granted.
Those who are usually not pardoned by a general amnesty shall also have their sentences reduced or commuted."
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng's troops recovered Ráozhōu and Dūliáng.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Héng Fú was relieved due to illness,
and Wén Yù was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì,
Tán Tíngxiāng as Governor of Shāndōng,
Dèng Ěrhéng as Governor of Shǎnxī,
and Hé Guànyīng was appointed acting Governor of Guìzhōu.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Sēnggélínqìn reported that the Niǎn bandits had infiltrated Shāndōng,
and a force was dispatched to pursue and suppress them.
They reached Hézé,
but suffered a defeat.
An imperial decree stated:
"Sēnggélínqìn commands heavy troops,
and the northern region relies on him as a screen.
Yet, with weary and hungry soldiers,
he pursued a rapidly expanding enemy,
with no support from the flanks.
It is fitting that he suffered a defeat.
He possesses courage,
but lacks prudence.
He should select new soldiers and generals,
guard key positions strictly,
and act only after careful planning;
he must not advance rashly again."
On the *wùshēn* day,
an imperial edict to Yuán Jiǎsān and others stated:
"Since the Niǎn bandits have coerced law-abiding citizens,
it is not appropriate to indiscriminately execute them.
They should be earnestly persuaded
and measures should be taken to disperse them.
Those who surrender shall be pardoned,
and those who kill bandits shall be rewarded.
Lǐ Shìzhōng should also be informed to recruit and pacify them accordingly."
On the *xīnhài* day,
Guìzhōu government troops recaptured Dúshān.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Wēng Tóngshū reported that Chén Fǔliàn and Miáo Pèilín had plundered Shòuzhōu,
and were acting extraordinarily defiant.
An imperial edict instructed Lǐ Xùyí to handle the matter as he saw fit.
Hénán Niǎn bandits invaded Dōngmíng and Chángyuán.
On the *jǐwèi* (1st) day of the second month,
Yúnnán government troops recaptured Jìnnìng.
On the *rénxū* day,
the Jīnzhōu Naval Camp in Fèngtiān was re-established.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
an imperial edict approved the return of French church land in Shāndōng,
and ordered that in cases of foreign disputes in Zhílì and other provinces,
officials should handle them discreetly and request instructions from the throne,
and not shirk responsibility.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Zhāng Yùliáng's army recaptured Jiāngshān and Chángshān.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Zēng Guófān reported that Zuǒ Zōngtáng defeated the rebels at Jǐngdézhèn,
and Bào Chāo defeated the rebels at Shíményángtáng.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Zhèjiāng troops recaptured Fùyáng.
Bandits in Cháoyáng, Rèhé, captured the city;
Kèxīng'ā was ordered to suppress them.
Míng Yì and Míng Xù were ordered to jointly survey the Russian border,
and Yīng Yùn and Kuí Yīng were to handle trade with the Russians.
Niǎn bandits attacked the Wén Hé;
Deputy Commander Yīxīng'ā and Commander Téng Jiāshèng fought against them and died in battle.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Chén Yùchéng gathered Niǎn bandits and attacked Qíshuǐ in Húběi from Yīngshān;
Hú Línyì was ordered to return with his troops to counter them.
On the *gēngchén* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"A previous decree
set a date for the imperial procession's return.
However, in the past ten days,
My health has not fully recovered.
Therefore, await another decree in autumn."
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the King of Cháoxiǎn sent an envoy to pay respects at the imperial sojourn.
A gentle decree stopped him,
and bestowed upon him brocades, precious artifacts,
and his envoy.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
an imperial edict ordered the selection of soldiers to practice with firearms and cannons sent by Russia.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the local militia in Hēilóngjiāng was disbanded and returned to farming.
On the *jǐchǒu* (1st) day of the third month,
an imperial edict appointed Chónglún and Chónghòu as ministers to handle treaty negotiations, granting them full discretionary powers.
Assistant Minister Chéng Qí was ordered to go to Xīngkǎi Hú to jointly survey the Russian border demarcation.
Dàoyuan Liánjié was granted the rank of fourth-grade metropolitan official
to manage river defenses.
On the *rénchén* day,
Prince Gōng Yìxīn requested to go to the imperial sojourn to inquire about His Majesty's health.
His Majesty replied with a handwritten decree:
"Half a year has passed since we parted,
and I often think of clasping hands and talking.
However, I have had a continuous cough recently,
and occasionally bloody phlegm,
so I still need quiet recuperation
and should not speak too much.
Let us wait until autumn to talk face-to-face."
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
an imperial edict ordered that the First Imperial Prince begin schooling on the seventh day of the fourth month,
and Lǐ Hóngzǎo was appointed his tutor.
On the *wùxū* day,
Dū Xīng'ā reported that the naval vessels of Zhèn and Yáng had deteriorated with age,
and requested that Guǎngdōng be ordered to purchase and transport red-painted ships for use;
this was approved.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Shèng Bǎo was ordered to oversee the suppression of bandits in Zhílì and Shāndōng.
Jiǎ Zhēn was appointed acting Governor of Ānhuī.
On the *gēngxū* day,
British and French troops withdrew from the provincial capital of Guǎngdōng.
On the *xīnhài* day,
former Grand Secretary Péng Yùnzhāng was appointed acting Minister of War.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Zhèjiāng rebels captured Hǎiyán, Pínghú, and Zhàpǔ;
Deputy Commander Xīlíng'ā died.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Guǎngxī local bandits captured Tàipíng Fǔ and Yǎnglì Zhōu.
On the *jǐwèi* (1st) day of the fourth month of summer,
Yán Shùsēn reported that bandits attacked Rǔníng,
and Dàoyuan Zhāng Yào repelled them.
On the *wùchén* day,
Shāndōng Niǎn bandits and sectarian rebels successively captured seven counties in Guǎntáo.
Sēnggélínqìn entered Téngxiàn and fortified his position;
Shèng Bǎo was ordered to dispatch troops to reinforce him.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"I have heard that various places are soliciting donations,

including designated donations, borrowed donations, cannon boat donations, acreage donations, rice donations, provisions donations, dike construction donations, boat donations, house donations, salt donations, plank donations, and 'living' donations.
The names are too numerous and confusing,
and the officials involved are disorderly.
In reality, much is extorted from the people,
but little goes to the public coffers.
In recent years, military expenses have been enormous,
and We have had no choice but to rely on the resources of the people and merchants.
However, only if every drop goes to the public coffers
and is used sparingly
will it truly be effective.
If the demands are endless like this,
impoverishing the people,
what kind of government system will remain?
All ministers and governors-general,
you should strictly investigate,
eliminate corrupt officials and parasites,
to fulfill My intention."
On the *yǐhài* day,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng defeated the rebels at Lèpíng.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Shāndōng sectarian rebels attacked and besieged Dàmíng;
Liánjié repelled them.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Ānhuī rebels again invaded Zhèjiāng,
captured Chángshān and Jiāngshān,
and advanced to threaten Qúzhōu.
In the fifth month, on the day `Guǐsì`,
Tián Zàitián reported that Miáo Liàn had invaded Fúlí.
An imperial edict ordered Sēnggélínqìn to dispatch troops to reinforce them.
On the day `Jiǎwǔ`,
Dèng Érhéng was murdered in Qǔjìng.
Liú Yuánhào was ordered to investigate and handle the matter.
Yīng Qǐ was appointed Governor of Shǎnxī.
On the day `Gēngzǐ`,
Shèng Bǎo reported the recapture of Guǎntáo.
On the day `Xīnchǒu`,
Jiǎ Zhēn and Lǐ Shìzhōng were ordered to assist Yuán Jiǎsān in military affairs.
On the day `Jiǎchén`,
Duōlóng'ā was ordered to assist Guān Wén and Hú Línyì in military affairs.
On the day `Yǐsì`,
the rebels captured Shòuchāng, Jīnhuá, Lóngyóu, Tāngxī, and Chángxīng in Zhèjiāng,
then advanced to capture Lánxī and Wǔyì.
An imperial decree urged Zuǒ Zōngtáng to go to their aid.
In the sixth month, on the first day `Wùwǔ`,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day `Gēngshēn`,
Zēng Guófān and Hú Línyì reported:
"Since our army laid a long siege to the provincial capital of Ānqìng,
the rebel chieftain Chén Yùchéng led his followers back to relieve Ānqìng,
and firmly constructed four redoubts outside Jíxián Guān on Chìgāng Lǐng.
Bào Chāo and Chéng Dàjí, in conjunction with Duōlóng'ā's cavalry, made strenuous efforts to advance and suppress them,
bombarding them day and night.
On the first day of the fifth month,
three redoubts surrendered.
Those who were coerced were released,
while all the old 'long-haired' rebels were executed.
Liú Cānglín, the rebel occupying the first redoubt,
absconded stealthily overnight.
Bào Chāo annihilated him at Mǎtàshí,
and the rest were almost completely wiped out by the navy,
with Liú Cānglín's body being identified, dismembered, and displayed as a warning."
An imperial edict of commendation was received.
Brusya (Prussia) exchanged treaties for trade.
On the day `Xīnyǒu`,
Russians were permitted to trade in Kùlún and Qiàkètú.
On the day `Yǐchǒu`,
the Qīntiān Jiān reported that on the first day of the eighth month,
the sun and moon would be in conjunction,
and five planets would be in alignment.
An imperial edict stated
that this need not be recorded in the imperial archives.
On the day `Jiǎxū`,
the rebels captured Suìchāng, Sōngyáng, and Yǒngkāng in Zhèjiāng.
On the day `Bǐngzǐ`,
Muslim rebels attacked and harassed Kāshígá'ěr.
An imperial edict ordered Jǐnglián to proceed to Ākèsū for defense and suppression.
On the day `Bǐngxū`,
the Zhèjiāng government forces recaptured Chángxīng.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day `Dīnghài`,
an imperial edict stated that if the annual sacrifices by princes and dukes to the two imperial tombs in autumn
should be impeded by rising waters,
they could wait on the road until the path cleared,
then proceed.
If they did not arrive by the appointed time,
the guarding `Bèi​lè` and dukes would perform the rites.
On the day `Jiǎwǔ`,
Zēng Guófān reported the recapture of Huīzhōu, Ānhuī.
On the day `Wùxū`,
a temple was decreed for Yáng Xīn,侍衛 `Zhāoyǒng Hóu` (Marquis of Illustrious Courage) from Sìchuān, who died in battle.
On the day `Xīnchǒu`,
the Emperor was unwell.
On the day `Rényín`,
the Emperor's illness became critical.
Princes and high officials were summoned to write an imperial decree in vermillion,
establishing the eldest imperial son as Crown Prince.
On the day `Guǐmǎo`,
the Emperor passed away at the traveling palace,
aged thirty-one.
In the tenth month,
the imperial coffin was moved to the capital.
In the twelfth month,
a respectful posthumous title was bestowed.
In the ninth month of the fourth year of Tóngzhì,
he was interred in Dìnglíng.
Commentary states: Wénzōng encountered a period of grave misfortune,
personally facing an era of distress.
Foreign powers pressed for treaties,
while internal rebellions erupted,
a full twelve years passed in an instant,
without a single day of peace.
Yet he was able to appoint worthy and talented individuals,
and possessed deep insight to respond to all situations.
In levying taxes, he first prevented excessive burdens;
in governing the military, he carefully maintained control.
The selection of his chief assistants
all stemmed from his strategic calculations.
If he had been granted more years to rule,
how could there have been later hidden troubles?
Annals 21, Annals of Mùzōng 1

Mùzōng, who "continued the heavenly mandate, initiated good fortune, held the central position, rectified the state, preserved greatness, established merit, was sagacious, wise, sincere, filial, trustworthy, diligent, respectful, benevolent, broad-minded, and resolute," the Emperor `Xiǎndì`,
whose personal name was Zàichún,
was the eldest son of Wénzōng.
His mother was Empress Xiàqīnxiǎn, of the Nārā clan.
On the twenty-third day of the third month of the sixth year of Xiánfēng,
he was born in Chúxiù Gōng.
In the eleventh year,
he began his studies,
with compiler Lǐ Hóngzǎo as his tutor.
In the seventh month,
Wénzōng was unwell.
On the day `Rényín`,
his illness became critical.
He summoned the Grand Ministers of the Imperial Guard, Zàiyuán, Duānhuá, Jǐngshòu, and Sùshùn,
and Grand Councilors Mùyìn, Kuāngyuán, Dùhàn, and Jiāo Yǒuyíng to announce his establishment as Crown Prince.
He ordered Zàiyuán, Duānhuá, Jǐngshòu, Sùshùn, Mùyìn, Kuāngyuán, Dùhàn, and Jiāo Yǒuyíng to assist in governing affairs.
On the day `Guǐmǎo`,
Wénzōng passed away.
Chén Fú'ēn and Wén Yù were summoned to the traveling palace.
On the day `Jiǎchén`,
the Empress and the Sacred Mother were both honored as Empresses Dowager.
The Grand Council was ordered to sign "Grand Ministers Assisting in Governing Affairs" after all memorials and documents.
On the day `Yǐsì`,
Dūn Qīnwáng, Gōng Qīnwáng, Chún Jùnwáng, Zhōng Jùnwáng, and Fú Jùnwáng were exempted from routine audiences, banquets, bestowals, and kowtows.
Tributes of local products from various provinces were suspended.
On the day `Bǐngwǔ`,
the Shùntiān civil provincial examination was rescheduled for the ninth month,
the `Ēnkē` (special imperial examination) military metropolitan examination for the tenth month,
and the Shùntiān military provincial examination for the eleventh month.
Luò Bǐngzhāng was appointed Governor-General of Sìchuān,
to oversee military affairs.
The Governor-General of Yún-Guì, Liú Yuánhào, was summoned to the capital,
and Fú Jì was appointed to replace him.
Chóngshí was appointed General of Chéngdū,
and soon after was ordered to assist in Sìchuān military affairs.
Húběi government forces recaptured Wǔchāng, Xiánníng, Tōngchéng, and other counties, as well as Yìníng Zhōu in Jiāngxī.
On the day `Wùshēn`,
Jǐngwén was appointed Resident Minister in Tibet.
On the day `Jǐyǒu`,
Gōng Qīnwáng was permitted to go to the traveling palace to pay his respects to the imperial coffin.
On the day `Gēngxū`,
Xuē Huàn requested permission to invite merchants to try transporting Huái salt to fund the military.
This was approved.
On the day `Xīnhài`,
the Cantonese rebels captured Jí'ān.
Guǎngxī government forces recaptured Bīnzhōu.
On the day `Guǐchǒu`,
additional posthumous titles were bestowed upon Emperor Xuānzōng and his empresses.
On the day `Jiǎyín`,
the Cantonese rebels captured Jìng'ān, Wǔníng, and Yìníng (all `Zhōu` and counties).
On the day `Yǐmǎo`,
the reign title was set as Qíxiáng.
In the eighth month, on the first day `Dīngsì`,
the sun and moon were in conjunction,
and five planets were in alignment.
The Cantonese rebels captured Yánzhōu,
but it was soon recaptured.
On the day `Wùwǔ`,
government forces recaptured Xīnchāng, Fèngxīn, Ruìzhōu, and Shànggāo.
On the day `Jǐwèi`,
Jǐnglián was ordered to go to Yè'ěrqiāng to investigate Yīngyùn's unauthorized collection of money and killings.
Zēng Guófān's request was granted,
to move the steamships currently docked in Shànghǎi to Wǎn Jiāng,
for his army to train with them.
On the day `Xīnyǒu`,
Húběi government forces recaptured Dé'ān.
On the day `Rénxū`,
Jiāngxī government forces recaptured Wǔníng and Jìng'ān.
On the day `Guǐhài`,
the will of the deceased Emperor was promulgated.
Shèng Bǎo's army recaptured Púzhōu.
On the day `Dīngmǎo`,
the Niǎn bandits crossed the Grand Canal.
An edict ordered Shèng Bǎo and Sēnggélínqìn to intercept and suppress them,
preventing their flight north.
On the day `Wùchén`,
Hú Línyì requested leave due to illness.
Lǐ Xùyí was ordered to temporarily act as Governor of Húběi.
On the day `Gēngwǔ`,
Censor Dǒng Yuánchún requested that the Empress Dowager temporarily oversee court affairs,
and that one or two `Jiǎn Qīnwáng` (princes of the first rank, usually close relatives) assist her.
Zàiyuán and others drafted an edict to refute and reprimand this.
On the day `Jiǎxū`,
Zēng Guóquán's army recaptured Ānqìng.
On the day `Wùyín`,
Guǎngxī government forces recaptured Xúnzhōu.
On the day `Gēngchén`,
Sìchuān tribal rebels captured Sōngpān.
On the day `Xīnsì`,
in recognition of the merit in recapturing Ānqìng,
Guān Wén and Zēng Guófān were promoted to `Tàizǐ Shǎobǎo` (Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent),
Hú Línyì to `Tàizǐ Tàibǎo` (Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent),
and all were granted the hereditary post of `Qí Dūwèi` (Commandant of Cavalry);
Lǐ Xùyí was awarded a yellow riding jacket;
Yáng Zàifú and Duōlóng'ā were granted the hereditary post of `Yún Qíwèi` (Cloud Cavalry Commandant).
On the day `Guǐwèi`,
the posthumous title of the deceased Emperor was respectfully bestowed as "Emperor Xié​tiān Yìyùn Zhízhōng Chuímóu Màodé Zhènnǔ Shèngxìao Yuāngōng Qiānrén Kuānmǐn Xiǎndì",
with the temple name Wénzōng.
Miáo Pèilín captured Zhèngyáng and Huòqiū,
and besieged Shòuzhōu.
In the ninth month, on the day Bǐngxū, the first day of the month,
the Empress Dowager, the Emperor's Mother, was granted the honorific title Cí'ān.
The Holy Mother, the Empress Dowager, was granted the honorific title Cíxǐ.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Yáng Zàifú's army recaptured Chízhōu.
On the day Rénchén,
Niǎn bandits fled to Sìshuǐ and Gǒngxiàn.
The imperial army repelled them.
Zhāng Liàngjī was summoned to the capital.
An earthquake occurred in Jīnzhōu.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Sichuan army suppressed the Huílǐ bandits.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the memorial by Yuè Bīn and others was approved,
stating that the Sālā Huí bandits had surrendered,
and the imperial army was to be withdrawn.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the Sichuan army recaptured Míngshān.
On the day Rényín,
Duōlóng'ā, Zēng Guóquán, and others recaptured Tóngchéng, Sùsōng, Qízhōu, Huángméi, and Guǎngjì.
Péng Yùlín, Chéng Dàjí, and others recaptured Huángzhōu.
Hú Línyì, the Governor of Húběi, passed away.
Lǐ Xùyí was transferred to be the Governor of Húběi,
to remain stationed at the border of È and Wǎn,
supervising military affairs.
Péng Yùlín was promoted to be the Governor of Ānhuī.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Zhèjiāng imperial army recaptured Yúqián and Chānghuà.
The Yuè bandits fled to Yánzhōu,
and Zhāng Yùliáng's army was defeated.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Britain and France withdrew their garrisons from Guǎngzhōu.
Britain withdrew its cavalry from Tiānjīn.
On the day Yǐsì,
Sēnggélínqìn suppressed the Niǎn who had fled to Qīngzhōu and other places,
and was reinstated as Grand Minister of the Imperial Guard and awarded the Yellow Riding Jacket.
On the day Wùshēn,
the Emperor escorted the late Emperor's coffin back to the capital,
and exempted Chéngdé and Wǎnpíng prefectures and counties from land tax.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Miáo Pèilín rebelled.
Yuán Jiǎsān was ordered to unite with Jiǎ Zhēn's armies to suppress him.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Emperor escorted the Empress Dowager and the Holy Mother, the Empress Dowager, back to the palace.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
for presumptuously altering imperial edicts
and strongly obstructing the regency behind a curtain,
Zài Yuán, Duān Huá, and Sù Shùn were dismissed from their posts.
Jǐng Shòu, Mù Yìn, Kuāng Yuán, Dù Hàn, and Jiāo Yòuyíng were dismissed from the Grand Council.

Gōng Qīnwáng was ordered to collaborate with the Grand Secretaries, the Six Boards, the Nine Ministers, the Hanlin Academy, the Grand Secretariat, and the Censorate to investigate and report according to the law.
Jiǎ Zhēn, Zhōu Zǔpéi, Shěn Zhàolín, and Zhào Guāng memorialized, requesting that political power be controlled by the sovereign,
and also discussed the protocol for the Empress Dowager to summon ministers and the procedures for handling affairs.
Shèng Bǎo memorialized, requesting that the Empress Dowager personally manage major state affairs,
and that a close Prince be appointed as regent.
The Princes, ministers, Grand Secretaries, and others were ordered to deliberate and report their conclusions.
Chún Jùnwáng Yìxuān was summoned to the capital.
On this day, Zài Yuán, Duān Huá, and Sù Shùn were stripped of their noble ranks and offices,
arrested, and interrogated for their crimes.
Ruì Qīnwáng Rénshòu and Chún Jùnwáng Yìxuān were ordered to arrest Sù Shùn and bring him to the capital.
An edict commanded all civil and military yamen to take turns on duty from the sixteenth day of the tenth month onwards.
Bāo Chāo's army recaptured Yánshān.
In this month,
the extra taxes from Xīníng and Niǎnbó, which had been disturbed, were remitted.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Bǐngchén, the first day of the month,
Gōng Qīnwáng Yìxīn was appointed Prince Regent,
to serve in the Grand Council.
Grand Secretary Guì Liáng, Minister of Revenue Shěn Zhàolín, and Vice Ministers Bǎo Yún and Wén Xiáng were all appointed Grand Councillors.
Cáo Yùyīng, Junior Secretary of the Court of Dependencies, was to learn and serve as a Grand Councillor.
Wō Rén, Vice Minister of Revenue in Shèngjīng, was summoned to the capital.
On the day Dīngsì,
an edict was issued requesting advice,
and the palace gates were strictly guarded.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the late Emperor's coffin arrived in the capital,
and was interred in the Qiánqīnggōng.
On the day Gēngshēn,
an edict changed the reign title from Qíxiáng to Tóngzhì.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Gōng Qīnwáng and others proposed that Zài Yuán, Duān Huá, and Sù Shùn be subjected to slow slicing according to the law for great treason.
An edict granted Zài Yuán and Duān Huá permission to commit suicide,
and Sù Shùn was executed by beheading.
Jǐng Shòu, Mù Yìn, Kuāng Yuán, Dù Hàn, and Jiāo Yòuyíng were stripped of their offices.
Mù Yìn was exiled to a military post.
On the day Rénxū,
Chén Fú'ēn, Huáng Zōnghàn, Liú Kūn, Chéng Qí, Dékèjīntài, and Fù Jì were stripped of their offices.
An edict stated that past transgressions would not be investigated,
and ministers were not to request further investigation of factions.
Princes, Dukes, and civil and military ministers, both inside and outside the court, were warned against abusing power and accepting bribes.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Emperor ascended the throne in the Tàihédiàn,
and held court.
An edict was issued to the whole empire,
declaring the next year as the first year of Tóngzhì,
and granting imperial favors both within and outside the court.
Crimes not covered by ordinary amnesty
were all pardoned.
Dūn Qīnwáng, Gōng Qīnwáng, Chún Jùnwáng, Zhōng Jùnwáng, and Fú Jùnwáng were exempted from having their names mentioned in edicts and memorials.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
an imperial decree, due to the difficulty of resources,
warned the Imperial Household Department
that palace utensils
should be used with utmost frugality.
Sēnggélínqìn was reinstated as Bóduōlègátái Qīnwáng.
The Ministry of Justice was ordered to investigate and conclude the Wǔyǔ banknote case.
An edict was issued to both internal and external officials to clear up ordinary lawsuits.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Miáo Pèilín captured Shòuzhōu.
In the southeast, there was a sound like thunder.
An edict ordered the immediate halt of unfinished projects in Rèhé.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
commanders of all routes were warned against embellishing reports and procrastinating,
thereby allowing bandits to harm the populace.
The martial metropolitan examination for the tenth year of Xiánfēng, which had been deferred, was held.
On the day Jǐsì,
General Fēng Zǐcái was ordered to supervise military affairs in Zhènjiāng.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
an edict instructed the Prince Regent and others to assist in managing state affairs,
without avoiding minor disputes.
On the day Rényīn,
an edict instructed commanders to truly assess merits and demerits,
rewarding justly and punishing certainly.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Yuè bandits captured Yánzhōu and Yúháng.
Zēng Guófān was ordered to command military affairs in Sū, Wǎn, Gàn, and Zhè,
exercising control over all officials from governors and provincial commanders downwards.
Ruì Chāng was to assist in Zhèjiāng military affairs.
Zuǒ Zōngtáng, Junior Secretary of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was to go to Zhèjiāng to suppress bandits,
and deploy officials from provincial commanders and brigade generals downwards.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
an edict reiterated that the suburban sacrifices should remain fixed at the Three Ancestors and Five Progenitors,
and the deceased Emperor was to be enshrined in the ancestral temple and called "Zōng".
Grand Secretary Qí Jùnzǎo, Wēng Xīncún, and former Grand Secretary of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Lǐ Tángjiē, who had been granted leave, were reinstated.
Chén Fú'ēn's property was confiscated,
and he was imprisoned and punished.
The imperial army recaptured Wúwéi and Suízhōu.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
court ministers were warned against procrastination in handling affairs.
An edict instructed Guān Wén, Zēng Guófān, and others to properly plan for the suppression and pacification of Miáo militias.
Yuè bandits captured Xiāoshān, Shàoxīng, Jiāngshān, and Chángshān.
Zuǒ Zōngtáng's army was urged to provide swift reinforcement.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Beizi Délèkèsèlèng was released from prison.
On the day Xīnsì,
court ministers deliberated on the regulations for the regency behind a curtain,
and an imperial decree approved the deliberation.
An edict announced the opening of an extra examination.
Originally,
the pearl harvesting in Wūlā had been suspended for eight years.
By this time,
an edict ordered its continued suspension.
On the day Réngwǔ,
Chén Fú'ēn was exiled to Xīnjiāng.
Vice Ministers Bǎo Yún and Dǒng Xún were ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
French troops left Tiānjīn.
In the eleventh month, on the *yǐyǒu* day, the first day of the month,
the Empress Dowagers Cí'ān and Cíxǐ ascended to the Yǎngxīndiàn Hall and listened to government affairs behind a curtain.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
an imperial edict was issued to the provinces regarding disputes between the populace and missionaries,
instructing them to distinguish between good and bad elements
and handle matters impartially.
On the *dīnghài* day,
an edict was issued to define the crimes of those who misappropriated funds from the Hùbù's five-character banknotes.
Officials Xīlín and others were reinstated.
On the *gēngyín* day,
all armies were ordered to recommend military talents.
On the *rénchén* day,
religious bandits in Shāndōng revolted.
Chénglù and others suppressed them.
The bandit leader Yán Xiùlún was captured and executed.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
previously, Zhāng Liàngjī had reported that Hé Yǒubǎo, a vice-general in Yúnnán, had murdered Dèng Érhéng,
suspecting Xú Zhīmíng as the instigator.
At this time,
Zhīmíng embellished his military achievements in a memorial
and requested a reward for Yǒubǎo.
Fú Jì was commanded by edict to investigate the matter,
remove Zhīmíng from his post, and severely impeach him.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Shí Dákāi fled to Suíníng.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
an edict was issued calling for talent from within and outside the government,
citing Zēng Guófān, Hú Línyì, and Luò Bǐngzhāng as models.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Cantonese bandits captured Shàoxīng and Zhūjì.
Wáng Lǚqiān was stripped of his office and arrested for questioning.
On the *rén'yín* day,
Fú Jì was stripped of his office for being timid, hesitant, and taking advantage.
Pān Duó was granted a second-rank button
and appointed acting Governor-General of Yún-Guì.
Sēnggélínqìn suppressed the secret society bandits at Shòuzhāng and other places,
achieving a great victory.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Péng Yùlín was ordered to assist Yuán Jiǎsān in military affairs.
Government troops recaptured Lái'ān.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Gāo Yánhù, a supervising censor, impeached Xú Zhīmíng for greed, debauchery, and absurdity,
as well as the wantonness of the drilling party in Yúnnán province.
Pān Duó was ordered to investigate.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
an imperial decree ordered all provinces to seek out honest and upright officials,
and also to inquire about scholars of suitable conduct and learning.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Wú Táng was appointed Provincial Administration Commissioner of Jiāngníng,
concurrently acting as Governor-General of Grain Transport,
and superintendent of the Jiangbei Grain Bureau.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
the Cantonese bandits captured Chǔzhōu.
In the twelfth month, on the *jiǎyín* day, the first day of the month,
Zēng Guófān was ordered to comprehensively plan the strategy for advancing and suppressing the rebels.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Tán Tíngxiāng was ordered to go to Dōngchāng to plan river defenses.
The religious bandits in Pú and Fàn were suppressed.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Shèng Bǎo memorialized that he had received and pacified bandit leaders Liú Zhànkǎo and Sòng Jǐngshī.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Guó Ruì's army recaptured Fànxiàn.
The Cantonese bandits captured Níngbō, Zhènhǎi, and various districts of Shàoxīng.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
an edict was issued to rectify salt administration.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng was ordered to quickly reinforce Hángzhōu.
Zhāng Yùnlán was put under his command,
and allowed to memorialize on military affairs independently.
On the *rénxū* day,
Kuí Yù, the Vice-General of Jiāngníng, was ordered to assist in military affairs at Zhènjiāng.
Based on Máo Hóngbīn's memorial,
the governors-general, governors, and commanding generals were instructed to select generals according to local conditions,
and not solely rely on Chǔ Yǒng.
Yuán Jiǎsān's army recaptured Dìngyuǎn.
Gurkha's tributary tribute was approved to be presented in the *dīngmǎo* year.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
secret society bandits in Fújiàn captured Fúdǐng,
but it was soon recaptured.
Niǎn bandits from Hénán fled to Zǎoyáng.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Zēng Guófān declined to command the military affairs of four provinces,
which was disallowed.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the posthumous title "Xiàodé Wēnhuì Chéngshùn Cízhuāng Gōngtiān Zànsheng Xiǎnhuánghòu" was bestowed upon Empress Xiàodé.
Qìng Yīng, a Vice Minister of War, was stripped of his office for crimes
and exiled to Xīnjiāng.
Gāngsēng Quèduōbù, a *Zhásàkè bèilè* of Qīnghǎi, was appointed leader of the Left Wing Banner.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Yù Kē was stripped of his office.
Shěn Bǎozhēn was promoted to Governor of Jiāngxī.
Gōng Qīnwáng and Chún Qīnwáng were ordered to oversee Ruìlín, Wénxiáng, and others in managing the Shénjīyíng.
Zēng Guófān memorialized to dispatch Daoist official Lǐ Hóngzhāng to command naval and land forces to Zhènjiāng to plan the recapture of Sūzhōu and Chángzhōu,
which was approved.
The Dēng-Lái-Qīng Dao was stationed in Yāntái
to supervise the customs duties of the Dōnghǎi.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Duān Huá and Zài Yuán's hereditary peerages were reduced to *Bùrùbāfēn Fǔguógōng*.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the annual land tax for Ānhuī, Jiāngsū, and Zhèjiāng that had been affected by the rebels was remitted for the coming year.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Jiāng Zhōngyì's request for full mourning leave was approved.
Tián Xīngshù was appointed acting Governor of Guìzhōu,
and later Hán Chāo was appointed to act in that capacity.
Zhāng Liàngjī was ordered to supervise military affairs in Yúnnán.
Xú Zhīmíng was removed as Governor of Yúnnán,
and Liàngjī was appointed to act in his place.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Duō Lóng'ā's army attacked Lúzhōu.
Shí Dákāi fled to Yuánjiāng and Qiányáng,
approaching the borders of Sìchuān.
Luò Bǐngzhāng and Tián Xīngshù were ordered to jointly attack him.
The Cantonese bandits from Liǎnghuái captured Hángzhōu.
Ruìchāng and Wáng Yǒulíng died in the conflict.
Qìng Duān, the Governor-General of Mǐn-Zhè, was stripped of his office,
but allowed to remain in his post.
Zuǒ Zōngtáng was appointed Governor of Zhèjiāng.
Péng Yùlín declined the governorship
and requested to specialize in suppressing the rebels,
which was granted,
and he was appointed Admiral of the Navy.
Lǐ Xùyí was transferred to be Governor of Ānhuī,
and Yán Shùsēn to be Governor of Húběi.
Zhèng Yuánshàn was appointed Governor of Hénán.
On the *wùyín* day,
Qí Jùnzǎo was appointed Minister of Rites with the title of Grand Secretary.
Péng Yùlín was reappointed as an expectant Vice Minister of War.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Niǎn bandits besieged Yǐngzhōu.
Shèng Bǎo impeached Yán Shùsēn.
An edict instructed him
"to reflect upon himself,
preserve his reputation and integrity,
and live up to the late Emperor's trust."
Based on Xuē Huàn's memorial,
the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén was ordered to consult with Britain and France on borrowing troops to suppress the rebels.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Emperor's second younger brother was posthumously enfeoffed as Mǐn Jùnwáng.
Zuǒ Zōngtáng was urged to advance and take Zhèjiāng.
Shèng Bǎo was ordered to lead his troops to Yǐngzhōu.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Sēnggélínqìn attacked and annihilated the fleeing bandits south of the Hé'nán shore in Cáozhōu.
In the spring of the first year of Tóngzhì (1862), the Rénxū year, the first month, on the Jiǎshēn day,
Empress Dowager Cí'ān and Empress Dowager Cíxǐ held court at Cínínggōng.
The Emperor, leading the princes and high ministers, performed the rites.
He received congratulations at Qiánqīnggōng.
Thereafter, this practice was followed every year.
Línkuí and Zēng Guófān were commanded to assist as Grand Secretaries.
On the Yǐyǒu day,
an imperial decree was issued to consider withdrawing the acreage tax and the lijin tax,
to comfort the families of the officers and soldiers who participated in campaigns,
and to console the descendants of those soldiers who were wounded or died.
As Jiāngxī was pacified,
Bāo Chāo was awarded the yellow jacket.
Lǐ Shìzhōng recaptured Lùhé,
and received a similar reward.
On the Bǐngxū day,
Zēng Guófān and Zuǒ Zōngtáng were ordered to secure Qúzhōu and advance to relieve the siege of Huīzhōu.
Zēng Guófān was commanded to select generals to defend Shànghǎi.
Jiǎng Yìlǐ's forces were transferred to Zuǒ Zōngtáng's army.
On the Gēngyín day,
Shèng Bǎo moved his army to Yǐngzhōu,
and Deputy Commander Zhēkèdūnbù and Circuit Intendant Wáng Róngjí were commanded to take over the defense.
On the Xīnmǎo day,
the Sichuan army recaptured Dānléng,
and the rebel leader Lán Cháodǐng was executed.
The government forces recaptured Píngyuè.
On the Rénchén day,
Lǐ Shìzhōng's army recaptured Tiāncháng.
On the Guǐsì day,
the Guangdong rebels under Lǐ Xiùchéng captured Fèngxián, Nánhuì, and Chuānshā.
Dū Xīng'ā was commanded to blockade the Wúsōng estuary with his boat forces.
On the Bǐngshēn day,
Lè Bīn was dismissed from his post and summoned for questioning
due to his indulgence of bandits which harmed the populace.
Línkuí was appointed acting Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù,
to suppress and pacify the rebellious Muslims with Shěn Zhàolín.
The Guangdong rebels advanced on Shànghǎi.
Xuē Huàn spoke of various British and French officers cooperating in the defense and suppression.
The Emperor praised him for this.
On the Dīngyǒu day,
initially,
Mián Xìng requested a change in the collection of Muslim taxes,
and Jǐng Lián went to Ākèsū to investigate and handle the matter.
By this time,
Jǐng Lián submitted a report impeaching him,
and Mián Xìng was dismissed from his post for his offenses,
and soon after was exiled to Jílín.
The Muslim prince Àimǎtè was sent back to Kùchē for restraint.
A stern warning was issued to the high ministers of the Muslim territories not to collect additional levies.
Yīng Yùn was commanded to investigate and prohibit the private mortgaging of Muslim lands in the various cities of Ākèsū.
On the Wùxū day,
the Guangdong rebels attacked Zhènjiāng,
and Fény Zǐcái's army repelled them.
The Niǎn bandits overran Shùyáng.
Sēnggélínqìn was ordered to consider both north and south.
The government forces recaptured Xīnxìan.
On the Jǐhài day,
Línkuí died.
Lǐ Shìzhōng's army captured Jiāngpǔ and Pǔkǒu.
Qìng Duān was removed from his post,
and Qí Líng was commanded to go to Mǐn (Fújiàn) to take over the military affairs for aiding Zhè (Zhèjiāng).
On the Gēngzǐ day,
Bāo Chāo was promoted to Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Zhèjiāng,
and Fény Zǐcái to Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Guǎngxī.
On the Guǐmǎo day,
Qiáo Sōngnián was commanded to supervise the organization of local militia along the river.
On the Bǐngwǔ day,
the former Governor of Ānhuī, Wēng Tóngshū, was
dismissed from office and arrested for questioning for the loss of Shòuzhōu and Dìngyuǎn;
he was later condemned to beheading.
On the Dīngwèi day,
additional coins were minted for Ākèsū.
On the Wùshēn day,
Wén Yù and others submitted matters concerning the defense of Běitáng,
which were approved.
British and French troops remained stationed at the Dàgū forts.
The Yunnan government forces recaptured Lìjiāng,
and Muslim bandits overran Kūnmíng.
On the Gēngxū day,
the Guangdong rebels overran Sōngjiāng,
and the government forces, joined by foreign troops, met and suppressed them,
defeating them utterly.
The American foreign general Huá Ěr (Frederick Townsend Ward) wished to become a Chinese national,
and was awarded a fourth-rank button and a peacock feather.
On the Rénzǐ day,
Zhāng Liàngjī was commanded to recruit troops to go to Diān (Yúnnán).
On the Guǐchǒu day,
Zhēkèdūnbù and others were ordered to jointly suppress the Niǎn bandits in Hétào.
In the second month, on the Jiǎyín day,
the government forces recaptured Láifèng.
On the Yǐmǎo day,
an imperial decree was issued that the Emperor should enter Hóngdédiàn to study,
with Qí Jùnzǎo and Wēng Xīncún as his tutors.
On the Bǐngchén day,
Zēng Guóquán was promoted to Financial Commissioner of Jiāngsū,
and also ordered to handle military affairs,
without needing to recuse himself.
On the Dīngsì day,
the Guangdong rebels captured Huángyán.
The government forces relieved the sieges of Zhènjiāng and Huīzhōu.
On the Xīnyǒu day,
Duō Huì, the Minister in charge of Xīníng affairs, and Tídū Chéng Ruì, for falsely reporting that Muslim bandits had surrendered,
were both dismissed from their posts and deliberated for punishment;
they were later condemned to beheading.
Lè Bīn was exiled to Xīnjiāng
for his dismissal due to sheltering.
On the Rénxū day,
Dū Xīng'ā was commanded to dispatch troops to station in Tiāncháng and Lùhé,
and Lǐ Shìzhōng to move his troops to Jiāngpǔ and Pǔkǒu,
to work together wholeheartedly.
The Guangdong rebels captured Ānyì,
but it was soon recaptured.
On the Guǐhài day,
the Niǎn bandits besieged Shíxìan.
On the Jiǎzǐ day,
the records of ancient emperors and the memorials of ancient and modern officials submitted by Wō Rén
were displayed in Hóngdédiàn for study and practice.
On the Yǐchǒu day,
Sēnggélínqìn's army achieved a great victory against the Niǎn bandits,
who fled from Shíxìan to Tōngxǔ,
and were pursued and suppressed.
On the Wùchén day,
Shí Dákāi overran Fēngdū.
Tián Xīngshù's request to be relieved as Imperial Commissioner
and lead his troops to Chuān (Sìchuān),
subordinating to Luò Bǐngzhāng, was granted.
Hán Chāo was commanded to plan for defense and suppression in Guìzhōu.
On the Jǐsì day,
Xuē Huàn spoke of the British and French armies jointly suppressing the bandit stronghold at Gāloqiáo,
and capturing it.
The American Báiqíwén (Henry Andrea Burgevine) wished to become a Chinese national,
and was awarded a fourth-rank button and a peacock feather.
On the Rénshēn day,
the Guangdong rebels from Jīnlíng crossed the river and harassed Jiāngpǔ and other places.
Zēng Guófān and Dū Xīng'ā were ordered to dispatch war boats to intercept them.
On the Guǐyǒu day,
Duōlóng'ā's army attacked Lúzhōu.
On the Bǐngzǐ day,
due to the fall of Zhūjìng in Shànghǎi,
Tídū Zēng Bǐngzhōng was dismissed from his post.
The Shànghǎi government forces, joined by British and French armies, suppressed and cleared the bandit stronghold at Xiāotáng.
Chóng Hòu and Chéng Míng were commanded to supervise the maritime defenses of Tiānjīn.
On the Dīngchǒu day,
the hereditary peerages of Prince Zhèng and Prince Yí were restored.
Lǐ Xùyí was ordered to resettle the displaced people in northern Ānhuī.
This month,
the extra taxes for the disturbed areas of Tíngzhōu and other places were remitted.
On the *guǐwèi* day of the third month,
the Niǎn bandits fled to Tàihé.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
permission was granted for British and French gunboats to proceed to the Yangtze River to assist in suppression campaigns.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Cantonese bandits fled to Shànghǎi.
Xuē Huàn's army defeated them.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the bandits captured Qīngtián.
Zheng Yuánshàn's request was granted,
appointing Bùzhèngshǐ Zhāng Yào, who was in mourning, to exclusively handle bandit suppression.
On the *gēngyín* day,
since the first month there had been no rain.
An imperial edict called for self-reflection [xiūxǐng]
and solicited frank advice.
Zuǒ Zōngtáng recaptured Suì'ān.
Sòng Jǐngshī's surrendered followers rebelled at Lányí.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Cantonese bandits attacked Lúzhōu, Hézhōu, and Jiāngpǔ.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Shèng Bǎo's army advanced to reinforce Yǐngzhōu
and achieved a great victory.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Zheng Yuánshàn proposed recalling Sòng Jǐngshī,
allowing him to atone for his crimes by rendering service.
This was approved.
On the *wùxū* day,
Lǐ Xùyí and Zheng Yuánshàn were ordered to assist Shèng Bǎo in military affairs.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
former Fǔyǐn Zhuāng Qílíng responded to the summons,
proposing twelve policies including promoting orthodox learning,
streamlining official careers,
limiting allowances and tax extractions,
and raising military provisions.
The proposals were approved for implementation,
except for discontinuing "nourishing honesty" stipends [yǎnglián] and investigating informal practices [lòuguī],
as these were deemed detrimental to the political system and disallowed.
An imperial edict ordered all provinces to recommend "filial and incorrupt" [xiàolián fāngzhèng] individuals,
stressing the need to find true Confucian scholars.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Shěn Zhàolín was ordered to lead troops to Xīníng to suppress the Sǎ bandits.
On the *yǐsì* day,
for the Wànshòu Festival,
the reception of congratulations was suspended.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Zēng Guófān was urged to divide his forces to reinforce Húzhōu.
On the *dìngwèi* day,
the compilation of "Imperial Governance and Historical Records of Regent Affairs" was completed,
and named *Zhìpíng Bǎojiàn*.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Vice Censor-in-Chief Yàn Duānshū was ordered to Guǎngdōng to supervise *líjīn* collection,
and Wú Táng was ordered to supervise *tuánliàn* in Jiāngběi.
Xuē Huàn was appointed Minister for Trade with the highest official rank [tóupǐn dǐngdài].
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was appointed acting Governor of Jiāngsū.
Hǎi Quán, Vice General Commandant of Jīngkǒu, suffered a defeat against the bandits
and died.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
old and new tribute items due from Huíjiāng were remitted.
That month,
the Emperor personally visited Dàgāo Hall three times to pray for rain.
On the *jiǎyín* day of the fourth month,
an edict instructed the commanding ministers to exercise caution with military provisions [xiǎngxǔ]
and eliminate excessive expenses.
Jǐng Qíjùn presented "Examples of Rulers Through the Ages,"
which the Emperor praised and accepted.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Luò Bǐngzhāng's request to retain Tián Xīngshù to continue handling Guìzhōu military affairs was granted.
On the *dìngsì* day,
the Cantonese bandits captured Yíyáng,
but it was soon recovered.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
it rained.
Bāo Chāo's army recaptured Qīngyáng.
Zēng Guóquán's army recaptured Cháoxiàn, Hánshān, and Hézhōu.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Pǔ Chéngyáo was sent to garrison Tái.
Zēng Guófān and others stated that the request from Sūzhōu gentry to borrow British and French troops to recover Sūzhōu and Chángzhōu
was absolutely unfeasible.
The Emperor endorsed their view.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was ordered to regulate Wá'ěr's Ever Victorious Army.
Lǐ Shìxián, a Cantonese bandit, fled to Jiāngxī.
Shěn Bǎozhēn went to Guǎngxìn to supervise defense and suppression.
Belgium requested to revise the treaty.
An edict instructed Xuē Huàn to carefully deliberate and handle the matter.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the posthumous title of Empress Xiàojìngchéng was elevated to Empress Xiàojìng Kāngcí Yìzhāo Duānhuì Bìtiān Fǔshèngchéng.
On the *rénxū* day,
Xuē Huàn was appointed plenipotentiary minister [quánquán dàchén]
to manage commercial affairs with Belgium.
On the *guǐhài* day,
bandits captured Hànzhōng.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Sichuan army recaptured Qīngshén.
Zuǒ Zōngtáng relieved the siege of Qúzhōu and Jiāngshān.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Niǎn leader Zhāng Luòxíng fled north.
An edict instructed Sēnggélínqìn and others to prepare defenses.
Due to the defeat of the Fújiàn army,
Qìng Duān concealed the report,
and was severely reprimanded for it.
On the *wùchén* day,
Zēng Zhēngàn recaptured Fánchāng.
Bāo Chāo recaptured Shídài, Tàipíng, and Jīngxiàn.
The Shànghǎi army, in conjunction with British and French forces, pacified the bandit strongholds in Nánxiáng,
and recaptured Jiādìng.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Dūxīng'ā defeated the bandits who fled from Yángzhōu.
Government forces recaptured Yǐngshàng.
The Cantonese bandits captured Xiàoyì and Zhèn'ān.
The Yùnán army recaptured Yǒngníng.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
due to the illegal collection of donations by Yè'ěrqiāng Āqímù Bóké Jùnwáng Ākèlāyī,
and his unauthorized killing of Muslim people,
he was stripped of his princely title.
Yīngyùn was charged with a crime.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Wūlándōu, Vice General Commandant of Xī'ān, suffered a defeat against the bandits.
An edict instructed Guān Wén and Zheng Yuánshàn to dispatch troops to Shǎnxī.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Taiwanese secret society bandits captured Zhānghuà.
The Cantonese bandits fled and pressed towards Xī'ān.
Guān Wén and Zheng Yuánshàn were urged to order their troops to collectively suppress them.
On the *dìngchǒu* day,
honorary titles [huīhào] were conferred upon Empress Dowager Cí'ān and Empress Dowager Cíxǐ,
and an imperial edict proclaimed a general amnesty with varying degrees.
On the *wùyín* day,
Duōlóng'ā's army captured Lúzhōu.
Bandit leader Chén Yùchéng fled to Shòuzhōu territory,
where Miáo Pèilín lured and captured him.
Miáo Pèilín's crimes were pardoned by imperial order.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Zhāng Yùnlán's army recaptured Jīngdé.
Zēng Zhēngàn's army recaptured Nánlíng.
Sǎ Muslim rebels besieged Bāyánrónggé.
Shěn Zhàolín reinforced and suppressed them.
Shànghǎi government forces recaptured Qīngpǔ.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Hé Guìqīng was apprehended and brought to the capital.
The Grand Secretaries were ordered to convene with the Ministry of Punishments to try and sentence him.
That month,
arrears of land tax were remitted for Ánzhōu and other prefectures and counties affected by floods.
On the *rénwǔ* day of the fifth month,
imperial forces recaptured Níngbō and Zhènhǎi.
