On the *guǐwèi* day,
Zhèng Yuánshàn moved his army to Rǔníng.
The Cantonese rebels seized Shānyáng in Shǎnxī.
Duōlóng'ā was ordered to oversee military affairs in Shǎnxī.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
it rained.
Wú Zhènyù was ordered to hasten to Shānxī to assist in defense and suppression.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Míngyì was ordered to quickly proceed to Tǎchéng to jointly survey the border with Russia,
and Xú Zōnggàn was to suppress rebels in Táiwān.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Xú Fǔ and 193 other individuals were granted the *jìnshì jí dì* and other degrees.
On the *dīnghài* day,
as Bāo Lìshēn, a farmer from Zhūjì, had organized local militia to kill rebels,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng was instructed to consider employing him.
Lǐ Shìzhōng's army intercepted and suppressed the rebel reinforcements in Jiāngnán,
achieving a great victory.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Guǎngxī imperial forces recaptured Tàipíng.
Liú Chángyòu went to Xúnzhōu to supervise the suppression.
The Cantonese rebels seized Wèinán.
On the *rénchén* day,
Wáng Lǚqiān was stationed in Xīnjiāng.
The Cantonese rebels besieged Wēnzhōu and Ruì'ān.
Qìngduān and others were instructed to advance and reinforce,
and Zuǒ Zōngtáng was also ordered to keep an eye on the situation.
The Cantonese rebels attacked Tóngguān.
Shěn Zhàolín was instructed to dispatch Mǎ Dézhāo to reinforce Shǎn.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Péng Yùlín's and Zēng Guóquán's armies recaptured Tàipíng and the cities of Wúhú, Jīnzhùguān, and the passes of Dōngliángshān.
Lǐ Chéngmóu was awarded a yellow riding jacket.
Imperial forces, together with British and French armies, captured the cities of Nánqiáo, Zhélín, and Fèngxián.
When Nánqiáo was captured,
the French admiral, Bu Luódé, died in battle.
The Emperor praised and mourned him,
granted a sacrifice,
and awarded precious items to his family.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the Cantonese rebels fled to Shǎnzhōu.
As the Miáo and sectarian rebels in Tóngrén and Shíqiān were rampant,
Máo Hóngbīn and Hán Chāo were instructed to suppress them jointly.
On the *wùxū* day,
Assistant Minister Héngqí was ordered to jointly handle trade affairs with Portugal with Chónghòu.
At this time, Britain intended to dispatch Indian troops to assist in the suppression.
Zēng Guófān and others were instructed to quickly capture Jīnlíng, Sū, and Cháng,
to prevent covetousness.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Cantonese rebels seized Xīngyì.
Imperial forces recaptured Huòqiū.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Lǐ Tángjiē, former Junior Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, memorialized, requesting that in addition to the master's assistance and correction,
precautions be taken against the gradual rise of attendants and close confidants,
and also that the Imperial Commentary on the *Zīzhì Tōngjiàn Jílǎn* and the *Dàxué Yǎnyì* be expounded.
He received a gracious edict in response.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
imperial forces recaptured Xiānjū, Huángyán, and six other counties in Táizhōu Prefecture.
Rebel leaders Wú Jiànyíng and others surrendered Nánhuì.
Imperial forces recaptured Chuānshā.
Rebels seized Jiādìng.
Arrears of banner rents in Zhílì were remitted.
On the *rén'yín* day,
imperial forces attacked Yǔhuātái.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Zēng Guófān's proposal was approved,
that Ānqìng should remain the provincial capital,
and a Naval Commander of the Yangtze River be established,
stationed at Wúhú.
Héngqí was appointed Plenipotentiary Minister for trade affairs with Portugal.
The Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén reported that the French envoy had sent a dispatch,
stating that Tián Xīngshù had abused and harmed Christians.
Luò Bǐngzhāng and Láo Chóngguāng were ordered to investigate and handle the matter.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Chén Yùchéng was escorted to the capital,
and an edict ordered his dismemberment en route.
Lǐ Zhānmóu, a militia leader from Rǔzhōu, rebelled,
and imperial forces suppressed him.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Lǐ Shìzhōng's army crossed the river and captured rebel strongholds at Lóngtán and other places.
They advanced to attack Jiǔfúzhōu.
Zēng Guófān was instructed to exercise control.
Míngyì was instructed to analyze border issues with Russia according to the treaty map,
and Xī Lín was to assist in handling the northern border demarcation.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
imperial forces recaptured Shānyáng in Shǎnxī.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the rebels occupying Shānyáng fled to Yúnxī.
Yīng Yùn was stationed in Shèngjīng.
Sichuan rebels seized Tàipíng Tīng [District],
and fled to harass Dìngyuǎn in Shǎnxī.
Zhāng Fú pacified the rebellious Hui in Líntóng County,
but was captured
and died.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Péng Yùlín's, Zēng Guóquán's, and other armies captured the passes of Mòlíngguān,
and pressed on towards Jīnlíng.
The Cantonese rebels seized Húzhōu.
Zhào Jǐngxián, a former grain intendant of Fújiàn, died at home.
On the *rénzǐ* day of the sixth month,
Qílíng was dismissed from office for delaying reinforcement to Zhèjiāng,
but remained in his post.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Lǐ Xùyí was instructed to manage the suppression of the Niǎn in Huáiběi,
and also to restrain Miáo Pèilín.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Sēnggélínqìn's and other armies captured the rebel stronghold at Jīnlóu.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the Six Boards and Nine Ministers were ordered to re-deliberate Hè Guìqīng's crimes.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Sichuan rebels seized Xīxiāng.
Imperial forces recaptured Dìngyuǎn.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng supervised Chéng Xuéqǐ's and other armies in suppressing the Cantonese rebels,
and inflicted a great defeat upon them.
Han and Hui in Xī'ān and Tóngzhōu engaged in armed conflict,
burning and killing in villages and towns north of the Wèi River.
An edict instructed to differentiate between suppression and pacification,
but to distinguish right from wrong,
regardless of whether they were Han or Hui.
On the *rénxū* day,
Sichuan forces recaptured Tàipíng.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Cantonese rebels seized Yúnxī.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Hè Guìqīng was ordered to be decapitated.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
locusts appeared in Zhílì.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Cantonese rebels fled south from Yī and Luò.
Shèng Bǎo was ordered to supervise their suppression.
Hui from Shǎn attacked Xī'ān and Tóngzhōu.
Léi Zhèngwǎn was urged to enter the pass.
On the *wùchén* day,
commanding ministers were sternly warned against deception and indiscriminate promotion,
and governors-general and governors were strictly forbidden from allowing prefectures and counties to request delays due to disasters,
while still privately levying taxes.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
rebels seized Tiānzhù.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Grand Secretary Guìliáng passed away,
and was posthumously granted the title of Grand Tutor.
An imperial edict of commendation was issued to the King of Guō'ěrkā.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
an imperial edict proclaimed that refugees who had fallen into rebel hands and returned
should generally be pardoned.
The law regarding the loss of cities was strictly re-emphasized.
A trade treaty with Belgium was finalized.
Cháng Qīng and others reported that the Russians claimed that the Khazar Khan Ālētǎshālá already belonged to Russia.
An edict ordered an investigation and appropriate handling,
and instructed the various *tàijí* to elect a successor to the Khanate.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Wén Yù and others were strictly ordered to apprehend horse bandits in Zhílì.
Tán Tíngxiāng was instructed to go to Yǎn and Yí to supervise the suppression of various bandits and the fleeing Niǎn.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
imperial forces recaptured Qīngtián.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Sēnggélínqìn's request was approved,
to pacify and recruit Miáo Pèilín.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Shí Dákāi fled to Qíjiāng.
Imperial forces decisively defeated him,
whereupon he fled to Gǒng, Gāo, and other counties.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Duōlóng'ā was urged to reinforce Xī'ān and suppress the Hui rebels,
and not to be misled by pacification negotiations,
but still to disperse the coerced and good Hui.
In this month,
arrears of grain and miscellaneous taxes in Zhílì and Hénán were remitted.
In the autumn, on the *rénwǔ* day of the seventh month, the new moon began.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the bandit Wōlǐhǎn (倭里罕) from Ānjíyán (安集延) invaded and harassed Kēshígá'ěr Kǎ (喀什噶爾卡).
The government troops defeated them.
There was unrest in Hàohǎn (浩罕), and
Bókè Mài Lǐ (伯克邁里) was killed.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Jǐngwén (景紋) was ordered to mobilize Dámù (達木) Mongolian soldiers and other tribal troops, such as the Huǒ'ěr (夥爾) people, to go to Tibet.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
because the Shǎnxī (陝西) Hui brutally massacred Hàn (漢) civilians,
Duōlóng'ā (多隆阿) and others were urged to enter the passes.
Soon after, an edict rebuked them for their delay,
and Shèngbǎo (勝保) was ordered to divide his forces to reinforce Shǎnxī.
Yuán Jiǎsān (袁甲三) was relieved due to illness,
and Lǐ Xùyí (李續宜) was appointed Imperial Commissioner,
to supervise military affairs.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng's (李鴻章) army recaptured Jīnshānwèi (金山衞).
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Sāhuí (撒回) in Gānsù (甘肅) surrendered.
The Ānjíyán (安集延) bandits fled out of the passes.
The Russians claimed the Khalkhas and Buruts as their territory.
Chángqīngchá (常清察) was ordered to investigate thoroughly,
the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén (總理各國事務衙門) was to deliberate on the matter,
and Míngxù (明緒) and Míngyì (明誼) were to jointly survey the western border affairs.
On the *rénchén* day,
Wōrén (倭仁) was ordered to assist as a Grand Secretary.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Chuān (川) bandits captured Yángxiàn (洋縣).
On the *wùxū* day,
the Chuān (川) army recaptured Chángníng (長寧).
Àirén (愛仁) and Wáng Màoyīn (王茂蔭) were ordered to secretly investigate the administration in Shǎnxī.
Zhīzhōu Qín Jùkuí (知州秦聚奎) was promoted to Dàshùn Guǎng Dào (大順廣道),
and was to jointly manage the defense of Zhí (直) and Dōng (東) with Zhēkèdūnbù (遮克敦布).
On the *jǐhài* day,
due to allowing soldiers to loot,
Zǒngbīng Tián Zàitián's (總兵田在田) post was stripped.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Shěn Zhàolín (沈兆霖) supervised the suppression of the Sāhuí (撒回).
While returning to Píngfān (平番),
a flash flood erupted,
and he died.
The Yuè (粵) bandits fled to Nányáng (南陽).
Shèngbǎo (勝保) was ordered to enter Shǎnxī to supervise military affairs,
and command all armies.
Xīlín (熙麟) was appointed Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù.
Féng Zǐcái's (馮子材) request to
select and purge the Zhènjiāng (鎮江) army was granted.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Máo Hóngbīn (毛鴻賓) achieved consecutive victories in suppressing the Qián (黔) bandits.
Hán Chāo (韓超) was ordered to reclaim lost territory,
Liú Chángyòu (劉長佑) to disperse the Yáo (瑤) people,
and Máo Hóngbīn (毛鴻賓) to jointly suppress the various bandits in Qián and Guì (桂).
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the Mǐn (閩) army recaptured Xuānpíng (宣平), Sōngyáng (松陽), and Ruì'ān (瑞安).
Qìngduān (慶端) was appointed General of Fúzhōu (福州),
and Qílíng (耆齡) was appointed Governor-General of Mǐn (閩) and Zhè (浙).
On the *yǐsì* day,
Lǐ Xùyí's (李續宜) mother passed away.
An imperial edict ordered him to forgo mourning and temporarily serve as Governor of Ānhuī (安徽).
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
a comet was seen in the northwest.
A commercial treaty between China and Portugal was concluded.
Sēnggélínqìn (僧格林沁) was ordered to command the military affairs of Yù (豫) and Lǔ (魯),
and to regulate all officials from governors-general and governors downwards,
and to discuss and manage the suppression of bandits in Ānhuī with Lǐ Xùyí (李續宜).
The Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén (總理各國事務衙門) requested the establishment of a Tóngwénguǎn (同文館)
to learn foreign languages and scripts,
which was granted.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Bào Chāo's (鮑超) army recaptured Níngguó (寧國).
The government troops recaptured Jǐngníng (景寧) and Yúnhé (雲和).
The È (鄂) army recaptured Yúnxī (鄖西).
The Board of Punishments was ordered to clear up all prisons.
Initially,
in Gǔangdōng's (廣東) Ēnpíng (恩平), Yángchūn (陽春), Xīnxīng (新興) and other counties, there was fighting between local (土) and guest (客) communities,
which had remained unresolved for nine years.
At this point,
Láo Chóngguāng (勞崇光) was ordered to pacify them with an edict,
and to prepare for post-conflict arrangements.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an edict was issued seeking frank opinions due to an astrological anomaly.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Lín Fúxiáng (林福祥) and Mǐ Xīngcháo (米興朝) were beheaded for losing a stronghold and fleeing.
Dūxīng'ā (都興阿) was ordered to verify the likin taxes along the river.
Hui bandits in Yúnnán (雲南) captured Yǒngchāng (永昌), Lónglíng (龍陵), and Téngyuè (騰越).
In this month,
arrears of land tax and reed tax in Yìníng (義寧) and other prefectures and counties in Jiāngxī (江西) were remitted.
In the eighth month, on the *xīnhài* day, the new moon began.
Because the popular militia of Táizhōu (台州) recaptured the prefecture and counties,
an imperial edict exempted the land and grain taxes for the first and second years of Tóngzhì (同治).
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng's (李鴻āng) army recaptured Qīngpǔ (青浦).
An edict was again issued to governors-general and governors to thoroughly eliminate the abuses of donations, likin levies, and coercion.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
it was approved that the salaries of Beijing officials be discounted and paid partly in cash.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Hui bandits surrounded Xiányáng (咸陽) and other cities.
Shèngbǎo (勝保) was ordered to enter Tóngguān (潼關) to supervise the suppression.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the title and yellow bridle of Lázhēng Hútúkètú (哷徵呼圖克圖) were stripped.
As the Tibetan affairs were pacified,
the mobilization of tribal soldiers and Sichuan grain levies was suspended.
An imperial edict ordered the extermination of locusts in Shùnzhí (順直).
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Xú Zhīmíng (徐之銘) requested to prevent Zhāng Liàngjī (張亮基) from leading troops into Diān (滇).
An edict rebuked him for being constrained by the Hui people,
and the request was denied.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
an edict strictly warned against the Shǎnxī (陝西) bandits colluding with the Gān (甘) Hui.
On the *rénxū* day,
Shèngbǎo (勝保) was ordered to dispatch troops to Shānxī (山西),
and Yīngguì (英桂) was to plan the defense of Jìn (晉) province.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Shèngbǎo (勝保) was ordered to suppress bandits north of the Wèi (渭) River,
and Duōlóng'ā (多隆阿) to suppress Hui bandits south of the Wèi River,
also giving consideration to Zhènpíng (鎮平).
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Lín Zìqīng (林自清) was provided with funds to train troops and return to Diān (滇).
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Shǎnxī (陝西) Hui surrounded Cháoyì (朝邑).
Tèpǔqīn (特普欽) and others reported that settlers in Hūlán (呼蘭) were increasing daily,
and requested the establishment of posts such as Lǐshì Tóngzhī (理事同知),
which was approved for implementation.
Fù Zhènbāng (傅振āng) was ordered to assist Tán Tíngxiāng (譚廷襄) in military affairs.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
all provinces were ordered to investigate the backgrounds of drifters.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Lǐ Xùyí (李續宜) was granted leave to mourn,
and Táng Xùnfāng (唐訓方) temporarily took his place.
Fújì (福濟) was ordered to jointly manage Tibetan affairs with Jǐngwén (景紋).
Sēnggélínqìn (僧格林沁) was ordered to command the Huáinán (淮南) army,
and to suppress and pacify the Miáo (苗) and Niǎn (捻).
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Shǎnxī (陝西) Hui fled west to Tóngzhōu (同州),
and the road to Cháoyì (朝邑) was cleared.
The rebel leader Hóng Rónghǎi (洪容海) went to Bào Chāo's (鮑超) army and surrendered,
leading his troops to recapture Guǎngdé (廣德).
On the *rénshēn* day,
the siege of Běixīnjīng (北新涇) was lifted,
and the defense of Hù (滬) was secured.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Gān (甘) Hui fled to Fèngxiáng (鳳翔).
The Yuè (粵) and Niǎn (捻) forces jointly attacked Xīchuān (淅川),
capturing Zhúxī (竹谿) and Zhúshān (竹山).
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the request of the princes and ministers was granted
to suspend the relocation of the imperial mausoleum,
and discussions were ordered regarding a close relative prince to respectfully preside over the ceremony.
A customs office was established in Zhènjiāng (鎮江) to collect foreign taxes.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Shèngbǎo (勝保) was ordered to issue a summons for Mǎ Dézhāo's (馬德昭) army to be stationed in the Chángwǔ (長武) area,
to guard against Hui bandits fleeing to Gān (甘).
Léi Zhèngwǎn (雷正綰) was promoted to Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Shǎnxī.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Táwān (臺灣) army lifted the siege of Jiāyì (嘉義).
The government troops recaptured Chùzhōu (處州) and Jìnyún (縉雲).
Zǒngbīng Huáng Kāibǎng (總兵黃開榜) was ordered to take command of Tián Zàitián's (田在田) army.
On the *wùyín* day,
the request for Zhílì (直隸) to recruit more cavalry to catch horse bandits was granted.
The government troops recaptured Qīngxī (青谿).
Qílíng (耆齡) was ordered to exclusively manage the military affairs of reinforcing Zhè (浙).
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Shāndōng (山東) army achieved a great victory in suppressing the Niǎn (捻) bandits.
Shèngbǎo (勝保) reported defeating Hui bandits at Xiékǒu (斜口),
lifting the siege of Xī'ān (西安),
and the bandits fled north of the Wèi (渭) River.
He was admonished to take responsibility for acting on his own initiative.
Léi Zhèngwǎn (雷正綰) was ordered to assist Shèngbǎo (勝保) in military affairs.
Yúyáo (餘姚) in Zhèjiāng (浙江) was recaptured,
and Yángshuò (陽朔) in Guǎngxī (廣西).
As the Yuè (粵) bandits fled to Wénxiāng (閿鄉),
Zhèng Yuánshàn's (鄭元善) army was urged to proceed to Hé (河) and Luò (洛).
On the *xīnsì* day of the intercalary eighth month,
the Qìngduān Army recaptured Jìnyún.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Duōlóng'ā's army captured Jīngzǐguān.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the È Army recaptured Zhúshān and Zhúxī.
The Qián Army recaptured Tiānzhù and Qióngshuǐ.
The Cantonese bandits fled to Lǎohékǒu.
The Hui bandits besieged Jīngyáng.
Ráo Zhèngwǎn's army was ordered to advance and suppress them.
The martial law in Xī'ān was lifted.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Hui people in Fǎkùmén fought each other,
and Yùmíng and others dispersed them.
Wén Yù and Tán Tíngxiāng were urged to capture horse bandits on the borders of Zhílì and Dōng 省 (East Province).
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the Hui bandits again attacked Xī'ān.
The Diān bandits fled from Chuān to Zhuānpíng.
The Cantonese bandits fled from Wénxiāng to Yǒngníng.
It was approved for Hénán to collect Chánglú salt *líjìxiǎng* (tax for military provisions).
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Hóng Rónghǎi's surrendered followers rebelled again,
occupying Guǎngdé.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Duōlóng'ā's army achieved a great victory against the Niǎn bandits,
lifting the siege of Shāngnán.
The Jí and Hēi cavalry stationed in Nányuàn were transferred to Shānxī.
On the *rénchén* day,
Hán Chāo was instructed to discuss military affairs in Guìzhōu with Admiral Jiāng Zhōngyì,
to block Lín Zìqīng from leading his followers into Qián.
Lǐ Tángjiē was appointed Grand Secretary of the Military Council.
Délèkèduō'ěrzì and others were ordered to reinforce the river defenses.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the provinces were instructed to abolish superfluous expenses in departments and districts.
The Ancha Envoy was solely made responsible for interrogating cases of *jīngkòng* (appeals to the capital).
On the *yǐwèi* day,
an imperial edict was issued to recommend talents.
Xuē Huàn and Lǐ Hóngzhāng were ordered to handle the treaty exchange with Pǔ Province.
The provinces were urged to quickly remit funds to the capital.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Wō Rén was appointed Grand Secretary.
Duōlóng'ā was instructed to hold Wǔguān.
On the *wùxū* day,
Duōlóng'ā achieved a great victory in suppressing the Niǎn bandits fleeing west from Bó and Yǐng,
and was awarded a yellow riding jacket.
The Cantonese bandits again captured Cíxī.
The government army, in collaboration with British and French forces, recaptured it.
Huá'ěr died in battle.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Láo Chóngguāng and others were instructed to arrange for the provision of rice and grain for the capital granaries,
and the new grain tax from Jiāngsū and other provinces was to be remitted to the capital in kind.
Zhāng Liàngjī impeached Xú Zhīmíng and Cén Yùyīng for being overbearing.
It was approved for the French general Lèbólèdōng to remain stationed in Níngbō.
Pān Duó was instructed to pacify the Han and Hui people in Yúnnán.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Yuán Jiǎsān's return to his hometown was approved.
Táng Xùnfāng was ordered to Línhuái to take over military affairs.
Mǎ Xīnyí was temporarily put in command of Jiǎsān's army.
Zēng Guófān requested that a Grand Secretary be appointed to assist in military affairs.
The emperor did not permit it,
but still comforted and encouraged him,
and also issued an imperial decree inquiring about the sick and epidemic-stricken officers and soldiers.
Jǐng Lún and others were instructed to strictly apprehend the cult bandits in Jílín.
On the *rényín* day,
Fùmíng'ā was ordered to rush to Yángzhōu to assist in Dū Xīng'ā's military affairs.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Shèng Bǎo requested to pacify the Hui bandits in Sānyuán and other places.
This was not permitted.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Liú Chángyòu was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng.
Tián Xīngshù was allowed to temporarily remain in Guìzhōu to suppress bandits.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Shí Dákāi fled to Qíjiāng and other places.
The government army attacked and defeated him.
The Hui bandits fled to Bīnzhōu, Bǎojī, and other places.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Lǐ Rúyīng, a Niǎn bandit from Hénán, surrendered.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Shí Dákāi fled to Rénhuái.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Guān Wén was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wénhuá Hall,
and Wō Rén was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wényuān Pavilion.
On the *xīnhài* day of the ninth month,
Empress Xiàojìngchéng was enshrined in the Tàimiào (Imperial Ancestral Temple).
An imperial edict was issued, granting varying degrees of grace.
The Yù Niǎn bandits fled to Nèixiāng and Xīnyě.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Censor Liú Qìng requested that the performance of prefectures and districts be assessed based on their ability to attract displaced people and reclaim land.
This was approved.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Shěn Bǎozhēn's request was approved
to select and train extra troops,
and to appropriately plan for subsidies.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
due to Emperor Wénzōng's coffin being moved to the imperial tombs,
the regular taxes of the passing prefectures and districts were remitted.
Wén Yù was instructed to select capable officials to plan water conservancy in the capital region.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the heretics Wáng Shǒuqīng and others from Zhílì compiled rebellious writings.
The incident was exposed, and they were executed.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Zhèng Yuánshàn and Máo Chǎngxī were instructed to jointly suppress the Niǎn bandits on the southwest and two other routes.
Zēng Guófān stated that in handling Miáo Pèilín,
it was advisable to pardon his crimes but not utilize his strength.
This was approved.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the local bandits Huáng Jīnlóng, Lǐ Zhíhuái, and others in Guǎngdōng initiated a rebellion.
The government army suppressed them.
Duōlóng'ā was urged to lead his troops into Shǎn.
For the bandits fleeing to Suí and Zǎo,
Mùtúshàn's army was ordered to suppress them.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Shèng Bǎo requested to transfer Miáo Pèilín to Shǎn to assist in the suppression.
This was not permitted.
The Chuān bandits fled to Níngshǎn.
The government army defeated them at Zǐwǔgǔ.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Shí Dákāi fled to Tóngzǐ.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the provinces of Mǐn, Yuè, and Lǔ were criticized for neglecting military funds,
and their governors were severely reprimanded.
Punishments for overdue remittances of capital funds were also strictly defined.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Cantonese chieftain Lǐ Xiùchéng launched a large-scale relief effort for Jīnlíng.
Chén Décái captured Yìngchéng and Xiàogǎn.
The government army recaptured them.
The Ānhuī army captured the bandit stronghold of Húgōu.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Sēnggélínqìn's army captured the Niǎn stronghold of Bózhōu.
The Shǎn Hui besieged Fèngxiáng.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Féng Zǐcái captured the bandit stronghold of Tānggāng.
The Hui people of Língzhōu rebelled.
Lǐ Xùyí was urged to join the army.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Hui masses attacked Tóng and Cháo.
Shèng Bǎo was instructed to personally supervise the suppression,
and Léi Zhèngwǎn was to supervise the suppression north of Xiányáng.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Zhè Army recaptured Shòuchāng.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
due to extorting Hui merchants,
Kùlún Minister Sèkètōng'é was stripped of his position
and exiled to Xīnjiāng.
The abusive practice of tea tickets in Kùlún was abolished.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng's army, in conjunction with British and French forces, recaptured Jiādìng.
The Netherlands was allowed to establish treaty trade.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the È Army recaptured Jīngshān.
The Cantonese bandits fled to Huángpí and Huáng'ān.
Zēng Guófān and others were instructed to select military officers to learn foreign military tactics in Shànghǎi and Níngbō,
and Mǐn, Yuè, and other provinces were ordered to follow suit.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the Yù Army captured the bandit stronghold of Lóngjǐng.
Sū Tíngkuí, Zēng Wàngyán, Liú Xīzài, Huáng Péngnián, Zhū Qí, and others were summoned to the capital,
and the provinces were still ordered to conduct local militia training.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
an imperial edict ordered the implementation of the "strengthen walls and clear fields" strategy in the capital region.
Zēng Guófān and others were instructed to pre-select generals and officers to practice foreign ships and cannons.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
a sacrificial ceremony was held at the Tàimiào.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *gēngchén* (庚辰) day, the first day of the month,
the Chuān (川) army captured Lóngchǎng (龍●場).
Bandit chiefs Lǐ Yǒnghé (李永和) and others were executed.
Tídū (提督) Hú Zhōnghé (胡中和) was awarded a yellow riding jacket.
On the *xīnsì* (辛巳) day,
large contingents of Yuè (粵) bandits besieged the Hù (滬) army at Nánxiáng (南翔) and other places.
Shèngbǎo (勝保) went to Tóngguān (潼關) to suppress bandits.
On the *guǐwèi* (癸未) day,
Húnán (湖南) reinforcements reunited and recaptured Xiūrén (修仁).
Láo Chóngguāng (勞崇光) was ordered to Qíng (黔) to investigate Tián Xīngshù's (田興恕) case of killing missionaries.
Zhāng Kǎisōng (張凱嵩) was appointed to take over Guǎngxī (廣西) military affairs.
On the *bǐngxū* (丙戌) day,
Wénzōng Xiǎnhuángdì (文宗顯皇帝) and Xiàodé Xiǎnhòuhòu (孝德顯皇后) were installed in the Fèngxiān Diàn (奉先殿) ancestral temple.
The Emperor personally went to perform the rites.
On the *wùzǐ* (戊子) day,
Ruìcháng (瑞常) was ordered to assist as Dàxuéshì (大學士).
On the *jǐchǒu* (己丑) day,
Cáo Yùyīng (曹毓瑛) was appointed as a Jūnjī Dàchén (軍機大臣).
On the *gēngyín* (庚寅) day,
the Yù (豫) army achieved victory in suppressing the Niǎn (捻) bandits,
relieving the siege of Línyǐng (臨潁).
Shèngbǎo (勝保) was urged to go to Tóng (同) and Cháo (朝) to suppress bandits.
Shèngbǎo (勝保) still requested the transfer of Miáo Pèilín (苗沛霖) to Shǎnxī (陝).
An imperial edict severely rebuked him.
Government troops recaptured Fènghuà (奉化).
Xú Zhīmíng (徐之銘) spoke of pacifying the Xīngyì (興義) Huí (回) bandits.
An edict stated that he was controlled by the Diān (滇) Huí (回).
Pān Duó (潘鐸) was ordered to intercept the commissioner,
preventing Zhīmíng (之銘) from interfering in Qíng (黔) affairs.
On the *xīnmǎo* (辛卯) day,
Huí (回) bandits in Yán'ān (延安) revolted.
Yīngguì (英桂) organized local militia in Héqǔ (河曲) and Bǎodé (保德).
Lǐ Hóngzhāng (李鴻章) was ordered to select generals to command the Chángshèngjūn (常勝軍),
and was formally appointed Jiāngsū Xúnfǔ (江蘇巡撫).
Gān (甘) Huí (回) bandits intruded and pressed towards Huāmǎchí (花馬池).
On the *guǐsì* (癸巳) day,
Qíng (黔) troops defeated Shí Dákāi (石達開),
and the siege of Zūnyì (遵義) was lifted.
Shí Dákāi (石達開) fled to Rénhuái (仁懷).
On the *yǐwèi* (乙未) day,
an edict ordered Fèngtiān (奉天) to strictly apprehend bandits.
The troops previously commanded by the foreign general Wá'ěr (華爾) were disbanded.
Russian warships were permitted to assist in suppression at Shànghǎi (上海),
but not to enter the river.
It was decreed that thereafter, foreigners commanding troops should not easily change their uniforms.
Déleéng'é's (德楞額) army was routed in Shāndōng (山東).
An imperial edict stripped him of his post and ordered an investigation.
On the *bǐngshēn* (丙申) day,
the Níngxià (寧夏) army suffered a defeat in suppressing the Huí (回).
Shǎn (陝) Huí (回) bandits fled to Qīngshuǐ (清水).
On the *wùxū* (戊戌) day,
Sēnggélínqìn (僧格林沁) was ordered to suppress the Fú (幅) bandits in Shāndōng (山東).
On the *jǐhài* (己亥) day,
the Jiāngnán (江南) army repelled the bandits of Jīnzhùguān (金柱關).
On the *gēngzǐ* (庚子) day,
Tán Tíngxiāng (譚廷襄) was dismissed.
Yán Jìngmíng (閻敬銘), an Ànchásǐ (按察使) in mourning, was ordered to act as Shāndōng Xúnfǔ (山東巡撫),
and to manage military affairs.
On the *guǐmǎo* (癸卯) day,
Mùténg'ā (穆騰阿) was ordered to assist Shèngbǎo (勝保) in military affairs.
On the *yǐsì* (乙巳) day,
an edict to the Xíngbù (刑部) stated:
"This year, the practice of suspending executions (jùjué, 句決) has been stopped by precedent.
Hé Guìqīng (何桂清) lost control of his troops,
and was merely sentenced to 'beheading with a stay of execution',
which was already an act of mercy beyond the law.
Now the time has come.
If, due to the suspension, it is delayed again,
and the public execution is long postponed,
how can we apologize to those who died in service and the countless common people?
He is to be executed immediately.
From now on, in years where executions are suspended,
for offenders whose crimes are serious,
a special memorial should still be submitted to request an imperial decree."
Originally,
Xú Zhīmíng (徐之銘) appointed the Huí (回) person Mǎ Liánshēng (馬聯升) to act as Ányì Zhèn (安義鎮).
Because of this, Huí (回) bandits occupied Pǔ'ān Chéng (普安城).
By this time,
the matter was reported.
An edict ordered Zhīmíng (之銘) to recall Mǎ Liánshēng (馬聯升),
and to quickly investigate the circumstances of the rebellion and report.
In the eleventh month, on the *jǐyǒu* (己酉) day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Shěn Hóngfù (沈宏富) was appointed acting Guìzhōu Tídū (貴州提督),
taking over Tián Xīngshù's (田興恕) military affairs.
On the *gēngxū* (庚戌) day,
Dīng Bǎozhēn (丁寶zhen), the Zhīfǔ (知府) of Chángshā (長沙), was promoted to acting Shāndōng Ànchásǐ (山東按察使).
On the *rénzǐ* (壬子) day,
Zhèng Yuánshàn (鄭元善) was demoted to Dàoyuán (道員) due to dereliction of duty.
Zhāng Zhīwàn (張之萬) was appointed acting Hénán Xúnfǔ (河南巡撫).
An edict ordered Máo Chǎngxī (毛昶熙) to disband his troops.
Táiwān (臺灣) secret society bandits captured Dǒuliù Mén (斗六門).
On the *jiǎyín* (甲寅) day,
Huáng Bīn (黃彬) was stripped of his post,
and his assistance was withdrawn.
Wú Quánměi (吳全měi) was ordered to take over command of the navy,
and be subordinate to Zēng Guófān (曾國藩) and Dūxīng'ā (都興阿).
On the *bǐngchén* (丙辰) day,
Wēng Xīncún (翁心存) died,
and was posthumously granted Tàibǎo (太保).
Zēng Guóquán's (曾國荃) army achieved a great victory in suppressing the reinforcing bandits of Jīnlíng (金陵).
Guóquán (國荃) and Xiāo Fúsì (蕭孚泗) were awarded yellow riding jackets.
On the *wùwǔ* (戊午) day,
government troops, together with British and French forces, recaptured Shàngyú (上虞), Shèng (嵊), and Xīnchāng (新昌).
On the *jǐwèi* (己未) day,
Péng Yùnzhāng (彭蘊章) died.
On the *gēngshēn* (庚申) day,
Jīnlíng (金陵) Yuè (粵) bandits raided Gāozī (高 資).
Féng Zǐcái's (馮子材) army repelled them.
On the *rénxū* (壬戌) day,
Shèngbǎo (勝保) was accused of arrogance, deceit, and fraud.
He was stripped of his post and arrested for questioning.
An edict ordered Zhílì (直隸) to implement the *bǎojiǎ* (保甲) system.
An edict ordered Ruìlín (瑞麟) to strictly apprehend bandits in Rèhé (熱河).
On the *guǐhài* (癸亥) day,
Qín Jùkuí (秦聚奎) died in battle while suppressing bandits in Guànxiàn (冠縣).
Bandits from Jiǔfú Zhōu (九洑洲) recaptured Hézhōu (和州), Hánshān (含山), and Cháoxiàn (巢縣).
On the *yǐchǒu* (乙丑) day,
Shèngbǎo's (勝保) crimes were publicly announced.
His property was confiscated.
His troops were rewarded.
Duōlóng'ā (多隆阿) was appointed Qīnchāi Dàchén (欽差大臣),
taking over command of the various armies previously under Shèngbǎo (勝保).
On the *bǐngyín* (丙寅) day,
Chuān (川) bandits captured Fó Píng (佛坪),
but government troops recaptured it.
Chuān (川) bandits then recaptured Lüèyáng (略陽).
On the *jǐsì* (己巳) day,
Yuè (粵) bandits invaded and captured Qímén (祁門).
Píngluó (平羅) Huí (回) bandits revolted.
On the *xīnwèi* (辛未) day,
Yán Jìngmíng (閻敬銘) requested to complete his mourning period,
which was not granted.
On the *yǐhài* (乙亥) day,
Shāndōng (山東) surrendered rebels revolted,
capturing Púzhōu (濮州).
Zhāng Liàngjī (張亮基) was appointed acting Guìzhōu Xúnfǔ (貴州巡撫) with the title of Zǒngdū (總督),
and concurrently acting Tídū (提督).
Acting Xúnfǔ (巡撫) Hán Chāo (韓超) and acting Tídū (提督) Tián Xīngshù (田興恕) were removed from their posts,
pending investigation.
On the *bǐngzǐ* (丙子) day,
Shí Dákāi (石達開) captured Yúnlián (筠連).
Chuān (川) bandits captured Liǎngdāng (兩當),
but it was soon recaptured.
On the *dīngchǒu* (丁丑) day,
the French envoy held Tián Xīngshù (田興恕) responsible for the killing of a missionary
and demanded compensation,
which was refused.
On the *wùyín* day of the twelfth month, the first day of the lunar month,
an edict was issued to Jiāng, Zhè, and other places, concerning those who had been coerced into joining the rebels.
Those who sincerely surrender,
regardless of how long or short their time with the rebels,
are all permitted to pledge allegiance.
An edict was issued to Zēng Guófān and Táng Xùnfāng to divide their forces and station them at Zhèngyángguān and Shòuzhōu.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Bái Qíwén, having committed an offense, was stripped of his button and plume,
and arrested for trial.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Duōlóng'ā defeated the Huí bandits at Tóngzhōu.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Sāsābù, Vice Commander-in-Chief of Jīngzhōu, was ordered to go to Zhí and Lǔ to suppress bandits.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the Jiāngnán army recaptured Jìxī and Qímén.
Bào Chāo was in mourning for his mother,
so he was ordered to serve in an acting capacity,
and remain in the camp.
The government troops recaptured Púzhōu.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng's army recaptured Yánzhōu.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Léi Zhèngwǎn was ordered to assist Duōlóng'ā with military affairs,
and General Mùténg'ā and Yīngqǐ were to manage the defense of the provincial capital.
On the *dīnghài* day,
an edict was issued to Zuǒ Zōngtáng and others to recommend talented individuals from Xiāng.
Bandits in Guǎngxī captured Xīníng.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Huí bandits captured Jīngyáng.
Sòng Jǐngshī rebelled in Shānxī.
Troops from the Ālāshàn and È'ěrdūosī Mongol banners were dispatched to assist in suppressing the Huí bandits in Níngxià Píngluó.
An edict was again issued to recommend filial and upright scholars.
Guǎng bandìts advanced to Pínglì.
Huí bandits in Hézhōu rampaged,
and Ēnlín suppressed them.
Permission was granted to exchange treaties with Prussia.
Diān bandits captured Jǐngdōng.
Xí Bǎotián's army was re-ordered to reinforce Jiāngxī.
An edict was issued to Jiāng Zhōngyì to control the various armies reinforcing Guì.
Roving bandits from Shāndōng harassed Jìzhōu and Zǎojiàng,
and an edict was issued to Wén Yù and others to suppress them jointly.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Guì Wéncàn, a *jǔrén* from Guǎngdōng, presented a collection of classical studies,
and an imperial decree commended him.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
government troops recaptured Xīnníng,
and recaptured Huòqiū.
Shí Dákāi again captured Gāoxiàn,
but it was subsequently recaptured.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Assistant Minister Chónghòu was ordered to assist in the defense and suppression efforts in Zhílì.
Liú Chángyòu was summoned to the capital,
and Yàn Duānshū and Kūnshòu were ordered to discuss and manage military affairs in Guǎngdōng.
On the *wùxū* day,
Guǎng bandits advanced from Yúnyáng to Xīng'ān,
and an edict was issued to Duōlóng'ā and others to suppress them jointly.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
rebel leaders Luò Guózhōng and others surrendered Chángshú and Zhāowén.
On the *rénchén* day,
an edict was issued to Mùténg'ā and Yīngqǐ to manage the defense and suppression efforts in Xī'ān,
with Duōlóng'ā also overseeing provincial defense.
Gān bandits advanced and captured Lǒngzhōu,
and Zhīzhōu Shào Fǔ died there.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Xuē Huàn was summoned to the capital,
and Lǐ Hóngzhāng was temporarily appointed Acting Minister of Trade.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
bandits advanced to Yǒngnián, Hándān, and other places,
and Wén Yù and Zhēkèdūnbù were stripped of their positions and
banished for procrastination and dereliction of duty.
Liú Chángyòu was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì,
and Yàn Duānshū was appointed Acting Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng.
An edict was issued to Tídú Bǎo Shān to take over affairs at the border between Zhí and Dōng.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the combined ancestral rites were offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Guǎng bandits again advanced to Níngshǎn.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Guǎng bandits besieged Xīng'ān,
and divided their forces to Hànzhōng.
In this month,
taxes in Róngchāng and other counties in Sìchuān, and ōuníng and other counties in Fújiàn, were remitted due to bandit harassment,
as were accumulated land rents for lakeshores and shoals in Jiāngnán.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú paid tribute.
On the *wùshēn* day of the first lunar month in the second year, *guǐhài* spring, the first day of the lunar month,
the court audience was exempted.
Zhāng Zhīwàn was appointed Governor of Hénán.
On the *xīnhài* day,
generous solace was given to the wounded and deceased foreign officer LèbóLètōng at Shàoxīng.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
an imperial decree ordered Zēng Guófān, Dū Xīng'ā, and others to recommend suitable naval commanders-in-chief.
Bandits captured Wǔyì,
but government troops subsequently recaptured it.
The Guǎngxī army recaptured Liántáng.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Guǎng bandits captured the prefecture and town of Xīng'ānfǔ.
Shǎnxī Huí bandits advanced to Hùxiàn,
and following Yīngqǐ's request,
Mǎ Dézhāo was kept to manage provincial defense.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Bào Chāo's army and others recaptured Qīngyáng.
On the *wùchén* day,
Lǐ Huán was ordered to go to Shǎn,
to take over military affairs in Hànnán.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Zānduì chieftain Jiūdé'ěrgètè Tǔsī harassed Bātáng and Mùtáng.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the roving bandits in Jīnán were pacified.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
as Fèngxiáng had been under siege for half a year,
an imperial decree criticized Yīngqǐ for dereliction of duty,
and urged Léi Zhèngwǎn to rush to relieve the siege.
On the *dīngchǒu* day of the second month, the first day of the lunar month,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng's army recaptured Jīnhuá, Tāngxī, Lóngyóu, and Lánxī.
On the *wùyín* day,
based on Lǐ Hóngzhāng's suggestion,
an edict was issued to Liǎnghú to purchase and transport rice to the capital using canal transport fees,
exempting it from tax.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Lǐ Xiùchéng and others crossed the river to invade the north,
and government troops defeated them.
The Chuān army suppressed Shí Dákāi,
and defeated him.
Guìzhōu Huí bandits captured Ānnán and Xīngyì.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the Jílín army defeated the Chaoyang roving bandits at Xīngkǎi Hú,
and an edict warned against allowing them to cross into Russian territory.
Duōlóng'ā achieved a great victory in suppressing the Huí bandits,
capturing the bandit dens at Qiāngbáizhèn and elsewhere.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Shǎnxī militia recaptured Xīng'ān.
Guǎng bandits advanced to Hànyīn and Zǐyáng.
Lǐ Shìzhōng requested to be stripped of his position to atone for Shèng Bǎo's crime,
but this was not permitted.
Guǎng bandits advanced and captured Bāochéng,
but it was subsequently recaptured.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Yǒngkāng and Wǔyì were recaptured.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Tán Tíngxiāng went to Dōngchāng to suppress bandits.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng moved his army to Lánxī.
The bandits occupying Dōngyáng, Yìwū, and Pǔjiāng all fled.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Sēnggélínqìn's army captured the bandit den at Zhìhé Jí,
and the Niǎn leader Zhāng Luòxíng was executed.
An imperial decree granted commendation,
and his hereditary princely title was to remain perpetual and unchangeable.
Money and grain taxes in Méng, Bó, and other jurisdictions were remitted for two years.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Huí bandits of Níngxià Píngluó surrendered.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Qìngyún was appointed General of Níngxià.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Jīnán bandit Zhāng Xīzhū advanced to Dàmíng,
and Chónghòu was severely reprimanded for missing the opportunity,
and Liú Chángyòu was urged to go to Zhílì.
Féng Zǐcái defeated the bandits at Zhènjiāng.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng's army recaptured Shàoxīng and Tónglú.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Mǎn Qìng and others suppressed the rebellious bandits of Zānduì.
Huáng Guóruì's army captured the bandit den at Chángchéng, Tánchéng County.
Due to delay in pursuing the bandits,
Chónghòu was stripped of his position,
but remained in office.
Eastern bandits advanced to Qǔzhōu and Píngxiāng.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
an edict was issued to Ēnlín and others,
stating that no easy agreement should be reached with the Gānsù Huí bandits.
On the *rénchén* day,
Píng Ruì's request was granted,
to reclaim unused wasteland and horse pastures in Wūlǔmùqí and other places,
and levy taxes to fund military expenses,
and distribute the garrisoned land
to the garrison troops.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Guǎng bandits captured Jiāngpǔ.
Guǎngdōng bandits occupied Xìnyí,
and Kūnshòu suppressed them.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Eastern Zhè was cleared,
and money and grain taxes in the newly recaptured prefectures, departments, and counties were remitted for two years.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Yán Jìngmíng was urged to go to Dōngchāng to manage military affairs.
Huí bandit Mǎ Huàlóng gathered a party to besiege Língzhōu,
but subsequently went to Gùyuán to surrender.
Shí Dákāi advanced from Diān to Yǒng.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
an imperial decree ordered provincial officials to carefully select magistrates,
to lighten taxes and corvée,
to abolish bothersome and harsh regulations,
and to start anew with the people.
In this month,
arrears of taxes for two years were remitted for Qīngshén due to military disturbances.
In the third month, on the day Wùshēn,
a ban was issued against Hénán's collecting advance grain taxes.
On the day Xīnhài,
Chónghòu was ordered to return to his post as Minister Superintendent of Trade for the Three Ports.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Liú Chángyòu was ordered to take command of all the troops in Zhílì.
Shěn Bǎozhēn was instructed to maintain fairness in handling diplomatic affairs,
to prevent conflicts from arising between gentry and commoners.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Zēng Guófān was instructed to comprehensively plan the military affairs north of the Yangtze.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the Cantonese bandits in southern Shǎnxī captured Zǐyáng,
but it was soon recovered.
The rebellious bandits in Yúnnán's Yíxī region attacked Kūnmíng,
and Pān Duó died there.
Jiǎ Hóngzhào was appointed Governor of Yúnnán.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng's army captured Fúshān Pass.
The British General Gēdēng (Gordon) was ordered to restrain the Ever Victorious Army.
On the day Dīngsì,
the Niǎn bandits captured Máchéng.
On the day Wùwǔ,
they pressed close to the provincial capital of Wǔchāng.
Chǔ and Yù forces were ordered to combine and attack them.
On the day Jǐwèi,
grain taxes for two years were remitted for Xī'ān in Zhèjiāng.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Dān (Denmark) sent envoy Lāsīnàfú (Larsenfuss) to negotiate a commercial treaty.
The foreign general Dá'ěrdìfú (D'Alerteville) died in battle,
and was granted generous posthumous honors.
Muslim bandits besieged Píngliáng.
Due to the prolonged delay in suppressing the bandits in Gānsù,
acting Provincial Commander Dìng'ān was stripped of his post
and arrested for questioning.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Qílíng was promoted to General of Fúzhōu.
Zuǒ Zōngtáng was appointed Governor-General of Mǐnzhè,
to command the military affairs of both provinces.
Zēng Guóquán was appointed Governor of Zhèjiāng,
while continuing to lead troops to besiege Jīnlíng;
Zuǒ Zōngtáng concurrently held this acting post.
The annual customary tribute from Fújiàn for this year was suspended.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the Imperial Princes and Ministers were ordered to re-examine Shèngbǎo's crimes and circumstances.
The Cantonese bandits from Níngguó fled to Dōngliú and Jiàndé.
Qín scholar Máo Hēng and Míng scholar Lǚ Nán were granted concomitant sacrifice in the Temple of Literature.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Niǎn leader Jiǎ Wénbīn in Méngchéng was executed.
Cantonese bandits in southern Shǎnxī captured Miǎnxìan.
Guìzhōu General Luó Xiàolián's army recovered Dìngfān, Chángzhài, Dúshān, and Lìbō.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Zēng Guófān was demoted for the loss of Jiāngpǔ and other cities,
and Lǐ Shìzhōng was stripped of his assistant status.
Wú Táng was formally appointed Governor-General of Grain Transport,
and retained command of military affairs north of the Yangtze.
An edict was issued to console the refugees north of the Yangtze.
On the day Jǐsì,
for the Emperor's birthday,
the customary congratulatory ceremony was suspended.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Miáo Pèilín rebelled again.
Guān Wén and others intercepted and suppressed the fleeing bandits in Qízhōu.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Xú Zhīmíng was stripped of his post
and arrested for questioning.
Pān Duó was granted a hereditary post.
Due to scarce rainfall,
an edict was issued to review criminal cases.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Fújí and Jǐngwén were ordered to investigate the incident of hostilities in Xīzàng (Tibet).
On the day Yǐhài,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng's army recovered Tàicāng.
Muslim bandits caused disturbances in Lóngdé.
Huáng Guóruì's army pacified the stick-wielding bandits in Yízhōu.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
an edict was issued to investigate and provide relief to the good Muslim people who suffered and died in Shǎnxī and Gānsù;
soon after, an edict extended this to Yúnnán.
In this month,
the Emperor repeatedly went to the Dàgāo Hall to pray for rain.
In summer, fourth month, on the day Wùyín,
Censor Wú Táishòu was stripped of his post
for a memorial that favored Shèngbǎo.
Miáo Pèilín captured Huáiyuǎn.
Bandit Liú Dépeí occupied Zīchuān in Shāndōng.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the government forces suppressed bandits in the southern capital region;
Zhāng Xīzhū and others fled to Gāotáng,
and were later executed.
On the day Gēngchén,
Cantonese and Niǎn bandits harassed Lújiāng, Tóngchéng, Shūchéng, and Huángzhōu.
Zēng Guófān was instructed to garrison Ānqìng,
and not to withdraw the siege of Jīnlíng.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Duōlóng'ā's army captured the bandit stronghold of Xiàoyì.
Liú Róng was ordered to lead troops to reinforce Shǎnxī.
Land taxes were remitted for the occupied areas of Zhèjiāng.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Miáo Pèilín besieged Shòuzhōu and Liù'ān,
and Sēnggélínqìn was urgently ordered to suppress him.
Cantonese bandits occupied Tàipíng and Shídài;
Zuǒ Zōngtáng and Shěn Bǎozhēn jointly defended against them.
Duōlóng'ā's army captured the bandit stronghold of Cāngtóu,
and eastern Shǎnxī was cleared.
Miáo Pèilín captured Yǐngshàng
and attacked Méngchéng.
Liú Chángyòu was ordered to supervise bandit suppression in the border areas of Zhí, Lǔ, and Yù.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Liú Diǎn's army recovered Yīxìan.
Assistant Minister Xuē Huàn was ordered to work in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén (Office for the General Management of Foreign Affairs).
On the day Wùzǐ,
Yīngguì was allowed to return to garrison Tàiyuán.
On the day Gēngyín,
Liú Chángyòu reported that bandit leaders Yáng Mínglǐng and others had surrendered.
Muslim bandits in Gānsù captured Yánchá,
and attacked Jìngníng;
Mǎ Dézhāo proceeded to Qìngyáng to suppress them.
On the day Rénchén,
the Gàn army defeated the bandits at Qímén,
and rebel chief Hú Dǐngwén was executed.
On the day Guǐsì,
Lǐ Xùyí requested to vacate his acting post,
which was granted.
Táng Xùnfāng was appointed Governor of Ānhuī.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng dispatched Chéng Xuéqǐ's army and others to approach Kūnshān.
The Jīngzhōu army attacked Muslim bandits
and defeated them.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Ministry of Rites deliberated and set the order of precedence for the sacrifice to former worthies and scholars,
and promulgated it to all provinces.
On the day Yǐwèi,
rice paddies were reclaimed in the Xīnchéng area of Zhílì.
Yán Jìngmíng proceeded to Zīchuān to supervise the suppression.
Niǎn bandits fled back to Hénán,
and General Yú Jìchāng and others died;
Zhāng Yào was ordered to take command of their army.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
due to the scattered flight of Ānhuī bandits into Jiāng and È,
and the vulnerability of Ānqìng,
Zēng Guófān was instructed by edict to withstand the difficulties
with even greater caution.
Zuǒ Zōngtáng's army recovered Yīxìan.
Láo Chóngguāng was appointed Governor-General of Yúnguì.
Tián Xīngshù was arrested and brought to justice to appease the French.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Cantonese and Niǎn bandits attacked Fèngtái and Dìngyuǎn;
the government army repelled them.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Wēng Zēngyuán and two hundred others were granted jinshì and other degrees.
The acre donation in Sìchuān was suspended.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Chéng Xuéqǐ's army and others recovered Kūnshān and Xīnyáng.
The government army defeated bandit chief Lǐ Xiùchéng at Shíjiànpù.
On the day Yǐsì,
Muslim bandits attacked Xī'ān again,
and were repelled.
In this month,
there were continuous prayers for rain.
Land taxes for Tàicāng and other prefectures and counties were remitted.
In the fifth month, on the day Wùshēn,
Miáo Pèilín besieged Méngchéng.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Bāo Chāo's army recaptured Cháoxiàn.
On the day Gēngxū,
Li Yúnlín, a director in the imperial court, was rewarded with the title Jīngqīng,
and given command of the defensive troops in Hànnán and the Sichuan relief forces.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the Cantonese (Taiping) and Niǎn rebels jointly attacked Tiāncháng,
and the government forces defeated them.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Jiāng Zhōngyì was ordered to lead troops to reinforce Jiāngxī.
On the day Dīngsì,
the cult bandits in Zōuxiàn were pacified,
and their leader Liú Shuāngyìn was captured.
The Cantonese rebels captured Gǔzhōu.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Russian troops entered Kēbùduō territory,
and seized the Tàijí.
On the day Rénxū,
it rained.
On the day Guǐhài,
the Cantonese rebels harassed Fùyáng,
and the government forces repelled them,
but Commander-in-Chief Xióng Jiànyì and others died in battle.
The government forces suffered a defeat in relieving Píngliáng,
and Duō Lóng'ā was urged to dispatch troops for rapid reinforcement.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the Muslim rebels in Níngxià rebelled again.
Bāo Chāo's army recaptured Cháo, Hé, and Hánshān.
Yàn Duānshū was summoned to the capital,
Máo Hóngbīn was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng,
and Yùn Shìlín was appointed Governor of Húnán.
The Ming dynasty official Fāng Xiàorú was granted posthumous veneration in the Temple of Confucius.
On the day Wùchén,
an edict was issued to purchase steamboats to be commanded by Zēng Guófān and Lǐ Hóngzhāng.
On the day Jǐsì,
Zēng Guófān declined the governorship of Zhèjiāng for his brother Guóquán,
and the Emperor commended him,
but did not accept the resignation.
Muslims in Xīníng colluded with Sā bandits to attack Dāngá'ěr Tīng.
Hui rebels in Huìyuǎn revolted,
and government forces captured and executed them.
A trade treaty with Denmark was established.
On the day Réshēn,
Péng Yùlín's army and others recaptured Jiāngpǔ, Pǔkǒu, and Jiǔfúzhoū.
On the day Yǐhài,
Guǎngxī forces recaptured Xúnzhōu.
On the first day of the sixth month, Bǐngzǐ,
Qián forces recaptured Pǔ'ān and Ānnán.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Míng Yì was ordered to go to Tǎchéng to meet Míng Xù and others to handle boundary demarcation.
On the day Wùyín,
an imperial edict instructed Zēng Guófān, Zuǒ Zōngtáng, and others to discuss reducing the grain tribute from Cháng and Zhèn prefectures in Jiāngsū,
and Háng, Jiā, Hú prefectures in Zhèjiāng.
On the day Gēngchén,
for their success in recapturing cities,
Lǐ Cháobīn and others, and Sòng Guóyǒng and others were rewarded with a yellow jacket.
The regular tribute from Shǎnxī was suspended.
On the day Dīnghài,
Sichuan forces annihilated the bandits at Dàdùhé,
captured Shí Dákāi,
and executed him.
Luò Bǐngzhāng was promoted to the title of Tàizǐ Tàibǎo,
and Commander-in-Chief Táng Yǒugēng was promoted to Tiánú.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the Muslim populace in Píngluó rebelled again.
Hui rebels in Wǎtíng besieged Lóngdé,
and were repelled.
The river burst its banks in Kāizhōu, Kǎochéng, and Hézé.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Miáo Pèilín captured Shòuzhōu,
and Prefect Máo Wéiyì died there.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Shǎnxī forces recaptured Níngqiāng.
On the day Jǐhài,
due to the Russians forcefully occupying pastures,
Cháng Qīng and others were urged to demarcate the boundary,
persuade the Russian troops to withdraw,
and pacify and receive the Kazakhs and Buruts seeking to join the empire.
On the day Rén'yín,
government forces recaptured Zīchuān,
captured Liú Dépéi and others, and executed them.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the local bandits in Bǎoqìng were pacified.
Liú Róng, the Provincial Administration Commissioner of Sìchuān, was ordered to oversee military affairs in Hànnán.
This month,
the disturbed outstanding taxes in Shùnchāng and other counties in Fújiàn were remitted,
as were the accumulated arrears and miscellaneous taxes in Yìníng and other prefectures and counties in Jiāngxī.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Yǐsì,
Miáo Pèilín pressed towards Línhuái,
and Táng Xùnfāng attacked him.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng's army recaptured Wújiāng and Zhènzé.
Yù forces captured the bandit stronghold of Zhānggāng.
Yīngqǐ committed a crime,
and was stripped of his office.
Liú Róng was appointed Governor of Shǎnxī,
and Zhāng Jíxīn acted in his stead.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was ordered to temporarily concurrently serve as Commissioner for Trade in the Southern Seas.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Qián forces recaptured Gǔzhōu.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Yuán Jiǎsān died in the army.
On the day Rénxū,
Shèng Bǎo was granted permission to commit suicide.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
government forces captured the bandit strongholds in Shāwō and other places.
The collection of commuted grain tribute in Jiāngběi was still permitted.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Liú Róng was also ordered to command the Húběi relief forces.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
government forces repelled the Miáo populace at Lángshān,
and the road to Méngchéng was opened.
Chóng Hòu was appointed plenipotentiary minister
to handle the trade treaty with the Netherlands.
Dian (Yunnan) Hui rebels captured Píngyí,
and Cén Yùyīng's army recaptured it.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Míng Yì and others were ordered to cooperate with the Russian envoy to handle various boundary demarcation matters.
The Báiliánchí cult bandits in Shāndōng were pacified.
Wén Yù was released.
Niǎn rebels threatened Kāifēng.
This month,
the disturbed old and new outstanding taxes in Dūyún and other prefectures, departments, and counties were remitted,
as were the accumulated arrears of rent on riverine lands in Fènghuáng and other departments and counties.
In the eighth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
Chéng Xuéqǐ's army and others inflicted a major defeat on the rebels at Tàihú, Fēngjīng and other places,
and advanced to threaten Sūzhōu.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Cáo Kèzhōng's army in Shǎnxī captured the bandit strongholds in Fùshěng and other places.
On the day Wùyín,
Han and Hui in Xīníng, Dídao, and Hézhōu fought each other.
Kazakhs colluded with Russian soldiers to harass Yīlí.
Hé Shèngbì's army in Sìchuān was urged to reinforce Gān(sù).
On the day Gēngchén,
Wǎn forces captured Chánghuáiwèi.
On the day Xīnsì,
Mǎ Dézhāo was stripped of his office for cowardice.
Duō Lóng'ā's army reached Xī'ān,
and Wèinán was pacified.
Chén Guóruì was ordered to assist Wú Táng in military affairs.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Sū forces captured Jiāngyīn.
On the day Dīnghài,
Yīngqǐ was exiled to Xīnjiāng.
Dū Xīng'ā dispatched troops to reinforce Línhuái.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Wú Hóngyuán was stripped of his office
and arrested for questioning
due to improper command in suppressing the bandits in Táiwān.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng went to Jiāngyīn to oversee the suppression.
Chén Guóruì was ordered to reinforce Méngchéng.
Shàn Qìng's cavalry unit was transferred to reinforce Línhuái.
Xī Lín dispatched troops to reinforce Píngliáng.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Duō Lóng'ā's request was granted,
Cáo Kèzhōng was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Hézhōu,
and it was also stipulated that henceforth vacancies for Tiánú and Zhèndú should not be arbitrarily requested.
Sòng Jǐngshī escaped to Kāizhōu.
Zhāng Jíxīn was ordered to consult with Mù Téng'ā to prepare for the defense of Xī'ān.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Qián forces captured the bandit stronghold of Tóngzǐ.
Pǔ'ān fell,
but was soon recaptured.
Liú Róng was ordered to command Máo Zhènshòu's and Lǐ Yúnlín's respective armies.
Troops from Wūlǔmùqí and Ākèsū were dispatched to assist the Yīlí forces in resisting Russia.
The succession of the Khagan title by the Kazakh Chuòtán was approved.
On the day Jǐhài,
Lín Wénchá was urged to cross to Táiwān to suppress bandits.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Hui rebels captured Píngliáng.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Yán Jìngmíng moved his army to Dōngchāng.
The treaty with the Netherlands was finalized.
Liú Chángyòu went to Jǐngzhōu to oversee the suppression.
This month,
outstanding taxes in Qìnzhōu and other prefectures, departments, and counties were remitted.
On the *yǐsì* day of the ninth month,
orders were given to Mǎ Dézhāo to proceed to Qìngyáng camp.
Shěn Bǎozhēn requested leave due to illness,
but was persuaded to stay and granted leave.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng's request to transfer magistrate Dīng Rìchāng to Shànghǎi to supervise the manufacture of firearms was granted.
Lù Kūnhéng, magistrate of Shíquán, organized local militias to suppress bandits,
and an imperial edict commended him.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Zhè army recaptured Fùyáng.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the Yuè army recaptured Guǎnghǎizhài city.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Sēnggélínqìn was instructed to take the artillery corps to Méngchéng to assist in suppression.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Yuè bandits captured Chénggù.
Niǎn leaders Zhāng Zǒngyú and others fled south from Rǔzhōu.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Duōlóng'ā's army recovered Gāolíng.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Mùlóng'ā was dismissed from his post for submitting a false report.
Duōlóng'ā was transferred as General of Xī'ān.
Fùmíng'ā was appointed General of Jīngzhōu.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Duōlóng'ā's army captured the bandit lairs at Sūjiāgōu and Wèichéng.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Yuè bandits captured Huìtóng and Suíníng,
but they were soon recovered.
The Shǎnxī corps recovered Miǎnxuàn.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Lǐ Xiùchéng reinforced Wúxī,
but Chéng Xuéqǐ and others repelled him.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Sēnggélínqìn completely suppressed the bandit faction of Sòng Jǐngshī.
Sòng Jǐngshī fled.
Due to the defeat of the Chuān army reinforcing Shǎnxī,
Tídū Xiāo Qìnggāo was dismissed from his post
but retained in the camp.
Due to the incident in Hànzhōng,
Bùzhèngshǐ Máo Zhènshòu was dismissed from his post.
Liú Chángyòu and Yán Jìngmíng were instructed to manage rehabilitation in Zhílì and Lǔ.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Yùshǐ Mǎ Yuánruì submitted a memorial detailing four matters: lighten taxes, be cautious in litigation, govern kindly, and diligently issue clear proclamations.
His requests were implemented.
In this month,
arrears of salt tax for households in Cāngzhōu and other prefectures and counties in Zhílì,
and Hǎifēng and other salt fields in Shāndōng were remitted.
In the winter, on the *yǐhài* day of the tenth month,
Yán Jìngmíng requested to observe the full mourning period,
but this was not granted.
Government troops captured Zhū Dēngfēng and other Zhí-Dōng bandits
and executed them all.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Niǎn leader Zhāng Zǒngyú fled south from Lǔshān and Nánzhào.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Táo Màolín's army lifted the siege of Fèngxiáng,
and Táo Màolín was formally appointed Tídū of Gānsù.
Tíngyōu Zǒngbīng Chéng Lù was ordered to remain in the camp.
Lǐ Tàiguó was dismissed,
and Hèdé was appointed to manage the Inspectorate General of Customs.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Yuè bandits invaded Lóngshèng,
and Zǒngbīng Hú Yuánchāng died there.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Luò Bǐngzhāng was instructed to deploy troops to suppress Zhānduì
and clear the Tibetan roads.
An edict forbade French missionaries from entering Tibet to preach.
On the *dīnghài* day,
remaining bandits from Cháoyáng raided Chāngtú.
An imperial edict urged officials to strive for frugality.
Jiǎ Hóngzhào was ordered to proceed to Zhāotōng.
Zānsàkè Táijí Míngzhū'ěrdō'ěrzhì was granted the title of Bèizǐ for donating horses.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Lǐ Yúnlín's army suffered a defeat,
and Yuè bandits captured Shānyáng, Shǎnxī.
Zhāng Zǒngyú fled to Dèngzhōu.
Lài, Cáo, and other chiefs fled to Fèngxiàn and Liǎngdāng.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng's army defeated the bandits occupying Hángzhōu and Yúháng.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Lán rebels captured Zhōuzhì.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Emperor's mourning period having expired,
Qí Jùnzǎo, Wō Rén, and Lǐ Hóngzǎo requested that extravagance be eliminated to solidify imperial virtue.
An imperial decree stated:
"All matters of frivolous amusement, sightseeing, and construction are to be set aside.
Qí Jùnzǎo and others shall give advice morning and night
to cultivate noble virtue
and thus rectify the root of governance and diligently practice it."
Rebel chief Gǔ Lóngxián surrendered,
and Shídài, Tàipíng, and Jīngdé were recovered.
Zēng Guóquán's army recovered Mòlíngguān.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the Guì army recovered Róngxiàn.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Chéng Xuéqǐ's army captured Hǔxùguān.
On the *jǐhài* day,
government troops failed to suppress the Chāngtú bandits,
and Yùmíng was reprimanded for concealment.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Yīng Guì was transferred to General of Fúzhōu,
and Shěn Guìfēn was appointed acting巡撫 of Shānxī.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Lǐ Xiùchéng reinforced Sūzhōu,
but Lǐ Hèzhāng's army defeated him.
Fùmíng'ā was ordered to assist Sēnggélínqìn with military affairs.
In this month,
new and old taxes for Yǒng'ān and other prefectures, departments, and counties in Guǎngxī that had suffered disturbances were remitted.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day of the eleventh month,
Fèngtiān bandits raided Jílín,
and Yùmíng and others jointly suppressed them.
The Wǎn army recovered Huáiyuǎn and Bàngfǔ.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Sēnggélínqìn led the various armies to attack and suppress Miáo Pèilín
and executed him.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng led his army to recover Sūzhōu,
and Yuè chief Gào Yúnguān and others surrendered.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was granted the title of Tàizǐ Shǎobǎo,
and Chéng Xuéqǐ was granted a hereditary title
and a yellow riding jacket.
On the *wùshēn* day,
rebel chiefs Yáng Yǒuqīng and others surrendered Hùgāo, Níngguó, Jiànpíng, and Lìshuǐ.
Lǐ Yúnlín and others recovered Shānyáng.
The Yuè army recovered Xìnyí.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Liú Diǎn's army recovered Chànghuà.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Lán rebels fled to Shāngnán.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Zhāng Zǒngyú fled to Xīchuān.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Sēnggélínqìn's army recovered Xiàcài and Shòuzhōu.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng executed Gào Yúnguān and others
and disbanded the surrendered forces.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Lǐ Hèzhāng's army captured Wúxī and Jīnkuì.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Lǐ Xùyí died.
Bandits Zhāng Běngōng and others from Qiūxiàn gathered a crowd to resist grain collection,
and they were captured and executed.
Yán Jìngmíng was formally appointed Shāndōng Xúnfǔ.
Huí people from Qiānyáng surrendered.
On the *rénxū* day,
government troops recovered Yǐngshàng and Zhèngyáng.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Mǎ Huàlóng captured Níngxià and Língzhōu.
For his merits in suppressing the Miáo rebels,
Lǐ Shìzhōng's post was restored.
Zēng Guóquán's army captured Chunhuà and other passes
and advanced to Xiàolíng.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
government troops captured Zhāngjīnghuì in Jiāshàn.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the rebel Huí besieged the Manchu city of Níngxià.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Sū army recovered Pínghú.
Bandit leaders surrendered Zhàpǔ and Jiāshàn.
In this month,
money and grain for Sǐshuǐ and other prefectures and counties in Shāndōng affected by disaster and disturbance,
and taxes for Wǔqīng and other prefectures and counties in Zhílì affected by disaster were remitted.
Disaster relief was provided for Dǎshēngwūlā in Jílín.
On the *dīngchǒu* day of the twelfth month,
Tídū Jiāng Zhōngyì died in Jiangxi during military operations.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Sū army captured Píngwàng.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Táng Xùnfāng was dismissed,
and Qiáo Sōngnián was appointed Ānhuī Xúnfǔ.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Táng Yǒugēng was appointed Yúnnán Tídū
and ordered to proceed to Zhāotōng.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Tán Tíngxiāng spoke about the overall planning for the lower reaches of the Yellow River,
requesting the dredging of branch canals to reduce flooding
and the reinforcement of earthen dikes to protect farmland.
Liú Chángyòu and Yán Jìngmíng were instructed to jointly plan and implement this.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Shǎnxī Huí and Yuè bandits scattered and fled into Gān territory.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the reduction of price for tribute grain from Sū, Sōng, and Tài was granted.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Emperor held a grand banquet in the Fǔchén Hall,
hosting Mongolian princes and dukes,
and bestowed various rewards.
This was done every year.
Zhānghuà was recovered,
and the two routes of bandits in Táiwān were pacified.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Wēng Tóngshū was granted clemency and exiled.
Zuǒ Zōngtáng was ordered to eliminate long-standing abuses in land and poll taxes in Zhèdōng.
Shǎn, È, and Chuān were instructed to jointly suppress the rebel bandits in Hánnán.
In this month,
new and old taxes for disturbed prefectures and counties in Shāndōng and Shǎnxī,
as well as granary grain for Xiàoyì and other departments and counties, were remitted.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn paid tribute.
In the third year, *Jiǎzǐ*, on the first day of the first lunar month, *Guǐmǎo*, in spring,
the Emperor led the *Wáng*, *Dàchén* to congratulate the two Empresses Dowager (Liǎnggōng Huángtàihòu).
After the ceremony,
he presided over the *Tàihédiàn* to receive court.
From then on, this was done every year.
On *Jiǎchén*,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng's army attacked the rebels aiding Chángzhōu at Bēnnú Zhèn,
achieving a great victory.
On *Bǐngwǔ*,
the Huímín of Fèngxiáng requested pacification,
which was granted.
Bandits from Shāngnán absconded to Yúnxī.
Húběi's Shí Qīngjí's army was transferred to Shǎn.
The Chuān army reinforcing Shǎn suffered a defeat at Qīngshí Guān.
On *Gēngxū*,
the Niǎn bandits from Hénán absconded to Suízhōu.
On *Guǐchǒu*,
the Yù army attacked Zhāng Zǒngyú at Zhàozhuāng Shānkǒu,
suffering a defeat.
On *Jǐwèi*,
the government army recaptured Xiūwén and Cèhēng.
On *Gēngshēn*,
troops from Zhí and Jìn were transferred to reinforce Níngxià.
An edict was issued to Ālāshàn Qí prohibiting Mongolians from colluding with Huí bandits.
On *Jiǎzǐ*,
Lǐ Shìxián absconded to Jīxī.
On *Bǐngyín*,
Dūxīng'ā was ordered to Suíyuǎn to jointly manage defense affairs.
Fùmíng'ā went to Yángzhōu to take over military affairs.
On *Jǐsì*,
the Zhè army recaptured Hǎiníng.
The bandit leader Dài Wànshēng of Zhānghuà was executed.
The Yuè bandits absconded to Shíquán, Hànyīn, and Níngshǎn.
This month,
arrears of taxes due to poor harvests in Ānzhōu and other places were remitted.
On the first day of the second lunar month, *Rénshēn*,
the government army recaptured Hánzhōng Liúbà.
The Qián army recaptured Lónglǐ.
On *Yǐhài*,
the Yuè bandits absconded to Guǎngxìn and Jiànchāng.
On *Gēngchén*,
the Huí bandits of Níngxià attacked Zhōngwèi and other places,
and Xīlín dispatched troops to reinforce them.
On *Rénwǔ*,
the local bandits of Sānshān, Guǎngdōng, were pacified.
On *Guǐwèi*,
the Yuè bandits captured Zhèn'ān,
but it was soon recaptured.
On *Dīnghài*,
Duōlóng'ā's siege of Zhōuzhì had long failed to take it,
and he was severely reprimanded.
The *mǔjuān* in Shāndōng was suspended,
following Yán Jìngmíng's request.
On *Wùzǐ*,
the Guì army conquered Cāngwú and other counties.
On *Gēngyín*,
Zēng Guóquán and other armies conquered Zhōngshān Shílěi,
completing the encirclement of Jīnlíng.
Jiǎng Yìlǐ's army recaptured Tóngxiāng.
The Yuè bandits pressed on Mǐn territory,
and Zhāng Yùnlán's army reinforced it.
On *Rénchén*,
the Yù army conquered the bandit strongholds of Xīxiàn and Guāngzhōu.
On *Jiǎwǔ*,
the Yuè bandits absconded to Guǎngfēng and Yìyáng.
On *Gēngzǐ*,
the bandits of Shǎnnán absconded to Nèixiāng.
On *Rényín* in the third lunar month,
Chéng Xuéqǐ and other armies conquered Jiāxīng.
The Gàn army took Jīnxī.
The Jiāngnán army recaptured Lìyáng.
The Shǎn army conquered Zhōuzhì,
Duōlóng'ā was granted leave due to injury,
and Mùtúshàn temporarily oversaw military affairs.
Léi Zhèngwǎn and other armies advanced to suppress the rebellious Huí.
The Chuān bandit Lán Èrshùn absconded to Xúnyáng.
On *Bǐngwǔ*,
Sēnggélínqìn led his entire army to Yù,
advancing to Xǔzhōu.
The Jiāngnán army recaptured Guǎngdé.
The Jiāyì bandit leader Lín Gànshèng was executed.
On *Jǐyǒu*,
Gēdēng (Gordon) was wounded while attacking Jīntán,
and an order was given to express sympathy.
Cén Yùyīng and other armies conquered Tāláng and Zhèn​yuán.
On *Gēngxū*,
Duōlóng'ā was ordered to oversee military affairs in Shǎn and Gān.
On *Rénzǐ*,
Jiǎng Yìlǐ's armies recaptured Hángzhōu and Yúháng.
Zuǒ Zōngtáng was given the title of *Tàizǐ Shǎobǎo*,
and Yìlǐ was rewarded with a yellow jacket (huángmǎguà),
and later a hereditary post (shìzhí).
On *Jiǎyín*,
taxes for two years were remitted in the newly recovered areas of Háng and Jiā.
Mùtúshàn was ordered to assist Duōlóng'ā in military affairs,
and temporarily act as *Qīnchāi Dàchén*.
The Chuān army attacked the Sōngpān bandits,
and recaptured Diéxī Yíngchéng.
On *Dīngsì*,
the Diān army recaptured Jǐngdōng, Yuánmóu, and Chǔxióng.
On *Guǐhài*,
the Gàn bandits absconded to Fújiàn.
On *Yǐchǒu*,
the rebel leader Lán Dàshùn was executed.
On *Bǐngyín*,
the Zhè army recaptured Wǔkāng, Déqīng, and Shímén.
An edict was issued to Zuǒ Zōngtáng to take in refugees from Hángzhōu.
On *Jǐsì*,
Commander Chéng Xuéqǐ died in the army.
On *Gēngwǔ*,
Zhāng Zǒngyú absconded to Zhènpíng.
The Gānsù Huí bandit Mǎ Sānwá captured Chìjīnbǎo,
and the government army suppressed and pacified them.
This month,
arrears of taxes were remitted for the disturbed prefectures, departments, subprefectures, and counties of Guìzhōu.
On the first day of the fourth lunar month, *Xīnwèi*, in summer,
there was a solar eclipse.
On *Rénshēn*,
Bào Chāo's army recaptured Jùróng.
On *Bǐngzǐ*,
Dūxīng'ā was ordered to Dìngbiān to take command of Nàqīn's various armies,
and advance to suppress the bandits occupying Nínglíng.
On *Dīngchǒu*,
Lǐ Shìxián and others absconded to Jiāngxī.
Bào Chāo's army recaptured Jīntán.
The Niǎn and Yuè bandits together absconded to Zǎoyáng.
The Shǎnnán bandits absconded to Hénán,
capturing Jīngziguān.
On *Wùyín*,
the Xiāng army jointly recaptured Gǔzhōu.
On *Xīnsì*,
excessive tax collections in Shàoxīng were investigated and reduced,
and this was established as a permanent rule.
On *Jiǎshēn*,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng's army conquered Chángzhōu.
Féng Zǐcái and other armies recaptured Dānyáng.
The crown prince of the late King Lǐ ● of Cháoxiǎn was to inherit the title,
and Minister Zàobǎo and Vice-Commander Wénqiān were ordered to confer the title.
On *Bǐngxū*,
as Minister Xuē Huàn and Grand Secretary Wáng Zhěng mutually accused each other,
both were demoted,
and officials were warned again.
Guān Wén went to Ānlù to oversee the army,
and Yán Shùsēn managed the defense of the provincial capital.
On *Gēngyín*,
Duōlóng'ā died in the army.
Dūxīng'ā was ordered to oversee military affairs in Gānsù,
with Léi Zhèngwǎn assisting him.
On *Xīnmǎo*,
the Gàn army lifted the siege of Yùshān.
On *Guǐsì*,
Yán Shùsēn was demoted due to impeachment by Guān Wén,
Wú Chāngshòu was made Governor of Húběi,
and Táng Xùnfāng was appointed acting Governor.
Yáng Yuèbīn was ordered to oversee military affairs in Jiāngxī and southern Ān.
On *Xīnmǎo*,
Sēnggélínqìn joined the Chǔ army to suppress the Yuè and Niǎn at Suízhōu,
greatly defeating them.
On *Dīngyǒu*,
as the lower reaches of the river defense were cleared,
warships were reduced,
and the ban on sealing the river was lifted.
On *Wùxū*,
the Yuè bandits captured Yìyáng.
The Yuè rebels from Shǎnnán absconded to Dé'ān Fǔ,
and Sēnggélínqìn's army pursued and suppressed them.
On *Jǐhài*,
commanding ministers were warned against embellishing their reports.
This month,
the current year's fixed taxes for Wǔjìn and Yánghú were remitted.
On the *gēngzǐ* day of the fifth month,
the Qián-bandits captured Chángzhài, Dìngfān, and Guǎngshùn.
They were subsequently recovered.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the Yuè-bandits fled to Tiānmén, Yìngchéng, Dé'ān, and Suízhōu.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Yuè-bandits captured Nínghuà.
It was subsequently recovered.
Xīlín was dismissed due to illness.
Yáng Yuèbīn was appointed Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù,
with Dū Xīng'ā acting in his stead.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Spain was permitted to establish a treaty for trade.
Xuē Huàn and Chóng Hòu were ordered to serve as plenipotentiary ministers
to handle the matter appropriately.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was instructed to dispatch elite troops to assist in attacking Jīnlíng.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Lǐ Shìxián attacked Fǔzhōu.
The government forces repelled him,
and recovered Yìyáng.
Gēdēng was awarded a yellow riding jacket and a peacock feather,
as well as the insignia of a Grandee.
The Ever Victorious Army was reorganized, with foreign officers dismissed.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the government forces recovered Dūjiāng, Shàngjiāng, and other cities.
The Yuè-bandits advanced and threatened Xī'ān.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Liú Róng and Lǐ Yúnlín were stripped of their posts,
but retained their duties.
Mùtúshàn was ordered to remain in Xī'ān to collectively plan defense and suppression.
The Qián-bandits fled to Xiùshān.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Bào Chāo requested leave to bury his relative.
An imperial edict comforted him and asked him to stay.
Lǐ Shìxián captured Yíhuáng and Chóngrén.
Nánchāng was put under martial law.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the Huí-bandits captured Díliáo.
It was subsequently recovered.
On the *rénxū* day,
the Yuè-bandits fled to Huángpí.
Guān Wén moved his troops to Xiàogǎn.
On the *guǐhài* day,
an imperial decree ordered Ruìcháng, Bǎoyún, Zàilíng, Shàn Màoshuī, and Xú Tóng to take turns delivering lectures on the *Zhìpíng Bǎojiàn*.
The Yuè-bandits again captured Jiànníng and Nínghuà.
They were subsequently recovered.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Léi Zhèngwǎn's army recovered Píngliáng.
On the *wùchén* day,
provincial governors were instructed to cooperate across boundaries
in apprehending border bandits.
Lǐ Héngsōng and Liú Xúngāo were ordered to exchange treaties with the Danish envoy Bìlēi in Shànghǎi.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Guì army captured the bandit stronghold in Guìxiàn.
Xúnzhōu was pacified.
On the *rénshēn* day of the sixth month,
ministers of various departments were warned not to revert to their former slackness.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Yuè-bandits fled to Máchéng and Huánggāng.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
it rained.
The Sū army recovered Chángxīng.
The Qián army recovered Pǔ'ān.
Mǎ Rúlóng and Cén Yùyīng's armies suppressed the Huí-bandits in Yíxī,
and recovered Zhōngdiàn, Wéixī, Sīmáo, Wēiyuǎn, and the bandit strongholds at Shígāojǐng.
On the *wùyín* day,
Han Chinese and Huí rebelled in Kùchē.
The Resident Minister Wényì and the Huí Prince Àimòtè died in the conflict.
Kazakh people were settled southeast of Zhāisāng Nàoyīr.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the Gàn army captured the bandit fort at Guìxī.
Zēng Guóquán's army captured the outer city of Jīnlíng.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
it rained.
The Huí-bandits captured Bùgǔ'ěr and Kù'ěrlè.
An edict ordered the withdrawal of Nàqīn's army.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Zhè army recovered Xiàofēng.
On the *wùxū* day,
the government forces recovered Jiāngníng.
Hóng Xiùquán had already committed suicide.
His son, Hóng Fúzhèn, escaped.
Bandit chiefs Hóng Réná and Lǐ Xiùchéng were captured.
Jiāngnán was pacified.
Prince Chún was dispatched to the Imperial Hall of Wénzōng to offer sacrifices on behalf of the Emperor.
The Emperor visited the two Empresses Dowager to congratulate them on the victory.
In recognition of their merits,
Zēng Guófān was promoted to a first-class marquis;
Zēng Guóquán to a first-class earl,
with the added title of Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince;
Grandee Lǐ Chéndiǎn to a first-class viscount,
and awarded a yellow riding jacket;
Xiāo Fúsì to a first-class baron: all were awarded double-eyed peacock feathers.
Surveillance Commissioner Liú Liánjié and others were awarded hereditary posts,
with varying promotions.
Hóng Xiùquán's corpse was ordered to be mutilated,
and his head paraded in all provinces.
In recognition of the achievements in suppressing bandits across various fronts,
Sēnggélínqìn's son, Bóyànnèimóhù, was enfeoffed as a *Bèilè*.
Guān Wén was made a first-class earl.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was made a first-class earl.
Luò Bǐngzhāng was made a first-class Light Chariot Commandant.
All were awarded double-eyed peacock feathers.
Yáng Yuèbīn and Péng Yùlín were given the added title of Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince.
Bào Chāo was also made a first-class Light Chariot Commandant.
Dū Xīng'ā, Fùmíng'ā, and Féng Zǐcái were made Cavalry Commandants.
Kuí Yù was made a Cloud Chariot Commandant.
The Huí rebels captured Kālāshā'ěr.
The Resident Minister Yīqílǐ and others all died there.
This month,
arrears of tribute from counties like Jiànníng in Fújiàn that suffered disturbances were remitted.
In the autumn, on the *gēngzǐ* day of the seventh month,
in recognition of the pacification of Jiāngnán,
the Deliberative Prince Gōngqīnwáng's son Zài Chéng was promoted to *Bèilè*.
Zài Jùn was made a Prince of the Second Rank who does not participate in the Eight Divisions.
Zài Yíng was made a Prince of the Second Rank who does not participate in the Eight Divisions.
Grand Councillor Wén Xiáng was given the added title of Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince.
Bǎoyún and Lǐ Tángjiē were given the added title of Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince.
Special favors were bestowed upon imperial relatives, grand ministers of the Imperial Council, and ministers of the Imperial Household Department.
Other rewards and appointments varied.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
as it was the *jiǎzǐ* year,
an edict ordered the suspension of trials for certain severe criminal cases.
The edict stated:
"Jiāngnán has been newly recovered,
and the people's lives are devastated.
Officials should recruit and provide relief.
In provinces where military affairs are not yet pacified,
commanding ministers, governors-general, and governors must encourage their officers and soldiers,
to strive for achievement."
Russian soldiers entered the fort at Kēbùduō,
seizing the commissioner and the Zāsàkè.
On the *rénkǎ* day,
imperial clansmen and collateral imperial clansmen were forbidden from residing secretly in the outer city.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
those who had aided Miáo Pèilín were retrospectively punished.
General Bó Chóngwǔ and others were exiled to Xīnjiāng.
Surveillance Commissioner Zhāng Xuéchún was exiled to Jūntái.
The Yuè-bandits fled and occupied Luótián.
The Guì-bandits captured Guīshùn.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
an edict ordered the restoration of Míng Tàizǔ's tomb.
The *líjīn* tax in Jiāngběi was abolished.
The salt administration of Liǎnghuái was restored.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Shěn Guìfēn was formally appointed Governor of Shānxī.
Zhèng Dūnjǐn was appointed Governor-General of River Conservancy for Héjīang.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the Danish treaty was successfully exchanged.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Hóng Réná and Lǐ Xiùchéng were executed.
Wāng Hǎiyáng fled and occupied Xǔwān.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Hóng Fúzhèn entered Húzhōu.
The Huí-bandits of Yánchá and Gùyuán rebelled again,
fleeing north to Nínglíng,
and disturbing Zhōngwèi and Jìngyuǎn.
The Sāhuí bandits conspired and captured Xúnhuà Tīng.
