Han Chinese and Huí in Tuólǔfān's Tuōkèsùn also revolted.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Vice Minister of Revenue Wú Tíngdòng reported the victory at Jīnlíng
and requested increased reverence and caution.
His suggestion was graciously accepted.
On the *dīngsì* day,
due to blocked roads in Guǎngxī,
Việt Nam's tribute was suspended.
Han Chinese and Huí revolted in Qítái.
Gǔchéng and Wūlǔmùqí simultaneously became unstable.
Wén Guāng's army advanced to reinforce Kùchē,
but suffered a defeat,
and was annihilated at Wūshātǎkèlā,
where they died.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the Dí and Hé Huí-bandits conspired with the Sāhuí to disturb Hézhōu.
The Gàn army recovered Chóngrén and Dōngxiāng.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Jīnxī was recovered.
On the *rénxū* day,
Qí Jùnzǎo requested retirement due to illness.
He was ordered to retain his Grand Secretary title and serve in the Hóngdé Hall.
Government forces captured bandits Liú Fāhǎo and others from Chāngtú,
and executed them.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the princely titles of Zhèngqīnwáng and Yíqīnwáng were restored.
In recognition of the achievements of deceased officials,
Hú Línyì was granted a first-class Light Chariot Commandant.
Lǐ Xùbīn was granted a second-class Light Chariot Commandant.
Tǎqíbù, Zhāng Guóliáng, Jiāng Zhōngyuán, and Chéng Xuéqǐ were granted third-class Light Chariot Commandants.
Jiāng Zhōngjì, Luó Zénán, Duōlóng'ā, and Zēng Guóhuá were additionally awarded a Cloud Chariot Commandant.
The Gàn army recovered Yíhuáng.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Xǔwān was captured.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Sēnggélínqìn defeated bandits in Máchéng.
Zēng Guóquán requested leave due to illness.
He was gently persuaded to stay.
Lǐ Chéndiǎn died in the army from his wounds.
This month,
arrears of tribute from various disturbed areas in Jiāngsū and Ānhuī were remitted.
On the *jǐsì* day of the eighth month, the first day of the lunar month,
the seating order of the various princes was fixed,
and established as a regulation.
The Gàn army recaptured Nánfēng.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Urumqi *cānjīang* rebelled.
The *tídū* Yèpǔchōng'é died in the conflict.
Yīlí was in critical danger,
so Qílǎbāhātái Khalkha Mongol troops were dispatched to reinforce it.
An edict instructed Liú Róng to take sole charge of military affairs in Shǎnxī,
and Mùtúshàn to lead his forces to Gān,
to plan military affairs with Léi Zhèngwǎn.
Yáng Yuèbīn was urged to immediately proceed to his post in Shǎnxī and Gān.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
an edict instructed Zhāng Jíxīn to go to Gùyuán and Yánchá to manage pacification and relief matters.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the imperial forces of Sū and Zhè jointly recaptured Húzhōu and Ānjí.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the Gàn army recaptured Xīnchéng,
and Chén Bǐngwén surrendered.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the imperial forces recaptured Guǎngdé.
Guō Sōnglín was awarded a hereditary title,
and Yáng Dǐngxūn and Zhōu Shèngbō were awarded yellow riding jackets.
The bandits in Guìxiàn were suppressed.
Liú Míngchuán was promoted to *zhílì tídū*.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Hui bandits captured Gǔchéng Hánchéng.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Léi Zhèngwǎn's army recaptured the bandit lair at Zhāngjiāchuān.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Sēnggélínqìn suffered a defeat while suppressing bandits fleeing Luóshān,
and the *dūtǒng* Shūtōng'é and others died.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Jiǎ Hóngzhào, the Governor of Yúnnán, was stripped of his office
for feigning illness to evade duty.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Tǔxiètúhàn and Chēchénhàn Mongol troops were dispatched to Urumqi and other places to assist in the suppression.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Zhè army pursued bandits to Chānghuà and Chún'ān,
capturing and executing bandit chiefs Huáng Wénjīn and others.
Lín Hóngnián was appointed Governor of Yúnnán.
On the *guǐsì* day,
an edict ordered the various ministers in Xīnjiāng to separately manage suppression and pacification.
The Hui Prince Bóxī'ěr was commended
for rallying the various cities to kill bandits.
Hui bandits rioted in Kù'ěrkǎlāwūsū and other places,
and the imperial forces suffered a defeat.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Línxìng was ordered to manage border demarcation affairs in Wūlǐyǎsūtái.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Sēnggélínqìn suffered a defeat while suppressing bandits,
and the *zǒngbīng* Bāyáng'ā and others died.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Léi Zhèngwǎn's attack on Liánhuāchéng was unsuccessful,
and the Hui bandits again captured Gùyuán.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Hé and Dí Hui bandits raided Lánzhōu and Jīnxiàn.
On the *jǐhài* day of the ninth month, the first day of the lunar month,
Liú Míngchuán's various armies defeated bandits fleeing Níngguó and other places.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the Gàn army recaptured Yúdū.
Lǐ Yúnlín was stripped of his office
for feigning illness to evade duty,
and the Lǒng army he commanded was disbanded.
On the *rénwèi* day,
Zēng Guóquán requested to be relieved of duty due to illness,
and this was granted.
Mǎ Xīnyí was appointed Governor of Zhèjiāng,
and was ordered to remain and manage defensive affairs in Ānqìng.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Mùtúshàn was ordered to assist Dūxīng'ā in military affairs.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Yáng Yuèbīn requested leave due to illness,
but was kindly persuaded to stay.
Lǐ Shìxián attacked Nán'ān,
and the imperial forces repelled him.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Hui bandits captured Yè'ěrqiāng,
and the acting *cānzàn* Kuídòng died.
The military officers of Kāshígá'ěr and Yīngjíshā'ěr jointly rebelled.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Hui populace of Xīníng surrendered.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Hui bandits from Zhāngjiāchuān attacked Qìngyáng.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Gàn bandits fled to Nánxióng.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Yuè bandits captured Kāihuà,
and fled to Jiāngxī.
Huáng and Má bandits fled to Shāngchéng.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Spain exchanged treaties.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the Imperial Household Department was enjoined to strive for economy.
Zhákètōng'ā was ordered to act as minister of Hāmì.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Xīníng Hui bandits rebelled again.
On the *wǔwǔ* day,
Yuè bandits Cài DéRóng and others fled and captured Jiēzhōu.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
an edict ordered the renovation of the Sage Temple in Qūfù and the academies in various provinces.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the sea wall of Zhèjiāng was repaired.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Niǎn bandits fled to Qīshuǐ,
and the È army suffered a defeat.
The *zǒngbīng* Shí Qīngjí died.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Russian troops illegally entered Ā'ěrtài Nàor.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Shěn Guìfēn requested to raise funds to resettle banner people to relieve them.
On the *wùchén* day of the tenth month in winter, the first day of the lunar month,
Yáng Yuèbīn was granted leave to return home to visit his parents,
and to recruit volunteers for Gān.
Mián Sēn, Minister of Punishments, and Wú Tíngdòng, Vice Minister of Revenue, were ordered to investigate the Cháhā'ěr prison case.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Wénxiáng, the *tídū* of Urumqi, had his name changed to Wénqí.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
General Cháng Qīng was stripped of his office,
Míngxù was appointed to replace him,
and Liánjié was appointed Assistant Minister.
Wǔlóng'ā was ordered to command the various armies reinforcing Urumqi,
exercising control over all officials from the leader of the vanguard downwards.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Bāo Chāo's army achieved a great victory against the bandits,
and he was awarded a double-eyed peacock feather.
Xí Bǎotián's army captured bandit chief Hóng Rén'gān and others.
The areas north and south of Ān were cleared.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Hui bandits captured the Manchu city of Urumqi and Suīlái,
and the *dūtǒng* Píng Ruì and others died.
Han and Hui people revolted in Hāmì.
Bǎo Héng was ordered to act as *dūtǒng* of Urumqi,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng to act as Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
Wú Táng to act as Governor of Jiāngsū,
and Fùmíng'ā to act as Governor-General of the Grain Transport.
On the *wùyín* day,
Hóng Fútián was captured in Shíchéng,
and executed.
Zhěn Bǎozhēn was awarded the hereditary title of First Class Light Chariot Commandant.
Bāo Chāo was enfeoffed as a First Class Viscount.
For his功 in recovering all of Zhèjiāng,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng was enfeoffed as a First Class Earl,
and Jiǎng Yìlǐ was awarded a Cavalry Commandant.
Yuè bandits captured Ruìjīn,
but it was soon recaptured.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Yuè bandits captured Zhāngzhōu, Lóngyán, Nánjìng, and Wǔpíng,
and the Judicial Commissioner Zhāng Yùnlán and others died.
Liú Róng divided his forces to guard Bīnzhōu and other places.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Míngyì exchanged border demarcation treaties with the Russian envoy.
The fortifications of Kēbùduō city, Outer Mongolia,
and the Ā'ěrtài Nàor Wūliánghǎi all belonged to Russia.
Bāo Chāo was granted leave,
and his subordinate forces, led by Sòng Guóyǒng and others, were dispatched to reinforce Mǐn,
under the command of Zuǒ Zōngtáng.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Léi Zhèngwǎn's army recaptured Liánhuāchéng,
and Cáo Kèzhōng was awarded a yellow riding jacket.
Sēnggélínqìn achieved a great victory against the bandits,
and Guō Bǎochāng and others were awarded yellow riding jackets,
while bandit leader Mǎ Rónghé surrendered with his followers.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Sìchuān relief forces recaptured Rénhuái.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Yuè bandits captured Pínghé.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Jiāyīng and Dàpǔ were captured.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Zēng Guófān was instructed to remain stationed in Jīnlíng,
and Lǐ Hóngzhāng and others were to return to their original posts.
In this month,
the disturbed areas of Xìnyáng and other places in Hénán were exempted from their levied taxes,
and the outstanding taxes of Xī'ān and other counties in Zhèjiāng were remitted.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jǐhài,
the grain tax of Jiāngníng prefecture and its dependencies was remitted for three years.
On the day Rén'yín,
the Huí bandits captured Hézhōu.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Golden Dike of Púzhōu was constructed.
On the day Yǐsì,
Wénqí and Bóxī'ěr suppressed and pacified the Hāmì Huí.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
the annual apportionment and indemnification silver for the prefectures and counties of Jiāngsū was remitted,
and the practice of apportionments was permanently prohibited.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Shěn Bǎozhēn requested an order to dispatch reinforcements to Mǐn,
and to guard against the escape of bandits and Huí.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Yuè army recaptured Wǔpíng.
Orders were given for the Mǐn, Zhè, and Gàn armies to jointly suppress them,
preventing them from escaping into the sea.
The Huí bandits captured Ākèsū and Wūshí,
and Bànshì Dàchén Fùzhūlǐ, Wénxīng, and others died.
On the day Guǐhài,
Sēnggélínqìn's attack on the bandits fleeing Xiāng and Zǎo was unsuccessful,
and the Fà and Niǎn bandits then fled to Dèngzhōu.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
an edict was issued ordering the armies of Liú Liánjié and Liú Míngchuán to advance,
and to be placed under the command of Sēnggélínqìn.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Léi Zhèngwǎn's army and others defeated the Gùyuán Huí bandits.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Wénqí and others suppressed the Bālǐkūn Huí bandits,
and pacified them.
The Huí bandits captured Kù'ěrkǎlāwūsū,
and Yīlí was placed under martial law.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Mǎnqìng said that Wāngqǔjiébù had died,
and requested that the title Qīngráo Wāngqǔnuòménhǎn be bestowed,
to assist in handling commercial affairs in Xīzàng,
which was granted.
In this month,
the outstanding taxes of Shàngyuán and other counties in Jiāngsū that had been disturbed were remitted.
In the twelfth month, on the new moon day Wùchén,
the Mǐn army's suppression of the Zhāngzhōu bandits was unsuccessful,
and Lín Wénchá and others died.
On the day Jǐsì,
Wú Táng was ordered to continue concurrently managing affairs north of the Jiāng.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the Kè bandits of Zhàoqìng were pacified.
Dūxīng'ā's army and others captured Qīngshuǐbǎo.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the tribute of jujubes from Hénán was suspended.
Sea dikes were constructed in Zhèjiāng.
On the day Yǐhài,
the Huí bandits captured Jīnxiàn.
Cáo Kèzhōng's army captured Yánguān.
On the day Wùyín,
the Yīlí government forces were defeated,
and the commanding officer Tuōkètuōnài and others died.
Míngxù's request to borrow Russian troops to assist in the suppression was granted.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the Jìmùsà government forces were defeated.
On the day Gēngchén,
generous pensions were granted to the righteous civilians Bāo Lìshēn and others from Zhūjì.
Wú Táng's request
to try out river transport was granted.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Táo Màolín's army recaptured Jīnxiàn.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Lǐ Yuándù's army was garrisoned at Tái.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Sēnggélínqìn moved his army to Bǎofēng to suppress the bandits,
and won.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the government forces achieved a great victory against the Huí bandits,
the siege of Yīlí was lifted,
and Míngxù was awarded a yellow riding jacket.
In this month,
the outstanding taxes of Ruì'ān, Zhèjiāng, that had been disturbed were remitted,
as were the disturbed and disaster taxes of Tàicāng and other prefectures, departments, and counties in Jiāngsū,
and Huái'ān and other garrisons.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú presented tribute.
In the fourth year, Yǐchǒu, spring, first month, on the new moon day Dīngyǒu,
the government forces captured the bandit stronghold of Jìngníng.
The Huí bandits captured Gǔchéng and Hànchéng.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the city of Bāyàndài was besieged,
and the government forces were unsuccessful.
Chén Fú'ēn and Lè Bīn were released,
and ordered to assist in managing military provisions for Yīlí.
On the day Rén'yín,
following Zēng Guófān's request,
Liú Míngchuán's army was transferred to Mǐn,
and Bāo Chāo recruited Chuān troops to Gān.
Posthumous titles were granted to the deceased officials Dàoyuán Hé Guìzhēn, Zhīzhōu Liú Ténghóng, and Yóujī Bì Jīnkē.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Wénqí, the Tídū of Wūlǔmùqí, died at Bālǐkūn.
The Huí bandits captured Mùlěi and other places.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Zhāng Jíxīn was dismissed from office due to his crimes.
The previously dismissed Tídū Mǎ Dézhāo was reinstated to his original position.
The Píng and Gù Huí bandits raided Língtái, as well as Qiānyáng and Lǒngzhōu.
On the day Wùshēn,
Bóxī'ěr was ordered to act as the Bāngbàn Dàchén of Hāmì.
On the day Xīnhài,
the Huì bandits of Táiwān were pacified.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Yuè bandits captured Yǒngdìng and Yúnxiāo.
On the day Bǐngchén,
the Huáiyáng River Affairs Military Preparedness Circuit was re-established,
and the Xúhǎi River Affairs Military Preparedness Circuit was established.
On the day Dīngsì,
the Yuè and Niǎn bandits simultaneously fled to Lǔshān,
and Hùjūn Tǒnglǐng Hénglíng and others died.
On the day Guǐhài,
the Huí bandits captured Jìmùsà.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Qián bandits captured Dìngfān,
then it was recaptured,
and they again captured Qiánxī.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the Huí bandits fled to Yǒngchāng.
In the second month, on the day Xīnwèi,
as the Mongolian troops assisting Gǔchéng
were unsuccessful in battle,
an edict was issued to withdraw all deployed troops back to their banners.
On the day Rénshēn,
the Shǎn army defeated the Huí bandits at Lǐquán,
and Hú Zhōnghé was ordered to take overall command of the advance and suppression.
On the day Wùyín,
as the officials and gentry of Lín'ān, Yúnnán, did not side with the Huí rebels,
an edict was issued commending them.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Shěn Bǎozhēn's request for leave to visit his parents was granted.
On the day Guǐwèi,
due to hail and thunder calamities in various Zhílì provinces,
an imperial edict was issued for self-reflection.
Léi Zhèngwǎn's army recaptured Gùyuán and other places.
Cáo Yuánxīng, a Cāncānjiāng of Guìzhōu, plotted rebellion,
and was executed.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the local bandits of Chángyáng were pacified.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Yǒngdìng and Lóngyán were recaptured.
Wǔlóng'é's army and others, reinforcing Bāyàndài city,
were defeated.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the Qiánxī bandits captured Dàdìng.
The Miáo bandits captured Tiānzhù and Gǔzhōu.
As Mǎ Rúlóng and Cén Yùyīng had pacified Qǔjìng and Xúndiàn,
and captured and executed the rebel leader Mǎ Liánshēng and others,
they were greatly rewarded.
On the day Guǐsì,
the Fújiàn government forces achieved a great victory in suppressing Lǐ Shìxián and Wāng Hǎiyáng's factions at Gǔtián and Zhāngzhōu.
In the third month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
because Tián Xīngshù 田興恕 disregarded military affairs
and cruelly massacred missionaries,
he was banished to Xīnjiāng 新疆.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Táo Màolín 陶茂林 suppressed the Hui bandits at Guōjiāyì 郭家驛 and other places.
An edict instructed Sēnggélínqìn 僧格林沁
to "station troops, command, and deploy,
but not to lightly approach the front lines,
lest he fall into peril."
On the *rényín* day,
Gōng Qīnwáng 恭親王 was dismissed from the Grand Council
and his deliberative duties were revoked.
Wénxiáng 文祥 and others were ordered to manage the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén 總理各國事務衙門 (Zongli Yamen) affairs.
The Yue bandits captured Zhào'ān 詔安,
and the county magistrate Zhào Rénchéng 趙人成 died there.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Hui multitudes in Liángzhōu 涼州 rebelled,
but were suppressed.
Britain and France were permitted to trade in Jiāngníng 江寧.
Bào Chāo 鮑超 was ordered to prepare for a western expedition
and allowed to submit memorials directly.
Dūn Qīnwáng 惇親王 stated that the impeachment of Gōng Qīnwáng 恭親王 was unsubstantiated,
and the matter was submitted to the princes, grand secretaries, and others for detailed deliberation and report.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Hui in Tǎchéng 塔城 revolted.
Xī Lín 錫霖 requested to resign due to illness,
was dismissed,
and ordered to proceed to Yīlí 伊犁,
to be deployed by Míng Xù 明緒.
Tán Shèngdá 譚勝達, the Provincial Commander, was stripped of his position for embezzling soldier's rations,
but was still ordered to join Bào Chāo's 鮑超 army.
Wǔlóng'é 武隆額 was appointed acting Councilor-in-Chief of Tǎ'ěrbāhātái 塔爾巴哈台.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Sèpǔshīxīn 色普詩新, the Chief Commander of Bālǐkūn 巴里坤, went to reinforce Gǔchéng 古城 with troops,
encountered bandits,
suffered a defeat,
and died.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Mǐn 閩 army defeated the bandits occupying Tīngzhōu 汀州 and Liánchéng 連城.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Gān 甘 army repelled the Hui bandits at Gùlàng 古浪 and Píngfān 平番.
On the *xīnhài* day,
following the request of the princes and grand ministers,
Gōng Qīnwáng 恭親王 was ordered to continue serving in the inner court
and also manage the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén 總理各國事務衙門.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Guān Wén 官文 was ordered to simplify and reduce the number of soldiers and brave volunteers.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Yáng Yuèbīn 楊岳斌 was ordered to go to Gān (Gansu).
Shěn Bǎozhēn 沈葆楨 was observing mourning for his mother,
but an imperial edict ordered him to forgo mourning and act as the Governor of Jiāngxī 江西.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the Xīníng 西寧 Hui bandits rebelled again
and captured Dàtōng 大通.
On the *rénxū* day,
the Guì 桂 army recaptured Yǒngchún 永淳.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Máo Chǎngxī 毛昶熙 was ordered to return to the capital.
This spring,
tax arrears and duties were remitted for various areas suffering from calamities in Zhí (Zhili), Sū (Jiangsu), Wǎn (Anhui), and Gàn (Jiangxi).
In summer, on the first day of the fourth month, *yǐchǒu*,
the cultivation of land within the red stakes of the Rèhé 熱河 imperial hunting ground was prohibited.
The Sùzhōu 肅州 Hui bandits occupied Jiāyù Guān 嘉峪關
and besieged the prefectural city,
and the Fǔyí 撫彝 Hui bandits also rose up.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Péng Yùlín 彭玉麟 submitted a memorial resigning as Grain Transport Governor
and requested to focus solely on naval affairs;
this was granted.
Wú Táng 吳棠 was retained as Grain Transport Governor-General,
to manage the defenses of Qīng (Jiangsu) and Huái (Anhui).
On the *jǐsì* day,
the government army recaptured Yánchálíng 鹽茶廳,
and the crime of the dismissed Provincial Commander Chéng Ruì 成瑞 was remitted.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Hui bandits captured Gǔchéng 古城,
and the Chief Commander Huì Qìng 惠慶 and others died.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Táiwān 臺灣 was pacified.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Qián 黔 army recaptured Yùpíng 玉屏 and Tiānzhù 天柱.
Gōng Qīnwáng 恭親王 was ordered to continue serving in the Grand Council,
but no longer to deliberate on state affairs.
The Gānzhōu 甘州 Hui bandits captured Yǒnggù Bǎo 永固堡.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Yue bandits again captured Shù (Shuyang) 沭 and Sù (Suqian) 宿.
Eighteen battalions of the Tíng 霆 army, unwilling to go on the western expedition,
mutinied at Jīnkǒu 金口.
Bào Chāo's 鮑超 western expedition was halted,
and he was ordered to recruit the disbanded brave volunteers to go to Mǐn (Fujian) to suppress the bandits.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Níngxià 寧夏 government army achieved a great victory against the bandits.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Yue and Nian bandits jointly retreated to Yǎn (Yanzhou) 兗 and Jì (Jining) 濟;
Liú Míngchuán 劉銘傳 was ordered to go to Zhílì 直隸 to set up defenses.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Chóng Qǐ 崇綺 and 265 others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with different ranks.
On the *rénchén* day,
as the bandit forces in Shāndōng 山東 spread,
Zēng Guófān 曾國藩 was ordered to leave the province to command the army,
and cooperate with Sēnggélínqìn's 僧格林沁 army in a pincer attack from north and south.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Sēnggélínqìn 僧格林沁 engaged the bandits at Wújiādiàn 吳家店 south of Hézé 菏澤,
suffered a defeat,
and he, along with Grand Secretary Quán Shùn 全順 and Brigade General Hé Jiàn'áo 何建鼇, all died.
When the news reached court,
court was suspended for three days,
and he was specially granted the honor of being enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
Zēng Guófān 曾國藩 was ordered to command the army to suppress the bandits,
and Lǐ Hóngzhāng 李鴻章 was appointed acting Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng 兩江.
On the first day of the fifth month, *yǐwèi*,
Chéng Lù 成祿 was ordered to advance and suppress the bandits occupying Sùzhōu 肅州.
The rebellious brave volunteers of the Tíng 霆 battalions fled from Jiāngxī 江西 to Fújiàn 福建.
The Yue and Nian bandits jointly fled to Kāizhōu 開州 and Dōngmíng 東明.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Táo Màolín's 陶茂林 army was defeated,
the Hui bandits besieged Āndìng 安定,
and Lánzhōu 蘭州 was put under martial law.
On the *wùxū* day,
Zēng Guófān 曾國藩 was ordered to oversee the military defenses of the three provinces of Zhí (Zhili), Yù (Henan), and Lǔ (Shandong).
Disbanded brave volunteers from Gānsù 甘肅 fled and caused disturbances in Shǎnxī 陝西.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Lǐ Yuándù 李元度's banishment was remitted.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the Yue and Nian bandits jointly crossed the Grand Canal,
fleeing east to Jìníng 濟寧, Yǎn (Yanzhou) 兗, and Tài (Taian) 泰.
On the *wùshēn* day,
strict orders were issued to Shèngjīng 盛京 and Jílín 吉林 to suppress horse bandits.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
due to ineffective bandit suppression,
Guān Wén 官文, Zhāng Zhīwàn 張之萬, and Máo Chǎngxī 毛昶熙 were stripped of their positions,
but all were retained in their posts,
and Guān Wén's 官文 palace titles were also revoked.
Bào Chāo 鮑超 was urged to proceed to Jiāngxī 江西.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Wèi Róngguāng 衞榮光, a Reader-Academician, was ordered to go to Dōngchāng 東昌 to supervise the organization of local militia along the river.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the government army recaptured Zhāngzhōu 漳州 and Nánjìng 南靖.
Shěn Bǎozhēn 沈葆楨 was permitted to complete his mourning period.
Zēng Guófān 曾國藩 declined the responsibility of overseeing the military affairs of the three provinces,
but this was not allowed.
The Hui bandits captured Sùzhōu 肅州.
The Yue and Nian bandits separately fled to Fēng (Fengxian) 豐 and Pèi (Peixian) 沛.
An edict was issued to rectify and consolidate the coastal navy.
The disbanded brave volunteers who fled to Shǎnxī 陝西 were pacified.
Liú Chángyòu 劉長佑 was ordered to be stationed in Zhí (Zhili),
and Chóng Hòu 崇厚 in Dōngchāng 東昌,
to deploy defenses along the river.
The Qián 黔 bandits captured Guǎngshùn 廣順,
but it was soon recaptured.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
it rained.
The Yue bandits besieged Yǒngdìng 永定.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Sū (Jiangsu) army recaptured Zhāngpǔ 漳浦.
Liú Kūnyī 劉坤一 was appointed Governor of Jiāngxī 江西.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
due to delays in defense and suppression,
Provincial Commander Liú Míngchuán 劉銘傳 was stripped of his position,
but retained in his post.
Yáng Yuèbīn 楊岳斌 requested to be relieved of his duties,
but this was not allowed,
and he was still ordered to proceed to Gān (Gansu).
On the *rénxū* day,
the Qítái 奇台 government army recaptured Jìmùsà 濟木薩.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the government army recaptured Jiēzhōu 階州.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day of the intercalary fifth month, the new moon,
Shěn Bǎozhēn was appointed to supervise the defense and suppression efforts in Jiāngxī.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Cantonese bandits fled from Fújiàn to Jiāyīng.
On the *wùchén* day,
the Cantonese army recovered Pínghé and Zhào'ān.
The Sichuan army recovered Zhèng'ān.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the Sìchéng bandits were pacified.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the grain tribute of Hángzhōu, Jiāxīng, and Húzhōu prefectures was reduced by 260,000 *shí*.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Wāng Hǎiyáng turned back to attack Yǒngdìng,
and the government forces suffered a defeat;
commander Dīng Chángshèng and others died.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Muslim bandits occupied Fùkāng.
Zhāng Zǒngyú fled south to Zhìhéjí;
an imperial decree ordered Liú Míngchuán, Wú Táng, and others to jointly suppress him.
The Cantonese bandits captured Zhènpíng in Guǎngdōng.
The Zūnyì bandits surrendered.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Ördös Mongolian soldiers repelled the Huāmǎchí Muslim bandits.
The Qián bandits captured Suíyáng.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Emperor attended the funeral of Prince Sēngzhōng (Sēnggélínqīn),
and offered condolences.
His grandson Nà'ěrsū was bestowed the title of *Bèilè*, and Wēnsūdū that of *Fúguógōng*.
Zēng Guófān's army was stationed at Línhuái.
Tèkèshèn died;
Zàobǎo was ordered to investigate the boundary dispute with Bā'ěrhǔ;
Ēnhé was appointed Jílín General.
On the *gēngyín* day,
due to the prolonged drought,
an imperial decree was issued to encourage self-reflection and seek advice.
On the *guǐsì* day,
an imperial decree stated that since Qíyīng had incurred culpability,
there was no need to clear his name.
Sùshùn's sons were forbidden from holding office.
This was due to Qíyīng's son Qìngxī's complaint of injustice,
claiming that his death was caused by Sùshùn.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day of the sixth month, the new moon,
the circuit of Ānlúchúhé in Ānhuī was newly established.
The Fèngfúyǐng Circuit was changed to Fèngyǐngliùsì Circuit,
and continued to oversee the Fèngyáng Customs.
Liú Chángyòu was ordered to return to Bǎodìng;
Pān Dǐngxīn's army was stationed at Jìníng.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the local militia of Gānsù recovered Jiāyùguān.
Due to the Muslim rebellion in Ānxī, Yùmén, and other counties,
Yáng Yuèbīn was ordered to advance and garrison Lánzhōu.
On the *jǐhài* day,
an imperial edict was repeatedly issued to all provinces to carefully select prefects and magistrates.
On the *rènyín* day,
the Muslim bandits of Tǎ'ěrbāhātái lured and murdered Counselor Xīlín and others,
and besieged the city,
but were repelled by the lama Gùngá Zhálāsān's troops.
Wǔlóng'é was transferred to be Counselor Minister of Tǎ'ěrbāhātái.
Étēng'é was appointed Counselor Minister of Yè'ěrqiāng.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
it rained.
Zài Huá and others were found guilty of embezzlement in their work;
Zài Huá was stripped of his title of *Bèizǐ*, and Ēnbì of *Fúguógōng*,
and both were re-imprisoned for two years.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Shěn Guìfēn resigned due to mourning;
Zēng Guóquán was appointed Governor of Shānxī.
The Qián bandits again captured Tiānzhù,
and harassed Huìtóng in Húnán;
Láo Chóngguāng and Lǐ Hànzhāng jointly suppressed them.
The Qián army recovered Qiánxī,
but suffered a defeat at Dúshān.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the Muslim bandits of Mínzhōu rebelled,
murdered prefect Zēng Qǐ and others,
and harassed Táozhōu.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Sichuan army reinforcing Qián recovered Zhèng'ān.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Qítái and Hāmì fell;
Zhákèdāng'ā, the minister handling affairs in Hāmì, died.
Wénlín retreated to Bālǐkūn.
Yáng Yuèbīn, Chénglù, and Liánjié's armies were ordered to attack the Sùzhōu bandits.
The Muslim *Tái jí* Lùbùqìn surrendered.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Censor Mù Jíxiāng'ā requested careful selection of attendants and servants.
An imperial decree ordered the Imperial Household Department to investigate anyone who was opportunistic or fawning,
and to severely punish them upon verification.
This summer,
the disturbed prefectures and counties in Shǎnxī, Zhèjiāng, and Fújiàn were exempted from additional taxes,
as were the grain levies disturbed by the Hāmì military.
On the *guǐhài* day of the seventh month, the new moon,
Liú Róng was ordered to strictly guard Dìngbiān, Fū, Yán, Bīn, and Lǒng;
Yáng Yuèbīn was to guard against the Muslim chief Hè Míngtáng.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Muslim bandits captured Bāyàndài,
and Mùkèdéng'é, the commander of Yīlí, and others died.
The collaborating *Bèikè* Dūlǔsù and others were stripped of their positions.
The government forces recovered Kù'ěrkǎlāwūsū.
Bù'ěrhédé was appointed acting commander
to reinforce Tǎchéng.
Léi Zhèngwǎn's armies suffered a defeat attacking Jīnjībǎo,
and retreated to Wéizhōu.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Wǔlóng'é suppressed the rebellious Muslims of Lǐbàisì,
and pacified them.
The Qián bandits captured Shíqiān;
Prefect Yán Jǐn died in battle,
but the government forces soon recovered the city.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Dǒng Xún and Chónghòu were appointed plenipotentiary ministers
to handle commercial treaty affairs.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Prince Bóyànnàmohù of Kē'ěrqìn was granted the hereditary title of Prince Bóduōlègǎtái.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Censor Cài Shòuqí was stripped of his office for reckless speech.
The Qián bandits captured Dàdìng,
but it was soon recovered.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
mounted bandits from Fèngtiān harassed Zūnhuà and Jìzhōu;
Yùmíng was dismissed
and severely censured.
Ēnhé was appointed acting General of Shèngjīng.
The treaty with the Netherlands was exchanged.
On the *gēngyín* day,
an imperial decree forbade French missionaries from interfering in military affairs.
On the *rénchén* day,
Chén Guóruì was dismissed from his post as Assistant Supervisor of Military Affairs.
On the *gēngzǐ* day of the eighth month,
due to delays caused by peace negotiations,
Ēnlín was stripped of his office,
and Chéng Ruì was exiled to Hēilóngjiāng.
Qí Jùnzǎo retired from office.
The Cantonese and Nian rebels fled into the borders of Ānhuī and Hénán.
On the *rènyín* day,
a machinery bureau was established in Shànghǎi.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Muslim bandits attacked Bālǐkūn;
Nè'ěrzì repelled them.
Wénlín's army suffered a defeat at Kuísū.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the *Yītáng* foreign affairs were concluded.
Luò Bǐngzhāng, Governor-General of Sìchuān, was granted leave;
Chóngshí was appointed acting Governor-General.
Línxīng was sternly ordered to personally investigate and establish the boundary of Tángnǔ Wūliánghǎi.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng was ordered to be stationed in Guǎngdōng,
and to control the armies of the three provinces of Gàn, Yuè, and Mǐn.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Zēng Guófān was ordered to advance and garrison Xǔzhōu,
to jointly suppress the Nian rebels in Hénán.
On the *xīnhài* day,
an order was issued to Yīlí to capture and execute officers and soldiers who had joined the rebellion.
Móngkùbāyǎ'ěr, the general superintendent of the Ölüds, and others who had performed meritoriously in suppressing the rebels, were rewarded accordingly.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Yùmíng was stripped of his office.
Guō Sōngtāo requested to resign his post,
but was severely reprimanded for his words being overly defiant.
The excessive collection of *dīngcáo* taxes in Jiāngxī was reduced.
The various burdensome fees levied by prefectures and counties were abolished.
The Cantonese chief Wāng Hǎiyáng killed Lǐ Shìxián.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Cantonese bandits captured Chánglè in Guǎngdōng.
Britain and France returned the Dàgù Forts at Tiānjīn estuary.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Dūxīng'ā resigned as Supervisor of Military Affairs,
but was refused.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng and others were ordered to properly discuss the simultaneous river and sea transport of new grain tribute north of the Yangtze.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the prefectures of Sūzhōu, Sōngjiāng, Hángzhōu, Jiāxīng, and Húzhōu suffered from floods,
and relief was provided.
Shrines were erected for the men and women of the Lóngxī village militia who died heroically,
and the village was named Zhōngyì Xiāng (Loyalty and Righteousness Village).
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Chóngshí and others were ordered to investigate the Yǒuyáng missionary case.
In the ninth month, on the jiǎzǐ day,
the Emperor personally escorted Wénzōng's coffin to Dínglínɡ for interment.
He commanded Sù Qīnwánɡ Huáfēnɡ and others to remain in the capital to manage affairs.
The Chánɡlè rebels surrendered the city to the Yuè army.
On the bǐnɡyín day,
the land tax in areas through which Wénzōng's coffin passed was remitted.
On the wùchén day,
as the Niǎn leader Zhānɡ Zǒnɡyú and the rebels Lài and Rèn were fleeing and causing disturbance in Yù and Lǔ,
Lǐ Hónɡzhānɡ was ordered to jointly suppress them.
Wú Tánɡ was appointed acting Governor-General of Liǎnɡjiānɡ,
and Lǐ Zōnɡxī was appointed acting Governor-General of Cáoyùn.
Zēnɡ Guófān was ordered to remain stationed in Xúzhōu.
On the jǐsì day,
permission was granted to invite merchants to operate the Yúnnán Copper Mine.
On the gēnɡwǔ day,
Jiangnan gunboats were dispatched to the Shānxī river defenses to train in naval warfare.
On the rénshēn day,
the Huí followers at Hǎoshuǐchuān surrendered.
The imperial army lifted the siege of Nányánɡ.
Táo Màolín's army was again routed.
On the jiǎxū day,
the imperial army recovered Zhènpínɡ.
On the bǐnɡzǐ day,
Léi Jūn's generals Hú Dàɡuì and Léi Hénɡ rebelled,
besieging Jīnɡzhōu.
Commander Zhōu Xiǎnchénɡ repelled them.
Mǎ Huàlónɡ and Hú Dàɡuì scattered into different parts of Shǎnjìnɡ.
Zhānɡ Zhīwàn was appointed Governor-General of Hédōnɡ Hédào.
On the jǐmǎo day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the two Empresses Dowager, departed.
Yuè bandits attacked Lónɡnán,
and Liú Kūnyī went to Gànzhōu to supervise the suppression.
On the jiǎshēn day,
Wénzōng was buried at Dínglínɡ.
On the yǐyǒu day,
the imperial procession returned.
Hénɡyí, the magistrate of Qítái, with local militias, recovered Qítái, Jìmùsà, and Gǔchénɡ.
On the dīnɡhài day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the wùzǐ day,
Emperor Wénzōng and Empress were enshrined in the Tàimiào.
The next day, an imperial edict was issued granting special favors with various distinctions.
On the gēnɡyín day,
Táo Màolín, the Commander of Gānsù, was dismissed from his post,
and Cáo Kèzhōnɡ was appointed in his place.
Brigade-General Táo Shēnɡlín and others were arrested for trial.
Zuǒ Zōnɡtánɡ declined command over the three provinces,
but it was not approved.
That autumn,
outstanding taxes in areas like Xiàoyì in Shǎnxī and Lánxī in Zhèjiānɡ, which had been disturbed, were remitted.
In winter, on the first day of the tenth month, rénchén,
Tibetan troops captured Zhānduì.
Huí bandits attacked Qìnɡyánɡ,
and the imperial army repelled them.
On the kuǐsì day,
the treaty with Belgium was finalized.
On the jiǎwǔ day,
Xú Jìyú was ordered to serve in the Zǒnɡlǐ Gèɡuó Shìwù Yámén with the rank of a third-grade metropolitan official.
It was ordered that Guō'ěrkā's tributary payments be presented together every six years.
On the gēnɡzǐ day,
the excess collection of southern rice for tribute in Zhèjiāng was reduced.
On the rényín day,
Yuè bandits captured Hépínɡ.
On the yǐsì day,
Wánɡ Rónɡjí reported that Lù Salt was stagnant
and requested a differentiated suspension and reduction of additional tax tickets.
The proposal was approved.
On the dīnɡwèi day,
Huí bandits besieged Gǒnɡchānɡ and Nínɡyuǎn.
On the jǐyǒu day,
Zhè troops captured the bandit stronghold at Nántián.
On the xīnhài day,
Liú Rónɡ was appointed acting Governor of Shǎnxī.
On the rénzǐ day,
with the enshrinement ceremony completed,
a grand sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
Chún Qīnwánɡ declined to train the Eight Banners.
An edict was issued to continue inspections and reviews,
and to diligently intensify training.
On the jiǎyín day,
mounted bandits approached Fènɡtiān,
and the imperial army suffered a defeat.
On the gēnɡshēn day,
Fúxīnɡ was ordered to command the Jí and Hēi cavalry and the Shénjīyínɡ troops to suppress them.
On the xīnyǒu day,
Miánxìnɡ was released.
In the eleventh month, on the kuǐhài day,
Lài and Rèn's bandits fled to Wǔyánɡ and Yánchénɡ,
joining forces with Zhānɡ Zǒnɡyú.
An edict was issued for Ò and Yù to attack from both sides.
On the bǐnɡyín day,
the levy of rice and beans in Sū, Sōnɡ, Chánɡ, Zhèn, and Tàicānɡ was reduced by over 540,000 shi.
On the rényín day,
the Fènɡ army suffered a defeat in suppressing the mounted bandits.
Lǐ Tánɡjiē died.
Lǐ Hónɡzǎo was ordered to learn and serve as a Grand Councilor.
Zhènɡ Dūnjǐn, Governor of Húběi, was brought into the capital as Vice Minister of the Hùbù,
and Lǐ Hènián replaced him.
On the yǐhài day,
for the crime of disregarding a commanding general,
Chénɡ Bǎo was sentenced to decapitation,
and Guō Bǎochānɡ was exiled to Xīnjiānɡ.
On the bǐnɡzǐ day,
Xú Diǎn, a bandit leader from Fènɡtiān, rebelled again at Guǎnɡnínɡ.
On the gēnɡchén day,
Yuè bandits captured Jiāyīnɡ.
The siege of Gǒnɡchānɡ was lifted.
On the bǐnɡxū day,
the imperial army suffered a defeat at Jìmùsà,
and Hénɡyí died there.
On the dīnɡhài day,
Liú Chánɡyòu was ordered to be stationed at the border passes to supervise the suppression of mounted bandits.
On the jǐchǒu day,
Chuān troops suppressed the Fān rebels in Sōnɡpān,
pacifying them.
Qián bandits attacked Yǒnɡ and Qíjiānɡ.
On the gēnɡyín day,
Zuǒ Zōnɡtánɡ was ordered to personally go to Jiāyīnɡ to inspect the troops.
In the twelfth month, on the first day, rénchén,
Zēnɡ Guófān moved his army to Zhōujiākǒu.
Mínɡxù's request to send Rónɡquán to Russia to borrow troops and loan grain was approved.
On the jiǎwǔ day,
Qián bandits captured Qīnɡzhèn County,
but it was soon recovered.
Zhōu Dáwǔ was appointed Commander of Guìzhōu.
On the yǐwèi day,
Liánjié was impeached for corruption and disturbance,
and was removed from his position as Assistant to Military Affairs,
and assigned to Chénɡlù's army as an imperial bodyguard.
On the jǐhài day,
Lí Xiàn's army was routed at Sùzhōu.
On the xīnchǒu day,
mounted bandits retreated and fled to Chānɡtú.
The request from the Hùbù was granted
to allocate funds from salt taxes and other sources to increase inner court expenses by 300,000.
On the rényín day,
Rèhé troops recovered Cháoyánɡ.
On the kuǐmǎo day,
Bóyànnèmóhù was ordered to return to his banner to convene the various league leaders and issue a proclamation to Mongol soldiers to assist in suppressing mounted bandits.
Wénlín was appointed Minister for Affairs in Hāmì.
On the yǐsì day,
the rebel leader Gōnɡbùlánɡjié and others from Zhānduì were executed,
and the three Zhān territories were all placed under the administration of the Dálài.
On the bǐnɡwǔ day,
the Jīnzhōu bandits made a false surrender,
then fled to Tiělínɡ.
Wénxiánɡ and others were ordered to manage defense affairs in Fènɡtiān.
On the rénzǐ day,
due to delayed rain,
an edict was issued to clear up ordinary judicial cases,
and to bury exposed human remains.
On the yǐmǎo day,
Ēnhé was dismissed from his post for dereliction of military duty.
Commander Chénɡ Dàjí's army was routed at Máchénɡ.
On the bǐnɡchén day,
the Yuè army jointly recovered Nínhǎifǔ city in Yuènán.
Dūxīnɡ'ā was transferred to be the General of Shènɡjīnɡ.
Mùtúshàn was ordered to supervise military affairs in Gānsù,
taking over command of all troops previously under Dūxīnɡ'ā.
On the gēnɡshēn day,
the Emperor presided over a banquet in the Báohédiàn,
to which foreign vassals who came for the New Year's audience were invited.
From then on, this practice was followed every year.
Diān troops recovered Lìjiānɡ and Hèqìnɡ.
That winter,
outstanding taxes in the disturbed prefectures, sub-prefectures, and counties like Sōnɡpān in Sìchuān and Chálínɡ in Húnán were remitted.
In the fifth year, _bǐngyín_, spring, the first month, _xīnyǒu_ first day of the month,
banquets were suspended.
_Jiǎzǐ_,
Nian bandits harassed È,
Zēng Guófān ordered Liú Míngchuán to reinforce Huángzhōu.
Mǎ Huàlóng begged for pacification,
and offered Níngxià Hànchéng.
_Yǐchǒu_,
the Guì army recaptured Nàtán.
Fújiàn’s regular tribute was remitted.
_Jǐsì_,
Mùtúshàn was ordered to handle the aftermath of pacifying the Hui.
_Gēngwǔ_,
Yúnnán Governor Lín Hóngnián went to Zhāotōng.
_Yǐhài_,
mounted bandits occupied Bódūnnà,
and then Shuāngchéngbǎo,
Jílín was in crisis.
Wénxiáng and Bǎoshàn ordered Hēilóngjiāng troops and cavalry to reinforce them.
_Jǐmǎo_,
Huángyán General Gāng Āntài was patrolling the seas,
encountered boat bandits,
and died.
_Guǐwèi_,
Lín Hóngnián was dismissed from office for timidity and causing delays,
Liú Yuèzhāo replaced him.
Zuǒ Zōngtáng commanded various armies to recapture Jiāyìng,
and the Yuè bandits were pacified.
Zuǒ Zōngtáng then discussed merits and rewards.
_Bǐngxū_,
mounted bandits fled and captured Ālèchǔkā and Lālínchéng,
Fùmíng'ā went to Jílín to suppress them.
Tèpǔqīn was ordered to return to Hēilóngjiāng to set up defenses.
Wú Chāngshòu was demoted,
Lǐ Hènián was transferred to be Hénán Governor,
and Zēng Guóquán was made Húběi Governor.
_Wùzǐ_,
the Feng army recaptured Bāmiànchéng.
_Jǐchǒu_,
an edict strictly ordered the arrest of Gēlǎohuì bandits in army camps.
Second month, _xīnmǎo_ first day of the month,
an imperial edict ordered Zuǒ Zōngtáng and others to delay the withdrawal of the Jiāng and Mǐn armies,
and to prepare for their transfer to the northern route to assist in suppressing the Nian and Hui bandits.
Qian Hui captured Yǒngníng,
and then it was recaptured.
_Rénchén_,
Zhàochēn was ordered to go to Zhènyuǎn to manage military affairs.
_Xīnchǒu_,
the imperial army recaptured Huángpí.
_Dīngwèi_,
Dūxīng'ā was dismissed from office but retained for his troops' wanton killing.
_Wùshēn_,
Guǎngdōng Army General Gāo Liánshēng was ordered to take up his post to suppress local bandits.
Bóyànnèménghù suppressed mounted bandits at Zhèngjiātún,
achieving a great victory.
Mǎ Xīnyí was ordered to plan for sea dikes.
_Xīnhài_,
the Dìng'ān army suppressed mounted bandits at Chángchūn,
and was victorious,
an edict restored his title of Deputy Commander.
_Rénzǐ_,
Déyīng was dismissed due to mourning,
and Fùmíng'ā was made Jílín General.
_Bǐngchén_,
Guō Sōngtāo was summoned to the capital,
and Jiǎng Yìlǐ was appointed acting Guǎngdōng Governor.
_Jǐwèi_,
the Húnán army repelled the Qián Miao.
Third month, _rénxū_,
Zēng Guófān moved his army to Jìníng,
and supervised the suppression of Zhāng Zǒngyú.
_Yǐchǒu_,
Ālèchǔkā, Bódūnnà, and Shuāngchéngbǎo were recaptured.
_Jǐsì_,
the Feng army suppressed the northern and southern mounted bandits,
and thoroughly defeated them.
Silver and rice for areas in Fèngtiān and Jílín that were harassed were remitted.
_Gēngwǔ_,
Míngyì pleaded illness,
Línxìng was ordered to command Mongol troops to reinforce Yīlí.
_Yǐhài_,
Lài Wénguāng and others fled and pressed towards Kāifēng.
_Wùyín_,
the tribute of livestock and servants of Hēilóngjiāng, who were accompanying the expedition, was remitted.
An edict ordered internal and external officials to study laws and regulations.
_Jǐmǎo_,
mounted bandits fled and harassed Rèhé.
_Gēngchén_,
the surrender of Mǎ Huàlóng and others was accepted.
_Jiǎshēn_,
Zhāng Zǒngyú fled to Pú and Fàn,
Lài Wénguāng and others fled from Yù to Yùnchéng and Jùyě,
Zēng Guófān and others were ordered to guard the Grand Canal,
and Qíáo Sōngnián's army intercepted and suppressed them.
_Yǐyǒu_,
mounted bandits captured Niúzhuāng.
_Bǐngxū_,
Cáo Yùyīng died.
_Dīnghài_,
the Mǐn army recaptured Chóng'ān and Jiànyáng.
_Wùzǐ_,
Lǐ Hóngzǎo was appointed Grand Councilor,
and Hú Jiāyù was assigned to study in the Grand Council.
This spring,
accumulated arrears of money and grain in Hénán were remitted,
as were extra taxes for areas in Zhílì's Ānzhōu, Fèngtiān's Xīnmín, and other prefectures and counties affected by floods or harassment.
Summer, fourth month, _jǐchǒu_ first day of the month,
the bandit leader Mǎ Shǎzi from northern Fèngtiān was executed,
the rest of his followers surrendered.
The imperial army recaptured Niúzhuāng.
Yuè and Nian bandits attacked the river banks of Zhílì,
and were repelled.
_Xīnmǎo_,
Zēng Guóquán's request to reduce troops and merge military funds was approved,
and Liú Liánjié, Péng Yùjú, Zhū Nánguì, and Guō Sōnglín were transferred to Húběi.
_Bǐngshēn_,
a Hui leader surrendered Tāozhōu to Cáo Kèzhōng's army.
_Wùxū_,
Mǎ Rúlóng was appointed acting Yúnnán General.
_Gēngzǐ_,
Wénxiáng and Fúxìng were summoned back to the capital,
Dūxīng'ā was ordered to take over Fèngtiān military affairs,
and to command all armies.
_Xīnchǒu_,
Nà'ěrjì recaptured Mùlěi, Qítái, and Gǔchéng,
and recruited local militias for defense.
_Guǐmǎo_,
the imperial army recaptured Suíyáng.
_Jiǎchén_,
Hui bandits captured Jìngyuǎn.
_Wùshēn_,
an edict ordered Fèngtiān and Jílín to jointly suppress bandits inside and outside the mountains.
_Jǐyǒu_,
Tán Yùlóng's army collapsed,
Cáo Kèzhōng was ordered to concurrently command his army.
_Rénzǐ_,
Hui bandits fled back to Qìngyáng.
Pīléng mobilized all his troops and pressed towards Bùlǔkèbā,
Jǐngwén was ordered to go to the border pass to investigate.
_Jiǎyín_,
Wǔyuán bandits were pacified.
_Bǐngchén_,
Yuè and Nian bandits harassed Tóng, Pèi, and Sìzhōu, Língbì.
Láo Chóngguāng advanced and garrisoned Kūnmíng.
Dù Wénxiù again captured Lìjiāng, Hèqìng, and Jiànchuān.
_Wùwǔ_,
Hui bandits attacked Lánzhōu,
the imperial army repelled them.
Fifth month, _rénxū_,
Qián bandits again captured Xīngyì, Zhēnfēng, and Yǒngníng.
The Russian envoy strongly insisted on trade in Hēilóngjiāng's interior.
Tèpǔqīn was ordered to rectify military camps.
_Yǐchǒu_,
a grand examination of Hanlin and Zhan shi scholars was held,
Sūn Yùwèn and four others were promoted to the first rank,
the rest were promoted or demoted with varying degrees.
_Wùchén_,
Mǎ Cháoqīng surrendered,
Língzhōu was recaptured.
_Xīnwèi_,
Hui bandits Huò Sān and others fled back to Fèng and Qí,
the imperial army repelled them,
Yáng Yuèbīn and Liú Róng were ordered to jointly attack,
and not allow them to re-enter Shǎn.
_Jiǎxū_,
Hui bandits captured Tǎ'ěrbāhātái,
Wǔlóng'é died.
Déxīng'ā was made Councillor Minister,
Kuíchāng was appointed acting Kēbùduō Councillor.
Chénglù was strictly ordered to quickly leave the pass.
_Yǐhài_,
Hui bandits captured Yīlí,
Míngxù and others died.
Róngquán was appointed acting Yīlí General.
Kùkèjítài was ordered to oversee Xīnjiāng military affairs.
_Dīngchǒu_,
an imperial edict ordered the clearing of pending judicial cases.
_Rénwǔ_,
due to prolonged lack of rain,
an imperial edict sought direct criticisms,
and forbade mistreatment of prisoners.
_Jiǎshēn_,
an edict ordered the recommendation of officials who diligently served the people.
_Dīnghài_,
the imperial army recaptured Lìbō.
This month,
arrears of taxes in Guǎngdōng's Jiāyìng and other harassed areas were remitted.
In the sixth month, on the day of Gēngyín,
there was rain.
It was approved that Zuǒ Zōngtáng requested
the establishment of a factory in Fújiàn to trial-build steamships.
On the day of Rénchén,
an imperial edict exhorted inner and outer ministers to diligent service.
On the day of Xīnchǒu,
Chénglù's army advanced and besieged Sùzhōu.
On the day of Rényín,
an imperial edict commanded Fùmíng'ā to search for and capture remaining bandits in mountain areas.
On the day of Jiǎchén,
the Língshān bandits were pacified.
On the day of Wùshēn,
the Uliyasutai General Míngyì was dismissed due to illness.
On the day of Jǐyǒu,
Délèkè Duōěrjì was appointed Uliyasutai General,
and Fúxīng was appointed Suiyuancheng General.
On the day of Gēngxū,
the Huí bandits of Yán and Gù surrendered.
On the day of Xīnhài,
the bandits of Língyún and Yángwàn were pacified.
On the day of Yǐmǎo,
an imperial edict commanded Yáng Yuèbīn to suppress the Huí bandits of Dí and Hé.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day of Gēngshēn,
Guǎngfèng and Túěrkù were stripped of their posts
and arrested for interrogation.
Minister Kuílíng and others were ordered to be envoys to Cháoxiǎn
to confer the title upon the queen.
On the day of Rénxū,
the imperial army recovered Hāmì.
On the day of Jiǎzǐ,
an imperial edict commanded the rectification of civil administration, military affairs, and tax collection in Guǎngdōng.
On the day of Yǐchǒu,
Lǐ Hóngzǎo observed mourning for his mother.
An imperial decree ordered that after one hundred days, he should resume his duties in the Hóngdé Diàn and the Jūnjī Chù.
On the day of Gēngwǔ,
the Xiāng army captured the bandit stronghold in Sīnán.
On the day of Rénshēn,
Lǐ Hóngzǎo requested to complete his mourning period,
but it was not granted.
On the day of Guǐyǒu,
the excess collection of over 370,000 shí of rice was reduced in Sū, Sōng, Cháng, and Tài,
and over 1,670,000 guàn of excess money collection was reduced.
On the day of Bǐngzǐ,
Chónghòu met with the Spanish envoy to exchange treaties.
On the day of Jǐmǎo,
Qían bandits captured Shíqiān,
but it was soon recovered.
On the day of Gēngchén,
the Uryankhai Seven Banners were exempted from paying half of their tribute.
On the day of Yǐyǒu,
the Hé'nán River burst its banks at Hújiātún.
In the eighth month, on the day of Wùzǐ,
Liú Róng was dismissed due to illness.
Qiáo Sōngnián was transferred as Shǎnxī Governor,
and Yīnghàn was appointed Ānhuī Governor.
On the day of Jǐchǒu,
the Púzhōu River burst its banks.
On the day of Gēngyín,
the Xún and Yù bandits were pacified.
The Shānhǎiguān Supervisor was abolished,
and the Fèngjǐn Shānhǎiguān Dào was established instead.
On the day of Xīnchǒu,
Lǐ Yúnlín was awarded the First Class Imperial Guard
and assigned to assist in military affairs in Xīnjiāng.
On the day of Guǐmǎo,
Yáng Yuèbīn was dismissed due to illness.
Zuǒ Zōngtáng was transferred as Shǎnxī-Gānsù Governor-General,
Wú Táng as Fújiàn-Zhèjiāng Governor-General,
and Zhāng Zhīwàn as Grain Transport Governor-General.
Ruìlín was officially appointed Guǎngdōng-Guǎngxī Governor-General.
On the day of Jiǎchén,
the imperial army captured the bandit stronghold of Dàgūshān,
and Xú Zōnglǐ was executed.
On the day of Yǐsì,
the imperial army annihilated the Zhāng, Niú, and other Niǎn bandits.
Using the lunar eclipse as a warning,
court officials were instructed to reflect and mend their ways.
On the day of Dīngwèi,
following the request of Censor Qìngfú,
grain was stockpiled in Zhāngjiākǒu and Suīyuǎncchéng
to be transported to Xīnjiāng
to relieve the people's food shortages.
In the ninth month, on the new moon Dīngsì,
Tán Tíngxiāng was ordered to assist Chónghòu in handling the Italian trade treaty affairs.
On the day of Guǐhài,
the bandits in Xīnghuà, Fújiàn, were pacified.
On the day of Jiǎzǐ,
an imperial edict commanded Lǐ Yúnlín and Línxīng and others to rectify the northern defense army.
Zàobǎo was ordered to go to Guīhuà to supervise the transport of funds and provisions to Xīnjiāng.
Huí bandits captured Fùkāng.
Qí Jùnzǎo passed away.
On the day of Xīnwèi,
Diān Huí bandits captured Ānníng and other prefectures and counties.
On the day of Guǐwèi,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng requested to reduce soldiers and increase pay for the Lǜyíng in Fújiàn and Zhèjiāng,
and to train soldiers with the allocated funds.
It was approved.
This autumn,
the fixed taxes for Guìzhōu, Guǎngdōng, Shāndōng, Fújiàn (disturbed areas),
Jiāngxī (disaster-stricken areas), and other places were remitted,
as were the outstanding taxes for Zhèjiāng and other counties.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day of Xīnmǎo,
Liú Chángyòu was ordered to strictly verify the troop numbers in the capital region.
On the day of Guǐsì,
Zhāng Zǒngyú fled from Shǎnxìzhōu to Pínglù,
and the imperial army repulsed him.
On the day of Yǐwèi,
Shěn Bǎozhēn was ordered to be in overall charge of Fújiàn shipbuilding affairs.
Liú Diǎn was ordered to assist Zuǒ Zōngtáng in military affairs.
On the day of Jǐhài,
Zhāng Zǒngyú fled west,
capturing Huáyīn and Wèinán.
Gān Huí bandits raided Yíjūn and Sānshuǐ.
An imperial edict reprimanded Zēng Guófān for allowing the bandits to spread.
On the day of Xīnchǒu,
Lǐ Hóngzǎo's sick leave was approved.
Fùmíng'ā was ordered to manage rehabilitation affairs in Jílín,
and Wāng Yuánfāng was appointed Grand Councillor.
On the day of Rényín,
Qían Huí bandits captured Xīngyì,
but it was soon recovered,
along with Ānpíng and Zhènníng.
On the day of Yǐsì,
Zēng Guófān requested sick leave,
asked to resign from all his posts,
to serve in the camp,
and to cancel his marquis title.
An imperial edict consoled and retained him,
ordering him to have an audience after his recovery.
Mùtúshàn was ordered to assist Shǎnxī.
On the day of Bǐngwǔ,
the Hǎiníng stone embankment was repaired.
This month,
new and old fixed taxes were remitted for Ānhuī, Shòuzhōu, and other prefectures and counties affected by floods.
In the eleventh month, on the day of Bǐngchén,
Zēng Guófān was ordered to return as Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng
and concurrently acting Minister of Commerce.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was appointed Imperial Commissioner,
with authority over the Xiāng and Huái armies,
and solely responsible for bandit suppression.
On the day of Wùwǔ,
Shāndōng Governor Yán Jìngmíng was granted leave,
and Dīng Bǎozhēn was appointed acting governor.
On the day of Gēngshēn,
Liú Míngchuán and others suppressed the Rèn and Lài bandits in Jīnxiāng,
achieving a great victory.
On the day of Yǐchǒu,
the Three Zás and Two Leagues' western expeditionary Mongol troops collapsed,
and Lǐ Yúnlín returned to Wūchéng.
Kùkèjítài was ordered to quickly advance with the Jí and Hēi armies.
On the day of Dīngmǎo,
the Chuān army captured the bandit stronghold in Tóngzǐ.
On the day of Dīngyǒu,
Zēng Guóquán impeached Guān Wén for greed, extravagance, and arrogance.
He was ordered to be removed from office and investigated.
On the day of Jǐmǎo,
the regulations for Fújiàn shipbuilding were established.
In the twelfth month, on the day of Dīnghài,
Censor Xún Luánwěi was severely reprimanded for his inaccurate impeachment,
and he was admonished,
leading to an imperial edict instructing Censors to be cautious in their speech.
On the day of Jǐchǒu,
Guō Sōnglín and others decisively defeated the Rèn and Lài bandits in Dé'ān.
On the day of Gēngyín,
as the Yellow River shifted north,
Sū Tíngkuí was ordered to inspect the entire course
and to jointly plan embankment construction with the Zhí, Lǔ, and Yù provinces.
Gān Huí bandits recaptured Hāmì.
Hú Jiāyù was dismissed from the Grand Council,
stripped of his rank but retained his post,
for accepting bribes from Guān Wén.
On the day of Jiǎwǔ,
Zēng Guófān again submitted a memorial requesting to resign from his posts.
A warm imperial edict consoled and retained him.
On the day of Jǐhài,
Léi Zhèngwǎn's army recovered Píngliáng.
The Hūlán bandits were pacified.
On the day of Gēngzǐ,
the Xiāng army reinforcing Qían suppressed Miáo bandits in Tóngrén,
achieving a great victory.
On the day of Jǐyǒu,
Huí bandits besieged Qìngyáng,
and Commander Zhōu Xiǎnchéng and others died fighting bravely.
On the day of Jiǎyín,
the Shǎnxī army suppressed Zhāng Zǒngyú,
suffering a defeat at Bàqiáo,
and Brigade-General Xiāo Déyáng and others died.
As the Niǎn's power was rampant,
Zēng Guófān and others were ordered to widely devise strategies.
This year,
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú paid tribute.
Annals 22, Annals of Mùzōng, Part 2
In the sixth year, the _dīngmǎo_ year, in the spring, the first month, on the _jǐwèi_ day,
the bandits Rèn and Lài fled to Xiàogǎn and Dé'ān.
The government troops were defeated.
General-in-Chief Zhāng Shùshān died there.
On the _rénxū_ day,
Jìngyuǎn was recovered.
On the _bǐngyín_ day,
Guānwén was stripped of his position as Governor-General
and summoned to the capital.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was appointed Governor-General of Húguǎng.
Lǐ Hànzhāng was transferred to be Governor of Jiāngsū.
Liú Kūn was appointed Governor of Húnán.
On the _jǐsì_ day,
Zhāng Xīróng suppressed the Niǎn bandits at Yúhuàzhèn in Xī'ān
and died there.
Liú Sōngshān's army achieved a great victory.
Qiáo Sōngnián was ordered to exclusively manage military affairs in Shǎnxī.
On the _xīnwèi_ day,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng was appointed Imperial Commissioner
to oversee military affairs in Shǎn and Gān.
Liú Diǎn was granted the third-rank official title of卿 _qīng_
to assist in military affairs.
On the _yǐhài_ day,
the Huí bandits from Hāmì encroached upon Bālǐkūn.
The government troops repelled them.
Nà'ěrjì was relieved due to illness.
Yīlètún was appointed Commander of Bālǐkūn.
On the _bǐngzǐ_ day,
Xú Jìyú was ordered to continue serving in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén
and manage the affairs of the newly established Tóngwénguǎn.
On the _jǐmǎo_ day,
the government troops recovered Zhènxíóng.
In the second month, on the _yǐyǒu_ day (the first day of the lunar month),
Liú Míngchuán pursued and suppressed Rèn and Lài in Zhōngxiáng
and was defeated.
Bào Chāo advanced and attacked,
inflicting a great defeat upon them.
On the _gēngyín_ day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was ordered to lead troops to Yù.
On the _rénchén_ day,
there was an epidemic in the capital.
On the _jiǎwǔ_ day,
Liú Sōngshān was promoted to Provincial Commander-in-Chief of the Land Forces of Guǎngdōng.
On the _dīngyǒu_ day,
the Shǎn Huí, including Mǎ Shēngyàn, surrendered.
The collection of grain commutation silver in Guǎngzhōu prefecture was reduced by over 190,000 _liǎng_,
and this was made an order.
On the _yǐsì_ day,
the Guì army recovered Sìchéng.
On the _gēngxū_ day,
Dīng Bǎozhēn was appointed Governor of Shāndōng.
On the _xīnhài_ day,
Táozhōu fell again.
On the _rénzǐ_ day,
Láo Chóngguāng, Governor-General of Yún-Guì, died.
Zhāng Kǎisōng was appointed to replace him.
In the third month, on the _dīngsì_ day,
the È army suppressed the rebels in Qíshuǐ
and was defeated.
Intendant Péng Yùjú and others died there.
On the _guǐhài_ day,
General-in-Chief Duàn Bùyún's army collapsed in Fūzhōu.
On the _wùchén_ day,
Bào Chāo repeatedly begged to be relieved due to illness,
but an edict ordered him to still proceed to Huángzhōu.
On the _yǐhài_ day,
Wōrén was ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
He declined,
but it was not permitted.
On the _dīngchǒu_ day,
an edict instructed Lǐ Yúnlín and others to resettle the refugees in Xīnjiāng.
On the _xīnsì_ day,
Cáo Kèzhōng's army recovered Táozhōu.
On the _rénwǔ_ day,
the Huí bandits, including Mǎ Zhàn'áo, attacked Xīníng.
This spring,
the disrupted overdue taxes of Rénhé and other salt fields in Zhèjiāng, and the outstanding granary grain owed by the common people in Píngdìng and other places in Shānxī were remitted.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the _dīnghài_ day,
the petition for students from the Ryūkyū Kingdom to enter the Imperial Academy for study was granted.
Bào Chāo was granted sick leave.
On the _wùzǐ_ day,
Hé Guǎn's army recovered Hāmì.
On the _jǐchǒu_ day,
Zhōu Zǔpéi died.
On the _guǐsì_ day,
the horse bandits in Jílín were pacified.
On the _bǐngshēn_ day,
the Spanish envoy arrived to exchange treaties.
On the _rénwǔ_ day,
Liú Sōngshān greatly defeated the Niǎn and Huí in Tóngzhōu.
On the _bǐngwǔ_ day,
Bóxī'ěr, the Jasagh Prince of the Hāmì who died as a martyr, was posthumously granted the title of Prince.
A shrine was built for him.
Délèkè Duō'ěrjǐ was relieved due to illness.
Línxìng was appointed General of Wūlǐyàsūtái.
Róngquán was transferred to be a Councillor.
On the _dīngwèi_ day,
Dàgài Zhébù, the aboriginal chieftain of Zhānduì, was apprehended and executed.
On the _gēngxū_ day,
the Huí bandits of Guìdé rebelled
and captured the prefectural city.
In the fifth month, on the _jiǎyín_ day,
the Hāmì Huí bandits encroached upon Yùmén.
The government troops repelled them.
Due to drought,
an edict ordered the relief of refugees, the nurturing of infants, the burial of the exposed dead, and the support of the families of those killed in battle.
On the _wùwǔ_ day,
an edict ordered the extensive purchase of books,
and the reprinting of the imperially compiled and sanctioned classics and histories,
to be distributed to various schools.
On the _jǐwèi_ day,
the armies of Guō Bǎochāng and Liú Sōngshān defeated Zhāng Zǒngyú in Cháoyì.
Guō Bǎochāng's banishment was remitted.
On the _xīnyǒu_ day,
Zēng Guófān was appointed Grand Secretary.
Luò Bǐngzhāng was appointed Associate Grand Secretary.
On the _bǐngyín_ day,
an imperial decree ordered the streamlining of legal cases.
On the _dīngmǎo_ day,
the Guì army recovered Lìbō and Yìníng.
On the _wùchén_ day,
an imperial decree sought candid advice
and ordered a strict reduction in imperial palace expenditures.
On the _jǐsì_ day,
the Niǎn bandits crossed the Grand Canal.
Dīng Bǎozhēn was subjected to severe deliberation.
On the _gēngwǔ_ day,
the rebels encroached upon Chángyuán.
The government troops repelled them.
On the _guǐyǒu_ day,
due to his lack of success in suppressing the rebels,
Zēng Guóquán's official hat and button were stripped.
He and Lǐ Hènián were sent to the board for severe deliberation.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was ordered by edict to atone for his mistakes by achieving merits.
There was an earthquake in the capital.
On the _gēngchén_ day,
Dǒng Fúxiáng captured Gānquán in Shǎnxī.
In the sixth month, on the _jiǎshēn_ day,
the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén reported that the Russians were eyeing Xīnjiāng.
Grand Secretaries, Ministers, and the Censor-in-Chief of the Left were ordered to consult with the Princes and Ministers of the Zǒnglǐ Yámén for a proper deliberation.
On the _bǐngxū_ day,
the prohibition against excessive collection of grain tax by prefectures and counties was reissued.
On the _jiǎwǔ_ day,
Wōrén pleaded illness.
He was relieved of his duties
but retained his Grand Secretary title and continued to serve in the Hóngdé Diàn.
On the _yǐwèi_ day,
the government troops defeated the Niǎn bandits in Jìmò.
On the _gēngzǐ_ day,
Shùnzhí had a prolonged drought,
leading to famine.
Relief was provided.
Bào Chāo was permitted to return home.
On the _xīnchǒu_ day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng ordered Liú Míngchuán, Pān Dǐngxīn, and other armies to defend the Grand Canal
and block Jiāo and Lái.
Chénglù was ordered to command the armies of Huáng Zǔgàn and Wáng Rénhé.
Due to the severe drought in the capital region,
300,000 _liǎng_ from the likin taxes of Mǐn, Guǎng, and Gàn,
and 350,000 _liǎng_ from the foreign customs duties of Zhè and Mǐn were allocated for relief needs.
On the _guǐmǎo_ day,
the Gān Huí captured Huátíng in Shǎnxī,
but it was soon recovered.
On the _dīngwèi_ day,
the customary tribute fruits from Chāngpíng were remitted.
On the _jǐyǒu_ day,
since the lack of rain in the third month,
the Emperor frequently prayed for rain.
On this day, it rained.
This month,
the disaster-affected fixed taxes of Gānzhōu and other prefectures in Shǎnxī were remitted.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the _jǐwèi_ day,
it rained.
The Shǎn army recovered Gānquán.
On the _gēngwǔ_ day,
the Yǒngdìng River burst its banks.
On the _jǐmǎo_ day,
due to the Niǎn bandits crossing the Jiāo-Lái River,
an edict ordered all routes to defend the river and canal defenses.
Dīng Bǎozhēn was stripped of his position
but retained in office.
This month,
the disrupted overdue taxes of Huàngzhōu in Húnán were remitted.
In the eighth month, on the day `bǐng-xū`,
the winter hunt in Fèngtiān was suspended.
On the day `wù-zǐ`,
Liú Hànzhōng, the bandit leader from Húběi, was executed.
On the day `gēng-yín`,
Lí Péijìng was ordered to assist in the pacification and land reclamation affairs in Guìzhōu.
On the day `rén-chén`,
the Fèng army pacified the bandits in Gūshān, Fǎkù, and other places.
On the day `xīn-mǎo`,
Zhào Déguāng, acting Provincial Military Commander of Guìzhōu, fought bandits in Ānpíng
and died there.
On the day `bǐng-shēn`,
the armies of Mùlóng'ā and others fought owl-bandits in Wén'ān
and suffered a defeat.
Local bandits in Jìyáng revolted
and were pacified.
On the day `dīng-yǒu`,
the Húi rebels from Yíxī attacked Yáozhōu.
On the day `wù-xū`,
Zhāng Liàngjī, Governor of Guìzhōu, was dismissed and subjected to strict investigation.
Zēng Bìguāng was ordered to act in his stead,
and Yán Shùsēn, Provincial Administration Commissioner, was stripped of his post for dilatoriness.
On the day `rén-yín`,
Chén Guóruì was summoned to the capital.
On the day `bǐng-wǔ`,
as the Huái and Chǔ armies caused disturbance wherever they went,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was commanded to strictly enforce military discipline.
On the day `jǐ-yǒu`,
the timber tax in Rèhé was abolished.
On the day `gēng-xū`,
the Fújiàn shipyard was founded.
In the ninth month, on the day `rén-zǐ`,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng’s request to transfer Cáo Kèzhōng to Shǎnxī was granted.
On the day `bǐng-chén`,
the bandits Lài and Rèn and others attacked the Grand Canal,
and Niú Shīhán’s army repelled them.
On the day `dīng-sì`,
the Húi people of Hé, Dí, and Xīníng surrendered.
On the day `gēng-shēn`,
the customary tribute from Shāndōng was suspended.
On the day `xīn-yǒu`,
the nomadic Èlǔtè were settled at the Èrqísī River.
On the day `jiǎ-zǐ`,
the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén proposed making preparations for treaty revisions.
Zēng Guófān and others were commanded to present their respective views.
On the day `jǐ-sì`,
Dīng Rìchāng was ordered to go to Shànghǎi to handle the treaty exchange with Italy.
On the day `rén-shēn`,
relief was provided to the flood victims in Wūshān.
On the day `dīng-chǒu`,
Róngquán and Gùn'gázhálā were ordered to jointly plan the pacification and suppression strategy for the Khazakhs.
On the day `jǐ-mǎo`,
Féng Zǐcái was ordered to go to Zuǒjiāng
to exclusively manage the military affairs of Nán and Tài.
Relief was distributed to the disaster victims in Xiāngyáng and other prefectures.
In the tenth month of winter, on the day `guǐ-wèi`,
the commanders of all armies and the provincial governors were commanded to strictly enforce military discipline.
On the day `jiǎ-shēn`,
Sè'ěrgùshàn, Military Governor of Cháhā'ěr, died,
and Wénshèng, Minister-Resident at Kùlún, was appointed to replace him.
On the day `yǐ-yǒu`,
Zhāng Tíngyuè was appointed Minister-Resident at Kùlún.
On the day `bǐng-xū`,
the Shǎn army recovered Níngtiáo Liáng and Yíjūn.
Xí Bǎotián’s army was ordered to go to Yuánzhōu
to take overall command of the Guìzhōu relief efforts.
On the day `rén-chén`,
the Húi rebels from Yíxī captured Dìngyuǎn and Dàyáo.
On the day `guǐ-sì`,
Wāng Yuánfāng died.
Shěn Guìfēn was ordered to learn to serve as a Grand Councilor.
On the day `bǐng-shēn`,
Zēng Guóquán was dismissed due to illness.
Guō Bǎoyìn was appointed Governor of Húběi,
and Sū Fèngwén was appointed Governor of Guǎngxī.
Relief was distributed to the flood victims in Shāndōng.
On the day `yǐ-sì`,
Anson Burlingame, former American envoy, was dispatched to the treaty nations to handle Sino-foreign diplomatic affairs.
On the day `jǐ-yǒu`,
the Húi bandits captured Bǎojī and Zhèngníng
and then recovered them.
On the first day of the eleventh month, `gēng-xū`,
Dàoyuán Zhìgāng and Lángzhōng Sūn Jiāgǔ were appointed as Ministers to handle diplomatic affairs with the treaty nations.
On the day `rén-zǐ`,
the armies of Liú Míngchuán and others fought bandits in Gànyú
and won a great victory,
executing Rèn Zhù.
On the day `guǐ-chǒu`,
due to the rampant owl-bandits,
Liú Chángyòu was stripped of his post
but was still held responsible for his service.
Guān Wén was ordered to act as Governor-General of Zhílì.
On the day `bǐng-chén`,
the Shǎn army fought the Nian rebels in Luòchuān
but encountered Húi bandits
and suffered a defeat.
Lǐ Xiánghé, Provincial Military Commander, died.
On the day `guǐ-hài`,
Zhāng Zǒngyú captured Yánchuān and Suídé.
On the day `jiǎ-zǐ`,
the office of Minister-Resident at Bùlúntuōhǎi was established,
with Lǐ Yúnlín as its head,
Míngyáo as Assistant Minister-Resident,
and Fú Jì as Assistant Minister-Resident at Kēbùduō.
On the day `jiǎ-yín`,
Liú Míngchuán’s army fought bandits in Zhūchéng
and won a great victory.
On the day `dīng-chǒu`,
the Shǎn army recovered Yánchuān and Suídé.
In the twelfth month, on the day `rén-wǔ`,
Zhāng Zǒngyú fled to Jízhōu.
Zuǒ Zōngtáng and Zhào Chánglíng were both stripped of their posts but retained their duties.
Chéng Lù fought Húi bandits in Sùzhōu
and suffered a defeat,
and Huáng Zǔgàn, Brigade-General, died.
On the day `guǐ-wèi`,
Chén Guóruì was awarded the title of first-class Imperial Bodyguard
and was assigned to Zuǒ Zōngtáng’s army.
Liú Míngchuán and others fought bandits in Shòuguāng
and won a great victory.
The Húi rebels from Yíxī captured Lùfēng, Guǎngtōng, and Yuánmóu.
On the day `jǐ-chǒu`,
the government army recovered Jízhōu.
On the day `rén-chén`,
the owl-bandits in Zhílì were pacified.
On the day `jiǎ-wǔ`,
Liú Chángyòu was awarded the third-rank button
and ordered to lead his troops back to his hometown.
The Yongdìng River embankment work was completed.
On the day `bǐng-shēn`,
Jiǎng Yìlǐ was ordered to be a candidate for Surveillance Commissioner
and assigned to Zuǒ Zōngtáng’s army,
leading the Chǔ Braves back to his hometown.
On the day `dīng-yǒu`,
Luò Bǐngzhāng died.
Liú Sōngshān and others defeated Zhāng Zǒngyú in Hóngdòng.
Wú Táng was transferred to be Governor-General of Sìchuān,
Mǎ Xīnyí was appointed Governor-General of Mǐnzhè,
Lǐ Hànzhāng was transferred to be Governor of Zhèjiāng,
and Dīng Rìchāng was appointed Governor of Jiāngsū.
On the day `wù-xū`,
the Huái army fought bandits in Gāoyóu and won a great victory,
capturing Lài Wénguāng and others,
and executing them.
On the day `xīn-chǒu`,
the Eastern Nian were pacified.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng and Zēng Guófān were further rewarded with hereditary posts.
Liú Míngchuán, Yīnghàn, and Guō Sōnglín, Yáng Dǐngxūn, Shànqìng were rewarded with hereditary posts of varying ranks,
and Zēng Guóquán’s button was restored.
On the day `rén-yín`,
as Zuǒ Zōngtáng was appointed commander-in-chief to enter Jìn,
Kùkèjítài, Qiáo Sōngnián, and Liú Diǎn were ordered to supervise the military affairs in Shǎnxī.
On the day `jiǎ-chén`,
Yáng Zhàn'áo was ordered to act as Provincial Military Commander of Gānsù
and take over the military affairs of the western route.
On the day `wù-shēn`,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng ordered Xǐchāng, Liú Sōngshān, and others to go to Cízhōu to meet and suppress.
Zhāng Yào, Liú Míngchuán, and others were commanded to jointly suppress.
On the day `jǐ-yǒu`,
Zhèng Dūnjǐn was ordered to go to Shānxī to investigate incidents.
This month,
the salt tax on uncultivated salt fields in Rénhé and other localities in Zhèjiāng, and the shortage grain quota in Sōngmíng and other districts in Yúnnán were remitted.
This year,
Cháoxiǎn and Liúqiú paid tribute.
In the seventh year, the *wùchén* year, in spring, the first month, on the *gēngxū* new moon day,
the Niǎn (捻) leaders Lǐ Yǔn (李允) and others led their followers to surrender at Xūyí (盱眙).
An imperial edict ordered their execution
and the dispersal of their remaining followers.
Zhū Fèngbiāo (朱鳳標) was appointed to assist as Grand Secretary (*dàxuéshì*).
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Huí (回) bandits again captured Zhèngníng (正寧).
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Xǐchāng (喜昌) and others attacked Zhāng Zǒngyú (張總愚) in Hénèi (河內),
achieving a great victory.
The Xīníng (西寧) Huí (回) rebels captured Běichuān (北川).
Lǐ Yúnlín (李雲麟) requested leave due to illness.
This was denied.
Xīlún (錫綸) was appointed Assistant Minister (*bàngbàn dàchén*) for Bùlúntuōhǎi (布倫托海).
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Zhāng Zǒngyú (張總愚) fled north to Dìngzhōu (定州),
and Bǎodìng (保定) was placed under martial law.
Guān Wén (官文) and Zuǒ Zōngtáng (左宗棠) were both dismissed from their posts but retained in their positions.
An edict instructed Yùliàng (玉亮) to command the Divine Machine Battalion (*Shénjī Yíng*, 神機營) troops to suppress the rebels.
On the *rénxū* day,
Zhāng Zǒngyú (張總愚) attacked Qīngyuàn (清苑).
Liú Sōngshān (劉松山), Guō Bǎochāng (郭寶昌), and other armies circumvented the rebels and attacked them from the front,
receiving commendation.
Chén Guóruì (陳國瑞), Sòng Qìng (宋慶), and Zhāng Yào (張曜) all arrived in Bǎodìng (保定) with their troops.
The Dalai Lama requested pardon for the death sentence of Dōngdēng Gōngbù (東登工布), an offender from Zhātáng (𩹉塘).
This was granted.
Jiǎ Zhēn (賈楨) and others were ordered to establish the General Bureau for Local Defense (*Tuánfáng Zǒngjú*, 團防總局).
On the *guǐhài* day,
an edict ordered the Tianjin foreign rifle and trained army units to proceed to Héjiān (河間),
to coordinate with the Shandong (山東) army for defense and suppression.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng (李鴻章) dispatched Zhōu Shèngbō (周盛波) and other armies north to reinforce.
Zuǒ Zōngtáng (左宗棠) was urged to go to the northern part of Bǎodìng (保定) to supervise the suppression.
Gōng Qīnwáng (恭親王) was ordered to jointly manage patrol and defense with the Divine Machine Battalion (*Shénjī Yíng*, 神機營) princes and ministers.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Yīnghàn (英翰) was permitted to guard the capital region (*Jījīng*, 畿疆).
He was ordered to command Niúshī Hánjūn (牛師韓軍) and station them south of the Yellow River.
Chéng Wénbǐng (程文炳)'s army was ordered to go to Héjiān (河間) to join the suppression.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Zhāng Zǒngyú (張總愚) captured Ráoyáng (饒陽),
but it was soon recovered.
Jiǎ Zhēn (賈楨) retired due to illness.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng (左宗棠) was appointed commander-in-chief of all routes of government forces.
In the second month, on the *xīnsì* day,
government forces recovered Wèiyuán (渭源).
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Gōng Qīnwáng (恭親王) was appointed to command all ministers leading troops along various routes.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the Huí (回) bandits again captured Níngtiáoliáng (寧條梁).
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Huí (回) bandits fled to Yīkèshābā'ěr (伊克沙巴爾),
and government forces repulsed them.
Zhào Chánglíng (趙長齡) and Chén Shí (陳湜) were dismissed from their posts
and exiled.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Shǎnxī (陝) army recovered Bǎojī (寶雞).
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Diān (滇) army lifted the siege of Zhènxíóng (鎮雄).
The Yǐxī (迤西) Huí (回) rebels captured Chǔxióng (楚雄).
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Yù (豫) and Wǎn (皖) armies defeated Zhāng Zǒngyú (張總愚) at Shùlù (束鹿).
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng (左宗棠), Lǐ Hóngzhāng (李鴻章), and other armies suppressed the rebels,
defeating them repeatedly.
The Huí (回) bandits captured Huáiyuǎn (懷遠) and Shénmù (神木).
On the *rénýín* day,
the Báiní Yáo (白泥●) Miao (苗) bandits surrendered.
On the *yǐsì* day,
due to Cháoxiǎn (朝鮮)'s request to strictly enforce border prohibitions,
Yánxù (延煦) and Yìróng (奕榕) were ordered to go to Fèngtiān (奉天)
to meet with Dūxīng'ā (都興阿) to investigate and expand border affairs.
In the third month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
Zhāng Kǎisōng (張凱嵩) requested leave due to illness.
An edict reprimanded him for dawdling and evading duty,
and he was dismissed from his post.
The Huí (回) bandits captured Fūzhōu (鄜州).
Liú Diǎn (劉典) was stationed in Sānyuán (三原) to supervise the suppression.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Liú Yuèzhāo (劉嶽昭) was appointed Governor-General (*Zǒngdū*, 總督) of Yúnguì (雲貴),
and Cén Yùyīng (岑毓英) was appointed Governor (*Xúnfǔ*, 巡撫) of Yúnnán (雲南).
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Shǎnxī (陝) army recovered Fūzhōu (鄜州).
On the *guǐhài* day,
an edict instructed that *shùjíshì* (庶吉士) who had completed their training (*sànguǎn*) should still be tested on poetry and prose.
On the *wùchén* day,
Zhāng Zǒngyú (張總愚) fled to Yánjīn (延津) and Fēngqiū (封丘).
Liú Sōngshān (劉松山) and Guō Bǎochāng (郭寶昌) defeated them.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Shěn Guìfēn (沈桂芬) was appointed Grand Councillor (*Jūnjī Dàchén*, 軍機大臣).
On the *yǐhài* day,
Zhū Fèngbiāo (朱鳳biāo) was appointed Grand Secretary (*dàxuéshì*).
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the Yǐxī (迤西) Huí (回) rebels captured Yìmén (易門).
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Zhāng Zǒngyú (張總愚) fled to Huáxiàn (滑縣),
and was defeated.
In this month,
arrears of taxes were remitted for waterlogged areas in Ānzhōu (安州) and other places in Zhílì (直隸).
In summer, the fourth month, on the *jǐmǎo* new moon day,
the Hāmì (哈密) Huí (回) rebels captured Wǔbǎo (五堡),
and government forces repulsed them.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Zhāng Zǒngyú (張總愚) captured Nánpí (南皮).
On the *dīnghài* day,
an edict instructed Zuǒ Zōngtáng (左宗棠), Lǐ Hóngzhāng (李鴻āng), Dīng Bǎozhēn (丁寶楨), and others
to supervise various armies in defending and suppressing the rebels in separate routes, east and west of the Grand Canal.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Miao (苗) bandit Hé Zhèngguān (何正觀) surrendered.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Shǎnxī (陝) army suppressed the Huí (回) bandits in Bīnzhōu (邠州),
suffering a defeat.
Tán Yùlóng (譚玉龍) died in action.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Yǒngdìng (永定) River burst its banks.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Dūxīng'ā (都興阿) was summoned to the capital.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Lízhǒng (黎種) Miao (苗) rebels attacked various areas in Huàng (晃) and Yuán (沅).
Government forces repulsed them.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Níngtiáoliáng (寧條梁) Huí (回) rebels harassed the nomadic tribes of È'ěrdūosī (鄂爾多斯).
Bèizǐ (貝子) Zhánàgé'ěrjì (札那格爾濟) repulsed them.
The Huí (回) bandits attacked Hāmì (哈密).
Yīlětún (伊勒屯) and others jointly repulsed them.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Hóng Jūn (洪鈞) and 270 others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with differing ranks.
In this month,
three years of rent and taxes were remitted for various *tǔsī* (土司) in Sìchuān (四川).
In the intercalary fourth month, on the *wùshēn* new moon day,
the Yǐxī (迤西) Huí (回) rebels fled and captured Kūnyáng (昆陽), Xīnxīng (新興), Jìnníng (晉寧), Chénggòng (呈貢), and Sōngmíng (嵩明).
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the Huí (回) bandits again captured Shénmù (神木).
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Shǎnxī (陝) army recovered Yáncháng (延長).
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Dǒng Fúxiáng (董福祥) pledged allegiance.
An edict instructed him to redeem himself by achieving merits.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Huí (回) bandits occupied the Wūshēn Banner (烏紳旗),
and spread their disturbance to the Zhǔngá'ěr Banner (準噶爾旗),
逼迫 Tóukètuō (托克托) City.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Chéng Wénbǐng (程文炳), Chén Guóruì (陳國瑞), Liú Sōngshān (劉松山), and other armies attacked Zhāng Zǒngyú (張總愚) at Gāotáng (高唐), Chípíng (茌平), and Bópíng (博平),
achieving a great victory.
The rebels fled to Dōngguāng (東光).
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Huí (回) bandits again captured Qìngyáng (慶陽), as well as Níngzhōu (寧州) and Héshuǐ (合水).
The county magistrate Yáng Bǐnghuá (楊炳華) died in action.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Dūxīng'ā (都興阿) was appointed Imperial Commissioner (*Qīnchāi Dàchén*, 欽差大臣),
to jointly suppress the Niǎn (捻) rebels with Zuǒ Zōngtáng (左宗棠) and Lǐ Hóngzhāng (李鴻āng), and to command the four armies of Chūnxǐ (春喜), Chén Guóruì (陳國瑞), Zhāng Yào (張曜), and Sòng Qìng (宋慶).
Chónghòu (崇厚) was appointed to assist in military affairs.
In the fifth month, on the *wùyín* day,
Liú Sōngshān (劉松山) and other armies suppressed Zhāng Zǒngyú (張總愚) at Yánshān (鹽山) and Hǎifēng (海豐),
achieving a great victory.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Yangtze River naval force was established,
and Grand Commanders (*zǒngbīngguān*) for the four garrisons of Yuèzhōu (岳州), Hànyáng (漢陽), Húkǒu (湖口), and Guāzhōu (瓜州) were appointed.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the Shǎnxī (陝) army repulsed the Huí (回) bandits who had fled to Bīn (邠) and Fèng (鳳).
On the *rénchén* day,
the Běishān (北山) bandits attacked Yán'ān (延安).
Government forces suffered a defeat.
Vice-General (*fùjiàng*) Liú Wénhuá (劉文華) and others were killed in battle.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the Diān (滇) army recovered Yuánmóu (元謀), Wǔdìng (武定), Lùquàn (祿勸), and Luócì (羅次).
In this month,
arrears of taxes were remitted for the disturbed areas of Huàngzhōu (晃州) in Húnán (湖南).
In the sixth month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
Guō Sōnglín (郭松林) and others suppressed the Niǎn (捻) rebels at Línyì (臨邑), Bīnzhōu (濱州), and Yángxìn (陽信),
achieving a great victory.
An edict instructed the navy to strictly guard the Canal.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the Guì (桂) army recovered Guīshùn (歸順).
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Jīn (金) bandits fled to the Nínggǔtǎ (寧古塔) border,
and government forces suppressed them.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Shǎnxī (陝) army captured Yíchuān (宜川).
