On the *bǐngyín* day,
Zhāng Zǒngyú (張總愚) attacked the bank of the Grand Canal.
Government forces defeated him,
and many Niǎn (捻) followers surrendered.
On the *wùchén* day,
they were again attacked at Shānghé (商河),
achieving a great victory.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Lǐ Yúnlín (李雲麟) was dismissed from his post and investigated.
Míngyáo (明瑤) was appointed Minister in charge of Affairs (*bànshì dàchén*) for Bùlúntuōhǎi (布倫托海).
The seawall project in Zhèjiāng (浙江) was completed.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
taxes on land in the various prefectures and counties of Zhílì, Lǔ, and Yù that had been harassed were remitted.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Chūnshòu was dismissed from office for deception and embellishment.
On the day Rénwǔ,
relief was provided to the distressed refugees in Cāngzhōu and other areas.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Zhāng Zǒngyú drowned himself,
and the Niǎn rebels were pacified.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng and Zuǒ Zōngtáng were granted the title of Tàizǐ Tàibǎo.
Hóngzhāng, as Governor-General of Húguǎng, concurrently held the office of Xiébàn Dàxuéshì.
Dīng Bǎozhēn, Yīnghàn, and Chónghòu were all granted the title of Tàizǐ Shàobǎo.
Guān Wén's official title and peacock feather were restored.
Liú Míngchuán was promoted to first-class Nán.
Guō Sōnglín was promoted to first-class Qīngchē Dūwèi.
Sòng Qìng and Shàn Qìng were rewarded with second-class Qīngchē Dūwèi.
Liú Sōngshān was rewarded with a huángmǎguà and third-class Qīngchē Dūwèi.
Guō Bǎochāng, Zhāng Yào, and Wēndélèxī were rewarded with Qí Dūwèi.
Huáng Yìshēng was promoted to Yún Qíwèi.
Chén Guóruì's hereditary post of Tídū was restored.
The rest received promotions of varying degrees.
Dūn Qīnwáng was ordered to offer sacrifices at the Dìnglíng mausoleum.
Péng Yùlín's request to return home to observe mourning was granted.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng and Lǐ Hóngzhāng were summoned for an audience.
On the day Dīnghài,
the Yíngzér River burst its banks.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Máo Chǎngxī stated that as military affairs were gradually settling,
there should be an increasing focus on caution and reverence.
Subsequently, Censor Zhāng Xùkǎi submitted a memorial requesting the preservation of prosperity and the maintenance of abundance,
and timely lectures,
both of which were graciously accepted.
On the day Rénchén,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng's request
to provide travel expenses for surrendered troops to return to their hometowns was granted.
On the day Guǐsì,
the Qìnhé River dike in Wǔzhì burst.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Zēng Guófān was transferred to be Governor-General of Zhílì,
Mǎ Xīnyí to be Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
and Yīng Guì to be Governor-General of Mǐnzhè.
Péng Yùlín was ordered to Gāng and Wǎn to jointly plan affairs concerning the Yangtze River Navy.
On the day Wùxū,
an edict was issued to the prefectures of Sū, Wǎn, Yù, and Lǔ to repair dikes and stockades,
and to organize local militia.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the Sòng Confucian scholar Yuán Xiè was granted the privilege of having his tablet placed in the Temple of Confucius for worship.
The Guìqián army from Sìchuān recaptured Lónglǐ and Guìdìng.
The Sìchuān army suppressed the Yí rebels in Yuèxī,
and defeated them,
capturing their chieftain Lèwūlì.
Zēng Bìguāng was appointed Governor of Guìzhōu.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
rebels from Bùlúntuō Hǎi fled to Wūlónggǔ River.
Délèkè Duōěrzǐ died.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
relief was provided to the flood victims in Yíng and Zhèng.
Gān Huí rebels harassed Báishuǐ and Hépáng,
and the Shǎnxī army repelled them.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the Xiāng army supporting Guìqián recaptured Wèng'ān.
Eighth month, on the first day Yǐsì,
Censor Dètài was dismissed from office,
for requesting the repair of the imperial gardens.
The treasury official Guìxiáng made false claims for personal gain,
and was exiled as a slave to Hēilóngjiāng.
The Yǒngdìng River burst its banks.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
an edict was issued to Míngyáo and others to restore the old system of Bùlúntuō Hǎi.
Mǎ Xīnyí was ordered to concurrently manage the affairs of the Minister of Commerce.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the Yán'ān bandit Hù Zhāng surrendered.
On the day Guǐhài,
an edict was issued to Zuǒ Zōngtáng to concurrently oversee military affairs in Shānxī.
On the day Wùchén,
an edict was issued to Jílín to strictly define the boundaries for reclaiming wasteland.
On the day Xīnwèi,
an edict was issued to Jīn Shùn to solely handle military affairs assisting Shǎnxī.
This month,
arrears of land tax for many years in the harassed areas of Wǎn, Sū, Lǔ, Yù, and È were remitted.
Ninth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
government troops recaptured Qìngyáng.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Sùzhōu rebels attacked Dūnhuáng,
and government troops repelled them.
An edict was issued to Yīlètún and others to plan the establishment of military farms in Bālǐkūn.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the Sìchuān army supporting Guìqián jointly recaptured Píngyuè.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Yánxù was ordered to go beyond the pass to investigate and handle matters of border expansion in Fèngtiān.
On the day Guǐsì,
the Diān army recaptured Jìnníng and Chénggòng.
This month,
the salt tax on poor harvests at Hēngpǔ and other salt fields in Zhèjiāng was remitted.
Winter, tenth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
Huí rebels attacked Jīngzhōu and Língtái,
and were repelled.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Wénlín arrived at Hāmì,
and an edict was issued to promote military farms in Cáibāshíhú and other areas.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Mùtúshàn captured Hézhōu.
Relief was provided for flood victims in Nán and Wǔdìng.
On the day Dīngsì,
Lǐ Yúnlín was exiled to Hēilóngjiāng.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Lǐ Hóngzǎo was ordered to continue his duties in the Hóngdédiàn and the Grand Council.
On the day Gēngshēn,
for his meritorious service in defending Kēbùduō,
Tǔěrhùtè Jùnwáng Língzhàdònglǔbù was granted the title of Qīnwáng.
On the day Jǐsì,
Miáo rebels in Guìqián recaptured Xīngyì,
but it was subsequently recovered.
Eleventh month, on the day Jiǎxū,
the Sìchuān army supporting Guìqián recaptured Máhā.
On the day Dīnghài,
Zhōu Shèngbō, Commander-in-Chief of Liángzhōu, was dismissed from office
for failing to restrain his subordinates.
Huí rebels harassed the Èěrdūs and other banners,
and fled to Yúlín.
Dìng'ān and others were ordered to intercept and suppress them.
On the day Rénchén,
an edict was issued to eliminate the accumulated abuses of petty officials.
On the day Jǐhài,
the Guìqián army captured Dūyún,
and Zhāng Wéndé was rewarded with a huángmǎguà.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the British consul in Táiwān allowed a foreign officer to plunder a ship,
occupy the yamen,
burn the bureau and treasury,
and extort military expenses.
The Zǒngshǔ was ordered to investigate and handle the matter,
and Yīng Guì and others were instructed to select officials to negotiate.
On the day Rényín,
the Rèhé rebels were pacified.
The land tax on military farms in Shuāngchéngbǎo, Jílín, that were flooded was remitted.
Twelfth month, on the first day Jiǎchén,
the Sìchuān army suppressed the Yí rebels in Xīchāng,
achieving continuous victories,
and various Yí tribes surrendered.
The Xiāng army supporting Guìqián recaptured Tiānzhù.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Huí rebels attacked Bāotóu,
and the Mongol army suffered a defeat.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Mílèsēnggé, the Rèhé rebel leader, was executed.
On the day Jiǎyín,
based on Zēng Guófān's statement that Sìchuān private salt caused difficulties for Húbù,
an edict was issued to devise regulations to stop Sìchuān salt from supplying Húbù,
and to withdraw the bureau and halt the tax.
On the day Dīngsì,
the Diān army recaptured Chéngjiāng.
On the day Gēngshēn,
a renewed edict was issued to all provinces to prohibit the cultivation of opium poppies.
On the day Rénxū,
Miáo rebels from Guìqián harassed Héchí,
and government troops repelled them.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
an edict was issued that those whose capital punishment was suspended for three or more times during the autumn assize should also have their sentences reduced.
The Yǒngdìng River project was completed.
On the day Wùchén,
Qíqìng was dismissed,
and Qìngchūn was appointed Dūtǒng of Rèhé.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Liú Sōngshān suppressed bandits in Dàlǐchuān,
achieving a great victory.
On the day Réngshēn,
two hundred and ten thousand taels of Èquán funds were withheld to relieve the disaster in Hénán.
This month,
grain tax on barren land in Jiāngsū,
and arrears of grain tax in harassed areas of Tái'ān in Shāndōng and Rǔníng in Hénán were remitted.
This year,
Cháoxiǎn paid tribute.
In the eighth year, Jǐsì, spring, first month, on the first day Guǐyǒu,
banquets were suspended.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the Sì, Xiāng, Qián, and Guì armies suppressed Miáo rebels,
and the Guìqián army recaptured Chángzhài.
On the day Wùyín,
the Diān army captured Fùmín.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Liú Sōngshān's army and others attacked various Tǔ and Huí bandits,
and defeated them at Qīngjiàn.
Chénglù captured Sùzhōu,
and he and Yáng Zhànao were both rewarded with huángmǎguà.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Yíng project was completed, and the dikes were joined.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Liú Sōngshān's army defeated bandits at Jìngbiān,
and Dǒng Shìyǒu and others surrendered with Zhènzhìngbǎo and Jìngbiān.
Huí rebels from Yǐxī attacked Kūnmíng,
and Cén Yùyīng and others repelled them.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Léi Zhèngwǎn captured Dǒngjiābǎo in Jīngzhōu.
Second month, on the day Wùshēn,
Yuán Bǎohéng was ordered to supervise the logistics for the western campaign.
In the third month, on the day Guǐyǒu (the first day of the month),
Lín Zìqīng murdered the Zhīxiàn of Xīngyì.
Tídū Chén Xīxiáng lured and executed him,
and Chén Xīxiáng was rewarded with a huángmǎguà.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the Xiāng Army reinforcing Qián recovered Zhènyuǎnfǔ and Wèi, both cities.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the troops of Gānsù Tídū Gāo Liánshēng mutinied,
murdering Gāo Liánshēng.
His subordinate Jiàng Zhōu Shàolián attacked the rebel faction in Tóngguān,
annihilating them.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
an edict was issued to the Dūfǔ to carefully select Mùlìng for the recovered Zhōuxiàn,
and to comfort and settle the refugees.
On the day Gēngyín,
the Huí bandits captured Dèngkǒu.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Tǔlǔfān Huí bandits attacked Hāmì,
and the government troops repeatedly defeated them.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the Guì Army recaptured Píngxiáng.
On the day Jǐhài,
an imperial decree was issued, stating that
for the Grand Wedding Ceremony,
frugality should be strongly emphasized.
This spring,
the additional taxes in areas such as Shānyáng in Jiāngsū and Ānzhōu in Zhílì, which were affected by disaster and unrest, were remitted,
as were the outstanding hearth taxes in Fù'ān and other salt fields of Liǎnghuái.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Guǐmǎo (the first day of the month),
the Huí of Yǐxī captured Yánglíngyíng.
Liú Yuèzhāo retreated to defend Qǔjìng,
and was severely reprimanded.
On the day Yǐsì,
Lín Xīng was dismissed from office for timidity.
Fú Jì was appointed Wūlǐyǎsūtái Jiāngjūn,
and Wén Shuò was appointed Bùlúntuōhǎi Bànshì Dàchén.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Léi Zhèngwǎn and Huáng Dǐng's armies recovered Zhènyuán and Qìngyáng.
The Chuān Army reinforcing Qián recovered Wèng'ān.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the Xiāng Army reinforcing Qián jointly recovered Qīngjiāng.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Liú Míngchuán's request for sick leave was granted.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Chén Shí's banishment was remitted.
This month,
arrears of taxes in areas such as Dōngchāng in Shāndōng were remitted.
In the fifth month, on the day Gēngchén,
the Xiāng Army reinforcing Qián recovered Shībǐng,
and advanced to attack the bandit stronghold of Huángpiāo,
but suffered a defeat.
Ànchásǐ Huáng Rùnchāng, Dàoyuán Dèng Zǐyuán, and Tídū Liú Chánghuái died.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Huí bandits captured Chéngjiāng.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Dù Mǎ'ěr and other armies thoroughly defeated the bandits in Hángjǐnqí.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was ordered to go to Sìchuān to investigate the impeachment case against Wú Táng.
Cén Yùyīng was warned about appointing militia leaders who colluded with bandits
and extorting donations from the people.
Mǎ RúLóng was appointed Yúnnán Tídū.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the government troops suppressed bandits in Bǎo'ān,
achieving a great victory,
and bandit leaders Yuán Dàkuí and others were executed.
From the first month of spring until this month, there was no rain,
so the emperor frequently prayed.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
it rained.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnhài,
the reinforcing armies jointly recaptured Xúndiàn.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Dǒng Xún and Chóng Hòu were ordered to handle the treaty exchange with Aosīmǎjiā (Austria-Hungary).
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Yǒngdìng Hé burst its banks.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Tídū Róng Wéishàn, Zǒngbīng Luó Zhìhóng, and others who died in the Huángpiāo incident were granted hereditary posts and promotions.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the Wǔyīng Diàn suffered a fire.
On the day Guǐhài,
Wō Rén, Xú Tóng, and Wēng Tónghé requested diligent cultivation of imperial virtue
to avert disasters,
and the emperor praised and accepted their advice.
On the day Bǐngyín,
an edict was issued to the Dūfǔ to assess and evaluate agriculture and sericulture.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the Huí bandits attacked Ālāshàn Dìngyuányíng,
and the Mongolian troops were defeated.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Xīnwèi (the first day of the month),
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Zhāng Yào and other armies defeated the Huí bandits in Cháhàn Nà'ěr.
Wú Kūnxiū was ordered to go to the various areas along the river to comfort and relieve disaster victims.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the Diān Army recovered Sōngmíng
and captured Báiyánjǐng.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the Guì Army, together with the Yuènán Army, captured Jiǔfēng, Luòyáng, and other passes.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
an edict was issued to Xí Lún to provide relief to the Ělǔtè people.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Cháoxiǎn requested a ban on migrants building houses and reclaiming land north of the Yālù Jiāng.
Dōu Xīng'ā and others were urged to handle it appropriately.
On the day Rénchén,
Hé Guǎn's army defeated the bandits in Mùlěi Hé and other places.
This month,
arrears of taxes in Huàngzhōu, which were affected by unrest, were remitted.
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngzǐ (the first day of the month),
Russian merchant ships docked at the Hūlán Hé estuary,
seeking to open trade in the interior of Jí and Hēi.
The Zǒngshǔ was ordered to stop them according to the treaty,
and military and civilians were prohibited from private trade.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the imperial eunuch Ān Déhǎi left the capital,
and Dīng Bǎozhēn memorialized for his execution.
The Qián bandits again captured Dōuyún.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Guì Army jointly recovered Gāopíng in Yuènán.
On the day Gēngxū,
a severe edict was issued to restrain eunuchs.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the government troops suppressed the fleeing Huí bandits in Hángjǐnqí.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Níngxià government troops suffered a defeat in suppressing bandits,
and Fùjiàng Fāng Dàshùn died in battle.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Gùn Gāzhálācān's army recovered Bùlúntuōhǎi,
and bandit leader Zhāng Gé and others were executed.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the government troops suppressed the fleeing bandits in Dálātèqí,
annihilating them.
This month,
relief was provided for the water disaster in Háng and Hú prefectures of Zhèjiāng,
and Ānxiāng and other counties of Húnán.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
the Gāotái brave troops collapsed.
Chéng Lù was dismissed from office,
but retained in his post.
On the day Rénshēn,
three hundred thousand taels of imperial funds were allocated for engineering and relief work in Wǔ, Hàn, and other areas.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Mǎ Huàlóng rebelled again,
attacking and capturing Língzhōu.
The government troops recovered Wēiróngbǎo and Shuǐluòchéng.
On the day Wùyín,
the Diān Army recovered Yìmén.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Xiānluó (Siam) was exempted from supplementing its annual tribute.
On the day Gēngyín,
Uūlǔmùqí bandits fled to Hāmì,
and Hé Guǎn and others defeated them.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Fújiàn's newly built first steamship was completed,
and Chóng Hòu was ordered to inspect it.
On the day Wùxū,
an edict was issued to Fú Jì and others that the Ělǔtè people should all return to their old dwellings,
the monks residing south of the Ā'ěrtài Shān,
and the common people residing along the Qīnggélǐ Hé.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Liú Sōngshān defeated the Huí bandits in Wúzhōngbǎo and other places.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Jīn Shùn again defeated them in Nàjiāzhá.
Yáng Zhàn'áo was appointed acting Gānsù Tídū,
to handle the aftermath in Sùzhōu.
The French envoy Luóshúyà and his naval commander went to Gàn, È, and Chuān provinces with warships to investigate missionary cases,
and the local authorities were ordered to treat them according to the treaty.
On the day Yǐsì,
Léi Zhèngwǎn and Huáng Dǐng defeated the Huí bandits in Gùyuán and Yánchá.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Máo Chàngxī and Shěn Guìfēn were ordered to work in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Wén Shuò and others were ordered to jointly survey and demarcate the border of Bùlúntuōhǎi,
and Dǒng Xún was to handle the treaty exchange with the United States.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Diān Army recovered Chǔxióng, Nán'ān, and Dìngyuǎn.
Liú Yuèzhāo moved his army to Kūnmíng.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the Hāmì government troops suppressed the Western Route Huí bandits,
achieving a great victory.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Fènghuángchéng bandit leaders Wáng Qìng and others were executed.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Liú Sōngshān's army recovered Língzhōu.
This month,
relief was provided for the water disaster in Yúnnán,
and the drought in Zhílì.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day of the eleventh month,
the bandit leader Sūn Shàngwén and others from Chípíng plotted rebellion,
and were apprehended and executed.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the newly established minister overseeing the Bùlúntuōhǎi (Lake Zaysan) office was abolished.
On the *gēngchén* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Jiāngníng.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the tribute of sable from the Kobdo region was remitted.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Diān army recaptured Kūnyáng.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Gān army recaptured Jìngyuǎn.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Yongding River mouth was closed.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Wénshuò was ordered to come to the capital,
and Kuíchāng was reassigned to manage boundary demarcation.
In this month,
tax arrears were remitted for Dōngmíng and other areas in Zhílì affected by flooding and disturbance,
and for Wúwéi and other prefectures, counties, and garrisons in Ānhuī affected by water damage.
On the *gēngzǐ* day of the twelfth month,
the Chuān army reinforcing Diān captured Lǔdiàn.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Liú Sōngshān’s army attacked Jīnjībǎo,
and Brigade-General Jiǎn Jìnglín and others died there.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Pīléng encroached upon various places in Zhémèngxióng,
and the Guōěrkā (Gurkhas) and Tánggǔtè (Tibetans) developed animosity.
A decree was issued to Ēnlín to maintain defense and provide guidance.
There was internal strife among the Bùlǔkèbā.
Ēnlín was also decreed to mediate and pacify them.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the bandits in Yuènán were pacified.
Sū Fèngwén was decreed to strictly enforce border prohibitions.
On the *guǐhài* day,
relief was provided for disaster victims in Jīnán.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn, Yuènán, and Liúqiú presented tribute.
In the spring of the ninth year, *gēngwǔ*, on the *dīngmǎo* day, the first day of the first month,
banquets were suspended.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Diān army recaptured Lùfēng.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the Gān army defeated the reinforcing bandits at Wángjiātú.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Huí bandits captured Dìngbiān.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
a fire broke out in the wooden storehouse of the Shénwǔmén,
and an edict was issued calling for self-reflection and reform.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Huí bandits captured Āndìng.
The Shǎn army recaptured Dìngbiān.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Mǎ Dézhāo was kept to manage the defense of Tóngguān.
On the *xīnchǒu* day of the second month,
Liú Sōngshān personally directed the suppression of the Huí bandits at Jīnjībǎo,
and died from cannon fire.
Daoyuan Liú Jǐntáng was awarded the title of Third-Rank Minister,
and appointed to take command of his army.
Regarding the Russian officials going to Qíqíhāěr and Jílín to discuss border affairs,
Fù Míng'ā and Dé Yīng were decreed to treat them according to the treaty,
and not to make concessions.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Huí bandits split and fled to Ānbiān and Qīngjiàn,
and the Shǎn army attacked and repelled them.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
they again split and fled to Huāmǎchí and Yúlín,
and Sòng Qìng’s army suppressed them.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the imperial army defeated the bandits fleeing from Mǐzhī.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was ordered to go to Shǎnxī to supervise military affairs.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the Huí bandits fled to Tóngguān and Yíjūn,
and the Shǎn army attacked and defeated them.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the French envoy used the missionary case as an excuse to exert pressure with military threats.
A decree was issued to all provincial governors and trade ministers to quickly settle the negotiations.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the various forts in Níngxià that had surrendered rebelled again.
On the *dīngmǎo* day, the first day of the third month,
the Huí bandits fled to the Zhǔngáěr Banner,
and Mǎ Yùkūn defeated them.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Léi Zhèngwǎn was stripped of his office but retained in the camp
for lax defense of Xiákǒu.
A decree warned the western expeditionary armies against reckless pursuit of glory.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Diān army recaptured Mídù, Bīnchuān, Lìchuān, and Miǎnníng.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Huí bandits split to harass Qí and Fèng,
and Lǐ Huīwǔ defeated them.
In the summer of the fourth month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
Tán Tíngxiāng died.
On the *gēngwǔ* day of the fifth month,
Chóngshí was ordered to go to Guìzhōu,
to jointly investigate the missionary case with Zēng Bìguāng.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
permission was finally granted for Britain to set up telegraph lines at various coastal ports.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the Chuān army reinforcing Qián captured Huángpiāo, Báibǎo, and other Miáo stockades.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Tianjin residents and Catholics clashed,
destroying churches
and beating the French consul to death.
Zēng Guófān and Chónghòu were ordered to consult and handle the matter.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
provincial governors were decreed to prohibit the spread of rumors to mislead the public,
and to protect trade and missionary areas.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng led his army through the pass,
and requested the transfer of Guō Bǎochāng’s army,
which was granted.
Chónghòu was appointed as the minister plenipotentiary to France.
Chénglín was appointed acting minister for the three treaty ports.
In this month,
tax arrears for Ānzhōu and other areas in Zhílì were remitted.
On the *wùxū* day of the sixth month,
Kuíchāng went to Tǎěrbāhātái (Tarbagatai),
to survey and demarcate the border with the Russian envoy.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Mongolian troops of the Sàiyīnnáoyán Department suffered a defeat while suppressing Huí bandits.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the Diān army recaptured Wēiyuǎn.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Péng Yùlín was ordered to go to Jiāngnán,
to jointly reorganize the Yangtze River navy with the governors-general and governors along the river.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Gān army defeated the Huí bandits at Gǒngchāng.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Yongding River burst its banks.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Tiānjīn Prefect Zhāng Guāngzǎo and Magistrate Liú Jié were stripped of their offices
for lax defense, which led to conflicts between the populace and missionaries,
and sent to the appropriate ministry for punishment.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the Diān army recaptured Yáozhōu.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Máo Chǎngxī was ordered to jointly investigate the missionary case with Zēng Guófān.
Zēng Guófān stated:
“To maintain a harmonious situation well
is the way to protect the people.
To prepare against unforeseen dangers
is the foundation for establishing a nation.”
An imperial decree expressed commendation.
Dīng Rìchāng was ordered to go to Tiānjīn to assist in managing foreign affairs.
In the autumn of the seventh month, on the *wùchén* day,
due to the complex border affairs in Húnchūn,
the title of Assistant Commander was added,
which became a fixed practice.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
French envoy Ruōshúyà (Rochechouart) returned to the capital
because Zēng Guófān did not agree to sentence the prefect and magistrate.
Guófān was decreed to swiftly apprehend the principal culprits
and quickly settle the matter.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Chónghòu was recalled.
Máo Chǎngxī was appointed acting minister for the three treaty ports.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Zhōu Shèngchuán and others suppressed and dispersed the remaining bandits in Běishān.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
an edict stated:
“The navy on the sea
is distinctly different from the navy on the rivers.
To defend against foreign aggression and strive for self-strengthening,
it will not be easy to achieve results
in less than twenty years.
However, if, due to the difficulty and arduousness of the matter,
one shrinks back and does nothing,
then there will never be a day of self-strengthening.
In recent years, internal and external officials,
when faced with urgent matters,
only caused alarm.
Once the calamity was slightly pacified,
they resorted to temporizing measures.
Even if regulations for warfare and defense were established,
they were not effectively implemented,
making the court’s deliberations mere formalities.
With accumulated habits and inertia,
how can anxiety be relieved?
Now, the steamships from the Mǐn and Hù shipyards are completed.
Mǎ Xīnyí, Dīng Rìchāng, Yīngguì, and Shěn Bǎozhēn should each select commanders to go out to sea,
train year-round,
to prepare for unforeseen circumstances.
Guǎngdōng should also make preparations for steamships,
and Ruìlín and Lǐ Fútài must diligently manage this.
For officers who are proficient in wind, waves, and sand lines,
they should be selected and recommended at any time.
Even those from the mountains or countryside who are skilled in naval warfare
should also be sought out at any time,
and promoted according to their talents.
All governors-general and governors should take an overall view of the situation
to fulfill their commission.”
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Southern Route Gān army recaptured Wèiyuán and Dídào.
In this month,
tax arrears for Huàngzhōu, which was affected by disturbance, were remitted.
In the eighth month, on the *dìngyǒu* day,
Zhāng Wénxiáng from Rǔyáng assassinated Mǎ Xīnyí.
Zēng Guófān was ordered to be the Governor-General of the Liǎngjiāng;
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was transferred to be the Governor-General of Zhílì;
Lǐ Hànzhāng was made the Governor-General of Húguǎng.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Yellow River naval force was established.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Lǐ Fánjué, the bandit leader of Běishān, was executed.
On the *rényín* day,
Zhāng Zhīwàn was ordered to jointly interrogate Zhāng Wénxiáng with Kuí Yù.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Máo Chǎngxī was recalled.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was ordered to jointly investigate the Tiānjīn missionary case with Zēng Guófān.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
the Guìjūn (Guǎngxi Army) suppressed the bandits of Ānbiān and Héyáng,
and Liáng Tiānxī was executed.
Tributes and trained elephants from Yuènán were accepted.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Lǐ Chéngmóu was appointed as the commander of the newly established steamship fleet.
In the ninth month, on the *wùchén* day,
the Diānjūn (Yúnnán Army) recaptured Xīnxīng.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
an edict ordered Chóngshí to still proceed to Zūnyì to handle the missionary case.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
for the crime of instigating conflict between civilians and missionaries in Tiānjīn,
Zhāng Guāngzǎo and Liú Jié were exiled,
and fifteen perpetrators who committed brutal killings were executed.
This autumn,
Chuān Dōng (Eastern Sìchuān), Jīngzhōu, and Rèhé suffered from floods,
and relief was provided.
In the winter, tenth month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
Shěn Bǎozhēn went into mourning,
but was ordered to resume managing maritime affairs after one hundred days.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Liú Míngchuán was ordered to oversee military affairs in Shǎnxī.
An edict strictly forbade arbitrary levies by prefectures and counties in Sìchuān.
Funds were allocated for continued relief for the refugees of Běishān.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
due to the obstruction of grain barges in Jiāngběi by shallow waters,
they were transported overland to Línqīng.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the Tiānjīn Arsenal was completed.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Japan requested a treaty for commerce,
and the Zǒngshǔ (Grand Council) was allowed to select officials to negotiate the treaty.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the tribute of sable fur from Kēbùduō (Khovd) was exempted.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the position of Commissioner of Three Treaty Ports was abolished,
and the Governor-General of Zhílì was ordered to manage these affairs,
following the precedent of the Nányáng Dàchén (Commissioner for Southern Ports),
and was given the seal of a Qīnchāi Dàchén (Imperial Commissioner).
Provincial officials were strictly enjoined to handle diplomatic negotiations with caution and secrecy,
and any who leaked information would be immediately executed.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
due to repeated occurrences of floods and droughts,
an edict called for self-reflection and reform.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Zhōu Shèngchuán’s army was moved to guard the Jīfǔ (Capital Region).
The Shǎnxī Hui rebels, Yǔ Shēngyàn and others, fled to Píngfān,
where government forces suffered a defeat,
and Commander Zhāng Wànměi and others died.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the Zhílì Jīnhǎiguān Dào (Zhílì Jin Coastal Customs Intendant) was established.
Liú Jǐntáng’s forces captured Hánbó and other fortresses,
and jointly besieged Jīnjībǎo.
In the intercalary tenth month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Russian envoy Wōliánggēlǐ (Valeriy Grigorovich Gribovsky) arrived in the capital.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Xiāngtán secret society was pacified.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the Diānjūn recaptured Yǒngběi, Hèqìng, Zhènnán, and Chǔxióng.
Hui rebels captured Wūlǐyǎsūtái (Uliastai).
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the Yǒngdìng Hé (River) was closed.
Zēng Guófān was ordered to plan for river transport.
On the *wùyín* day,
Wú Yàzhōng and others from Yuènán were executed.
In the eleventh month, on the *guǐsì* day,
Zhèng Dūnjǐn was ordered to jointly hear the case of Zhāng Wénxiáng.
Soon after, the verdict was finalized,
and Zhāng Wénxiáng was executed by slow slicing in Jiāngníng.
On the *dìngyǒu* day,
Hui rebels fled to Liángzhōu,
Vice General Xiè Yuánxīng died in battle,
and Wáng Rénhé repelled them.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Xiāngjūn (Húnán Army) reinforcing Qián (Guìzhōu) recaptured Táigǒng.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Fú Jì and Róng Quán were stripped of their posts but retained in service because bandits had entered Wūlǐyǎsūtái.
Zēng Guófān was appointed concurrent Commissioner of Commerce.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Zhōu Dōngxīng, the General Soldier of Gānsù, embezzled relief funds,
and was ordered to be executed before the army.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Liú Kūnyī was stripped of his post but retained in service for leaking a secret edict.
In the twelfth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an edict strictly prohibited various abuses such as embezzlement and unauthorized reductions in river conservancy projects.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Diānjūn recaptured Dèngchuān and Làngqióng.
The Hui leader Mǎ Yuánfā assassinated Commander Dīng Xiánfā and others,
and was captured and executed.
This winter,
arrears in taxes due to disaster and disruption were remitted for Wèi (Guìzhōu) and other prefectures and counties in Xīngyì, and Suídé and other prefectures and counties in Shǎnxī.
This year,
Cháoxiǎn (Joseon) paid tribute.
In the tenth year, *xīnwèi*, spring, first month, on the *xīnmǎo* day (the first day of the month),
banquets were suspended.
On the *rénchén* day,
government forces captured the bandit stronghold of Héxī Wángtuǎn,
Jīn Shùn was awarded the yellow jacket,
and Zhāng Yào was granted an additional Yúnqíwèi.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Qiánjūn (Guìzhōu Army) pacified bandit strongholds in Guìdìng and other places,
and captured Dūyún.
Commander Lín Cóngtài and General Soldier Hé Xiónghuī were awarded yellow jackets.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Féng Zǐcái was ordered to proceed to Tàipíng to suppress the Mùmǎ and Liángshān bandits.
On the *rényín* day,
Guān Wén died.
This month,
excessive taxes for areas like Ānzhōu in Zhílì affected by floods were remitted.
In the second month, on the *rénxū* day,
Liú Jǐntáng’s forces captured Jīnjībǎo,
and the bandit leader Mǎ Huàlóng and others were executed.
Zuǒ Zōngtáng was granted an additional Yīqídūwèi,
Liú Jǐntáng was awarded Yúnqíwèi and the yellow jacket,
Réi Zhèngwǎn’s punishment was revoked,
and Chén Shí’s original post was restored.
Huáng Dǐng and Jīn Yùnchāng were awarded yellow jackets.
The surrendered Shǎnxī Hui people were settled in Huàpíng Chuān in Huátíng,
and a Tōngpàn (Assistant Prefect) and Dūsī (Battalion Commander) were appointed to pacify them.
Péng Qìngzhāng, the former magistrate of Língzhōu, was executed
for plotting for the bandits.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the rebel general Sòng Jǐngshī was captured
and executed.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Yīng Bǎoshí, the Judicial Commissioner of Jiāngsū, was transferred to Tiānjīn
to plan for commerce with Japan.
Ruì Cháng was appointed Grand Secretary,
and Wén Xiáng was appointed Associate Grand Secretary.
In the third month, on the *guǐsì* day,
Jīn Shùn’s forces captured Níngxià,
and the bandit leader Mǎ Wànxuǎn was executed.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Diānjūn recaptured Chéngjiāng,
captured Jiāngnà Tǔchéng,
and the bandit leader Mǎ Hé and others were executed.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Prussian envoy Lǐ Fúsī (Max von Brandt) presented a national letter,
stating that the German states and the three free cities of Hànxièchéng (Hanseatic cities) had reunified,
and accepted the honorary title of Emperor of Germany.
A letter of congratulations was sent in return.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Wō Rén was appointed Grand Secretary of Wénhuá Diàn,
and Ruì Cháng was appointed Grand Secretary of Wényuān Gé.
From early spring until this month,
the Emperor continuously prayed for rain.
On the *gēngxū* day,
it rained.
In the summer, fourth month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
the Xiāngjūn reinforcing Qián (Guìzhōu) recaptured Xīnchéng, Yánménsī, and other cities,
and captured Gāopō and other Miáo villages.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Hui population of Níngxià Nàjiāzhá surrendered.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Shǎnxī Hui rebels raided Píngfān and Niǎnbó,
and government forces repelled them.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Wō Rén died.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Liáng Yàoshū and 322 others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with different ranks.
The fortresses of Dàgū and Běitáng were built.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Fú Jì was dismissed from office,
and Jīn Shùn was appointed General of Wūlǐyǎsūtái.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Hui rebels again raided Sàiyīnnàoyán Bù (Sain Noyon Aimag), burning and plundering Gùěrbānsàihàn and other places.
On the Gēngyín day of the fifth month, the first day of the lunar month,
it rained.
On the Yǐwèi day,
Zǔo Zōngtáng requested to prohibit and suppress the new sects of the Huímin,
but this was not permitted.
On the Wùxū day,
Miao chiefs Wén Guóxīng and others surrendered,
and cities like Bāzhài were all recovered.
On the Rénchén day,
Huí bandits disturbed Wūlātè.
Dù●'ěr and Sàsābù’s armies jointly attacked them.
On the Bǐngwǔ day,
the Hunan Army reinforcing Qián recovered cities like Dānjiāng and Kǎilǐ.
Sū Yuánchūn was awarded a yellow riding jacket.
On the Jǐyǒu day,
Lǐ Shìzhōng was dismissed from office for seeking revenge and engaging in fierce fighting,
Chén Guóruì for creating trouble by staging a play.
Lǐ Shìzhōng was stripped of his position,
Chén Guóruì was demoted to Dūsi,
both were ordered to return to their hometowns,
and placed under the supervision of local officials.
On the Xīnhài day,
Zhèng Qīnwáng Chéngzhì was found guilty,
stripped of his title and arrested for trial.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was ordered to handle the Japan trade treaty,
with Yìng Bǎoshí and Chén Qīn as assistants.
On the Yǐmǎo day,
Jīn Shùn requested leave to observe mourning for his parent.
This was not granted.
On the Jǐwèi day,
the Yunnan Army recovered Yúnlóng.
On the Rénxū day of the sixth month,
Tàibái (Venus) was seen in daylight.
The secret societies in Yìyáng and other places were pacified.
On the Jǐsì day,
the Shǎnxī Huí Bái Yànhǔ gathered the Huí people of Xīníng to disturb Hézhōu.
On the Gēngwǔ day,
the Qián Army captured Yǒngníng, Zhènníng, and the Miao strongholds of Guīhuà,
and broke through the various fortified villages and settlements of Lángdài and Shuǐchéng.
On the Yǐhài day,
Ruìlín was appointed Grand Secretary,
but remained in his post as Governor-General of Guǎngdōng and Guǎngxī.
On the Jǐmǎo day,
bandits from Fǔyáng disturbed Shěnqiū and Rǔyáng,
and the imperial army captured and executed them.
On the Xīnsì day,
due to rampant banditry in Guǎngdōng,
an edict was issued ordering strict apprehension.
On the Dīnghài day,
Dézōng was born at Chún Dǐ.
On the Wùzǐ day,
relief was provided for the disaster in Tiānjīn.
In autumn, on the Jǐchǒu day of the seventh month, the first day of the lunar month,
the Guì Army suppressed the bandits fleeing into Yuènán,
captured Chángqìng,
and beheaded the bandit leader Zhào Xióngcái.
On the Rénchén day,
Dù●'ěr’s army attacked bandits in Bùlātè,
and won.
On the Jiǎwǔ day,
the Yǒngdìng Hé breached again.
On the Bǐngshēn day,
Mùtúshàn went to Běishān to suppress bandits.
Jīn Yùnchāng’s army suppressed bandits fleeing into Wūlātè,
and won.
On the Dīngwèi day,
the Qìn Hé in Hénèi breached.
On the Yǐmǎo day,
bandits from Chāngtú caused disturbance.
Dūxīng'ā dispatched troops to suppress and pacify them.
On the Rénshēn day of the eighth month,
Vice Commander-in-chief Qìngzhì was granted the inherited title of Zhèng Qīnwáng.
On the Jiǎxū day,
the Guì Army captured the bandit stronghold of Ānshì,
pursued and suppressed the bandits fleeing from Tàiyuán,
and Sū Guóhàn went to Guǎngdōng to surrender.
On the Dīngchǒu day,
an imperial edict ordered all provinces to establish bureaus to shelter displaced orphans and widows.
On the Bǐngshēn day of the ninth month,
the corrupt practice of collecting grain in Gāoyóu was abolished.
On the Dīngyǒu day,
the Gān Army captured the strategic pass of Kāngjiāyá.
Róng Quán was urged to proceed to Yīlí.
Liú Míngchuán was granted three months' leave.
On the Rénchén day,
an edict was issued to Fèng and Jí to rectify official administration
and strictly apprehend bandits.
Ēnxī was ordered to go to Shànghǎi to handle the treaty exchange with Austria.
On the Dīngwèi day,
Qiáo Sōngnián and others jointly blocked the breach at Hóujiālín.
This autumn,
disaster relief was provided for various prefectures and counties in Shùnzhí and Hézé.
Taxes in Púzhōu affected by floods and Huàngzhōu affected by disturbances were remitted.
In winter, on the Wùwǔ day of the tenth month, the first day of the lunar month,
Dá'ěrzì was stripped of his position and arrested for negligence in withdrawing his camp and allowing bandits to escape.
He was arrested for trial.
Cáo Kèzhōng was ordered to take command of Liú Míngchuán’s army,
and proceed to Sùzhōu for defense and suppression.
On the Gēngshēn day,
due to bandit disturbances in Húnán,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was ordered to investigate and handle the matter.
On the Rénchén day,
Jǐnglián was appointed Military Governor of Wūlǔmùqí.
On the Guǐwèi day,
an imperial edict pardoned officials, soldiers, and civilians in Yīlí who had been coerced.
Staff officer Gòngguǒ'ěr was ordered to take command of Dá'ěrzì’s army.
On the Guǐsì day of the eleventh month,
the Gān Army captured Hézhōu,
and Yǔ Déyàn and others surrendered.
On the Dīngwèi day,
Huí bandits from Xīníng escaped to Wūlātè and Zhōngwèi.
Zhāng Yào’s army repelled them.
On the Yǐmǎo day,
Huí bandits from Sùzhōu attacked Dūnhuáng again.
Wénlín reinforced and suppressed them.
On the Xīnwèi day of the twelfth month,
the earlier scholar Zhāng Lǚxiáng was given the honor of being enshrined in the Temple of Literature.
On the Dīngchǒu day,
bandits from Xiāngshān, such as Zēng Dà'é Fú, rebelled,
and were captured and executed.
This year,
Cháoxiān (Korea), Liúqiú (Ryukyu), and Yuènán (Vietnam) sent tribute.
In the spring of the eleventh year, on the Bǐngxū day of the first month, the first day of the lunar month,
banquets were suspended.
On the Jǐchǒu day,
an edict announced a reduction in punishments to commemorate the new reign year.
Wénshuò was stripped of his position for feigning illness.
On the Xīn Mǎo day,
the Guì Army recovered Cónghuà in Yuènán,
and captured Zhènshān.
On the Guǐsì day,
the Gān Army successively broke through bandit strongholds at Gānpíng, Dàbèipíng, and other places,
and advanced to attack Tàizǐsì.
On the Gēngzǐ day,
the Qián Army captured Qīngpíng, Huángpíng, and Zhòng'ān.
On the Xīnchǒu day,
the Hunan Army reinforcing Qián captured Huángpiāo and the Miao stronghold of Báibǎo.
On the Xīnhài day,
Secretary Chónghòu and Taichangsi Shaoqing Xià Jiāgǎo were ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén (Office of General Management of State Affairs).
On the Gēngshēn day of the second month,
Jiangsu was permitted to trial river transport for rice,
while the tribute grain and tax silver continued to be transported by sea.
On the Bǐngyín day,
Zēng Guófān died,
and was posthumously granted the title of Grand Tutor.
On the Wùchén day,
Liú Míngchuán was stripped of his position,
but retained his first-class viscount title due to his previous merits.
On the Gēngwǔ day,
Péng Yùlín was recalled to inspect the Yangtze River naval forces.
On the Jiǎshēn day,
the breach at Hóujiālín was closed.
Yuènán bandit leaders Sū Guóhàn and others were executed.
This month,
disaster relief was provided for various prefectures in Sìchuān.
On the Yǐyǒu day of the third month, the first day of the lunar month,
the Qián Army recovered Zhēnfēng.
On the Bǐngxū day,
the Gān Army suffered a defeat while suppressing Huí bandits at Tàizǐsì.
Admiral Fù Xiānrǒng and Xú Wénxiù died.
Admiral Yáng Shìjùn was stripped of his yellow riding jacket
and demoted to参将 (Assistant General).
On the Jiǎwǔ day,
Dá'ěrzì and others were pardoned of their crimes,
but remained stripped of their positions and ordered to serve.
On the Dīngyǒu day,
due to bandits from Fèng disturbing the Korean border,
strict apprehension was ordered.
On the Xīnchǒu day,
Ruìcháng died.
This spring,
taxes in Huángpí in Húběi, Ānzhōu in Zhílì, and Hézhōu in Gānsù, affected by disturbances, were remitted.
In summer, on the Bǐngchén day of the fourth month,
Huí bandits escaped to Dìngbiān and Jìngbiān.
The Shǎnxī Army repelled them.
On the Jǐwèi day,
the Xīníng Huí chief Mǎ Zhàn'áo, Shǎnxī Huí Cuī Sān, and Mǐlāgōu Huí chief Zhì Chénglín and others
surrendered one after another.
On the Bǐngyín day,
the practice of handling "huójì" (miscellaneous goods) at Huáiguān was stopped.
The Imperial Household Department was enjoined to strive for frugality.
On the Jǐmǎo day,
Wáng Wéizhēn, Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission, submitted a memorial advocating for upholding the emperor's intentions and wishes,
and making filial piety a guiding principle.
He was given a severe reprimand,
and subsequently stripped of his position.
This month,
taxes in Xīngyì and other prefectures in Guìzhōu, affected by disturbances, were remitted.
On the *jiǎshēn* day of the fifth month, the first day of the lunar month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Taxes and levies for the banner people and commoners in Réhé (熱河) were remitted for three years.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
from the first ten days of the third month,
Empress Dowager Cíxǐ (慈禧太后) was unwell,
and for over a month did not hold court.
By this time,
Censor Lǐ Hóngmó (李宏謨) requested frequent imperial audiences.
An edict reprimanded him for his presumption
and strictly admonished him.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Xú Zhànbīao's (徐占彪) army repeatedly achieved victories in suppressing the Huí (回) rebels.
Zuǒ Zōngtáng (左宗棠) impeached Chéng Lù (成祿) for squandering funds and delaying matters.
Mùtúshàn (穆圖善) was ordered to investigate.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Miáo (苗) rebels in Guìzhōu (貴州) were pacified,
and Xí Bǎotián (席寶田) was awarded the hereditary title of Qídūwèi (騎都尉).
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Sòng Quándé (宋全德) and other Huí rebels in Shǎnxī (陝西) surrendered.
Chén Fú'ēn (陳孚恩), the disgraced former Grand Secretary who perished in Yīlí (伊犁), and his family were granted commendations and enhanced pensions.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng (李鴻章) was appointed Grand Secretary
but remained in his post as Governor-General of Zhílì (直隸).
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Diān (滇) army captured Yǒngpíng (永平) and Yúnnán (雲南).
On the *jiǎwǔ* day of the sixth month,
Zhū Fèngbīao (朱鳳標) retired from office.
Wénxiáng (文祥) was appointed Grand Secretary,
and Quánqìng (全慶) Assistant Grand Secretary.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
an edict ordered the suspension of this year's autumn and court assizes for capital punishment decisions.
Shàn Màozhīan (單懋謙) was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary.
On the *guǐwèi* day of the seventh month, the first day of the lunar month,
the Diān army jointly captured Xīngyì (興義).
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the customary tribute from Guōěrkā (廓爾喀) was remitted.
Relief was provided to the disaster-stricken soldiers and commoners of Dámù Měnggǔ (達木蒙古) and the thirty-nine tribes.
On the *wùxū* day,
Huí rebels raided and harassed the western route of Níngxià (寧夏) and the Āláshàn (阿拉善) Banner;
the imperial army repulsed them.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Zhílì presented auspicious wheat.
Censor Bīan Bǎoquán (邊寶泉) memorialized on the matter.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng (李鴻章) was instructed to diligently care for the people and relieve their distress,
compensate for localized disasters,
and not exaggerate auspicious omens.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the lower section of the Yǒngdìng Hé (永定河) overflowed.
In this month,
arrears of taxes for the harassed residents of Huàngzhōu (晃州), Húnán (湖南), were remitted.
On the *gēngwǔ* day of the eighth month,
over 100,000 *shí* of grain from the Jiangbei (江北) transport was intercepted to relieve the flood-stricken people in Jīfǔ (畿輔).
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Jīn Shùn (金順) was dismissed for procrastination.
Cháng Shùn (常順) was appointed acting General of Wūlǐyǎsūtái (烏里雅蘇臺).
On the *xīnsì* day,
Shàn Màozhīan (單懋謙) was appointed Grand Secretary.
On the *guǐwèi* day of the ninth month,
the Diān army captured Zhàozhōu (趙州), Ménghuà (蒙化), and the upper and lower passes of Dàlǐ (大理).
Yáng Yùkē (楊玉科) and Lǐ Wéishù (李維述) were awarded yellow jackets.
Zuǒ Zōngtáng (左宗棠) reported the discovery of auspicious wheat and grain.
An edict rejected it.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Empress Ālǔtè (阿魯特) was formally enthroned.
From the imperial princes and ministers downwards, special favors and rewards were extended,
and an imperial edict was issued to the empire,
granting varying degrees of grace.
The coffer-dam of the Yǒngdìng Hé (永定河) project was closed.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Péng Yùlín's (彭玉麟) request to return home due to illness was granted,
but he was still ordered to annually inspect the Yangtze (長江) naval forces.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Róng Quán (榮全) requested that Qìngfú (慶符) be ordered to pacify the Chán (纏) and common people,
and that Yīnglíam (英廉) and others' cavalry be stationed at Kùěrkālāwūsū (庫爾喀喇烏蘇)
and appropriately recruit local militia;
this was granted.
On the *dīngsì* day of the tenth month,
Féng Gāoshān (馮高山) and other leaders of the defeated Gānsù (甘肅) militia were executed.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
additional honorific titles were bestowed upon the two Empress Dowagers.
On the *wùchén* day,
the local bandits in Lóng'ān (隆安) and Cénxī (岑溪), Guǎngxī (廣西),
and the Miáo (苗) rebels in Xīlóng (西隆) were pacified.
On the *rénchén* day,
an edict instructed the commanding generals to restrain their deputies
and punish those who harassed and exceeded their authority.
The request of Gōng Qīnwáng (恭親王) was granted,
restoring the old system of the Grand Council.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Hé Jǐng (何璟) was dismissed due to mourning.
Zhāng Shùshēng (張樹聲) was appointed acting Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng (兩江).
On the *yǐyǒu* day of the eleventh month,
Korean pirate ships crossed the border and harassed.
Dūxīng'ā (都興阿) and others' naval forces pursued and suppressed them.
Huí rebels harassed Hāmì (哈密) Dōngshān (東山);
the imperial army suppressed and defeated them.
Bribery and impersonation were forbidden in the imperial, provincial, and metropolitan examinations.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the local bandits in Qióngzhōu (瓊州) were pacified,
and their leader Hé Yàwàn (何亞萬) and others were executed.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Diān army suppressed bandits occupying Guǎnyì (館驛) and other places.
Yǐdōng (迤東) and Yǐnán (迤南) were cleared.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Huí rebels from Sù (肅) fled to the Zāsàkèhàn (扎薩克汗) Banners.
The imperial army repulsed them.
The Qián (黔) army jointly captured Xīnchéng (新城).
Miáo (苗) rebels in Xiàjiāng (下江) revolted.
Zhāng Wéndé's (張文德) army suppressed and eliminated them.
The entire Guìzhōu (黔) province was pacified.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Niǎn (捻) bandits harassed Tàihú (太湖).
The naval forces suppressed and pacified them.
Soldiers and commoners who joined the Gēlǎohuì (哥老會) were permitted to surrender and be pardoned.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the cultivation of poppies in all provinces was strictly forbidden again.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Liú Jǐntáng (劉錦棠) and other armies suppressed Huí (回) rebels,
achieving a great victory.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the Shǎn (陝) army suppressed the fleeing bandits in Èrdàohé (二道河) and other places in northern Shǎnxī (陝西),
exterminating them.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng (李鴻章) memorialized for the establishment of the China Merchants' Steam Navigation Company,
to test the use of steamships for transporting grain tribute in Jiāng (江) and Zhè (浙).
On the *jǐwèi* day of the twelfth month,
Dé Tài (德泰), the Assistant Resident Commissioner in Tibet, was dismissed from office and returned to his banner due to an incident.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
an edict was issued to the Board of Civil Office, the Board of War, and the Court of Colonial Affairs,
stating that after the Emperor assumed personal rule,
all memorials and military dispatches requesting imperial instructions from various departments
should be written in Chinese.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Tían Xīngshù (田興恕) was released and returned home.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng (左宗棠) requested leave due to illness.
A kind imperial decree refused the request.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the comprehensive ancestral sacrifice was performed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn (朝鮮) sent tribute.
On the *xīnsì* day of the first month of spring in the twelfth year, the *guǐyǒu* year, the first day of the lunar month.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the imperial army engaged Huí (回) rebels at Nàmǎtèjígànzhāo (那瑪特吉幹昭)
and defeated them.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Lǐ Zōngxī (李宗羲) was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng (兩江),
concurrently serving as Minister for Treaty Ports.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Chéng Lù (成祿) was accused of imposing exorbitant taxes and treason,
dismissed from office and arrested for questioning.
Jīn Shùn (金順) was urgently ordered to take command of his army.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the Diān (滇) army captured Dàlǐ (大理).
The Huí (回) chieftains Dù Wénxiù (杜文秀), Yáng Róng (楊榮), Cài Tíngdòng (蔡廷棟), and others were executed.
Cén Yùyīng (岑毓英) was awarded a yellow jacket and the hereditary post of Qídūwèi (騎都尉).
Liú Yuèzhāo's (劉嶽昭) punishment was revoked.
Yáng Yùkē (楊玉科) was awarded the hereditary post of Qídūwèi (騎都尉).
On the *yǐsì* day,
the two Empress Dowagers, as the Emperor's assumption of personal rule was imminent,
issued an imperial decree encouraging the Emperor
“to reverently uphold the family traditions,
diligently study the selection of officials and governance,
and not neglect classical studies.”
They also exhorted court officials and officials both within and outside the capital
“to be loyal and diligent in their duties,
and greatly aid in overcoming difficulties.”
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Emperor assumed personal rule,
and issued an edict
“to respectfully follow the empress dowagers' instructions,
revere Heaven and emulate the ancestors,
and be diligent in governance and love the people.”
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
an edict instructed the Imperial Household Department to strictly verify and economize,
and not to borrow beyond the annual expenditure of 600,000.
On the *gēngxū* day of the second month, the first day of the lunar month,
the Grand Councilors, the Six Boards, and the Nine Ministers met to discuss measures for the Yellow River and the Grand Canal.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng (李鴻章) was instructed to carefully plan and report.
An edict was issued for self-reflection and reform,
seeking frank advice.
Edicts were issued to the provinces to recommend talented individuals
and prevent corruption.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
additional honorific titles were bestowed upon the two Empress Dowagers.
The next day, an edict was issued granting varying degrees of grace.
Liú Jǐntáng's (劉錦棠) army captured Dàtōng Xiàngyángbǎo (大通向陽堡).
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
for the visit to the Eastern Tombs,
Dūn Qīnwáng (惇親王) and others were ordered to remain in the capital to handle affairs.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Jīn Shùn's (金順) army reached Sùzhōu (肅州) to suppress Huí (回) rebels
and defeated them.
In the third month, on the day *Guǐwèi*,
the Emperor, accompanying the Two Empresses Dowager, visited the Eastern Mausoleums (Dōnglíng).
On the day *Dīnghài*,
the imperial procession returned.
The regular land tax (èfù) for the current year was remitted for areas through which the imperial retinue (bìlù) passed.
On the day *Jǐchǒu*,
the various Hui communities of Dàtōng, Bāyàn Rónggé, and Wǔgōng Sālā surrendered.
The bandit leader Mǎ Guìyuán and others from Xīníng were executed.
On the day *Gēngyín*,
the Emperor, accompanying the Two Empresses Dowager, returned to the palace.
On the day *Bǐngshēn*,
the Hui bandit Bái Yànhǔ and others fled to Gānzhōu.
An order was given to deliberate and establish the etiquette for foreign envoys' audiences.
Róngquán requested leave due to illness,
but it was not granted.
On the day *Gēngzǐ*,
Yīnglián was appointed Councillor Minister (Cānzàn Dàchén) of Tǎěrbāhātái.
On the day *Dīngwèi*,
the Diān (Yúnnán) army captured Shùnníng.
This spring,
arrears of grain tax (būfù) for areas disturbed by bandits in Pīzhōu, Jiāngsū, Fūzhōu, Shǎnxī, and other prefectures were remitted.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day *Yǐmǎo*,
the Northern Customs (Běihǎiguān) of Liánzhōu was established.
On the day *Bǐngchén*,
the treaty with Japan was concluded.
On the day *Yǐchǒu*,
Hui bandits fled to the Ālāshàn Banner and Ābìěrmǐtè.
An edict ordered Yùdìng'ān to dispatch troops to jointly defend and launch a pincer attack.
On the day *Jǐsì*,
the imperial army captured the bandit stronghold of Tǎěrwān in Sùzhōu.
In the fifth month, on the day *Gēngyín*,
the Diān (Yúnnán) army captured Yúnzhōu.
On the day *Dīngyǒu*,
foreign envoys' audiences were permitted.
On the day *Guǐmǎo*,
Chénglù was handed over to the Board of Punishments (Xíngbù) for trial and punishment.
On the day *Bǐngwǔ*,
Chéngruì was ordered to act as Commander-in-Chief (Tídū) of Wūlǔmùqí.
In the sixth month, on the day *Rénzǐ*,
the Emperor visited Yíngtái.

The Japanese envoy Soejima Taneomi (Fùdǎo Zhǒngchén), Russian envoy Vsevolod Vsevolozhsky (Wōliáng***lǐ), American envoy Frederick Ferdinand Low (Lóufěidí), British envoy Thomas Francis Wade (Wēituǒmǎ), French envoy Jules Auguste Dufaure (Rèfúlǐ), and Dutch envoy Frederik Nicolaas van Baren (Fèiguǒsūn) had an audience at the Zǐguānggé
and presented their credentials.
On the day *Gēngshēn*,
Jīnshùn was sternly urged to depart through the pass.
On the day *Dīngmǎo*,
the Gān (Gānsù) army recovered Xúnhuà,
and the bandit leaders Mǎ Yùlián and others were executed.
In the intercalary sixth month, on the day *Jiǎshēn*,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng submitted a report stating that the old courses of the Yellow River (Huánghé) and Grand Canal (Yùnhé) in the Huái and Xú regions were difficult to restore,
and requested to continue sea transport.
For the dried-up lands of the old riverbed,
the tax assessment (shēngkè) would be adjusted accordingly.
This proposal was approved.
On the day *Bǐngxū*,
Zhū Fèngbiāo died.
The Diān (Yúnnán) army captured Téngyuè.
Cén Yùyīng was granted the hereditary title of First Class Light Chariot Captain (Yīděng Qīngchē Dūwèi),
Liú Yuèzhāo was rewarded with a yellow jacket (huángmǎguà),
and Yáng Yùkē was granted First Class Light Chariot Captain.
As the military campaign in Yúnnán had lasted eighteen years,
and many prefectures and counties had been ravaged by bandits,
an imperial edict remitted accumulated grain taxes (liángfù) from eleven years prior,
and permanently abolished the collection of "grain for military aid" (jìjūnlígu).
Liú Yuèzhāo was ordered to carefully select prefects and magistrates (mùlìng)
and to inspect officials and pacify the people.
On the day *Jiǎwǔ*,
there were prolonged rains in the capital region (Jīngjī),
and the Emperor prayed for clear weather.
On the day *Bǐngshēn*,
an edict ordered an investigation into various provincial taxes such as "acreage donations" (mǔjuān), "likin donations" (líjuān), and irregular "head and grain taxes" (dīngcáo),
to be progressively abolished.
On the day *Gēngzǐ*,
the Gān (Gānsù) army pursued and attacked Bái Yànhǔ and others at Dūnhuáng,
suffered a defeat,
and Deputy General (Fùjiàng) Lǐ Tiānhé and others died.
The Yǒngdìng Hé burst its banks.
The mink tribute from the seven banners of Āěěrtài Wūliánghǎi was remitted.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day *Xīnhài*,
the Guì (Guǎngxī) army attacked and pacified the bandits of Xīlín and Xīlóng.
On the day *Jiǎzǐ*,
disaster relief was provided in Shùntiān.
This month,
new and old regular taxes (xīn jiù èfù) in Qīngchéng, Shāndōng, affected by floodwaters, were remitted.
In the eighth month, on the day *Dīngchǒu*, the first day of the month,
Dūxīng'ā requested leave due to illness,
but he was consoled and asked to remain.
On the day *Xīnsì*,
the Grand Canal (Yùnhé) dike in Zhílì burst.
Róngquán again requested resignation due to illness,
but it was not granted.
Fùhé was found guilty and stripped of his office.
On the day *Wùzǐ*,
Bái Yànhǔ and others captured the营堡 (yíngbǎo) of Mǎliánjǐng.
Liú Yuèzhāo was summoned for an imperial audience,
and Cén Yùyīng was concurrently appointed Acting Governor-General (Zǒngdū) of Yún-Guì.
On the day *Rénchén*,
Bái Yànhǔ and others besieged Hāmì
and attacked Bālǐkūn,
where the imperial army suffered a defeat.
On the day *Yǐwèi*,
an edict ordered Jǐnglián to lead troops to reinforce the area,
transferred Xīlún to be the General-in-Chief (Lǐngduì Dàchén) of Wūlǔmùqí,
and appointed Míngchūn as Assistant Minister (Bāngbàn Dàchén) for Hāmì.
This month,
disaster relief was provided for various prefectures in Zhílì, the prefectures under Yǒngshùnfǔ, and Gōng'ān due to flooding.
In the ninth month, on the day *Bǐngyín*,
the Grand Councillors (Jūnjī Dàchén) were ordered to meet with the Board of Punishments (Xíngbù) to deliberate and determine Chénglù's punishment.
On the day *Guǐyǒu*,
the Yǒngdìng Hé embankment was closed (hélóng).
In winter, the tenth month, on the day *Bǐngzǐ*, the first day of the month,
Censor Shěn Huái submitted a memorial requesting a delay in the renovation of Yuánmíngyuán.
An edict ordered the Imperial Household Department (Nèiwùfǔ) to only repair the Ānyòu Palace (Ānyòugōng) as a temporary residence for the Emperor,
with all other constructions to be stopped.
On the day *Jǐhài*,
the imperial army captured Sùzhōu,
and the rebel bandit Mǎ Wénlù was executed.
The Emperor visited the Two Empresses Dowager to congratulate them on the victory.
On the day *Gēngzǐ*,
in recognition of merits,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng was ordered to assist as Grand Secretary (Dàxuéshì) while serving as Governor-General of Shǎn-Gān,
and was granted First Class Light Chariot Captain;
Jīnshùn's office was restored,
and his yellow jacket (huángmǎguà) was returned;
Xú Zhànbīao and Mùtúshàn were granted Cloud Cavalry Commandant (Yúnqíwèi).
In the eleventh month, on the day *Jǐwèi*,
the King of Yuènán (Vietnam) submitted a memorial requesting a joint suppression of bandits in the borderlands of Héyáng, Xīnghuà, Shānxī, and Xuānguāng.
Liú Chángyòu and Féng Zǐcái were ordered to deliberate and report.
On the day *Xīnyǒu*,
France and Yuènán (Vietnam) engaged in hostilities;
French troops breached the provincial capital of Hénèi,
and Vietnamese bandits disturbed Běiníng.
The Vietnamese sought aid.
An edict ordered Ruìlín to dispatch troops from Qīnzhōu through the pass
to join the Guì (Guǎngxī) army in reinforcing and suppressing the bandits.
On the day *Jiǎzǐ*,
Censor Wú Kědú requested that Chénglù be punished by public execution according to law.
On the day *Jǐsì*,
Cén Yùyīng memorialized on rectifying official administration and military camps,
and requested the disbandment of militias (yǒng) and cessation of donations (juān),
starting from Yúnnán.
An edict praised this.
On the day *Gēngwǔ*,
the Grand Canal (Yùnhé) was dredged.
On the day *Rénshēn*,
Chénglù was sentenced to decapitation.
Wú Kědú was demoted for "improperly listening to court affairs" (cìtīng cháozhèng).
In the twelfth month, on the day *Jiǎshēn*,
Hui bandits disturbed the Wūliánghǎi and other tribes,
and Xīlún's army pursued and suppressed them,
defeating them.
On the day *Wùzǐ*,
due to the absurdities found in the examination paper of Xú Jǐngchūn, a successful candidate from Shùntiān,
the examiners, including Minister (Shàngshū) Quánqìng and Censor-in-Chief (Dū Yùshǐ) Hú Jiāyù, were demoted and dismissed in varying degrees.
On the day *Xīnmǎo*,
Èlèhébù was ordered to go to Wūlǐyāsūtái to investigate and handle affairs.
On the day *Bǐngshēn*,
the late Commander-in-Chief (Tídū) Liú Sōngshān was posthumously awarded First Class Light Chariot Captain.
Zhāng Yào and Jīnshùn were ordered to divide their forces and advance westward.
On the day *Rényín*,
for the fortieth birthday celebration of Empress Dowager Cíxǐ,
favors were extended to close imperial princes and dukes, and to central and foreign ministers,
with rewards varying according to rank.
This year,
Cháoxiǎn (Korea) offered tribute.
In the thirteenth year, *Jiǎxū*, spring, the first month, on the day *Yǐsì*, the first day of the month,
feasts and banquets were suspended.
On the day *Jiǎyín*,
the Xiāng (Húnán) army suppressed the Miáo bandits of Gǔzhōu,
pacifying them.
On the day *Bǐngchén*,
Compiler (Biānxiū) Zhāng Yīnglín and Reviser (Jiǎntǎo) Wáng Qìngqí were ordered to serve as lecturers (zhí) in the Hóngdé Hall.
On the day *Xīnyǒu*,
due to mutual impeachment between Liú Kūnyī and Hú Jiāyù,
Kūnyī was demoted to a third-rank button (sānpǐn dǐngdài) and stripped of his office but retained in his post,
while Jiāyù was demoted five ranks and transferred.
On the day *Guǐhài*,
an edict ordered the construction of the Dōngmíng long dike.
On the day *Jǐsì*,
the imperial army reinforced Shāshānzi and attacked Hui bandits,
achieving victory.
Fúzhūlǐ was rewarded with a yellow jacket (huángmǎguà).
In the second month, on the day *Jǐmǎo*,
Hui bandits disturbed the border of Bālǐkūn,
and Míngchūn and others jointly suppressed them.
On the day *Bǐngshēn*,
as France had taken Yuènán (Vietnam) territory,
and Vietnamese bandits disturbed Shānxī
and approached the Diān (Yúnnán) border,
Cén Yùyīng was ordered to deploy border defenses.
Private minting in the capital (Jīngshī) was prohibited.
On the day *Dīngyǒu*,
the Emperor, accompanying the Two Empresses Dowager, visited the Western Mausoleums (Xīlíng).
In the third month, on the day Jiǎchén,
returned to the palace.
On the day Yǐsì,
provided relief to the disaster victims in Fèngtian.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
ordered Bǎo Yún to assist in handling the affairs of Grand Secretary.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
repaired the seawall in Hǎiníng.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
regarding the merits of pacifying Guìzhōu,
reinstated Táo Màolín as Provincial Commander,
and awarded hereditary positions to Provincial Commander Hé Shìhuá and others.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Japanese warships anchored at Xiàmén.
An edict ordered Shěn Bǎozhēn to lead troops there by steamer
and make arrangements as circumstances required.
Li Hóngzhāng was ordered to confer with the Peruvian envoy on matters concerning Chinese laborers.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Jiǎxū,
an imperial decree allocated 100,000 taels of silver to relieve and console the tribes affected by disaster and disturbance in Wūlǐyǎsūtái.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the Emperor visited Yíngtái.
Shàn Màozqiān requested retirement due to illness,
which was granted.
The Russian envoy Bùcè and others were granted an audience at Zǐguānggé.
On the day Xīnsì,
the Emperor visited Yuánmíngyuán and returned to the palace.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Manasi Hui rebels attacked Kuítún and other places.
The government forces suffered a defeat in their suppression efforts.
Jǐng Lián led troops to reinforce them.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Japanese warships arrived at Táiwān and landed,
provoking the indigenous people.
Shěn Bǎozhēn was ordered to manage coastal defense
and concurrently act as a minister handling foreign affairs,
with steamers from various ports along the coasts of Jiāng and Guǎng
to be dispatched as needed.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Cháng Shùn was dismissed from his post due to an incident.
Élèhébù was appointed General of Wūlǐyǎsūtái.
Qìng Chūn was appointed Military Governor of Cháhā'ěr.
Tuōlúnbù was appointed Counselor Minister of Kēbùduō.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Lù Rùnxiáng and 337 others were granted the Jinshì degree with various distinctions.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Jǐng Lián again requested leave due to illness,
but it was not granted.
In the fifth month, on the first day Rén yín,
the peace treaty between France and Vietnam was concluded.
An edict ordered border generals to pacify and settle the displaced refugees who had moved inland.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the Emperor visited Yuánmíngyuán and returned to the palace.
Japan attacked indigenous villages in Táiwān.
On the day Dīngsì,
on the occasion of Empress Dowager Cíxǐ's birthday,
grace awards were given to banner officials in the capital aged sixty and above,
and the determination of sentences for prisoners in this year's autumn and court reviews was suspended.
On the day Jǐwèi,
a comet was sighted.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
an imperial decree provided relief to the disaster victims in Fèngtian.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Shěn Bǎozhēn's request was granted:
to construct coastal forts in Táiwān,
to pacify the indigenous tribes,
and to withdraw fatigued troops.
On the day Wùchén,
Japanese warships cruised along various coastal ports in Fújiàn.
Japanese envoy Liǔyuán Qiánguāng discussed the Táiwān military affair with the Grand Council ministers.
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐhài,
an edict ordered Commander Sūn Kāihuá to take over the defense of Xiàmén.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Yáng Yuèbīn, Zēng Guóquán, Yán Jìngmíng, Zhào Dézhé, Dīng Rìchāng, Bào Chāo, Jiǎng Yìlǐ, and Guō Sōngtāo were summoned to the capital.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the surrendered troops from Wūsuǒzhài rebelled again.
The Yunnan army suppressed them.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng's request was granted:
the Xúzhōu army of Táng Dìngkuí was to cross the sea to Táiwān.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
an edict ordered the Board of Revenue to economize on non-essential expenditures
and to plan in advance for coastal defense funds.
An edict ordered Shěn Bǎozhēn to deploy defenses along the northern and southern routes.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Wēng Tónghé was ordered to continue his duties at Hóngdédiàn.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Dīngwèi,
Lǐ Hènián requested the establishment of trained forces for the land routes in the Fújiàn province,
which was approved.
On the day Gēngxū,
Manas Hui rebels attacked Xīhú.
The government forces repelled them.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng was appointed Grand Secretary,
and remained in his post as Governor-General of Shǎanxi and Gānsù.
Jǐng Lián was appointed Imperial Commissioner
to supervise military affairs in Xīnjiāng.
Jīn Shùn was appointed Assistant Supervisor of military affairs.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the Belgian envoy Xiè'ēnshī and others were granted an audience at Zǐguānggé.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Minister of the Imperial Household Guì Bǎo, for
deceitfully reporting on timber donations by Prefect Lǐ Guāngzhāo
during his tenure as a director,
was severely discussed and dismissed from office.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
bandits on horseback captured Nínggǔtǎ,
but it was soon recovered.
Fújiàn's military expenditure was permitted to borrow 2 million foreign dollars,
to be repaid annually from customs duties.
On the day Jǐsì,
the construction project of Yuánmíngyuán was suspended.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
an edict reprimanded Prince Gōng for impropriety during an audience,
stripped him of his hereditary princely title,
demoted him to Prince of a Commandery,
but he remained a Grand Councilor.
In addition, Zài Chéng was stripped of his Bèi Lè and Prince of a Commandery titles.
Bái Yànhǔ and others attacked Jìmùsà.
The government forces defeated them.
In the eighth month, on the first day Xīnwèi,
an imperial decree reinstated Prince Gōng's hereditary title and Zài Chéng's princely title,
and admonished them.
An edict ordered the renovation of the Sānhǎi project,
stressing utmost economy.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Locus in Hénán.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Lǐ Guāngzhāo was sentenced to decapitation.
On the day Gēngyín,
an edict ordered all provinces to rectify their policing affairs.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng was ordered to supervise the logistics and transport for the Western Expedition,
with Cabinet Grand Secretary Yuán Bǎohéng appointed as assistant supervisor.
An imperial decree ordered all provinces to appropriately reduce the number of lí (likin) bureaus
and to prohibit the cultivation of poppies.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the Emperor visited Nányuàn.
On the day Wùxū,
the Emperor reviewed the archery of imperial princes, ministers, and Qianqing Gate guards.
On the day Jǐhài,
the Emperor went hunting.
In the ninth month, on the first day Gēngzǐ,
the Emperor visited Liàngyīngtái
and scattered the hunting net.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the Emperor visited Liàngyīngtái
and reviewed the Shenjiying troops.
On the day Rényín,
the Emperor reviewed the archery of princes, ministers, guards, and others.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Ruì Lín died.
Yīng Hàn was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng.
On the day Gēngxū,
Japan subsequently dispatched Dàjiǔbǎo Lìtōng (Ōkubo Toshimichi)
to discuss the Táiwān indigenous village military affair with the Grand Council ministers.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Wáng Wénshuān, the bandit leader in Nínggǔtǎ, was executed.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the Grand Council ministers reached an agreement with the Japanese envoy:
troops were to be withdrawn and return to Japan,
and Japan was to be given 500,000 in total for disaster relief for Japanese victims and Táiwān military expenses.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Jiǎ Zhēn died.
On the day Bǐngyín,

an edict ordered Lǐ Hóngzhāng and others to submit memorials to the Grand Council detailing matters concerning coastal defense, troop training, equipment selection, shipbuilding, fundraising, personnel deployment, and long-term strategies,
for thorough deliberation and reporting.
In the tenth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
on the occasion of Empress Dowager Cíxǐ's fortieth birthday,
Liú Míngchuán was reinstated as Provincial Commander.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the Emperor's celebratory ceremony was completed.
Dismissed officials were granted their official titles.
Princes, dukes, and civil and military officials were exempted from punishment.
Others received various promotions.
On the day Gēngchén,
relief was provided for the hurricane disaster in Guǎngdōng.
On the day Guǐsì,
Guǎng Shòu and Xià Tóngshàn were ordered to Shǎanxi to investigate matters.
On the day Jǐhài,
the Emperor was unwell.
Lǐ Hóngzǎo was ordered to review memorials on his behalf.
In the eleventh month, on the day of Jiǎchén,
Gōng Qīnwáng was ordered to revise and reply to Qing language memorials.
On the day of Dīngwèi,
relief was provided for flood victims in Xú and Hǎi.
On the day of Jǐyǒu,
it was ordered that all memorials, both from within and outside the court, be submitted for the perusal of the two Empresses Dowager.
Bǎo Yún was appointed Grand Secretary.
On the day of Rénzǐ,
Japan withdrew its troops.
On the day of Guǐchǒu,
it was the Winter Solstice.
Sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Yuánqiū Altar,
with Chún Qīnwáng acting on behalf of the Emperor.
One and a half million taels from the Board's treasury were disbursed to construct dikes at Shíhuànghù.
On the day of Jiǎyín,
the Emperor, due to the two Empresses Dowager's protection and care leading to his recovery,
conferred an honored title upon them.
An edict was issued to the Ministry of Punishments and all provinces to reduce sentences for criminals according to their cases.
On the day of Gēngshēn,
the establishment of trained armies in Hénán was debated.
On the day of Jiǎzǐ,
as the Shíhuànghù dikes were difficult to complete,
Dīng Bǎozhēn's request was granted
to build a dam and dikes in the Jiǎzhuāng area.
In the twelfth month, on the day of Xīnwèi,
an edict exempted the disturbed and barren lands of Yúnnán from land taxes for ten years.
On the day of Jiǎxū,
Lǐ Zōngxī retired due to illness,
and Liú Kūnyī was appointed acting Governor-General of the Two Jiāng.
The Emperor's illness worsened dramatically;
he passed away in the Yǎngxīn Hall
at the age of nineteen.
Empress Dowager Cí'ān and Empress Dowager Cíxǐ summoned Dūn Qīnwáng Yìzōng, Gōng Qīnwáng Yìxīn, Chún Qīnwáng Yìkuàng,
Fú Jùnwáng Yìhuì, Huì Jùnwáng Yìxiáng,
Bèilè Zǎizhì, Zǎichéng,
Gōng Yìmó,
Grand Ministers of the Imperial Guard Bóyànnèmóhù, Yìkuàng, Jǐngshòu,
Grand Councillors Bǎo Yún, Shěn Guìfēn, Lǐ Hóngzǎo,
Ministers of the Imperial Household Department Yīngguì, Chónglún, Kuílíng, Rónglù, Míngshàn, Guìbǎo, Wénxī,
Academicians of the Hóngdé Hall Xú Tóng, Wēng Tónghé, Wáng Qìngqí,
and those of the Southern Study Huáng Yù, Pān Zǔyìn, Sūn Yíyīng, Xú Fǔ, Zhāng Jiāxiáng, to receive the imperial decree:
the son of Chún Qīnwáng was to succeed Wénzōng as the heir Emperor.
In the second month of the first year of Guāngxù, on the day of Wùzǐ,
Empress Ālǔtèshì passed away.
In the third month, on the day of Jǐhài,
the Emperor was posthumously granted the honorific title Jìtiān Kāiyùn Shòuzhōng Jūzhèng Bǎodà Dìnggōng Shèngzhì Chéngxiào Xìnmǐn Gōngkuān Yì Huángdì,
and the temple name Mùzōng.
In the third month of the fifth year, on the day of Gēngwǔ,
he was interred in Huìlíng.
Commentary: Mùzōng ascended the throne at a young age,
with the Empresses Dowager ruling from behind a curtain.
The nation experienced a resurgence;
within ten years,
bandits were suppressed,
and peace reigned both domestically and abroad.
If not for the harmony between the court and the imperial household,
and the cooperation between generals and ministers,
how could such a state have been achieved?
When the Emperor personally handled major political affairs,
he did not indulge in leisure.
He reformed himself in response to changes,
showing utmost diligence.
Upon hearing of disasters, he provided remissions and relief,
showing utmost benevolence.
He did not speak of auspicious omens,
showing utmost clarity.
Had he lived to an average age,
and continually renewed and glorified his reign,
how could he not have rivaled the glories of antiquity?
But alas, he suddenly abandoned his subjects,
his work unfinished.
What a pity!
Basic Annals Twenty-Three: Basic Annals of Dézōng One
Dézōng Tóngtiān Chóngyùn Dàzhōng Zhìzhèng Jīngwén Wěiwǔ Rénxiào Ruìzhì Duānjǐan Kuānqín Jǐng Huángdì,
personal name Zǎitián,
was Wénzōng's adopted son and Mùzōng's cousin.
His biological father was Chúnxián Qīnwáng Yìkuàng,
the seventh son of Xuānzōng.
His biological mother was of the Yèhènālā clan,
the younger sister of Empress Xiàoqīn.
In the sixth month of the tenth year of Tóngzhì,
he was born at the residence near Tàipíng Lake.
In the thirteenth year,
he received the stipend of an Fǔguó Gōng.
In the twelfth month, on the day of Guǐyǒu,
Mùzōng passed away,
without an heir.
Empress Dowager Cí'ān and Empress Dowager Cíxǐ summoned Dūn Qīnwáng Yìzōng, Gōng Qīnwáng Yìxīn, Chún Qīnwáng Yìkuàng,
Fú Jùnwáng Yìhuì, Huì Jùnwáng Yìxiáng,
Bèilè Zǎichéng,
Zhènguó Gōng Yìmó,
along with the Grand Ministers of the Imperial Guard, Grand Councillors, Ministers of the Imperial Household Department,
and officials from the Hóngdé Hall and Southern Study, to make a decision.
An imperial decree was issued
that the Emperor was to become the son of Wénzōng,
to inherit the great imperial line,
and be the heir Emperor.
When the heir Emperor had a son,
that son would then succeed the deceased Emperor.
On the day of Yǐhài,
the princes and ministers, with the imperial will, escorted the Emperor from his private residence,
to pay respects before the deceased Emperor's bier.
On the day of Bǐngzǐ,
the Emperor escorted Empress Dowager Cí'ān to reside in Zhōngcuì Palace,
and Empress Dowager Cíxǐ to reside in Chángchūn Palace.
Following the request of the princes and ministers,
the two Empresses Dowager ruled from behind a curtain.
The Empresses Dowager's instructions were called "Yìzhǐ,"
and the Emperor's were called "Yùzhǐ."
An edict halted the Sānhǎi construction project.
On the day of Yǐmǎo,
the tribute of local products from all provinces was suspended.
On the day of Réngwǔ,
the deceased Emperor's last will was promulgated.
An imperial decree stated
that Chún Qīnwáng Yìkuàng would inherit his princely title perpetually and without alteration.
Wáng Qìngqí, a lecturer in the Hanlin Academy, was found guilty
and stripped of his office.
Mourning rites were established:
plain white garments for one hundred days,
followed by plain clothes for twenty-seven months.
Bóyànnèmóhù and Jǐngshòu were both appointed to manage the Divine Machine Camp.
On the day of Guǐwèi,
an edict decreed that Dūn Qīnwáng, Gōng Qīnwáng, and Fú Jùnwáng should not sign their names on imperial decrees and memorials,
and were exempt from kowtowing during audiences, banquets, and bestowals.
On the day of Jiǎchén,
an edict declared the following year to be the first year of Guāngxù.
On the day of Dīnghài,
the deceased Emperor was posthumously granted the honorific title Jìtiān Kāiyùn Shòuzhōng Jūzhèng Bǎodà Dìnggōng Shèngzhì Chéngxiào Xìnmǐn Gōngkuān Yì Huángdì,
and the temple name Mùzōng.
On the day of Wùzǐ,
an imperial decree enfeoffed the Empress as Jiāshùn Empress,
and the Imperial Noble Consort as Dūnyí Imperial Noble Consort.
An edict instructed all civil and military officials,
regarding the appointment of personnel and administration,
to truthfully and directly state their views.
It ordered officials and commoners to abandon extravagance and uphold practicality.
It commanded all Governors-General and Governors to inquire into the hardships of the people,
carefully select magistrates,
examine and verify their subordinates,
and reform and clarify military preparations.
On the day of Rénchén,
the imperial will was promulgated to Cháoxiǎn.
On the day of Jiǎwǔ,
officials of the Imperial Household Department were forbidden from colluding with eunuchs.
On the day of Yǐwèi,
Ministers of the Imperial Household Department Guìbǎo and Wénxī were stripped of their offices.
On the day of Bǐngshēn,
Zǔo Zōngtáng was ordered to suppress the rebellious Huí in Hézhōu.
On the day of Dīngyǒu,
a combined sacrifice was held at the Tàimiào.
In this month,
salt field taxes for disaster-stricken areas in Zhèjiāng were remitted.
In the first year of Guāngxù, spring, first month, on the first day of Jǐhài,
new year's greetings were suspended.
