Yīngguì, Minister of the Board of Civil Office, and Shěn Guìfēn, Minister of the Board of War, were both appointed Associate Grand Secretaries.
On the day of Wùshēn,
a temple was granted for the Ming dynasty's former vassal Zhū Chénggōng in Táiwān,
and he was posthumously honored with the title Zhōngjié.
On the day of Gēngxū,
Shěn Bǎozhēn was ordered to survey and manage the construction of cities and towns in Lángyá,
and to plan matters for opening mountains and pacifying indigenous tribes.
On the day of Xīnhài,
prayers for harvest were offered to Shàngdì.
A relief factory was established in Qīngjiāng
to take in flood-stricken and starving people from Xú and Hǎi.
Guǎng'ān, an academician of the Grand Secretariat, memorialized to request a court discussion on issuing iron certificates for the succession of the deceased Emperor,
which was rejected.
On the day of Bǐngchén,
Vietnamese bandit groups encroached upon the Yúnnán border.
Governor Cén Yùyīng suppressed them.
On the day of Wùwǔ,
the Emperor ascended the Tàihé Hall,
and formally assumed the imperial throne,
issuing an edict of amnesty
and opening an special examination.
On the day of Xīnyǒu,
an edict was reiterated to Governors-General and Governors to promote the virtuous and punish the corrupt,
and to eliminate favoritism and opportunism.
In the second month, on the day of Dīngchǒu,
the Ministry of Punishments was ordered to clear accumulated cases.
On the day of Wùyín,
sacrifices were offered to the Great Earth God and Great Grain God,
with Yù Qīnwáng Běngé acting on behalf.
From then on, all major sacrifices were performed by proxies,
until the Winter Solstice sacrifice at the Yuánqiū Altar in the twelfth year, when the Emperor personally attended.
On the day of Réngwǔ,
the British translator Mǎ Jiālǐ was murdered in Yúnnán.
Liú Jǐntáng and others recaptured Hézhōu.
On the day of Jiǎshēn,
the indigenous people of Táiwān rebelled,
and Admiral Táng Dìngkuí suppressed them.
On the day of Bǐngxū,
the King of Ryūkyū was granted satin brocade, and his envoys were granted satin.
On the day of Wùzǐ,
Empress Jiāshùn passed away.
In the third month, on the *wùxū* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the grand posthumous title and temple name were bestowed upon the late Emperor.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the closure of the Jiǎzhuāng River project in Shāndōng was completed.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the Vietnamese bandit leaders Sūyà Dèng and others were executed.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Jǐng Lián was recalled to the capital,
and Zuǒ Zōngtáng was appointed Imperial Commissioner
to oversee military affairs in Xīnjiāng,
with Jīn Shùn as the Deputy Military Governor of Wūlǔmùqí.
In this month,
arrears of grain taxes for all provinces were generally remitted,
and outstanding taxes in Jiāngxī and Shānxī from before the sixth year of Tóngzhì were remitted.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day, the first day of the month,
sacrifices were offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Mùtúshàn was ordered to bring his cavalry unit to the capital,
to be attached to the Shénjī Battalion,
stationed in Nányuàn.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Táng Dìngkuí captured the aboriginal villages in the southern route of Táiwān.
On the *rénchén* day,
Shěn Bǎozhēn was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
concurrently Minister Superintendent of Trade,
and Supervisor of Nányáng coastal defense,
while Lǐ Hóngzhāng supervised Běiyáng coastal defense.
In the fifth month, on the *wùxū* day,
water conservancy projects were initiated in Zhílì
to protect the military-farmed rice paddies of Xiánshuǐgū.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the grand examination for the Hànlín and Zhānlùn Academies was held,
and Wú Bǎoshù, Qú Hóngjī, Niǔ Yùgēng, and Sūn Yíjīng were promoted to the first class,
with others promoted or demoted according to their performance.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the tribute of green jade hairpins and bracelets from Zhèjiāng was suspended,
and all items commissioned for manufacture by the various weaving bureaus were also suspended.
Liú Yuèzhāo supervised the attack on Vietnam,
recovering towns such as Tóngwén Tǔzhōu.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the Empress Xiàozhé Jiāshùn was posthumously honored with the title Xiàozhé Jiāshùn Shūshèn Xiánmíng Xiàntiān Zhāngshèng Yìhuánghòu.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the Imperial Storehouse of the Board of Works caught fire.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the record office of the Board of Punishments caught fire.
Lǐ Hànzhāng was ordered to Yúnnán to investigate the Mǎjiālǐ case,
and Xuē Huàn was subsequently sent to jointly examine it.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the summer solstice,
sacrifices were offered to the Earth at Fāngzé.
In the sixth month, on the *wùchén* day,
Yìróng, the General of Jílín, was dismissed from his post and banished.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
bandits in Fèngtiān occupied Dàdōnggōu and rebelled,
but Chóngshí pacified them.
The regular tribute from Gānsù was suspended.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the arrears of civilian and banner tenant rents and supplementary taxes in Zhílì from before the tenth year of Tóngzhì were remitted.
An Imperial decree ordered Prince Chún and the Imperial Bodyguards to recommend officials from various departments who were familiar with the discipline of the Green Standard and Brave battalions,
and Imperial Bodyguards who were capable of commanding troops.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
when the Imperial coffin of Emperor Mùzōng and his Empress was to be moved to the imperial mausoleum,
officials were preemptively warned not to prepare the imperial route
and soon after, excessive harassment was prohibited.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *wùxū* day,
outstanding taxes and grain levies in Zhílì from before the sixth year of Tóngzhì were remitted.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the Yǒngdìng River burst its banks.
An edict instructed all provinces to carefully review all judicial cases appealed to the capital.
Granary grain from Tàiyuán and other counties was loaned to relieve the people's food shortages.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Liú Diǎn was granted the third-rank京堂 (Jīngtáng) position,
to assist in military affairs in Shǎnxī and Gānsù.
Rice and grain *lijin* taxes in Húběi were remitted.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the treaty with Peru was concluded.
The Zǒngshǔ was instructed to jointly plan for the protection of Chinese laborers.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
on the Empress Dowager Cí'ān's birthday,
the banquet was canceled.
On the *rénxū* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng and Dīng Rìchāng were ordered to negotiate the Mǎjiālǐ case with British envoy Wēituǒmǎ (Wade).
Guō Sōngtāo, a probationary Vice Minister, and Xǔ Qínshēn, a probationary Dao official, were appointed ministers to Great Britain.
In the eighth month, on the *wùyín* day,
the fixed taxes of Shǎnxī affected by war were remitted.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the tribute items from Chánglú and Liǎnghuái salt administrations were exempted.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Dīng Rìchāng was ordered to oversee Fújiàn shipbuilding.
In the ninth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
Mùtúshàn was ordered to rectify official administration and banner camps in Jílín.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the treaty regarding foreigners traveling inland was re-stipulated.
Wú Táng supervised the suppression of bandits fleeing into Yǒng Hall.
On the *xīnhài* day,
five-tenths of the fixed taxes of Dàxīng and other prefectures and counties through which the Imperial coffin passed were remitted,
and seven-tenths for Zūnhuà.
Silver for seeds was awarded for destroyed wheat fields,
and remaining money and grain taxes as well as banner tenant rents were remitted.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the Imperial coffin was ceremonially placed at Lóngfú Temple.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor visited the various mausoleums.
He inspected the projects at Pǔxiángyù and Pútúoyù.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
he inspected the Huìlíng project.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the two Empress Dowagers were escorted back to the palace.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
they arrived from Lóngfú Temple.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Wáng Kǎitài was instructed to manage the indigenous people of Táiwān.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Liú Chángyòu defeated the Vietnamese bandits,
and the bandit chiefs Huáng Chóngyīng and Zhōu Jiànxīn were executed.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day, the first day of the month,
sacrifices were offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
on the Empress Dowager Cíxǐ's birthday,
the banquet was canceled.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Dīng Bǎozhēn's request was granted
to build炮臺 (pàotái) at Yāntái, Wēihǎi Wèi, and Dēngzhōufǔ,
and establish machinery bureaus.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the ban on Nántián Island in Zhèjiāng was lifted,
allowing people to cultivate it.
On the *gēngchén* day,
silver for cotton clothes was awarded to the poor people of the capital,
and this was to be done annually.
Bandits Lǐ Zēngyuán and others caused trouble in Yǒng,
but Commander Lǐ Yǒuhéng suppressed them.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
one month's worth of money and grain rations was awarded to the various camps of the Eight Banners,
to be made a regular annual practice.
Bandits caused trouble in Xīnhuà, Héng, and Yǒng in Húnán,
but General Xiè Jìnjūn and Commander Zhào Liánshēng suppressed them.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Jí Hé, a scattered-rank minister, and Wūlāxǐ Chóng'ā, an academician of the Grand Secretariat, were commissioned as envoys to Cháoxiǎn,
to enfeoff Lǐ Xī's son Tuò as Crown Prince.
In the eleventh month, on the *wùxū* day,
Cén Yùyīng captured Zhènxíong Dàzhài,
and the bandit leader Jū Zhànnéng was executed.
Liú Yuèzhāo was dismissed from his post for negligence.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Lángzhōng Chén Lánbīn was granted a probationary Jīngtáng position,
to serve as Minister to America, Japan, and Peru.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
bandits in Dàtōnggōu, Fèngtiān were pacified.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the winter solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at Yuánqiū.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the court felicitations were remitted.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the spirit tablets of Emperor Mùzōng and his Empress were enshrined in Fèngxiān Hall.
In the twelfth month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
the divine tablet was ceremonially placed in Shòuhuáng Hall.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the fixed taxes for the pastoral lands in Shèngjīng were abolished.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
an Imperial decree stated:
"For the Emperor's studies,
Wēng Tónghé, an academician of the Grand Secretariat, and Xià Tóngshàn, a Vice Minister, are to instruct him in Yùqìng Palace.
The Imperial Bodyguards are to teach him Manchu and Mongolian languages and scripts, and equestrian archery."
Grand Secretary Wénxiáng requested to be relieved of his duties,
but he was persuaded to stay.
On the *wùyín* day,
new and old taxes for disaster-stricken Zhèjiāng were remitted.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
prayers for snow were offered at altars and temples.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the grand joint sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn, Liúqiú, and Miǎndiàn paid tribute.
In the second year, the *bǐngzǐ* year, in spring, the first month, on the *guǐsì* day, the first day of the month,
the court felicitations were remitted.
On the *wùxū* day,
an edict instructed all provinces to widely preach the Sacred Edict and Maxims.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the課糧 (kèliáng) for uncultivated salt pans in Rénhé and other salt fields was remitted.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Qíán bandits captured Xiàjiāng,
but it was soon recovered.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
prayers for rain were offered.
From then on, prayers for rain were frequent.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the barbarian bandits in Sìchuān were pacified.
On the *yǐchǒu* day of the second month,
an edict was issued that starting from the first month of summer this year,
before the Emperor personally assumed power,
he would personally attend the seasonal sacrifices at the Tàimiào and the great sacrifices (such as the *xiáp* sacrifice)
on the day before to perform the rites.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the quota taxes for salt furnaces in Hǎishā, Lúlì, and other fields were remitted.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the bandit leaders Luó Hóngchāng and Xiàng Hé from Dèngchuān were executed.
Arrears of land tax in Zhèjiāng were remitted.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Cén Rùnqīng, the sub-prefect of Yángwàntǔ Zhōuzhōu, rebelled,
and Yán Shùsēn suppressed him.
On the *rénchén* day,
bandits in Dōngxiāng gathered a crowd to resist officials.
On the *bǐngshēn* day of the third month,
due to drought,
an edict was issued to review all criminal cases.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Wú Zànchéng was granted the third-grade京táng rank
to oversee the Fújiàn shipyards.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the dismissed Dū Sī Chén Guóruì was exiled to Hēilóngjiāng.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
arrears of land tax in sixty-six prefectures and counties of Shǎnxī were remitted.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
an edict was issued that in celebration of Empress Dowager Cí'ān’s fortieth birthday,
this year's autumn executions were to be suspended.
The bandit strongholds in Sìjiǎoniú and the six caves in Guìzhōu were pacified.
On the *wùshēn* day,
as rain was overdue,
an imperial rescript was issued for all internal and external officials to speak frankly about shortcomings.
On the *yǐhài* day of the fourth month in summer,
the tribute of local products from Shǎnxī was suspended,
and arrears of land tax in Huái, Yáng, and other prefectures from before the sixth year of Tóngzhì were remitted.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Emperor began to study in the Yùqìnggōng.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Cáo Hóngxūn and 324 others were granted the *jìnshì jí dì chūshēn* in varying ranks.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Sūrèdárèbìgá'ěrmǎsāhā presented a memorial of mourning,
and an imperial edict was issued in reply,
along with gifts of silk fabric.
On the *yǐwèi* day of the fifth month,
Wénxiáng passed away.
On the *yǐsì* day,
due to severe drought in the capital region,
and the hardship faced by common people in Zhílì, Shāndōng, and the prefectures of Hénán and Héběi,
a rescript was issued for officials to provide relief and comfort,
and to catch locusts and their nymphs.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Censor Pān Dūnyǎn requested a change to the posthumous title of Empress Xiàozhé.
He was severely reprimanded
and soon after dismissed from office.
On the *xīnyǒu* new moon of the intercalary fifth month,
relief was provided for the drought in the capital region.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
relief was provided for the floods in Fújiàn.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
an edict was issued for self-reflection and cultivation due to the drought.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the great stele tower at Xiàolíng suffered a disaster.
There had been no rain since the first month of spring,
until this day when it rained.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Zhāi bandits in Jiēzhōu were pacified.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
a rescript was issued to Liú Kūnyī to defend the coast and train troops,
and to urgently plan for reorganization.
On the *gēngyín* new moon of the sixth month,
a rescript was issued to Wénkūn and others to severely punish those who propagated evil cults.
On the *rénchén* day,
the trained troops in Téngyuè occupied the city and rebelled,
and also captured Shùnníng and Yúnzhōu.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was appointed Plenipotentiary Minister
to Yāntái to negotiate the settlement of the Mǎ Jiālǐ (Margary) case with the British envoy, Wēituǒmǎ (Thomas Wade).
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
there was a locust plague in Ānhuī.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the practice of donating for official positions was opened in Yúnnán.
On the *xīnhài* day,
due to bandit disturbances in Jiāng, Wǎn, Lǔ, and Yù,
a rescript was issued to Shěn Bǎozhēn and others to deploy troops to search and suppress them,
and to disband those coerced into joining.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Commander Kǒng Cái attacked Mànásī,
and beheaded the bandit leader Mǎ Démíng and others.
This month,
relief was provided for floods in Nánfēng, Nánchāng, and Fújiàn.
This summer,
arrears of land tax in Huái, Yáng, and other prefectures were remitted,
as were arrears of land tax in Shèngjīng from before the sixth year of Tóngzhì,
furnace taxes in various fields of Chánglú from before the tenth year of Tóngzhì,
and arrears of land tax in Zhílì from the tenth year of Tóngzhì onwards.
On the *xīnyǒu* day of the seventh month in autumn,
honorary titles were conferred upon the two Empresses Dowager.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the sales territory for Huái salt in Chǔ was restored.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the bandit leader Yuán Tíngjiāo from Dōngxiāng was executed.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Liú Chángyòu and Pān Dǐngxīn recaptured the cities in Téngyuè,
and the bandit leader Sū Kāixiān was executed.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the Mǎ Jiālǐ case was settled,
and the officials involved were exempted from punishment.
On the *xīnmǎo* day of the eighth month,
Liú Jǐntáng and Jīn Shùn defeated the Húi chieftain Bái Yànhǔ,
and recaptured Wūlǔmùqí and Díhuà City,
and soon after recaptured Chāngjí, Hūtúbì, and Jǐnghuà cities.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Xǔ Qínshēn was appointed Minister to Japan.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
relief was provided for floods in Zhèjiāng.
On the *xīnhài* day,
relief was provided for floods in Jiāngxī.
Kǒng Cái and others recaptured the North City of Mànásī.
On the *wùwǔ* new moon of the ninth month,
the two counties of Shàngyuán and Jiāngníng were granted commemorative arches and pensions for 35 families and 195 people who perished as one family.
On the *rénxū* day,
additional gruel kitchens were established in Shùntiān.
On the *jǐsì* day,
regulations for envoys to various countries were established.
Due to disputes between civilians and missionaries in the prefectures and counties of Sìchuān,
a rescript was issued to Kuíyù and others to adjudicate fairly.
On the *rénshēn* day,
a rescript was issued to Wényù and others to strictly apprehend secret society bandits in Fújiàn, Jiāngxī, Ānhuī, and other provinces.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day of the tenth month in winter,
relief was provided for the drought in northern Ānhuī.
Jǐnglián and Lǐ Hóngzǎo were ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Róngquán was summoned to the capital,
and Jīn Shùn was appointed General of Yīlí.
On the *dīngsì* day,
relief was provided for famine in Kǒuběi, Shāndōng, Ānhuī, and Jiāngběi.
On the *dīngmǎo* day of the eleventh month,
Jīn Shùn and Xīlún captured the South City of Mànásī,
and the bandit leaders Hé Lù and Mǎ Yǒucái were executed.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
as the northern route of Xīnjiāng was pacified,
funds were allocated to dismiss Jīn Shùn's troops.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
ten thousand *shí* of grain tax were withheld,
and granary grain was allocated to aid disaster victims in Sū and Cháng.
On the *wùzǐ* day of the twelfth month,
Lecturer Hé Rúzhāng was appointed Minister to Japan.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Governors-General and Governors were ordered to strictly inspect prefectures and counties,
not to conceal disasters,
and to adjudicate civil and missionary cases in all provinces fairly.
On the *wùshēn* day,
relief was provided for the Huái and Hǎi disasters in Jiāngběi.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Húi bandits raided Kēbùduō,
and Counselor Bǎo Yīng was severely reprimanded for his slow deployment of troops.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
furnace taxes on undeveloped land in Háng, Jiā, Sōng, and other areas were remitted.
On the *dīngsì* new moon of the first month in spring of the third year (*dīngchǒu*),
court congratulations were suspended.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Jǐnglián, Left Censor-in-Chief, was appointed Grand Secretary of the Grand Council.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the Jìlóng Hútúkètú of Former Tsang was ordered to manage commercial and upper affairs until the reincarnation of the Dálài Lǎma appeared,
and was granted
the title
“Dáshàn”.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Yīngguì was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tǐrén Gé,
and Zàilíng, as Minister of the Board of Civil Office, served as Assistant Grand Secretary.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
arrears of rent for the sandbanks of Hóngzéhú were remitted.
On the *wùzǐ* day of the second month,
the Yí bandits of Mùpíng were executed.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
a rescript was reissued to all provinces to reclaim wasteland,
prohibit armed brawls,
carefully select and impeach,
and rectify military regulations.
Relief was provided for famine-stricken returning migrants in Zhílì, Shāndōng, Shānxī, Hénán, Ānhuī, Jiāngxī, and Fújiàn.
On the *sìhài* day,
arrears of land tax in Húběi were remitted.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
an imperial decree stated:
“As the imperial coffin is in repose,
and the Emperor is young,
apart from the grand ceremony of court congratulations,
the ceremonies for awarding merits, celebrations, and entertaining foreign guests shall be temporarily postponed.”
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the sales territory for Huái salt was restored.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Ministry of Punishments overturned the unjust case of Gě Pǐnlián, a commoner from Zhèjiāng;
Governor Yáng Chāngjùn and Vice Minister Hú Ruìlán were dismissed from office,
and officials from the Zhīfǔ down were punished according to their varying degrees of guilt.
A rescript was reissued to all provinces regarding the administration of justice,
emphasizing that the facts must be true and the punishment appropriate,
without recklessness.
In the third month, on the *dīngsì* day, which was the first day of the month,
the Emperor shed his mourning attire.
As the imperial tombs (lit. mountains and mausoleums) were not yet settled,
court banquets and theatrical performances were still forbidden within the palace.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the grain tax was remitted for three years for those in Huáyīn affected by flooding.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Liú Xīhóng was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to Germany.
Relief was provided for flood victims in Shùyáng.
On the *xīnsì* day,
miscellaneous levies in Táiwān Fǔ were abolished,
and relief was given to starving indigenous people in the interior mountains.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
the seasonal *yú* sacrifice was held,
sacrificing to Heaven at the Yuánqiū.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Luǒyí of Mǎbiān, allied with the Yěfān and Hēiyí, launched raids,
and Kuíyù and others suppressed them.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
arrears of tax were remitted for Élíng Xiàn due to flooding.
On the *wùxū* day,
Liú Jǐntáng and others captured Qīkēténmù and Pìzhǎn,
recovering the Manchu and Han cities of Tǔlǔfān.
Soon after, they attacked and captured Dábǎn and the rebel strongholds of Tuōkèsùn,
and the Andijan chieftain Pàxià committed suicide.
On the *jǐhài* day,
General Zhāng Qíguāng attacked the Shuàimángfān settlement in Táiwān,
and captured it.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
silver for seeds was lent to banner households in Yìzhōu.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
relief was provided for earthquake victims in Guìyáng.
On the *rénchén* day,
bandits caused unrest in Zhāotōng and Guǎngnán,
and government troops suppressed them.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
regarding the fraudulent practices of officials and scribes in connection with delayed tax collection in disaster areas,
an edict was issued for all provinces to rectify the situation.
Wéi Bìxié, an advanced student from Gāoyóu who lived contentedly in poverty, was commended.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Viet Nam sent envoys to present local products,
and their king was presented with silk fabrics.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Wáng Rénkān and three hundred and twenty-nine others were granted the *jìnshì jí dì* or equivalent degrees according to their ranks.
This month,
Jiangsu and Anhui suffered from locusts.
In the fifth month, on the *wùchén* day,
Japan obstructed the tribute mission from Liúqiú,
and sent the incoming envoys back to their country.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Shānxī suffered from drought,
and two hundred thousand *liáng* (taels) from the capital's treasury were allocated for relief.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the sect leader Wáng Huáizhāng and others rebelled in Jiānlì,
and were executed.
One million two hundred thousand taels of silver were allocated from the imperial treasury and sent to the Western Expedition's grain office.
On the *wùyín* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Fúzhōu.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
an imperial decree stated that as the Emperor's birthday fell during a period of fasting and abstinence,
the celebratory rites would be rescheduled for the twenty-sixth day of the sixth month,
and this was to be established as a regulation.
Shānxī experienced a severe drought,
and Governor Zēng Guóquán requested the bestowal of a plaque as a form of prayer.
As this was not a customary practice,
it was not permitted.
The edict stated:
"Prayer lies in sincerity.
You must diligently strive for good governance,
and clear up legal cases,
to invite peace and sweet rain."
In the sixth month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
an imperial edict declared that Luóbùzàng Tǎbùkèjiǎmùcuò, the son of Gōnggárénqīng, was to be recognized as the *Hūbìlèhǎn* (reincarnation) of the Dálài Lǎma,
without the need for drawing lots from the golden urn.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Běijiāng embankment in Guǎngdōng broke,
and Liánzhōu suffered a great flood.
An edict was issued to provide relief and comfort to the victims.
On the *wùxū* day,
previously, regarding the seating order for Mùzōng's temple tablet in the ancestral temple,
an imperial decree had instructed ministers to convene a discussion.
Prince Chún again requested a long-term plan to be established.
Junior Compiler Wénzhì,
Court of Imperial Entertainments Minister Xú Shùmíng, Junior Minister Wénshuò,
Grand Secretariat Reader-Scholar Zhōng Pèixián, and Chancellor of the Directorate of Education Bǎo Tíng had all submitted memorials.
At this point,
the princes and ministers were again ordered to deliberate in detail and report,
and Lǐ Hóngzhāng was also instructed to provide a suitable proposal.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
as disasters were repeatedly observed,
ministers were admonished to cultivate and introspect.
On the *gēngxū* day,
it was the Emperor's birthday,
and he received felicitations at the Qiánqīng Gōng.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the *dīngsì* day,
sea defense funds were allocated to assist Shānxī with relief.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Prince Dūn and others discussed the seating order for the spirit tablets of Emperor Mùzōng and his empresses,
requesting that in the central hall of the Tàimiào, four bays on the east and west sides,
following the example of the newly added shrine seats in the rear hall of the Fèngxiān Diàn at the beginning of the Dàoguāng reign,
be repaired and redecorated.
They also adopted Prince Chún's request
that from now on,
the precedent of never being removed from the temple after a hundred generations should not be invoked.
On the *wùchén* day,
three-tenths of the allocated taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken counties such as Jiāngníng and Shàngyuán.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the silver from the capital's grain transport tax commutation was used for relief in Hénán during the famine.
In the eighth month, on the *dīnghài* day,
an edict was issued for all provinces to repair agricultural water conservancy projects.
On the *rénchén* day,
one hundred thousand taels from Tiānjīn's training funds were allocated to assist Shānxī with relief.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Táiwān was exempted from the grain tribute of the tenth year of Tóngzhì and the commutation of glutinous rice for other grains.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
an edict instructed Liú Kūnyī and others to rectify the police administration in Guǎngdōng.
On the *wùshēn* day,
four hundred thousand taels of silver were allocated for disaster relief in Shānxī and Hénán,
and forty thousand *dàn* each of Jiāng'ān grain transport rice were retained and sent to Shānxī and Hénán for relief.
In the ninth month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
Chén Zǐ'áo, the bandit leader from Luótián, was executed.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
former Vice-Minister Yán Jìngmíng was ordered to go to Shānxī to investigate relief efforts.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the prohibition on poppy cultivation in Shānxī was reiterated,
and it was changed to planting mulberries and cotton.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
eighty thousand *dàn* of Shāndōng's winter grain transport were allocated to continue relief for disasters in Shānxī and Hénán.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Liú Dé, the King Xiàn of Héjiān and a Han Confucian scholar, was granted the honor of being enshrined in the Confucian Temple.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
an imperial edict sought frank advice.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Lǐ Hènián was ordered to go to Hénán to investigate relief efforts.
On the *wùchén* day,
the amount of military provisions to be contributed by Shānxī and Hénán for the Western Expedition was reduced and delayed.
On the *gēngchén* day,
additional rations were distributed to disaster victims in Xiángfú and other counties.
On the *xīnsì* day,
relief was provided for typhoon victims in Xīnghuà Fǔ.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *rénchén* day,
relief was provided for hail damage in Sānxìng.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
an edict instructed all provinces to comfort and settle migrating famine victims.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
silver and grain taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken Sānxìng.
Additional rations were distributed to disaster victims in Yángqǔ and other counties.
On the *yǐsì* day,
additional porridge kitchens were established inside the city walls.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Liú Jǐntáng advanced and recovered the cities of Kèlāsābā'ěr and Kùchē,
and soon after recovered Aksù and Wūshén cities.
In the eleventh month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
an edict admonished all ministries and departments against idleness and procrastination.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
a new canal was opened for grain transport in Shāndōng.
On the *dīngsì* day,
an edict instructed Governors-General, Governors, and Prefects to diligently improve administration.
In the twelfth month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
the fur tribute from the Hèzhé was delayed.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
tax exemption for the next year's grain was granted in advance to disaster-stricken prefectures and counties in Shānxī and Hénán.
This winter,
repeated prayers for snow were offered.
A total of one hundred and twenty thousand *dàn* of the following year's grain transport rice from Jiāngnán and Húběi were allocated for relief in Shānxī,
and imperial funds were issued for relief in Shǎnxī.
This year,
Shānxī and Shǎnxī suffered a severe drought,
and people resorted to cannibalism.
In the fourth year, in the *wùyín* spring, in the first month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
relief was provided for the famine in Hénán.
Guō Sōngtāo was ordered to concurrently serve as Minister Plenipotentiary to France.
The Western Army recovered Yè'ěrqiāng and Kāshígá'ěr,
and the Hui people of Hétián surrendered.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
an edict instructed all provinces to clear up lawsuits.
On the *xīnsì* day of the second month, the new moon,
repairs were made to the Dūjiāngyàn in Chéngdū.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
an edict was issued to promote water conservancy in the north.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Wáng Wénsháo (王文韶), acting Junior Vice Minister of War, was appointed Grand Councilor.
On the *gēngyín* day,
an edict was issued to commend local officials who effectively implemented famine relief policies.
On the *rénchén* day,
Xīnjiāng was pacified;
the bandit leader Bái Yànhǔ (白彥虎) fled into Russia.
For their merits,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng (左宗棠) was advanced to second-class marquis,
Liú Jǐntáng (劉錦棠) to second-class baron,
and Admiral Yú Hǔ'ēn (余虎恩) and others were granted hereditary titles of varying ranks.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
an edict was issued to clear ordinary prisons.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
famine relief was provided in Hūlán (呼蘭).
On the *jǐhài* day,
an imperial edict was issued, blaming himself for the misfortunes.
Famine relief was provided in Shānxī and Hénán.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
remains of disaster victims were buried.
On the *gēngxū* day,
land tax and corvée labor were remitted in Hóuguān (侯官) due to flooding.
On the *jiǎyín* day of the third month,
an edict was issued for disaster-stricken provinces to try the *qūtiánfǎ* (區田法) (ridge-and-furrow farming method).
On the *rénshēn* day,
famine relief was provided in Zhílì;
three thousand horses from the Cháhā'ěr (察哈爾) herds were distributed to the poor for plowing.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the Imperial Household Department was ordered
to reduce expenditures
and eliminate fraudulent claims.
On the *wùyín* day,
Yīngguì (英桂) retired.
This month,
it rained in Hénán.
On the *rénwǔ* day of the fourth month,
Shěn Bǎozhēn (沈葆楨) requested the abolition of the military examinations,
which was rejected.
On the *rénchén* day,
typhoon relief was provided in Guǎngdōng.
On the *gēngxū* day of the fifth month, the new moon,
an edict was issued for all provinces to widely plant mulberries and tea.
Zǎilíng (載齡) was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tǐrén Gé (體仁閣),
managing the Board of Works;
Quánqìng (全慶), as Minister of Justice, assisted as Grand Secretary.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Chónghòu (崇厚) was appointed minister plenipotentiary to Russia.
On the *bǐngxū* day of the sixth month,
arrears of tribute were remitted in Shǎnxī.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the prohibition against private coining was strictly enforced.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
typhoon relief was provided in Táiwān.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the Board of Punishments was ordered to severely punish county officials who embezzled relief funds.
In the autumn, on the *yǐmǎo* day of the seventh month,
imperial troops in Yúnnán recaptured Gěngmǎ Tǔchéng (耿馬土城).
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Wáng Wénsháo (王文韶), Junior Vice Minister of Rites, and Zhōu Jiāmēi (周家楣), Governor of Shùntiān Fǔ, were ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén (總理各國事務衙門) (Office of Foreign Affairs).
On the *rénshēn* day,
punishments for delayed and neglected murder cases were strictly enforced.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Zēng Jìzé (曾紀澤) was appointed minister plenipotentiary to Britain and France.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the autumn tax for the current year was remitted in Píngyáng, Pú, Jiě, and Jiàng.
This month,
famine relief was provided in the prefectures of Jīn, Qú, Yán, etc.,
and in counties like Fúliáng, etc., due to floods.
On the *jǐmǎo* day of the eighth month,
the Yǒngdìng Hé (永定河) breached its banks.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Qìn Hé (沁河) breached its banks.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
flood relief was provided in Chóng'ān (崇安) and Pǔchéng (浦城).
On the *dīngsì* day of the ninth month,
an edict was issued to officials in the southeast frontier to prepare for floods,
to clear and organize the *bǎojiǎ* (保甲) system,
and to prevent secret societies from inciting disaster victims.
On the *guǐhài* day,
drought relief was provided in Shānxī;
arrears of tribute were remitted in Yángqǔ (陽曲) and other counties,
as well as the autumn grain tax in Xúgōu (徐溝) and other counties.
On the *wùchén* day,
flood relief was provided in Lántián (藍田).
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the Fánkǒu (樊口) river embankment was repaired.
In winter, on the *rénwǔ* day of the tenth month,
Lǐ Yángcái (李揚才), a former Brigade General residing in Guǎngxī, rebelled;
Féng Zǐcái (馮子材) was ordered to suppress him.
Arrears of tribute and various miscellaneous taxes were remitted in Tōng, Hǎi,
and the four garrisons of Huái'ān (淮安).
On the *dīnghài* day,
flood relief was provided in Pú, Fàn, and Shòuyáng (壽陽).
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Qìn Hé (沁河) breached its banks again.
Flood relief was provided in Fèngtiān.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Běixīncāng (北新倉) caught fire.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Jiālǐwǎn (加禮宛) and other communities in Hòushān (後山), Táiwān, submitted,
capturing and presenting the aboriginal chiefs,
who were then executed.
Old and new fixed taxes were remitted in Guìzhōu due to military events.
On the *bǐngchén* day of the eleventh month,
the dikes of the Běiyùn Hé (北運河) were repaired.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Bái Yànhǔ (白彥虎) raided the border;
Liú Jǐntáng (劉錦棠) defeated him.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Lǐ Yángcái (李揚才) occupied Chángqìng (長慶) in Vietnam;
Yáng Chóngyǎ (楊重雅) suppressed him.
On the *jǐsì* day,
an imperial edict instructed governors-general and governors to discipline themselves and their subordinates.
Grand Councilors were admonished not to avoid suspicions or resentment,
and ministers of the Six Boards and Censorate were strongly urged to abandon procrastination.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
at the Winter Solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Yuánqiū (圜丘) Altar.
On the *yǐhài* day,
court congratulations were suspended.
On the *jǐchǒu* day of the twelfth month,
an imperial edict permanently abolished the practice of solicited donations.
This year,
arrears of taxes were remitted twice for the Rénhé (仁和) salt fields.
Cháoxiǎn (朝鮮) and Guō'ěrkā (廓爾喀) paid tribute.
In the spring of the fifth year, *jǐmǎo*, on the *yǐsì* day of the first month, the new moon,
banquets were suspended.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
a renewed edict suspended the practice of fundraising donations for military provisions.
The Gāochún (高淳) dike was repaired.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
famine relief was provided in Shānxī.
On the *rénwǔ* day of the second month,
Duàn Dǐngyào (段鼎耀), Prefect of Jízhōu (吉州), was executed for embezzling relief funds.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
an imperial edict restored river transport.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Shānxī was ordered to clear barren land,
register households and population,
and equalize corvée labor.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the imperial coffin was interred in the imperial mausoleum;
local officials were forbidden from imposing levies or disturbing the people.
Flood relief was provided in Wén'ān (文安) and other prefectures and counties.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day of the third month,
the bandit leader Zhōng Wànxīn (鍾萬新) joined Lǐ Yángcái (李揚才) in attacking Xuānguāng (宣光);
Féng Zǐcái (馮子材) joined forces in Vietnam to attack them.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the fixed taxes of Dàxīng, Tōng, Sānhé, Jì, and Zūnhuà (遵化), through which the imperial coffin passed, were remitted.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
a decree was issued to the Jílóng Hútúkètú (吉嚨呼圖克圖) (Jilung Khutuktu),
along with presentation of *hádá* (哈達) (ceremonial scarves) and python brocade.
The Bùlǔtè (布魯特) Hui chieftain, with the Ānjíyán (安集延) bandit chieftain, raided the border;
Liú Jǐntáng (劉錦棠) defeated them.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Two Empresses Dowager visited the Eastern Mausoleums.
On the *jǐsì* day,
they visited Zhāoxī (昭西) and Xiàodōng (孝東) mausoleums.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Mùzōng (穆宗) was interred in Huìlíng (惠陵),
with Empress Xiàozhé (孝哲) interred alongside him.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
they returned from the Eastern Mausoleums.
On the *yǐhài* day of the intercalary third month,
Mùzōng's (穆宗) spirit tablet was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple,
and an imperial edict was issued to the realm.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Lǐ Yángcái (李揚才) occupied Zhěyán (者巖).
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the river dikes of Xiāngyáng, Miǎnyáng, and Tiānmén (天門) were repaired.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Wú Kědú (吳可讀), a Secretary in the Board of Civil Office, committed suicide by taking poison at the Eastern Mausoleums,
leaving behind a memorial requesting the pre-establishment of the imperial succession.
An imperial decree ordered
the princes and grand councilors to convene and report their discussion.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Lǐ Fèngbāo (李鳳苞), holding the rank of Third-Grade Minister, was appointed minister plenipotentiary to Germany.
In summer, on the *wùshēn* day of the fourth month,
the Běiyùn Hé (北運河) in Tōngzhōu (通州) was repaired.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Wú Kědú (吳可讀) was granted posthumous honors.
An imperial decree ordered
that Kědú's (可讀) original memorial and the discussion memorials,
as well as the memorials of Xú Tóng (徐桐), Bǎo Tíng (寶廷), Zhāng Zhīdòng (張之洞) and others,
and all previous and subsequent edicts, be recorded and stored in Yùqìng Gōng (毓慶宮).
The grain tribute tax and arrears of taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken prefectures and counties in Hénán.
On the *jǐsì* day,
previously, Zhū Yǒngkāng (朱永康), Prefect of Yìxiàn (嶧縣), was sentenced to exile for the premeditated murder of Commissioner Gāo Wénbǎo (高文保),
and the case was later submitted for court deliberation.
Now,
the memorial was presented,
and an imperial edict stated that his crime exceeded the penalty,
and the sentence was changed to death.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day of the fifth month,
it was the summer solstice.
Sacrifices were made to the Earth at Fāngzé.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
arrears of taxes were remitted for various salt fields in Liǎnghuái, Tàizhōu, and Hǎizhōu.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Henan suffered from locusts.
On the *jǐhài* day,
government troops suppressed the bandits of Zhěyán.
That month,
relief was provided for wind disasters in Qīnghé and Āndōng.
Shanxi had rain.
Jiēzhōu, Wénzhōu, and Xīhé experienced earthquakes for thirteen days.
On the *rénzǐ* day of the sixth month,
the Ministry of Punishments reported on the Dōngxiāng prison case,
involving false accusations of rebellion and arbitrary killings.
The disgraced magistrate Sūn Dìngyáng and governor Lǐ Yǒuhéng were sentenced to death.
Soon after, Wén Gé and Dīng Bǎozhēn were both implicated and stripped of their posts.
An order was issued to allocate two hundred thousand taels from the treasury
and three hundred thousand taels of *dīnglí* silver
to meet the relief needs of Shanxi.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
an edict was issued to officials who offered advice, stating that
matters submitted to the ministry for discussion and memorialization
must not be presented presumptuously,
nor should they be redundant or merely echo others,
leading to a flood of petitions.
Accumulated grain owed by the common people in Shanxi over many years was entirely remitted.
The Wūlātè, Ālāshàn, and other banners suffered from locusts.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an imperial decree granted Chún Qīnwáng Yìxuǎn permission to reside at home to recuperate from illness
and relieved him of his duties.
Relief was provided for earthquake disasters in Bīnzhōu, Qiánzhōu, Hànzhōng, and Fèngxiáng.
On the *gēngchén* day of the seventh month,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Zhílì.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
due to unusual celestial phenomena and earthquakes, frank advice was sought.
An edict was issued regarding grain reserves in all provinces.
Summer taxes and salt taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken areas in Jiàngzhōu, Púzhōu, and Yángchéng.
On the *gēngyín* day,
sea transport was restored.
On the *wùshēn* day of the eighth month,
sacrifices were made to Dàshè and Dàjì.
An imperial decree ordered all provinces to recommend civil and military officials fit for appointment.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the retired Grand Secretary Shàn Màojiān passed away.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Bóshān and other prefectures and counties.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
various areas in Jiangsu and Anhui suffered from locusts.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
relief was provided for earthquake and flood disasters in Jiēzhōu, Wénzhōu, and Xīhé.
On the *jiǎxū* day of the ninth month,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Zhílì.
On the *rénchén* day,
additional posthumous honorific titles were conferred upon Wénzōng and Mùzōng.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Chóngqìng and other prefectures and counties experienced earthquakes,
and relief was provided.
On the *xīnchǒu* day, the first day of the tenth month in winter,
taxes were remitted for Quwò and other prefectures and counties due to poor harvests.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
land taxes for banner people and commoners in Fèngtiān were remitted to offset relief grain provisions.
On the *dīngsì* day,
an edict was issued for the navy to also practice land warfare.
On the *guǐhài* day,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Xiùshān and other places.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Yīngguì passed away.
Grain taxes for Qíqíhā'ěr, Hēilóngjiāng, and Mò'ěrgēn were remitted,
along with previously borrowed seed grain.
On the *yǐhài* day of the eleventh month,
Lǐ Yángcái was executed.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
it was the winter solstice,
and sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Yuánqiū.
On the *gēngchén* day,
court felicitations were suspended.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Shěn Bǎozhēn passed away.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Liú Kūnyī was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
concurrently serving as Minister for the Southern Ocean.
On the *gēngyín* day,
an imperial decree denounced Chónghòu for concluding the treaty of Yīlí with the Russians
and for returning to the capital without authorization.
The proposed treaty
was to be discussed by court officials.
On the *rénchén* day,
deed taxes were remitted for severely disaster-stricken prefectures and counties in Shanxi.
On the *jǐyǒu* day of the twelfth month,
an imperial decree stated that
the court's discussion on the Russian treaty and subsequent memorial
should be sent to the princes and grand ministers for further deliberation,
with Chún Qīnwáng also participating in the discussion and reporting the findings.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Chónghòu was stripped of his position
and imprisoned.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
an edict was issued to repair community granaries
and promote community schools.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
autumn grain taxes were remitted for Yǒngjì and other prefectures and counties.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
a comprehensive sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
An imperial decree ordered Assistant Secretary Zhāng Zhīdòng to consult on the Russian treaty.
On the *wùchén* day,
the Shandong canal was repaired.
That year,
Joseon and Gurkha paid tribute.
On the *jǐsì* day, the first day of the first month in spring of the sixth year, *gēngchén*,
banquets were suspended.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Zēng Jìzé was appointed Minister to Russia
to renegotiate the treaty.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
an edict ordered an investigation into phantom enlistments and fraudulent employment in the military.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the Miao rebels in Xīlín were pacified.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
former Minister of Public Works Lǐ Hóngzǎo was reinstated as Grand Secretary of the Military Council.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Súndiàn suffered from banditry,
and government troops suppressed them.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
an imperial decree ordered officials both inside and outside the capital to recommend talented individuals,
and border officials to strengthen border and coastal defenses.
Wú Dàchéng, Circuit Intendant of Héběi, was ordered to assist in military affairs in Jílín,
and Liú Jǐntáng, Transmission Commissioner, to assist in military affairs in Xīnjiāng.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Chónghòu's crime was determined,
and he was sentenced to decapitation.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Ministry of Revenue presented ten proposals for raising provisions,
and an imperial decree ordered their implementation in all provinces.
That month,
the *dīngyín* tax on barren land in all areas of Shanxi was abolished,
and summer taxes on barren swamps in Rénhé and other salt fields were remitted.
On the *yǐsì* day of the second month,
the tribute of melons from Yúcì was permanently abolished.
On the *rénxū* day,
Xiāo Zhàoyuán, Commander-in-Chief of Gansu, was sentenced to decapitation
for embezzling military provisions.
On the *jiǎxū* day of the third month,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Shùnzhílì.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng was dispatched to Hāmì,
Jīn Shùn guarded Jīnghé,
and Zhāng Yào and Liú Jǐntáng advanced separately towards Yīlí.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
barren land taxes for Hóngdòng and Xīnzhōu in Shanxi were remitted for three or four years.
On the *gēngzǐ* day of the fourth month,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Yuánqiū.
Eight *kǎlún* (guard posts) officials and soldiers were re-established at Kēbùduō Chāngjí Sītái, Huòní Màilāhù, and other places.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
a factory was established in Sānxìng to build steamboats.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Tibetan bandits Hālì and others in Jiēzhōu rebelled,
and were executed.
On the *rénxū* day,
Huáng Sīyǒng and three hundred thirty-three others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with varying ranks.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Lǐ Chánglè was transferred as Provincial Commander of Zhílì,
commanding four battalions of the Wǔyì Army,
and Bāo Chāo was appointed Provincial Commander of Húnán
and summoned to the capital.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day of the fifth month,
relief was provided for hail disasters in Luòyáng and other counties.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Tibetan bandits Gǔdànbā and others in Jiēzhōu were executed.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
in response to the Russian request,
Chónghòu was spared death,
but remained imprisoned.
On the *dīngyǒu* day, the first day of the sixth month,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Fujian.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was granted plenipotentiary powers
to negotiate a treaty with Brazil.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
excessive levies and forced discounts in grain collection were prohibited.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Guǎngzhōu and other places.
On the *dīngsì* day,
uncollected taxes on barren land in Jiāochéng and other counties were remitted.
Zēng Guóquán was ordered to supervise defense affairs at Shānhǎiguān.
On the *rénshēn* day of the seventh month,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng was summoned to the capital
to supervise affairs outside the passes.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Chónghòu was released from prison.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
relief was provided for wind disasters in Yángzhōu.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
former Zhejiang Provincial Commander Huáng Shǎochūn was ordered to manage Zhejiang's defense affairs.
In the eighth month, on the day *jǐhài*,
the trade agreement with Bāxī was concluded.
On the day *wùshēn*,
Liú Míngchuán was summoned to the capital.
On the day *gēngxū*,
telegraph lines were first installed in the Northern and Southern Oceans.
On the day *rénzǐ*,
locusts were caught in Jiāngsū.
On the day *guǐhài*,
Cháoxiǎn reported its negotiations and engagement with Rìběn.
In the ninth month, on the day *jǐsì*,
Wú Chángqìng, the Provincial Commander-in-chief of Zhèjiāng, was ordered to assist in Shāndōng's defense,
and to command the defensive forces.
On the day *gēngwǔ*,
the tribute of dried persimmons from Yǒngjì was exempted.
On the day *xīnwèi*,
Cháoxiǎn's request to send artisans to Tiānjīn to learn to build machinery was granted.
On the day *rénshēn*,
disaster relief was provided in Púchéng and other places.
On the day *rénwǔ*,
Zēng Guóquán was granted sick leave,
and Qíyuán was ordered to command the various armies.
On the day *guǐwèi*,
the horse tribute from the Fān ethnic groups in Liángzhōu and Sùzhōu was reduced.
On the day *jǐchǒu*,
disaster relief was provided in Zīyáng and Qīngxī.
On the day *gēngyín*,
Yìndù presented musical instruments and a treatise on music,
and was awarded a golden jewel star.
On the day *guǐsì*,
the tenant rent and tax of Lālín Banner were abolished.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day *bǐngwǔ*,
the Chámùduō Pàkèbālā Hútúkètú presented tribute,
and was given *hádá* and large brocade.
On the day *jǐyǒu*,
the Dōngmíng River burst its banks.
On the day *xīnhài*,
Máo Chǎngxī, former President of the Board of Civil Office, was ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the day *jiǎyín*,
flood relief was provided in Wéichǎng Hǎilóngchéng and Hézé.
On the day *jiǎzǐ*,
an imperial edict appointed Chún Qīnwáng to manage the affairs of the Shénjīyíng.
In the eleventh month, on the day *yǐchǒu* (first day of the month),
Xǔ Jǐngchéng, a court lecturer, was appointed Minister to Rìběn.
On the day *jǐsì*,
Quán Qìng was made Grand Secretary of the Tǐrén Gédàxuéshì,
and Líng Guì was made Assistant Grand Secretary, while serving as President of the Board of Civil Office.
On the day *jiǎshēn*,
on the Winter Solstice,
heaven was worshipped at the Yuánqiū.
On the day *bǐngxū*,
the Jiānghuá Yáo bandits were suppressed.
On the day *guǐsì*,
outstanding taxes in Yǒngpíng and its subordinate areas were exempted.
In the twelfth month, on the day *bǐngwǔ*,
Yáng Chāngjùn was ordered to assist in the post-war reconstruction of Xīnjiāng.
On the day *bǐngchén*,
the additional land tax in Wén'ān, which had suffered from flooding, was exempted.
On the day *gēngshēn*,
an imperial edict ordered the Shénjīyíng to select officers and soldiers to go to Tiānjīn to learn to manufacture foreign firearms.
On the day *xīnyǒu*,
the Grand Canal waterways were dredged.
This winter,
prayers for snow were offered multiple times.
This year,
Cháoxiǎn and Kuò'ěrkā paid tribute.
In the seventh year, *xīnsì*, spring, the first month, on the day *jiǎzǐ* (first day of the month),
banquets were suspended.
Shěn Guìfēn died.
On the day *guǐyǒu*,
an imperial edict instructed all provinces to carefully select *xiàolián* and *fāngzhèng*.
On the day *yǐhài*,
the Dálài Lǎmā sent envoys to present *hádá* and Buddhist incense,
and was ordered to offer them at Huìlíng,
and was given *hádá* and silk fabrics.
On the day *wùyín*,
the desolate and collapsed salt pans of Rénhé and other areas in Zhèjiāng were exempted from taxes,
as were six years of outstanding taxes and additional grain levies for desolate and newly cultivated land in all prefectures, departments, counties, and garrisons.
On the day *xīnmǎo*,
Yuènán requested government troops to assist in suppressing accumulated bandits,
but this was not allowed.
Six years of outstanding taxes in Hǎiyáng were exempted.
On the day *rénchén*,
Zuǒ Zōngtáng was appointed Grand Councillor,
overseeing the Board of War,
and also serving in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
Outstanding taxes from quicksilver and other factories in Guìzhù, Xīngyì, and Bāzhài were abolished.
In the second month, on the day *guǐsì* (first day of the month),
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was ordered to plan the defenses of Shānhǎiguān,
and to command the various armies.
Zēng Guóquán was appointed Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù.
On the day *wùxū*,
the Rìběn envoy, Shō Dù Jī, came to discuss the Ryūkyū terms,
but an agreement was not reached,
and an imperial edict ordered coastal defenses to be on alert.
On the day *jǐyǒu*,
the Lǎolóng Stone Embankment in Xiāngyáng was repaired.
On the day *xīnhài*,
the dam works in Jìyáng were repaired.
On the day *jiǎyín*,
Liú Xīhóng, a consultant in the Court of Judicature and Revision, was dismissed from office for falsely impeaching Lǐ Hóngzhāng.
In the third month, on the day *jiǎzǐ*,
the rent and tax on official lands in Jǐnzhōu were abolished.
On the day *dīngmǎo*,
the cannon fort at Jiāoshān Dūtiānmìao was rebuilt.
On the day *jǐsì*,
Lǐ Fèngbāo was appointed concurrent Minister to Yìhélì and Àodìlì,
and Lí Shùchāng was appointed Minister to Rìběn.
On the day *xīnwèi*,
Cí'ān Huángtàihòu fell ill,
on the day *rénshēn*,
she passed away in Zhōngcuìgōng.
On the day *guǐwèi*,
the late Empress Dowager was posthumously honored with the title Xiàozhēn Cí'ān Yùqìng Héjìng Yìtiān Zuòshèng Xiǎn Huánghòu.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day *guǐsì*,
the Léibō Yí bandits were suppressed.
On the day *jǐhài*,
Wú Dàchéng was ordered to supervise the defense and agricultural settlement of Sānxìng, Nínggǔtǎ, and Húnchūn in Jílín.
Six years of outstanding taxes in Xiánníng and sixty-one other sub-prefectures, departments, and counties in Shǎnxī were exempted.
On the day *xīnchǒu*,
the posthumous edict of Xiàozhēn Xiǎn Huánghòu was promulgated to Cháoxiǎn.
On the day *jǐyǒu*,
Zēng Jìzé successfully revised the new treaty with Russia.
On the day *bǐngchén*,
private reclamation of land at the Míng Tombs was permanently prohibited.
On the day *jǐwèi*,
an imperial edict ordered
Gōng Qīnwáng and Chún Qīnwáng, together with Zuǒ Zōngtáng and Lǐ Hóngzhāng, to discuss promoting water conservancy in the Jīfǔ region.
The office of Assistant Military Governor of Húnchūn was first established.
On the day *gēngshēn*,
relief was provided for the earthquake disaster in Táiběi.
In the fifth month, on the day *rénxū* (first day of the month),
there was a solar eclipse.
Government troops scattered the accumulated bandits in Yuènán.
On the day *dīngmǎo*,
an imperial decree ordered border officials to report monthly on major cases of murder and robbery,
and those who delayed would be punished.
On the day *wùyín*,
agricultural settlements in Wūlǐyǎsūtái were abolished.
On the day *jǐchǒu*,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Yányuán.
Zhèng Zǎorú was awarded the rank of Third-Rank Minister,
and appointed Minister to Měiguó, Rìběn, and Mìlú.
In the sixth month, on the day *jǐhài*,
a comet was seen,
and an imperial edict ordered self-reflection.
On the day *bǐngchén*,
on the Emperor's birthday,
court congratulations were suspended.
On the day *jǐwèi*,
Lǐ Hóngzǎo was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day *guǐhài*,
Zhū Cìqí, a former county magistrate in Guǎngdōng known for his pure conduct and scholarship, and Chén Lǐ, a *jǔrén*, were both awarded the rank of Fifth-Rank Minister.
On the day *wùzǐ*,
Liú Kūnyī was summoned to the capital,
and Péng Yùlín was appointed acting Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng and Minister of the Southern Ocean.
Relief was provided for the earthquake disaster in Jiēzhōu and other places.
In the intercalary seventh month, on the day *rénchén*,
an edict instructed all provinces to audit the revenue and expenditure of *líkǎ* (likin stations),
and to decide whether to abolish or retain them.
On the day *guǐsì*,
relief was provided for the salt pan disasters in Liǎnghuái and Táizhōu.
On the day *jiǎwǔ*,
five years of outstanding taxes in Yúshè and other counties were exempted.
On the day *jǐhài*,
Jīn Shùn was ordered to supervise the handover of Yīlí affairs,
and Xī Lún was appointed special envoy
to negotiate border issues with the Russians.
Subsequently, Shēng Tài was also appointed special envoy.
On the day *jiǎchén*,
Bào Chāo was ordered to reorganize his subordinate troops.
On the day *yǐsì*,
the office of Assistant Military Governor of Hūlúnbèi'ěr was first established.
On the day *gēngxū*,
prefectures and counties were prohibited from concealing or embellishing major criminal cases.
This month,
flood relief was provided in Jiāngsū, Fújiàn, and Sìchuān,
and hail disaster relief in Shǎnxī.
In the eighth month, on the day *jiǎzǐ*,
twenty thousand taels of imperial gold were issued to support the displaced people of Huòshuòtè.
On the day *xīnsì*,
because the Empress Dowager recovered from her illness,
the Board of Punishments was ordered to suspend autumn executions.
Those whose executions had been deferred three times and those not yet deferred three times,
were to be differentiated and reduced accordingly.
On the day *guǐwèi*,
Xiàozhēn Xiǎn Huánghòu was interred,
and the rent and tax of the prefectures and counties she passed through were exempted.
Liú Jǐntáng was appointed Imperial Commissioner,
to supervise military affairs in Xīnjiāng,
with Zhāng Yào as his deputy.
On the day *bǐngxū*,
the tax quota on barren land in Bódūnnà was abolished.
Quán Qìng retired.
In the ninth month, on the *Jiǎwǔ* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Nínghǎi and other counties.
On the *Yǐwèi* day,
Péng Yùlín was granted permission to resign from his post,
but was to continue inspecting the Yangtze River.
Liú Kūnyī was dismissed,
and Zuǒ Zōngtáng was appointed Governor-General of the Liǎngjiāng,
concurrently serving as Minister of the Southern Ocean.
On the *Bǐngwǔ* day,
Empress Xiàozhēn Xiǎn Hòur was interred in the Dìngdōng Líng.
On the *Dīngwèi* day,
the Nian rebels in Rǔníng and Guāngzhōu were suppressed.
On the *Jǐyǒu* day,
the grain tribute quota for Jīntán was further reduced by one-tenth and four hundredths.
Eight tribes of Tibetan nomads residing in Qīnghǎi were granted over eight hundred *shí* of highland barley annually.
On the *Xīnwèi* day,
the spirit tablet of Empress Xiàozhēn Xiǎn Hòu was enshrined in the Tàimiào.
On the *Bǐngchén* day,
relief was provided for hurricane victims in Táiwān.
In this month,
Gānsù and Táiwān experienced earthquakes.
In winter, on the *Jǐsì* day of the tenth month,
on the occasion of the Empress Dowager's birthday,
banquets were suspended.
On the *Gēngwǔ* day,
the bandits Lù Sōngshān and others rebelled in Zhāotōng,
and the government troops attacked and beheaded them.
On the *Guǐyǒu* day,
Língguì was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tǐrén Gé,
and Wén Yù, Minister of the Board of Punishments, was appointed Associate Grand Secretary.
On the *Jiǎxū* day,
the French occupied the northern border of Yuènán,
and an edict instructed Yúnnán and Yuè to jointly devise strategies to prevent conflict.
On the *Jiǎshēn* day,
an edict ordered the implementation of the *chádiǎn* (supervisory review system),
stipulating that there should be no impeachments without corresponding accusations.
Relief was provided for flood victims in Tàihé and other counties.
On the *Dīnghài* day,
the previously cashiered Tídū of Ānhuī, Lǐ Shìzhōng, arbitrarily detained the *gòngshēng* Wú Tíngjiàn and others;
Yùlù reported the matter,
and an edict sentenced him to execution.
In the eleventh month, on the *Gēngyín* day,
land rent for official estates and Bódūnnà in Jílín affected by floods was remitted.
On the *Bǐngshēn* day,
Yáng Dēngjùn, a leader of the Huìfěi in Shīná, was executed.
On the *Dīngyǒu* day,
the silt in Wúsōng was dredged.
On the *Wùxū* day,
Zhào Sūqí, a bandit leader in the Guǒhuà Tǔzhōu of Guǎngxī, was executed.
Relief was provided for flood victims in Guì Xiàn and other places.
On the *Jiǎchén* day,
relief was provided for disaster victims in Táiwān and Pénghú.
In the twelfth month, on the *Yǐhài* day,
Zǎihuáng, the son of Prince Gōng, was granted the title of *bù rù bāfēn gōng*,
and Zǎiguāng, the son of Prince Chún, was granted the title of *fèng ēn fǔguó gōng*.
In this month,
land tax for fallow land and newly cultivated land in various prefectures, subprefectures, counties, and garrisons of Zhèjiāng was remitted,
as were salt production taxes for Rénhe and other salt fields.
Fixed grain quotas for waterlogged land in Ānzhōu, Rènxiàn, and Wén'ān were remitted.
Rent and tax for barren land in Jílín were abolished.
This winter,
frequent prayers for snow were offered.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn and Yuènán paid tribute.
In the eighth year, *Rénwǔ*, in spring, on the *Wùzǐ* day, the first day of the first month,
the New Year's court assembly was suspended.
On the *Xīnmǎo* day,
the dikes of Dòngtíng Xīhú were repaired.
There had been no rain from the eleventh month of the previous year until this month.
On the *Jǐhài* day,
it snowed.
On the *Gēngxū* day,
the dikes of the Hūtúo Xīnhé and Zǐyá Hé were repaired.
In the second month, on the *Jǐwèi* day,
the Wénmiào in Jiāngsū caught fire.
On the *Rénxū* day,
regarding Cháoxiǎn's occupation and cultivation of borderland in Jílín for many years,
they were ordered to obtain permits, pay rent, and register the land.
On the *Guǐchǒu* day,
gate restrictions were strictly enforced,
and regulations for inspection and guard duties were revised.
On the *Rénwǔ* day,
the private felling of trees around the Míng Líng was strictly prohibited again.
On the *Yǐyǒu* day,
previously, a suspicious legal case occurred in Jiāngníng;
Línshū and Xuē Yǔnshēng were ordered to investigate.
By this time, the facts were clarified,
and the commissioner Hú Jīnchuán was sentenced to execution for cruel torture.
An edict instructed border officials to meticulously review major criminal cases,
to prevent miscarriages of justice.
In the third month, on the *Yǐwèi* day,
Chén Lánbīn, Deputy Censor-in-Chief of the Left, was appointed to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *Gēngxū* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng mourned his mother,
repeatedly submitting memorials to request permission to complete the full mourning period,
which was granted;
he was ordered to be stationed in Tiānjīn to train troops after a hundred days,
and still provisionally manage commercial affairs.
On the *Xīnhài* day,
the French and Yuènán engaged in hostilities,
and Lǐ Hóngzhāng, Zuǒ Zōngtáng, Zhāng Shùshēng, and Liú Chángyòu were ordered to prepare border defenses.
On the *Yǐmǎo* day,
forts were built at the river mouths in Zhèjiāng.
In this month,
the Russians returned Yīlí to us.
This spring,
outstanding grain taxes in Yángqǔ, fixed taxes in Dàchéng, and accumulated outstanding taxes were remitted.
In summer, on the *Bǐngchén* day, the first day of the fourth month,
land tax for barren land in Shānxī was permanently remitted.
On the *Wùwǔ* day,
outstanding taxes from the previous year in Shǎnxī were remitted.
On the *Jǐsì* day,
the French entered Dōngjīng, Yuènán.
Zēng Guóquán was appointed acting Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng.
On the *Jiǎxū* day,
Quánqìng passed away.
On the *Jiǎshēn* day,
Cháoxiǎn requested to send envoys to be stationed in the capital,
which was not permitted,
but trade was allowed at already opened ports.
In the fifth month, on the *Bǐngxū* day, the first day,
an edict instructed Jīnshùn to plan for Yīlí,
with Chángshùn surveying and delineating the northwestern border,
and Shākèdùlínzhábù surveying and delineating the southwestern border.
On the *Wùzǐ* day,
relief was provided for hurricane victims in Dīngzhōu.
On the *Rénchén* day,
Liú Chángyòu was summoned to the capital,
and Cén Yùyīng was appointed acting Governor-General of Yúnguì.
On the *Yǐsì* day,
the Jílín Fēnxún Dào was first established.
On the *Gēngxū* day,
Zhílì suffered from locusts.
In the sixth month, on the *Dīngsì* day,
Wēn Shàotáng, a Reader in the Hànlín Yuàn, memorialized that current affairs were difficult,
requesting the Empress Dowager to be diligent and assiduous in governance.
An edict stated that the Empress Dowager had not yet fully recovered,
and instructed him.
An order was given to reform the Eight Banners official schools.
On the *Yǐhài* day,
Qīng'ān reported that Russian troops had arrived at the Hābā Hé.
An edict instructed Chángshùn to carefully and thoroughly survey the border,
to prevent covetousness.
On the *Wùyín* day,
Cháoxiǎn was in rebellion,
and Zhāng Shùshēng was ordered to suppress it.
Soon after, Tídū Dīng Rǔchāng went to provide assistance,
and Wú Chángqìng led troops across to the east.
On the *Guǐwèi* day,
Cháoxiǎn burned the Japanese embassy,
and Japan sent warships.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was ordered to Tiānjīn to deploy land and naval forces to investigate and handle the matter.
In this month,
relief was provided for flood victims in Ānhuī,
and in Zhèjiāng and Jiāngxī.
In autumn, on the *Yǐyǒu* day, the first day of the seventh month,
the San Yán indigenous people submitted.
On the *Yǐsì* day,
an imperial decree reduced palace expenses for the autumn festival,
and provided relief for disaster victims in the three provinces of Ānhuī, Zhèjiāng, and Jiāngxī.
On the *Dīngwèi* day,
Wú Chángqìng's army entered Cháoxiǎn,
and arrested Dàyuànjūn Lǐ Shìyīng.
The Xīnjiāng Ākèsū and Kāshígáěr Fēnxún Dào were first established.
On the *Guǐchǒu* day,
the Cháoxiǎn rebellion was suppressed.
In the eighth month, on the *Bǐngchén* day,
an edict stated:
"Regarding the Kēbùduō border issue,
Chónghòu caused errors previously,
and Zēng Jìzé vigorously contended later.
Now that a new treaty is being drafted,
the original map should be used for demarcation,
and new borders should be appropriately determined.
Qīng'ān and others should discuss and negotiate with Russian officials to advance this,
so that peace may prevail between both sides in the future."
On the *Dīngsì* day,
an edict instructed officials to carefully review autumn assizes.
On the *Jiǎzǐ* day,
an edict ordered Táng Jiǒng, the Provincial Administration Commissioner of Yúnnán, to go beyond the pass to inspect border defenses.
On the *Yǐchǒu* day,
Lǐ Shìyīng was resettled in Bǎodìng.
Soon after, the King of Cháoxiǎn begged for his release and return,
which was not permitted.
On the *Dīngchǒu* day,
a comet was again seen in the southeast,
and an edict instructed internal and external officials to self-reflect and reform.
In the ninth month, on the *Yǐyǒu* day,
the river breached its banks in Huìmín, Shānghé, and Bīnzhōu, Shāndōng.
On the *Guǐsì* day,
bandits rebelled in Yùlín,
and government troops suppressed them.
This autumn,
relief was provided for flood victims in Sìchuān, Zhèjiāng, Shāndōng, Shǎnxī, Fújiàn, Jiāngxī, and Guìzhōu,
for fire victims in Zīzhōu,
and for hurricane and flood victims in Táiwān.
In the tenth month of winter, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
an imperial edict instructed the capital to rigorously pursue and arrest,
without concealment or hindrance.
On the *rénxū* day,
the Yellow River burst its banks at Lìchéng.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an imperial edict ordered the arrest of the *guō* bandits.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Wáng Wénsháo repeatedly submitted memorials requesting to resign.
A warm imperial decree retained him.
In the eleventh month, on the *dīnghài* day,
Wáng Wénsháo again requested to resign, citing the need to care for his parents,
and it was granted.
Wēng Tónghé was appointed Grand Councillor.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Pān Zǔyìn was appointed Grand Councillor.
The bandit leader Wáng Jīnmǎn from Táizhōu had long evaded execution;
the relevant authorities were ordered to rigorously pursue his arrest.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
trade with Cháoxiǎn (Korea) was approved.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the new southern river of the Tāhédiàn in Tiānjīn was opened.
On the *rén yín* day,
due to an earthquake, an imperial edict instructed officials to diligently perform their duties and scrutinize local administrations.
On the *gēngxū* day,
an imperial edict ordered officials throughout the empire to recommend talented individuals.
This month,
the coal and iron mines in Tóngshān County were opened.
In the twelfth month, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
Yóu Bǎichuān was ordered to go to Shāndōng to inspect river works.
On the *rénxū* day,
coastal telegraph lines were established between Hù (Shanghai) and Yuè (Guǎngdōng).
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
an imperial edict ordered officials throughout the empire to clear accumulated cases.
On the *rénshēn* day,
after continuous prayers for snow since last month,
snow fell.
This winter,
relief was provided for earthquake victims in Zhílì,
and for hail victims in Sìchuān and Shǎnxī.
Land taxes were remitted for deficient lands in Qíqíhā'ěr and Mò'ěrgēn,
old and new military colony lands in the prefectures, counties, and garrisons of Zhèjiāng,
and the fixed salt tax quotas for Rén-Hé and other salt fields and pans.
This year,
Cháoxiǎn (Korea) offered tribute.
In the ninth year, *guǐwèi*, of spring, the first month, on the first day, *guǐwèi*,
banquets were suspended.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Liú Jǐntáng reported that Shākèdūlíngzhábù and the Russian envoy had surveyed and demarcated the southern border of Xīnjiāng,
which did not conform to the old treaty.
An imperial edict instructed Chángshùn and others to question them according to the treaty.
Subsequently, an imperial edict instructed Zēng Jìzé to vigorously contend for a resurvey.
On the *wùxū* day,
Wú Tíngfēn, a Department Director of the Zōngrénfǔ, was ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
an imperial edict remitted money and grain taxes;
for those who had already paid the government,
it could be offset against the principal tax of the following year,
and not be double-collected.
On the *yǐsì* day,
thirty thousand *shí* of Húběi grain transport were allocated to relieve famine in Shùn-Zhí.
This month,
the Vietnamese bandit Tán Sìdì and others surrendered.
In the second month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
migrants from Zhí (Zhílì) and Lǔ (Shāndōng) converged on the capital,
and officials were instructed to provide relief and comfort.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the Yellow River burst its banks at Lìchéng, Shāndōng,
damaging the people's dikes in Qíhé and other counties.
Yóu Bǎichuān and others were ordered to provide relief and comfort to the victims.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
previously, Jǐngruì, the General of Mǎlánzhèn, repaired barracks,
which were secretly accused by the camp soldiers.
General Guì Áng requested troops, leading to a mutiny.
Bóyànnèmǔhù and Yán Jìngmíng were dispatched to investigate.
Upon their report,
Jǐngruì was stripped of his position,
and Guì Áng was subsequently also stripped of his position.
Cruel officials in all provinces were forbidden from using illegal tortures.
Xú Yánxù, the Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guǎngxī, was ordered to leave the pass and prepare defenses.
On the *wùchén* day,
Zhāng Mèngyuán, the Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Fújiàn, was appointed to oversee Fújiàn shipbuilding.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Mò Yùlín, a Regional Commander of Gāozhōu, incited rebellion
and was executed.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Board of Punishments reported that in the case of Hú Tǐ'ān in Hénán,
the original judgment was erroneous,
and the retrial was protective.
An imperial edict stripped Lǐ Hènián, the Governor, and Méi Qǐzhào, the Grand Canal Governor of Hédōng, of their positions.
The original judges were condemned to exile, with varying degrees of severity.
In the third month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
Zhènguógōng Pǔtài accepted prohibited reclamation lands from the *diàn* (lake/wetland) areas,
was stripped of his noble title,
and imprisoned for one year.
The French captured Nándìng.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Táng Jiǒng was ordered to command the defense army to guard the Yúnnán border.
Ní Wénwèi was instructed to protect Běiqí.
This spring,
summer grain taxes were remitted for Qiánshān and other counties,
and land and poll taxes for drought-stricken areas of Shǎnxī were converted to rice.
Relief was provided for flood victims in Jǐnán and Wǔdìng,
and earthquake victims in Táiwān.
In the fourth month of summer, on the *jǐwèi* day,
Russia withdrew its troops from Yīlí.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an imperial edict ordered strict arrest of bandits in the capital region.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Liú Chángyòu was dismissed due to illness,
and Cén Yùyīng was appointed Governor-General of Yún-Guì.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Chén Miǎn and 308 others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with varying ranks.
In the fifth month, on the *xīnsì* day,
an imperial edict ordered Lǐ Hóngzhāng to return to Běiyáng to assume his post,
and arrange coastal defenses.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Shēng Tài was ordered to demarcate the southwestern border of Tǎ'ěrbāhātái with the Russian envoy.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Fāng Xuě'áo, a leader of a secret society in Húnán, instigated rebellion,
and was captured and executed.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
private coin casting was prohibited.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Cén Yùyīng and others were instructed to select and recruit border residents,
to hold important passes between Diān (Yúnnán) and Yuè (Vietnam) with the government troops.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an imperial decree ordered Chún Qīnwáng to collectively plan affairs concerning France and Vietnam.
Previously,
Censor Chén Qǐtài memorialized that Zhōu Ruìqīng, a Minister of the Tàichángsì, had misappropriated funds for Yúnnán expense reports.
Censor Hóng Liángpǐn and Supervising Secretary Dèng Chéngxiū, as the matter involved Grand Councillors Jǐnglián and Wáng Wénsháo,
successively impeached them.
Dūn Qīnwáng, Yán Jìngmíng, Pān Zǔyìn, Zhāng Zhīwàn, Línshū, Wēng Tónghé, and Xuē Yǔnshēng were successively ordered to jointly investigate.
Upon their report,
Ruìqīng and others were punished according to the law.
Jǐnglián, the President of the Board of Revenue,
former Vice Presidents Wáng Wénsháo and Kuí Rùn,
former President Dǒng Xún,
and former Governor-General of Yún-Guì Liú Chángyòu were all demoted three ranks.
Others received varying punishments.
In the sixth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
the Yellow River in Shāndōng burst its banks,
damaging the people's dikes in Lìchéng, Qídōng, and Lìjīn.
An imperial edict ordered both dike repair and relief work to proceed simultaneously.
Vietnamese General Liú Yǒngfú and French soldiers fought at Hénèi (Hanoi),
and the French were defeated.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Qìn River dikes were repaired.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
France sent envoy Tuōlì Gǔlái to negotiate a peace treaty.
Eunuch Wáng Yǒnghé stole imperial clothing and articles.
An imperial edict ordered the Board of Punishments to sentence him according to the law,
without implicating others.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Xiǎoqīng River in Shāndōng was dredged.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
due to floods, Shāndōng initiated relief donations.
This summer,
land rents for native chieftaincies in Yúnnán were remitted,
as were old arrears of grain and taxes in Gānsù.
Additionally, fixed grain taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken Màogōng and flood-stricken Tóngrén.
A total of 100,000 *shí* of grain transport and 160,000 *liǎng* of capital funds were retained to relieve disaster in Shāndōng.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
200,000 *liǎng* of capital funds were retained for the Guǎngxī army.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Wú Quánměi and Fāng Yào were instructed to patrol the seas off Lián and Qióng, and the border of Qīnzhōu.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
an imperial edict ordered the opening of mines in Yúnnán.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Wáng Jīnmǎn, the bandit leader from Táizhōu, led his followers to surrender.
An imperial edict remitted his death sentence,
and he and his followers were retained in the camp to serve.
In the eighth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
the French captured the cannon forts on the Thuận Hóa riverbank,
and the Vietnamese ceased hostilities to negotiate peace.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the Yǒngdìng River burst its banks.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
officials of the Boards and Grand Secretariat were inspected.
An imperial edict ordered the construction of coastal dikes and other works,
and the relief and comfort of disaster-stricken households.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
an imperial edict called for the recommendation of individuals excelling in both strategy and courage, suitable for appointment.
On the *jǐsì* day,
an imperial edict ordered Péng Yùlín to go to Guǎngdōng,
to collectively arrange defense matters with Zhāng Shùshēng.
In the ninth month, on the *xīnsì* day,
France and Vietnam negotiated peace
and established a new treaty.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Hé Rúzhāng was appointed to oversee Fújiàn shipbuilding,
Ní Wénwèi as Governor of Guǎngdōng,
and Xú Yánxù as Governor of Guǎngxī.
On the *jǐhài* day,
100,000 *liǎng* of silver from the Guǎngxī treasury were allocated to support Liú Yǒngfú's army.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Táng Jiǒng was stripped of his position for leading his troops back to the province without authorization,
but was retained in his post.
In this autumn,
over 50,000 shí of grain from the capital granaries and tribute grain were allocated,
and 100,000 in treasury funds,
to relieve Shùntiān Zhílì.
50,000 shí of tribute grain were kept back
to relieve Shāndōng.
Disaster relief was provided for the floods in Rèhé, Chángyáng, Guōxiàn, and other places.
Disaster relief was provided for Jiāngnán.
In the winter, 10th month, on the day of wùchén,
an imperial edict was issued to all provinces in the northern and southern oceans, and along rivers and coasts, to maintain strict vigilance.
On the day of xīnwèi,
the river broke its banks in Qídōng, Pútái, and Lìjīn.
On the day of bǐngzǐ,
an imperial edict commanded Lǐ Hóngzhāng to recommend military talents.
Cén Yùyīng was ordered to leave the pass and station in Shānxī,
and Táng Jiǒng to return to Diān to raise provisions.
In the 11th month, on the day of xīnsì,
Zhāng Pèilún, acting Zǔofùdūyùshǐ, was ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the day of rénwǔ,
Xú Yánxù was urged to leave the pass to provide support.
On the day of xīnmǎo,
the inner and outer city gate controls were strictly enforced.
On the day of rénchén,
the Vietnamese people revolted,
killing the heir to the throne, Ruǎn Fúshí.
Zhāng Shùshēng was ordered to suppress it,
but soon after, Cén Yùyīng was reassigned to quell the rebellion.
On the day of gēngzǐ,
an imperial decree was issued
to establish a factory in Qīngjiāng to house disaster victims,
and the Hùbù was ordered to allocate 10,000 in treasury funds for relief,
and also 40,000 each to Shùnzhí and Shāndōng,
30,000 to Húběi,
and 20,000 to Ānhuī.
On the day of rényín,
the French occupied Shānxī,
and Liú Yǒngfú retreated.
On the day of guǐmǎo,
an imperial edict stated that Shàngshū Wén Yù was impeached,
and in his reply, accumulated salary reached 360,000,
so he was ordered to donate 100,000 silver taels to the public treasury.
Lín Zhàoyuán was dismissed from office for the emptiness of the treasury reserves.
In the 12th month, on the day of wùshēn,
prayers for snow were offered.
