On the day of gēngxū,
the French attacked Běiníng,
planning to invade Qióngzhōu.
Péng Yùlín was ordered to dispatch the Xiāngchǔ army to join Wú Quánměi's fleet for strict defense,
and Yáng Yuèbīn was appointed to Fújiàn to jointly manage coastal defense.
The government army greatly defeated the French at Liàngshān.
On the day of jǐwèi,
as disaster victims from Shāndōng, Huái, and Xú gathered in Qīngjiāng and other places,
the responsible officials were ordered to provide relief,
and to provide assistance and send them away as needed.
On the day of gēngshēn,
an edict was issued to Jiāngxī to raise 20,000 in provisions to aid Wáng Débǎng's army.
On the day of dīngchǒu,
the hereditary post of the late Zǒngbīng Chén Guóruì was reinstated.
In this winter,
the autumn tax in Shùntiān Zhílì and other prefectures and counties was remitted,
as was the quota tax for disaster-stricken prefectures, counties, and guard posts in Zhèjiāng.
Arrears of land rent and grain in Fèngtái and other prefectures and counties in Shānxī were cancelled.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn and Yuènán paid tribute.
In the 10th year, the spring of jiǎshēn, 1st month, on the day of gēngyín,
Cén Yùyīng left Zhènnán Pass for Xīnghuà,
to command all armies beyond the border.
In the 2nd month, on the first day of dīngwèi,
the French attacked Xīnghuà,
and the government army repelled them.
Cén Yùyīng and Xú Yánxù advanced to attack Shānxī.
An edict commanded strict discipline,
not to disturb the Vietnamese territory.
50,000 shí each of tribute grain from Jiāng and Zhè were kept back to relieve the floods in Tōngzhōu and Tiānjīn.
Soon after, 30,000 shí of millet from the capital granaries were allocated to relieve the disaster in Shùntiān.
On the day of dīngchǒu,
the French occupied Běiníng,
and the government army retreated to defend Tàiyuán.
On the day of wùchén,
Húnán Xúnfǔ Pān Dǐngxīn was ordered to Gǔangxī to prepare defenses.
On the day of yǐhài,
the French occupied Tàiyuán,
and Xú Yánxù and Táng Jiǒng were stripped of their posts and arrested for questioning.
In the 3rd month, on the day of dīnghài,
Cén Yùyīng requested to be exempt from commanding the Chǔ and Yuè armies,
but this was not granted.
Due to the fall of Tàiyuán,
Tídū Huáng Guìlán and Dàoyuán Zhào Wò were both stripped of their posts and arrested for questioning.
On the day of wùzǐ,
an imperial decree stated that due to his procrastination and errors, Jūnjī Dàchén Gōngqīnwáng Yìxīn was dismissed and sent home to recuperate from illness,
Dàxuéshì Bǎoyún was retired at his original rank,
Xiébàn Dàxuéshì Lǐ Hóngzǎo and Jǐnglián were both demoted two ranks,
and Gōngbù Shàngshū Wēng Tónghé was dismissed but remained in office.
Lǐqīnwáng Shìduó,
Hùbù Shàngshū Èlèhébù and Yán Jìngmíng,
and Xíngbù Shàngshū Zhāng Zhīwàn were all appointed Jūnjī Dàchén.
Gōngbù Shìláng Sūn Yùwèn was ordered to study in the Jūnjī.
On the day of jǐchǒu,
an imperial decree stated that for important matters in the Jūnjīchù,
Chúnqīnwáng should be consulted for deliberation and execution.
On the day of rénchén,
Pān Dǐngxīn was appointed Guǎngxi Xúnfǔ,
and Zhāng Kǎisōng was appointed Yúnnán Xúnfǔ.
Zǒngbīng Chén Déguì lost the fort,
and Fùjiàng Dǎng Mǐnxuān retreated from the battlefield;
an edict ordered both to be executed before the army.
Yíqīnwáng Zàidūn was appointed Yuèbīng Dàchén.
Bèilè Yìkuāng was ordered to oversee the affairs of the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén,
and Nèigé Xuéshì Zhōu Dérùn was ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the day of guǐsì,
Zuǒshùzǐ Shèng Yù, Yòushùzǐ Xī Jūn, and Yùshǐ Zhào Ěrsùn each submitted memorials stating that Chúnqīnwáng should not be involved in state affairs,
but this was not reported.
Xíngbù Shìláng Xǔ Gēngshēn was ordered to study in the Jūnjī.
On the day of jiǎwǔ,
an imperial edict commanded Lǐ Hóngzhāng, Zuǒ Zōngtáng, Zēng Guóquán, and Cén Yùyīng to recommend their subordinate generals who were resolute, brave, and resourceful.
On the day of jǐhài,
Yán Jìngmíng and Xǔ Gēngshēn were both ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
Pān Dǐngxīn was ordered to Zhènnán Pass to take command of Xú Yánxù's army.
On the day of gēngzǐ,
the French advanced and occupied Xīnghuà.
In this spring,
the previous year's outstanding taxes for barren and marshy lands in Rénhé were remitted,
as were outstanding taxes and miscellaneous arrears in Xiánníng and other places in Shǎnxī.
The tribute of horses and fodder for the Mùpíng Tǔsī was remitted for ten years.
In the summer, 4th month, on the day of bǐngwǔ,
the demarcation of the southern border of Xīnjiāng was completed.
Shìjiǎng Xǔ Jǐngchéng was appointed minister plenipotentiary to Fǎ, Dé, Yì, and Ào.
On the day of gēngxū,
previously,
as the war between France and Vietnam was urgent,
the French naval commander Fúlùnuò, through the customs commissioner Décuīlín, proposed peace negotiations to cease hostilities.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng reported this,
and it was approved,
with an imperial edict ordering him to arrange it.
By this time,
he submitted a report stating,
“One must assess the situation, gauge one's strength,
and act with caution, awaiting the right moment.”
An imperial edict ordered a court deliberation.
An imperial decree stated that Chúnqīnwáng should also participate in the discussion.
Wú Chángqìng's troops were allowed to return.
On the day of xīnhài,
the breaches in Lìjīn and other places were closed.
On the day of guǐchǒu,
the excavation of Mǎjiáhé was stopped,
Xuānhuìhé was dredged,
and the canal dikes in Dézhōu were repaired.
On the day of wùwǔ,
Tōngzhèngshǐ Wú Dàchéng was ordered to jointly manage the affairs of Běiyáng,
Nèigé Xuéshì Chén Bǎochēn to jointly manage the affairs of Nányáng,
and Shìjiǎng Xuéshì Zhāng Pèilún to jointly manage the coastal defense affairs of Fújiàn;
all were granted the privilege of submitting independent memorials.
Soon after, Pèilún was granted the rank of Sānpǐn Qīng.
Fúlùnuò presented five private proposals,
which Lǐ Hóngzhāng reported to the throne.
An imperial edict commanded Hóngzhāng
“to resolutely prevent cunning schemes,
and always maintain vigilance.”
An imperial edict commanded the Hùbù to cut redundant expenses.
On the day of gēngshēn,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was appointed minister plenipotentiary
to negotiate a treaty with the French envoy.
On the day of guǐhài,
the quota tax for land near the river in Bāochéng was remitted.
On the day of yǐchǒu,
prayers for rain were offered.
On the day of bǐngyín,
granary rice was again issued to relieve Shùntiān.
On the day of wùchén,
Wú Dàchéng resigned from his position as Běiyáng Joint Manager.
The emperor reprimanded him for making excuses
and did not permit it.
On the day of rénshēn,
Zhāng Shùshēng requested to be excused from his current post due to illness,
to focus solely on military affairs,
which was granted.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day of the fifth month,
Lǐ Chéng was ordered to be the commander-in-chief of the army and navy in Jiāngnán.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Cén Yùyīng resigned as commander-in-chief of the various armies in Yuè and Chǔ,
which was granted.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Wén Yù was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wǔyīng Diàn.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Élèhébù and Yán Jìngmíng were both appointed Minister of the Board of Revenue and concurrently Associate Grand Secretary.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
due to a prolonged drought in the capital,
an edict was issued to officials to regulate grain prices.
Zhāng Yīnhuán, Intendant of Huī-Níng-Tài-Guǎng, was awarded the rank of a third-grade minister,
and ordered to serve and gain experience in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
an imperial edict called for recommendations of civil and military talents from within and outside the capital.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
an imperial edict proclaimed a halt to
autumn executions for the Empress Dowager's fiftieth birthday.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
an imperial edict commanded officials inside and outside the capital
"to lead their subordinates in fulfilling their duties,
and not to indulge in idleness and pleasure, or pursue ostentation."
On the *wùxū* day,
an imperial edict reinstated Zuǒ Zōngtáng as a Grand Councillor,
exempting him from constant duty,
and also placed him in charge of the Shénjīyíng.
The grain quota for the two guards of Wǔchāng and Huángzhōu was remitted.
On the *rényín* day,
an imperial edict called for recommendations of talents from the imperial clan and hereditary officials, both Bannermen and Han.
On the *yǐsì* day of the intercalary fifth month,

Fúkūn, Minister of the Board of Works, Kūngāng, Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs, Xīzhēn, Censor-in-chief of the Left, Xú Yòngyí, Vice Minister of the Board of Works, and Liáo Shòuhéng, Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, were all ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the former Admiral Liú Míngchuán was ordered to supervise affairs in Táiwān.
Xīzhēn, Liáo Shòuhéng, Chén Bǎochēn, and Wú Dàchéng went to Tiānjīn to discuss a treaty with the French.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Xú Shùmíng, Grand Master of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was ordered to survey the newly opened transverse river in Xiànxiàn.
The French attacked Guānyīnqiáo,
and Pān Dǐngxīn defeated them.
On the *xīnhài* day,
river embankment work in Shāndōng was completed.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
as the French envoy spoke of peace,
Pān Dǐngxīn's various armies were recalled to Liángshān,
and Cén Yùyīng's army remained stationed in Bǎoshèng.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
it had not rained since the fourth month;
on this day, rain finally fell.
Regulations for remitting and postponing taxes were promulgated.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Mò Mèngbì, the bandit leader of Sī'ēn, was executed.
On the *bǐngyín* day, French warships attacked the Mǐn Sea.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
an edict stated:
"The French envoy is delaying treaty negotiations,
and Gūbá's demands are unreasonable.
Our army must be on high alert.
If they attack us,
we shall unite our forces and strike them.
Any who dare to retreat
shall be immediately dealt with by military law."
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Zēng Guóquán was appointed Plenipotentiary Minister
to negotiate a treaty with the French envoy in Shànghǎi,
and Chén Bǎochēn was ordered to assist.
On the *guǐyǒu* day, the first day of the sixth month,
because the judgment of Yú Qióngfāng's case in Yúnxī was found to be untrue,
Governor-General Biàn Bǎodì and Provincial Governor Péng Zǔxián were referred to the Board for deliberation,
and the investigating officials were demoted or dismissed to varying degrees.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the river burst its banks in Lìchéng and other counties.
In recognition of her appeal for aid to defend the city,
Shěn Bǎozhēn's wife, Madame Lín, was posthumously granted the honor of being enshrined alongside Bǎozhēn in his exclusive ancestral temple in Guǎngxìn.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Yáng Chángqīng, the bandit leader of Jiànchāng and Duōlún, was executed.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Wú Chángqìng passed away;
his son, the Director Bǎo Chū, was commended for his filial piety.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
an edict was issued to inspect local officials in the directly administered provinces.
On the *rénchén* day,
the French captured Jīlóng.
An imperial edict ordered a meeting of court officials to discuss peace or war.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Liú Míngchuán recaptured Jīlóng.
On the *jǐhài* day,
an imperial decree ordered that
three thousand infantry and cavalry be selected from the Shénjīyíng,
and two thousand trained soldiers be selected from the five patrol battalions.
Dūtǒng Shànqìng was appointed Commander-in-chief,
and former Front-Vanguard Commander Tuōlúnbù as Assistant Commander,
to be stationed in eastern Jī.
Additionally, trained troops from Zhílì were transferred to assist in defense.
Zēng Guóquán and Chén Bǎochēn were ordered to return to Jiāngníng to arrange defenses.
In this month,
relief was provided for wind disasters in Shùndé and Qīngpǔ,
and a flood disaster in Yèxiàn.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *yǐsì* day,
Wú Yuánbǐng was ordered to survey river works and coastal defenses in Shāndōng.
Zhāng Zhīdòng was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the French attacked the Mǎwěi forts and dockyard,
but the ground forces repelled them.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Qúnwáng, Chún brought a memorial from Yán Xù impeaching Zuǒ Zōngtáng,
which was denounced as disrespectful and disloyal,
uttering wild accusations,
and wantonly reversing facts.
An imperial decree stripped Yán Xù of his rank but allowed him to retain his post,
and fined him one year's salary.
An edict declared war on the French.
Yáng Chāngjùn proceeded to Fújiàn to supervise military affairs.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
the French destroyed the Chángmén forts.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Mùtúshàn and Zhāng Pèilún were ordered not to retreat to the provincial capital.
An edict appointed Zuǒ Zōngtáng as Imperial Commissioner
to supervise military affairs in Fújiàn.
Mùtúshàn, General of Fúzhōu, and Yáng Chāngjùn, Governor-General of Grain Transport, were his deputies.
Zhāng Pèilún served as Associate Minister and concurrently acting Minister of Naval Affairs.
Zēng Guóquán was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng,
and concurrently Minister of Nányáng.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
concerning the crime of the loss of Běiníng,
the disgraced *dàoyuán* Zhào Wò and Admiral Chén Cháogāng were both sentenced to beheading.
On the *wùchén* day,
Yáng Chāngjùn was appointed Governor-General of Mǐn-Zhè.
General relief was provided for disaster victims in Lìchéng and other counties.
In this month,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Fúliáng and Qíhé, Cháng'ān, and other places.
In the eighth month, on the *rénshēn* day,
Déng Chéngxiū, Minister of the Court of State Ceremonials, was ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
Regarding the merits and demerits of the Mǎwěi battle,
Hé Jǐng was stripped of his office and Zhāng Pèilún of his ministerial rank,
and referred to the Board for deliberation.
Admiral Huáng Chāoqún and others received various awards and promotions.
Zhāng Tíngyuán and other bandit leaders of Jiàn and Shào were executed.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the river burst its banks in Dōngmíng.
Relief was provided for flood disasters in Nánhǎi and other counties.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì and Minister of Běiyáng.
On the *wùyín* day,
an imperial decree bestowed upon Zǎi Fēng, son of Chúnqīnwáng, the title of *Bùrù Bāfēn Fǔguógōng*.
Wén Yù was excused due to illness.
Chónghòu, Chónglǐ, Wénxī, and Wénxiān were ordered to contribute funds and provisions.
On the *gēngchén* day,
relief was provided for wind disasters in Táiwān.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the French recaptured Jīlóng.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Dàoyuán Xú Chéngzǔ was appointed Minister to Japan.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
an imperial edict ordered that all serious cases from the Board of Punishments this year, as well as officials involved in autumn and court reviews,
be exempted from investigation and prosecution.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Sū Yuánchūn engaged the French in battle on land,
and defeated them.
Yáng Yuèbīn was ordered to assist Zuǒ Zōngtáng in military affairs.
Relief was provided for flood disasters in Xīngzǐ.
On the *wùxū* day,
the French attacked Hùwěi, and Admiral Sūn Kāihuá defeated them.
In the ninth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Táng Jǒng was arrested and interrogated in prison.
On the day Yǐsì,
fifty thousand taels of silver from the imperial treasury were allocated to reward Liú Yǒngfú's army.
On the day Xīnhài,
a strict imperial edict ordered all ships of the Northern and Southern Ocean Fleets to assist Táiwān.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Liú Míngchuán was appointed Fújiàn巡撫 (Xúnfǔ),
stationed in Táiwān to oversee defense.
Sū Yuánchūn was made Assistant Administrator for Pān Dǐngxīn's military affairs.
Yáng Chāngjùn and others were assigned to defend Pénghú.
Zhāng Zhàodòng and Hé Rúzhāng were both stripped of their posts.
An imperial edict exempted Yúnnán from land tax,
allowing a temporary three-year deferment for barren lands,
and a ten-year exemption for permanently barren lands.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Liú Míngchuán requested punishment for himself,
but an imperial edict pardoned him.
On the day Wùwǔ,
one hundred thousand units of new grain tax were reserved for winter relief in Shāndōng.
On the day Gēngshēn,
due to the victory at Húwěi (Tamsui),
General Sūn Kāihuá was granted a hereditary rank,
and ten thousand taels of silver from the imperial treasury were issued to reward the army.
Èlèhébù was appointed Tǐrén Gé Dàxuéshì.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Ēnchéng, Minister of the Board of Punishments, was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary.
On the day Bǐngyín,
relief was provided for flood victims in Fènghuángchéng.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the imperial army and French forces fought on land,
and the French were defeated again.
Sū Yuánchūn was granted a hereditary rank.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Xīnjiāng was reorganized into a province,
with one巡撫 (Xúnfǔ) and one 布政使 (Bùzhèngshǐ) appointed.
The positions of Southern and Northern Route Commander-in-Chief (Dūtǒng), Advisor (Cānzàn), Administrator (Bànshì), and Detachment Commander (Lǐngduì) were abolished.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Rénshēn (the first day of the month),
an imperial decree promoted Yìkuāng to Qìng Jùnwáng,
and Yìmó to Gùshān Béizi.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Liú Jǐntáng was appointed Gānsù Xīnjiāng巡撫 (Xúnfǔ).
On the day Wùyín,
relief was provided for flood and hail disaster victims in Jiāngběi Tīng and other areas.
On the day Xīnsì,
on the occasion of the Empress Dowager's fiftieth birthday,
the Emperor, accompanied by princes, civil and military officials and others, went to Cíníng Gōng to offer congratulations.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Bāo Chāo, having repeatedly missed military deadlines,
was severely reprimanded.
On the day Guǐsì,
Wáng Hóngshùn, Commander-in-Chief (Tídū), was stripped of his post
for feigning illness to evade duty.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Zhāng Shùshēng passed away.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Cháoxiǎn (Korea) was again in turmoil.
Wú Dàchéng was sent to investigate and manage the situation.
Xùchāng was his deputy.
Wén Yù passed away.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Liú Yǒngfú and French forces fought at Xuānguāng,
suffering a defeat.
In the eleventh month, on the day Dīngwèi,
Commander-in-Chief (Tídū) Sūn Kāihuá was ordered to assist in Táiwān's military affairs.
On the day Wùshēn,
Xú Yánxù was arrested and interrogated in prison.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng dispatched troops to Cháoxiǎn (Korea).
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Pǔ'ěr experienced an earthquake.
On the day Bǐngchén,
prefectures and counties were prohibited from reporting disasters and famines.
On the day Dīngsì,
the breach at Dōngmíng was closed.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Lǐ Bǐnghéng proceeded to Lóngzhōu to deploy defense troops.
On the day Jǐwèi,
prayers for snow were offered.
The Bāmán tribes in Yúnnán surrendered.
On the day Wùchén,
an imperial edict ordered all provinces to store grain.
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùyín,
the imperial army defeated the French at Zhǐzuòshè.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Táng Jǒng and Xú Yánxù were both sentenced to beheading.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the imperial army recaptured the three provinces of Xuānguāng, Xīnghuà, and Shānxī,
along with Ānpíng Fǔ, and two prefectures and five counties.
On the day Rénchén,
the Luquàn aboriginal bandits were pacified.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
there was rain and snow.
Zhāng Pèilún and Hé Rúzhāng were both stripped of their posts and exiled.
In this year,
arrears of land tax for barren lands in Zhènxī Tīng were exempted,
as were fixed taxes for flooded lands in Wén'ān and four other prefectures and counties.
Cháoxiǎn (Korea) paid tribute.
King Ruǎn Yīngdēng of Yuènán (Vietnam) committed suicide.
The French enthroned his younger brother as king.
In the eleventh year, on the day Guǐmǎo of the first month of spring (Yǐyǒu year),
Féng Zǐcái was ordered to assist in military affairs outside the pass in Guǎngxī.
On the day Yǐsì,
the French captured Liàngshān.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the imperial army besieged Xuānguāng,
and recaptured Měiliáng Chéng.
On the day Jiǎyín,
French forces attacked Zhènnán Guān,
and General Yáng Yùkē died there.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the British general Gordon was granted a pension.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the French fleet withdrew from Táiwān.
Zuǒ Zōngtáng and other forces reinforced Zhèjiāng.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was appointed Plenipotentiary Minister,
to negotiate Cháoxiǎn (Korean) affairs with the Japanese envoy, accompanied by Wú Dàchéng.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the Cháoxiǎn (Korean) rebellion was pacified.
An envoy came to express gratitude,
and was rewarded.
In the second month, on the day Jiǎxū,
Ōuyáng Lìjiàn, Commander-in-Chief (Tídū) of Zhèjiāng, defeated the French at Zhènhǎi Kǒu.
On the day Wùyín,
Pān Dǐngxīn was stripped of his post.
Lǐ Bǐnghéng was appointed Acting Guǎngxī巡撫 (Xúnfǔ).
Sū Yuánchūn was made Commander-in-Chief for Guǎngxī military affairs.
On the day Xīnsì,
Qínzhōu experienced an earthquake.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Féng Zǐcái and Wáng Xiàoqí utterly defeated the French outside Zhènnán Guān,
and subsequently recaptured Liàngshān.
Yáng Yùkē and others were granted hereditary ranks.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the French requested peace.
This was granted.
On the day Rénchén,
an imperial edict ordered a ceasefire and troop withdrawal.
The Burmese bandits were pacified.
On the day Wùxū,
Cén Yùyīng reported a great victory by the imperial army at Líntáo.
In the third month, on the day Yǐsì,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was appointed Plenipotentiary Minister
to negotiate a treaty with the French envoy.
Xīzhēn, Minister of the Board of Punishments, and Déng Chéngxiū, Grand Herald (Hónglú Qīng), went to Tiānjīn for discussions.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Cháoxiǎn (Korean) treaty was concluded.
On the day Gēngxū,
Cén Yùyīng recaptured Miànwàng, along with the villages of Qīngshuǐ and Qīngshān.
He captured and executed Yuènán (Vietnamese) rebel minister Huáng Xié and others.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Wú Dàchéng and Yīkètáng'ā were ordered to jointly survey the eastern border of Jílín.
On the day Bǐngchén,
arrears of rent and tax owed by the populace for many years in Yǒngpíng, Zhāngjiākǒu, Shùntiān, and ten other prefectures and sub-prefectures were exempted.
On the day Guǐhài,
Féng Zǐcái was ordered to oversee the defense of Qīn and Lián.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
arrears of grain tax from the previous year in Shǎnxī, Xiánníng, and other areas were exempted.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
prayers for rain were offered.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Cén Yùyīng was urged to withdraw his troops,
to avoid breaking the agreement and starting hostilities.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
an imperial edict ordered the elimination of long-standing abuses in the Dīngcáo (poll tax and grain tribute) in Jiāngxī.
On the day Rénchén,
Liú Yǒngfú was urged to withdraw his Bǎoshèng army.
The new Sino-French treaty was concluded in Tiānjīn.
In the fifth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
an imperial decree ordered the inspection and repair of the Northern and Southern Sea projects.
An imperial edict ordered the reorganization of the navy,
and the thorough development of the naval forces,
assigning the Northern and Southern Ocean Ministers and others to deliberate on this.
French troops withdrew from Jīlóng.
Yáng Yuèbīn and others were ordered to manage affairs throughout Táiwān.
Arrears of tax from the early Guāngxù reign in Fújiàn were remitted.
On the day Xīnhài,
Zà'yā was permitted to pay tribute with Càmùduō.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Sū Yuánchūn and Féng Zǐcái were granted the rank of Third-Class Light Chariot Captain (Qīngchē Dūwèi).
Wáng Xiàoqí and Cén Yùyīng were granted the rank of Cloud Cavalry Commandant (Yúnqí Wèi).
Wáng Débǎng was restored to his original official position with commendation.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
prayers for rain were offered again.
On the day Rénxū,
it rained.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Zhāng Yào was appointed Guǎngxī巡撫 (Xúnfǔ).
In this month,
relief was provided for war victims in Jīlóng, flood victims in Tóngchéng and other counties, and flood victims in Zhèngǎn.
In the sixth month, on the day Jǐsì,
an imperial edict ordered the suspension of autumn executions.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
an imperial decree commanded Wénxiān, Chónglǐ, Chónghòu, and Wénxī to oversee the construction of the Sānhǎi project.
Xǔ Jǐngchéng was also appointed Minister to Belgium.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the registration of Vietnamese defectors as Chinese subjects was finalized.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Zēng Jìzé concluded the Yāntái Treaty.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
an edict was issued to Cén Yùyīng to investigate copper mines in Yúnnán.
A general edict was issued to Zēng Guóquán and others to survey various mines in the southeast.
Famine relief was provided for the flood disaster in Yùzhōu.
On the day Guǐwèi,

Sūn Yùwèn, Vice Minister of the Board of Works, Shěn Bǐngchéng, Governor of Shùntiān Prefecture, and Xù Chāng, Judicial Commissioner of Húnán, were all ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
Zēng Jìzé was summoned to the capital.
Liú Ruìfēn, Provincial Administration Commissioner of Jiāngxī, was appointed Minister to Britain and Russia.
Zhāng Yīnhuán was appointed Minister to the United States, Japan, and Peru.
French troops departed from Pénghú.
Zǔo Zōngtáng and others were ordered to select officers and deploy warships for coordination.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the new treaty with Yuènán was concluded.
It was proclaimed both domestically and abroad.
An imperial edict warned officials offering advice against private motives and slanders.
The accusations by Censor Wú Xún against Yán Jìngmíng and by Compiler Liáng Dǐngfēn against Lǐ Hóngzhāng were posthumously deemed false accusations against high officials,
and severe repercussions were announced.
Subsequently, they were each demoted five ranks.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Sūn Yùwèn was appointed Grand Councillor.
This month,
flood relief was provided in Hénán, Guǎngdōng, Guǎngxī, Jiāngnán, Ānhuī, and Jiāngxī.
In the autumn, on the first day of the seventh month, Dīngyǒu,
a telegraph line was established from Nánníng, Guǎngxī, to Yúnnán.
On the day Jǐhài,
an imperial decree allocated 60,000 taels of silver from the imperial treasury for flood relief in the two Guǎng provinces.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Zǔo Zōngtáng repeatedly requested leave due to illness,
which was granted.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Zhōu Déyùn was ordered to Yúnnán,
and Dèng Chéngxiū to Guǎngxī,
to jointly survey the China-Vietnam border with Cén Yùyīng and Zhāng Kǎisōng.
On the day Rénxū,
the Yellow River burst its banks in Chángqīng, Shāndōng.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
copper and iron mines were opened in Sìchuān and Diān.
This month,
flood relief was provided in Qiányáng, Xiāngtán, Huīxiàn, Qīngjiāng, Dāngtú, Fényáng, and other places.
In the eighth month, on the first day Dīngmǎo,
flood relief was provided in Fèngtiān.
On the day Jǐsì,
100,000 shí of grain tribute were diverted for disaster relief in Shùnzhí.
Famine relief was provided for hail and flood disasters in Gāolán and other places.
On the day Yǐhài,
flood relief was provided in Chángshā and other places.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
floods occurred in Lìchéng, Zhāngqiū, and other places in Shāndōng.
50,000 taels from the imperial treasury were issued for relief.
Due to the floods,
the Sānhǎi project was suspended.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng discussed overland trade between Diān and Yuè with the French envoy.
On the day Wùyín,
Lǐ Shìyìng was released and returned to Cháoxiǎn.
On the day Xīnsì,
Sū Yuánchūn was ordered to pacify and settle the Vietnamese refugees who had entered the pass.
Flood relief was provided in Xiāngchéng.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Zǔo Zōngtáng passed away,
and was posthumously granted the title of Grand Mentor.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
typhoon relief was provided in Fújiàn.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
an imperial decree appointed
Prince Chún as the chief administrator of naval affairs.
Yìkuāng and Lǐ Hóngzhāng were to assist.
Shànqìng, Manchu Commander of the Eight Banners, and Zēng Jìzé, Vice Minister of the Board of War, were to be assistant administrators.
The title of Fújiàn Governor was changed to Táiwān Governor,
and the duties of the Fújiàn Governor were transferred to the Governor-General of Mǐn-Zhè.
The British envoy came to discuss trade between India and Xīzàng.
An edict was issued to Dīng Bǎozhēn, Sèlèng'é, and others to guide the Tibetan barbarians not to cause trouble.
On the day Rén'yín,
Língguì passed away.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the office of Ili Counselor Minister was abolished,
and two Deputy Lieutenant-Generals were established instead.
The Manchu Banner Commander in Tǎ'ěrbāhātái was abolished,
while the Ölöt Banner Commander remained.
On the day Jiǎyín,
hail disaster relief was provided in Bīnchuān, Ēn'ān, and other places.
In winter, on the first day of the tenth month, Bǐngyín,
King Lǐ Xī of Cháoxiǎn, due to uneradicated bandits,
came to request pacification.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng dispatched troops to defend him.
On the day Wùchén,
disaster relief was provided in Cháoyáng.
On the day Gēngchén,
50,000 taels from next year's capital tribute silver were diverted for winter relief in Shāndōng.
On the day Xīnsì,
Yìkuāng and Xǔ Gēngshēn were ordered to exchange treaties with the French envoy.
Liú Ruìfēn was to exchange the Yāntái Treaty in the British capital,
and also discuss special provisions for foreign opium.
On the day Dīnghài,
Mùtúshàn was appointed Imperial Commissioner,
to train troops in conjunction with the generals of the Three Eastern Provinces,
exercising command over Deputy Lieutenant-Generals and below.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
50,000 taels of silver for annual imperial court expenses were allocated for disaster relief in Shāndōng.
Entry and exit through the Forbidden City gates were strictly controlled.
In the eleventh month, on the day Rén'yín,
prayers for snow were offered.
On the day Yǐsì,
an earthquake occurred in Yúnnán.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Hui officials in various cities of Xīnjiāng were dismissed.
On the day Guǐhài,
an imperial decree
ordered the Eight Banners' General-Commanders to eliminate various abuses in the banner garrisons.
Ēnchéng was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tǐrén Pavilion.
Yán Jìngmíng was appointed Grand Secretary of the Dōng Pavilion.
Fúkūn, Minister of the Board of Revenue, and Zhāng Zhīwàn, Minister of the Board of Punishments, were both appointed Associate Grand Secretaries.
Due to the British conquest of Miǎndiàn,
border defenses in Sìchuān were strengthened.
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
land telegraph lines were further established in Sānxìng and Hēilóngjiāng.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
an imperial edict prohibited the Internal Affairs Department from false reporting and extravagant waste.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the breach at Zhàozhuāng was closed.
This winter,
flood relief was provided in Cháozhōu and Wànxiàn,
and typhoon relief in Táiwān.
The poll tax on flooded land in Yǒngníng was remitted.
The land tax on abandoned and newly cultivated land in various prefectures and counties of Zhèjiāng was remitted.
Grain taxes on low-lying land in Wén'ān and Tiānjīn were reduced.
The silver tax on flooded land in Xúgōu and Fényáng was remitted.
In the twelfth year, in the spring, on the first day of the first month, Yǐwèi,
banquets were suspended.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
arrears of taxes in Húběi were remitted.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the breach at Zuīgōu in Shāndōng was closed.
Old arrears of tribute grain in Táiwān were remitted.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the fixed tax on drought-stricken land in Qítái was remitted.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Tè'ěrqìng'ā and others were ordered to train troops with Mùtúshàn.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
an imperial edict announced that due to the emperor's visit to the imperial tombs,
this year's Metropolitan Examination would commence on the tenth day of the third month.
In the second month, on the first day Yǐchǒu,
the Yellow River burst its southern bank in Shāndōng.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Zhāng Yào went to inspect the breach at Héwángzhuāng.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
arrears of fixed taxes on perennially flooded land in Mǎngpǔ were remitted.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Suíhuà Hall was established in Hēilóngjiāng.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, visited the Eastern Tombs.
Four-tenths of the taxes and grain tribute in the passing prefectures and counties were remitted.
In the third month, on the day Yǐwèi,
the imperial tombs were visited.
The emperor proceeded to the Dìngdōng Tombs.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
he returned from the Eastern Tombs.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
disaster relief was provided in Guǎngníng.
This month,
100,000 shí of new grain tribute from Shāndōng were reserved for flood victims in Héwángzhuāng, Zhāngqiū, Jìyáng, and Huìmín.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Zhào Yǐjiǒng and 339 others were granted the degree of Jìnshì and other ranks.
This month,
an earthquake occurred in Qiūběi and a fire in Guǎngxī Prefecture.
Relief was provided.
In the fifth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
over 400 indigenous communities in Táiwān,
comprising over 70,000 people, were assimilated.
Disaster relief was provided for wind and hail disasters in Líntóng and other counties.
On the day Rén'yín,
the Naval Commander-in-Chief of Yángjiāng Garrison was abolished,
and a Combined Naval and Land Commander-in-Chief of Běihǎi Garrison was established.
The Land Commander-in-Chief of Gāozhōu Garrison was changed to a Combined Naval and Land Commander-in-Chief.
In the sixth month, on the day Rénshēn,
an imperial decree
ordered the Qīntiānjian to select a date for the Emperor's assumption of personal rule in the first month of next year.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the seawall at Hǎiyán was repaired.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Prince Chún and the princely ministers jointly memorialized requesting the Empress Dowager to continue governing.
This was not permitted.
The Emperor's assumption of personal rule was set for the fifteenth day of the first month of next year.
Grand Councillors were ordered to convene and discuss
the reform of the currency system.
On the day Gēngchén,
Prince Chún and Prince Lǐ and others reiterated their request for the Empress Dowager to continue governing.
Shī Zhēn, Minister, and Guì Xián, Censor, also spoke in favor.
An imperial decree reluctantly agreed to it.
Prince Chún was ordered to continue managing various affairs.
In the seventh month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the *tǔsī* of Mùbāng requested to become part of the interior administration,
but this was refused.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Jīnshùn died.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
fifty thousand *shí* of grain tribute from Jiāngsū were retained to relieve disaster in Shùn[tiān] and Bǎo[dìng].
On the *yǐsì* day,
the currency reform proposals were finalized and submitted.
They were approved for implementation.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Tàiyuán and other counties.
In the eighth month, on the *rénxū* day,
Sèlēng'é was appointed as the General of Yīlí.
Relief was provided for flood victims in Rèhé.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Lǐ Qīnwáng and the court ministers requested to bestow an honorific title upon the Empress Dowager,
but an imperial decree forbade it.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
another fifty thousand *shí* of grain tribute from Jiāngběi were allocated to relieve flood victims in Shùntiān and Tōngzhōu,
and twenty thousand *liǎng* of treasury silver were also distributed to the victims,
and arrears of land tax on barren fields in Xiánníng, Shǎnxī, and other places were remitted.
On the *wùchén* day,
due to the overflowing of the North Grand Canal,
one hundred thousand *liǎng* of treasury silver were allocated for urgent relief in various prefectures of Yǒngpíng,
and another twenty thousand *liǎng* of imperial treasury silver were issued to supplement it.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the Tàipíng Guīshùn Circuit of Guǎngxī was newly established,
and the commander-in-chief was relocated to station in Lóngzhōu.
The Liǔqìng Garrison Commander-in-Chief was newly established and stationed in Liǔzhōu.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the breached embankment of the Báihé River in Huáiróu was repaired.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Censor Zhū Yīxīn memorialized on self-reflection in times of disaster,
and to prevent the abuses of eunuchs,
stating that when Chún Qīnwáng inspected Běiyáng,
the chief eunuch Lǐ Liányīng accompanied him,
fearing a repeat of the Tang dynasty's abuses by eunuch military supervisors.
An imperial decree ordered a re-memorialization.
Soon after, the memorial was resubmitted,
and he was demoted to *zhǔshì* for his mistaken insistence.
In the ninth month, on the *xīnmǎo* day, the first day of the month,
relief was provided for flood victims in Fèngtiān and Zhèjiāng.
On the *guǐsì* day,
relief was provided for hail and flood victims in Gānsù,
and flood victims in Liúbà and Nánzhèng.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
due to the floods in Shùn[tiān] and Zhí[lì], the land rent for various prefectures and banner estates, and other rental quotas, were reduced.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Bāo Chāo died.
On the *yǐsì* day,
relief was provided for hail victims in Guāngshān.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Liú Míngchuán suppressed the rebellious indigenous tribes in Sūlǔmǎnàbāng.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Shàngráo and other counties.
In the eleventh month, on the *gēngyín* day, the first day of the month,
the breach at Shòuzhāng was closed.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Xú Yánxù and Táng Jiǒng were pardoned for their crimes;
Xú Yánxù was exiled to Xīnjiāng,
and Táng Jiǒng to Yúnnán.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Zēng Jìzé was ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *gēngxū* day,
another thirty thousand *shí* of millet from the imperial granaries were allocated for spring relief in Shùntiān.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Winter Solstice,
a sacrifice to Heaven was offered at the Yuánqiū,
for the first time by the emperor himself.
The extra tax in Lóngkēchéng was remitted.
In the twelfth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
grain taxes on waterlogged land in Ānzhōu, Héjiān, and Lóngpíng were reduced.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
a prayer for snow was offered.
On the *gēngchén* day,
an imperial decree again instructed Zēng Guóquán and others to thoroughly deliberate on methods for managing the rivers of Liǎngjiāng.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the combined sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn offered tribute.
In the thirteenth year, in spring, the first month, on the *jǐchǒu* day, the first day of the month,
banquets were suspended.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
on account of assuming personal rule, officials were dispatched to announce to Heaven, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the gods of Soil and Grain,
and to pray for harvest to the Lord on High.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the emperor began personal rule,
issuing an imperial edict to the entire realm,
granting various degrees of universal grace.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
one hundred thousand *shí* of grain tribute from Jiāngsū were allocated to relieve disaster victims in Shùn[tiān] and Zhí[lì].
An imperial decree ordered the purchase of machinery in Tiānjīn for minting coins,
with one *wén* equating to one *qián* by standard,
and no discrepancies allowed between the capital and the provinces.
In the second month, on the *rénxū* day,
it rained and snowed.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Gōngtáng was reprimanded and ordered to vigorously suppress horse bandits,
and to reorganize the existing trained army.
The construction of telegraph lines connecting Chuān and Diān was completed.
On the *wùchén* day,
sacrifices were offered to the Great Altar of Soil and the Great Altar of Grain.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Táng Jiǒng was granted the title of巡撫 (*xúnfǔ*) [governor],
to oversee mining affairs in Yúnnán.
This month,
an imperial decree granted Chún Qīnwáng the hereditary rank of *qīnwáng* without limitation,
and he was still to be consulted on important national affairs.
In the third month, on the *jǐchǒu* day, the first day of the month,
the emperor first visited the Fèngxiān Diàn to perform rites.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, visited the Xīlíng,
and three-tenths of the allocated taxes for the passing prefectures and counties were remitted.
On the *jǐhài* day,
they visited the imperial tombs.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
they returned from Xīlíng.
On the *xīnsì* day,
a sacrifice was offered to Xiānnóng,
and the emperor personally tilled the sacrificial field,
completing three furrows,
and added one more furrow,
making this a regular practice from this year onwards.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Liú Jǐntáng requested to resign his post to visit his parents and seek medical treatment,
but this was not allowed;
he was granted three months' leave,
to recuperate in his post.
Eighty thousand *liǎng* of treasury silver from the Zhí[lì] provincial treasury were allocated to relieve famine victims in its jurisdiction.
Land rent on barren land in Wén'ān and other places was remitted.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *wùwǔ* day, the first day of the month,
a banquet was held at the Tàimiào.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Lín Wéiyuán, a侍讀學士 (*shìdú xuéshì*) of the Grand Secretariat, was ordered to supervise the construction of railways and commercial affairs in Táiwān.
On the *jǐsì* day,
a prayer for rain was offered.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the regular *yú* sacrifice was held,
a sacrifice to Heaven at the Yuánqiū.
In the intercalary fourth month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
arrears of taxes and levies in various prefectures and counties of Jiāngsū were remitted.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Kūnmíng and other counties.
In the fifth month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
Summer Solstice,
a sacrifice to Earth was offered at the Fāngzé.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Hóng Jūn, former Grand Secretariat Academician, was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to Russia, Germany, and Austria-Hungary,
and Liú Ruìfēn, Grand Judge, was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to Great Britain, France, Italy, and Belgium.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Lǒngzhōu and other places.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
it rained.
In the sixth month, on the *dīnghài* day, the first day of the month,
relief was provided for flood victims in Fùyáng and its various jurisdictions.
On the *yǐsì* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Huáiníng and other counties.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the Dàxīnzhuāng River in Kāizhōu overflowed,
inundating parts of Shāndōng;
fifty thousand *shí* of new grain tribute were retained to relieve disaster victims in Púzhōu and other places.
On the *gēngxū* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Luótián and Shíshǒu.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Wēnsù and Wūshén.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
relief was provided for wind and hail victims in Língyún.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *bǐngchén* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the Yǒngdìnghé and Cháobáihé Rivers both overflowed one after another.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
a new Garrison Commander-in-Chief for Pēnghú, Fújiàn, was established.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Nányáng and other places.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
long-standing arrears of silver, grain, and miscellaneous taxes owed by the common people in Gānsù were remitted.
Relief was provided for hail victims in Tàozhōu and its various jurisdictions.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the Lín'ān Kāiguǎng Circuit of Yúnnán was newly established.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Lǐ bandits were pacified.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Dàoyuán Lí Shùchāng was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to Japan.
In the eighth month, on the day *wùzǐ*,
sacrifices were offered to the Great Earth God and the Great Grain God.
On the day *jiǎchén*,
the Qìn Hé burst its banks.
Relief was provided for flood victims in Píngyí.
On the day *bǐngwǔ*,
Mǐnyáng and other prefectures and counties suffered from floods.
Three hundred thousand *shí* of winter grain tribute were retained for relief.
The Hé burst its banks in Zhèngzhōu,
flowing south into the Huái.
Hé Dū Chéng Fú was stripped of his office
but remained in his post.
On the day *jǐyǒu*,
fifty thousand *shí* of grain tribute from the Imperial Granary were allocated for relief in Shùntiān and Tōngzhōu and their subordinate areas.
Three hundred thousand *liǎng* of silver, converted from the capital's grain tribute, were retained for relief in Hénán.
On the day *guǐchǒu*,
an imperial decree ordered the release of one hundred thousand *liǎng* of silver from the imperial private treasury for flood relief.
In the ninth month, on the first day *yǐmǎo*,
arrears of tribute from the previous year were remitted for all prefectures, departments, subprefectures, and counties in Shǎnxī.
On the day *xīnyǒu*,
due to the burst of the Hé in Zhèngzhōu,
the grain tribute and transport fees for next year from Jiāngběi and Jiāngsū were pre-allocated for relief.
On the day *xīnwèi*,
permission was granted for Ràngzhēng Hútúkètú to bring tribute.
On the day *yǐhài*,
Xuē Yǔnshēng was ordered to Hénán to inspect the Zhèngzhōu river works.
On the day *dīngchǒu*,
Lǐ Hóngzǎo went to Hénán to jointly inspect the river works.
This month,
relief was provided for floods in Wǔzhì, Ān Xiàn, Yúnyáng, and northern Wǎn,
floods in Hànkǒu and Lóngzhōu,
and hail disasters in Jiànshuǐ and Tōnghǎi.
In winter, the tenth month, on the first day *jiǎshēn*,
relief was provided for a fire disaster in Róng Xiàn.
On the day *dīnghài*,
Féng Zǐcái resigned due to illness.
He was ordered to remain in Guǎngdōng to manage the defense of Qīnzhōu and Liánzhōu.
He requested retirement,
but it was not granted.
On the day *jǐchǒu*,
relief was provided for wind disasters in Huìzhōu, Gāozhōu, Liánzhōu, Léizhōu, Qióngzhōu, Chìxī, and Yángjiāng.
On the day *jǐhài*,
Mùtúshàn died.
Food rations were distributed to poor civilians in disaster areas such as Zhèngzhōu.
On the day *rényín*,
Shànqìng was appointed Fúzhōu General,
assisting in naval affairs
and concurrently managing the Shénjīyíng.
Autumn tribute was remitted for flood-affected prefectures and counties in Shùnzhí.
On the day *yǐsì*,
relief was provided for a snow disaster in Zhènxī Tīng.
On the day *wùshēn*,
His Majesty attended to Her Imperial Majesty the Empress Dowager to visit Chún Qīnwáng who was ill.
From then on, he frequently visited the sick,
until the seventh month of next year when he recovered.
On the day *gēngxū*,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Cháng'ān and its subordinate areas.
On the day *guǐchǒu*,
relief was provided for a frost disaster in Suīlái.
In the eleventh month, on the day *yǐmǎo*,
Dìng'ān was appointed Imperial Commissioner,
to jointly manage military training with the Generals of the Three Eastern Provinces,
exercising authority over those below the rank of Vice Commander.
On the day *xīnyǒu*,
on the winter solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Yuánqiū.
On the day *rénxū*,
Wénshuò was instructed to search for the Húbìlèhǎn,
and draw lots according to the established system.
On the day *rénshēn*,
prayers for snow were offered.
In the twelfth month, on the day *dīnghài*,
Lǐ Hóngzǎo was ordered to supervise the Zhèngzhōu river works.
On the day *jǐchǒu*,
the fixed tribute for barren land in Ēnlóng, Bǎisè, and other places was abolished.
Relief was provided for fire disasters in Guìlín and other places.
On the day *rénchén*,
tax arrears were remitted for disaster-affected counties such as Yángchéng.
On the day *dīngyǒu*,
there was rain and snow.
On the day *wùxū*,
an imperial decree restored Yán Jìngmíng, Fúkūn, Wēng Tónghé, Sōngshēn, Sūn Yíjīng, Jǐngshàn, and Sūn Jiānài to their positions after their punishments.
On the day *gēngzǐ*,
due to the disaster in northern Wǎn,
one hundred thousand *liǎng* of silver, consisting of the Ānhuī grain tribute conversion and the regular taxes from Wúhú Customs, were allocated
for next year's spring relief.
On the day *xīnchǒu*,
the Yītǎ Dào, Yīlí Fǔ, Huò'ěrguǒsī Tīng, and Tǎchéng Tīng were established in Xīnjiāng,
and officials such as Dào, Fǔ, Fǔmín Tōngpàn, and Tóngzhī were appointed.
On the day *rényín*,
Shípíng and Jiànshuǐ experienced earthquakes.
On the day *jǐyǒu*,
fifty thousand *shí* of winter grain tribute from Shāndōng were allocated for Hénán's winter relief next year.
This year,
Cháoxiǎn brought tribute.
In the fourteenth year, the *wùzǐ* spring, the first month, on the first day *guǐchǒu*,
His Majesty personally went to the Tángzǐ to perform rites.
On the day *bǐngchén*,
there was snow.
Summer grain taxes were remitted for flood-affected prefectures and counties in Ānhuī, such as Tàihé.
On the day *jǐwèi*,
the Mòhé gold mine in Hēilóngjiāng was opened.
On the day *gēngshēn*,
the Chānghuà malachite copper mine in Guǎngdōng was opened.
On the day *xīnyǒu*,
the telegraph line from Téngyuè to Yúnnán Shěngyuán was extended.
On the day *yǐhài*,
Liú Jǐntáng requested leave due to illness.
He was persuaded to stay,
and granted another four months of leave.
On the day *rénwǔ*,
an imperial edict ordered the official casting of "ten cash" coins,
those weighing two *qián* or more each
were to be circulated uniformly.
This month,
a total of one hundred and thirty thousand *shí* of grain tribute, retained from the Imperial Granary and transported by sea, were allocated for disaster relief in Shùnzhí.
In the second month, on the day *yǐyǒu*,
relief was provided for a fire disaster in Wúzhōu.
On the day *bǐngxū*,
Péi Yīnsēn was granted the third-rank *Jīngtáng* title,
to supervise the Fújiàn Naval Administration.
On the day *gēngyín*,
Wénshuò was stripped of his office
for unauthorizedly submitting a secret memorial draft to the Dūcháyuan.
On the day *xīnhài*,
sacrifices were offered to Xiannóng,
and His Majesty personally ploughed the sacrificial field.
This month,
an imperial edict ordered the renovation of the Yíhéyuán,
in preparation for Her Imperial Majesty the Empress Dowager's visit.
In the third month, on the day *bǐngchén*,
arrears of tribute from before Guāngxù year five were remitted for Zhèjiāng.
On the day *bǐngyín*,
Hádá, prayer beads, and *rúyì* were bestowed upon the reincarnation Húbìlèhǎn of the Bānchán É'ěrdéní.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day *gēngyín*,
the breach in the Yǒngdìng Hé was closed.
On the day *xīnmǎo*,
His Majesty accompanied Her Imperial Majesty the Empress Dowager on their first visit to Xīyuàn.
On the day *jiǎwǔ*,
the Guǎngdōng telegraph line was extended from Jiǔjiāng to Dàyǔlǐng.
On the day *dīngyǒu*,
there was rain and hail.
On the day *xīnhài*,
Zhāng Yào was ordered to assist in naval affairs.
Relief was provided for flood disasters in Huìzhōu and its subordinate areas.
In the fifth month, on the day *yǐmǎo*,
Jīngshī, Fèngtiān, and Shāndōng experienced earthquakes.
On the day *guǐhài*,
on the summer solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Earth at the Fāngzé.
On the day *dīngmǎo*,
prayers for rain were offered.
In the sixth month, on the day *guǐsì*,
there was rain.
On the day *jǐhài*,
an imperial decree stated
that the Emperor's grand wedding ceremony
would be held in the first month of next year.
On the day *jiǎchén*,
Péng Yùlín was relieved of his post as Minister of War due to illness,
but continued his inspection of the Chángjiāng naval forces as before.
On the day *rényín*,
an imperial decree stated
that the abdication of power would take place on the third day of the second month of next year.
In the seventh month, on the day *gēngshēn*,
due to delays in river works,
Lǐ Hóngzǎo and Ní Wénwèi were stripped of their offices
but remained in their posts.
Lǐ Hènián and Chéng Fú were exiled to military garrisons.
On the day *jiǎzǐ*,
the Yǒngdìng Hé burst its banks again.
On the day *bǐngyín*,
Yán Jìngmíng was dismissed.
On the day *dīngchǒu*,
Wú Dàchéng was instructed to inspect and verify the river works.
This month,
the Jīngū Railway was completed.
In the eighth month, on the day *dīnghài*,
relief was provided for various departments, subprefectures, and counties in Fèngtiān,
and flood-affected counties in Ānhuī such as Huáiníng.
On the day *jǐchǒu*,
an imperial edict ordered the clearance of minor cases in the directly governed provinces.
On the day *rénchén*,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Cāngwú and other places.
On the day *dīngyǒu*,
the Jiāngběi grain tribute was retained for relief in Sūzhōu and Wǎn.
On the day *yǐsì*,
Chún Qīnwáng, as the date of abdication of power was approaching,
requested to be relieved of his duties.
An imperial decree stated
that the Ministry of Naval Affairs and the Shénjīyíng would continue under his management as before,
but after the abdication of power, his memorials should not bear his official title.
In the ninth month, on the day *bǐngchén*,
last year's tribute arrears in Shǎnxī were remitted.
On the day *jiǎxū*,
the breach in the Yǒngdìng Hé was closed.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day, the new moon began.
Sacrifices were offered at the Tàimiào.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
an imperial decree appointed Lady Yèhènàlā as Empress.
On the *guǐsì* day,
20,000 *shí* of capital grain tribute were allocated for winter relief in Shùntiān Prefecture.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the poll tax and land tax in Shuǐchéng and other places were remitted.
Relief was provided for drought in Dāntú and floods in Nánchāng and other counties.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the *lí* tax on Korean red ginseng was remitted.
In the eleventh month, on the *rénxū* day,
the telegraph line connecting the Diānyuè border with China and France was completed.
The position of Běiyáng Naval Admiral was established for the first time,
and Dīng Rǔchāng was appointed to it.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
on the winter solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Huánqiū Altar.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the New Year's court felicitations were remitted.
On the *wùchén* day,
land rent in Jìnghǎi for areas with standing water was remitted.
In the twelfth month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
relief was provided for plague in Āmí, Méngzì, and other places.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
an imperial edict announced that the *Ēnkē Xiāngshì* (Imperial Examination at the provincial level) would be held in the fifteenth year of Guāngxù's reign,
and the *Ēnkē Huìshì* (Imperial Examination at the metropolitan level) in the sixteenth year.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
additional officials, including a General Commandant, were appointed for the Jílín Naval Camp.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Tàihémén suffered a disaster.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
an imperial edict called for self-reflection and reform,
and commanded officials and workers to diligently perform their duties.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the arrears of money and grain from the previous year owed by the people of Shǎnxī were remitted.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
an imperial decree
ordered the suspension and reduction of work at the Yíhéyuán due to floods.
Censor Yú Liányuán, Tú Rénshǒu, and Hóng Liángpǐn each submitted memorials requesting the cessation of railway construction.
Xú Huìfēng and others submitted proposals.
All were sent down to the Hǎijūnshǔ (Naval Ministry) to be discussed with the Jūnjīdàchén (Grand Councilors).
Soon after, Wēng Tónghé, Kuí Rùn, Yóu Bǎichuān, Wén Zhì, and others also stated that railways should not be built.
These were also sent down for deliberation.
Lín Wéiyuán, Assistant Minister of the Tàipú Temple, was ordered to assist in the land reclamation and pacification of aboriginals in Táiwān.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
relief was provided for flood disaster in Wēiyuǎn Tīng.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Circuit Intendant Xú Chéngzǔ, who had previously served as envoy to Japan,
was found guilty of embezzlement,
stripped of his post for investigation,
and his property confiscated.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the breach at Zhèngzhōu was closed.
Wú Dàchéng was appointed Governor-General of River Conservancy for Héngdōng (east of the Yellow River).
Lǐ Hóngzǎo and Ní Wénwèi were restored to their original posts,
and received special commendations.
Chéng Fú and Lǐ Hènián were released and returned.
In the fifteenth year, *jǐchǒu*, in spring, in the first month, on the *dīngwèi* day, the new moon began.
Banquets were suspended.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
an earthquake occurred in Jìngyuǎn and Gāolán.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Zhāng Zhīwàn was appointed Grand Secretary of the Dōnggé.
Xú Tóng, as Minister of the Board of Civil Office, assisted in the duties of a Grand Secretary.
The Hǎijūnshǔ, together with the Jūnjī, deliberated on and rejected the various memorials requesting the cessation of railways,
and then requested further detailed deliberation.
An imperial decree stated:
"Qìngyù, Dìng'ān, Zēng Guóquán, Zhāng Zhīdòng, Huáng Péngnián, and others,
according to the current situation,
each submit their views for consideration."
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Dūn Qīnwáng passed away.
The Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, offered condolences.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Censor Tú Rénshǒu submitted a memorial stating:
"The Emperor's assumption of full power is imminent,
and the affairs of the time are urgent.
For secret memorials,
I request that they still be addressed to the Empress Dowager for her imperial perusal,
and actions be taken after her review."
An imperial decree denounced his absurdity,
dismissed him from his position as Censor,
sent his case to the appropriate board for deliberation,
and returned the original memorial.
On the *wùchén* day,
Censor Lín Shàonián requested a ban on provincial governors and governors-general making voluntary contributions.
An imperial decree rebuked him.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Grand Wedding ceremony was completed.
In the second month, on the *wùyín* day,
Wú Dàchéng requested an imperial edict to deliberate on the ceremony for honoring Chún Qīnwáng.
An imperial decree rebuked him,
and widely circulated the message to officials and common people both inside and outside the capital.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Empress Dowager officially relinquished political power.
The Emperor ascended the Tàihédiàn to receive felicitations,
and issued an imperial edict to the empire.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
various taxes and grain levies for areas affected by disaster in Jiāng and Huái during the early years of Guāngxù's reign were remitted.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
due to floods in Qídōng and other prefectures and counties,
50,000 *liǎng* from the Shāndōng provincial treasury were allocated for relief.
On the *rénchén* day,
additional honorific titles were bestowed upon the Empress Dowager,
and an imperial edict granting extensive favors with differing degrees was issued.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Cháoxiān congratulated on the Empress Dowager's relinquishment of power,
presented local products,
and bestowed silk fabrics upon its king and queen.
In the third month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day, the new moon began.
Lecturer Cuī Guóyīn was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to America, Japan, and Peru.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Péng Yùlín resigned from his post as Imperial Inspector.
A warm imperial edict consoled him and asked him to stay.
A river breach occurred in Púzhōu.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
as Chief Bùlǔkèbā assimilated,
he was granted a title, a seal, and an imperial edict.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
20,000 *liǎng* from the Hēilóngjiāng provincial treasury were allocated to further aid flood victims in the Hūlán region.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Empress offered sacrifices to the Goddess of Silkworms.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
additional honorific titles were again bestowed upon the Empress Dowager.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
taxes and grain levies for villages and strongholds in Yúnnán affected by bandits were remitted.
On the *wùchén* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, visited the Yíhéyuán,
and observed naval and land drills.
Yán Jìngmíng was permitted to return to his hometown to recuperate.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *wùyín* day,
100,000 *shí* of southern grain tribute were allocated for relief in Shāndōng.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
relief was provided for disaster victims in Fèngtiān and Jílín.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Xuē Fúchéng, Judicial Commissioner of Húnán, was granted a third-rank metropolitan official position,
and appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to Great Britain, France, Italy, and Belgium.
An imperial decree allocated 100,000 *liǎng* of silver from the imperial treasury for relief in Shāndōng.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Zhāng Jiànxūn and 330 other individuals were granted the *jìnshì jí dì* degree and other varying degrees.
In the fifth month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
autumn executions were suspended.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
relief was provided for fire disaster in Lúzhōu.
In the sixth month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Cén Yùyīng passed away.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Wáng Wénsháo was appointed Governor-General of Yúnnán and Guìzhōu.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Tàihémén was reconstructed.
On the *dīnghài* day,
relief was provided for fire disaster in Zhōujiākǒu.
On the *rénchén* day,
there was a breach in the Yǒngdìnghé River.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng recommended capable officials for the task.
The Emperor suspected a shift of power to Kuíbǐng,
and issued a reprimand.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
a river breach occurred in Zhāngqiū.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the fixed tax quota for Xīliángshān in Guìzhōu was abolished.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
a river breach occurred in Qíhé.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
a river breach occurred in Qìnhé.
In this month,
relief was provided for hail disaster in Jǔzhōu and Yíshuǐ,
flood disaster in Zhōujiākǒu,
and flood and hail disasters in Cháng'ān, Xīxiāng, and Fūzhōu.
Relief was provided for flood disasters in Kūnyáng and Tàihé in Yúnnán,
and Huòqiū and other prefectures and counties in Ānhuī.
In the eighth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng and Zhāng Zhīdòng were ordered to jointly plan the Lúhàn Railway with the Hǎijūnshǔ.
On the *dīnghài* day,
100,000 *shí* of new grain tribute were kept aside for relief in Shāndōng.
On the *rénchén* day,
due to floods in Sìchuān,
50,000 *liǎng* were donated for disaster relief.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the Qíniándiàn in the Tiāntán suffered a disaster.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
relief was provided for earthquake disaster in Yīlí, Suídìng, and other places.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
uncollected taxes and arrears of money and grain from the people in prefectures, departments, subprefectures, counties, and garrisons in Guìzhōu that had been affected by bandits were remitted.
In the ninth month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
the Qíniándiàn was reconstructed.
Relief was provided for wind and flood disasters in Wēnzhōu and other places.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
arrears of tribute from the previous year for various localities in Shǎnxī were remitted.
Relief was provided for flood and hail disasters in Xiánníng and other places.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Gāolán and other places.
On the *rénchén* day,
the dike at Chángyuán breached,
and the Yellow River water inundated Huáxiàn.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
an edict instructed Dìng'ān and others to eliminate malpractices in military training in the Three Eastern Provinces.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
it was decided that the prayer for good harvests next year would temporarily be held at the Huánqiū Altar.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
relief was provided for hail and flood disasters in Yángqǔ and other areas.
On the *wùyín* day,
a telegraph line was established from Xī'ān to Jiāyùguān.
Relief was provided for flood disasters in the prefectures of Hángzhōu, Jiāxīng, and Húzhōu.
On the *dīnghài* day,
due to rain disasters in Jiāngsū and Zhèjiāng,
each province was allocated 50,000 *liǎng* from their provincial treasuries,
and an additional 50,000 *liǎng* from the imperial household's private funds were disbursed for relief.
Regarding Zhāng Zhīdòng's ordering of machinery,
and his hasty signing of contracts,
an imperial edict sternly rebuked him.
Henceforth, for any new undertakings,
unless first reported to the throne,
no rash actions should be taken.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
100,000 *liǎng* from the Wǔchāng treasury was allocated to Húběi for disaster relief.
On the *rénchén* day,
an imperial edict reaffirmed that the two provincial commissioners (*liǎngsī*) in each province should continue to report to the throne via sealed memorials.
There was a rebellion by indigenous tribes in Táiwān.
Vice General Liú Cháodài and others died in battle.
Liú Míngchuán was ordered to suppress and handle the matter.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
an additional 150,000 *liǎng* from the Zhèjiāng treasury was allocated for relief in Hángzhōu, Jiāxīng, and Húzhōu.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Dàzhài River embankment project in Shāndōng was closed.
On the *rényín* day,
remaining funds from Sūzhōu and Ānhuī disaster donations were allocated to repair the Grand Canal.
Relief was provided for hail and flood disasters in Suídé and other prefectures.
In the eleventh month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
the Ministry of Revenue's request was granted for the Naval Yámen
to receive an annual allocation of 2,000,000 *liǎng* to initiate railway construction.
On the *dīngsì* day,
an imperial edict ordered the reduction of redundant officials
and the elimination of extravagant expenses.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
30,000 *liǎng* of grain transport commutation silver from Ānhuī was allocated for relief in Ānqìng, Níngguó, and Sīzhōu.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Zhèjiāng distributed grain from its Ever-Normal Granaries for the relief of disaster victims in Tiāntái, Xiānjū, and other areas.
In the twelfth month, on the *rénshēn* day, the first day of the month,
the collection of grain transport tribute, white rice tribute, and land and poll taxes due from Hángzhōu, Jiāxīng, and Húzhōu was remitted.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
40,000 *shí* of Shāndōng grain transport tribute rice was retained for relief.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
an additional 50,000 *liǎng* from the Wǔchāng treasury was allocated for Húběi disaster relief.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the breach at Xīzhǐfáng in Shāndōng was closed.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the accumulation of malpractices in the administration of remissions and deferments was strictly prohibited.
Taxes and levies were remitted for villages and stockades in Yúnnán affected by bandit disturbances.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
taxes and levies were remitted for Zhèngzhōu, Huáiníng, Wèishì, and other prefectures and counties.
Taxes and levies were remitted for Ránhé and other counties,
and the grain tax for the Hángzhōu and Yánzhōu Garrisons.
This year,
Cháoxiǎn paid tribute.
In the sixteenth year, the *gēngyín* year, in spring, in the first month, on the *rényín* day, the first day of the month,
banquets were suspended.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
salt taxes from before the thirteenth year in Zhílì were remitted.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
an edict declared that there was no need to offer sacrifices for the Empress Dowager's birthday this year,
the ascension ceremony was suspended,
and senior civil and military officials from all provinces were exempted from coming to the capital to offer congratulations.
In the second month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
Zhāng Yào reported that the total estimated cost for the Shāndōng river works was 2,880,000 *liǎng* and more.
The responsible authorities were ordered to raise the funds.
On the *rénchén* day,
Yǒu Mǐn and other chieftains of indigenous communities in the interior of Táiwān were executed.
This month,
arrears of taxes from the thirteenth year were remitted for Yúlín and other prefectures and counties.
Taxes on official lands in Dōngchuān affected by floods were remitted.
Arrears of rent from ponds and lakes in Wén'ān, Jìnghǎi, and Bàzhōu, and land taxes from Bódūnà were remitted.
In the intercalary second month, on the *rényín* day,
relief was provided for fire disasters in various prefectures of Guìlín.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Zhāng Yīnhuán, Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud (*Tàipúsì Qīng*), was ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, visited the Eastern Tombs (*Dōnglíng*),
and three-tenths of the land tax was remitted in the areas they passed through.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the Emperor personally offered sacrifices at the garden tomb of Crown Prince Duānhuì.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Emperor returned from the Eastern Tombs.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Zēng Jìzé passed away,
and he was subsequently granted a special posthumous title.
An edict instructed Lǐ Hóngzhāng to reorganize the Běiyáng land and naval forces,
and Dìng Ān and others to train troops in the Three Eastern Provinces.
In the third month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
an imperial decree from the Empress Dowager stated
that Liú Míngchuán was to assist in naval affairs.
There was an earthquake in Xīníng,
and relief was provided.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
for the Empress Dowager's sixtieth birthday,
an imperial edict was issued throughout the empire,
granting varying degrees of grace.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Southern Lake (*Nánhú*) in Yúháng was dredged.
The Zhānduì chieftain Sā Lāyǒngzhū colluded with Bā Zōng Lǎma and wild tribes to rebel.
Government troops suppressed them.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *gēngyín* day,
Péng Yùlín passed away.
On the *gēngxū* day,
an edict ordered the reorganization of the native medicine tax (*tǔyào shuìlí*).
Gāng Yì was ordered to thoroughly investigate the production and actual tax revenue of native medicine in Xúzhōu,
and to strictly formulate regulations for its reorganization.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Wú Lǔ and 336 other individuals were granted the *jìnshì* degree with various ranks.
In the fifth month, on the *jǐsì* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Sèlèng'é passed away,
and Cháng Gēng was appointed General of Yīlí.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Shēng Tài was appointed Resident Minister in Xīzàng.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor went to the Dàgāo Hall to pray for rain.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor reviewed the guards' archery skills from the Huàfǎng Zhāi.
This continued until the *rénchén* day.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
it rained.
Stone dams were constructed along the river in Wénxiāng.
Relief was provided for wind disasters in Huáiníng and other counties.
In the sixth month, on the *jǐhài* day, the first day of the month,
over 2,000 households of villagers along the river in various prefectures and counties of Qídōng were relocated.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the Sānxìng gold mine was opened.
On the *wùshēn* day,
as the affairs in Xīzàng had been settled,
an imperial edict and seal were granted to Bùlǔkèbā, the tribal chief.
From the *guǐmǎo* day to the *jǐyǒu* day, prayers for clear weather were offered continuously.
On the *xīnhài* day,
heavy rain caused disasters in the imperial domain (*jìnjī*).
Porridge kitchens were additionally set up outside the six gates of the capital.
An order was given to allocate 15,000 *shí* of rice from the imperial granaries for cooking and relief,
and 50,000 *liǎng* from the imperial household's private funds were disbursed for relief.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the Yǒngdìng River breached its banks.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Zhāng Tiānxī, a chieftain of the local gentry in Yǒngběi, plotted rebellion.
Government troops attacked and executed him.
On the *dīngsì* day,
tribute grain from Fèngtiān designated for the capital,
and retained grain transport tribute rice from Jiāngběi,
were allocated for disaster relief in Tiānjīn.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Empress Dowager's birthday,
the Emperor received congratulations in the Qiánqīng Palace.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the *yǐhài* day,
the local ethnic groups in Zhènkāng rebelled,
and they were suppressed.
An imperial edict rebuked Lǐ Hóngzhāng for failing to close the breach in the Yǒngdìng River.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
50,000 *liǎng* from the imperial treasury,
500,000 strings of large coins,
and 100,000 *shí* of rice
were issued for disaster relief in various prefectures of Shùntiān.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
an edict strictly punished those who embezzled or defrauded relief funds.
On the *gēngyín* day,
a total of 300,000 *liǎng* from the Board of Revenue's treasury and customs silver were allocated
to aid the Yǒngdìng River project.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Xǔ Jǐngchéng, a Reader of the Hànlín Academy, was appointed Minister to Russia, Germany, and Austria,
and Dáoyuán Lǐ Jīngfāng was appointed Minister to Japan.
Relief was provided for flood disasters in Húběi, Guǎngxī, Shǎnxī, and Yúnnán.
In the eighth month, on the *rényín* day,
an additional 100,000 *shí* of rice from the imperial granaries was allocated for Shùntiān disaster relief.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Emperor visited the residence of Prince Chún to inquire about his illness.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Liú Jǐntáng requested to return home.
He was still granted leave.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
due to Liú Míngchuán's unauthorized establishment of commercial mines
and flawed regulations,
an edict ordered him to stop,
and the matter was referred to the ministries for deliberation.
On the *dīngsì* day,
50,000 *shí* of grain transport tribute rice was retained,
and 100,000 *liǎng* from the provincial treasury was allocated
for Shāndōng relief.
On the *rénxū* day,
due to the floods in Shùn and Zhílì,
an edict ordered the reduction of rents on the estates of princes, dukes, and capital banner families.
This month,
arrears of taxes in Shǎnxī and Jiāngxī were remitted.
Relief was provided for flood and hail disasters in Shǎnxī,
flood disasters in Yúnnán,
and wind disasters in Táiwān.
In the ninth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
the Board of Revenue reported a deficit of 150,000 *shí* of stipendiary grain in the granaries.
The Assistant Ministers of Granaries and Grain Transport, Xīnglián and Yóu Bǎichuān, were subjected to departmental deliberation,
and soon after, both were stripped of their positions.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Húnchūn and Nínggǔtǎ.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Censor Wú Zhàotài requested the halt of the Summer Palace (*Yíhéyuán*) project,
and was subjected to severe reprimand.
The breach in the Yǒngdìng River was sealed.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
relief was provided for hail disasters in Gānsù.
On the *rénchén* day,
secret society members caused unrest in Shídài,
and it was suppressed.
On the *guǐsì* day,
funds from the Board's treasury and granary rice were allocated to Shùntiān for disaster relief.
In the tenth month of winter, on the *dīngwèi* day,
Liú Kūnyī was appointed Governor-General of the Two Jiāngs and concurrently Minister Superintendent of Southern Ocean Trade (*Nányáng Dàchén*).
On the *gēngxū* day,
Zēng Guóquán passed away,
and was posthumously granted the title of Grand Tutor (*Tàifù*).
On the *xīnhài* day,
another 50,000 *shí* of imperial granary rice were allocated for disaster relief in Shùntiān.
Miscellaneous grain taxes and levies were exempted for merchants and peddlers in Fèngtiān, Zhílì, Lǔ, and Yù.
In the eleventh month, on the *yǐhài* day,
relief was provided for flood-affected prefectures and counties in Húnán.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, visited the residence of Prince Chún to inquire about his illness.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Prince Chún passed away.
Court was suspended for seven days.
The Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, visited the residence to attend the laying out of the coffin.
The Empress Dowager bestowed a sacrificial offering.
Prince Zǎifēng, Duke of the First Rank (*Zhènguó Gōng*), was commanded to immediately inherit the princely title.
The Emperor entered mourning attire.
An Imperial Edict decreed his title as
"Emperor's Biological Father" (*Huángdì Běnshēng Kǎo*).
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
an Imperial Edict bestowed the posthumous title Xián.
The Emperor observed a year of mourning.
In the twelfth month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
an Imperial Edict promoted Prince Zǎixún, Duke of the Second Rank (*Fǔguó Gōng*), to Duke of the First Rank (*Zhènguó Gōng*) with eight privileges,
and Prince Zǎitáo, Commander of the First Rank (*Zhènguó Jiāngjūn*), to Duke of the Second Rank (*Fǔguó Gōng*) without eight privileges.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the golden coffin of Prince Chúnxián was moved to the garden residence.
The Emperor saw it off to Shìyuán.
On the *rénxū* day,
the Nányuàn project was postponed.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
arrears of taxes from the early Guāngxù reign were remitted for various prefectures, departments, and counties in Zhèjiāng.
In the first month of spring of the 17th year, *xīnmǎo*, on the *guǐsì* day,
Yi rebels in Léibō, Sìchuān, submitted.
In the second month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
160,000 *shí* of sea-transported grain were retained for spring relief in Shùn-Zhí.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Censor Gāo Xièzēng requested the implementation of daily lectures (*rìjiǎng*).
An edict stated that it would be a name without substance,
and did not accept it.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng and Zhāng Yào were ordered to jointly review the Běiyáng Navy.
Liú Jǐntáng resigned due to mourning.
Táo Mó was appointed Governor of Xīnjiāng.
Bandits rebelled in Yúnnán,
capturing Fùmín and Lùquàn county seats,
and they were suppressed.
This month,
arrears of taxes from before the 13th year were remitted for Húběi and Shānxī.
In the third month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
an edict was issued to provide funds for the return of refugees to their hometowns.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Empress offered sacrifices to the Ancestral Silkworm Goddess.
On the *rénshēn* day,
river works in various prefectures and counties including Bǎodí, Tōng, and Jì were repaired.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was ordered to supervise the construction of the Guāndōng Railway.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Shākèdōulínzhábù was ordered to inspect the Hābā River with Érqìng'é.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Liú Míngchuán was relieved of his duties due to illness.
In the fourth month of summer, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
a temple for Prince Chúnxián was established.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the ancestral shrine was rebuilt.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the Summer Palace (*Yíhéyuán*) project was completed.
The Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, began visiting it from this time.
From the *dīngmǎo* day to the *gēngwǔ* day in the fifth month, it rained continuously.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Empress personally performed sericulture.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
relief was provided for wind disasters in Qīngjiāng and other places.
This month,
locusts appeared in the capital region (*Jīngjī*).
The Zǒnglǐ Yámén reported that missionary cases were occurring repeatedly in various provinces,
and requested strict handling.
An edict stated:
"The propagation of foreign religions
is stipulated in treaties.
Merchants, common people, and missionaries
in all provinces must vigorously protect their persons and property.
However, the burning of churches
is occurring simultaneously.
It is clear that bandits are spreading rumors and creating trouble.
All governors-general and governors shall arrest and punish them,
so that no one is disturbed or harmed."
In the sixth month, on the *wùxū* day,
an edict was issued for the strict apprehension of secret society members.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an imperial decree granted amnesty to secret society members who surrendered themselves and to those who secretly reported bandit leaders, leading to their apprehension.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Wáng Wénsháo memorialized for the execution of Bāo Hǔ, a colonel (*cāncún*) who had joined the rebellion.
Lù Wènrèn, the barbarian chieftain of Pīshā, Qiǎojiā Prefecture, was executed,
and twenty-one villages of Dianzhi Yi submitted.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *guǐwèi* day,
based on Wáng Wénsháo's report, the Tusi of Měngcān, Měngjiǎo, and Měngdǒng in Yúnnán resolved their disputes by demarcation.
Hǎn Zhōngbāng, the native prefect (*tǔ zhīfǔ*) of Měngdìng, was granted the title of Pacification Commissioner (*Xuānfǔ Shǐ*).
The native headman (*tǔmù*) Hǎn Rónggāo was appointed to administer Měngjiǎo and Měngdǒng,
and was granted the hereditary title of Native Battalion Commander (*tǔ qiānzǒng*).
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Zhāng Yào passed away.
On the first day of the eighth month, *rénchén*,
Shǐ Mènglín, an esteemed scholar (*qírú*) from Lètíng, was granted the title of fourth-rank minister (*sìpǐn qīngxián*).
On the *guǐsì* day,
