Yìkuàng was ordered to oversee naval affairs as Director-General (*Zǒnglǐ*),
with Dìng'ān and Liú Kūnyī assisting.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the translation of Emperor Shìzǔ's Imperial Edict on Exhortations to Virtue (*Quànshàn Yàoyán*) into Chinese was completed,
and distributed to educational officials in all provinces.
It was to be expounded alongside the Sacred Edict Amplified Instructions (*Shèngyù Guǎngxùn*) on the first and fifteenth days of each month.
Bǎoyún passed away.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
an edict was issued to provincial authorities to discipline the military,
eliminate old habits,
and strictly prohibit collusion and protection.
In the ninth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
arrears of taxes from the previous year were remitted for Shǎnxī.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
originally,
envoys from foreign countries,
since the twelfth year of Tóngzhì,
had all been received at the Zǐguāng Gé.
This month,
German envoy Bālán Dégé considered this treatment as if they were vassal states,
and repeatedly spoke of changing the venue.
By this time,
Austrian envoy Bìgé Lǐběn arrived,
and was consequently received at the Chéngguāng Diàn.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the native sub-prefecture (*tǔ zhōutóng*) of Běishèng, Yúnnán, was reformed from native to regular administration.
In the tenth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
arrears of taxes and banner rents were remitted for Xí, Yúcì, and other places.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
an imperial decree ordered the Panchen Lama É'ěrdéní Hūbìlèhǎn to be enthroned in the first month of next year.
Shēngtài and Sūhūnòménlán were to go and observe,
and an imperial letter and precious items were sent.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Sòng dynasty Confucian Yóu Zuò was granted the honor of being enshrined in the Temple of Confucius (*Wénmiào*).
On the *wùwǔ* day,
bandits rebelled in Cháoyáng, Rèhé.
Admiral Yè Zhìchāo and Niè Shìchéng suppressed them.
In the eleventh month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
with the capture and execution of the Rèhé bandit leaders,
an edict was issued stating that regardless of whether people had joined the societies,
they were all permitted to renew themselves,
and those who withdrew and returned would be pardoned.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Chónglǐ, Assistant Minister of the Board of Revenue, and Hóngjūn, Assistant Minister of the Board of War, were both ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
a sea transport granary caught fire.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
due to bandit unrest in Kālāqìn Banner,
30,000 *ku* of treasury funds were allocated for relief and pacification.
Relief was provided for the fire disaster in Hànkǒu.
In the twelfth month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
arrears of taxes from the early Guāngxù reign were remitted for Hénán.
On the *yǐsì* day,
relief was provided for bandit-affected areas in Rèhé.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an edict was reiterated to the Imperial Household Department (*Nèiwù Fǔ*) to economize on expenditures.
This winter,
this year's outstanding civilian taxes and grain levies were remitted for Zhèjiāng and Shǎnxī.
In the first month of spring of the 18th year, *rénchén*, on the *dīnghài* day,
the Grand Canal was dredged.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
50,000 *ku* of treasury funds were allocated to Rèhé,
for relief of the Mongols of the Áohǎn and Nàimàn Banners.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
British troops entered Kǎnjùtí,
and the Muslim leader fled to Sèlèkù'ěr.
Relief and pacification were provided.
In the third month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
Yán Jìngmíng passed away.
In the fourth month of summer, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
Prince Chúnxián was buried.
This month,
indigenous communities in the inner mountains of Táiwān rebelled,
and they were suppressed.
On the *wǔyùe jiǎzǐ* (fifth month, *jiǎzǐ*) day,
bandits in Yángjiāng rebelled.
The chief rebel, Tán Yùnqīng, was executed.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
prayers for rain were offered.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Liú Fúyáo and 316 others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with varying ranks.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Héféi and other prefectures and counties suffered from drought and locusts;
relief was provided.
This month,
bandit leaders Mò Zìxián and others from Shànglín and Bīnzhōu were executed.
On the *liùyùe gēngyín* (sixth month, *gēngyín*) day,
prayers for rain were offered.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
it rained.
On the *rényín* day,
Wāng Fèngzǎo, a compiler, was appointed Imperial Envoy to Japan.
On the *rùnliùyùe jǐwèi* (intercalary sixth month, *jǐwèi*) day,
the Yǒngdìng Hé burst its banks.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
relief was provided for the drought in Fénzhōu and the seven departments of Guīsuī.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
fifty thousand *shí* each of grain for river transport from Jiāngsū and Jiāngběi were kept in Shùnzhí for disaster relief.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Ākèdáchūn was dismissed from his post
as Governor of Shānxī for a gaffe during an imperial audience.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
due to floods in the imperial environs,
one hundred thousand *tài* from the Board's treasury were allocated for relief.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Ēnchéng died.
This month,
locusts infested the capital region.
On the *qiūqīyùe xīncchǒu* (autumn seventh month, *xīnchǒu*) day,
one hundred thousand *tài* from the imperial treasury were disbursed for relief in various parts of Yúnnán.
On the *rényín* day,
locusts infested Hénán.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Táng Jiǒng was instructed to regulate copper transport.
On the *bāyùe bǐngyín* (eighth month, *bǐngyín*) day,
Kuíhuàn was ordered to negotiate a trade treaty between India and Tibet with the British envoy, Pǎor (Paul).
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Fúkūn was appointed a Grand Secretary of the Tǐrén Gé,
and Línshū was made an Assistant Grand Secretary.
New grain levies from Shāndōng were retained for relief.
On the *jiǔyùe gēngyín* (ninth month, *gēngyín*) day,
fifty thousand *shí* of grain from Jiāngběi were allocated for relief in various parts of Zhènjiāng.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Chén Gǒng, a bandit leader from Déhuà, Fújiàn, was executed.
On the *rényín* day,
arrears in money and grain taxes owed by the people of Shǎnxī from the previous year were remitted.
On the *shíyùe yǐmǎo shuò* (tenth month, *yǐmǎo* day, new moon),
thirty thousand *shí* of grain from Jiāngnán were retained for relief in various counties of Jiāngníng.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Dèng Hǎishān, a bandit leader from Lǐlíng, was executed.
On the *jǐsì* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Shāchē.
Grain rents and miscellaneous taxes in Tōngzhōu and other places in Zhílì were remitted.
On the *shíyīyùe yǐyǒu shuò* (eleventh month, *yǐyǒu* day, new moon),
outstanding taxes in Tōngzhōu and other places in Zhílì were remitted.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Táiwān and other places.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng, Sūn Jiānài, and others were instructed to investigate relief efforts.
Any officials in disaster-stricken prefectures and counties who neglected the people's suffering
were to be severely impeached and reported.
On the *rényín* day,
outstanding taxes in various departments, prefectures, counties, and garrisons of Jiāngsū were remitted.
On the *gēngxū* day,
one hundred thousand *tài* from the imperial treasury were disbursed for flood, drought, frost, and hail relief in Tàiyuán and its subordinate areas.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
twenty thousand *tài* from the inner treasury were disbursed for disaster victims in various parts of Shùnzhí.
On the *shíèryùe yǐmǎo shuò* (twelfth month, *yǐmǎo* day, new moon),
an imperial edict ordered princes and high officials to organize the celebration of the Empress Dowager's sixtieth birthday.
They were to consult with the Boards of Revenue, Rites, and Works,
and the Imperial Household Department to extensively research old precedents
and deliberate on details before reporting.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Liú Jǐntáng was summoned to the capital.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
another forty thousand *shí* of rice from the imperial granaries were disbursed
for relief to disaster victims in Shùntiān.
On the *yǐsì* day,
an imperial decree
ordered that all aspects of the celebration
be conducted with utmost frugality.
The customary tributes from officials, both inside and outside the court, were to be exempted.
A special allocation from the inner treasury was granted for disaster relief in the Shùnzhí area,
and this was to be made annually.
It was to be given to the Shùntiān Fǔ and the Governor-General of Zhílì to provide permanent relief to the impoverished.
Each province was to be awarded twenty thousand *tài* of silver,
starting from the following year, *Jiǎwǔ*.
This was to be disbursed from the inner treasury to the provincial governors for distribution.
An edict stated that the deceased *Bèilè* Nàrsū, as the grandson of Sēnggélínqìn,
was remembered for his past services,
and was posthumously enfeoffed as a Prince.
This was not to set a precedent for future cases.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Yáng Rú, the Daotai of Huī-Níng-Chí-Tài-Guǎng, was awarded the fourth-rank official title for a Beijing court official,
and appointed Imperial Envoy to America, Japan, and Spain.
This year,
Cháoxiǎn (Korea) paid tribute.
On the *shíjiǔnián guǐsì chūzhēng yuè yǐyǒu shuò* (nineteenth year *Guǐsì*, spring first month, *yǐyǒu* day, new moon),
an imperial edict announced that in anticipation of the Empress Dowager's sixtieth birthday the following year,
an *Enkē* provincial examination (*xiāngshì*) would be held this year,
and an *Enkē* metropolitan examination (*huìshì*) would be held the following year, *Jiǎwǔ*.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
winter grain taxes in Chángzhōu and other prefectures and counties were remitted.
On the *jǐhài* day,
outstanding taxes in Chángshā and other prefectures and counties were remitted.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
an imperial edict ordered that the Mongolian and Inner Zásàk princes, dukes, and *tàijí* who were due to come to the capital next year to offer birthday felicitations,
apart from those with fixed-term attendances,
were all to be stopped from coming to the capital.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
due to disasters in the seven departments outside the passes and in Dàtóng and other prefectures,
Zhílì and Jìn were ordered to remit taxes on commercial grain transport,
and one hundred thousand *tài* from the Board's treasury were allocated for relief.
On the *èryùe wùwǔ* (second month, *wùwǔ*) day,
fifty thousand *shí* of grain from Jiāngsū were retained for relief in Ānzhōu and other places.
On the *wùchén* day,
the German envoy Bālándé (Baron) was received at the Chéngguāng Diàn.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
fifty thousand *liǎng* of imperial provisions were retained for relief to disaster victims in Shǎnxī's Běishān and other places.
On the *sānyùe xīnmǎo* (third month, *xīnmǎo*) day,
sixty thousand *shí* of grain from the two Hú provinces were ordered to be sold for relief in Shānxī.
On the *xiàsìyùe bǐngzǐ* (summer fourth month, *bǐngzǐ*) day,
prayers for clear weather were offered.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
due to continuous drought in the grazing lands of Ālāshàn Zásàk Héshuò Qīnwáng Duōluō Tèsèlèng,
thirty thousand *tài* from the imperial treasury were disbursed for relief.
On the *wǔyùe yǐyǒu* (fifth month, *yǐyǒu*) day,
the Běixīncāng granary caught fire.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
due to continuous drought in the grazing lands of Yīkèzhāo Méng Zhǎng Zásàk Gùshān Bèizǐ Zhánájíěrdì,
ten thousand *tài* from the imperial treasury were disbursed for relief.
On the *liùyùe yǐmǎo* (sixth month, *yǐmǎo*) day,
Zhílì province was ordered to select and recommend individuals proficient in astronomy, medicine, divination, mathematics, and geomancy
to the Imperial Household Department.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
thirty thousand *tài* from the Board's treasury were allocated for relief in Lǐlíng and other places.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the German envoy Shēnkē (Schenck) was received at the Chéngguāng Diàn.
On the *guǐhài* day,
prayers for clear weather were offered.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Liú Yànfēi and other bandit leaders from Pǔ'ān were executed.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the capital suffered from floods.
An imperial edict ordered the establishment of six porridge kitchens outside the six gates,
and ten thousand *shí* of rice from the imperial granaries were allocated for relief.
On the *yǐhài* day,
additional millet from Fèngtiān and grain from Jiāngnán and Jiāngběi were allocated for relief in Shùnzhí.
The Yǒngdìng Hé burst its banks,
with both northern and southern sections overflowing.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
accumulated outstanding taxes in Ānhuī were remitted,
as were previous arrears in summer grain taxes in Qiánshān and other counties and garrisons.
On the *qiūqīyùe jiǎshēn* (autumn seventh month, *jiǎshēn*) day,
the Shùntiān Fǔ was instructed to sell grain at stable prices.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
as accumulated floodwaters in the imperial environs gradually receded,
an edict ordered the displaced poor to return to their hometowns.
On the *bāyùe xīnhài* (eighth month, *xīnhài*) day,
Zēng Guóquán's grandson, Guǎnghàn, was granted a fourth- or fifth-rank official title for a Beijing court official.
The ban on overseas Chinese was lifted;
henceforth, merchants and people overseas,
regardless of how long they had been away,
were all permitted to return to their home country to live and acquire property,
and their overseas trade was also permitted.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
miscellaneous grains from Fèngtiān, Yù, and Lǔ provinces were purchased and distributed for relief in Shùnzhí.
On the *jiǔyùe guǐwèi* (ninth month, *guǐwèi*) day,
sixty thousand *shí* of new grain levies from Shāndōng were retained for relief to disaster victims in prefectures and counties along the river.
Another one hundred thousand *shí* of grain from Jiāngnán and Jiāngběi were commuted to cash payments,
and eighty thousand *shí* of grain from Jiāngsū were retained for relief in Shùnzhí,
with half being distributed.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
thirty thousand *shí* of rice from the imperial granaries were disbursed for relief in Shùntiān.
This month,
outstanding taxes and regular levies in various parts of Shǎnxī were remitted.
On the *dōngshíyùe jǐyǒu shuò* (winter tenth month, *jǐyǒu* day, new moon),
the sea walls of four prefectures and counties in Tàicāng were repaired.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Gōng Zhàoyuàn, the Provincial Administration Commissioner of Sìchuān, was awarded a third-rank official title for a Beijing court official,
and appointed Imperial Envoy to Britain, France, Italy, and Belgium.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the Board of Revenue was ordered to pay the Imperial Household Department five hundred thousand *tài* of silver annually.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
grain taxes in Tōngzhōu and other places were remitted.
On the *jǐchǒu* day of the eleventh month,
the ban on private coining was re-emphasized.
Those found melting down, recasting, or transporting such coins
would be severely investigated and punished by the authorities.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
an earthquake struck Gānsù and Xīnjiāng.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Xǔ Zhènyī was ordered to collaborate with Lǐ Hóngzhāng to survey the Yǒngdìng Hé.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
autumn taxes were remitted for Dàxīng and other counties.
On the *xīnhài* day of the twelfth month,
Xú Yòngyí, Minister of the Board of Civil Office, was ordered to learn to serve in the Grand Council.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
an edict called for strict examination and review during the *Jīngchá*.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the ban on inland people going out to sea was lifted.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
relief was provided for the plague in Ānrén.
On the *rénxū* day,
rent and taxes for Guīhuà and seven other departments were remitted.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Wūlā was exempted from collecting Eastern Pearls (*Dōng Zhū*).
On the *rénshēn* day,
fifty thousand *shí* of grain from the Jīngdōng granary were allocated for spring relief in Shùntiān.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Board of Punishments reported that the dismissed official Zhōu Fúqīng had communicated secret information during his journey as an examiner;
the proposed sentence was caning and exile,
which was changed to execution with a stay.
In the spring of the twentieth year, on the *jǐmǎo* day, the first day of the first month,
an Imperial Decree stated:
for the Empress Dowager's sixtieth birthday celebration,
consorts and concubines would be promoted in rank and title,
the guards of Gōng Qīnwáng would be increased,
Yìkuāng would be promoted to Qīnwáng,
and Chún Qīnwáng Zǎi Fēng and others would receive various rewards.
Starting from central and foreign ministers, civil and military high officials, Mongolian princes, and so forth, all would receive imperial favors in due order.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Xǔ Zhènyī's survey of the Yǒngdìng Hé project
was ordered to be jointly planned with Lǐ Hóngzhāng.
An annual increase of forty thousand for repair expenses was granted,
along with an allocation of three hundred thousand from the imperial treasury for funds.
On the *jǐhài* day,
an earthquake struck Kùchē.
Arrears of taxes for Zhèn and Dí prefectures were remitted.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
regulations for examination halls were re-emphasized.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Ōlúnchūn were exempted from tribute sables.
On the *rén'yín* day,
the Yunnan-Burma supplementary treaty was concluded.
On the *xīnhài* day of the second month,
an edict ordered the examination ministers for the palace examinations to be fair and prudent in selecting candidates, and not to be indiscriminate.
The Tōnghuì Hé was dredged,
and sluice gates and dams were built.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was ordered to review the navy.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
prefectures and counties were prohibited from premature collection of taxes out of season and from the indiscriminate use of torture.
Xǔ Zhènyī's request was granted:
a river defense bureau was established at Lúgōuqiáo,
following the established method of Qiú Yuēxiū,
with one hundred and twenty dredging boats.
On the *wùyín* day, the first day of the third month,
there was a solar eclipse.
An imperial decree warned border officials against indiscriminately recommending subordinates.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
an edict ordered the suspension of autumn executions.
This spring,
tax arrears for various prefectures in Xīnjiāng were remitted,
as were fixed taxes and miscellaneous levies for various prefectures in Yúnnán.
In the summer, on the *wùshēn* day of the fourth month,
banditry in Sháozhōu and Nánxióng was
suppressed.
On the *jǐyǒu* day, Chén Běihǎi, the bandit leader of Wǎngpǔ, was executed.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
a grand examination was held for the Hànlǐn and Zhǎnlǐn Academies;
Wén Tíngshì and six others were promoted to the first rank,
while others were promoted or demoted in varying degrees.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the Italian envoy Baldi and others were received at the Chéngguāng Diàn.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Zhāng Jiàn and three hundred and ten others were granted various *jìnshì* degrees.
On the *rénshēn* day,
an imperial decree ordered the provinces to clear accumulated cases of appeals directly to the capital.
On the *dīnghài* day of the fifth month,
due to frequent banditry in the capital region,
an imperial decree ordered strict efforts to capture them.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
an edict stipulated that Resident Commissioners and Assistant Resident Commissioners in Tibet, upon completing their three-year terms, might request an audience,
and this was made into a regulation.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
previously,
Cháoxiǎn had requested military aid due to banditry.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng dispatched Admiral Yè Zhìchāo and Brigade-General Niè Shìchéng to lead troops there.
The Emperor, fearing insufficient military strength,
then decreed that to pacify the tributary state,
it was essential to ensure complete security,
and more troops must be mobilized and dispatched
to guarantee victory.
On the *rén'yín* day,
exemptions were granted for lost or washed-away tribute grain transported by sea in Jiāngsū.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Liú Míngchuán was summoned to the capital.
The Ōlúnchūn Commander-in-Chief was abolished,
and the Bùtèhā Commander-in-Chief was promoted to Vice-General.
On the *jǐyǒu* day of the sixth month,
an edict ordered the suspension of donations for *dào* and *fǔ* officials.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
heavy rain fell in the capital,
and prayers for clear weather were offered.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Japanese envoy Komura Jutarō was received at the Chéngguāng Diàn.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Wēng Tónghé and Lǐ Hóngzǎo were ordered to meet with the Grand Council and the Zǒnglǐ Yámén to discuss Cháoxiǎn affairs.
On the *rénxū* day,
naval donations were suspended.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
an imperial decree stated:
"The commutation price for Húnán's imperial tribute grain
shall be used for relief in Shùntiān.
The existing funds for disaster relief
shall also be reported, remitted, and stored."
All these measures would begin this year
and become annual practice.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Liú Yǒngfú, Brigade-General of Nán'ào Garrison, was ordered to go to Táiwān.
On the *wùchén* day,
Liú Jǐntáng was summoned to the capital.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
on the Emperor's twentieth birthday,
he presided over a congratulatory banquet in the palace.
Xú Yòngyí was appointed Grand Councillor.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Wāng Fèngzǎo, the envoy to Japan, was recalled to China.
In the autumn, on the *yǐhài* day, the first day of the seventh month,
Japan invaded Cháoxiǎn,
and an imperial edict declared war.
On the *wùyín* day,
Lǐ Hànzhāng was ordered to destroy the books written by Kāng Zǔyí, a *jǔrén* from Nánhǎi.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
an imperial decree dispatched Daoist Yuán Shìkǎi to Píngrǎng to pacify and rally the people.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Táng Jǐngsōng, Provincial Administration Commissioner of Táiwān, and Liú Yǒngfú, Brigade-General of Nán'ào Garrison, were ordered to assist Shào Yǒulián in preparing defenses.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was instructed to expand the navy,
carefully select military talents,
diligently improve training,
and submit a comprehensive and well-considered plan.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
land taxes for Bīnchuān and other prefectures and counties were remitted.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Shénjī Yíng troops were ordered to defend the vicinity of the capital,
stationed at Tōngzhōu,
then moved to Nányuàn.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Duān Qīnwáng Zǎi Yī and Jìngxìn were ordered to train Manchu banner troops,
selecting from the Manchu Firearm Battalion, the Jiànruì Yíng, the Yuánmíngyuán Eight Banner Rifle Battalion, and the Han Chinese rifle squads.
Zǎi Yī soon took command of the Shénjī Yíng.
An imperial decree ordered the suspension of non-urgent projects.
Wú Dàchéng's request was granted
to lead the Xiāng Army to Cháoxiǎn to supervise the battle.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
relief was provided for the disasters in Huìtóng and Huìlè counties.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Yè Zhìchāo was appointed Commander-in-Chief of all forces stationed at Píngrǎng.
Jìngxìn and Wāng Míngluán both served in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the treaty on the protection of Chinese laborers abroad was re-negotiated.
In the eighth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Wú Dàchéng led his army out of the pass
and volunteered to assist in naval affairs,
but was not permitted.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the first ceremony of offering sacrifices to Confucius was held.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Liú Jǐntáng died.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the Empress Dowager's honorary title was conferred,
and an edict was issued granting various imperial favors.
On the *rénxū* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng, due to the prolonged lack of success of the army,
was stripped of his three-eyed peacock feather and yellow jacket.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
an imperial decree issued three million from the inner treasury for military expenses.
Sòng Qìng, Provincial Commander of Sìchuān, was ordered to assist in military affairs in Běiyáng.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Guìxiáng, Duke of Chéng'ēn, was ordered to lead various cavalry and infantry battalions to be stationed at Shānhǎiguān.
On the *wùchén* day,
Zuǒ Bǎoguì, Brigade-General of Gāozhōu Garrison and commander of the Fèngtiān relief army, fought the Japanese at Píngrǎng,
suffered a defeat,
and died.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Wú Dàchéng's army was ordered to be stationed at Lètíng.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
an imperial decree stated
that the sixtieth birthday celebration at the Yíhéyuán for receiving congratulations would be suspended.
Thirty thousand *shí* of grain from the imperial granary were allocated for flood relief in various prefectures of Shùntiān.
On the *jiǎxū* day of the ninth month, which was the first day of the month,
an imperial decree appointed Gōng Qīnwáng Yìxīn to serve directly in the inner court,
to manage the Zǒngshǔ (Grand Council) and Hǎijūnshǔ (Admiralty),
and to jointly handle military affairs.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Sòng Qìng was ordered to command the armies of Zhí Lì and Fèng Tiān.
Yè Zhìchāo was dismissed as commander-in-chief.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
an edict instructed the resident Tídū Cáokèzhōng to recruit Jīnjīng Yǒng (Tianjin Braves) to be stationed at Shānhǎiguān.
Wáng Wénsháo was summoned to the capital.
Huáng Shàochūn was transferred to be the Chángjiāng Shuǐshī Tídū (Commander-in-Chief of the Yangtze Naval Forces).
On the *gēngchén* day,
Wáng Wénjǐn, Shìláng of the Board of War, and others were ordered to organize local militias.
On the *xīnsì* day,
land taxes were remitted in Xiánníng, Shǎnxī, and other areas afflicted by drought.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Hǎijūn Fùjiāng (Vice Admiral) Dèng Shìchāng engaged the Japanese in battle at Dàdōnggōu
and died.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Zhāng Zhīdòng was summoned to the capital.
On the *dīnghài* day,
relief was provided for flood-stricken counties such as Ruìchāng.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
due to their collapse in the face of the enemy,
Yè Zhìchāo and Wèi Rǔguì were dismissed as commanders,
and Niè Shìchéng was appointed to command both armies.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Japanese troops crossed the Yālù Jiāng.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Jiǔliánchéng fell.
On the *rényín* day,
Chángshùn was ordered to lead Jílín troops to Fèngtiān to assist in suppression,
and Fēngshēn was to command the three provinces' trained armies to defend the eastern border.
On the *jiǎchén* day of the tenth month in winter, which was the first day of the month,
an edict instructed Yùlù to prepare Kǔnzhōu for battle.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Tídū Táng Rénlián was ordered to recruit twenty battalions of volunteers,
to join Dìng'ān and Yùlù in defense and suppression.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
an imperial edict summoned all provinces of Shānxī to defend the capital.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an imperial edict appointed Gōng Qīnwáng to oversee military affairs,
and all commanders of various routes were to be under his command.
Wáng Dàchén (Princes and Grand Ministers) and others were ordered to manage patrol and local defense separately.
Hú Yùfēn, the Ànchásǐ (Provincial Surveillance Commissioner) of Guǎngxī, was stationed in Tiānjīn to supervise grain provisions,
and was granted the privilege of direct memorials to the throne.
Liú Kūnyī was summoned to the capital,
and Zhāng Zhīdòng was appointed acting Liǎngjiāng Zǒngdū (Governor-General of Two Jiāng provinces) and concurrently Nányáng Dàchén (Minister of Nányáng).
Wèi Rǔguì, Zǒngbīng (Commander-in-Chief) of the Níngxià Garrison, was
stripped of his post and arrested for retreating in the face of the enemy.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Wēng Tónghé, Lǐ Hóngzǎo, and Gāngyì were appointed concurrently as Jūnjī Dàchén (Grand Councilors).
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the Japanese captured Jīnzhōu,
and Fùdūtǒng (Deputy Military Governor) Liánshùn abandoned the city and fled.
Xú Bāngdào fought the Japanese
but was defeated.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
relief was provided for the poor residents along the river in the eastern province,
and funds were allocated for their solace and comfort.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
envoys from various nations presented credentials
to congratulate the Empress Dowager on her sixtieth birthday,
and the Emperor received them in the Wénhuá Diàn.
On the *rénxū* day,
the Japanese captured Xiùyán Zhōu,
and Fēngshēng'ā and Niè Guìlín both abandoned the city and fled.
Élèhébù and Zhāng Zhīwàn were dismissed from the Jūnjī.
Dìng'ān, having achieved no success in the face of the enemy,
was stripped of his titles as Qīnchāi Dàchén (Imperial Commissioner) and Hànjūn Dūtǒng (Manchu-Chinese Military Governor),
but temporarily retained to train troops in the Three Eastern Provinces.
Yīkètáng'ā was stripped of his post for his timidity in commanding troops,
and ordered to serve to atone for his crime.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Japanese attacked the Lǚshùn dockyard,
and Zǒngbàn (Director-General) Gōng Zhàoyǔ fled to Yāntái.
Huáng Shìlín, Zhào Huáiyè, and Wèi Rǔchéng followed him.
Xú Bāngdào, along with Zhāng Guāngqián, Jiāng Guìtí, and Chéng Yǔnhé, fled to Fùzhōu to join Sòng Qìng.
Lǐ Bǐnghéng was ordered to strictly defend Wēihǎi.
Wú Dàchéng requested to take charge of the Shānhǎiguān defenses,
and to retake Cháoxiǎn (Korea) once the armies had gathered.
The edict stated:
"To be fearful in the face of danger
is an ancient and clear teaching.
Do not take things lightly,
lest your words and actions contradict each other in the future."
Due to the fall of Lǚshùn,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was reprimanded for his mismanagement
and stripped of his post but retained in office.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Dīng Rǔchāng was stripped of his title as Hǎijūn Tídū (Commander-in-Chief of the Navy),
but temporarily retained in office.
Sòng Qìng requested self-punishment
but was specifically pardoned.
An imperial edict ordered all commanders to maintain strict discipline,
to prohibit disturbances to the populace,
and those who violated this would be immediately punished by military law.
Yè Zhìchāo was stripped of his post.
On the *guǐyǒu* day of the eleventh month, which was the first day of the month,
Gōng Zhàoyǔ was stripped of his post
and subsequently arrested for questioning.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
due to the fall of Jīnzhōu,
Fùdūtǒng Liánshùn was stripped of his post,
and Chéng Zhīwěi was also stripped of his post.
Zhào Huáiyè was arrested and brought to the capital for punishment.
On the *gēngchén* day,
an imperial decree reinstated Gōng Qīnwáng Yìxīn as a Jūnjī Dàchén.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the fixed taxes for flood-affected prefectures and counties in Shùnzhí were remitted.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Japanese captured Fùzhōu.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Japanese troops gathered at the two prefectures of Jīnzhōu and Fùzhōu.
Sòng Qìng was ordered to lead all armies in a decisive battle.
Fēngshēng'ā and Niè Guìlín fled from Xiùyán to Xīmùchéng,
but upon hearing of the enemy's approach,
their army again collapsed,
and the Japanese took Xīmùchéng.
Chéng Wénbǐng was appointed Lùlù Tídū (Commander-in-Chief of Land Forces).
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Sòng Qìng fought the Japanese at Hǎichéng,
was defeated,
and retreated to defend Tiánzhuāngtái.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Yīkètáng'ā fought the Japanese at Fènghuángchéng,
and Shìwèi (Imperial Guard) Yǒngshān died.
Rónglù was ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén (Zongli Yamen).
On the *rénchén* day,
Fēngshēng'ā and Niè Guìlín were arrested for questioning.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Yè Zhìchāo and Dīng Rǔchāng were arrested for punishment.
On the *wùxū* day,
Tídū Chéng Yǔnhé, Zhāng Guāngqián, and Zǒngbīng Jiāng Guìtí were stripped of their posts,
but all were retained in their camps to serve.
On the *guǐmǎo* day of the twelfth month,
the banquets at Zǐguāng Gé and Báohé Diàn for this month were suspended.
Tídū Wèi Rǔchéng was stripped of his post
and arrested for questioning.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Yùshǐ (Censor) Ān Wéijùn, for his criticism of Lǐ Hóngzhāng,
was stripped of his post for making groundless remarks
and exiled to a military station.
Liú Kūnyī was appointed Qīnchāi Dàchén,
and all armies inside and outside the passes were placed under his command.
Tídū Huáng Shìlín was stripped of his post
and arrested for questioning.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Zhāng Yīnhuán and Shào Yǒulián were appointed Plenipotentiary Ministers to go to Japan for peace talks,
but were soon recalled.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
one hundred twenty thousand *shí* of Jiangsū tribute rice were allocated for spring relief in Shùnzhí.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Zhāng Gāoyuán fought the Japanese at Gàipíng
but was defeated.
Fèngtiān troops fought again,
Tídū Yáng Shòushān died,
and the city fell.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
an imperial decree stated that
Liú Kūnyī should be stationed at Shānhǎiguān to plan advances and retreats.
Wú Dàchéng was urgently ordered to lead his army out of the pass
to join Sòng Qìng in the offensive.
Due to the high price of rice in the nearby capital area,
miscellaneous grains from Hénán and Shāndōng were transported for fair-price sales.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Wèi Rǔguì was beheaded.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Sòng Qìng and Wú Dàchéng were ordered to assist Liú Kūnyī in military affairs.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
another thirty thousand *shí* of capital granary rice were allocated for spring relief in Shùntiān.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Japanese captured Róngchéng.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Wáng Wénsháo was ordered to assist in Běiyáng military affairs.
In this year,
Cháoxiǎn paid tribute.
Annals of Dèzōng, Part 2, Volume 24
In the spring, first month, on the *guǐyǒu* day, the first day of the month, of the 21st year, *yǐwèi*,
banquets were suspended.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Japanese troops attacked Wēihǎi.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
our navy engaged in battle on the South Shore
and was defeated.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Wú Dàchéng first left the pass to inspect the troops.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Wēihǎi fell,
and the defending general Dài Zōngqiān died.
Niè Shìchéng was reappointed to lead troops into the pass.
On the *dīnghài* day,
an imperial edict reprimanded Lǐ Hóngzhāng.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Liúgōngdǎo fell,
the navy was destroyed,
and Dīng Rǔchāng and Commander-in-Chief Liú Bùchán died.
Zhāng Zhīdòng and Sōngchūn were instructed to defend the sea, Gàn, and Qīngjiāng strategic water and land routes,
and to ensure smooth transportation in Qīng and Huái.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was appointed first-class plenipotentiary minister
to Japan.
On the *rénchén* day,
he met with envoys from various countries in the Wénhuá Diàn.
Táo Mó reported that households in Kǎshígáěr, Shāchē, Hétián and other prefectures
were being bought as slaves by the British Indian Department,
and should be redeemed and freed by the government;
this was approved.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Yè Zhìchāo and Gōng Zhàoyú were both sentenced to decapitation.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Japanese captured Wéndēng and Nínghǎi,
and pressed towards Yāntái.
Sòng Qìng and others fought the Japanese at Tàipíng Shān
and were defeated,
fleeing.
In the second month, on the *yǐsì* day,
Sòng Qìng and Wú Dàchéng defeated the Japanese at Liàngjiǎ Shān;
Battalion Commander Liú Yúnguì and Garrison Commander Zhào Yúnqí died in battle.
Relief was provided to disaster victims in Jǐnzhōu and Níngyuǎn.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Niè Shìchéng was appointed commander-in-chief of the defense forces at Jīn and Gū sea ports.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Japanese troops approached Liáoyáng,
but Chángshùn and Táng Rénlián repelled them.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Japanese troops captured Niúzhuāng;
Wú Dàchéng retreated,
and the Japanese then raided Yíngkǒu.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Mǎ Yùkūn defeated the Japanese at Tiánzhuāngtái.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
they fought again
and were defeated.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Japanese troops captured Tiánzhuāngtái.
Wú Dàchéng fled to Jǐnzhōu,
and Sòng Qìng retreated to Shuāngtái.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Wú Dàchéng's troops were criticized
for their repeated failures.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Prince Gōng and others memorialized to abolish the Naval Department.
Land taxes were remitted in Shàngyuán, Jiāngníng and other places,
as well as garrisons in Huái'ān and other areas.
Relief was provided for flood victims in Zhílì.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
troops from the Shénjī Battalion were deployed to Xǐfēngkǒu.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Wú Dàchéng was ordered to relinquish his military duties and assist in the capital;
the Húnán and Húběi armies were placed under the command of Wèi Guāngtáo.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
100,000 taels from the treasury were allocated for additional relief to disaster victims in Jìzhōu and other areas.
On the *wùchén* day,
Prefect Xú Qìngzhāng organized local militias to firmly defend Liáoyáng;
Yùlù was ordered to provide provisions and weapons.
On the *jǐsì* day,
relief was provided for flood victims in Yùtián, Luánzhōu, and Lètíng.
The Japanese ambushed Lǐ Hóngzhāng,
wounding his cheek with a bullet.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Japanese attacked Pénghú.
In the third month, on the *rénshēn* day, the first day of the month,
Wú Dàchéng was ordered to return to his post as Governor of Húnán.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Gāojiāzhǐfāng River in Jìyáng burst its banks.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Japanese troops captured Pénghú.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Admiral Jiǎng Xīyí was stripped of his position
and arrested for questioning.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Guō Bǎochāng was ordered to assist Liú Kūnyī in defense matters.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng held a conference in Mǎguān with Japanese plenipotentiaries Itō Hirobumi and Mutsu Munemitsu.
A peace treaty was concluded,
establishing Cháoxiǎn as an independent and sovereign state,
ceding the southern part of Liáo, Táiwān, and the Pénghú islands,
indemnifying war expenses of 200 million,
increasing treaty ports,
allowing Japanese merchants and civilians to engage in industry and manufacturing,
and temporarily stationing troops in Wēihǎi.
In the summer, fourth month, on the *wùshēn* day,
rice from the capital granaries was allocated for fair pricing in Shùntiān.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Tiānjīn experienced a sea surge;
Wáng Wénsháo requested to be dismissed,
but this was not granted.
An imperial edict stated:
"In times of extraordinary calamities,
we, the monarch and ministers, must cultivate virtue and be vigilant
to avert heavenly disasters."
Rebellious Huí in Gānsù captured Xúnhuà Tīng;
Léi Zhèngwǎn suppressed them.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Daoist officials Lián Fāng and Wǔ Tíngfāng were ordered to Yāntái to exchange the treaty with Japan.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"The peace treaty has been agreed upon,
and court officials have repeatedly memorialized that territory should not be abandoned
and expenses should not be indemnified,
but rather the treaty should be abandoned and war resumed.
Their words certainly stem from loyalty and indignation,
but they do not fully understand the court's hardship.
Since the hasty outbreak of hostilities,
there has not been a single victory.
Recently, the situation has become more pressing;
in the north, Liáo and Shěnyáng could be threatened,
and in the south, the capital region could be invaded.
Shěnyáng is a vital imperial mausoleum area,
and the capital concerns the ancestral altars.
Moreover, the Imperial Mother has been enjoying peace for more than twenty years;
if she were to be startled,
how could I, the Emperor, bear to question myself?
Furthermore, heaven has shown warnings,
and a tsunami has caused disaster,
making it even more difficult to manage defense and offense.
We weighed the two harms of peace and war,
and then decisively settled on this plan.
The extreme difficulties of the situation
were not detailed by the memorialists,
but all officials and people under heaven should understand it.
Now that the treaty has been ratified,
we specifically declare the reasons for the past and present handling of affairs.
We, the monarch and ministers, only hope to remain resolute,
and thoroughly eliminate accumulated弊病(evils)."
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the Grand Councilors and all officials were instructed
that since peace had been achieved,
there should be no further memorials on the matter.
100,000 *shi* of grain from Shāndōng were retained for relief in Nínghé and other places.
Yùlù was ordered to provide relief supplies to Níng, Jǐn, and other prefectures.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
former Magistrate Sūn Bǎotián of Sùsōng County was granted the Fifth-Rank official title.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the Dalái Lǎmā completed his ordination
and was presented with *hādá*, prayer beads, and other items.
On the *guǐhài* day,
30,000 *shi* of tribute rice from Húběi were allocated
for relief in Níng, Jǐn, and other prefectures.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
fair pricing for grain was implemented in the capital.
Lǐ Jīngfāng was appointed plenipotentiary commissioner for the transfer of territory in Táiwān.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Luò Chéngxiáng and 282 others were granted the *jìnshì* degree with various ranks.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Táng Jǐngsōng was summoned to the capital.
In the fifth month, on the *xīnwèi* day, the first day of the month,
relief was provided for flood victims in Línzhāng and other counties.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Jiǎng Xīyí was sentenced to decapitation.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Russian envoy Kashini and French envoy Schaland met in the Wénhuá Diàn.
On the *rénchén* day,
Japan returned the southern Liáo territory to us.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
land taxes for the previous year's disaster-stricken fields in Xīnhuà, Húnán,
and Āmí, Bǎoshān, Kūnmíng, Yúnnán were remitted.
Relief was provided for flood and hail disaster victims in Chángwǔ and other counties.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Táng Jǐngsōng retired from office.
On the *xīnchǒu* day of the intercalary fifth month, the first day of the lunar month,
two hundred thousand *kùtáng* (treasury funds) from Shāndōng were allocated to aid the famine relief in Fèngtiān.
On the *rényín* day,
over ten thousand boatmen and their families, who had been involved in grain transport and awaiting inspection in Jiāngnán and Zhèjiāng, were given relief.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Grand Secretary Fúkūn retired.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Niè Shìchéng, the Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Zhílì, was ordered to take command of the Huái Army stationed at Tiānjīn and Gū;
Wèi Guāngtáo, the Provincial Administration Commissioner of Jiāngxī, was ordered to take command of the Zhè Army stationed at Shānhǎiguān;
Sòng Qìng, the Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Sìchuān, was ordered to take command of the Yì Army stationed at Jǐnzhōu.
All were subject to the orders of the Minister of the Northern Ocean.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Wú Dàchéng was dismissed.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Yùgēng, the circuit intendant of Huìcháo-Jiāyīng, was granted a fourth-rank京堂 (court official) position,
and appointed as Envoy Extraordinary and Minister Plenipotentiary to Japan.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
an edict stated:
"Recently, officials both domestic and foreign have submitted memorials on current affairs,
such as building railways,
minting currency,
manufacturing machinery,
opening mines,
commuting the southern grain tribute,
reducing military personnel,
establishing a postal service,
training a modern army,
reorganizing the navy,
and establishing schools.
These proposals generally prioritize fundraising and military training as urgent tasks,
and fostering commerce and benefiting industry as fundamental.
All should be implemented in a timely manner.
As for rectifying *líjīn*,
strictly verifying customs duties,
investigating uncultivated land,
and eliminating redundant officials,
all these measures greatly benefit the national economy and the livelihood of the people.
The provincial governors and governors-general should, in accordance with local conditions,
deliberate on appropriate measures and report them."
On the *jiǎxū* day of the sixth month,
Sūn Yùwèn was relieved due to illness.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
famine relief was provided to the starving people of Rèhé.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Grand Councillor Xú Yòngyí was dismissed.
Línshū was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wǔyīng Diàn;
Kūngāng, as Minister of Rites, was made Associate Grand Secretary.
Qián Yìngpǔ was appointed Grand Councillor;
Wēng Tónghé and Lǐ Hóngzǎo were both appointed to serve concurrently in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
flood relief was provided in Zhōngxiáng and other areas.
In autumn, on the *jiǎchén* day of the seventh month,
the Qìn Hé burst its banks.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Xíngzé Hé burst its banks.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
an imperial edict ordered Lǐ Hóngzhāng to join the Grand Secretariat and handle affairs.
Wáng Wénsháo was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì and concurrently Minister of the Northern Ocean.
On the *wùshēn* day,
relief was provided for flood and hail disasters in Shāngzhōu, Qīngjiàn, and other areas.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Sòng dynasty scholar Lǚ Dàlín was granted the honor of being enshrined in the Temple of Confucius.
The rivers in Shòuzhāng and Qídōng burst their banks.
Fēngshēng'ā was sent to a military post for exile.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
flood relief was provided in Zhèn'ān and other counties.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Dèxīn, the Governor of Jiāngxī, was found guilty and stripped of his office.
An earthquake occurred in Sèlèkù'ěr.
On the *rénxū* day,
due to the rampant activities of the Muslim populace,
Commander-in-Chief Tāng Yànhé was stripped of his office;
Yáng Chāngjùn and Léi Zhèngwǎn were both stripped of their offices but retained in their posts.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the previously dismissed Provincial Commander-in-Chief Huáng Shìlín was sentenced to decapitation.
In the eighth month, on the *rénshēn* day,
flood relief was provided in Fùchuān and Róngxiàn.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
flood relief was provided in Jiēzhōu, Wénxiàn, Xīníng, and other prefectures and counties.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Liú Bǐngzhāng, the Governor-General of Sìchuān, was stripped of his office for failing to protect churches.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Qìngcháng, a director in the Board of Works, was appointed as a fifth-rank京堂 (court official) and Envoy Extraordinary and Minister Plenipotentiary to France.
On the *guǐsì* day,
land taxes in Wēiyuǎn, Yúnnán, which had suffered disaster, were remitted.
In the ninth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
fire relief was provided in the prefecture of Wúzhōu.
New grain tribute from Shāndōng was retained to provide disaster relief for counties along the riverbanks.
On the *yǐsì* day,
thirty thousand *shí* of winter grain tribute from Húběi were retained for relief needs in Zhōngxiáng and other counties.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Wèi Guāngtáo was ordered to lead troops to reinforce Gānsù.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the corvée labor in Wàngdū was remitted,
and fifty percent of the land tax for reclaimed land was remitted.
This was established as a permanent regulation.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
arrears from the previous year in Shǎnxī were remitted,
as well as the land tax for land occupied by the canal in Huázhōu.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the British Minister, Sir Claude MacDonald (Ōugénà), was received at the Wénhuá Diàn.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
refugees in various disturbed areas of Gānsù were relieved.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
relief was provided for dragon-related disasters in Línxiāng.
Thirty thousand *táng* (treasury funds) were allocated to purchase stored grain
in preparation for drought disasters in Chángdé and Héngzhōu.
On the *rénxū* day,
the German Minister, Baron Clemens von Ketteler (Kèluóbó), was received at the Wénhuá Diàn.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Wú Tíngfēn, a Secretary of the Imperial Clan Court, was appointed to serve concurrently in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Panchen Lama of Tsang, Bānchán É'ěrdéní, came to the capital to visit the imperial mausoleum
and present local products.
Earthquakes occurred in Jiēyáng, Cháoyáng, Pǔníng, and other counties.
In the tenth month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Yáng Chāngjùn was dismissed;
Táo Mó was appointed acting Governor-General of Shǎnxī and Gānsù.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng and the Japanese Minister exchanged the treaty returning Liáodōng.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Chánglín and Wāng Míngluán were both stripped of their offices for making presumptuous remarks during an imperial audience.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the newly established New Army was first formed,
and Yuán Shìkǎi, the Intendant of Wēnzhōu and Chùzhōu, was ordered to supervise its training.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
land taxes in Jiāngchuān, which had suffered disaster, were remitted for two years.
Relief was provided for flood and drought disasters in Hèqìng and other prefectures and counties.
On the *yǐyǒu* day of the eleventh month, the first day of the lunar month,
the breach at Zhàojiākǒu in Shāndōng was closed.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the regular tax on imperial farms in Shèngjīng, which had been submerged, was remitted.
On the *wùshēn* day,
eighty thousand *shí* of commuted grain tribute from Hénán were retained for relief work in Nèihuáng and other counties.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Wáng Zhīchūn, the Provincial Administration Commissioner of Húběi, was appointed envoy for the Russian Emperor's coronation.
On the *gēngxū* day,
land taxes for two years, and also accumulated arrears, were remitted for both banner people and commoners in areas of Fèngtiān that had suffered from military conflict.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Liú Yǒngfú was dismissed.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Lǐ Péiróng, the Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Gānsù, was stripped of his office for delaying his relief mission to Xīníng.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Dǒng Fúxiáng was transferred to be the Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Gānsù,
and remained in command of the Gān Army;
all front-line generals were subject to his command.
Relief was provided for dragon-related disasters in Bǎoshān.
In the twelfth month, on the *wùyín* day,
the breach at Shòuzhāng was closed.
On the *gēngchén* day,
sixty thousand *kùtáng* (treasury funds) were allocated for spring relief in Húběi.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was reappointed as envoy to Russia,
with Shào Yǒulián as his deputy.
In this month,
arrears from the previous year in Shǎnxī, and reed taxes and imperial farm taxes from the previous year in Fèngtiān, were remitted.
Relief was provided for disasters in Shèngjīng and Píngxiāng.
One hundred thousand *táng* (treasury funds) each were allocated
for disaster relief in various areas of Húnán, Yúnnán, and Shǎnxī.
In the spring of the twenty-second year, *bǐngshēn*, on the *bǐngshēn* day of the first month, the first day of the lunar month,
banquets were suspended.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
due to the special dispatch of Lǐ Hóngzhāng as envoy to Russia,
Shào Yǒulián and Wáng Zhīchūn were instructed not to go.
On the *jǐhài* day,
relief was provided for flood and drought disasters in various prefectures of Chángshā.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
foreign ministers were received at the Wénhuá Diàn.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Féng Zǐcái was ordered to return to Guǎngdōng
to oversee the defense of Qīnzhōu and Liánzhōu.
In the second month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
the commander of the Èlǔtè Banner in Tǎ'ěrbāhātái was relocated to Bùlúnbùlākè;
the commander of the Yīlí Cháhār Camp was relocated to Bóluótǎlā.
On the *rénshēn* day,
discussions began on establishing a postal service and joining international associations.
The Lóngzhōu railway was opened.
Liú Míngchuán passed away.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the Board of Revenue caught fire.
In the third month, on the *wùxū* day,
Élèhébù retired.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Hángzhōu was opened as a commercial port.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Wáng Wénsháo and Zhāng Zhīdòng were ordered to oversee the construction of the Lúhàn railway.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Muslim bandits encroached upon Zhūlèdūsī.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Dǒng Fúxiáng was ordered to be stationed in Xīníng,
specifically for suppression and pacification;
Wèi Guāngtáo returned to be stationed in Hézhōu,
and was soon after appointed Governor of Shǎnxī.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Rénshēn,
a disaster struck Púsàdǐng on Wǔtái Shān.
On the day Yǐhài,
summer taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken Kūnmíng and Qiūběi.
On the day Xīnsì,
Rónglù was ordered to inspect the newly established army in Tiānjīn.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Kūngāng was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tǐrén Pavilion,
and Rónglù, as Minister of War, assisted in the Grand Secretariat.
Fifth month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
an edict was issued to Lǐ Bǐnghéng to investigate grain taxes in departments and districts;
excessive levies were to be reduced.
Arrears of taxes for disaster-stricken Ēn'ān were remitted.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
a disaster struck the Temple of Confucius in Zhèngzhōu.
That month,
the Emperor repeatedly attended the Empress Dowager in visiting the residence of Chún Wáng to inquire about the illness of his Fújìn.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Chúnxián Qīnwáng's Fújìn, of the Yèhènālā clan, passed away.
Court was suspended for eleven days.
The Emperor attended the Empress Dowager in visiting the residence to view the encoffining,
and the next day returned for the offering and sacrifice.
An imperial decree stated that
Chúnxián Qīnwáng's Fújìn having passed away,
she should be referred to as
"the Emperor's birth mother."
On the day Yǐsì,
the Emperor put on mourning attire.
On the day Rénzǐ,
arrears of taxes for Anhuī from previous years were remitted.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the tribute of livestock and sable from the Èlúnchūn was deferred.
Sixth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
an edict was issued to Kuíshùn to provide relief and comfort to the Mongolian people of Qīnghǎi.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the river breached its banks in Lìjīn.
On the day Wùchén,
arrears of salt tax for all salt fields in Zhèjiāng from previous years were remitted.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
disaster relief was provided for the storm-stricken areas of Zhèjiāng.
On the day Rénshēn,
the golden coffin of Chúnxián Qīnwáng's Fújìn was moved,
and the Emperor personally attended to see it off.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the Emperor attended the Empress Dowager in visiting Chún Wáng's garden residence to make offerings before the Fújìn's golden coffin.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
an edict was issued to reorganize the Yangtze River navy.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Yùlù was ordered to concurrently serve as Minister of Naval Affairs.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the Fān people of Sōngpān rebelled,
and the government troops suppressed them.
On the day Dīnghài,
the request of the princes and ministers was granted:
the Shénjī Battalion training grounds were to train troops in the Western style.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the Yǒngdìng Hé overflowed.
That month,
relief was provided for the sea inundation disaster in Dàdōnggōu,
and flood disasters in Ānhuī and Húběi.
Autumn, seventh month, on the day Jiǎwǔ, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the southeastern prefectures of Shùntiān were flooded,
and Sūn Jiānài and others were ordered to swiftly devise plans for relief supplies.
On the day Yǐsì,
one hundred thousand shi of southern grain tribute were kept in Tiānjīn for disaster relief.
Eighth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
as the Huí bandits inside and outside the passes were gradually pacified,
an edict was issued to Táo Mó and Dǒng Fúxiáng to resettle the surrendered populace
and to search for the remaining bandits.
On the day Jǐsì,
Sìchuān troops attacked Zhānduì,
repeatedly capturing strategic passes,
and pressed towards Zhōngzhān.
On the day Gēngchén,
an edict was issued to Lù Chuánlín:
"The military campaign in Zhānduì
is a temporary measure.
Whether Fān officials should be re-established after the matter is settled
should be thoroughly reviewed again.
Do not on this account harshly blame the lamas,
thereby creating other conflicts.
Be very careful not to act rashly."
On the day Jǐchǒu,
an edict was issued to the Ministry of Justice that trials should be concluded quickly,
without allowing delays.
On the day Rénchén,
the arbitrary use of torture in various provinces was forbidden.
Ninth month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
Fúkūn passed away.
Arrears of taxes for Shǎnxī from the previous year were remitted.
On the day Jǐhài,
the Eastern Tombs suffered an insect plague.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Shèng Xuānhuái was awarded the rank of fourth-grade capital official.
Previously,
Wáng Wénsháo and Zhāng Zhīdòng had requested the establishment of the China Merchants Steam Navigation Company,
and Shèng Xuānhuái was appointed to oversee it.
At this time,
an imperial decree was issued,
also granting him the right of independent memorialization.
Grand Secretary Zhāng Zhīwàn retired.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the German envoy He Jing and the Belgian envoy Feige were received at the Wénhuá Diàn.
On the day Gēngxū,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Lǐ Bǐnghéng reported that the lower course of the Yellow River had been surveyed,
and it was proposed to dredge a new river on the east bank of the old Yellow River,
still guiding it back into the old river to flow into the sea.
An edict stated that this great undertaking must
aim for lasting peace and stability,
to fulfill the commission.
That autumn,
disaster relief was provided for floods in Hénán, Fèngtiān, Húběi, Ānhuī, Shāndōng, Shānxī, Jílín, and Hēilóngjiāng;
flood disasters in Húnán;
and floods and hail disasters in Shǎnxī and Gānsù;
locust and hail disasters in Xīnjiāng;
and storm disasters in the coastal waters of Guǎngdōng.
Winter, tenth month, on the day Rénxū, the first day of the month,
relief was provided for flood disasters in the Jiāng and Hàn rivers of Húběi.
On the day Guǐhài,
winter relief was managed in Hézhōu.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
four customs barriers were added in Sūzhōu, Hángzhōu, Shāshì, and Sīmáo.
On the day Bǐngyín,
an edict was issued to Táo Mó to select upright, clear-minded, and virtuous officials,
to harmoniously unite the Han and Hui peoples.
Should there be occasional disputes,
only right and wrong should be discussed,
judging according to reason and fairness to achieve impartiality,
and also providing differentiated relief to areas affected by military operations.
For the merit of pacifying the Hui,
Dǒng Fúxiáng was granted the hereditary rank of Qí Dūwèi,
Táo Mó was appointed Governor-General of Shǎnxī-Gānsù,
Ráo Yìngqí was appointed Governor of Xīnjiāng,
Kuíshùn and Wèi Guāngtáo were given special commendations,
and others were duly recognized according to their contributions.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the breach in the Yǒngdìng Hé was closed.
On the day Wùyín,
it was decided that consuls would be established in Cháoxiǎn (Korea),
but no treaties would be concluded,
no envoys would be dispatched,
and no national credentials would be exchanged.
One consul-general would be stationed in its capital city.
On the day Gēngchén,
Yáng Rú, Censor-in-Chief of the Left, was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to Russia, Austria, and the Netherlands;
Luó Fēnglù, a circuit intendant, was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to Britain, Italy, and Belgium;
Huáng Zūnxiàn was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to Germany;
and Wǔ Tíngfāng was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to the United States, Japan, and Peru.
On the day Guǐwèi,
autumn taxes and miscellaneous levies for Wǔqīng and other departments and districts were remitted.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Huázhōu and other places.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Xú Tóng was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tǐrén Pavilion,
and Lǐ Hóngzǎo, as Minister of Rites, assisted in the Grand Secretariat.
Eleventh month, on the day Wùshēn,
Winter Solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Yuánqiū altar.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
court congratulations were suspended.
On the day Xīnhài,
disaster-stricken taxes and levies in Hé and Táozhōu and other places were remitted.
On the day Dīngsì,
Xǔ Jǐngchéng, Vice Minister of Works, was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to Germany.
That month,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Shāndōng and Sìchuān.
Twelfth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
initially,
Lù Chuánlín repeatedly memorialized that Zhānduì should be suppressed,
and proposed to establish Han officials after its recovery.
The Emperor, fearing to displease the Dálài Lāmá,
ordered Lù Chuánlín, Wénhǎi, and others to deliberate in detail.
At this time,
a memorial was submitted reporting on the submission of the Zhānduì people and
the awe felt by the Tibetan Fān people.
Therefore, an edict was issued to earnestly persuade the Dálài Lāmá,
aiming to ensure that there would be no impediments to the protection of Tibet and Sìchuān.
Relief was provided for disasters in Dōngxiāng and other prefectures of Sìchuān.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
grain taxes for various villages and settlements in Liáoyáng were remitted,
as were arrears of grain taxes for Suídé and other departments and districts.
Twenty-third year, Dīngyǒu spring, first month, on the day Xīnmǎo, the first day of the month,
banquets were suspended.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
arrears of taxes for Shāndōng from the early Guāngxù reign were remitted.
On the day Xīnhài,
grain tribute from Húběi was retained for public works and disaster relief.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the envoys from the United States, France, Britain, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, Russia, Italy, Japan, and Austria were received at the Wénhuá Diàn.
Second month, on the day Rénxū,
Zhāng Yīnhuán, Vice Minister of Revenue, was appointed envoy to Britain.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the river breached its banks in Lìchéng and Zhāngqiū.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Chónglǐ and Xǔ Yīngkuí were ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
In the third month, on the day *Guǐsì*,
an imperial decree ordered the reduction of superfluous troops.
On the day *Jiǎchén*,
an imperial edict disbursed 100,000 from the imperial treasury to relieve Sìchuān,
and 50,000 to relieve Húběi.
In addition, 100,000 from the state treasury were added to relieve the three prefectures of Kuí, Suí, and Zhōng in Sìchuān.
On the day *Xīnhài*,
the land tax for the flooded fields in Tóngrén and Qīngxī was remitted.
On the day *Dīngsì*,
a commissioner for Hǎishēnwēi was first established.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day *Yǐhài*,
Lǐ Bǐnghéng memorialized to reduce the money and grain taxes in Shāndōng.
In the fifth month, on the day *Bǐngshēn*,
an imperial decree approved Guàngězālāsēn Hútúkètú Jiāmǔbātúduōpǔ's reincarnation as the Hútúkètú of Bāyīngōu Chénghuà Temple.
On the day *Jiǎchén*,
Zhāng Zhīwàn died
and was posthumously granted the title of Tàibǎo.
On the day *Dīngwèi*,
the Emperor visited the garden tomb of his birth mother, the Fújìn of Chúnxián Qīnwáng,
and observed the one-year mourning period's end.
On the day *Rénzǐ*,
Lǚ Hǎihuán was granted the fourth-rank capital office,
and appointed minister plenipotentiary to Germany and the Netherlands.
In the sixth month, on the day *Jǐmǎo*,
relief was distributed for the floods in Chóngyáng and other counties.
This summer,

the Emperor received the Austro-Hungarian minister, Qígàn (Baron von Czikann), the Russian minister, Wūěrtāmùsīkē (Count Wlassow), the British minister, Dòunàlè (Sir Claude MacDonald), and the Japanese minister, Shǐyě Wénxióng (Yano Fumio), at the Wénhuá Hall.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day *Gēngyín*,
Lǐ Hóngzǎo died.
On the day *Bǐngshēn*,
Liáo Shòuhéng was ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the day *Xīnchǒu*,
the former Shǎnxī Gùyuán Tídū Léi Zhèngwǎn was restored to his original office.
On the day *Jiǎchén*,
the annual tribute of horses from the twenty-four temples of Mínzhōu Wèi was remitted,
and the horse tribute was also temporarily deferred.
On the day *Jiǎyín*,
a mountain in Píngyáo Pǔdòngcūn collapsed into the ground.
In the eighth month, on the day *Jǐsì*,
Jìngxī experienced an earthquake.
On the day *Rénshēn*,
Wēng Tónghé was appointed Hùbù Shàngshū and Xiébàn Dàxuéshì.
On the day *Guǐwèi*,
the mining prohibition in Kēbùduō Zhāhāqìn Bǎorjí was lifted,
allowing Měng and Hàn people to mine.
On the day *Yǐyǒu*,
due to Lù Chuánlín's mishandling of affairs concerning the Déěrgétè Tǔsī,
the proposal for "reforming the native administration and bringing it under direct rule" was abolished.
Tǔsī Ángwēng Jiàngbáirénqīng and his family members were released,
and returned to Déěrgétè to manage Tǔsī affairs.
In the ninth month, on the day *Wùzǐ*,
Lù Chuánlín was dismissed.
On the day *Jǐchǒu*,
troops were ordered to withdraw from Déěrgétè.
On the day *Wùxū*,
the Emperor received the Norwegian minister, Báigù (Peter Bierkow), at the Wénhuá Hall.
On the day *Jiǎchén*,
the Dálài Lǎmā requested the return of the Zhānduì territory.
Gōngshòu and others were ordered to deliberate and report.
On the day *Bǐngwǔ*,
the breach at Lìjīn was closed.
On the day *Yǐmǎo*,
the former Shǎnxīgān Zǒngdū Yáng Chāngjùn was restored to his office.
This autumn,
relief was distributed for hail and flood disasters in Shǎnxī,
floods in Húnánběi, Jiāngxī, Guǎngdōng, Ānhuī, Yúnnán, and Guìzhōu,
and a locust plague in Xīnjiāng.
In the tenth month, on the day *Wùwǔ*,
Shǐ Niànzǔ, the Fǔshǐ of Guǎngxī, was dismissed from office due to an incident.
On the day *Rénshēn*,
bandits in Cáozhōu murdered German missionaries.
Lǐ Bǐnghéng was ordered to investigate.
On the day *Wùyín*,
German warships entered Jiāo'ào.
On the day *Rénwǔ*,
the fixed tax for disaster-stricken areas in Lèting and other prefectures and counties was remitted.
This month,
relief was distributed for a typhoon in Guǎngdōng,
hail in Shǎnxī,
and floods in Húnán and Jiāngnán.
In the eleventh month, on the day *Xīnmǎo*,
30,000 *shí* of grain from Jiāngběi was allocated
for relief in Xúzhōu and Hǎizhōu prefectures.
On the day *Jiǎwǔ*,
an imperial decree abolished the proposal for "reforming the native administration and bringing it under direct rule" for Sānzhān,
which was to remain under the Dálài Lǎmā.
On the day *Xīnchǒu*,
an edict ordered the pacification of famine victims in various prefectures of Jiāngsū.
On the day *Dīngwèi*,
the British minister, Dòunàlè (Sir Claude MacDonald), was received in audience.
On the day *Guǐchǒu*,
the winter solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Yuánqiū.
On the day *Jiǎyín*,
morning congratulations were suspended.
The banditry in Zhāowūdá Alliance banners was quelled.
In the twelfth month, on the day *Jiǎzǐ*,
the Lìjīn river breached.
On the day *Jǐsì*,
land rent for flooded land in Ānzhōu was remitted.
On the day *Yǐhài*,
the wild tribes of Sānyán submitted,
and a native *qiānhù* was established,
subordinate to Bātáng.
The proposal to bring the two Tǔsī of Zhūwō and Zhānggǔ under direct rule was abolished.
On the day *Wùyín*,
an imperial decree ordered all provinces to protect churches and missionaries.
The fixed tax in Dídao, Bāyánrónggé, and other places was remitted.
In the twenty-fourth year, on the first day of the first month of spring, *Yǐyǒu*,
there was a solar eclipse.
New Year's Day ceremonies were moved to the Qiánqīng Palace,
and the imperial clan banquet was suspended.
On the day *Wùzǐ*,
an imperial decree ordered high officials in all provinces to deliberate on raising funds and training troops,
and to report their findings promptly.
On the day *Gēngyín*,
the special examination for economic talent and the annual recommendation system were established.
Officials were ordered to recommend suitable candidates, both Chinese and foreign, for the special examination.
On the day *Yǐwèi*,
the summer grain tax for drought-stricken Jiànshuǐ was remitted.
On the day *Jǐyǒu*,
the Emperor received foreign ministers at the Wénhuá Hall.
On the day *Rénzǐ*,
the summer grain tax for Shípíng and Kūnmíng was remitted.
In the second month, on the day *Jiǎzǐ*,
Liáo Shòuhéng was ordered to learn and serve as a Grand Councilor.
On the day *Bǐngyín*,
the horse tribute silver from the Ālīkèfān tribe in Qīnghǎi was remitted.
On the day *Yǐsì*,
10,000 *shí* of grain from Jiāngběi was retained to relieve the disaster in Xúzhōu.
On the day *Dīngchǒu*,
the Shénjī Battalion was ordered to select and train a vanguard unit.
On the day *Gēngchén*,
an imperial decree ordered the martial arts examination to change to testing spears and cannons,
and the silent recitation of martial classics was suspended.
In the third month, on the day *Dīnghài*,
an imperial decree ordered the establishment of public granaries.
On the day *Wùzǐ*,
the Russian minister, Bābùluófú (Mikhail Nikolaevich de Giers), was received in audience.
On the day *Yǐsì*,
the fixed tax for flood-stricken Xīnhuà was remitted.
This month,
the ports of Běidàihé to Qínwángdǎo in Zhílì, Yuèzhōu in Húnán, and Sāndū'ào in Fújiàn were opened.
In the intercalary third month, on the day *Yǐmǎo*,
Zhāng Zhīdòng was summoned to the capital.
On the day *Bǐngchén*,
Línshū died.
On the day *Gēngshēn*,
due to Germans entering the Jìmò Wénmiào [Confucian Temple]
and destroying images of sages and worthies,
the Zǒngshǔ was ordered to investigate.
On the day *Yǐchǒu*,
the Emperor visited Gōng Qīnwáng's residence to inquire about his illness.
On the day *Jiǎxū*,
the Emperor, accompanied by the Huáng Tàihòu, visited the Wàihuǒqìyíng drill ground
to review the drills of the Huǒqì, Jiànruì, Shénjī three battalions and the Wǔshèng new corps,
which lasted for three days.
On the day *Dīngchǒu*,
due to the burning of a church in Shāshì, Húběi,
Zhāng Zhīdòng was ordered to return to his post.
Relief for Xúzhōu and Hǎizhōu disasters was continued.
On the day *Wùyín*,
the Emperor received German Prince Hēnglì (Prince Heinrich of Prussia) at the Yùlán Hall.
On the day *Jǐmǎo*,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
The fixed tax for drought-stricken Xīnxīng was remitted.
On the day *Gēngchén*,
the Emperor received the French minister, Bìshèng (Auguste Gérard), at the Wénhuá Hall.
On the day *Rénwǔ*,
Fèngyáng, Yǐngzhōu, and Sìzhōu in Ānhuī suffered disasters.
This spring,
Jiāozhōuwān was leased to Germany,
and Lǚshùnkǒu, Dàliánwān, and the Liáodōng Peninsula were leased to Russia.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day rén-chén,
Gōng Qīnwáng Yìxīn passed away.
Court was suspended for five days,
and plain clothes were worn for fifteen days.
The emperor personally visited his residence to offer condolences.
An imperial decree specially granted him the posthumous title Zhōng.
The number of households guarding his garden tomb was increased,
and an official was to manage each sacrifice.
His grandson, Bèilè Pǔwěi, inherited the title.
On the day jiǎ-wǔ,
an imperial decree stated:
"Gōngzhōng Qīnwáng rendered great service to the state and its altars,
and should be honored in the Tàimiào."
An edict commanded all officials, both within and outside the capital, to emulate Gōngzhōng Qīnwáng,
each expressing their loyalty and sincerity,
and together overcoming the difficulties of the time.
On the day jǐ-hài,
Rónglù was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wényuān Gé,
and Gāngyì was appointed Minister of War and Associate Grand Secretary.
On the day yǐ-sì,
an edict declared the establishment of national policy,
and commanded:
"All officials, great and small, within and outside the capital,
from princes and dukes to scholars and commoners,
should all exert themselves to excel.
They should establish their foundation in the teachings of the sagely and virtuous regarding righteousness and principles,
and also broadly study Western learning pertinent to current affairs.
They must earnestly pursue these studies
to become talented individuals who are well-versed and capable of adapting to change.
The Jīngshī Dàxuétáng (Imperial University of Peking) should set an example for the provinces,
and should be established first.
The Grand Councilors and princely ministers are to deliberate thoroughly and report."
On the day bǐng-wǔ,
an edict ordered the establishment of Bureaus of Commerce in all provinces.
Xià Tónghé and 341 others were granted the jìnshì and related degrees, with varying ranks.
On the day jǐ-yǒu,
Wēng Tónghé was dismissed.
Imperial princes and dukes were selected to travel abroad for study.
Princes and bèilè of close lineage
were personally inspected by the Emperor;
dukes and below, as well as idle personnel,
were to be recommended by the Zōngrénfǔ.
Wáng Wénsháo was summoned to the capital.
The Dūdàn Jūnwù Chù (Bureau for Supervising Military Affairs) was abolished.
On the day gēng-xū,
Kāng Yǒuwéi, a director in the Board of Works, was granted an audience,
and ordered to serve as a secretary in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the day xīn-hài,
the Dàlài Lǎma of Qiánzàng presented tribute.
In the fifth month, on the first day guǐ-chǒu,
an edict ordered the army to be reorganized and trained in Western drills,
commanding officers who had mastered them to serve as trainers.
From the north, personnel from the Xīnjiàn Lùjūn (Newly Established Army) were to be dispatched,
and from the south, from the Zìqiáng Jūn (Self-Strengthening Army).
Each provincial governor was given six months
to propose a plan for consolidating military funds, training soldiers, and stationing troops,
and to report it.
Regarding armaments and cannons,
the various provincial machinery bureaus were to standardize models
and strive for precise manufacturing.
On the day jiǎ-yín,
relief was provided for the fire disaster in Qīxiá.
On the day dīng-sì,
an edict announced that starting from the next examinations,
the xiāng, huì, suì, and kē exams,
which had previously used "four books essays,"
would be changed to policy essays.
Sūn Jiānài was ordered to serve as Minister of Personnel and Associate Grand Secretary,
and Wáng Wénsháo as Minister of Revenue and Grand Councilor, concurrently serving in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
Rónglù was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì and concurrently Nányáng Dàchén.
On the day gēng-shēn,
Shèng Xuānhuái was urged to immediately commence work on the Lúhàn Railway,
and also to begin construction on the Yuèhàn and Nínghù railways.
On the day jiǎ-zǐ,
an edict ordered that the annual economic examinations be merged into the regular examinations,
and that the suì and kē exams be entirely changed to policy essays,
without waiting for the following year.
On the day dīng-mǎo,
an edict ordered the establishment of the Jīngshī Dàxuétáng,
and Sūn Jiānài was commanded to manage it.
The jǔrén Liáng Qǐchāo was granted a sixth-rank title,
and appointed to manage the Translation Bureau.
On the day wù-chén,
an edict ordered the promotion of agricultural studies.
It commanded:
"The revitalization of various affairs
first requires the encouragement of talent.
For scholars and commoners in the various provinces who write new books,
or create new methods,
or invent new instruments
that are practically useful,
rewards should be offered to encourage them.
They may be appointed to actual positions,
or bestowed with official attire.
For instruments produced, certificates shall be issued,
granting exclusive patent rights for sale for a limited number of years.
Those who single-handedly establish schools,
develop natural resources,
or build gun and cannon factories
shall also be rewarded according to military merit regulations."
On the day xīn-wèi,
the land tax for water-damaged fields in Lùquàn was remitted.
On the day guǐ-yǒu,
an edict ordered that half of the troops in the eight banners' two wings
be retrained in Western rifles and spear drills.
Yìkuāng and others were appointed to manage the Xiāoqíyíng,
and Chónglǐ and others to manage the Hùjūnyíng.
On the day jiǎ-xū,
an edict ordered that the academies in the various prefectures of the provinces be reformed into schools that teach both Chinese and Western subjects,
with provincial academies becoming higher schools,
prefectural academies becoming middle schools,
and zhou and county academies becoming primary schools.
The local charity schools and community schools were to follow suit.
On the day yǐ-hài,
Yùlù was appointed Grand Councilor.
On the day bǐng-zǐ,
an imperial command was issued to all provinces, prefectures, and counties to earnestly protect churches.
On the day dīng-chǒu,

officials of third rank and above in the capital, as well as provincial governors, viceroys, and education commissioners, were ordered to recommend individuals suitable for the special economic examinations.
Regulations for rewarding scholars and commoners for writing books,
making instruments, and initiating new policies were promulgated.
Officials within and outside the capital were ordered to recommend talented individuals in manufacturing, navigation, acoustics, optics, chemistry, and electricity.
On the day wù-yín,
an edict ordered all provinces to protect commerce.
The previous year's outstanding taxes for disaster-stricken Hǎikāng and Suíxī were remitted.
Relief was provided for flood and hail disasters in Cháng'ān and other prefectures and counties.
In the sixth month, on the first day guǐ-wèi,
an edict announced a revision of the imperial examination system.
On the day bǐng-xū,
relief was provided for disasters in Xú and Hǎi.
On the day jǐ-chǒu,
an edict promulgated Zhāng Zhīdòng's work Quànxuépiān,
ordering its publication in the provinces.
Kāng Yǒuwéi was ordered to oversee the official gazette.
On the day rén-chén,
Rónglù was ordered to jointly supervise the Lúhàn Railway with Zhāng Zhīdòng.
Bandits from Yùlín and Wúzhōu, together with secret society rebels, caused unrest,
capturing the three counties of Róng, Xīngyè, and Lùchuān.
The government troops suppressed them.
On the day bǐng-shēn,
Ráo Yìngqí presented tribute gold from the Huíbù.
On the day dīng-yǒu,
officials from the Hànlín Academy, the Imperial Secretariat, and the Censorate were ordered to hold rotating audiences with the emperor.
Clerks from the Boards and Censorate were to list current affairs,
and department heads were to present them on their behalf.
Scholars and commoners were allowed to submit memorials on current affairs.
A General Bureau for Mines and Railways was established in the capital,
with Wáng Wénsháo and Zhāng Yīnhuán as its special administrators.
On the day gēng-zǐ,
two gun and cannon factories were established in Húnán.
On the day xīn-chǒu,
relief was provided for the fire disaster in Níngqiāng,
and for flood and hail disasters in Xúnyáng and other counties.
On the day guǐ-mǎo,
Wǔ Tíngfāng was ordered to provide relief to Chinese residents in Gǔbā.
On the day yǐ-sì,
an imperial command stated:
"The current situation is difficult,
and urgent measures for self-strengthening are needed.
Officials within and outside the capital adhere rigidly to old regulations.
An earlier edict commanded them to study current affairs,
and not to fall into the old habits of the Sòng and Míng dynasties,
with earnest instructions.
However, the crucial tasks for renewal
are vast in scope
and numerous in detail,
making it necessary to widely gather strengths
and reconcile differences to arrive at the best solution.
When deliberating on matters, all officials
should consult broadly and inquire extensively,
discussing in detail.
They must not embellish with classical scholarship
or force ancient meanings,
nor should they rigidly cling to preconceived notions
or harbor selfish motives.
If they outwardly comply but inwardly dissent,
thus deviating from the court's fundamental principle of seeking truth from facts,
this is not what I expect.
I deeply reflect on the meaning of 'when at its extreme, change leads to continuity,'
and my creation of all these things
truly comes from an unavoidable difficulty.
Therefore, I reiterate this command to all of you officials:
May each of you purify your hearts,
forcefully remove all obstructions,
and let sincerity prevail between superiors and subordinates,
then the national policy will be settled,
and the path of governance will steadily progress."
The Northern and Southern Ocean Ministers were commanded to plan for naval, road, and mining schools.
An imperial command was issued to all provinces to widely open treaty ports.
Huáng Zūnxuàn was appointed a third-rank Metropolitan Official to serve as Minister Resident in Cháoxiǎn.
This summer,
the Kowloon Peninsula in Guǎngdōng and Wēihǎiwèi in Shāndōng were both leased to England.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *jiǎyín* day,
an edict was issued to suspend the court examination for newly advanced *jìnshì*,
and to abolish the examination of poetry and *fù* compositions.
Relief was provided to the prefectures and counties in Fèngtiān that were devastated by bandits.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
an edict established the Bureau of Agriculture, Industry, and Commerce in the capital,
with Duānfāng, Xú Jiànyín, and Wú Màodǐng appointed as its supervisors,
