and all were granted the rank of Third-Grade Minister.
It was decreed that envoys abroad should establish schools for overseas Chinese in England, America, and Japan.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Yellow River overflowed its banks in the upper and middle reaches of Shāndōng,
and six counties, including Jìyáng, were simultaneously inundated.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
an imperial edict determined that Her Imperial Majesty the Empress Dowager would visit Tiānjīn on the fifteenth day of the ninth month to review the troops.
The supervisor of the Shāshì Customs, the Intendant of Jīngyíshī, and the Magistrate of Jiānglíng County were all moved to reside in Shāshì Town.
On the *rénxū* day,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Nányáng.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
an edict was issued to abolish the Court of Imperial Household (Zhānshìfǔ),
the Office of Transmission (Tōngzhèngsī),
and the Courts of Judicial Review (Dàlǐsì), Imperial Entertainments (Guānglùsì), Imperial Stud (Tàipúsì), and Imperial Receptions (Hónglúsì).
Their affairs were consolidated and placed under the concurrent management of the Grand Secretariat (Nèigé), Board of Rites (Lǐbù), Board of War (Bīngbù), and Board of Punishments (Xíngbù).
The Governors (Xúnfǔ) of Húběi, Guǎngdōng, and Yúnnán were abolished,
with their duties concurrently managed by the Governors-General (Zǒngdū).
The Governor-General of Riverways in Hédōng was merged with the Governor of Hénán.
The Grain Intendants (Liángdào) and Salt Intendants (Yándào) of various provinces were also abolished.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
for obstructing freedom of speech
and being the first to defy imperial edicts,
Huáitābù and Xǔ Yīngkuí, Presidents of the Board of Rites,
along with the Vice-Presidents Kūnxiù, Xú Huìfēng, Pǔtíng, and Zēng Guǎnghàn, were stripped of their posts.
Wáng Zhào, a Principal who submitted memorials, was rewarded with a Fourth-Grade Metropolitan position.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Zēng Guófān's regulations for judicial rectitude in prefectures and counties, and the criteria for merits and demerits, were promulgated to all provinces,
and the merits and demerits for intendants (dàofǔ) were also increased.
An edict was issued to dredge the rivers and canals in the capital,
and to repair roads and pathways.
An edict instructed all provinces to implement *tuánliàn* (local militia).

Yáng Ruì, Reader of the Grand Secretariat; Lín Xù, Secretary of the Grand Secretariat; Liú Guāngdì, Principal of the Board of Punishments; and Tán Sìtóng, Prefect of Jiāngsū, were all granted the additional rank of Fourth-Grade Minister,
to participate in the New Policies.
Relief was provided for the flood disaster in Jiànshuǐ.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was dismissed from serving in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén (Office for the General Management of Foreign Affairs).
Yùlù was appointed President of the Board of Rites,
and served in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Third, Fourth, and Fifth-Grade Ministers were established,
along with Third, Fourth, Fifth, and Sixth-Grade Academicians.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Tàihé.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Yuán Shìkǎi was summoned to the capital.
An imperial edict stated:
"The nation is revitalizing various administrative matters,
and adopting Western methods.
It is sincerely believed that establishing policies for the people
is common to both China and the West,
and Western methods can supplement what we lack.
Today, officials and scholars, ignorant of views from beyond our borders,
often claim that there are no principles or teachings whatsoever in those lands.
They do not know that the myriad aspects of Western governance
are generally aimed at enlightening the people's wisdom
and enriching their households.
Their essence is even capable of refining character and prolonging life.
The benefits to human life
are extensively promoted without omission.
I, day and night assiduously,
have reformed a hundred systems,
not out of a desire for novelty.
Rather, I cherish my people,
all bestowed by Heaven,
and inherited from my ancestors.
Unless all of them are made prosperous, joyful, and harmonious,
my duty is not fully discharged.
Furthermore, as various nations press upon us,
unless we adopt their strengths,
we cannot preserve what we possess.
My efforts are arduous,
yet the common people remain unaware.
This is due to unworthy officials and conservative scholars who fail to widely propagate my intentions.
They even stir up rumors,
causing the common people to waver in confusion and fear.
I deeply lament
that even people in remote mountains and valleys, relying on their staffs,
have not heard of the New Policies.
Now, the meaning of these reforms
will be proclaimed to the whole empire,
so that all the people may understand my heart
and know that their sovereign can be relied upon.
With upper and lower united in purpose,
to achieve the New Policies,
and to strengthen China,
I harbor no small hopes."
An edict instructed all provinces to abolish post stations
and establish postal services.
Strictly prohibited the export of grain.
In the eighth month, on the *rénwǔ* day, the first day of the lunar month,
the Board of Revenue (Hùbù) was ordered to compile and promulgate tables of annual income and expenditure.
An edict instructed envoys abroad to recruit and send overseas Chinese back to the country for official appointments.
Yuán Shìkǎi was appointed as a Vice-Minister on probation,
specifically to manage military training affairs.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Itō Hirobumi, a Japanese marquis, and Hayashi Gonsuke, the acting envoy, were received in the Qínzhèng Diàn.
Relief was provided for flood disasters in Shèhóng and other counties,
and for flood and hail disasters in Lüèyáng and other counties.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the Empress Dowager resumed her regency behind a curtain in the Bìandiàn to govern.
An edict declared Kāng Yǒuwéi to have formed a faction for personal gain,
and to have spread treacherous words to disturb governance.
He was stripped of his position,
and he and his brother, Guǎngréng, were both arrested and imprisoned.
Yǒuwéi escaped.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
an edict was issued to arrest Kāng Yǒuwéi and Liáng Qǐchāo.
On the *gēngyín* day,

Zhāng Yīnhuán, Vice-President of the Board of Revenue; Xú Zhìjìng, Academician-Reader of the Hanlin Academy; Yáng Shēnxiù, Censor; along with Yáng Ruì, Lín Xù, Liú Guāngdì, and Tán Sìtóng, were all implicated as Kāng Yǒuwéi's associates, arrested, and imprisoned.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Emperor claimed illness,
and sought physicians from across the empire.
Rónglù was summoned to the capital.
Orders were issued to arrest Wén Tíngshì
and capture Sūn Wén.
On the *rénchén* day,
an edict reinstated the Court of Imperial Household (Zhānshìfǔ),
the Office of Transmission (Tōngzhèngsī),
and the Courts of Judicial Review (Dàlǐsì), Imperial Entertainments (Guānglùsì), Imperial Stud (Tàipúsì), and Imperial Receptions (Hónglúsì).
Prohibited officials and commoners from unauthorized submission of sealed memorials.
The "Official Gazette on Current Affairs" (Shíwù Guānbào) was abolished.
Temples and shrines in various provinces were not to be converted into schools.
Xú Yòngyí, Vice-President of the Board of Civil Office (Lìbù), was ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *guǐsì* day,
eighty thousand *shí* of Jiangnan tribute grain were diverted to be commuted to silver,
to be used for disaster relief in Xúzhōu and Hǎizhōu.
Relief was provided for the flood disaster in Gāozhōu.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Yáng Shēnxiù, Yáng Ruì, Lín Xù, Liú Guāngdì, Tán Sìtóng, and Kāng Guǎngréng were all executed by decapitation.
Zhāng Yīnhuán was exiled to Xīnjiāng.
Xú Zhìjìng was imprisoned.
Rónglù was appointed Grand Councillor (Jūnjī Dàchén).
Yùlù was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì and concurrent Minister Superintendent of Northern Ocean Affairs (Běiyáng Dàchén).
On the *yǐwèi* day,
due to Kāng Yǒuwéi's high treason and disrespect,
and his incitement of conspiracy,
a vermilion edict was promulgated to declare this to his subordinates.
The inspection tour to Tiānjīn for military review was cancelled.
Rónglù was ordered to take charge of the Board of War,
and concurrently to supervise the Northern Ocean Armies and Sòng Qìng's forces.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the properties of Kāng Yǒuwéi and Liáng Qǐchāo were confiscated.
Zhào Shūqiáo was ordered to collaborate with Wáng Wénsháo in supervising the General Bureau of Mines and Railways.
An edict stipulated that new tribute grain from Sūzhōu and Zhèjiāng be transported to the capital,
and the proposal for commutation was abolished.
New tribute grain from Shāndōng was retained for disaster relief.
On the *wùxū* day,
Yuán Chǎng was rewarded with a Third-Grade Metropolitan position,
and served in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Lǐ Duānfēn was stripped of his post for excessive recommendations
and banished to Xīnjiāng.
Wáng Zhào was stripped of his post,
his property confiscated,
and he was arrested.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Wén Tì, former Censor, was rewarded with a Prefectural position.
On the *rén'yín* day,
Huáng Zūnxian was excused due to illness.
Lǐ Shèngduó was rewarded with a Fourth-Grade Metropolitan position and appointed Envoy to Japan.
Chén Bǎozhēn was stripped of his post as Governor of Húnán for excessive recommendations.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
an edict instructed frontier officials to rectify governance,
cultivate talent,
open up financial sources,
improve military preparedness,
impeach or promote local officials,
and reorganize military camp regulations.
An edict instructed officials responsible for counsel to point out the gains and losses in national affairs,
but those who confused right and wrong or attacked others were to be punished.
On the *yǐsì* day,
an Imperial Decree reinstated the old system of provincial (*xiāngshì*) and metropolitan (*huìshì*) examinations, and annual (*suìkǎo*) and triennial (*kēkǎo*) examinations,
abolished the special economic examination (jīngjì tèkē),
and abolished the Bureaus of Agriculture, Industry, and Commerce.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Duānfāng presented the "Song for Encouraging Goodness" he had compiled,
and an edict ordered its promulgation.
An Imperial Decree instructed frontier officials to protect the lives of the people,
carefully select upright and benevolent individuals,
and rectify the *bǎojiǎ* and *tuánliàn* systems.
All matters concerning water conservancy and sericulture,
as well as manufacturing and trade,
which benefit the common people,
were to be taught and guided in a timely manner.
Reaffirmed the prohibition against forming associations by joint signature.
Rónglù was appointed Imperial Commissioner.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Yùlù was ordered to co-manage the Lú-Hàn and other railway lines.
Water conservancy bureaus were established in Shànghǎi and Hànkǒu.
On the *xīnhài* day of the ninth month, which was the first day of the lunar month,
an imperial decree was issued, stating:
"All political matters concerning national welfare and the people's livelihood,
whether old or new,
shall continue to be implemented in due course.
The memorials submitted by ministers offering suggestions must be beneficial to the current situation,
and they must not make wild conjectures."
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
twenty *wàn* taels were disbursed from the imperial treasury to relieve the flood disaster in Shāndōng.
There was an earthquake in Gānsù and Xīnjiāng.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the bandits in Guǎngxī were suppressed.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the Grand Councilors were ordered to convene with the Grand Secretaries and ministers of the Six Boards and Censorate to deliberate on strategies for river management.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
previously,
in cases of robbery with violence,
no distinction was made between principals and accessories.
By this time,
the Grand Councilors and the judicial authorities were ordered to deliberate in detail on how to differentiate between them.
There was an earthquake in Dàizhōu.
On the *rénxū* day,
outstanding taxes in Xiánníng and other places in Shǎnxī were remitted.
On the *wùchén* day,
the old system of the military provincial examinations (*wǔxiāng*), metropolitan military examinations (*huìshì*), and preliminary military examinations for children (*tóngshì*) was restored.
However, military *jìnshì* and military *jǔrén* who were designated for service were required to practice firearms and artillery.
The positions of Provincial Governor (*xúnfǔ*) of Húběi, Guǎngdōng, and Yúnnán were restored,
as was the Governor-General of River Conservancy for Hédōng.
The abolition of the grain transport intendants (*liángdào*) and other posts was rescinded.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Xǔ Jǐngchéng was ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the old system of judicial reviews for criminal cases was restored,
except for military districts and cases of major significance,
where summary execution on the spot was still permitted;
otherwise, it was not allowed.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Hú Yùfēn was ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the manufacturing operations of the Fúzhōu Shipyard were temporarily suspended.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was ordered to inspect the Yellow River in Shāndōng.
This month,
disaster relief was provided to various provinces including Zhí, Shǎn, Chuān, È, Sū, Diān, Jìn, and Xīn.
In the winter, on the *xīnsì* day of the tenth month, which was the first day of the lunar month,
sacrifices were offered at the Tàimiào.
Lǐ Qīnwáng Shìduó presided over the ceremony.
Thereafter, sacrificial rites at the suburban altars and ancestral temples were all performed by deputies.
It was not until the winter of the *xīnchǒu* year, upon his return to the capital from Xī’ān,
that he personally attended these rites.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Circuit Intendant Zhāng Yì was ordered to supervise mining affairs in Zhílì and Rèhé,
and a company was established.
Disaster relief was provided to various prefectures in Shùntiān.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
disaster relief was provided to Hánchéng and other counties.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to allocate eighty *qiān* taels from the treasury for disaster relief in Ānhuī.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Wēng Tónghé's official titles were retroactively stripped.
The former Provincial Governor of Húnán, Wú Dàchéng, was stripped of his office for an offense.
The breach at Jìyáng was sealed.
On the *rénwín* day,
a reward was offered for the capture of Kāng Yǒuwéi, Liáng Qǐchāo, and Wáng Zhào.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Rónglù's request was granted,
to divide the forces of Sòng Qìng, Niè Shìchéng, Yuán Shìkǎi, and Dǒng Fúxiáng into four armies,
and recruit an additional ten *qiān* men to form the central army.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Gě'ěrsī, the Russian envoy, was received at the Qínzhèng Diàn.
Hú Yùfēn was ordered to supervise the Jīnjhèn Railway,
with Zhāng Yì as his deputy.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
relief was provided for flood and hail disasters in Luópíng.
In the eleventh month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
Zhāng Rǔméi was instructed to handle disaster relief in Shāndōng.
Guìchūn was awarded the Third Rank Metropolitan Official title,
and ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Qǐxiù was appointed Grand Councilor,
and Zhào Shūqiáo and Lián Yuán were both ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the grain commutation funds (*cáozhé*) from Hénán were retained in Huáxiàn for disaster relief.
Two hundred *qiān* taels from the treasury were allocated to Jiāngsū for disaster relief.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Pǔliáng was ordered to investigate disaster relief in Shāndōng.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Yùgēng was ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
frontier officials were ordered to concurrently hold the title of Minister of the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *rénshēn* day,
relief was provided for flood and locust disasters in Tǔlǔfān and other places.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
due to feigned illness, the customary year-end court banquet was suspended.
On the *wùyín* day,
the drilled armies (*liànjūn*) in Zhílì were disbanded.
In the twelfth month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
Zēng Hé, the Provincial Governor of Húběi, was dismissed from office for an offense.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Mǎ Yùkūn was ordered to Hénán to manage defense and suppression.
Hú Yùfēn was dismissed as Superintendent of the Jīnlú Railway,
and Xǔ Jǐngchéng was appointed in his place.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the assessed taxes (*éfù*) for disaster-stricken prefectures and counties such as Hànyáng were remitted.
On the *rényín* day,
the Hǎnkǒu Assistant Prefect (*tóngzhī*) in Húběi was renamed the Xiàkǒu Assistant Prefect for Civil Affairs (*fǔmín tóngzhī*).
On the *wùshēn* day,
fifty *qiān* taels from the imperial treasury were allocated to Qīng and Huái for disaster relief.
In the twenty-fifth year, the *jǐhài* year, in spring, on the *gēngxū* day of the first month,
disaster victims in prefectures and counties of Yù and Wǎn that were afflicted by bandits were given relief.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
an imperial edict was issued to clear ordinary prison cases.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
taxes and grain levies for Wōyáng and other prefectures and counties afflicted by bandits were remitted.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
foreign envoys stationed in the capital were stopped from offering congratulations.
On the *rénxū* day,
an additional fifty *qiān* taels from the Ministry's treasury were allocated to Ānhuī for disaster relief.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Lǐ Bǐnghéng was summoned to the capital.
In the second month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
the provinces were emphatically instructed to manage stored grain, clear lawsuits, organize local militias (*tuánliàn*), and implement the *bǎojiǎ* system.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the new Wǔshèng Battalion was named Hǔshényíng.
The *bǎojiǎ* system was implemented in the capital.
On the *wùxū* day,
German soldiers in Jiāozhōuwān, using the pretext of protecting missionaries,
entered the territory of Yízhōu.
Lǚ Hǎihuán was ordered to inform the German Foreign Office
to stop their advance.
Given the effective training of the newly established army,
Yuán Shìkǎi was granted special commendation.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Deputy Commander-in-Chief Shòushān was ordered to recruit and train sixteen battalions,
to form the Zhènbiān New Army.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
German soldiers reached Lánshān.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Rìzhào city was captured.
In the third month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
an edict was issued to all prefectures, subprefectures, and counties with grain transport duties,
stating that from this winter onwards,
they should collect actual grain for transport to the capital.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Sū Yuánchūn was summoned to the capital.
In summer, on the *guǐwèi* day of the fourth month,
an edict stated:
"Recently, due to difficult times,
the court has diligently sought governance,
repeatedly instructing frontier officials to rectify all matters.
While the subsequent reports on training troops, raising funds, *bǎojiǎ*, *tuánliàn*, and grain storage were not empty words,
they still lacked concrete results.
Therefore, it is re-emphasized that all planned matters
must be promptly implemented.
Furthermore,
whether or not they achieve results
must be truthfully reported."
Frontier officials were emphatically instructed to thoroughly inspect military camps.
They were also instructed to survey barren land,
encourage the people to reclaim it,
not allow clerks and yamen runners to extort,
and not to hastily propose new land taxes.
Italian warships arrived,
intending to land at Sānménwān,
and strict preparations were ordered.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Gāngyì was ordered to visit the provinces of Jiāngnán to verify the actual figures of treasury receipts and disbursements.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Niè Shìchéng's four cavalry and infantry battalions were ordered to be stationed in Rèhé,
to strengthen border defenses.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Liú Kūnyī and others were instructed to gather heavy troops in preparation;
if Italian soldiers landed,
they were to be met and attacked immediately.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Surveillance Commissioner Lǐ Guāngjiǔ was ordered to supervise defense and suppression in Zhèjiāng,
and Chángshùn was sent to Jílín to inspect troop training.
On the *yǐsì* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Customs duties, *líjīn*, and salt taxes
have annual regular expenditures,
but frontier officials are swayed by personal connections
and cannot forcefully eliminate accumulated abuses.
The Grand Secretaries and Grand Councilors shall meticulously review and deliberate on this and report."
In the fifth month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
Wú Tíngfēn was ordered to serve in the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
there was a fire at the arsenal and gunpowder magazine of the Shénjīyíng.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Yùgēng, a Junior Supervisor of the Court of the Imperial Stud, was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to France.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Yáng Yùshū, the Brigade-General of Zhèngdìng Garrison, was ordered to command the trained troops stationed in Rèhé.
Land taxes on flooded fields in Ānhuà, Wǔgāng, and Xīnníng were remitted.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Yuèzhōu was opened as a commercial port,
the Yuèchánglǐ Circuit Intendant was moved there to reside,
and concurrently served as Superintendent of the Yuèzhōu Customs.
On the _wùzǐ_ day of the sixth month,
taxes in arrears were remitted for Dǐhuà and other districts.
On the _dīngyǒu_ day,
an edict was issued to reorganize the navy
and eliminate its long-standing malpractices.
On the _gēngzǐ_ day,
disaster relief was provided for flood-stricken Lúlíng and other counties.
In autumn, on the _gēngxū_ day of the seventh month,
due to the French leasing Guǎngzhōuwān,
Sū Yuánchūn was ordered to go and conduct a joint survey.
On the _yǐmǎo_ day,
a commercial treaty with Cháoxiǎn was concluded.
On the _dīngsì_ day,
Qínhuángdǎo was opened as a commercial port.
On the _jǐsì_ day,
Gāngyì was ordered to Guǎngdōng to clear up financial matters.
On the _gēngwǔ_ day,
Sū Yuánchūn was ordered to go to Huái and Xú to train troops,
subject to Rónglù's command.
On the _dīnghài_ day of the eighth month,
a Hui rebellion occurred in Hǎichéng, Gānsù,
which was suppressed by government forces.
On the _jǐhài_ day,
an imperial decree ordered all provinces to preach the Sacred Edict and Amplified Instructions.
On the _jiǎchén_ day,
banditry broke out in Jǐnzhōu and Guǎngníng,
which was suppressed.
On the _dīngwèi_ day of the ninth month,
due to drought, an edict called for frank criticism.
On the _gēngxū_ day,
an edict ordered the clearing of lawsuits
and deferment of tax collection.
Provincial officials were instructed to rectify themselves and lead their subordinates,
uphold justice,
and follow public sentiment.
On the _jǐwèi_ day,
Vice Commander Shòucháng was stripped of his position and exiled for neglecting military affairs.
Rónghé was stripped of his position and arrested for questioning.
On the _xīnyǒu_ day,
Lǐ Zhēngyōng was appointed Imperial Commissioner for Commercial and Mining Affairs in Sìchuān.
On the _jiǎxū_ day,
more Italian warships arrived,
and Zhí, Lǔ, Jiāng, and Zhè were ordered to maintain strict defenses.
This autumn,
disaster relief was provided for floods in Zhèjiāng, Húnán, and Gānsù,
and for drought in Shǎnxī.
In winter, on the _gēngyín_ day of the tenth month,
Lǐ Bǐnghéng was ordered to inspect the Yangtze River Fleet.
On the _bǐngshēn_ day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was appointed Minister for Commercial Affairs
to inspect commercial ports.
On the _rényín_ day,
taxes in arrears from the previous year in Xiánníng and other places in Shǎnxī were remitted.
On the _guǐchǒu_ day of the eleventh month,
Xú Shòupéng, Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, was appointed Minister to Hánguó.
On the _jiǎyín_ day,
Liáo Shòuhéng was dismissed as Grand Councilor,
and Zhào Shūqiáo was ordered to learn the duties of a Grand Councilor.
Taxes in arrears from the previous year for Běiliú, which had suffered from bandits, were remitted.
On the _rénxū_ day,
the crimes of Kāng Yǒuwéi and Liáng Qǐchāo were again publicized,
and a large reward was offered for their capture.
On the _wùchén_ day,
Sūn Jiānài was relieved of his duties due to illness.
On the _jǐsì_ day,
Wáng Wénsháo, Minister of Revenue, was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary.
On the first day of the twelfth month, _jiǎxū_,
an edict ordered the cancellation of the New Year's ascending-to-the-hall banquet.
On the _bǐngzǐ_ day,
the Censorate's review was held,
and strict orders were given against fraud.
On the _yǐyǒu_ day,
taxes on disaster-stricken fields in Yúlín and other places were remitted.
On the _jǐchǒu_ day,
Sū Yuánchūn was dismissed from training troops in Jiāngnán
and returned to his post as Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Guǎngxī.
On the _yǐwèi_ day,
Chén Zélín was ordered to recruit volunteers and station them north of the Yangtze for training,
to serve as the Vanguard Right Army of the Wǔwèi.
On the _dīngyǒu_ day,
an edict declared Pǔjùn, son of Prince Duān Zǎiyì, as heir to Mùzōng,
and he was enfeoffed as Imperial Prince.
Chóngqǐ was ordered to serve in the Hóngdé Hall
to instruct Imperial Prince Pǔjùn.
On the _rényín_ day,
an edict announced that for the upcoming year's 30th birthday celebration,
court congratulations and banquets would be suspended,
and only high-ranking civil and military officials would come to the capital to offer felicitations.
A special grace examination was decreed,
with the provincial examination in the following year, _gēngzǐ_,
and the metropolitan examination in the year after that, _xīnchǒu_.
The regular provincial and metropolitan examinations
were postponed to the _xīnchǒu_ and _rényín_ years respectively.
This winter,
disaster relief was provided for Shānxī, Yúnnán, Shǎnxī, Gānsù, Shāndōng and other affected areas.
This year,
Guǎngzhōuwān was leased to France,
and the Diān-Yuè railway was opened.
On the first day of the first month, _jiǎchén_, in the 26th year, _gēngzǐ_, of spring,
an edict announced special favors for imperial relatives and close officials
on the occasion of the 30th birthday celebration.
On the _jǐyǒu_ day,
Prince Chún Zǎifēng was ordered to serve in the Inner Court,
and Lecturer Bǎofēng was ordered to serve in the Hóngdé Hall.
The autumn executions for this year were suspended.
On the _rénzǐ_ day,
previously,
Prefect Jīng Yuánshàn had jointly submitted a memorial advising against the establishment of an heir.
Now,
an edict ordered his strict capture and punishment,
and his property was soon confiscated.
On the _wùzǐ_ day,
an edict ordered a widespread search for Kāng Yǒuwéi and Liáng Qǐchāo,
the destruction of their writings,
and punishment for those who read their newspapers.
On the _rénxū_ day,
the Yí and Píng tribes were once again strictly pacified,
and various native official positions were added in Bātáng and other places.
On the _guǐhài_ day,
the Zǒngshǔ negotiated the Guǎngzhōuwān lease with the French,
setting the term at ninety-nine years.
On the _jiǎzǐ_ day,
thirty thousand _shí_ of southern grain tribute were retained to relieve disaster victims in Héběi.
This month,
the Boxer bandits rose in Shāndōng,
calling themselves
"Yìhéquán Huì" (Society of Righteous Harmonious Fists).
Under the guise of anti-Christian sentiment,
they engaged in robbery and murder,
spreading harm.
On the _bǐngzǐ_ day of the second month,
the Yellow River breached its banks in Bīnzhōu.
On the _yǐyǒu_ day,
disaster-stricken Kūnmíng and other prefectures and counties were exempted from their fixed taxes.
On the _wùxū_ day,
a treaty with Mexico was concluded.
On the _wùshēn_ day of the third month,
Lǐ Shèngduó was appointed envoy to Japan
to congratulate its crown prince on his marriage;
Lǚ Hǎihuán was appointed envoy to Germany
to congratulate its crown prince on his coming of age.
On the _rénzǐ_ day,
the breach at Bīnzhōu was closed.
On the _guǐchǒu_ day,
due to drought, an edict ordered the review of prisoners inside and outside the capital.
On the _jiǎyín_ day,
Gāo Gēng'ēn was awarded a fourth-rank京堂 (Jīngtáng) official position
and ordered to serve in the Hóngdé Hall.
On the _dīngsì_ day,
Cabinet Academician Guìchūn was appointed Minister to Russia,
and soon after was also appointed Minister to Austria.
One hundred thousand taels from the Board of Revenue were allocated to relieve flood victims in Shāndōng and Guìzhōu.
On the _jǐwèi_ day,
the Jìngyuǎn Yí were pacified and brought to allegiance,
and their native officials were established.
On the _rénxū_ day,
Yuán Shìkǎi was ordered to gather twenty battalions of new troops,
forming an additional army,
named the Vanguard Detachment of the Wǔwèi Right Army.
In summer, on the _yǐyǒu_ day of the fourth month,
Shànlián was dismissed,
and Xǔ Yìngkuí was concurrently put in charge of naval administration.
On the _gēngyín_ day,
the Yìhéquán entered the capital,
and the Commander of the Gendarmerie and others were ordered to convene and discuss defensive measures.
On the _xīnmǎo_ day,
Xuānwēi and Sōngmíng, affected by floods, were exempted from autumn taxes.
On the _bǐngshēn_ day,
relief was provided for flood and drought disasters in Chóngqìng and other places.
On the _dīngyǒu_ day,
the Zǒngshǔ reported that the Boxer society was spreading rumors and inciting people,
causing public unrest
and easily leading to conflicts.
The relevant authorities were ordered to deliberate thoroughly.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was appointed Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng.
On the _gēngzǐ_ day,
Xīnhuà and other prefectures and counties affected by floods were exempted from their fixed taxes.
This month,
the Boxer bandits burned and destroyed the railroad at Bǎodìng,
and Deputy General Yáng Fútóng went to suppress them,
but on his way to Láishuǐ,
he was murdered.
In the fifth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
the Boxers destroyed the railway stations, bureaus, and factories at Liúlíhé and Chángxīndiàn.
Niè Shìchéng was ordered to protect the Lúbǎo and Jīnlú routes
and defend them.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Zǎiyī was ordered to manage the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén (Tsûng-li Kôkuo Ssûwu Yamên, Office for General Management of Foreign Affairs).
Qǐxiù, Pǔxīng, and Nàtóng were simultaneously appointed to act in an interim capacity.
Liáo Shòuhéng was dismissed.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the Boxers killed Sugiyama Akira, a secretary of the Japanese legation, outside Yǒngdìngmén.
On the day Dīngsì,
an imperial edict ordered Mǎ Yùkūn to proceed to the west of the capital to suppress the Boxers.
Dàgū was put under martial law.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the Boxers disturbed the five city districts,
and blood flowed in the markets.

An imperial decree ordered the Bùjūn Tǒnglǐng (Commander of the Gendarmerie), the Shénjī Yíng (Divine Machine Camp), the Hǔshén Yíng (Tiger Spirit Camp), and the Wǔwèi Zhōngjūn (Central Army of the Guards) to patrol together.
Ministers were to inspect the streets
and be stationed at the nine gates to monitor their opening and closing.
Lǐ Hóngzhāng and Yuán Shìkǎi were summoned to guard the capital.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Rónglù, with the Wǔwèi Zhōngjūn, protected the foreign legations.
Lǐ Duānyù and Wáng Yìróng were appointed as Jīngshī Tuánliàn Dàchén (Ministers for Militia Affairs of the Capital).
Lǐ Bǐnghéng and Mǎ Yùkūn were summoned to lead troops to the capital.
That evening,
the Boxers burned the Zhèngyángmén gate tower,
and the neighborhoods and markets turned to ashes.
On the day Gēngshēn,
an imperial decree ordered Gāngyì and Dǒng Fúxiáng to recruit able-bodied Boxers to form an army,
while the rest were to be disbanded.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
an imperial decree ordered each province to send troops to guard the capital.
Foreign forces attacked Dàgūkǒu.
The Tídū (Admiral) Luó Róngguāng could not defend it
and fled to Tiānjīn,
where he died.
Dàgū subsequently fell.
Yùlù reported a victory,
and an imperial decree released one hundred thousand from the imperial treasury to reward the army.
On the day Rénxū,
Xú Tóng and Chóngqǐ were ordered to consult with Yìkuāng, Zàilián, and others on military affairs.
On the day Guǐhài,
Xǔ Jǐngchéng and Nàtóng were ordered to inform the foreign envoys to leave the capital quickly.
From the day Gēngshēn until this day,
the Empress Dowager repeatedly summoned the princes and high officials for audiences,
seeking their opinions.
Zǎiyī strongly advocated for war.
Zǎixūn, Zàilián, Zǎilán, Xú Tóng, Chóngqǐ, Qǐxiù, Pǔliáng, Xú Chéngyù, and others
followed suit.
Rónglù wavered in between.
Only Xǔ Jǐngchéng and Yuán Chàng stated that the Boxers should be suppressed
and that a conflict should not be initiated.
Killing envoys
violated international law,
and their words were very direct and urgent.
Hence, this order was given.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Boxers assassinated the German envoy Klemens von Ketteler inside Chóngwénmén.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
an imperial decree, stating that a conflict had erupted between China and foreign powers,
ordered preparations for war.
Chónglǐ was dismissed as Bùjūn Tǒnglǐng.
Zǎixūn replaced him.
Granary rice was released for sale to aid the people's food supply.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Lù Chuánlín was summoned to the capital.
In the sixth month, on the first day Xīnwèi,
an edict ordered Shùntiān Fǔ and the five city districts to sell grain at stable prices
and bury the exposed bodies of Christian converts.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Liú Ēnpǔ, the Cāngcháng Shìláng (Vice Minister of the Granary), was ordered to go to Tiānjīn to recruit strong men for water transport,
organize them into an army,
and station them in Zhílì with the militia from Tōngzhōu, Wǔqīng, and Dōng'ān,
providing them with provisions and weapons.
The granary in Tōngzhōu was opened for sale.
Chángcuì and others stated that the water route to Tiānjīn was blocked
and requested a temporary halt to grain transport,
which was not permitted.
On the day Yǐhài,
an edict ordered each province to protect missionaries and send them back to their home countries,
and Christian converts who repented and surrendered would be allowed to start anew.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the southern grain transport was blocked,
so an office was ordered to be established at Qīngjiāngpǔ
to purchase and transport grain to the capital.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was transferred as Zhílì Zǒngdū (Governor-General of Zhílì) and Běiyáng Dàchén (Minister of Beiyang),
and was urged to hasten to the capital.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
an imperial decree postponed this year's ēn kē xiāngshì (special provincial examination)
to the eighth day of the third month of next year,
and the huìshì (metropolitan examination) to the eighth day of the eighth month.
The regular Gēngzǐ xiāngshì and huìshì would be postponed accordingly.
Foreign forces attacked Tiānjīn.
Niè Shìchéng fought at Bālǐtái
and died.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Lǚ Běnyuán was appointed Zhílì Tídū (Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Zhílì).
Tiānjīn fell.
Yùlù, Sòng Qìng, and Mǎ Yùkūn all retreated to Běicāng.
On the day Gēngyín,
Gù Huáng and Zhāng Rénfǔ were ordered to jointly manage the Hénán Tuánfáng (Henan Militia).
Hùbù Shàngshū (Minister of Revenue) Lìshān was imprisoned.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
an imperial decree ordered the apprehension of the culprits who assassinated the German envoy.
Élèhébù died.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
on the thirtieth birthday of the Emperor,
the Dōnghuámén was not opened,
and all officials entered for congratulations through the Shénwǔmén.
The extra taxes for a year in Shūfù and Báichéng, which had suffered disasters, were remitted.
Relief was provided for the flood disaster in Fújiàn.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the first day Gēngzǐ,
Lǐ Bǐnghéng was ordered to assist in military affairs of the Wǔwèi Army,
and the armies of Zhāng Chūnfā, Chén Zélín, Wàn Běnhuá, and Xià Xīnyǒu were all placed under his command.
On the day Rényín,
Lìbù Shìláng (Vice Minister of Personnel) Xǔ Jǐngchéng and Tàicháng Sì Qīng (Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices) Yuán Chàng were killed.
On the day Yǐsì,
Mǎ Yùkūn was transferred as Zhílì Tídū.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Rónglù was ordered to escort the foreign envoys to Tiānjīn with troops.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
foreign forces occupied Běicāng.
On the day Gēngxū,
Yángcūn fell,
and Zhílì Zǒngdū Yùlù committed suicide.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng was appointed Plenipotentiary Minister
to negotiate a ceasefire with the foreign powers.
Foreign forces attacked Càicūn.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Lǐ Bǐnghéng fought at Càicūn
and was defeated.
Foreign forces advanced and occupied Héxīwù.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Zēngqí reported that Gàipíng and Xióngyuè had fallen one after another.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Hùbù Shàngshū Lìshān, Bīngbù Shàngshū (Minister of War) Xú Yòngyí, and Nèigé Xuéshì (Grand Secretary of the Cabinet) Lián Yuán were killed.
Lǐ Bǐnghéng was defeated at Zhāngjiāwān
and died.
On the day Dīngsì,
foreign forces captured Tōngzhōu.
Gāngyì was ordered to assist in military affairs of the Wǔwèi Army.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the combined forces of eight nations—Germany, Austria, America, France, Britain, Italy, Japan, and Russia—captured the capital.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, proceeded to Tàiyuán.
The imperial procession passed through the market.
On the day Rényīn,
they reached Huáilái.
Rónglù, Xú Tóng, and Chóngqǐ were ordered to remain in the capital to handle affairs.
On the day Guǐhài,
Cén Chūnshuān, the Guǎngdōng Bùzhèngshǐ (Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangdong), led troops to guard the capital,
and was then ordered to escort the imperial retinue.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
they reached Shābǎopú.
An imperial decree ordered Cén Chūnshuān to supervise the supply train for the front route.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
they reached Jīmíng Yì,
where an edict was issued blaming the Emperor himself
and admonishing all officials, both Chinese and foreign.
On the day Bǐngyín,
they reached Xuānhuà.
Wàn Běnhuá, Sūn Wànlín, and Qí Kèshēn were ordered to array their troops under Mǎ Yùkūn's command
and be stationed on the rear route.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
an imperial decree called for frank advice.
The land taxes for one year in Wǎnpíng, Chāngpíng, and other places passed by the imperial procession were remitted.
On the *gēngwǔ* day of the eighth month, the first day of the lunar month,
we arrived at Zuǒwèi.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
we arrived at Huái'ān.
On the *rénshēn* day,
we arrived at Tiānzhèn.
An imperial decree ordered Yìkuāng to return to the capital
to meet Lǐ Hóngzhāng and negotiate peace.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
we arrived at Yánggāo.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
we arrived at Jùlèzhèn.
Eunuch Zhāng Tiānshùn harassed an imperial post station,
and was executed.
On the *yǐhài* day,
we arrived at Dàtóng.
Liú Kūnyī and Zhāng Zhīdòng were ordered to discuss the peace settlement.
Zài Yī was appointed Grand Minister of the Military Council.
On the *wùyín* day,
allowances of silver were bestowed upon the princes and dukes, and all officials, great and small, who were accompanying the imperial retinue.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
we arrived at Huáirén.
Imperial departments, bureaus, ministries, and directorates in the capital, as well as those serving in the inner court,
were ordered, except for those staying in the capital,
to lead their clerks to the temporary imperial residence.
On the *xīnsì* day,
we arrived at Guǎngwǔzhèn.
Chéng Wénbǐng was ordered to command troops stationed at Tóngguān.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
we arrived at Yángmíngbǎo.
An edict instructed Rónglù to collect and reorganize the Central Army of the Imperial Guards.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
we arrived at Yuánpíngzhèn.
An edict instructed Tíngyōng to oversee the suppression of Boxer rebels in Zhílì.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
we arrived at Xīnzhōu.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
we arrived at Tàiyuán,
and the provincial governor's yamen was used as the temporary imperial residence.
The regular taxes for this year were remitted for the prefectures and counties of Tiānzhèn and Yánggāo, through which the imperial retinue had passed.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Xi'ān and other prefectures suffered from drought.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
an edict instructed Rónglù to restrain the Central Army of the Imperial Guards.
On the *guǐsì* day,
an imperial decree ordered officials to encourage local Christians to settle down in their occupations,
and Boxer members who had been coerced were ordered to return to farming.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
disaster relief was provided to various prefectures in Sìchuān.
On the *gēngzǐ* day of the intercalary eighth month, the first day of the lunar month,
relief was provided for flood victims in Líshuǐ and other counties.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
a memorial service was held for the deceased German envoy Klinde (*KèlínDé*),
and Kūngāng was ordered to go and offer condolences.
For the crime of shielding Boxers and initiating hostilities,
Prince Zhuāng Zài Xūn, Prince Yí Pǔ Jìng, Beile Zài Lián, and Zài Yíng were stripped of their princely titles.
Zài Yī, Zài Lán, Gāng Yì, Zhào Shūqiáo, and Yīng Nián were dismissed from their posts,
and referred to the Imperial Clan Court and relevant ministries for deliberation.
Lù Chuánlín was appointed Grand Minister of the Military Council.
On the *rénnyín* day,
as the Japanese scribe Sugiura Shin (*Shānyuán Bīn*) had been murdered,
Nà Tóng was dispatched as an envoy to Japan to offer sacrifices and condolences.
Yù Xián was dismissed.
On the *yǐsì* day,
an imperial decree announced the imperial visit to Xi'ān.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the imperial retinue departed.
On this day,
we arrived at Xúgōu.
On the *wùshēn* day,
we arrived at Qíxiàn.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
we arrived at Píngyáo.
On the *gēngxū* day,
we arrived at Jièxiū.
On the *xīnhài* day,
we arrived at Língshí.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
we arrived at Huòzhōu.
Rónglù was summoned to the temporary imperial residence.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
an imperial decree ordered the Shǎnxī Provincial Governor's Yamen to be converted into a temporary imperial residence.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
we arrived at Píngyáng.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
we arrived at Shǐcūn Post Station.
An edict ordered the five northern provinces to strictly apprehend members of the Zìlì Huì secret society.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
we arrived at Wénxǐ.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
an imperial decree stated that due to the imperial visit to the west,
the imperial mausoleums and altars had long been neglected,
and ordered Yìkuāng to select close relatives among the princes and beiles to offer sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the Eastern and Western Mausoleums on behalf of the Emperor,
while the Court of Imperial Sacrifices would dispatch officials to sacrifice at the altars.
Subsequently, it was ordered that the sacrificial ceremonies for New Year's Eve this year and New Year's Day next year
should also be carried out by proxies.
Urgent orders were sent to nearby provinces to remit funds to the capital to provide stipends and provisions for officials and officers in the capital.
Yìkuāng was granted plenipotentiary powers
to negotiate a peace treaty with Lǐ Hóngzhāng,
with Liú Kūnyī and Zhāng Zhīdòng still participating in the discussions.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
we arrived at Línjìn.
On the *guǐhài* day,
we arrived at Púzhōu.
An edict ordered Jiāngsū and other provinces to remit one million *kuǎn* (taels) to support the capital's stipends and provisions.
The regular taxes for this year were remitted for Tàiyuán, Yángqǔ, and other prefectures through which the imperial retinue had passed.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
we arrived at Tóngguān.
Relief was provided for flood victims in Fúzhōu.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
we arrived at Huáyīn.
Jìngxìn and Pǔxīng were ordered to manage the Tiger God Battalion.
On the *wùchén* day,
we arrived at Huázhōu.
On the *jǐsì* day of the ninth month, the first day of the lunar month,
we arrived at Wèinán.
On the *rénshēn* day,
we reached Xi'ān Prefecture,
and the provincial governor's yamen was used as the temporary imperial residence.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Yùgāng was appointed Minister Resident in Tibet.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Wang Yìróng, who died a martyr, was posthumously granted an inherited official position,
and his wife, Lady Xiè, and daughter-in-law, Lady Zhāng, were honored.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng memorialized for the execution of Táán Wénhuàn, a Daoist official who had sided with bandits and caused chaos.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Germans captured Zǐjīngguān,
and Provincial Administration Commissioner Shēngyǔn retreated to Fútúyì.
Subsequently, he memorialized that the German troops had retreated to Yìzhōu,
but the Emperor, deeming his report exaggerated and panicked,
severely rebuked him.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the tribute of frozen fish from the Yellow River, traditionally offered by Bǎodé, was abolished.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Zài Yī was stripped of his princely title,
and together with Zài Xūn, Pǔ Jìng, and Zài Yíng, was handed over to the Imperial Clan Court for imprisonment.
Zài Lán and Yīng Nián had their ranks reduced.
Zhào Shūqiáo was dismissed from office but retained in his post.
Gāng Yì died of illness,
and deliberation was waived.
Yù Xián was exiled to the extreme frontier.
On the *rénchén* day,
condolences were given to the families of Hēilóngjiāng General Yán Mào, Libationer Xī Yuán, Reader Bǎo Fēng, Chóng Shòu, and others who had committed self-immolation with their entire families.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
relief was provided for famine in Shǎnxī.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
outstanding taxes for Xiánníng and other counties in Shǎnxī were remitted.
On the *wùxū* day,
outstanding taxes for disaster-stricken departments, prefectures, counties, and native chieftains in Yúnnán were remitted.
On the *wùshēn* day of the tenth month of winter,
on the Empress Dowager's birthday,
banquets were suspended.
On the *gēngxū* day,
an imperial decree stated that Dǒng Fúxiáng was unfamiliar with foreign affairs
and acted recklessly in matters,
so he was stripped of his post as Provincial Commander-in-Chief
but retained in his duties.
On the *xīnhài* day,
four hundred thousand taels from the imperial treasury were allocated for famine relief in Shǎnxī,
and Jiāngsū and Húběi were urged to transport grain and purchase provisions to assist.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Wáng Wénsháo was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tǐrén Pavilion,
and Chóng Lǐ and Xú Fǔ were made Assistant Grand Secretaries.
On the *dīngsì* day,
an edict instructed Gǔ'ěrkā, Anterior and Posterior Zàng, and various native chieftains to temporarily suspend their tributes.
On the *guǐhài* day,
a system of donations for actual official positions in Qín and Jìn was opened to relieve the drought.
On the *rénshēn* day of the eleventh month,
five tenths of the regular taxes for Cháng'ān were remitted.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Miáo rebels led by Wáng Lǎojiǔ and others caused unrest in Qīngpíng,
and imperial troops suppressed and captured them.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Yáng Rú was appointed Plenipotentiary Minister
to negotiate with Russia regarding the handover of the Three Eastern Provinces.
On the *xīnsì* day,
due to drought in Chángshā and other prefectures,
a system of disaster relief donations was opened.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
two tenths of the regular taxes for various prefectures and counties in Shānxī through which the imperial retinue had passed were remitted.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Shèng Xuānhuái was appointed Assistant Minister of Commerce.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Xú Shòupéng was ordered to go to the capital to assist with commercial treaty matters.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Ānhuī opened a system of donations for military provisions.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Zēng Qí was strictly criticized for unilaterally concluding a provisional agreement with the Russians for the return of Fèngtiān,
and was subsequently
stripped of his post.
In the twelfth month, on the jiǎchén day,
an edict was issued exempting the New Year's Day ceremonies for the coming year.
On the dīngwèi day,
an edict was issued to discuss reforms.

The Grand Councilors (Jūnjī Dàchén), Grand Secretaries (Dàxuéshì), the Six Boards (Liù Bù), the Nine Chief Ministers (Jiǔ Qīng), envoys abroad (Chūshǐ Dàchén), and governors-general and governors of the provinces (Zhíshěng Dūfǔ) were to consult on important Chinese and Western policies,
and propose them to the throne.
On the gēngxū day,
an imperial decree was issued to all officials, great and small, in the directly administered provinces (Zhíshěng) to protect foreign residents.
Violators would be severely punished.
The prohibition against forming societies hostile to religions (huì chóujiào) was strictly enforced,
with offenders to be sentenced to death.
On the rénzǐ day,
Zhāng Bǎixī, the Left Censor-in-Chief (Zuǒ Dū Yùshǐ), was appointed as plenipotentiary envoy to England.
On the jiǎyín day,
the ministers remaining in the capital reported that banditry was rampant in the capital (Jīngshī),
and requested the temporary application of harsh laws.
This was granted.
On the gēngshēn day,
Zhāng Pèilún was rewarded with the title of Compiler (Biānxiū),
and was to assist Lǐ Hóngzhāng in diplomatic negotiations.
On the rénxū day,
an edict was issued to restore the positions of the unjustly implicated officials Lìshān, Xú Yòngyí, Xǔ Jǐngchéng, Lián Yuán, and Yuán Chǎng.
Further discussion was made regarding the crimes of the officials who were the chief instigators of the banditry and rebellion.
Zài Lán's noble title and official position were revoked.
He and Zài Yī were banished to Xīnjiāng and imprisoned.
Gāng Yì's position was stripped.
Yīng Nián and Zhào Shūqiáo were both stripped of their positions and sentenced to beheading.
Xú Tóng and Lǐ Bǐnghéng were posthumously stripped of their positions.
Qǐ Xiù and Xú Chéngyù were stripped of their positions and awaited inquiry.
Dǒng Fúxiáng was stripped of his position and dismissed from office.
On the guǐhài day,
an edict was issued taking self-blame,
displaying to the world the difficult circumstances and bitter struggles of the time.
It also admonished all officials, both Chinese and foreign, to inspire loyalty,
discard selfishness,
break old habits,
and strive for revitalization.
In the 27th year, xīnchǒu
the imperial residence was in Xī'ān.
In spring, the first month, on the wùchén new moon day,
an edict was issued to aid the provinces of Shùn and Zhí afflicted by military disasters,
opening the practice of purchasing official ranks (shíguān juānlì).
The annual tribute of sea otter furs from Duōlúnnuò'ěr was abolished.
On the gēngwǔ day,
Zài Xūn was granted permission to commit suicide.
On the xīnwèi day,
Yù Xián was executed by beheading.
On the guǐyǒu day,
Yīng Nián and Zhào Shūqiáo were both granted permission to commit suicide.
Gāng Yì, Xú Tóng, and Lǐ Bǐnghéng were all sentenced to beheading,
which was previously averted.
On the yǐhài day,
Qǐ Xiù and Xú Chéngyù were executed by beheading.
On the gēngchén day,
taxes on barren fields in Rénhé and other counties were remitted.
On the sīnsì day,
the tribute of oranges from Xīnhuì was remitted.
In the second month, on the jǐhài day,
one million taels from the Board of Revenue (bùtáng) were allocated to Shānxī for disaster relief.
On the rénzǐ day,
Lí Guólián, a doctor (lángzhōng) from Guǎngdōng, and others presented local products,
and were promoted accordingly.
In the third month, on the wùchén day,
tax grain was remitted in areas traversed by the imperial carriage (bìlù) and in disaster-stricken areas like Xiánníng in Shǎnxī.
On the jǐsì day,
an edict was issued to establish the Bureau for Supervising Government Affairs (Dūbàn Zhèngwù Chù).
Yì Kuāng, Lǐ Hóngzhāng, Róng Lù, Kūngāng, Wáng Wénsháo, and Lù Chuánlín were appointed as supervising ministers,
while Liú Kūnyī and Zhāng Zhīdòng were to participate remotely.
On the jiǎxū day,
arrears of grain taxes in Lín'ān, Yúnnán, and other places were remitted.
On the dīngchǒu day,
punishments were determined for those who failed to protect against Boxer rebels (quánfěi) and anti-Christian activities.
The late Governor-General Yù Lù and the Resident Minister in Tibet (Zhùzàng Dàchén) Qìng Shàn were stripped of their original positions.
The Governor of Zhèjiāng, Liú Shùtáng, was stripped of his position.
The Provincial Administration Commissioner (Bùzhèngshǐ) Róng Quán and Vice Commander-in-Chief (Fù Dūtǒng) Jìn Chāng were stripped of their positions and exiled to the farthest borders.
The Circuit Intendant (dàoyuán) Zhèng Wénqīn, Magistrate (zhīxiàn) Bái Chǎng, and Commandant (dūshī) Zhōu Zhīdé were all executed by beheading.
The rest were stripped of their positions or exiled to varying degrees.
Fifty thousand shi of grain from Shāndōng's grain transport (cáomǐ) were allocated to relieve disaster victims in Zhílì.
On the rénwǔ day,
an imperial decree was issued to exempt officials who came from the capital (Jīng) to the imperial residence (xíngzài) from salary deductions for their temporary appointments.
In summer, the fourth month, on the dīngyǒu day,
the imperial princes and all officials in the capital were granted half their salaries,
and banner (qí) and Green Standard (lǜyíng) soldiers were granted one month's pay and provisions.
On the xīnchǒu day,
Mǎ Yùkūn was ordered to suppress the remaining bandits in the vicinity of the capital (jìnjī),
and Qú Hóngjī was appointed to learn and serve as a Grand Councilor.
On the dīngwèi day,
Qú Hóngjī was also appointed as a Minister of the Bureau for Supervising Government Affairs.
On the jǐyǒu day,
relief was provided for the drought in Zhílì.
On the rénzǐ day,
an edict was issued to establish a special examination for economic affairs (jīngjì tèkē),
and officials from China and abroad were ordered to recommend qualified candidates.
Regular tributes from all provinces were remitted,
except for tea, medicinal herbs, and tribute items for sacrifices at the passes.
All foodstuffs were completely abolished.
On the guǐchǒu day,
Zài Fēng was appointed as plenipotentiary envoy to Germany.
On the gēngshēn day,
an edict was issued to comply with the agreement of various nations,
suspending examinations for five years in the provinces of Shùntiān, Fèngtiān, Hēilóngjiāng, Zhílì, Shānxī, Hénán, Shǎnxī, Zhèjiāng, Jiāngxī, and Húnán.
On the rénxū day,
Zhāng Bǎixī and others were ordered to repair the imperial carriage road (bìlù) in the capital (Jīngshī).
On the guǐhài day,
this year's tribute from Jílín was suspended.
In the fifth month, on the yǐchǒu day,
Nà Tóng was appointed as plenipotentiary envoy to Japan.
The provincial examinations (xiāngshì) of grace and regular session for this year in Shānxī were postponed.
On the guǐwèi day,
the Circuit Intendant (dàoyuán) Cài Jūn was rewarded with a fourth-grade capital official position (jīngtáng),
and appointed as envoy to Japan.
On the jiǎwǔ day,
relief was provided for disasters in Mò'ěrgēn and other places.
In the sixth month, on the bǐngshēn day,
Vice Commander-in-Chief (Fù Dūtǒng) Yìn Chāng was appointed as envoy to Germany,
and later also appointed as envoy to the Netherlands.
Prefect (zhīfǔ) Xǔ Táishēn was rewarded with the position of Circuit Intendant (dàoyuán),
and appointed as envoy to Korea.
On the gēngzǐ day,
for the Empress Dowager's birthday (wànshòujié),
court felicitations and banquets were suspended.
On the guǐmǎo day,
an edict was issued to establish the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Wàiwù Bù),
re-establishing it from the Zǒnglǐ Gèguó Shìwù Yámén.
Yì Kuāng was appointed as Chief Minister (zǒnglǐ),
Wáng Wénsháo as Associate Minister (huìbàn dàchén),
Qú Hóngjī as Minister (shàngshū) and Associate Minister,
and Xú Shòupéng and Lián Fāng as Vice Ministers (shìláng).
On the gēngxū day,
the allied forces of various nations departed from the capital (Jīngshī).
On the rénzǐ day,
fifty thousand taels from the imperial treasury (nèitáng) were sent to Jiāngxī for disaster relief.
Relief was also provided for the fire disaster in Qīxiá.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the jiǎzǐ new moon day,
Dèng Zēng was ordered to command the troops escorting the imperial family.
The land tax (éfù) was remitted in areas traversed by the imperial carriage in Shǎnxī, Hénán, and Zhílì.
On the yǐchǒu day,
an edict was issued to abolish the accumulated abuses in grain transport (cáowù).
Both river and sea transport were changed to collection in silver (zhéshǎi),
and goods were to be collected, transported, received, and stored in the capital's granaries.
Shì Duó was dismissed from his position on the Grand Council.
On the jǐsì day,
the river burst its banks in Zhāngqiū and Huìmín.
On the jǐmǎo day,
an edict was issued to reform the imperial examination system (kējǔ) starting from the next year.
The current affairs essays (shíwén) and rhymed prose (shìtiē) were abolished.
Candidates would be tested on classical exegesis (jīngyì) and policy questions on current affairs (shíwù cèwèn).
The military examinations (wǔkē) were suspended.
Luó Fēnglù was granted a third-grade capital official position (jīngtáng),
and appointed as envoy to Russia.
On the wùzǐ day,
the plenipotentiary ministers Yì Kuāng and Lǐ Hóngzhāng concluded the negotiation of twelve articles of the peace treaty with the envoys of eleven nations.
On the jǐchǒu day,
the provincial examinations (xiāngshì) in Shǎnxī were postponed to the next year.
On the rénchén day,
an edict was issued to permanently abolish the practice of purchasing official ranks (shíguān juānlì).
An imperial decree was issued to all provinces to establish military academies (wǔbèi xuétáng).
On the guǐsì day,
an imperial decree was issued to all provinces to reduce troops and brave battalions (bīngyǒng),
and reorganize them into standing armies (chángbèi), reserve armies (xùbèi), and police forces.
In the eighth month, on the jiǎwǔ new moon day,
as the imperial return to the capital (huílú) was imminent,
officials were dispatched to offer sacrifices to the Western and Central Sacred Mountains.
Famous mountains and great rivers, ancient imperial tombs, and shrines and tombs of former Confucian scholars and famous ministers along the imperial carriage road (bìlù)
were also to have sacrifices offered by officials dispatched by the provincial authorities (jiānglì).
On the yǐwèi day,
an edict was issued to establish schools (xuétáng) in the directly administered provinces (Zhíshěng).
On the wùshēn day,
memorials on general matters (tíběn) from various internal and external offices were abolished.
Except for congratulatory memorials (hèběn),
all were to be changed to confidential memorials (zòu).
On the rénzǐ day,
Shèng Xuānhuái was appointed as Minister for Commercial Taxes.
On the guǐchǒu day,
an edict was issued to announce to the world the reforms aimed at strengthening the nation,
and the proposals of Liú Kūnyī and Zhāng Zhīdòng were to be comprehensively considered by all provincial authorities (jiānglì).
On the dīngsì day,
the imperial carriage departed from Xī'ān.
On the jǐwèi day,
Shēng Yǔn reported that Xià Liángcái, the magistrate of Líntóng, had mismanaged provisions,
and requested his dismissal.
The Empress Dowager (Huáng Tàihòu) ordered a lenient discussion.
Shēng Yǔn requested punishment for himself,
but was excused.
In the ninth month, on the jǐyǒu day,
Lǐ Hóngzhāng passed away.
He was posthumously granted the title of Grand Tutor (Tàifù)
and elevated to a first-class Marquis (Yīděng Hóujué).
Wáng Wénsháo was appointed acting plenipotentiary minister,
and Yuán Shìkǎi was appointed acting Governor-General of Zhílì and concurrent Minister Superintendent of Northern Ports (Běiyáng Dàchén).
In this autumn,
one hundred fifty thousand taels from the imperial treasury (nèitáng) were allocated for disaster relief in Shǎnxī and Ānhuī.
One hundred thousand taels of grain transport funds (cáokuǎn) and sixty thousand shi of grain from grain transport (cáomǐ) were reserved for relief in Ānhuī and Jiāngsū.
Relief was also provided for floods in Húguǎng (Liǎinghú), Ānhuī, and Yúnnán,
and for tidal disasters in Jiāngsū.
In winter, on the *guǐsì* day, the first day of the tenth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Imperial procession arrived at Kāifēng.
The breach at Huìmín was closed.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Dàoyuán Zhāng Déyí was awarded the third-rank official title of Qīng,
and appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to Great Britain,
then ordered concurrently to serve as envoy to Italy and Belgium.
On the *rényín* day,
the Empress Dowager's birthday,
the court felicitations were suspended.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
an Imperial Edict rescinded Pǔjùn's title of Imperial Prince.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
an Imperial Decree postponed the Metropolitan Examinations until the *guǐmǎo* year.
The following year's Shùntiān Provincial Examination and the *guǐmǎo* Metropolitan Examinations
were temporarily moved to the Hénán Provincial Examination Hall.
In the eleventh month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
it was specially decreed to establish a memorial temple in the capital for the late Grand Secretary Lǐ Hóngzhāng.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Yí Gǔ was appointed to supervise reclamation and cultivation affairs on the Jìn border.
The breach at Zhāngqiū was closed.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Emperor and Empress Dowager returned from Xī'ān.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
an Imperial Decree posthumously promoted Concubine Zhēn to Noble Consort,
as she had died for the state in the palace the previous year.
The officials of the Hànlín Academy, Supervising Censorate, and various departments and bureaus
were ordered to prepare daily for Imperial audiences.
In the twelfth month, on the *guǐsì* day,
Wáng Wénsháo was ordered to continue supervising railway and mining affairs,
Qú Hóngjī was appointed as his deputy,
Yuán Shìkǎi was appointed to supervise railway affairs within and outside the passes,
and Hú Yùfēn was appointed as associate supervisor.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
an Imperial Edict was reiterated to domestic and foreign officials,
emphasizing the importance of international relations
and the pacification of the populace.
Because of their involvement in the Boxers,
and their association with powerful nobles,
Zuǒ Fù Dū Yùshǐ Hé Nǎiyíng, Shìjiǎng Xuéshì Péng Qīnglí, Biānxiū Wáng Lóngwén, Zhīfǔ Lián Wénchōng, and Zēng Lián were stripped of their offices.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
relief was distributed to the poor within thirty *lǐ* of the Imperial road.
On the *jǐhài* day,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Yuánqiū.
From the eighth month of the *wùxū* year until this month,
the Emperor personally attended for the first time.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
sacrifices were offered at the Great Altar of Soil and the Great Altar of Grain.
Ruì Qīn Wáng Kuíbīn and others were sent to offer sacrifices at the Fāngzé, the Altar to the Morning Sun, and the Altar to the Evening Moon.
Gōng Qīn Wáng Pǔwěi and Béizǐ Pǔlún went to the Eastern and Western Imperial Tombs to offer sacrifices.
On the *rényín* day,
Yuán Shìkǎi was appointed to participate in the Zhèngwù Chù.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Zhèn Guó Jiāngjūn Zàizhèn was appointed Special Envoy to Great Britain
to congratulate its monarch on his coronation,
and was subsequently promoted to the rank of Béizǐ.
Three tenths of the regular taxes were remitted for the prefectures and counties of Hénán along the Imperial road.
Relief was provided for a fire disaster in Guǎngxī.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the two Majesties received the envoys of various nations in the Qiánqīng Gōng.
Arrears of copper factory dues from the people of Yúnnán were remitted.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Qú Hóngjī was appointed Grand Minister of the Military Council.
Sūn Jiānài was appointed Tǐrén Gé Dàxuéshì.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the two Majesties received the envoys of various nations and their wives in the Yǎngxìng Diàn.
On the *dīngsì* day,
accumulated tax arrears and granary grains from the prefectures and counties of Shānxī were remitted.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the combined sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the Emperor resumed holding court in the Bǎohé Diàn,
hosting a banquet for Mongolian princes and dukes, and civil and military officials.
Land and grain taxes for uncultivated land in the prefectures and counties of Rén and Qián in Zhèjiāng,
and the two guards of Hángyán and Jiāhú were remitted.
In the 28th year, on the *gēngwǔ* day of the first month of spring,
sacrifices were offered at the Tàimiào.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
prayers for grain were offered to Shangdì.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Sìchuān Tídū Sòng Qìng passed away,
and was posthumously enfeoffed as a third-rank baron.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Zhāng Yì was appointed Director-General of railway and mining affairs,
Wáng Wénsháo and Qú Hóngjī were appointed Supervisors,
and Lǚ Hǎihuán was to consult with Shèng Xuān huái on trade treaties.
On the *wùyín* day,
the Hedong River Governor-General was abolished.
The high officials of each province were ordered to clarify the system of military colonies,
to convert military colony provisions into poll taxes,
to recall guard officials to the barracks,
and to dismiss military colonists and transport soldiers.
An Imperial Edict ordered each province to establish agricultural and industrial schools.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the Zhānshì Fǔ and the Tōngzhèng Shǐsī were abolished.
In the second month, on the *rénchén* day, the first day of the month,
Zhāng Déyí was appointed Special Envoy to Spain
to congratulate its monarch on his coronation.
On the *guǐsì* day,
an Imperial Edict ordered each province to urgently establish schools and military academies,
and to open offices to compile new laws.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Guǎngxī bandits assassinated a French military officer,
and were consequently suppressed.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
sacrifices were offered to the Former Master (Confucius).
On the *wùxū* day,
sacrifices were offered at the Great Altar of Soil and the Great Altar of Grain.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Liú Kūnyī requested leave due to illness,
but was persuaded to remain in office.
In the third month, on the *xīnyǒu* day, the first day of the month,
the treaty for the retrocession of the Three Eastern Provinces was concluded.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Italian envoy Gālínà was received in the Qiánqīng Gōng.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
sacrifices were offered to the Former Farmer,
and the Emperor personally ploughed the ceremonial field.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Emperor and Empress Dowager visited the Eastern Imperial Tombs,
and three tenths of the regular taxes were remitted for the prefectures and counties along the Imperial road.
From the *jǐsì* to the *gēngwǔ* day,
various Imperial Tombs were visited.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the Imperial procession went to the Nányuàn,
stopping at the Tuánhé Imperial Lodge.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
they returned from the Eastern Imperial Tombs.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the Empress offered sacrifices to the Former Sericulturalist.
This spring,
disaster relief was provided for military colonies in Xuānwēi, Kūnmíng, and Qíqíhā'ěr, Mo'ěrgēn Banner.
Arrears of taxes in Yúlín and other places were remitted,
and two tenths of the autumn grain tax in Xī'ān and other prefectures and counties were remitted.
In summer, on the *rénchén* day of the fourth month,
the Russian envoy Léi Sà'ěr was received in the Qiánqīng Gōng.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the regular rain sacrifice was offered to Heaven.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Shěn Jiābèn and Wǔ Tíngfāng were appointed to participate in the revision of existing laws.
On the *wùxū* day,
Lǐ Jīngxī was removed from his post as Governor of Yúnnán
due to inappropriate remarks in a memorial,
and the matter was referred to the Board for deliberation.
On the *rényín* day,
Xǔ Yù was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to Italy,
Wú Dézhāng was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to Austria,
and Yáng Zhàoyǔn was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to Belgium.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Empress personally gathered mulberry leaves.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the three treasuries for silver, silk and satin, and pigments were abolished,
and the treasury superintendents were dismissed.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
land taxes for disaster-stricken areas in Luánpíng were remitted.
In the fifth month, on the *rénxū* day,
Yuán Shìkǎi was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì and concurrently Minister of the Northern Ocean.
Arrears of taxes in Shuāngchéng were remitted.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the envoys of various nations were received in the Lèshòu Táng.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Guǎngxī bandits captured Guīzhāo in Guǎngnán,
but the Yúnnán government forces repelled them,
and recaptured the city.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the summer solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Earth at the Fāngzé.
On the *wùyín* day,
the American envoy Kānggé and others were received in the Qiánqīng Gōng.
In the sixth month, on the *jǐchǒu* day, the first day of the month,
miscellaneous taxes for disaster-stricken areas in Hèqìng and Bīnchuān were remitted.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Sūn Bǎoqí was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to France,
Hú Wéidé was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to Russia,
and Liáng Chéng was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to America, Japan, and Mexico.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the American envoy Kānggé and the President of the Exposition Bálǐdé were received in the Qiánqīng Gōng.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Zhāng Zhīdòng was appointed Minister for Commerce.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
relief was provided for disaster-stricken areas in Nánchōng, Jiǎn, and other prefectures of Sìchuān.
In autumn, on the *gēngwǔ* day of the seventh month,
regulations for schools were promulgated.
In the eighth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Yúnnán Yǐxī Circuit office was moved to Téngyuè,
and concurrently supervised customs affairs.
On the *wùxū* day,
Yuán Shìkǎi requested to abolish illegal fees and increase public funds,
and other provinces were ordered to follow suit.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the river breached at Lìjīn, Shòuzhāng, and other places.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the German envoy Gé'ěrsì and others were received in the Rénshòu Diàn.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the river again breached at Huìmín.
In the ninth month, on the day of Guǐsì,
Liú Kūnyī, the Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng, passed away.
He was posthumously enfeoffed as a first-class baron
and granted the title of Grand Tutor (Tàifù).
Zhāng Zhīdòng was ordered to temporarily assume the post of Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng and Minister for the Southern Seas (Nányáng Dàchén).
Exemption was granted for both existing and new levies in Tiānjīn due to military occupation.
On the day of Dīngyǒu,
the French envoy Jiasina and others were received at the Rénshòu Diàn.
On the day of Jiǎchén,
envoys from various countries were received at the Rénshòu Diàn.
On the day of Rénzǐ,
Yuán Shìkǎi was appointed as the Minister for Commerce (Dūbàn Shāngwù Dàchén),
with Wǔ Tíngfāng as his deputy,
to concurrently negotiate commercial treaties with various countries.
That autumn,
three hundred thousand taels of silver were disbursed from the imperial treasury,
an additional one hundred and twenty thousand were allocated for famine relief,
and aid was prepared for Sìchuān.
Relief was also provided for floods in Shāndōng, Guǎngdōng, Yúnnán, Fújiàn, Guìzhōu, and other prefectures.
In the winter, on the tenth month, on the day of Wùzǐ,
the Sino-British Commercial Treaty was concluded.
On the day of Jǐchǒu,
Liú Chángrú, the Commander of Húnán, was executed for failing to protect missionaries.
That month,
disaster relief was provided for various prefectures in Shān and Shǎn.
Jiànchuān and Hèqìng Zhōu in Yúnnán,
along with Shūlè and other sub-prefectures and counties in Xīnjiāng, all experienced earthquakes.
In the eleventh month, on the day of Wùwǔ,
an imperial edict decreed that starting from the next metropolitan examination,
all those appointed as compilers (biān), revisers (jiǎn), or promoted to probationary Hanlin academicians (shùcháng) or clerks in the Six Boards
must study at the Jīngshī Dàxuétáng (Imperial University of Peking).
Only after obtaining a diploma
would they be permitted to disperse from the Hanlin Academy or be recommended for retention.
Magistrates (zhīxiàn) in various provinces were also to enter the official training academies for study.
On the day of Jǐwèi,
Yǒutài was appointed as the Minister Resident in Tibet (Zhùzàng Dàchén).
On the day of Xīnyǒu,
fifty thousand taels each from the imperial privy purse and the Board of Revenue were dispatched to Shāndōng for disaster relief.
On the day of Rénxū,
Wèi Guāngtáo was transferred to be the Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng and Minister for the Southern Seas.
On the day of Bǐngyín,
exemption was granted for five years from land taxes in Líntóng due to flooding.
On the day of Gēngchén,
it was the Winter Solstice,
and sacrifices to Heaven were offered at the Huánqiū Altar.
That month,
the French envoy Lǚ Bān and the American envoy Kānggé were received at the Qiánqīng Gōng.
In the twelfth month, on the day of Guǐmǎo,
Yuán Shìkǎi was appointed as the Minister for Telegraph Affairs (Dūbàn Diànwù Dàchén).
On the day of Xīnhài,
Yáng Xīchén, the son of Yáng Rú, the Minister to Russia who died in a foreign land in the line of duty, was commended for his filial piety.
That month,
exemption was granted from existing levies for various sub-prefectures, departments, counties, and garrisons in Jiāng and Zhè,
and from land rent for Yíliáng due to flooding.
In the twenty-ninth year, in spring, on the first month, on the first day of Dīngsì,
banquets were suspended.
As the Empress Dowager's seventieth birthday was approaching next year,
an imperial edict announced a "Celebratory Examination" (Qìngbǎng):
this year's provincial examination would be the Guǐmǎo Ēnkē (Special Grace Examination),
and next year's metropolitan examination would be the Jiǎchén Ēnkē (Special Grace Examination);
the regular provincial and metropolitan examinations would be held in the subsequent session.
On the day of Yǐchǒu,
the American envoy Kānggé and others were received at the Qiánqīng Gōng.
On the day of Dīngmǎo,
Róngqìng was ordered to jointly manage the affairs of the Imperial University.
On the day of Jǐsì,
envoys from various countries were received at the Yǎngxìng Diàn.
On the day of Dīnghài,
grain taxes and levies were exempted for Zhènxī and Shūfù due to disaster.
In the second month, on the day of Rénzǐ,
the breach in Huìmín was closed.
In the third month, on the first day of Bǐngchén,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day of Gēngshēn,
Prince Henry of Germany and envoy Gélǐshì and others were received at the Qiánqīng Gōng.
An imperial edict decreed that when visiting the imperial tombs via railway,
the imposition of corvée and levies was prohibited,
and escorts were exempted from providing supplies.
On the day of Xīnyǒu,
the Manchu and Han presidents and instructors of the official schools were dismissed.
On the day of Guǐhài,
sacrifices were offered to the God of Agriculture (Xiānnóng),
and the Emperor personally ploughed the sacrificial field.
The Emperor, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, visited the Western Tombs.
On the day of Yǐchǒu,
the imperial entourage stopped over in Bǎodìng Fǔ,
and three-tenths of the existing levies in the prefectures and counties along the imperial route were exempted.
On the day of Jǐsì,
Rónglù passed away.
He was posthumously granted the title of Grand Tutor,
and promoted to a first-class baron.
The stamp tax and all other harsh and trivial miscellaneous levies were abolished;
those who extorted or embezzled through levies were to be punished according to the law.
On the day of Gēngwǔ,
Yìkuāng was appointed as a Grand Councilor (Jūnjī Dàchén).
On the day of Guǐhài,
the imperial entourage visited Nányuàn.
On the day of Jiǎxū,
the imperial entourage stopped over at Tuánhé.
On the day of Gēngchén,
Yìkuāng and Qú Hóngjī were ordered to jointly organize the finances of the Board of Revenue.
A General Mint (Yínqián Zhùzào Zǒngchǎng) was established in the capital.
Zàizhèn, Yuán Shìkǎi, and Wǔ Tíngfāng were ordered to jointly draft commercial laws.
On the day of Xīnsì,
the imperial entourage returned from Nányuàn.
That month,
outstanding taxes from the Gēngzǐ year in Shǎnxī were exempted.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the day of Jǐhài,
envoys from various countries were received at the Rénshòu Diàn.
On the day of Jǐyǒu,
bandits in Yúnnán captured the city of Lín'ān Fǔ.
On the day of Gēngxū,
banner rents in the prefectures and counties along the imperial route were exempted.
On the day of Xīnhài,
Chónglǐ was appointed as Grand Secretary of the Dōnggé (Dōnggé Dàxuéshì),
and Jìngxìn as Associate Grand Secretary (Xiébàn Dàxuéshì).
In the fifth month, on the day of Guǐhài,
Tiělíng was ordered to jointly train the Metropolitan Banner soldiers with Yuán Shìkǎi.
On the day of Wùchén,
the Board of Revenue caught fire.
On the day of Jiǎxū,
Yáng Shū was appointed as the Minister Plenipotentiary to Japan.
On the day of Yǐhài,
the Luǒyí rebellion in Yúnnán was suppressed.
On the day of Rénwǔ,
Wáng Shòupéng and 315 others were granted the Jinshi degree with varying ranks.
In the intercalary fifth month, on the first day of Jiǎshēn,
Féng Zǐcái was ordered to jointly handle military affairs in Guǎngxī with Cén Chūnxuān.
On the day of Bǐngxū,
Zhāng Zhīdòng was ordered to jointly revise the regulations of the Imperial University with Zhāng Bǎixī and Róngqìng.
On the day of Gēngyín,
the Yúnnán army recaptured the city of Lín'ān Fǔ,
and Zhōu Yúnxiáng, the bandit leader of Shípíng, was executed.
On the day of Rénchén,
it had not rained since the fourth month,
until this day when it rained.
On the day of Bǐngshēn,
Wáng Zhīchūn, the Governor of Guǎngxī, and Sū Yuánchūn, the Provincial Commander-in-Chief (Tídū), were both dismissed from their posts;
Kē Féngshí was appointed as Governor of Guǎngxī,
and Liú Guāngcái as Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Guǎngxī.
On the day of Jǐhài,
personnel for the Special Examination in Statecraft were tested in the Bǎohé Diàn.
On the day of Rényín,
Mǎ Yùkūn was ordered to patrol and suppress bandits in the vicinity of the capital.
On the day of Jiǎchén,
the supplementary Sino-British Commercial Treaty was concluded.
In the sixth month, on the day of Rénxū,
Yuán Jiágǔ and others who passed the special examination were promoted with varying ranks.
On the day of Guǐhài,
Sū Yuánchūn was arrested and imprisoned.
On the day of Dīngmǎo,
Shìduó and others requested to add an honorific title to the Empress Dowager.
An imperial decree (Yìzhǐ) refused, stating that the military situation in Guǎngxī was urgent
and the people were suffering.
It was not allowed.
On the day of Dīngchǒu,
the river burst its banks at Lìjīn.
That month,
the Japanese envoy Uchida Kōsai and others, and the Italian envoy Gālí'nà and others were received at the Rénshòu Diàn.
Yāntái in Shāndōng experienced floods,
and relief was provided.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day of Yǐyǒu,
Xiàmén and Gǔlàngyǔ were opened as international settlements.
On the day of Xīnmǎo,
Zhèng Xiàoxù was awarded the fourth-rank 京堂 (Jīngtáng) position,
appointed to oversee border defense in Guǎngxī,
and granted the right of direct memorial.
Kūngāng retired.
On the day of Wùxū,
the Ministry of Commerce (Shāngbù) was first established,
with Zàizhèn as its President (Shàngshū).
In the eighth month, on the first day of Rénzǐ,
princes and all officials prematurely requested to make contributions from their salaries as a sign of respect for the Empress Dowager's seventieth birthday next year;
an imperial decree stopped them.
On the day of Guǐchǒu,
land taxes for riverside areas in Língzhōu were exempted.
On the day of Dīngmǎo,
the Japanese Commercial Treaty was concluded.
On the day of Gēngyín,
envoys from various countries were received at the Rénshòu Diàn.
On the day of Rénshēn,
Jìngxìn was appointed as Grand Secretary of the Tǐrén Gé,
and Yùdé as Associate Grand Secretary.
On the day of Dīngchǒu,
the French envoy Lǚ Bān and the German envoy Mùmò were received at the Rénshòu Diàn.
In the ninth month, on the day of Bǐngshēn,
Róngqìng was ordered to learn to serve as a Grand Councilor.
