Nàtóng was transferred to be President of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Wàiwù Bù Shàngshū) and concurrently Associate Minister.
On the day of Dīngyǒu,
Nàtóng was ordered to jointly organize the finances of the Board of Revenue with Yìkuāng and Qú Hóngjī,
and Róngqìng was appointed as Minister of the Council for Government Affairs (Zhèngwù Chù Dàchén).
On the day of Wùxū,
Sūn Jiānài and Zhāng Bǎixī were both appointed as Ministers of the Council for Government Affairs.
That autumn,
relief was provided for floods in Húběi, Shǎnxī, and other prefectures,
hail disaster in Huáiróu,
floods, droughts, and hail disasters in various prefectures of Yúnnán,
and locust plagues and frost disasters in Zhènxī and Suīlái.
On the *xīnhài* day of the tenth month, the first day of the lunar month,
an audience was granted to the Dutch envoy Hītèsī at the Qiánqīnggōng.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Yīngxiù was appointed to take over the administration of the leased territory of Àlèťái.
As there was a proposal to postpone this,
Ruìxún was ordered to investigate.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
a Bureau for Military Training (Liànbīngchù) was established.
Yìkuāng was appointed Director-General,
and Yuán Shìkǎi and Tiěliáng were appointed Deputy Directors.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Cén Chūnshuān was appointed Commander-in-Chief of all Guangxī forces.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Yáng Shèng was granted the title of Fourth-Rank Minister
and appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to Austria.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Yuán Shìkǎi impeached Zhāng Yì for unauthorized sale of the Kāipíng coal mine and the Qínwángdǎo port to foreigners.
An imperial edict stripped him of his office
and ordered the recovery of the properties.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day of the eleventh month,
an edict stated:
"Promoting education and nurturing talent
is the most urgent task.
According to the educational regulations jointly drafted by Zhāng Zhīdòng and the Ministers of Education,
the school system and the imperial examination system are to be integrated into a single path,
so that all scholars possess practical knowledge,
and all learning has practical application.
Starting from the *bǐngwǔ* cohort,
the quotas for the provincial (*xiāng*) and metropolitan (*huì*) examinations,
and the academic quotas for each province,
shall be progressively reduced with each cohort.
Once schools in all provinces are fully established and effective,
the quotas for the imperial examinations shall be abolished by category,
and thereafter, all qualifications shall be obtained through school examinations."
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the title of Minister of Education (Guǎnxué Dàchén) was changed to Minister of Academic Affairs (Xuéwù Dàchén),
and Sūn Jiānài was appointed to the post.
On the *bǐngchén* day of the twelfth month,
Qín Zhìfā and other bandit leaders in Guangxī were executed.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
an imperial edict ordered the Neìwùfǔ to further reduce palace expenditures
and suspend all non-urgent work.
On the *jǐsì* day,
academicians of the Hànlín Academy were appointed to compose texts,
the number of positions was increased,
and their ranks were re-evaluated.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
due to the outbreak of war between Japan and Russia,
China adopted a policy of strict neutrality,
and an edict was issued to officials and common people.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Róngqìng was appointed Grand Councilor (Jūnjī Dàchén).
In this month,
land taxes and grain levies were remitted for areas affected by floods in Ānzhōu and drought in Kūnmíng.
This winter,
relief was provided for flood disasters in various prefectures and counties of Gānsù and Yúnnán,
for crocodile disasters in Nánzhōu and Xīnhuà,
and for fire disasters in Lúzhōu.
In the first month of spring in the *jiǎchén* year, the thirtieth year [of Guāngxù's reign], on the *guǐwèi* day,
the Guǎngxī Salt Intendant was moved to Wúzhōu
and also served as Customs Supervisor.
The Yellow River burst its banks at Wángzhuāng in Lìjīn.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
an audience was granted to the envoys from America, Britain, France, Germany, Japan, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands, and Portugal, including Kānggé, at the Qiánqīnggōng.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Zhāng Chūnfā, the Provincial Commander-in-Chief of Yúnnán, was found guilty,
stripped of his office, and exiled to a military post.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
to celebrate the Empress Dowager's seventieth birthday,
the Emperor attended the Tàihédiàn,
issued an imperial edict to the empire,
and bestowed various acts of grace.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Gāo Déyuán, the Brigade-General of Pǔ'ěr Town in Yúnnán, was executed for letting bandits run rampant and harming the populace.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
an imperial edict suspended the autumn executions for this year.
On the *gēngxū* day of the second month, the first day of the lunar month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
an audience was granted to the Portuguese envoy Báilánggǔ at the Qiánqīnggōng.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the breach at Lìjīn was closed.
On the *gēngchén* day of the third month, the first day of the lunar month,
an audience was granted to the German envoy Mùmò and others at the Qiánqīnggōng.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Censor Jiǎng Shìxīng was reprimanded and returned to his original post
because his impeachment of Yìkuāng lacked factual basis.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Wáng Zhào was imprisoned.
On the *gēngyín* day,
arrears of taxes were remitted for Yúlín and other prefectures and counties.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Zhāng Déyí concluded the treaty on labor protection with Britain.
In the summer, on the *xīnhài* day of the fourth month,
an audience was granted to German Prince Ālábàiběr and Minister Mùmò at the Qiánqīnggōng.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Sū Yuánchūn was exiled to Xīnjiāng.
In this month,
disaster relief grain from the previous year was remitted for Dèngchuān,
for areas affected by crocodiles in Xīnhuà,
and for areas affected by military incursions in Hūlán, Suíhuà, and other jurisdictions.
On the *xīnsì* day of the fifth month,
Daoyuan Yuán Dàhuà was ordered to manage mining affairs in Ānhuī.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Rèhé Imperial Traveling Palace suffered a disaster (fire).
On the *bǐngxū* day,
an Imperial Edict granted a special pardon to those involved in the *Wùxū* political faction.
Excluding Kāng Yǒuwéi, Liáng Qǐchāo, and Sūn Wén,
those stripped of office had their original titles restored,
and those wanted, imprisoned, or under surveillance were released and exempted.
On the *wùxū* day,
rebels in Guangxī captured Liǔchéng,
and Commander Zǔ Shéngwǔ was beheaded before the army.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Fàn Fèngyí, a *gòngshēng* from Xíngtái who lived with nine generations under one roof, was honored.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Liú Chūnlín and 273 others were granted the *jìnshì jíyì* degree of various ranks.
On the *yǐsì* day,
an Imperial Edict stated:
this year's seventieth birthday celebration will not include banquets;
Generals, Governors-General, and Governors are not to come to the capital to offer congratulations,
and all tributes are remitted.
The Customs Supervisors for Yuèhǎi and Huái'ān,
and the Jiāngníng Textile Commissioner were abolished.
On the *jǐyǒu* day of the sixth month,
an edict stated:
"The times are difficult, the people are suffering,
officials are obstructive,
and the voices of the lower classes are not heard.
Even in prefectures and counties, land taxes are over-collected and embezzled,
debts are declared for payments made,
and countless abuses proliferate,
greatly betraying the imperial court's intention to care for the people.
All Governors-General and Governors shall promptly compile clear and concise tables and reports detailing
how much the official grain quota is,
how much is actually collected,
how much is collected as standard surcharges or converted into silver.
Furthermore, they shall explicitly list
whether there are any extra fees,
without concealing or omitting anything,
and report truthfully to the throne."
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Tiěliáng was ordered to go to Jiāngnán to investigate manufacturing facilities,
plan appropriately,
and inspect income and expenditure accounts,
as well as the pros and cons of various treasuries and bureaus.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Cén Chūnshuān was urged to proceed to Guìzhōu and Liǔzhōu to supervise the troops.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Chēlín Duōduōbù and other league leaders of the nomadic tribes in Qīnghǎi
requested to bring tribute gifts to the capital to offer congratulations during their annual visit.
An Imperial Edict highly praised them,
but still declined the request.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Yǒngdìng River burst its banks.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the river burst its banks at Bózhuāng in Lìjīn.
In autumn, on the *wùyín* day of the seventh month,
an audience was granted to the Belgian envoy Géfēiyè at the Qiánqīnggōng.
The office of Naval Commander-in-Chief of Fújiàn was abolished
and merged with that of the Army Commander-in-Chief,
who was relocated to Xiàmén.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Yǒngdìng River again burst its banks at the lower Xùn section.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
one hundred thousand taels from the Privy Purse were allocated for flood and drought relief in Sìchuān.
On the *rénchén* day,
British troops entered Tibetan territory,
the Dálài fled,
his title was stripped,
and Bānchán É'ěrdéní was ordered to take over.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Yellow River in Gānsù burst its banks,
Gāolán was affected by the disaster,
and Sōngfán was ordered to provide relief.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the tribute of porcelain from Jiǔjiāng was suspended.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Lǐ Xīngruì was appointed Acting Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng and Minister of the Southern Ocean.
In this month,
Tāng Shòuqían was granted the title of Fourth-Rank Minister
and appointed Director-General of Zhejiang Railways.
On the *dīngwèi* day of the eighth month, the first day of the lunar month,
staff members of the Neìwùfǔ were reduced and merged.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Táng Shàoyí was granted the title of Deputy Military Governor
and dispatched to Xīzàng to investigate the situation.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
an audience was granted to the Italian envoy Gānínà at the Rénshòudiàn.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
an audience was granted to the Mexican envoy Lìhuá at the Qiánqīnggōng.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day of the ninth month, the new moon,
an audience was granted to British envoy Sir Ernest M. Satow (Sàdàoyì) in the Qiánqīnggōng.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Jìngxìn was relieved of his duties due to illness.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Lǐ Xīngruì died.
Zhōu Fù was ordered to act as the Governor-General of Liǎngjiāng and Minister of Southern Affairs (Nányáng Dàchén).
As British troops entered Tibet,
the Dalai Lama requested assistance.
Délín was ordered to pacify the situation.
The British troops subsequently withdrew.
Táng Shàoyí was appointed Plenipotentiary Minister for treaty negotiations.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Húběi Grain Intendant (Liángdào) was changed to the Shīhè Military Preparedness Circuit Intendant (Bīngbèidào).
This autumn,
arrears of taxes were remitted for Jílín due to military conflicts, and for Yúnnán due to floods, droughts, and military disasters.
The fixed levies of Wǔwēi and Jīnzhōu were also remitted.
Relief was provided for flood disasters in Yúnnán, Shùntiān, Fújiàn, Gānsù, and Jiāngxī,
and for other disasters in Shānxī, Zhèjiāng, Guǎngdōng, and elsewhere.
In winter, on the *bǐngwǔ* day of the tenth month,
Lǚ Hǎihuán concluded the renewal of the Sino-Portuguese commercial treaty.
Yùdé was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tǐréngé.
Shìxù was appointed Associate Grand Secretary.
On the *gēngxū* day,
audiences were granted to the envoys of Austria, America, Germany, Russia, and Belgium, including Qígàn, in the Huángjídiàn.
The breach in the Yǒngdìnghé was closed.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
His Majesty, accompanied by the Empress Dowager, attended the Rénshòudiàn,
where a banquet was given for close imperial relatives and vassal lords.
Princes (*wáng*), *bèilè*, *bèizǐ*, and *gōng* led a dance performance.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
it was the Empress Dowager's birthday.
His Majesty proceeded to the Páiyúndiàn to present a memorial of congratulations.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
audiences were granted to the envoys of Britain, Japan, France, and Korea, including Sàdàoyì, in the Huángjídiàn.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
an imperial edict (yìzhǐ) prohibited provinces from cunningly creating new names for new policies
to impose harsh and petty private levies.
All matters concerning education and vocational training in schools and workshops
should be officially encouraged,
and funded by gentry and commoners themselves,
without giving rise to harsh disturbances.
The status of "degenerate people" (*duòmín*) in Zhèjiāng was abolished,
allowing them to enroll in schools.
Those who graduated would be granted official status (*chūshēn*).
On the *yǐhài* day of the eleventh month, the new moon,
Yìnchāng was reappointed Minister to Germany.
Zēng Guǎngquán was appointed Minister to Korea.
An earthquake occurred in Dǎjiànlú, Sìchuān.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
an audience was granted to Italian envoy Baroli (Bālèlǐ) in the Qiánqīnggōng.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Guangxi bandit leader Lù Yàfā was executed.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the new army's official system (guānzhì) was established.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Zēngqí was ordered to provide relief and pacification for the refugees in the Three Eastern Provinces (Dōngsānsěng).
In the twelfth month, on the *wùshēn* day,
audiences were granted to Italian envoy Bālèlǐ, Dutch envoy H.J. von der Heyde (Xītèsī), and Portuguese envoy Almeida (Āméidá) in the Huángjídiàn.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the Jiāng'ān Grain Intendant was abolished,
and the Jiāngnán Salt Intendant was changed to the Salt and Grain Intendant.
On the *dīngsì* day,
300,000 *liǎng* from the imperial treasury (nèitǎng) were disbursed for the relief of refugees in Fèngtiān.
On the *rénxū* day,
public bonds (gōngzhàipiào) were first issued in Zhílì.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Grand Canal Grain Transport Governor-General (Cáoyùn Zǒngdūd) was abolished,
and a Jiānghuái Governor (Xúnfǔ) was established.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Aristocratic School (Guìzhòu Xuétáng) was established.
On the *wùchén* day,
a巡道 (Xúndào) with the title of Surveillance Commissioner (Ànchásǐ Xián) was established in Hēilóngjiāng,
as well as the Lánsuíhǎi Military Preparedness Circuit Intendant (Bīngbèidào),
and the two prefectures of Hūlán and Suíhuà.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Dūjiāngyàn in Sìchuān was repaired.
This winter,
the Governors (Xúnfǔ) of Húběi and Yúnnán were abolished,
as were the Grain Intendants of Húnán and Shǎnxī.
Autumn grain taxes for Shípíng and Zhàozhōu were remitted,
as were arrears of taxes for Chénliú and other prefectures and counties,
and the fixed levies for Cháoyì due to flooding.
In the spring of the first month of the 31st year, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
audiences were granted to the envoys of Germany, Britain, Japan, France, Netherlands, Belgium, Italy, Japan, Portugal, Mexico, America, Korea, and Austria in the Qiánqīnggōng.
The Dalai Lama requested to build a temple and chant scriptures in Kùlún,
but this was not permitted.
He was ordered to return to Tibet
and to treat all beings kindly.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Tiěliáng reported that upon inspecting the military camps (yíngwǔ) of various provinces,
the Húběi Army (Lùjūn) was found to be the best.
An imperial edict (zhào) commended them.
The commanders of the various armies in Jiāngnán received varying punishments.
Táng Shàoyí was appointed Minister to Great Britain.
In the second month, on the *yǐsì* day,
an imperial edict (yìzhǐ) disbursed 300,000 *liǎng* from the imperial treasury for the relief and resettlement of refugees in the Three Eastern Provinces.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Chánggēng and Xú Shìchāng were ordered to inspect and reorganize the three divisions (sānzhèn) of the new army.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Lóng'ēndiàn of the Jǐnglín Mausoleum suffered a disaster.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
an audience was granted to American envoy E.H. Conger (Kānggé) in the Hǎiyàntáng.
On the *rénshēn* day,
relief was provided for the nomadic people of Ālāshàn.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
arrears of grain taxes from the previous year in Shǎnxī were remitted.
In the third month, on the *yǐhài* day,
Fèngtiān suffered from famine.
Russian troops entered Chángchūn
and occupied it.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Tibetan people (*fānrén*) in Bātáng burned down a French church.
The Assistant Resident in Tibet (Zhùzàng Bāngbàn) Fèngquán, while suppressing and apprehending them,
was ambushed and killed.
Mǎ Wéiqí, the Provincial Commander-in-Chief (Tídū) of Sìchuān, was ordered to suppress them.
Kē Féngshí was ordered to manage the unified opium tax (tǔgāo tǒngjuān) affairs of the eight provinces.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
audiences were granted to German Prince Friedrich Leopold (Fú Lǐliúbó) and Minister A. von Mumm (Mùmò) in the Qiánqīnggōng.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
an imperial edict (zhào) ordered Governors-General and Governors (dūdū xúnfǔ) to recommend capable military commanders (tízhèn guān).
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the provincial capital of Yúnnán was opened as a commercial port.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the newly established Jiānghuái Governor was abolished.
The Commander-in-Chief (Zǒngbīng) of Huáiyáng was changed to the Grand Commander (Tídū) of Jiāngběi.
On the *guǐsì* day,
an imperial edict (yù) ordered a revision of the laws.
Capital punishment was limited to decapitation (zhǎnjué).
Lingering death (língchí), displaying the head (xiāoshǒu), and desecration of corpses (lùshī) were abolished.
Punishments for decapitation (zhǎn), strangulation (jiǎo), and awaiting execution (jiānhòu) were successively reduced.
All articles concerning guilt by association (yuánzuò),
except for those involving conscious complicity (zhīqíng),
were all leniently remitted.
All regulations concerning tattooing (cìzì) were also abolished.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
regarding the prohibition of torture (xíngxùn),
the modification of flogging with light or heavy bamboo (chī zhàng),
and the clearing and inspection of prisons and detention centers,
Governors-General and Governors (dūdū xúnfǔ) were ordered to earnestly implement these measures.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
bandits caused unrest in Qiánwéi.
Government troops suppressed them.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Zhōu Fù was ordered to go to Jiāngběi to plan for official administration, coastal defense, river works, and policing.
In summer, on the *jiǎchén* day of the fourth month,
as Russian warships reached the South Seas (Nányáng),
local authorities were ordered to take precautions,
and merchants were prohibited from transporting coal to supply them.
Regulations for theft (qièdào) were revised.
All offenses punishable by flogging with light or heavy bamboo were changed to forced labor.
On the *yǐsì* day,
an imperial edict ordered all provincial, prefectural, and county authorities to establish vocational training centers (xíyìsuǒ) for criminals.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Liú Yǒngqìng was granted the title of Vice Minister (shìláng xián),
and was appointed acting Grand Commander of Jiāngběi,
with all military commanders (zhèn) and intendants (dào) below him under his command.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the Guǎngdōng Grain Intendant was abolished,
and a Liánqīn Military Preparedness Circuit Intendant was established.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Chéng Déquán was ordered to act as the General (Jiāngjūn) of Hēilóngjiāng.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
German warships suddenly arrived in Hǎizhōu for surveying.
Strict inquiries were ordered.
In the fifth month, on the *dīnghài* day,
audiences were granted to Japanese envoy G. Casati (Jiǎsīlǐ) and American envoy W.W. Rockhill (Róukèyì) in the Qiánqīnggōng.
On the *guǐsì* day,
an audience was granted to Mexican envoy J.F. Huertas (Húěrdá) in the Huángjídiàn.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Wáng Wénsháo was dismissed as Grand Councillor (Jūnjī Dàchén).
Xú Shìchāng was ordered to learn and serve as a Grand Councillor,
concurrently serving as Minister of Political Affairs (Zhèngwùchù Dàchén).
Tiěliáng and Xú Shìchāng were to jointly manage military training affairs.
In the sixth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
an audience was granted to Russian envoy D. Pokotilov (Púkēdì) in the Rénshòudiàn.
Arrears of taxes for Zhōngmóu and other prefectures and counties were remitted.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
students studying abroad who passed examinations, such as Jīn Bāngpíng, were granted various degrees of *jìnshì* and *jǔrén*.
Zǎizé, Dài Hóngcí, Xú Shìchāng, and Duān Fāng were ordered to travel to various Western and Eastern countries to investigate political systems.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
an imperial edict ordered the establishment of Ministers Guarding the Three Mausoleums (Sānlíng Shǒuhù Dàchén) in Shèngjīng.
The Vice Ministers (Shìláng) of the Five Boards (Hù, Lǐ, Bīng, Xíng, Gōng) in Shèngjīng were abolished.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Shìxù was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tǐréngé.
Nàtóng was appointed Associate Grand Secretary.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Guǎngdōng Governor (Xúnfǔ) was abolished.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
bandits in Qián (Guìzhōu) captured the four stockades of Dūyún.
Government troops recaptured them.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day of the seventh month,
the imperial censors' inspections of the five inner cities and street offices were abolished.
The "trained volunteers" (*liànyǒng*) were reorganized into "patrol constables" (*xúnbǔ*).
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Shào Yīng was again appointed Imperial Commissioner to investigate foreign political systems.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
due to military matters in Bātáng,
the donation system for official posts was suspended for one year.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Tíng Jié was granted the title of Vice Minister and
sent to Fèngtiān to manage land reclamation affairs.
Chángdé and Xiāngtán were opened as commercial ports.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Tiě Liáng was ordered to study and serve in the Grand Council,
and soon after, also served concurrently as Minister of the Council for Government Affairs.
On the *rén yín* day of the eighth month,
an edict stated:
"The boycotts of American goods by merchants and industrialists in various provinces
are detrimental to foreign relations
and also harm commerce.
Provincial officials should earnestly guide them
and investigate them from time to time."
On the *jiǎchén* day,
an imperial decree abolished the imperial examination system.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Fèngtiān Prefect and Assistant Prefect were abolished,
and the Educational Commissioner for the Three Eastern Provinces (*Dōngsānshěng xuézhèng*) was established instead.
Liú Shìxùn was appointed Envoy to France and Japan,
Huáng Gào was appointed Envoy to Italy,
and Zhōu Róngyào was appointed Envoy to Belgium.
Róngyào was subsequently dismissed,
and Lǐ Shèngduó was appointed instead.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
taxes for troops in the northern route of Fèngtiān that had been levied were remitted.
On the *xīnhài* day,
30,000 *tài* (taels) from the imperial treasury were dispatched to Jiāngsū for emergency relief.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
an imperial decree ordered that provincial educational commissioners (*xuézhèng*) be solely responsible for examining schools;
thereafter, matters concerning educational commissioners
would fall under the purview of the Minister of Education for assessment.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Pān Xiàosū, the Governor of Xīnjiāng, was stripped of his post for embezzlement of funds
and banished to a military outpost.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Yuán Shìkǎi and Tiě Liáng were ordered to review the new army's autumn maneuvers.
On the *rénxū* day,
Wāng Dàxiè was appointed Envoy to the United Kingdom,
Yáng Shèng was appointed Envoy to Germany,
and Lǐ Jīngmài was appointed Envoy to Austria.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Hǎizhōu was opened as a commercial port.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Lǐ Jīngfāng was reassigned as Minister for Commercial Treaties.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Zài Zé and others set out.
As soon as they boarded the carriage,
someone suddenly threw a bomb.
Upon reporting the incident,
an imperial decree ordered a strict hunt for the perpetrators and severe punishment.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Bātáng rebellion was quelled,
and the bandit leaders, Lamas Āzé and Lóngběn Lángjí, were executed.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day of the ninth month,
Zhōu Róngyào, a third-rank Metropolitan Official, having previously served as a customs clerk,
was found to have embezzled a large amount from the treasury.
He was stripped of his post, arrested, and prosecuted,
and his assets were confiscated.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Ministry of Police (*Xúnjǐngbù*) was first established,
with Xú Shìchāng as its Minister.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Běixīncāng granary caught fire.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
for their achievements in pacifying Guǎngxī,
Cén Chūnxuān was promoted to the title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent,
and Lǐ Jīngxī received special commendation.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the German Envoy, Mù Mò, was received at the Qínzhèng Diàn.
On the *wùxū* day,
Shàng Qíhēng and Lǐ Shèngduó were ordered to accompany Zài Zé and others to various countries to investigate political systems.
That autumn,
relief was provided for flood disasters in various prefectures of Guìzhōu and Yúnnán,
a wind disaster in Tàikāng,
and hail and wind disasters in Zhènfān and Bāyàn Rónggé.
In the tenth month of winter, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Japanese Minister, Uchida Kōsai, and others were received at the Qínzhèng Diàn.
The Hā'ěrbīn Circuit of Jílín was established.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the Lúhàn Railway was completed.
British troops entered Tibet,
demanding compensation of over 1.2 million *tài* (taels).
An edict stated that the state would pay on their behalf
to alleviate the hardship of the Tibetans.
On the *rénxū* day,
regulations for minting silver coins and their circulation were established.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Lù Zhēngxiáng was appointed Envoy to the Netherlands,
also concurrently managing affairs of the Hague Peace Conference.
On the *wùchén* day,
the Bureau for Political Research (*Kǎochá Zhèngzhì Guǎn*) was established.
It was to select political and legal systems from various countries suitable for China's governance,
deliberate on their merits and demerits,
compile them into a book,
and seek imperial approval for adoption.
An imperial decree stated:
"Recently, there have been unruly individuals
spreading revolutionary and anti-Manchu doctrines,
forming factions,
and secretly engaging in rebellion.
All provincial officials should strictly prohibit and secretly apprehend them.
All principal and accessory offenders
shall be punished according to the law for treason."
On the *gēngwǔ* day, the first day of the eleventh month,
bandit activities in Shǎn and Luò were quelled.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Yù Dé passed away.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the envoy to Korea was abolished,
and a consul-general was appointed instead.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
an imperial decree established the Ministry of Education (*Xuébù*),
into which the Guózǐjiàn (Imperial Academy) was merged,
and Róng Qìng was transferred to serve as its Minister.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the new Sino-Japanese treaty was concluded.
On the *xīnhài* day of the twelfth month,
Nà Tóng was granted the title of Grand Secretary of the Tǐrén Pavilion,
and Róng Qìng was appointed Associate Grand Secretary.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the General Police Headquarters for the Inner and Outer Cities of the Capital (*Jīngshī Nèi Wài Chéng Xúnjǐng Zǒngtīng*) was established.
The Bureau of Industry and Patrol (*Gōngxún Jú*) was abolished.
Xú Shìchāng and Tiě Liáng were both appointed Grand Councillors.
This month,
arrears of taxes for troops in various banners of Shèngjīng and various prefectures of Shǎnxī were remitted,
as were land rents for areas affected by accumulated flooding in Ānzhōu and by floods in Hánchéng.
That winter,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Huìzé,
flood disasters in Jīngzhōu,
and flood and hail disasters in Yīngjíshā'ěr.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day of the first month of spring in the thirty-second year (*bǐngwǔ*),
the tribute of sable fur from the Bùtèhā was deferred.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Envoys Mù Mò (German) and others from Germany, Britain, France, America, Japan, the Netherlands, Italy, Russia, Austria, Belgium, Portugal, and Mexico were received at the Qiánqīng Gōng.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Zhāng Yīng, the bandit leader from Zhāngpǔ, was executed.
On the *rénchén* day,
Xú Fǔ was dismissed for an inspection error.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Qú Hóngjī was appointed Associate Grand Secretary.
On the *wùchén* day of the second month,
an imperial decree ordered all provinces to protect churches and the lives and property of foreigners.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the German Envoy Mù Mò and others were received at the Qínzhèng Diàn.
This month,
100,000 *tài* (taels) from the imperial treasury were allocated to aid disaster relief in Japan.
On the *wùchén* day, the first day of the third month,

the five major principles of loyalty to the monarch, veneration of Confucius, promotion of public welfare, promotion of military spirit, and promotion of practical knowledge were declared as the aims of education,
and an imperial decree to that effect was issued throughout the realm.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the selection of *xiùnǚ* (beautiful women) from the Eight Banners was abolished.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Wāng Dàxiè was ordered to congratulate the Japanese monarch on his wedding.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Tōngzhōu, Jiāngsū, was opened as a commercial port.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
an earthquake occurred in San Francisco, USA,
and 100,000 *tài* (taels) from the imperial treasury were allocated to aid Chinese residents.
This month,
Austrian Envoy Gusinsky, Italian Envoy Barrelet and others, German Envoy Mù Mò and others, and French Envoy Robin met for audiences in succession.
That spring,
various salt fields in Rénhe and other places in Zhèjiāng and various prefectures and counties,
salt taxes from the three salt administrations of Háng, Yán, and Qú, and miscellaneous taxes on barren lands and mountain ponds,
disaster relief grain from Yúnnán, Húnán, and Xīnjiāng,
and tax arrears from Shǎnxī were remitted.
On the *wùxū* day, the first day of the fourth month of summer,
Lù Zhēngxiáng was ordered to go to Switzerland to negotiate the Red Cross Convention.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the provincial educational commissioners (*xuézhèng*) were abolished,
and educational intendants (*tíxuéshǐ*) were established instead.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the Japanese Minister, Uchida Kōsai, was received at the Qínzhèng Diàn.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Tiě Liáng was appointed Minister for Supervising Tax Affairs,
and Táng Shàoyí was his deputy.
On the *dīngsì* day,
100,000 *tài* (taels) from the Húnán treasury were dispatched for flood relief.
On the *bǐngxū* day of the intercalary fourth month,
due to untimely rain and sunshine,
and repeated reports of localized disasters,
an imperial decree admonished both monarch and subjects to be vigilant.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Táng Jiǒng was relieved of his duties in Yúnnán mining affairs due to old age and illness.
On the *wùxū* day of the fifth month,
50,000 *tài* (taels) from the imperial treasury were dispatched for flood relief in Guǎngdōng.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Qìnhé River in Hénán overflowed,
and disaster victims were relieved.
This month,
French Envoy Baster and Italian Prince Ferdinando and others were received at the Qiánqīng Gōng.
In the sixth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
Germany reduced its stationed troops in Zhílì,
returning Lángfáng, Yángcūn, Běidàihé, Qínwángdǎo, and Shānhǎiguān territories to us.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Qín Jiāwèi, the bandit leader from Yuánlíng, was executed.
This summer,
arrears in Làngqióng were remitted,
Shāchē’s barren land tax quota was reinstated,
and the disaster-stricken Gānsù and Yúnnán provinces were remitted their tax arrears.
Relief was provided for the flood disaster in Wǔzhì
and the fire disaster in Cháoyáng.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *wùxū* day,
a Minister for Border Affairs of Sìchuān and Yúnnán was established,
with Zhào Érfēng appointed to the post,
and granted the title of Attendant Minister.
The Qìnhé River breach was closed.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the banner-garrison troops of the land and naval camps in Jiāngsū were reorganized into patrol squads.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Zài Zé and others, the Ministers for Investigating Politics, returned to the capital,
and submitted confidential memorials.
They were commanded to be publicly reviewed by the Prince Chún, the Ministers of the Grand Council and the Government Affairs Office, the Grand Secretaries, and the Beiyang Minister,
to determine the course of action.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Dàdōnggōu in Fèngtiān was opened as a commercial port,
a customs office was established,
and the Eastern Circuit Intendant concurrently supervised it.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an edict stated:
“Zài Zé and others have memorialized,
stating that the nation’s weakness
stems from the discord between superiors and subordinates,
and the estrangement between those within and outside the government.
Officials do not know how to protect the people,
and the people do not know how to defend the country.
The reason for the wealth and strength of other nations
lies in implementing a constitution
and basing decisions on public opinion.
In the present circumstances,
the only course is to emulate constitutional government,
concentrating supreme authority in the court,
and making all public affairs subject to public opinion.
The foundations for constitutional preparation
must be earnestly strengthened by all officials, both within and outside the government.
After a few years, when the framework is roughly established,
drawing upon the successful practices of various nations,
a specific timeframe for implementation will then be set.”
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
an edict was issued regarding constitutional preparation,
stating that the official system must first be clarified and standardized,
commanding ministers to compile it,
with Yì Kuāng, Sūn Jiānài, and Qú Hóngjī jointly responsible for its review and approval,
and to implement it according to imperial decree.
Duān Fāng was transferred to be Governor-General of the Two Jiāngs and concurrently Southern Ocean Minister.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
one hundred thousand units of treasury reserves from Jiāngsū were allocated to relieve the flood disasters in Xú, Hǎi, and Huáixī.
In the eighth month, on the *dīnghài* day,
the quota tax for flood-damaged land in Línchuān was remitted.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Prince Higashifushimi Yorihito of Japan and Minister Hayashi Gonsuke were received at the Rénshòu Diàn.
This month,
relief was provided for the flood disaster in Ānhuī,
the typhoon disaster in Guǎngdōng,
and the waterlogging disaster in Húzhōu.
In the ninth month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
envoys from various nations were received at the Rénshòu Diàn.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Chén Jǐntāo and others who had graduated from overseas studies were awarded jinshi and juren degrees of varying ranks.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
an imperial edict announced a revision of the official system.
The Grand Secretariat, Grand Council, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Personnel, Ministry of Rites, Ministry of Education, Imperial Clan Court, and Hanlin Academy remained unchanged.
The Ministry of Police was renamed the Ministry of Civil Affairs,
the Ministry of Revenue was renamed the Ministry of Finance,
the Ministry of War was renamed the Ministry of the Army,
the Ministry of Punishments was renamed the Ministry of Justice,
the Ministry of Works was merged into the Ministry of Commerce to become the Ministry of Agriculture, Industry, and Commerce,
and the Court of Colonial Affairs was renamed the Ministry of Colonial Affairs.
Each ministry was to have one Minister,
and two Vice-Ministers,
without distinction between Manchu and Han.
The Censorate was to have one Censor-in-Chief
and two Deputy Censors-in-Chief.
The Censors of the Six Bureaus were renamed Censors,
and the Grand Court of Revision was renamed the Grand Court of Appeals.
New establishments included the Ministry of Posts and Communications, the Ministry of the Navy, the Office of Military Consultation, the Consultative Council, and the Audit Office.
The Department of Finance was assigned to the Ministry of Finance,
and the three courts of the Grand Court of Imperial Sacrifices, the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and the Court of State Ceremonials were assigned to the Ministry of Rites.
The Court of the Imperial Stud and the Office of Military Training were assigned to the Ministry of the Army.
All Ministers of the various ministries were concurrently appointed Ministers of the Political Affairs Council.
Shì Xù was appointed Grand Councillor,
Lín Shàonián was appointed Grand Councillor on probation,
Lù Chuánlín, Róng Qìng, Xú Shìchāng, and Tiě Liáng were all dismissed from the Grand Council,
to focus solely on their ministerial duties.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
one hundred thousand units of treasury reserves from Guǎngdōng were allocated to relieve the typhoon disasters in Hong Kong and the prefectures of Cháo, Gāo, Léi, Qīn, and Lián.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Political Affairs Office was renamed the Council for Political Affairs.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Zēng Guǎngquán was appointed Minister to Germany with the rank of a third-grade metropolitan official.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
for the Empress Dowager's birthday,
banquets were suspended.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
British Minister Sir John Jordan and Belgian Minister Baron de Cartier were received at the Qiánqīng Gōng.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Army and Naval Commanders of Guǎngdōng were merged into one Guǎngdōng Commander.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Japanese Minister Hayashi Gonsuke and others were received at the Qínzhèng Diàn.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Wáng Yǒngqiú and Chén Xiǎnlóng, bandit leaders from Liúyáng and Lǐlíng, instigated a rebellion,
and the government troops captured and executed them.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
three hundred thousand taels from grain tribute commutation were allocated as relief for Jiāngsū.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
an Official Gazette Bureau was established in the capital.
In the eleventh month, on the *jǐhài* day,
one hundred thousand units of Guǎngdōng's jingxiang (capital-bound funds) were retained for relief.
On the *rénchén* day,
the wellhead tax for antimony mines in Guǎngxī was remitted.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
eighty thousand units of official funds from Shǎnxī were allocated to assist relief efforts in Jiāngsū.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an imperial edict elevated Confucius to a great sacrifice,
and the relevant authorities were ordered to discuss the rituals and report.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
an imperial edict commanded all provinces to deliberate on currency reform.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Qūfù Academy was founded,
and one hundred thousand units from the imperial treasury were disbursed to fund its construction.
This month,
Mexican Minister Ignacio Allende y Fernández de Huidobro was received at the Qínzhèng Diàn,
and German Minister Baron von Rex, French Minister Paul Beau, and British Minister Sir John Jordan were received at the Qiánqīng Gōng.
In the twelfth month, on the *guǐhài* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the *yǎglián* (integrity allowance) for metropolitan officials was increased.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
envoys to various nations were reclassified as second-rank actual officials.
This winter,
relief was provided for disasters in Pǔníng, Zhàozhōu, Luópíng, and Shīzōng,
and for floods in Jiāngníng and Yángzhōu.
Grain taxes for waterlogging disasters in Luánpíng and Ānzhōu were remitted,
as were the quota taxes in Yǒngchéng,
tax arrears in Xiánníng and other places in Shǎnxī,
and outstanding grain taxes in disaster-stricken areas of Yǒngpíng, Tàihé, and Kūnmíng.
In the thirty-third year, on the *dīngwèi* spring, the first month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
envoys from various nations were received at the Qiánqīng Gōng.
On the *gēngxū* day,
minor metropolitan officials in various ministries were dismissed.
In the second month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Yǒu Tài was dismissed from his post for mishandling Tibetan affairs
and banished to a military outpost.
On the *rénshēn* day,
one hundred and fifty thousand units of Sū grain tribute were retained for relief.
In the third month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
Japanese Minister Hayashi Gonsuke and others were received at the Qínzhèng Diàn.
On the *wùxū* day,
Chángchūn and Hāěrbīn were opened as commercial ports.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the General of Shèngjīng was renamed Governor-General of the Three Eastern Provinces,
the Generals of Jílín and Hēilóngjiāng were abolished,
and three Provincial Governors for Fèng, Jí, and Hēi were established instead.
Xú Shìchāng was appointed Imperial Commissioner
and Governor-General of the Three Eastern Provinces.
On the *rénchén* day,
Sūn Bǎoqí, the Prefectural Magistrate, was appointed Minister to Germany.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Liáng Dūnyàn, the Tiānjīn Circuit Intendant, was appointed Minister to the United States, Mexico, and Peru.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Lù Zhēngxiáng was appointed Special Envoy Plenipotentiary for the Hague Peace Conference,
Lǐ Jīngfāng was appointed Minister to Great Britain,
and Qián Xún was appointed Minister to the Netherlands.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Kūngāng passed away.
This spring,
tax arrears for flood-affected areas in Zhōngwèi and subordinate areas like Yúlín were remitted,
as were outstanding grain taxes and quota taxes for drought-stricken prefectures and counties in Yúnnán.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day of the fourth month,
the *mínzhuàng bǔyì* (civilian constables and runners) of each province were abolished,
and replaced with *xúnjǐng* (police).
There was an earthquake in Suīlái.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Censor Zhào Qǐlín was dismissed from office for slandering imperial relatives and nobles.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the official system of the Three Eastern Provinces (Dōngsānshěng) was revised.
Fèngtiān, Jílín, and Hēilóngjiāng each established an *xíngshěng gōngshǔ* (provincial administration office),
with a *zǒngdū* (governor-general) as the chief official,
and a *xúnfǔ* (governor) as the second official.
Left and Right *cānzàn* (counselors) were appointed,
to separately head the *Chéngxuān* (Administration) and *Zīyì* (Consultation) departments.

Seven divisions were separately established: *Jiāoshè* (Foreign Affairs), *Qíwù* (Banner Affairs), *Mínzhèng* (Civil Affairs), *Tíxué* (Education), *Dùzhī* (Finance), *Quànyè* (Industrial Promotion), and *Méngwù* (Mongolian Affairs).
Each had a *sīshǐ* (division head),
as well as officials like *tífǎshǐ* (judicial commissioner) and *dūliànchù* (inspectorate of training).
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
prayers for rain were offered.
On the *xīnsì* day,
due to flooding north of the Jiāng River,
a strict ban was imposed on the export of grain.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the military officer system for the army and navy was established.
The Army Department (Lùjūnbù) was to have two departments and ten divisions,
the Military Advisory Office (Jūnzīchù) five divisions,
and the Navy Department (Hǎijūnbù) six divisions.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Kǒng Língyí, the Duke Yǎnshèng, was ordered to inspect educational affairs in Shāndōng.
On the *guǐsì* day of the fifth month,
Lamas from Bātáng and other regions incited the Western barbarians (Héxī Mán) to revolt;
the imperial army suppressed them.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Wáng Shìzhēn was ordered to act as *Tídū* (commander-in-chief) for Jiāngběi (north of the Jiāng River) with the title of *shìláng* (vice minister).
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
forest fires were prohibited in Xīlíng.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Qú Hóngjī was dismissed.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Lù Chuánlín was appointed Grand Councilor (*Jūnjī Dàchén*).
Prince Chún was ordered to serve directly in the Grand Council.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Wáng Wénzhào was dismissed,
and Zhāng Zhīdòng was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary (*Xiébàn Dàxuéshì*).
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Chónglǐ died.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the *ànchásǐ* (provincial surveillance commissioner) was changed to *tífǎshǐ* (judicial commissioner).
*Xúnjǐng* (police) and *Quànyè Dào* (industrial promotion intendant) were established.
The *fēnshǒu* (defending) and *fēnxún* (patrolling) *dào* (circuits) were abolished.
The *bīngbèidào* (military preparedness intendant) was selectively retained,
and *shěnpàntīng* (judicial courts) were separately established,
to prepare for judicial independence,
and assistant administrators (*zuǒzhìyuán*) were increased and replaced,
to prepare for local self-governance,
with the aim of full implementation within fifteen years.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
an edict stated:
“Regarding the constitution (*xiànfǎ*),
both officials and commoners bear responsibility.
Anyone who knows how to prepare for it or the order of its implementation
is permitted to itemize and present it,
and the authorities shall select and report it.”
Xú Xīlín, a probationary *dào* (circuit intendant) in Ānhuī, assassinated Governor Ēnmíng.
Xīlín was captured and executed.
On the *xīnyǒu* day of the sixth month,
Lǐ Jiājū was appointed Minister to Japan (*Chūshǐ Rìběn Dàchén*).
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Censor Zhào Qǐlín was reinstated.
On the *rénshēn* day,
after no rain since the fourth month, it rained on this day.
Zhāng Zhīdòng was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tǐrén Pavilion (*Tǐrén Gé Dàxuéshì*),
and Lù Chuánlín was appointed Assistant Grand Secretary (*Xiébàn Dàxuéshì*).
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the *Wànshòu* (Empress Dowager's birthday) banquets were suspended.
The Yǒngdìng River burst its banks.
This summer,
taxes and levies for *Xīnhuà* and other areas affected by floodwaters,
and arrears in tuition for *Yītōng* affected by bandits,
and silver and rice for counties in Yúnnán affected by drought were remitted.
Relief was provided for famine in Yúnnán and flood disasters in Zhílì.
On the *xīnmǎo* day of the seventh month of autumn,
an edict ordered officials at home and abroad to discuss the assimilation of Manchus and Han.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the *Kǎochá Zhèngzhì Guǎn* (Bureau for the Examination of Politics) was renamed *Xiànzhèng Biānchá Guǎn* (Bureau for the Compilation and Examination of Constitutional Government).
Meetings of the Grand Councilors (*Jūnjī Dàchén*), Grand Secretaries (*Dàxuéshì*), and Ministers Participating in Government Affairs (*Cānyù Zhèngwù Dàchén*)
were to be held in the Grand Secretariat (*Nèigé*).
On the *rénchén* day,
an imperial decree dispatched Yáng Shìqí to inspect various ports in the Nányáng (Southeast Asia) region,
to commend overseas Chinese.
Taxes and levies for Zàozhōu and Lùfēng affected by disaster were remitted.
Relief was provided for disaster victims in Shùntiān and other regions,
and for those affected by dragon (jiao) disasters in Liúyáng and Shàoyáng.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
an edict stated that conspiratorial bandits
often used revolutionary terms
to skillfully incite rebellion.
Governors-general and governors should find ways to disperse them.
Captured offenders sentenced
should be distinguished as traitors or bandits for different judgments,
and those coerced or whose families were unaware should not be implicated.
Zhāng Yīntáng was appointed Plenipotentiary Minister (*Quánquán Dàchén*)
to negotiate the Tibet treaty with the British.
Jìngxìn died.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
it was decided to limit the training of the army to thirty-six divisions (*zhèn*) within a specified number of years.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Zhāng Zhīdòng and Yuán Shìkǎi were both appointed Grand Councilors (*Jūnjī Dàchén*),
and Yuán Shìkǎi was appointed President of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (*Wàiwùbù Shàngshū*).
On the *dīngsì* day,
Yáng Shìxiáng was ordered to act as Governor-General of Zhílì and concurrently Minister of Beiyang (*Běiyáng Dàchén*).
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Lǐ Jīngmài was excused due to his mother's illness,
and Léi Bǔtóng was appointed Minister to Austria (*Chūshǐ Àoguó Dàchén*).
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the river burst its banks in Mèngxiàn.
On the *xīnyǒu* day of the eighth month,
the Emperor was unwell,
and an edict ordered all provinces to recommend those skilled in medicine.
Wāng Dàxiè was appointed Minister to Britain (*shǐ Yīngguó*),
Dáshòu Minister to Japan (*shǐ Rìběn*),
and Yú Shìméi Minister to Germany (*shǐ Déguó*),
all concurrently serving as Ministers for Constitutional Investigation (*Kǎochá Xiànzhèng Dàchén*).
On the *rénxū* day,
the Capital High Court (*Jīngshī Gāoděng Shěnpàntīng*) was established.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Chief Procuratorate (*Zǒngjiǎnchátīng*) was established.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the Advisory Council (*Zīzhèng Yuàn*) was established,
with Prince Bèi Zǐ Pǔlún and Sūn Jiānài as presidents.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Wǔ Tíngfāng was appointed Minister to the United States (*Chūshǐ Měiguó Dàchén*),
and Sà Yīntú was appointed Minister to Russia (*Chūshǐ Éguó Dàchén*).
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
an edict stated that the Manchu garrisons in the provinces were accustomed to idleness,
and ordered the generals and others to allocate land and supervise cultivation.
After returning to farming,
all matters were to be managed by the local authorities (*yǒusī*).
On the *gēngchén* day,
the courier stations (*yìzhàn*) in Fèngtiān were abolished,
and a news bureau (*wénbàojú*) was established.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
an edict ordered officials at home and abroad to study the system of constitutional monarchy (*jūnzhǔ lìxiàn zhèng tǐ*).
Regulations for local self-governance (*zìzhì zhāngchéng*) were promulgated.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the German envoy Réikèsī and the Japanese envoy Ābù Shǒutàiláng were received at the Rénshòu Hall.
An edict placed the Imperial Guards of the Divine Machine Camp (*Shénjīyíng Wèiduì*) and its officers and soldiers under the jurisdiction of the Army Department.
On the *xīnmǎo* day of the ninth month,
an edict ordered discussion and establishment of Manchu and Han ceremonial rites and criminal laws,
and examination and establishment of a uniform system for weights and measures.
On this day,
due to continued opium habits,
Prince Zhuāng Zàigōng, Prince Ruì Kuíbīn, Imperial Censor Dū Yùshǐ Lù Bǎozhōng, and Vice Imperial Censor Fù Dū Yùshǐ Chén Míngkǎn were reprimanded and dismissed from office,
and ordered to quickly quit their habit.
It was also decreed to civil and military officials, both inside and outside the court,
that they must be completely free of the habit within three months,
otherwise they would be severely punished.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Shěn Jiābèn, Yú Liánsān, and Yīng Ruì were appointed Ministers for Law Revision (*Xiūdìng Fǎlǜ Dàchén*).
On the *jǐhài* day,
each province was ordered to establish an Advisory Council (*Zīyì Jú*)
and publicly elect members,
and also to prepare for the establishment of *zhōu* (prefecture) and *xiàn* (county) deliberative assemblies (*yìshìhuì*).
On the *rénchén* day,
Japan requested grain due to floods,
and 600,000 *shí* of grain were transported from Jiāngsū, Ānhuī, Zhèjiāng, Húběi, and other provinces to assist them.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
each province was ordered to establish an Investigation Bureau (*Diàochá Jú*),
and each ministry and court to establish a Statistics Office (*Tǒngjì Chù*).
Graduates from overseas studies, such as Zhāng Zōngyuán, were given *jìnshì* and *jǔrén* (scholarly degrees) status with different ranks.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Liáng Dǐngfēn, the *Ànchásǐ* (Provincial Surveillance Commissioner) of Húběi, spoke about rescuing the current situation,
saying nothing was more urgent than prohibiting bribery
and stopping illicit requests,
and impeaching Yìkuāng, Yuán Shìkǎi, and others for forming cliques,
being corrupt, and endangering the country.
An imperial decree, deeming it an intentional act to gain reputation,
repudiated him.
This month,
tax and grain levies for counties in Yúnnán and other areas affected by drought were remitted.
Relief was provided for flood disasters in Huáiníng and other counties.
On the *yǐchǒu* day of the tenth month of winter,
Sūn Jiānài, Róngqìng, Lù Rùnxiáng, Zhāng Yīnglín, Táng Jǐngchóng, Bǎoxī, and Zhū Yìfān were appointed to lecture on classics and history, as well as current dynasty's historical precedents.
The Yǒngdìng River's dikes were closed.
On the *wùchén* day,
on the occasion of the Empress Dowager's birthday,
banquets were suspended.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the Japanese envoy Lín Quánzhù and others were received at the Qínzhèng Hall.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
In the eleventh month, on the day Gēngyín,
bandits in Guǎngxī occupied the Nánguān battery,
and Zhāng Míngqí was ordered to suppress them.
They were soon recovered.
On the day Wùshēn,
a ban was placed on public gatherings and speeches.
An edict was issued to all provinces to reorganize schools
and revise the methods of assessment, encouragement, and admonition.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the Russian envoy, Pūkēdì (Pokotilov), and others were received at the Qiánqīnggōng.
Regarding the proposals from internal and external officials on currency reform,
whether to use liǎng or yuán,
both had advantages and disadvantages,
so an edict was issued to all governors and viceroys to investigate and deliberate and report back.
Five hundred thousand taels were disbursed from the treasury to aid the Guǎngxī army.
In the twelfth month, on the first day Wùwǔ,
the posts of Army Commander-in-Chief and Navy Commander-in-Chief for Guǎngdōng were re-established.
On the day Guǐhài,
the Assistant Commander-in-Chief of Jílín was abolished,
and three departments—Jiaōshè (Foreign Affairs), Mínzhèng (Civil Affairs), and Dùzhī (Finance)—as well as a Tífǎshǐ (Chief Justice) and a Quànyèdào (Industrial Promotion Intendant) were established.
Yáng Zhàolín and other graduates of the Jìnshìguǎn's study abroad program were promoted with various ranks.
On the day Rénshēn,
the Grain Intendant of Shāndōng was abolished,
and two intendants—Xúnjǐng (Police) and Quànyè (Industrial Promotion)—were established.
On the day Jiǎxū,
an edict was issued for the Rèhé Imperial Hunting Ground to undertake tūn kěn (military-agricultural colonization)
and the stationed officers and soldiers were abolished.
On the day Yǐhài,
Lǚ Hǎihuán was appointed Minister in charge of the Tiānjīn-Púkǒu Railway.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Nà Tóng was concurrently appointed Minister in charge of Taxation.
On the day Xīnsì,
Sir Robert Hart, the Inspector-General of Customs, was awarded the title of Shàngshū (Minister).
On the day Bǐngxū,
the tribute of sable from Bùtèhā (Butha) was again suspended for one year.
This winter,
arrears of taxes were remitted for Yúnnán (affected by drought), Zhílì (affected by floods), and Shǎnxī.
Relief was provided for areas in Yúnnán affected by jiaōzāi (dragon disasters, i.e., floods),
Sìchuān for floods,
and Guǎngdōng for typhoon and flood disasters.
In the spring of the thirty-fourth year, Wùshēn, in the first month, on the first day Dīnghài,
Aīxīnjuéluó Zaìfēng, Prince Chún, was appointed Grand Councillor.
On the day Gēngyín,
envoys from various countries were received at the Qiánqīnggōng.
On the day Jǐhài,
due to the sudden rise in silver prices in the capital,
which caused a surge in commodity prices,
five hundred thousand taels were disbursed from the treasury,
and the Prefect of Shùntiānfǔ was ordered to buy back currency at reduced prices,
and also to instruct mints in all provinces to cast ten-cash copper coins,
and to additionally cast an extra thirty percent of new one-cash coins
to remedy the situation.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Lánzhōu Yellow River Iron Bridge was constructed.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Austrian envoy, Gùxīnsījī (Güsinski), was received at the Qínzhèngdiàn.
This month,
arrears of taxes were remitted for Kūnmíng and other counties in Yúnnán,
salt taxes for Rénhé and other salt fields in Zhèjiāng,
and fixed taxes for Shàoyáng in Húnán.
In the second month, on the day Wùwǔ,
sacrifices were offered to Dàshè (Great God of the Land) and Dàjì (Great God of Millet).
Thereafter, the Emperor was unable to personally perform these sacrificial rites,
and always sent a substitute.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Zhào Ěrfēng was awarded the title of Shàngshū,
appointed Resident Minister in Xīzàng,
and concurrently held the position of Minister of Border Affairs.
On the day Guǐhài,
an imperial edict increased the stipends (yǎmlián) for Manchu ministers and officers of all banners by 100%,
and revised the allowances for officials below the Imperial Bodyguard.
On the day Bǐngyín,
an edict was issued to clear ordinary prisons in the capital and provinces.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the Jīngshī Quàngōng Chénlièsuǒ (Beijing Industrial Exhibition Hall) suffered a fire.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
an edict stated that
"the agreement to prohibit opium has been reached,
the British have promised to reduce shipments annually,
and this reduction is already being implemented.
It was agreed to try this for three years,
and further reductions would be pushed for after the period expires.
The deadline will soon arrive,
how can we respond to friendly nations?
The Mínzhèng and Dùzhī Ministries are to quickly formulate audit regulations,
and hold the governors and viceroys responsible for instructing their subordinates to genuinely implement the reduction of cultivation and consumption,
and report on it."
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Dáshòu was recalled,
Lǐ Jiājū was appointed Minister to Investigate Constitutional Government,
and Hú Wéidé was appointed Minister to Japan.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Huáng Gào was dismissed,
Qián Xún was transferred to be Minister to Italy,
and Lù Zhēngxiáng was appointed Minister to the Netherlands.
In the third month, on the day Rénchén,
Aīxīnjuéluó Pǔwěi, Prince Gōng, Lù Chuánlín, Jǐngxīng, and Dīng Zhènduó were appointed Ministers for Opium Prohibition,
and戒烟所 (opium prohibition offices) were established
to specialize in inspection and verification.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Gurkha offered tribute of local products.
On the day Jiǎyín,
because of his profound mastery of classical scholarship,
Wáng Kǎiyùn, a Jǔrén from Xiāngtán, was bestowed the title of Jiǎntǎo (compiler).
This month,
new and old fixed taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken areas in Yúnnán.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
the Japanese envoy, Lín Quánzhù (Hayashi Gonsuke), and others were received at the Qínzhèngdiàn.
Yí Gǔ, the General of Suíyuǎnchéng, was found guilty and stripped of his post,
arrested and imprisoned in the Xíngbù (Board of Punishments),
and his property was soon confiscated.
Xìnqín was appointed Minister of Reclamation,
concurrently acting as General of Suíyuǎnchéng.
On the day Dīngsì,
the Ānhuī Ānlúchúhé Intendant was abolished.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Vietnamese bandits captured Hékǒu,
and Liú Chūnlín, with the rank of Third Grade Grand Secretary, was ordered to assist in managing the Yúnnán border defense,
with all front-line troops under his command.
On the day Wùchén,
the Grain Intendant of Guìzhōu and the Guìxī Intendant were abolished.
On the day Jǐsì,
envoys from various countries, including Xītèsī (Hetes), were received at the Rénshòudiàn,
and a banquet was given.
On the day Gēngchén,
Yúnnán government troops defeated bandits at Tiánfáng,
recovered the Four Passes,
and subsequently retook Dàxiǎo Nánxī and Hékǒu,
and funds were disbursed from the treasury to reward the army.
In the fifth month, on the first day Yǐyǒu,
the Yúnnán bandits were pacified.
On the day Dīnghài,
the native chieftains (tǔsī) of Bātáng and Lǐtáng were abolished,
and regular officials were appointed.
On the day Rénchén,
His Majesty's illness recurred,
and officials from the directly governed provinces were ordered to recommend those skilled in medical principles.
On the day Guǐsì,

the descendants of the meritorious officials of the restoration—Duōlóng'ā, Xiàng Róng, Jiāng Zhōngyuán, Luó Zénán, Luò Bǐngzhāng, Zhāng Guóliáng, Lǐ Xùbīn, Péng Yùlín, Yáng Yuèbīn, Bào Chāo, Lǐ Mèngqún, Chéng Xuéqǐ, Liú Sōngshān, Féng Zǐcái, and others—were recorded
and promoted with various ranks.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Kǒngzǐ Temple in Qūfù was renovated.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Xiānghé (Xiang River) burst its banks,
and a hurricane caused disaster.
On the day Gēngxū,
Cáo Yuánbì, a Director, presented his work, Lǐjīng Jiàoshì (Collated and Annotated Rites Classic),
and was awarded the title of Biānxiū (compiler).
On the day Guǐchǒu,
there was heavy rain in Guǎngdōng,
and the three rivers, Dōngjiāng, Xījiāng, and Běijiāng, all overflowed,
breaching embankments.
In the sixth month, on the day Dīngsì,

Wáng Xiānqiān, former Chancellor of the Guózǐjiàn, presented his works, Shàngshū Kǒngchuán Cānzhèng (Rectifications for Kong's Commentary on the Classic of Documents), Hànshū Bǔzhù (Supplementary Annotations to the Book of Han), Xúnzǐ Jíjiě (Collected Explanations of Xunzi), and Rìběn Yuánliú Kǎo (Investigation of the Origins of Japan),
and was awarded the title of Nèigé Xuéshì (Academician of the Grand Secretariat).
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
two taxes—on mining and export—for Guǎngxī mining areas were remitted for five years.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Lí Zhànzhī and other graduates of the Jìnshìguǎn's study abroad program were promoted with various ranks.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Zhāng Zhīdòng was appointed concurrently as Minister in charge of the Yuèhàn (Guǎngdōng-Húběi) Railway.
On the day Yǐhài,
the Dalai Lama's request for an audience was granted.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
as the United States reduced its indemnity payment,
Táng Shàoyí was appointed Special Envoy to express gratitude,
and also to inspect finance in the Western and Eastern Oceans.
It was proposed to abolish likin and increase other taxes.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Yáng Shìxiáng was appointed Governor-General of Zhílì and concurrently Minister of Beīyáng.
On the day Xīnsì,
Chén Jǐngrén, a Director in the Fǎbù (Board of Punishments), and others requested the establishment of a parliament after three years.
An imperial edict stated that Chén Jǐngrén instigated trouble,
and he was stripped of his post and placed under supervision.
This summer,
arrears of fixed taxes were remitted for Yúnnán (affected by flood, drought, and hail disasters) and Féngtiān (affected by floods and barren land).
Relief was provided for Jiāngsū (affected by wind and hail disasters),
and Húběi (affected by floods).
Fifty thousand taels from the Board's treasury were disbursed to aid Cháhā'ěr Mongolian banners and the two wings' pastoral communities affected by disaster,
and another one hundred thousand taels from the Board's treasury were disbursed to aid Guǎngzhōu, Zhàoqìng, and Yángjiāng prefectures in Guǎngdōng affected by floods.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day Rénchén,
the three deputy military superintendents (fùdūtǒng) of Hēilóngjiāng Àihuī, etc., were abolished.
The Àihuī Circuit (dào) and Hūlúnbèi’ěr Circuit were established.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Sū Yuánchūn was released and returned.
On the day Jǐhài,
railway public and private taxes were exempted for three years.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
because political discussion societies (zhèngwénshè) established in various provinces were accumulating wealth and forming factions,
secretly disturbing public order,
an edict was issued strictly prohibiting them in their localities.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the sea dikes in Zhèjiāng were repaired.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the patrol brave (xúnyǒng) in Guǎngxī mutinied,
killing their commanding generals.
Zhāng Rénjùn was ordered to suppress them.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Hú Guólián, a third-rank minister with an honorary title (sānpǐnqīngxián), was appointed to oversee the reclamation and mining affairs in Qióngzhōu and Yáxiàn.
On the day Gēngxū,
a diplomatic commissioner (jiāoshèshǐ) was established in Yúnnán.
That month,
there were locust plagues in Shāndōng and Ānhuī.
On the first day of the eighth month, Jiǎyín,
the Constitutional Compilation and Review Bureau (Xiànzhèng Biāncházhìguǎn) and the Council of State (Zīzhèngyuàn) submitted the main principles of the constitution, parliament, and elections,
as well as the annual preparation matters.
An imperial edict ordered their promulgation to official agencies in the capital and the provinces,
to be implemented within the prescribed period.
Every six months,
a list of achievements was to be reported.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Jiāng Guìtí was appointed to command the Left Army of the Imperial Guards (Wǔwèi Zuǒjūn).
On the day Wùyín,
the Russian envoy Korsakov and the Dutch envoy Geerts, among others, were received at the Rénshòu Hall.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Yìnchāng and Duānfāng were ordered to review the autumn maneuvers.
On the day Gēngchén,
Mǎ Yùkūn died,
and was posthumously promoted to a second-class Light Chariot Commandant (Qīngchē Dūwèi).
On the day Xīnsì,
Yìnchāng was appointed minister plenipotentiary to Germany.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Grand Minister of the Imperial Presence (Yùqián Dàchén) Bódísū was dispatched to Bǎodìng to welcome the Dalai Lama.
On the first day of the ninth month, Guǐwèi,
the former Confucian scholars Gù Yánwǔ, Wáng Fūzhī, and Huáng Zōngxī were granted concomitant sacrifices in the Confucian Temple (Wénmiào).
On the day Yǐyǒu,
American warships sailed to Xiàmén.
Bèilè Yùlǎng and Liáng Dūnyàn were dispatched to offer condolences and greetings.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the Níngxià canal was opened for land reclamation.
On the day Gēngyín,
the Dalai Lama arrived in the capital,
and was soon received in audience at the Rénshòu Hall.
On the day Guǐsì,
a unified currency system was promulgated.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the request of the Ministry of Posts and Communications (Yóuchuán Bù) was granted,
to trial-issue domestic public bonds.
On the day Wùxū,
those who graduated from the Jinshì Hall (Jìnshìguǎn), such as Chén Yúnzàogào, were granted official ranks of varying degrees.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the British envoy Jordan, among others, was received at the Rénshòu Hall.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
those who graduated from overseas studies, such as Chén Zhènnxiān, were granted official qualifications;
and those who graduated from the Jinshì Hall, such as Yè Guāngqí, were granted official ranks of varying degrees.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
the Chéngmiánlóngmào Circuit (dào) in Sìchuān was abolished,
and two new circuits, the Patrol Police Circuit (Xúnpǐng Dào) and the Industrial Promotion Circuit (Quànyè Dào), were established.
On the day Xīnhài,
an edict stated that there were still incomplete matters concerning the previous preparations for constitutional government.
It ordered all ministries and bureaux, following the previous format,
to list and report in phases, each according to its duties,
submitting them to the Constitutional Compilation and Review Bureau for review,
and then to await imperial instructions for compliance.
That autumn,
arrears of taxes in Huìzé, Yúnnán, due to flooding,
and fixed grain taxes in Chǔxióng and other counties, and Wǎngpǔ in Húnán, due to flooding, were exempted.
One hundred thousand taels of silver were disbursed from the treasury to relieve disaster victims in Húběi and Húnán.
Relief was also provided for disasters in Gānsù,
typhoon and flood disasters in Guǎngdōng,
and flood disasters in Guǎngxī, Zhèjiāng, Hēilóngjiāng, and Fújiàn.
In the tenth month of winter, on the day Jiǎyín,
the Japanese envoy Ijūin Hikokichi was received at the Qínzhèng Hall.
Hurricane disasters occurred in Guǎngzhōu, Zhàoqìng, and other prefectures.
An edict ordered urgent relief.
On the day Wùwǔ,
a banquet was bestowed upon the Dalai Lama at the Zǐguāng Pavilion.
On the day Rénxū,
on the occasion of the Empress Dowager's birthday,
the banquet was suspended.
The Dalai Lama offered congratulations and presented local products.
An imperial decree (yìzhǐ) additionally enfeoffed him as Chéngshùn Zànhuà Xītiān Dàshàn Zìzài Fó,
and granted him an annual stipend of ten thousand gold taels,
and he was sent back to Tibet.
On the day Rénshēn,
the Emperor's illness worsened significantly.
An imperial decree
ordered Pǔyí, the son of Prince Chún Zàiqǐng, to be raised and educated in the palace,
and further appointed Zàiqǐng as regent with the title Prince Regent (Shèzhèng Wáng).
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the Emperor's illness became critical;
he passed away at the Hányuán Hall on Yíngtái,
at the age of thirty-eight.
A testamentary edict declared that Pǔyí, the son of Prince Regent Zàiqǐng, should inherit the great imperial lineage
and become the successor emperor.
The Empress Dowager's imperial decree
ordered the successor emperor to inherit Mùzōng as his heir,
and concurrently to carry on the ancestral sacrifices of the late Emperor.
In the first month of the first year of Xuāntǒng, on the day Jǐyǒu,
the Emperor was posthumously honored with the full title Tóngtiān Chóngyùn Dàzhōng Zhìzhèng Jīngwén Wěiwǔ Rénxiào Ruìzhì Duānjǐan Kuānqín Jǐng Huángdì,
with the temple name Dézōng,
and was interred in the Chónglíng Mausoleum.
Commentary states: When Dézōng personally governed,
he was in the prime of his life
and harbored grand ambitions.
He desired to launch punitive expeditions
to wipe away national humiliation.
However, his armies were defeated,
territory was ceded, and peace was bought.
Consequently, he introduced new and minor officials,
eagerly seeking reform,
as a plan for revival and self-strengthening.
Yet, those who sought fame and success
were reckless and self-important,
forgetting the idiom "to fear to throw a stone at a rat lest one break the precious vase"
and caring not if their efforts would be fruitless.
Speaking of it can only evoke sorrow.
When the curtain was drawn again (Empress Dowager Cíxǐ resumed power),
he was confined to Yíngtái.
The external invasions
had their origins internally.
Ultimately, the armies of eight nations allied,
and the Emperor fled west.
After Gēngzǐ (1900),
he suffered from depression and despair,
which quickly led to his demise,
and the fate of the nation also declined as a result.
Alas,
was this not fate?
Annals 25: Annals of Emperor Xuāntǒng
Emperor Xuāntǒng, personal name Pǔyí,
was the great-grandson of Xuānzōng,
the grandson of Prince Chún Xián Yīxuǎn,
and the son of the Prince Regent Zàiqǐng.
To Dézōng, he was a biological nephew.
His mother was the principal consort of the Prince Regent, the Sūwán Guāěrjiā clan.
On the fourteenth day of the first month of spring in the thirty-second year of Guāngxù (1906),
he was born in the Prince Chún's residence.
In the winter of the thirty-fourth year of Guāngxù (1908), on the day Rénshēn,
Emperor Dézōng's illness became critical,
and the Empress Dowager Grand (Tài Huáng Tàihòu) ordered him to be raised and educated in the palace.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Emperor Dézōng passed away.
By imperial decree of the Empress Dowager Grand,
he was to inherit the great imperial lineage
as the successor emperor,
succeeding Mùzōng,
and concurrently carrying on the ancestral sacrifices of the late Emperor.
He was three years old at the time.
Prince Regent Zàiqǐng was ordered by imperial decree of the Empress Dowager Grand to oversee the nation.
Military and state affairs,
as well as memorials from within and outside the capital,
were all handled by the Prince Regent,
who issued edicts accordingly.
Major matters were also subject to the Empress Dowager's imperial decree.
An edict commanded three years of mourning.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the Emperor's paternal grandmother, Cíxǐ Duānyòu Kāngyí Zhāoyù Zhuāngchéng Shòugōng Qīnxuàn Chóngxī Huáng Tàihòu, was honored as the Empress Dowager Grand,
and the concurrently revered mother-empress, the Empress, was honored as the Empress Dowager.
Before this,
the Empress Dowager Grand had also fallen ill.
On this day,
she passed away.
On the *yǐhài* day,
strict security was imposed on the palace gates.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Wénzōng's Qí Guìfēi was honored and elevated to Qí Huángguì Tàifēi;
Mùzōng's Yú Guìfēi to Yú Huángguìfēi;
Xún Guìfēi to Xún Huángguìfēi;
Gā Fēi to Gā Guìfēi;
and the late Emperor's Jǐn Fēi to Jǐn Guìfēi.
On the *wùyín* day,
the presentation of local products by various provinces was suspended.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
an imperial edict was issued admonishing all officials.
The edict stated:
"Matters of state and military affairs
shall be decided by the Prince Regent,
in accordance with the last will of the late Grand Empress Dowager.
From Us downwards,
all shall obey implicitly.
Henceforth, if any princes, dukes, or officials
should be found procrastinating or defying,
or overstepping their bounds,
altering established rules,
or confusing national policies,
they shall immediately be punished according to the law of the land.
This is to avoid failing the heavy trust placed by the late Grand Empress Dowager,
and to satisfy the hopes of officials and common people alike."
On the *gēngchén* day,
the late Emperor's last will was promulgated.
A military rebellion in Ānqìng
was quelled.
On the *yǐyǒu* day of the eleventh month,
the late Grand Empress Dowager's last edict was promulgated.
An edict ordered that in the祝版 (*zhùbǎn*) for seasonal sacrifices,
Chún Xián Qīnwáng be referred to as
"Our birth-father, Chún Xián Qīnwáng,"
and his legal consort as
"Our birth-mother, Chún Xián Qīnwáng's legal consort."
Relief was provided for flood victims in Lǐzhōu and other prefectures of Húnán.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
an imperial decree from the Empress Dowager stated
that the Emperor's birthday celebrations,
after the period of mourning,
should be changed to the thirteenth day of the first lunar month each year.
On the *gēngyín* day,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven and Earth, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the Altars of Land and Grain, and the Former Master Kǒngzǐ, prior to the enthronement.
Sacrifices were also offered at the funeral altars of the late Grand Empress Dowager and the late Emperor.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Emperor was enthroned in the Tàihé Diàn,
and the following year was designated Xuāntǒng first year.
An imperial edict was issued to the realm,
pardoning all crimes except those of a particularly heinous nature.
An edict declared that, in accordance with the late Grand Empress Dowager's will,
it was still decided that in the ninth year,
the eighth year of Xuāntǒng, a constitution would be promulgated
and a parliament convened.
Xuāntǒng coins were minted.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the plaque bearing the inscription
"Zhōnghé Wèiyù"
was presented to the Wén Miào.
On the *rén yín* day,
the Grand Secretariat and other government offices jointly submitted the "General Regulations for the Protocol of the Prince Regent,"
which was promulgated by imperial edict.
Regulations for guarding palace gates were established,
and Bèi lè Zài Tāo, Yù Lǎng, and Shàngshū Tiě Liáng were ordered to oversee inspections.
Fù Dūtǒng Kūnyuán was appointed to manage the Cháhā'ěr herds.
The rank of the leading *zhāngjīng* of the Jūnjī Chù was set at third-rank junior,
and the assistant leading *zhāngjīng* at fourth-rank junior.
For the floods in Lóngxī, Nánjìng, and other counties in Fújiàn,
40,000 *liǎng* of silver were disbursed for relief.
On the *yǐsì* day,
an imperial edict ordered governors and governors-general of all provinces to supervise *sīdào* in investigating their subordinates
and impartially selecting suitable officials.
Incompetent prefects and magistrates who failed to care for the people's suffering
were to be severely punished.
A Bureau for Modifying Banner Regulations was established,
and Bèizi Pǔ Lún, Zhènguó Gōng Zài Zé, Nā Tóng, Bǎo Xī, Xī Yàn, and Dá Shòu were ordered to take charge of its affairs.
An imperial decree urged officials both inside and outside the capital to be frugal
and to avoid extravagance.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
officials were dispatched to offer sacrifices at Kǒngzǐ Quèlǐ, the imperial tombs of past dynasties, the Five Sacred Mountains, and the Four Great Rivers.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an imperial decree from the Empress Dowager
suspended visits to the Yíhé Yuán.
Special favor was granted to Qìng Qīnwáng Yìkuàng, making his princely title hereditary and perpetual.
Bèi lè Zài Xún and Zài Tāo were granted the title of *Jùnwáng*.
The Empress Dowager's father, Gōng Guìxiáng, received double salary.
Grand Secretaries and other officials,
received varying grants.
On the *xīnhài* day,
during the Winter Solstice,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Yuánqiū,
with Zhuāng Qīnwáng Zài Gōng officiating.
From then on, he officiated at all major sacrifices at the altars and temples.
On the *rénzǐ* day, the first day of the twelfth month,
additional posthumous titles were conferred upon Mùzōng Yì Huángdì, Xiàojìng Chéng Huánghòu, Xiàodé Xiǎn Huánghòu, Xiàozhēn Xiǎn Huánghòu, and Xiàozhé Yì Huánghòu.
The Xuāntǒng first year almanac was promulgated.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the Imperial Guard was established,
and Bèi lè Zài Tāo, Yù Lǎng, and Shàngshū Tiě Liáng were ordered to be solely responsible for its training.
The position of *yóujī* of the Zhènxī Battalion in Húnán and the *xiéshǒubèi* of Qiánzhōu Garrison were abolished,
and the number of troops in various battalions of the Qiánzhōu Garrison was reduced.
Yu Shì, the concubine of the late Zhílì Tídū Mǎ Yùkūn, who died for her country, was honored.
Relief was provided for flood victims in Hēilóngjiāng, Mò'ěrgēn, Bùtèhā, Hēishuǐ, Dàlài, and other cities and departments.
Land taxes and rents for disaster-stricken areas in Héjiān and eight other prefectures and counties in Zhílì were remitted.
On the *dīngsì* day,
prayers for snow were offered.
Zhāng Zhīdòng was ordered to concurrently supervise the Chuānhàn Railway as its Grand Minister.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the retired Grand Secretary Wáng Wénsháo died,
and was posthumously granted the title of Tàibǎo.
A posthumous title was granted to the late Yún Guì Zǒngdū Zhāng Liàngjī.
The Ministry of Civil Affairs submitted regulations and forms for household registration surveys.
On the *rénxū* day,
Yuán Shìkǎi was dismissed,
and Grand Secretary Nā Tóng was appointed as a Jūnjī Dàchén.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Liáng Dūnyàn was appointed Shàngshū of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and concurrently Hùibàn Dàchén.
Nā Tóng was relieved of his post as Commander of the Infantry,
and Yù Lǎng was appointed in his place.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
an imperial edict designated Jīnlóngyù in the Western Tombs as the imperial tomb of Dézōng Jǐng Huángdì,
to be known as Chónglíng.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
prayers for snow were offered again.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Ministry of Finance submitted regulations for financial reorganization.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Zhāng Xūn's Huái Army was ordered to remain stationed in the Three Eastern Provinces
to handle matters of bandit suppression and pacification.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
due to an earthquake disaster in Italy,
50,000 *liǎng* of silver were disbursed for relief.
The Bureau for Constitutional Compilation and Investigation reported
that the initial and second selections for the Beijing banners
should be handled by the Shùntiān Fǔ.
On the *yǐhài* day,
an imperial decree ordered all provinces to clear and remit accumulated arrears in taxes and grain.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
prayers for snow were offered again.
On this day,
it snowed.
Arrears in taxes from the 32nd year of Guāngxù in various prefectures and counties of Shǎnxī were remitted.
On the *wùyín* day,
it snowed again.
The Bureau for Constitutional Compilation and Investigation submitted a report on reviewing urban and rural local self-governance,
and also drafted new election regulations,
which were promulgated by imperial edict.
The production of medals (*bǎoxīng*) began,
and they were awarded to the President, Vice President, and envoys to various countries of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
On the *gēngchén* day,
judicial courts and procuratorates of various levels were established in Fèngtiān.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the Jiāngxī Dūliáng Dào was abolished,
and two new *dào* were established: Xúnpǐng Dào and Quànyè Dào.
In the spring of the first year of Xuāntǒng, the *jǐyǒu* year, on the *rénwǔ* day, the first day of the first month,
due to the great deceased being in mourning,
no imperial audience or congratulations were accepted.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
arable land that had fallen into disuse in twenty-eight departments, prefectures, and counties, including Chángzhōu in Jiāngsū, was exempted from taxes,
