as were the grain and silver for military colonies in seven counties: Zhāowén, Jīntán, Dāntú, Kūnshān, Xīnyáng, Jìngjiāng, and Lìyáng.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
border guard posts (kǎlún) were established along the Hūlúnbèi’ěr frontier.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Grand Imperial Commissioner and Governor-General of the Three Eastern Provinces, Xú Shìchāng, requested dismissal due to illness,
but it was denied.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
on the occasion of the Empress Dowager's birthday,
banquets were suspended,
and congratulations were not received.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the unpaid taxes of Ámí Prefecture in Yúnnán, which had suffered from disaster, were remitted.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Ministry of Finance proposed a revised currency system
and requested that it be further submitted for deliberation.
It was sent to the Department of Political Affairs for further deliberation.
A tin mine was opened in Fùchuān County, Guǎngxī.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the purchase and sale of slaves were prohibited.
On the *wùxū* day,
regarding the newly established yámens in recent years
and newly formed provinces,
which required the allocation of personnel,
and for which increased funding was requested,
making it impossible to comprehensively examine their names and actual needs,
an imperial decree ordered a practical review, reduction, and elimination both domestically and abroad,
without any arbitrary limits.
The United States of America held an International Opium Conference in Shànghǎi, Jiāngsū,
and Duān Fāng attended.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Chén Bì was impeached and dismissed,
and Xú Shìchāng was appointed Minister of Posts and Communications.
Xī Liáng was transferred to be Grand Imperial Commissioner and Governor-General of the Three Eastern Provinces,
also overseeing military affairs in the three provinces.
Lǐ Jīngxī was appointed Governor-General of Yún-Guì.
On the *rényín* day,
Gāo Érqiān, the Diplomatic Commissioner for Yúnnán, was ordered to go to Àomén (Macau) to survey the border.
The Ministry of Civil Affairs submitted regulations for reorganizing the police administration inside and outside the capital and adjusting district divisions.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the posthumous honorific title for the Great Empress Dowager was conferred,
and an imperial edict was issued to the whole empire the following day.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an imperial edict ordered the preparation for constitutional government affairs,
stating that all matters to be carried out by the provinces this year
must be completed by the deadline
without delay.
An imperial decree ordered the review and approval of the new criminal law
for promulgation next year.
Sū Yuánchūn, the former Commander-in-Chief of Guǎngxī, was reinstated to his original post.
The imperial tribute of swallows' nests from Xiàmén, Fújiàn, was abolished.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the posthumous honorific title and temple name for the Great Emperor were conferred,
and an imperial edict was issued to the whole empire the following day.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the navy was reorganized,
and Prince Sù, Shànqí, Prince of the First Rank, Zàizé, Minister Tiě Liáng, and Admiral Sà Zhènbīng were ordered to plan it,
with Prince Qìng, Yīkuāng, overseeing inspections.
Tiě Liáng's exclusive appointment as Minister for Training the Imperial Guards was abolished.
In the second month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
the Veritable Records of Dézōng were compiled.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
an imperial decree ordered judicial yámens in the capital and provinces to clear lawsuits
and eliminate malpractices.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the Ministry of Agriculture, Industry, and Commerce reported
that the Netherlands was about to establish new laws
to naturalize overseas Chinese,
requesting the establishment of a nationality law.
It was sent to the Ministers for Revising Laws to confer with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
taxes on salt fields in Rénhe and other places in Zhèjiāng were remitted.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the principle of implementing preparatory constitutional government was announced,
and an imperial edict stated:
"The national policy has been settled,
and its achievement is certain.
All officials, great and small, inside and outside the government,
must collectively understand this intention
and assist in the new plans.
Censors and other officials
should also frankly express
the gains, losses, advantages, and disadvantages of all new policies."
On the *dīngmǎo* day,

Xī Yàn, Qiáo Shùnán, Liú Tíngchēn, Wú Shìjiàn, Zhōu Zìqí, Láo Nǎixuān, Zhào Bǐnglín, and Tán Xuéhéng were ordered to lecture daily, along with Róng Qìng, Lù Rùnxiáng, Zhāng Yīnglín, Táng Jǐngchóng, Bǎo Xī, and Zhū Yìfān.
The lecture notes were to be reviewed and approved by Sūn Jiānài and Zhāng Zhīdòng.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Bureau for Constitutional Compilation and Investigation submitted statistical tables.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the opium ban was reiterated.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
silver and grain taxes were remitted for disaster-stricken villages in Xuānwēi Prefecture, Yúnnán.
In the intercalary second month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
an imperial edict strictly enforced accountability for preparatory constitutional government,
warning ministers and provincial officials against procrastination and perfunctory action,
and abandoning their responsibilities.
Regarding mourning rituals, which are crucial to human relations,
an imperial edict stated that henceforth, all Manchu and Han officials,
both inside and outside the capital, who suffered the loss of their parents, should leave their posts to complete their mourning.
Former Grand Academician of the Grand Secretariat Chén Bǎochēn was appointed Director-General of the Academy of Rites.

Taxes on wasteland, fields, and ponds, as well as head and transport taxes in silver and grain, were remitted for thirty-two prefectures and counties, including Rénhe in Zhèjiāng, and the two garrisons of Hángzhōu and Yánzhōu, and the three garrisons of Hángzhōu, Qúzhōu, and Yánzhōu.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Grand Councillor and Grand Academician Nà Tóng mourned his mother.
An imperial decree ordered him to set aside his grief and continue in office,
and after 100 days of mourning, he would assume the acting appointment,
continuing his official duties.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
judicial officers were appointed in Kùlún.
The wellhead tax on new mines in Guǎngdōng was remitted.
Generous condolences were granted to Chén Chāngyǒng, the deceased commander of the Artillery Battalion in Ānhuī.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Regent, supervising the state, held an audience for the princes, dukes, and all officials in the Wénhuà Hall.
A new Consul-General was established in Hǎishēnwǎi (Vladivostok).
Stamp duty taxes from the Ministry of Finance were promulgated.
Financial supervisors were established for the directly governed provinces.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,

the posts of Deputy General, Brigade General, Mobile Corps Commander, Company Commander, and Central Army Garrison Commander in Huángzhōu, Jīngmén, Yúnwáng, Yíchāng, Shīnán, and Dé’ān in Húběi were abolished.
Minister Plenipotentiary Wǔ Tíngfāng concluded an arbitration treaty with the United States.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the Chónglíng Mausoleum was repaired.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Law and Political Science School for Imperial Relatives was established,
and Bèilè Yùlǎng was ordered to be its Director-General.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Lǐ Shēngcháo, a Hui Muslim from Gùyuán Prefecture, Gānsù, who was over one hundred years old, was commended and rewarded
with an imperial plaque
inscribed with calligraphy.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
due to the great deceased being in mourning,
the annual imperial audience for the Khans, Princes, Bèilè, Bèizi, Dukes, Táijí, Tǎbùnáng, and others of the Jasaq Mongols,
as well as the Hutuktu Lamas,
Tibetan Khenpo,
Chámǔduō Pákèbālā,
the Begs of the Hui Muslims,
Tǔsī, Tǔshè,
and Gurkhas was suspended, and they were not to come to the capital.
In the third month, on the *xīnhài* day, Police Circuit Intendants and Industrial Circuit Intendants were added in Zhèjiāng.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Lǐ Hènián, the former Governor of Hénán, was reinstated to his original post.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
by imperial decree of the Empress Dowager,
the Ministry of Finance's annual payment of 280,000 taels of silver for special holiday funds
was suspended from now on.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the coffin of Emperor Dézōng Jǐng was moved to the Liánggézhuāng temporary palace in the Western Mausoleums.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the China Merchants Steam Navigation Company was placed under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Posts and Communications.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Police Circuit Intendant of Fèngtiān was again abolished.
Military Preparedness Intendants were added in Táochāng and other places,
and Military Preparedness Intendants with divided patrol duties were added in Línchánghǎi and other places.
The Fèngjǐn Shānhǎiguān Circuit Intendant was renamed the Jǐnxīn and other places Military Preparedness Intendant, concurrently serving as Shānhǎiguān Superintendent,
and the Eastern Border Circuit Intendant was renamed the Xīngfèng and other places Military Preparedness Intendant.
Xīngjīng Department was upgraded to Xīngjīng Prefecture.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
five-tenths of this year's regular taxes were remitted for the five departments and counties of Wǎnpíng, Liángxiāng, Zhuōzhōu, Fángshān, and Láishuǐ, through which the imperial coffin passed,
and seven-tenths for Yìzhōu,
and the people were awarded one *qián* of silver per *mǔ* for flattened wheat fields.
On the *jǐsì* day,

an imperial edict reinstated Lì Shān, former Minister of Revenue, Xú Yòngyí, Minister of War, Xǔ Jǐngchéng, Vice Minister of Personnel, Lián Yuán, Grand Academician of the Grand Secretariat, and Yuán Chǎng, Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, to their original posts,
and conferred posthumous titles.
Wú Lùzhēn, Associate General of the Army, was ordered to supervise border affairs in Jílín.
The Yànpíng Circuit Intendant of Shānxī was abolished.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Yáng Shū, former Left Councillor of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to Belgium.
Yàdōng, Jiāngzī, and Gádàkè were opened as treaty ports with customs houses.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Huīnán Direct-ruled Department was added in Fèngtiān.
On the *wùyín* day,
Zhào Érsùn, Governor-General of Sìchuān, and Zhào Érfēng, Resident Minister in Tibet, were praised for vigorously promoting education,
and the ministry was ordered to give them preferential treatment.
Zhào Érsùn donated his salary to support his clan,
and was awarded an imperial plaque
inscribed with
"Profound Kinship."
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Gēngchén,
due to various nations sending envoys to offer condolences,
Bèizǐ Zàizhèn was ordered to serve as minister to Japan, with the title of Zhènguó Jiāngjūn.
Fǎbù Shàngshū Dài Hóngcí was sent as minister to Russia to express gratitude.
For other nations, resident ministers were ordered to handle the matters.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the Dùzhībù established a Currency System Investigation Bureau
and minted circulating silver coins.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
all outstanding taxes from the fourteenth year of Guāngxù (1888) to the thirty-third year of Guāngxù (1907) in the directly administered provinces were remitted.
On the day Guǐsì,
the Assistant Military Governors (Fùdūtǒng) of Húnchūn, Sānxìng, Nínggǔtǎ, Bódūnnà, and Ālèchǔkā in Jílín were abolished.
The Húnchūn Military Preparation Circuit (Bīngbèidào)
and Sānxìng Military Preparation Circuit were established.
Suīfēn, Yánjí, Wǔcháng, Shuāngchéng, Bīnzhōu, and Línjiāng prefectures were upgraded, reformed, or newly established,
along with the Yītōng Directly Administered Department (Zhílìzhōu),
Yúshù Directly Administered Department (Zhílìtīng),
Bǎoqīng and Suīyuǎn departments,
Húnchūn, Bīnjiāng, and Dōngníng sub-prefectures,
and Fùjǐn, Mùléng, Hélóng, Huàchuān, Línhú, Wāngqīng, and Émù counties.
Subsequently, Shūlán, Āchéng, Bólì, and Ráohé counties were re-established.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Nèigé, Bùyuàn, Hànlín, Kēdào were ordered to convene a meeting regarding the grand ceremony for Dèzōng's ancestral enshrinement.
On the day Yǐwèi,
prayers for rain were offered.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
various districts in Gānsù, including Lánzhōu, Liángzhōu, Gǒngchāng, Niǎnbó, and Huìníng, suffered disasters.
Sixty thousand taels of silver were disbursed from the treasury for relief.
On the day Rènyín,
the Left and Right Councillors (Cānzàn) of Fèngtiān
and the Chéngxüān and Zīyì offices were abolished.
On the day Jiǎchén,
prayers for rain were offered again.
On the day Wùshēn,
the Imperial Edict commanded the Ministers for Opium Prohibition to conduct strict examinations,
allowing no favoritism or perfunctory actions.
For civil and military officials' schools in the outer provinces,
Governors-general (Dū), Governors (Fǔ), Generals (Jiāngjūn), and Military Governors (Dūtǒng) were held responsible for strict investigation and prohibition.
On the first day of the fifth month, Jǐyǒu,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Xīnhài,
one hundred and twenty students who had graduated from overseas studies, including the Jinshì Huáng Dézhāng, were given the palace examination,
and granted various official positions.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Yú Shìméi stated
that the regulations for provincial Consultative Councils (Zīyìjú) were not consistent with the local assembly system of Prussia.
This matter was remitted to the Xiànzhèng Biānchá Guǎn for proper deliberation.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Chén Qǐtài died.
Ruìchéng was appointed Governor of Jiāngsū.

The request by the gentry of Zhèjiāng to establish a shrine at Xīhú in Zhèjiāng for the late Minister of War (Bīngbù Shàngshū) Xú Yòngyí, the Right Vice-Minister of Personnel (Lìbù Yòushìláng) Xǔ Jǐngchéng, and the Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices (Tàicháng Sìqīng) Yuán Chǎng was granted.
On the day Jiǎyín,
prayers for rain were offered again.
The Governor-general of Shǎnxī and Gānsù, Shēng Yǔn, was dismissed after presenting a memorial on the pros and cons of constitutionalism.
Chánggēng was appointed to replace him.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Guǎngfú was appointed acting General of Yīlí.
On the day Dīngsì,
Lián Yù and Wēn Zōngyáo submitted a memorial outlining matters for training troops and establishing schools in Xīzàng.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Shìxù was appointed acting Associate Minister (Huìbàn Dàchén) of the Wàiwù Bù.
Yáng Shìxiáng died.
Duānfāng was appointed Governor-general of Zhílì and concurrently Minister for Commercial Affairs (Bànlǐ Tōngshāng Shìwù Dàchén).
Zhāng Rénjùn was appointed Governor-general of Liǎngjiāng and concurrently Minister for Commercial Affairs.
Sūn Bǎoqí was appointed acting Governor of Shāndōng.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
as the Zhà Yā area had previously belonged to Sìchuān,
it was ordered to be placed under the jurisdiction of the Minister for Border Affairs.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Nónggōngshāng Bù was ordered to urge the provinces to vigorously promote policies related to agriculture, forestry, and industry.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
prayers for rain were offered again.
On this day, it rained.
On the day Wùchén,
Wēng Tónghé, former Associate Grand Secretary (Xiéyì Dàxuéshì) and Minister of Revenue (Hùbù Shàngshū), was reinstated to his original offices.
On the day Jǐsì,
Táng Shàoyí was removed as Governor of Fèngtiān
and appointed to await appointment as a Vice-Minister (Shìláng).
On the day Xīnwèi,
the Yóuméi Xuéwù Chù (Bureau for Educational Affairs for Students in America) was established.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the military camp system in Hénán Province was reorganized.
On the day Jiǎxū,
relief was provided for the earthquake disaster in Nánníngzhōu, Yúnnán.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
an imperial edict established the Jūnzī Chù (Military Advisory Bureau),
with Bèilè Yùlǎng as its head.
The Regent (Shèzhèng Wáng) was appointed acting Grand Marshal (Dàyuánshuài) of the Army and Navy.
Bèilè Zàixún and Admiral Sà Zhènbīng were both appointed Ministers for Naval Preparations (Chóubàn Hǎijūn Dàchén).
Relief was provided for the flood disaster in Lǐzhōu, Húnán.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Bèilè Zàitāo was ordered to manage the affairs of the Jūnzī Chù.
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
Qìng Qīnwáng Yìkuāng was relieved of the responsibility of managing the Lùjūn Bù (Ministry of the Army).
Relief was provided for the flood disaster in Hányáng and other prefectures in Húběi.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Yīlí began to organize and train an army.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Chéng Déquán was appointed Governor of Fèngtiān.
Chén Zhāocháng was appointed Governor of Jílín.
Zhōu Shùmó was appointed Governor of Hēilóngjiāng.
On the day Dīnghài,
canals were opened in Gāolán County, Xīnchéng, and Xīgùchéng in Gānsù,
using labor in place of relief.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
relief was provided for earthquake disasters in Mílè County, Bì'ěr, and other places in Yúnnán.
Land taxes for the previous year were remitted for disaster-stricken fields in Tàihé County, Yúnnán.
On the day Gēngyín,
the late Máo Hóngbīn, who had been demoted from Governor-general of Liǎngguǎng, was reinstated to his original office.

A posthumous award was granted to the late Yuè Chāng, Sub-Prefect (Tōngpàn) of Chángzhōu Prefecture, Jiāngsū, who died heroically resisting bandits, and a shrine was ordered to be built for him in Chángzhōu Prefecture.
Relief was provided for the flood disaster in Āndōng, Fèngtiān.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Lǚ Hǎihuán was dismissed.
Xú Shìchāng was appointed Minister-in-charge of the Jīnpǔ Railway,
and Shěn Yúnpèi was appointed his deputy.
The Jǐnxīn Circuit (Dào) of Fèngtiān was renamed Jǐnxīn Yíngkǒu and Other Places Circuit for Patrols and Military Preparedness (Fēnxún Bīngbèidào).
On the day Yǐwèi,
Jílín suffered a major flood.
Sixty thousand taels of silver were disbursed from the treasury for relief.
Relief was provided for flood disasters in Lǐzhōu, Ānxiāng, Chángdé, Yuèzhōu, and other departments, prefectures, and counties in Húnán.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Jīngzhōu and Hányáng prefectures in Húběi suffered floods.
Sixty thousand taels of silver were disbursed from the treasury,
and another two hundred thousand taels were ordered to be raised for urgent relief.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the special rent on land occupied for new army barracks in Rèhé was abolished.
On the day Rènyín,
relief was provided for flood disasters in Qiántáng and eleven other counties in Zhèjiāng.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Zhāng Xūn was dismissed as Chief of Staff (Yìzhǎng) of the East Three Provinces Mobile Headquarters,
and ordered to assume the post of Admiral (Tídū) in Gānsù.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Wǔ Tíngfāng and Qián Xún were both ordered to come to the capital.
Zhāng Yīntáng, acting Right Vice-Minister (Yòuchéng) of the Wàiwù Bù, was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary (Chūshǐ Dàchén) to the four nations of America, Mexico, Peru, and Cuba.
Wú Zōnglián, acting Right Councillor (Yòucānyì) of the Wàiwù Bù, was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to Italy.
Zhào Ěrxùn submitted a memorial on pacifying the qiǎnshuǐ luǒyí in Níngyuǎn, Sìchuān.
On the day Yǐsì,
silver for cotton clothing was awarded to the poor people of the capital,
which later became a regular practice.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Lǐ Zhǔn was appointed Admiral of the Guǎngdōng Navy.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day, Wùshēn,

various brigades (xié) and battalions (yíng) in Húnán, including Chángdé, Bǎoqìng, Yǒngshùn, Yuèzhōu, Lǐzhōu, Línwǔ, Guìyáng, Xuānfèng, Yǒngzhōu, Wǔgāng, Yuánzhōu, Suījìng, Chénzhōu, and Lǐngdōng, were abolished,

along with officials such as Brigade-General (Fùjiàng), Colonel (Cānjīang), Major (Yóujī), Captain (Dūsī), and Lieutenant (Shǒubèi) of the Provincial Governor's (Fǔbiāo) and Admiral's (Tíbiāo) headquarters.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Liáohé River was dredged.
On the day Bǐngchén,
the Ministers for Naval Preparations presented diagrams and explanations for proposed naval officer flag styles and uniforms.
The managers of the Jūnzī Chù presented proposed provisional regulations for the Jūnzī Chù.
Relief was provided for flood disasters in Píngxiāng and other counties in Jiāngxī.
On the day Dīngsì,
the autumn executions were suspended.
The Fǎbù submitted supplementary revised trial regulations for higher-level courts and proposed a general outline for the organization of courts in the outer provinces.
The Lóngwáng Dòng coal and iron mine in Jiāngběi Sub-prefecture, Chóngqìng, Sìchuān, was opened.
On the day Wùwǔ,
taxes on disaster-stricken fields and silver/rice in Lǔdiàn and Zhènxíong departments in Yúnnán were remitted.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the Nányáng was preparing to establish an Industrial Promotion Exhibition (Quànyè Huì).
Zhāng Rénjùn, Minister of the Nányáng and Governor-general of Liǎngjiāng, was appointed President.
Provinces were ordered to prepare associations,
and exhibition products were exempt from taxes and duties.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the coffin of Dèzōng Jǐng Huángdì was moved to the imperial tomb.
Rent for banner land (qízū) in all passing prefectures and counties was remitted,
and silver for seeds was awarded.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Food and Salt Circuit (Liángyándào) of Hénán was abolished.
The Patrol Police (Xúnjǐng) and Industrial Promotion (Quànyè) circuits were newly established.
On the day Wùchén,
the Imperial Edict ordered the directly administered provinces to rectify stored grain.
A posthumous award was granted to Yǒnglín, a ninth-rank park deputy (Bāpǐn Yuànfù) who died after submitting a memorial regarding the Yíhé Yuán.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
additional consuls were established for various islands in the Nányáng.
On the day Rénshēn,
the Xuébù established a library in the capital.
Yáo Rénshān, a bandit from the Hóngjiāng Society, was executed.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
grain prices were stabilized in Húběi.
On the *dīngchǒu* day of the eighth month, the first day of the lunar month,
Lǐ Jiājū (李家駒), a minister for investigating constitutional government, submitted works such as *Kǎo Rìběn Sīfǎ Zhìdù* (考日本司法制度, "An Examination of the Japanese Judicial System").
On the *xīnsì* day,
the Mò'ěrgēn (墨爾根), Nènjiāng (嫩江), and Gānhé (甘河) coal mines in Hēilóngjiāng (黑龍江) were opened.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Jílín Bīnjiāng Dào (吉林濱江道) was renamed Xīběi Lù Dào (西北路道),
Xīlù Dào (西路道) was renamed Xīnán Lù Dào (西南路道),
and these, along with the previously established Dōngběi Lù Dào (東北路道) and Dōngnán Lù Dào (東南路道), were all named Fēnxún Bīngbèi Dào (分巡兵備道).
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
relief was provided for a wind disaster in Fúzhōu (福州), Fújiàn (福建),
and for floods in Kālǔ (開魯) and Píngquán (平泉) prefectures and counties in Rèhé (熱河).
On the *bǐngxū* day,
as the Zàngfān (藏番) were restless,
Zhào Ěrfēng (趙爾豐) suppressed them.
Lǐ Jiājū (李家駒), a probationary Grand Secretary (內閣學士), was appointed to assist in the affairs of the Zīzhèngyuàn (資政院).
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the Jīng-Zhāng (京張) Railway was completed.
Taxes on silver and grain were exempted for the dredging of rivers and the reclamation of abandoned civilian furnaces and fields in Zhènhǎi (鎮海) county, Zhèjiāng (浙江).
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Píngjiāng (平江) gold mine in Húnán (湖南) was opened,
along with the Xīnhuà (新化) antimony mine,
and the Chángníng (常寧) lead mine.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Chén Hóngwěi (陳鴻偉), a *jǔrén* (舉人) from Huángpí (黃陂) county, Húběi (湖北), who sacrificed his life to save his father, was commended for his filial piety,
and his deeds were ordered to be recorded in the Imperial Historiography Institute (史館).
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Grand Secretaries Sūn Jiānài (孫家鼐) and Zhāng Zhīdòng (張之洞) both requested retirement due to illness.
An imperial edict was issued to console and retain them.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Ministry of Agriculture, Industry, and Commerce (農工商部) memorialized to trial the issuance of "enrichment lottery public bonds."
On the *jǐhài* day,
Grand Secretary Zhāng Zhīdòng (張之洞) passed away;
he was posthumously granted the title of Grand Guardian (太保)
and entered into the Shrine of Worthies (賢良祠).
Dài Hóngcí (戴鴻慈) was ordered to serve and gain experience among the Grand Councillors (軍機大臣).
Tíngjié (廷杰) was appointed Minister of Justice (法部尚書),
and Gě Bǎohuá (葛寶華) was appointed Minister of Rites (禮部尚書).
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Chéngxūn (誠勳) was transferred to be the Military Governor (都統) of Rèhé (熱河),
and Pǔliáng (溥良) was made Military Governor of Cháhā'ěr (察哈爾).
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
factories were opened in the capital to cook porridge to relieve the poor,
distributing over 2,500 *shí* (石) of grain;
those already residing in converted charitable institutions and vocational training centers (教養局、習藝所) still received provisions,
and this was made a permanent practice annually.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the ministers for revising laws submitted the compiled and revised existing penal code,
which was sent to the Bureau for Constitutional Review (憲政編查館) for deliberation.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
an imperial edict proclaimed the first day of the ninth month as the date for provincial assembly members to convene and open discussions,
with special admonitions emphasized.
The edict stated:
"The members of the Advisory Councils (諮議局) should earnestly point out local advantages and disadvantages
and plan wisely.
They should not harbor selfish motives to hinder public welfare,
nor act on impulse to disrupt established rules,
nor be overly confident in their views, leading to overly aggressive discussions,
nor define their powers ambiguously, which might lead to encroachment.
All Governors-General (督撫) should also humbly accept [their proposals],
deliberate and implement them,
so that superiors and subordinates are of one mind,
gradually achieving ideal governance.
Furthermore, after the councils are opened,
all Governors-General should especially adhere to the regulations
and rigorously supervise,
ensuring that resolutions do not in any way exceed their authority
or violate laws.
By working together with loyalty and patriotism
to achieve prosperity and strength,
We have great hopes."
In this month,
Zài Xún (載洵) and Sà Zhènbīng (薩鎮冰) traveled abroad to investigate naval affairs.
On the *dīngwèi* day of the ninth month, the first day of the lunar month,
noble titles were first created and bestowed.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the Hague Peace Convention (和蘭保和會條約) was concluded,
and separate approvals and signatures were made.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Zhào Ěrsùn (趙爾巽) was ordered to concurrently act as the General of Chéngdū (成都).
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Grand Secretariat (內閣) jointly memorialized on the grand ceremony for Dèzōng's (德宗) enshrinement in the ancestral temple.
An imperial edict declared that Emperor Mùzōng Yì (穆宗毅皇帝) and Emperor Dèzōng Jǐng (德宗景皇帝) should both be temples not to be moved for a hundred generations,
and should be arranged according to *zhāomù* (昭穆) on the left and right,
not distinguishing between superior and inferior based on *zhāomù*.
It was decided that Dèzōng (德宗) would be enshrined in the middle hall of the Tàimiào (太廟),
in the fifth room, second pillar to the west, in the *mù* (穆) position.
In the front hall, after Emperor Wénzōng Xiǎn (文宗顯皇帝),
a *mù* (穆) position facing east and sitting west would be respectfully arranged.
The Fèngxiān Diàn (奉先殿) would follow this precedent.
This was to be a permanent system.
On the *dīngsì* day,
students graduating from the Army Noblemen's School (陸軍貴冑學堂), such as Zǐjué Chéngquán (子爵成全), were awarded positions as imperial guards,
and others received promotions accordingly.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the Zīzhèngyuàn (資政院) submitted the election regulations.
On the *rénxū* day,
German travelers in Yúnnán (雲南) were harmed by the Nù Yí (怒夷),
who were then captured and executed.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Hé River (豫河) was calm.
Relief was provided for floods in Guǎngdōng (廣東) province's capital and various Nánhǎi (南海) counties.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Xīlínguǒlè (錫林果勒) League, including Ābā (阿巴), Ābāhānà'ěr (阿巴哈那爾), Hàoqítè (浩齊特), and Wūzhūmùqìn (烏珠穆沁), suffered disasters,
and 30,000 *liǎng* (兩) of treasury silver were disbursed for relief.
Relief was provided for floods in Zhènxíong (鎮雄) and other prefectures and counties in Yúnnán (雲南).
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Yellow River (黃河) was calm.
Lù Chuánlín (鹿傳霖) was appointed Grand Academician of the Tǐrén Gé (體仁閣),
and Lù Rùnxiáng (陸潤庠), Minister of Personnel (吏部尚書), was appointed Associate Grand Academician (協辦大學士).
Students who graduated from study abroad, such as Xiàng Xiāng (項驤), were awarded the *jǔrén* (舉人) degree.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the rank of Reader (侍講學士) of the Hanlin Academy (翰林院) was raised to 正四品 (Orthodox Fourth Rank),
Lecturers (侍讀) and Readers (侍講) to 從四品 (Auxiliary Fourth Rank),
Drafting Secretaries (撰文秘書郎) and Compilers (修撰) to 正五品 (Orthodox Fifth Rank),
and Revisers (編修) and Reviewers (檢討) to 從五品 (Auxiliary Fifth Rank).
Plaques were bestowed for schools established by overseas Chinese in Java.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Southern River (南河) was calm.
In this month,
the Korean Ān Zhònggēn (安重根) assassinated Itō Hirobumi (伊藤博文), the former Resident-General of Korea, in Hā'ěrbīn (哈爾濱).
On the *dīngchǒu* day of the tenth month, the first day of winter and the lunar month,
the Yí (夷) bandits of Èrbǎnfáng (二板房) on the border of Xīchāng (西昌) and Huìlǐ (會理) in Sìchuān (四川) caused unrest,
and the government troops suppressed them.
Mǎ Liàng (馬亮), the General of Chéngdū (成都), passed away.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Empress Xiàqīn Xiǎnpèihòu (孝欽顯皇后) was interred in the Pútuóyù Dìngdōnglíng (菩陀峪定東陵);
local fixed taxes for prefectures and counties through which the coffin passed were exempted,
and silver was granted as compensation for destroyed wheat fields and seeds.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the spirit tablet of Empress Xiàqīn Xiǎnpèihòu (孝欽顯皇后) was enshrined in the Tàimiào (太廟),
and an edict was issued to the empire the next day.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
it was decided that the General of Chéngdū (成都) should not have jurisdiction over Sōngpān (松潘) and Jiànchāng (建昌).
Yùkūn (玉崑) was appointed General of Chéngdū (成都).
On the *dīnghài* day,
Duānfāng (端方), Governor-General of Zhílì (直隸), was stripped of his office for violating regulations.
Chén Kuílong (陳夔龍) was transferred to be Governor-General of Zhílì (直隸)
and concurrently managed the affairs of the Minister of Commerce (通商事務大臣);
Ruìchěng (瑞澂) was acting Governor-General of Húguǎng (湖廣);
Bǎofēn (寶棻) was Governor of Jiāngsū (江蘇).
Sūn Bǎoqí (孫寶琦) was appointed Governor of Shāndōng (山東),
and Dīng Bǎoquán (丁寶銓) was appointed Governor of Shānxī (山西).
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
an edict concerning the first and second stages of constitutional preparations stated that
all officials, both central and local, should wholeheartedly bear their responsibilities,
and also ordered the Bureau for Constitutional Review (憲政編查館) to audit the reported achievements;
those who procrastinated, were perfunctory, or delayed in their actions
would be investigated and reported.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Bureau for Constitutional Review (憲政編查館) submitted regulations for standardizing the official system of provincial judicial commissioners (提法使).
The Hālāgénángwéi (哈拉格囊圍) gold mine in Kùlún (庫倫) was opened.
Yánzhǐ (延祉) was dismissed due to illness,
and Sānduō (三多) was ordered to act as Minister for Kùlún (庫倫) Affairs.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Liúyáng (溧陽), Jīntán (金壇), Jīngxī (荊溪), Yíxīng (宜興), Dāntú (丹徒), Dānyáng (丹陽), Zhènzé (震澤) and other counties in Jiāngsū (江蘇) suffered disasters,
and 30,000 *liǎng* (兩) of treasury silver were disbursed for relief.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Ministry of Civil Affairs (民政部) memorialized,
citing precedents and requesting awards of grain and silver;
the actual required amounts for various factories and institutions were determined
for housing the poor,
and an imperial edict approved its implementation.
Relief was provided for floods in Dàyáo (大姚), Wénshān (文山) and other counties in Yúnnán (雲南).
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Grand Secretary Sūn Jiānài (孫家鼐) passed away;
he was posthumously granted the title of Grand Tutor (太傅),
entered into the Shrine of Worthies (賢良祠),
and awarded silver for funeral expenses.
An imperial edict declared Wāng Zōngyí (汪宗沂), the deceased fifth-rank titular Prefect of Shānxī (山西), a forthwith-appointed county magistrate (即用知縣), to be outstanding in classical studies,
and his deeds were ordered to be recorded in the Imperial Historiography Institute (史館).
One month's money and provisions were awarded to unemployed imperial clan members and *juéluó* (覺羅) who received stipends,
and half a month's money and provisions to orphans and widows,
and half a month's money and provisions to officers and soldiers of the Eight Banners (八旗), Green Standard (綠營), and various infantry battalions,
which was made a permanent practice annually.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
taxes on silver and grain for flooded fields in Yuánjiāng (元江) prefecture, Yúnnán (雲南), were exempted.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the Yellow River (黃河) in Dōngmíng (東明) was calm.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
rewards for capturing bandits (*huāhóng*, 花紅) in Guǎngdōng (廣東) were abolished;
henceforth, any civil or military official who again accepted *huāhóng* would be treated as having committed embezzlement.
Lǐ Duānfēn (李端棻), former Minister of Rites (禮部尚書), was reinstated to his original post.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the pearl tribute from Jílín (吉林) was suspended for this year.
On the *yǐsì* day,
gentry from Shùntiān (順天) requested the establishment of shrines for the deceased Minister of Revenue (戶部尚書) Lìshān (立山) and Grand Secretary (內閣學士) Liányuán (聯元),
which was granted.
In the eleventh month, on the day Wùshēn,
the quota of land taxes and banner rents was remitted for eleven prefectures and counties, including Wǔqīng in Zhílì.
The quota of land taxes for the three prefectures and counties of Kāizhōu, Dōngmíng, and Chángyuán was also remitted.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
His Majesty bestowed the posthumous title of Empress Dowager on the Empress Dowager, who was concurrently honored as his mother, naming her Lóngyù Huáng Tàihòu.
The imperial edict was promulgated throughout the empire the next day.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Ministry of Civil Affairs submitted the Regulations for Self-Government Elections in Prefectures, Departments, Sub-prefectures, and Counties.
On the day Guǐhài,
Zhāng Zhàodòng, the former Governor of Fújiàn, was reinstated to his original office.
Twenty border guard posts (kǎlún) were established along the Àihuī border in Hēilóngjiāng,
extending from the É'ěrgǔnà River to the mouth of the Xùn River.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
a Minister for Salt Administration (Dūbàn Yánzhèng Dàchén) was appointed,
with Zài Zé holding the position.
The Governors-General and Governors of the salt-producing provinces were made Associate Ministers for Salt Administration (Huìbàn Yánzhèng Dàchén),
and the Governors-General and Governors of the salt-selling provinces all held concurrent titles.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Lù Rùnxiáng was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tǐrén Gét,
and Dài Hóngcí was appointed Associate Grand Secretary as a Minister (Shàngshū).
On the day Xīnwèi,
Bèilè Yùlǎng was appointed Commander of the Gendarmerie (Bùjūn Tǒnglǐng).
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the Censorate (Dūcháyuan) submitted the Rules for Mutual Election.
On the day Yǐhài,
the Ministry of Education (Xuébù) submitted the Regulations for Female Students' Attire and Colors.
The late candidate for Circuit Prefect (Tóngzhī) and Sub-prefectural Magistrate (Zhīzhōu) of Zhílì, Huà Héngfāng, a specialist in discontinued studies,
along with his late younger brother Shìfāng, a former Sub-prefectural Judge (Zhōupàn) of Zhílì,
and the late Xú Shòu, who held a second-rank enfeoffment, were all ordered to be enshrined in the Imperial Historiography Institute (Shǐguǎn).
In the twelfth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
an edict was issued requesting frank advice.
On the day Xīnsì,
two new counties, Āntú and Fǔsōng, were added in Fèngtiān.
On the day Rénwǔ,
those who had studied abroad, such as Zhān Tiānyòu, were awarded the degrees of Jinshì in engineering, liberal arts, and law,
and Jǔrén in engineering and physical sciences.
On the day Guǐwèi,
taxes in cash and grain for the current year were remitted for eighty-nine prefectures and counties, including Qīngchéng in Shāndōng, and for the salt fields of the military garrisons (wèisuǒ).
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the spirit tablet of Dékzōng Jǐng Huángdì was enshrined in the Fèngxiān Diàn.
Rice and cloth were awarded to Zhāng Liúshì, a common woman from Zhàichéng County, Hénán, and Tián Lìshì, a common woman from Tōngxǔ County, both of whom had given birth to triplets.
Relief was provided to thirteen prefectures and counties, including Fóshān in Guǎngdōng, which suffered from disaster.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the Director of the Imperial Academy of Medicine (Tàiyīyuàn Yuànshǐ) was designated as a fourth-rank official.
On the day Wùzǐ,
records were made of the descendants of meritorious officials who had pacified the Fà, Niǎn, and Huí rebels during the Xiánfēng and Tóngzhì reigns,
and official ranks were granted accordingly.
Rent was exempted for the land occupied by the military barracks of Húnchūn from the banner households.
On the day Gēngyín,
Zhào Érfēng reported that the Tǔsī Duōgé Shēngjí of Dégé in Sìchuān had surrendered land,
and a system of appointed officials was implemented.
The Tǔshè Dūsī were granted hereditary succession.
On the day Rénchén,
Qìng Qīnwáng Yìkuāng was relieved of the duty of managing the Army Noblemen's Academy (Lùjūn Guìzhòu Xuétáng),
and Bèilè Zài Rùn replaced him.
On the day Guǐsì,
Lónghuà County was added in Rèhé.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the Bureau for Constitutional Reform (Xiànzhèng Biānchá Guǎn) submitted the Anti-Opium Regulations,
which were promulgated.
The late Chén Bǎozhēn, former Governor of Húnán, was reinstated to his original office.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the Bureau for Constitutional Reform submitted articles prohibiting the buying and selling of people.
On the day Wùxū,
the Ministry of Justice (Fǎbù) submitted the Regulations for the Discipline of Judges.
On the day Jǐhài,
the Bureau for Constitutional Reform submitted the Regulations for Self-Government Elections in the Capital (Jīngshī).
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the Left and Right Court Judges (Zuǒ Yòu Yuànpàn) of the Imperial Academy of Medicine were promoted to fifth rank.
On the day Rényín,
the Bureau for Constitutional Reform submitted the Regulations for Local Self-Government in Prefectures, Departments, Sub-prefectures, and Counties,
and the Regulations for the Election of Council Members for Prefectural, Departmental, and Sub-prefectural Councils.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Bureau for Constitutional Reform submitted the Organizational Law for Courts,
along with provisional regulations for the examination and appointment of judges, the division of judicial districts, and the jurisdiction of cases for elementary and local courts.
In the second year, in spring, the first month, on the day Bǐngwǔ, which was the first day of the month (shuò),
court congratulations were not received.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
the New Army in Guǎngzhōu rebelled,
and the trained army suppressed them.
On the day Xīnhài,
an edict stated that due to the unrest among the people,
the proliferation of factions and societies,
their infiltration into military camps,
and their instigation and incitement,

the Bureau of Military Counsel (Jūnzī Chù), the Ministry of the Army (Lùjūnbù), the Northern and Southern Ministers of the Beiyang Army (Nánběi Yáng Dàchén), and all new and old armies were ordered to conduct strict investigations.
Military personnel, in particular, were to emphasize obedience to their superior officers' commands.
Any gatherings for meetings or speeches
were to be strictly investigated and prohibited.
Dàtōng County in Jílín was relocated to the south bank of the Sōnghuā River
and renamed Fāngzhèng County.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Wáng Zhànkuí and other revolutionaries in Guǎngdōng were executed.
On the day Dīngsì,
the Dalai Lama, fearing the arrival of Sìchuān troops,
fled.
An edict instructed Lián Yù and others to still dispatch officials to escort him back to Tibet.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
an edict stripped Āwàng Luóbùcáng Tǔbùdān Jiǎcuò Jìzhài Wāngqǔ Quèlèlángjié Dalai Lama of his title.
The Salt Administration Office submitted the Provisional Regulations for the Minister for Salt Administration.
On the day Guǐhài,
Associate Grand Secretary Dài Hóngcí passed away.
He was posthumously granted the title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent (Tàizǐ Shàobǎo)
and awarded silver for funeral expenses.
Lǚ Hǎihuán and others submitted the Regulations for the Chinese Red Cross Society,
and Shèng Xuānhuái was appointed its president.
Censor Jiāng Chūnlín was dismissed and sent back to his original yamen for criticizing Qìng Qīnwáng Yìkuāng for harming the nation.
Xú Shìchāng, Minister of the Ministry of Posts and Communications (Yóuchuánbù), was appointed Associate Grand Secretary,
and Wú Yùshēng, Grand Academician of the Grand Secretariat (Nèigé Xuéshì), was assigned to learn and assist in the Grand Council (Jūnjī Dàchén).
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Bèilè Dài Tāo, who managed the Bureau of Military Counsel, requested permission to visit Japan, America, Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Austria, and Russia to inspect their armies.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Britain held the International Congress on Penal Law Reform.
The Ministry of Justice requested permission to send Public Prosecutor Xú Qiān to attend.
On the day Jiǎxū,
an edict stated:
"In preparing for a constitutional government,
old prejudices should be eliminated,
and all differences should be resolved.
From now on, all Manchu and Han civil and military officials, when submitting memorials,
shall uniformly address themselves as 'Your servant' (Chén),
to demonstrate uniformity and promote harmony."
In the second month, on the day Yǐhài, which was the first day of the month,
Lián Yù requested that the new Gélèdān Chíbā Luóbùcáng Dānbā act as an agent for the affairs of former Tibet.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
foreign merchants were prohibited from purchasing and transporting rice from Húnán.
On the day Xīnsì,
Tiě Liáng was relieved of his duties due to illness.
Yìn Chāng was appointed Minister of the Ministry of the Army,
and Liáng Dūnyàn was appointed Associate Minister of the Tax Office (Shuìwùchù).
Arrears from the first year of Xuāntǒng were remitted for the four salt fields of Rén hé, Hǎishā, Bàoláng, and Lúlì in Zhèjiāng, and the two desolate salt pans of Héngpǔ and Pǔdōng in Jiāngsū.
On the day Réwǔ,
old debts were remitted for four prefectures and counties, including Yúlín in Shǎnxī,
and for the grain and fodder in the granary of Yúlín Prefecture.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Liáng Chéng, Academician of the Grand Secretariat (Nèigé Shìdú Xuéshì), was appointed Minister to Germany.
On the day Dīnghài,
the Ministry of Civil Affairs submitted a revised Press Law,
which was forwarded to the Bureau for Constitutional Reform for review and memorialization.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
thirty thousand taels of silver were again disbursed from the treasury for disaster relief in Ānhuī.
On the day Rénchén,
arrears from the first year of Xuāntǒng were remitted for Wǔcháng Department and Huàdiàn County in Jílín.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Lián Yù reported that the monks and laypeople of Lālǐ, and the Tibetan soldiers of Gōngbù, had surrendered and assimilated.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Gě Bǎohuá passed away.
Róng Qìng was transferred to be Minister of the Ministry of Rites (Lǐbù Shàngshū),
and Táng Jǐngchóng was appointed Minister of the Ministry of Education.
On the day Jǐhài,
generous pensions were granted to the late Xià Yùxiù, Provincial Commander (Tídū) of Húběi.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the Bureau for Constitutional Reform submitted the Outline of Administration (Xíngzhèng Gāngmù).
The Minister for Naval Affairs (Chóubàn Hǎijūn Dàchén) submitted the names and duties of the various departments.
In the third month, on the day Yǐsì, which was the first day of the month,
Wáng Shìzhēn was relieved of his duties due to illness.
Léi Zhènchūn was appointed acting Provincial Commander of Jiāngběi.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
evil bandits from Wēiníng, Yúnnán, attacked Zhāochéng.
Government troops annihilated them,
and the bandit leader Lǐ Lǎomò was executed.
On the day Xīnhài,
the people of Húnán, suffering from famine, instigated rebellion.
An edict ordered the capture of the ringleaders
and the dispersal of those coerced.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Cén Chūnzhē, Governor of Húnán, was dismissed,
and Yáng Wéndǐng was appointed to temporarily replace him.
Yáng Shìqí was dispatched to the Nányáng to serve as Chief Inspector of the Industrial Exhibition.
On the day Dīngsì,
prayers for rain were held.
On the day Gēngshēn,
it rained.
The late Dīng Rǔchāng, former Admiral of the Navy (Hǎijūn Tídū), was posthumously restored to his original office.
The old system of autumn review and re-trial was abolished.
An edict instructed the Governors-General and Governors of the provinces along the river to stabilize grain prices.
Wú Zhòngxī, Governor of Hénán, was dismissed,
and Bǎo Fēn replaced him.
Chéng Déquán was transferred to be Governor of Jiāngsū.
On the day Réxū,
a temple was ordered to be built in Wúhú County, Ānhuī, for the late Yuán Chàng, former Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices (Tàicháng Sìqīng), who was beloved by the people.
On the day Guǐhài,
the office of Governor of Fèngtiān was abolished.
Guǎng Fú was appointed General of Yīlí.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the revolutionaries Wāng Zhàomíng, Huáng Fùshēng, and Luó Shìxūn conspired to bomb the Regent with explosives.
The plot was discovered,
and they were arrested and imprisoned in the Ministry of Justice.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Pānshì, wife of Kǒng Lìngbǎo from Qūfù, Shāndōng, a virtuous woman who died for her husband, was commended
and ordered to be enshrined in the Imperial Historiography Institute.
In the fourth month of summer, on the *jiǎxū* day,
an imperial edict was issued for the Zīzhèngyuàn to open on the first day of the ninth month of this year.

Eighty-eight members, consisting of imperial clan princes (*wáng*), dukes (*gōng*) with hereditary titles, other imperial clan members (*zōngshì*), *juéluó*, officials from various ministries and departments (*bùyuàn guān*), and scholars (*shuòxué tōngrú*), were specially selected
and summoned to convene in advance.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the Fújiàn Dūliángdào was abolished.
A Xúnjǐngdào and a Quànyèdào were established.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Zài Tāo was appointed Special Envoy Minister
to offer condolences in England.
On the *wùyín* day,

Wú Kuāngshí and six other graduates from study abroad programs were awarded the *gōngkē jìnshì* (engineering *jìnshì*) and *fǎzhèngkē jǔrén* (law and political science *jǔrén*) degrees, with varying ranks.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Xìanzhèng Biānchácháng Xiūdìng Fǎlǜ Dàchén presented the revised current criminal code (*xínglǜ*).
It was ordered to be promulgated.
An imperial edict stated:
"This criminal code
is a preparation for adopting a new legal system.
All judicial yamen, both within and outside the capital,
must diligently study it
and make judgments according to the law.
They must not arbitrarily alter decisions,
lest they cause injustice or unwarranted leniency."
On the *guǐwèi* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"The establishment of the Xúnjǐng and Quànyè Daos in each province
is intended to safeguard public order and
promote industries.
The governors-general and governors (*dūfǔ*) must carefully examine the already appointed personnel.
If they are found incompetent,
or unsuitable for their posts,
they should be reported to the throne for replacement,
without showing favoritism or protecting them."
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Lián Yù requested that a commissioner be appointed in each of the following places in Xīzàng: Qūshuǐ, Hālāwūsū, Jiāngdá, Shānnán, Shuòbānduō, and the thirty-nine tribes.
He also requested the suspension of the two Tibetan factories for manufacturing guns and minting coins.
Qián Xún, the former envoy to Italy, submitted a translated interpretation of the peace treaty.
On the *dīnghài* day,
due to the erratic activities of salt smugglers (*yánxiāo*) and secret society members (*huìfěi*) north of the Jiāng River,
Léi Zhènchūn was ordered to suppress and pacify them.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Dùzhībù submitted regulations for currency exchange.
An imperial edict stated:
"The unit of national currency
is named *yuán*.
For now, silver shall be the standard,
with one *yuán* as the main currency,
weighing seven *qián* and two *fēn* of the *kùpíng* standard.
Additionally, three types of silver coins—five *jiǎo*, two *jiǎo* five *fēn*, and one *jiǎo*—
as well as a five-*fēn* nickel coin,
and four types of copper coins—two *fēn*, one *fēn*, five *lí*, and one *lí*—shall serve as subsidiary currencies.
The *yuán*, *jiǎo*, *fēn*, and *lí*
shall each follow a decimal system,
which is hereby established as a permanent regulation."
Lián Fāng was appointed General of Jīngzhōu.
On the *gēngyín* day,
it was decided to additionally select ten high-taxpaying individuals as councillors.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Wāng Dàxiè, Vice Minister of the Yóuchuánbù, was appointed Envoy Minister to Japan.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Liáng Dūnyàn was relieved due to illness.
Zōu Jiālái was appointed Acting Shàngshū of the Wàiwùbù and concurrent Huìbàn Dàchén.
Rent and reed taxes in Wényìzhōu, Shíshǒuxiàn, Húběi, were remitted.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Cén Chūnqǐng, Governor of Húnán, was dismissed from office.
In the fifth month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
the Xúnjiǎn of Ālāsuǒ, Níngyuǎn, Sìchuān, was promoted to Fǔyí Tōngpàn of Yánbiāntīng.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Chángdé fǔ, Húnán, suffered from floods.
Twenty thousand taels of treasury silver were disbursed for relief.
Lǐ Jīngxī memorialized that Zhènkāng tǔzhōu, under Yǒngchāng fǔ, Yúnnán, should be converted to a regular magistracy,
and Yǒngkāngzhōu be newly established.
Arrears of silver and grain due to drought in Lùliángzhōu, Yúnnán, were remitted.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
flood victims in Hǎizhōu and other places north of the Jiāng River were relieved.
On the *guǐhài* day,

the Dūcháyuàn transmitted a petition from Sūn Hóngyī and other councillors of the Zīyìjú, as well as representatives of the banner garrisons in the direct provinces, requesting the immediate convocation of a national assembly.
An imperial edict reiterated that after nine years of complete preparation,
another decree would be issued to set a date for convening the assembly and proclaiming it.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
rent arrears for tenant farmers in the Miao areas of Húnán were remitted,
as were accumulated grain arrears for *túnzū* (military colony rents) in the seven departments and counties of Fènghuáng, Qiánzhōu, Yǒngsuī, Bǎojìng, Lúxī, Máiyáng, and Gǔzhàngpíng in Húnán.
On the *jǐsì* day,
disaster relief was provided in Húběi.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Héfáng Tóngzhī of Tóngjiāng tīng, Fèngtiān, was abolished.
In the sixth month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
Hēilóngjiāng suffered a disaster.
Twenty thousand taels of treasury silver were disbursed for relief.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Wāng Dàxiè presented various books compiled from his investigation into the British constitutional system.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Bèilè Zài Xún, Minister for Naval Affairs, was appointed Minister of Participation in Government Affairs (*Cānyù Zhèngwù Dàchén*).
On the *rénchén* day,
Hú Wéidé, Vice Minister of the Wàiwùbù, was appointed Assistant Minister for the Tax Office (*Shuìwùchù Bāngbàn Dàchén*).
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"The governors-general and governors (*dūfǔ*) in each province labor diligently in administration
and are eager to raise funds,
but are often negligent in supervising officials (*chálì*).
They do not realize that if local governance (*lìzhì*) is not reformed,
it will burden the people and squander resources,
and disorder will arise from this.
How then can the new policies be implemented?
Therefore, each must carefully select prefects and magistrates (*mùlìng*),
choosing the right person for the locality.
This is the utmost plan for pacifying the region."
On the *wùxū* day,
an imperial edict instructed all ministries, departments, governors-general, and governors to strictly impeach corrupt officials,
and also enjoined imperial relatives, high-ranking officials both within and outside the capital to cultivate integrity and strive for excellence,
and to regulate themselves and lead their subordinates.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Zài Zé and Shòu Xūn, together with Āmù'ěr Língguī and Zài Rùn, were ordered to investigate the Qiánféngyíng and the Hùjūnyíng of the three banners under the Nèiwùfǔ,
and to report on the finalized regulations.
This month,
in Láiyáng, Shāndōng, gentry and commoners were at odds.
The bandit leader Qū Sīwén gathered over ten thousand people,
besieged cities and towns,
and looted and killed government soldiers.
Hǎiyáng also saw unrest due to tax collection.
These disturbances were subsequently pacified.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *jiǎchén* day,
the Fújiàn Dūliángdào was abolished,
and a Quànyèdào was established.
Ruì Xìng was relieved,
and Zhì Ruì was appointed General of Hángzhōu.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Ruì Chéng and Yáng Wéndǐng memorialized that banditry was spreading in Húnán province,
and proposed implementing the *qīngxiāng* (rural pacification) method,
which was approved.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an imperial edict instructed the Nónggōngshāngbù to collaborate with the governors-general and governors to investigate mineral resources
and carefully plan for their development.
On the *gēngxū* day,
an imperial edict urged all governors-general and governors to survey and map official and civilian uncultivated land, as well as climate and soil conditions,
and to promote industrial enterprises,
reporting to the Nónggōngshāngbù for presentation to the throne.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the Nónggōngshāngbù established a factory for manufacturing weights and measures.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Bèilè Zài Tāo memorialized on his investigation of military administration in various countries, stating that
when military personnel commit crimes,
all cases are to be tried and judged by military courts,
not by ordinary tribunals.
It was ordered to be implemented accordingly.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Shì Xù and Wú Yùshēng were relieved as Grand Ministers of the Military Council (*Jūnjī Dàchén*).
Yù Lǎng and Xú Shìchāng were appointed Grand Ministers of the Military Council.
Táng Shàoyí was appointed Acting Shàngshū of the Yóuchuánbù.
Yù Lǎng was relieved of his posts as Commander of the Infantry (*Bùjūn Tǒnglǐng*) and Minister Solely Responsible for Training the Imperial Guards (*Zhuānsī Xùnliàn Jìnwèijūn Dàchén*).
Wū Zhēn was appointed concurrent Acting Commander of the Infantry.
Intercourse Commissioners (*Jiāoshè Shǐ*) were established in each province.
Tián Xīnián, a battalion officer of the Xīnjiāng Army, was executed for instigating a rebellion through unauthorized killing.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Anhuī's Wǎnnán, Nánlíng, Sùzhōu, Língbì, and other areas suffered from floods.
Forty thousand taels of treasury silver were disbursed for relief.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Fǎbù submitted articles for autumn assize (*qiūshěn*).
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Tāng Shòuqían, former Provincial Education Commissioner of Jiāngxī and General Manager of the Zhèjiāng Railway,
was stripped of his office for impeaching Shèng Xuānhuái as the "arch-culprit and instigator" of the Sū-Zhè Railway issue.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
famine relief was provided in Wǎnběi (Northern Anhuī).
Zhōng Ruì was appointed Minister Resident in Kobdo (*Kēbùduō Bànshì Dàchén*).
Lián Kuí was relieved as Governor of Xīnjiāng,
and Hé Yànshēng was appointed in his place.
The Provincial Surveillance Commissioners (*Ànchásǐ*) in each province were renamed Provincial Judicial Commissioners (*Tífǎshǐ*).
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Grand Secretary Lù Chuánlín passed away.
He was posthumously granted the title of Grand Guardian (*Tàibǎo*),
enshrined in the Xiánliángcí,
and awarded silver for his funeral expenses.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Shěn Ruìlín, Councillor of the Wàiwùbù, was appointed Envoy Minister to Austria,
and Liú Yùlín, Right Vice Minister of the Wàiwùbù, was appointed Plenipotentiary for the International Opium Commission in Holland.
On the *wùchén* day,
Húludǎo Port was opened in Fèngtiān.
On the *jǐsì* day,
a Tóngzhī for Nèhé Zhílìtīng was established in Hēilóngjiāng.
This month,
Zài Xún and Sà Zhènbīng again went to the United States and Japan to inspect their navies.
In the eighth month, on the *Jiǎxū* day,
Fèngtiān Zhèndōng County was established.
On the *Yǐhài* day,
Qīngruì was dismissed,
and Tiěliáng was appointed as the Jiāngníng General.
On the *Guǐwèi* day,
Shěn Jiābĕn was ordered to serve as the Vice President of the Zīzhèngyuàn.
On the *Jiǎshēn* day,
Liú Yùlín, Assistant Minister of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to Great Britain.
On the *Dīnghài* day,

the Lǐfānbù memorialized to revise old regulations such as prohibiting people from crossing the border to reclaim land, commoners from marrying Mongolian women, Inner and Outer Mongolia from employing Han clerks and teachers, and official documents from arbitrarily using Chinese characters;
and Mongols from using Chinese characters for names, etc.
It was permitted.
Jiāojué County in Sìchuān was newly established.
On the *Jǐchǒu* day,
Liánfāng was dismissed,
and Fèngshān was appointed as the Jīngzhōu General.
Yìnchāng was ordered to concurrently hold the position of Minister for the training of various divisions in the immediate vicinity of the capital.
On the *Jiǎzǐ* day,
it was ordered that all army divisions in the immediate vicinity of the capital be placed under the jurisdiction of the Lùjūnbù.
The training office for the immediate vicinity of the capital was abolished.
A Salt Commissioner for Fèngtiān was newly established.
The Salt and Tea Intendancy of Sìchuān was reformed into a Salt Commissioner,
and tea affairs were placed under the administration of the Quànyèdào.
On the *Yǐwèi* day,
regarding the embellished reports on the prohibition of opium poppy cultivation,
the Governors-General and Governors of Jílín, Hēilóngjiāng, Hénán, Shānxī, Fújiàn, Guǎngxī, Yúnnán, and Xīnjiāng provinces were referred to the ministry for deliberation,
and an edict was issued to all provinces to strictly and thoroughly enforce the prohibition.
On the *Bǐngwǔ* day,
Xú Shìchāng was granted the title of Grand Secretary of the Tǐrén Gé,
and Lǐ Diànlín, Minister of the Lìbù, was appointed to assist as Grand Secretary.
On the *Dīngyǒu* day,
because Bìrètíbì Bìgáěrmǎshēng Xiězhèrè Zēnggābágádùrè Sāhā, the King of Gorkha, Èrdéwéi, refused to send troops to aid Tibet,
an imperial edict commended him.
On the *Gēngzǐ* day,
relief was provided for the flood disasters in Huá and Wèinán two prefectures and counties in Shǎnxī.
In the ninth month, on the *Xīnchǒu* day, the first day of the lunar month,
the Zīzhèngyuàn held its opening ceremony,
and the Regent, supervised the nation, attended the meeting and delivered an instructional speech.
On the *Rényín* day,

459 graduates from overseas studies, including Wú Nǎichēn, were granted various ranks of *jìnshì* and *jǔrén* in literature, medicine, natural sciences, agriculture, industry, commerce, and law and politics.
On the *Guǐmǎo* day,

grain taxes and fodder for disaster-stricken land in the prefectures and counties of Hé, Jīn, Wèiyuán, Fúqiāng, Āndìng, Huìníng, Nínglíng, Xúnhuà, and Qínjiǔtīng in Gānsù from the previous year were exempted.
On the *Bǐngwǔ* day,
Xúzhōu and other areas north of the river suffered from rain and flood disasters,
and the Dùzhībù was ordered to issue funds for relief.
On the *Yǐsì* day,
Xìnqín, acting General of Suíyuǎn City and Minister for垦务, was dismissed due to illness,
and Kūnxiù was transferred to replace him.
Kuífāng was appointed as the Wūlǐyásūtái General.
On the *Wùshēn* day,
the Dùzhībù was ordered to issue an additional 20,000 taels of silver for disaster relief in northern Ānhuī.
On the *Rénzǐ* day,
Zhāng Rénjùn, due to the critical situation in the Shànghǎi market,
requested to borrow foreign funds for adjustment,
and to transfer 500,000 taels of silver from the treasury.
This was granted.
On the *Guǐchǒu* day,
the Yǒngdìng Hé was peaceful.
Relief was provided for flood disasters in Miánzhú and other prefectures and counties in Sìchuān.
On the *Jiǎyín* day,
the Director-General of Hǎilóng Wéichǎng was abolished.
On the *Bǐngchén* day,
an imperial edict ordered the recommendation of virtuous and upright individuals from the directly governed provinces,
to be strictly selected.
On the *Jǐwèi* day,
the deeds of Wǔxùn, a virtuous beggar from Dángyì, Shāndōng, who accumulated wealth to promote education, were ordered to be recorded in the official archives.
The Prefectural Magistrate of Chángdé Prefecture and the Prefectural Magistrate of Cháng'ān Camp of Bǎoqìng Prefecture in Húnán were abolished.
On the *Guǐhài* day,
an edict stated that reclamation affairs in Suíyuǎn City were of vital importance,
and officials below the rank of border *dào* or *tīng*,
who were involved in reclamation affairs,
should all be subject to the control of the Minister of Reclamation.
On the *Bǐngyín* day,
Yáng Shū was dismissed due to illness,
and Lǐ Guójíe, Assistant Minister of the Nónggōngshāngbù, was appointed Minister Plenipotentiary to Belgium.
Relief was provided for flood disasters in Hēilóngjiāng.
On the *Dīngmǎo* day,
Yuán Shùxūn was dismissed due to illness,
and Zhāng Míngqí was appointed acting Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng.
Shěn Bǐngkūn was appointed Governor of Yúnnán.
On the *Wùchén* day,
the positions of Vice General, Guerrilla Commander, Company Commander, and Garrison Commander in Guìzhōu were abolished.
Arrears of grain taxes and seeds for the people in Dǐhuà and eleven other prefectures and counties in Xīnjiāng were exempted.
In the tenth month, on the *Guǐyǒu* day,
an imperial edict announced the change to open the National Assembly in the fifth year of Xuāntǒng,
because many Governors-General and Governors of the directly governed provinces had spoken against it,
and further, people's representatives from the advisory councils of Shùntiān and various Zhílì provinces had petitioned for an early opening of the National Assembly,
hence this order.
On the *Jiǎxū* day,
Pǔlún and Zàizé were appointed Ministers for drafting the constitution.
On the *Yǐhài* day,
the Huáng Hé was peaceful.
On the *Dīngchǒu* day,
a bandit rebellion broke out in Cēnxī, Guǎngxī,
which was suppressed by government troops,
and the bandit leader Chén Róng'ān was executed.
Chéng Wénbǐng passed away,
and Chéng Yúnhé was appointed Admiral of the Chángjiāng Naval Forces,
and Zhāng Xūn, Admiral of Gānsù, was ordered to take command of the various battalions in Pǔkǒu, Jiāngnán.
Flood relief silver and rice for Língzhōu, Gānsù, were exempted.
On the *Gēngchén* day,
Zēngyùn memorialized that Zhèjiāng's Green Standard Army was to be reorganized into naval forces.
On the *Xīnsì* day,
an imperial edict, regarding the accelerated opening of the Parliament in the fifth year of Xuāntǒng,
tasked all responsible government agencies with earnest preparations,
stating that the Ministries of Mínzhèng, Dùzhī, Fǎ, and Xué all had responsibilities to bear,
and should plan comprehensively in advance,
categorizing them into most important and secondary,
and reporting in detail.
It also exhorted and encouraged the Governors-General and Governors of the directly governed provinces to exert their utmost effort,
strictly comply,
and no longer procrastinate or shirk responsibility,
so as not to miss the deadline.
On the *Rénwǔ* day,
Hé Yànshēng passed away,
and Yuán Dàhuà was appointed Governor of Xīnjiāng.
On the *Wùxū* day,
a temple was ordered to be built in the provincial capital of Jiāngníng for the late Grand Secretary and former acting Governor-General of Liǎngguǎng, Zhāng Zhīdòng.
In the eleventh month, on the *Guǐmǎo* day,
the positions of Minister, Vice-Minister, Assistant Ministers (left and right), and Counselors of the Lùjūnbù were abolished,
and one Minister and one Vice-Minister of the Lùjūnbù were established instead.
The Hǎijūnbù was established,
with one Minister and one Vice-Minister of the Hǎijūnbù.
Yìnchāng was appointed Minister of the Lùjūnbù,
and Shòuxūn was his Vice.
Bèi Lè Zàixún was appointed Minister of the Hǎijūnbù,
and Tán Xuéhéng was his Vice.
On the *Yǐsì* day,
Sà Zhènbīng, Admiral of the Navy, was ordered to command the patrol fleets of the ocean and the Chángjiāng.
On the *Bǐngwǔ* day,
a popular uprising occurred in Dàyáo County, Yúnnán,
where people entered the city, raided the prison, and killed people.
Government troops suppressed it,
and the bandit leaders Chén Wénpéi and Dèng Liángchén were both executed.
On the *Jǐyǒu* day,
Fěng Xù, former Governor of Ānhuī, was appointed Minister for disaster relief efforts in Jiāng and Wǎn.
On the *Rénzǐ* day,
the Nónggōngshāngbù presented an edited illustrated explanation of cotton.
On the *Dīngsì* day,
the Zīzhèngyuàn stated that the responsibilities of the Grand Councilors were unclear,
making it difficult for them to assist the sovereign,
and requested the establishment of a responsible cabinet.
An imperial edict stated that the court had its own considerations,
which the Zīzhèngyuàn was not authorized to interfere with,
and rejected it.
Léi Zhènchūn was dismissed,
and Duàn Qíruì was appointed acting Admiral of Jiāngběi.
On the *Gēngshēn* day,
Chén Kuílong memorialized that the Shùnzhí Advisory Council had petitioned for the National Assembly to be opened next year,
and an edict stated that early preparations had already been deemed insufficient,
so how could any further changes be discussed.
It was ordered to explicitly declare
that no further demands or disrespectful petitions would be permitted.
An additional 60 *shi* of grain from the Pǔjì Jiàoyǎngjú granary was granted,
to be given monthly as a regular payment.
On the *Xīnyǒu* day,
Higher Courts and Procuratorates were established in each province,
with Assistant Ministers and Chiefs;
Húnán's establishment was postponed.
On the *Guǐhài* day,
representatives from the three northeastern provinces who petitioned for a National Assembly arrived in the capital,
presenting a request for the National Assembly to be opened next year.
The Grand Councilors reported this.
An imperial edict ordered the Mínzhèngbù and the Headquarters of the Infantry Commander to compel them to return to their native places,
without delay,
and warned that any further arrivals in the capital or gatherings in the provinces would be investigated and punished.
On the *Jiǎzǐ* day,
an imperial edict urged the Xiànzhèng Biāncházhuǎn to draft a detailed list of preparations,
and the cabinet's organizational structure was to be compiled and memorialized.
A temple was ordered to be built in the provincial capital of Húběi for the late Grand Secretary Zhāng Zhīdòng.
On the *Yǐchǒu* day,
Qìng Qīnwáng Yìkuāng requested to be relieved of his duties as Grand Councilor and President of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs,
and a gracious imperial edict retained him in his posts.
On the *Jǐsì* day,
the Zīzhèngyuàn requested a clear imperial edict on cutting hair and changing clothes.
On *rénshēn* day of the twelfth month,
an edict was issued to all provinces to notify schools
to prohibit students from interfering in politics
or gathering crowds to make demands.
Violators would be severely punished.
On *bǐngzǐ* day,
Táng Shàoyí (唐紹儀) was excused due to illness,
and Shèng Xuānhuái (盛宣懷) was appointed Minister of Posts and Communications (Yóuchuán Bù Shàngshū 郵傳部尚書).
On *dīngchǒu* day,
the Right Wing Four Banners of Cháhār (察哈爾) Mongols suffered from a disaster,
and ten thousand taels of silver were issued for relief.
On *jǐmǎo* day,
Zhì Ruì (志銳) requested a flexible approach to abolishing the old system of Banner archives.
On *xīnsì* day,
Zēng Qí (增祺) was summoned for an audience,
and Fú Qí (孚琦) was ordered to act as the General of Guǎngzhōu (廣州 Jiāngjūn 將軍).
On *rénwǔ* day,
Zhào Ěrxùn (趙爾巽) was summoned for an audience.
On *guǐwèi* day,
the ban on opium was re-emphasized.
Local officials who continued to cover up the situation would be punished,
and the Ministries of Civil Affairs (Mínzhèng Bù 民政部) and Finance (Dùzhī Bù 度支部) were ordered to assess the situation.

The governors-general of all provinces were ordered to consult with the princes and ministers of the Constitutional Review and Compilation Bureau (Xiànzhèng Biānchá Guǎn Wáng Dàchén 憲政編查館王大臣) to revise the official system of the outer provinces.
On *yǐyǒu* day,
prefectures and counties in Jiāngsū (江蘇) were merged,
and judicial courts were established.
In Jiāngníng (江寧), Jiāngníng was merged into Shàngyuán (上元).
In Sūzhōu (蘇州), Chángzhōu (長洲) and Yuánhé (元和) were merged into Wú (吳).
Jiāngdū (江都) was merged into Gānquán (甘泉).
Zhāowén (昭文) was merged into Chángshú (常熟).
Xīnyáng (新陽) was merged into Kūnshān (崑山).
Zhènzé (震澤) was merged into Wújiāng (吳江).
Lóu (婁) was merged into Huátíng (華亭).
Yánghú (陽湖) was merged into Wǔjìn (武進).
Jīnkuì (金匱) was merged into Wúxī (無錫).
Jīngxī (荊溪) was merged into Yíxīng (宜興).
On *dīnghài* day,
the Constitutional Review and Compilation Bureau submitted a revised list of matters to be prepared annually, as proposed.
The naval camp officers and soldiers in Jílín (吉林) were abolished.
On *wùzǐ* day,
bandits in Sìchuān (四川) occupied Qiánjiāng (黔江) County and caused disturbances.
The government troops repelled them
and recaptured the city.
On *jǐchǒu* day,

Lǐ Jiājū (李家駒), the Minister for Constitutional Investigation (Kǎochá Xiànzhèng Dàchén 考察憲政大臣), presented his "Study of Japan's Tax System" (Rìběn Zūshuì Zhìdù Kǎo 日本租稅制度考) and "Study of Japan's Accounting System" (Huìjì Zhìdù Kǎo 會計制度考).
On *guǐsì* day,
Wēn Cháozhōng (溫朝鍾), a bandit leader from Sìchuān, fled into Xiánfēng (咸豐) County in Húběi (湖北),
where he was captured and executed.
On *yǐwèi* day,
Zài Zhèn (載振), a *Bèizǐ* (貝子) with the title of Prince of the Second Rank (Zhènguó Jiāngjūn 鎮國將軍), was appointed First-Class Special Envoy (Tóuděng Zhuānshǐ Dàchén 頭等專使大臣)
to congratulate the British monarch on his coronation.
The National Assembly (Zīzhèng Yuàn 資政院) passed the General Principles and Specific Articles of the New Criminal Code (Xīn Xínglǜ Zǒngzé, Fēnzé 新刑律總則、分則),
which were promulgated by imperial edict.
On *bǐngshēn* day,
arrears of taxes from the 33rd year of Guāngxù (光緒) were remitted for Xiánníng (咸寧) and 63 other prefectures, departments, and counties in Shǎnxī (陝西),
along with grain and fodder in public granaries.
On *dīngyǒu* day,
the National Assembly submitted a resolution on unifying the national treasury regulations.
On *wùxū* day,
the National Assembly submitted a memorial on the passed resolution for the total annual budget of expenditures and revenues for the third year of Xuāntǒng (宣統).
Tíng Jié (廷杰) passed away,
and Shào Chāng (紹昌) was appointed Minister of Justice (Fǎ Bù Shàngshū 法部尚書).
On *jǐhài* day,
the Lánzhōu (蘭州) Circuit in Gānsù (甘肅) was abolished,
and an Industrial Promotion Circuit (Quànyè Dào 勸業道) was established.
In this month,
there was a famine in Jiāng (江) and Huái (淮),
and people resorted to cannibalism.
There was an epidemic in the Three Eastern Provinces (Dōng Sānshěng 東三省).
On the first day of the first month, *gēngzǐ*, in the spring of the third year of Xīnhài (辛亥),
due to epidemic prevention outside Shānhǎiguān (山海關),
and the cold weather and blocked roads,
an edict was issued to Chén Kuílong (陳夔龍) and Xī Liáng (錫良) to resettle workers from various provinces.
On *bǐngwǔ* day,
Féng Xù (馮煦) memorialized on his investigation into the disaster situation in Xú (徐) and Huái (淮).
On *jǐyǒu* day,
land tax and silver grain were remitted for Chángzhōu (長洲) and 39 other departments and counties in Jiāngsū.
On *gēngxū* day,
relief was provided for flood-stricken counties in Jiāngsū, including Gāoyóu (高郵), Bǎoyìng (寶應), Qīnghé (清河), Āndōng (安東), Shānyáng (山陽), and Fùníng (阜寧).
On *jiǎyín* day,
the Ministry of Finance submitted the national budget regulations.
On *bǐngchén* day,
the period of mourning ended.
Censor Hú Sījìng (胡思jìng 胡思敬) impeached the Constitutional Review and Compilation Bureau,
stating that new officials should not be indiscriminately appointed
and old officials should not be entirely dismissed;
righteous people should be employed to draft documents,
and public opinion should be adopted for promulgation.
His memorial was sent to the Department of Political Affairs (Zhèngwù Chù 政務處).
On *gēngshēn* day,
Zhì Ruì (志銳) was transferred to become the General of Yīlí (伊犂 Jiāngjūn 將軍),
and Guǎng Fú (廣福) became the General of Hángzhōu (杭州 Jiāngjūn 將軍).
On *yǐchǒu* day,
torture for non-capital crimes was abolished.
For crimes below banishment or exile,
judicial torture was not to be used.
The Ministry of Justice memorialized that Yí Gǔ (貽穀), the dismissed General of Suíyuǎn City (Suíyuǎnchéng Jiāngjūn 綏遠城將軍), was sentenced to death.
An imperial edict changed the sentence to penal servitude in Xīnjiāng (新疆) to atone for his crimes.
On *yǐsì* day,
Zhōu Shùmó (周樹模) was ordered to jointly investigate the Sino-Russian border.
In this month,
there was an epidemic among the people of Zhílì (直隸) and Shāndōng (山東).
On the first day of the second month, *gēngwǔ*,
a memorial hall was granted to the late Grand Secretary (Dàxuéshì 大學士) and former Governor of Húnán (Húnán Xúnfǔ 湖南巡撫), Wáng Wénsháo (王文韶), in the provincial capital of Húnán.
Féng Xù (馮煦) requested the dredging of the Suīhé (睢河).
The Ministry of Civil Affairs submitted the compiled household registration law.
On *rénshēn* day,
an edict was issued to the relevant authorities for epidemic prevention,
stating that they should not use it as a pretext for harassment,

and also ordered the Ministry of Civil Affairs, the Commander of the Infantry (Bùjūn Tǒnglǐng Yámén 步軍統領衙門), and the Shùntiān Prefecture (Shùntiān Fǔ 順天府) to issue an edict to the people with the intent of protecting their livelihoods.
On *yǐhài* day,
the three local chieftains (Tǔsī 土司) of Dégé (德格), Chūn kē (春科), and Gāorì (高日) in Sìchuān were replaced with appointed officials.
The Běibiān Dào (邊北道) was established,
along with Dēngkē Fǔ (登科府),
the two prefectures of Déhuà (德化) and Báiyù (白玉),
and the two counties of Shíqu (石渠) and Tóngpǔ (同普).
It was decided that criminals sentenced to military service at postal stations in Xīnjiāng should instead be sent to Bā (巴) or Zàng (藏).
On *bǐngzǐ* day,
land tax, silver, and rice were remitted for the disaster-stricken lands in Kūnmíng (昆明) and two other prefectures and counties in Yúnnán (雲南).
On *dīngchǒu* day,
barren land tax, money, and grain were remitted for Rénshān (仁和) and 29 other prefectures and counties in Zhèjiāng (浙江),
the two garrisons of Háng (杭) and Yán (嚴),
and the two stations of Qú (衢) and Yán (嚴).
On *wùyín* day,

the titles of Ministers and Vice-Ministers of the Ministry of the Army (Lùjūn Bù 陸軍部) and the Ministry of the Navy (Hǎijūn Bù 海軍部) were changed to Principal Commandant (Zhèng Dūtǒng 正都統) and Vice Commandant (Fù Dūtǒng 副都統) respectively.
Yìn Chāng (廕昌), Shòu Xūn (壽勳), Zài Xún (載洵), and Tán Xuéhéng (譚學衡) remained in their positions.
The British occupied Piànmǎ (片馬).
On *guǐwèi* day,
Lǐ Jiājū (李家駒) was ordered to draft lecture notes and submit them in rotation.
On *bǐngxū* day,
the Assistant Resident Agent (Bāngbàn Dàchén 幫辦大臣) in Tibet (Zàng 藏) was abolished,
and Left and Right Counselors (Zuǒ Yòu Cānzàn 左右參贊) were established.
On *dīnghài* day,
a framed plaque with the inscription
"Chaste Heart, Resolute Will" (Zhēn Xīn Yì Lì 貞心毅力) was bestowed upon the Huìxīng (惠興) Girls' School in Zhèjiāng.
On *jǐchǒu* day,
the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Wàiwù Bù 外務部) submitted regulations for the bestowal of medals and awards.

Chén Bāngruì (陳邦ruì 陳邦瑞), Right Vice-Minister of Finance (Dùzhī Bù Yòu Shìláng 度支部右侍郎), Lǐ Jiājū (李家駒), Right Vice-Minister of Education (Xué Bù Yòu Shìláng 學部右侍郎), and Wāng Róngbǎo (汪榮寶), Left Counselor of Civil Affairs (Mínzhèng Bù Zuǒ Cānyì 民政部左參議), were ordered to jointly compile the constitution.
Chéng Xūn (誠勳) was appointed General of Guǎngzhōu (廣州 Jiāngjūn 將軍),
and Pǔ ● (溥●) was appointed Military Governor (Dūtǒng 都統) of Rèhé (熱河).
Bèizǐ Pǔ Lún (貝子溥倫) was appointed Minister of Agriculture, Industry, and Commerce (Nóng Gōng Shāng Bù Shàngshū 農工商部尚書).
Shì Xù (世續) was appointed President of the National Assembly (Zīzhèng Yuàn Zǒngcái 資政院總裁),
Lǐ Jiājū (李家駒) as Vice-President,
and Liú Ruòcéng (劉若曾) as Minister for Revising Laws (Xiūdìng Fǎlǜ Dàchén 修訂法律大臣).
On *rénchén* day,
foreign merchants were prohibited from importing salt.
The title of British Consul General in Penang (Bīnlángyǔ 檳榔嶼) was changed.
In the third month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
Liú Ruìhéng was appointed as the Provincial Commander-in-Chief (*Tídū*) of Yúnnán.
The Office for Inspecting Guards was abolished,
and the Office for Managing the Vanguard and Imperial Guard Battalions was established.
The Imperial Guards of the Three Banners remained under the Household Department (*Nèiwùfǔ*).
The Ministry of War (*Lùjūnbù*) reported that
Jiāo Diān, a surveyor from the Bureau of Surveying of the Three Eastern Provinces, had bribed and sold secret maps,
and he was executed.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Chéngdé and Jǐn counties in Fèngtiān were abolished.
On the *rényín* day,
the General Commanders (*Zǒngbīngguān*) of the two garrisons, Chuānběi and Chóngqìng, in Sìchuān, were abolished.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,

six edicts were issued to military personnel: Be utterly loyal and devoted (*jìnzhōngjié*), observe rites and discipline (*shǒulǐjié*), uphold martial bravery (*shàngwǔyǒng*), esteem trustworthiness and righteousness (*chóngxìnyì*), be simple and honest (*dūnpúsu*), and value integrity and shame (*zhòngliánchǐ*).
On the *dīngwèi* day,

officials such as Hé Zōnglián and Lǐ Kuíyuán, who were General Commanders (*Tǒngzhì*) and Commanders (*Tǒnglǐng*) of various divisions and brigades in the army, were granted the titles of Army Vice-Commander-in-Chief (*Fùdūtǒng*) and Brigade Commander (*Xiédūtǒng*) respectively, with some variations.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the navigation channel of the Tǔmén Jiāng in Jílín was dredged and opened to the sea.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Wú Zōnglián, the Minister to Italy, was appointed as a special envoy
to congratulate Italy on its national day celebrations.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Revolutionary Party members used explosive darts to assassinate Fúqí, the acting General of Guǎngzhōu.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Sà Zhènbīng was appointed as the Navy Vice-Commander-in-Chief (*Hǎijūn Fùdūtǒng*).
Zhào Ěrfēng reported on the pacification of the savage tribes of Sānyán,
and the two native chieftaincies (*tǔsī*) of Kǒngsā and Máshū were reorganized,
with civil officials appointed.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Zhāng Míngqí was appointed as the Governor-General (*Zǒngdū*) of Liǎngguǎng.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Zài Zé, the Minister of the Ministry of Finance (*Dùzhībù Shàngshū*), concluded a loan agreement with banks from Britain, America, Germany, and France.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Zhì Ruì, the General of Yīlí, was granted the title of Minister (*Shàngshū*),
and all civil and military officials in the Yīlí region were placed under his control.
The land and pond taxes for the second year of Xuāntǒng were exempted for Ránhé and thirty-six other prefectures and counties, as well as military garrisons (*wèisuǒ*), in Zhèjiāng.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
due to disasters in Jiāngsū, Ānhuī, and Hénán,
Féng Xù was ordered to convene with the Governor-Generals and Provincial Governors (*Dūfǔ*) of the three provinces to plan for spring relief.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the Netherlands held an anti-opium conference in The Hague,
and Liáng Chéng, the Minister to Germany, was ordered to attend.
Disaster relief was provided for the nomadic Zāhǎqìn Mongols in Kēbùduō.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Xī Liáng was relieved due to illness.
