Wú Shì, Shào Xuéguì's wife, a commoner in Qiántáng Xiàn; Liú Shì, Chǔ Bóxián's wife, a commoner in Tiāntái Xiàn; and Gāo Yào's wife, a commoner in Xiāoshān Xiàn, all gave birth to three boys at one time.
Xià Shì, Zhōu Yìshì's wife, a commoner in Xīnjiàn Xiàn, gave birth to three boys at one time.
Sòng Shì, Luó Hànshēng's wife, a commoner in Péngzé Xiàn, gave birth to three boys at one time.
Chén Shì, Gōng Shàoyī's wife, a commoner in Héféi, gave birth to three boys at one time.
Xuē Shì, Féng Wéimíng's wife, a commoner in Ānyì Xiàn, gave birth to three boys at one time.
Cuī Shì, Wáng Jìnlù's wife, a commoner in Shī Xiàn, gave birth to three boys at one time.
In the eighth year
Sūn Zuòshèng's wife, a commoner in Shāng Xiàn, gave birth to three boys at one time.
Gāo Cóngyì's wife, a commoner in Huáng Xiàn, gave birth to three boys at one time.
Yán Shì, Yáng Dàchéng's wife, a commoner in Qiántáng Xiàn, and Máo Shì, Hóng Wénxī's wife, a commoner in Suí'ān Xiàn, both gave birth to three boys at one time.
Lǐ Shì, a certain commoner's wife in Húguān, gave birth to four boys at one time.
Wáng Shì, Sūn Wénlín's wife, a commoner in Chóngyáng Xiàn, gave birth to three boys at one time.
Gōng Zhāngchún's wife, a commoner in Xīng'ān, gave birth to three boys at one time.
Lín Shì, Xiàng Rúmào's wife, a commoner in Línhǎi Xiàn, and Yīng Shì, Chén Dàocái's wife, a commoner in Zhènhǎi Xiàn, both gave birth to three boys at one time.
In the tenth year
Zhèng Shì, Xǔ Yuánshēng's wife, a commoner in Hóngdòng Xiàn, gave birth to three boys at one time.
Zhāng Shì, Zhào Yùxī's wife, gave birth to three boys at one time.
Wǔ Shì, Yàn Jūyǔ's wife, a commoner in Jièxiū, gave birth to three boys at one time.
Qín Yù's wife, a commoner in Língchuān, gave birth to three boys at one time.
Dù Mǒu's wife, a commoner in Shífāng Xiàn, gave birth to three boys at one time.
Lín Shì, Lǐ Tiānxī's wife, a commoner in Yǒngjiā Xiàn, gave birth to three boys at one time.
Lǐ Shì, Wèi Jīngwǔ's wife, a commoner in Fúliáng Xiàn, gave birth to three boys at one time.
Wú Shìguì's wife, a commoner in Fáng Xiàn, gave birth to three boys at one time.
In the eleventh year
Xuē Shì, Bái Qǐ's wife, a commoner in Jìzhōu, gave birth to three boys at one time.
Hú Shì, Jiāng Zìzhōu's wife, a commoner in Suí'ān Xiàn, gave birth to three boys at one time.
In the spring of the twelfth year
Guān Shì, Liú Fèn's wife, a commoner in Qíhé, and Zhào Yǔnzhōng's wife, a commoner in Xīnchéng, both gave birth to three boys at one time.
In the sixth month,
Wāng Zhùsān's wife, a commoner in Qiánshān, gave birth to three boys at one time.
Bì Màozēng's wife, a commoner in Kāihuà Xiàn, gave birth to three boys at one time.
In the fourth month of the thirteenth year
Zhāng Défú's wife, a commoner in Luánzhōu, gave birth to three boys at one time.
In the ninth month,

On the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month of the twenty-third year of Jiāqìng (1818),
a long star fell,
with a sound like thunder.
Local people observed a pit formed where it fell.
When dug,
a stone was found,
over two chǐ long,
over one chǐ wide,
square in shape with rounded corners.
When broken,
it was five-colored inside.
On the thirtieth day of the seventh month of the eleventh year of Xiánfēng (1861),
three stars fell in Guānghuà,
turning into stones.
On the fourteenth day of the sixth month of the twelfth year of Tóngzhì (1873),
in Zhāngxiàn, at Mǎchénglóng Chuān, three huge sounds occurred,
heard for tens of lǐ.
Three stones fell from the sky,
each about four chǐ five cùn high.
In the tenth month (1873),
a meteorite fell in Luótián,
shattering upon impact with the ground.
On the twenty-second day of the first month of the twentieth year of Guāngxù (1894),
a star fell in Gāolán like a fireball.
Local people identified its location.
When dug,
an iron egg was found.
On the ninth day of the second month of the eleventh year of Shùnzhì (1654),
the water of Xiāngshān River was like blood,
returning to normal the next day;
the water of Dōng Lìzhītáng in Yázhōu was red like blood,
only ceasing after ten days.
In the twelfth year (1655),
the water of Wànquán Well was black.
In the thirteenth year (1656),
the spring water in Jiāngzhōu suddenly became red like blood.
In the third month of the fourteenth year (1657),

In the fourth month of the fifteenth year (1658),

In the eighth month of the eighteenth year (1661),

In the ninth month of the fifteenth year of Kāngxī (1676),

In the seventh month of the second year of Yōngzhèng,

Annals Sixteen: Disasters and Anomalies 2
The *Hóngfàn* says:
“Fire ascends flaming.”
If fire does not ascend flaming,
then it is an ominous sign.
All prolonged warmth, unusual plants, aberrations of feathered creatures, and misfortunes involving sheep—
their calamity is fire.
Red phantoms and red auspicious signs are all related to fire.

In Luánzhōu, a cut gourd bled,
and those who ate it immediately fell ill.
In the first month of the third year,
it rained five-colored, variegated beans in Yǒngfēng.
In the third month,
it rained beans in Jǐngníng and Shèngxiàn.
In the fifth month,
it rained black, shiny beans in Jīngshān Xiàn.
In the second month of the sixth year,
it rained grass seeds like buckwheat in Qīxiá.
In summer,
it rained beans in Shèngxiàn.
In the seventh year,
beans grew in Gǎochéng resembling human faces,
with all five features complete.
In the tenth month of the ninth year,
it rained black outside, red inside grain in Suíchāng;
it rained black inside, white outside beans in Déxīng.
In the third month of the eleventh year,
it rained red beans and buckwheat in Jìmò.
In the fourth month of the second year of Guāngxù,
it rained beans in Qīngtián.
In the third month of the ninth year,
it rained red wheat in Xiánníng.
In the eighth month of the tenth year,
the bamboo in Xiàoyì Tīng bore fruit.
In the eleventh month,
mountain bamboo in Táozhōu flowered and bore fruit.
In the fourteenth year of Shùnzhì,
crows carried fire in Wǔchāng,
gathering in people's houses,
frequently causing disasters,
which ceased after one month.
In the sixteenth year of Kāngxī,
a strange bird gathered in the forest in Hǎifēng for three days.
It was six or seven chǐ tall,
its neck stretching over ten chǐ.
It pecked chickens and ducks to eat.
Residents vigorously attacked it
and divided its flesh to eat,
but subsequently fell ill and died.
In the seventh month of the first year of Shùnzhì,
a large yellow sheep was seen in the suburbs of Shāngzhōu.
It was over ten chǐ long.
The common people fought and killed it.
Its meat weighed five hundred jīn.
In the fifth month of the fourth year,
a sheep in a common household in Shānyīn gave birth to a lamb
with three legs,
two in front and one behind.
In the fifth year,
a sheep in a common household in Hángzhōu gave birth to a lamb
with three legs.
In the twelfth year of Kāngxī,
a sheep was born in a common household in Běishān
with one horn and one eye,
and died shortly after.
In the twenty-fourth year,
a sheep in Shùndé gave birth to a lamb
with three legs,
one in front and two behind.
In the fourth month of the first year of Qiánlóng,
mountain goats entered the city of Liánzhōu.
Their hooves and horns were very large.
People chased and caught them.
In the fifty-fifth year,
a three-legged sheep was seen in Yúnmèng.
In the eighth month of the seventeenth year of Dàoguāng,
a sheep was born in a common household in Wǔjìn
with a human head and sheep's feet,
and died immediately after falling to the ground.
In the eighth month of the tenth year of Xiánfēng,
white sheep appeared in flocks on the Xīshān mountains of Jiāngshān,
and then disappeared.
In the third year of Tóngzhì,
a sheep in a common household in Níngzhōu gave birth to a lamb
with five horns.
In the ninth month of the ninth year of Guāngxù,
a sheep in a common household in Xiàoyì Tīng gave birth to a lamb
with a human face and a sheep's body.
In the twenty-fifth year,
a sheep in a common household in Níngzhōu gave birth to a lamb
with two heads.
In the third month of the twenty-seventh year,
in Dāngá'ěr there was a two-headed sheep;
and a three-legged lamb.
In the thirty-third year,
a sheep in a common household in Níngzhōu gave birth to a lamb
with a human face.

The Hóngfàn says:
"Wood is characterized by being crooked or straight."
If wood is not crooked or straight,
it is a sign of calamity.
All prolonged rain, madmen, aberrant clothing, chicken calamities, rat anomalies, wooden ice, wooden monsters, green omens, and green portents
are all attributed to wood.

If metal does not follow change,

Before this, there was a children's rhyme that said:
"Enter the cave to count,

It came true at this time.
In the fourteenth year of Kāngxī,

The inscription on the tablet read:
"The broken old dragon wounds Yuèxiù,
eight winds blow arrows into Tuóchéng.
Planting willows in past years held sorrow,
how can viewing flowers today be without feeling?
Withered flowers themselves mourn their scattering,
why must snapped willows concern rise and fall?
Pitiable are the traces of wild ghosts in yellow sand,
awaiting only the neighing of Liú Zhōng's horse."
It was like a poem, like a prophecy,
and no one could understand it.

Records of Nineteen Calamities and Anomalies (Part Five)
The Hóngfàn says:
"Earth is for sowing and reaping."
If it fails, it is a sign of calamity.

All constant strong winds and dust, dimness and obscurity, flower spirits, insect plagues, cattle disasters, earthquakes, mountain collapses, rain of hair, growth of hair on the ground, famine years, yellow blights, and yellow auspicious signs are attributed to Earth.

In the eighth month of the seventeenth year of Shùnzhì's reign,
black insects covered the mountains in Yùpíng,
and all plants were consumed.
In the autumn of the tenth year of Kāngxī's reign,
five-colored insects appeared in Cháozhōu,
as large as fingers,
three inches long,
eating crops.
In the seventh month of the eleventh year,
insects rained in Hángzhōu,
eating grain.
In the seventh month of the twelfth year,
insects ate grain in Wànzài.
In the third month of the thirteenth year,
black insects appeared on the roofs in Níngdū,
causing great pain when they touched people.
In the seventh month of the seventeenth year,
two-headed insects appeared in Chóngmíng,
with mouths at both ends,
nibbling grass as if mown.
In the sixth month of the nineteenth year,
green insects harmed crops in Wùyuán.
In the second month of the twentieth year,
there was an insect plague in Yúnyáng.
In the fifth month of the twenty-first year,
there was an insect plague in Jīnhuá.
In the fourth month of the twenty-second year,
there was an insect plague in Ēnshī.
In the fifth month of the twenty-third year,
there were tens of thousands of *hú* of insects in Qúxiàn,
resembling locusts,
black,
with sharp heads,
and wings,
and they smelled very foul.
In the seventh month of the twenty-seventh year,
there was an insect plague in Sūzhōu and Qīngpǔ.
In the fourth month of the twenty-ninth year,
white and black insects ate grain in Qìnshuǐ,
forming cocoons.
In the third month of the thirtieth year,
green insects ate grain in Wànzài.
In the thirty-sixth year,
insects appeared in Zūnhuà Zhōu,
resembling *huái* worms but black,
eating almost all the crops.
In the thirty-ninth year,
insects appeared in Guìxiàn,
eating beans.
In the forty-second year,
caterpillar-like insects appeared in Zhāohuà,
eating grain.
In the second month of the forty-fifth year,
insects ate grain in Fángxiàn.
In summer,
insects resembling mantises but golden in color appeared in Zhānhuà;
those who recognized them said,
"These are *cāngzhū*,
and their appearance portends a bad harvest."
In the fifth month of the forty-ninth year,
five-colored insects appeared in Jǐngxíng.
In the fifty-sixth year,

hairy,

In the fifth month of the eleventh year (1733),

covered in scales,
with fleshy nodules like beans along both sides of its spine down to its tail,
golden in color,
a deer's body,
eight legs,
and cow hooves.
At birth, wind and rain arrived simultaneously,

In the second month of the thirteenth year (1735),
