The monastic officials included Guóshī, Chánshī, Zāfúkè Dàlǎmā, Zāfúkè Lǎmā, Dàlǎmā, Fùlǎmā,
all supervised by Kānbù.
The Tibetan region was divided into four parts: Wèi, Zàng, Kāmù, and Ālǐ.
Each was governed by a Gábùlún,
with very important responsibilities.
From Zǎipéng downwards,
they were officials assisting in state affairs.
From Dàipéng downwards,
they were military commanders in various cities.
From Biānyíngguān downwards,
they were civil officials in various cities.
From Guóshī to Lǎmā,
they were exclusively responsible for religious affairs.
Resident ministers (Zhùzàng Dàchén) were established to supervise them.
This began in the third year of Yōngzhèng
but they were still not on par with the Dálài Lǎmā and Bānchán Lǎmā.
It was not until the fifty-seventh year of Qiánlóng
that officials from Gábùlún downwards became subject to their authority,
and the power of the ministers became equal to theirs.
One Dàipéng was also added
(originally there were five,
which was settled at this time),
twelve Rúpéng,
and one hundred and twenty Dìngpéng,
with promotions and appointments made according to their respective ranks.
As for the Gáxià, Xiǎozhōngyì, and Zhuóníěr,
talented individuals from Dōngkē (meaning children of aristocratic families) were selected for these positions.
Various Tǔsī Officials During the Míng dynasty,
the tǔsī were lewd, muddle-headed, cruel, and tyrannical.
The regions of Bōzhōu, Shuǐxī, Lìnzhōu, and Lùchuān
suffered constant border troubles.
The Qīng dynasty, learning from previous mistakes,
repeatedly debated converting these tǔsī territories into regular administration (guīliú).
In the past, two tǔsī were subordinate to outer feudatories,
and seven to regular provinces.
During the prosperous reigns of Kāngxī and Yōngzhèng,
Sǎnmáo in Húběi (formerly a Xuānfǔsī,
administering the Dàwàng Ānfǔsī,
and the Dōngliú
and Lìbì Zhǎngguānsī.
In the 13th year of Yōngzhèng, it was reformed into Láifèng Xiàn),
Shī'nán (formerly Shīzhōu Wèi,
administering the Zhōngjiàn and Zhōngxiào Xuānfǔsī;
the Zhōnglù, Zhōngdòng, Dōngxiāng Wǔlù, Gāoluó, Lóngtán, and Jīndòng Ānfǔsī;
and the Mùcè, Shàng'àichádòng, Xià'àichádòng, Zhènnán, Yáobǎdòng, Zhènyuǎnmányí, Lóngtàimányí, Xīpíngmányí, Jiànnán, Sīnán, and Tángyá Zhǎngguānsī.
In the 13th year of Yōngzhèng, it was reformed into Ēnshī, Xuān'ēn, Xiánfēng, and Lìchuān four counties),
and Róngměi (formerly a Xuānwèisī,
administering the Pánshùnshuǐ, Jìnyuán, and Tōngtǎpíng Ānfǔsī;
and the Jiāoshān, Mǎnáo, Shíliáng, Xiàdòng, Xiàgāng, Píngchá, Wǔfēng, and Shíbǎo Zhǎngguānsī.
In the 13th year of Yōngzhèng, it was reformed into Hèfēng Zhōu and Chánglè Xiàn);
Yǒngshùn in Húnán (formerly a Xuānwèisī,
administering the Shīróng Ānfǔsī;
the Xiàdòng, Tiánjiādòng, Lǘchídòng, Lārědòng, Màizhùhuángdòng, and Báiyádòng Zhǎngguānsī;
and the Nánwèi and Shàngxī two tǔguān.
In the 7th year of Yōngzhèng, it was reformed into Yǒngshùn and Lóngshān two counties),
Bǎojìng (formerly a Xuānwèisī,
administering the Wǔzhài and Gānzipíng two Zhǎngguānsī.
In the 7th year of Yōngzhèng, it was reformed into a county),
Sāngzhí (formerly an Ānfǔsī.
Administering the Měipíng, Cháonán, Nàbù, Rénshì, Huánghé, Yúlóng, Jiáshí, Kǔnán, Gǎnpíng, Cánliáo, Jīncáng, Tuòshān, Làndòng, Huángjiā, Bǎnshān, Lóngtán, and Shūluò seventeen dòng;
and the Ānfúsuǒ Shàng and Xià two dòng.
In the 7th year of Yōngzhèng, it was reformed into a county),
and Yǒngsuí (the six-lǐ red Miáo land.
In the 8th year of Yōngzhèng, it was changed to a regular official administration),
Gānzhōu, and Fènghuángyíng (the Gānbīan red Miáo land.
In the 43rd year of Kāngxī, it was changed to a regular official administration),
along with the assimilation of the Shēngmiáo,
were all designated as prefectures and counties.
In Sìchuān, Jiànchāng (formerly a Zhǐhuī Sī.
In the early Shùnzhì reign, it was changed to a Wèi.
In the 4th year of Yōngzhèng, Níngyuǎn Fǔ was established),
Sōngfān (formerly a Wèi.
In the 9th year of Yōngzhèng, it was changed to a regular administration),
Tiānquán (formerly the Liùfān Zhāotǎosī.
In the 7th year of Yōngzhèng, it was changed to a regular administration),
Dǎjiànlú (formerly the Chánghéxī Yútōng Ānyuǎn Xuānfǔsī.
In the 7th year of Yōngzhèng, it was changed to a regular administration);
in Guǎngxī, Zhèn'ān (formerly a Tǔfǔ.
In the 2nd year of Kāngxī, it was changed to a regular administration),
Sīchéng (formerly a Zhōu.
In the 15th year of Shùnzhì, it was promoted to a Fǔ.
Later it became a Tǔfǔ.
In the 5th year of Yōngzhèng, it was changed to a regular administration);
in Yúnnán, Kāihuà (formerly the Jiàohuà, Wánglòng, and Ānnán three Zhǎngguānsī.
In the 6th year of Kāngxī, it was changed to a regular administration),
Zhāotōng (formerly Měngdì.
In the 5th year of Yōngzhèng, it was transferred from Sìchuān.
The next year, it was changed to a regular administration),
Lìjiāng (formerly a Tǔfǔ.
In the early Yōngzhèng reign, it was changed to a regular administration),
Zhènyuán (formerly a Tǔzhōu.
In the 3rd year of Yōngzhèng, it was changed to a regular administration.
In the 4th year, it was transferred from Sìchuān),
Ménghuà (formerly a Tǔfǔ.
In the 4th year of Kāngxī, it was changed to a regular administration),
Wēiyuǎn (formerly a Tǔzhōu.
In the 3rd year of Yōngzhèng, it was changed to a regular administration.
The next year, it was transferred from Sìchuān);
in Guìzhōu, Wēiníng (formerly the Shuǐxī Xuānwèisī.
In the 1st year of Kāngxī, Qiánxī Fǔ was established,
Bǐlātǎ was changed to Píngyuǎn Fǔ,
Dàfāng Chéng to Dàdìng Fǔ,
and Mǎsā in Sìchuān to Wēiníng.
After being transferred,
the various prefectures in Qiánxī were changed to Zhōu
and all subordinated to Wēiníng),
Lángdài (In the 9th year of Yōngzhèng, it was changed to a regular administration),
Guīhuà (the Kāngzuǒ and Zhòngmiáo lands.
In the 12th year of Yōngzhèng, it was changed to a regular administration),
and Yǒngfēng (the Ānlóng Zhǎngguānsī land.
In the 5th year of Yōngzhèng, it was changed to a regular administration),
were all adjusted as circumstances dictated,
and regular officials were widely appointed.
From Qiánlóng onwards,
the Dà Jīnchuān and Xiǎo Jīnchuān regions once again required military force.
Yǒuyáng (formerly a Xuānwèisī.
In the 1st year of Qiánlóng, it was changed to a regular administration),
Shígù (formerly a Xuānfǔsī.
In the 27th year, it was changed to a regular administration),
were completely reformed from their wild state.
The fierce Miǎn and Yánhuāng regions
eagerly turned inward.
(In the 13th year, Miǎnníng Tīng was established).
The border regions of Diānnán
were struck with awe upon hearing this.
(In the 31st year, after pacifying the Mǎng bandits,
various tribes submitted,
and Zhěngmài and Jǐngxiàn and other Sī were established.
Details follow).
During the Jiāqìng and Dàoguāng eras,
in Guìzhōu, the Shǒubèi (in the 25th year of Jiāqìng, one person from Guīhuà Tīng's jurisdiction was abolished.
In the 1st year of Dàoguāng, one person from Ānshùn Fǔ's jurisdiction was abolished.
In the 4th year, one person from Pǔ'ān Tīng's jurisdiction was abolished.
In the 12th year, one person from Pǔdìng Xiàn's jurisdiction was abolished),
Qiānzǒng (in the 1st year of Dàoguāng, two people from Ānshùn Fǔ's jurisdiction were abolished.
In the 4th year, one person from Guīhuà Tīng's jurisdiction's Shēngmiáo Zhī and one from Cèhēng Zhōutóng's jurisdiction's Shàngfēntíng were abolished.
In the 10th year, one person from Pǔ'ān Xiàn's jurisdiction's Shàngwǔyuàn Zhī was abolished),
and Bǎzǒng (in the 1st year of Dàoguāng, five people from Pǔdìng Xiàn's jurisdiction and one from Lángdài Tīng's jurisdiction's Liùzhī were abolished.
In the 4th year, one from Luòhé Zhī and one from Cèhēng Zhōutóng's jurisdiction's Xiàfēntíng were abolished.
In the 6th year, one person from Píngyuǎn Xiàn's jurisdiction was abolished.
In the 8th year, one person from Zhēnfēng Zhōu Luólàngtíng was abolished.
In the 20th year, one person from Chángsài Tīng was abolished),
saw even greater reductions.
Around the Guāngxù and Xuāntǒng periods,
Fùzhōu and Zhènkāng in Yúnnán,
and Bātáng, Yūtáng, Dé'ěrgétè, Gāorì, Chūnkē, Zhānduì, and Càmǔduō in Sìchuān
were still governed by officials according to old customs.
(Bātáng was renamed Bā'ān Zhílì Tīng Jīnglì,
stationed at Yánjǐng.
Yūtáng was renamed Shùnhuà Xiàn Xúnjiǎn,
stationed at Zhōngdùhé.
Xiāngchéng was renamed Dìngxiāng Xiàn Xiànchéng,
stationed at Dàobà.
All were subordinate to the Biānwù Dàchén.
They also administered the various Mán tribes of Míngzhèng, Huò'ěr, Wǔjiā, Dàowù, and Lěngqì).
In Guǎngxī, the various zhōu of Zhōngzhōu, Nándān, Wànchéng, Míngyíng, Quánmíng, Jié'ān, Zhènyuǎn, Jiāngzhōu, Xiàshíxī, Shàngxiàdòng, Xiàléi, and Nàdì;
Luóbái, one xiàn;
the various xúnsī of Gǔlíng, Dìngluó, Āndìng, and Xiàwàng;
the Yǒngdìng Zhǎngguānsī;
the Yǒngshùn Fùsī;
and the Qiānlóngdòng tǔguān,
had their hereditary positions abolished.
The various zhōu of Xiàngwǔ, Dūkāng, Ānpíng, Píngxiáng, and Sīzhōu;
the various xiàn of Shànglín, Xīnchéng, and Luóyáng;
the Dōnglán and Fèngshān Zhōutóng;
and the various xúnsī of Shànglóng, Báishān, and Xīnglóng,
were replaced by Han officials.
Examining the actual situation,
along the Lǒng, the old system was preserved.
In Xiāng and Chǔ, territories were thoroughly cleansed.
In Diān and Shǔ, three to four tenths were converted to regular administration.
As for the Zhǎngguān Zhōu and Xiàn in Qián and Guì,
comparing the present to the past,
barely half remain,
but a detailed investigation of records
still reveals hundreds.
Their hereditary lineages,
and their lands,
as well as all military officials who were not hereditary,
and the monastic officials of the tribal regions,
are appended below,
to provide a basis for study.

Zǒnglǐ Gōngchéngchù (Office for General Management of Works) staff members had no fixed quota.
Cháhéfáng (Audit Office), Dūcuīfáng (Supervision and Urging Office), Huìgǎochù (Draft Compilation Office),
all selected staff members to concurrently manage their affairs.
The zǒngguǎn dàchén (Minister of General Superintendence) managed the internal affairs and decrees of the nèifǔ (Imperial Household Department),
overseeing all matters related to
the provision of imperial supplies and services.
The táng lángzhōng (Director of the Main Hall) and zhǔshì (Secretary) managed the selection of civil officials,
memorials, and official documents.
The guǎngchú (Department of Extensive Storage) managed the receipt and disbursement of the six treasuries;
the zhīzào (Weaving Manufactory) and zhīrǎnjú (Dyeing Bureau) were subordinate to it.
The kuàijī (Department of Accounting) managed the receipts and disbursements of the department,
and at the end of each year, it would audit and report on all matters concerning orchards, farmlands, households, and corvée labor.
The zhǎnglǐ (Department of Rites) managed the sacrifices, ceremonies, music, and dances of the department,
as well as inspecting the ranks of eunuchs
and the taxes from orchards.
The dūyú (Department of Policing and Supplies) managed the selection of military officials,
audited stipends, rations, and imperial favors,
the annual tribute of pearls,
and the annual submission from tenants and fishermen,
and determined their quotas for supply.
The shènxíng (Department of Justice) managed judicial matters of the department,
proposed punishments according to the law,
and for serious cases, transferred them to the sān fǎsī (Three Judicial Offices) for joint interrogation and resolution;
the fānyìchù (Foreigner's Affairs Office) was subordinate to it.
The yíngzào (Department of Construction) managed the repairs of the department,
procuring materials and supervising workers,
and directed the six treasuries and three workshops to fulfill orders.
The qìngfēng (Department of Abundant Harvest) managed the herds of cattle and sheep
and provided sacrificial animals for auspicious offerings.
The qiánliáng yámén (Money and Grain Yamen) managed the estate taxes of the sānqí (Three Banners)
and administered rewards, punishments, and exemptions.
The nèiguǎnlǐngchù (Internal Superintendence Office) managed the duties assigned by the zhōnggōng (Empress)
and also inspected the supplies of the guānsāncāng (Three Official Granaries) and the grain rations from the ēnfēngcāng (Graceful Abundance Granary).
The guānfáng zūkù (Official Housing and Rent Treasury) managed the collection of house taxes.
The yǎngxīndiàn zàobànchù (Hall of Mental Cultivation Workshop) managed the manufacturing of utensils.
The zhōngzhèngdiàn gè sīyuán (Officials of the Hall of Central Uprightness) managed the chanting of sutras by lāmǎs (lamas).
The wǔyīngdiàn xiūshūchù (Wuying Hall Book Compilation Office) managed the supervision and printing of books.
The yǒnghé (Yonghe Palace) and níngshòu (Ningshou Palace) liǎnggōng sīyuán (Officials of the Two Palaces) managed the arrangement of furnishings and sweeping,
as well as inspecting the diligence of palace eunuchs.
The yùshūchù (Imperial Calligraphy Office) managed the carving and copying of imperial writings.
The yùcháshànfáng (Imperial Tea and Food Department) managed the provision of food and drink.
The yùyàofáng (Imperial Pharmacy) managed the compounding of pills and powders.
The xīshēngsuǒ (Sacrificial Animal Office) managed the raising of black oxen.
The zǒnglǐ gōngchéngchù (General Engineering Office) managed the work of traveling camps.
For any engineering project,
it would select and appoint jǐankāngū dàchén (ministers for inspection, survey, and estimation) and chéngxiū dàchén (ministers for undertaking repairs);
after the completion of the project, jǐancháyàn dàchén (ministers for inspection and verification) would be appointed.
In the initial system,
the Nèiwùfǔ (Imperial Household Department) was established,
with former subordinate officials managing its affairs.
After entering the pass,
people from the thirty-two wèis (guards) of the Míng dynasty were attached to it,
and the Nèiguǎnlǐngchù (Internal Superintendence Office) was established,
with eight Nèiguǎnlǐngs (Internal Superintendents) appointed.
(In Shùnzhì 3rd year, four more were added;
in 11th year, eight more were added,
subordinated to the Sānqí.
In Kāngxī 24th year, four more were added;
in 30th year, three more were added;
in 34th year, three more were added.)
A cháfànchù (Tea and Meal Office) was established,
with three zǒnglǐngs (general supervisors) each,
thirty-five fànshàngréns (meal attendants),
and seventeen cháshàngréns (tea attendants).
(In Kāngxī 20th year, one fànshàngrén was appointed as acting zǒnglǐng.
In Yōngzhèng 1st year, it was stipulated that zǒnglǐngs would be granted the title of èrděng shìwèi (second-class imperial guard);
six fànshàngréns would be granted sānděng shìwèi (third-class imperial guard),
and seven would be granted lánlíng shìwèi (blue-plumed imperial guard);
three cháshàngréns would be granted sānděng shìwèi,
and four would be granted lánlíng shìwèi;
further, one acting zǒnglǐng was appointed from the cháshàng shìwèi (tea room imperial guards).
In Qiánlóng 8th year, it was stipulated that within the sānděng shìwèi, one would be granted yīděng shìwèi (first-class imperial guard) each.
In 15th year, the fànfáng (meal room) was changed to wàishànfáng (external food department).
In 24th year, zǒnglǐngs were changed to shàngshànzhèng (Director of Imperial Meals) and shàngcházhèng (Director of Imperial Tea),
and fùzǒnglǐngs (deputy general supervisors) were changed to shàngshànfù (Deputy Director of Imperial Meals) and shàngcháfù (Deputy Director of Imperial Tea).)
Ten chéngyìngzhǎngs (chief attendants) were appointed,
(In Kāngxī 61st year, one was added.
In Yōngzhèng 1st year, one was added.)
and three páozhǎngs (chief cooks).
(In Kāngxī 56th year, six were added;
in 61st year, one was added.
In Yōngzhèng 1st year, two were added.)
and zhīzàoguān (weaving officials) for Sūzhōu, Jiāngníng, and Hángzhōu.
(In Guāngxù 30th year, the one for Jiāngníng was abolished.)
In Shùnzhì 11th year,
the Bùbù (Board of Works) was ordered to establish the shísān yámén (Thirteen Departments),

setting up eight jiāns (superintendencies): Sīlǐ (Ceremonial Department), Yùyòng (Imperial Utensils Department), Yùmǎ (Imperial Stables Department), Nèiguān (Eunuch Affairs Department), Shàngyī (Imperial Clothing Department), Shàngshàn (Imperial Meals Department), Shàngbǎo (Imperial Seals Department), and Sīshè (Arrangements Department);
and three sī (offices): Shàngfāng (Imperial Storehouse Office), Xīxīn (Firewood Office), and Zhōnggǔ (Bell and Drum Office);
and two jú (bureaus): Bīngzhàng (Weapons Bureau) and Zhīrǎn (Weaving and Dyeing Bureau);
and the Sānqí Niúyángqúnmùchù (Three Banners Cattle and Sheep Herding Office),
with six yuánwàilángs (assistant directors) appointed.

six yuánwàilángs,

and one cuīzǒng (chief collector).

with three lángzhōngs (directors) appointed,

six yuánwàilángs,
(In Guāngxù 30th year, one was abolished.)
and eight cuīzǒngs (chief collectors).
(There were frequent additions and reductions during the Kāngxī reign.
In Jiāqìng 11th year, it was decided to retain five cuīzhǎngs with official hats.)
In 18th year,
the Yùyòngjiān (Imperial Utensils Department) established four treasuries: Yín (Silver), Pí (Leather), Duàn (Silk), and Yī (Clothing),
with three lángzhōngs (directors) appointed,
eight yuánwàilángs (assistant directors),
and forty kùshǐs (treasury keepers).
(In Kāngxī 9th year, twenty were added;
in 14th year, twenty-four were added;
the following year, four were abolished;
in 28th year, twelve were added.
In Qiánlóng 12th year, twelve were promoted to fùsīkù (deputy treasury keepers).)
In the first year of Kāngxī's reign,
the inner eunuchs Wú Liángfǔ and his associates were executed.
The Nèiwùfǔ was re-established with the Bāoyī of the Three Banners.
The Shàngshànjiān was reorganized into the Cǎipǔ Yámén,
with three Lángzhōng positions established.
(One was eliminated in the 38th year.)

(One was eliminated in the 61st year.)
Four Cuīzǒng were established.

with three Lángzhōng positions established.
(One was eliminated in the 38th year.)
Six Yuánwàiláng were established.
(Two were added in the 16th year.
Two were eliminated in the 30th year of Guāngxù's reign.)
Twelve Wúpǐnjí Kùzhǎng were established.
(Two were added in the 35th year.
Three were added in the 3rd year of Yōngzhèng's reign,
and one was added the following year.
Eight Kùshǒu and Nèifùkùzhǎng were subsequently added.
Later, these were changed to twelve Kùzhǎng and twelve Fùkùzhǎng respectively,
and one Pàozuò Kùzhǎng and one Fùkùzhǎng each.)
One Bāpǐn Cuīzǒng was established.
(Added in the 4th year of Yōngzhèng's reign.
Wúpǐnjí.
One Cuīzǒng was established,
and three Wěishǔ were added from among the Lǐngcuī.
In the 24th year of Qiánlóng's reign, the Wěishǔ Cuīzǒng were changed to Wěishǔ Sījiàng.)
Fifty-nine Kùshǒu were established.
(Eight were added in the 35th year.)
Also, Zǒngguǎndàchén were established,
who also held the ranks of Gōng or Qīng,
with no dedicated positions.
In the 3rd year,
six Yuánwàiláng for the Qiánliáng Yámén were established.
(Four were merged into the Shènxíng Sī in the 2nd year of Xiánfēng's reign.)
In the 9th year,
each of the four Kù established two Liùpǐn Sīkù.
In the 12th year,
two Kùzhǎng for the Yùyàofáng were established.
The following year,
the Zǒngguǎndàchén also oversaw the Nèisānyuàn.
In the 16th year,
one Tángzhǔshì was established.
The Yùyòngjiān was reorganized into the Guǎngchúsī,
the Xuānhuīyuàn into the Huìjīsī,
the Lǐyíyuàn into the Zhǎngyísī,
and the Niúyángqúnmùchù was merged into it.
Two Zhǎngguǒ were established,
and twelve Guǒshàngrén.
The Shàngfāngyuàn became the Shènxíngsī,
the Cǎipǔ Yámén became the Dūyúsī,
and the Nèigōngbù became the Yíngzàosī.
In the 23rd year,
the Qìngfēngsī was further separated from the Zhǎngyísī,
with two Lángzhōng established.
(One was merged into the Níngshòugōng in the 40th year of Qiánlóng's reign.
One was added again in the 57th year.)
These were the Seven Sī.
By this point, the eunuchs' power had entirely reverted to the Fǔ.
In this year, twenty Nèifùguǎnlǐng were established.
(Four were added in the 24th year,
three in the 30th year,
and three in the 34th year.)
In the 25th year,
the Gānròukù was established in the Cháfànfáng,
with one Kùzhǎng.
(One was added in the 30th year,
two in the 58th year.
One was added in the 5th year of Yōngzhèng's reign,
and one in the 12th year.)
In the 28th year,
the Cí and Chá Kù were established in the Guǎngchúsī,
each with two Yuánwàiláng,
two Sīkù.
(The Six Kù had a total of twelve, including the old ones.
Six were eliminated in the 30th year of Guāngxù's reign.)
Six Jiàngyì Cuīzǒng were established.
(Two Mǎibàn Cuīzǒng were added in the 2nd year of Qiánlóng's reign,
and in the 24th year, the Mǎibàn Cuīzǒng were changed to Cuīzhǎng,
and the Jiàngyì Cuīzǒng to Sījiàng.)
Four Wúpǐnjí Cuīzǒng were established.
(Changed to Fùcuīzhǎng in the 24th year of Qiánlóng's reign.)
These were the Six Kù.
The following year,
the Wénshūguǎn was reorganized into the Wǔyīngdiàn Xiūshūchù,
with six Jiānzàoguān established.
(Eliminated in the 2nd year of Yōngzhèng's reign,
restored in the 4th year.
In the 47th year of Qiánlóng's reign, the Zhèngjiānzào was designated as Yuánwàiláng,
and the Fùjiānzào as Fùnèiguǎnlǐng.)
Four Jiānzàoguān for the Yùshūchù were established.
(Two were added in the 46th year.
Eliminated in the 2nd year of Yōngzhèng's reign.
One was established in the 8th year.
In the 47th year of Qiánlóng's reign, the Jiānzào was designated as Sīkù.)
In the 25th year,
the Cháitànkù was established in Chàngchūnyuán,
with two Wúpǐnjí Kùzhǎng
and eight Kùshǒu.
In the 42nd year,
one Tánglángzhōng was established.
(Qí Sūlè was appointed as the Fēnsī of the Yǒngdìng Hé,
but the position was not refilled after his promotion.)
In the 45th year,
two Fùzhǎngguǒ for the Zhǎngyísī were established.
In the 60th year,
the Guānfángzūkù was established,
with one Kùzhǎng.
In the 1st year of Yōngzhèng's reign,
the Qiánliáng Yámén was established,
with one Lángzhōng
and ten Tángsī Wěishǔ Zhǔshì.
(Eliminated in the 12th year.
Restored in the 22nd year of Qiánlóng's reign.
One Tángshàng was added in the 4th year of Jiāqìng's reign.
Eliminated in the 30th year of Guāngxù's reign.
One from Qìngfēngsī was retained.)
The following year,
the Yǎngxīndiàn Zàobànchù was established,
with four Liùpǐn Kùzhǎng.
(Two were added in the 30th year of Qiánlóng's reign.
Four were added in the 4th year of Jiāqìng's reign.
Four were eliminated in the 30th year of Guāngxù's reign.)
One Yùshūchù Kùzhǎng was established.
(Two were added in the 4th year of Qiánlóng's reign.
In the 47th year, one was changed to Fùjiānzào.)
One Jīchá Yùshǐ was established.
(Eliminated in the 11th year.
In the 3rd year of Qiánlóng's reign, surveillance was changed to be carried out by personnel dispatched from the Dūcháyuàn.)
In the 3rd year,
one Wúpǐnjí Cuīzǒng for the Qiánliáng Yámén was established.
(One was added in the 7th year.
One was added in the 4th year of Qiánlóng's reign.
Three Fùcuīzǒng were further added from among the Lǐngcuī.
Changed to Fùcuīzhǎng in the 24th year.
In the 3rd year of Jiāqìng's reign, three Dǐngdài Cuīzhǎng and three Fùcuīzhǎng were retained.)
In the 4th year,
one Cháfànfáng Zhǔshì was established.
The responsibility for handling fresh fish was transferred from the Dūyúsī to the Zhǎngyísī,
and one Cuīzǒng was added.
(One was added in the 8th year.
In the 8th year of Qiánlóng's reign, two Chéngbàn Jiāngsuàn Lǐngcuī and Nèifùcuīzǒng were added.
In the 24th year, their names were changed to Fùcuīzhǎng.)
In the 13th year,
a Zuòbàn Tánglángzhōng was re-established,
and the Dūcuīsuǒ was eliminated and its functions merged.
In the 1st year of Qiánlóng's reign,
one Qiánliáng Yámén Zhǔshì was established.
(Transferred to Níngshòugōng in the 40th year.)
In the 5th year,
one Zàobànchù Zhuānguǎn Kùwùguān and one Zàobàn Shìwùguān were established,
and one Yùyàofáng Zhǔshì was established.
In the 7th year,
two Yùshūchù Kùzhǎng were established.
(One was added in the 8th year,
one in the 15th year,
and two in the 44th year.)
One Guānfángzūkù Wěishǔ Zhǔshì was established.
(Later eliminated.)
In the 12th year,
two Wěishǔ Sīkù were established for each of the Six Kù,
later changed to Fùsīkù.
In the 23rd year,
the Zàobànchù Kùwù Shìwùguān were reorganized as Lángzhōng,
one for each,
two Yuánwàiláng,
one Zhǔshì and one Wěishǔ Zhǔshì each,
and one Yùyàofáng Wěishǔ Zhǔshì.
In the 26th year,
one Zǒnglǐ Gōngchéngchù Wěishǔ Zhǔshì was established.
(Later overseen concurrently by Sīyuán.)
In the 40th year,
two Lángzhōng and two Yuánwàiláng for the Níngshòugōng were established,
and one Zhǔshì.
In the 6th year of Xiánfēng's reign,
four Dúzhùguān were added.
Traditionally,
the Nèifǔ Dúzhùguān were appointed by requesting Zànlǐláng from the Tàichángsì;
only then were fixed positions established.
In the 1st year of Xuāntǒng's reign,
to avoid the imperial taboo, the Zhǎngyísī was renamed Zhǎnglǐ.
In the initial system,
for the Sīlì, Xuānhuī, Lǐyí, Shàngfāng and other Yuàn,
one Zǒnglǐ
and one Zuǒ and Yòu Xiélǐ each were established.
For the Yùyòng, Yùmǎ, Shàngyī, Shàngshàn and other Jiān,
one Dūguǎn
and one Zuǒ and Yòu Fùguǎn each were established.
For the Shàngbǎo and Xīxīn two Sī,
one Dūzhī
and one Zuǒ and Yòu Cānzhī each were established.
For the Sīshè and Bīngzhàng two Jú,
one Zǒngxiá
and one Zuǒ and Yòu Zuǒxiá each were established.
For the Wénshūguǎn,
one Chéngzhì
and one Zuǒ and Yòu Qiānchéng each were established.
Later, all these were eliminated.
The Grand Manager (zǒngguǎn) for the Eastern Tombs (Dōnglíng) affiliated with Pánshān: one person.
(Of rank cōngwǔpǐn.
Established in the 29th year of Qiánlóng.) Commanders (qiānzǒng) for the inner perimeter: seven people,
(of rank liùpǐn.) Acting Commanders (wěishǔ qiānzǒng): seven people
(of ranks qī, bāpǐn used concurrently.)
Commanders for the outer barracks: one person.
Corporals (bǎzǒng): seven people.
(Stationed at Pánshān, Yànjiāo, Báijiàn, Táohuā Sì, Lóngfú Sì, Dàxīng Zhuāng, and Gējí Shān.
The Grand Manager for the Western Tombs (Xīlíng) affiliated with Huángxīnzhuāng: one person.
(Established in the 29th year of Qiánlóng.)
Commanders for the inner perimeter, Acting Commanders, and Corporals for the outer barracks: four people each.
(Stationed at Huángxīnzhuāng, Bànbì Diàn, Qiūlán Cūn, and Liánggē Zhuāng.
The Grand Manager for the Hot Springs (Tāngquán): one person.
(Established in the 54th year of Kāngxī as an eighth-rank Grand Leader (zǒnglǐng).
Re-established in the 6th year of Qiánlóng.) Park Administrator (yuànchéng): one person,
(holding a sixth-rank title but drawing an eighth-rank salary.
Established in the 17th year of Jiāqìng.) Assistant Park Administrator (yuànfù): one person
(not yet entered into the official ranks.)
Commanders for the inner perimeter: six people.
Acting Commanders: six people.
Corporals for the outer barracks: nine people.
(Stationed at Shícáo, Sānjiā Diàn, Mìyún Xiàn, Yàotíng, Luójiā Qiáo, and Huáiróu Xiàn.
All Commanders from Pánshān downwards
were established during the Qiánlóng period.)
The Grand Manager for Rèhé: one person.
(Established in the 42nd year of Kāngxī.
In the 16th year of Qiánlóng, designated as an extra Department Director (lángzhōng) of this prefecture.
In the 21st year, the title was changed to Company Commander (zuǒlǐng).
In the 35th year, given a fourth-rank title.
In the 30th year of Guāngxù, it was abolished and subsumed under the General-in-Chief (dūtǒng).)
The Deputy Grand Manager: one person.
(Established in the 21st year of Qiánlóng,
designated as a Department Director title.
In the 35th year, three people were added,
their rank set at fifth-rank;
later changed to Assistant Park Administrator.
Abolished in the 30th year of Guāngxù.)
Park Administrators: four people.
(Established in the 54th year of Qiánlóng by changing Assistant Park Administrators.)
Assistant Park Administrators: four people.
(Established after the 35th year of Qiánlóng with three people;
in the 45th year, one person was added.
In the 54th year, changed to Park Administrator.
After the 18th year of Jiāqìng,
it was re-established by changing ten Commanders.
In the 20th year, one person was added.
In the 24th year, it was stipulated that they could be interchanged and supplemented with Commanders.
From then on, the number of personnel had no fixed system.
In the 18th year of Dàoguāng, four people were abolished,
and in the 28th year, another four were abolished.)
Commanders for the inner perimeter: eighteen people.
(Established in the 9th year of Qiánlóng.
In the 12th year of Dàoguāng, two people were abolished,
and in the 18th year, another two were abolished.)
Acting Commanders: twenty-eight people.
(In the 9th year of Dàoguāng, one seventh-rank person was abolished.
In the 18th year, twelve seventh-rank and twelve eighth-rank people were abolished.

Commanders and Acting Commanders are stationed at Liǎngjiānfáng, Bākèshíyíng, Chángshānyù, Wángjiāyíng, Kālāhétún, Diàoyútái, Huángtǔkǎn, Zhōngguān, Shíbālǐtái, Tàibōluòhétún, Zhāngsānyíng, and Jíěrhālāgōngyuán.)
From the Grand Manager downwards, they are in charge of guarding the temporary imperial residences
and inspecting the furnishings.
From the Commander downwards, they are in charge of overseeing the artifacts,
inspecting the inner perimeter,
and directing the sweeping of the riverbanks.
Grand Minister for Managing Affairs (zǒngguǎn shìwù dàchén) of Yuánmíng Yuán: no personnel limit.
(Specially appointed.)
Its subordinates: Department Director: one person.
Secretary (zhǔshì): one person.
Assistant Director (yuánwàiláng): two people.
Park Administrators: six people,
(of ranks liù, qīpǐn used concurrently.)
Assistant Park Administrators: sixteen people,
(of ranks qī, bāpǐn used concurrently.)
Acting Assistant Park Administrators: thirteen people.
(Holding a ninth-rank title.)
Acting Warehouse Manager (wěishǔ kùzhǎng) for the silver treasury and artifact treasury: one person.
Warehouse Guard (kùshǒu): sixteen people.
Scribe (bǐtiěshì): fourteen people.
In the 1st year of Yōngzhèng,
a Grand Minister was established.
(There were also officials assisting in affairs,
either appointed by imperial decree
or specially commissioned,
with no fixed quota.)
The following year,
six Grand Leaders were established.
(In the 16th year of Qiánlóng,
after Chángchūn Yuán was completed,
one sixth-rank person was established.
In the 24th year, changed to Park Administrator.
In the 32nd year, one sixth-rank person for Xīchūn Yuán was added.
In the 46th year, one seventh-rank person for Chūnxī Yuàn was added.
In the 7th year of Jiāqìng, one person from Chūnxī Yuàn was abolished and moved to Xīchūn Yuán.
In the 16th year, one seventh-rank person from Chàngchūn Yuán was changed to Assistant Park Administrator for this garden.
In the 10th year of Xiánfēng, two sixth-rank people were abolished.
In the 30th year of Guāngxù, one sixth-rank person was abolished.)
Twelve Deputy Grand Leaders (fùzǒnglǐng).
(In the 8th year of Qiánlóng, one seventh-rank and one eighth-rank person were added.
In the 16th year, one seventh-rank and one eighth-rank person for Chángchūn Yuán were added.
In the 24th year, changed to Assistant Park Administrator.
In the 39th year, one seventh-rank person for Qǐchūn Yuán was added.
In the 45th year, one eighth-rank person for Chūnxī Yuàn was added.
In the 7th year of Jiāqìng, one person from Chūnxī Yuàn was abolished
and converted into an official vacancy for this garden.
In the 16th year, one eighth-rank person from Chàngchūn Yuán was again abolished
and converted into an official vacancy for this garden.
In the 2nd year of Dàoguāng, four people from Chàngchūn Yuán were abolished and moved to Qǐchūn Yuán.
In the 10th year of Xiánfēng, two seventh-rank and three eighth-rank people were abolished.
In the 30th year of Guāngxù, one seventh-rank and two eighth-rank people were abolished.)
In the 7th year,
the Grand Leaders were designated as sixth-rank, wearing blue feathers.
(Later, sixth and seventh ranks were used concurrently.)
Deputy Grand Leaders were of seventh and eighth ranks, half the number.
In the 6th year of Qiánlóng,
two Acting Deputy Grand Leaders were established.
(In the 16th year, five were added.
In the 32nd year, changed to Acting Assistant Park Administrators,
and nine more were added.
In the 16th year of Jiāqìng, two were added.
In the 10th year of Xiánfēng, two were abolished.
In the 30th year of Guāngxù, three were abolished.)
In the 8th year,
one Secretary was established.
In the 14th year,
one Warehouse Manager was established,
(in the 38th year, designated as sixth-rank,
and one seventh-rank person was added.
All were abolished in the 30th year of Guāngxù.)
One Acting Warehouse Manager,
(in the 32nd year, one was added,
in the 38th year, one was abolished.)
Six Warehouse Guards.
(In the 46th year, twelve were added.
In the 10th year of Xiánfēng, two were abolished.)
In the 22nd year,
one Acting Secretary was added.
(Abolished in the 30th year of Guāngxù.)
The following year,
one Department Director and one Assistant Director assisting in affairs were designated.
In the 2nd year of Dàoguāng,
the Department Director of Chàngchūn Yuán was changed to the Department Director of Qǐchūn Yuán,
(abolished in the 10th year of Xiánfēng.)
And its Assistant Director, one person, was abolished,
ordering him to exclusively manage Chángchūn Yuán affairs.
Grand Minister for Managing Affairs of Chàngchūn Yuán: no personnel limit.
(Specially appointed.)
Its subordinates: Park Administrators: three people,
(of ranks liù, qīpǐn used concurrently.)
Assistant Park Administrators: five people,
(of eighth-rank.)
Acting Assistant Park Administrators: six people,
(holding a ninth-rank title.)
Scribes: three people.
During the Kāngxī period,
one Department Director was established,
(in the 2nd year of Dàoguāng, abolished and moved to Qǐchūn Yuán.)
Three eighth-rank Grand Leaders,
(in the 43rd year, two for Xīhuā Yuán were added.
In the 5th year of Qiánlóng, one was abolished and moved to Jìngmíng Yuán.
In the 24th year, changed to Park Administrator.
In the 32nd year, one sixth-rank and three seventh-rank people were appointed.
In the 16th year of Jiāqìng, one seventh-rank person was abolished.)
Ten Grand Leaders without rank.
(In the 43rd year, one for Xīhuā Yuán was added.
In the 5th year of Qiánlóng, one was abolished and moved to Jìngmíng Yuán.
In the 32nd year, changed to Acting Assistant Park Administrators,

In the 12th year of Jiāqìng, two were abolished and moved to Yuánmíng Yuán.
In the 2nd year of Dàoguāng, four were abolished and moved to Qǐchūn Yuán.)
In the 29th year,
a Grand Minister was established.
In the 32nd year of Qiánlóng,
six eighth-rank Assistant Park Administrators were established.
(In the 16th year of Jiāqìng, one was abolished and moved to Yuánmíng Yuán.)
The Grand Ministers-in-charge of the Yíhéyuán, Jìngmíngyuán, and Jìngyíyuán,
with no limit to their number.
(Specially appointed.)
Their subordinates include: one Lángzhōng,
three Yuánwàiláng,
seventeen Yuànchéng
(eleven for Yíhéyuán,
three each for Jìngmíngyuán and Jìngyíyuán,
all concurrently holding sixth and seventh ranks),
twenty-three Yuànfù
(thirteen for Yíhéyuán,
six for Jìngmíngyuán,
four for Jìngyíyuán,
all concurrently holding sixth and seventh ranks),
seven acting Yuànfù
(three for Jìngmíngyuán,
four for Jìngyíyuán,
all with ninth-rank titles),
and fourteen Bǐtiēshì.
In the fifteenth year of Qiánlóng,
Wēngshān was renamed Wànshòushān,
and an imperial traveling palace was built there.
(Jīnhǎi was renamed Kūnmínghú.
The following year, it was renamed Qīngyīyuán.
In the fourteenth year of Guāngxù, it was renamed Yíhéyuán.)
One acting Zǒngcuī with an eighth-rank title was established.
(In the forty-eighth year, promoted to sixth-rank Yuànchéng.)
In the sixteenth year,
a Grand Minister concurrently managing Jìngmíngyuán and Jìngyíyuán affairs was established,
along with one sixth-rank Zǒnglǐ.
(In the nineteenth year, two more sixth-rank officials were added.
In the twenty-fourth year, they were changed to Yuànchéng.
In the fifth year of Jiāqìng, one was abolished and transferred to Jìngmíngyuán.
In the tenth year, two more sixth-rank officials were added.
After the fourteenth year of Guāngxù,
four sixth-rank and six seventh-rank officials from Jìngmíngyuán were transferred
and continuously established as the quota for this garden.
In the thirtieth year, two sixth-rank and two seventh-rank officials were abolished.)
Two seventh-rank and two eighth-rank Fùzǒnglǐ were established.
(In the eighteenth year, six more seventh-rank officials were added.
In the twenty-fourth year, they were changed to Yuànfù.
In the tenth year of Xiánfēng, one eighth-rank official was abolished.
After the fourteenth year of Guāngxù,
eight eighth-rank officials from Jìngmíngyuán were transferred
and continuously established as the quota for this garden.
In the thirtieth year, four eighth-rank officials were abolished.)
One eighth-rank Cuīzǒng was established.
(In the twenty-fourth year, changed to Cuīzhǎng.
In the forty-sixth year, promoted to sixth-rank Yuànchéng.
In the forty-eighth year, fixed at sixth-rank.)
In the eighteenth year,
twelve acting Fùzǒnglǐ were established.
(Soon after, six were abolished.
In the tenth year of Xiánfēng, two were abolished.
In the thirtieth year of Guāngxù, four were abolished.)
In the twenty-second year,
one Yuánwàiláng was established,
concurrently overseeing Jìngmíngyuán affairs.
(In the twenty-sixth year, one more was added.)
In the fourth year of Jiāqìng,
one Lángzhōng was established,
assisting in the administration of the three gardens.
(Míngshàntáng, Guānmiàotáng, and Xīshuǎngcūn were all subordinate to him.
For the external Jiànyuǎntáng, Zǎojiàntáng, Chàngguāntáng, Jǐngmínglóu, Fènghuángdūn, Zhìjìnggé, Gēngzhītú,

the ministers would select officials from their own department to manage these affairs.)
Yùquánshān Jìngmíngyuán was initially Chéngxīnyuán.

One ungraded Zǒnglǐ was established.

In the eighth year, the rank was set at seventh-rank.
In the twenty-fourth year, changed to Yuànchéng.
In the thirty-fourth year, one more sixth-rank official was added.
In the fourth year of Jiāqìng, one more sixth-rank official was added,

Two Fùzǒnglǐ.
(In the thirtieth year of Kāngxī, one more was added.
In the fifth year of Qiánlóng, one more was added.
In the ninth year, one was abolished and transferred to Jìngyíyuán.
In the eighteenth year, the rank was set at eighth-rank.
In the twenty-fourth year, one more eighth-rank official was added,
and changed to Yuànfù.
In the thirty-fourth year, two more eighth-rank officials were added.
In the fifth year of Jiāqìng, two seventh-rank officials were added.
In the twenty-third year of Dàoguāng, one eighth-rank official was abolished.
In the tenth year of Xiánfēng, one eighth-rank official was abolished.
In the thirteenth year of Guāngxù, eight more eighth-rank officials were added.
Later, they were abolished and transferred to Yíhéyuán.)
In the twenty-fourth year of Qiánlóng,
two acting Fùzǒnglǐ were established.
Two Sānshǒu.
(In the thirty-fourth year, two more were added.
In the fifth year of Jiāqìng, one more was added.
In the twenty-third year of Dàoguāng, two were abolished.)
Jìngyíyuán was initially Xiāngshān Xínggōng.
(It was renamed in the twelfth year of Qiánlóng.)
In the ninth year of Qiánlóng,
one Yuánwàiláng was established.
(Abolished in the twenty-third year of Dàoguāng.)
Two Fùzǒnglǐ.
(In the twenty-fourth year, changed to Yuànfù.)
In the tenth year,
one eighth-rank Zǒnglǐ was established.
(In the twelfth year, one more was added.
In the sixteenth year, the rank was set at seventh-rank,
and one more was added.
In the twenty-fourth year, changed to Yuànchéng.
In the thirty-fourth year, one more seventh-rank official was added.

The Běi'ān Vault is in charge of imperial saddles and bridles, umbrellas and parasols, and tents;
the Umbrella House, Tent House, and Saddle Panel Workshop are subordinate to it.

the Tanned Leather Workshop is subordinate to it.
The Jiǎ Vault is in charge of helmets and armor, swords and weapons, flags and banners, and implements;
the Leather Workshop is subordinate to it.
The Zhān Vault is in charge of bows and arrows, boots and shoes, and felt pieces;
the Hat Maker's Workshop, Boot Leather Workshop, Felt Workshop, Shāhé Felt Workshop, Cap Workshop, and Miscellaneous Works Workshop (below the Cap Workshop, one foreman each is established)

The Qīng manage the prohibitions of the imperial gardens and parks,
repairing them in due course for imperial visits.
Officials from Lángzhōng downwards are responsible for managing the various sections of the imperial gardens, parks, and waterways.
The Zhāigōng is in charge of furnishings and cleaning.
The Dàotián Chǎng is responsible for supplying rice and grain to the inner court,
and concurrently for collecting land taxes.
The officials of the Nányuàn are in charge of collecting land taxes in the Nányuàn
and managing garden affairs.

the thirteen yámén were granted official ranks for their tài​jiàn.
(In the eighteenth year, this was abolished,
and the Nèi​wù​fǔ dà​chén was put in overall charge.) In the sixteenth year of Kāngxī,

with a zǒng​guǎn and a fù​zǒng​guǎn.
